Q171.name: wiki
Q171.blurb: Wikipedia, a free wiki content encyclopedia, is launched (Wikipedia Day).

Q264.name: Hurricane Sandy
aliases: Effects of Hurricane Sandy in the United States
Hurricane Sandy effects in the United States
Hurricane Sandy in the United States
Preparation and impact of Hurricane Sandy in the United States
Q264.blurb: Hurricane Sandy hits the east coast of the United States, killing hundreds, while leaving nearly $70 billion in damages and causing major power outages.

Q276.name: Eurovision Song Contest
aliases: Grand Prix Eurovision de la Chanson
Relegation in the Eurovision Song Contest
Semi-finals in the Eurovision Song Contest
Q276.blurb: The first Eurovision Song Contest is held in Lugano, Switzerland.

Q361.name: World War I
aliases: The War to End All Wars
Economic costs of World War I
Economic effects of World War I
Economic impact of World War I
Interlocking alliances of World War I
The Outbreak of World War I
Q361.blurb: World War I: The Battle of Gallipoli concludes with an Ottoman Empire victory when the last Allied forces are evacuated from the peninsula.

Q362.name: World War II
aliases: The Origins and Commencement of World War II
Q362.blurb: World War II: The German Luftwaffe launches Operation Bodenplatte, a massive, but failed, attempt to knock out Allied air power in northern Europe in a single blow.

Q443.name: Ich bin ein Berliner
aliases: Remarks of President John F. Kennedy at the Rudolph Wilde Platz
Remarks at the Rudolph Wilde Platz
Q443.blurb: Cold War: U.S. President John F. Kennedy gives his "Ich bin ein Berliner" speech, underlining the support of the United States for democratic West Germany shortly after Soviet-supported East Germany erected the Berlin Wall.

Q486.name: Chernobyl disaster
aliases: Meltdown at the Chernobyl atomic electrical station
Q486.blurb: The Chernobyl disaster occurs in the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic.

Q488.name: atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
aliases: American nuclear bombing of the Japanese cities Hiroshima and Nagasaki
Atomic bombing of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
Atomic bombing of Nagasaki and Hiroshima
Atomic bombings against the cities of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
Atomic bombings of Nagasaki and Hiroshima
Atomic bombings on hiroshima and nagasaki
Bombing of Hiroshima and Nagasaki in World War II
Dropping of the atomic bomb on Hiroshima and Nagasaki
Dropping of the atomic bomb on Japan
Nuclear attacks on Hiroshima and Nagasaki
Nuclear bombing of Nagasaki and Hiroshima
Nuclear bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
The WW2 Bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
The atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
Q488.blurb: World War II: Nagasaki is devastated when an atomic bomb, Fat Man, is dropped by the United States B-29 Bockscar. Thirty-five thousand people are killed outright, including 23,200–28,200 Japanese war workers, 2,000 Korean forced workers, and 150 Japanese soldiers.

Q844.name: James Bond
aliases: List of actors who portayed James Bond
List of actors who portrayed James Bond
Q844.blurb: The first of the James Bond film series, based on the novels by Ian Fleming, Dr. No, is released in Britain.

Q886.name: The Simpsons
aliases: Criticism of the declining quality of The Simpsons
Criticisms of the declining quality of The Simpsons
Culturally significance phrases from The Simpsons
Culturally significant neologisms from The Simpsons
Culturally significant phrases from The Simpsons
Culturally significant words and phrases from The Simpsons
List of made-up words in The Simpsons
List of neologisms and phrases on The Simpsons
List of neologisms in The Simpsons
List of neologisms on The Simpsons
Q886.blurb: The Simpsons premieres on television with the episode "Simpsons Roasting on an Open Fire".

Q1077.name: Star Trek: The Original Series
Q1077.blurb: The landmark American science fiction television series Star Trek premieres with its first-aired episode, "The Man Trap".

Q1092.name: Star Trek
aliases: History of the Star Trek franchise
Philosophy and Religion in Star Trek
Q1092.blurb: The science fiction show Star Trek made its American premiere with "The Man Trap", launching a media franchise that has since created a cult phenomenon and has influenced the design of many current technologies.

Q1932.name: space race
Q1932.blurb: Space Race: Soviet spacecraft Soyuz 4 and Soyuz 5 perform the first-ever docking of crewed spacecraft in orbit, the first-ever transfer of crew from one space vehicle to another, and the only time such a transfer was accomplished with a space walk.

Q2305.name: Franklin's lost expedition
Q2305.blurb: Captain Sir John Franklin and his ill-fated Arctic expedition depart from Greenhithe, England.

Q2487.name: Thirty Years' War
aliases: Danish intervention in the Thirty Years' War
French intervention in the Thirty Years' War
Q2487.blurb: Thirty Years' War: Bavaria, Cologne, France and Sweden sign the Truce of Ulm.

Q2763.name: The Holocaust
Q2763.blurb: The Holocaust: Nazi Germany begins deporting Jews from the Łódź Ghetto to Chełmno extermination camp.

Q3588.name: European Revolutions of 1848
aliases: Nationalist revolts in Europe in the 1840s
Q3588.blurb: Revolutions of 1848: A rebellion arises in Milan which in five days of street fighting drove Marshal Radetzky and his Austrian soldiers from the city.

Q3699.name: Revolutions of 1848 in the German states
aliases: The Revolutions of 1848 in the German states
Q3699.blurb: The German revolutions of 1848–1849 begin in Vienna.

Q4373.name: Battle of White Mountain
Q4373.blurb: The Battle of White Mountain takes place near Prague, ending in a decisive Catholic victory in only two hours.

Q4411.name: Battle of Valmy
Q4411.blurb: French troops stop an allied invasion of France at the Battle of Valmy.

Q4576.name: Marshall Plan
Q4576.blurb: The Marshall Plan, an economic recovery program established by U.S. Secretary of State George Marshall to assist the post-World War II re-building of Europe, was signed into law.

Q4670.name: Moscow theater hostage crisis
Q4670.blurb: Approximately 50 Chechen terrorists and 150 hostages die when Russian special forces troops storm a theater building in Moscow, which had been occupied by the terrorists during a musical performance three days before.

Q6076.name: Kemerovo Oblast
Q6076.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 593 crashes into the Kuznetsk Alatau mountain, Kemerovo Oblast, Russia, killing 75.

Q6271.name: Second Punic War
Q6271.blurb: Second Punic War: Commanded by Hannibal, the Carthaginians ambushed a Roman army at the Battle of Lake Trasimene, capturing or killing 25,000 men.

Q6286.name: First Punic War
Q6286.blurb: First Punic War: Battle of the Aegates: The Romans sink the Carthaginian fleet bringing the First Punic War to an end.

Q6534.name: French Revolution
aliases: French Revolution up to the storming of the Bastille
Q6534.blurb: French Revolution: After being found guilty of high treason by the National Convention, Louis XVI was guillotined in Paris.

Q6539.name: Storming of the Bastille
Q6539.blurb: Storming of the Bastille in Paris. This event escalates the widespread discontent into the French Revolution. Bastille Day is still celebrated annually in France.

Q6683.name: Mexican-American War
aliases: War crimes in the Mexican-American War
War crimes in the Mexican–American War
Q6683.blurb: Mexican–American War: The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo is signed.

Q6740.name: Burchardi flood
Q6740.blurb: The Burchardi flood kills around 15,000 in North Friesland, Denmark and Germany.

Q6743.name: May 68
aliases: Beneath the Paving Stones, the Beach
Beneath the paving stones, the beach!
Under the Paving Stones, the Beach
Under the paving stones, the beach!
Q6743.blurb: Charles de Gaulle reappears publicly after his flight to Baden-Baden, West Germany, and dissolves the French National Assembly by a radio appeal. Immediately after, less than one million of his supporters march on the Champs-Élysées in Paris. This is the turning point of the May 1968 events in France.

Q6752.name: Saint Marcellus's flood
Q6752.blurb: Saint Marcellus's flood kills at least 25,000 people on the shores of the North Sea.

Q7310.name: Nazism
aliases: Nazism in relation to other concepts
Q7310.blurb: World War II: The Nazis arrest the members of the White Rose movement.

Q8080.name: 1896 Summer Olympics
aliases: The Games of the I Olympiad
Q8080.blurb: Summer Olympics: The Olympic marathon is run ending with the victory of Greek athlete Spyridon Louis.

Q8105.name: 1906 Intercalated Games
Q8105.blurb: The 1906 Intercalated Games open in Athens.

Q8118.name: 1912 Summer Olympics
Q8118.blurb: Thirty years after his death, the International Olympic Committee presented commemorative medals to the family of American athlete Jim Thorpe, who had been stripped of his gold medals for playing semi-professional baseball before the 1912 Summer Olympics.

Q8128.name: 1920 Summer Olympics
Q8128.blurb: The 1920 Summer Olympics, having started four months earlier, officially open in Antwerp, Belgium, with the newly adopted Olympic flag and the Olympic oath being raised and taken at the Opening Ceremony for the first time in Olympic history.

Q8132.name: 1924 Summer Olympics
Q8132.blurb: Paavo Nurmi wins the 1,500 m and 5,000 m events at the Paris Olympics, with just an hour between the two races.

Q8150.name: 1936 Summer Olympics
aliases: The Games of the XI Olympiad
Q8150.blurb: The Olympics open in Berlin with a ceremony presided over by Adolf Hitler.

Q8403.name: 1948 Summer Olympics
Q8403.blurb: Olympic Games: The Games of the XIV Olympiad: After a hiatus of 12 years caused by World War II, the first Summer Olympics to be held since the 1936 Summer Olympics in Berlin, open in London.

Q8407.name: 1952 Summer Olympics
Q8407.blurb: Opening of the Summer Olympics in Helsinki, Finland.

Q8411.name: 1956 Summer Olympics
Q8411.blurb: At the Melbourne Olympics, 14-year-old swimmer Sandra Morgan became the youngest Australian to win an Olympic gold medal.

Q8414.name: Amundsen's South Pole expedition
Q8414.blurb: Roald Amundsen's South Pole expedition makes landfall on the eastern edge of the Ross Ice Shelf.

Q8415.name: 1960 Summer Olympics
Q8415.blurb: The Games of the XVII Olympiad commence in Rome, Italy.

Q8420.name: 1964 Summer Olympics
aliases: Tokyo bid for the 1964 Summer Olympics
Q8420.blurb: The Tokyo Summer Olympics opening ceremony is the first to be relayed live by satellites.

Q8429.name: 1968 Summer Olympics
Q8429.blurb: At the Summer Olympics in Mexico City, American athlete Bob Beamon (pictured) achieved a distance of 8.90 m (29.2 ft) in the long jump event, setting a world record that stood for 23 years.

Q8438.name: 1972 Summer Olympics
Q8438.blurb: The Games of the XX Olympiad open in Munich, West Germany.

Q8444.name: 1976 Summer Olympics
aliases: Games of the XXI Olympiad Montreal 1976
Long Life to the Montréal Games
Q8444.blurb: The opening of the Summer Olympics in Montreal is marred by 25 African teams boycotting the games because of New Zealand's participation. Contrary to rulings by other international sports organizations, the IOC had declined to exclude New Zealand because of their participation in South African sporting events during apartheid.

Q8450.name: 1980 Summer Olympics
Q8450.blurb: Opening of the Summer Olympics in Moscow.

Q8456.name: 1984 Summer Olympics
aliases: XXIII Olympiad of the modern era
Q8456.blurb: The Soviet Union announced the boycott of the Summer Olympics in Los Angeles, citing security concerns.

Q8531.name: 1996 Summer Olympics
Q8531.blurb: In Atlanta, United States, a pipe bomb explodes at Centennial Olympic Park during the 1996 Summer Olympics.

Q8567.name: 2008 Summer Olympics
aliases: The Games of the XXIX Olympiad
The games of the twenty-ninth olympiad
二零零八年北京夏季奥运
二零零八年北京夏季奧運
Q8567.blurb: The 29th modern summer Olympic Games take place in Beijing, China until August 24.

Q8628.name: War in the Vendée
Q8628.blurb: The Battle of Savenay: A decisive defeat of the royalist counter-revolutionaries in War in the Vendée during the French Revolution.

Q8663.name: Korean War
aliases: Initial phase of the Korean War
South Korea in the Korean War
War Between South Korea and North Korea
War between North Korea And South Korea
War to Resist America and Aid Korea
War to Resist U.S. Aggression and Aid Korea
War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea
War to Resist the United States and aid North Korea
Q8663.blurb: Korean War: Chinese and North Korean forces capture Seoul for the second time.

Q8669.name: Arab–Israeli conflict
aliases: Financial cost of the Arab-Israeli conflict
Financial cost of the Arab–Israeli conflict
Religious aspects of the Arab-Israeli conflict
Religious aspects of the Arab–Israeli conflict
Q8669.blurb: Arab–Israeli conflict: In response to a Fatah landmine incident, the Israeli military conducted a large cross-border assault on the Jordanian-controlled West Bank village of Samu.

Q8676.name: American Civil War
aliases: Civil War in the United States
Civil War of the United States
Military history of the Confederate States
Q8676.blurb: American Civil War: The Emancipation Proclamation takes effect in Confederate territory.

Q8683.name: Cold War
aliases: Confrontation between the US and the Soviet Union
The Cold War in the 1950s and 1960s
Western europe during the cold war
Q8683.blurb: Cold War: The American and British occupation zones in Allied-occupied Germany, after World War II, merge to form the Bizone, which later (with the French zone) became part of West Germany.

Q8690.name: Cultural Revolution
aliases: Great Cultural Revolution of the Proletariat
Q8690.blurb: Cultural Revolution: The Shanghai People's Commune is established following the seizure of power from local city officials by revolutionaries.

Q8698.name: Great Depression
aliases: Great Depression in the Soviet Union
The depression and the new deal
Q8698.blurb: Great Depression: President Franklin D. Roosevelt submits the Emergency Banking Act to Congress, the first of his New Deal policies.

Q8707.name: Meiji restoration
aliases: Destruction of cultural heritage during the Meiji Restoration
Q8707.blurb: Meiji Restoration in Japan: The Tokugawa shogunate is abolished; agents of Satsuma and Chōshū seize power.

Q8729.name: Russian Revolution
Q8729.blurb: Russian Revolution: Tsar Nicholas II was forced to abdicate in the February Revolution, ending three centuries of Romanov rule.

Q8736.name: Treaty of Versailles
aliases: Treaty of Peace between the Allied and Associated Powers and Germany
Q8736.blurb: The Treaty of Versailles takes effect, officially ending World War I for all combatant nations except the United States.

Q8740.name: Vietnam War
aliases: Allied war crimes during the Vietnam War
United States war crimes in Vietnam
War Against the Americans to Save the Nation
War crimes during the Vietnam War
Q8740.blurb: Vietnam War: The Viet Cong wins its first major victory, at the Battle of Ap Bac.

Q8807.name: 2002 Venezuelan coup d'état attempt
Q8807.blurb: Over two hundred thousand people march in Caracas towards the presidential palace to demand the resignation of President Hugo Chávez. Nineteen protesters are killed.

Q8951.name: Third Republic of Venezuela
Q8951.blurb: Simón Bolívar becomes President of the Third Republic of Venezuela.

Q9538.name: South American dreadnought race
Q9538.blurb: The crews of three Brazilian warships – all commissioned only months before – and several smaller vessels mutinied against perceived "slavery" being practised in the Brazilian Navy.

Q9583.name: 1924 Winter Olympics
Q9583.blurb: The 1924 Winter Olympics opens in Chamonix, in the French Alps, inaugurating the Winter Olympic Games.

Q9615.name: 1948 Winter Olympics
Q9615.blurb: The closing ceremony of the first Olympics held after World War II was held in St. Moritz, Switzerland.

Q9652.name: 1980 Winter Olympics
Q9652.blurb: At the Winter Olympics in Lake Placid, New York, the United States ice hockey team defeated the Soviet team in an unlikely victory that became known as the Miracle on Ice.

Q9664.name: 1998 Winter Olympics
Q9664.blurb: American figure skater Tara Lipinski, at the age of 15, becomes the youngest Olympic figure skating gold-medalist at the 1998 Winter Olympics in Nagano, Japan.

Q9678.name: 2014 Winter Olympics
Q9678.blurb: The International Olympic Committee bans Russia from competing at the 2018 Winter Olympics for doping at the 2014 Winter Olympics.

Q9680.name: 2018 Winter Olympics
aliases: Cayman Islands at the 2018 Winter Olympics
Q9680.blurb: Winter Olympics: Opening ceremony is performed in Pyeongchang County in South Korea.

Q9683.name: Tang dynasty
Q9683.blurb: Tang forces led by Li Shimin defeated and captured Dou Jiande at the Battle of Hulao in the civil war that followed the collapse of the Sui dynasty.

Q10806.name: September 11 attacks
aliases: 2001 attacks on the World Trade Center
9/11 terror attack of the World Trade Center
Attacks on the United States on September 11
Persons missing after the September 11, 2001 attacks
Terrorist attack in New York City on September 11, 2001
Terrorist attacks on New York and Washington
Terrorist attacks on New York, Washington, and Pennsylvania
Terrorist attacks on the 11th of September 2001
Terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center and the Pentagon
World political effects arising from the September 11, 2001 attacks
Q10806.blurb: The September 11 attacks, a series of coordinated terrorist attacks killing 2,977 people using four aircraft hijacked by 19 members of al-Qaeda. Two aircraft crash into the World Trade Center in New York City, a third crashes into The Pentagon in Arlington County, Virginia, and a fourth into a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania.

Q10818.name: 7 July 2005 London bombings
aliases: Casualties of the 7 July 2005 London bombings
Conspiracy Theories about the July 2005 London bombings
July 7, 2005 London bombings memorials and services
Rumors and conspiracy theories about the July 2005 London bombings
Rumours about the July 2005 London bombings
Rumours and conspiracy theories about the July 2005 London bombings
Secret Group of Al Qaeda's Jihad in Europe
Q10818.blurb: A series of four explosions occurs on London's transport system, killing 56 people, including four suicide bombers, and injuring over 700 others.

Q10859.name: Spanish Civil War
aliases: Bibliography of the Spanish Civil War
Casualties of the Spanish Civil War
Economic impact of the Spanish Civil War
Overview of the Spanish Civil War
Political parties of the Spanish Civil War
Q10859.blurb: Spanish Civil War: Nationalists and Republicans both withdraw after suffering heavy losses, ending the Second Battle of the Corunna Road.

Q10951.name: Second Council of Lyon
Q10951.blurb: In France, the Second Council of Lyon opens; it ratified a decree to regulate the election of the Pope.

Q11117.name: Eurovision Song Contest 1999
Q11117.blurb: Charlotte Perrelli, representing Sweden, won the Eurovision Song Contest, the first edition not to feature an orchestra or live accompaniment.

Q11146.name: Maastricht Treaty
Q11146.blurb: The Maastricht Treaty is signed, leading to the creation of the European Union.

Q11148.name: The Guardian
aliases: The Guardian Footballer of the Year
The Manchester Guardian and British Volunteer
The Newsroom - Guardian and Observer Archive and Visitor Centre
Q11148.blurb: The first edition of The Manchester Guardian, now The Guardian, is published.

Q11240.name: 1993 World Trade Center bombing
aliases: 1993 bombing of the World Trade Center
Bombing of the World Trade Center in 1993
Q11240.blurb: World Trade Center bombing: In New York City, a truck bomb parked below the North Tower of the World Trade Center explodes, killing six and injuring over a thousand people.

Q11264.name: Cuban Revolution
Q11264.blurb: Cuban Revolution: Fulgencio Batista, dictator of Cuba, is overthrown by Fidel Castro's forces.

Q11611.name: Natchez Massacre
Q11611.blurb: Natchez Indians revolted against French colonists near modern-day Natchez, Mississippi, killing approximately 230 people.

Q11914.name: 2010 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix
aliases: Etihad Airways Abu Dhabi Grand Prix
Q11914.blurb: Red Bull Racing's Sebastian Vettel won the Drivers' Championship after winning the final race of the season, becoming the youngest Formula One champion.

Q12199.name: HIV/AIDS
aliases: Acquired immune deficiency syndrome or acquired immunodeficiency syndrome
Human Immunodeficiency Virus and Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome
Human immunodeficiency virus infection and acquired immune deficiency syndrome
Human immunodeficiency virus infection and acquired immunodeficiency syndrome
Human immunodeficiency virus/acquired immune deficiency syndrome
Q12199.blurb: The first clinical cases of AIDS were published by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

Q12428.name: Battle of Dorylaeum
Q12428.blurb: Battle of Dorylaeum: Crusaders led by prince Bohemond of Taranto defeat a Seljuk army led by sultan Kilij Arslan I.

Q12546.name: Crusades
Q12546.blurb: Crusades: The Council of Nablus is held, establishing the earliest surviving written laws of the Crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem.

Q12551.name: Hundred Years' War
Q12551.blurb: Hundred Years' War: Rouen surrenders to Henry V of England, completing his reconquest of Normandy.

Q12562.name: Protestant Reformation
Q12562.blurb: Beginning of the Protestant Reformation: After the Second Diet of Speyer bans Lutheranism, a group of rulers (German: Fürst) and independent cities protest the reinstatement of the Edict of Worms.

Q12583.name: Spanish–American War
aliases: Spanish declaration of war on the United States
Q12583.blurb: Spanish–American War: The Treaty of Paris, a peace treaty between the United States and Spain, is ratified by the United States Senate.

Q13582.name: Berlin Conference
aliases: Congo Conference on colonization of Africa (1884)
General Act of the Berlin Conference
Q13582.blurb: The Berlin Conference of 1884–1885 met on 15 November 1884, and after an adjournment concluded on 26 February 1885, with the signature of a General Act, regulating the European colonisation and trade in Africa during the New Imperialism period.

Q14665.name: Emu War
Q14665.blurb: The conclusion of the Emu War, after the Australian Government ordered the withdrawal of all Australian forces from the conflict.

Q14689.name: Battle of the Ice
aliases: Battle on the Ice (Battle of Lake Peipus)
Q14689.blurb: During the Battle on the Ice of Lake Peipus, Russian forces, led by Alexander Nevsky, rebuff an invasion attempt by the Teutonic Knights.

Q15251.name: handover of Hong Kong
aliases: transfer of sovereignty over Hong Kong
Q15251.blurb: China resumes sovereignty over the city-state of Hong Kong, ending 156 years of British colonial rule. The handover ceremony is attended by British Prime Minister Tony Blair, Charles, Prince of Wales, Chinese President Jiang Zemin and U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright.

Q16068.name: Deutsche Mark
Q16068.blurb: Britain, France and the United States announce that on June 21, the Deutsche Mark will be introduced in western Germany and West Berlin. Over the next six days, Communists increasingly restrict access to Berlin.[citation needed]

Q16422.name: Hurricane Katrina
aliases: Damage to infrastructure by Hurricane Katrina
Effect of Hurricane Katrina on the United States
Q16422.blurb: Hurricane Katrina makes landfall in Florida.

Q16468.name: Moors murders
Q16468.blurb: Myra Hindley and Ian Brady are sentenced to life imprisonment for the Moors murders in England.

Q16470.name: Normandy landings
aliases: First day of the invasion of Normandy
Q16470.blurb: World War II: Nine German E-boats attack US and UK units during Exercise Tiger, the rehearsal for the Normandy landings, killing 946.

Q17181.name: Expedition 1
Q17181.blurb: Expedition 1 arrived at the International Space Station for the first long-duration stay onboard. From this day to present, a continuous human presence in space on the station remains uninterrupted.

Q17183.name: Expedition 2
Q17183.blurb: Space Shuttle Discovery launches on STS-102, carrying the Expedition 2 crew to the International Space Station.

Q17185.name: Expedition 3
Q17185.blurb: Space Shuttle program: The Space Shuttle Discovery is launched on STS-105 to the International Space Station, carrying the astronauts of Expedition 3 to replace the crew of Expedition 2.

Q17186.name: Expedition 4
Q17186.blurb: Space Shuttle Endeavour launches on STS-108, carrying the Expedition 4 crew to the International Space Station.

Q17187.name: Expedition 5
Q17187.blurb: Space Shuttle Endeavour launches on STS-111, carrying the Expedition 5 crew to the International Space Station to replace the Expedition 4 crew. Astronaut Franklin Chang-Díaz becomes the second person to have flown on seven spaceflights.

Q17188.name: Expedition 6
Q17188.blurb: Space Shuttle Endeavour launches on STS-113 to the International Space Station carrying the Expedition 6 crew and the P1 truss.

Q17335.name: Treaty of Oliva
Q17335.blurb: Treaty of Oliva is established between Sweden and Poland.

Q17423.name: same-sex marriage in Spain
aliases: Public opinion of same-sex marriage in Spain
Recognition of same-sex unions in Ceuta
Recognition of same-sex unions in Melilla
Recognition of same-sex unions in Spain
Recognition of same-sex unions in the Canary Islands
Same-sex marriage in the Canary Islands
Q17423.blurb: Same-sex marriage became legal in Spain under a law passed by the Cortes Generales.

Q17447.name: Same-sex marriage in Canada
Q17447.blurb: The Civil Marriage Act legalizes same-sex marriage in Canada.

Q17449.name: Same-sex marriage in Denmark
Q17449.blurb: Denmark introduces the world's first legal same-sex registered partnerships.

Q17461.name: same-sex marriage in South Africa
Q17461.blurb: The law on same-sex marriage comes into force in South Africa, legalizing same-sex marriage for the first time on the African continent.

Q17463.name: Same-sex marriage in the Netherlands
Q17463.blurb: Same-sex marriage becomes legal in the Netherlands, the first contemporary country to allow it.

Q17466.name: same-sex marriage in Sweden
Q17466.blurb: Same-sex marriage in Sweden is legalized.

Q17476.name: same-sex marriage in the United States
aliases: gay marriage in the United States
Q17476.blurb: The U.S. Supreme Court granted federal recognition to same-sex marriage when it overturned the Defense of Marriage Act.

Q17550.name: California Gold Rush
Q17550.blurb: California Gold Rush: James W. Marshall finds gold at Sutter's Mill near Sacramento.

Q17554.name: Oikos University shooting
Q17554.blurb: A mass shooting at Oikos University in California leaves seven people dead and three injured.

Q17594.name: Battle of Dresden
Q17594.blurb: French Emperor Napoleon I defeats a larger force of Austrians, Russians, and Prussians at the Battle of Dresden.

Q18173.name: Japan Air Lines Flight 123
aliases: 日航ジャンボ機墜落事故
Q18173.blurb: Japan Air Lines Flight 123, a Boeing 747, crashes into Osutaka ridge in Gunma Prefecture, Japan, killing 520, becoming the worst single-plane air disaster.

Q18180.name: Korean Air Lines Flight 007 crash
Q18180.blurb: Cold War: Korean Air Lines Flight 007 is shot down by a Soviet jet fighter after the commercial aircraft strayed into Soviet airspace, killing all 269 on board, including Congressman Lawrence McDonald.

Q18375.name: Ariane 1
Q18375.blurb: The first Ariane 1 rocket is launched from ELA-1 at the Guiana Space Centre.

Q18379.name: Ariane 2
Q18379.blurb: The Ariane 2 rocket is launched on its maiden flight, carrying Intelsat VA F-14, but the mission ends in failure.

Q18381.name: Ariane 3
Q18381.blurb: The Ariane 3 rocket is launched for the first time, carrying the Eutelsat I F-2 and Télécom 1A satellites into geosynchronous transfer orbit.

Q18387.name: Ariane 4
Q18387.blurb: The last Ariane 4 rocket is launched from the Guiana Space Centre, carrying Intelsat 907.

Q18817.name: War of the First Coalition
aliases: The War of the First Coalition
Q18817.blurb: War of the First Coalition: The siege of Kehl by Habsburg and Württembergian forces ended when French troops withdrew from their fortifications.

Q18937.name: Mesopotamian campaign
Q18937.blurb: World War I: Mesopotamian campaign: Baghdad falls to Anglo-Indian forces commanded by General Frederick Stanley Maude.

Q19024.name: Boston Tea Party
aliases: Boston Tea Party Ships and Museum
Destruction of the Tea in Boston
The Destruction of the Tea in Boston
Q19024.blurb: American Revolution: Boston Tea Party: Members of the Sons of Liberty disguised as Mohawk Indians dump hundreds of crates of tea into Boston harbor as a protest against the Tea Act.

Q19085.name: killing of Osama bin Laden
aliases: Assassination attempts against Osama bin Laden
Assassination attempts on Osama bin Laden
Critiques of Osama bin Laden burial at sea
History of Osama bin Laden death reports
Legal debate over the killing of Osama bin Laden
Raid that killed Osama bin Laden
U.S. mission to kill Osama bin Laden
Q19085.blurb: Osama bin Laden was killed by U.S. Navy SEAL Team Six in his private residential compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan.

Q19184.name: Buncefield fire
aliases: Major explosions at UK oil depot
Q19184.blurb: The Buncefield Oil Depot catches fire in Hemel Hempstead, England.

Q20871.name: North Sea flood of 1962
Q20871.blurb: Flooding in the coastal areas of West Germany kills 315 and destroys the homes of about 60,000 people.

Q22949.name: Atlas
Q22949.blurb: First successful flight of SM-65 Atlas; the first operational intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM), developed by the United States and the first member of the Atlas rocket family.

Q23137.name: 1869 Saxby Gale
Q23137.blurb: The Saxby Gale devastates the Bay of Fundy region in Canada.

Q24202.name: 1828 Treaty of Montevideo
Q24202.blurb: Brazil and Argentina recognize the sovereignty of Uruguay in the Treaty of Montevideo.

Q24728.name: Siege of Salvador
Q24728.blurb: Bahia Independence Day: The Siege of Salvador ends Portuguese rule in Brazil, with the final defeat of the Portuguese crown loyalists in the province of Bahia.

Q24932.name: 2012 Shwebo earthquake
Q24932.blurb: A strong earthquake with the magnitude 6.8 hits northern Burma, killing at least 26 people.

Q25094.name: first inauguration of Barack Obama
Q25094.blurb: In Washington, D.C., Barack Obama was inaugurated as the first African-American president of the United States.

Q25173.name: Titanic
Q25173.blurb: The ill-fated RMS Titanic begins sea trials.

Q25628.name: Great stand on the Ugra river
aliases: Great Standing on the Ugra River
Great standing at the Ugra river
Great standing on the Urgu River
The Great Stand on the Ugra River
Q25628.blurb: The Great Stand on the Ugra River puts an end to Tatar rule over Moscow

Q25809.name: Battle of Krasnoi
Q25809.blurb: Napoleonic Wars: The Battle of Krasnoi ends in French defeat, but Marshal of France Michel Ney's leadership leads to him becoming known as "the bravest of the brave".

Q25857.name: War of Devolution
Q25857.blurb: The French Royal Army crosses the border into the Spanish Netherlands, starting the War of Devolution opposing France to the Spanish Empire and the Triple Alliance.

Q25861.name: Regency era
Q25861.blurb: The Carlton House Fête is held in London to celebrate the establishment of the Regency era.

Q25904.name: Dumbarton Oaks Conference
aliases: Washington Conversations on International Peace and Security Organization
Q25904.blurb: Dumbarton Oaks Conference, prelude to the United Nations, begins.

Q25977.name: Cyclone Nisha
Q25977.blurb: Cyclone Nisha strikes northern Sri Lanka, killing 15 people and displacing 90,000 others while dealing the region the highest rainfall in nine decades.

Q25980.name: Gleiwitz incident
Q25980.blurb: Nazi forces, posing as Poles, staged an attack against the German radio station Sender Gleiwitz in Gleiwitz, Upper Silesia, Germany, creating an excuse to invade Poland the next day.

Q26013.name: War of 1812
aliases: Southwestern theater of the War of 1812
Q26013.blurb: War of 1812: Battle of New Orleans: Andrew Jackson leads American forces in victory over the British.

Q26189.name: Western Schism
Q26189.blurb: Western Schism: The Roman Catholic Church is led into a double schism as Petros Philargos is crowned Pope Alexander V after the Council of Pisa, joining Pope Gregory XII in Rome and Pope Benedict XIII in Avignon.

Q26195.name: German–Soviet Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Demarcation
aliases: German-Soviet Treaty Of Friendship, Cooperation And Demarcation
German-Soviet Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation, and Demarcation
German–Soviet Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation, and Demarcation
Q26195.blurb: World War II: Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union agree on a division of Poland.

Q26293.name: 1967 Caracas earthquake
Q26293.blurb: During the fourth day of celebrating its 400th anniversary, the city of Caracas, Venezuela is shaken by an earthquake, leaving approximately 500 dead.

Q26330.name: 1999 Chamoli earthquake
Q26330.blurb: A magnitude 6.8 earthquake in India strikes the Chamoli district in Uttar Pradesh, killing 103.

Q26493.name: Battle of Dandanaqan
Q26493.blurb: The Seljuks defeat the Ghaznavids in the battle of Dandanaqan.

Q26496.name: Battle of Surabaya
Q26496.blurb: Heavy fighting in Surabaya between Indonesian nationalists and returning colonialists after World War II, today celebrated as Heroes' Day (Hari Pahlawan).

Q26718.name: Continental Congress
aliases: Provisional government of the United States
Q26718.blurb: The Continental Congress officially names its union of states the United States.

Q26749.name: War of the Second Coalition
aliases: The War of the Second Coalition
Q26749.blurb: War of the Second Coalition: At the Battle of Abukir, a British force under Sir Ralph Abercromby lands in Egypt with the aim of ending the French campaign in Egypt and Syria.

Q26977.name: Great Train Wreck of 1918
Q26977.blurb: In Nashville, Tennessee, an inbound local train collides with an outbound express, killing 101 and injuring 171 people, making it the deadliest rail accident in United States history.

Q27169.name: Member of the European Parliament
Q27169.blurb: Members of the European Parliament, including Vice President Eva Kaili (pictured), and their associates are arrested in connection with the Qatar corruption scandal.

Q27608.name: 2012 Guatemala earthquake
Q27608.blurb: An earthquake off the Pacific coast of Guatemala kills at least 52 people.

Q27702.name: October Crisis
Q27702.blurb: Canada's October Crisis escalates when Quebec Vice Premier Pierre Laporte is kidnapped by members of the Front de libération du Québec.

Q27759.name: Battle of Crécy
Q27759.blurb: Hundred Years' War: At the Battle of Crécy, an English army easily defeats a French one twice its size.

Q27900.name: Siege of Constantinople
Q27900.blurb: Arab–Byzantine wars: The Arabs abandond the Second Arab Siege of Constantinople due to failure to secure enough supplies, defeat of their relief army by the Byzantines and an outbreak of plague in the camp.

Q28479.name: Kumanovo Agreement
Q28479.blurb: Yugoslav Wars: The Kumanovo Agreement was signed, bringing an end to the Kosovo War the next day.

Q28835.name: Fields medal
aliases: International Medal for Outstanding Discoveries in Mathematics
List of Fields medalists affiliated with the Institute for Advanced Study
Q28835.blurb: Grigori Perelman is awarded the Fields Medal for his proof of the Poincaré conjecture in mathematics but refuses to accept the medal.

Q29065.name: 2011 England riots
Q29065.blurb: A series of riots broke out in several London boroughs and in cities and towns across England in response to the shooting of Mark Duggan by Metropolitan Police officers.

Q29122.name: First Anglo-Burmese War
Q29122.blurb: First Anglo-Burmese War: The British officially declare war on Burma.

Q29198.name: 2011 Egyptian revolution
aliases: List of Egyptian Revolution of 2011 victims
Q29198.blurb: The first wave of the Egyptian revolution begins throughout the country, marked by street demonstrations, rallies, acts of civil disobedience, riots, labour strikes, and violent clashes.

Q29269.name: First Chechen War
aliases: War crimes in the First Chechen War
Q29269.blurb: First Chechen War: Chechen separatists launch a raid against the helicopter airfield and later a civilian hospital in the city of Kizlyar in the neighboring Dagestan, which turns into a massive hostage crisis involving thousands of civilians.

Q29321.name: Soviet–Lithuanian Peace Treaty
Q29321.blurb: The Soviet–Lithuanian Peace Treaty is signed, by which Soviet Russia recognizes the independence of Lithuania.

Q29662.name: Edict of Expulsion
Q29662.blurb: King Edward I of England issues the Edict of Expulsion, banishing all Jews (numbering about 16,000) from England.

Q30801.name: Isner–Mahut match at the 2010 Wimbledon Championships
aliases: John Isner–Nicolas Mahut match at the 2010 Wimbledon Championships
Isner-Mahut match at the 2010 Wimbledon Championships
John Isner-Nicolas Mahut match at the 2010 Wimbledon Championships
Mahut-Isner match at the 2010 Wimbledon Championships
Mahut–Isner match at the 2010 Wimbledon Championships
Nicolas Mahut vs. John Isner match
Q30801.blurb: At Wimbledon, John Isner of the United States defeats Nicolas Mahut of France, in the longest match in professional tennis history.

Q31087.name: calculator
Q31087.blurb: IBM dedicates the first program-controlled calculator, the Automatic Sequence Controlled Calculator (known best as the Harvard Mark I).

Q31631.name: 1936 Soviet Constitution
Q31631.blurb: The 1936 Soviet constitution, also known as the "Stalin constitution", was adopted.

Q31672.name: 1925 German presidential election
Q31672.blurb: Paul von Hindenburg defeats Wilhelm Marx in the second round of the German presidential election to become the first directly elected head of state of the Weimar Republic.

Q31900.name: Battle of Marathon
Q31900.blurb: Battle of Marathon: The conventionally accepted date for the Battle of Marathon. The Athenians and their Plataean allies defeat the first Persian invasion force of Greece.

Q31944.name: Mahdist War
Q31944.blurb: Mahdist War: The siege of Khartoum ended as Mahdist forces defeated the Egyptian garrison and captured the city.

Q32610.name: 2011 Virginia earthquake
Q32610.blurb: A magnitude 5.8 (class: moderate) earthquake occurs in Virginia. Damage occurs to monuments and structures in Washington, D.C. and the resulted damage is estimated at 200 million–300 million USD.

Q32832.name: Battle of Varna
Q32832.blurb: Battle of Varna: The crusading forces of King Władysław III of Poland (aka Ulaszlo I of Hungary and Władysław III of Varna) are defeated by the Turks under Sultan Murad II and Władysław is killed.

Q32929.name: War of the Austrian Succession
aliases: The War of the Austrian Succession
Q32929.blurb: War of the Austrian Succession: The Battle of Toulon causes several Royal Navy captains to be court-martialed, and the Articles of War to be amended.

Q33132.name: Battle of Gettysburg
Q33132.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Gettysburg begins.

Q33143.name: Seven Years' War
aliases: European theater of the Seven Years' War
Great Britain during the Seven Years War
Great Britain in the Seven Years war
Q33143.blurb: During the Seven Years' War the leading burghers of Königsberg submit to Elizabeth of Russia, thus forming Russian Prussia (until 1763).

Q33162.name: Top Gear
aliases: The Greatest TV Shows of the Noughties (Channel 4)
The Worst Car in the History of the World
Q33162.blurb: Top Gear, the revived popular British TV motoring magazine, premieres on BBC.

Q33297.name: Wow! signal
Q33297.blurb: The Big Ear, a radio telescope operated by Ohio State University as part of the SETI project, receives a radio signal from deep space; the event is named the "Wow! signal" from the notation made by a volunteer on the project.

Q33511.name: Rolling Stone
aliases: Rolling Stone 10 Greatest Films of All Time
Q33511.blurb: The first issue of Rolling Stone, an American magazine focusing on music, politics and popular culture, was published.

Q33570.name: Battle of Grunwald
Q33570.blurb: Polish–Lithuanian–Teutonic War: Battle of Grunwald: The allied forces of the Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania defeat the army of the Teutonic Order.

Q33745.name: Peloponnesian War
Q33745.blurb: Admiral Lysander and King Pausanias of Sparta blockade Athens and bring the Peloponnesian War to a successful conclusion.

Q33761.name: Arab Spring
aliases: 2010-11 Middle East and North African protests
2010-2011 Middle East and North Africa Protests
2010-2011 Middle East and North Africa protest areas
2010-2011 North Africa and Middle East protests
2010-2011 North Africa and Western Asia protests
2010–2011 Middle East and North Africa protest areas
2010–2011 Middle East and North Africa protests
2010–2011 North Africa and Western Asia protests
2011 Middle East and North Africa protests
2011 North Africa and Middle East protests
Q33761.blurb: Arab Spring: Tunisian president Zine El Abidine Ben Ali fled the country after several violent protests.

Q33773.name: Convention of Moss
Q33773.blurb: A cease fire agreement, called the Convention of Moss, ended the Swedish–Norwegian War.

Q33933.name: Entebbe raid
aliases: Rescue of hijack victims at Entebbe Airport (1976)
Q33933.blurb: Air France Flight 139 (Tel Aviv-Athens-Paris) is hijacked en route to Paris by the PFLP and redirected to Entebbe, Uganda.

Q34316.name: Doctor Who
Q34316.blurb: The first episode of Doctor Who ("An Unearthly Child") is broadcast by the BBC, which is now the world's longest running science fiction drama.

Q35637.name: Nobel Peace Prize
aliases: Criticism of the Nobel Peace Prize
Q35637.blurb: Martin Luther King Jr. receives the Nobel Peace Prize for combating racial inequality through nonviolence.

Q36204.name: 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami
aliases: 2011 The Great East (tohoku) earthquake and tsunami
2011 earthquake off the coast of Tohoku
2011 earthquake off the coast of Tōhoku
2011 off the Pacific coast of Tohoku Earthquake
Great East Japan Earthquake and Tsunami
The 2011 off the Pacific coast of Tohoku Earthquake
Tōhoku region Pacific Ocean offshore earthquake
東北地方太平洋沖地震
Q36204.blurb: An earthquake measuring 9.0 in magnitude strikes 130 km (81 mi) east of Sendai, Japan, triggering a tsunami killing thousands of people. This event also triggered the second largest nuclear accident in history, and one of only two events to be classified as a Level 7 on the International Nuclear Event Scale.

Q36749.name: Beer Hall Putsch
aliases: List of Nazis killed in the Beer Hall Putsch
List of Nazis who died in the Beer Hall Putsch
Q36749.blurb: Beer Hall Putsch: In Munich, Adolf Hitler leads the Nazis in an unsuccessful attempt to overthrow the German government.

Q36756.name: Kristallnacht
Q36756.blurb: Kristallnacht occurs, instigated by the Nazis using the killing of German diplomat Ernst vom Rath by Herschel Grynszpan as justification.

Q37285.name: 2006 FIFA World Cup
aliases: 2006 FIFA World Cup full team ranking
2006 Federation Internationale de Football Association World Cup
2006 Fédération Internationale de Football Association World Cup
List of 2006 FIFA World Cup broadcasters
List of 2006 FIFA World Cup broadcasting rights
List of 2006 FIFA World Cup matches
Q37285.blurb: Following a 31-year wait, Australia defeats Uruguay in a penalty shootout to qualify for the 2006 FIFA World Cup.

Q37643.name: Gulf War
aliases: American Casualties in Operation Desert Storm
Operations Desert Shield and Desert Storm
Q37643.blurb: Persian Gulf War: An act of the U.S. Congress authorizes the use of American military force to drive Iraq out of Kuwait.

Q37853.name: Baroque
Q37853.blurb: Euridice, the earliest surviving opera, receives its première performance, beginning the Baroque period.

Q38166.name: modern art
Q38166.blurb: The Armory Show (commemorative button pictured), the first large modern-art exhibition in the United States, opened at the 69th Regiment Armory in New York City.

Q38789.name: Battle of Stalingrad
Q38789.blurb: World War II: Beginning of the Battle of Stalingrad.

Q38821.name: 2012 Northern Italy earthquakes
Q38821.blurb: At least 27 people are killed and 50 others injured when a 6.0-magnitude earthquake strikes northern Italy.

Q39040.name: Battle of Yamazaki
Q39040.blurb: Battle of Yamazaki: Toyotomi Hideyoshi defeats Akechi Mitsuhide.

Q39379.name: Scientific American
aliases: Scientific American / Farrar, Straus and Giroux
Q39379.blurb: The first issue of Scientific American magazine is published.

Q39392.name: Compromise of 1850
Q39392.blurb: The Compromise of 1850 transfers a third of Texas's claimed territory to federal control in return for the U.S. federal government assuming $10 million of Texas's pre-annexation debt.

Q39472.name: Greensboro massacre
Q39472.blurb: Greensboro massacre: Five members of the Communist Workers Party are shot dead and seven are wounded by a group of Klansmen and neo-Nazis during a "Death to the Klan" rally in Greensboro, North Carolina, United States.

Q40144.name: Battle of Coronel
Q40144.blurb: World War I: The first British Royal Navy defeat of the war with Germany, the Battle of Coronel, is fought off of the western coast of Chile, in the Pacific, with the loss of HMS Good Hope and HMS Monmouth.

Q40625.name: occupation of the Ruhr
aliases: French occupation of Ruhr Region, Germany, 1923-1925
Q40625.blurb: Occupation of the Ruhr: Troops from France and Belgium occupy the Ruhr area to force Germany to make its World War I reparation payments.

Q40949.name: American Revolutionary War
aliases: American Revolutionary War/Article from the 1911 Encyclopedia Part 1
American Revolutionary War/Article from the 1911 Encyclopedia Part 2
Caribbean theater of the American Revolutionary War
Liberation War of the United States of America
Q40949.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Burning of Norfolk – Norfolk, Virginia, is burned to the ground by combined Royal Navy and Continental Army action.

Q41044.name: Russian ruble
aliases: Commemorative banknotes of the Russian ruble
Q41044.blurb: Following a currency reform, Russia begins to circulate new rubles to stem inflation and promote confidence.

Q41302.name: 2011 Canadian federal election
Q41302.blurb: The Conservative Party of Canada won enough seats in the federal election to establish their first majority government.

Q41320.name: Battle of Denain
Q41320.blurb: War of the Spanish Succession: The French under Marshal Villars win a decisive victory over Eugene of Savoy at Denain.

Q41894.name: Battle of New Orleans
Q41894.blurb: War of 1812: Battle of New Orleans: Andrew Jackson leads American forces in victory over the British.

Q42005.name: Black Death
aliases: How the black plague got to europe
Q42005.blurb: The Jewish population of Basel, believed by the residents to be the cause of the ongoing Black Death, is rounded up and incinerated.

Q42761.name: Watergate scandal
aliases: Wiretapping of the Democratic Party's headquarters
Q42761.blurb: Watergate scandal: The trial of seven men accused of illegal entry into Democratic Party headquarters at Watergate begins.

Q42937.name: Trojan War
Q42937.blurb: Traditional reckoning of the Fall of Troy marking the end of the legendary Trojan War, given by chief librarian of the Library of Alexandria Eratosthenes, among others.

Q42976.name: October Revolution
Q42976.blurb: The October Revolution, which gets its name from the Julian calendar date of 25 October, occurs, according to the Gregorian calendar; on this date, the Bolsheviks storm the Winter Palace.

Q43297.name: Time
aliases: Time magazine's 100 best TV shows of all-TIME
Time magazine's list of the 100 Best TV Shows of All-TIME
Q43297.blurb: US magazine Time publishes its first issue.

Q43378.name: Thousand Days' War
aliases: La Guerra de los Mil Días
The War of A Thousand Days
Q43378.blurb: Thousand Days' War: The Colombian Conservative Party turns the tide of war in their favor with victory against the Colombian Liberal Party in the Battle of Palonegro.

Q43777.name: 2010 Haiti earthquake
Q43777.blurb: An earthquake in Haiti occurs, killing between 220,000 and 300,000 people and destroying much of the capital Port-au-Prince.

Q44310.name: 2011 Alexandria bombing
Q44310.blurb: A bomb explodes as Coptic Christians in Alexandria, Egypt, leave a new year service, killing 23 people.

Q44700.name: European Theater of World War II
aliases: Eastern European theatre of World War II
European Theatre in World War II
European Theatre of Second World War
Q44700.blurb: Nazi Germany mounts a false flag attack on the Gleiwitz radio station, creating an excuse to attack Poland the following day, thus starting World War II in Europe.

Q44732.name: Battle of the Golden Spurs
aliases: The Battle of the Golden Spurs
Q44732.blurb: Battle of the Golden Spurs (Guldensporenslag in Dutch): A coalition around the Flemish cities defeats the king of France's royal army.

Q45156.name: Operation Wooden Leg
Q45156.blurb: Israel-Palestinian conflict: Israel attacks the Palestine Liberation Organization's Tunisia headquarters during Operation Wooden Leg.

Q45334.name: Burning of Falmouth
Q45334.blurb: American Revolutionary War: The Burning of Falmouth (now Portland, Maine).

Q45578.name: 2008 United States presidential election
aliases: Comparison of 2008 presidential candidates' religious associations
Health care reform in the United States presidential election, 2008
President of the United States in 2008
Religion and politics in the 2008 U.S. presidential campaign
Religion and politics in the U.S. 2008 presidential campaign
U.S. presidential election, 2008/Lists of potential candidates
United States presidential election swing states, 2008
Voter suppression during the United States presidential election, 2008
Q45578.blurb: Barack Obama (pictured) became the first person of biracial or African-American descent to be elected President of the United States.

Q45745.name: New Economic Policy
aliases: New Economic Policy of Soviet Union
Q45745.blurb: The New Economic Policy is implemented by the Bolshevik Party in response to the economic failure as a result of war communism.

Q45810.name: Gunpowder Plot
aliases: Attempted assassination of James VI and I
Q45810.blurb: Gunpowder Plot: The trial of Guy Fawkes and other conspirators begins, ending with their execution on January 31.

Q46057.name: 1936–1939 Arab revolt in Palestine
Q46057.blurb: First day of the Arab revolt in Mandatory Palestine.

Q46083.name: Franco-Prussian War
aliases: Occupation of France by Germany from 1870 to 1873
Q46083.blurb: Franco-Prussian War: In the Siege of Paris, Prussia wins the Battle of St. Quentin. Meanwhile, the French attempt to break the siege in the Battle of Buzenval will end unsuccessfully the following day.

Q46333.name: Long March
Q46333.blurb: Chinese Communists begin the Long March to escape Nationalist encirclement.

Q46362.name: Congress of Vienna
aliases: Final Act of the Congress of Vienna
Q46362.blurb: Participants at the Congress of Vienna declare Napoleon an outlaw following his escape from Elba.

Q46525.name: Pulitzer Prize
Q46525.blurb: The Pulitzer Prize–winning photograph Burst of Joy is taken, depicting a former prisoner of war being reunited with his family, which came to symbolize the end of United States involvement in the Vietnam War.

Q46603.name: Sakuradamon Incident
Q46603.blurb: Sakuradamon Incident: Japanese chief minister (Tairō) Ii Naosuke is assassinated by rōnin samurai outside the Sakurada Gate of Edo Castle.

Q46611.name: Apollo program
aliases: List of documentary films about the Moon
Q46611.blurb: Apollo program: NASA announces plans to build the C-5 rocket launch vehicle, then known as the "Advanced Saturn", to carry human beings to the Moon.

Q46615.name: Summit Series
Q46615.blurb: Against the backdrop of the Cold War, the Canadian ice hockey team defeated the Soviet team in the Summit Series.

Q46904.name: Global System for Mobile Communications
aliases: Extended Global System for Mobile Communications
Global system for mobile cellular communications
Q46904.blurb: The Finnish operator Radiolinja is launched as the world's first GSM network.

Q46934.name: 1982 FIFA World Cup
aliases: 1982 Federation Internationale de Football Association World Cup
1982 Fédération Internationale de Football Association World Cup
Q46934.blurb: Italy defeats West Germany 3–1 to win the FIFA World Cup.

Q46938.name: 1986 FIFA World Cup
aliases: 1986 Federation Internationale de Football Association World Cup
1986 Fédération Internationale de Football Association World Cup
Q46938.blurb: The Argentina national football team wins the FIFA World Cup held in Mexico after defeating the West Germany national football team by a score of 3–2 in the final at the Estadio Azteca.

Q46943.name: 1978 FIFA World Cup
aliases: 1978 Federation Internationale de Football Association World Cup
1978 Fédération Internationale de Football Association World Cup
Q46943.blurb: Hosts Argentina defeat the Netherlands by a score of 3–1 in the final to win their first ever FIFA World Cup.

Q46959.name: Tunisian revolution
aliases: Fall of Zine El Abidine Ben Ali
Q46959.blurb: Arab Spring: Tunisian president Zine El Abidine Ben Ali fled the country after several violent protests.

Q47170.blurb: Ben S. Bernanke, Douglas W. Diamond and Philip H. Dybvig are jointly awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences.

Q47359.name: Kyoto Protocol
aliases: Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
Doha Amendment to the Kyoto Protocol
Q47359.blurb: The Kyoto Protocol comes into force, following its ratification by Russia.

Q47735.name: 2002 FIFA World Cup
aliases: 2002 FIFAワールドカップ 韓国/日本
2002 Federation Internationale de Football Association World Cup
2002 Fédération Internationale de Football Association World Cup
List of 2002 FIFA World Cup matches
Q47735.blurb: The Australia national men's soccer team sets a world record for the largest victory in an international association football match, winning the game 31–0 against American Samoa at the 2002 FIFA World Cup qualifiers for OFC. Australia's Archie Thompson also breaks the record for most goals scored by a player in an international match by scoring 13 goals.

Q48163.name: Battle of Custoza
Q48163.blurb: Austro-Prussian War:  In the Battle of Custoza an Austrian army defeats the Italian army.

Q48249.name: Falklands War
aliases: Casualties of the Battle of Bluff Cove
Casualties of the Bluff Cove disaster
United States involvement in the Falklands War
Q48249.blurb: Falklands War: Argentinian forces land on South Georgia Island, precipitating war with the United Kingdom.

Q48253.name: Battle of Kulm
Q48253.blurb: First Battle of Kulm: French forces are defeated by an Austrian-Prussian-Russian alliance.

Q48314.name: Battle of Waterloo
Q48314.blurb: Napoleonic Wars: The Battle of Waterloo results in the defeat of Napoleon Bonaparte by the Duke of Wellington and Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher, forcing Napoleon to abdicate the throne of France for the second and last time.

Q48432.name: 1930 FIFA World Cup
aliases: 1930 Federation Internationale de Football Association World Cup
1930 Fédération Internationale de Football Association World Cup
Q48432.blurb: The inaugural FIFA World Cup begins in Uruguay.

Q48537.name: civil rights movement
aliases: Civil Rights Movement in the United States
Civil rights in the United States
Civil rights of the United States
Q48537.blurb: In the United States, Civil Rights Movement leader Martin Luther King Jr.'s home is bombed in retaliation for the Montgomery bus boycott.

Q48766.name: Babi Yar
Q48766.blurb: World War II: The Babi Yar massacre comes to an end.

Q48776.name: Battle of Palmito Ranch
Q48776.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Palmito Ranch: The first day of the last major land action to take place during the Civil War, resulting in a Confederate victory.

Q48883.name: Goguryeo–Sui War
Q48883.blurb: Goguryeo-Sui War: In response to a Goguryeo (Korean) incursion into Liaoxi, Emperor Wéndi of Sui orders his youngest son, Yang Liang (assisted by the co-prime minister Gao Jiong), to conquer Goguryeo during the Manchurian rainy season, with a Chinese army and navy.

Q49077.name: Six-Day War
aliases: 1967 occupation of the West Bank and East Jerusalem
Q49077.blurb: Six-Day War: President Gamal Abdel Nasser of Egypt demands dismantling of the peace-keeping UN Emergency Force in Egypt.

Q49092.name: 1948 Arab–Israeli War
Q49092.blurb: Arab–Israeli War: The port city of Haifa is captured by Jewish forces.

Q49097.name: 1948 Palestine war
Q49097.blurb: Palestine war: Fighters from the Zionist paramilitary groups Irgun and Lehi attacked the village of Deir Yassin near Jerusalem, killing more than 100 Palestinian Arabs.

Q49100.name: Yom Kippur War
aliases: Casualties of the Yom Kippur War
Q49100.blurb: Yom Kippur War: Israeli forces withdraw from the west bank of the Suez Canal.

Q49101.name: Suez Crisis
Q49101.blurb: Suez Crisis: The Suez Canal is reopened following the introduction of UNEF peacekeepers to the region.

Q49103.name: 1982 Lebanon War
aliases: 1982 Israeli Invasion and Occupation of Lebanon
Human rights violations during the 1982 Lebanon War
Q49103.blurb: 1982 Lebanon War: The war begins as forces under Israeli Defense Minister Ariel Sharon invade southern Lebanon during Operation Peace for the Galilee, eventually reaching as far north as the capital Beirut.

Q49104.name: 2006 Lebanon War
aliases: Attacks affecting Lebanese industry in the 2006 Israel-Lebanon conflict
Attacks affecting Lebanese industry in the 2006 Lebanon war
Environmental impact of the 2006 Lebanon War
Media coverage of the 2006 Lebanon War
Q49104.blurb: Lebanon War: The Israeli Air Force attacked a three-story building near the Lebanese village of Qana, killing at least 28 civilians, including 16 children.

Q49105.name: First Intifada
Q49105.blurb: First Intifada: Israeli police kill 17 Palestinians and wound over 100 near the Dome of the Rock.

Q49106.name: Second Intifada
aliases: Accusations against Israel of war crimes during the Al-Aqsa Intifada
Allegations against Israel of war crimes during the Al-Aqsa Intifada
Alleged human rights violations by Israel during Al-Aqsa Intifada
Economic costs of the Second Intifada
Israeli-Palestinian cease fire agreement of June 2001
Q49106.blurb: Second Intifada: Israeli forces seized MV Karine A, which was carrying 50 tons of smuggled weapons on behalf of the Palestinian Authority.

Q49107.name: Oslo 1 Accord
aliases: Declaration of Principles on Interim Self-Government Arrangements
Q49107.blurb: The Israeli army withdraws from Nablus pursuant to the terms of Oslo Accord.

Q49964.name: Council of Clermont
Q49964.blurb: The Council of Clermont begins: called by Pope Urban II, it led to the First Crusade to the Holy Land.

Q50726.name: Operation Big Bang
Q50726.blurb: The Operation Big Bang, the largest non-nuclear man-made explosion to that time, destroys bunkers and military installations on the North Sea island of Heligoland, Germany.

Q51122.name: Unification of Italy
Q51122.blurb: Italian unification: The Siege of Gaeta ends with the capitulation of the defending fortress, effectively bringing an end of the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.

Q51402.name: Stonewall riots
Q51402.blurb: Stonewall riots begin in New York City, marking the start of the Gay Rights Movement.

Q51414.name: solar eclipse of November 13, 2012
Q51414.blurb: A total solar eclipse occurs in parts of Australia and the South Pacific.

Q51649.name: First Crusade
Q51649.blurb: A First Crusade army led by Bohemond of Taranto wins a major battle against the Seljuq emir Ridwan of Aleppo during the siege of Antioch.

Q51650.name: People's Crusade
aliases: People’s Crusader Army of Peter the Hermit
Q51650.blurb: A Seljuk Turkish army successfully ambushes the People's Crusade at the Battle of Civetot.

Q51651.name: Rhineland massacres
aliases: Persecution of Jews during the First Crusade
Persecution of Jews in the First Crusade
Q51651.blurb: The largest of the Rhineland massacres (depicted) took place in Mainz, where at least 1,100 Jews were killed by the People's Crusade.

Q51654.name: Second Crusade
Q51654.blurb: The Siege of Damascus ends in a decisive crusader defeat and leads to the disintegration of the Second Crusade.

Q51655.name: Third Crusade
Q51655.blurb: Third Crusade: Frederick I Barbarossa drowns in the river Saleph while leading an army to Jerusalem.

Q51656.name: Fourth Crusade
Q51656.blurb: Troops of the Fourth Crusade entered Constantinople and began a sack of the city, temporarily dissolving the Byzantine Empire.

Q51657.name: Albigensian Crusade
Q51657.blurb: Albigensian Crusade: The Cathar stronghold of Carcassonne falls to the crusaders.

Q51659.name: Fifth Crusade
Q51659.blurb: The Fifth Crusade leaves Acre for Egypt.

Q51660.name: Sixth Crusade
Q51660.blurb: The Sixth Crusade: Frederick II, Holy Roman Emperor, signs a ten-year truce with al-Kamil, regaining Jerusalem, Nazareth, and Bethlehem with neither military engagements nor support from the papacy.

Q51661.name: Seventh Crusade
Q51661.blurb: Seventh Crusade: Crusaders engage Ayyubid forces in the Battle of Al Mansurah.

Q52162.name: Project Mercury
aliases: Summary of Project Mercury manned missions
Q52162.blurb: Project Mercury: Mercury-Redstone 2: The chimpanzee Ham travels into outer space.

Q52226.name: Battle of Mogadishu
Q52226.blurb: An American attack against a warlord in Mogadishu fails; eighteen US soldiers and over 350 Somalis die.

Q52418.name: Attack on Pearl Harbor
Q52418.blurb: World War II: Attack on Pearl Harbor: The Imperial Japanese Navy carries out a surprise attack on the United States Pacific Fleet and its defending Army and Marine air forces at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii. (For Japan's near-simultaneous attacks on Eastern Hemisphere targets, see December 8.)

Q52843.name: Treaty of Lisbon
aliases: Treaty of Lisbon amending the Treaty on European Union and the Treaty establishing the European Community
Opposition To The Treaty Of Lisbon In Ireland
Q52843.blurb: The Treaty of Lisbon entered into force in the European Union.

Q52967.name: Poznań 1956 protests
Q52967.blurb: Polish workers demanding better working conditions began massive protests in Poznań, but were later violently repressed by the Polish People's Army and the Internal Security Corps.

Q53600.name: Luxor massacre
Q53600.blurb: Sixty-two people were killed by Islamist terrorists outside Deir el-Bahari (temple pictured) in Luxor, one of Egypt's top tourist attractions.

Q53692.name: 2012 Gaza War
aliases: 2012 Israeli operation in the Gaza Strip
Q53692.blurb: Israel launches a major military operation in the Gaza Strip in response to an escalation of rocket attacks by Hamas.

Q54340.name: People's Daily
Q54340.blurb: People's Daily publishes the April 26 Editorial which inflames the nascent Tiananmen Square protests.

Q54430.name: 2007 Brazilian Grand Prix
Q54430.blurb: Finnish race drivers Kimi Räikkönen of Scuderia Ferrari won the Brazilian Grand Prix in Formula One. With this result, Räikkönen became world champion, surpassing McLaren drivers Lewis Hamilton and Fernando Alonso by one point in the drivers' standings.

Q54431.name: 2008 Brazilian Grand Prix
Q54431.blurb: Lewis Hamilton (pictured) overtook Timo Glock in the final corners of the Brazilian Grand Prix to win the Formula One championship by one point.

Q54434.name: War of Jenkins' Ear
Q54434.blurb: War of Jenkins' Ear: The British began an assault against Spanish forts in the Caribbean in the Battle of Cartagena de Indias.

Q55529.blurb: The 730: Okinawa Prefecture changes its traffic on the right-hand side of the road to the left-hand side.

Q56039.name: German reunification
aliases: Cost of unification of East and West Germany
Q56039.blurb: East and West Germany merge their economies.

Q58395.name: King's Cross fire
Q58395.blurb: King's Cross fire: In London, 31 people die in a fire at the city's busiest underground station, King's Cross St Pancras.

Q58412.name: 1987 Hipercor bombing
Q58412.blurb: Basque separatist group ETA commits one of its most violent attacks, in which a bomb is set off in a supermarket, Hipercor, killing 21 and injuring 45.

Q58459.name: Battle between HMAS Sydney and German auxiliary cruiser Kormoran
Q58459.blurb: World War II: Battle between HMAS Sydney and HSK Kormoran. The two ships sink each other off the coast of Western Australia, with the loss of 645 Australians and about 77 German seamen.

Q58473.name: Occupation of the Baltic states
aliases: Occupation and annexation of the Baltic states
Occupation of Estonia by Soviet Union 1940
Occupation of Estonia by Soviet Union 1944
Occupation of Lithuania by Soviet Union 1940
Occupation of Lithuania by Soviet Union 1944-1945
Occupation of the Baltic states during World War II
Occupation of the Baltic states in World War II
Russian government view on Soviet occupation
Second Soviet occupation of the Baltic states
Soviet occupation of the Baltic States
Q58473.blurb: June deportation: The first major wave of Soviet mass deportations of Estonians, Latvians, and Lithuanians from the occupied Baltic states begins.

Q58672.name: dissolution of Austria-Hungary
Q58672.blurb: Dissolution of Austria-Hungary: Austria becomes a republic. After the proclamation, a coup attempt by the communist Red Guard is defeated by the social-democratic Volkswehr.

Q58732.name: Siege of Malta
aliases: "Nothing is better known than the siege of Malta."
Nothing is better known than the siege of Malta
Nothing is better known than the siege of Malta.
Q58732.blurb: The Great Siege of Malta begins, in which Ottoman forces attempt and fail to conquer Malta.

Q58884.name: Melodifestivalen
Q58884.blurb: The first Melodifestivalen is held at Cirkus in Stockholm, Sweden.

Q58947.name: Paraguayan War
aliases: The War of the Triple Alliance
War of the Triple Alliance (South America)
Women in the War of the Triple Alliance
Q58947.blurb: Paraguayan War: Marshal Francisco Solano López died at the Battle of Cerro Corá.

Q59886.name: Bombing of Tokyo
aliases: Bombing of Tokyo in World War II
Q59886.blurb: World War II: Allied forces carry out firebombing over Tokyo, destroying most of the capital and killing over 100,000 civilians.

Q60022.name: Tennis Court Oath
aliases: Le Serment du Jeu de Paume
Q60022.blurb: Deputies of the French Third Estate take the Tennis Court Oath.

Q60266.name: United Airlines Flight 173
Q60266.blurb: United Airlines Flight 173 crashes in a residential neighborhood near Portland International Airport, killing 10 people.

Q60270.name: Battle of the Dukla Pass
Q60270.blurb: World War II: Units of the 1st Czechoslovak Army Corps enter Czechoslovakia during the Battle of the Dukla Pass.

Q60323.name: Viasa Flight 897
Q60323.blurb: Viasa Flight 897 crashes after takeoff from Lisbon Airport, killing 61.

Q60372.name: solar eclipse of March 20, 2015
Q60372.blurb: A solar eclipse, equinox, and a supermoon all occur on the same day.

Q60489.name: Albanian–Venetian War
Q60489.blurb: Skanderbeg and Gjergj Arianiti signed a peace treaty to end the Albanian–Venetian War.

Q60830.name: Lisbon Massacre
Q60830.blurb: The Lisbon Massacre begins, in which about two thousand Jews who had been forcibly converted to Christianity are slaughtered by Portuguese Catholics.

Q60963.name: Red Army invasion of Georgia
Q60963.blurb: Bolsheviks launch a revolt in Georgia as a preliminary to the Red Army invasion of Georgia.

Q61100.name: Battle of Civitate
Q61100.blurb: Battle of Civitate: Three thousand Norman horsemen of Count Humphrey rout the troops of Pope Leo IX.

Q61553.name: Last use of capital punishment in Spain
Q61553.blurb: The last use of capital punishment in Spain sparks worldwide protests.

Q62417.name: Battle of Turaida
Q62417.blurb: Residents of Riga and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania defeat the Livonian Order in the Battle of Turaida.

Q63210.name: solar eclipse of December 14, 2020
Q63210.blurb: A total solar eclipse is visible from parts of the South Pacific Ocean, southern South America, and the South Atlantic Ocean.

Q63468.name: Battle of Pavia
Q63468.blurb: A Spanish-Austrian army defeats a French army at the Battle of Pavia.

Q63843.name: 1930 FIFA World Cup Final
Q63843.blurb: In Montevideo, Uruguay wins the first FIFA World Cup by beating Argentina.

Q63863.name: Operation Focus
Q63863.blurb: Following Israel's initiation of Operation Focus with the goal to neutralise the Egyptian Air Force, Syrian Air Force, and the Royal Jordanian Air Force, the Six-Day War begins.

Q64064.name: War of the Limburg Succession
Q64064.blurb: The Battle of Worringen ends the War of the Limburg Succession, with John I, Duke of Brabant, being one of the more important victors.

Q64160.name: TNA iMPACT!
Q64160.blurb: Headlined by Hulk Hogan and Ric Flair, TNA Wrestling moves its flagship program, TNA Impact!, to Monday night. This effort to go "big time live" failed but is notable in the history of professional wrestling television.

Q64876.name: Syrian occupation of Lebanon
Q64876.blurb: Cedar Revolution: Under international pressure, Syria withdraws the last of its 14,000 troop military garrison in Lebanon, ending its 29-year military domination of that country (Syrian occupation of Lebanon).

Q64879.name: Siege of Malakand
Q64879.blurb: Anglo-Afghan War: The Siege of Malakand ends when a relief column is able to reach the British garrison in the Malakand states.

Q65429.name: 2002 Al Ayyat train fire
Q65429.blurb: A cooking gas cylinder explodes on board an Egyptian National Railways train in El Ayyat, causing a fire and killing over 370 people.

Q68478.name: Peruvian War of Independence
aliases: Guerra de la Independencia del Perú
Q68478.blurb: Peruvian War of Independence: Argentine general José de San Martín declared the independence of Peru from the Spanish Empire.

Q68750.name: Mexican War of Independence
aliases: Causes of the Mexican War of Independence
Q68750.blurb: Mexican War of Independence: In the Battle of Calderón Bridge, a heavily outnumbered Spanish force of 6,000 troops defeats nearly 100,000 Mexican revolutionaries.

Q68962.name: Pannonian Avars
Q68962.blurb: The Avars and Sassanids besiege Constantinople, held by Byzantine troops under Patrician Bonus.

Q68969.name: Croatian War of Independence
aliases: Croatian war crimes in the Yugoslav Wars
Q68969.blurb: During the Croatian War of Independence, the Army of the Republic of Serb Krajina fires cluster bombs at Zagreb, killing seven and wounding over 175 civilians.

Q69772.name: Philippine Declaration of Independence
Q69772.blurb: Philippine Declaration of Independence: General Emilio Aguinaldo declares the Philippines' independence from Spain.

Q69934.name: 2010 Formula One World Championship
Q69934.blurb: Red Bull Racing's Sebastian Vettel won the Drivers' Championship after winning the final race of the season, becoming the youngest Formula One champion.

Q70520.name: Great Chicago Fire
Q70520.blurb: The Great Chicago Fire (pictured), began and proceeded to destroy much of the city's central business district, killing 300 people and leaving 90,000 others homeless.

Q72251.name: 1876 United States presidential election
Q72251.blurb: Just two days before inauguration, the U.S. Congress declares Rutherford B. Hayes the winner of the 1876 U.S. presidential election even though Samuel J. Tilden had won the popular vote.

Q72533.name: Garfield
Q72533.blurb: Garfield's first comic strip, originally published locally as Jon in 1976, goes into nationwide syndication.

Q72835.name: 1908 United States presidential election
Q72835.blurb: William Howard Taft is elected the 27th President of the United States.

Q73194.name: Battle of Dogger Bank
Q73194.blurb: World War I: British Grand Fleet battle cruisers under Vice-Admiral Sir David Beatty engage Rear-Admiral Franz von Hipper's battle cruisers in the Battle of Dogger Bank.

Q73670.name: Siege of Krujë
Q73670.blurb: A large Ottoman force begins the siege of Albanian rebel forces in Krujë, that ultimately will fail.

Q73736.name: Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky Air Flight 251 (2012)
Q73736.blurb: Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky Air Flight 251 crashes on approach to Palana Airport, killing 10 and injuring four.

Q73974.name: Institut für Sexualwissenschaft
aliases: Institute for the Science of Sexuality
Q73974.blurb: As part of Nazi Germany's persecution of transgender people, thousands of books taken from the Institute for Sexual Science were burned in Bebelplatz square  for being "un-German".

Q74011.name: Norman conquest of southern Italy
aliases: The Norman conquest of southern Italy
Q74011.blurb: Lombard Revolt: Lombard forces led by Melus revolt in Bari against the Byzantine Catepanate of Italy.

Q74623.name: Great Turkish War
Q74623.blurb: Great Turkish War: Forces led by Prince Eugene of Savoy decisively defeated Ottoman troops at the Battle of Zenta in present-day Serbia, ending the Turkish threat to Europe.

Q74659.name: Manfalut railway accident
Q74659.blurb: At least 50 schoolchildren are killed in an accident at a railway crossing near Manfalut, Egypt.

Q75665.name: Second Macedonian War
Q75665.blurb: The Roman Republic under its new consuls Publius Sulpicius Galba and Gaius Aurelius Cotta declares war on Philip V of Macedon, starting the Second Macedonian War.

Q75756.name: Second Congo War
Q75756.blurb: Second Congo War: Congolese President Laurent-Désiré Kabila is assassinated by one of his own bodyguards in Kinshasa.

Q75844.name: Zanzibar Revolution
Q75844.blurb: Rebels in Zanzibar begin a revolt known as the Zanzibar Revolution and proclaim a republic.

Q76118.name: Third Macedonian War
Q76118.blurb: Battle of Pydna: Romans under Lucius Aemilius Paullus defeat Macedonian King Perseus who surrenders after the battle, ending the Third Macedonian War.

Q76210.name: The Blue Lotus
Q76210.blurb: The Blue Lotus, the fifth volume of The Adventures of Tintin by the Belgian cartoonist Hergé and noted for its emphasis on countering negative misconceptions of Chinese people, began serialisation.

Q76421.name: 26/11 Mumbai attacks
aliases: Attack on The Taj Mahal Palace Hotel
Casualties of the November 2008 Mumbai attacks
List of victims of the November 2008 Mumbai attacks
Q76421.blurb: Mumbai attacks, a series of terrorist attacks killing approximately 175 citizens by 10 members of Lashkar-e-Taiba, a Pakistan based extremist Islamist terrorist organisation.

Q76986.name: Belovezh Accords
aliases: Denunciation of the Treaty on the Creation of the USSR
Agreement establishing the Commonwealth of Independent States
Agreement on the Creation the Commonwealth of Independent States
Agreement on the Establishment the Commonwealth of Independent States
Minsk Agreement on the creation the Commonwealth of Independent States
Q76986.blurb: Belarusian, Russian and Ukrainian leaders signed the Belovezh Accords, agreeing to dissolve the Soviet Union and establish the Commonwealth of Independent States.

Q78994.name: Napoleonic Wars
aliases: Military intelligence in the Napoleonic Wars
Q78994.blurb: Napoleonic Wars: A British naval squadron captured or destroyed five French ships of the line at the Battle of San Domingo (pictured) in the Caribbean Sea.

Q79721.name: dot-com bubble
Q79721.blurb: The Dot-com bubble peaks with the NASDAQ Composite stock market index reaching 5,048.62.

Q79859.name: 2014 FIFA World Cup
aliases: 2014 Federation Internationale de Football Association World Cup
2014 Fédération Internationale de Football Association World Cup

Copa do Mundo da FIFA Brasil 2014
List of 2014 FIFA World Cup Man of the Match

List of 2014 FIFA World Cup matches
Q79859.blurb: In the 2014 FIFA World Cup semi-final at the Mineirão, Germany defeated Brazil 7–1 (players pictured), breaking several tournament records.

Q79911.name: Russian Civil War
aliases: Casualties of the Russian Civil War
Fictional depictions of the Russian Civil War
Left wing uprisings against the Bolsheviks
Q79911.blurb: Russian Civil War: Bolshevik forces suppressed a rebellion of sailors and civilians in Kronstadt.

Q79967.name: 2011 Norway attacks
Q79967.blurb: Norway attacks: A bomb explodes, targeted at government buildings in central Oslo, followed by a massacre at a youth camp on the island of Utøya.

Q80034.name: Armenian Genocide
aliases: International reactions to the Armenian genocide
Q80034.blurb: The Armenian genocide in the Ottoman Empire began with the arrest and deportation of hundreds of prominent Armenians in Constantinople.

Q80130.name: Nuremberg trials
aliases: Charter of the International Military Tribunal
London Charter of the International Military Tribunal
London Charter of the Military Tribunal
The Trial of German Major War Criminals
Trial of the Major War Criminals Before the International Military Tribunal
Q80130.blurb: The London Charter is signed by France, the United Kingdom, the Soviet Union and the United States, establishing the laws and procedures for the Nuremberg trials.

Q80330.name: English Civil War
aliases: Episcopacy during the English Civil War
Tactics of the English Civil War
Wales in the English Civil War
Weapons of the English Civil War
Q80330.blurb: English Civil War: Bolton Massacre by Royalist troops under the command of James Stanley, 7th Earl of Derby.

Q80880.name: 1997 Asian financial crisis
Q80880.blurb: The 1997 Asian financial crisis causes a crash in the Dow Jones Industrial Average.

Q81321.name: Tel Aviv central bus station massacre
Q81321.blurb: A suicide bombing at the Tel Aviv central bus station kills 23 people and injures over 100 more.

Q81545.name: Libyan Civil War
Q81545.blurb: First Libyan Civil War: The United Nations Security Council adopted Resolution 1973, authorizing military intervention in Libya to protect civilians.

Q82241.name: 2012 South Korean presidential election
Q82241.blurb: Park Geun-hye is elected the first female president of South Korea.

Q82407.name: 2012 Buenos Aires rail disaster
Q82407.blurb: A train crash in Buenos Aires, Argentina, kills 51 people and injures 700 others.

Q82542.name: Tet Offensive
Q82542.blurb: Vietnam War: Tet Offensive launch by forces of the Viet Cong and North Vietnamese Army against South Vietnam, the United States, and their allies.

Q82698.name: Battle of Dervenakia
Q82698.blurb: First day of the three-day Battle of Dervenakia, between the Ottoman Empire force led by Mahmud Dramali Pasha and the Greek Revolutionary force led by Theodoros Kolokotronis.
