Q83157.name: 2010 Africa Cup of Nations
aliases: Palanquinha (2010 Africa Cup of Nations mascot)
Q83157.blurb: Gunmen from an offshoot of the Front for the Liberation of the Enclave of Cabinda attack a bus carrying the Togo national football team on its way to the 2010 Africa Cup of Nations, killing three people and injuring another nine.

Q83224.name: Battle of Hastings
Q83224.blurb: Following the death of Harold II at the Battle of Hastings, Edgar the Ætheling is proclaimed King of England by the Witan; he is never crowned, and concedes power to William the Conqueror two months later.

Q83516.name: 1968 Democratic National Convention
Q83516.blurb: The Chicago Seven are found not guilty of conspiring to incite riots at the 1968 Democratic National Convention.

Q83863.name: Australia 31–0 American Samoa
Q83863.blurb: In a FIFA World Cup qualifying match, Australia defeated American Samoa 31–0, the largest margin of victory recorded in international football.

Q86584.name: 2002 Bali bombings
Q86584.blurb: Terrorists detonate bombs in two nightclubs in Kuta, Bali, Indonesia, killing 202 and wounding over 200.

Q87138.name: Greco-Turkish War
aliases: Western Front of the Turkish War of Independence
Q87138.blurb: Greco-Turkish War: The First Battle of İnönü, the first battle of the war, begins near Eskişehir in Anatolia.

Q87779.name: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest
aliases: Quintilius Varus, give me back my legions!
The Battle of the Teutoburg Forest
Q87779.blurb: The Battle of the Teutoburg Forest ends: The Roman Empire suffers the greatest defeat of its history and the Rhine is established as the border between the Empire and the so-called barbarians for the next four hundred years.

Q93484.name: Topoľčany pogrom
Q93484.blurb: Dozens of Jews were injured in the Topoľčany pogrom, one of the worst episodes of anti-Jewish violence in postwar Czechoslovakia.

Q94080.name: Time of Troubles
Q94080.blurb: During the Time of Troubles, Polish troops are expelled from Moscow's Kitay-gorod by Russian troops under the command of Dmitry Pozharsky (22 October O.S.).

Q94247.name: Interstate Highway System
aliases: Dwight D. Eisenhower National System of Interstate and Defense Highways

Q94247.blurb: The Federal Aid Highway Act of 1956 is signed by U.S. President Dwight D. Eisenhower, officially creating the United States Interstate Highway System.

Q94916.name: Second Italo-Ethiopian War
aliases: Italy's invasion and occupation of Ethiopia
Q94916.blurb: Second Italo-Abyssinian War: Italian troops launch the Battle of Amba Aradam against Ethiopian defenders.

aliases: Censorship of the 1989 Tiananmen Square Massacre

Q99717.blurb: Tiananmen Square protests of 1989: In Beijing, around 100,000 students gather in Tiananmen Square to commemorate Chinese reform leader Hu Yaobang.

Q100021.name: PIA Flight 661
Q100021.blurb: Pakistan International Airlines Flight 661, a domestic passenger flight from Chitral to Islamabad, operated by an ATR-42-500 crashes near Havelian, killing all 47 on board.

Q101534.name: February Revolution
Q101534.blurb: First demonstrations in Saint Petersburg, Russia. The beginning of the February Revolution (March 8 in the Gregorian calendar).

Q101751.name: 1994 FIFA World Cup
aliases: 1994 Federation Internationale de Football Association World Cup
1994 Fédération Internationale de Football Association World Cup
List of 1994 FIFA World Cup matches
Q101751.blurb: Most of the Zambia national football team lose their lives in a plane crash off Libreville, Gabon en route to Dakar, Senegal to play a 1994 FIFA World Cup qualifying match against Senegal.

Q105570.name: 20 July plot
Q105570.blurb: World War II: Claus von Stauffenberg and four fellow conspirators are executed for the July 20 plot to assassinate Adolf Hitler.

aliases: Casualties of the 2003 invasion of Iraq
Military preparations for 2003 invasion of Iraq

Public relations plans for war on Iraq

War crimes in the 2003 invasion of Iraq
Q107802.blurb: Invasion of Iraq: A group of people leave London, England, for Baghdad, Iraq, to serve as human shields, intending to prevent the U.S.-led coalition troops from bombing certain locations.

Q108413.name: Wounded Knee Massacre
Q108413.blurb: Wounded Knee Massacre: On Pine Ridge Indian Reservation, 300 Lakota are killed by the United States 7th Cavalry Regiment.

Q109251.name: Samnite Wars
Q109251.blurb: The first temple to Venus, the Roman goddess of love, beauty and fertility, is dedicated by Quintus Fabius Maximus Gurges during the Third Samnite War.

Q109886.name: 1st Academy Awards
aliases: Academy Award for Best Engineering Effects
Academy Award for Best Title Writing
Academy Award for Best Unique and Artistic Picture
Academy Award for Best Unique and Artistic Production
Academy Award for Unique and Artistic Picture
Academy Award for Unique and Artistic Production
Q109886.blurb: The first Academy Awards ceremony was held at the Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel in Los Angeles, California.

Q111648.name: Battle of Stony Point
Q111648.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Light infantry of the Continental Army seize a fortified British Army position in a midnight bayonet attack at the Battle of Stony Point.

Q112183.name: Treaty of Amiens
Q112183.blurb: The Treaty of Amiens is signed as a "Definitive Treaty of Peace" between France and the United Kingdom.

Q112524.name: Red Turban Rebellion
Q112524.blurb: Amidst the Red Turban Rebellions, Han Lin'er, a claimed descendant of Emperor Huizong of Song, is proclaimed emperor of the restored Song dynasty in Bozhou.

Q113024.name: Invasion of Martinique of 1809
Q113024.blurb: Britain invades and captures the French colony of Martinique.

Q113382.name: 1966 Palomares B-52 crash
Q113382.blurb: Palomares incident: A B-52 bomber collides with a KC-135 Stratotanker over Spain, killing seven airmen, and dropping three 70-kiloton nuclear bombs near the town of Palomares and another one into the sea.

Q113621.name: Battle of Milne Bay
Q113621.blurb: World War II: Battle of Milne Bay: Japanese marines assault Allied airfields at Milne Bay, New Guinea, initiating the Battle of Milne Bay.

Q116123.name: end of the Han dynasty
Q116123.blurb: Emperor Xian of Han is forced to abdicate the throne by Cao Cao's son Cao Pi, ending the Han dynasty.

Q116688.name: 2003 Boumerdès earthquake
Q116688.blurb: The 6.8 Mw Boumerdès earthquake shakes northern Algeria with a maximum Mercalli intensity of X (Extreme). More than 2,200 people were killed and a moderate tsunami sank boats at the Balearic Islands.

Q117320.name: Moscow Trials
aliases: Show trials in the Soviet Union
Q117320.blurb: The trial of the anti-Soviet Trotskyist center sees seventeen mid-level Communists accused of sympathizing with Leon Trotsky and plotting to overthrow Joseph Stalin's regime.

Q117571.name: Porajmos
aliases: Genocide of Romani people in the Independent State of Croatia
Roma persecution in the second world war
Q117571.blurb: The Holocaust: In the Romani Holocaust, Nazi official Heinrich Himmler ordered that the Romani were to be put "on the same level as Jews and placed in concentration camps".

Q117693.name: Raising the Flag on Iwo Jima
aliases: Photograph of Flag Raising on Iwo Jima
Photograph of Flag Raising on Iwo Jima (NAID 520748)
Photograph of Flag Raising on Iwo Jima, 02/23/1945
Raised the flag on Iwo Jima
Q117693.blurb: American photographer Joe Rosenthal took the Pulitzer Prize–winning photograph Raising the Flag on Iwo Jima during the Battle of Iwo Jima, an image that was later reproduced on the Marine Corps War Memorial.

Q118373.name: Charkhi Dadri mid-air collision
Q118373.blurb: A Saudi Arabian Airlines Boeing 747 and a Kazakhstan Airlines Ilyushin Il-76 collided in mid-air near New Delhi, killing 349 people, the deadliest such collision in history.

Q118951.name: Battle of Meloria
Q118951.blurb: The Republic of Pisa is defeated in the Battle of Meloria by the Republic of Genoa, thus losing its naval dominance in the Mediterranean.

Q119129.name: United States Exploring Expedition
Q119129.blurb: The Wilkes Expedition, which would explore the Puget Sound and Antarctica, weighs anchor at Hampton Roads.

Q119524.name: February 1974 United Kingdom general election
Q119524.blurb: The British election ends in a hung parliament after the Jeremy Thorpe-led Liberal Party achieved their biggest vote share since 1929.

Q119939.name: Southampton Plot
Q119939.blurb: Thomas Grey is executed for participating in the Southampton Plot.

Q120843.name: Second Chechen War
aliases: Environmental impact of the Second Chechen War
The Analyses and Reports of the Second Chechen War
Q120843.blurb: Second Chechen War: As the Battle of Grozny came to a close, Russian forces summarily executed at least 60 civilians in Grozny's Novye Aldi suburb.

Q122100.name: Continuation War
aliases: Soviet–Finnish Front of the Great Patriotic War
Finnish Front of the Great Patriotic War
Finnish occupation of the Soviet Union
Q122100.blurb: World War II: During the Continuation War, the Soviet Union demands unconditional surrender from Finland during the beginning of partially successful Vyborg–Petrozavodsk Offensive. The Finnish government refuses.

Q122371.name: Treaty of Brest-Litovsk
Q122371.blurb: Russia signs the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk, agreeing to withdraw from World War I, and conceding German control of the Baltic States, Belarus and Ukraine. It also conceded Turkish control of Ardahan, Kars and Batumi.

Q122442.name: Treaty of Jassy
Q122442.blurb: Treaty of Jassy between Russian and Ottoman Empire is signed, ending the Russo-Turkish War of 1787–92.

Q123069.name: Cumbria shootings
Q123069.blurb: Twelve people are killed and eleven others injured in a spree shooting in Cumbria, England, before the perpetrator takes his own life.

Q123070.name: Sixth Russo-Turkish War
Q123070.blurb: Russo-Turkish War (1768–74): Russia and the Ottoman Empire sign the Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca ending the war. It is the first time that an Ottoman ruler surrendered territory largely populated by Muslims and the first time that a separation of secular and spiritual authority in the Ottoman Empire was established.

Q123170.name: Cinema Rex fire
Q123170.blurb: In Iran, the Cinema Rex fire causes more than 300 deaths.

Q123210.name: Seventh Russo-Turkish War
Q123210.blurb: Russo-Turkish war (1787–1792): Greek privateer Lambros Katsonis loses three of his ships in the Battle of Andros.

Q123227.name: Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca
Q123227.blurb: Russo-Turkish War (1768–74): Russia and the Ottoman Empire sign the Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca ending the war. It is the first time that an Ottoman ruler surrendered territory largely populated by Muslims and the first time that a separation of secular and spiritual authority in the Ottoman Empire was established.

Q123737.name: Emmy Award
aliases: National Capital / Chesapeake Bay Emmy Awards
Pacific Southwest Chapter of the National Television Academy
San Francisco / Northern California Emmy Award
San Francisco / Northern California Emmy Awards
Q123737.blurb: The first Emmy Awards are presented in the United States; the venue is the Hollywood Athletic Club.

Q124649.name: Second Battle of Algeciras
Q124649.blurb: British ships inflict heavy damage on Spanish and French ships in the Second Battle of Algeciras.

Q124693.name: Parsley massacre
Q124693.blurb: Rafael Trujillo orders the execution of Haitians living in the border region of the Dominican Republic.

Q125953.name: Tunguska event
Q125953.blurb: The Tunguska Event, the largest impact event on Earth in human recorded history, resulting in a massive explosion over Eastern Siberia.

Q125955.name: Nemmersdorf massacre
Q125955.blurb: World War II: The Nemmersdorf massacre against German civilians takes place.

Q126065.name: Iranian Revolution
aliases: Overthrow of the Shah of Iran
Q126065.blurb: Iranian Revolution: Protests took place in Qom after an article insulting Ruhollah Khomeini was published.

Q126306.name: Decembrist revolt
Q126306.blurb: Imperial Russian Army officers led about 3,000 soldiers in protest against Nicholas I's assumption of the throne after his elder brother Konstantin removed himself from the line of succession.

Q126413.name: German–Polish declaration of non-aggression
Q126413.blurb: German–Polish declaration of non-aggression is signed.

Q126631.name: Hannah Montana
aliases: All Eyes On Me (Miley Cyrus Song)
Q126631.blurb: Hannah Montana, starring Miley Cyrus as an actress whose alter ego is the titular character, premiered.

Q126876.name: Saratoga campaign
Q126876.blurb: American Revolutionary War: British General John Burgoyne surrenders his army at Saratoga, New York.

Q127013.name: Final Solution
aliases: Final Solution to the Jewish question
Final Solution of the Jewish Question
Solution of the Jewish Question in Europe
The final solution of the Jewish question
Q127013.blurb: The Holocaust: Reinhard Heydrich and other senior Nazi officials met at the Wannsee Conference near Berlin to discuss the implementation of the "Final Solution to the Jewish Question".

Q127050.name: Manhattan Project
aliases: United States. Army. Corps of Engineers. Manhattan District
Q127050.blurb: Convicted Manhattan Project spy Klaus Fuchs is released after only nine years in prison and allowed to emigrate to Dresden, East Germany where he resumes a scientific career.

Q127299.name: Battle of Kolín
Q127299.blurb: Battle of Kolín between Prussian forces under Frederick the Great and an Austrian army under the command of Field Marshal Count Leopold Joseph von Daun in the Seven Years' War.

Q127547.name: Battle of Debre Abbay
Q127547.blurb: Ras Marye of Yejju marches into Tigray and defeats and kills Dejazmach Sabagadis in the Battle of Debre Abbay.

Q127751.name: Wars of the Roses
Q127751.blurb: Wars of the Roses in England: Lancastrian King Henry VI is deposed by his House of York cousin, who then becomes King Edward IV.

Q127912.name: United States Declaration of Independence
aliases: Declaration of Indepedence of the United States
Declaration of Independence of the United States
That these colonies are, and of right ought to be, free and independent states
The Declaration of Independence of the United States of America
The Unanimous Declaration of the Thirteen United States of America
The declaration of independence of the thirteen colonies
The year of the Independence of the United States of America
When in the Course of human events
Q127912.blurb: The United States Declaration of Independence received its first formal public reading, in Philadelphia.

Q128160.name: Cuban Missile Crisis
aliases: United States naval quarantine of Cuba
Q128160.blurb: Following the Cuban Missile Crisis, the Soviet Union and the United States sign an agreement to establish the so-called "red telephone" link between Washington, D.C., and Moscow.

Q128168.name: Counter-Reformation
Q128168.blurb: The Council of Trent begins as the embodiment of the Counter-Reformation.

Q128293.name: Battle of Silva Arsia
Q128293.blurb: Publius Valerius Publicola celebrates the first triumph of the Roman Republic after his victory over the deposed king Lucius Tarquinius Superbus at the Battle of Silva Arsia.

Q128535.name: Norway Debate
Q128535.blurb: A three-day debate began in the House of Commons that resulted in British prime minister Neville Chamberlain being replaced by Winston Churchill (pictured).

Q128869.name: Muradiye earthquake of 1976
aliases: Terremoto de Çaldıran y Muradiye de 1976
Q128869.blurb: The Çaldıran–Muradiye earthquake in eastern Turkey kills between 4,000 and 5,000 people.

Q128875.name: Battle of Debre Tabor
Q128875.blurb: Battle of Debre Tabor: Ras Ali Alula, Regent of the Emperor of Ethiopia defeats warlord Wube Haile Maryam of Semien.

Q129029.name: Bhopal disaster
Q129029.blurb: Bhopal disaster: A methyl isocyanate leak from a Union Carbide pesticide plant in Bhopal, India, kills more than 3,800 people outright and injures 150,000–600,000 others (some 6,000 of whom later died from their injuries) in one of the worst industrial disasters in history.

Q129053.name: partition of India
aliases: Collapse of the British Indian Empire
Places in Pakistan with Hindu and Sikh Populations before 1947
Population transfers during the Partition of India
Q129053.blurb: Partition of India: The Maharaja of Kashmir and Jammu signs the Instrument of Accession with India, beginning the Indo-Pakistani War of 1947–1948 and the Kashmir conflict.

Q129151.name: 1938 Yellow River flood
Q129151.blurb: Second Sino-Japanese War: The Chinese Nationalist government creates the 1938 Yellow River flood to halt Japanese forces. Five hundred thousand to nine hundred thousand civilians are killed.

Q129811.name: Wenzhou train collision
Q129811.blurb: A high-speed train rear-ends another on a viaduct on the Yongtaiwen railway line in Wenzhou, Zhejiang province, China, resulting in 40 deaths.

Q129864.name: Indian Mutiny of 1857
aliases: The First War of Indian Independence
Q129864.blurb: Indian Rebellion of 1857: The Bawani Imli massacre saw 52 Indian freedom fighters hanged by British forces.

Q129968.name: Government of Ireland Act 1920
Q129968.blurb: Under the British Government of Ireland Act, Ireland was partitioned into two self-governing territories, Northern and Southern Ireland.

Q130754.name: 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake
aliases: 2004 Indian Ocean Earthquake Countries That Were Not Directly Affected But Have Lost Citizens
2004 Sunda Trench earthquake and resulting Indian Ocean tsunami
Q130754.blurb: The 9.1–9.3 Mw Indian Ocean earthquake shakes northern Sumatra with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent). One of the largest observed tsunamis, it affected coastal and partially mainland areas of Thailand, India, Sri Lanka, the Maldives, Malaysia, Myanmar, Bangladesh, and Indonesia; death toll is estimated at 227,898.

Q130783.name: Night of the Long Knives
aliases: Law Regarding Measures of State Self-Defense
The Night of the Long Knives
The knight of the long knives
Q130783.blurb: The Night of the Long Knives, Adolf Hitler's violent purge of his political rivals in Germany, takes place.

Q130796.name: Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact
aliases: Treaty of Non-Aggression between Germany and the Soviet Union
Day of remembrance for the victims of Stalinism and Nazism
Secret protocol of the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact
Secret protocol of the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact
The Treaty of Nonaggression between Germany and the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics
Treaty of Non-Aggression Between Germany and the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics
Q130796.blurb: Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union signed the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact (pictured), a ten-year mutual non-aggression treaty, which also secretly divided northern and eastern Europe into German and Soviet spheres of influence.

Q130838.name: Today
aliases: Everyone Has a Story (The Today Show)
Where in the World is Matt Lauer
Q130838.blurb: NBC's long-running morning news program Today debuts, with host Dave Garroway.

Q130847.name: Battle of Verdun
Q130847.blurb: Battle of Verdun: German attack captures Côte 265 at the west end of Mort-Homme but the French 75th Infantry Brigade manages to hold Côte 295 at the east end.

Q130861.name: Battle of Kursk
Q130861.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Kursk, the largest full-scale battle in history and the world's largest tank battle, begins in the village of  Prokhorovka.

Q131075.name: 1954 FIFA World Cup
aliases: 1954 Federation Internationale de Football Association World Cup
1954 Fédération Internationale de Football Association World Cup
Q131075.blurb: The FIFA World Cup quarterfinal match between Hungary and Brazil, highly anticipated to be exciting, instead turns violent, with three players ejected and further fighting continuing after the game.

Q131144.name: Tom and Jerry
Q131144.blurb: Puss Gets the Boot, the first Tom and Jerry cartoon, was released to theaters.

Q131297.name: 1994 Genocide against Tutsi
aliases: Arms sales to Rwanda during the Rwandan genocide
Genocide Against the Tutsi in Rwanda
Glossary and supplements for the Rwandan Genocide
Note Relative à la Propagande d’Expansion et de Recrutement
Rwandan Genocide (A million dead in Rwanda)
Q131297.blurb: The Rwandan genocide begins when the aircraft carrying Rwandan president Juvénal Habyarimana and Burundian president Cyprien Ntaryamira is shot down.

Q131311.name: Smolensk air disaster
aliases: Aftermath of the Smolensk air disaster
International response to the 2010 Polish Air Force Tu-154 crash
Parliamentary Team for the Investigate the Causes of the TU-154 M Disaster of April 10, 2010
Parliamentary Team for the Investigation of the Causes of the TU-154 M Disaster of April 10, 2010
Q131311.blurb: Polish Air Force Tu-154M crashes near Smolensk, Russia, killing 96 people, including Polish President Lech Kaczyński, his wife, and dozens of other senior officials and dignitaries.

Q131386.name: Battle of Alesia
Q131386.blurb: Gallic Wars: Vercingetorix, leader of the Gauls, surrenders to the Romans under Julius Caesar, ending the siege and battle of Alesia.

Q131478.name: Der Spiegel
aliases: SPIEGEL-Verlag Rudolf Augstein GmbH & Co. KG
Q131478.blurb: German newspaper Der Spiegel publishes a report by the Federal Intelligence Service accusing figures in Liechtenstein of cooperating with organized crime.

Q131482.name: Hijra
Q131482.blurb: The Hijrah of Muhammad begins, marking the beginning of the Islamic calendar.

Q132515.name: 1950 FIFA World Cup
aliases: 1950 Federation Internationale de Football Association World Cup
1950 Fédération Internationale de Football Association World Cup
Q132515.blurb: Uruguay won the decisive match of the fourth FIFA World Cup, defeating Brazil 2–1 at the Maracanã Stadium in Rio de Janeiro.

Q132568.name: Battle of the Somme
Q132568.blurb: World War I: First day on the Somme: On the first day of the Battle of the Somme 19,000 soldiers of the British Army are killed and 40,000 wounded.

Q133331.name: First Council of Nicaea
Q133331.blurb: The First Council of Nicaea is formally opened, starting the first ecumenical council of the Christian Church.

Q133423.name: Valley of the Kings
aliases: Valley of the Gates of the Kings
Valley of the Tombs of the Kings
Q133423.blurb: Hatshepsut dies at the age of 50 and is buried in the Valley of the Kings.

Q133641.name: Age of Discovery
Q133641.blurb: Age of Discovery: The Treaty of Tordesillas is ratified by Spain.

Q133907.name: Hull note
Q133907.blurb: World War II: The Hull note is given to the Japanese ambassador, demanding that Japan withdraw from China and French Indochina, in return for which the United States would lift economic sanctions. On the same day, Japan's 1st Air Fleet departs Hitokappu Bay for Hawaii.

Q134114.name: Battle of Austerlitz
aliases: The Battle of the Three Emperors
Q134114.blurb: War of the Third Coalition: Battle of Austerlitz: French troops under Napoleon decisively defeat a joint Russo-Austrian force.

Q134202.name: 1966 FIFA World Cup
aliases: 1966 Federation Internationale de Football Association World Cup
1966 Fédération Internationale de Football Association World Cup
World Championship Jules Rimet Cup England 1966
Q134202.blurb: In London, the England national football team won the FIFA World Cup, winning the final against West Germany 4–2 after extra time.

Q134301.name: Katyn massacre
Q134301.blurb: World War II: German news announced the discovery of a mass grave of Polish prisoners of war killed by Soviet forces in Katyn, Russia, causing a diplomatic rift between the Polish government-in-exile and the Soviet Union.

Q134484.name: Typhoon Nina
Q134484.blurb: Typhoon Nina pummels the Philippines with category 5 winds of 265 km/h (165 mph) and a surge that destroys entire villages. At least 1,036 deaths are attributed to the storm.

Q134949.name: Winter War
Q134949.blurb: Winter War: Battle of Raate Road: The Finnish 9th Division finally defeat the numerically superior Soviet forces on the Raate-Suomussalmi road.

Q135475.name: don't ask, don't tell
aliases: Do not ask do not tell
Do not ask, do not tell
Don't ask, don't tell, don't harass, don't pursue
Don't ask, don't tell, don't pursue
National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 1994
Q135475.blurb: The United States military ends its "don't ask, don't tell" policy, allowing gay men and women to serve openly for the first time.

Q136208.name: ZIP code
aliases: List of ZIP codes in Texas
Postal codes in the United States
Postal codes in the United States Virgin Islands
Q136208.blurb: ZIP codes are introduced for United States mail.

Q136344.name: Battle of Köse Dağ
Q136344.blurb: Mongol conquest of Anatolia: Mongols achieved a decisive victory over the Seljuk Turks, leading to the decline and disintegration of the Seljuk state.

Q136935.name: 2012 Dhaka fire
Q136935.blurb: A fire at a clothing factory in Dhaka, Bangladesh, kills at least 112 people.

Q137847.name: treaty of Adrianople
Q137847.blurb: The Ottoman Empire signs the Treaty of Adrianople with Russia, thus ending the Russo-Turkish War.

Q138107.name: War of the Sixth Coalition
aliases: The War of the Sixth Coalition
Q138107.blurb: War of the Sixth Coalition: France engages Russia and Prussia in the Battle of Brienne.

Q139274.name: 2012 phenomenon
Q139274.blurb: 2012 phenomenon: Festivities are held in parts of Mesoamerica to commemorate the conclusion of b'ak'tun 13, a roughly 5,126-year-long cycle in the Mesoamerican Long Count Calendar whose passing many New Age spiritualists had earlier held to portend a variety of cataclysmic or transformative events.

Q139564.name: Atlantic City
aliases: Atlantic City City, Atlantic County, New Jersey
History of Atlantic City, New Jersey
List of people from Atlantic City, New Jersey
Q139564.blurb: In Atlantic City, New Jersey, the first Miss America Pageant, a two-day event, is held.

Q139758.name: Feast of Christ the King
aliases: Solemnity of Jesus Christ, King of the Universe
Solemnity of Our Lord Jesus Christ, King of the Universe
Solemnity of our Lord Jesus Christ, Universal King
Q139758.blurb: Pope Pius XI promulgated the encyclical Quas primas, establishing the Feast of Christ the King.

Q139808.name: Battle of the Maureaco Fields
aliases: The Battle of the Catalaunian Plains
Q139808.blurb: Battle of Chalons: Flavius Aetius battles Attila the Hun. After the battle, which was inconclusive, Attila retreats.  Despite suffering catastrophic losses that led to the collapse of their alliance with the Goths and the destruction of much of the Roman army, the Romans nevertheless proclaimed victory despite the lack of any clear military success.

Q139871.name: Kinmon Incident
Q139871.blurb: Bakumatsu: Kinmon incident: The Chōshū Domain attempts to expel the Satsuma and Aizu Domains from Japan's imperial court.

Q140392.name: Zagreb rocket attacks
Q140392.blurb: During the Croatian War of Independence, the Army of the Republic of Serb Krajina fires cluster bombs at Zagreb, killing seven and wounding over 175 civilians.

Q142493.name: Australia at the 1980 Summer Olympics
Q142493.blurb: The Quietly Confident Quartet of Australia wins the men's 4 x 100 metre medley relay at the Moscow Olympics, the only time the United States has not won the swimming event at Olympic level.

Q142529.name: Algerian Civil War
aliases: Massacres during the Algerian Civil War
Q142529.blurb: During the Algerian Civil War, the Oued Bouaicha massacre sees fifty-two people, mostly infants, killed with axes and knives.

Q143304.name: 2009 Iranian presidential election
Q143304.blurb: A disputed presidential election in Iran leads to wide-ranging local and international protests.

Q143493.name: Twenty One
Q143493.blurb: Quiz show scandals: Twenty-One game show contestant Charles Van Doren admits to a Congressional committee that he had been given questions and answers in advance.

Q143866.name: Fête de la Fédération
aliases: Party of the national day of France
Q143866.blurb: Inaugural Fête de la Fédération is held to celebrate the unity of the French people and the national reconciliation.

Q149560.name: Battle of Stallupönen
Q149560.blurb: World War I: Battle of Stallupönen: The German army of General Hermann von François defeats the Russian force commanded by Paul von Rennenkampf near modern-day Nesterov, Russia.

Q149734.name: Peace of Bautzen
Q149734.blurb: Poland and the Holy Roman Empire conclude the Peace of Bautzen.

Q150229.name: Boxer Rebellion
aliases: Eight-Nation Alliance occupation of northern China
The Society of Right and Harmonious Fists
The Society of Righteous and Harmonious Fists
War of righteous and harmonious fists
Q150229.blurb: Boxer Rebellion: Western Allied and Japanese forces capture the Taku Forts in Tianjin, China.

Q150701.name: War of the Spanish Succession
aliases: The War Of The Spanish Succession
Q150701.blurb: War of the Spanish Succession: The Grand Alliance armies routed the Franco-Spanish-Bavarian army in Ramillies, present-day Belgium.

Q150812.name: 1939 Invasion of Poland
aliases: Nazi German and Soviet invasion of Poland
Q150812.blurb: German forces attacked multiple locations in Poland, including Wieluń and Westerplatte, starting World War II in Europe.

Q150820.name: Playboy
Q150820.blurb: American men's magazine Playboy was founded in Chicago by Hugh Hefner and his associates.

Q150939.name: Operation Weserübung
Q150939.blurb: World War II: Operation Weserübung: Germany invades Denmark and Norway.

Q150974.name: Tehran Conference
Q150974.blurb: World War II: Tehran Conference: U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill and Soviet Premier Joseph Stalin meet in Tehran, Iran, to discuss war strategy.

Q150995.name: Peace of Westphalia
Q150995.blurb: The Peace of Westphalia is signed, marking the end of the Thirty Years' War and the Eighty Years' War.

Q151005.name: Battle of Leipzig
Q151005.blurb: The Sixth Coalition attacks Napoleon in the four-day Battle of Leipzig.

Q151018.name: Battle of the Bulge
Q151018.blurb: World War II: The Battle of the Bulge ends.

Q151052.name: Operation Bagration
Q151052.blurb: World War II: Opening day of the Soviet Union's Operation Bagration against the Army Group Centre.

Q151060.name: Civil Code of the French
Q151060.blurb: Code Napoléon is adopted as French civil law.

Q151187.name: Potsdam Conference
Q151187.blurb: World War II: The Potsdam Conference ends.

Q151290.name: Battle of Moscow
Q151290.blurb: World War II: In the Battle of Moscow, Georgy Zhukov launches a massive Soviet counter-attack against the German army.

Q151340.name: Battle of France
Q151340.blurb: World War II: Germany's conquest of France begins, as the German army crosses the Meuse. Winston Churchill makes his "blood, toil, tears, and sweat" speech to the House of Commons.

Q151423.name: congress of Berlin
aliases: I have returned from Germany with peace for our time
Q151423.blurb: Start of the Congress of Berlin in which the major powers of Europe revise the Treaty of San Stefano, signed on March 3 the same year, that Russia had imposed on a defeated Ottoman Empire.

Q151616.name: Great Northern War
Q151616.blurb: Great Northern War: The battle of Napue between Sweden and Russia is fought in Isokyrö, Ostrobothnia.

Q151622.name: Israeli–Palestinian conflict
aliases: Conflict between Israel and the Palestinians
Societal attitudes toward the Israeli-Palestinian conflict
Q151622.blurb: Israeli–Palestinian conflict: Israeli forces seize the Palestinian freighter Karine A in the Red Sea, finding 50 tons of weapons.

Q151663.name: Revolt of the Comuneros
aliases: Guerra de las Comunidades de Castilla
Q151663.blurb: The Revolt of the Comuneros begins in Spain against the rule of Charles V.

Q151835.name: 2010 Chile earthquake
Q151835.blurb: An earthquake measuring 8.8 on the moment magnitude scale strikes central parts of Chile leaving over 500 victims, and thousands injured. The quake triggers a tsunami which strikes Hawaii shortly after.

Q151850.name: February 2011 Christchurch earthquake
Q151850.blurb: New Zealand's second deadliest earthquake, the 2011 Christchurch earthquake, kills 185 people.

Q151860.name: Siege of Leningrad
Q151860.blurb: World War II: The 872-day Siege of Leningrad is lifted.

Q152004.name: War of the Pacific
aliases: Causes of the War of the Pacific
Consequences of the War of the Pacific
Q152004.blurb: The War of the Pacific breaks out when the Chilean Army occupies the Bolivian port city of Antofagasta.

Q152006.name: partitions of Poland
aliases: Partitions of the Polish Lithuanian Commonwealth
The Partitions of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
Q152006.blurb: Partitions of Poland: The Duchy of Courland and Semigallia, a northern fief of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, ceases to exist and becomes part of Imperial Russia.

Q152008.name: Operation Michael
Q152008.blurb: First World War: On the third day of the German Spring Offensive, the 10th Battalion of the Royal West Kent Regiment is annihilated with many of the men becoming prisoners of war.

Q152033.name: 2008 Sichuan earthquake
Q152033.blurb: An earthquake (measuring around 8.0 magnitude) occurs in Sichuan, China, killing over 69,000 people.

Q152120.name: Wannsee Conference
Q152120.blurb: World War II: At the Wannsee Conference held in the Berlin suburb of Wannsee, senior Nazi German officials discuss the implementation of the "Final Solution to the Jewish question".

Q152142.name: Bombing of Dresden
aliases: Bombing of Dresden in World War 2
Bombing of Dresden in World War II
Bombing of Dresden in the Second World War
Q152142.blurb: World War II: On the first day of the bombing of Dresden, the British Royal Air Force and the United States Army Air Forces begin fire-bombing Dresden.

Q152195.name: Anti-Comintern Pact
Q152195.blurb: Nazi Germany and the Empire of Japan signed the Anti-Comintern Pact, agreeing that, if the Soviet Union attacked one of them, they would consult each other on what measures to take to "safeguard their common interests".

Q152218.name: Nine Years' War
aliases: War of the League of Augsburg
The War of the English Succession
The War of the Grand Alliance
The War of the League of Augsburg
The War of the Palatine Succession
War of the Grand Alliance (Continental European Theatre)
Q152218.blurb: Nine Years' War: At the Battle of Sant Esteve d'en Bas, Catalan miquelets attacked a column of French regular infantry and caused them to surrender.

Q152283.name: Central Powers
aliases: Central Powers of World War I
Q152283.blurb: World War I: The Central Powers' defeat at the Battle of Dobro Pole played a role in the Bulgarian withdrawal from the war and led to the subsequent liberation of Vardar Macedonia.

Q152295.name: Battle of Worringen
Q152295.blurb: The Battle of Worringen ends the War of the Limburg Succession, with John I, Duke of Brabant, being one of the more important victors.

Q152314.name: Cyclone Nargis
Q152314.blurb: Cyclone Nargis makes landfall in Burma killing over 138,000 people and leaving millions of people homeless.

Q152486.name: Battle of Poltava
Q152486.blurb: Peter I of Russia defeats Charles XII of Sweden at the Battle of Poltava, thus effectively ending Sweden's status as a major power in Europe.

Q152499.name: Peninsular War
aliases: British intervention in the Peninsular War
Napoleonic invasion of the Iberian peninsula
Q152499.blurb: Peninsular War: The British defeat the French at the Battle of La Coruña.

Q152521.name: Ziegfeld Follies
Q152521.blurb: Florenz Ziegfeld Jr. staged his first Follies on the roof of the New York Theater in New York City.

Q152758.name: Spanair Flight 5022
Q152758.blurb: Spanair Flight 5022, from Madrid, Spain to Gran Canaria, skids off the runway and crashes at Barajas Airport. Of the 172 people on board, 146 die immediately, and eight more later die of injuries sustained in the crash.

Q152772.name: 2009 World Championships in Athletics
aliases: 2009 World Championships in Athletics medal table
Zimbabwe at the 2009 World Championships in Athletics
Q152772.blurb: At the World Championships in Athletics in Berlin, Usain Bolt ran the 100 metres in 9.58 seconds, breaking his own record set a year earlier.

Q152925.name: Locarno Treaties
Q152925.blurb: Nazi German forces re-occupied the demilitarized Rhineland, violating both the Treaty of Versailles and the Locarno Treaties that were signed after World War I.

Q152946.name: Volkswagen Beetle
Q152946.blurb: The last Volkswagen Beetle made in Germany leaves VW's plant in Emden. Beetle production in Latin America continues until 2003.

Q152989.name: Western Front
aliases: Western Front in World War I
Western Front of World War I
Q152989.blurb: World War I: Western Front: Battle of Belleau Wood: Allied Forces under John J. Pershing and James Harbord engage Imperial German Forces under Wilhelm, German Crown Prince.

Q153081.name: Soweto uprising
Q153081.blurb: Soweto uprising: A non-violent march by 15,000 students in Soweto, South Africa, turns into days of rioting when police open fire on the crowd.

Q153122.name: Tripartite Pact
Q153122.blurb: World War II: The Tripartite Pact is signed in Berlin by Germany, Japan and Italy.

Q153214.name: German occupation of Luxembourg during World War I
Q153214.blurb: World War I: The German occupation of Luxembourg begins.

Q153286.name: Treaty of Nystad
Q153286.blurb: The Great Northern War between Sweden and Russia ends in the Treaty of Nystad.

Q153316.name: Battle of Crete
Q153316.blurb: World War II: Battle of Crete: German paratroops invade Crete.

Q153325.name: Operation Harvest Festival
Q153325.blurb: The Holocaust: The largest massacre of Jews by German forces began at Majdanek concentration camp.

Q153341.name: Operation Sea Lion
aliases: Nazi invasion of the United Kingdom
Planned German invasion of the United Kingdom
Q153341.blurb: World War II: Due to setbacks in the Battle of Britain and approaching autumn weather, Hitler postpones Operation Sea Lion.

Q153376.name: Second Battle of El Alamein
aliases: Fourth Battle of Tell el Eisa
The II Battle of El Alamein
Q153376.blurb: World War II: Allied forces commence the Second Battle of El Alamein, which proves to be the key turning point in the North African campaign.

Q153650.name: Austro-Prussian War
Q153650.blurb: Austro-Prussian War: Italy and Prussia sign a secret alliance against the Austrian Empire.

Q153712.name: Battle of Parabiago
Q153712.blurb: The Milanese army and the St. George's (San Giorgio) Mercenaries of Lodrisio Visconti clash in the Battle of Parabiago; Visconti is defeated.

Q153858.name: Battle of Tannenberg
Q153858.blurb: World War I: Germans defeat the Russians in the Battle of Tannenberg.

Q153867.name: Triple Alliance
Q153867.blurb: The Triple Alliance between the German Empire, Austria-Hungary and the Kingdom of Italy is formed.

Q153992.name: Reichstag fire
Q153992.blurb: Reichstag fire: Germany's parliament building in Berlin, the Reichstag, is set on fire; Marinus van der Lubbe, a young Dutch Communist claims responsibility.

Q154001.name: Council of Constance
Q154001.blurb: The Council of Constance, called by Emperor Sigismund, a supporter of Antipope John XXIII, burns Jerome of Prague following a trial for heresy.

Q154008.name: Vogue
Q154008.blurb: First issue of Vogue is published.

Q154031.name: German Peasants' War
aliases: Engels' and Marx's Interpretation of the Peasants' War
Q154031.blurb: Insurgent peasants led by Anabaptist pastor Thomas Müntzer are defeated at the Battle of Frankenhausen, ending the German Peasants' War in the Holy Roman Empire.

Q154102.name: Peace of Pressburg
Q154102.blurb: Austria and France sign the Treaty of Pressburg.

Q154182.name: Battle of Berlin
Q154182.blurb: World War II: The Red Army begins the final assault on German forces around Berlin, with nearly one million troops fighting in the Battle of the Seelow Heights.

Q154255.name: Munich agreement
Q154255.blurb: Britain, France, Germany and Italy sign the Munich Agreement, whereby Germany annexes the Sudetenland region of Czechoslovakia.

Q154288.name: Black September
Q154288.blurb: Black September: The Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine hijacked four airliners, landing two at Dawson's Field in Jordan and one in Cairo, while the last hijacking attempt was foiled near London.

Q154295.name: Take Ichi convoy
Q154295.blurb: World War II: The Japanese Take Ichi convoy arrived at Halmahera in the Dutch East Indies after losing many ships and thousands of troops to Allied attacks while attempting to carry two divisions of troops from China to New Guinea.

Q154426.name: Battle of Jena–Auerstedt
Q154426.blurb: War of the Fourth Coalition: Napoleon decisively defeats Prussia at the Battle of Jena–Auerstedt.

Q154439.name: Concordat of Worms
Q154439.blurb: Pope Callixtus II and Holy Roman Emperor Henry V agree to the Concordat of Worms to put an end to the Investiture Controversy.

Q154483.name: Augsburg Confession
aliases: Augsburg Confession of the Catholic Faith
The Augsburg Confession of the Catholic Faith
Q154483.blurb: At the Diet of Augsburg the Augsburg Confession is presented to the Holy Roman Emperor by the Lutheran princes and Electors of Germany.

Q154494.name: Aktion T4
aliases: Killing of people with disabilities in Nazi Germany
Q154494.blurb: Adolf Hitler ordered the suspension of the T4 euthanasia program of the mentally ill and disabled, although killings continued in secret for the remainder of World War II.

Q154510.name: Great Recession
Q154510.blurb: The stock market crashes with the Dow Jones dropping a then record 778 points after the United States House of Representatives vote on the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act fails during the beginning stages of the Great Recession.

Q154573.name: WWI Eastern Front
aliases: Eastern Front of World War I
Eastern front in World War I
Q154573.blurb: World War I: Ignoring orders to retreat, Hermann von François led a successful counterattack defending East Prussia at the Battle of Stallupönen and scored the first German victory in the Eastern Front.

Q154577.name: Peace of Augsburg
Q154577.blurb: The Peace of Augsburg is signed by Emperor Charles V and the princes of the Schmalkaldic League.

Q154596.name: Treaties of Tilsit
Q154596.blurb: The first Treaty of Tilsit between France and Russia is signed, ending hostilities between the two countries in the War of the Fourth Coalition.

Q154607.name: Warsaw Ghetto
Q154607.blurb: Holocaust in Poland: The Warsaw Ghetto is established.

Q154635.name: Battle of Blenheim
Q154635.blurb: War of the Spanish Succession: Battle of Blenheim: English and Imperial forces are victorious over French and Bavarian troops.

Q154674.name: Peace of Utrecht
aliases: Tratado de Spain, United States and Países Bajos
Q154674.blurb: France and Great Britain sign the Treaty of Utrecht, bringing an end to the War of the Spanish Succession (Queen Anne's War). Britain accepts Philip V as King of Spain, while Philip renounces any claim to the French throne.

Q154681.name: Anschluss
Q154681.blurb: Anschluss: German troops occupy and annex Austria.

Q154697.name: French and Indian War
aliases: Britain in the French and Indian War
Financial costs of the French and Indian War
Great Britain in the French and Indian War
Q154697.blurb: French and Indian War: French regulars, Canadien militia and Indigenous forces ambushed Rogers' Rangers forces in the Battle on Snowshoes.

Q154705.name: unification of Germany
Q154705.blurb: The German Empire was formed by the unification of previously independent German states, under the rule of Kaiser Wilhelm I.

Q154720.name: Battle of Britain
aliases: Countries in the battle of britain
Q154720.blurb: World War II: Due to setbacks in the Battle of Britain and approaching autumn weather, Hitler postpones Operation Sea Lion.

Q154764.name: Investiture controversy
Q154764.blurb: Pope Callixtus II and Holy Roman Emperor Henry V agree to the Concordat of Worms to put an end to the Investiture Controversy.

Q154860.name: Siege of Sevastopol
Q154860.blurb: World War II: The 250-day Siege of Sevastopol in the Crimea ends when the city falls to Axis forces.

Q154940.name: Lapland War
aliases: World War II events in Finnish Lapland
Q154940.blurb: World War II: The last German troops retreat from Finnish soil in Lapland, ending the Lapland War. Military actions of the Second World War end in Finland.

Q154942.name: Battle of Königgrätz
Q154942.blurb: Austro-Prussian War is decided at the Battle of Königgrätz, enabling Prussia to exclude Austria from German affairs.

Q154981.name: Second Schleswig War
Q154981.blurb: Second Schleswig War: Prussian forces crossed the border into Schleswig, starting the war.

Q155008.name: Operation Uranus
Q155008.blurb: World War II: Soviet troops launched Operation Uranus at the Battle of Stalingrad with the goal of encircling Axis forces, turning the tide of the battle in their favour.

Q155103.name: Siege of Budapest
Q155103.blurb: World War II: The siege of Budapest concludes with the unconditional surrender of German and Hungarian forces to the Red Army.

Q155311.name: Voyager program
Q155311.blurb: Voyager program: NASA launches the Voyager 2 spacecraft.

Q155620.name: Second Battle of Kharkov
Q155620.blurb: World War II: Second Battle of Kharkov: In eastern Ukraine, Red Army forces under Marshal Semyon Timoshenko launch a major offensive from the Izium bridgehead, only to be encircled and destroyed by the troops of Army Group South two weeks later.

Q155629.name: Sesame Street
aliases: A Visit to the Sesame Street Hospital
A Visit to the Sesame Street Museum
Q155629.blurb: The children's television series Sesame Street premiered in the United States.

Q155723.name: NATO bombing of Yugoslavia
aliases: 1999 NATO bombing of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia
NATO bombing of Federal Republic of Yugoslavia
NATO bombing of Serbia and Montenegro
NATO bombing of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia
Strategic Bombardment in the Kosovo War
Strategic bombing during the Kosovo War
Q155723.blurb: NATO bombing of Yugoslavia: A U.S. Air Force F-117 stealth aircraft was shot down by a Yugoslav Army unit.

Q155726.name: Battle of Narva
Q155726.blurb: Great Northern War: Swedish forces led by King Charles XII defeated the Russian army at the Battle of Narva.

Q155796.name: Treaty of Rapallo
Q155796.blurb: The Treaty of Rapallo, pursuant to which Germany and the Soviet Union re-establish diplomatic relations, is signed.

Q155801.name: Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia
aliases: Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia—People's Army
Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionarias de Colombia - Ejército del Pueblo
Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionarias de Colombia – Ejército del Pueblo
Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionarias de Colombia—Ejército del Pueblo
Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia - People's Army
Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia - People’s Army
Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia – People's Army
Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia – People’s Army
The Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia
Q155801.blurb: Civic mobilizations in Colombia against FARC, under the name A million voices against the FARC.

Q155995.name: Operation Spring Awakening
Q155995.blurb: World War II: Cologne is captured by American troops. On the same day, Operation Spring Awakening, the last major German offensive of the war, begins.

Q156086.name: Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle
Q156086.blurb: Signing of the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle ends the War of the Austrian Succession.

Q156211.name: Treaty of Paris (1763)
Q156211.blurb: French and Indian War: The Treaty of Paris ends the war and France cedes Quebec to Great Britain.

Q156447.name: Treaty of Lunéville
Q156447.blurb: War of the Second Coalition: French forces defeated Austrian and Bavarian troops at the Battle of Hohenlinden, eventually resulting in the Austrians signing the Treaty of Lunéville.

Q156554.name: Battle of Jutland
aliases: There seems to be something wrong with our bloody ships to-day
There seems to be something wrong with our bloody ships today
Q156554.blurb: World War I: Battle of Jutland: The British Grand Fleet engages the High Seas Fleet in the largest naval battle of the war, which proves indecisive.

Q156556.name: Treaty of Kiel
aliases: Norway's loss of the Faroe Islands
Q156556.blurb: Treaty of Kiel: Frederick VI of Denmark cedes the Kingdom of Norway to Charles XIII of Sweden in return for Pomerania.

Q156649.name: Imperial German Navy
aliases: German Navy in World War I
Q156649.blurb: The second German Naval Law calls for the Imperial German Navy to be doubled in size, resulting in an Anglo-German naval arms race.

Q156681.name: Battle of Sedan
Q156681.blurb: Franco-Prussian War: The Battle of Sedan is fought, resulting in a decisive Prussian victory.

Q157146.name: French Resistance
aliases: French Resistance during World War II
Q157146.blurb: World War II: French Resistance coup in Algiers, in which 400 civilian French patriots neutralize Vichyist XIXth Army Corps after 15 hours of fighting, and arrest several Vichyist generals, allowing the immediate success of Operation Torch in Algiers.

Q157445.name: Prague offensive
Q157445.blurb: World War II: The Prague Offensive, the last major battle of the Eastern Front, begins.

Q157548.name: War of the Bavarian Succession
aliases: The War of the Bavarian Succession
Q157548.blurb: War of the Bavarian Succession: Russian and French mediators at the Congress of Teschen negotiate an end to the war. In the agreement Austria acquires the Innviertel.

Q157627.name: Battle of the Atlantic
aliases: Battle of the Atlantic (World War II)
World War II/Battle of the Atlantic
Q157627.blurb: World War II: Battle of the Atlantic: HMS Venturer sinks U-864 off the coast of Fedje, Norway, in a rare instance of submarine-to-submarine combat.

Q157648.name: Fourteen Points
Q157648.blurb: U.S. President Woodrow Wilson announces his "Fourteen Points" as conditions for ending World War I.

Q157682.name: East German uprising of 1953
aliases: The Uprising of 1953 in East Germany
Workers Uprising of 1953 in East Germany
Workers' Uprising of 1953 in East Germany
Q157682.blurb: Cold War: East Germany Workers Uprising: In East Germany, the Soviet Union orders a division of troops into East Berlin to quell a rebellion.

Q157873.name: Third Battle of Kharkov
Q157873.blurb: World War II: In the early phases of the Third Battle of Kharkov, Red Army troops re-enter the city.

Q158044.name: Operation Reinhard
Q158044.blurb: The Holocaust: The first mass killings of Jews began at Belzec extermination camp in occupied Poland, the first of the Operation Reinhard camps to begin operation.

Q158054.name: Battle of Lissa
Q158054.blurb: Austro-Prussian War: Battle of Lissa: The Austrian Navy, led by Admiral Wilhelm von Tegetthoff, defeats the Italian Navy near the island of Vis in the Adriatic Sea.

Q158102.name: Winnenden school shooting
Q158102.blurb: Winnenden school shooting: Fifteen are killed and nine are injured before recent graduate Tim Kretschmer shoots and kills himself, leading to tightened weapons restrictions in Germany.

Q158287.name: Case Blue
Q158287.blurb: World War II: Adolf Hitler issues Fuhrer Directive No. 41 summarizing Case Blue, including the German Sixth Army's planned assault on Stalingrad.

Q158322.name: Stern
Q158322.blurb: The West German news magazine Stern begins publishing excerpts from the purported diaries of Adolf Hitler, later revealed to be forgeries.

Q158462.name: Lynyrd Skynyrd
aliases: Best of the Rest (Lynyrd Skynyrd album)
One More From The Road Tour
Q158462.blurb: A plane carrying the rock band Lynyrd Skynyrd crashes in woodland in Mississippi, United States. Six people, including three band members, are killed.

Q158822.name: Pontcysyllte Aqueduct
Q158822.blurb: Official opening of Thomas Telford's Pontcysyllte Aqueduct.

Q159065.name: Vistula–Oder Offensive
Q159065.blurb: World War II: The Vistula–Oder Offensive forces German troops out of Warsaw.

Q159072.name: Battle of Ulm
Q159072.blurb: War of the Third Coalition: Napoleon surrounds the Austrian army at Ulm.

Q159512.name: Battle of Legnica
Q159512.blurb: Battle of Liegnitz: Mongol forces defeat the Polish and German armies.

Q159644.name: Treaty on the Final Settlement with Respect to Germany
aliases: Treaty of the Final Settlement With Respect to Germany
Treaty on the Final Settlement with Respect to Germany (Two-Plus-Four Treaty)
Vertrag über die abschließende Regelung in Bezug auf Deutschland
Q159644.blurb: Cold War: The Treaty on the Final Settlement with Respect to Germany comes into effect, granting full sovereignty to the Federal Republic of Germany.

Q159821.name: Summer Olympic Games
aliases: History of the Summer Olympic Games
List of Olympic medal leading countries
Q159821.blurb: Olympic Games: The Games of the XIV Olympiad: After a hiatus of 12 years caused by World War II, the first Summer Olympics to be held since the 1936 Summer Olympics in Berlin, open in London.

Q159950.name: Russo-Japanese War
Q159950.blurb: Russo-Japanese War: Battle of Port Arthur concludes.

Q160011.name: Battle of the Falkland Islands
Q160011.blurb: World War I: A squadron of Britain's Royal Navy defeats the Imperial German East Asia Squadron in the Battle of the Falkland Islands in the South Atlantic.

Q160056.name: Pan-European Picnic
Q160056.blurb: Several hundred East Germans cross the frontier between Hungary and Austria during the Pan-European Picnic, part of the events that began the process of the Fall of the Berlin Wall.

Q160077.name: Fall of Constantinople
aliases: Fall of the Eastern Roman Empire
Q160077.blurb: Four years before the fall of Constantinople, Constantine XI Palaiologos (pictured) assumed the throne as the last Byzantine emperor.

Q160161.name: Warsaw Ghetto Uprising
aliases: Leaders of the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising
Q160161.blurb: Warsaw Ghetto Uprising: The first uprising of Jews in the Warsaw Ghetto.

Q160205.name: Treaty of Meerssen
Q160205.blurb: Treaty of Meerssen: King Louis the German and his half-brother Charles the Bald partition the Middle Frankish Kingdom into two larger east and west divisions.

Q160211.name: Schuman Declaration
Q160211.blurb: Robert Schuman presents the "Schuman Declaration", considered by some to be the beginning of the creation of what is now the European Union.

Q160387.name: Battle of Actium
aliases: Defeat of Antony and Cleopatra at Actium
Q160387.blurb: Final War of the Roman Republic: Battle of Actium: Off the western coast of Greece, forces of Octavian defeat troops under Mark Antony and Cleopatra.

Q160721.name: Nuremberg Medical Trial
aliases: United States v. Karl Brandt, et al.
United States of America v. Karl Brandt, et al.
Q160721.blurb: The subsequent Nuremberg trials begin with the Doctors' Trial, prosecuting physicians and officers alleged to be involved in Nazi human experimentation and mass murder under the guise of euthanasia.

Q160774.name: Operation Deliberate Force
aliases: 1995 NATO bombing campaign in Bosnia and Herzegovina
1995 NATO air campaign in Bosnia and Herzegovina
1995 NATO bombing in Bosnia and Herzegovina
1995 NATO bombing intervention in Bosnia and Herzegovina
1995 NATO bombing of Bosnia and Herzegovina
Q160774.blurb: Bosnian War: NATO launches Operation Deliberate Force against Bosnian Serb forces.

Q160813.name: 1962 FIFA World Cup
aliases: 1962 Federation Internationale de Football Association World Cup
1962 Fédération Internationale de Football Association World Cup
Q160813.blurb: During the FIFA World Cup, police intervene multiple times in fights between Chilean and Italian players in one of the most violent games in football history.

Q161141.name: Kapp Putsch
Q161141.blurb: The Kapp Putsch begins when the Marinebrigade Ehrhardt is ordered to march on Berlin.

Q161227.name: Yalta Conference
Q161227.blurb: World War II: The Yalta Conference between the "Big Three" (Churchill, Roosevelt, and Stalin) opens at the Livadia Palace in the Crimea.

Q161325.name: Battle of Ramillies
Q161325.blurb: War of the Spanish Succession: The Grand Alliance armies routed the Franco-Spanish-Bavarian army in Ramillies, present-day Belgium.

Q161376.name: Miss Universe
aliases: List of countries yet to compete in Miss Universe pageant
Q161376.blurb: The first Miss Universe pageant is held. Armi Kuusela from Finland wins the title of Miss Universe 1952.

Q161859.name: Pact of Steel
aliases: Pact of Friendship and Alliance between Germany and Italy
Q161859.blurb: Germany and Italy signed the Pact of Steel, a military and political alliance.

Q162228.name: Malmedy massacre
Q162228.blurb: World War II: In retaliation for the massacre of captured Americans by Waffen SS soldiers, U.S. Army personnel killed an estimated 80 Wehrmacht prisoners near Chenogne, Belgium.

Q162250.name: First Battle of El Alamein
aliases: Second Battle of Tel el Eisa
The First Battle of El Alamein
Third Battle of Tel el Eisa
Q162250.blurb: World War II: start of the First Battle of El Alamein.

Q162287.name: Battle of Hürtgen Forest
aliases: World War II/Battle of Hurtgen Forest
Q162287.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Hürtgen Forest begins. It will become the second-longest individual battle that the U.S. Army has ever fought.

Q162333.name: Italian Campaign
aliases: Italian Campaign of the Second World War
Italian campaign of World War II
Q162333.blurb: World War II:  the Brazilian Expeditionary Force defeat the German forces in the Battle of Monte Castello on the Italian front.

Q162357.name: Battle of Smolensk
Q162357.blurb: World War II: The German army launches its offensive to encircle several Soviet armies near Smolensk.

Q162401.name: Prague Spring
Q162401.blurb: Alexander Dubček comes to power in Czechoslovakia, effectively beginning the "Prague Spring".

Q162546.name: Vienna offensive
Q162546.blurb: World War II: Soviet forces invade Austria and capture Vienna. Polish and Soviet forces liberate Danzig.

Q162665.name: Nika Riots
Q162665.blurb: Nika riots in Constantinople: A quarrel between supporters of different chariot teams—the Blues and the Greens—in the Hippodrome escalates into violence.

Q162932.name: 1st United States Congress
aliases: First Congress of the United States
Q162932.blurb: In New York City, the first Congress of the United States meets, putting the United States Constitution into effect.

Q163107.name: Überlingen mid-air collision
aliases: Bashkirian Airlines Flight 2937 & DHL Flight 611 collision
Bashkirian Airlines Flight 2937 & DHL Flight 611 mid-air collision
Bashkirian Airlines Flight 2937 And DHL Flight 611 Mid-Air Collision
DHL Boeing 757 and Bashkirian Airlines TU-154 Over Uberlingen, Germany
Q163107.blurb: Bashkirian Airlines Flight 2937 and DHL Flight 611 collided in mid-air over Überlingen, Germany, killing all 71 people aboard both aircraft.

Q163244.name: Potsdam Declaration
aliases: Proclamation Defining Terms for Japanese Surrender
Q163244.blurb: World War II: The Potsdam Declaration is signed in Potsdam, Germany.

Q163476.name: Ottoman–Safavid War
Q163476.blurb: The treaty of Zuhab ends the fifteen-year-long war between the Ottomans and the Safavids.

Q163573.name: Algeciras Conference
Q163573.blurb: The Algeciras Conference gives France and Spain control over Morocco.

Q163730.name: Christmas truce
Q163730.blurb: World War I: The "Christmas truce" begins.

Q163780.name: Slovak National Uprising
aliases: Slovakian resistance movement in World War II
Q163780.blurb: World War II:  Slovak National Uprising takes place as 60,000 Slovak troops turn against the Nazis.

Q163883.name: Ten-Day War
Q163883.blurb: Three months after the end of the Ten-Day War, the last soldier of the Yugoslav People's Army leaves the territory of the Republic of Slovenia.

Q163891.name: St. Bartholomew's Day massacre
Q163891.blurb: French Wars of Religion: Mob violence against thousands of Huguenots in Paris results in the St. Bartholomew's Day massacre.

Q164348.name: Hungarian Revolution of 1956
Q164348.blurb: Secret police shoot several anti-communist protesters, igniting the Hungarian Revolution.

Q164393.name: Treaty of Ryswick
Q164393.blurb: The Treaty of Ryswick is signed by France, England, Spain, the Holy Roman Empire and the Dutch Republic, ending the Nine Years' War.

Q164432.name: Eighty Years' War
Q164432.blurb: Eighty Years' War: The Treaty of Münster and Osnabrück is signed, ending the conflict between the Netherlands and Spain.

Q164679.name: Great Fire of London
Q164679.blurb: The Great Fire of London breaks out and burns for three days, destroying 10,000 buildings, including Old St Paul's Cathedral.

Q164697.name: Battle of Riade
Q164697.blurb: After a ten-year truce, German King Henry the Fowler defeats a Hungarian army at the Battle of Riade near the Unstrut river.

Q164706.name: The Watchtower Announcing Jehovah's Kingdom
aliases: Zion's Watch Tower & Herald of Christ's Presence
Zion's Watch Tower and Herald of Christ's Presence
Q164706.blurb: Charles Taze Russell publishes the first edition of the religious magazine The Watchtower.

Q164746.name: The Wall Street Journal
aliases: History of The Wall Street Journal
Political stance of The Wall Street Journal
Q164746.blurb: The first issue of The Wall Street Journal is published.

Q164771.name: Agadir Crisis
Q164771.blurb: Germany dispatches the gunboat SMS Panther to Morocco, sparking the Agadir Crisis.

Q164815.name: Woodstock Festival
Q164815.blurb: The Woodstock Music & Art Fair opens in Bethel, New York, featuring some of the top rock musicians of the era.

Q164983.name: Gallipoli Campaign
Q164983.blurb: World War I: The Battle of Gallipoli concludes with an Ottoman Empire victory when the last Allied forces are evacuated from the peninsula.

Q165136.name: Swabian War
Q165136.blurb: The Treaty of Basel concludes the Swabian War.

Q165425.name: Battle of Lepanto
aliases: Allegory of the Battle of Lepanto
Allegory of the Battle of Lepanto (Veronese)
Q165425.blurb: The Battle of Lepanto is fought, and the Ottoman Navy suffers its first defeat.

Q165720.name: 1860 Oxford evolution debate
Q165720.blurb: The 1860 Oxford evolution debate at the Oxford University Museum of Natural History takes place.

Q165725.name: Balkan Wars
Q165725.blurb: In the aftermath of the Balkan Wars, Greeks living in southern Albania proclaimed the short-lived Autonomous Republic of Northern Epirus.

Q166001.name: Scanian War
Q166001.blurb: Scanian War: The Swedish warship Kronan, one of the largest ships in the world at the time, sank at the Battle of Öland (depicted) with the loss of around 800 men.

Q166015.name: Battle of Lesnaya
Q166015.blurb: Peter the Great defeats the Swedes at the Battle of Lesnaya.

Q166087.name: 2007–08 Kenyan crisis
Q166087.blurb: Riots erupt in Mombasa, Kenya, after Mwai Kibaki is declared the winner of the presidential election, triggering a political, economic, and humanitarian crisis.

Q166210.name: Tampico Affair
Q166210.blurb: Mexican Revolution: The last of U.S. forces withdraw from Veracruz, occupied seven months earlier in response to the Tampico Affair.

Q166283.name: 1997 Central Texas tornado outbreak
Q166283.blurb: The 1997 Central Texas tornado outbreak occurs, spawning multiple tornadoes in Central Texas, including the F5 that killed 27 in Jarrell.

Q166495.name: Catalonia Offensive

Q166877.name: Emperor of Austria

Q166961.name: Battle of Shrewsbury
Q166961.blurb: Battle of Shrewsbury: King Henry IV of England defeats rebels to the north of the county town of Shropshire, England.

Q166981.name: Act of Independence of Lithuania
aliases: Act of Restoration of Independence of Lithuania

Q167143.name: Raid on Berlin
Q167143.blurb: Seven Years' War: Russian and Austrian troops briefly occupy Berlin.

Q167246.name: Bosnian Crisis
aliases: Annexation of Bosnia and Herzegovina by Austria-Hungary
Austrian annexation of Bosnia and Herzegovina
Austro-Hungarian annexation of Bosnia and Herzegovina
Q167246.blurb: Serbia formally withdraws its opposition to Austro-Hungarian actions in the Bosnian Crisis.

Q167259.name: Battle of Lützen
Q167259.blurb: King Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden was killed at the Battle of Lützen during the Thirty Years' War.

Q167396.name: Balkan Pact
Q167396.blurb: The Balkan Entente is formed between Greece, Romania, Yugoslavia, and Turkey.

Q167455.name: First Moroccan Crisis
Q167455.blurb: Kaiser Wilhelm II of Germany declares his support for Moroccan independence in Tangier, beginning the First Moroccan Crisis.

Q167457.name: Treaty of Rome

Treaty establishing the European Economic Community 1957

Q168268.name: Peace of Prague
Q168268.blurb: The Austro-Prussian War ends with the Treaty of Prague.

Q168708.name: Dallas
Q168708.blurb: The American soap opera Dallas aired the episode "A House Divided", which led to eight months of international speculation on "Who shot J.R.?"

Q169023.name: Battle of Talavera
Q169023.blurb: Peninsular War: Sir Arthur Wellesley's British, Portuguese and Spanish army repulse a French force led by Joseph Bonaparte in the Battle of Talavera.

Q169072.name: Colombian conflict
aliases: Economic impact of the Colombian conflict
United States of America in the Colombian conflict
Q169072.blurb: Colombian conflict: leftist guerrillas of the 19th of April Movement seize control of the Palace of Justice in Bogotá.

Q169401.name: Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty

United States withdrawal from the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty
Q169401.blurb: The Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty comes into effect.

Q169436.name: Battle of Rostov
Q169436.blurb: World War II: During the preliminaries of the Battle of Rostov, German forces reach the Sea of Azov with the capture of Mariupol.

Q169598.name: Honnō-ji Incident
Q169598.blurb: Sengoku period: Oda Nobunaga, the most powerful of the Japanese daimyōs, is forced to commit suicide by his own general Akechi Mitsuhide.

Q169789.name: Second Vatican Council
aliases: Second Ecumenical Council of the Vatican
Reforms of the Second Vatican Council
Q169789.blurb: The Second Vatican Council becomes the first ecumenical council of the Roman Catholic Church in 92 years.

Q170018.name: 110th United States Congress
Q170018.blurb: The 110th United States Congress convenes, electing Nancy Pelosi as the first female Speaker of the House in U.S. history.

Q170108.name: 1967 Gibraltar sovereignty referendum
Q170108.blurb: The people of Gibraltar vote to remain a British dependency rather than becoming part of Spain.

Q170113.name: Battle of Saint Gotthard
Q170113.blurb: Ottoman forces are defeated in the battle of Saint Gotthard by an Austrian army led by Raimondo Montecuccoli, resulting in the Peace of Vasvár.

Q170170.name: Ramsar Convention

Ramsar Convention on Wetlands of International Importance
Ramsar Convention on Wetlands of International Importance Especially as Waterfowl Habitat
Q170170.blurb: The international Ramsar Convention for the conservation and sustainable utilization of wetlands is signed in Ramsar, Mazandaran, Iran.

Q170265.name: Battle of Bautzen
Q170265.blurb: Napoleon Bonaparte leads his French troops into the Battle of Bautzen in Saxony, Germany, against the combined armies of Russia and Prussia. The battle ends the next day with a French victory.

Q170306.name: German Revolution of 1918–1919
Q170306.blurb: The German Revolution of 1918–19 begins when 40,000 sailors take over the port in Kiel.

Q170314.name: Second Sino-Japanese War
aliases: War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression
