Q170334.name: Srebrenica massacre
Q170334.blurb: Yugoslav Wars: Srebrenica massacre begins, lasting until 22 July.

Q170351.name: Bombing of Guernica
Q170351.blurb: Spanish Civil War: The Bombing of Guernica by the Condor Legion of the Luftwaffe resulted in a devastating firestorm that caused widespread destruction and civilian deaths and inspired one of Pablo Picasso's most famous paintings.

Q170360.name: Armistice of 22 June 1940
Q170360.blurb: World War II: France is forced to sign the Second Compiègne armistice with Germany, in the same railroad car in which the Germans signed the Armistice in 1918.

Q170413.name: Sputnik programme
Q170413.blurb: Sputnik program: Korabl-Sputnik 2: The Soviet Union launches the satellite with the dogs Belka and Strelka, 40 mice, two rats and a variety of plants.

Q170422.name: 2010 Summer Youth Olympics
Q170422.blurb: The inaugural edition of the Youth Olympic Games opened in Singapore for athletes aged between 14 and 18.

Q170531.name: Council of Chalcedon
Q170531.blurb: The first session of the Council of Chalcedon begins.

Q170652.name: Great Blizzard of 1888
Q170652.blurb: The Great Blizzard of 1888 begins along the eastern seaboard of the United States, shutting down commerce and killing more than 400 people.

Q170682.name: Gaza War (2008–2009)
aliases: December 2008 Gaza Strip Airstrikes and Ground Offensive
Q170682.blurb: Operation Cast Lead: Israel launches three-week operation on Gaza.

Q170850.name: Anglo-Zanzibar War
Q170850.blurb: Anglo-Zanzibar War: The shortest war in world history (09:02 to 09:40), between the United Kingdom and Zanzibar.

Q171178.name: Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster
aliases: 2011 Fukushima I nuclear reactor blast crisis
Safety history of the Fukushima I Nuclear Power Plant
Q171178.blurb: An earthquake measuring 9.0 in magnitude strikes 130 km (81 mi) east of Sendai, Japan, triggering a tsunami killing thousands of people. This event also triggered the second largest nuclear accident in history, and one of only two events to be classified as a Level 7 on the International Nuclear Event Scale.

Q171328.name: Charter of the United Nations
aliases: Charter of the United Nations Amendment Act 1993
Chapter I of the United Nations Charter
Chapter XIX of the UN Charter
Chapter XIX of the United Nations Charter
The Charter of the United Nations
Q171328.blurb: The United Nations Charter is signed by 50 Allied nations in San Francisco, California.

Q171416.name: Battle of Trafalgar
Q171416.blurb: Napoleonic Wars: A British fleet led by Lord Nelson defeats a combined French and Spanish fleet under Admiral Villeneuve in the Battle of Trafalgar.

Q171503.name: nakfa
Q171503.blurb: Eritrea adopts the nakfa as its official currency.

Q171552.name: 1994 San Marino Grand Prix
Q171552.blurb: Three-time Formula One champion Ayrton Senna is killed in an accident during the San Marino Grand Prix.

Q171704.name: 1973 Dutch Grand Prix
Q171704.blurb: Driver Roger Williamson is killed during the Dutch Grand Prix, after a suspected tire failure causes his car to pitch into the barriers at high speed.

Q171784.name: Eurovision Song Contest 1956
aliases: Austria in the Eurovision Song Contest 1956
Denmark in the Eurovision Song Contest 1956
Grand Prix Eurovision de la Chanson Européenne 1956
United Kingdom in the Eurovision Song Contest 1956
Q171784.blurb: The first edition of the Eurovision Song Contest was held in Lugano, Switzerland.

Q171855.name: 1970 Italian Grand Prix
Q171855.blurb: During the practice session of the Italian Grand Prix at Monza Circuit, Jochen Rindt was killed and subsequently became motor racing's only posthumous world champion.

Q171938.name: 1961 Italian Grand Prix
Q171938.blurb: In the Italian Grand Prix, a crash causes the death of German Formula One driver Wolfgang von Trips and 15 spectators who are hit by his Ferrari, the deadliest accident in F1 history.

Q172068.name: World War II in Yugoslav Macedonia
Q172068.blurb: Beginning of the National Liberation War of Macedonia.

Q172129.name: 2001 Japan Airlines mid-air incident
Q172129.blurb: Two Japan Airlines planes nearly collide over Suruga Bay in Japan.

Q172316.name: Effects of Hurricane Katrina in New Orleans
Q172316.blurb: Hurricane Katrina devastates much of the U.S. Gulf Coast from Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle, killing up to 1,392 people and causing $125 billion in damage.

Q172368.name: Battle of Sirmium
Q172368.blurb: The Byzantines defeat the Hungarian army decisively at Sirmium, forcing the Hungarians to sue for peace.

Q172991.name: Council of Trent
aliases: A Protestant view of the Council from Schaff-Herzog Encyc of Religion
Q172991.blurb: The Council of Trent establishes an official distinction between Roman Catholicism and Protestantism.

Q173025.name: 1950 Italian Grand Prix
Q173025.blurb: "Nino" Farina becomes the first Formula One Drivers' champion after winning the 1950 Italian Grand Prix.

Q173034.name: Battle of Midway
Q173034.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Midway begins. Japanese Admiral Chūichi Nagumo orders a strike on Midway Island by much of the Imperial Japanese Navy.

Q173069.name: 1951 British Grand Prix
Q173069.blurb: Ferrari take their first Formula One grand prix victory at the British Grand Prix at Silverstone.

Q173075.name: 1950 British Grand Prix
Q173075.blurb: The inaugural Formula One World Championship race takes place at Silverstone Circuit. The race was won by Giuseppe Farina, who would go on to become the inaugural champion that year.

Q173077.name: Battle of Tours
aliases: Battle of the Highway of the Martyrs
Q173077.blurb: Charles Martel's forces defeat an Umayyad army near Tours, France.

Q173129.name: 1976 German Grand Prix
Q173129.blurb: Niki Lauda has a severe accident that almost claims his life at the German Grand Prix at Nürburgring.

Q173161.name: 2005 United States Grand Prix
aliases: Michelin's tyre mistake sends US Formula One Grand Prix into farce
XXXIV Foster's United States Grand Prix
Q173161.blurb: Only six race cars competed in the United States Grand Prix at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway in Indianapolis, Indiana, after all the Michelin-shod entrants were withdrawn due to safety concerns.

Q173220.name: 2007 Formula One espionage controversy
Q173220.blurb: The McLaren F1 team are found guilty of possessing confidential information from the Ferrari team, fined $100 million, and excluded from the constructors' championship standings.

Q173457.name: Dreyfus affair
aliases: Public scandal of the Dreyfus Affair
The public scandal of the Dreyfus Affair
Trial and conviction of Alfred Dreyfus
Q173457.blurb: Dreyfus affair: French army officer Alfred Dreyfus is stripped of his rank and sentenced to life imprisonment on Devil's Island.

Q173973.name: Swissair Flight 306
Q173973.blurb: Swissair Flight 306 crashes near Dürrenäsch, Switzerland, killing all 80 people on board.

Q174205.name: Tenth Russo-Turkish War
Q174205.blurb: Russo-Turkish War (1877–78): Sofia is liberated from Ottoman rule.

Q174450.name: Roman Tetrarchy
Q174450.blurb: Roman Emperors Diocletian and Maximian appoint Galerius as Caesar to Diocletian, beginning the period of four rulers known as the Tetrarchy.

Q174990.name: Gwangju Uprising
Q174990.blurb: Students in Gwangju, South Korea begin demonstrations calling for democratic reforms.

Q175636.name: treaty of Corbeil
Q175636.blurb: Louis IX of France and James I of Aragon sign the Treaty of Corbeil, renouncing claims of feudal overlordship in one another's territories and separating the House of Barcelona from the politics of France.

Q175653.name: Siege of Sarajevo
Q175653.blurb: The Siege of Sarajevo officially ends.

Q175767.name: Johnson South Reef skirmish
Q175767.blurb: In the Johnson South Reef Skirmish Chinese forces defeat Vietnamese forces in an altercation over control of one of the Spratly Islands.

Q176883.name: 2010 FIFA World Cup
aliases: 2010 FIFA World Cup South Africa on CBC
2010 Federation Internationale de Football Association World Cup
2010 Fédération Internationale de Football Association World Cup
List of 2010 FIFA World Cup matches
Q176883.blurb: The first FIFA World Cup held on African soil kicks off in South Africa.

Q176930.name: Declaration by United Nations
Q176930.blurb: The Declaration by United Nations is signed by twenty-six nations.

Q177109.name: Slovak–Hungarian War
aliases: Weapons employed in the Slovak-Hungarian War
Weapons employed in the Slovak–Hungarian War
Q177109.blurb: The Hungarian air force attacks the headquarters of the Slovak air force in Spišská Nová Ves, killing 13 people and beginning the Slovak–Hungarian War.

Q177258.name: 1492 papal conclave
Q177258.blurb: The first conclave to be held in the Sistine Chapel elected Roderic Borja as Pope Alexander VI to succeed Innocent VIII.

Q177283.name: Altmark Incident
Q177283.blurb: World War II: Altmark incident: The German tanker Altmark is boarded by sailors from the British destroyer HMS Cossack. A total of 299 British prisoners are freed.

Q177470.name: Battle of Stoney Creek
Q177470.blurb: War of 1812: In the Battle of Stoney Creek, considered a critical turning point in the war, a British force of 700 under John Vincent defeats an American force twice its size under William Winder and John Chandler.

Q177859.name: Triple Entente
Q177859.blurb: The Ukrainian People's Republic asks the Entente and the United States for help fighting the Bolsheviks.

Q177918.name: First Balkan War
Q177918.blurb: First Balkan War: Greece completes its capture of the eastern Aegean island of Chios, as the last Ottoman forces on the island surrender.

Q178275.name: 1918–1920 flu pandemic
aliases: 1918 swine flu outbreak in the United Kingdom
Q178275.blurb: The 1918 influenza epidemic spreads to Western Samoa, killing 7,542 (about 20% of the population) by the end of the year.

Q178346.name: Treaty of Dancing Rabbit Creek
Q178346.blurb: The Treaty of Dancing Rabbit Creek, the first removal treaty in accordance with the Indian Removal Act, is proclaimed. The Choctaws in Mississippi cede land east of the river in exchange for payment and land in the West.

Q178510.name: Battle of Mohács
Q178510.blurb: Battle of Mohács: The Ottoman Turks led by Suleiman the Magnificent defeat and kill the last Jagiellonian king of Hungary and Bohemia.

Q178687.name: First Sino-Japanese War
Q178687.blurb: The First Sino-Japanese War begins when the Japanese fire upon a Chinese warship.

Q178810.name: Syrian Civil War
aliases: Background of the Syrian civil war
Cultural impact of the Syrian Civil War
Films about the Syrian Civil War
Humanitarian impact of the Syrian Civil War
Non-state parties in the Syrian Civil War
Q178810.blurb: Syrian civil war: The Movement for a Democratic Society (TEV-DEM) is established with the stated goal of re-organizing Syria along the lines of democratic confederalism.

Q178912.name: Battle of Cape St. Vincent
Q178912.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Battle of Cape St. Vincent.

Q179077.name: Pontiac's War
Q179077.blurb: Pontiac's War begins with Pontiac's attempt to seize Fort Detroit from the British.

Q179250.name: French invasion of Russia
aliases: List of French commanders in the Russian 1812 Campaign
Q179250.blurb: French invasion of Russia: The Battle of Borodino, the bloodiest battle of the Napoleonic Wars, is fought near Moscow and results in a French victory.

Q179272.name: Cocos Islands Mutiny
Q179272.blurb: World War II: Gunners of the Ceylon Garrison Artillery on Horsburgh Island in the Cocos Islands rebel in the Cocos Islands Mutiny. Their mutiny is crushed and three of them are executed, the only British Commonwealth soldiers to be executed for mutiny during the Second World War.

Q179275.name: insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
Q179275.blurb: War in North-West Pakistan: The Pakistani Armed Forces open Operation Rah-e-Nijat against the Taliban and other Islamist rebels in the South Waziristan area of the Federally Administered Tribal Areas.

Q179338.name: 2008 Singapore Grand Prix
Q179338.blurb: The Singapore Grand Prix is held as Formula One's inaugural night race, with Fernando Alonso winning the event. Almost a year later it was revealed that Alonso's team-mate Nelson Piquet Jr. had been ordered to crash his car to help bring out the safety car and give Alonso the advantage and win.

Q179591.name: Battle of Cannae
Q179591.blurb: The Carthaginian army led by Hannibal defeats a numerically superior Roman army at the Battle of Cannae.

Q179670.name: Battle of Gaugamela
Q179670.blurb: Alexander the Great defeats Darius III of Persia in the Battle of Gaugamela.

Q179826.name: First Council of Constantinople
aliases: First Council of Constantinople (Second Ecumenical Council)
Q179826.blurb: The end of the First Council of Christian bishops convened in Constantinople by the Roman emperor Theodosius I.

Q179868.name: 1932 United States presidential election
aliases: 1932 Convention of the Socialist Party of America
Q179868.blurb: Franklin D. Roosevelt is elected as the 32nd President of the United States, defeating incumbent president Herbert Hoover.

Q179975.name: Chinese Civil War
aliases: Civil war between Nationalists and Communists
War of Liberation of the People's Republic of China
Q179975.blurb: Chinese Civil War: The Communist forces take over Tianjin from the Nationalist government.

Q180182.name: Battle of Iwo Jima
Q180182.blurb: World War II: Battle of Iwo Jima: About 30,000 United States Marines land on the island of Iwo Jima.

Q180654.name: Occupy Wall Street
aliases: List of notable Occupy Wall Street supporters
Pepper spraying at the Occupy Wall Street demonstration
Pepper spraying of the Occupy Wall Street demonstrators
Q180654.blurb: Occupy Wall Street movement begins in Zuccotti Park, New York City.

Q180659.name: Battle of Wilson's Creek
Q180659.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Wilson's Creek: A mixed force of Confederate, Missouri State Guard, and Arkansas State troops defeat outnumbered attacking Union forces in the southwestern part of the state.

Q180834.name: 2006 protests in Hungary
aliases: protests against the government of Hungary in 2006
Q180834.blurb: An audio tape of a private speech by Hungarian Prime Minister Ferenc Gyurcsány is leaked to the public, in which he confessed that his Hungarian Socialist Party had lied to win the 2006 election, sparking widespread protests across the country.

Q180897.name: Treaty of Tordesillas
Q180897.blurb: Age of Discovery: The Treaty of Tordesillas is ratified by Spain.

Q181013.name: Little Boy
Q181013.blurb: World War II: The USS Indianapolis arrives at Tinian with components and enriched uranium for the Little Boy nuclear bomb.

Q181146.name: Dos de Mayo Uprising
Q181146.blurb: Outbreak of the Peninsular War: The people of Madrid rise up in rebellion against French occupation. Francisco de Goya later memorializes this event in his painting The Second of May 1808.

Q181289.name: Bodo League massacre
Q181289.blurb: Korean War: Suspected communist sympathizers (between 60,000 and 200,000) are executed in the Bodo League massacre.

Q181293.name: Battle of Rozgony
Q181293.blurb: At the Battle of Rozgony, King Charles I of Hungary wins a decisive victory over the family of Palatine Amade Aba.

Q181480.name: Battle of Vítkov Hill
Q181480.blurb: Battle of Vítkov Hill, decisive victory of Czech Hussite forces commanded by Jan Žižka against Crusade army led by Sigismund, Holy Roman Emperor.

aliases: Domovinski rat u Bosni i Hercegovini
Unrest in SR Bosnia and Herzegovina
War crimes in the Bosnian War

Q181902.name: Treaty of Trianon

Q181902.blurb: Hungary loses 71% of its territory and 63% of its population when the Treaty of Trianon is signed in Paris.

Q181943.name: I Love Lucy
aliases: List of all I Love Lucy Cast
Lucy, you got some 'splaining to do
Q181943.blurb: Almost 72 percent of all television sets in the United States are tuned into I Love Lucy to watch Lucy give birth.

Q182062.name: Greek War of Independence
Q182062.blurb: Greek War of Independence: Demetrios Ypsilantis is elected president of the legislative assembly.

Q182085.name: 2011 Lokomotiv Yaroslavl air disaster
Q182085.blurb: The Lokomotiv Yaroslavl plane crash in Russia kills 43 people, including nearly the entire roster of the Lokomotiv Yaroslavl Kontinental Hockey League team.

Q182240.name: Siege of Warsaw
Q182240.blurb: World War II: The siege of Warsaw comes to an end.

Q182323.name: Ford Model T
Q182323.blurb: The last Ford Model T rolls off the assembly line after a production run of 15,007,003 vehicles.

Q182515.name: Treaty of Sèvres
Q182515.blurb: World War I: Ottoman sultan Mehmed VI's representatives sign the Treaty of Sèvres that divides up the Ottoman Empire between the Allies.

Q182776.name: Jyllands-Posten Muhammad cartoons controversy

Economic and human costs on the Jyllands-Posten Muhammad cartoons controversy
Economic and social consequences of the Jyllands-Posten Muhammad cartoons controversy
Q182776.blurb: Controversial drawings of Muhammad are printed in a Danish newspaper.

Q182798.name: 2012 Summer Paralympics
Q182798.blurb: The XIV Paralympic Games open in London, England, United Kingdom.

Q182803.name: Zimbabwean dollar
Q182803.blurb: Zimbabwe officially abandons the Zimbabwean dollar as its official currency.

Q182814.name: Antarctic Treaty System

Q182831.name: Battle of Schliengen
Q182831.blurb: War of the First Coalition: The Battle of Schliengen was fought between the French and Austrian armies, who both claimed victory.

Q183140.name: ozone depletion

Q183249.name: Battle of the Sit River
Q183249.blurb: The Battle of the Sit River begins two centuries of Mongol horde domination of Rus.

Q183286.name: Battle of Cēsis
Q183286.blurb: Estonian War of Independence: The decisive defeat of the Baltische Landeswehr in the Battle of Cēsis; this date is celebrated as Victory Day in Estonia.

Q183375.name: Seventeen Point Agreement

中央人民政府和西藏地方政府關於和平解放西藏辦法的協議

Q183421.name: My Lai Massacre

Q183447.name: Capture of the Dutch fleet at Den Helder
Q183447.blurb: After crossing the frozen Zuiderzee, the French cavalry capture 14 Dutch ships and 850 guns, in a rare occurrence of surrender of naval vessels to land forces.

Q183644.name: Pravda

Q184172.blurb: French explorer René Caillié reached Timbuktu in present-day Mali, and later received a 9,000-franc prize from the Société de Géographie for being the first European to return with a description of the city.

Q184183.blurb: Second Balkan War: The Greeks defeat the Bulgarians in the Battle of Doiran.

Q184310.name: Cedar Revolution

Q184320.name: Battle of Borodino
Q184320.blurb: French invasion of Russia: The Battle of Borodino, the bloodiest battle of the Napoleonic Wars, is fought near Moscow and results in a French victory.

Q184332.name: First Council of Ephesus
Q184332.blurb: The Council of Ephesus, the third ecumenical council, begins, dealing with Nestorianism.

Q184637.name: Ten Years' War
Q184637.blurb: The Ten Years' War begins against Spanish rule in Cuba.

Q184928.name: Russian Revolution of 1905
Q184928.blurb: Russian Revolution of 1905: Grand Duke Sergei Alexandrovich of Russia is assassinated in the Moscow Kremlin by Socialist Revolutionary Ivan Kalyayev.

Q185203.name: transit of Venus
Q185203.blurb: Jeremiah Horrocks and William Crabtree made the first successful observation  of a transit of Venus (example pictured) from Earth.

Q185380.name: Air France Flight 447
Q185380.blurb: Air France Flight 447 crashes into the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of Brazil on a flight from Rio de Janeiro to Paris. All 228 passengers and crew are killed.

Q185407.name: La Violencia
Q185407.blurb: Jorge Eliécer Gaitán's assassination provokes a violent riot in Bogotá (the Bogotazo), and a further ten years of violence in Colombia.

Q185517.name: war on drugs
aliases: Alternatives to the War on Drugs
Economic effects of the War on Drugs
Economic impact of the War on Drugs
Financial costs of the War on Drugs
Public opinion on the War on Drugs
Public opposition to the War on Drugs
Social effects of the War on Drugs
Social impact of the War on Drugs
Socio-economic effects of the War on Drugs
Socioeconomic effects of the War on Drugs
U.S. foreign policy and the War on Drugs
U.S. government involvement in drug trafficking
Q185517.blurb: War on drugs: In one of the largest drug busts in American history, the United States Coast Guard intercepts a ship with over 4,300 kilograms (9,500 lb) of cocaine on board.

Q185642.name: Bloody Sunday
Q185642.blurb: Bloody Sunday occurs in Saint Petersburg, beginning the 1905 revolution.

Q185729.name: War on Terrorism
aliases: Casualtes of the war on terror
Casualties of the Global War on Terrorism
Casualties of the War on Terror
Civilians killed in the war on terror
Costs of the war on terror
Financial cost of the War on Terror
National Military Strategic Plan for the War on Terror
National Military Strategic Plan for the War on Terrorism
The Global Struggle Against Violent Extremism
Q185729.blurb: In an address to a joint session of Congress and the American people, U.S. President George W. Bush declares a "war on terror".

Q186033.name: 1893 Sea Islands hurricane
Q186033.blurb: The Sea Islands hurricane strikes the United States near Savannah, Georgia, killing between 1,000 and 2,000 people.

Q186107.name: Battle of Stockach
Q186107.blurb: War of the Second Coalition: In their second battle in seven days, the French Army of the Danube and Habsburg forces battled for control of the Hegau region.

Q186166.name: 1900 Galveston hurricane
Q186166.blurb: Galveston hurricane: A powerful hurricane hits Galveston, Texas killing about 8,000 people.

Q186291.name: Great Hurricane of 1780
aliases: Great Hurricane of the West Indies
Q186291.blurb: The deadliest Atlantic hurricane on record began to impact the Caribbean, killing at least 20,000 people across the Antilles over the subsequent days.

Q186356.name: New Deal
aliases: EMIC (Emergency Maternity and Infant Care Program)
Emergency Maternity and Infant Care Program
Q186356.blurb: New Deal: Under the authority of the newly-enacted Federal Emergency Relief Administration, President Franklin D. Roosevelt issues Executive Order 7034 to create the Works Progress Administration.

Q186444.name: Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons
aliases: Treaty on the Nonproliferation of Nuclear Weapons
Q186444.blurb: The Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons goes into effect after ratification by 43 nations.

Q187152.name: Balfour Declaration
Q187152.blurb: The Balfour Declaration proclaims British support for the "establishment in Palestine of a national home for the Jewish people" with the clear understanding "that nothing shall be done which may prejudice the civil and religious rights of existing non-Jewish communities".

Q187201.name: Second Council of Nicaea
Q187201.blurb: The Second Council of Nicaea begins at the Church of Holy Wisdom in the city of Nicaea in Bithynia.

Q187270.name: 1881 Atlantic hurricane season
Q187270.blurb: The Georgia hurricane makes landfall near Savannah, Georgia, resulting in an estimated 700 deaths.

Q187425.name: RMS Lusitania
Q187425.blurb: Cunard Line's RMS Lusitania is launched from the John Brown Shipyard, Glasgow (Clydebank), Scotland.

Q187515.name: 1891 Martinique hurricane
Q187515.blurb: A major hurricane strikes Martinique, leaving 700 dead.

Q187621.name: Hurricane Irene
aliases: Effects of Hurricane Irene in Connecticut
Impact and aftermath of Hurricane Irene (2011)
Q187621.blurb: Hurricane Irene strikes the United States east coast, killing 47 and causing an estimated $15.6 billion in damage.

Q187650.name: Great Purge
aliases: Great Purge in the Soviet Union
Q187650.blurb: Great Purge: The Soviet Union under Joseph Stalin executes eight army leaders.

Q187719.name: Corpus Juris Civilis
Q187719.blurb: First Corpus Juris Civilis, a fundamental work in jurisprudence, is issued by Eastern Roman Emperor Justinian I.

Q187742.name: Guelphs and Ghibellines
aliases: War of the Guelphs and Ghibellines
Wars of the Guelphs and Ghibellines
Q187742.blurb: Wars of the Guelphs and Ghibellines: Troops of the Lombard League defeated forces of the Holy Roman Empire at the Battle of Legnano in present-day Italy.

Q187771.name: Bombing of Hildesheim in World War II
Q187771.blurb: World War II: The city of Hildesheim, Germany, is heavily damaged in a British air raid, though it had little military significance and Germany was on the verge of final defeat.

Q188163.name: Fat Man
Q188163.blurb: World War II: Nagasaki is devastated when an atomic bomb, Fat Man, is dropped by the United States B-29 Bockscar. Thirty-five thousand people are killed outright, including 23,200–28,200 Japanese war workers, 2,000 Korean forced workers, and 150 Japanese soldiers.

Q188289.name: Pakistani rupee
Q188289.blurb: Widespread rioting erupts in Karachi, Pakistan, after the assassination of a local politician, leaving at least 85 dead and at least 17 billion Pakistani rupees (US$200 million) in damage.

Q188371.name: Great Irish Famine
Q188371.blurb: Great Famine of Ireland: Tipperary Revolt: In County Tipperary, Ireland, then in the United Kingdom, an unsuccessful nationalist revolt against British rule is put down by police.

Q188495.name: Battle of Agincourt
Q188495.blurb: Hundred Years' War: Henry V of England, with his lightly armoured infantry and archers, defeats the heavily armoured French cavalry in the Battle of Agincourt.

Q188559.name: Foreign Legion
aliases: French Foreign Legion in popular culture
Q188559.blurb: The French Foreign Legion is created by Louis Philippe, the King of France, from the foreign regiments of the Kingdom of France.

Q188596.name: Tsar Bomba
Q188596.blurb: The Soviet Union detonates the Tsar Bomba, the most powerful explosive device ever detonated.

Q188799.name: Virginia Tech shooting
aliases: List of those killed in the Virginia Tech massacre
List of victims and perpetrator of the Virginia Tech massacre
List of victims in the Virginia Tech massacre
List of victims of Virginia Tech massacre
List of victims of the Virginia Tech Massacre
Shooting at Virginia Tech college in USA
Victims of the Virginia Tech massacre
Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University massacre
Q188799.blurb: Virginia Tech shooting: Seung-Hui Cho murders 32 people and injures 17 before committing suicide.

Q188972.name: Greek Civil War
Q188972.blurb: Greek Civil War: The Political Committee of National Liberation is established in Greece by the National Liberation Front.

Q189066.name: Treaty establishing a Constitution for Europe
aliases: Constitutional Treaty for the European Union
Draft Treaty establishing a Constitution for Europe
History of the Treaty establishing a Constitution for Europe
List of potential signatories of the EU Constitution
Proposed amendments to the European Constitution
Structure of the Draft EU Constitution
Structure of the proposed EU Constitution
Treaty for a Constitution of Europe
Q189066.blurb: Spain becomes the first country to vote in a referendum on ratification of the proposed Constitution of the European Union, passing it by a substantial margin, but on a low turnout.

Q189079.name: Van earthquake of 2011
Q189079.blurb: A powerful 7.2 magnitude earthquake strikes Van Province, Turkey, killing 582 people and injuring thousands.

Q189266.name: Eastern Front
aliases: Eastern Front of World War II
East Front of the Second World War
Eastern Front in World War II
Invasion of Germany by the Soviet Union
Military history of the Soviet Union in World War II
World War II Soviet military history
Q189266.blurb: World War II: The Prague Offensive, the last major battle of the Eastern Front, begins.

Q189444.name: Mozart family grand tour
Q189444.blurb: The Mozart family grand tour of Europe begins, lifting the profile of son Wolfgang Amadeus.

Q189508.name: Glorious Revolution
aliases: Abdication of James II of England
Abdication of King James II of England
Deposition of James II of England
Deposition of King James II of England
Overthrow of James II of England
Overthrow of King James II of England
Q189508.blurb: Glorious Revolution: Provincial militia and citizens in Boston revolted, arresting officials of the Dominion of New England.

Q189930.name: Operation Market Garden
Q189930.blurb: World War II: Allied airborne troops parachute into the Netherlands as the "Market" half of Operation Market Garden and British XXX Corps advances into the Netherlands as the "Garden" half of the Operation.

Q190029.name: Kosovo War
aliases: Albania's role in the Kosovo War
FR Yugoslav airstrikes on KLA insurgents and targets
FR Yugoslav airstrikes on KLA targets
Q190029.blurb: Kosovo War: NATO begins attacks on Yugoslavia without United Nations Security Council (UNSC) approval, marking the first time NATO has attacked a sovereign country.

Q190108.name: Pioneer program
Q190108.blurb: Pioneer program: Pioneer 10 sends back the first close-up images of Jupiter.

Q190315.name: Dayton Agreement
aliases: General Framework Agreement for Peace in Bosnia and Herzegovina
Q190315.blurb: The Dayton Agreement is initialed at the Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, near Dayton, Ohio, ending three and a half years of war in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

Q190517.name: Xinhai Revolution
aliases: Massacre of Manchus during 1911 Chinese revolution
Q190517.blurb: The Xinhai Revolution began with the Wuchang Uprising, marking the beginning of the collapse of the Qing dynasty and the establishment of the Republic of China.

Q190712.name: First Battle of the Marne
aliases: Battle of the Marshes of Saint-Gond
The First Battle of the Marne
Q190712.blurb: World War I: First Battle of the Marne begins. Northeast of Paris, the French attack and defeat German forces who are advancing on the capital.

Q190758.name: War in Darfur
aliases: Timeline of the War in Darfur
Q190758.blurb: President Omar al-Bashir of Sudan was indicted by the International Criminal Court on charges of war crimes and crimes against humanity committed during the War in Darfur.

Q190819.name: Bloody Sunday
Q190819.blurb: The Troubles: Bloody Sunday: British paratroopers open fire on anti-internment marchers in Derry, Northern Ireland, killing 13 people; another person later dies of injuries sustained.

Q190857.name: First Vatican Council
Q190857.blurb: The First Vatican Council decrees the dogma of papal infallibility.

Q190951.name: Singapore dollar
aliases: Commemorative banknotes of the Singapore dollar
Q190951.blurb: The first banknotes of the Portrait Series of the Singapore dollar were introduced by the Board of Commissioners of Currency.

Q191055.name: 1755 Lisbon earthquake
Q191055.blurb: In Portugal, Lisbon is totally devastated by a massive earthquake and tsunami, killing an estimated 40,000 to 60,000 people.

Q191282.name: First Opium War
aliases: First Opium War, First Anglo-Chinese War
Q191282.blurb: The United Kingdom captures Hong Kong as a base as it prepares for the First Opium War with Qing China.

Q191293.name: 1556 Shaanxi earthquake
Q191293.blurb: One of the deadliest earthquakes in history struck Shaanxi, China, resulting in at least 100,000 direct deaths.

Q191577.name: Operation Morvarid
Q191577.blurb: Iran–Iraq War: Operation Morvarid: The bulk of the Iraqi Navy is destroyed by the Iranian Navy in the Persian Gulf. (Commemorated in Iran as Navy Day.)

Q191721.name: Bay of Pigs invasion
Q191721.blurb: Bay of Pigs Invasion: A group of Cuban exiles financed and trained by the CIA lands at the Bay of Pigs in Cuba with the aim of ousting Fidel Castro.

Q191745.name: Left SR Uprising
Q191745.blurb: The Left SR uprising in Russia starts with the assassination of German ambassador Wilhelm von Mirbach by Cheka members.

Q191874.name: Tony Awards
aliases: Antoinette Perry Award for Excellence in Broadway Theatre
Antoinette Perry Award for Excellence in Theatre
Antoinette Perry Awards for Excellence in Theatre
Q191874.blurb: The first Tony Awards are presented for theatrical achievement.

Q191985.name: Orient Express
Q191985.blurb: The first regularly scheduled Orient Express departs Paris.

Q192050.name: assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
aliases: assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria
Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand and Sophie, Duchess of Hohenberg
Assassination of Austrian Archduke Franz Ferdinand
Assassination of Sophie, Duchess of Hohenberg
Death of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria
Murder of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria
Q192050.blurb: Archduke Franz Ferdinand and his wife Sophie, Duchess of Hohenberg, were assassinated in Sarajevo by Gavrilo Princip (pictured), a Yugoslav nationalist, sparking the outbreak of World War I.

Q192055.name: Nanjing Massacre
Q192055.blurb: Second Sino-Japanese War: During the Nanking Massacre, the Nanking Safety Zone International Committee is renamed "Nanking International Rescue Committee", and the safety zone in place for refugees falls apart.

Q192303.name: treaty of Karlowitz
Q192303.blurb: For the first time, the Ottoman Empire permanently cedes territory to the Christian powers.

Q192341.name: I Have a Dream
aliases: They will not be judged by the color of their skin, but by the content of their character
Q192341.blurb: American civil-rights leader Martin Luther King Jr. delivered the speech "I Have a Dream" during the March on Washington, calling for civil and economic rights and an end to racism in the United States.

Q192372.name: Luna programme
Q192372.blurb: Luna programme: The Soviet Union lands Lunokhod 1 on Mare Imbrium (Sea of Rains) on the Moon. This is the first roving remote-controlled robot to land on another world and is released by the orbiting Luna 17 spacecraft.

Q192408.name: Taiping Rebellion
Q192408.blurb: Taiping Rebellion: Hong Xiuquan proclaims the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom, starting the Jintian Uprising.

Q192473.name: Battle of Adrianople
Q192473.blurb: Gothic War: Battle of Adrianople: A large Roman army led by Emperor Valens is defeated by the Visigoths. Valens is killed along with over half of his army.

Q192632.name: NME
aliases: 100 Gigs You Should Have Been At
Q192632.blurb: The New Musical Express publishes the first regular UK Singles Chart.

Q192660.name: Battle of Okinawa
Q192660.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Okinawa ends when the organized resistance of Imperial Japanese Army forces collapses in the Mabuni area on the southern tip of the main island.

Q192769.name: American Revolution
aliases: Revolution in the United States of America
Revolution of the United States of America
Q192769.blurb: American Revolution: British soldiers fired into a crowd in Boston, killing five people.

Q192924.name: Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye
Q192924.blurb: The Republic of German-Austria signs the Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye, ceding significant territories to Italy, Yugoslavia, and Czechoslovakia.

Q193155.name: Louisiana Purchase
Q193155.blurb: After traveling through the Louisiana Purchase and reaching the Pacific Ocean, explorers Lewis and Clark and their Corps of Discovery begin their arduous journey home.

Q193245.name: Carnation Revolution
Q193245.blurb: Carnation Revolution: A leftist military coup in Portugal overthrows the authoritarian-conservative Estado Novo regime.

Q193258.name: Treaty of Lausanne
aliases: Treaty of Peace with Turkey Signed at Lausanne
Q193258.blurb: The Treaty of Lausanne, settling the boundaries of modern Turkey, is signed in Switzerland by Greece, Bulgaria and other countries that fought in World War I.

Q193270.name: Lateran Treaty
Q193270.blurb: The Lateran Treaty is ratified, bringing Vatican City into existence.

Q193484.name: assassination of John F. Kennedy
aliases: Assassination attempt of John F. Kennedy
Assassination of President John F. Kennedy
Assassination of US President John F. Kennedy
Assassination of United States President John F. Kennedy
The assassination of John F. Kennedy
You certainly can't say Dallas doesn't love you, Mr. President
Q193484.blurb: The Zapruder film of the assassination of John F. Kennedy is shown in motion to a national TV audience for the first time by Robert J. Groden and Dick Gregory.

Q193515.name: Acts of Union 1707
aliases: Act Ratifying and Approving the Treaty of Union of the Two Kingdoms of SCOTLAND and ENGLAND
Act for a Treaty with England 1705
Acts of Union of England and Scotland
An Act for a Union of the Two Kingdoms of England and Scotland
Q193515.blurb: The Act of Union joining England and Scotland to form the Kingdom of Great Britain takes effect.

Q193547.name: Reign of Terror
aliases: No freedom for the enemies of freedom
No freedoms for the enemies of freedom
Q193547.blurb: Branded a traitor during the Reign of Terror, French chemist Antoine Lavoisier, who was also a tax collector with the Ferme générale, is tried, convicted and guillotined in one day in Paris.

Q193689.name: Easter Rising
aliases: Seizure of the Dublin General Post Office (GPO)
Q193689.blurb: Easter Rising: Irish rebels, led by Patrick Pearse and James Connolly, launch an uprising in Dublin against British rule and proclaim an Irish Republic.

Q193733.name: Beslan school siege
Q193733.blurb: The Beslan school siege begins when armed terrorists take schoolchildren and school staff hostage in North Ossetia, Russia; by the end of the siege, three days later, more than 385 people are dead (including hostages, other civilians, security personnel and terrorists).

Q193740.name: Live Aid
Q193740.blurb: The Live Aid benefit concert takes place in London and Philadelphia, as well as other venues such as Moscow and Sydney.

Q193892.name: Live 8
Q193892.blurb: The Live 8 benefit concerts takes place in the G8 states and in South Africa. More than 1,000 musicians perform and are broadcast on 182 television networks and 2,000 radio networks.

Q194082.name: Apollo 1
Q194082.blurb: A fire during a launch simulation for the Apollo 1 mission at Cape Kennedy killed astronauts Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee.

Q194110.name: Nanfan Treaty
aliases: Deed from the Five Nations to the King, of their Beaver Hunting Ground
Q194110.blurb: Representatives of the Iroquois Confederacy sign the Nanfan Treaty, ceding a large territory north of the Ohio River to England.

Q194113.name: Treaty of San Stefano
Q194113.blurb: Start of the Congress of Berlin in which the major powers of Europe revise the Treaty of San Stefano, signed on March 3 the same year, that Russia had imposed on a defeated Ottoman Empire.

Q194132.name: Operation Torch
Q194132.blurb: World War II: French Resistance coup in Algiers, in which 400 civilian French patriots neutralize Vichyist XIXth Army Corps after 15 hours of fighting, and arrest several Vichyist generals, allowing the immediate success of Operation Torch in Algiers.

Q194226.name: Battle of Yarmouk
Q194226.blurb: Arab–Byzantine wars: The Battle of Yarmouk between the Byzantine Empire and the Rashidun Caliphate begins.

Q194230.name: leap second
Q194230.blurb: The first leap second is added to the UTC time system.

Q194284.name: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
aliases: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)
General Agreement on Trade and Tariffs
The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
Q194284.blurb: At a GATT ministerial meeting in Marrakesh, Morocco, representatives of 123 countries and the European Communities signed an agreement to establish the World Trade Organization.

Q194329.name: Battle of Five Forks
Q194329.blurb: American Civil War: Union troops led by Philip Sheridan decisively defeat Confederate troops led by George Pickett, cutting the Army of Northern Virginia's last supply line during the Siege of Petersburg.

Q194631.name: Italicus Express bombing 1974
Q194631.blurb: A bomb explodes in the Italicus Express train at San Benedetto Val di Sambro, Italy, killing 12 people and wounding 22.

Q195216.name: Black Tom explosion
Q195216.blurb: The Black Tom explosion in New York Harbor kills several people and destroys some $20,000,000 worth of military goods.

Q195983.name: Franco-Flemish War
Q195983.blurb: Franco-Flemish War: Flemish infantry defeated a large French army near Kortrijk at the Battle of the Golden Spurs.

Q196122.name: Israeli disengagement from the Gaza Strip
aliases: Israel's disengagement from the Gaza Strip
Israeli retreat from the entire Gaza Strip
Q196122.blurb: Israel's unilateral disengagement plan to evict all Israelis from the Gaza Strip and from four settlements in the northern West Bank begins.

Q196176.name: Uprising of Asen and Peter
Q196176.blurb: The Uprising of Asen and Peter begins on the feast day of St. Demetrius of Thessaloniki and ends with the creation of the Second Bulgarian Empire.

Q196409.name: Livonian Crusade
Q196409.blurb: Livonian Crusade: In the Battle of Karuse, the Grand Duchy of Lithuania achieved a decisive victory over the Livonian Order on the frozen surface of the Baltic Sea.

Q196502.name: Armistice of Cassibile
aliases: Armistice between Italy and Allied armed forces
Surrender of Italy to the Allies
Q196502.blurb: World War II: The Armistice of Cassibile is proclaimed by radio. OB Süd immediately implements plans to disarm the Italian forces.

Q196742.name: Burning of Louvain
Q196742.blurb: World War I: The library of the Catholic University of Leuven is deliberately destroyed by the German Army. Hundreds of thousands of irreplaceable volumes and Gothic and Renaissance manuscripts are lost.

Q198670.name: Burning of Norfolk
Q198670.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Burning of Norfolk – Norfolk, Virginia, is burned to the ground by combined Royal Navy and Continental Army action.

Q198822.name: 1909 Monterrey hurricane
Q198822.blurb: The 1909 Monterrey hurricane dissipated; one of the deadliest Atlantic tropical cyclones on record, it killed an estimated 4,000 people throughout Mexico.

Q198961.name: 1915 Galveston hurricane
Q198961.blurb: A Category 4 hurricane hits Galveston, Texas with winds at 135 miles per hour (217 km/h).

Q199174.name: 1926 Miami hurricane
Q199174.blurb: A hurricane devastates Miami, Florida, killing 372 people.

Q199367.name: 1872 Scotland vs England football match
Q199367.blurb: The first-ever international football match takes place at Hamilton Crescent, Glasgow, between Scotland and England.

Q199371.name: Battle of Megiddo
Q199371.blurb: World War I: The end of the Battle of Megiddo, the climax of the British Army's Sinai and Palestine campaign under General Edmund Allenby.

Q199416.name: 2012 Benghazi attack
Q199416.blurb: The U.S. embassy in Benghazi, Libya is attacked, resulting in four deaths.

Q199820.name: Paris Peace Conference
aliases: Supreme Council of the Paris Peace Conference
Q199820.blurb: Paris Peace Conference: Woodrow Wilson overturns Japan's Racial Equality Proposal, stating that unanimous support was required.

Q199955.name: Hundred Days
aliases: Declaration at the Congress of Vienna
The War of the Seventh Coalition
Q199955.blurb: War of the Seventh Coalition: Napoleon fought and lost his final battle, the Battle of Waterloo (depicted), in present-day Belgium.

Q200032.name: Battle of Manzikert
Q200032.blurb: The Seljuq Turks defeat the Byzantine army at the Battle of Manzikert, and soon gain control of most of Anatolia.

Q200056.name: Battle of Zama
Q200056.blurb: Second Punic War: At the Battle of Zama, Roman legions under Scipio Africanus defeat Hannibal Barca, leader of the army defending Carthage.[citation needed]

Q200472.name: Paris massacre of 1961
Q200472.blurb: Directed by their chief Maurice Papon, Paris police massacre scores of Algerian protesters.

Q200485.name: Norman conquest of England
Q200485.blurb: The Norman conquest of England begins with the Battle of Hastings.

Q200682.name: Battle of Queenston Heights
Q200682.blurb: War of 1812: Sir Isaac Brock's British and native forces repel an invasion of Canada by General Rensselaer's United States forces.

Q200716.name: Battle of Chaeronea
Q200716.blurb: An allied army led by Philip II of Macedon overcame the forces of city-states led by Athens and Thebes at the Battle of Chaeronea, securing Macedonian hegemony over the majority of ancient Greece.

Q200749.name: Day of the Tiles
Q200749.blurb: French Revolution: Day of the Tiles: Civilians in Grenoble toss roof tiles and various objects down upon royal troops.

Q200790.name: Algerian War
aliases: War crimes during the Algerian War
Q200790.blurb: Algerian War: Some units of European volunteers in Algiers stage an insurrection known as the "barricades week", during which they seize government buildings and clash with local police.

Q200855.name: Battle of Vienna
Q200855.blurb: Austro-Ottoman War: Battle of Vienna: Several European armies join forces to defeat the Ottoman Empire.

Q201358.name: The Flintstones
aliases: Loyal Order of Water Buffaloes Lodge No. 26
Q201358.blurb: The Flintstones animated sitcom premieres on ABC television.

Q201424.name: nuclear warfare
aliases: List of nuclear targets made by the United States
Q201424.blurb: The Russell–Einstein Manifesto calls for a reduction of the risk of nuclear warfare.

Q201684.name: Wall Street crash of 1929
aliases: Wall Street stock market crash of October 1929
Q201684.blurb: "Black Thursday" on the New York Stock Exchange, the first day of the panic in the markets that contributes to the Great Depression.

Q201692.name: Battle of Poitiers
Q201692.blurb: Battle of Poitiers: An English army under the command of Edward the Black Prince defeats a French army and captures King John II.

Q202040.name: won
aliases: Banknotes of the South Korean won
Coins of the South Korean won
Q202040.blurb: Typhoon Ewiniar made landfall in South Korea, causing damages across the country amounting to 2.06 trillion won (US$1.4 billion).

Q202161.name: Gallic War
aliases: Julius Caesar and the war in Gaul
Q202161.blurb: Gallic Wars: Vercingetorix, leader of the Gauls, surrenders to the Romans under Julius Caesar, ending the siege and battle of Alesia.

Q202311.name: Roman Egypt
Q202311.blurb: War of Actium: Octavian defeated the forces of Mark Antony and Cleopatra at Alexandria, establishing Roman Egypt.

Q202465.name: Uganda–Tanzania War
Q202465.blurb: Uganda–Tanzania War: Ugandan government forces fled Masaka as the Tanzania People's Defence Force bombarded and captured the town.

Q202512.name: 2012 Aurora shooting
Q202512.blurb: James Holmes opened fire at a movie theater in Aurora, Colorado, killing 12 and injuring 70 others.

Q202578.name: First Jewish-Roman War
aliases: Primum populi Romani bellum in Iudaeos
Q202578.blurb: First Jewish–Roman War: Titus and his armies breach the walls of Jerusalem. (17th of Tammuz in the Hebrew calendar).

Q202894.name: Mariner program
Q202894.blurb: Mariner program: Mariner 9 is launched to map 70% of the surface, and to study temporal changes in the atmosphere and surface, of Mars.

Q203159.name: Monterey International Pop Festival
Q203159.blurb: American musician Jimi Hendrix burned his guitar on stage at the end of a performance at the Monterey International Pop Festival in California.

Q203225.name: Battle of Stamford Bridge
Q203225.blurb: In the Battle of Stamford Bridge, Harald Hardrada, the invading King of Norway, is defeated by King Harold II of England.

Q203233.name: Battle of Plassey
Q203233.blurb: Battle of Plassey: Three thousand British troops under Robert Clive defeat a 50,000-strong Indian army under Siraj ud-Daulah at Plassey.

Q203354.name: Finnish markka
Q203354.blurb: The declaration on the introduction of the Finnish markka as an official currency is read in different parts of the Grand Duchy of Finland.

Q203681.name: Battle of Pharsalus
Q203681.blurb: Caesar's Civil War: Battle of Pharsalus: Julius Caesar decisively defeats Pompey at Pharsalus and Pompey flees to Egypt.

Q203824.name: Italo-Turkish War
Q203824.blurb: Italo-Turkish War: Italian forces are the first to use airships for military purposes, employing them for reconnaissance behind Turkish lines.

Q204213.name: Romanian Revolution (1989)
aliases: Fall of the Socialist Republic of Romania
Q204213.blurb: Romanian Revolution: Protests break out in Timișoara, Romania, in response to an attempt by the government to evict dissident Hungarian pastor László Tőkés.

Q205073.name: Kellogg-Briand pact
aliases: General Treaty for the Renunciation of War (Pact of Paris, Kellogg-Briand Pact), 1928
Renunciation of War Treaty, Paris, Aug. 27, 1928
General Pact for the Renunciation of War
General Treaty for Renunciation of War as an Instrument of National Policy
General Treaty for the Renunciation of War
Q205073.blurb: The Kellogg–Briand Pact, renouncing war as an instrument of foreign policy, goes into effect (it is first signed in Paris on August 27, 1928, by most leading world powers).

Q205227.name: Second Council of Constantinople
Q205227.blurb: The Second Council of Constantinople begins.

Q205379.name: Battle of Breitenfeld
Q205379.blurb: Sweden wins a major victory at the Battle of Breitenfeld against the Holy Roman Empire during the Thirty Years' War.

Q205422.name: Battle of the Little Bighorn
aliases: Battle of the Little Big Horn
Bibliography of the Battle of Little Bighorn
Legacy of the Battle of Little Big Horn
The Battle of Little Big Horn
The Battle of the Greasy Grass
The Battle of the Little Big Horn
The Battle of the Little Bighorn
Q205422.blurb: American Indian Wars: Battle of the Little Bighorn: 300 men of the U.S. 7th Cavalry Regiment under Lieutenant Colonel George Armstrong Custer are wiped out by 5,000 Lakota, Cheyenne and Arapaho, led by Sitting Bull and Crazy Horse.

Q205512.name: 2010 Gaza flotilla raid
Q205512.blurb: Israeli Shayetet 13 commandos board the Gaza Freedom Flotilla while still in international waters trying to break the ongoing blockade of the Gaza Strip; nine Turkish citizens on the flotilla were killed in the ensuing violent affray.

Q206392.name: 1928 Okeechobee hurricane
Q206392.blurb: The Okeechobee hurricane first struck the island of Guadeloupe; eventually it reached the United States and caused over 4,000 deaths overall.

Q206414.name: Principate
Q206414.blurb: Roman emperor Caligula accepts the titles of the Principate, bestowed on him by the Senate.

Q206612.name: 1933 Chesapeake–Potomac hurricane
Q206612.blurb: The Chesapeake–Potomac hurricane made landfall in the Outer Banks of North Carolina and went on to cause at least 47 deaths in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic region.

Q206752.name: Treaty of Campo Formio
aliases: Dissolution of the Republic of Venice
Q206752.blurb: Treaty of Campo Formio is signed between France and Austria, ending the War of the First Coalition.

Q206825.name: 1935 Labor Day hurricane
Q206825.blurb: The Labor Day Hurricane, the most intense hurricane to strike the United States, makes landfall at Long Key, Florida, killing at least 400.

Q206897.name: 1938 New England hurricane
Q206897.blurb: The Great Hurricane of 1938 makes landfall on Long Island in New York. The death toll is estimated at 500–700 people.

Q206979.name: Civil Constitution of the Clergy
aliases: The Civil Constitution of the Clergy
Q206979.blurb: The Civil Constitution of the Clergy is passed in France by the National Constituent Assembly.

Q207066.name: McCarthyism
aliases: Are you now or have you ever been a Communist
Are you now or have you ever been a member of the Communist Party
Are you now or have you ever been a member of the Communist Party?
Q207066.blurb: Second Red Scare: US Senator Joseph McCarthy accuses the United States Department of State of being filled with Communists.

Q207165.name: Battle of the Coral Sea
aliases: The Battle Of The Coral Sea
Q207165.blurb: World War II: During the Battle of the Coral Sea, United States Navy aircraft carrier aircraft attack and sink the Imperial Japanese Navy light aircraft carrier Shōhō; the battle marks the first time in naval history that two enemy fleets fight without visual contact between warring ships.

Q207250.name: Battle of Lake Trasimene
Q207250.blurb: A Carthaginian force under Hannibal ambushes and defeats a Roman army commanded by Gaius Flaminius in the battle of lake Trasimene during the Second Punic War.

Q207318.name: French Revolutionary Wars
Q207318.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: A naval battle between a French ship of the line and two British frigates off the coast of Brittany ends with the French vessel running aground, resulting in over 900 deaths.

Q207327.name: Sicilian Vespers
Q207327.blurb: Sicilians began to rebel against the rule of the Angevin King Charles I of Naples, starting the War of the Sicilian Vespers.

Q207329.name: Soyuz programme
Q207329.blurb: Soviet Soyuz Programme: Soyuz 13, crewed by cosmonauts Valentin Lebedev and Pyotr Klimuk, is launched from Baikonur in the Soviet Union.

Q207342.name: Trinity
aliases: First atomic explosion in New Mexico
Q207342.blurb: The United States conducted the first detonation of a nuclear weapon during the Trinity test (pictured).

Q207420.name: 1939 New York World's Fair
Q207420.blurb: The 1939–40 New York World's Fair opens.

Q207487.name: 1942 Atlantic hurricane season
Q207487.blurb: The Matagorda hurricane, the most intense and costliest tropical cyclone of the 1942 Atlantic hurricane season, dissipated after causing $26.5 million in damages and eight deaths.

Q207504.name: 1943 Surprise Hurricane
Q207504.blurb: As the Surprise Hurricane struck Texas, a United States Army Air Forces pilot made the first reconnaissance flight into a hurricane.

Q207513.name: Domodedovo International Airport bombing
Q207513.blurb: At least 35 are killed and 180 injured in a bombing at Moscow's Domodedovo Airport.

Q207541.name: Eurovision Song Contest 1974
aliases: Celui Qui Reste Et Celui Qui S'En Va
Krasi, Thalasa Ke T' Agori Mu
Krasi, Thalassa Kai T' Agori Mou
Krasi, Thalassa Ke T' Agori Mou
Q207541.blurb: ABBA won the Eurovision Song Contest representing Sweden with the song "Waterloo".

Q207559.name: 1945 Southeast Florida hurricane
Q207559.blurb: A hurricane strikes southern Florida and the Bahamas, destroying 366 airplanes and 25 blimps at Naval Air Station Richmond.

Q207576.name: First Turkish Siege of Vienna
Q207576.blurb: The Siege of Vienna begins when Suleiman I attacks the city.

Q207815.name: Eurovision Song Contest 1996
Q207815.blurb: Ireland won the Eurovision song contest for the seventh time, the highest number of wins for any country before Sweden tied it in 2023.

Q207918.name: 2009 L'Aquila earthquake
Q207918.blurb: A 6.3 magnitude earthquake strikes near L'Aquila, Italy, killing 307.

Q208037.name: Third Council of Constantinople
Q208037.blurb: The Third Council of Constantinople deposes patriarch Macarius I of Antioch.

Q208127.name: Battle of Tsushima
aliases: Battle of the Sea of Japan
Naval Battle of the Sea of Japan
Naval tactics at the Battle of Tsushima
Q208127.blurb: Russo-Japanese War: The Battle of Tsushima begins.

Q208133.name: Slovenian tolar
Q208133.blurb: A catastrophic landslide in Log pod Mangartom, Slovenia, kills seven, and causes millions of SIT of damage. It is one of the worst catastrophes in Slovenia in the past 100 years.

Q208156.name: Mongol invasions of Japan
Q208156.blurb: Mongol invasion of Japan: The Mongolian fleet of Kublai Khan is destroyed by a "divine wind" for the second time in the Battle of Kōan.

Q208191.name: Asian–African Conference
Q208191.blurb: The Bandung Conference ends: Twenty-nine non-aligned nations of Asia and Africa finish a meeting that condemns colonialism, racism, and the Cold War.

Q208199.name: Sabra and Shatila massacre
aliases: Shatila and Burj al Barajinah Massacre
Siege of Shatila, Sabra and Burj al Barajinah
Q208199.blurb: Lebanon War: The Sabra and Shatila massacre in Lebanon takes place.

Q208297.name: Irish War of Independence
Q208297.blurb: Irish War of Independence: One of the biggest engagements of the war takes place at Crossbarry, County Cork. About 100 Irish Republican Army (IRA) volunteers escape an attempt by over 1,300 British forces to encircle them.

Q208300.name: Kronstadt rebellion
Q208300.blurb: The Kronstadt rebellion began following mass protests in Petrograd demanding greater freedom in Russia with sailors and citizens taking up arms against the Bolsheviks.

Q208401.name: 2010 FIFA World Cup Final
Q208401.blurb: In Johannesburg, Spain defeat the Netherlands 1–0 after extra time to win their first FIFA World Cup title.

Q208484.name: Lebanese Civil War
Q208484.blurb: During the Lebanese Civil War, 83 Tiger militants are killed during what will be known as the Safra massacre.

Q208526.name: New Taiwan dollar
Q208526.blurb: A 7.7 Mw earthquake struck Jiji, Taiwan, killing 2,415 people, injuring more than 11,000 others and causing about NT$300 billion (US$10 billion) in damage across the island.

Q208529.name: Battle of Dunkirk
Q208529.blurb: Second World War: The Allies began a mass evacuation of British, French and Belgian troops cut off by the German army during the Battle of Dunkirk.

Q208645.name: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
aliases: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
United Nations Framework Convention for Climate Change
United Nations Framework Convention on Climate
Q208645.blurb: The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change enters into force.

Q208694.name: Sino-Indian War
aliases: Battle of Se La and Bomdi La
International reactions to the Sino-Indian War
Q208694.blurb: The Nathu La pass between India and China, sealed during the Sino-Indian War, re-opens for trade after 44 years.

Q208708.name: autogyro
Q208708.blurb: Juan de la Cierva makes the first autogyro flight.

Q208759.name: Apollo–Soyuz
Q208759.blurb: Apollo–Soyuz Test Project: An American Apollo and a Soviet Soyuz spacecraft dock with each other in orbit marking the first such link-up between spacecraft from the two nations.

Q208855.name: Jallianwala Bagh massacre
Q208855.blurb: Jallianwala Bagh massacre: British Indian Army troops led by Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer kill approximately 379–1,000 unarmed demonstrators including men and women in Amritsar, India. Approximately 1,500 are injured.

Q208958.name: Good Friday Agreement
Q208958.blurb: The Good Friday Agreement is signed in Northern Ireland.

Q209297.name: Farroupilha Revolution
Q209297.blurb: The decade-long Ragamuffin War starts when rebels capture Porto Alegre in Brazil.

Q209312.name: Eighth Russo-Turkish War
Q209312.blurb: Russo-Turkish War: Admiral Dmitry Senyavin destroys the Ottoman fleet in the Battle of Athos.

Q209339.name: two-cent piece
Q209339.blurb: U.S. Congress passed the Coinage Act, which authorized the minting of the two-cent piece (pictured), the first U.S. coin to bear the phrase "In God We Trust".

Q209359.name: Battle of Vimeiro
Q209359.blurb: Battle of Vimeiro: British and Portuguese forces led by General Arthur Wellesley defeat French force under Major-General Jean-Andoche Junot near the village of Vimeiro, Portugal, the first Anglo-Portuguese victory of the Peninsular War.

Q209387.name: Battle of Ankara
Q209387.blurb: Ottoman-Timurid Wars: Battle of Ankara: Timur, ruler of Timurid Empire, defeats forces of the Ottoman Empire sultan Bayezid I.

Q209601.name: Austro-Hungarian Compromise of 1867
Q209601.blurb: The Austro-Hungarian Compromise of 1867 ("the Compromise") is born through Act 12, which establishes the Austro-Hungarian Empire.

Q210005.name: 2011 Yemeni revolution
Q210005.blurb: Arab Spring: The Yemeni Revolution begins as over 16,000 protestors demonstrate in Sanaa.

Q210137.name: 2005 Kashmir earthquake
Q210137.blurb: The 7.6 Mw Kashmir earthquake leaves 86,000–87,351 people dead, 69,000–75,266 injured, and 2.8 million homeless.

Q210354.name: Battle of Kulikovo
Q210354.blurb: Battle of Kulikovo: Russian forces defeat a mixed army of Tatars and Mongols, stopping their advance.

Q210714.name: 2011 military intervention in Libya
aliases: 2011- UN intervention in Libya during civil unrest
Q210714.blurb: First Libyan Civil War: The United Nations Security Council adopted Resolution 1973, authorizing military intervention in Libya to protect civilians.

Q210981.name: 2007 Peru earthquake
Q210981.blurb: An 8.0-magnitude earthquake off the Pacific coast devastates Ica and various regions of Peru killing 514 and injuring 1,090.

Q211035.name: Calvin and Hobbes
aliases: Commander Coriander Salamander and 'er Singlehander Bellylander
Hamster Huey and the Gooey Kablooie
Minor characters in Calvin and Hobbes
Q211035.blurb: The first comic of Calvin and Hobbes is published in ten newspapers.

Q211087.name: Pan Am Flight 103
Q211087.blurb: A bomb explodes on board Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie, Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland, killing 270. This is to date the deadliest air disaster to occur on British soil.

Q211211.name: Battle of Kelja
Q211211.blurb: Winter War: Finland holds off a Soviet attack in the Battle of Kelja.

Q211386.name: 1906 San Francisco earthquake
aliases: Great San Francisco Earthquake and Fire
The Great San Francisco Earthquake of 1906
Q211386.blurb: The 7.9 Mwearthquake and fire destroy much of San Francisco, California, killing more than 3,000 people, making one of the worst natural disasters in American history.

Q211395.name: treaty of Passarowitz
Q211395.blurb: The Treaty of Passarowitz between the Ottoman Empire, Austria and the Republic of Venice is signed.

Q211484.name: Eurovision Song Contest 1994
Q211484.blurb: Riverdance was performed for the first time, as the interval act for the Eurovision Song Contest.

Q211582.name: Zong massacre
Q211582.blurb: The crew of the British slave ship Zong murders 54 Africans by dumping them into the sea to claim insurance, beginning the Zong massacre.

Q211674.name: Sykes–Picot Agreement
Q211674.blurb: The Manchester Guardian publishes the 1916 secret Sykes-Picot Agreement between the United Kingdom and France.

Q211855.name: Finnish Civil War
Q211855.blurb: Finnish Civil War: The first serious battles take place between the Red Guards and the White Guard.

Q212220.name: Battle of Nicopolis
Q212220.blurb: Ottoman Emperor Bayezid I defeats a Christian army at the Battle of Nicopolis.

Q212234.name: Treaty of Roskilde
Q212234.blurb: Treaty of Roskilde: After a devastating defeat in the Northern Wars (1655–1661), Frederick III, the King of Denmark–Norway is forced to give up nearly half his territory to Sweden.

Q212618.name: 1960 Valdivia earthquake
Q212618.blurb: The Great Chilean earthquake, measuring 9.5 on the moment magnitude scale, hits southern Chile, becoming the most powerful earthquake ever recorded.

Q212983.name: Jacobitism
aliases: Proposed French invasion of Scotland of 1708
Q212983.blurb: Jacobite risings: A French fleet anchored near Fife Ness as part of a planned French invasion of Britain.

Q213380.name: Supreme Court of India
aliases: Corruption in the Supreme Court of India
Criticism of the Supreme Court of India
History of the Supreme Court of India
Landmark rulings of the Supreme Court of India
Q213380.blurb: Supreme Court of India decriminalised all consensual sex among adults in private, making homosexuality legal on the Indian lands.

Q213394.name: Sri Lankan civil war
aliases: Aftermath of the Sri Lankan Civil War
Economic impact of the Sri Lankan Civil War
End of the Sri Lankan Civil War
Q213394.blurb: Sri Lankan Civil War: The Sri Lanka Navy kill 35–100 civilians on the Jaffna Lagoon.

Q213531.name: 2004 Madrid train bombings
aliases: Casualties of the 11 March 2004 Madrid bombings
Casualties of the 2004 March 11 Madrid bombings
Q213531.blurb: Madrid train bombings: Simultaneous explosions on rush hour trains in Madrid, Spain kill 191 people.

Q214028.name: July Revolution
Q214028.blurb: July Revolution: Charles X of France abdicates the throne in favor of his grandson Henri.

Q214148.name: Haymarket affair
Q214148.blurb: Rallies are held throughout the United States demanding the eight-hour work day, culminating in the Haymarket affair in Chicago, in commemoration of which May 1 is celebrated as International Workers' Day in many countries.

Q214426.name: Mexican Revolution
aliases: Books and Journals for Mexican Revolution
Q214426.blurb: Mexican Revolution: Mexicali is captured by the Mexican Liberal Party, igniting the Magonista rebellion of 1911.

Q214456.name: Philippine–American War
Q214456.blurb: The Philippine–American War begins when four Filipino soldiers enter the "American Zone" in Manila, igniting the Battle of Manila.

Q214524.name: Gettysburg Address
aliases: Four score and seven years ago
Four score and seven years ago our fathers brought forth upon this continent, a new nation, conceived in Liberty, and dedicated to the proposition that all men are created equal
Government of the people, by the people, for the people
Government of the people, by the people, for the people, shall not perish from the earth
Of the people by the people for the people
Of the people, by the people, for the people
Q214524.blurb: American Civil War: U.S. President Abraham Lincoln delivers the Gettysburg Address at the dedication ceremony for the military cemetery at Gettysburg, Pennsylvania.

Q214790.name: 2010 Copiapó mining accident
aliases: 2010 San José de Copiapó mining accident
Miners' survival during 2010 Copiapo mining accident
Miners' survival during 2010 Copiapó mining accident
Rescue plans for 2010 Copiapo mining accident
Rescue plans for 2010 Copiapó mining accident
Rescue plans for the 2010 Copiapó mining accident
San José de Copiapó mining accident
Survival during the 2010 Copiapó mining accident
Q214790.blurb: The Copiapó mining accident occurs, trapping 33 Chilean miners approximately 2,300 ft (700 m) below the ground for 69 days.

Q214866.name: Great Hanshin Earthquake
Q214866.blurb: The 6.9 Mw Great Hanshin earthquake shakes the southern Hyōgo Prefecture with a maximum Shindo of 7, leaving 5,502–6,434 people dead, and 251,301–310,000 displaced.

Q214996.name: Project Gemini
Q214996.blurb: Project Gemini: Gemini 12 completes the program's final mission, when it splashes down safely in the Atlantic Ocean.

Q215112.name: Second Boer War
Q215112.blurb: Second Boer War: Having already besieged the fortress at Ladysmith, Boer forces attack it, but are driven back by British defenders.

Q215231.name: Great Fire of Rome
Q215231.blurb: The Great Fire of Rome causes widespread devastation and rages on for six days, destroying half of the city.

Q215337.name: 1981 Spanish coup d'état attempt
Q215337.blurb: In Spain, Antonio Tejero attempts a coup d'état by capturing the Spanish Congress of Deputies.

Q215687.name: Boston Massacre
aliases: The Bloody Massacre on King Street
Q215687.blurb: Boston Massacre: Five Americans, including Crispus Attucks, are fatally shot by British troops in an event that would contribute to the outbreak of the American Revolutionary War (also known as the American War of Independence) five years later.

Q216047.name: Le Figaro
Q216047.blurb: Publication of the Futurist Manifesto in the French journal Le Figaro.

Q216108.name: BBC Two
Q216108.blurb: The world's longest running music show Top of the Pops is broadcast for the last time on BBC Two. The show had aired for 42 years.

Q216165.name: Union of Utrecht
Q216165.blurb: The Union of Utrecht forms a Protestant republic in the Netherlands.

Q216184.name: Western Front
aliases: Western Front in World War II
Western Front of World War II
Q216184.blurb: World War II: Operation Nordwind, the last major Wehrmacht offensive on the Western Front, begins.

Q216340.name: 1923 24 Hours of Le Mans
Q216340.blurb: French drivers André Lagache and René Léonard completed the most laps during the first edition of the sports car race the 24 Hours of Le Mans.

Q216532.name: 1999 24 Hours of Le Mans
Q216532.blurb: BMW win 1999 24 Hours of Le Mans.

Q217145.name: Guadalcanal campaign
Q217145.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Guadalcanal begins as the United States Marines initiate the first American offensive of the war with landings on Guadalcanal and Tulagi in the Solomon Islands.

Q217197.name: European sovereign-debt crisis
aliases: Controversies surrounding the European sovereign-debt crisis
Q217197.blurb: Silvio Berlusconi tenders his resignation as Prime Minister of Italy, effective November 16, due in large part to the Euro area crisis.

Q217305.name: The New Yorker
aliases: The Complete Cartoons of the New Yorker
Q217305.blurb: The New Yorker publishes its first issue.

Q217398.name: Berne Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works
aliases: International Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works
Berne Union for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Property
Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works
The Berne Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works
Q217398.blurb: Brazil becomes a member of the Berne Convention copyright treaty.

Q217429.name: Metre Convention
Q217429.blurb: Signing of the Metre Convention by 17 nations leading to the establishment of the International System of Units.

Q217450.name: Treaty of Paris (1783)
aliases: The Paris Peace Treaty of September 30, 1783
Q217450.blurb: The Treaty of Paris, ratified by the United States Congress on January 14, 1784, is ratified by King George III of the Kingdom of Great Britain, ending the American Revolutionary War. Copies of the ratified documents are exchanged on May 12, 1784.

Q217528.name: Oklahoma City bombing
aliases: McVeigh bombing of the Oklahoma City federal building
Media coverage of the Oklahoma City bombing
Tenth Anniversary of the Oklahoma City bombing
Q217528.blurb: Oklahoma City bombing: The Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City, US, is bombed, killing 168 people including 19 children under the age of six.

Q217824.name: 2,500 year celebration of the Persian Empire
aliases: 2,500th Year of the Foundation of the Imperial State of Iran
Celebration of the 2,500th Anniversary of the Founding of the Persian Empire
Q217824.blurb: The 2,500 year celebration of the Persian Empire begins.

Q217981.name: Allied invasion of Sicily
aliases: War crimes in the Allied invasion of Sicily
Q217981.blurb: World War II: Operation Husky, the Allied invasion of Sicily, begins.

Q218446.name: Khojaly Massacre
aliases: 2012 Khojaly Massacre protest rally in Istanbul
Day of the Khojaly Genocide and National Mourning
Justice for Khojaly, Freedom for Karabakh
Q218446.blurb: First Nagorno-Karabakh War: Khojaly Massacre: Armenian armed forces open fire on Azeri civilians at a military post outside the town of Khojaly leaving hundreds dead.

Q219217.name: tulip mania
Q219217.blurb: Tulip Mania collapses within the Dutch Republic.

Q219230.name: Marco Polo Bridge incident
aliases: World War II/Battle of Lugou Bridge
Q219230.blurb: The Marco Polo Bridge Incident (Lugou Bridge) provides the Imperial Japanese Army with a pretext for starting the Second Sino-Japanese War (China-Japan War).

Q219355.name: Roswell incident
aliases: Air Force Reports on Roswell UFO Incident
Air Force reports on the Roswell UFO incident
The Truth About the UFO Crash at Roswell
U.F.O. crash at Roswell, New Mexico
Q219355.blurb: Following reports of the capture of a "flying disc" by U.S. Army Air Forces personnel near Roswell, New Mexico, the military stated that the crashed object was a conventional weather balloon.

Q219384.name: 1955–56 European Cup
aliases: First season of the European Cup
Q219384.blurb: Spanish football club Real Madrid CF wins the inaugural European Cup, UEFA's premier club competition, by winning 4–3 against French club Stade de Reims in the final.

Q219438.name: Montreal Protocol
aliases: Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer
Montreal Protocol for the Protection of the Ozone Layer
Montreal Protocol on Ozone Depleting Substances
Q219438.blurb: The Montreal Protocol comes into force, stopping the use of chemicals contributing to ozone depletion.

Q219447.name: Bill of Rights 1689
aliases: An Act Declaring the Rights and Liberties of the Subject and Settling the Succession of the Crown
Q219447.blurb: Convention Parliament: The Declaration of Right is embodied in the Bill of Rights.

Q219470.name: Rose Revolution
Q219470.blurb: Rose Revolution: Georgian president Eduard Shevardnadze resigns following weeks of mass protests over flawed elections.

Q219697.name: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
aliases: Battle of the Navas de Tolosa
The Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
Q219697.blurb: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa: After Pope Innocent III calls European knights to a crusade, the forces of kings Alfonso VIII of Castile, Sancho VII of Navarre, Peter II of Aragon and Afonso II of Portugal defeat those of the Berber Muslim leader Almohad, thus marking a significant turning point in the Reconquista and in the medieval history of Spain.

Q219698.name: Salem Witch Trials
Q219698.blurb: Salem witch trials: Bridget Bishop is hanged at Gallows Hill near Salem, Massachusetts, for "certaine Detestable Arts called Witchcraft and Sorceries".

Q220208.name: 1964 United Kingdom general election
Q220208.blurb: Malcolm X visits Smethwick near Birmingham following the racially-charged 1964 United Kingdom general election.

Q220359.name: Zoot Suit Riots
Q220359.blurb: In Los Angeles, California, white U.S. Navy sailors and Marines attack Latino youths in the five-day Zoot Suit Riots.

Q220497.name: New York City draft riots
Q220497.blurb: Four days of rioting began in New York City in response to laws passed by the U.S. Congress to draft men to fight in the American Civil War.

Q220602.name: Soviet–Japanese War
Q220602.blurb: Soviet-Japanese War: Battle of Shumshu: Soviet forces land at Takeda Beach on Shumshu Island and launch the Battle of Shumshu; the Soviet Union's Invasion of the Kuril Islands commences.

Q220635.name: carrack
Q220635.blurb: The carrack Santa María, commanded by Christopher Columbus, runs onto a reef off Haiti due to an improper watch.

Q220827.name: Mars Exploration Rover
Q220827.blurb: Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity landed on Mars and rolled into Eagle crater, a small crater on the Meridiani Planum.

Q221111.name: Operation Dragoon
Q221111.blurb: World War II: Operation Dragoon: Allied forces land in southern France.

Q221382.name: 1991 Soviet coup d'état attempt
Q221382.blurb: Coup attempt against Mikhail Gorbachev collapses.

Q221469.name: First Battle of Bull Run
aliases: First Battle of the Bull Run
The First Battle of Bull Run
Q221469.blurb: American Civil War: First Battle of Bull Run: At Manassas Junction, Virginia, the first major battle of the war begins and ends in a victory for the Confederate army.

Q221519.name: Burma Campaign
Q221519.blurb: World War II: The end of fighting in the Battle of Hill 170 during the Burma Campaign, in which the British 3 Commando Brigade repulsed a Japanese counterattack on their positions and precipitated a general retirement from the Arakan Peninsula.

Q221719.name: one-child policy
Q221719.blurb: China announces the end of its one-child policy after 35 years.

Q221891.name: Second Battle of Artois
Q221891.blurb: World War I: Second Battle of Artois between German and French forces.

Q221905.name: Big Four
aliases: The Big Four of the New Railway Era
Q221905.blurb: British Railways came into existence when the "Big Four" railway companies were nationalised.

Q221941.name: War of the Quadruple Alliance
aliases: The War of the Quadruple Alliance
Q221941.blurb: War of the Quadruple Alliance: Spanish forces began a failed assault on the British settlement of Nassau in the Bahamas.

Q221967.name: Brusilov Offensive
Q221967.blurb: World War I: Russia opens the Brusilov Offensive with an artillery barrage of Austro-Hungarian lines in Galicia.

Q222013.name: Battle of Bosworth Field
Q222013.blurb: The Battle of Bosworth Field occurs; King Richard III of England's death in battle marks the end of the reigning Plantagenet dynasty and the beginning of the Tudors under Henry VII.

Q222520.name: Battle of Bannockburn
Q222520.blurb: First War of Scottish Independence: The Battle of Bannockburn (south of Stirling) begins.

Q223085.name: Hundred Hour War
Q223085.blurb: A cease fire is announced between Honduras and El Salvador, six days after the beginning of the "Football War".

Q223126.name: Chaco War
aliases: List of Chaco War weapons of Bolivia
List of Chaco War weapons of Paraguay
Q223126.blurb: Chaco War ends: A truce is called between Bolivia and Paraguay who had been fighting since 1932.

Q223288.name: Tenerife airport disaster
aliases: Collision between KLM and PanAm Boeing 747's at Tenerife
Q223288.blurb: Tenerife airport disaster: Two Boeing 747 airliners collide on a foggy runway on Tenerife in the Canary Islands, killing 583 (all 248 on KLM and 335 on Pan Am). Sixty-one survived on the Pan Am flight. This is the deadliest aviation accident in history.

Q223604.name: Greco-Italian War
Q223604.blurb: Greco-Italian War: The Greek army captured the strategically important Klisura Pass in Albania.

Q223622.name: Battle of Prague
Q223622.blurb: Battle of Prague: A Prussian army fights an Austrian army in Prague during the Seven Years' War.

Q223732.name: Declaration of the Establishment of the State of Israel
aliases: Declaration of Independence of the State of Israel
Creation of the State of Israel
Declaration of Establishment of State of Israel
Declaration of the Establishment of the State of Israel, May 14, 1948
Establishment of the State of Israel
Proclamation of the State of Israel
Proclamation of the establishment of the State of Israel
The founding of the State of Israel
Q223732.blurb: Israel is declared to be an independent state and a provisional government is established. Immediately after the declaration, Israel is attacked by the neighboring Arab states, triggering the 1948 Arab–Israeli War.

Q224794.name: Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824
Q224794.blurb: The Anglo-Dutch Treaty is signed in London, dividing the Malay archipelago. As a result, the Malay Peninsula is dominated by the British, while Sumatra and Java and surrounding areas are dominated by the Dutch.

Q226032.name: Morant Bay rebellion
Q226032.blurb: Hundreds of black men and women march in Jamaica, starting the Morant Bay rebellion.

Q228284.name: Expedition of the Thousand
Q228284.blurb: Led by Italian general Giuseppe Garibaldi, the volunteer Expedition of the Thousand set sail from Genoa on a campaign to conquer the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies, a crucial event of the unification of Italy.

Q228338.name: 1995 Palo Verde, Arizona derailment
Q228338.blurb: An Amtrak Sunset Limited train is derailed by saboteurs near Palo Verde, Arizona.

Q228368.name: Zug massacre
Q228368.blurb: In Switzerland, a gunman shoots 18 citizens, killing 14 and then himself.

Q229007.name: Munich massacre
aliases: Palestinian terror attack during the 1972 Summer Olympics in Munich, West Germany
Massacre of the Israeli Olympic athletes
Q229007.blurb: Munich massacre: A Palestinian terrorist group called "Black September" attacks and takes hostage 11 Israeli athletes at the Munich Olympic Games. Two die in the attack and nine are murdered the following day.

Q230186.name: Pan American Games
aliases: List of Pan American Games Medalists
Overview of the Pan American Games
U.S. Virgin Islands at the Pan American Games
Q230186.blurb: The first Pan American Games are officially opened in Buenos Aires by Argentine President Juan Perón.

Q232388.name: Dual Alliance
Q232388.blurb: Germany and Austria-Hungary sign the "Twofold Covenant" and create the Dual Alliance.

Q233219.name: Second Battle of Ypres
Q233219.blurb: World War I: The use of poison gas in World War I escalates when chlorine gas is released as a chemical weapon in the Second Battle of Ypres.

Q233278.name: Operation Spark
