Q233278.blurb: World War II: In Operation Iskra, the Red Army established a narrow land corridor to Leningrad, partially easing the protracted German siege of the city.

Q233343.name: Second Battle of Bull Run
aliases: Second Battle of the Bull Run
Q233343.blurb: American Civil War: The Second Battle of Bull Run, also known as the Battle of Second Manassas, begins in Virginia.  The battle ends on August 30 with another Union defeat.

Q233360.name: Second Battle of Corinth
Q233360.blurb: American Civil War: The two-day Second Battle of Corinth begins as Confederate forces under General Earl Van Dorn attack Union defenses led by General William Rosecrans around Corinth, Mississippi.

Q233399.name: Battle of Mantinea
Q233399.blurb: Battle of Mantinea: The Thebans, led by Epaminondas, defeat the Spartans.

Q233405.name: Second Battle of Porto
Q233405.blurb: British contingents under Arthur Wellesley force a French army under general Soult to retreat in the battle of Oporto.

Q233414.name: Battle of Panipat
Q233414.blurb: Second Battle of Panipat: Fighting begins between the forces of Hem Chandra Vikramaditya, the Hindu king at Delhi and the forces of the Muslim emperor Akbar.

Q233417.name: Battle of the Assunpink Creek
Q233417.blurb: American Revolutionary War: American forces under the command of George Washington repulsed a British attack at the Battle of the Assunpink Creek near Trenton, New Jersey.

Q233426.name: Second Battle of Zurich
Q233426.blurb: War of the 2nd Coalition: French troops defeat Austro-Russian forces, leading to the collapse of Suvorov's campaign.

Q233430.name: Second Battle of Cape Finisterre
Q233430.blurb: War of the Austrian Succession: A British fleet under Admiral Edward Hawke defeats the French at the Second Battle of Cape Finisterre.

Q233486.name: Second Constitutional Era
Q233486.blurb: The Second Constitution is accepted by the Ottomans.

Q233507.name: Second Anglo-Afghan War
aliases: Battles of the Second Anglo-Afghan War
Q233507.blurb: Second Anglo-Afghan War: Battle of Maiwand: Afghan forces led by Mohammad Ayub Khan defeat the British Army in battle near Maiwand, Afghanistan.

Q233532.name: Second Peace of Thorn (1466)
Q233532.blurb: The Thirteen Years' War between Poland and the Teutonic Order ends with the Second Treaty of Thorn.

Q233568.name: Battle of Hattin
aliases: Battle of the Horns of Hattin
The Battle of the Horns of Hattin
Q233568.blurb: The Crusades: Battle of Hattin: Saladin defeats Guy of Lusignan, King of Jerusalem.

Q233583.name: Indo-Pakistani War of 1965
aliases: United Nations India Pakistan Observation Mission
Q233583.blurb: The Indo-Pakistani war of 1965 begins as Pakistani soldiers cross the Line of Control dressed as locals.

Q233642.name: Second Anglo-Maratha War
Q233642.blurb: Second Anglo-Maratha War: The Battle of Assaye is fought between the British East India Company and the Maratha Empire in India.

Q233663.name: Second Anglo-Mysore War
Q233663.blurb: Second Anglo-Mysore War: British troops surrendered the fortress of Bednore in southwestern India to French and Mysorean forces; many of the prisoners were later murdered.

Q233688.name: Treaty of Paris
Q233688.blurb: The Second Treaty of Paris is signed, returning the French frontiers to their 1790 extent, imposing large indemnities, and prolonging the occupation by troops of Great Britain, Austria, Prussia, and Russia for several more years.

Q233702.name: Second Silesian War
Q233702.blurb: Prussia declared its intervention in the War of the Austrian Succession on behalf of Charles VII, beginning the Second Silesian War.

Q234132.name: Hillsborough disaster
Q234132.blurb: Hillsborough disaster: A human crush occurs at Hillsborough Stadium, home of Sheffield Wednesday, in the FA Cup Semi-final, resulting in the deaths of 97 Liverpool fans.

Q234188.name: Battle of Sekigahara
Q234188.blurb: Tokugawa Ieyasu defeats the leaders of rival Japanese clans in the Battle of Sekigahara and becomes shōgun of Japan.

Q234738.name: Turkish War of Independence
Q234738.blurb: Battle of Dumlupınar: The final battle in the Greco-Turkish War (Turkish War of Independence).

Q235344.name: Battle of the Alamo
Q235344.blurb: Texas Revolution: Battle of the Alamo: After a thirteen-day siege by an army of 3,000 Mexican troops, the 187 Texas volunteers, including frontiersman Davy Crockett and colonel Jim Bowie, defending the Alamo are killed and the fort is captured.

Q235753.name: Nikkō-shi
Q235753.blurb: Boshin War: Troops of the Tokugawa shogunate withdrew from the Battle of Utsunomiya Castle and retreated north towards Nikkō and Aizu.

Q236163.name: Kielce pogrom
Q236163.blurb: The Kielce pogrom against Jewish Holocaust survivors in Poland.

Q238262.name: Treaty of Nanjing
aliases: Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Commerce between Her Majesty the Queen of Great Britain and Ireland and the Emperor of China
Peace Treaty between the Queen of Great Britain and the Emperor of China
Q238262.blurb: Treaty of Nanking comes into effect; Hong Kong Island is ceded to the British "in perpetuity".

Q238440.name: Battle of Navarino
Q238440.blurb: Greek War of Independence: In the Battle of Navarino, a combined Turkish and Egyptian fleet is defeated by British, French and Russian naval forces in the last significant battle fought with wooden sailing ships.

Q239060.name: Arab Revolt
Q239060.blurb: The Arab Revolt against the Ottoman Empire is declared by Hussein bin Ali, Sharif of Mecca.

Q239255.name: Battle of Arras
Q239255.blurb: World War I: The Battle of Arras: The battle begins with Canadian Corps executing a massive assault on Vimy Ridge.

Q239344.name: Salt March
Q239344.blurb: At the end of the Salt March, Gandhi raises a lump of mud and salt and declares, "With this, I am shaking the foundations of the British Empire."

Q239514.name: Quiet Revolution
Q239514.blurb: The Asbestos Strike begins in Canada. The strike marks the beginning of the Quiet Revolution in Quebec.

Q239937.name: Pokémon
aliases: List of Pokémon characters & voice actors in the anime series
List of characters in the Pokemon anime series
List of characters in the Pokémon anime series
Q239937.blurb: "Dennō Senshi Porygon", an episode of the Japanese television series Pokémon, induced epileptic seizures in 685 children.

Q240352.name: Gulf of Tonkin Resolution
Q240352.blurb: Vietnam War: The U.S. Congress passes the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution giving U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson broad war powers to deal with North Vietnamese attacks on American forces.

Q241108.name: Battle of Friedland
Q241108.blurb: Emperor Napoleon's French Grande Armée defeats the Russian Army at the Battle of Friedland in Poland (modern Russian  Kaliningrad Oblast) ending the War of the Fourth Coalition.

Q242099.name: Mukden incident
Q242099.blurb: Imperial Japan instigates the Mukden incident as a pretext to invade and occupy Manchuria.

Q242352.name: Yugoslav Wars
aliases: Civil war in the former Yugoslavia
War crimes in the Yugoslav Wars
Q242352.blurb: Yugoslav Wars: The Kumanovo Agreement was signed, bringing an end to the Kosovo War the next day.

Q242644.name: Battle of Caporetto
Q242644.blurb: World War I: Italy suffers a disastrous defeat at the Battle of Caporetto on the Austro-Italian front.

Q242864.name: 2011 Bahraini uprising
Q242864.blurb: Bahraini uprising: Tens of thousands of people march in protest against the deaths of seven victims killed by police and army forces during previous protests.

Q243585.name: Second Serbian Uprising
Q243585.blurb: The Second Serbian Uprising: A second phase of the national revolution of the Serbs against the Ottoman Empire, erupts shortly after the annexation of the country to the Ottoman Empire.

Q243590.name: Second Anglo-Sikh war
Q243590.blurb: Second Anglo-Sikh War: The Siege of Multan ends after nine months when the last Sikh defenders of Multan, Punjab, surrender.

Q243618.name: Second Vienna Award
Q243618.blurb: The Second Vienna Award reassigns the territory of Northern Transylvania from Romania to Hungary.

Q243620.name: Somali Civil War
aliases: Spillover of the Somali civil war
Q243620.blurb: Somali Civil War: The United States Embassy to Somalia in Mogadishu is evacuated by helicopter airlift days after the outbreak of violence in Mogadishu.

Q243640.name: Second Battle of Sabine Pass
Q243640.blurb: American Civil War: In the Second Battle of Sabine Pass, a small Confederate force thwarts a Union invasion of Texas.

Q243684.name: Eighth Crusade
Q243684.blurb: The Eighth Crusade ends by an agreement between Charles I of Anjou (replacing his deceased brother King Louis IX of France) and the Hafsid dynasty of Tunis, Tunisia.

Q243709.name: Second Battle of Sirte
Q243709.blurb: Second World War: British and Italian naval forces fought the Second Battle of Sirte in the Gulf of Sidra north of Libya.

Q243721.name: Year of the Five Emperors
aliases: The Year of the Five Emperors
Q243721.blurb: Year of the Five Emperors: Septimius Severus was proclaimed Roman emperor by his troops at Carnuntum in modern-day Austria.

Q243979.name: Battle of the Nile
Q243979.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: Battle of the Nile (Battle of Aboukir Bay): Battle begins when a British fleet engages the French Revolutionary Navy fleet in an unusual night action.

Q243987.name: Bombardment of Yeonpyeong
Q243987.blurb: Bombardment of Yeonpyeong: North Korean artillery attack kills two civilians and two marines on Yeonpyeong Island, South Korea.

Q244356.name: Battle of Ain Jalut
Q244356.blurb: After defeating the Mongols at the Battle of Ain Jalut and assassinating the previous Mamluk sultan, Qutuz, Baybars ascends to the Egyptian throne as the fourth sultan of the Mamluk Sultanate.

Q244926.name: May 15 Incident
Q244926.blurb: In an attempted coup d'état, the Prime Minister of Japan, Inukai Tsuyoshi, is assassinated.

Q244939.name: 228 Incident
Q244939.blurb: February 28 incident: In Taiwan, civil disorder is put down with the death of an estimated 18,000 - 28,000 civilians.

Q244941.name: Xi'an Incident
Q244941.blurb: The beginning of Xi'an incident. As a result, Chiang Kai Shek is captured.

Q244980.name: Siege of Belgrade
Q244980.blurb: Ottoman–Hungarian wars: The Siege of Nándorfehérvár (Belgrade) begins.

Q245530.name: Cyclone Gonu
Q245530.blurb: Cyclone Gonu develops from an area of convection in the Arabian Sea, becoming the worst recorded natural disaster in Oman.

Q245541.name: Cyclone Sidr
Q245541.blurb: Cyclone Sidr hits Bangladesh, killing an estimated 5,000 people and destroying parts of the world's largest mangrove forest, the Sundarbans.

Q245551.name: 1970 Bhola cyclone
Q245551.blurb: The 1970 Bhola cyclone makes landfall on the coast of East Pakistan, becoming the deadliest tropical cyclone in history.

Q245743.name: Battle of Kassel
Q245743.blurb: World War II: United States Army troops capture Kassel.

Q245811.name: Battle of Chemnitz
Q245811.blurb: Thirty Years' War: Forces of the Holy Roman Empire and Electorate of Saxony are defeated by the Swedes at the Battle of Chemnitz, ending the military effectiveness of the Saxon army for the rest of the war and allowing the Swedes to advance into Bohemia.

Q245831.name: Cyprus problem
aliases: Population exchange between Greek and Turkish Cypriots
Q245831.blurb: Cyprus dispute: The United Nations Security Council authorizes the UNFICYP to create the "Green Line", dividing Cyprus into two zones.

Q246080.name: Gurindji strike
Q246080.blurb: The start of the Wave Hill walk-off by Gurindji people in Australia, lasting eight years, a landmark event in the history of Indigenous land rights in Australia, commemorated in a 1991 Paul Kelly song and an annual celebration.

Q246501.name: Treaty of Fort Stanwix
Q246501.blurb: The Treaty of Fort Stanwix is signed, the purpose of which is to adjust the boundary line between Indian lands and white settlements set forth in the Royal Proclamation of 1763 in the Thirteen Colonies.

Q246652.name: Battle of Tacuarí
Q246652.blurb: Paraguayan forces defeat Manuel Belgrano at the Battle of Tacuarí.

Q246863.name: Livonian War
Q246863.blurb: Livonian War: A Lithuanian surprise attack resulted in a decisive defeat of numerically superior Russian forces.

Q247253.name: Battle of Khe Sanh
aliases: Battle of Khe Sanh in popular culture
Q247253.blurb: Vietnam War, Battle of Khe Sanh: One of the most publicized and controversial battles of the war begins.

Q247395.name: Battle of Hamburger Hill
Q247395.blurb: The Battle of Hamburger Hill in Vietnam ends.

Q247885.name: Typhoon Bopha
Q247885.blurb: At least 475 people are killed after Typhoon Bopha makes landfall in the Philippines.

Q248542.name: Ivy Mike
Q248542.blurb: Nuclear weapons testing: The United States successfully detonates Ivy Mike, the first thermonuclear device, at the Eniwetok atoll. The explosion had a yield of ten megatons TNT equivalent.

Q248979.name: Battle of Modder River
Q248979.blurb: The Second Boer War: A British column is engaged by Boer forces at the Battle of Modder River; although the Boers withdraw, the British suffer heavy casualties.

Q249232.name: War of the Third Coalition
aliases: The War of the Third Coalition
Q249232.blurb: War of the Third Coalition: A French corps defeats an Austrian attempt to escape encirclement at Ulm.

Q249367.name: Montgomery bus boycott
Q249367.blurb: The Civil Rights Movement:  the Montgomery bus boycott begins, led by E. D. Nixon and Rosa Parks.

Q249691.name: Treaty of Paris
Q249691.blurb: The Armistice of Cherasco is signed by Napoleon Bonaparte and Vittorio Amedeo III, King of Sardinia, expanding French territory along the Mediterranean coast.

Q249708.name: Aleutian Islands Campaign
aliases: Battle of the Aleutian Islands detailed account
Q249708.blurb: World War II: Aleutian Islands Campaign: Imperial Japanese soldiers begin occupying the American islands of Attu and Kiska, in the Aleutian Islands off Alaska.

Q250309.name: Battle of Tarawa
Q250309.blurb: World War II: Battle of Tarawa (Operation Galvanic) begins: United States Marines land on Tarawa Atoll in the Gilbert Islands and suffer heavy fire from Japanese shore guns and machine guns.

Q250439.name: Adam Air Flight 574
aliases: Adam Air KI-574 Passengers' Families Association
Q250439.blurb: Adam Air Flight 574 breaks apart in mid-air and crashes near the Makassar Strait, Indonesia, killing all 102 people on board.

Q250578.name: Panama–Pacific International Exposition
Q250578.blurb: The Liberty Bell leaves Philadelphia by special train on its way to the Panama–Pacific International Exposition.  This is the last trip outside Philadelphia that the custodians of the bell intend to permit.

Q250652.name: Battle of Sarikamish
Q250652.blurb: World War I: During the Battle of Sarikamish, Ottoman forces mistook one another for Russian troops. The following friendly fire incident leaves 2,000 Ottomans dead and many more wounded.

Q250747.name: Race to the Sea
Q250747.blurb: World War I: The Race to the Sea begins.

Q250766.name: Zagreb train disaster
Q250766.blurb: A Belgrade–Dortmund express train derails at the main train station in Zagreb killing 153 passengers.

Q251039.name: US Airways Flight 1549
aliases: US Airways Plane Crash In Hudson River
US Airways Plane Crashes In Hudson River
US Airways jet makes emergency landing in river by New York City
Q251039.blurb: US Airways Flight 1549 ditches safely in the Hudson River after the plane collides with birds less than two minutes after take-off. This becomes known as "The Miracle on the Hudson" as all 155 people on board were rescued.

Q251184.name: Battle of Signal Hill
Q251184.blurb: Seven Years' War: Battle of Signal Hill.

Q251597.name: Battle of Dornach
Q251597.blurb: Battle of Dornach: The Swiss decisively defeat the army of Maximilian I, Holy Roman Emperor.

Q252032.name: Mahmudiyah killings
Q252032.blurb: U.S. Army soldiers gang-raped a 14-year-old Iraqi girl and murdered her along with her family members.

Q252612.name: First Continental Congress
Q252612.blurb: First Continental Congress assembles in Philadelphia.

Q252649.name: Provisional Irish Republican Army campaign
Q252649.blurb: The Provisional Irish Republican Army announced the formal end of its armed campaign to overthrow British rule in Northern Ireland and create a united Ireland.

Q252698.name: Battle of Wesenberg
Q252698.blurb: The Battle of Wesenberg is fought between the Livonian Order and Dovmont of Pskov.

Q253224.name: Armistice of Compiègne
aliases: Eleventh day of the eleventh month
Eleventh hour of the eleventh day of the eleventh month
Q253224.blurb: The armistice between the German Empire and the Allies was signed in a railway carriage in the Forest of Compiègne of France (signatories pictured).

Q253684.name: French invasion of Egypt and Syria
aliases: French campaign in Egypt and Syria
Q253684.blurb: French campaign in Egypt and Syria: Napoleon's forces defeat an Ottoman-Mamluk army near Cairo in the Battle of the Pyramids.

Q253774.name: An Lushan Rebellion
Q253774.blurb: An Lushan Rebellion: Emperor Xuanzong of Tang is ordered by his Imperial Guards to execute chancellor Yang Guozhong by forcing him to commit suicide or face a mutiny. General An Lushan has other members of the emperor's family killed.

Q254106.name: Crimean War
aliases: Baltic theatre of the Crimean War
Q254106.blurb: Crimean War: France and Britain declare war on Russia.

Q254599.name: Battle of Shanghai
aliases: Battle at the ports of Shanghai
Q254599.blurb: Second Sino-Japanese War: The Battle of Shanghai begins.

Q254652.name: Starfish Prime
Q254652.blurb: Starfish Prime tests the effects of a nuclear explosion at orbital altitudes.

Q255352.name: Basmachi movement
Q255352.blurb: Enver Pasha dies in a skirmish between the Bolshevik Red Army and Basmachi troops, to whom he had defected earlier.

Q255997.name: Houthi insurgency
aliases: Child soldiers in the Houthi insurgency in Yemen
Use of child soldiers in the Houthi insurgency in Yemen
Q255997.blurb: Yemen's Houthi rebels claim responsibility for an attack on Saudi Arabian oil facilities.

Q256563.name: Battle of the Dardanelles
Q256563.blurb: A joined Hospitaller-Venetian fleet defeats a numerically superior Ottoman fleet in the battle of the Dardanelles.

Q256608.name: Outer Space Treaty
aliases: Treaty on Principles Governing the Activities of States in the Exploration and Use of Outer Space, including the Moon and Other Celestial Bodies
List of parties to the Outer Space Treaty
Treaty on Principles Governing the Activities of States in the Exploration and Use of Outer Space
Treaty on principles governing the activities of states in the exploration and use of outer space including the moon and other bodies
Q256608.blurb: The Outer Space Treaty comes into force.

Q256664.name: Doctors' plot
Q256664.blurb: Nine Moscow doctors were accused of a plot to poison members of the Soviet political and military leadership.

Q256812.name: Corona
Q256812.blurb: The Corona reconnaissance satellite program, in existence from 1959 to 1972, is declassified.

Q257724.name: Ethiopian Civil War
Q257724.blurb: Mengistu Haile Mariam, president of the People's Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, flees Ethiopia, effectively bringing the Ethiopian Civil War to an end.

Q258081.name: Continental System
Q258081.blurb: Napoleonic Wars: France issues the Milan Decree, which confirms the Continental System.

Q258873.name: Waco Siege
aliases: God help us we want the press
Q258873.blurb: The 51-day FBI siege of the Branch Davidian building in Waco, Texas, US, ends when a fire breaks out. Seventy-six Davidians, including 18 children under age 10, died in the fire.

Q259060.name: Walking Purchase
Q259060.blurb: The Walking Purchase concludes, which forces the cession of 1.2 million acres (4,900 km2) of Lenape-Delaware tribal land to the Pennsylvania Colony.

Q259430.name: Treaty of Gandamak
Q259430.blurb: Russia and the United Kingdom sign the Treaty of Gandamak establishing an Afghan state.

Q259431.name: Council of Sutri
Q259431.blurb: Emperor Henry III convenes the synod of Sutri to mediate between different claimants to the papacy.

Q259502.name: Australian dollar
Q259502.blurb: A severe hailstorm strikes Sydney, Australia causing A$2.3 billion in insured damages, the most costly natural disaster in Australian history.

Q259526.name: Battle of Long Tan
Q259526.blurb: Vietnam War: The Battle of Long Tan ensues after a patrol from the 6th Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment clashes with a Viet Cong force in Phước Tuy Province.

Q260447.name: Rentenmark
Q260447.blurb: The German Rentenmark is introduced in Germany to counter hyperinflation in the Weimar Republic.

Q261738.name: Battle of Kilrush
Q261738.blurb: Irish Confederate Wars: A Confederate Irish militia is routed in the Battle of Kilrush when it attempts to halt the progress of a Royalist Army.

Q262648.name: Battle of Höchstädt
Q262648.blurb: War of the Second Coalition: Battle of Höchstädt results in a French victory over Austria.

Q263047.name: Monday demonstrations in East Germany
Q263047.blurb: In Leipzig, East Germany, the first of weekly demonstration for the legalisation of opposition groups and democratic reforms takes place.

Q263142.name: Battle of the Java Sea
Q263142.blurb: World War II: During the Battle of the Java Sea, an Allied strike force is defeated by a Japanese task force in the Java Sea in the Dutch East Indies.

Q263249.name: Plan of San Luis Potosí
Q263249.blurb: Mexican Revolution: Francisco I. Madero issues the Plan de San Luis Potosí, denouncing Mexican President Porfirio Díaz, calling for a revolution to overthrow the government of Mexico, effectively starting the Mexican Revolution.

Q263716.name: Eight Trigrams Uprising of 1813
Q263716.blurb: Followers of the Eight Trigram Sect loyal to Lin Qing attack the Forbidden City in a failed attempt to oust the Jiaqing Emperor of the Qing dynasty.

Q263898.name: 1934 Masters Tournament
Q263898.blurb: The first Masters Tournament is held at Augusta National Golf Club in Georgia.

Q264915.name: Fall of Krak des Chevaliers
Q264915.blurb: Fall of Krak des Chevaliers: In Syria, sultan Baibars conquers the Krak des Chevaliers.

Q266532.name: The Addams Family
Q266532.blurb: The first television adaptation of Charles Addams's "The Addams Family" premieres on ABC Television.

Q267299.name: World Chess Championship 1894
Q267299.blurb: Germany's Emanuel Lasker defeated Wilhelm Steinitz to become the world chess champion, beginning a record 27-year reign.

Q267339.name: Battle of Grand Port
Q267339.blurb: Napoleonic Wars: The French Navy defeats the British Royal Navy, preventing them from taking the harbour of Grand Port on Île de France.

Q267418.name: Uzbin Valley ambush
Q267418.blurb: War of Afghanistan: The Uzbin Valley ambush occurs.

Q268567.name: 2006 FIFA World Cup Final
Q268567.blurb: Italy win their fourth World Cup title, defeating France 5–3 on penalties following a 1–1 draw after extra time.

Q268661.name: 2008 attack on the American Embassy in Yemen
Q268661.blurb: Seven al-Qaeda fighters attack the embassy of the United States in Sanaa, Yemen, leaving 20 people dead.

Q269442.name: 2010 eruptions of Eyjafjallajökull
Q269442.blurb: Plumes of ash from a major eruption of the Eyjafjallajökull volcano in Iceland led to widespread disruption of air travel throughout Europe for several days.

Q269464.name: Rosenstrasse protest
Q269464.blurb: The Holocaust: In Berlin, the Gestapo arrest 1,800 Jewish men with German wives, leading to the Rosenstrasse protest.

Q269655.name: Treaty of Shimonoseki
Q269655.blurb: The Treaty of Shimonoseki between China and Japan is signed. This marks the end of the First Sino-Japanese War, and the defeated Qing Empire is forced to renounce its claims on Korea and to concede the southern portion of the Fengtian province, Taiwan and the Penghu to Japan.

Q269893.name: 2010 Moscow Metro bombings
Q269893.blurb: Two suicide bombers hit the Moscow Metro system at the peak of the morning rush hour, killing 40.

Q270517.name: Dieppe Raid
Q270517.blurb: World War II: Operation Jubilee (The Dieppe Raid): The 2nd Canadian Infantry Division leads an amphibious assault by allied forces on Dieppe, France and fails.

Q270642.name: Irish pound
Q270642.blurb: The decimalisation of the currencies of the United Kingdom and Ireland is completed on Decimal Day.

Q273011.name: Battle of Marengo
Q273011.blurb: The French Army of First Consul Napoleon Bonaparte defeats the Austrians at the Battle of Marengo in Northern Italy and re-conquers Italy.

Q273069.name: Battle of Lechfeld
Q273069.blurb: Battle of Lechfeld: Otto I, Holy Roman Emperor defeats the Magyars, ending 50 years of Magyar invasion of the West.

Q273095.name: Great Exhibition
aliases: Great Exhibition of the Works of Industry of All Nations
The Great Exhibition of the Works of Industry of All Nations
Exhibition of the Works of Industry of All Nations
Q273095.blurb: Queen Victoria opens The Great Exhibition at The Crystal Palace in London.

Q273348.name: Italian Wars
Q273348.blurb: The second of two treaties making up the Peace of Cateau-Cambrésis is signed, ending the Italian Wars.

Q273659.name: Iran–Contra affair
Q273659.blurb: Iran–Contra affair: The Tower Commission rebukes President Ronald Reagan for not controlling his national security staff.

Q274365.name: 8888 Uprising
Q274365.blurb: The 8888 Uprising begins in Rangoon (Yangon), Burma (Myanmar). Led by students, hundreds of thousands join in nationwide protests against the one-party regime. On September 18, the demonstrations end in a military crackdown, killing thousands.

Q274489.name: Yngsjö murder
Q274489.blurb: Anna Månsdotter, found guilty of the 1889 Yngsjö murder, becomes the last woman to be executed in Sweden.[better source needed]

Q274498.name: 1923 Great Kantō Earthquake
Q274498.blurb: The Great Kantō Earthquake devastates Tokyo and Yokohama, killing about 105,000 people.

Q274811.name: Élysée Treaty
aliases: Vertrag zwischen der Bundesrepublik Deutschland und der Französischen Republik über die deutsch-französische Zusammenarbeit
Vertrag zwischen der Französischen Republik und der Bundesrepublik Deutschland über die französisch-deutsche Zusammenarbeit
Q274811.blurb: The Élysée Treaty of cooperation between France and West Germany is signed by Charles de Gaulle and Konrad Adenauer.

Q275618.name: occupation of Czechoslovakia
aliases: Czech Republic during World War II
Czech Republic in World War II
German occupation of Czechoslovakia in World War II
Nazi Germany's occupation of the Sudetenland
Occupation of Czechoslovakia by Nazi Germany

Q275683.name: Bulgarian unification
Q275683.blurb: Bulgarian victory in the Serbo-Bulgarian War preserves the Unification of Bulgaria.

Q275837.name: Sports Illustrated
Q275837.blurb: The first issue of Sports Illustrated is published.

Q276059.name: Battle of Vitoria
Q276059.blurb: Peninsular War: Wellington defeats Joseph Bonaparte at the Battle of Vitoria.

Q276294.name: Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina
aliases: Air Force of Bosnia and Herzegovina
Military equipment of Bosnia and Herzegovina
Military history of Bosnia and Herzegovina
Q276294.blurb: Bosnian War: The Bosnian Army executes a surprise attack at the village of Kravica in Srebrenica.

Q276656.name: Battle of Penghu
Q276656.blurb: Manchu Qing dynasty naval forces under commander Shi Lang defeat the Kingdom of Tungning in the Battle of Penghu near the Pescadores Islands.

Q277072.name: Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women
aliases: Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women
Committee on the Elimination of all forms of Discrimination Against Women
Convention for the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women
Convention of the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women
Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Descrimination against Women
Convention on the Elimination of all Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW)
The Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women
The Convention on the Elimination of all Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW)
Treaty for the Rights of Women
UN Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women
United Nations Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women
United Nations Convention for the Elimination of All Discrimination against Women (CEDAW)
United Nations Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women
Q277072.blurb: The Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, an international bill of rights for women, is instituted by the United Nations.

Q277337.name: Battle of Changjin Reservoir
Q277337.blurb: Korean War: Communist Chinese troops launch a massive counterattack (Battle of the Ch'ongch'on River and Battle of Chosin Reservoir) against United Nations and South Korean forces.

Q277343.name: Torrijos–Carter Treaties
aliases: The Treaty Concerning the Permanent Neutrality and Operation of the Panama Canal
Q277343.blurb: The Torrijos–Carter Treaties between Panama and the United States on the status of the Panama Canal are signed. The United States agrees to transfer control of the canal to Panama at the end of the 20th century.

Q277392.name: Polish–Ottoman War of 1620–1621
Q277392.blurb: Polish–Ottoman War: The Ottoman Empire defeats the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth during the Battle of Cecora.

Q277450.name: Aceh War
Q277450.blurb: A Dutch military expedition was launched to bombard Banda Aceh, the capital of the Aceh Sultanate in present-day Indonesia, beginning the Aceh War.

Q277560.name: de-Stalinization
Q277560.blurb: In Tbilisi, Georgia, soldiers suppressed mass demonstrations against Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev's policy of de-Stalinization.

Q277985.name: 1st Ukrainian Front
Q277985.blurb: World War II: The 1st Ukrainian Front liberates Kyiv from German occupation.

Q278147.name: Ajankohtainen kakkonen
Q278147.blurb: The Finnish Yle TV2 channel's Ajankohtainen kakkonen current affairs program airs controversial Homoilta episode (literally "gay night"), which leads to the resignation of almost 50,000 Finns from the Evangelical Lutheran Church.

Q278960.name: Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty
aliases: Treaty Banning Nuclear Weapon Tests in the Atmosphere, in Outer Space and Under Water
Treaty Banning Nuclear Weapon Tests in the Atmosphere, in Outer Space, and Under Water
Treaty Banning Nuclear Weapons Tests in the Atmosphere, in Outer Space, and Under Water
Q278960.blurb: President Kennedy signs the ratification of the Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty.

Q279611.name: Siege of Haengju
Q279611.blurb: Japanese invasions of Korea: A force of 3,000 Korean soldiers successfully defended Haengju Fortress against 30,000 Japanese invaders.

Q279662.name: Cristero War
Q279662.blurb: New Mexican oil legislation goes into effect, leading to the formal outbreak of the Cristero War.

Q279790.name: May Fourth Movement
aliases: May Fourth Movement for Science and Democracy
Q279790.blurb: May Fourth Movement: Student demonstrations take place in Tiananmen Square in Beijing, China, protesting the Treaty of Versailles, which transferred Chinese territory to Japan.

Q280468.name: Battle of Ap Bac
Q280468.blurb: Vietnam War: The Viet Cong wins its first major victory, at the Battle of Ap Bac.

Q281648.name: Battle of Dupplin Moor
Q281648.blurb: Wars of Scottish Independence: Battle of Dupplin Moor: Scots under Domhnall II, Earl of Mar are routed by Edward Balliol.

Q282999.name: Aero Caribbean Flight 883
Q282999.blurb: Aero Caribbean Flight 883 crashes into Guasimal, Sancti Spíritus; all 68 passengers and crew are killed.

Q283062.name: Battle of Benevento
Q283062.blurb: Battle of Benevento: An army led by Charles, Count of Anjou, defeats a combined German and Sicilian force led by Manfred, King of Sicily. Manfred is killed in the battle and Pope Clement IV invests Charles as king of Sicily and Naples.

Q283364.name: Battle of Legnano
Q283364.blurb: Battle of Legnano: The Lombard League defeats Emperor Frederick I.

Q283397.name: Brașov Rebellion
Q283397.blurb: In Brașov, Romania, workers rebel against the communist regime of Nicolae Ceaușescu.

Q283511.name: Triple Alliance
Q283511.blurb: The Netherlands, Great Britain, and France sign the Triple Alliance.

Q284163.name: 2022 FIFA World Cup
aliases: 2022 FIFA World Cup team base camps
Supreme Committee for Legacy and Delivery
Q284163.blurb: The 2022 FIFA World Cup begins in Qatar. This is the first time the tournament was held in the Middle East.

Q284697.name: 2010 G20 Toronto summit
Q284697.blurb: A G20 summit, the largest and most expensive security operation in Canadian history, began in downtown Toronto.

Q285280.name: Transnistria War
aliases: Foreign involvement in the Transnistria War
Q285280.blurb: Start of the war in Transnistria.

Q285406.name: World's Columbian Exposition
Q285406.blurb: Opening ceremonies for the World's Columbian Exposition are held in Chicago, though because construction was behind schedule, the exposition did not open until May 1, 1893.

Q286436.name: Al-Qaeda insurgency in Yemen
Q286436.blurb: Yemen declares an open war against the terrorist group al-Qaeda.

Q286474.name: German AB-Aktion in Poland
aliases: German AB Action operation in Poland
Q286474.blurb: German AB-Aktion in Poland: After capturing Lwów, the Nazis executed professors of the University of Lwów along with their families.

Q286655.name: Tonkin Campaign
Q286655.blurb: Tonkin Campaign: French forces capture the Sơn Tây citadel.

Q287405.name: Miracle on Ice
Q287405.blurb: Miracle on Ice: In Lake Placid, New York, the United States hockey team defeats the Soviet Union hockey team 4–3.

Q287422.name: Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty
aliases: Treaty on the Limitation of Anti-Ballistic Missile Systems
Q287422.blurb: The United States withdraws from the Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty.

Q287424.name: Moorgate tube crash
Q287424.blurb: In London, an underground train fails to stop at Moorgate terminus station and crashes into the end of the tunnel, killing 43 people.

Q287942.name: Ninth Russo-Turkish War
Q287942.blurb: The Ottoman Empire signs the Treaty of Adrianople with Russia, thus ending the Russo-Turkish War.

Q288045.name: Hōei eruption
Q288045.blurb: The most recent eruption of Mount Fuji.

Q288229.name: The Station nightclub fire
Q288229.blurb: During a Great White concert in West Warwick, Rhode Island, a pyrotechnics display sets the Station nightclub ablaze, killing 100 and injuring over 200 others.

Q288251.name: Cisplatine War
Q288251.blurb: Returning to Buenos Aires with troops who fought in the Cisplatine War, Juan Lavalle (pictured) deposed provincial governor Manuel Dorrego, reigniting the Argentine Civil Wars.

Q288345.name: Battle of Lincoln
Q288345.blurb: The Battle of Lincoln, at which Stephen, King of England is defeated and captured by the allies of Empress Matilda.

Q288601.name: Operation Frankton
Q288601.blurb: World War II: British commandos conduct Operation Frankton, a raid on shipping in Bordeaux harbour.

Q289492.name: Battle of the Zab
Q289492.blurb: In the Battle of the Zab, the Abbasid rebels defeat the Umayyad Caliphate, leading to the overthrow of the dynasty.

Q296754.name: Battle of Singapore
Q296754.blurb: World War II: Japan invades Singapore.

Q298864.name: Neapolitan War
Q298864.blurb: Neapolitan War: Joachim Murat, King of Naples, is defeated by the Austrians at the Battle of Tolentino, the decisive engagement of the war.

Q300593.name: A Time for Choosing
Q300593.blurb: Actor Ronald Reagan delivered a speech on behalf of Republican presidential candidate Barry Goldwater, launching his own political career, which culminated in him serving two full terms as U.S. president.

Q301300.name: Battle of Java
Q301300.blurb: The Battle of Java ends with the surrender of the American-British-Dutch-Australian Command to the Empire of Japan in Bandung, West Java, Dutch East Indies.

Q301448.name: Coastal Road massacre
Q301448.blurb: Coastal Road massacre: At least 37 are killed and more than 70 are wounded when Fatah hijack an Israeli bus, prompting Israel's Operation Litani.

Q301487.name: Battle of Brandywine
Q301487.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Battle of Brandywine: The British celebrate a major victory in Chester County, Pennsylvania.

Q302045.name: Post-Soviet states
aliases: Countries of the former Soviet Union
Former countries of the Soviet Union
List of C.I.S countries by GDP per capita
List of CIS countries by GDP (PPP)
List of CIS countries by GDP (PPP) per capita
List of CIS countries by GDP PPP
List of former Soviet Republics by GDP
List of former Soviet Republics by GDP (Nominal)
List of former Soviet Republics by GDP (PPP)
List of former Soviet Republics by GDP (PPP) per capita
List of former Soviet Republics by GDP (nominal) per capita
Lists of former Soviet Republics by GDP (PPP)
Lists of former Soviet Republics by GDP (PPP) per capita
Newly Independent States of the Former Soviet Union
Q302045.blurb: The current flag of Uzbekistan was adopted, making the country the first newly independent republic in Central Asia to choose a new flag.

Q302519.name: Battle of Adwa
Q302519.blurb: Battle of Adwa: An Ethiopian army defeats an outnumbered Italian force, ending the First Italo-Ethiopian War.

Q303176.name: Battle of Manila
Q303176.blurb: Spanish–American War: Spanish and American forces engage in a mock battle for Manila, after which the Spanish commander surrendered in order to keep the city out of Filipino rebel hands.

Q303438.name: Mountain Meadows massacre
Q303438.blurb: Mountain Meadows massacre: Mormon settlers slaughter most members of a peaceful emigrant wagon train.

Q303998.name: Battle of Tourcoing
Q303998.blurb: Battle of Tourcoing during the Flanders Campaign of the War of the First Coalition.

Q304290.name: Rugrats
Q304290.blurb: Nickelodeon's first line of "Nicktoons" (Doug, Rugrats & Ren & Stimpy) premiere on the channel.

Q304403.name: Operation Biting
Q304403.blurb: World War II: Operation Biting launches its overnight raid on the German coastal radar station at Bruneval to retrieve a Würzburg installation.

Q304939.name: Uman–Botoşani Offensive
Q304939.blurb: World War II: The Red Army begins the Uman–Botoșani offensive in the western Ukrainian SSR.

Q305149.name: Battle of Mogyoród
Q305149.blurb: Battle of Mogyoród: Dukes Géza and Ladislaus defeat their cousin Solomon, King of Hungary, forcing him to flee to Hungary's western borderland.

Q305276.name: treaty of Corbeil
Q305276.blurb: The kingdom of France and the kingdom of Scotland agree on a treaty of mutual aid at Corbeil.

Q305409.name: Battle of Mine Run
Q305409.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Mine Run: Union forces under General George Meade take up positions against troops led by Confederate General Robert E. Lee.

Q306123.name: Austrian Civil War
Q306123.blurb: The Austrian Civil War ends with the defeat of the Social Democrats and the Republikanischer Schutzbund.

Q306535.name: Austrian State Treaty
Q306535.blurb: The Austrian State Treaty restores Austrian sovereignty.

Q307716.name: abdication of Edward VIII
Q307716.blurb: Half a year after abdicating the British throne, Edward, Duke of Windsor, married American socialite Wallis Simpson in a private ceremony in France.

Q308923.name: Munich air disaster
aliases: 1958 BEA Airspeed Ambassador Munich air disaster
Q308923.blurb: Eight Manchester United F.C. players and 15 other passengers are killed in the Munich air disaster.

Q308999.name: Battle of Leyte Gulf
aliases: Second Battle of the Philippine Sea
Q308999.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Leyte Gulf begins.

Q309029.name: Alaska Purchase
Q309029.blurb: United States takes possession of Alaska after purchasing it from Russia for $7.2 million. Celebrated annually in the state as Alaska Day.

Q309184.name: Boshin War
aliases: War of the Year of the Dragon
Q309184.blurb: Boshin War: The Battle of Toba–Fushimi begins, between forces of the Tokugawa shogunate and pro-Imperial factions; it will end in defeat for the shogunate, and is a pivotal point in the Meiji Restoration.

Q309204.name: Camp David Accords
aliases: 1978 Camp David Peace Accords between Egypt and Israel
Q309204.blurb: Camp David Accords: Menachem Begin and Anwar Sadat begin peace discussions at Camp David, Maryland.

Q310218.name: Enabling Act of 1933
aliases: Law to Remedy the Distress of the People and the Reich
Gesetz zur Behebung der Not von Volk und Reich
Law for the Alleviation of the People's and the Reich's Misery
Law to Remedy the Distress of the People and the Nation
Q310218.blurb: The Reichstag passes the Enabling Act of 1933, making Adolf Hitler dictator of Germany.

Q311721.name: Hindenburg Line
Q311721.blurb: World War I:  The Hindenburg Line is broken by an Allied attack.

Q311726.name: Battle of the Plains of Abraham
aliases: Battle at the plains of abraham
The Battle of the Plains of Abraham
Q311726.blurb: Battle of the Plains of Abraham: the British defeat the French near Quebec City in the Seven Years' War, known in the United States as the French and Indian War.

Q311773.name: Sonderkommando
Q311773.blurb: The Holocaust: Sonderkommando work-unit members in Auschwitz concentration camp revolted upon learning that they were due to be killed; although a few managed to escape, most were massacred on the same day.

Q312212.name: Battle of Nördlingen
Q312212.blurb: Thirty Years' War: In the Battle of Nördlingen, the Catholic Imperial army defeats Swedish and German Protestant forces.

Q312268.name: Siege of Constantinople
Q312268.blurb: The Avars and Sassanids besiege Constantinople, held by Byzantine troops under Patrician Bonus.

Q312388.name: Bleiburg repatriations
aliases: Independent State of Croatia evacuation to Austria
Partisan pursuit of Independent State of Croatia collaborators
Yugoslav Partisan crimes after World War II
Yugoslav Partisan death march of Nazi collaborators
Yugoslav Partisan death march of collaborators repatriated at Bleiburg
Yugoslav Partisan killings of prisoners of war
Yugoslav Partisan pursuit of Independent State of Croatia collaborators
Yugoslav Partisan pursuit of Nazi collaborators
Yugoslav death march of Nazi collaborators
Yugoslav death march of collaborators repatriated at Bleiburg
Yugoslav pursuit of Independent State of Croatia collaborators
Q312388.blurb: The British Army directed fleeing Croatian soldiers to surrender to the Yugoslav Partisans, beginning the Bleiburg repatriations.

Q313102.name: Pragmatic Sanction of 1713
aliases: Pragmatic Sanction of Emperor Charles VI
Q313102.blurb: France, Prussia, Bavaria and Saxony refuse to honour the Pragmatic Sanction, and the War of the Austrian Succession begins.

Q313329.name: Spartacist uprising
Q313329.blurb: Rosa Luxemburg and Karl Liebknecht, two of the most prominent communists in Germany, are clubbed and then shot to death by members of the Freikorps at the end of the Spartacist uprising.

Q313349.name: Treaty of the Pruth
Q313349.blurb: The treaty of Pruth between the Ottoman and Russian Empire is signed.

Q313404.name: Eschede derailment
Q313404.blurb: After suffering a mechanical failure, a high speed train derails at Eschede, Germany, killing 101 people.

Q313435.name: Battle of Leuthen
Q313435.blurb: Seven Years' War: Battle of Leuthen: Frederick II of Prussia leads Prussian forces to a decisive victory over Austrian forces under Prince Charles Alexander of Lorraine.

Q314087.name: Ramstein air show disaster
Q314087.blurb: Ramstein air show disaster: Three aircraft of the Frecce Tricolori demonstration team collide and the wreckage falls into the crowd. Seventy-five are killed and 346 seriously injured.

Q314701.name: Decision on the Capital of Germany
Q314701.blurb: The German Bundestag returns to Berlin.

Q315310.name: Battle of Restigouche
Q315310.blurb: British forces defeat French forces in the last naval battle in New France.

Q315342.name: Burgundian Wars
Q315342.blurb: Burgundian Wars: The Old Swiss Confederacy hands Charles the Bold, Duke of Burgundy, a major defeat in the Battle of Grandson in Canton of Neuchâtel.

Q315395.name: May Uprising in Dresden
Q315395.blurb: The May Uprising in Dresden begins: The last of the German revolutions of 1848–49.

Q315921.name: Thirteen Years' War
Q315921.blurb: Thirteen Years' War: The Secret Council of the Prussian Confederation sends a formal act of disobedience to the Grand Master of the Teutonic Knights, sparking the Thirteen Years' War.

Q316139.name: Battle of Oudenarde
Q316139.blurb: A coalition army of Dutch, English and German troops under the duke of Marlborough defeats a French army under the duke of Burgundy and the Marshal Vendome in the battle of Oudenarde.

Q316743.name: Ninth Crusade
Q316743.blurb: Shortly after his return from the Ninth Crusade, Edward I (pictured) was crowned King of England at Westminster Abbey, nearly two years after his father's death.

Q316817.name: 1973 oil crisis
Q316817.blurb: In response to the 1973 oil crisis, the United States implements the Emergency Daylight Saving Time Energy Conservation Act, switching to permanent daylight saving time for a trial period.

Q316843.name: Battle of Bautzen
Q316843.blurb: World War II: Battle of Bautzen: Last successful German tank-offensive of the war and last noteworthy victory of the Wehrmacht.

Q316868.name: Bombing of Hamburg in World War II
Q316868.blurb: World War II: Operation Gomorrah: The Royal Air Force bombs Hamburg, Germany causing a firestorm that kills 42,000 German civilians.

Q316877.name: Battle of Nancy
Q316877.blurb: Battle of Nancy: Charles the Bold is defeated and killed in a conflict with René II, Duke of Lorraine; Burgundy subsequently becomes part of France.

Q316897.name: Battle of Malplaquet
Q316897.blurb: Battle of Malplaquet: Great Britain, Netherlands, and Austria fight against France.

Q317295.name: Big Week
Q317295.blurb: World War II: The "Big Week" begins with American bomber raids on German aircraft manufacturing centers.

Q318161.name: Helsinki Accords
aliases: Final Act of the Helsinki Conference
Q318161.blurb: The final act of the CSCE meeting is signed in Helsinki, Finland.

Q318250.name: Ogaden War
Q318250.blurb: Somalia and Ethiopia sign a truce to end the Ethio-Somali War.

Q319260.name: Treaty of Paris
Q319260.blurb: The Treaty of Paris is signed, ending the Crimean War.

Q320394.name: Battle of Almansa
Q320394.blurb: A coalition of Britain, the Netherlands and Portugal is defeated by a Franco-Spanish army at Almansa (Spain) in the War of the Spanish Succession.

Q321032.name: Council of Florence
aliases: Council of Basel Ferrara and Florence
Q321032.blurb: The Council of Basel suspends Pope Eugene IV.

Q321531.name: Adolf Eichmann trial
Q321531.blurb: Eichmann trial: Adolf Eichmann is sentenced to death after being found guilty by an Israeli court of 15 criminal charges, including charges of crimes against humanity, crimes against the Jewish people, and membership of an outlawed organization.

Q321851.name: May 17 Agreement
aliases: Peace Treaty between Lebanon and Israel
Q321851.blurb: Lebanon, Israel, and the United States sign an agreement on Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon.

Q321865.name: 1975 Algiers Agreement
Q321865.blurb: Algiers Accord: Iran and Iraq announce a settlement of their border dispute.

Q321885.name: Erdut Agreement
aliases: Basic Agreement on the Region of Eastern Slavonia, Baranja and Western Sirmium
Q321885.blurb: Erdut Agreement regarding the peaceful resolution to the Croatian War of Independence is reached.

Q321925.name: Sunningdale Agreement
Q321925.blurb: British and Irish authorities sign the Sunningdale Agreement in an attempt to establish a power-sharing Northern Ireland Executive and a cross-border Council of Ireland.

Q322260.name: Able Archer 83
Q322260.blurb: Cold War: The command post exercise Able Archer 83 begins, eventually leading to the Soviet Union to place air units in East Germany and Poland on alert, for fear that NATO was preparing for war

Q322450.name: Cologne school massacre
Q322450.blurb: World War II veteran Walter Seifert attacks an elementary school in Cologne, Germany, killing at least eight children and two teachers, and seriously injuring several more, with a home-made flamethrower and a lance.

Q322607.name: War of Attrition
Q322607.blurb: War of Attrition: The Battle of Karameh took place between the Israel Defense Forces and allied troops of the Palestine Liberation Organization and the Jordanian Armed Forces.

Q322936.name: AMIA bombing
aliases: Memorandum of understanding between Argentina and Iran

Memorandum of understanding between the Government of Argentina and the Government of Islamic Republic of Iran on the issues related to the terrorist attack against AMIA headquarter in Buenos Aires on July 18, 1994
Q322936.blurb: The bombing of the Asociación Mutual Israelita Argentina (Argentine Jewish Community Center) in Buenos Aires kills 85 people (mostly Jewish) and injures 300.

Q322943.name: Paris Peace Treaties
Q322943.blurb: The Paris Peace Treaties are signed by Italy, Romania, Hungary, Bulgaria, Finland and the Allies of World War II.

Q323888.name: Heysel Stadium disaster
Q323888.blurb: Heysel Stadium disaster: Thirty-nine association football fans die and hundreds are injured when a dilapidated retaining wall collapses.

Q324438.name: War of the Pyrenees
Q324438.blurb: War of the Pyrenees: France regained nearly all the land it lost to Spain the previous year with its victory in the Second Battle of Boulou.

Q324916.name: Battle of Solferino
aliases: Battle of Solferino and San Martino
Q324916.blurb: Battle of Solferino (Battle of the Three Sovereigns): Sardinia and France defeat Austria in Solferino, northern Italy.

Q325314.name: Tecumseh's War
Q325314.blurb: Tecumseh's War: The Battle of Tippecanoe is fought near present-day Battle Ground, Indiana, United States.

Q325486.name: Battle of Blue Licks
Q325486.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Battle of Blue Licks: The last major engagement of the war, almost ten months after the surrender of the British commander Charles Cornwallis following the Siege of Yorktown.

Q325656.name: Road to Canossa
Q325656.blurb: Walk to Canossa: The excommunication of Henry IV, Holy Roman Emperor, is lifted after he humbles himself before Pope Gregory VII at Canossa in Italy.

Q325985.name: Siege of Acre
Q325985.blurb: Fall of Acre, the end of Crusader presence in the Holy Land.

Q326028.name: Great Peace of Montreal
Q326028.blurb: Great Peace of Montreal between New France and First Nations is signed.

Q326241.name: Hijacking of Lufthansa Flight 181
Q326241.blurb: Hijacking of Lufthansa Flight 181 by the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine.

Q326417.name: Battle of Marston Moor
Q326417.blurb: English Civil War: Battle of Marston Moor.

Q326668.name: Operation Enduring Freedom
Q326668.blurb: Battle of Wanat begins when Taliban and al-Qaeda guerrillas attack US Army and Afghan National Army troops in Afghanistan. The U.S. deaths were, at that time, the most in a single battle since the beginning of operations in 2001.

Q326989.name: Battle of Morgarten
Q326989.blurb: Growth of the Old Swiss Confederacy: The Schweizer Eidgenossenschaft ambushes the army of Leopold I in the Battle of Morgarten.

Q327035.name: Battle of Gazala
Q327035.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Gazala begins, in present-day Libya.

Q327044.name: Operation Nordwind
Q327044.blurb: World War II: Operation Nordwind, the last major Wehrmacht offensive on the Western Front, begins.

Q327052.name: Battle of Aachen
Q327052.blurb: World War II: The city of Aachen falls to American forces after three weeks of fighting, the first German city to fall to the Allies.

Q327056.name: 2011 Germany E. coli O104:H4 outbreak
Q327056.blurb: An E. coli outbreak strikes Europe, mostly in Germany, leaving more than 30 people dead and many others are taken ill.

Q327099.name: Battle of Kasserine Passe
Q327099.blurb: World War II: Battle of Kasserine Pass in Tunisia begins.

Q327150.name: Byzantine–Norman Wars
Q327150.blurb: Byzantine–Norman wars: After a siege of almost three years, Italo-Norman forces conquered the city of Bari, the capital of the Catepanate of Italy, ending more than five centuries of Byzantine presence in the region.

Q327576.name: 2005 Sharm el-Sheikh attacks
aliases: Many dead in Egyptian resort blasts
Q327576.blurb: Three bombs explode in the Naama Bay area of Sharm El Sheikh, Egypt, killing 88 people.

Q327895.name: Łódź Ghetto
Q327895.blurb: The Holocaust: Nazi Germany begins deporting Jews from the Łódź Ghetto to Chełmno extermination camp.

Q327959.name: 2000 United States presidential election
aliases: List of candidates in the United States Presidential election, 2000
United States presidential election swing states, 2000
United States third party and independent presidential candidates, 2000
Q327959.blurb: The controversial US presidential election is later resolved in the Bush v. Gore Supreme Court case, electing George W. Bush as the 43rd President of the United States.

Q328357.name: Belgrade offensive
Q328357.blurb: World War II: The Soviet Red Army and Yugoslav Partisans liberate Belgrade.

Q328499.name: Armistice of Mudros
Q328499.blurb: World War I: The Ottoman Empire signs the Armistice of Mudros with the Allies.

Q329203.name: First Boer War
Q329203.blurb: First Boer War: The Battle of Majuba Hill takes place.

Q329838.name: Crisis of the Third Century
aliases: Roman Emperor (Crisis of the Third Century)
Q329838.blurb: Roman emperor Severus Alexander is murdered, marking the start of the Crisis of the Third Century.

Q331170.name: Battle of Montjuïc
Q331170.blurb: Reapers' War: Battle of Montjuïc, decisive victory of the Catalan army (with French support) over the Spanish army.

Q331347.name: Battle of Eylau
Q331347.blurb: Napoleonic Wars: Napoleon finds Bennigsen's Russian forces taking a stand at Eylau. After bitter fighting, the French take the town, but the Russians resume the battle the next day.

Q331588.name: Convention on Cluster Munitions
aliases: Dublin Diplomatic Conference on Cluster Munitions
Q331588.blurb: Convention on Cluster Munitions is adopted.

Q331590.name: Indigenous and Tribal Peoples Convention, 1989
aliases: C169 - Indigenous and Tribal Peoples Convention, 1989 (No. 169)
Convention concerning Indigenous and Tribal Peoples in Independent Countries
Q331590.blurb: The current international law defending indigenous peoples, Indigenous and Tribal Peoples Convention, 1989, is ratified for the first time by Norway.

Q331721.name: 1907 Tiflis bank robbery
Q331721.blurb: Organized by Vladimir Lenin and Joseph Stalin, among others, Bolshevik revolutionaries robbed a bank stagecoach in Tiflis, present-day Georgia.

Q331725.name: Battle of Domstadtl
Q331725.blurb: Seven Years' War: Habsburg Austrian forces destroy a Prussian reinforcement and supply convoy in the Battle of Domstadtl, helping to expel Prussian King Frederick the Great from Moravia.

Q331875.name: Abscam
Q331875.blurb: Reports surface that the FBI is targeting allegedly corrupt Congressmen in the Abscam operation.

Q331905.name: abolition of the han system
aliases: Abolition of feudal domains and the establishment of prefectures
Q331905.blurb: Emperor Meiji orders the abolition of the han system and the establishment of prefectures as local centers of administration. (Traditional Japanese date: July 14, 1871).

Q332543.name: Battle of the Pyramids
Q332543.blurb: French campaign in Egypt and Syria: Napoleon's forces defeat an Ottoman-Mamluk army near Cairo in the Battle of the Pyramids.

Q333269.name: August 2009 Baghdad bombings
Q333269.blurb: A series of bombings in Baghdad, Iraq, kills 101 and injures 565 others.

Q333343.name: Bristol Channel floods, 1607
Q333343.blurb: Low-lying areas flooded around the coasts of the Bristol Channel in southwest England and south Wales, resulting in around 2,000 deaths.

Q333349.name: 1966 flood of the Arno
Q333349.blurb: The Arno River floods Florence, Italy, to a maximum depth of 6.7 m (22 ft), leaving thousands homeless and destroying millions of masterpieces of art and rare books. Venice is also submerged on the same day at its record all-time acqua alta of 194 cm (76 in).

Q333363.name: 2009 Jeddah floods
Q333363.blurb: Jeddah floods: Freak rains swamp the city of Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, during an ongoing Hajj pilgrimage. Three thousand cars are swept away and 122 people perish in the torrents, with 350 others missing.

Q334029.name: Battle of Bunker Hill
aliases: Don't fire until you see the whites of their eyes
Q334029.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Colonists inflict heavy casualties on British forces while losing the Battle of Bunker Hill.

Q334720.name: Abu Ghraib torture and prisoner abuse
aliases: Abu Ghraib prisoner torture and abuse
Abuse of Iraqi prisoners by coalition forces
Coalition prisoner abuse at Abu Ghraib prison
Q334720.blurb: U.S. media release graphic photos of American soldiers committing war crimes against Iraqi prisoners at Abu Ghraib prison.

Q335259.name: 1999 F-117A shoot-down
Q335259.blurb: Kosovo War: An American Lockheed F-117A Nighthawk is shot down by a Yugoslav Army SAM, the first and only Nighthawk to be lost in combat.

Q335288.name: Battle of Monte Cassino
Q335288.blurb: World War II: The assault on Monte Cassino, Italy, begins.

Q335330.name: Battle of Philippi
Q335330.blurb: Liberators' civil war: Mark Antony and Octavian decisively defeat an army under Brutus in the second part of the Battle of Philippi, with Brutus committing suicide and ending the civil war.

Q337044.name: BSAA Star Dust accident
Q337044.blurb: Star Dust, a British South American Airways airliner, crashed into Mount Tupungato in the Argentine Andes; its wreckage was not found until 1998.

Q339052.name: Battle of Großbeeren
Q339052.blurb: At the Battle of Großbeeren, the Prussians under Von Bülow repulse the French army.

Q339207.name: Geneva Frequency Plan of 1975
Q339207.blurb: The Geneva Frequency Plan of 1975 goes into effect, realigning many of Europe's longwave and mediumwave broadcasting frequencies.

Q339291.name: Wuchang Uprising
Q339291.blurb: An accidental bomb explosion triggers the Wuchang Uprising against the Qing dynasty, beginning the Xinhai Revolution.

Q339321.name: Battle of the Milvian Bridge
Q339321.blurb: Constantine the Great is said to have received his famous Vision of the Cross.

Q339486.name: 1948 Accra Riots
Q339486.blurb: The 1948 Accra riots erupt following a march by ex-servicemen of the Gold Coast Regiment towards the seat of the colonial government at Christiansborg Castle, where they were fired upon by Superintendant Colin Imray, leading to the killing of Sergeant Adjetey, Corporal Attipoe and Private Odartey Lamptey and the arrest of the Big Six in the Gold Coast.

Q339747.name: hippie
Q339747.blurb: The Mantra-Rock Dance (poster pictured), called the "ultimate high" of the hippie era, took place in San Francisco, featuring Swami Bhaktivedanta, Janis Joplin, the Grateful Dead, and Allen Ginsberg.

Q339883.name: 2005 Cronulla riots
Q339883.blurb: Cronulla riots: Thousands of White Australians demonstrate against ethnic violence resulting in a riot against anyone thought to be Lebanese in Cronulla, New South Wales; these are followed up by retaliatory ethnic attacks on Cronulla.

Q339963.name: Surveyor program
Q339963.blurb: Surveyor program: Surveyor 7, the last spacecraft in the Surveyor series, lifts off from Cape Canaveral Launch Complex 36A.

Q346847.name: 1968 Thule Air Base B-52 crash
Q346847.blurb: A B-52 bomber crashes near Thule Air Base, contaminating the area after its nuclear payload ruptures. One of the four bombs remains unaccounted for after the cleanup operation is complete.

Q351722.name: Adams–Onís Treaty
aliases: Treaty of Amity Settlement and Limits
Treaty of Amity, Settlement, and Limits
Treaty of Amity, Settlement, and Limits Between the United States of America and His Catholic Majesty
Treaty of Amity, Settlement, and Limits, 1819
Q351722.blurb: By the Adams–Onís Treaty, Spain sells Florida to the United States for five million U.S. dollars.

Q352182.name: Agreed Framework
Q352182.blurb: North Korea and the United States sign an Agreed Framework that requires North Korea to stop its nuclear weapons program and agree to inspections.

Q364322.name: Battle of Lundy's Lane
Q364322.blurb: War of 1812: An American attack on Canada is repulsed.

Q364915.name: Nishapur train disaster
Q364915.blurb: Up to 295 people, 182 of which being rescue workers, die near Nishapur, Iran, when a runaway freight train carrying sulfur, petrol and fertilizer catches fire and explodes.

Q365640.name: Battle of Beaver Dams
Q365640.blurb: Battle of Beaver Dams: A British and Indian combined force defeats the United States Army.

Q367025.name: Battle of Lena
Q367025.blurb: The Battle of Lena takes place between King Sverker the Younger of Sweden and his rival, Prince Erik Knutsson, whose victory puts him on the throne as King Eric X.

Q367449.name: 1999 İzmit earthquake
Q367449.blurb: The 7.6 Mw İzmit earthquake shakes northwestern Turkey with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent), leaving 17,118–17,127 dead and 43,953–50,000 injured.

Q368689.name: First Serbian Uprising
Q368689.blurb: Karađorđe leads the First Serbian Uprising against the Ottoman Empire.

Q368842.name: Battle of Verona
Q368842.blurb: The Ostrogoths under Theoderic the Great defeat the forces of Odoacer for the second time.

Q369291.name: Anglo-Spanish War
Q369291.blurb: Anglo-Spanish War: In pursuit of retreating Spanish troops, English soldiers sacked the city of Panama.

Q369560.name: Siege of Baghdad
Q369560.blurb: The Siege of Baghdad ends with the surrender of the last Abbasid caliph to Hulegu Khan, a prince of the Mongol Empire.

Q369893.name: Battle of Angamos
Q369893.blurb: War of the Pacific: The Chilean Navy defeats the Peruvian Navy in the Battle of Angamos.

Q370143.name: 2003 Baghdad DHL attempted shootdown incident
Q370143.blurb: Baghdad DHL attempted shootdown incident: Shortly after takeoff, a DHL Express cargo plane is struck on the left wing by a surface-to-air missile and forced to land.

Q370145.name: Qana airstrike
Q370145.blurb: An Israeli airstrike kills 28 Lebanese civilians, including 16 children.

Q370307.name: Battle of Kandahar
Q370307.blurb: The army of Mohammad Ayub Khan is routed by the British at the Battle of Kandahar, ending the Second Anglo-Afghan War.

Q370524.name: DeLorean DMC-12
Q370524.blurb: Production of the DeLorean sports car begins in Dunmurry, Northern Ireland, United Kingdom.

Q370555.name: Gimli Glider
Q370555.blurb: Gimli Glider: Air Canada Flight 143 runs out of fuel and makes a deadstick landing at Gimli, Manitoba.

Q370671.name: Battle of Franklin
Q370671.blurb: American Civil War: The Confederate Army of Tennessee led by General John Bell Hood suffers heavy losses in an attack on the Union Army of the Ohio under General John Schofield in the Battle of Franklin.

Q370706.name: Iranian Embassy Siege
Q370706.blurb: The Iranian Embassy siege begins in London.

Q371247.name: Oslo II Accord
aliases: Interim Agreement on the West Bank and the Gaza Strip
Q371247.blurb: In accordance with the Oslo II Accord, Israeli troops withdrew from Bethlehem in preparation for the transfer of control to the Palestinian National Authority.

Q371394.name: Bangladesh Liberation War
aliases: Breakup of East and West Pakistan
International reactions to the Bangladesh Liberation War
Q371394.blurb: Bangladesh Liberation War: The Pakistan Army massacre more than a thousand people in Keraniganj Upazila, Bangladesh.

Q371573.name: Philippines campaign of 1944–1945
aliases: Philippines campaigns in World War Two
Q371573.blurb: World War II: Fulfilling a promise he made two years previously, General Douglas MacArthur landed on Leyte to begin the recapture of the Philippines.

Q372958.name: Battle of Medenine
Q372958.blurb: World War II: Generalfeldmarschall Erwin Rommel launches the Battle of Medenine in an attempt to slow down the British Eighth Army. It fails, and he leaves Africa three days later.

Q373401.name: Battle of Cape St. Vincent
Q373401.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: Battle of Cape St. Vincent: John Jervis, (later 1st Earl of St Vincent) and Horatio Nelson (later 1st Viscount Nelson) lead the British Royal Navy to victory over a Spanish fleet in action near Gibraltar.

Q374212.name: Shusha pogrom
Q374212.blurb: Azeri and Turkish army soldiers with participation of Kurdish gangs attack the Armenian inhabitants of Shushi (Nagorno Karabakh).

Q374696.name: defenestrations of Prague
Q374696.blurb: The Third Defenestration of Prague precipitates the Thirty Years' War.

Q375409.name: Trans-en-Provence Case
Q375409.blurb: A local farmer reports a UFO sighting in Trans-en-Provence, France, claimed to be "perhaps the most completely and carefully documented sighting of all time".

Q376154.name: Battle of Copenhagen
Q376154.blurb: Napoleonic Wars: The British Royal Navy bombards Copenhagen with fire bombs and phosphorus rockets to prevent Denmark from surrendering its fleet to Napoleon.

Q376921.name: Dagen H
Q376921.blurb: Dagen H in Sweden: Traffic changes from driving on the left to driving on the right overnight.

Q377269.name: Dutch–Portuguese War
Q377269.blurb: Dutch–Portuguese War: The Dutch siege of Malacca against the Portuguese ended when Dutch troops seized the city's citadel (depicted).

Q377542.name: Whiskey Rebellion
Q377542.blurb: U.S. President George Washington invokes the Militia Acts of 1792 to suppress the Whiskey Rebellion in western Pennsylvania.

Q377665.name: 1992 Guadalajara explosions
Q377665.blurb: A series of gas explosions rip through the streets in Guadalajara, Mexico, killing 206.

Q377682.name: Watts riots
Q377682.blurb: Race riots (the Watts Riots) begin in the Watts area of Los Angeles, California.

Q377753.name: St. Brice's Day massacre
Q377753.blurb: King Æthelred II (pictured) ordered the massacre of all Danes in England.

Q378227.name: Battle of Barking Creek
Q378227.blurb: World War II: The British Royal Air Force suffers its first fighter pilot casualty of the Second World War at the Battle of Barking Creek as a result of friendly fire.

Q378293.name: Council of Nablus
Q378293.blurb: Crusades: The Council of Nablus is held, establishing the earliest surviving written laws of the Crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem.

Q379346.name: Battle of Tippecanoe
Q379346.blurb: Tecumseh's War: The Battle of Tippecanoe is fought near present-day Battle Ground, Indiana, United States.

Q379433.name: Operation Ten-Go
aliases: Battle of the East China Sea
Q379433.blurb: World War II: U.S. forces sank the Japanese battleship Yamato during Operation Kikusui I in the East China Sea.

Q381183.name: Aero Flight 311
Q381183.blurb: Aero Flight 311 crashes into the forest in Kvevlax, Finland, killing 25 people.

Q381375.name: First Nagorno-Karabakh War
aliases: Media coverage of the First Nagorno-Karabakh War
War crimes in the First Nagorno-Karabakh War
Q381375.blurb: First Nagorno-Karabakh War: Armenian troops massacre more than 20 Azerbaijani civilians during the Capture of Garadaghly.

Q381461.name: Aeroflot Flight 593
aliases: Russia Aeroflot Airbus A310 air disaster
Q381461.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 593 crashes into the Kuznetsk Alatau mountain, Kemerovo Oblast, Russia, killing 75.

Q381468.name: Aeroflot Flight 821
Q381468.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 821, a Boeing 737-500, crashes into a section of the Trans-Siberian Railway while on approach to Perm International Airport, in Perm, Russia, killing all 88 people on board.

Q381558.name: Aeroméxico Flight 498
Q381558.blurb: Aeroméxico Flight 498 collides with a Piper PA-28 Cherokee over Cerritos, California, killing 67 in the air and 15 on the ground.

Q381615.name: Aeroperú Flight 603
Q381615.blurb: Aeroperú Flight 603 crashes into the ocean near Peru, killing all 70 people on board.

Q381766.name: 2010 Yushu earthquake
Q381766.blurb: Nearly 2,700 people were killed in an earthquake registering 6.9 Mw in Yushu Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, China.

Q382180.name: Affair of the Placards
Q382180.blurb: Following the Affair of the Placards, the French king leads an anti-Protestant procession through Paris.

Q382286.name: Chesapeake–Leopard Affair
Q382286.blurb: In the Chesapeake–Leopard affair, the British warship HMS Leopard attacks and boards the American frigate USS Chesapeake.

Q382861.name: Revolutions of 1989
aliases: Economic reforms after the collapse of socialism
Fall of Communism in Western Europe
Fall of communism in Eastern Europe
The end of communism in Europe
The fall of the Iron Curtain
The fall of the Iron Curtain in 1989
The falling of the Iron Curtain
The falling of the Iron Curtain that took place in 1989
Q382861.blurb: Revolutions of 1989: Imre Nagy, the former Hungarian prime minister, is reburied in Budapest following the collapse of Communism in Hungary.

Q382967.name: Siege of Damascus
Q382967.blurb: The Siege of Damascus ends in a decisive crusader defeat and leads to the disintegration of the Second Crusade.

Q383067.name: Battle of Saragarhi
Q383067.blurb: Tirah campaign: In the Battle of Saragarhi, ten thousand Pashtun tribesmen suffer several hundred casualties while attacking 21 Sikh soldiers in British service.

Q383549.name: 2011 Minsk Metro bombing
Q383549.blurb: An explosion in the Minsk Metro, Belarus, kills 15 people and injures 204 others.

Q383991.name: 2012 Indian Ocean earthquakes
Q383991.blurb: A pair of great earthquakes occur in the Wharton Basin west of Sumatra in Indonesia. The maximum Mercalli intensity of this strike-slip doublet earthquake is VII (Very strong). Ten are killed, twelve are injured, and a non-destructive tsunami is observed on the island of Nias.

Q384052.name: Operation Buster-Jangle
Q384052.blurb: Operation Buster–Jangle: Six thousand five hundred United States Army soldiers are exposed to 'Desert Rock' atomic explosions for training purposes in Nevada. Participation is not voluntary.

Q384291.name: Aberfan disaster
Q384291.blurb: A colliery spoil tip slips onto houses and a school in the village of Aberfan in Wales, killing 144 people, 116 of whom were schoolchildren.

Q384845.name: American Airlines Flight 587
Q384845.blurb: In New York City, American Airlines Flight 587, an Airbus A300 en route to the Dominican Republic, crashes minutes after takeoff from John F. Kennedy International Airport, killing all 260 on board and five on the ground.

Q385065.name: April 2009 Moldovan parliamentary election protests
Q385065.blurb: Mass protests began across Moldova against the results of the parliamentary election.

Q385180.name: Battle of the Yalu River
Q385180.blurb: Battle of the Yalu River, the largest naval engagement of the First Sino-Japanese War.

Q385677.name: Battle of Myeongnyang
Q385677.blurb: Imjin War: Korean Admiral Yi Sun-sin routs the Japanese Navy of 300 ships with only 13 ships at the Battle of Myeongnyang.

Q385820.name: French conquest of Tunisia
Q385820.blurb: Under threat of invasion, Muhammad III as-Sadiq, Bey of Tunis, signed the Treaty of Bardo to make Tunisia a French protectorate.

Q385906.name: Val di Stava dam collapse
Q385906.blurb: The Val di Stava dam collapses, killing 268 people in Val di Stava, Italy.

Q386051.name: Battle of Cuito Cuanavale
Q386051.blurb: Angolan and Cuban forces defeat South Africa in the Battle of Cuito Cuanavale.

Q386074.name: Nedelin catastrophe
Q386074.blurb: Nedelin catastrophe: An R-16 ballistic missile explodes on the launch pad at the Soviet Union's Baikonur Cosmodrome space facility, killing over 100 people, including Field Marshal Mitrofan Nedelin.

Q386634.name: Őszöd speech
aliases: Ferenc Gyurcsány's speech in Balatonőszöd in May 2006
Q386634.blurb: An audio tape of a private speech by Hungarian Prime Minister Ferenc Gyurcsány is leaked to the public, in which he confessed that his Hungarian Socialist Party had lied to win the 2006 election, sparking widespread protests across the country.

Q386799.name: Ajka alumina plant accident
Q386799.blurb: The Ajka plant accident in Hungary releases a million cubic metres of liquid alumina sludge, killing nine, injuring 122, and severely contaminating two major rivers.

Q387093.name: Battle of Arnhem
Q387093.blurb: Second World War: British troops began their withdrawal from the Battle of Arnhem in the Netherlands, ending the Allies' Operation Market Garden in defeat.

Q387892.name: Afriqiyah Airways Flight 771
Q387892.blurb: Afriqiyah Airways Flight 771 crashes on final approach to Tripoli International Airport in Tripoli, Libya, killing 103 out of the 104 people on board.

Q388210.name: Battle of Carabobo
Q388210.blurb: Battle of Carabobo: Decisive battle in the war of independence of Venezuela from Spain.

Q388689.name: Battle of York
Q388689.blurb: War of 1812: American troops capture York, the capital of Upper Canada, in the Battle of York.

Q389024.name: 1936 German parliamentary election and referendum
Q389024.blurb: The 1936 German parliamentary election and referendum seeks approval for the recent remilitarization of the Rhineland.

Q389091.name: Upper Canada Rebellion
Q389091.blurb: Canadian journalist and politician William Lyon Mackenzie calls for a rebellion against the United Kingdom in his essay "To the People of Upper Canada", published in his newspaper The Constitution.

Q389104.name: 1994 FIFA World Cup Final
Q389104.blurb: Brazil won the FIFA World Cup final against Italy 3–2 on penalties, following a 0–0 draw after extra time.

Q389646.name: Baltic Way
Q389646.blurb: Singing Revolution: Approximately two million people joined hands to form a human chain spanning 675.5 kilometres (419.7 mi) across the Estonian, Latvian and Lithuanian Soviet republics to demonstrate their desire for independence.

Q390115.name: Hurricane Mitch
aliases: Effects of Hurricane Mitch in Honduras
Q390115.blurb: Hurricane Mitch, the second deadliest Atlantic hurricane in history, makes landfall in Honduras.

Q390710.name: Ponce massacre
Q390710.blurb: Ponce massacre: Nineteen unarmed civilians in Ponce, Puerto Rico are gunned down by police in a terrorist attack ordered by the US-appointed Governor, Blanton Winship.

Q391358.name: Emancipation Proclamation
Q391358.blurb: Over two years after the Emancipation Proclamation, slaves in Galveston, Texas, United States, are officially informed of their freedom. The anniversary was officially celebrated in Texas and other states as Juneteenth. On June 17, 2021, Juneteenth officially became a federal holiday in the United States.

Q391478.name: Emergen
aliases: unfair bailout of Wall Street banks
Q391478.blurb: The Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008 for the U.S. financial system is signed by President George W. Bush.

Q392121.name: Battle of Fehmarn
Q392121.blurb: A Swedish–Dutch fleet defeats the Danish fleet at Fehmarn and captures about 1,000 prisoners.

Q392179.name: Quebec Conference
Q392179.blurb: World War II: First Québec Conference of Winston Churchill, Franklin D. Roosevelt, and William Lyon Mackenzie King begins.

Q392213.name: Siege of Orléans
Q392213.blurb: Joan of Arc arrives to relieve the Siege of Orléans.

Q392538.name: Battle of Sagrajas
Q392538.blurb: Spanish Reconquista: At the Battle of Sagrajas, the Almoravids defeat the Castilians, but are unable to take advantage of their victory.

Q392541.name: Treaty of San Francisco
Q392541.blurb: The Treaty of San Francisco comes into effect, restoring Japanese sovereignty and ending its state of war with most of the Allies of World War II.

Q392601.name: Shays's Rebellion
Q392601.blurb: Shays' Rebellion: The rebellion's largest confrontation, outside the Springfield Armory, results in the killing of four rebels and the wounding of twenty.

Q392858.name: Rhodesian dollar
Q392858.blurb: The Republic of Zimbabwe (formerly Rhodesia) comes into being, with Canaan Banana as the country's first President. The Zimbabwean dollar replaces the Rhodesian dollar as the official currency.

Q393299.name: Battle of Vimy Ridge
Q393299.blurb: France grants "one square kilometer" at Vimy Ridge "freely, and for all time, to the Government of Canada, the free use of the land exempt from all taxes".

Q394387.name: Treaty of Paris
Q394387.blurb: Kings Louis IX of France and Henry III of England agree to the Treaty of Paris, in which Henry renounces his claims to French-controlled territory on continental Europe (including Normandy) in exchange for Louis withdrawing his support for English rebels.

Q394864.name: Agni Air Flight CHT
Q394864.blurb: Agni Air Flight CHT crashes in Nepal after a failed go-around, killing 15 people.

Q399224.name: Battle of Camarón
Q399224.blurb: A 65-man French Foreign Legion infantry patrol fights a force of nearly 2,000 Mexican soldiers to nearly the last man in Hacienda Camarón, Mexico.

Q399999.name: prohibition in the United States
aliases: alcohol prohibition in the United States
prohibition of alcohol in the United States
Prohibition Era in the United States
Q399999.blurb: Alcohol Prohibition begins in the United States as the Volstead Act goes into effect.

Q400061.name: Mongol conquest of the Song dynasty
Q400061.blurb: Mongol conquest of Song China: Zhao Bing (pictured), the last Song emperor, drowned at the end of the Battle of Yamen, bringing the Song dynasty to an end after three centuries.

Q400500.name: Black Wednesday
Q400500.blurb: Black Wednesday: The British pound is forced out of the European Exchange Rate Mechanism by currency speculators and is forced to devalue against the German mark.

Q402312.name: Battle of Dettingen
Q402312.blurb: In the Battle of Dettingen, George II becomes the last reigning British monarch to participate in a battle.

Q403063.name: 1910 London to Manchester air race
Q403063.blurb: Frenchman Louis Paulhan wins the 1910 London to Manchester air race, the first long-distance aeroplane race in the United Kingdom.

Q403416.name: Battle of Pliska
aliases: Battle of Pliska (Battle of Varbica pass) 813
Battle of Pliska (Battle of Vărbica pass) 813
Q403416.blurb: Battle of Pliska: Byzantine Emperor Nikephoros I is killed and his heir Staurakios is seriously wounded.

Q404517.name: Kargil War
Q404517.blurb: Infiltration of Pakistani soldiers on Indian side results in the Kargil War.

Q405475.name: Constitutional Convention
aliases: Constitutional Convention of the United States
Q405475.blurb: After a delay of 11 days, the United States Constitutional Convention formally convenes in Philadelphia after a quorum of seven states is secured.

Q406486.name: Air France Flight 296
Q406486.blurb: The first crash of an Airbus A320 occurs when Air France Flight 296Q crashes at Mulhouse–Habsheim Airfield in Habsheim, France, during an air show, killing three of the 136 people on board.

Q406503.name: Air France Flight 358
Q406503.blurb: Air France Flight 358 lands at Toronto Pearson International Airport and runs off the runway, causing the plane to burst into flames, leaving 12 injuries and no fatalities.

Q406535.name: Air France Flight 4590
Q406535.blurb: Air France Flight 4590 , a Concorde en route from Paris to New York, crashed in Gonesse, France, killing all 109 passengers on board and four people on the ground.

Q406582.name: Air India Express Flight 812
Q406582.blurb: Air India Express Flight 812, a Boeing 737 crashes over a cliff upon landing at Mangalore, India, killing 158 of 166 people on board, becoming the deadliest crash involving a Boeing 737 until the crash of Lion Air Flight 610.

Q406588.name: Air India Flight 182
aliases: Commission of Inquiry into the Investigation of the Bombing of Air India Flight 182
