Q406588.blurb: A terrorist bomb explodes at Narita International Airport near Tokyo, killing two and injuring four. An hour later, the same group detonates a second bomb aboard Air India Flight 182, bringing the Boeing 747 down off the coast of Ireland killing all 329 aboard.

Q406599.name: Air New Zealand Flight 901
Q406599.blurb: Air New Zealand Flight 901, a DC-10 sightseeing flight over Antarctica, crashes into Mount Erebus, killing all 257 people on board.

Q406609.name: Air Transat Flight 236
Q406609.blurb: Air Transat Flight 236 loses all engine power over the Atlantic Ocean, forcing the pilots to conduct an emergency landing in the Azores.

Q408058.name: Airblue Flight 202
Q408058.blurb: Airblue Flight 202 crashes into the Margalla Hills north of Islamabad, Pakistan, killing all 152 people aboard. It is the deadliest aviation accident in Pakistan history and the first involving an Airbus A321.

Q408192.name: United States Numbered Highway System
Q408192.blurb: The United States Numbered Highway System is established.

Q415434.name: Acacian schism
Q415434.blurb: Pope Felix III excommunicated patriarch Acacius of Constantinople for his support of the Henoticon and his support of the removal of patriarch John Talaia, leading to the Acacian schism.

Q417820.name: protests against SOPA and PIPA
Q417820.blurb: More than 115,000 websites engage in an online protest against the Stop Online Piracy Act and the Protect IP Act in the US.[citation needed] The websites involved viewed the laws as infringing on the right to free speech and many of them temporarily shut down in protest.

Q418151.name: Second Opium War
Q418151.blurb: Second Opium War: France and the United Kingdom declare war on China.

Q422082.name: Philippine Revolution
Q422082.blurb: Philippine Revolution: After Spanish victory in the Battle of San Juan del Monte, eight provinces in the Philippines are declared under martial law by the Spanish Governor-General Ramón Blanco y Erenas.

Q424764.name: Italian Hall disaster
Q424764.blurb: The Italian Hall disaster in Calumet, Michigan results in the deaths of 73 striking workers families at a Christmas party participants (including 59 children) when someone falsely yells "fire".

Q425617.name: Battle of Verneuil
Q425617.blurb: Hundred Years' War: Battle of Verneuil: An English force under John, Duke of Bedford defeats a larger French army under Jean II, Duke of Alençon, John Stewart, and Earl Archibald of Douglas.

Q425773.name: Battle of Guilford Court House
Q425773.blurb: The British under Charles Cornwallis defeat American forces under Nathanael Greene in the battle of Guilford Court House.

Q426026.name: Battle of Laon
Q426026.blurb: Emperor Napoleon I is defeated at the Battle of Laon in France.

Q426099.name: Siege of Antwerp
Q426099.blurb: World War I: The Siege of Antwerp comes to an end.

Q426227.name: Third Battle of Ypres
Q426227.blurb: World War I: The Battle of Passchendaele begins near Ypres in West Flanders, Belgium.

Q426722.name: Rwandan Civil War
Q426722.blurb: Rwandan Civil War: The Rwandan genocide began a few hours after the assassination of President Juvénal Habyarimana, with hundreds of thousands killed in the following 100 days.

Q426759.name: League of Nations mandate
aliases: League of Nations Class B Mandate
Mandate of the League of Nations
Q426759.blurb: At the San Remo conference, the principal Allied Powers of World War I adopt a resolution to determine the allocation of Class "A" League of Nations mandates for administration of the former Ottoman-ruled lands of the Middle East.

Q426926.name: Battle of Warsaw
Q426926.blurb: The Battle of Warsaw ends with a Swedish-Brandenburger victory over a larger Polish-Lithuanian force.

Q427958.name: Battle of Sinop
Q427958.blurb: Crimean War: Battle of Sinop: The Imperial Russian Navy under Pavel Nakhimov destroys the Ottoman fleet under Osman Pasha at Sinop, a sea port in northern Turkey.

Q427994.name: 1972 Australian federal election
Q427994.blurb: Gough Whitlam is elected the 21st Prime Minister of Australia in the 1972 Australian federal election, defeating William McMahon and leading the Australian Labor Party back into office after 23 years in Opposition.

Q428208.name: Yenice–Gönen earthquake of 1953
aliases: Terremoto de Yenice y Gönen de 1953
Q428208.blurb: An earthquake hits western Turkey, killing at least 1,070 people.

Q428362.name: Super Outbreak
Q428362.blurb: The 1974 Super Outbreak occurs, the second largest tornado outbreak in recorded history (after the 2011 Super Outbreak). The death toll is 315, with nearly 5,500 injured.

Q428369.name: Battle of Nagashino
Q428369.blurb: Sengoku period of Japan: The combined forces of Oda Nobunaga and Tokugawa Ieyasu are victorious in the Battle of Nagashino.

Q428518.name: 1872 FA Cup Final
Q428518.blurb: In the inaugural final of the FA Cup Wanderers defeated Royal Engineers 1–0 in London.

Q428598.name: 2005 United Kingdom general election
aliases: 2005 UK general election result in Cornwall
2005 United Kingdom general election result in Cornwall
2005 United Kingdom general election results in London
Q428598.blurb: Keir Starmer is appointed Prime Minister by Charles III, becoming the first Labour prime minister since Gordon Brown in 2010 and the first one to win a general election since Tony Blair at the 2005 general election.

Q428972.name: Battle of Wittstock
Q428972.blurb: Thirty Years' War: The Swedish Army defeats the armies of Saxony and the Holy Roman Empire at the Battle of Wittstock.

Q429230.name: Conquest of 1759-1760
Q429230.blurb: French and Indian War: French surrender Montreal to the British, completing the latter's conquest of New France.

Q429655.name: Battle of Cedar Mountain
Q429655.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Cedar Mountain: At Cedar Mountain, Virginia, Confederate General Stonewall Jackson narrowly defeats Union forces under General John Pope.

Q430135.name: Trial of Louis XVI
Q430135.blurb: French Revolution: King Louis XVI of France is put on trial for treason by the National Convention.

Q430700.name: Khatyn massacre
Q430700.blurb: World War II: The entire village of Khatyn (in present-day Republic of Belarus) is burnt alive by Schutzmannschaft Battalion 118.

Q430726.name: Anglo-Spanish War
Q430726.blurb: Anglo-Spanish War: The English navy defeated a Spanish–Portuguese fleet off Sesimbra, Portugal, and captured a carrack.

Q430803.name: 1982–83 UEFA Cup
Q430803.blurb: During a UEFA Cup match between Spartak Moscow and Haarlem, a large number of attendees trying to leave the Central Lenin Stadium resulted in a stampede that caused 66 deaths.

Q431177.name: Mongol invasion of Khwarazmian Empire and Eastern Iran
aliases: Mongol conquest of the Khwarazmian Empire
Mongol invasion of Khwarezmia and Eastern Iran
Mongol invasion of the Khwarezmian Empire
Q431177.blurb: Mongol invasion of the Khwarazmian Empire: the city of Bukhara was captured and looted by the Mongol army of Genghis Khan.

Q431538.name: Transatlantic flight of Alcock and Brown
Q431538.blurb: John Alcock and Arthur Whitten Brown depart from St. John's, Newfoundland on the first nonstop transatlantic flight.

Q431657.name: 1996 Taiwanese presidential election
Q431657.blurb: Taiwan holds its first direct elections and chooses Lee Teng-hui as President.

Q431806.name: Arauco War
Q431806.blurb: Arauco War: The first Parliament of Quillín is celebrated, putting a temporary hold on hostilities between Mapuches and Spanish in Chile.

Q431888.name: killing of Muammar Gaddafi
Q431888.blurb: Libyan Crisis: Rebel forces capture Libyan dictator Muammar Gaddafi and his son Mutassim in his hometown of Sirte and kill them shortly thereafter, ending the first Libyan civil war.

Q431972.name: AFL–NFL merger
Q431972.blurb: U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson signs into law an antitrust exemption allowing the National Football League to merge with the upstart American Football League.

Q432515.name: First Battle of Algeciras
Q432515.blurb: First Battle of Algeciras: Outnumbered French Navy ships defeat the Royal Navy in the fortified Spanish port of Algeciras.

Q434319.name: Altamont Free Concert
Q434319.blurb: Altamont Free Concert: At a free concert performed by the Rolling Stones, eighteen-year old Meredith Hunter is stabbed to death by Hells Angels security guards.

Q435223.name: Birgenair Flight 301
Q435223.blurb: Birgenair Flight 301 crashed off the coast of the Dominican Republic, killing all 189 people on board. This is the deadliest aviation accident involving a Boeing 757.

Q435572.name: British Airways Flight 5390
Q435572.blurb: British Airways Flight 5390 lands safely at Southampton Airport after a blowout in the cockpit causes the captain to be partially sucked from the cockpit. There are no fatalities.

Q435605.name: British Airways Flight 009
aliases: We have a small problem. All four engines have stopped.
Q435605.blurb: "The Jakarta Incident": British Airways Flight 009 flies into a cloud of volcanic ash thrown up by the eruption of Mount Galunggung, resulting in the failure of all four engines.

Q435806.name: China Airlines Flight 611
aliases: China Airlines Boeing 747-200 in the Straits of Taiwan
Q435806.blurb: China Airlines Flight 611 disintegrates in mid-air and crashes into the Taiwan Strait, with the loss of all 225 people on board.

Q438252.name: Old Zürich War
Q438252.blurb: Battle of St. Jakob an der Sihl in the Old Zürich War.

Q444003.name: Altona Bloody Sunday
Q444003.blurb: Altona Bloody Sunday: A riot between the Nazi Party paramilitary forces, the SS and SA, and the German Communist Party ensues.

Q444159.name: Saturday Night Massacre
Q444159.blurb: Watergate scandal: "Saturday Night Massacre": United States President Richard Nixon fires U.S. Attorney General Elliot Richardson and Deputy Attorney General William Ruckelshaus after they refuse to fire special prosecutor Archibald Cox, who is finally fired by Solicitor General Robert Bork.

Q444530.name: Clayton–Bulwer Treaty
Q444530.blurb: Britain and the United States sign the Hay–Pauncefote Treaty, which nullifies the Clayton–Bulwer Treaty and withdraws British objections to an American-controlled canal in Panama.

Q444590.name: Battle of Faesulae
Q444590.blurb: The Western Roman army under Stilicho corners and defeats the Ostrogothic army in the battle of Faesulae.

Q444698.name: Operation Paperclip
Q444698.blurb: The United States Secretary of State approves the transfer of Wernher von Braun and his team of Nazi rocket scientists to the U.S. under Operation Paperclip.

Q449076.name: Treaty of Le Goulet
Q449076.blurb: King John of England and King Philip II of France sign the Treaty of Le Goulet.

Q449550.name: Alvor Agreement
Q449550.blurb: The Alvor Agreement is signed, ending the Angolan War of Independence and giving Angola independence from Portugal.

Q449661.name: Hun speech
Q449661.blurb: Kaiser Wilhelm II makes a speech comparing Germans to Huns; for years afterwards, "Hun" would be a disparaging name for Germans.

Q451046.name: Preußenschlag
Q451046.blurb: In the Preußenschlag, German President Hindenburg places Prussia directly under the rule of the national government.

Q451404.name: Battle of St. Jakob an der Sihl
Q451404.blurb: Battle of St. Jakob an der Sihl in the Old Zürich War.

Q451853.name: Battle of St. Jakob an der Birs
Q451853.blurb: Battle of St. Jakob an der Birs: A vastly outnumbered force of Swiss Confederates is defeated by the Dauphin Louis (future Louis XI of France) and his army of 'Armagnacs' near Basel.

Q452286.name: Interstate 80 in Iowa
Q452286.blurb: The first section of Interstate 80 in Iowa opened in the Des Moines metropolitan area.

Q453870.name: Battle on the Raxa
Q453870.blurb: King Otto I defeats a Slavic revolt in what is now Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.

Q455408.name: 1812 New Madrid earthquake
Q455408.blurb: The strongest in a series of earthquakes strikes New Madrid, Missouri.

Q456343.name: Mykonos restaurant assassinations
Q456343.blurb: An Iranian Kurdish leader and his two joiners are assassinated by political militants in Berlin.

Q456993.name: Siege of Jerusalem
Q456993.blurb: First Crusade: The Siege of Jerusalem begins.

Q457509.name: Tumult of Thorn
Q457509.blurb: Tumult of Thorn: Religious unrest is followed by the execution of nine Protestant citizens and the mayor of Thorn (Toruń) by Polish authorities.

Q458321.name: Korean Air Lines Flight 902
Q458321.blurb: Korean Air Lines Flight 902 was shot down after violating Soviet airspace and was forced to make an emergency landing.

Q458646.name: 76th Academy Awards
Q458646.blurb: Angelina Jolie wears a White Marc Bouwer dress to the 76th Academy Awards, which has since been placed on numerous lists for best Oscars fashion.

Q459282.name: United States invasion of Panama
aliases: Casualties of the United States invasion of Panama
Q459282.blurb: United States invasion of Panama: Manuel Noriega, former leader of Panama, surrenders to American forces.

Q459447.name: Siege of Yorktown
Q459447.blurb: American Revolution: French and American forces backed by a French fleet begin the siege of Yorktown.

Q460143.name: Lawrence Massacre
Q460143.blurb: Lawrence, Kansas is destroyed by pro-Confederate guerrillas known as Quantrill's Raiders.

Q460280.name: Hamburg Uprising
Q460280.blurb: German October: Due to a miscommunication with the party leadership, a militant section of the Communist Party of Germany launches an insurrection in Hamburg.

Q460476.name: One-Two-GO Airlines Flight 269
Q460476.blurb: One-Two-Go Airlines Flight 269 carrying 130 crew and passengers crashes in Thailand, killing 90 people.

Q460731.name: sinking of the Rainbow Warrior
Q460731.blurb: The Greenpeace vessel Rainbow Warrior is bombed and sunk in Auckland harbour by French DGSE agents, killing Fernando Pereira.

Q460844.name: Unified Task Force
Q460844.blurb: U.S. president George H. W. Bush ordered American troops into Somalia to help provide humanitarian aid and restore order during the ongoing Somali Civil War.

Q460887.name: murder of James Bulger
aliases: R v Secretary of State for the Home Dept ex parte Venables and Thompson
Q460887.blurb: Two-year-old James Bulger is abducted from New Strand Shopping Centre by two ten-year-old boys, who later torture and murder him.

Q461599.name: Battle of Leuctra
Q461599.blurb: The Battle of Leuctra shatters Sparta's reputation of military invincibility.

Q461891.name: Svalbard Treaty
Q461891.blurb: Under the terms of the Svalbard Treaty, international diplomacy recognizes Norwegian sovereignty over Arctic archipelago Svalbard, and designates it as demilitarized.

Q461911.name: Swissair Flight 111
Q461911.blurb: Swissair Flight 111 crashes near Peggy's Cove, Nova Scotia; all 229 people on board are killed.

Q462195.name: 1976 Tangshan earthquake
Q462195.blurb: The Tangshan earthquake measuring between 7.8 and 8.2 moment magnitude flattens Tangshan in the People's Republic of China, killing 242,769 and injuring 164,851.

Q462716.name: Turkish Airlines Flight 981
Q462716.blurb: Turkish Airlines Flight 981 crashes at Ermenonville near Paris, France killing all 346 aboard.

Q462847.name: United Airlines Flight 585
Q462847.blurb: United Airlines Flight 585 crashes on its final approach to Colorado Springs killing everyone on board.

Q462876.name: United Airlines Flight 811
Q462876.blurb: United Airlines Flight 811, bound for New Zealand from Honolulu, rips open during flight, blowing nine passengers out of the business-class section.

Q462964.name: November Uprising
Q462964.blurb: November uprising: The Battle of Warsaw effectively ends the Polish insurrection.

Q463197.name: American Airlines Flight 191
Q463197.blurb: American Airlines Flight 191: A McDonnell Douglas DC-10 crashes during takeoff at O'Hare International Airport, Chicago, killing all 271 on board and two people on the ground.

Q463206.name: 2001 failed shoe bomb attempt
Q463206.blurb: Richard Reid attempts to destroy a passenger airliner by igniting explosives hidden in his shoes aboard American Airlines Flight 63.

Q463447.name: American Bandstand
Q463447.blurb: American Bandstand, a show dedicated to the teenage "baby-boomers" by playing the songs and showing popular dances of the time, debuts on the ABC television network.

Q463999.name: The Cosby Show
aliases: The opening credits of The Cosby Show
Q463999.blurb: The Cosby Show, which became one of three U.S. television shows to have the highest ratings five years in a row, premiered with its pilot episode.

Q464048.name: Oktoberfest terror attack
Q464048.blurb: A terrorist bombing at the Oktoberfest in Munich, Germany, kills 13 people and injures 213 others.

Q464075.name: 2004 United States presidential election
aliases: Results of the U.S. presidential election, 2004
United States presidential election swing states, 2004
Q464075.blurb: The Arabic-language news network Al Jazeera broadcasts an excerpt from a 2004 Osama bin Laden video in which the terrorist leader first admits direct responsibility for the September 11, 2001 attacks and references the 2004 U.S. presidential election.

Q464226.name: Battle of Lagos
Q464226.blurb: Begin of the battle of Lagos, in which a British fleet defeats a French fleet trying to slip through Gibraltar.

Q464399.name: Entente Cordiale
Q464399.blurb: France and the United Kingdom signed the Entente Cordiale, agreeing to a peaceful coexistence after centuries of intermittent conflict.

Q464512.name: Battle of Balaclava
Q464512.blurb: The Battle of Balaclava takes place during the Crimean War. It is soon memorialized in verse as The Charge of the Light Brigade.

Q464555.name: Peronism
Q464555.blurb: Colonel Juan Perón, founder of the political movement that became known as Peronism, is elected to his first term as President of Argentina.

Q465627.name: Sack of Rome, 1527
Q465627.blurb: Spanish and German troops sack Rome; many scholars consider this the end of the Renaissance.

Q466876.name: Ranger program
Q466876.blurb: Project Ranger: The Ranger 8 probe launches on its mission to photograph the Mare Tranquillitatis region of the Moon in preparation for the crewed Apollo missions. Mare Tranquillitatis or the "Sea of Tranquility" would become the site chosen for the Apollo 11 lunar landing.

Q467200.name: Bombing of Pforzheim in World War II
Q467200.blurb: World War II: The German town of Pforzheim is annihilated in a raid by 379 British bombers.

Q467565.name: America's Most Wanted
Q467565.blurb: Murder of Adam Walsh: The head of John Walsh's son is found. This inspires the creation of the television series America's Most Wanted and the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children.

Q467777.name: Battle of Wagram
Q467777.blurb: The Battle of Wagram between the French and Austrian Empires begins.

Q468293.name: First Barbary War
Q468293.blurb: First Barbary War: Stephen Decatur leads a raid to burn the pirate-held frigate USS Philadelphia.

Q468754.name: Lufthansa Flight 2904
Q468754.blurb: Lufthansa Flight 2904, an Airbus A320, crashes into an embankment after overshooting the runway at Okęcie International Airport (now Warsaw Chopin Airport), killing two people.

Q468823.name: March on Rome
Q468823.blurb: Italian fascists led by Benito Mussolini march on Rome and take over the Italian government.

Q469733.name: Night of the Murdered Poets
Q469733.blurb: The Night of the Murdered Poets: Thirteen prominent Jewish intellectuals are murdered in Moscow, Russia, Soviet Union.

Q470596.name: Year of the Four Emperors
aliases: The Year of the Four Emperors
Q470596.blurb: The Roman Senate declares Vespasian emperor of Rome, the last in the Year of the Four Emperors.

Q471156.name: Bombing of Cologne in World War II
Q471156.blurb: World War II: One thousand British bombers launch a 90-minute attack on Cologne, Germany.

Q471625.name: Bombing of Lübeck in World War II
Q471625.blurb: The Bombing of Lübeck in World War II is the first major success for the RAF Bomber Command against Germany and a German city.

Q471700.name: 2006 Slovak Air Force Antonov An-24 crash
Q471700.blurb: A Slovak Air Force Antonov An-24 crashes near Hejce, Hungary, killing 42.

Q471815.name: Koniuchy massacre
Q471815.blurb: World War II: Approximately 38 people are killed and about a dozen injured when the Polish village of Koniuchy (present-day Kaniūkai, Lithuania) is attacked by Soviet partisan units.

Q472100.name: Bombing of Belgrade in 1941
aliases: bombing of Belgrade in World War II
Q472100.blurb: World War II: The Luftwaffe began Operation Retribution, bombing the Yugoslav capital of Belgrade in retaliation for a coup d'état that overthrew the government that had signed the Tripartite Pact.

Q472278.name: Togo national football team attack
Q472278.blurb: Gunmen from an offshoot of the Front for the Liberation of the Enclave of Cabinda attack a bus carrying the Togo national football team on its way to the 2010 Africa Cup of Nations, killing three people and injuring another nine.

Q472672.name: Battle of Iquique
Q472672.blurb: War of the Pacific: Two Chilean ships blocking the harbor of Iquique (then belonging to Peru) battle two Peruvian vessels in the Battle of Iquique.

Q472699.name: Nullification Crisis
Q472699.blurb: Nullification crisis: American vice president John C. Calhoun's South Carolina Exposition and Protest, written to protest the Tariff of Abominations, was presented to the South Carolina House of Representatives.

Q473206.name: The Monster Ball Tour
Q473206.blurb: Lady Gaga performed the first concert of The Monster Ball Tour, which became the highest-grossing tour in history for a debut headlining artist.

Q473215.name: 2006 state of emergency in the Philippines
Q473215.blurb: Philippine President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo declares Proclamation 1017 placing the country in a state of emergency in an attempt to subdue a possible military coup.

Q473566.name: solar eclipse of April 8, 2005
Q473566.blurb: A solar eclipse occurs, visible over areas of the Pacific Ocean and Latin American countries such as Costa Rica, Panama, Colombia and Venezuela.

Q473661.name: Treaty of Peace and love
Q473661.blurb: Chile and Bolivia sign the Treaty of Peace and Friendship, delimiting the border between the two countries.

Q473670.name: January Uprising
Q473670.blurb: The January Uprising breaks out in Poland, Lithuania and Belarus. The aim of the national movement is to regain Polish–Lithuanian–Ruthenian Commonwealth from occupation by Russia.

Q473716.name: Hungarian Revolution of 1848
aliases: Hungarian War of Independence of 1848 and 1849
Q473716.blurb: A revolution breaks out in Hungary, and the Habsburg rulers are compelled to meet the demands of the reform party.

Q473834.name: École Polytechnique massacre
Q473834.blurb: The École Polytechnique massacre (or Montreal Massacre): Marc Lépine, an anti-feminist gunman, murders 14 young women at the École Polytechnique in Montreal.

Q473845.name: Columbine High School massacre
aliases: Conspiracy theories about the Columbine High School massacre
List of victims of the Columbine High School massacre
Victims of the Columbine High School massacre
Q473845.blurb: Columbine High School massacre: Eric Harris and Dylan Klebold kill 14 people and injure 23 others before committing suicide at Columbine High School in Columbine, Colorado.

Q473862.name: 2009 Fort Hood shooting
Q473862.blurb: U.S. Army major Nidal Hasan went on a shooting rampage at Fort Hood, Texas, the worst shooting ever to take place on an American military base, killing 13.

Q473866.name: Alphen aan den Rijn shopping mall shooting
aliases: Alphen aan den Rijn shopping mall massacre
Q473866.blurb: Six people and the perpetrator are killed and 17 injured in a mass shooting at a shopping mall in Alphen aan den Rijn, Netherlands.

Q473868.name: Aramoana massacre
Q473868.blurb: In Aramoana, New Zealand, David Gray shoots dead 13 people in a massacre before being tracked down and killed by police the next day.

Q473877.name: Erfurt massacre
Q473877.blurb: Robert Steinhäuser kills 16 at Gutenberg-Gymnasium in Erfurt, Germany, before committing suicide.

Q473880.name: Hungerford massacre
Q473880.blurb: Hungerford massacre: In the United Kingdom, Michael Ryan kills sixteen people with a semi-automatic rifle and then commits suicide.

Q473889.name: tung tung balerina shooting
Q473889.blurb: Matti Saari kills ten people at a school in Finland before committing suicide.

Q473893.name: 2011 Liège attack
Q473893.blurb: A man threw grenades and fired a rifle at crowds in Liège, Belgium, causing 6 deaths and injuring more than 120 others, before killing himself.

Q473894.name: Nanterre massacre
Q473894.blurb: Nanterre massacre: In Nanterre, France, a gunman opens fire at the end of a town council meeting, resulting in the deaths of eight councilors; 19 other people are injured.

Q473896.name: San Ysidro McDonald's massacre
Q473896.blurb: McDonald's massacre in San Ysidro, California: James Oliver Huberty kills 21 people and injures 19 others before being shot dead by police.

Q473897.name: Rio de Janeiro school shooting
Q473897.blurb: A gunman opens fire at an elementary school in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, killing twelve children and injuring 22 others before committing suicide.

Q474757.name: Thermidorian Reaction
Q474757.blurb: French Revolution: Maximilien Robespierre is arrested after encouraging the execution of more than 17,000 "enemies of the Revolution".

Q474760.name: Super Bowl XXII
Q474760.blurb: Doug Williams becomes the first African American quarterback to play in a Super Bowl and leads the Washington Redskins to victory in Super Bowl XXII.

Q474843.name: Treaty of Vienna
Q474843.blurb: In accordance with the Treaty of Vienna, Austria cedes Veneto and Mantua to France, which immediately awards them to Italy in exchange for the earlier Italian acquiescence to the French annexation of Savoy and Nice.

Q475353.name: al-Shifa pharmaceutical factory
Q475353.blurb: The Al-Shifa pharmaceutical factory (pictured) in Sudan was destroyed by a missile attack launched by the United States in retaliation for the August 7 U.S. embassy bombings.

Q475678.name: Mexican drug war
aliases: Controversies surrounding the Mexican drug war
Guerra contra el narcotráfico en México
Human rights violations during the Mexican drug war
Mexican Drug War spillover in the United States
Q475678.blurb: Mexican drug war: Forty-four inmates died in a prison riot in Apodaca, Mexico, between members of Los Zetas and the Gulf Cartel.

Q475685.name: Częstochowa Ghetto
Q475685.blurb: The Holocaust and World War II: Jews in the Częstochowa Ghetto in Poland stage an uprising against the Nazis.

Q475780.name: Siege of Osaka
Q475780.blurb: Siege of Osaka: Forces under Tokugawa Ieyasu take Osaka Castle in Japan.

Q476345.name: Strasbourg massacre
Q476345.blurb: Strasbourg massacre: Several thousand Jews are burned to death by mobs while the remaining Jews are forcibly removed from Strasbourg after being accused of causing the Black Death.

Q476389.name: See It Now
Q476389.blurb: McCarthyism: CBS television broadcasts the See It Now episode, "A Report on Senator Joseph McCarthy", produced by Fred Friendly.

Q476634.name: Nanchang Uprising
Q476634.blurb: The Nanchang Uprising marks the first significant battle in the Chinese Civil War between the Kuomintang and Chinese Communist Party. This day is commemorated as the anniversary of the founding of the People's Liberation Army.

Q476638.name: 2010 Wimbledon Championships
Q476638.blurb: John Isner defeated Nicolas Mahut at the Wimbledon Championships, concluding the longest match in tennis history, which lasted 11 hours and 5 minutes over three days.

Q476855.name: Mau Mau rebellion
Q476855.blurb: The Mau Mau Uprising in Kenya is defeated.

Q477108.blurb: The Constitution of India comes into force, forming a republic. Rajendra Prasad is sworn in as the first President of India. Observed as Republic Day in India.

Q477324.name: suppression of the Society of Jesus
Q477324.blurb: Jesuits all over Chile are arrested as the Spanish Empire suppresses the Society of Jesus.

Q477392.name: Plebiscites in the regions of East- and Westprussia
Q477392.blurb: In the East Prussian plebiscite the local populace decides to remain with Weimar Germany.

Q477444.name: 1857 Fort Tejon earthquake
Q477444.blurb: The 7.9 Mw Fort Tejon earthquake shakes Central and Southern California with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent).

Q477519.name: 1886 Charleston earthquake
Q477519.blurb: The 7.0 Mw Charleston earthquake strikes southeastern South Carolina with a maximum Mercalli intensity of X (Extreme), killing 60 people and causing damage worth an estimated at $5 to $6 million.

Q477956.name: Gazimestan speech
Q477956.blurb: President Slobodan Milošević gave a speech at Gazimestan in which he described the possibility of "armed battles" in the future of Serbia's national development.

Q477958.name: February 26 Incident
aliases: List of active participants in 2-26 incident
List of active participants in the February 26 incident
Q477958.blurb: In the February 26 Incident, young nationalist Japanese military officers assassinate multiple cabinet statesmen and start a rebellion in downtown Tokyo, which is ended 3 days later.

Q477973.name: Gothic War of 535–554
Q477973.blurb: Gothic War: The Byzantine general Belisarius enters Rome unopposed; the Gothic garrison flees the capital.

Q478172.name: Singapore Airlines Flight 006
Q478172.blurb: Singapore Airlines Flight 006 crashes on takeoff from Taipei, killing 83.

Q478301.name: Hussite Wars
Q478301.blurb: Hussite Wars: Battle of Lipany: End of the war, the Utraquist defeat and annihilate Taborite forces.

Q479697.name: International Electro-Technical Exhibition – 1891
Q479697.blurb: The International Electrotechnical Exhibition opens in Frankfurt, Germany, featuring the world's first long-distance transmission of high-power, three-phase electric current (the most common form today).

Q479979.name: Battle of Abensberg
Q479979.blurb: Two Austrian army corps in Bavaria are defeated by a First French Empire army led by Napoleon at the Battle of Abensberg on the second day of a four-day campaign that ended in a French victory.

Q481367.name: Venezuela crisis of 1902–1903
Q481367.blurb: A blockade against Venezuela (depicted), caused by President Cipriano Castro's refusal to pay foreign debts, was lifted.

Q481578.name: Tallinn Offensive
Q481578.blurb: World War II: Soviet troops launch the Tallinn Offensive against Germany and pro-independence Estonian units.

Q482402.name: Gulf of Tonkin incident
Q482402.blurb: Second Gulf of Tonkin Incident: U.S. destroyers USS Maddox and USS Turner Joy mistakenly report coming under attack in the Gulf of Tonkin.

Q482407.name: Geneva Conference
Q482407.blurb: The Geneva Conference, an effort to restore peace in Indochina and Korea, begins.

Q482456.name: Fall of Saigon
aliases: Vietnamese atrocities after the fall of Saigon
Q482456.blurb: Fall of Saigon: Communist forces gain control of Saigon. The Vietnam War formally ends with the unconditional surrender of South Vietnamese president Dương Văn Minh.

Q482525.name: March First Movement
Q482525.blurb: March 1st Movement begins in Korea under Japanese rule.

Q482635.name: Kent State shootings
aliases: Kent State shootings in popular culture
Q482635.blurb: Vietnam War: Kent State shootings: The Ohio National Guard, sent to Kent State University after disturbances in the city of Kent the weekend before, opens fire killing four unarmed students and wounding nine others. The students were protesting the Cambodian Campaign of the United States and South Vietnam.

Q482859.name: assassination of Park Chung-hee
Q482859.blurb: Park Chung Hee, President of South Korea, is assassinated by Korean CIA head Kim Jae-gyu.

Q482979.name: Battle of Pusan Perimeter
Q482979.blurb: Korean War: U.S. Eighth Army and United Nations forces break out of the Pusan Perimeter in southeast Korea.

Q483039.name: Battle of Inchon
Q483039.blurb: Korean War: The U.S. X Corps lands at Inchon.

Q483088.name: Battle of Chilcheollyang
Q483088.blurb: Jeongyu War: Battle of Chilcheollyang: A Japanese fleet of 500 ships destroys Joseon commander Wŏn Kyun's fleet of 200 ships at Chilcheollyang.

Q483458.name: Jeju Uprising
Q483458.blurb: In Jeju Province, South Korea, a civil-war-like period of violence and human rights abuses known as the Jeju uprising begins.

Q483464.name: Battle of Chipyong-ni
Q483464.blurb: Korean War: Battle of Chipyong-ni, which represented the "high-water mark" of the Chinese incursion into South Korea, commences.

Q483725.name: Azerbaijani manat
Q483725.blurb: President Ilham Aliyev issued a decree on the redenomination of Azerbaijan's currency, with 1 new manat equal to 5000 old manats.

Q483875.name: 2008 Namdaemun fire
Q483875.blurb: The Namdaemun gate in Seoul, the first of South Korea's National Treasures, was severely damaged by arson (damage pictured).

Q483933.name: 2009 North Korean nuclear test
Q483933.blurb: North Korea conducted a nuclear test and several other missile tests that were widely condemned internationally and led to sanctions from the United Nations Security Council.

Q484271.name: Battle of Noryang
Q484271.blurb: Seven-Year War: Battle of Noryang: The final battle of the Seven-Year War is fought between the China and the Korean allied forces and Japanese navies, resulting in a decisive allied forces victory.

Q484437.name: Autumn Uprising of 1946
Q484437.blurb: The Daegu October incident occurs in Allied-occupied Korea.

Q484494.name: Battle of Osan
Q484494.blurb: Korean War: Task Force Smith: American and North Korean forces first clash, in the Battle of Osan.

Q485120.name: Korean Air Flight 801
Q485120.blurb: Korean Air Flight 801 crashed at Nimitz Hill, Guam, killing 229 of the 254 people on board.

Q485240.name: Billboard
aliases: Billboard - The International Newsweekly of Music, Video & Home Entertainment
Billboard - The International Newsweekly of Music, Video and Home Entertainment
Q485240.blurb: Billboard published its first music hit parade.

Q485343.name: Treaty on Basic Relations between Japan and the Republic of Korea
Q485343.blurb: The Treaty on Basic Relations between Japan and the Republic of Korea is signed.

Q485384.name: Sampoong Department Store collapse
Q485384.blurb: The Sampoong Department Store collapses in the Seocho District of Seoul, South Korea, killing 502 and injuring 937.

Q485415.name: United States expedition to Korea
Q485415.blurb: Sinmiyangyo: Captain McLane Tilton leads 109 US Marines in a naval attack on Han River forts on Kanghwa Island, Korea.

Q485728.name: Coup d'état of May Seventeenth
Q485728.blurb: General Chun Doo-hwan of South Korea seizes control of the government and declares martial law in order to suppress student demonstrations.

Q486045.name: Asiana Airlines Flight 991
Q486045.blurb: While flying from Seoul, South Korea to Shanghai, China, Asiana Airlines Flight 991 develops an in-flight fire in the cargo hold. The Boeing 747-400F freighter attempts to divert to Jeju International Airport, but crashes into the sea South-West of Jeju island, killing both crew members on board.

Q486124.name: Battle of Badr
Q486124.blurb: The Battle of Badr, the first major battle between the Muslims and Quraysh.

Q486226.name: Phong Nhi and Phong Nhat massacre
Q486226.blurb: Vietnam War:  The Phong Nhị and Phong Nhất massacre occurs, allegedly by South Korean troops.

Q486531.name: Battle of Unsan
Q486531.blurb: The People's Volunteer Army ambushed the South Korean II Corps at the Battle of Onjong, and elsewhere engaged the 1st Infantry Division at the Battle of Unsan, marking China's entry into the Korean War.

Q486814.name: wedding of Prince William and Catherine Middleton
aliases: Wedding of Prince William and Kate Middleton
Wedding of Prince William of Wales and Catherine Middleton
Wedding of Prince William, Duke of Cambridge and Catherine, Duchess of Cambridge
Wedding of Prince William, Duke of Cambridge, and Catherine Middleton
Wedding of The Duke and Duchess of Cambridge
Engagement of Prince William of Wales and Kate Middleton
Marriage of Prince William of Wales and Kate Middleton
Marriage of Prince William of Wales to Catherine Middleton
Royal Wedding of Prince William and Catherine Middleton
Royal Wedding of Prince William and Kate Middleton
The Royal Wedding of Prince William and Catherine Middleton
The Royal Wedding of Prince William and Kate Middleton
Wedding of Kate Middleton and Prince William of Wales
Wedding of Prince William of Wales and Kate Middleton
Wedding of Prince William of Wales and Miss Catherine Middleton
Wedding of Prince William of Wales to Kate Middleton
Wedding of Prince William of Wales, and Kate Middleton
Wedding of Prince William, Duke of Cambridge and Kate Middleton
Wedding of Prince William, Duke of Cambridge to Kate Middleton
Wedding of Prince William, Duke of Cambridge, and Kate Middleton
Wedding of William, Prince of Wales and Catherine, Princess of Wales
Wedding of William, Prince of Wales and Kate Middleton
Wedding of William, Prince of Wales, and Kate Middleton
Q486814.blurb: The wedding of Prince William and Catherine Middleton takes place at Westminster Abbey in London.

Q486866.name: Operation Linebacker II
Q486866.blurb: Vietnam War: Operation Linebacker II ends.

Q487076.name: Battle of Xuan Loc
Q487076.blurb: South Vietnamese forces withdraw from the town of Xuan Loc in the last major battle of the Vietnam War.

Q487163.name: Nepalese royal massacre
Q487163.blurb: Nepalese royal massacre: Crown Prince Dipendra of Nepal shoots and kills several members of his family including his father and mother.

Q487332.name: Battle of Hansan Island
Q487332.blurb: Imjin War: At the Battle of Hansan Island, the Korean Navy, led by Yi Sun-sin, Yi Ŏkki, and Wŏn Kyun, decisively defeats the Japanese Navy, led by Wakisaka Yasuharu.

Q487565.name: Second Battle of Yeonpyeong
Q487565.blurb: Naval clashes between South Korea and North Korea lead to the death of six South Korean sailors and sinking of a North Korean vessel.

Q487757.name: Second Manchu invasion of Korea
Q487757.blurb: The Qing dynasty of China, led by Emperor Hong Taiji, invades Joseon.

Q487810.name: May 16 coup
Q487810.blurb: Park Chung Hee leads a coup d'état to overthrow the Second Republic of South Korea.

Q488278.name: Battle of Uhud
Q488278.blurb: The Muslim army under Muhammad suffers a defeat against the Quraysh in the battle of Uhud.

Q488361.name: Typhoon Maemi
Q488361.blurb: Typhoon Maemi, the strongest recorded typhoon to strike South Korea, made landfall near Busan.

Q489416.name: April Revolution
Q489416.blurb: Students in South Korea hold a nationwide pro-democracy protest against president Syngman Rhee, eventually forcing him to resign.

Q489904.name: Air China Flight 129
Q489904.blurb: Air China Flight 129 crashes on approach to Gimhae International Airport in Busan, South Korea, killing 129 people.

Q489959.name: Operation Linebacker
Q489959.blurb: Vietnam War: Operation Linebacker, a US bombing campaign against North Vietnam in response to its Easter Offensive, ends after five months.

Q490035.name: Greek Resistance
Q490035.blurb: Greek Resistance: The United Panhellenic Organization of Youth is founded in Greece.

Q490176.name: Typhoon Ewiniar
Q490176.blurb: Typhoon Ewiniar made landfall in South Korea, causing damages across the country amounting to 2.06 trillion won (US$1.4 billion).

Q490223.name: Battle of Bornhöved
Q490223.blurb: A coalition of north-east German towns, counts and princes defeats King Valdemar II of Denmark in the Battle of Bornhöved.

Q490811.name: Daegu subway fire
Q490811.blurb: 192 people die when an arsonist sets fire to a subway train in Daegu, South Korea.

Q490844.name: Gukurahundi
Q490844.blurb: In Zimbabwe, the political parties ZANU and ZAPU reach an agreement that ends the violence in the Matabeleland region known as the Gukurahundi.

Q491018.name: Geochang massacre
Q491018.blurb: Korean War: The two-day Geochang massacre begins as a battalion of the 11th Division of the South Korean Army kills 719 unarmed citizens in Geochang, in the South Gyeongsang district of South Korea.

Q491188.name: Battle of Daecheong
Q491188.blurb: Ships of the South and North Korean navies skirmish off Daecheong Island in the Yellow Sea.

Q491269.name: 2006 North Korean missile test
Q491269.blurb: North Korea tests four short-range missiles, one medium-range missile and a long-range Taepodong-2. The long-range Taepodong-2 reportedly fails in mid-air over the Sea of Japan.

Q491346.name: kidnapping of Kim Dae-jung
Q491346.blurb: Kim Dae-jung, a South Korean politician and later president of South Korea, is kidnapped.

Q491520.name: Korean Air Cargo Flight 8509
Q491520.blurb: Just after taking off from London Stansted Airport, Korean Air Cargo Flight 8509 crashes into Hatfield Forest near Great Hallingbury, killing all four people on board.

Q491951.name: Treaty of Nemours
Q491951.blurb: The Treaty of Nemours abolishes tolerance to Protestants in France.

Q492324.name: Seven Days Battles
Q492324.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Malvern Hill takes place. It is the last of the Seven Days Battles, part of George B. McClellan's Peninsula Campaign.

Q492671.name: Battle of Triangle Hill
Q492671.blurb: Korean War: The Battle of Triangle Hill is the biggest and bloodiest battle of 1952.

Q492877.name: Hangang Bridge bombing
Q492877.blurb: Korean War: Packed with its own refugees fleeing Seoul and leaving their 5th Division stranded, South Korean forces blow up the Hangang Bridge in an attempt to slow North Korea's offensive. The city falls later that day.

Q492880.name: Battle of Taejon
Q492880.blurb: Korean War: beginning of the Battle of Taejon.

Q493252.name: Battle of Chonan
Q493252.blurb: Korean War: American troops withdrew from Cheonan, in modern-day South Korea, after suffering heavy casualties from a North Korean attack.

Q493313.name: Battle of the Ch'ongch'on River
Q493313.blurb: Korean War: Communist Chinese troops launch a massive counterattack (Battle of the Ch'ongch'on River and Battle of Chosin Reservoir) against United Nations and South Korean forces.

Q493534.name: St. Lucia's flood
Q493534.blurb: St. Lucia's flood: The Zuiderzee sea wall in the Netherlands collapses, killing over 50,000 people.

Q493565.name: All Saints' Flood
Q493565.blurb: The All Saints' Flood devastates the Dutch coast.

Q493922.name: Third Battle of Seoul
Q493922.blurb: Korean War: Chinese and North Korean troops captured Seoul from United Nations forces.

Q494043.name: Hill 303 massacre
Q494043.blurb: Korean War: Forty-two American prisoners of war were massacred by the Korean People's Army on a hill above Waegwan, South Korea.

Q494058.name: ROKS Cheonan sinking
Q494058.blurb: The South Korean Navy corvette Cheonan is torpedoed, killing 46 sailors. After an international investigation, the President of the United Nations Security Council blames North Korea.

Q494244.name: M*A*S*H
aliases: There Is Nothing Like A Nurse
Q494244.blurb: The final episode of M*A*S*H airs, with almost 110 million viewers.

Q494418.name: Rangoon bombing
Q494418.blurb: South Korean President Chun Doo-hwan survives an assassination attempt in Rangoon, Burma, but the blast kills 21 and injures 17 others.

Q494896.name: Battle of Dungan's Hill
Q494896.blurb: The Irish Confederate Wars and Wars of the Three Kingdoms: Battle of Dungan's Hill: English Parliamentary forces defeat Irish forces.

Q494961.name: 2002 FIFA World Cup qualification
Q494961.blurb: In a FIFA World Cup qualifying match, Australia defeated American Samoa 31–0, the largest margin of victory recorded in international football.

Q495446.name: No Gun Ri Massacre
Q495446.blurb: Korean War: After four days, the No Gun Ri Massacre ends when the US Army 7th Cavalry Regiment is withdrawn.

Q495558.name: Japan–Korea Treaty of 1910
aliases: にっかんへいごうじょうやく
Q495558.blurb: The Japan–Korea Treaty of 1910, also known as the Japan–Korea Annexation Treaty, becomes effective, officially starting the period of Japanese rule in Korea.

Q495739.name: Korean axe murder incident
Q495739.blurb: The Korean axe murder incident in Panmunjom results in the deaths of two US Army officers.

Q495953.name: Korean Air Flight 858
Q495953.blurb: North Korean agents plant a bomb on Korean Air Flight 858, which kills all 115 passengers and crew.

Q496095.name: Ganghwa massacre
Q496095.blurb: Korean War: Beginning of the Ganghwa massacre, in the course of which an estimated 200–1,300 South Korean communist sympathizers are slaughtered.

Q496145.name: Sancheong-Hamyang massacre
Q496145.blurb: Korean War: More than 700 suspected communist sympathizers are massacred by South Korean forces.

Q497145.name: 1999 Armenia, Colombia earthquake
Q497145.blurb: A 6.0 magnitude earthquake hits western Colombia killing at least 1,000.

Q497157.name: 1999 Athens earthquake
Q497157.blurb: The 6.0 Mw Athens earthquake affected the area with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent), killing 143, injuring 800–1,600, and leaving 50,000 homeless.

Q497194.name: June Struggle
Q497194.blurb: June Democratic Struggle: The June Democratic Struggle starts in South Korea, and people protest against the government.

Q497354.name: Asiana Airlines Flight 733
Q497354.blurb: Asiana Airlines Flight 733 crashes into a ridge on Mt. Ungeo on its third attempt to land at Mokpo Airport, South Korea. Sixty-eight of the 116 people on board are killed.

Q497797.name: Battle of Cold Harbor
Q497797.blurb: American Civil War: Overland Campaign: Battle of Cold Harbor: The Army of Northern Virginia engages the Army of the Potomac.

Q498871.name: Peasants' Revolt of 1381
Q498871.blurb: Beginning of the Peasants' Revolt in England.

Q498979.name: Panama Canal Zone
aliases: Postage stamps and postal history of the Panama Canal Zone
Q498979.blurb: The U.S. government hands control of the Panama Canal (as well all the adjacent land to the canal known as the Panama Canal Zone) to Panama. This act complied with the signing of the 1977 Torrijos–Carter Treaties.

Q499060.name: 2006 North Korean nuclear test
Q499060.blurb: North Korea conducts its first nuclear test.

Q499626.name: Battle of Stirling Bridge
aliases: William Wallace and the Battle of Stirling Bridge
Q499626.blurb: Battle of Stirling Bridge: Scots jointly led by William Wallace and Andrew Moray defeat the English.

Q499763.name: Prayer Book Rebellion
Q499763.blurb: Battle of Sampford Courtenay: The Prayer Book Rebellion is quashed in England.

Q500067.name: Treaty of Bucharest
Q500067.blurb: Second Balkan War: Delegates from Bulgaria, Romania, Serbia, Montenegro, and Greece sign the Treaty of Bucharest, ending the war.

Q500395.name: Cornish Rebellion of 1497
Q500395.blurb: Battle of Deptford Bridge: Forces under King Henry VII defeat troops led by Michael An Gof.

Q501208.name: 1991 Azerbaijani Mil Mi-8 shootdown
Q501208.blurb: First Nagorno-Karabakh War: An Azerbaijani military helicopter carrying a peacekeeping mission team was shot down in Nagorno-Karabakh, disrupting ongoing peace talks.

Q501663.name: Thomas & Friends
aliases: Thomas the Tank Engine and Friends
Ice Cream Vans (Thomas the Tank Engine)
It's Great to be an Engine
List of Shining Time Station characters
List of Thomas the Tank Engine & Friends Videos
Thomas the Tank Engine & Friends (2D Animated)
Thomas the Tank Engine & Friends Home Video Releases
Thomas the Tank Engine & Friends on DVD & Video
Thomas the Tank Engine and Friends (2D Animated)
Thomas the Tank Engine and Friends on DVD and Video
Thomas the Tank Engine home video
Very Best Of Thomas and Friends
Q501663.blurb: The popular children's television show Thomas The Tank Engine & Friends, based on The Railway Series by the Reverend Wilbert Awdry, premieres on ITV.

Q501866.name: 1983 Invasion of Grenada
Q501866.blurb: The United States and its Caribbean allies invade Grenada, six days after Prime Minister Maurice Bishop and several of his supporters are executed in a coup d'état.

Q502073.name: Halifax explosion
Q502073.blurb: Halifax Explosion: A munitions explosion near Halifax, Nova Scotia kills more than 1,900 people in the largest artificial explosion up to that time.

Q502093.name: Casablanca Conference
Q502093.blurb: World War II: Franklin D. Roosevelt and Winston Churchill begin the Casablanca Conference to discuss strategy and study the next phase of the war.

Q503347.name: Attack on Mers-El-Kebir
aliases: Destruction of the French Fleet at Mers-el-Kebir
Destruction of the French Fleet at Mers-el-Kébir
Scuttling of the French fleet in Mers-el-Kebir
Q503347.blurb: World War II: The Royal Navy attacks the French naval squadron in Algeria, to ensure that it will not fall under German control. Of the four French battleships present, one is sunk, two are damaged, and one escapes back to France.

Q504081.name: Greek junta
aliases: Regime of the colonels in Greece
Q504081.blurb: In protest against the dictatorship in Greece, the captain and crew on Greek naval destroyer Velos mutiny and refuse to return to Greece, instead anchoring at Fiumicino, Italy.

Q504172.name: Battle of Guadalete
Q504172.blurb: Umayyad conquest of Hispania: Battle of Guadalete: Umayyad forces under Tariq ibn Ziyad defeat the Visigoths led by King Roderic.

Q504347.name: Battle of the Philippine Sea
aliases: First Battle of the Philippine Sea
Q504347.blurb: World War II: The Battle of the Philippine Sea concludes with a decisive U.S. naval victory. The lopsided naval air battle is also known as the "Great Marianas Turkey Shoot".

Q504739.name: Battle of Pydna
Q504739.blurb: Battle of Pydna: Romans under Lucius Aemilius Paullus defeat Macedonian King Perseus who surrenders after the battle, ending the Third Macedonian War.

Q504934.name: North Sea flood of 1953
Q504934.blurb: A North Sea flood causes over 1,800 deaths in the Netherlands and over 300 in the United Kingdom.

Q505699.name: Battle of Heiligerlee
Q505699.blurb: Dutch rebels led by Louis of Nassau defeat Jean de Ligne and his loyalist troops in the Battle of Heiligerlee, opening the Eighty Years' War.

Q505802.name: Lewis and Clark Expedition
aliases: Dates to lewis and clarks voyage
Lewis and Clark's Corps of Discovery
Q505802.blurb: Lewis and Clark Expedition: The Corps of Discovery breaks camp among the Mandan tribe and resumes its journey West along the Missouri River.

Q505939.name: Battle of Vukovar
Q505939.blurb: The Battle of Vukovar begins. An 87-day siege of Vukovar by the Yugoslav People's Army (JNA), supported by various Serb paramilitary forces, between August and November 1991 (during the Croatian War of Independence).

Q506911.name: 1903 Tour de France
Q506911.blurb: Start of first Tour de France bicycle race.

Q506912.name: St. Peter's Flood
Q506912.blurb: St. Peter's Flood: A storm surge floods the Frisian coast, drowning 15,000 people.

Q506916.name: Battle of Dobro Pole
Q506916.blurb: World War I: Allied troops break through the Bulgarian defenses on the Macedonian front.

Q508006.name: Siege of the Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem
Q508006.blurb: The 38-day stand-off in the Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem comes to an end when the Palestinians inside agree to have 13 suspected terrorists among them deported to several different countries.

Q508258.name: 1959 Tibetan uprising
Q508258.blurb: Tibetan uprising: Fearing an abduction attempt by China, thousands of Tibetans surround the Dalai Lama's palace to prevent his removal.

Q508513.name: 12th Academy Awards
Q508513.blurb: At the 12th Academy Awards, Hattie McDaniel became the first African American to be awarded an Oscar, winning Best Supporting Actress for her role as Mammy in Gone with the Wind.

Q508923.name: 2008 UEFA Cup Final
Q508923.blurb: On the day of the UEFA Cup Final, violence erupted between football hooligan supporters of both teams and the Greater Manchester Police, resulting in 39 arrests and 39 injured officers.

Q509337.name: Great Locomotive Chase
Q509337.blurb: American Civil War: The Andrews Raid (the Great Locomotive Chase) occurs, starting from Big Shanty, Georgia (now Kennesaw).

Q509347.name: UEFA Euro 2004 finals
aliases: 2004 UEFA European Championship Match 31, Portugal v Greece
Q509347.blurb: Greece beats Portugal in the UEFA Euro 2004 Final and becomes European Champion for first time in its history.

Q509561.name: Soviet withdrawal from Afghanistan
Q509561.blurb: Soviet Defense Minister Dmitry Yazov orders the Soviet withdrawal from Afghanistan.

Q510468.name: Pacific Southwest Airlines Flight 182
Q510468.blurb: PSA Flight 182, a Boeing 727, collides in mid-air with a Cessna 172 and crashes in San Diego, killing all 135 aboard Flight 182, both occupants of the Cessna, as well as seven people on the ground.

Q510943.name: Battle of Preston
Q510943.blurb: The Parliamentarians defeat a English Royalist and Scottish army in the battle of Preston.

Q512700.name: Togoland campaign
Q512700.blurb: World War I: The German colony of Togoland surrendered to French and British forces after a 20-day campaign.

Q512914.name: Operation Tidal Wave
Q512914.blurb: World War II: Operation Tidal Wave, also known as "Black Sunday", is a failed American attempt to destroy Romanian oil fields.

Q513007.name: Battle of Sablat
Q513007.blurb: Thirty Years' War: Battle of Záblatí, a turning point in the Bohemian Revolt.

Q514064.name: 1984 Portuguese Grand Prix
Q514064.blurb: Niki Lauda claims his third and final Formula One Drivers' Championship Title by half a point ahead of McLaren team-mate Alain Prost at the Portuguese Grand Prix.

Q514382.name: Battle of al-Harrah
Q514382.blurb: The Battle of al-Harrah concludes, with Yazid I's army killing 11,000 people of the city of Medina.

Q516202.name: Battle of Cherbourg
Q516202.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Cherbourg ends with the fall of the strategically valuable port to American forces.

Q516282.name: Battle of Raszyn
Q516282.blurb: An Austrian corps is defeated by the forces of the Duchy of Warsaw in the Battle of Raszyn, part of the struggles of the Fifth Coalition. On the same day the Austrian main army is defeated by a First French Empire Corps led by Louis-Nicolas Davout at the Battle of Teugen-Hausen in Bavaria, part of a four-day campaign that ended in a French victory.

Q516760.name: Battle of Munda
Q516760.blurb: In his last victory, Julius Caesar defeats the Pompeian forces of Titus Labienus and Pompey the Younger in the Battle of Munda.

Q517262.name: Battle of Veracruz
Q517262.blurb: The French Army captures Veracruz in the Pastry War.

Q517486.name: Battle of Zenta
Q517486.blurb: Battle of Zenta: a major engagement in the Great Turkish War (1683–1699) and one of the most decisive defeats in Ottoman history.

Q517621.name: FIFA World Cup Trophy
Q517621.blurb: The Jules Rimet Trophy, awarded to the winner of the FIFA World Cup, was stolen from the offices of the Brazilian Football Confederation.

Q517941.name: 2008 Pakistan earthquake
Q517941.blurb: A pair of deadly earthquakes hits Baluchistan, Pakistan, killing 215.

Q518303.name: 1983 Beirut barracks bombing
Q518303.blurb: Lebanese Civil War: The U.S. Marines Corps barracks in Beirut is hit by a truck bomb, killing 241 U.S. military personnel.  A French Army barracks in Lebanon is also hit that same morning, killing 58 troops.

Q518753.name: Sharpeville massacre
Q518753.blurb: Apartheid: Sharpeville massacre, South Africa: Police open fire on a group of black South African demonstrators, killing 69 and wounding 180.

Q519139.name: Council of Hieria
Q519139.blurb: The Lateran Council ends by condemning the Council of Hieria and anathematizing its iconoclastic rulings.

Q519255.name: Dutch–Indonesian Round Table Conference
Q519255.blurb: The Dutch–Indonesian Round Table Conference ends with the Netherlands agreeing to transfer sovereignty of the Dutch East Indies to the United States of Indonesia.

Q519818.name: Battle of Zusmarshausen
Q519818.blurb: An allied French and Swedish army defeats Imperial and Bavarian forces in the Battle of Zusmarshausen.

Q520260.name: Schießbefehl
Q520260.blurb: Egon Krenz, the former East German leader, is convicted of a shoot-to-kill policy at the Berlin Wall.

Q520286.name: Cyclone Lothar
Q520286.blurb: The storm Lothar sweeps across Central Europe, killing 137 and causing US$1.3 billion in damage.

Q521199.name: North Yemen civil war
Q521199.blurb: The North Yemen Civil War begins when Abdullah al-Sallal dethrones the newly crowned Imam al-Badr and declares Yemen a republic under his presidency.

Q521306.name: Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty
Q521306.blurb: Representatives of 71 nations sign the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty at the United Nations.

Q521799.name: Battle of the Neva
Q521799.blurb: Swedish–Novgorodian Wars: A Novgorodian army led by Alexander Nevsky defeats the Swedes in the Battle of the Neva.

Q521923.name: Treaty of Hamburg
Q521923.blurb: Sweden and Prussia sign the Treaty of Hamburg.

Q522837.name: Bengal famine of 1943
aliases: Sex and gender in the Bengal famine of 1943
Q522837.blurb: Ian Stephens, editor of The Statesman, defied British censorship to publish pictures of death and misery (example pictured) on Calcutta's streets, informing the world of the Bengal famine of 1943.

Q523006.name: 1974 Belgian general election
Q523006.blurb: 1974 Belgian general election: Elections are held in Belgium for all 212 seats in the Chamber of Representatives, the Belgian Socialist Party taking the majority with 59.

Q523141.name: 1999 Iranian student protests
Q523141.blurb: Days of student protests begin after Iranian police and hardliners attack a student dormitory at the University of Tehran.

Q523154.name: Caucasus campaign
Q523154.blurb: Russia defeats Ottoman Turkey in the Battle of Sarikamish during the Caucasus Campaign of World War I.

Q523742.name: Bombardment of Papeete
Q523742.blurb: World War I: German naval forces bombarded Papeete in French Polynesia and sank a French gunboat.

Q523857.name: Battle of Germantown
Q523857.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Troops under George Washington are repelled by British troops under William Howe.

Q523883.name: death of Brian Wels
Q523883.blurb: In "one of the most complicated and bizarre crimes in the annals of the FBI", Brian Wells dies after becoming involved in a complex plot involving a bank robbery, a scavenger hunt, and a homemade explosive device.

Q524189.name: Cologne War
Q524189.blurb: Cologne War: Forces under Ernest of Bavaria defeat troops under Gebhard Truchsess von Waldburg at the Siege of Godesberg.

Q524208.name: Erzurum Offensive
Q524208.blurb: World War I: Imperial Russia begins the Erzurum Offensive, leading to the defeat of the Ottoman Empire's Third Army.

Q524251.name: Second Siege of Zaragoza
Q524251.blurb: Peninsular War: The Siege of Zaragoza begins.

Q524737.name: Mayaguez incident
Q524737.blurb: The Cambodian navy seized the American container ship SS Mayaguez in what they claimed to be Cambodian territorial waters.

Q524797.name: St. Elizabeth's flood
Q524797.blurb: St Elizabeth's flood: A dike in the Grote Hollandse Waard in the Netherlands breaks, killing about 10,000 people.

Q524828.name: Battle of the Monongahela
Q524828.blurb: The Braddock Expedition is soundly defeated by a smaller French and Native American force in its attempt to capture Fort Duquesne in what is now downtown Pittsburgh.

Q525565.name: Big Bottom Massacre
Q525565.blurb: Northwest Indian War: The Big Bottom massacre is committed by Lenape and Wyandot warriors in the Ohio Country, North America.

Q527130.name: ethnic clashes of Târgu Mureș
Q527130.blurb: The ethnic clashes of Târgu Mureș begin four days after the anniversary of the Revolutions of 1848 in the Austrian Empire.

Q528183.name: Battle of Newtown
Q528183.blurb: American Revolutionary War: American forces battle and defeat the British and Iroquois forces at the Battle of Newtown.

Q528550.name: Battle of Manila Bay
Q528550.blurb: Spanish–American War: Battle of Manila Bay: The Asiatic Squadron of the United States Navy destroys the Pacific Squadron of the Spanish Navy after a seven-hour battle. Spain loses all seven of its ships, and 381 Spanish sailors die. There are no American vessel losses or combat deaths.

Q529723.name: Anfal campaign
Q529723.blurb: Saddam Hussein begins the Anfal genocide against Kurds and Assyrians in northern Iraq.

Q531334.name: Air India Flight 245
Q531334.blurb: Air India Flight 245 crashes into Mont Blanc while on approach to Geneva Airport, killing all 48 people on board.

Q531346.name: Battle of Valverde
Q531346.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Valverde is fought near Fort Craig in New Mexico Territory.

Q531523.name: Truce of Ulm
Q531523.blurb: Thirty Years' War: Bavaria, Cologne, France and Sweden sign the Truce of Ulm.

Q531916.name: First Mongol invasion of Burma
Q531916.blurb: During the First Mongol invasion of Burma, the fort at Ngasaunggyan was overrun after a two-month siege.

Q532899.name: Battle of Molinella
Q532899.blurb: The Battle of Molinella: The first battle in Italy in which firearms are used extensively.

Q533034.name: Battle of Westerplatte
Q533034.blurb: German forces attacked multiple locations in Poland, including Wieluń and Westerplatte, starting World War II in Europe.

Q534358.name: Lufthansa Flight 540
Q534358.blurb: The first fatal crash of a Boeing 747 occurs when Lufthansa Flight 540 crashes while attempting to takeoff from Jomo Kenyatta International Airport in Nairobi, Kenya, killing 59 out of the 157 people on board.

Q534990.name: Battle of Göllheim
Q534990.blurb: Battle of Göllheim: Albert I of Habsburg defeats Adolf of Nassau-Weilburg.

Q536822.name: Diet of Worms
aliases: Here I stand, I can do no other
Q536822.blurb: The Diet of Worms begins, lasting until May 25.

Q536935.name: 1986 West Berlin discotheque bombing
Q536935.blurb: The Libyan secret service bombed a discotheque in West Berlin, resulting in three deaths and 229 others injured.

Q537052.name: Operation Sutton
Q537052.blurb: Falklands War: A British amphibious assault during Operation Sutton leads to the Battle of San Carlos.

Q537110.name: Eclipse of Thales
Q537110.blurb: A solar eclipse occurs, as predicted by the Greek philosopher and scientist Thales, while Alyattes is battling Cyaxares in the Battle of the Eclipse, leading to a truce. This is one of the cardinal dates from which other dates can be calculated. It is also the earliest event of which the precise date is known.

Q537143.name: Treaty of Saadabad
Q537143.blurb: Turkey, Iran, Iraq, and Afghanistan sign the Treaty of Saadabad.

Q537148.name: Sonderaktion Krakau
Q537148.blurb: As part of their plan to eradicate the Polish intellectual elite, the Gestapo arrested 184 professors, students and employees of the Jagiellonian University (location pictured) in Kraków.

Q537576.name: Massacre of the Acqui Division
Q537576.blurb: Second World War: The German Army began the Massacre of the Acqui Division on the Greek island of Cephalonia, executing 5,155 Italian soldiers in the next five days.

Q537616.name: 1982 Spanish general election
Q537616.blurb: The Spanish general election begins fourteen years of rule by the Spanish Socialist Workers' Party.

Q537923.name: Battle of Ridaniya
Q537923.blurb: The Ottoman Empire under Selim I defeats the Mamluk Sultanate and captures present-day Egypt at the Battle of Ridaniya.

Q538790.name: Freedom Riders
Q538790.blurb: The Journey of Reconciliation, the first interracial Freedom Ride begins through the upper South in violation of Jim Crow laws. The riders wanted enforcement of the United States Supreme Court's 1946 Irene Morgan decision that banned racial segregation in interstate travel.

Q540978.name: Second Italian War of Independence
Q540978.blurb: Italian Independence wars: In the Battle of Magenta, the French army, under Louis-Napoleon, defeat the Austrian army.

Q541191.name: Anglo-Irish Treaty
aliases: Articles of Agreement for a Treaty Between Great Britain and Ireland
Articles of Agreement for an Irish Peace
Q541191.blurb: The Anglo-Irish Treaty is signed in London by British and Irish representatives.

Q541195.name: Anglo-Japanese Alliance
Q541195.blurb: The first Anglo-Japanese Alliance is signed in London.

Q541283.name: Super Bowl XXXVIII halftime show controversy
Q541283.blurb: During the halftime show of Super Bowl XXXVIII, Janet Jackson's breast was exposed by Justin Timberlake in what was later referred to as a "wardrobe malfunction", resulting in an immediate crackdown and widespread debate on perceived indecency in U.S. broadcasting.

Q541293.name: Treaty of London
Q541293.blurb: The Emirate of Transjordan becomes independent from the United Kingdom as the Hashemite Kingdom of Transjordan after ratifying the Treaty of London and making their Amir, Abdullah I, their King.

Q541369.name: Anglo-Soviet invasion of Iran
aliases: Occupation of Persia by the Allies
Q541369.blurb: World War II: Anglo-Soviet invasion of Iran: The United Kingdom and the Soviet Union jointly stage an invasion of the Imperial State of Iran.

Q541506.name: Battle of Prokhorovka
Q541506.blurb: World War II: German and Soviet forces engaged each other at the Battle of Prokhorovka (tanks pictured), one of the largest tank battles in military history.

Q541626.name: Battle of Aspern-Essling
Q541626.blurb: The first day of the Battle of Aspern-Essling between the Austrian army led by Archduke Charles and the French army led by Napoleon I of France sees the French attack across the Danube held.

Q541723.name: Antioch earthquake of 526
Q541723.blurb: A catastrophic earthquake hits Antioch, killing several thousands including patriarch Euphrasius.

Q541958.name: Battle of Mulhouse
Q541958.blurb: The Battle of Mulhouse began with France's first attack of World War I in an ultimately unsuccessful attempt to recover the region of Alsace from Germany.

Q541997.name: Battle of Alam el Halfa
Q541997.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Alam el Halfa begins.

Q542191.name: Battle of Konzer Brücke
Q542191.blurb: Franco-Dutch War: Forces of the Holy Roman Empire defeat the French in the Battle of Konzer Brücke.

Q543028.name: Battle of Washita River
Q543028.blurb: American Indian Wars: Battle of Washita River: United States Army Lieutenant Colonel George Armstrong Custer leads an attack on Cheyenne living on reservation land.

Q543042.name: Latvian War of Independence
Q543042.blurb: Latvian forces defeat the West Russian Volunteer Army at Riga in the Latvian War of Independence.

Q543043.name: Attack on Aruba
Q543043.blurb: World War II: Attack on Aruba, first World War II German shots fired on a land based object in the Americas.

Q543075.name: Battle of Dutch Harbor
Q543075.blurb: World War II: Japan begins the Aleutian Islands Campaign by bombing Unalaska Island.

Q543076.name: Council of Vienne
Q543076.blurb: The Council of Vienne convenes for the first time.

Q543077.name: Bombardment of Ellwood
Q543077.blurb: World War II: Japanese submarines fire artillery shells at the coastline near Santa Barbara, California.

Q543094.name: Battle of Fort Stedman
Q543094.blurb: American Civil War: In Virginia during the Siege of Petersburg, Confederate forces temporarily capture Fort Stedman from the Union before being repulsed.

Q543110.name: Attack on Orleans
Q543110.blurb: World War I: An Imperial German Navy U-boat opened fire on a small convoy of barges and defending aircraft near the American town of Orleans, Massachusetts.

Q543154.name: Battle of Santa Cruz de Tenerife
Q543154.blurb: Battle of Santa Cruz de Tenerife: Battle between Spanish and British naval forces during the French Revolutionary Wars. During the Battle, Rear-Admiral Nelson is wounded in the arm and the arm had to be partially amputated.

Q543165.name: Battle of Fort Sumter
Q543165.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Fort Sumter. The war begins with Confederate forces firing on Fort Sumter, in the harbor of Charleston, South Carolina.

Q543202.name: Battle of Tremseh
Q543202.blurb: Syrian Civil War: Government forces target the homes of rebels and activists in Tremseh and kill anywhere between 68 and 150 people.

Q543255.name: Battle of Taranto
Q543255.blurb: World War II: In the Battle of Taranto, the Royal Navy launches the first all-aircraft ship-to-ship naval attack in history.

Q543279.name: 2011 NATO attack in Pakistan
Q543279.blurb: NATO attack in Pakistan: NATO forces in Afghanistan attack a Pakistani check post in a friendly fire incident, killing 24 soldiers and wounding 13 others.

Q543312.name: Marshalls–Gilberts raids
Q543312.blurb: World War II: U.S. Navy conducts Marshalls–Gilberts raids, the first offensive action by the United States against Japanese forces in the Pacific Theater.

Q544090.name: Battle of Cape Matapan
Q544090.blurb: World War II: First day of the Battle of Cape Matapan in Greece between the navies of the United Kingdom and Australia, and the Royal Italian navy.

Q545068.name: 2008 Tibetan unrest
Q545068.blurb: A series of riots, protests, and demonstrations erupt in Lhasa and subsequently spread elsewhere in Tibet.

Q545327.name: Eastern Mediterranean event
Q545327.blurb: Eastern Mediterranean event. A near-Earth asteroid estimated at ten meters in diameter explodes over the Mediterranean Sea between Greece and Libya. The explosion is estimated to have a force of 26 kilotons, slightly more powerful than the Nagasaki atomic bomb.

Q545449.name: Iraq War
aliases: Gulf War 2/battle of Ramadi/battle of Faluya
Economic cost of the Iraq War
Economic costs of the Iraq War
Foreign involvement in the Iraq War
War crimes during the Iraq War
War crimes in the Iraq War
Q545449.blurb: War in Iraq: Al-Qaeda carries out the Ashoura Massacre in Iraq, killing 170 and wounding over 500.

Q546317.name: Battle of Prestonpans
Q546317.blurb: A British government army led by Sir John Cope is defeated in less than 15 minutes by the Jacobite forces of Prince Charles Edward Stuart.

Q547247.name: Operation Rolling Thunder
Q547247.blurb: The US and Republic of Vietnam Air Force begin Operation Rolling Thunder, a sustained bombing campaign against North Vietnam.

Q547328.name: Kingsmill massacre
Q547328.blurb: The Troubles: Gunmen shoot dead ten Protestant civilians after stopping their minibus at Kingsmill in County Armagh, Northern Ireland, UK, allegedly as retaliation for a string of attacks on Catholic civilians in the area by Loyalists, particularly the killing of six Catholics the night before.

Q547896.name: Chemical Weapons Convention
aliases: Convention on the Banning of Chemical Weapons
Convention on the Prohibition of the Development, Production, Stockpiling and Use of Chemical Weapons and on their Destruction
Convention on the Universal Prohibition of Chemical Weapons
Convention on the prohibition of the development, production, stockpiling and use of chemical weapons and their destruction
Q547896.blurb: The Chemical Weapons Convention (CWC) is signed.

Q548067.name: Treaty of Portsmouth
Q548067.blurb: Russo-Japanese War: In New Hampshire, United States, the Treaty of Portsmouth, mediated by U.S. President Theodore Roosevelt, ends the war.

Q548252.name: Battle of Lorraine
Q548252.blurb: World War I: Start of the Battle of Lorraine, an unsuccessful French offensive.

Q548625.name: Battle of Maiwand
Q548625.blurb: Second Anglo-Afghan War: Battle of Maiwand: Afghan forces led by Mohammad Ayub Khan defeat the British Army in battle near Maiwand, Afghanistan.

Q548680.name: Second Battle of Champagne
Q548680.blurb: World War I: The Second Battle of Champagne begins.

Q548819.name: Battle of the Komandorski Islands
Q548819.blurb: World War II: Battle of the Komandorski Islands: In the Aleutian Islands the battle begins when United States Navy forces intercept Japanese attempting to reinforce a garrison at Kiska.

Q549544.name: Beatlemania
aliases: The Beatles in the United States
Q549544.blurb: As Beatlemania swept the United States, the Beatles (pictured) made their first appearance on The Ed Sullivan Show before a record-breaking audience, beginning a musical phenomenon known as the British Invasion.

Q549912.name: Declaration of Principles on Western Sahara by Spain, Morocco and Mauritania
aliases: Declaration of Principles on Western Sahara
Q549912.blurb: With the signing of the Madrid Accords, Spain abandons Western Sahara.

Q550172.name: War of the Breton Succession
aliases: The War of the Breton Succession
Q550172.blurb: War of the Breton Succession: Anglo-Bretons defeat the French in the Battle of Mauron.

Q551549.name: Battle of Chojnice
Q551549.blurb: Thirteen Years' War: In the Battle of Chojnice, the Polish army is defeated by the Teutonic knights.

Q552296.name: Battle of Carpi
Q552296.blurb: A Bourbon force under Nicolas Catinat withdraws from a smaller Habsburg force under Prince Eugene of Savoy in the Battle of Carpi.

Q553024.name: Treaty of Berlin
Q553024.blurb: The United States Senate accepts the Anglo-German treaty of 1899 in which the United Kingdom renounces its claims to the Samoan islands.

Q553157.name: Romania in World War I
Q553157.blurb: World War I: Germany declares war against France, while Romania declares its neutrality.

Q553492.name: Air Midwest Flight 5481
Q553492.blurb: Air Midwest Flight 5481 crashes at Charlotte-Douglas Airport, in Charlotte, North Carolina, killing all 21 people on board.

Q555473.name: Cerro Maravilla murders
Q555473.blurb: Puerto Rican police shoot two nationalists in the Cerro Maravilla murders.

Q555797.name: Bataan Death March
Q555797.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Bataan ends and the Bataan Death March begins.

Q555839.name: Battle of Berezina
Q555839.blurb: The Battle of Berezina begins during Napoleon's retreat from Russia.

Q555848.name: Moimenta-Alcafache train crash
Q555848.blurb: Moimenta-Alcafache train crash, the worst railway accident to occur in Portugal.

Q558503.name: Battle of Rudau
Q558503.blurb: Northern Crusades: Grand Duchy of Lithuania and the Teutonic Knights meet in the Battle of Rudau.

Q559069.name: British occupation of Manila
Q559069.blurb: Seven Years' War: The Battle of Manila concluded with a British victory over Spain, leading to a twenty-month occupation.

Q559181.name: First Silesian War
Q559181.blurb: Prussian forces, led by Frederick the Great, moved into the Habsburg region of Silesia, starting the First Silesian War.

Q559291.name: Wola massacre
Q559291.blurb: World War II: The Nazis begin a week-long massacre of between 40,000 and 50,000 civilians and prisoners of war in Wola, Poland.

Q559920.name: World Oceans Day
Q559920.blurb: The first World Oceans Day is celebrated, coinciding with the Earth Summit held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

Q560372.name: 1976 Tehran UFO incident
Q560372.blurb: Two Imperial Iranian Air Force F-4 Phantom II jets fly out to investigate an unidentified flying object.

Q560410.name: Operation Trio
Q560410.blurb: World War II: German and Italian forces began a large-scale counter-insurgency operation in occupied Yugoslavia.

Q561886.name: 1990 East German general election
Q561886.blurb: Germans in the German Democratic Republic vote in the first democratic elections in the former communist dictatorship.

Q562277.name: Battle of Havana
Q562277.blurb: Seven Years' War: British forces begin the Siege of Havana and temporarily capture the city.

Q567343.name: Operation Deny Flight
Q567343.blurb: Bosnian War: NATO forces began Operation Deny Flight to enforce a no-fly zone over Bosnia and Herzegovina ordered by the United Nations Security Council.

Q568387.name: Peasants' War
Q568387.blurb: Flemish and Luxembourgish peasants launch the rebellion against French rule known as the Peasants' War.

Q568445.name: 1999 FIFA Women's World Cup
Q568445.blurb: The United States defeated China in the final match of the third FIFA Women's World Cup, setting records in both attendance and television ratings for women's sports.

Q568458.name: 2004 Ukrainian presidential election
Q568458.blurb: The second round of the Ukrainian presidential election is held, giving rise to massive protests and controversy over the election's integrity.

Q568790.name: Battle of Fromelles
Q568790.blurb: World War I: Battle of Fromelles: British and Australian troops attack German trenches as part of the Battle of the Somme.

Q568880.name: massacre of Kondomari
Q568880.blurb: World War II: German paratroopers murder Greek civilians in the villages of Kondomari and Alikianos.

Q568942.name: Ansari X Prize
Q568942.blurb: Burt Rutan's Ansari SpaceShipOne performs a successful spaceflight, the first of two required to win the Ansari X Prize.

Q568973.name: 1948 United States presidential election
aliases: 1948 Convention of the Socialist Party of America
Q568973.blurb: The Chicago Daily Tribune published the erroneous headline "Dewey Defeats Truman" (pictured) in its early morning edition shortly after incumbent U.S. president Harry S. Truman officially upset the heavily favored governor of New York Thomas Dewey in the presidential election.

Q569195.name: 2012 Burgas bus bombing
Q569195.blurb: At least seven people are killed and 32 others are injured after a bomb explodes on an Israeli tour bus at Burgas Airport, Bulgaria.

Q569203.name: 2003 Marriott Hotel bombing
Q569203.blurb: A car bomb explodes in the Indonesian capital of Jakarta outside the Marriott Hotel killing 12 and injuring 150.

Q569278.name: 1992 attack on Israeli embassy in Buenos Aires
Q569278.blurb: Israeli Embassy attack in Buenos Aires: Car bomb attack kills 29 and injures 242.

Q569287.name: Bologna massacre
Q569287.blurb: A bomb explodes at the railway station in Bologna, Italy, killing 85 people and wounding more than 200.

Q569290.name: Battle of Fuentes de Oñoro
Q569290.blurb: The Anglo-Portuguese army under Lord Wellington tries to halt a larger French army under Marshal Masséna marching to relieve Almeida in the Battle of Fuentes de Oñoro. After intense fighting, the French are repulsed.

Q569292.name: 2007 Yazidi communities bombings
Q569292.blurb: The Kahtaniya bombings kill at least 500 people.

Q569392.name: Crossair Flight 3597
Q569392.blurb: Crossair Flight 3597 crashes in Bassersdorf near Zurich Airport, killing 24 people, including singer Melanie Thornton and two members of the German band Passion Fruit.

Q569394.name: 2003 Casablanca bombing
Q569394.blurb: In Morocco, 33 civilians are killed and more than 100 people are injured in the Casablanca terrorist attacks.

Q569454.name: Second Happy Time
Q569454.blurb: World War II: The Second Happy Time of Hitler's submarines comes to an end, as the increasingly effective American convoy system compels them to return to the central Atlantic.

Q569545.name: Operation Crossroads
Q569545.blurb: Crossroads Able is the first postwar nuclear weapon test.

Q569689.name: Bombing of Singapore
Q569689.blurb: World War II: Allied forces began a military campaign on Japanese-occupied Singapore.

Q569953.name: Battle of Fontenoy
Q569953.blurb: War of the Austrian Succession: French forces defeated those of the Pragmatic Allies at the Battle of Fontenoy in the Austrian Netherlands in present-day Belgium.

Q570204.name: Battle of the Kalka River
aliases: The Battle of the Kalka River
Q570204.blurb: Mongol invasion of the Cumans: Battle of the Kalka River: Mongol armies of Genghis Khan led by Subutai defeat Kievan Rus' and Cumans.

Q570224.name: Ottawa Treaty
aliases: Convention on the Prohibition of the Use, Stockpiling, Production and Transfer of Anti-Personnel Mines and on their Destruction
Prohibition of the Use, Stockpiling, Production and Transfer of Anti-Personnel Mines and on their Destruction
Q570224.blurb: The Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention is adopted.

Q570456.name: Battle of Warsaw
