Q570456.blurb: November uprising: The Battle of Warsaw effectively ends the Polish insurrection.

Q570841.name: Battle of Buzenval
Q570841.blurb: Franco-Prussian War: In the Siege of Paris, Prussia wins the Battle of St. Quentin. Meanwhile, the French attempt to break the siege in the Battle of Buzenval will end unsuccessfully the following day.

Q570919.name: Battle of Coulmiers
Q570919.blurb: The Battle of Coulmiers ends in a Pyrrhic victory for the French army during the Franco-German War of 1870.

Q571675.name: Battle of Piacenza
Q571675.blurb: War of the Austrian Succession: Austria and Sardinia defeat a Franco-Spanish army at the Battle of Piacenza.

Q571764.name: 1945 Bombing of Prague
Q571764.blurb: World War II: Navigational error leads to the mistaken bombing of Prague, Czechoslovakia by a United States Army Air Forces squadron of B-17s assisting in the Soviet Red Army's Vistula–Oder Offensive.

Q571891.name: 2011 Sikkim earthquake
Q571891.blurb: The 2011 Sikkim earthquake is felt across northeastern India, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and southern Tibet.

Q571893.name: 1939 German ultimatum to Lithuania
aliases: Treaty of the Cession of the Memel Territory to Germany
Q571893.blurb: Germany issued an ultimatum to Lithuania, demanding the return of the Klaipėda Region under threat of invasion.

Q572368.name: Oppau explosion
Q572368.blurb: A storage silo in Oppau, Germany, explodes, killing 500–600 people.

Q572676.name: St Nazaire Raid
Q572676.blurb: World War II: A British combined force permanently disables the Louis Joubert Lock in Saint-Nazaire in order to keep the German battleship Tirpitz away from the mid-ocean convoy lanes.

Q573358.name: Battle of Teugen-Hausen
Q573358.blurb: War of the Fifth Coalition: French general Louis-Nicolas Davout defeated an Austrian force in  Lower Bavaria, allowing him to rejoin the main French army.

Q573912.name: Christianization of Poland
Q573912.blurb: Mieszko I, the ruler of Poland, converted to Christianity, an event considered to be the founding of the Polish state.

Q573972.name: Battle of Rossbach
Q573972.blurb: Seven Years' War: Frederick the Great defeats the allied armies of France and the Holy Roman Empire at the Battle of Rossbach.

Q574321.name: Upper Silesia plebiscite
Q574321.blurb: The Upper Silesia plebiscite, mandated by the Versailles Treaty to determine a section of the border between Weimar Germany and Poland, is held.

Q574341.name: 2001 anthrax attacks
Q574341.blurb: Five letters containing anthrax spores were mailed to various media outlets in the United States.

Q574543.name: Operation Orchard
Q574543.blurb: Israel executes the air strike Operation Orchard to destroy a nuclear reactor in Syria.

Q574556.name: Anti-Secession Law
Q574556.blurb: Around 200,000 to 300,000 Taiwanese demonstrate in Taipei in opposition to the Anti-Secession Law of  China.

Q575347.name: King Michael's Coup
Q575347.blurb: World War II: King Michael of Romania dismisses the pro-Nazi government of Marshal Antonescu, who is later arrested. Romania switches sides from the Axis to the Allies.

Q575755.name: Schweinfurt–Regensburg mission
Q575755.blurb: World War II: The U.S. Eighth Air Force suffers the loss of 60 bombers on the Schweinfurt–Regensburg mission.

Q575834.name: 1975 Australian constitutional crisis
Q575834.blurb: The Australian Coalition sparks a constitutional crisis when they vote to defer funding for the government's annual budget.

Q575924.name: Battle of Saint-Mathieu
Q575924.blurb: The naval Battle of Saint-Mathieu, during the War of the League of Cambrai, sees the simultaneous destruction of the Breton ship La Cordelière and the English ship The Regent.

Q576015.name: St-Hilaire train disaster
Q576015.blurb: At least 99 people, mostly German and Polish immigrants, are killed in Canada's worst railway disaster after a train fails to stop for an open drawbridge and plunges into the Rivière Richelieu near St-Hilaire, Quebec.

Q576292.name: Fourth Anglo-Dutch War
Q576292.blurb: Fourth Anglo-Dutch War: Captain Thomas Shirley opens his expedition against Dutch colonial outposts on the Gold Coast of Africa (present-day Ghana).

Q576338.name: Japanese invasions of Korea
Q576338.blurb: Japanese invasion of Korea: Approximately 3,000 Joseon defenders led by general Kwŏn Yul successfully repel more than 30,000 Japanese forces in the Siege of Haengju.

Q576364.name: Revolt of the Batavi
Q576364.blurb: Batavian rebellion: The Batavians in Germania Inferior (Netherlands) revolt under the leadership of Gaius Julius Civilis.

Q576774.name: Battle of Carentan
Q576774.blurb: World War II: Battle of Carentan: American paratroopers of the 101st Airborne Division secure the town of Carentan, Normandy, France.

Q577081.name: Battle of Camperdown
Q577081.blurb: The Royal Navy decisively defeats the Batavian Navy at Camperdown during the French Revolutionary Wars.

Q578179.name: 1963 Skopje earthquake
Q578179.blurb: An earthquake in Skopje, Yugoslavia (present-day North Macedonia) leaves 1,100 dead.

Q578858.name: Lena massacre
Q578858.blurb: Russian troops open fire on striking goldfield workers in northeast Siberia, killing at least 150.

Q579159.name: Powder Alarm
Q579159.blurb: Massachusetts Bay colonists rise up in the bloodless Powder Alarm.

Q579179.name: Halabja massacre
Q579179.blurb: Halabja chemical attack: The Kurdish town of Halabja in Iraq is attacked with a mix of poison gas and nerve agents on the orders of Saddam Hussein, killing 5,000 people and injuring about 10,000 people.

Q579691.name: Heidi Game
Q579691.blurb: Viewers of the Raiders–Jets football game in the eastern United States are denied the opportunity to watch its exciting finish when NBC broadcasts Heidi instead, prompting changes to sports broadcasting in the U.S.

Q579971.name: Battle of Lake George
Q579971.blurb: French and Indian War: Battle of Lake George.

Q580021.name: Battle of Caldera Bay
Q580021.blurb: Chilean Civil War: The ironclad Blanco Encalada is sunk at Caldera Bay by torpedo boats.

Q580343.name: United Airlines Flight 232
Q580343.blurb: United Airlines Flight 232 crashes in Sioux City, Iowa, killing 111.

Q580651.name: Battle of Glorieta Pass
Q580651.blurb: American Civil War: In the Battle of Glorieta Pass, Union forces stop the Confederate invasion of the New Mexico Territory. The battle began on March 26.

Q580867.name: Space Shuttle Columbia disaster
Q580867.blurb: Space Shuttle Columbia disintegrated during the reentry of mission STS-107 into the Earth's atmosphere, killing all seven astronauts aboard.

Q581401.name: Battle of Blore Heath
Q581401.blurb: The Battle of Blore Heath, the first major battle of the English Wars of the Roses, is won by the Yorkists.

Q582584.name: First Anglo-Sikh War
aliases: Events leading to the First Anglo-Sikh War
Q582584.blurb: First Anglo-Sikh War: Battle of Sobraon: British defeat Sikhs in the final battle of the war.

Q582613.name: Livonian campaign of Stephen Báthory
Q582613.blurb: Livonian campaign of Stephen Báthory begins.

Q582706.name: Israeli settlement
aliases: Illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank
Illegal settlements in the West Bank
Israeli settlements in the West Bank
Israeli settlers in the Palestinian territories
Jewish settlers in the West Bank
Q582706.blurb: The first forced evacuation of settlers, as part of Israeli disengagement from Gaza, starts.

Q582997.name: Ufa train disaster
Q582997.blurb: Ufa train disaster: A natural gas explosion near Ufa, Russia, kills 575 as two trains passing each other throw sparks near a leaky pipeline.

Q583937.name: Santa María School massacre
Q583937.blurb: The Chilean Army commits a massacre of at least 2,000 striking saltpeter miners in Iquique, Chile.

Q584047.name: Battle of Kleidion
Q584047.blurb: Byzantine–Bulgarian wars: Battle of Kleidion: Byzantine emperor Basil II inflicts a decisive defeat on the Bulgarian army, and his subsequent treatment of 15,000 prisoners reportedly causes Tsar Samuil of Bulgaria to die of a heart attack less than three months later, on October 6.

Q584131.name: Dana Air Flight 992
Q584131.blurb: A plane carrying 153 people crashes in a residential neighborhood in Lagos, Nigeria, killing everyone on board plus six people on the ground.

Q584178.name: June 1990 Mineriad
Q584178.blurb: First day of the June 1990 Mineriad in Romania. At least 240 strikers and students are arrested or killed in the chaos ensuing from the first post-Ceaușescu elections.

Q584613.name: 2011 Lorca earthquake
Q584613.blurb: An earthquake of magnitude 5.1 hits Lorca, Spain.

Q584617.name: Treaty of London
Q584617.blurb: The Treaty of London is signed, ending the First Balkan War between the Balkan allies and the Ottoman Empire. The Ottomans cede all their European territories west of a straight line between Enos and Media and Albania becomes an independent nation.

Q585295.name: 1998 FIFA World Cup Final
aliases: Final of the 1998 FIFA World Cup
Q585295.blurb: France defeated the defending champions Brazil 3–0 to win their first FIFA World Cup title.

Q585962.name: Civil Rights Act of 1964
aliases: Act to enforce the constitutional right to vote, to confer jurisdiction upon the district courts of the United States to provide injunctive relief against discrimination in public accomodations, constitutional rights in public facilities ...
An Act to enforce the constitutional right to vote ...
United States Civil Rights Act of 1964
United States Laws, Statutes, etc. Civil Rights Act of 1964
Title I of the Civil Rights Act of 1964
Title II of the Civil Rights Act of 1964
Title III of the Civil Rights Act of 1964
Title IV of the Civil Rights Act of 1964
Title IX of the Civil Rights Act of 1964
Title V of the Civil Rights Act of 1964
Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964
Title VII of the Civil Rights Act
Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964
Title VIII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964
Title X of the Civil Rights Act of 1964
Title XI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964
Q585962.blurb: The Civil Rights Act of 1964 is approved after surviving an 83-day filibuster in the United States Senate.

Q586082.name: February strike
Q586082.blurb: The outlawed Communist Party of the Netherlands organises a general strike in German-occupied Amsterdam to protest against Nazi persecution of Dutch Jews.

Q586189.name: Battle of Powick Bridge
Q586189.blurb: First English Civil War: The Battle of Powick Bridge, the first engagement between the primary field armies of the Royalists and the Parliamentarians, ends in a Royalist victory.

Q586204.name: Battle of Malakoff
Q586204.blurb: Crimean War: The French assault the tower of Malakoff, leading to the capture of Sevastopol.

Q586385.name: Battle of Santiago
Q586385.blurb: One of the most violent football matches took place at the World Cup as Chile defeated Italy in a group match.

Q586755.name: RDS-1
aliases: First successful Russian test of an atomic bomb
Q586755.blurb: The Soviet Union conducted its first nuclear weapons test, detonating the 22-kiloton RDS-1.

Q586992.name: Battle of Barrosa
Q586992.blurb: Peninsular War: At the Battle of Barrosa, Anglo-Iberian forces trying to lift the Siege of Cádiz defeated a French attack but could not break the siege itself.

Q587095.name: Battle of Montaperti
Q587095.blurb: The Sienese Ghibellines, supported by the forces of Manfred, King of Sicily, defeat the Florentine Guelphs at Montaperti.

Q587127.name: 1976 Friuli earthquake
Q587127.blurb: The 6.5 Mw Friuli earthquake affects Northern Italy with a maximum Mercalli intensity of X (Extreme), leaving 900–978 dead and 1,700–2,400 injured.

Q587151.name: British invasions of the River Plate
aliases: British invasions of the Rio de la Plata
British invasions of the Río de la Plata
Q587151.blurb: Second British invasion of the Río de la Plata; John Whitelocke lands at Ensenada on an attempt to recapture Buenos Aires and is defeated by the locals.

Q588287.name: First United Front
Q588287.blurb: Shanghai massacre of 1927: Chiang Kai-shek orders the Chinese Communist Party members executed in Shanghai, ending the First United Front.

Q588300.name: New England's Dark Day
Q588300.blurb: New England's Dark Day, an unusual darkening of the day sky, is observed over the New England states and parts of Canada.

Q588774.name: Battle of Dong Xoai
Q588774.blurb: Fighting began between the Viet Cong and the Army of the Republic of Vietnam in the Battle of Đồng Xoài, one of the largest battles in the Vietnam War.

Q589276.name: Slavery Convention
aliases: Convention to suppress the slave trade and slavery (1926)
Q589276.blurb: The international Convention to Suppress the Slave Trade and Slavery is first signed.

Q589285.name: Battle of Tondibi
Q589285.blurb: At the Battle of Tondibi in Mali, Moroccan forces of the Saadi dynasty, led by Judar Pasha, defeat the Songhai Empire, despite being outnumbered by at least five to one.

Q589318.name: Battle of Falkirk
Q589318.blurb: Wars of Scottish Independence: Battle of Falkirk: King Edward I of England and his longbowmen defeat William Wallace and his Scottish schiltrons outside the town of Falkirk.

Q589673.name: Iran hostage crisis
aliases: 1979 seizure of the U.S. Embassy in Tehran
Timeline of the Iran hostage crisis negotiations
Q589673.blurb: Iran hostage crisis: United States and Iranian officials sign an agreement to release 52 American hostages after 14 months of captivity.

Q589853.name: 551 Beirut earthquake
Q589853.blurb: A major earthquake strikes Beirut, triggering a devastating tsunami that affects the coastal towns of Byzantine Phoenicia, causing thousands of deaths.

Q590195.name: Battle of Ngomano
Q590195.blurb: World War I: German forces defeat Portuguese army of about 1,200 at Negomano on the border of modern-day Mozambique and Tanzania.

Q591045.name: Goiânia accident
Q591045.blurb: Goiânia accident: A radioactive object is stolen from an abandoned hospital in Goiânia, Brazil, contaminating many people in the following weeks and causing some to die from radiation poisoning.

Q592069.name: Battle of Sellenberk
Q592069.blurb: Michael the Brave, Prince of Wallachia, defeats the Army of Andrew Báthory in the Battle of Șelimbăr, leading to the first recorded unification of the Romanian people.

Q592091.name: Battle of Salta
Q592091.blurb: Manuel Belgrano defeats the royalist army of Pío de Tristán during the Battle of Salta.

Q592354.name: same-sex marriage in Australia
aliases: Recognition of same-sex relationships in Australia
Q592354.blurb: Same-sex marriage in Australia became legal as the Marriage Amendment (Definition and Religious Freedoms) Act 2017 came into effect.

Q592810.name: Sverdlovsk anthrax leak
Q592810.blurb: A Soviet bio-warfare laboratory at Sverdlovsk accidentally releases airborne anthrax spores, killing 66 plus an unknown amount of livestock.

Q593024.name: Sétif and Guelma massacre
aliases: Massacres de Sétif, Guelma et Kherrata
Q593024.blurb: Hundreds of Algerian civilians are killed by French Army soldiers in the Sétif massacre.

Q593045.name: Battle of Berestechko
Q593045.blurb: The Battle of Berestechko between Poland and Ukraine starts.

Q593267.name: Fall of Tenochtitlan
Q593267.blurb: After an extended siege, forces led by Spanish conquistador Hernán Cortés capture Tlatoani Cuauhtémoc and conquer the Aztec capital of Tenochtitlan.

Q593307.name: 2005 Lake Tanganyika earthquake
Q593307.blurb: The 6.8 Mw Lake Tanganyika earthquake shakes the eastern provinces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo with a maximum Mercalli intensity of X (Extreme), killing six people.

Q593355.name: Treaty of Alcáçovas
Q593355.blurb: The Treaty of Alcáçovas is signed by the Catholic Monarchs of Castile and Aragon on one side and Afonso V and his son, Prince John of Portugal.

Q593774.name: 1953 Iranian coup d'état
Q593774.blurb: Cold War: The CIA and MI6 help to overthrow the government of Mohammad Mosaddegh in Iran and reinstate the Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi.

Q595321.name: Singing Revolution
Q595321.blurb: Singing Revolution: The Soviet economic blockade of Lithuania (pictured) was lifted when the Lithuanian parliament agreed to suspend the effects of their act to re-establish Lithuania as a state.

Q595545.name: Rákóczi’s War of Independence
Q595545.blurb: Rákóczi's War of Independence: The Habsburg Empire and Denmark win a military victory over the Kurucs from Hungary in the Battle of Zsibó.

Q595982.name: 1958 Canadian federal election
Q595982.blurb: In the Canadian federal election, the Progressive Conservatives, led by John Diefenbaker, win the largest percentage of seats in Canadian history, with 208 seats of 265.

Q596416.name: World Chess Championship 1972
Q596416.blurb: The first game of the World Chess Championship 1972 between challenger Bobby Fischer and defending champion Boris Spassky starts.

Q596667.name: 1944 United States presidential election
Q596667.blurb: Franklin D. Roosevelt is elected for a record fourth term as President of the United States.

Q597506.name: First Partition of Poland
aliases: First Partition of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
First Partition of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth
Q597506.blurb: First Partition of Poland: The representatives of Austria, Prussia, and Russia sign three bilateral conventions condemning the "anarchy" of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth and imputing to the three powers "ancient and legitimate rights" to the territories of the Commonwealth. The conventions allow each of the three great powers to annex a part of the Commonwealth, which they proceed to do over the course of the following two months.

Q597533.name: German–Polish Wars
Q597533.blurb: Henry II, Holy Roman Emperor, and Bolesław I, the Piast ruler of Poland, signed the Peace of Bautzen to end the German–Polish War.

Q598069.name: Battle of Homildon Hill
Q598069.blurb: Battle of Homildon Hill: An invading Scottish army under Murdoch Stewart, Duke of Albany and Archibald, Earl Douglas is decimated by a contingent of 500 English archers under the command of George, Earl of March and Henry Percy, 1st Earl of Northumberland.

Q598090.name: Battle of Maloyaroslavets
Q598090.blurb: Napoleonic Wars: The Battle of Maloyaroslavets takes place near Moscow.

Q598261.name: Battle of Tricamarum
Q598261.blurb: Byzantines led by Belisarius defeated the Vandal King Gelimer at the Battle of Tricamarum, completing the "Reconquest of North Africa" under Byzantine Emperor Justinian I.

Q598852.name: 2008 Paraguayan general election
Q598852.blurb: Fernando Lugo became the first candidate not from the Colorado Party candidate to be elected President of Paraguay in 61 years.

Q598854.name: Statuto Albertino
Q598854.blurb: Carlo Alberto di Savoia signs the Statuto Albertino that will later represent the first constitution of the Regno d'Italia.

Q598887.name: French Constitution of 1793
Q598887.blurb: The first Republican constitution in France is adopted.

Q599348.name: 1993 Big Bayou Canot train wreck
Q599348.blurb: A barge strikes a railroad bridge near Mobile, Alabama, causing the deadliest train wreck in Amtrak history. Forty-seven passengers are killed.

Q600016.name: Battle of Jargeau
Q600016.blurb: Hundred Years' War: Start of the Battle of Jargeau.

Q600068.name: Centennial Olympic Park bombing
Q600068.blurb: In Atlanta, United States, a pipe bomb explodes at Centennial Olympic Park during the 1996 Summer Olympics.

Q600131.name: Maxi Trial
Q600131.blurb: The Italian prosecuting magistrate Antonino Scopelliti is murdered by the 'Ndrangheta on behalf of the Sicilian Mafia while preparing the government's case in the final appeal of the Maxi Trial.

Q600609.name: Battle of Durbe
Q600609.blurb: The Livonian Order suffers its greatest defeat in the 13th century in the Battle of Durbe against the Grand Duchy of Lithuania.

Q600836.name: Jokela school shooting
Q600836.blurb: The Jokela school shooting in Jokela, Tuusula, Finland, takes place, resulting in the death of nine people.

Q601359.name: Battle of Fort Donelson
Q601359.blurb: American Civil War: General Ulysses S. Grant captures Fort Donelson, Tennessee.

Q603134.name: 1990 Manjil–Rudbar earthquake
Q603134.blurb: The 7.4 Mw Manjil–Rudbar earthquake affects northern Iran with a maximum Mercalli intensity of X (Extreme), killing 35,000–50,000, and injuring 60,000–105,000.

Q604175.name: Battle of Elli
Q604175.blurb: First Balkan War: The Royal Hellenic Navy defeats the Ottoman Navy at the Battle of Elli.

Q604185.name: Battle of Lemnos
Q604185.blurb: First Balkan War: The Battle of Lemnos begins; Greek admiral Pavlos Kountouriotis forces the Turkish fleet to retreat to its base within the Dardanelles, from which it did not venture for the rest of the war.

Q604428.name: OSIRIS-REx
aliases: Origins Spectral Interpretation Resource Identification and Security-Regolith Explorer
Origins, Spectral Interpretation, Resource Identification, Security, Regolith Explorer
Origins Spectral Interpretation Resource Identification Security Regolith Explorer
The Origins Spectral Interpretation Resource Identification Security Regolith Explorer spacecraft
Q604428.blurb: NASA launches OSIRIS-REx, its first asteroid sample return mission. The probe visited 101955 Bennu and returned with samples in September 2023.

Q604739.name: Siege of Zara
Q604739.blurb: Fourth Crusade: The Siege of Zara, the first attack on a Catholic city by Catholic crusaders, began in present-day Zadar, Croatia.

Q604897.name: Battle of Dien Bien Phu
aliases: The Battle of Dien Bien Phu
Q604897.blurb: The Battle of Điện Biên Phủ begins with an artillery barrage by Viet Minh forces under Võ Nguyên Giáp; Viet Minh victory led to the end of the First Indochina War and French withdrawal from Vietnam.

Q604938.name: Convention of Peking
aliases: Convention of Peace and Friendship between Great Britain and China
Convention of Peace between Her Majesty and the Emperor of China
Q604938.blurb: Convention of Peking: The Second Opium War formally comes to a close, with Qing China ceding Kowloon in perpetuity to the victorious British Empire.

Q605321.name: Battle of Panipat
Q605321.blurb: The last ruler of the Lodi dynasty, Ibrahim Lodi, is defeated and killed by Babur in the First Battle of Panipat.

Q605977.name: War of the Fourth Coalition
aliases: The War of the Fourth Coalition
Q605977.blurb: War of the Fourth Coalition: Napoleon decisively defeats Prussia at the Battle of Jena–Auerstedt.

Q606081.name: 1989 Sudanese coup d'état
Q606081.blurb: A coup d'état in Sudan deposes the democratically elected government of Prime Minister Sadiq al-Mahdi and President Ahmed al-Mirghani.

Q606132.name: Spam
Q606132.blurb: The Hormel Foods Corporation introduced Spam, the canned precooked meat product that would eventually enter into pop culture, folklore, and urban legend.

Q606621.name: Siege of Szigetvár
Q606621.blurb: Ottoman–Habsburg wars: Although Ottoman forces led by Suleiman the Magnificent captured the fortress of Szigetvár in Hungary, they were forced to end their campaign to take Vienna.

Q607257.name: Eritrean War of Independence
Q607257.blurb: Eritrean War of Independence: The Nadew Command, an Ethiopian army corps in Eritrea, is attacked on three sides by military units of the Eritrean People's Liberation Front in the opening action of the Battle of Afabet.

Q608613.name: fall of the western Roman Empire
aliases: historiography of the fall of the western Roman Empire
Collapse of the Western Roman Empire
Decline of the Western Roman Empire
Fall of the Roman Empire in Europe
Liquidation of the Western Roman Empire
The Fall of the Roman Empire
Q608613.blurb: Romulus Augustulus is deposed when Odoacer proclaims himself "King of Italy", thus ending the Western Roman Empire.

Q608727.name: Battle of Baekgang
Q608727.blurb: Silla–Tang armies crush the Baekje restoration attempt and force Yamato Japan to withdraw from Korea in the Battle of Baekgang.

Q609030.name: Battle of Peleliu
Q609030.blurb: World War II:  The Battle of Peleliu begins as the United States Marine Corps' 1st Marine Division and the United States Army's 81st Infantry Division hit White and Orange beaches under heavy fire from Japanese infantry and artillery.

Q609510.name: Ethnic cleansing of Georgians in Sukhumi
Q609510.blurb: The Sukhumi massacre takes place in Abkhazia.

Q609541.name: 1975 Australian federal election
Q609541.blurb: Australian constitutional crisis of 1975: Australian Governor-General Sir John Kerr dismisses the government of Gough Whitlam, appoints Malcolm Fraser as caretaker Prime Minister and announces a general election to be held in early December.

Q609836.name: Portuguese Colonial War
aliases: Economic impact of the Portuguese Colonial War
Q609836.blurb: The Angolan War of Independence and the greater Portuguese Colonial War begin.

Q610156.name: 1986 FIFA World Cup Final
Q610156.blurb: The Argentina national football team wins the FIFA World Cup held in Mexico after defeating the West Germany national football team by a score of 3–2 in the final at the Estadio Azteca.

Q610242.name: Battle of Rennell Island
Q610242.blurb: World War II: The first day of the Battle of Rennell Island, USS Chicago (CA-29) is torpedoed and heavily damaged by Japanese bombers.

Q610272.name: Geneva Convention of 1864
aliases: Geneva Convention for the Amelioration of the Condition of the Wounded and Sick in Armed Forces in the Field
Geneva Convention on the Wounded and Sick in Armed Forces in the Field
Convention for the Amelioration of the Condition of the Wounded in Armies in the Field
Q610272.blurb: Twelve nations sign the First Geneva Convention, establishing the rules of protection of the victims of armed conflicts.

Q610328.name: Battle of Castiglione
Q610328.blurb: The Battle of Castiglione in Napoleon's first Italian campaigns of the French Revolutionary Wars results in a French victory.

Q610851.name: 1947 Jerusalem riots
Q610851.blurb: Jerusalem Riots of 1947: Arabs riot in Jerusalem in response to the United Nations Partition Plan for Palestine.

Q611089.name: Siege of Tobruk
Q611089.blurb: World War II: German and Italian forces attack Tobruk, Libya.

Q612086.name: USS Cole bombing
Q612086.blurb: The USS Cole, a US Navy destroyer, is badly damaged by two al-Qaeda suicide bombers, killing 17 crew members and wounding at least 39.

Q612176.name: Battle of Alcolea
Q612176.blurb: The Battle of Alcolea causes Queen Isabella II of Spain to flee to France.

Q612396.name: Thai Airways International Flight 261
Q612396.blurb: Thai Airways Flight 261 crashes near Surat Thani Airport, killing 101. The pilot flying the Airbus A310-200 is thought to have suffered spatial disorientation.

Q612577.name: Treaty of Tientsin
Q612577.blurb: The Second Opium War finally ends at the Convention of Peking with the ratification of the Treaty of Tientsin, an unequal treaty.

Q612739.name: Operation Eagle Claw
Q612739.blurb: Eight U.S. servicemen die in Operation Eagle Claw as they attempt to end the Iran hostage crisis.

Q612741.name: United States National Forest
Q612741.blurb: El Yunque National Forest in Puerto Rico becomes part of the United States National Forest System as the Luquillo Forest Reserve.

Q613025.name: Independent Air Flight 1851
Q613025.blurb: Independent Air Flight 1851 strikes Pico Alto mountain while on approach to Santa Maria Airport in the Azores, killing all 144 passengers on board.

Q613291.name: Stresa Front
Q613291.blurb: Stresa Front: Opening of the conference between the British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald, the Italian Prime Minister Benito Mussolini and the French Minister for Foreign Affairs Pierre Laval to condemn the German violations of the Treaty of Versailles.

Q613432.name: Granville rail disaster
Q613432.blurb: Australia's worst rail disaster occurs at Granville, Sydney, killing 83.

Q613478.name: Battle of Djerba
Q613478.blurb: The Ottoman naval forces inflict a defeat on a Spanish fleet in the battle of Djerba. This marks the highpoint of Ottoman naval dominance in the Mediterranean, which starts declining five years later after the failed siege of Malta.

Q615020.name: EAS Airlines Flight 4226
Q615020.blurb: One hundred three people are killed and 51 are injured in a plane crash near Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport in Kano, Nigeria.

Q615231.name: 1980s oil glut
Q615231.blurb: Ronald Reagan lifts remaining domestic petroleum price and allocation controls in the United States, helping to end the 1979 energy crisis and begin the 1980s oil glut.

Q615324.name: First Battle of the Isonzo
Q615324.blurb: World War I:  The First Battle of the Isonzo between Italy and Austria-Hungary comes to an end.

Q616109.name: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo
aliases: Treaty of Peace, Friendship, Limits and Settlement between the United States of America and the Mexican Republic
Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo Act of 1851
Q616109.blurb: The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo is ratified by the United States Senate, ending the Mexican–American War.

Q616146.name: Croatian Spring
aliases: 1971 League of Communists of Yugoslavia Karađorđevo meeting
Q616146.blurb: Purge of Croatian Spring leaders starts in Yugoslavia at the meeting of the League of Communists at the Karađorđevo estate.

Q616307.name: Indian massacre of 1622
aliases: 1622 opechanconough surpise attack on virginian settlements
Q616307.blurb: Jamestown massacre: Algonquians kill 347 English settlers around Jamestown, Virginia, a third of the colony's population, during the Second Anglo-Powhatan War.

Q616846.name: Anglo-Spanish War
Q616846.blurb: Anglo-Spanish War: The United Kingdom captured Havana after a five-week siege, holding it until the Treaty of Paris the following year.

Q616939.name: Anglo-Egyptian War
Q616939.blurb: Anglo-Egyptian War: The Battle of Tel el-Kebir is fought.

Q616985.name: Szczekociny rail crash
Q616985.blurb: Two passenger trains collided near Szczekociny, Poland, resulting in 16 deaths and 58 injuries.

Q617263.name: Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1814
Q617263.blurb: The Convention of London, a treaty between the United Kingdom and the United Netherlands, is signed in London, England.

Q617333.name: Franco-Spanish War
Q617333.blurb: Franco-Spanish War: Turenne and the French army win a decisive victory over the Spanish at the battle of the Dunes.

Q617409.name: Argentine War of Independence
aliases: Guerra de Independencia de la Argentina
Q617409.blurb: Argentine War of Independence: José de San Martín and the Mounted Grenadiers Regiment defeated Spanish royalist forces in the Battle of San Lorenzo (depicted).

Q617411.name: Apalachin Meeting
Q617411.blurb: The "Apalachin meeting" in rural Tioga County in upstate New York is raided by law enforcement; many high-level Mafia figures are arrested while trying to flee.

Q617782.name: Fourth Anglo-Mysore War
Q617782.blurb: Fourth Anglo-Mysore War: The Battle of Seringapatam: The siege of Seringapatam ends when the city is invaded and Tipu Sultan killed by the besieging British army, under the command of General George Harris.

Q617827.name: Apache Wars
Q617827.blurb: Geronimo, Apache warrior, surrenders to the U.S. Army, ending the main phase of the Apache Wars.

Q618048.name: 1944 Bulgarian coup d'état
Q618048.blurb: World War II: The Fatherland Front takes power in Bulgaria through a military coup in the capital and armed rebellion in the country. A new pro-Soviet government is established.

Q618127.name: 1824 United States presidential election
Q618127.blurb: United States presidential election: Since no candidate received a majority of the total electoral college votes in the election, the United States House of Representatives is given the task of deciding the winner in accordance with the Twelfth Amendment to the United States Constitution.

Q618331.name: October 2012 Beirut bombing
Q618331.blurb: A bomb explosion kills eight people and injures 110 more in Lebanon.

Q618979.name: Victory over Japan Day
aliases: Dia da Vitória sobre o Japão
Dia da Vitória sobre o Japão (1945)
Surrender of the Japanese in the Dutch East Indies
Q618979.blurb: Ten days after World War II ends with Japan announcing its surrender, armed supporters of the Chinese Communist Party kill U.S. intelligence officer John Birch, regarded by some of the American right as the first victim of the Cold War.

Q619030.name: Battle of the Bagradas River
Q619030.blurb: Caesar's Civil War: Forces loyal to Julius Caesar led by Gaius Scribonius Curio were defeated by Pompeian Republicans under Publius Attius Varus and King Juba I of Numidia.

Q619049.name: Battle of Andernach
Q619049.blurb: Battle of Andernach: Otto I, Holy Roman Emperor, crushes a rebellion against his rule, by a coalition of Eberhard of Franconia and other Frankish dukes.

Q619749.name: Kurdistan Workers' Party insurgency
aliases: 2007 Turkish offensive on Iraqi territories against Kurdish rebels
Human rights abuses during the Kurdish-Turkish conflict
Human rights abuses during the Kurdish–Turkish conflict
Human rights abuses in the Kurdish-Turkish conflict
Human rights abuses in the Kurdish–Turkish conflict
Q619749.blurb: Kurdish–Turkish conflict: Acting on information that Kurdish militants were crossing the border from Iraqi territory, two Turkish F-16 jets fired at a group of villagers, killing 34 people.

Q620215.name: Battle of Mont Saint-Quentin
Q620215.blurb: World War I: Start of the Battle of Mont Saint-Quentin, a successful assault by the Australian Corps during the Hundred Days Offensive.

Q620244.name: Battle of Bentonville
Q620244.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Bentonville begins. By the end of the battle two days later, Confederate forces had retreated from Four Oaks, North Carolina.

Q620585.name: Battle of Mortimer's Cross
Q620585.blurb: Wars of the Roses: The Battle of Mortimer's Cross results in the death of Owen Tudor.

Q620735.name: Russo-Georgian War
aliases: Public investigation of the Ossetian War
Q620735.blurb: The start of the Russo-Georgian War over the territory of South Ossetia.

Q620854.name: Treaty of Tartu
Q620854.blurb: Finland and Soviet Russia sign the Treaty of Tartu, exchanging some territories.

Q620965.name: coup of 18 Brumaire
Q620965.blurb: Napoleon Bonaparte leads the Coup of 18 Brumaire ending the Directory government, and becoming First Consul of the successor Consulate Government.

Q620988.name: Israel–Jordan Treaty of Peace
aliases: Treaty of Peace Between the State of Israel and the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan
Q620988.blurb: Israel and Jordan signed a peace treaty, settling relations between the two countries and pledging that neither would allow its territory to become a staging ground for military strikes by a third country.

Q621676.name: Appomattox campaign
Q621676.blurb: American Civil War: The Appomattox campaign opened with the Battle of Lewis's Farm, in which the Confederate Army of Northern Virginia was forced into a series of retreats that would culminate in their surrender.

Q621827.name: 2012 Guinea-Bissau coup d'état
Q621827.blurb: The Guinea-Bissau military seized control in a coup amid a presidential election, later handing power to a transitional administration under Manuel Serifo Nhamadjo.

Q622059.name: April Uprising of 1876
Q622059.blurb: The April Uprising begins. Its suppression shocks European opinion, and Bulgarian independence becomes a condition for ending the Russo-Turkish War.

Q622354.name: Lincoln-Douglas debates
Q622354.blurb: The first of the Lincoln–Douglas debates is held in Ottawa, Illinois.

Q622365.name: Victory in Europe Day
aliases: Victory Day for World War II
Q622365.blurb: Poland's Soviet-allied Provisional Government of National Unity is formed over a month after V-E Day.

Q622495.name: The hand of God
Q622495.blurb: The famous Hand of God goal, scored by Diego Maradona in the quarter-finals of the 1986 FIFA World Cup match between Argentina and England, ignites controversy. This was later followed by the Goal of the Century. Argentina wins 2–1 and later goes on to win the World Cup.

Q622751.name: war communism
Q622751.blurb: The New Economic Policy is implemented by the Bolshevik Party in response to the economic failure as a result of war communism.

Q622762.name: N1
Q622762.blurb: The Soviet Union makes its final attempt at launching the N1 rocket.

Q622766.name: Merger Treaty
aliases: Treaty establishing a Single Council and a Single Commission of the European Communities
Q622766.blurb: Merger Treaty: The European Community is formally created out of a merger between the Common Market, the European Coal and Steel Community, and the European Atomic Energy Commission.

Q622774.name: French Revolution of 1848
Q622774.blurb: The French Revolution of 1848, which would lead to the establishment of the French Second Republic, begins.

Q622844.name: Treaty of Nagyvárad
Q622844.blurb: Treaty of Nagyvárad between Holy Roman Emperor Ferdinand I and King John Zápolya of Hungary and Croatia.

Q622946.name: Aqua Teen Hunger Force
Q622946.blurb: Emergency officials in Boston mistakenly identify battery-powered LED placards depicting characters from Aqua Teen Hunger Force as Improvised explosive devices (IEDs), causing a panic.

Q623164.name: Five Days of Milan
Q623164.blurb: Revolutions of 1848: A rebellion arises in Milan which in five days of street fighting drove Marshal Radetzky and his Austrian soldiers from the city.

Q623171.name: Sino-Vietnamese War
aliases: People's Liberation Army's withdrawal from Vietnam
Q623171.blurb: Third Indochina War: Cambodian–Vietnamese War: Phnom Penh falls to the advancing Vietnamese troops, driving out Pol Pot and the Khmer Rouge.

Q623391.name: Japan–Korea Treaty of 1876
Q623391.blurb: Japan and Korea sign the Treaty of Kangwha, which grants Japanese citizens extraterritoriality rights in Korea, opens three Korean ports to Japanese trade, and ends Korea's status as a tributary state of Qing dynasty China.

Q623429.name: Reconstruction Era
aliases: Reconstruction era of the United States
Reconstruction Era in the United States
Reconstruction during the american civil war
Reconstruction time period of the United States
The Reconstruction Era and Aftermath of the American Civil War
Q623429.blurb: Reconstruction Era: Virginia is readmitted to the Union.

Q623641.name: Coup d'état of December Twelfth
Q623641.blurb: Coup d'état of December Twelfth occurs in South Korea.

Q623994.name: Strategic Arms Limitation Talks
Q623994.blurb: SALT II is signed by the United States and the Soviet Union.

Q624137.name: Iri Station Explosion
Q624137.blurb: A munitions explosion at a train station in Iri, South Korea kills at least 56 people.

Q624154.name: Gwangju Student Independence Movement
Q624154.blurb: The Gwangju Student Independence Movement occurred.

Q624469.name: 1980 South Korean presidential election
Q624469.blurb: South Korean presidential election: After successfully staging the Coup d'état of May Seventeenth, General Chun Doo-hwan, running unopposed, has the National Conference for Unification elect him President of the Fourth Republic of Korea.

Q625151.name: electric locomotive
Q625151.blurb: The inaugural run of the Baltimore and Ohio Railroad's Royal Blue from Washington, D.C., to New York City, the first U.S. passenger train to use electric locomotives.

Q625316.name: Tangiwai disaster
Q625316.blurb: Tangiwai disaster: In New Zealand's North Island, at Tangiwai, a railway bridge is damaged by a lahar and collapses beneath a passenger train, killing 151 people.

Q625717.name: London Conference of 1832
Q625717.blurb: Greece's independence is recognized by the Treaty of London.

Q625798.name: Western Desert campaign
aliases: Second Battle of the Coast Road
Q625798.blurb: Second World War: Allied forces halted the Axis invasion of Egypt at the First Battle of El Alamein.

Q626003.name: Korean Air Flight 803
Q626003.blurb: While attempting to land at Tripoli International Airport in Libya, Korean Air Flight 803 crashes just short of the runway. Seventy-five of the 199 passengers and crew and four people on the ground are killed, in the second accident involving a DC-10 in less than two weeks, the first being United Airlines Flight 232.

Q626006.name: World War II in Yugoslavia
aliases: National Liberation War and Socialist Revolution
World War II in Kingdom of Yugoslavia
Yugoslav Front of World War II
Yugoslavian resistance during World War II
Q626006.blurb: World War II: The liberation of Yugoslavia from Axis occupation continues. Bajina Bašta in western Serbia is among the liberated cities.

Q626058.name: Battle of Karbala
Q626058.blurb: The Battle of Karbala marks the martyrdom of Husayn ibn Ali.

Q626191.name: Annexation of Goa
aliases: Annexation of Goa by the Republic of India
Q626191.blurb: India annexes Daman and Diu, part of Portuguese India.

Q626264.name: Ararat rebellion
Q626264.blurb: The Kurdish Ararat rebellion is suppressed by the Turks.

Q626796.name: Battle of Taierzhuang
Q626796.blurb: Second Sino-Japanese War: The Battle of Taierzhuang begins, resulting several weeks later in the war's first major Chinese victory over Japan.

Q627656.name: St. George's Night Uprising
Q627656.blurb: St. George's Night Uprising commences in the Duchy of Estonia.

Q628929.name: 1561 celestial phenomenon over Nuremberg
Q628929.blurb: A celestial phenomenon is reported over Nuremberg, described as an aerial battle.

Q629139.name: London, Midland and Scottish Railway
Q629139.blurb: Britain's Railways are grouped into the Big Four: LNER, GWR, SR, and LMS.

Q629485.name: 2007 Chūetsu offshore earthquake
Q629485.blurb: An earthquake of magnitude 6.8 and 6.6 aftershock occurs off the Niigata coast of Japan killing eight people, injuring at least 800 and damaging a nuclear power plant.

Q630099.name: St. Albans Raid
Q630099.blurb: American Civil War: Confederate agents based in Canada rob three banks in Saint Albans, Vermont.

Q630142.name: Battle of Nördlingen
Q630142.blurb: Thirty Years' War: The Second Battle of Nördlingen sees French forces defeating those of the Holy Roman Empire.

Q630259.name: Byzantine–Ottoman wars
Q630259.blurb: Byzantine–Ottoman wars: The heavily armed Byzantine army was defeated by Ottoman forces at the Battle of Pelekanon.

Q630781.name: Battle of Raphia
Q630781.blurb: Battle of Raphia: Ptolemy IV Philopator of Egypt defeats Antiochus III the Great of the Seleucid kingdom.

Q631163.name: Deluge
Q631163.blurb: The Deluge: Khmelnytsky Uprising: The Battle of Berestechko ends with a Polish victory.

Q631489.name: Klondike Gold Rush
aliases: Atlas of the Klondike Gold Rush
Q631489.blurb: A group including George Carmack and Skookum Jim Mason (pictured) discovered gold  near Dawson City, Canada, setting off the Klondike Gold Rush.

Q631498.name: Oklahoma Land Run of 1889
Q631498.blurb: At noon, thousands rush to claim land in the Land Rush of 1889. Within hours the cities of Oklahoma City and Guthrie are formed with populations of at least 10,000.

Q631991.name: Russo-Polish War
Q631991.blurb: Russo-Polish War (1654–67): The Russian army enters the capital of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, Vilnius, which it holds for six years.

Q632123.name: 2011 Malaysian motorcycle Grand Prix
Q632123.blurb: During the Malaysian motorcycle Grand Prix, Marco Simoncelli (pictured) collided with two other riders, resulting in his death due to serious trauma to the head, neck, and chest.

Q632741.name: Operation Rah-e-Nijat
Q632741.blurb: War in North-West Pakistan: The Pakistani Armed Forces open Operation Rah-e-Nijat against the Taliban and other Islamist rebels in the South Waziristan area of the Federally Administered Tribal Areas.

Q632787.name: Insurgency in the Maghreb
Q632787.blurb: Insurgency in the Maghreb: Two car bombs explode in Algiers, Algeria, one near the Supreme Constitutional Court and the other near the offices of the United Nations.

Q632926.name: Battle of Kranji
Q632926.blurb: The Imperial Japanese Army began the Battle of Kranji as part of their campaign to capture Singapore.

Q633870.name: UTair Flight 120
Q633870.blurb: UTair Flight 120 crashes after takeoff from Roshchino International Airport in Tyumen, Russia, killing 33 and injuring 10.

Q634171.name: Typhoon Tip
Q634171.blurb: Typhoon Tip becomes the largest and most intense tropical cyclone ever recorded.

Q634429.name: 1936 United States presidential election
Q634429.blurb: Franklin D. Roosevelt is reelected as President of the United States.

Q634483.name: 1888 Río de la Plata earthquake
aliases: Terremoto del Río de la Plata de 188llmmj
Q634483.blurb: The Rio de la Plata earthquake takes place.

Q634629.name: Battle of Towton
Q634629.blurb: Battle of Towton: Edward of York defeats Queen Margaret to become King Edward IV of England, bringing a temporary stop to the Wars of the Roses.

Q634839.name: Act of Abjuration
Q634839.blurb: Plakkaat van Verlatinghe (Act of Abjuration): The northern Low Countries declare their independence from the Spanish king, Philip II.

Q635051.name: Murders of White, Goodman, and Schrader
Q635051.blurb: Edgar Ray Killen is indicted for the 1964 murders of Chaney, Goodman, and Schwerner during the American Civil Rights Movement.

Q635533.name: Cambodian–Vietnamese War
aliases: Chiến dịch phản công biên giới Tây - Nam Việt Nam
Environmental impacts of the Cambodian-Vietnamese War
Environmental impacts of the Cambodian–Vietnamese War
Q635533.blurb: The Cambodian–Vietnamese War formally ended with the withdrawal of Vietnamese forces from the People's Republic of Kampuchea, a client state it had implemented to overthrow Democratic Kampuchea and the Khmer Rouge.

Q635624.name: Buddhist crisis
aliases: Buddhist crisis and military coup of 1963
Q635624.blurb: A protest against pro-Catholic discrimination during the Buddhist crisis is held outside South Vietnam's National Assembly, the first open demonstration during the eight-year presidency of Ngo Dinh Diem.

Q636264.name: Bombardment of Brussels
Q636264.blurb: French forces end the bombardment of Brussels.

Q636365.name: War of the League of Cambrai
aliases: The War of the League of Cambrai
War of the League of Cambray
Q636365.blurb: War of the League of Cambrai: Troops led by Pope Julius II captured Mirandola (depicted) after a brief siege.

Q636670.name: Battle of Peachtree Creek
Q636670.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Peachtree Creek: Near Atlanta, Georgia, Confederate forces led by General John Bell Hood unsuccessfully attack Union troops under General William T. Sherman.

Q636771.name: Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire
aliases: Spanish conquest of the Incan Empire
Q636771.blurb: Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire: Sapa Inca emperor Manco Inca Yupanqui's army began a ten-month siege of Cusco.

Q638374.name: Battle of Pälkäne
Q638374.blurb: Great Northern War: Russia defeats Sweden in the Battle of Kostianvirta in Pälkäne.

Q638530.name: Texas Revolution
Q638530.blurb: Texas Revolution: The Siege of the Alamo (prelude to the Battle of the Alamo) begins in San Antonio, Texas.

Q638587.name: Fifth Russo-Turkish War
Q638587.blurb: The Treaty of Niš is signed by the Ottoman Empire and Russia ending the Russian–Turkish War.

Q638601.name: Skirmish at Bender
Q638601.blurb: The Kalabalik or Skirmish at Bender results from the Ottoman Sultan Ahmed III's order that his unwelcome guest, King Charles XII of Sweden, be seized.

Q638761.name: Ardeatine massacre
Q638761.blurb: German troops massacre 335 Italian civilians in Rome.

Q638845.name: Treaty of The Hague
Q638845.blurb: War of the Spanish Succession: The Duke of Marlborough led Allied forces to a crucial victory at the Battle of Blenheim.

Q638850.name: Smyrniote crusades
Q638850.blurb: The lower town of Smyrna is captured by Latin Christians in response to Aydınid piracy during the Smyrniote crusades.

Q638903.name: 5 October 1910 revolution
Q638903.blurb: In a revolution in Portugal the monarchy is overthrown and a republic is declared.

Q639251.name: disappearance of Madeleine McCann
Q639251.blurb: The three-year-old British girl Madeleine McCann disappears in Praia da Luz, Portugal, starting "the most heavily reported missing-person case in modern history".

Q639285.name: Battle of Medellín
Q639285.blurb: Peninsular War: France defeats Spain in the Battle of Medellín.

Q639827.name: Siege of Damascus
Q639827.blurb: Siege of Damascus: The Rashidun Arabs under Khalid ibn al-Walid capture Damascus from the Byzantine Empire.

Q639989.name: Battle of Tolvajärvi
Q639989.blurb: Winter War: The Battle of Tolvajärvi, also known as the first major Finnish victory in the Winter War, begins.

Q640409.name: 1916 Cumberland vs. Georgia Tech football game
Q640409.blurb: Georgia Tech defeats Cumberland University 222–0 in the most lopsided college football game in American history.

Q640607.name: Overthrow of Slobodan Milošević
Q640607.blurb: Mass demonstrations in Serbia force the resignation of Slobodan Milošević.

Q640770.name: Climatic Research Unit email controversy
aliases: Climate Research University e-mail hacking incident
Climatic Research Unit e-mail hacking incident
Climatic Research Unit email hacking incident
Climatic Research Unit file release incident
Q640770.blurb: Administrators at the University of East Anglia's Climatic Research Unit discovered that their servers had been hacked, and thousands of emails and files on climate change had been stolen.

Q641064.name: Le Paradis massacre
Q641064.blurb: World War II: In the Le Paradis massacre, 99 soldiers from a Royal Norfolk Regiment unit are shot after surrendering to German troops; two survive.

Q641125.name: Battle of Bapaume
Q641125.blurb: In the Battle of Bapaume, an engagement in the Franco-Prussian War, General Louis Faidherbe's forces bring about a Prussian retreat.

Q641183.name: Battle of Kock
Q641183.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Kock is the final combat of the September Campaign in Poland.

Q641205.name: 1941 Iraqi coup d'état
Q641205.blurb: A military coup in Iraq overthrows the regime of 'Abd al-Ilah and installs Rashid Ali al-Gaylani as Prime Minister.

Q641479.name: Khmelnytsky Uprising
Q641479.blurb: The Deluge: Khmelnytsky Uprising: The Battle of Berestechko ends with a Polish victory.

Q641757.name: Battle of Oosterweel
Q641757.blurb: The Battle of Oosterweel, traditionally regarded as the start of the Eighty Years' War.

Q641898.name: Bloody Night
Q641898.blurb: The Portuguese Prime Minister and several officials are murdered in the Bloody Night coup.

Q642039.name: Banqueting House
Q642039.blurb: King Charles I, who was defeated in both the First and the Second English Civil Wars, was beheaded for high treason in front of the Banqueting House in London.

Q642117.name: Siege of Nicaea
Q642117.blurb: The Siege of Nicaea begins during the First Crusade.

Q642342.name: Scopes Trial
aliases: The State of Tennessee v. John Thomas Scopes
Scopes v. The State of Tennessee
State of Tennessee v. John Thomas Scopes
The State of Tennessee v. Scopes
Q642342.blurb: Scopes Trial: John T. Scopes is indicted for teaching human evolution in Tennessee.

Q642517.name: Battle of Champaubert
Q642517.blurb: Napoleonic Wars: The Battle of Champaubert ends in French victory over the Russians and the Prussians.

Q643015.name: 1988 United States presidential election
aliases: United States third party and independent presidential candidates, 1988
Q643015.blurb: U.S. Vice President George H. W. Bush is elected as the 41st president.

Q643925.name: War of Dagestan
Q643925.blurb: Russia begins the Second Chechen War in response to the Invasion of Dagestan by the Islamic International Peacekeeping Brigade.

Q644004.name: Battle of Wilhelmsthal
Q644004.blurb: Battle of Wilhelmsthal: The British-Hanoverian army of Ferdinand of Brunswick defeats French forces in Westphalia.

Q644021.name: Battle of Kruty
Q644021.blurb: Ukrainian–Soviet War: The Bolshevik Red Army, on its way to besiege Kyiv, is met by a small group of military students at the Battle of Kruty.

Q644161.name: 1972 United States presidential election
aliases: List of candidates in the United States presidential election, 1972
United States third party and independent presidential candidates, 1972
Q644161.blurb: United States presidential election: U.S. President Richard Nixon is re-elected in the largest landslide victory at the time.

Q644521.name: Challenger Expedition
aliases: Report on the Scientific Results of the Voyage of H.M.S. Challenger During the Years 1873-76
Report on the Scientific Results of the Voyage of H.M.S. Challenger During the Years 1873–76
Q644521.blurb: Challenger expedition: HMS Challenger, commanded by Captain George Nares, sails from Portsmouth, England.

Q644960.name: Battle of the Boyne
Q644960.blurb: Glorious Revolution: Battle of the Boyne in Ireland (as reckoned under the Julian calendar).

Q645257.name: Battle of Tucapel
Q645257.blurb: Battle of Tucapel: Mapuche rebels under Lautaro defeat the Spanish conquistadors and executes the governor of Chile, Pedro de Valdivia.

Q645288.name: Battle of the Thames
Q645288.blurb: War of 1812: The Army of the Northwest defeats a British and Native Canadian force threatening Detroit.

Q645426.name: Argentine economic crisis
Q645426.blurb: Argentine economic crisis: December riots: Riots erupt in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

Q645905.name: Battle of Cedynia
Q645905.blurb: Battle of Cedynia, the first documented victory of Polish forces, takes place.

Q645920.name: Protestation at Speyer
Q645920.blurb: Beginning of the Protestant Reformation: After the Second Diet of Speyer bans Lutheranism, a group of rulers (German: Fürst) and independent cities protest the reinstatement of the Edict of Worms.

Q645986.name: National Reorganization Process
Q645986.blurb: As the military dictatorship came to an end, Argentina's first democratic election in a decade resulted in Raúl Alfonsín being elected president.

Q646322.name: Franco-Dutch War
Q646322.blurb: Franco-Dutch War: French troops defeated Austrian and Brandenburg forces at the Battle of Turckheim (pictured) in Alsace.

Q646336.name: Second Battle of Seoul
Q646336.blurb: Korean War: United Nations troops recapture Seoul from North Korean forces.

Q646532.name: Battle of Castagnaro
Q646532.blurb: Battle of Castagnaro: Padua, led by John Hawkwood, is victorious over Giovanni Ordelaffi of Verona.

Q648304.name: Tintin in the Land of the Soviets
Q648304.blurb: Tintin in the Land of the Soviets, the first volume of The Adventures of Tintin by the Belgian cartoonist Hergé, began serialisation.

Q648413.name: Murder of Stephen Lawrence
Q648413.blurb: Eighteen-year-old Stephen Lawrence is murdered in a racially motivated attack while waiting for a bus in Well Hall, Eltham.

Q648535.name: Battle of Patay
Q648535.blurb: Charles VII's army defeats an English army under John Talbot at the Battle of Patay during the Hundred Years' War. The English lost 2,200 men, over half their army, crippling their efforts during this segment of the war.

Q649599.name: Treaty of 1818
aliases: Convention respecting fisheries, boundary and the restoration of slaves
Q649599.blurb: The Convention of 1818 is signed between the United States and the United Kingdom, which settles the Canada–United States border on the 49th parallel for most of its length.

Q649682.name: Windscale fire
Q649682.blurb: The Windscale fire results in Britain's worst nuclear accident.

Q650082.name: Siege of La Rochelle
Q650082.blurb: French Wars of Religion: Siege of La Rochelle ends.

Q650357.name: 1887 Diano Marina earthquake
Q650357.blurb: The French Riviera is hit by a large earthquake, killing around 2,000.

Q650411.name: Battle of Cecora
Q650411.blurb: Polish–Ottoman War: The Ottoman Empire defeats the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth during the Battle of Cecora.

Q650507.name: Battle of Fujigawa
Q650507.blurb: The Battle of Fujigawa: Minamoto forces (30,000 men) under Minamoto no Yoritomo defeat Taira no Koremori during a night attack near the Fuji River but he escapes safely with the routed army.

Q650567.name: Third Siege of Missolonghi
Q650567.blurb: The 10,500 inhabitants of the Greek town of Missolonghi begin leaving the town after a year's siege by Turkish forces. Very few of them survive.

Q650979.name: German–Polish Border Treaty
aliases: Treaty between the Federal Republic of Germany and the Republic of Poland on the confirmation of the frontier between them
Q650979.blurb: After German reunification, the Federal Republic of Germany and Poland sign a treaty confirming the Oder–Neisse line as the border between Germany and Poland.

Q651919.name: Battle of Culloden
Q651919.blurb: The Battle of Culloden is fought between the French-supported Jacobites and the British Hanoverian forces commanded by William Augustus, Duke of Cumberland, in Scotland.

Q652271.name: Siege of Haarlem
Q652271.blurb: Eighty Years' War: The Siege of Haarlem ends after seven months.

Q652285.name: Indo-Pakistani War of 1947–1948
aliases: Liberation of Jammu and Kashmir by India
Q652285.blurb: United Nations cease-fire takes effect in Kashmir from one minute before midnight. War between India and Pakistan stops accordingly.

Q652320.name: Battle of Toulouse
Q652320.blurb: Odo of Aquitaine defeats the Moors in the Battle of Toulouse.

Q652669.name: Cyclone Mahina
Q652669.blurb: Cyclone Mahina sweeps in north of Cooktown, Queensland, with a 12 metres (39 ft) wave that reaches up to 5 kilometres (3.1 mi) inland, killing over 300.

Q653112.name: Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip
aliases: 2010 easing of the blockade of the Gaza Strip
Commercial goods allowed/banned for import into Gaza
Economic effects of the blockade of the Gaza Strip
Economic impact of the blockade of the Gaza Strip
Goods allowed or banned for import into Gaza
Goods allowed/banned for import into Gaza
List of commercial goods allowed for import into Gaza
List of commercial goods allowed/banned for import into Gaza
The 2007 Blockade of the Gaza Strip
The 2007-2009 blockade of the Gaza Strip
The 2007–2009 blockade of the Gaza Strip
Q653112.blurb: Israeli Shayetet 13 commandos board the Gaza Freedom Flotilla while still in international waters trying to break the ongoing blockade of the Gaza Strip; nine Turkish citizens on the flotilla were killed in the ensuing violent affray.

Q653187.name: Montparnasse derailment
Q653187.blurb: In Paris, an express train derails after overrunning the buffer stop, crossing almost 30 metres (100 ft) of concourse before crashing through a wall and falling 10 metres (33 ft) to the road below.

Q653470.name: Battle of the Caucasus
Q653470.blurb: World War II: The German offensives Operation Edelweiss and Operation Braunschweig begin on the Eastern Front.

Q653482.name: Battle of Lugdunum
Q653482.blurb: Emperor Septimius Severus defeats usurper Clodius Albinus in the Battle of Lugdunum, the bloodiest battle between Roman armies.

Q653582.name: Siege of Marienburg
Q653582.blurb: End of the Siege of Marienburg: The State of the Teutonic Order repulses the joint Polish—Lithuanian forces.

Q653664.name: Battle of Trenton
Q653664.blurb: American Revolutionary War: In the Battle of Trenton, the Continental Army under General George Washington executes a successful surprise attack and defeats a garrison of Hessian forces serving Great Britain.

Q653707.name: Fimreite
Q653707.blurb: The naval Battle of Fimreite is won by the Birkebeiner pretender Sverre Sigurdsson. Sigurdsson takes the Norwegian throne and King Magnus V of Norway is killed.

Q653783.name: Operation Priboi
Q653783.blurb: The Soviet Union began mass deportations of more than 90,000 "undesirable" people from the Baltic states to Siberia.

Q654006.name: Second Northern War
Q654006.blurb: After a devastating defeat in the Second Northern War, King Frederick III of Denmark–Norway was forced to give up nearly half his Danish territory to Sweden to save the remainder.

Q654363.name: deportation of the Chechens and Ingush
aliases: Deportation of Chechen and Ingush peoples
Q654363.blurb: The Soviet Union begins the forced deportation of the Chechen and Ingush people from the North Caucasus to Central Asia.

Q654374.name: Battle of Cambrai
Q654374.blurb: World War I: Battle of Cambrai begins: British forces make early progress in an attack on German positions but are later pushed back.

Q655480.name: Quasi-War
Q655480.blurb: Quasi-War: An American convoy of four merchant vessels escorted by a schooner was attacked by a squadron of armed barges manned by Haitians.

Q655894.name: Peel Commission
Q655894.blurb: The Peel Commission Report recommends the partition of Palestine, which was the first formal recommendation for partition in the history of Palestine.

Q656046.name: Battle of San Juan
Q656046.blurb: Sir Ralph Abercromby attacks San Juan, Puerto Rico, in what would be one of the largest invasions of the Spanish territories in the Americas.

Q656186.name: Fronde
aliases: Battle of the Faubourg Saint Antoine
Q656186.blurb: The Frondeurs and the French government sign the Peace of Rueil.

Q656190.name: Battle of Hemmingstedt
Q656190.blurb: Duke Frederick of Schleswig-Holstein and King John of Denmark attempt to subdue the peasantry of Dithmarschen, Denmark, in the Battle of Hemmingstedt.

Q656545.name: Reinsurance Treaty
Q656545.blurb: The Reinsurance Treaty between Germany and Russia is signed.

Q656660.name: Plessy v. Ferguson
aliases: Homer A. Plessy v. John H. Ferguson
Homer Adolph Plessy v. The State of Louisiana
Q656660.blurb: The United States Supreme Court rules in Plessy v. Ferguson that the "separate but equal" doctrine is constitutional.

Q656787.name: Battle of the Iron Bridge
Q656787.blurb: Arab–Byzantine wars: Antioch surrenders to the Rashidun Caliphate after the Battle of the Iron Bridge.

Q657024.name: Bear River Massacre
Q657024.blurb: The Bear River Massacre: A detachment of California Volunteers led by Colonel Patrick Edward Connor engage the Shoshone at Bear River, Washington Territory, killing hundreds of men, women and children.

Q657055.name: Greco-Turkish War of 1897
aliases: Ottoman fleet organisation during the Greco-Ottoman War (1897)
Ottoman fleet organisation during the Greco-Turkish War (1897)
Q657055.blurb: The Greco-Turkish War is declared between Greece and the Ottoman Empire.

Q657494.name: demolition of Babri Masjid
Q657494.blurb: The Babri Masjid in Ayodhya, India, is demolished, leading to widespread riots causing the death of over 1,500 people.

Q657502.name: Battle of Elchingen
Q657502.blurb: War of the Third Coalition: A French corps defeats an Austrian attempt to escape encirclement at Ulm.

Q657631.name: Blood in the Water match
Q657631.blurb: A violent water polo match between Hungary and the USSR takes place during the 1956 Summer Olympics in Melbourne, against the backdrop of the Hungarian Revolution of 1956.

Q657967.name: Second Barons' War
Q657967.blurb: Second Barons' War: King Henry III was defeated at the Battle of Lewes and forced to sign the Mise of Lewes, making Simon de Montfort the de facto ruler of England.

Q658731.name: Battle of Achelous
Q658731.blurb: Battle of Acheloos: Tsar Simeon I of Bulgaria decisively defeats a Byzantine army.

Q659166.name: 1996 United States presidential election
aliases: United States presidential election swing states, 1996
Q659166.blurb: Bill Clinton is reelected President of the United States.

Q659385.name: North Hollywood shootout
Q659385.blurb: Two heavily armed bank robbers exchanged gunfire with officers of the Los Angeles Police Department in North Hollywood, in one of the most intense gun battles in American police history.

Q659410.name: German October
Q659410.blurb: German October: Due to a miscommunication with the party leadership, a militant section of the Communist Party of Germany launches an insurrection in Hamburg.

Q660025.name: Battle of Papudo
Q660025.blurb: Battle of Papudo: A Spanish navy schooner is defeated by a Chilean corvette north of Valparaíso, Chile.

Q660232.name: Makin Island raid
Q660232.blurb: World War II: U.S. Marines raid the Japanese-held Pacific island of Makin.

Q660345.name: Soyuz-U
Q660345.blurb: Soyuz 7K-ST No. 16L, intended to launch a crew to the Salyut 7 space station, explodes on the launch pad. The launch escape system is activated before the Soyuz-U rocket explodes, saving the crew.

Q661327.name: Battle of Mühlberg
Q661327.blurb: Battle of Mühlberg. Duke of Alba, commanding Spanish-Imperial forces of Charles I of Spain, defeats the troops of Schmalkaldic League.

Q661409.name: Battle of St. Quentin
Q661409.blurb: Franco-Prussian War: In the Siege of Paris, Prussia wins the Battle of St. Quentin. Meanwhile, the French attempt to break the siege in the Battle of Buzenval will end unsuccessfully the following day.

Q661686.name: Battle of Höchst
Q661686.blurb: The Battle of Höchst takes place during the  Thirty Years' War.

Q661759.name: Battle of Sempach
Q661759.blurb: The Old Swiss Confederacy makes great strides in establishing control over its territory by soundly defeating the Duchy of Austria in the Battle of Sempach.

Q661940.name: Battle of Novara
Q661940.blurb: War of the League of Cambrai: In the Battle of Novara, Swiss troops defeat the French under Louis II de la Trémoille, forcing them to abandon Milan; Duke Massimiliano Sforza is restored.

Q662051.name: solar storm of 1859
Q662051.blurb: The Carrington event is the strongest geomagnetic storm on record to strike the Earth. Electrical telegraph service is widely disrupted.

Q662379.name: Sierre coach crash
Q662379.blurb: The Sierre coach crash kills 28 people, including 22 children.

Q662637.name: Federal Charter of 1291
aliases: League of the Three Forest Cantons
Q662637.blurb: The Old Swiss Confederacy is formed with the signature of the Federal Charter.

Q662961.name: Battle of Vittorio Veneto
Q662961.blurb: World War I: Italian victory in the Battle of Vittorio Veneto.

Q663405.name: Battle of Zorndorf
Q663405.blurb: Seven Years' War: Frederick II of Prussia defeats the Russian army at the Battle of Zorndorf.

Q663435.name: Battle of Mollwitz
Q663435.blurb: War of the Austrian Succession: Prussia gains control of Silesia at the Battle of Mollwitz.

Q663450.name: Battle of Krefeld
Q663450.blurb: Seven Years' War: Battle of Krefeld: British, Hanoverian, and Prussian forces defeat French troops at Krefeld in Germany.

Q663574.name: Battle of Ticonderoga
Q663574.blurb: French and Indian War: Troops led by French brigadier general François-Charles de Bourlamaque attempted to blow up Fort Carillon, near present-day Ticonderoga, New York, rather than defending it against approaching British forces.

Q665554.name: Japanese Instrument of Surrender
Q665554.blurb: World War II: The Japanese Instrument of Surrender is signed by Japan and the major warring powers aboard the battleship USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay, thus marking the official end to the war.

Q665566.name: Aloha Airlines Flight 243
Q665566.blurb: Aloha Airlines Flight 243 experienced explosive decompression while airborne between Hilo and Honolulu, Hawaii, with one fatality as a flight attendant was ejected from the aircraft.

Q665946.name: 1954 FIFA World Cup Final
Q665946.blurb: In what is known as "The Miracle of Bern", West Germany defeated Hungary 3–2 to win the FIFA World Cup.

Q666536.name: 2005 conclave
Q666536.blurb: Cardinal Joseph Ratzinger is elected to the papacy and becomes Pope Benedict XVI.

Q666778.name: Prague Uprising
Q666778.blurb: World War II: The Prague uprising begins as an attempt by the Czech resistance to free the city from German occupation.

Q667080.name: Peace of Basel
Q667080.blurb: Peace of Basel between France and Prussia is made.

Q667179.name: Battle of Gibraltar
Q667179.blurb: Eighty Years' War: The Dutch fleet destroys the anchored Spanish fleet at Gibraltar.

Q667460.name: Battle of Näfels
Q667460.blurb: Despite being vastly outnumbered, forces of the Old Swiss Confederacy defeated an Austrian army at the Battle of Näfels.

Q668008.name: Battle of Grandson
Q668008.blurb: Burgundian Wars: The Old Swiss Confederacy hands Charles the Bold, Duke of Burgundy, a major defeat in the Battle of Grandson in Canton of Neuchâtel.

Q668403.name: Treaty of Salynas
Q668403.blurb: In the Treaty of Salynas, Lithuania cedes Samogitia to the Teutonic Knights.

Q668577.name: Siege of Compiègne
Q668577.blurb: Joan of Arc is captured at the Siege of Compiègne by troops from the Burgundian faction.

Q668595.name: Battle of Harlem Heights
Q668595.blurb: American Revolutionary War: American forces win the Battle of Harlem Heights after General George Washington orders a counterattack on advancing British light infantry.

Q668645.name: Surrender of Caserta
Q668645.blurb: World War II: The surrender of Caserta comes into effect, by which German troops in Italy cease fighting.

Q669528.name: Baedeker Blitz
Q669528.blurb: World War II: Baedeker Blitz: German bombers hit Exeter, Bath and York in retaliation for the British raid on Lübeck.

Q669661.name: Battle of Sultan Yacoub
Q669661.blurb: Lebanon War: The Syrian Arab Army defeats the Israeli Defense Forces in the Battle of Sultan Yacoub.

Q670489.name: Gorlice–Tarnów Offensive
Q670489.blurb: World War I: The German 12th Army occupies Warsaw during the Gorlice–Tarnów Offensive and the Great Retreat of 1915.

Q671297.name: 1983 West Bank fainting epidemic
Q671297.blurb: The first cases of the 1983 West Bank fainting epidemic begin; Israelis and Palestinians accuse each other of poison gas, but the cause is later determined mostly to be psychosomatic.

Q671479.name: Sino-British Joint Declaration
aliases: Joint Declaration of the Government of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and the Government of the People's Republic of China on the Question of Hong Kong
Sino-British Joint Declaration on the Question of Hong Kong
中华人民共和国政府和大不列颠及北爱尔兰联合王国政府关于香港问题的联合声明
中華人民共和國政府和大不列顛及北愛爾蘭聯合王國政府關於香港問題的聯合聲明
Q671479.blurb: The Sino-British Joint Declaration, stating that China would resume the exercise of sovereignty over Hong Kong and the United Kingdom would restore Hong Kong to China with effect from July 1, 1997, is signed in Beijing by Deng Xiaoping and Margaret Thatcher.

Q671528.name: Battle of Königsberg
Q671528.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Königsberg, in East Prussia, ends.

Q671542.name: June Days Uprising
Q671542.blurb: A photograph of the June Days uprising becomes the first known instance of photojournalism.

Q671604.name: China Southwest Airlines Flight 4509
Q671604.blurb: China Southwest Airlines Flight 4509, a Tupolev Tu-154 aircraft, crashes in Rui'an, Zhejiang, China. All 61 people on board are killed.

Q671819.name: Austro–Serbian Alliance of 1881
Q671819.blurb: The Austro–Serbian Alliance of 1881 is secretly signed.

Q672392.name: Padma Vibhushan
Q672392.blurb: India establishes its highest civilian awards, the Bharat Ratna and the Padma Vibhushan.

Q672556.name: Boxer Protocol
Q672556.blurb: With Beijing occupied by foreign troops from the Eight-Nation Alliance, Qing China was forced to sign the Boxer Protocol, an unequal treaty that ended the Boxer Rebellion.

Q672705.name: 1356 Basel earthquake
Q672705.blurb: Basel earthquake, the most significant historic seismological event north of the Alps, destroys the town of Basel, Switzerland.

Q673175.name: French Wars of Religion
Q673175.blurb: During the French Wars of Religion, Henry IV of France declares war on Spain.

Q673411.name: Battle of Arbedo
Q673411.blurb: Battle of Arbedo between the duke of Milan and the Swiss cantons.

Q673527.name: 1990 Polish presidential election
Q673527.blurb: Lech Wałęsa is elected President of Poland.

Q675228.name: Vel' d'Hiv Roundup
Q675228.blurb: Holocaust: Vel' d'Hiv Roundup (Rafle du Vel' d'Hiv): The government of Vichy France orders the mass arrest of 13,152 Jews who are held at the Vélodrome d'Hiver in Paris before deportation to Auschwitz.

Q675324.name: Battle of Wigan Lane
Q675324.blurb: A parliamentarian army defeats a royalist army under James Stanley, 7th Earl of Derby, in the battle of Wigan Lane during the Third English Civial War.

Q675516.name: Battle of Ivry
Q675516.blurb: Battle of Ivry: Henry of Navarre and the Huguenots defeat the forces of the Catholic League under Charles, Duke of Mayenne, during the French Wars of Religion.

Q675546.name: Lauda Air Flight 004
Q675546.blurb: Lauda Air Flight 004 breaks apart in mid-air and crashes in the Phu Toei National Park in the Suphan Buri province of Thailand, killing all 223 people on board.

Q676148.name: Battle of Mansfield
Q676148.blurb: American Civil War: Late-arriving reinforcements helped Confederate forces rout the Union Army at the Battle of Mansfield.

Q676340.name: Siege of Calais
Q676340.blurb: The city of Calais surrenders after a protracted siege to the English following the English defeat of a French relief fleet in the battle of Crotoy. It will remain in English hands for more than 200 years.

Q676676.name: Hay–Bunau-Varilla Treaty
Q676676.blurb: The Hay–Bunau-Varilla Treaty is signed by the United States and Panama, giving the United States exclusive rights over the Panama Canal Zone.

Q676692.name: Battle of Naulochus
Q676692.blurb: In the Battle of Naulochus, Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa, admiral of Octavian, defeats Sextus Pompey, son of Pompey, thus ending Pompeian resistance to the Second Triumvirate.

Q677660.name: Battle of Heligoland Bight
Q677660.blurb: World War I: The Royal Navy defeats the German fleet in the Battle of Heligoland Bight.

Q677754.name: Ludendorff Bridge
Q677754.blurb: World War II:  The Ludendorff Bridge in Remagen, Germany, collapses, ten days after its capture.

Q677929.name: Battle of Toulon
Q677929.blurb: War of the Austrian Succession: The Battle of Toulon causes several Royal Navy captains to be court-martialed, and the Articles of War to be amended.

Q677959.name: Battle of Hastenbeck
Q677959.blurb: A French army under Marshal d'Estrées defeats a smaller British-German army under the duke of Cumberland in the battle of Hastenbeck.

Q677982.name: Siege of Ascalon
Q677982.blurb: After a six month siege, Baldwin III of Jerusalem captures Ascalon, obtaining a vast amount of plunder and securing the southern border of the Kingdom of Jerusalem.

Q678227.name: Battle of Fleurus
Q678227.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: Battle of Fleurus marks the first successful military use of aircraft and turns the tide of the War of the First Coalition.

Q679519.name: 2012 Visayas earthquake
Q679519.blurb: A magnitude 6.7 earthquake hits the central Philippine island of Negros, leaving 112 people dead.

Q681391.name: Treaty of Teschen
Q681391.blurb: Negotiated by Russian and French mediators, the Treaty of Teschen was signed by Austria and Prussia, leading to the end of the War of the Bavarian Succession.

Q681401.name: Peace of Vasvár
Q681401.blurb: The Habsburg empire and the Ottoman empire sign the peace treaty of Vasvár, which results in peace until 1683.

Q681430.name: Battle of Magenta
Q681430.blurb: Italian Independence wars: In the Battle of Magenta, the French army, under Louis-Napoleon, defeat the Austrian army.

Q681691.name: 1982 NFL season
Q681691.blurb: NFL season: American football players in the National Football League begin a 57-day strike.

Q681712.name: Battle of Gangut
Q681712.blurb: The Battle of Gangut: The first important victory of the Russian Navy.

Q682452.name: Siege of Malta
Q682452.blurb: World War II: The Siege of Malta begins with a series of Italian air raids.

Q682482.name: Russo-Swedish War of 1741-1743
Q682482.blurb: The War of the Hats: The Swedish army surrenders to the Russians in Helsinki, ending the war and starting Lesser Wrath.

Q682699.name: Battle of Kolubara
Q682699.blurb: World War I: Austro-Hungarian forces launched an assault against Serbian defensive positions at the Kolubara river, beginning the Battle of Kolubara.

Q683044.name: Battle of Minden
Q683044.blurb: Seven Years' War: The Battle of Minden, an allied Anglo-German army victory over the French. In Britain this was one of a number of events that constituted the Annus Mirabilis of 1759 and is celebrated as Minden Day by certain British Army regiments.

Q683271.name: Operation Menu
Q683271.blurb: The United States begins secretly bombing the Sihanouk Trail in Cambodia, used by communist forces to infiltrate South Vietnam.

Q683341.name: Battle of Bicocca
Q683341.blurb: A Spanish-Imperial army defeats French-Venetian army in the battle of Bicocca. The battle marks the end of dominance of Swiss mercenaries on the battlefield and is one of the first where firearms play a decisive role.

Q683551.name: Sixteen Kingdoms
aliases: Five Hu and the Sixteen Kingdoms
Q683551.blurb: Sixteen Kingdoms: Sima Yao, age 10, succeeds his father Emperor Jianwen as Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin dynasty.

Q683848.name: Treaty of Vienna
Q683848.blurb: Second War of Schleswig: The Treaty of Vienna is signed, by which Denmark relinquishes one province each to Prussia and Austria.

Q683912.name: Operation Tractable
Q683912.blurb: World War II: Canadian and Polish units capture the strategically important town of Falaise, Calvados, France.

Q684191.name: Battle of Elizabeth City
Q684191.blurb: American Civil War: A Union naval flotilla destroys the bulk of the Confederate Mosquito Fleet in the Battle of Elizabeth City on the Pasquotank River in North Carolina.

Q684324.name: War of the Fifth Coalition
aliases: The War of the Fifth Coalition
Q684324.blurb: War of the Fifth Coalition: French general Louis-Nicolas Davout defeated an Austrian force in  Lower Bavaria, allowing him to rejoin the main French army.

Q684479.name: Battle of Wörth
Q684479.blurb: Franco-Prussian War: The Battle of Wörth results in a decisive German victory.

Q684762.name: July Revolt of 1927
Q684762.blurb: Massacre of July 15, 1927: Eighty-nine protesters are killed by Austrian police in Vienna.

Q684915.name: Crossing of the Rhine
Q684915.blurb: Vandals, Alans and Suebians cross the Rhine, beginning an invasion of Gaul.

Q685062.name: Siege of Madrid
Q685062.blurb: Spanish Civil War: The republican government flees from Madrid to Valencia, leading to the formation of the Madrid Defense Council in its stead.

Q685164.name: Treaty of Basel
Q685164.blurb: The Treaty of Basel concludes the Swabian War.

Q685181.name: Japanese conquest of Burma
Q685181.blurb: World War II: The Japanese conquest of Burma begins.

Q685201.name: Kragujevac massacre
Q685201.blurb: World War II: The Kragujevac massacre against Serbian men and boys takes place.

Q685372.name: Kraków Uprising
Q685372.blurb: Polish insurgents lead an uprising in Kraków to incite a fight for national independence.

Q685604.name: Trials of the Knights Templar
Q685604.blurb: Knights Templar officer Hugues de Pairaud is forced to confess during the Trials of the Knights Templar. He was persecuted on the charges of false idolism and sodomy.

Q685746.name: Port Said Stadium riot
Q685746.blurb: Seventy-four people are killed and over 500 injured as a result of clashes between fans of Egyptian football teams Al Masry and Al Ahly in the city of Port Said.

Q685798.name: Battle of Winterthur
Q685798.blurb: War of the Second Coalition: Austrian forces defeated the French Army of the Danube, capturing the strategically important Swiss town of Winterthur.

Q685849.name: 1348 Friuli earthquake
Q685849.blurb: A strong earthquake strikes the South Alpine region of Friuli in modern Italy, causing considerable damage to buildings as far away as Rome.

Q686018.name: Amagasaki derailment
Q686018.blurb: A seven-car commuter train derails and crashes into an apartment building near Amagasaki Station in Japan, killing 107, including the driver.

Q686944.name: Černová massacre
Q686944.blurb: Fifteen people are killed in Hungary when gendarmes opened fire on a crowd gathered at a church consecration.

Q687151.name: Golub War
