Q687151.blurb: After the brief Gollub War, the Teutonic Knights sign the Treaty of Melno with Poland and Lithuania.

Q687214.name: Formula Two
Q687214.blurb: Two-time Formula One British World Champion Jim Clark dies in an accident during a Formula Two race in Hockenheim.

Q688081.name: Battle of Mühldorf
Q688081.blurb: Louis IV, Holy Roman Emperor, defeats Frederick I of Austria in the Battle of Mühldorf.

Q688297.name: Sonderbund War
Q688297.blurb: The Sonderbund is defeated by the joint forces of other Swiss cantons under General Guillaume-Henri Dufour.

Q688308.name: Swedish War of Liberation
Q688308.blurb: Swedish War of Liberation: Swedish troops defeat a Danish force in the Battle of Västerås.

Q688339.name: Great Retreat
Q688339.blurb: World War I: The German 12th Army occupies Warsaw during the Gorlice–Tarnów Offensive and the Great Retreat of 1915.

Q688436.name: Siege of Barcelona
Q688436.blurb: Siege of Barcelona: Barcelona, capital city of the Principality of Catalonia, surrenders to Spanish and French Bourbon armies in the War of the Catalans, the last phase of the War of the Spanish Succession.

Q688448.name: Battle of Hohenfriedberg
Q688448.blurb: Battle of Hohenfriedberg: Frederick the Great's Prussian army decisively defeat an Austrian army under Prince Charles Alexander of Lorraine during the War of the Austrian Succession.

Q688821.name: Distomo massacre
Q688821.blurb: World War II: In Distomo, Boeotia, Greece, 228 men, women and children are massacred by German troops.

Q688847.name: Siege of Metz
Q688847.blurb: Franco-Prussian War: The Siege of Metz begins, resulting in a decisive Prussian victory on October 23.

Q688909.name: Armory Show
aliases: The International Exhibition of Modern Art
Q688909.blurb: The Armory Show opens in New York City, displaying works of artists who subsequently become some of the most influential painters of the early 20th century.

Q689032.name: Treaty of Saint Petersburg
Q689032.blurb: Russia and Prussia sign the Treaty of St. Petersburg.

Q689128.name: Haitian Revolution
Q689128.blurb: Haitian Revolution: Battle of Port-Républicain: British troops capture the capital of Saint-Domingue.

Q689220.name: March 1933 German federal election
Q689220.blurb: Adolf Hitler's Nazi Party receives 43.9% at the Reichstag elections, which allows the Nazis to later pass the Enabling Act and establish a dictatorship.

Q689359.name: Crossair Flight 498
Q689359.blurb: Crossair Flight 498, a Saab 340 aircraft, crashes in Niederhasli, Switzerland, after taking off from Zurich Airport, killing 13 people.

Q689433.name: Battle of Langport
Q689433.blurb: English Civil War: The Battle of Langport takes place.

Q689448.name: Canadian Pacific Air Lines Flight 402
Q689448.blurb: A Canadian Pacific Air Lines DC-8-43 explodes on landing at Tokyo International Airport, killing 64 people.

Q689471.name: Battle of Albuera
Q689471.blurb: Peninsular War: The allies Spain, Portugal and United Kingdom fight an inconclusive battle against the French at the Albuera. It is, in proportion to the numbers involved, the bloodiest battle of the war.

Q689527.name: Aster Revolution
Q689527.blurb: World War I: The Aster Revolution terminates the Austro-Hungarian Compromise of 1867, and Hungary achieves full sovereignty.

Q690197.name: Scuttling of the French fleet in Toulon
Q690197.blurb: World War II: At Toulon, the French navy scuttles its ships and submarines to keep them out of Nazi hands.

Q690308.name: Kerensky Offensive
Q690308.blurb: World War I: Russia launches an offensive against Austria-Hungary to capture Galicia, its final offensive of the war.

Q690331.name: Battle of Berne
Q690331.blurb: The FIFA World Cup quarterfinal match between Hungary and Brazil, highly anticipated to be exciting, instead turns violent, with three players ejected and further fighting continuing after the game.

Q690361.name: Long War
Q690361.blurb: Long War: Austria captures Transylvania in the Battle of Goroszló.

Q690391.name: Battle of Petrovaradin
Q690391.blurb: Austro-Turkish War (1716–1718):The Austrians defeat the Ottomans in the Battle of Petrovaradin. One-fifth of a Turkish army and the Grand Vizier are killed.

Q690413.name: Operation Banner
Q690413.blurb: Operation Banner, the presence of the British Army in Northern Ireland, and the longest-running British Army operation ever, comes to an end.

Q690464.name: Battle of Mikatagahara
Q690464.blurb: Battle of Mikatagahara: In Japan, Takeda Shingen defeats Tokugawa Ieyasu.

Q690470.name: Battle of Mohács
Q690470.blurb: Battle of Mohács: Charles of Lorraine defeats the Ottoman Empire.

Q690481.name: Battle of Slankamen
Q690481.blurb: An Imperial army under Ludwig of Baden defeats the Ottomans in the battle of Slankamen.

Q690489.name: Siege of Paris
Q690489.blurb: Franco-Prussian War: In the Siege of Paris, Prussia wins the Battle of St. Quentin. Meanwhile, the French attempt to break the siege in the Battle of Buzenval will end unsuccessfully the following day.

Q690883.name: Varig Flight 254
Q690883.blurb: Varig Flight 254 crashes in the Amazon rainforest near São José do Xingu in Brazil, killing 12.

Q690931.name: Kaprun disaster
Q690931.blurb: Kaprun disaster: One hundred fifty-five skiers and snowboarders die when a cable car catches fire in an alpine tunnel in Kaprun, Austria.

Q690959.name: Revolutions of 1848 in the Habsburg empire
aliases: Revolutions of 1848 in the Habsburg Areas
Revolutions of 1848 within the Austrian Empire
The Revolutions of 1848 in Habsburg areas
The Revolutions of 1848 in the Habsburg Areas
The Revolutions of 1848 in the Hapsburg areas
Q690959.blurb: Revolutions of 1848 in the Austrian Empire: After a month-long siege, Venice, which had declared itself independent as the Republic of San Marco, surrenders to Austria.

Q690989.name: Treaty of Fontainebleau
Q690989.blurb: The Treaty of Fontainebleau ends the War of the Sixth Coalition against Napoleon Bonaparte, and forces him to abdicate unconditionally for the first time.

Q691404.name: Johnstown Flood
Q691404.blurb: Johnstown Flood: Over 2,200 people die after a dam fails and sends a 60-foot (18-meter) wall of water over the town of Johnstown, Pennsylvania.

Q691565.name: Case Anton
Q691565.blurb: World War II: Germany invades Vichy France following French Admiral François Darlan's agreement to an armistice with the Allies in North Africa.

Q691882.name: Münster rebellion
Q691882.blurb: The Anabaptist state of Münster is conquered and disbanded.

Q692136.name: Carinthian Plebiscite
Q692136.blurb: The Carinthian plebiscite determines that the larger part of the Duchy of Carinthia should remain part of Austria.

Q692137.name: Landing at Kip's Bay
Q692137.blurb: American Revolutionary War: British forces successfully land at Kip's Bay, forcing the Continental Army, which was already withdrawing from New York City, to cede control of the lower half of Manhattan Island.

Q692146.name: Schleswig plebiscite
Q692146.blurb: In the second of the 1920 Schleswig plebiscites, about 80% of the population in Zone II votes to remain part of Weimar Germany.

Q692398.name: Bojinka plot
Q692398.blurb: A chemical fire in an apartment complex in Manila, Philippines, leads to the discovery of plans for Project Bojinka, a mass-terrorist attack.

Q692885.name: Operation Ivory Coast
Q692885.blurb: Vietnam War: Operation Ivory Coast: A joint United States Air Force and Army team raids the Sơn Tây prisoner-of-war camp in an attempt to free American prisoners of war thought to be held there.

Q693282.name: Siege of Turin
Q693282.blurb: War of the Spanish Succession: Siege of Turin ends, leading to the withdrawal of French forces from North Italy.

Q693742.name: 1968 United States presidential election
aliases: United States third party and independent presidential candidates, 1968
Q693742.blurb: Richard Nixon is elected as 37th President of the United States.

Q693964.name: Treaty of Melno
Q693964.blurb: The Treaty of Melno was signed, establishing the Prussian–Lithuanian border, which afterwards remained unchanged for about 500 years.

Q694068.name: Battle of Fraustadt
Q694068.blurb: During the Battle of Fraustadt Swedish forces defeat a superior Saxon-Polish-Russian force by deploying a double envelopment.

Q694073.name: Capture of Gibraltar
Q694073.blurb: War of the Spanish Succession: A combined Anglo-Dutch fleet under the command of George Rooke and allied with Archduke Charles captured Gibraltar from Spain.

Q694106.name: The Oprah Winfrey Show
aliases: You get a car! You get a car! Everybody gets a car!
Q694106.blurb: The final episode of The Oprah Winfrey Show, the highest-rated daytime talk show in U.S. television history, hosted by Oprah Winfrey (pictured), was broadcast.

Q694122.name: Battle of Napue
Q694122.blurb: Great Northern War: The battle of Napue between Sweden and Russia is fought in Isokyrö, Ostrobothnia.

Q694379.name: Battle of Krbava Field
Q694379.blurb: Battle of Krbava Field, a decisive defeat of Croats in Croatian struggle against the invasion by the Ottoman Empire.

Q694502.name: Battle of Málaga
Q694502.blurb: War of the Spanish Succession: An Anglo-Dutch fleet engaged a French naval force at the Battle of Málaga in the Mediterranean Sea.

Q694604.name: Treaty of Mutual Cooperation and Security Between the United States and Japan
aliases: Japan-United States Mutual Security Assistance Pact
Japan-United States Mutual Security Assistance Pact.
Japan-United States Treaty of Mutual Cooperation and Security
Nippon-koku to Amerika-gasshūkoku to no Aida no Sōgo Kyōryoku oyobi Anzen Hoshō Jōyaku
Treaty of Mutual Cooperation and Security
Treaty of Mutual Cooperation and Security (United States - Japan)
Treaty of Mutual Cooperation and Security (United States – Japan)
日本国とアメリカ合衆国との間の相互協力及び安全保障条約
Q694604.blurb: Japan and the United States sign the US–Japan Mutual Security Treaty

Q694619.name: Siege of Leiden
Q694619.blurb: The Siege of Leiden is lifted by the Watergeuzen.

Q694767.name: Treaty of Schönbrunn
Q694767.blurb: The Treaty of Schönbrunn is signed, ending the War of the Fifth Coalition, the final successful war in Napoleon Bonaparte's military career.

Q694835.name: Seventh Ottoman–Venetian War
Q694835.blurb: Seventh Ottoman–Venetian War: The Ottoman Empire captures Nauplia, the capital of the Republic of Venice's "Kingdom of the Morea", thereby opening the way to the swift Ottoman reconquest of the Morea.

Q695020.name: Massacres of Poles in Volhynia and Eastern Galicia
aliases: Ethnic cleansing in the Lviv, Tarnopol and Stanisławów voivodeships
Massacres against Poles in Volhynia and Eastern Galicia
Massacres of Jews in Volhynia and Eastern Galicia
Massacres of Poles in Wołyń Voivodeship
Wartime Massacres of Poles in Volhynia
Q695020.blurb: Massacres of Poles in Volhynia and Eastern Galicia by the Ukrainian Insurgent Army within the Reichskommissariat Ukraine (Volhynia) peak.

Q695052.name: hyperinflation in the Weimar Republic
Q695052.blurb: The German Rentenmark is introduced in Germany to counter hyperinflation in the Weimar Republic.

Q695107.name: Battle of Dybbøl
Q695107.blurb: Battle of Dybbøl: A Prussian-Austrian army defeats Denmark and gains control of Schleswig. Denmark surrenders the province in the following peace settlement.

Q695215.name: Treaty of Berlin (1926)
Q695215.blurb: The Treaty of Berlin is signed. Germany and the Soviet Union each pledge neutrality in the event of an attack on the other by a third party for the next five years.

Q695285.name: Moscow Peace Treaty
Q695285.blurb: The Moscow Peace Treaty was signed, ending the Winter War between Finland and the Soviet Union.

Q695290.name: Ethiopian Airlines Flight 409
Q695290.blurb: Ethiopian Airlines Flight 409 crashes into the Mediterranean Sea off the coast of Na'ameh, Lebanon, killing 90.

Q695485.name: Battle of Jumonville Glen
Q695485.blurb: French and Indian War: In the first engagement of the war, Virginia militia under the 22-year-old Lieutenant colonel George Washington defeat a French reconnaissance party in the Battle of Jumonville Glen in what is now Fayette County in southwestern Pennsylvania.

Q695487.name: Rome and Vienna airport attacks
Q695487.blurb: Palestinian guerrillas kill eighteen people inside the airports of Rome, Italy, and Vienna, Austria.

Q695566.name: Panic of 1873
Q695566.blurb: Der Krach: The Vienna stock exchange crash begins the Panic of 1873 and heralds the Long Depression.

Q695666.name: Operation Hannibal
Q695666.blurb: World War II: German admiral Karl Dönitz launches Operation Hannibal, the evacuation of areas along the eastern Baltic coast.

Q695673.name: First Battle of Cape Finisterre
Q695673.blurb: War of the Austrian Succession: A British fleet under Admiral George Anson defeats the French at the First Battle of Cape Finisterre.

Q695925.name: Battle of Hochkirch
Q695925.blurb: Third Silesian War: At the Battle of Hochkirch, an Austrian army under Leopold Joseph von Daun surprised the Prussians commanded by Frederick the Great, overwhelming them and forcing a general retreat.

Q696018.name: Operation Compass
Q696018.blurb: Second World War: As part of Operation Compass, Australian and United Kingdom forces attacked Italian forces at the Battle of Bardia in Egypt.

Q696094.name: Treaty of Nerchinsk
Q696094.blurb: The Treaty of Nerchinsk is signed by Russia and the Qing Empire (Julian calendar).

Q696187.name: 1992 Los Angeles riots
aliases: Korean armed resistance in the Los Angeles riots
Mass racial violence in the United States (1992)
Media coverage of the 1992 Los Angeles riots
Media coverage of the LA 1992 Race Riots
Q696187.blurb: Riots in Los Angeles begin, following the acquittal of police officers charged with excessive force in the beating of Rodney King. Over the next three days 63 people are killed and hundreds of buildings are destroyed.

Q696251.name: Occupation of Japan
aliases: The united states occupation of japan
Q696251.blurb: Occupation of Japan/Shinto Directive: General Douglas MacArthur orders that Shinto be abolished as the state religion of Japan.

Q696256.name: Soviet–Japanese Neutrality Pact
Q696256.blurb: A pact of neutrality between the USSR and Japan is signed.

Q696438.name: Naval Battle of Guadalcanal
aliases: Third Battle of the Solomon Sea
Third and Fourth Battles of Savo Island
Q696438.blurb: World War II: Naval Battle of Guadalcanal between Japanese and American forces begins near Guadalcanal. The battle lasts for three days and ends with an American victory.

Q696448.name: Operation Ichi-Go
Q696448.blurb: World War II: XX Bomber Command responds to the Japanese Operation Ichi-Go offensive by dropping five hundred tons of incendiary bombs on a supply base in Hankow, China.

Q696462.name: Philippines Campaign
Q696462.blurb: World War II: Battle of the Philippines: Imperial Japanese forces under the command of General Masaharu Homma land on Luzon.

Q696479.name: Battle of the Eastern Solomons
aliases: Second Battle of the Solomon Sea
Q696479.blurb: World War II: Second day of the Battle of the Eastern Solomons; a Japanese naval transport convoy headed towards Guadalcanal is turned back by an Allied air attack.

Q696482.name: Great Depression in the United States
Q696482.blurb: The COVID-19 recession causes the U.S. unemployment rate to hit 14.9 percent, its worst rate since the Great Depression.

Q696550.name: Washington Naval Treaty
aliases: Washington Treaty for the Limitation of Naval Armaments
Q696550.blurb: The Washington Naval Treaty is signed in Washington, D.C., limiting the naval armaments of United States, Britain, Japan, France, and Italy.

Q696557.name: Bombing of Darwin
Q696557.blurb: World War II: Nearly 250 Japanese warplanes attack the northern Australian city of Darwin, killing 243 people.

Q696607.name: Battle of the Denmark Strait
Q696607.blurb: World War II: Battle of the Atlantic: In the Battle of the Denmark Strait, the German battleship Bismarck sinks the pride of the Royal Navy, HMS Hood, killing all but three crewmen.

Q696664.name: Malayan campaign
Q696664.blurb: World War II: Allied forces are defeated by the Japanese at the Battle of Malaya and retreat to Singapore.

Q696689.name: Battle of Gross-Jägersdorf
Q696689.blurb: Battle of Gross-Jägersdorf: Russian force under Field Marshal Stepan Fyodorovich Apraksin beats a smaller Prussian force commanded by Field Marshal Hans von Lehwaldt, during the Seven Years' War.

Q696802.name: Paris Peace Accords
aliases: Agreement on Ending the War and Restoring Peace in Vietnam
Q696802.blurb: The Paris Peace Accords officially ends the Vietnam War. Colonel William Nolde is killed in action becoming the conflict's last recorded American combat casualty.

Q696815.name: Battle of Heligoland
Q696815.blurb: Second Schleswig War: The Battle of Heligoland (depicted), the last naval engagement fought by squadrons of wooden ships, took place between the Danish and Austro-Prussian fleets.

Q696835.name: Liberation of Paris
Q696835.blurb: World War II: Liberation of Paris: Paris, France rises against German occupation with the help of Allied troops.

Q696844.name: Battle of Anzio
Q696844.blurb: World War II: During the Anzio campaign, the 1st Ranger Battalion (Darby's Rangers) is destroyed behind enemy lines in a heavily outnumbered encounter at Battle of Cisterna, Italy.

Q696848.name: Anglo-Iraqi War
Q696848.blurb: During the Anglo-Iraqi War, British troops take Fallujah.

Q696894.name: Cairo Conference
Q696894.blurb: World War II: Cairo Conference: U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill, and Chinese Premier Chiang Kai-shek meet in Cairo, Egypt, to discuss ways to defeat Japan.

Q696900.name: Battle of Guam
Q696900.blurb: World War II: Battle of Guam: American troops land on Guam, starting a battle that will end on August 10.

Q696931.name: Battle of Manila
aliases: Battle for the Liberation of Manila
Q696931.blurb: World War II: The United States and the Philippine Commonwealth begin a month-long battle to retake Manila from Japan.

Q697053.name: Battle of Hue
Q697053.blurb: Vietnam War: Led by Ngô Quang Trưởng, South Vietnamese forces recaptured the citadel of Huế.

Q697059.name: Battle of Hong Kong
aliases: Battle of Kowloon and New Territories
Q697059.blurb: World War II: Battle of Hong Kong ends, beginning the Japanese occupation of Hong Kong.

Q697266.name: Battle of Gravelotte
Q697266.blurb: Franco-Prussian War: Battle of Gravelotte is fought.

Q697368.name: Treaty of Sistova
aliases: Treaty of Peace between Austria and Turkey
Q697368.blurb: The Treaty of Sistova is signed, ending the Ottoman–Habsburg wars.

Q697547.name: December 9th Movement
Q697547.blurb: Student protests occur in Beijing's Tiananmen Square, and are subsequently dispersed by government authorities.

Q697621.name: Siege of Fort Zeelandia
Q697621.blurb: Sino-Dutch conflicts: After besieging Fort Zeelandia for nine months, Ming loyalist Zheng Chenggong secured the Dutch East India Company's surrender and the end of their rule in Taiwan.

Q697625.name: German invasion of Belgium
Q697625.blurb: World War II: German forces commenced their invasion of Belgium.

Q697659.name: Remilitarization of the Rhineland
Q697659.blurb: Nazi German forces re-occupied the demilitarized Rhineland, violating both the Treaty of Versailles and the Locarno Treaties that were signed after World War I.

Q697680.name: Battle of Tali-Ihantala
Q697680.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Tali-Ihantala, the largest battle ever fought in the Nordic countries, begins.

Q697748.name: Battle of Cer
Q697748.blurb: World War I: Beginning of the Battle of Cer, the first Allied victory of World War I.

Q697823.name: Fall of Antwerp
Q697823.blurb: Eighty Years' War: Siege of Antwerp: Antwerp is captured by Spanish forces under Alexander Farnese, Duke of Parma, who orders Protestants to leave the city and as a result over half of the 100,000 inhabitants flee to the northern provinces.

Q697842.name: Invasion of Yugoslavia
Q697842.blurb: World War II: The Axis powers invasion of Yugoslavia is completed when it signs an armistice with Germany and Italy.

Q697897.name: Battle of Carillon
Q697897.blurb: French and Indian War: French forces defeated the British at Fort Carillon in the British colony of New York.

Q697913.name: Battle of Landeshut
Q697913.blurb: Seven Years' War: Battle of Landeshut: Austria defeats Prussia.

Q697986.name: Vienna Convention on Road Traffic
aliases: United Nations Economic and Social Council's Conference on Road Traffic
Q697986.blurb: The Vienna Convention on Road Traffic is signed to facilitate international road traffic and to increase road safety by standardising the uniform traffic rules among the signatories.

Q698027.name: Greater Poland uprising
Q698027.blurb: The Great Poland Uprising against the Germans begins.

Q698045.name: Sack of Magdeburg
Q698045.blurb: The city of Magdeburg in Germany is seized by forces of the Holy Roman Empire and most of its inhabitants massacred, in one of the bloodiest incidents of the Thirty Years' War.

Q698056.name: 1960 Agadir earthquake
Q698056.blurb: The 5.7 Mw Agadir earthquake shakes coastal Morocco with a maximum perceived intensity of X (Extreme), destroying Agadir and leaving 12,000 dead and another 12,000 injured.

Q698067.name: East Pomeranian Offensive
Q698067.blurb: World War II: Soviet forces invade Austria and capture Vienna. Polish and Soviet forces liberate Danzig.

Q698106.name: 1800 United States presidential election
aliases: 1801 United States Electoral College vote count
Q698106.blurb: United States presidential election: A tie in the Electoral College between Thomas Jefferson and Aaron Burr is resolved when Jefferson is elected President of the United States and Burr Vice President by the United States House of Representatives.

Q698170.name: Operation Winter Storm
Q698170.blurb: World War II: German troops began Operation Winter Storm, an attempt to relieve encircled Axis forces during the Battle of Stalingrad.

Q698178.name: Italian invasion of France
Q698178.blurb: World War II: Italy begins an unsuccessful invasion of France.

Q698226.name: Dutch East Indies campaign
aliases: Dutch declaration of war on Japan
Invasion of the Dutch East Indies
Japanese invasion of the Dutch East Indies
Q698226.blurb: World War II: Dutch East Indies unconditionally surrenders to the Japanese forces in Kalijati, Subang, West Java, and the Japanese complete their Dutch East Indies campaign.

Q698255.name: Sportpalast speech
Q698255.blurb: World War II: Joseph Goebbels delivers his Sportpalast speech.

Q698281.name: Italian War of 1521–1526
Q698281.blurb: Four Years' War: The combined forces of Spain and the Papal States defeated a French and Venetian army at the Battle of Bicocca.

Q698421.name: Italian invasion of Egypt
Q698421.blurb: World War II: Italian troops conquer Sidi Barrani.

Q698686.name: Treaty of Hubertusburg
Q698686.blurb: Prussia, Saxony and the Habsburg monarchy signed the Treaty of Hubertusburg, ending the Third Silesian War.

Q698706.name: Battle of Kosovo
Q698706.blurb: An Ottoman army defeats a Hungarian army at the Second Battle of Kosovo.

Q698778.name: Gran Sasso raid
Q698778.blurb: World War II: Benito Mussolini is rescued from house arrest by German commando forces led by Otto Skorzeny.

Q698828.name: Siege of Przemyśl
Q698828.blurb: World War I: The Siege of Przemyśl (present-day Poland) begins.

Q698842.name: 1860 United States presidential election
Q698842.blurb: United States presidential election: Abraham Lincoln wins the Republican Party presidential nomination over William H. Seward, who later becomes the United States Secretary of State.

Q698921.name: 2006 Hengchun earthquake
Q698921.blurb: Two earthquakes in Hengchun, Taiwan measuring 7.0 and 6.9 on the moment magnitude scale kill two and disrupt telecommunications across Asia.

Q698999.name: 1872 United States presidential election
Q698999.blurb: Susan B. Anthony is fined $100 for attempting to vote in the 1872 presidential election.

Q699055.name: China Airlines Flight 140
Q699055.blurb: China Airlines Flight 140 crashes at Nagoya Airport in Japan, killing 264 of the 271 people on board.

Q699096.name: Battle of Guningtou
Q699096.blurb: The Battle of Guningtou in the Taiwan Strait begins.

Q699120.name: 1880 United States presidential election
aliases: Results breakdown of the United States presidential election, 1880
Q699120.blurb: James A. Garfield was elected as president of the United States; the election is the closest to date by popular vote margin.

Q699127.name: Treasure Voyages
aliases: Seventh and last Ming treasure voyage
Zheng He Down the Western Ocean
Zheng He to the Western Ocean
Zheng He's voyage to the Western Ocean
Q699127.blurb: Marking the start of the Ming treasure voyages, a Chinese expeditionary fleet led by Zheng He set sail for foreign regions of the South China Sea and the Indian Ocean.

Q699154.name: 1948 Republic of China presidential election
Q699154.blurb: Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek wins the 1948 Republic of China presidential election and is sworn in as the first President of the Republic of China at Nanjing.

Q699195.name: Far Eastern Air Transport Flight 103
Q699195.blurb: Far Eastern Air Transport Flight 103 disintegrates in mid-air and crashes in Sanyi Township, Miaoli County, Taiwan. All 110 people on board are killed.

Q699227.name: 1900 United States presidential election
Q699227.blurb: President William McKinley is re-elected, along with his vice-presidential running mate, Governor Theodore Roosevelt of New York.

Q699238.name: Battle of Spicheren
Q699238.blurb: Franco-Prussian War: The Battle of Spicheren is fought, resulting in a German victory.

Q699247.name: Battle of Jasmund
Q699247.blurb: Second Schleswig War: In an attempt to end a Danish blockade, Eduard von Jachmann led a Prussian squadron in an attack against a Danish fleet led by Edvard van Dockum.

Q699262.name: Battle of Mars-la-Tour
Q699262.blurb: Franco-Prussian War: The Battle of Mars-la-Tour is fought, resulting in a Prussian victory.

Q699289.name: 1912 United States presidential election
Q699289.blurb: Woodrow Wilson is elected the 28th President of the United States, defeating incumbent William Howard Taft.

Q699295.name: Nanking incident of 1927
Q699295.blurb: Nanking Incident: Foreign warships bombard Nanjing, China, in defence of the foreign citizens within the city.

Q699318.name: 1916 United States presidential election
aliases: Planned presidential transition of Charles Evans Hughes
Q699318.blurb: Woodrow Wilson is reelected as President of the United States.

Q699343.name: 1920 United States presidential election
Q699343.blurb: The Ocoee massacre commences in Orange County, Florida on the day of the 1920 United States presidential election.

Q699400.name: Constantinople Conference
Q699400.blurb: The last day of the Constantinople Conference results in agreement for political reforms in the Balkans.

Q699411.name: Battle of the Barents Sea
Q699411.blurb: World War II: The Royal Navy defeats the Kriegsmarine at the Battle of the Barents Sea. This leads to the resignation of Grand Admiral Erich Raeder a month later.

Q699416.name: 1940 United States presidential election
Q699416.blurb: Franklin D. Roosevelt is the first and only President of the United States to be elected to a third term.

Q699475.name: Battle of Guinegate
Q699475.blurb: Battle of the Spurs (Battle of Guinegate): King Henry VIII of England and his Imperial allies defeat French Forces who are then forced to retreat.

Q699511.name: Italian Campaign of 1796-1797
Q699511.blurb: War of the First Coalition: A surprise Austrian attack at the Battle of Voltri marks the beginning of the Italian Campaign, the decisive campaign under Napoleon Bonaparte that will end the war a year later.

Q699527.name: Scuttling of the German Fleet in Scapa Flow
Q699527.blurb: Admiral Ludwig von Reuter scuttles the German fleet at Scapa Flow, Orkney. The nine sailors killed are the last casualties of World War I.

Q699548.name: 1952 United States presidential election
Q699548.blurb: Dwight D. Eisenhower resigns as Supreme Allied Commander of NATO in order to campaign in the 1952 United States presidential election.

Q699590.name: 1960 United States presidential election
aliases: Nixon's 1960 presidential defeat to John F. Kennedy
Q699590.blurb: John F. Kennedy is elected as the 35th President of the United States, defeating incumbent Vice President Richard Nixon, who would later be elected president in 1968  and 1972.

Q699646.name: 1964 United States presidential election
aliases: In your guts, you know he's nuts
In your heart, he's too far right
In your heart, he’s too far right
In your heart, you know he might
In your heart, you know he's right
Q699646.blurb: Lyndon B. Johnson is elected to a full term as U.S. president, winning 61% of the vote and 44 states, while Washington D.C. residents are able to vote in a presidential election for the first time, casting the majority of their votes for Lyndon Johnson.

Q699665.name: Battle of Dürenstein
Q699665.blurb: Napoleonic Wars: Battle of Dürenstein: Eight thousand French troops attempt to slow the retreat of a vastly superior Russian and Austrian force.

Q699669.name: Battle of the Santa Cruz Islands
Q699669.blurb: World War II: In the Battle of the Santa Cruz Islands during the Guadalcanal Campaign, one U.S. aircraft carrier is sunk and another carrier is heavily damaged, while two Japanese carriers and one cruiser are heavily damaged.

Q699716.name: 1980 United States presidential election
aliases: United States third party and independent presidential candidates, 1980
Q699716.blurb: Ronald Reagan is elected as the 40th President of the United States, defeating incumbent Jimmy Carter.

Q699776.name: 1992 United States presidential election
aliases: United States third party and independent presidential candidates, 1992
Q699776.blurb: Democratic Arkansas Governor Bill Clinton defeats Republican President George H. W. Bush and Independent candidate Ross Perot in the 1992 United States presidential election.

Q699872.name: 2016 United States presidential election
aliases: 2016 presidential election in the United States
2016 presidential election of the United States
Q699872.blurb: The Special Counsel investigation on the 2016 United States presidential election concludes when Robert Mueller submits his report to the United States Attorney General.

Q700027.name: Union of Arras
Q700027.blurb: The Union of Arras unites the southern Netherlands under the Duke of Parma (Ottavio Farnese), governor in the name of King Philip II of Spain.

Q700032.name: Battle of Savo Island
aliases: Battle of the Five Sitting Ducks
First Battle of the Solomon Sea
Q700032.blurb: World War II: Battle of Savo Island: Allied naval forces protecting their amphibious forces during the initial stages of the Battle of Guadalcanal are surprised and defeated by an Imperial Japanese Navy cruiser force.

Q700035.name: Pacification of Ghent
Q700035.blurb: Eighty Years' War: Pacification of Ghent: The States General of the Netherlands meet and unite to oppose Spanish occupation.

Q700067.name: Treaties of Stockholm
Q700067.blurb: In a treaty between Sweden and Hanover at the close of the Great Northern War, Sweden cedes the  Duchies of Bremen and Verden (in northern Germany) to Hanover.

Q700120.name: occupation of Poland (1939–1945)
aliases: German occupation of Poland in World War II
Nazi German military occupation of Poland
Occupation of Poland by Nazi Germany
Occupation of Poland during World War II
Treatment of Polish citizens by the occupants
Treatment of Polish citizens by the occupiers
Treatment of the Polish citizens by the occupants
Treatment of the Polish citizens by the occupiers
Q700120.blurb: The Holocaust: The Chełmno extermination camp in occupied Poland, the first such Nazi camp to kill Jews, began operations.

Q700194.name: Battle on the Marchfeld
Q700194.blurb: Ladislaus IV of Hungary and Rudolf I of Germany defeat Ottokar II of Bohemia in the Battle on the Marchfeld near Dürnkrut in (then) Moravia.

Q700238.name: Treaty of Adrianople
Q700238.blurb: The treaty of Adrianople ends the Russo-Turkish War of 1710–1713, which restores territory to the Ottomans while allowing the Russians to focus on their war against the Swedes.

Q700363.name: London Straits Convention
Q700363.blurb: Austria, Britain, France, Prussia and Russia conclude the London Straits Convention, which forbids warships to cross the Bosporus and Dardanelles in times of war.

Q700402.name: CBS Evening News
aliases: CBS Evening News With Jeff Glor
CBS Evening News With Katie Couric
CBS Evening News With Scott Pelley
CBS Evening News with Dan Rather
CBS Evening News with Norah O'Donnell
Q700402.blurb: CBS Evening News becomes U.S. network television's first half-hour weeknight news broadcast, when the show is lengthened from 15 to 30 minutes.

Q700442.name: Second Taiwan Strait Crisis
Q700442.blurb: Chinese Civil War: The Second Taiwan Strait Crisis begins with the People's Liberation Army's bombardment of Quemoy.

Q700533.name: Vyborg–Petrozavodsk Offensive
Q700533.blurb: World War II: Continuation War: The Vyborg–Petrozavodsk Offensive, the largest offensive launched by Soviet Union against Finland during the Second World War, ends to a strategic stalemate. Both Finnish and Soviet troops at the Finnish front dug to defensive positions, and the front remains stable until the end of the war.

Q700547.name: Operation Vengeance
Q700547.blurb: World War II: Operation Vengeance, Admiral Isoroku Yamamoto is killed when his aircraft is shot down by U.S. fighters over Bougainville Island.

Q700569.name: Sinking of Prince of Wales and Repulse
aliases: Sinking of Repulse and Prince of Wales
Sinking of the Prince of Wales and Repulse
Sinking of the Prince of Wales and the Repulse
Q700569.blurb: World War II: The Royal Navy capital ships HMS Prince of Wales and HMS Repulse are sunk by Imperial Japanese Navy torpedo bombers near British Malaya.

Q700705.name: Battle of Saipan
Q700705.blurb: World War II: The United States invades Saipan, capital of Japan's South Seas Mandate.

Q700710.name: Battle of Villers-Bocage
Q700710.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Villers-Bocage:  German tank ace Michael Wittmann ambushes elements of the British 7th Armoured Division, destroying up to fourteen tanks, fifteen personnel carriers and two anti-tank guns in a Tiger I tank.

Q700754.name: inner German border
Q700754.blurb: East German official Günter Schabowski mistakenly announced the immediate opening of the inner German border, resulting in the fall of the Berlin Wall that night (border crossing pictured).

Q700833.name: 2008 Taiwanese presidential election
Q700833.blurb: Taiwan opposition leader Ma Ying-jeou resigns as the chairman of the Kuomintang party after being indicted on charges of embezzlement during his tenure as the mayor of Taipei; Ma also announces his candidacy for the 2008 presidential election.

Q700841.name: Ottoman-Safavid War
Q700841.blurb: The Ottoman Empire and the Safavid Empire sign a peace treaty to end the Ottoman–Safavid War of 1532–1555.

Q700848.name: Convention of London
Q700848.blurb: The Great Powers of Europe conclude the convention of London in order to stabilise the Near East.

Q700860.name: Battle of Eckmühl
Q700860.blurb: The second day of the Battle of Eckmühl: The Austrian army is defeated by the First French Empire army led by Napoleon and driven over the Danube in Regensburg.

Q700864.name: Zeebrugge Raid
Q700864.blurb: World War I: The British Royal Navy makes a raid in an attempt to neutralise the Belgian port of Bruges-Zeebrugge.

Q700883.name: Treaty of Tientsin
Q700883.blurb: Treaty of Tientsin is signed to end the Sino-French War, with China eventually giving up Tonkin and Annam – most of present-day Vietnam – to France.

Q700886.name: Siege of Constantinople
Q700886.blurb: Ottoman Sultan Murad II besieges Constantinople, but is ultimately unsuccessful.

Q700893.name: Conquest of Tunis
Q700893.blurb: Combined forces loyal to Charles V attack and expel the Ottomans from Tunis during the Conquest of Tunis.

Q700924.name: end of World War II in Europe
aliases: Dissolution of the Greater Germanic Reich
End of World War 2 in Europe
End of the Second World War in Europe
German surrender in World War II
The end of World War II in Europe
Q700924.blurb: A parade in Sétif, French Algeria, celebrating the end of World War II in Europe became a riot and was followed by reprisals, carried out by colonial authorities over the following weeks, that killed thousands.

Q700960.name: Battle of Kiev
Q700960.blurb: World War II: The 1st Ukrainian Front liberates Kyiv from German occupation.

Q700983.name: German Instrument of Surrender
aliases: Surrender of Nazi Germany in World War II
Q700983.blurb: World War II: The German Instrument of Surrender signed at Berlin-Karlshorst comes into effect.  This is commemorated as Victory in Europe Day.

Q701094.name: Siege of Candia
Q701094.blurb: The Venetians surrender the fortress of Candia to the Ottomans, thus ending the 21-year-long Siege of Candia.

Q701139.name: Battle of Liegnitz
Q701139.blurb: Seven Years' War: Battle of Liegnitz: Frederick the Great's victory over the Austrians under Ernst Gideon von Laudon.

Q701180.name: Battle of Nanking
Q701180.blurb: Second Sino-Japanese War: Battle of Nanking: Japanese troops under the command of Lt. Gen. Yasuhiko Asaka launch an assault on the Chinese city of Nanking.

Q701335.name: Battle of Sisak
Q701335.blurb: Battle of Sisak: Allied Christian troops defeat the Ottomans.

Q701367.name: Battle of Jemmingen
Q701367.blurb: Eighty Years' War: in the Battle of Jemmingen, Fernando Álvarez de Toledo, Duke of Alva defeats Louis of Nassau.

Q701518.name: Armistice of Villa Giusti
Q701518.blurb: World War I: The Armistice of Villa Giusti between Italy and Austria-Hungary is implemented.

Q701967.name: Japanese occupation of Hong Kong
Q701967.blurb: The Japanese occupation of Hong Kong comes to an end.

Q702170.name: July 1932 German federal election
Q702170.blurb: The NSDAP (Nazi Party) wins more than 38% of the vote in German elections.

Q702189.name: Treaty of Niš
Q702189.blurb: The Treaty of Niš is signed by the Ottoman Empire and Russia ending the Russian–Turkish War.

Q702250.name: Kiel mutiny
Q702250.blurb: The German Revolution of 1918–19 begins when 40,000 sailors take over the port in Kiel.

Q702377.name: Battle of the Yellow Sea
Q702377.blurb: Russo-Japanese War: The Battle of the Yellow Sea between the Russian and Japanese battleship fleets takes place.

Q702568.name: Battle of Corregidor
Q702568.blurb: World War II: American forces land on Corregidor Island in the Philippines.

Q702579.name: Battle of Ko Chang
Q702579.blurb: Franco-Thai War: Vichy French forces inflict a decisive defeat over the Royal Thai Navy.

Q702729.name: Invasion of Lingayen Gulf
Q702729.blurb: World War II: The Sixth United States Army begins the invasion of Lingayen Gulf.

Q703179.name: Goguryeo–Tang War
Q703179.blurb: Goguryeo–Tang War: Led by Emperor Taizong, the Tang army was forced to abandon a siege of Ansi Fortress.

Q703363.name: Battle of Frankenhausen
Q703363.blurb: Insurgent peasants led by Anabaptist pastor Thomas Müntzer are defeated at the Battle of Frankenhausen, ending the German Peasants' War in the Holy Roman Empire.

Q703378.name: German Autumn
Q703378.blurb: German Autumn: A set of events revolving around the kidnapping of Hanns Martin Schleyer and the hijacking of a Lufthansa flight by the Red Army Faction (RAF) comes to an end when Schleyer is murdered and various RAF members allegedly commit suicide.

Q703436.name: Battle of Rain
Q703436.blurb: Battle of Rain: Swedes under Gustavus Adolphus defeat the Holy Roman Empire during the Thirty Years' War.

Q703482.name: Battle of Bataan
Q703482.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Bataan ends and the Bataan Death March begins.

Q703523.name: Battle of Stilo
Q703523.blurb: King Otto II and his Frankish army are defeated by the Muslim army of al-Qasim at Cape Colonna, Southern Italy.

Q703550.name: Axis occupation of Greece
aliases: Axis Occupation of Greece during WWII
Axis invasion of greece during world war 2
Axis occupation of Greece during World War II
Bulgarian occupation zone of Greece during WWII
Greece during the Second World War
Occupation of Greece by Nazi Germany
Q703550.blurb: World War II: German troops enter Athens.

Q703762.name: China Airlines Flight 006
Q703762.blurb: China Airlines Flight 006 experiences an aircraft upset over the Pacific Ocean, injuring 24.

Q704333.name: Battle of Macau
Q704333.blurb: Battle of Macau: The Dutch make a failed attempt to capture Macau.

Q704361.name: Laconia incident
Q704361.blurb: RMS Laconia was sunk by a U-boat off the coast of West Africa, which then attempted to rescue the passengers as it was acting under the old prize rules.

Q704481.name: 2010 Senkaku boat collision incident
Q704481.blurb: A Chinese fishing trawler collides with two Japanese Coast Guard patrol boats in disputed waters near the Senkaku Islands.

Q704536.name: London Naval Treaty
aliases: London treaty for the reduction of naval armaments
Treaty for the Limitation and Reduction of Naval Armament
Treaty for the Limitation and Reduction of Naval Armaments
Q704536.blurb: The United Kingdom, Japan and the United States sign the London Naval Treaty regulating submarine warfare and limiting shipbuilding.

Q704550.name: Battle of Hel
Q704550.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Hel begins, the longest-defended pocket of Polish Army resistance during the German invasion of Poland.

Q704627.name: Operation Starvation
Q704627.blurb: World War II: Operation Starvation, the aerial mining of Japan's ports and waterways begins. Argentina declares war on the Axis Powers.

Q704762.name: Battle of Klissow
Q704762.blurb: Great Northern War: A numerically superior Polish-Saxon army of Augustus II the Strong, operating from an advantageous defensive position, is defeated by a Swedish army half its size under the command of King Charles XII in the Battle of Klissow.

Q705083.name: Raid at Cabanatuan
Q705083.blurb: World War II: Raid at Cabanatuan: One hundred and twenty-six American Rangers and Filipino resistance fighters liberate over 500 Allied prisoners from the Japanese-controlled Cabanatuan POW camp.

Q705165.name: Bombing of Chongqing
Q705165.blurb: World War II: Four thousand Chongqing residents are asphyxiated in a bomb shelter during the Bombing of Chongqing.

Q705373.name: Third Taiwan Strait Crisis
Q705373.blurb: Third Taiwan Strait Crisis: The People's Liberation Army begins firing missiles into the waters north of Taiwan.

Q705813.name: Battle of Hohenlinden
Q705813.blurb: War of the Second Coalition: Battle of Hohenlinden: French General Jean Victor Marie Moreau decisively defeats the Archduke John of Austria near Munich. Coupled with First Consul Napoleon Bonaparte's earlier victory at Marengo, this will force the Austrians to sign an armistice and end the war.

Q705874.name: Battle of Mohi
Q705874.blurb: Batu Khan defeats Béla IV of Hungary at the Battle of Mohi.

Q705936.name: Battle of Quatre Bras
Q705936.blurb: Battle of Ligny and Battle of Quatre Bras, two days before the Battle of Waterloo.

Q706183.name: Sino-French War
Q706183.blurb: Sino-French War: Beginning of the Battle of Núi Bop.

Q706454.name: Netherlands in World War II
aliases: involvement of the Netherlands in World War II
Q706454.blurb: On her thirteenth birthday, Anne Frank (pictured) began keeping a diary during the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands in World War II.

Q706563.name: Siege of Tsingtao
Q706563.blurb: World War I: Siege of Tsingtao: A Japanese fleet commanded by Vice Admiral Sadakichi Kato imposes a blockade along the whole coastline of German Tsingtao, initiating the Siege of Tsingtao.

Q706755.name: Battle of Fort Washington
Q706755.blurb: American Revolutionary War: British and Hessian units capture Fort Washington from the Patriots.

Q706817.name: International Conference to Review the Global Vision of the Holocaust
Q706817.blurb: The International Conference to Review the Global Vision of the Holocaust is opened in Tehran, Iran, by then-president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad; nations such as Israel and the United States express concern.

Q707038.name: Dachau liberation reprisals
Q707038.blurb: World War II: The U.S. Army liberated Dachau, the first Nazi concentration camp, and killed German prisoners of war.

Q707269.name: Treaty of Taipei
Q707269.blurb: The Sino-Japanese Peace Treaty (Treaty of Taipei) is signed in Taipei, Taiwan between Japan and the Republic of China to officially end the Second Sino-Japanese War.

Q707497.name: China Airlines Flight 120
Q707497.blurb: China Airlines Flight 120 catches fire and explodes after landing at Naha Airport in Okinawa, Japan.

Q707547.name: Jedwabne pogrom
Q707547.blurb: Jedwabne pogrom: Massacre of Polish Jews living in and near the village of Jedwabne.

Q707956.name: Tungchow Mutiny
Q707956.blurb: Tongzhou mutiny: In Tongzhou, China, the East Hebei Army attacks Japanese troops and civilians.

Q708088.name: Battle of Corunna
Q708088.blurb: Peninsular War: The British defeat the French at the Battle of La Coruña.

Q708154.name: Typhoon Longwang
Q708154.blurb: Typhoon Longwang made landfall in China as the deadliest tropical cyclone in that year to impact the country.

Q708181.name: Siege of Bastogne
Q708181.blurb: World War II: George S. Patton's Third Army breaks the encirclement of surrounded U.S. forces at Bastogne, Belgium.

Q708189.name: Port Arthur massacre
Q708189.blurb: Port Arthur, China, falls to the Japanese, a decisive victory of the First Sino-Japanese War; Japanese troops are accused of massacring the remaining inhabitants.

Q708217.name: Battles of Narvik
Q708217.blurb: World War II: Norwegian, French, Polish and British forces recapture Narvik in Norway. This is the first Allied infantry victory of the War.

Q708235.name: Operation Veritable
Q708235.blurb: World War II: British and Canadian forces commence Operation Veritable to occupy land between the Maas and Rhine rivers.

Q708253.name: Colmar Pocket
Q708253.blurb: Audie Murphy engaged in action at the Colmar Pocket that won him a Medal of Honor and made him one of the most famous and decorated U.S. soldiers of World War II.

Q708321.name: Berlin Crisis of 1961
Q708321.blurb: Cold War: In the Vienna summit, the Soviet premier Nikita Khrushchev sparks the Berlin Crisis by threatening to sign a separate peace treaty with East Germany and ending American, British and French access to East Berlin.

Q708426.name: Air battle of Berlin
Q708426.blurb: World War II:  In the first action of the Berlin Air Offensive, four hundred and forty Royal Air Force planes bomb Berlin causing only light damage and killing 131. The RAF loses nine aircraft and 53 air crew.

Q708580.name: Battle of Salamanca
Q708580.blurb: Napoleonic Wars: Peninsular War: Battle of Salamanca: British forces led by Arthur Wellesley (later the Duke of Wellington) defeat French troops near Salamanca, Spain.

Q708601.name: Punctation of Olmütz
Q708601.blurb: The treaty, Punctation of Olmütz, is signed in Olomouc. Prussia capitulates to Austria, which will take over the leadership of the German Confederation.

Q708862.name: Treaty of Lübeck
Q708862.blurb: Albrecht von Wallenstein and King Christian IV of Denmark signed the Treaty of Lübeck to end Danish intervention in the Thirty Years' War.

Q709261.name: Hundred Regiments Offensive
Q709261.blurb: World War II: The Eighth Route Army launches the Hundred Regiments Offensive, a successful campaign to disrupt Japanese war infrastructure and logistics in occupied northern China.

Q709370.name: Kuril Islands landing operation
Q709370.blurb: Soviet-Japanese War: Battle of Shumshu: Soviet forces land at Takeda Beach on Shumshu Island and launch the Battle of Shumshu; the Soviet Union's Invasion of the Kuril Islands commences.

Q709396.name: Battle of Pingxingguan
Q709396.blurb: Second Sino-Japanese War: The Chinese Eighth Route Army gains a minor, but morale-boosting victory in the Battle of Pingxingguan.

Q709416.name: China Airlines Flight 676
Q709416.blurb: China Airlines Flight 676 crashes into a road and residential area near Chiang Kai-shek International Airport in Taiwan, killing all 196 aboard and six more on the ground.

Q709855.name: Jinan Incident
Q709855.blurb: The Jinan incident begins with the deaths of twelve Japanese civilians by Chinese forces in Jinan, China, which leads to Japanese retaliation and the deaths of over 2,000 Chinese civilians in the following days.

Q712645.name: Defense of Harbin
Q712645.blurb: Second Sino-Japanese War: The Chinese National Revolutionary Army begins the defense of Harbin.

Q712897.name: 1996 Qana massacre
Q712897.blurb: The Israeli military commits the Qana massacre in a deliberate shelling of a United Nations compound near the village of Qana in southern Lebanon, killing 106 Lebanese civilians who were taking shelter there and wounding over 100 more.

Q712907.name: 1964 Brinks Hotel bombing
Q712907.blurb: The Viet Cong bombed the Brinks Hotel in Saigon, killing two U.S. Army officers and raising fears of an escalation of the Vietnam War.

Q713006.name: Battle of Corregidor
Q713006.blurb: World War II: Japanese troops overcame fierce American and Philippine resistance to win the Battle of Corregidor.

Q713018.name: Battle of Kapyong
Q713018.blurb: Korean War: Assaulting Chinese forces are forced to withdraw after heavy fighting with UN forces, primarily made up of Australian and Canadian troops, at the Battle of Kapyong.

Q713516.name: Doolittle Raid
Q713516.blurb: World War II: The Doolittle Raid on Japan: Tokyo, Yokohama, Kobe and Nagoya are bombed.

Q713529.name: Battle of the River Plate
aliases: Battle of the Rio de la Plata
The Battle of the River Plate
Q713529.blurb: The Battle of the River Plate is fought off the coast of Uruguay; the first naval battle of World War II. The Kriegsmarine's Deutschland-class cruiser (pocket battleship) Admiral Graf Spee engages with three Royal Navy cruisers: HMS Ajax, HMNZS Achilles and HMS Exeter.

Q713540.name: comfort woman
aliases: Serial Kidnapping of Korean Women in 1930's
Serial Kidnapping of Korean Women in 1930s
Serial Kidnapping of Women in Korea in 1930's
Q713540.blurb: During a visit to South Korea, Japanese Prime Minister Kiichi Miyazawa apologizes for forcing Korean women into sexual slavery during World War II.

Q713544.name: Ryongchon disaster
Q713544.blurb: Flammable cargo exploded at a railway station in Ryongchon, North Korea, killing at least 54 people and injuring more than a thousand others.

Q714081.name: Einstein–Szilárd letter
Q714081.blurb: Leo Szilard penned a letter, signed by Albert Einstein and addressed to U.S. president Franklin D. Roosevelt, warning that Germany may develop atomic bombs, leading to the establishment of the Manhattan Project.

Q714196.name: Spring 1945 offensive in Italy
Q714196.blurb: World War II: American and Brazilian troops kick off Operation Encore in Northern Italy, a successful limited action in the Northern Apennines that prepares for the western portion of the Allied Spring offensive.

Q714253.name: Air Raid on Bari
Q714253.blurb: World War II: A Luftwaffe bombing raid on the harbour of Bari, Italy, sinks numerous cargo and transport ships, including the American SS John Harvey, which is carrying a stockpile of mustard gas.

Q714259.name: Operation Achse
Q714259.blurb: World War II: In the course of Operation Achse, German troops begin their occupation of Rome.

Q714320.name: 1999 Jiji earthquake
Q714320.blurb: The 7.7-magnitude Chi-Chi earthquake strikes central Taiwan, killing 2,400 people.

Q714349.name: Rotterdam Blitz
aliases: Bombing of Rotterdam by Nazi Germany
Bombing of Rotterdam during the Second World War
Bombing of Rotterdam in World War II
German bombing of Rotterdam in World War II
World War II bombing of Rotterdam
Q714349.blurb: World War II: Rotterdam, Netherlands, is bombed by the Luftwaffe of Nazi Germany despite a ceasefire, killing about 900 people and destroying the historic city center.

Q714684.name: Battle of Gabon
Q714684.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Gabon ends as Free French Forces take Libreville, Gabon, and all of French Equatorial Africa from Vichy French forces.

Q714706.name: 1940–1944 insurgency in Chechnya
Q714706.blurb: In response to an insurgency in Chechnya, the Soviet Union began the forced deportation of the native Chechen and Ingush of North Caucasus.

Q714749.name: Battle of Ia Drang
Q714749.blurb: Vietnam War: The Battle of Ia Drang begins. This is the first major engagement between regular American and North Vietnamese forces.

Q715282.name: PROTECT IP Act
aliases: Preventing Real Online Threats to Economic Creativity and Theft of Intellectual Property Act
Preventing Real Online Threats to Economic Creativity and Theft of Intellectual Property Act of 2011
Q715282.blurb: More than 115,000 websites engage in an online protest against the Stop Online Piracy Act and the Protect IP Act in the US.[citation needed] The websites involved viewed the laws as infringing on the right to free speech and many of them temporarily shut down in protest.

Q715416.name: Battle of An Lộc
Q715416.blurb: Vietnam War: The Battle of An Lộc begins.

Q715495.name: 1896 Sanriku earthquake
Q715495.blurb: One of the deadliest tsunamis in Japan's history kills more than 22,000 people.

Q715579.name: Battle of Utsunomiya Castle
Q715579.blurb: Boshin War: The Battle of Utsunomiya Castle ends as former Tokugawa shogunate forces withdraw northward.

Q715645.name: Japanese occupation of Singapore
Q715645.blurb: World War II: The Provisional Government of Free India is formally established in Japanese-occupied Singapore.

Q715683.name: South African Airways Flight 295
Q715683.blurb: South African Airways Flight 295 crashes into the Indian Ocean, killing all 159 people on board.

Q715791.name: Battle of Pyongyang
Q715791.blurb: First Sino-Japanese War: Japan defeats the Qing dynasty in the Battle of Pyongyang, causing the Qing army to withdraw to the Chinese border with Korea.

Q715886.name: Battle of the North Cape
Q715886.blurb: Second World War: The German battleship Scharnhorst was sunk at the Battle of the North Cape during an attempt to attack Arctic convoys.

Q716112.name: Treaty of Saint Petersburg
Q716112.blurb: China and Russia sign the Sino-Russian Ili Treaty.

Q716144.name: Sook Ching
Q716144.blurb: World War II: The Imperial Japanese Army begins the systematic extermination of perceived hostile elements among the Chinese in Singapore.

Q716425.name: Battle of Lwów
Q716425.blurb: A Polish-Lithuanian army under John III Sobieski defeats an Ottoman-Tartar army in the battle of Lwow.

Q716479.name: Battle of Świecino
Q716479.blurb: Thirteen Years' War: A Polish army under Piotr Dunin decisively defeats the Teutonic Order at the Battle of Świecino.

Q716521.name: deportation of Koreans in the Soviet Union
Q716521.blurb: The first group of around 172,000 Koreans were deported by Soviet authorities from the Russian Far East to the Kazakh and Uzbek SSRs; around 10 to 25 percent died.

Q716562.name: Battle of Hakodate
Q716562.blurb: One day after surrendering at the Battle of Hakodate, Enomoto Takeaki turned the fort of Goryōkaku over to Japanese forces, signaling the collapse of the Republic of Ezo.

Q717004.name: Battle of Leyte
Q717004.blurb: United States forces land in the Philippines.

Q717322.name: Battle of Palermo
Q717322.blurb: Franco-Dutch War: France ensures the supremacy of its naval fleet for the remainder of the war with its victory in the Battle of Palermo.

Q717346.name: Treaty of Windsor
Q717346.blurb: England and Portugal formally ratify their alliance with the signing of the Treaty of Windsor, making it the oldest diplomatic alliance in the world which is still in force.

Q717373.name: Japanese invasion of Taiwan
Q717373.blurb: Japanese invasion of Taiwan: Battle of Baguashan: The Empire of Japan decisively defeats a smaller Formosan army at Changhua, crippling the short-lived Republic of Formosa and leading to its surrender two months later.

Q717569.name: blood, toil, tears, and sweat
Q717569.blurb: World War II: Germany's conquest of France begins, as the German army crosses the Meuse. Winston Churchill makes his "blood, toil, tears, and sweat" speech to the House of Commons.

Q717780.name: Kaohsiung Incident
Q717780.blurb: Kaohsiung Incident: Taiwanese pro-democracy demonstrations are suppressed by the KMT dictatorship, and organizers are arrested.

Q718274.name: The Hump
Q718274.blurb: World War II: The United States Army Air Forces flew its first mission from India over the Hump (the eastern end of the Himalayas) to deliver materiel to China.

Q718605.name: Martial law in Poland
Q718605.blurb: Martial law in Poland is officially revoked.

Q718738.name: Soviet occupation of Latvia in 1940
aliases: the entry of Soviet army in Latvia
Q718738.blurb: World War II: The Soviet Union formally annexes Latvia.

Q718770.name: Battle of Khafji
Q718770.blurb: The first major ground engagement of the Gulf War began with the Iraqi invasion of Khafji, Saudi Arabia, recaptured three days later by Coalition forces.

Q718851.name: Battle of Nasiriyah
Q718851.blurb: Battle of Nasiriyah, first major conflict during the invasion of Iraq.

Q719252.name: Battle of Antietam
Q719252.blurb: American Civil War: Almost 23,000 total casualties were suffered at the Battle of Antietam near Sharpsburg, Maryland, where Confederate and Union troops fought to a tactical stalemate.

Q719524.name: Our Lady of Fátima
aliases: Our Lady of the Holy Rosary of Fátima
Q719524.blurb: Three children report the first apparition of Our Lady of Fátima in Fátima, Portugal.

Q719592.name: local council of Malta
aliases: List of Towns in Malta and Gozo
List of local councils of Malta
Q719592.blurb: Malta is officially subdivided into 68 local councils by the Local Councils Act.

Q719883.name: Statute of Westminster 1931
aliases: An Act to give effect to certain resolutions passed by Imperial Conferences held in the years 1926 and 1930
Q719883.blurb: New Zealand ratifies the Statute of Westminster and thus becomes independent of legislative control by the United Kingdom.

Q719992.name: Fourth Council of the Lateran
Q719992.blurb: The Fourth Council of the Lateran meets, defining the doctrine of transubstantiation, the process by which bread and wine are, by that doctrine, said to transform into the body and blood of Christ.

Q720348.name: Battle of Ras al-Ayn
Q720348.blurb: Syrian civil war: The Battle of Ras al-Ayn resumes between the People's Protection Units (YPG) and Islamist forces, beginning the Rojava–Islamist conflict.

Q720498.name: 13 Vendémiaire
Q720498.blurb: Napoleon first rises to prominence by suppressing counter-revolutionary rioters threatening the National Convention.

Q721168.name: Truce of Andrusovo
Q721168.blurb: The Truce of Andrusovo is signed, ending the Russian-Polish War of 1654-1667.

Q722051.name: Anglo-Ashanti wars
Q722051.blurb: The Ashantis defeat British forces in the Gold Coast during the First Anglo-Ashanti War.

Q722402.name: 1931 Hawke's Bay earthquake
Q722402.blurb: The Hawke's Bay earthquake, New Zealand's worst natural disaster, kills 258.

Q722529.name: EgyptAir Flight 990
Q722529.blurb: EgyptAir Flight 990 crashes into the Atlantic Ocean near Nantucket, killing all 217 people on board.

Q722699.name: Fashoda Incident
Q722699.blurb: The Fashoda Incident triggers the last war scare between Britain and France.

Q722791.name: Voskhod 2
Q722791.blurb: Cosmonaut Alexei Leonov ventured outside the Soviet spacecraft Voskhod 2, becoming the first person to walk in space.

Q722990.name: 2004 Ashura bombings in Iraq
Q722990.blurb: War in Iraq: Al-Qaeda carries out the Ashoura Massacre in Iraq, killing 170 and wounding over 500.

Q723608.name: Trajan's Dacian Wars
Q723608.blurb: Roman emperor Trajan dedicates a column celebrating and depicting his victory over the Dacians.

Q723800.name: Prussian uprisings
Q723800.blurb: The Great Prussian Uprising among the old Prussians begins against the Teutonic Knights.

Q725043.name: Operation Opera
Q725043.blurb: The Israeli Air Force attacked a nuclear reactor under the assumption that it was about to start producing plutonium to further an Iraqi nuclear-weapons program.

Q725571.name: Rush–Bagot Treaty
Q725571.blurb: The United States Senate ratifies the Rush–Bagot Treaty, limiting naval armaments on the Great Lakes and Lake Champlain.

Q725982.name: Osaka school massacre
Q725982.blurb: Mamoru Takuma kills eight and injures 15 in a mass stabbing at an elementary school in the Osaka Prefecture of Japan.

Q726261.name: Ottoman Interregnum
Q726261.blurb: Following the successful campaigns during the Ottoman Interregnum, Musa Çelebi, one of the sons of Bayezid I, becomes Sultan of the Ottoman Empire with the support of Mircea I of Wallachia.

Q726501.name: Dust Bowl
Q726501.blurb: Dust Bowl: A severe dust storm swept across Oklahoma and northern Texas, removing an estimated 300 million tons of topsoil from the prairies.

Q726731.name: Krazy Kat
Q726731.blurb: The final page of the comic Krazy Kat is published, exactly two months after its author George Herriman died.

Q727536.name: Sinai and Palestine Campaign
Q727536.blurb: First World War: The British Empire's Sinai and Palestine campaign began with a victory at the Battle of Romani.

Q727854.name: Missouri Compromise
Q727854.blurb: The Missouri Compromise is signed into law by United States President James Monroe. The compromise allows Missouri to enter the Union as a slave state, brings Maine into the Union as a free state, and makes the rest of the northern part of the Louisiana Purchase territory slavery-free.

Q728480.name: Battle of Rocroi
Q728480.blurb: Thirty Years' War: French forces under the duc d'Enghien decisively defeat Spanish forces at the Battle of Rocroi, marking the symbolic end of Spain as a dominant land power.

Q730553.name: Battle of Myriokephalon
Q730553.blurb: The Battle of Myriokephalon is the last attempt by the Byzantine Empire to recover central Anatolia from the Seljuk Turks.

Q730878.name: Hama Massacre
Q730878.blurb: Hama massacre: The government of Syria attacks the town of Hama.

Q731564.name: Battle of Block Island
Q731564.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Ships of the Continental Navy fail in their attempt to capture a Royal Navy dispatch boat.

Q731814.name: Catholic League
Q731814.blurb: Thirty Years' War: A Swedish–German army defeated the forces of the Catholic League at the Battle of Rain, mortally wounding their commander Johann Tserclaes, Count of Tilly.

Q732063.name: Cheers
Q732063.blurb: Cheers, an American television sitcom, debuted with its pilot episode on NBC.

Q732219.name: 28 May 1926 coup d'état
Q732219.blurb: The 28 May 1926 coup d'état: Ditadura Nacional is established in Portugal to suppress the unrest of the First Republic.

Q732816.name: Fourth Council of Constantinople
Q732816.blurb: The Fourth Council of Constantinople closes.

Q732992.name: Quebec Expedition
Q732992.blurb: Britain's Quebec Expedition loses eight ships and almost nine hundred soldiers, sailors and women to rocks at Pointe-aux-Anglais.

Q733364.name: Battle of Megiddo
Q733364.blurb: Battle of Megiddo: The first battle to have been recorded in what is accepted as relatively reliable detail.

Q733739.name: 1138 Aleppo earthquake
Q733739.blurb: A massive earthquake strikes Aleppo; it is one of the most destructive earthquakes ever.

Q734004.name: Black January
Q734004.blurb: Protests in Azerbaijan, part of the Dissolution of the Soviet Union.

Q734700.name: Battle of Avarayr
Q734700.blurb: Battle of Avarayr between Armenian rebels and the Sasanian Empire takes place. The Sasanids defeat the Armenians militarily but guarantee them freedom to openly practice Christianity.

Q734934.name: Four Days' Battle
Q734934.blurb: A four day long naval engagement between the Dutch and English fleet ends, with the English suffering heavier losses.

Q735043.name: Siege of Klis
Q735043.blurb: Croatian–Ottoman wars: After the execution of feudal lord Petar Kružić, Croatian forces at Klis surrendered to the Ottoman forces in exchange for their safe passage to northern locations.

Q735876.name: Battle of Siffin
Q735876.blurb: First Fitna: In the Battle of Siffin, troops led by Ali ibn Abu Talib clash with those led by Muawiyah I.

Q735960.name: Battle of the Vosges
Q735960.blurb: The Battle of Trippstadt between French forces and those of Prussia and Austria begins.

Q736140.name: Battle of Öland
Q736140.blurb: Battle of Öland: allied Danish-Dutch forces defeat the Swedish navy in the Baltic Sea, during the Scanian War (1675–79).

Q736268.name: Finnish War
Q736268.blurb: Finnish War: Sweden loses the fortress of Sveaborg to Russia.

Q736490.name: Battle of Vaal Krantz
Q736490.blurb: Second Boer War: British troops fail in their third attempt to lift the Siege of Ladysmith.

Q736968.name: 2008 Los Roques archipelago Transaven Let L-410 crash
Q736968.blurb: A Let L-410 Turbolet crashes in the Los Roques Archipelago in Venezuela, killing 14 people.

Q737542.name: Genpei War
Q737542.blurb: Genpei War: In the Battle of Ishibashiyama in Japan, the new military commander of the Minamoto clan, Minamoto no Yoritomo, is routed by Ōba Kagechika of the Taira clan.

Q737890.name: Hurricane Rita
Q737890.blurb: Hurricane Rita makes landfall in the United States, devastating portions of southwestern Louisiana and extreme southeastern Texas.

Q737967.name: 1972 Andes flight disaster
Q737967.blurb: Uruguayan Air Force Flight 571 crashes in the Andes mountains. Twenty-eight survive the crash. All but 16 succumb before rescue on December 23.

Q738813.name: Battle of Smoliani
Q738813.blurb: Napoleonic Wars: At the Battle of Smoliani, French Marshals Victor and Oudinot are defeated by the Russians under General Peter Wittgenstein.

Q738854.name: 1950 Assam–Tibet earthquake
Q738854.blurb: Measuring Mw 8.6, the largest earthquake on land occurs in the Assam-Tibet-Myanmar border, killing 4,800.

Q739644.name: Overland Campaign
Q739644.blurb: American Civil War: Overland Campaign: Battle of Cold Harbor: The Army of Northern Virginia engages the Army of the Potomac.

Q740404.name: Battle of Cane Hill
Q740404.blurb: American Civil War: In the Battle of Cane Hill, Union troops under General James G. Blunt defeat General John Marmaduke's Confederates.

Q740724.name: Treaty of Paris
Q740724.blurb: The First Treaty of Paris is signed, returning the French frontiers to their 1792 extent, and restoring the House of Bourbon to power.

Q740791.name: Serbo-Bulgarian War
Q740791.blurb: Serbo-Bulgarian War: The decisive Battle of Slivnitsa begins.

Q741098.name: Siege of Antioch
Q741098.blurb: First Crusade: The first Siege of Antioch ends as Crusader forces take the city; the second siege began five days later.

Q741126.name: Iran Aseman Airlines Flight 6895
Q741126.blurb: Sixty-five passengers are killed when Iran Aseman Airlines Flight 6895 crashes during an emergency landing at Manas International Airport in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan.

Q741398.name: 1996 Air Africa crash
Q741398.blurb: An Antonov An-32 cargo aircraft crashes into a crowded market in Kinshasa, Zaire, killing up to 223 people on the ground; two of six crew members are also killed.

Q741777.name: War of Mutina
Q741777.blurb: War of Mutina: Despite initial success, troops loyal to Mark Antony were defeated near the Via Aemilia in northern Italy by legions loyal to the Roman Senate.

Q741788.name: Battle of Alcântara
Q741788.blurb: War of the Portuguese Succession: Spanish victory at the Battle of Alcântara brings about the Iberian Union.

Q742687.name: Operation Arc Light
Q742687.blurb: Vietnam War: The United States Air Force uses B-52 bombers to attack guerrilla fighters in South Vietnam.

Q742728.name: 1972 Moroccan coup attempt
Q742728.blurb: In an unsuccessful coup d'état attempt, the Royal Moroccan Air Force fires upon Hassan II of Morocco's plane while he is traveling back to Rabat.

Q742731.name: Winnipeg general strike
Q742731.blurb: The Winnipeg general strike begins. By 11:00, almost the whole working population of Winnipeg had walked off the job.

Q742813.name: Chincha Islands War
Q742813.blurb: Chincha Islands War: Peru allies with Chile against Spain.

Q743060.name: Iran Air Flight 655 shootdown
Q743060.blurb: United States Navy warship USS Vincennes shoots down Iran Air Flight 655 over the Persian Gulf, killing all 290 people aboard.

Q743306.name: International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination
aliases: Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination
Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination
Committee on the Elimination of all forms of Racial Discrimination
Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Race Discrimination
Convention on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination
The U.N. Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination
UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination
United Nations Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination
Q743306.blurb: International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination is adopted.

Q743652.name: British expedition to Abyssinia
Q743652.blurb: At Arogee in Abyssinia, British and Indian forces defeat an army of Emperor Tewodros II. While 700 Ethiopians are killed and many more injured, only two British/Indian troops die.

Q743768.name: The Anarchy
Q743768.blurb: After Empress Matilda released her rival King Stephen, he in turn released Robert of Gloucester, her strongest supporter, thus prolonging the Anglo-Norman civil war known as The Anarchy.

Q744536.name: The Adventures of Tintin
aliases: List of The Adventures of Tintin locations
List of miscellany relating to The Adventures of Tintin
List of the main characters appearing in The Adventures of Tintin
Settings in The Adventures of Tintin
Q744536.blurb: Tintin in the Land of the Soviets, the first volume of The Adventures of Tintin by the Belgian cartoonist Hergé, began serialisation.

Q745110.name: Battle of Chaldiran
Q745110.blurb: The Battle of Chaldiran ends with a decisive victory for the Sultan Selim I, Ottoman Empire, over the Shah Ismail I, founder of the Safavid dynasty.

Q745979.name: Battle of Chancellorsville
Q745979.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Chancellorsville ends with a major defeat of the Union's Army of the Potomac under Joseph Hooker by the Confederate Army of Northern Virginia under Robert E. Lee.

Q746785.name: Mandala Airlines Flight 091
Q746785.blurb: Mandala Airlines Flight 091 crashes after takeoff from Polonia International Airport in Medan, Indonesia, killing 149.

Q746860.name: Battle of Manila
Q746860.blurb: The Philippine–American War begins when four Filipino soldiers enter the "American Zone" in Manila, igniting the Battle of Manila.

Q746993.name: Treaty of Accession 2005
Q746993.blurb: Bulgaria and Romania sign the Treaty of Accession 2005 to join the European Union.

Q747386.name: Battle of Craonne
Q747386.blurb: Emperor Napoleon I of France wins the Battle of Craonne.

Q747589.name: Battle of Isandlwana
Q747589.blurb: Anglo-Zulu War:  the Battle of Isandlwana results in a Zulu victory.

Q747804.name: 2006 Belarusian presidential election
Q747804.blurb: Protesters demanding a new election in Belarus, following the presidential vote days earlier, were arrested, including opposition leader Alyaksandr Kazulin.

Q748042.name: Irish Civil War
Q748042.blurb: The Irish Civil War begins with the shelling of the Four Courts in Dublin by Free State forces.

Q748162.name: 2013 enlargement of the European Union
aliases: Accession of Croatia to the EU
Accession of Croatia to the European Union
Croatia's accession to the European Union
Q748162.blurb: Croatia becomes the 28th member of the European Union.

Q748219.name: Battle of Brandy Station
Q748219.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Brandy Station in Virginia, the largest cavalry battle on American soil, ends Confederate cavalry dominance in the eastern theater.

Q748379.name: 1960 U-2 incident spy aircraft
Q748379.blurb: Cold War: U-2 incident: Francis Gary Powers, in a Lockheed U-2 spyplane, is shot down over the Sverdlovsk Oblast, Soviet Union, sparking a diplomatic crisis.

Q748667.name: 1950 United Kingdom general election
Q748667.blurb: General elections are held in the United Kingdom.

Q748780.name: First Indochina War
aliases: War crimes in the First Indochina War
Q748780.blurb: First Indochina War: The Battle of Vĩnh Yên begins.

Q749610.name: 1964 Alaska great earthquake and tsunami
Q749610.blurb: The Good Friday earthquake, the most powerful earthquake recorded in North American history at a magnitude of 9.2 strikes Southcentral Alaska, killing 125 people and inflicting massive damage to the city of Anchorage.

Q749811.name: Mutiny on the Bounty
Q749811.blurb: The Mutiny on the Bounty occurs, with  the ship's captain, Lieutenant William Bligh and 18 sailors, set adrift, and the rebel crew setting sail for Tahiti.  Eventually the majority of rebels sail for Pitcairn Island.

Q749970.name: insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir
aliases: Counter-terrorist operations in Jammu and Kashmir
Q749970.blurb: Exodus of Kashmiri Pandits from the Kashmir Valley in Indian-administered Kashmir due to an insurgency.

Q750138.name: Astor Place Riot
Q750138.blurb: Astor Place Riot: A riot breaks out at the Astor Opera House in Manhattan, New York City over a dispute between actors Edwin Forrest and William Charles Macready, killing at least 22 and injuring over 120.

Q750144.name: 2010 Canterbury earthquake
Q750144.blurb: A magnitude-7.1 earthquake (damage pictured) struck the Canterbury Region of New Zealand, causing two deaths and up to NZ$40 billion in damages.

Q750567.name: Spring Offensive
Q750567.blurb: World War I: The first phase of the German spring offensive, Operation Michael, begins.

Q751139.name: 1977 Vrancea earthquake
Q751139.blurb: The 1977 Vrancea earthquake in eastern and southern Europe kills more than 1,500, mostly in Bucharest, Romania.

Q751149.name: Earth Summit
aliases: United Nations Conference on Environments and Development
UN Conference on Environment and Development
UN World Commission on Environment and Development
United Nations Commission on Sustainable Development
United Nations Conference on Environment and Development
United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED)
Q751149.blurb: The first World Oceans Day is celebrated, coinciding with the Earth Summit held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

Q751186.name: Battle of Fredericksburg
Q751186.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Fredericksburg begins as the Army of the Potomac under Union General Ambrose Burnside crosses the Rappahannock River to clash with the Army of Northern Virginia led by Confederate General Robert E. Lee in Fredericksburg, Virginia.

Q751236.name: Battle of Dreux
Q751236.blurb: The Battle of Dreux takes place during the French Wars of Religion.

Q751398.name: International Opium Convention
Q751398.blurb: The First International Opium Convention is signed at The Hague.

Q751782.name: 2010 UEFA Champions League Final
Q751782.blurb: Inter Milan beat Bayern Munich 2–0 in the UEFA Champions League final in Madrid, Spain to become the first, and so far only, Italian team to win the historic treble (Serie A, Coppa Italia, Champions League).

Q752253.name: Battle of Mormans
Q752253.blurb: War of the Sixth Coalition: The Battle of Mormant.

Q752308.name: Eastern Air Lines Flight 537
Q752308.blurb: All 55 people on board Eastern Air Lines Flight 537 are killed when the Douglas DC-4 operating the flight collides in mid-air with a Bolivian Air Force Lockheed P-38 Lightning aircraft over Alexandria, Virginia.

Q753167.name: 74th Academy Awards
Q753167.blurb: At the 74th Academy Awards, Halle Berry became the first African American to win Best Actress, winning for her role as Leticia Musgrove in Monster's Ball.

Q753646.name: Exposition Universelle of 1900
Q753646.blurb: The world's fair Exposition Universelle opens in Paris.

Q754483.name: Uruguay v Brazil 1950
aliases: Brazil v Uruguay (1950 FIFA World Cup)
Uruguay vs Brazil (1950 FIFA World Cup)
Q754483.blurb: Uruguay won the decisive match of the fourth FIFA World Cup, defeating Brazil 2–1 at the Maracanã Stadium in Rio de Janeiro.

Q754842.name: Shuttle–Mir program
Q754842.blurb: Space Shuttle Discovery is launched on STS-91, the final mission of the Shuttle-Mir program.

Q755955.name: Battle of Copenhagen
Q755955.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: In the Battle of Copenhagen a British Royal Navy squadron defeats a hastily assembled, smaller, mostly-volunteer Dano-Norwegian Navy at high cost, forcing Denmark out of the Second League of Armed Neutrality.

Q755966.name: Battle of Nineveh
Q755966.blurb: Battle of Nineveh: A Byzantine army under Emperor Heraclius defeats Emperor Khosrau II's Persian forces, commanded by General Rhahzadh.

Q756118.name: Atlanta campaign
Q756118.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Jonesborough, alongside the overall Atlanta campaign, culminates in a Union victory for General William T. Sherman as Confederate General John Bell Hood orders the evacuation of Atlanta.

Q756253.name: Atlantic Southeast Airlines Flight 529
Q756253.blurb: Atlantic Southeast Airlines Flight 529, an Embraer EMB 120 Brasilia, attempts to divert to West Georgia Regional Airport after the left engine fails, but the aircraft crashes in Carroll County near Carrollton, Georgia, killing nine of the 29 people on board.

Q756784.name: 2005 Atlantic hurricane season
Q756784.blurb: Tropical Storm Alpha forms in the Atlantic Basin, making the 2005 Atlantic hurricane season the most active Atlantic hurricane season until surpassed by the 2020 season.

Q756984.name: Shelling of Mainila
Q756984.blurb: Shelling of Mainila: The Soviet Army orchestrates an incident which is used to justify the start of the Winter War with Finland four days later.

Q757299.name: Atlasjet Flight 4203
Q757299.blurb: Atlasjet Flight 4203 crashes in Keçiborlu while on approach to Isparta Süleyman Demirel Airport, killing 57.

Q757644.name: Atoms for Peace
Q757644.blurb: U.S. President Dwight D. Eisenhower delivers his "Atoms for Peace" speech, which leads to an American program to supply equipment and information on nuclear power to schools, hospitals, and research institutions around the world.

Q757669.name: Atomic Age
Q757669.blurb: Manhattan Project: The Atomic Age begins when the United States successfully detonates a plutonium-based test nuclear weapon near Alamogordo, New Mexico.

Q757870.name: Charge of the Light Brigade
aliases: The Charge Of The Light Brigade
Q757870.blurb: Crimean War: The ill-fated Charge of the Light Brigade was decisively repelled by Russian forces during the Battle of Balaclava.

Q757871.name: Indian Ocean raid
Q757871.blurb: World War II: An Indian Ocean raid by Japan's 1st Air Fleet sinks the British aircraft carrier HMS Hermes and the Australian destroyer HMAS Vampire.

Q757963.name: assassination of Martin Luther King Jr.
aliases: killing of Martin Luther King Jr.
murder of Martin Luther King Jr.
Assassination of Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr.
Assassination of Martin Luther King Jr
Assassination of Martin Luther King, Jr
Assassination of Martin Luther King, Jr.
Ben, make sure you play 'Take My Hand, Precious Lord' in the meeting tonight. Play it real pretty.
CORETTA SCOTT KING vs. LOYD JOWERS
Coretta Scott King v. Loyd Jowers
Death of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.
Death of Martin Luther King Jr.
Death of Martin Luther King, Jr
