Death of Martin Luther King, Jr.
Murder of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.
Murder of Martin Luther King, Jr.
Violence after Martin Luther King's Assassination
Q757963.blurb: Martin Luther King Jr. is assassinated by James Earl Ray at a motel in Memphis, Tennessee.

Q757965.name: assassination of Rafic Hariri
Q757965.blurb: In Beirut, 23 people, including former Prime Minister Rafic Hariri, are killed when the equivalent of around 1,000 kg of TNT is detonated while Hariri's motorcade drives through the city.

Q757979.name: attempted assassination of Ronald Reagan
aliases: Assassination attempt on President Ronald Reagan
I hope you are all Republicans
Q757979.blurb: U.S. President Ronald Reagan is shot in the chest outside a Washington, D.C., hotel by John Hinckley Jr.; three others are wounded in the same incident.

Q757980.name: 2008 East Timorese assassination attempts
Q757980.blurb: Rebel East Timorese soldiers invaded the homes of President José Ramos-Horta and Prime Minister Xanana Gusmão, seriously wounding the former.

Q757982.name: Petit-Clamart attack
Q757982.blurb: An assassination attempt orchestrated by the OAS takes place against Charles de Gaulle, although he is uninjured.

Q757986.name: 2011 Tucson shooting
Q757986.blurb: Sitting US Congresswoman Gabby Giffords is shot in the head along with 18 others in a mass shooting in Tucson, Arizona. Giffords survived the assassination attempt, but six others died, including John Roll, a federal judge.

Q759835.name: Civil Wars of the Tetrarchy
Q759835.blurb: Civil wars of the Tetrarchy: An outnumbered army led by Roman emperor Licinius defeated his rival Maximinus II's forces at the Battle of Tzirallum.

Q759837.name: Dissolution of the Monasteries
aliases: Dissolution of the Monasteries, England and Wales
Dissolution of the monasteries in Ireland
Q759837.blurb: Waltham Abbey in England is surrendered to King Henry VIII, the last religious community to be closed during the Dissolution of the Monasteries.

Q759988.name: Zanj Rebellion
Q759988.blurb: Abu al Abbas celebrates a victory parade in Bagdhad following the surpression of the Zanj Rebellion, the largest slave revolt in the Arab world.

Q760002.name: 1991 Iraqi uprisings
Q760002.blurb: Uprisings against Saddam Hussein begin in Iraq, leading to the deaths of more than 25,000 people, mostly civilians.

Q760020.name: Polish 1970 protests
Q760020.blurb: Polish protests: In Gdynia, soldiers fire at workers emerging from trains, killing dozens.

Q760023.name: Goudi coup
Q760023.blurb: A military coup against the government of Dimitrios Rallis began in the neighbourhood of Goudi in Athens, Greece.

Q760629.name: August Uprising
Q760629.blurb: The Georgian opposition stages the August Uprising against the Soviet Union.

Q761031.name: Battle of Arkansas Post
Q761031.blurb: American Civil War: The three-day Battle of Arkansas Post concludes as General John McClernand and Admiral David Dixon Porter capture Fort Hindman and secure control over the Arkansas River for the Union.

Q761454.name: Convention of Constantinople
Q761454.blurb: The Convention of Constantinople is signed, guaranteeing free maritime passage through the Suez Canal during war and peace.

Q761887.name: death of Michael Jackson
aliases: Life and death of Michael Jackson
Michael Jackson Estate vs. AEG Live
Reaction to the death of Michael Jackson
Reactions to the death of Michael Jackson
Q761887.blurb: Singer Michael Jackson died as a result of the combination of drugs in his body.

Q762191.name: Ottoman–Portuguese conflicts of 1538–1560
Q762191.blurb: Turkish–Portuguese War: Battle of Wofla: The Portuguese are scattered, their leader Christovão da Gama is captured and later executed.

Q762458.name: Battle of Ruspina
Q762458.blurb: Julius Caesar fights Titus Labienus in the Battle of Ruspina.

Q762717.name: Battle of Pollentia
Q762717.blurb: Stilicho defeats the Visigoths under Alaric in the Battle of Pollentia.

Q762732.name: Battle of Sardarabad
Q762732.blurb: Armenia defeats the Ottoman Army in the Battle of Sardarabad.

Q763104.name: Dawes Act
Q763104.blurb: The Dawes Act is enacted, authorizing the U.S. President to divide Native American tribal land into individual allotments.

Q763551.name: Battle of Brienne
Q763551.blurb: War of the Sixth Coalition: At the Battle of Brienne, both sides' commanders, Napoleon and Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher, were nearly captured.

Q764793.name: Battle of Fornovo
Q764793.blurb: First Italian War: Battle of Fornovo: Charles VIII defeats the Holy League.

Q764819.name: Battle of Gembloux
Q764819.blurb: Eighty Years' War: Spanish forces won a crushing victory at the Battle of Gembloux, threatening the States General of the Netherlands and contributing to its move from Brussels to Antwerp.

Q764967.name: Andijan massacre
Q764967.blurb: Andijan uprising, Uzbekistan: Troops open fire on crowds of protestors after a prison break; at least 187 people were killed according to official estimates.

Q765215.name: Second Battle of Winchester
Q765215.blurb: American Civil War: Second Battle of Winchester: A Union garrison is defeated by the Army of Northern Virginia in the Shenandoah Valley town of Winchester, Virginia.

Q765499.name: Red River Rebellion
Q765499.blurb: The Wolseley expedition reaches Manitoba to end the Red River Rebellion.

Q766006.name: Partnair Flight 394
Q766006.blurb: Partnair Flight 394 dives into the North Sea, killing 55 people. The investigation showed that the tail of the plane vibrated loose in flight due to sub-standard connecting bolts that had been fraudulently sold as aircraft-grade.

Q766136.name: Battle of Harlaw
Q766136.blurb: Battle of Harlaw, one of the bloodiest battles in Scotland, takes place.

Q766437.name: Rif War
Q766437.blurb: Rif War: The Spanish Army suffers its worst military defeat in modern times to the Berbers of the Rif region of Spanish Morocco.

Q766479.name: Battle of Aldie
Q766479.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Aldie in the Gettysburg campaign.

Q767124.name: Battle of Ctesiphon
Q767124.blurb: The Roman emperor Julian defeats the Sasanian army in the Battle of Ctesiphon, under the walls of the Sasanian capital, but is unable to take the city.

Q767221.name: CTV Television Network
Q767221.blurb: The CTV Television Network, Canada's first private television network, is launched.

Q767317.name: Treaty of Greenville
Q767317.blurb: Treaty of Greenville is signed, ending the Northwest Indian War in the Ohio Country.

Q767450.name: Treaty of Córdoba
Q767450.blurb: The Treaty of Córdoba is signed in Córdoba, now in Veracruz, Mexico, concluding the Mexican War of Independence from Spain.

Q767848.name: Battle of Adrianople (324)
Q767848.blurb: Battle of Adrianople: Constantine I defeats Licinius, who flees to Byzantium.

Q767935.name: Siege of Rhodes
Q767935.blurb: Ottomans begin the second Siege of Rhodes.

Q768155.name: 1967 Detroit riot
Q768155.blurb: Detroit Riots: In Detroit, one of the worst riots in United States history begins on 12th Street in the predominantly African American inner city. It ultimately kills 43 people, injures 342 and burns about 1,400 buildings.

Q768755.name: Paris Uprising of 1832
Q768755.blurb: The June Rebellion breaks out in Paris in an attempt to overthrow the monarchy of Louis Philippe.

Q768914.name: 1976 Zagreb mid-air collision
Q768914.blurb: A British Airways Hawker Siddeley Trident and an Inex-Adria DC-9 collide near Zagreb, Yugoslavia, killing 176.

Q769031.name: 1428 Catalonia earthquake
Q769031.blurb: An intense earthquake struck the Principality of Catalonia, with the epicenter near Camprodon. Widespread destruction and heavy casualties were reported.

Q769284.name: Second MacDonald ministry
Q769284.blurb: Resignation of the United Kingdom's Second Labour Government. Formation of the UK National Government.

Q769358.name: Battle of Taginae
Q769358.blurb: Battle of Taginae: Byzantine forces under Narses defeat the Ostrogoths in Italy, and the Ostrogoth king, Totila, is mortally wounded.

Q769377.name: Operation Storm
aliases: Fall of Republic of Serb Krajina
Q769377.blurb: Operation Storm, the last major battle of the Croatian War of Independence begins.

Q769581.name: Renville Agreement
Q769581.blurb: The Renville Agreement between the Netherlands and Indonesia is ratified.

Q769736.name: British Airways Flight 38
Q769736.blurb: British Airways Flight 38 crashes short of the runway at Heathrow Airport, injuring 47.

Q769960.name: August Revolution
Q769960.blurb: August Revolution: Viet Minh led by Ho Chi Minh take power in Hanoi, Vietnam.

Q770536.name: Battle of Inkerman
Q770536.blurb: Crimean War: Despite being severely outnumbered, and fighting in heavy foggy conditions, the allied armies of the United Kingdom and France defeated the Russians in present-day Inkerman, Ukraine.

Q770698.name: Syria–Lebanon campaign
Q770698.blurb: World War II: The Allies commence the Syria–Lebanon Campaign against the possessions of Vichy France in the Levant.

Q770935.name: Alaska Airlines Flight 261
Q770935.blurb: Alaska Airlines Flight 261 crash: An MD-83, experiencing horizontal stabilizer problems, crashes in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Point Mugu, California, killing all 88 aboard.

Q771423.name: Battle of Philippopolis
Q771423.blurb: Russo-Turkish War (1877–78): Battle of Philippopolis: Captain Aleksandr Burago with a squadron of Russian Imperial army dragoons liberates Plovdiv from Ottoman rule.

Q771451.name: Convention of Kanagawa
aliases: Japan-US Treaty of Peace and Amity
Japan–US Treaty of Peace and Amity
U.S.-Japan Treaty of Peace and Amity
Q771451.blurb: Commodore Matthew Perry signs the Convention of Kanagawa with the Tokugawa Shogunate, opening the ports of Shimoda and Hakodate to American trade.

Q772874.name: Pazzi conspiracy
Q772874.blurb: In a conspiracy to replace the Medici family as rulers of the Republic of Florence, the Pazzi family attacked Lorenzo de' Medici (pictured) and killed his brother Giuliano at Florence Cathedral.

Q772907.name: These Are My Children
Q772907.blurb: These Are My Children, the first television daytime soap opera, is broadcast by the NBC station in Chicago, United States.

Q773999.name: Convention for the Suppression of the Traffic in Persons and of the Exploitation of the Prostitution of Others
Q773999.blurb: Convention for the Suppression of the Traffic in Persons and of the Exploitation of the Prostitution of Others is adopted.

Q774054.name: 1948 Palestinian exodus from Lydda and Ramle
Q774054.blurb: Israeli Prime Minister David Ben-Gurion orders the expulsion of Palestinians from the towns of Lod and Ramla.

Q774314.name: 1949 Pelileo earthquake
Q774314.blurb: An earthquake registering 6.4 Ms struck near Ambato, Ecuador, killing 5,050 people.

Q775339.name: 1992 Nicaragua earthquake
Q775339.blurb: The 7.7 Mw Nicaragua earthquake affected the west coast of Nicaragua. With a Ms–Mw disparity of half a unit, this tsunami earthquake triggered a tsunami that caused most of the damage and casualties, with at least 116 killed. Typical runup heights were 3–8 meters (9.8–26.2 ft).

Q776215.name: Battle of Arausio
Q776215.blurb: Cimbrian War: Defeat at the Battle of Arausio of the Roman army of the mid-Republic

Q776552.name: Battle of Arcis-sur-Aube
Q776552.blurb: Napoleonic Wars: Austrian forces repel French troops in the Battle of Arcis-sur-Aube.

Q776609.name: Battle of the Bridge of Arcole
Q776609.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: Battle of the Bridge of Arcole: French forces defeat the Austrians in Italy.

Q778010.name: Battles of Lexington and Concord
aliases: The Battle of Lexington and Concord
The Battles of Concord and Lexington
The Battles of Lexington and Concord
Winner of the battle of concord
Q778010.blurb: American Revolutionary War: The war begins during the Battles of Lexington and Concord with a victory of American minutemen and other militia over British forces, later referred to as the "shot heard round the world".

Q778218.name: 1980 eruption of Mount St. Helens
Q778218.blurb: Mount St. Helens erupts in Washington, United States, killing 57 people and causing $3 billion in damage.

Q778800.name: First Battle of Abukir
Q778800.blurb: Napoleon Bonaparte defeats a numerically superior Ottoman army under Mustafa Pasha at the Battle of Abukir.

Q779851.name: Proclamation of the republic in Germany
Q779851.blurb: Kaiser Wilhelm II of Germany abdicates after the German Revolution, and Germany is proclaimed a Republic.

Q780367.name: Siege of Plevna
Q780367.blurb: Russo-Turkish War: The Russian Army captures Plevna after a 5-month siege. The garrison of 25,000 surviving Turks surrenders. The Russian victory is decisive for the outcome of the war and the Liberation of Bulgaria.

Q780457.name: Legislative Assembly
Q780457.blurb: First session of the French Legislative Assembly.

Q780730.name: Operation Frequent Wind
Q780730.blurb: Vietnam War: Operation Frequent Wind: The U.S. begins to evacuate U.S. citizens from Saigon before an expected North Vietnamese takeover. U.S. involvement in the war comes to an end. This happens after the Bombing of Tan Son Nhut Air Base.

Q780845.name: Franco-Thai War
Q780845.blurb: Franco-Thai War: Vichy French forces inflict a decisive defeat over the Royal Thai Navy.

Q780921.name: Battle of Paris
Q780921.blurb: The Sixth Coalition occupies Paris after Napoleon's Grande Armée capitulates.

Q781029.name: Saint-Sylvestre coup d'état
Q781029.blurb: Central African military officers led by Jean-Bédel Bokassa began a coup d'état against the government of President David Dacko.

Q781233.name: Australasian Antarctic Expedition (1911-1914)
Q781233.blurb: The Australasian Antarctic Expedition began as the SY Aurora departed London.

Q782441.name: Santa Cruz massacre
Q782441.blurb: Santa Cruz massacre: The Indonesian Army open fire on a crowd of student protesters in Dili, East Timor.

Q783183.name: Action of 1 August 1801
Q783183.blurb: First Barbary War: The American schooner USS Enterprise captures the Tripolitan polacca Tripoli in a single-ship action off the coast of modern-day Libya.

Q783192.name: Condemnations of 1210–1277
Q783192.blurb: The University of Paris issues the last in a series of condemnations of various philosophical and theological theses.

Q783193.name: Avianca Flight 052
Q783193.blurb: Avianca Flight 052 crashes in Cove Neck, New York, killing 73.

Q783597.name: American Airlines Flight 1420
Q783597.blurb: American Airlines Flight 1420 slides and crashes while landing at Little Rock National Airport, killing 11 people on a flight from Dallas to Little Rock.

Q783792.name: Battle of St. Quentin Canal
Q783792.blurb: World War I:  The Hindenburg Line is broken by an Allied attack.

Q784141.name: Eastern Air Lines Flight 401
Q784141.blurb: Eastern Air Lines Flight 401 (a Lockheed L-1011 TriStar) crashes in the Florida Everglades on approach to Miami International Airport, Florida, killing 101 of the 176 people on board.

Q784397.name: Battle of the Paracel Islands
Q784397.blurb: China gains control over all the Paracel Islands after a military engagement between the naval forces of China and South Vietnam.

Q784466.name: Itavia Flight 870
Q784466.blurb: The 'Ustica massacre': Itavia Flight 870 crashes in the sea while en route from Bologna to Palermo, Italy, killing all 81 on board.

Q786171.name: Ottoman–Habsburg Wars
Q786171.blurb: Ottoman–Habsburg wars: Although Ottoman forces led by Suleiman the Magnificent captured the fortress of Szigetvár in Hungary, they were forced to end their campaign to take Vienna.

Q786657.name: Battle of Calderón Bridge
Q786657.blurb: Mexican War of Independence: In the Battle of Calderón Bridge, a heavily outnumbered Spanish force of 6,000 troops defeats nearly 100,000 Mexican revolutionaries.

Q786906.name: 1949 Air France Lockheed Constellation crash
Q786906.blurb: An Air France Lockheed Constellation crashes in the Azores, killing all 48 people on board.

Q787963.name: Babington Plot
Q787963.blurb: A number of conspirators in the Babington Plot are hanged, drawn and quartered.

Q791234.name: Battle of Bassano
Q791234.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: Battle of Bassano: French forces defeat Austrian troops at Bassano del Grappa.

Q792340.name: German invasion of Belgium (1914)
Q792340.blurb: World War I: In response to the German invasion of Belgium, Belgium and the British Empire declare war on Germany. The United States declares its neutrality.

Q793448.name: Battle of Bergen
Q793448.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: French-Dutch victory against the Russians and British in the Battle of Bergen.

Q793828.name: Battle of Kharda
Q793828.blurb: The Battle of Kharda is fought between the Maratha Confederacy and the Nizam of Hyderabad, resulting in Maratha victory.

Q793922.name: Battle of Champion Hill
Q793922.blurb: American Civil War: During the Vicksburg campaign, the decisive Union victory by Ulysses S. Grant at the Battle of Champion Hill drives the Confederate army under John C. Pemberton back towards Vicksburg, Mississippi.

Q794695.name: Battle of Big Bethel
Q794695.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Big Bethel: Confederate troops under John B. Magruder defeat a much larger Union force led by General Ebenezer W. Pierce in Virginia.

Q794908.name: PEPCON disaster
Q794908.blurb: The PEPCON disaster rocks Henderson, Nevada, as tons of Space Shuttle fuel detonate during a fire.

Q794998.name: 1994 Fairchild Air Force Base B-52 crash
Q794998.blurb: A Boeing B-52 Stratofortress crashes at Fairchild Air Force Base near Spokane, Washington, killing four.

Q795269.name: Sierra Leone Civil War
aliases: Causes of the Sierra Leone Civil War
War crimes in the Sierra Leone Civil War
Q795269.blurb: The Sierra Leone Civil War is declared over.

Q796398.name: Ba Chúc massacre
Q796398.blurb: The Ba Chúc massacre begins, which precipitates the Cambodian–Vietnamese War the same year.

Q796847.name: BOAC Flight 911
Q796847.blurb: BOAC Flight 911, a Boeing 707 aircraft, breaks apart in mid-air due to clear-air turbulence and crashes into Mount Fuji, Japan, killing all 124 people on board.

Q799299.name: crushing The Rebellions of 1965–1966
aliases: Foreign involvement in the Indonesian mass killings of 1965-1966
Foreign involvement in the Indonesian mass killings of 1965–1966
International reactions to the Indonesian mass killings of 1965-1966
International reactions to the Indonesian mass killings of 1965–1966
Q799299.blurb: Seven Indonesian National Armed Forces officers, six of them generals, were murdered at dawn by a rebellious force in Jakarta; the Army then blamed the Communist Party, leading to a mass anti-communist purge that killed up to one million people.

Q800043.name: 1990 Guangzhou Baiyun airport collisions
Q800043.blurb: Xiamen Airlines Flight 8301 is hijacked and lands at Guangzhou, where it crashes into two other airliners on the ground, killing 132.

Q803887.name: Biological Weapons Convention
aliases: Convention on the Prohibition of the Development, Production and Stockpiling of Bacteriological (Biological) and Toxin Weapons and on their Destruction
Biological Weapons and Toxin Convention of 1972
Q803887.blurb: The Biological Weapons Convention comes into force.

Q804558.name: Bakumatsu
Q804558.blurb: Bakumatsu: Kinmon incident: The Chōshū Domain attempts to expel the Satsuma and Aizu Domains from Japan's imperial court.

Q804566.name: Bal des Ardents
Q804566.blurb: King Charles VI of France is nearly killed when several other dancers' costumes catch fire during a masquerade ball in Paris.

Q804715.name: Balcombe Street Siege
Q804715.blurb: Four members of the Provisional Irish Republican Army took two people hostage in a house on Balcombe Street in London, surrendering six days later.

Q805050.name: Maurice's Balkan campaigns
Q805050.blurb: Avar–Byzantine wars: The Avars lift the siege at the Byzantine stronghold of Tomis. Their leader Bayan I retreats north of the Danube River after the Avaro-Slavic army is decimated by the plague.

Q806498.name: 1991 Bangladesh cyclone
Q806498.blurb: A cyclone strikes the Chittagong district of southeastern Bangladesh with winds of around 155 miles per hour (249 km/h), killing at least 138,000 people and leaving as many as ten million homeless.

Q807843.name: Bishops' Wars
Q807843.blurb: Second Bishop's War: King Charles I's English army loses to a Scottish Covenanter force at the Battle of Newburn.

Q808027.name: Treaty of Bardo
Q808027.blurb: Under threat of invasion, Muhammad III as-Sadiq, Bey of Tunis, signed the Treaty of Bardo to make Tunisia a French protectorate.

Q811250.name: Tambov Rebellion
Q811250.blurb: The Tambov Rebellion breaks out, in response to the Bolshevik policy of Prodrazvyorstka.

Q812610.name: Bavarian Rummel
Q812610.blurb: During the Bavarian Rummel the rural population of Tyrol drove the Bavarian Prince-Elector Maximilian II Emanuel out of North Tyrol with a victory at the Pontlatzer Bridge and thus prevented the Bavarian Army, which was allied with France, from marching as planned on Vienna during the War of the Spanish Succession.

Q813350.name: Beauchamp–Sharp Tragedy
Q813350.blurb: Jereboam O. Beauchamp murdered Kentucky legislator Solomon P. Sharp; Beauchamp later became the first person legally executed in the state.

Q814223.name: Liberation of Khorramshahr
Q814223.blurb: Liberation of Khorramshahr: Iranians recapture the port city of Khorramshahr from the Iraqis during the Iran–Iraq War.

Q814484.name: Dyatlov Pass incident
aliases: Death of the Dyatlov Hiking Group
Q814484.blurb: Nine experienced ski hikers in the northern Ural Mountains in the Soviet Union die under mysterious circumstances.

Q814848.name: 1985 Beirut car bombing
Q814848.blurb: A supposed failed assassination attempt on Islamic cleric Sayyed Mohammad Hussein Fadlallah in Beirut, Lebanon kills 80 and injures 200 others.

Q814930.name: Treaty of Accession 2003
Q814930.blurb: The Treaty of Accession is signed in Athens admitting ten new member states to the European Union.

Q815102.name: Siege of Sidney Street
Q815102.blurb: A gun battle in the East End of London leaves two dead. It sparked a political row over the involvement of then-Home Secretary Winston Churchill.

Q815103.name: Siege of Acre
Q815103.blurb: King Baldwin I of Jerusalem begins the siege of Acre, then held by the Fatimids.

Q815104.name: Siege of Abadan
Q815104.blurb: Iran–Iraq War: Iran broke the Iraqi siege of Abadan by Operation Samen-ol-A'emeh.

Q815109.name: Siege of Acre
Q815109.blurb: The end of the Siege of Acre (1799): Napoleon Bonaparte abandons his siege of the Ottoman city of Acre after two months. This was the turning point of Bonaparte's Egyptian campaign and one of the first major defeats he suffered in his military career.

Q815112.name: Siege of Antioch
Q815112.blurb: The Principality of Antioch, a crusader state, falls to the Mamluk Sultan Baibars in the Siege of Antioch.

Q815116.name: Siege of Acre
Q815116.blurb: Third Crusade: The Crusaders begin the Siege of Acre under Guy of Lusignan.

Q815120.name: Siege of Bari
Q815120.blurb: Byzantine–Norman wars: After a siege of almost three years, Italo-Norman forces conquered the city of Bari, the capital of the Catepanate of Italy, ending more than five centuries of Byzantine presence in the region.

Q815121.name: Siege of Badajoz
Q815121.blurb: British forces under the command of the Duke of Wellington assault the fortress of Badajoz. This would be the turning point in the Peninsular War against Napoleon-led France.

Q815128.name: Siege of Boston
Q815128.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Following the Battles of Lexington and Concord, the Siege of Boston begins with American militias blocking land access to the British-held city.

Q815140.name: Siege of Dubrovnik
Q815140.blurb: Croatian War of Independence: The Siege of Dubrovnik begins.

Q815145.name: Great Siege of Gibraltar
Q815145.blurb: American Revolutionary War: French and Spanish forces lift the Great Siege of Gibraltar.

Q815146.name: Siege of Jasna Góra
Q815146.blurb: Second Northern War/the Deluge: Monks at the Jasna Góra Monastery in Częstochowa are successful in fending off a month-long siege.

Q815159.name: Siege of Khartoum
Q815159.blurb: The Siege of Khartoum begins. It lasts until January 26, 1885.

Q815161.name: Conquest of Jerusalem
Q815161.blurb: Saladin begins the Siege of Jerusalem.

Q815162.name: Siege of Kyiv
Q815162.blurb: Mongol invasion of Rus': Kyiv, defended by Voivode Dmytro, falls to the Mongols under Batu Khan.

Q815165.name: Siege of Lucknow
Q815165.blurb: Second relief of Lucknow: Twenty-four Victoria Crosses are awarded, the most in a single day.

Q815166.name: Siege of Kut
Q815166.blurb: World War I: The UK's 6th Indian Division surrenders to Ottoman Forces at the Siege of Kut in one of the largest surrenders of British forces up to that point.

Q815167.name: Siege of Constantinople
Q815167.blurb: Byzantine–Rus' War: A fleet of about 200 Rus' vessels sails into the Bosphorus and starts pillaging the suburbs of the Byzantine capital Constantinople.

Q815170.name: Siege of La Rochelle
Q815170.blurb: French Wars of Religion: The Siege of La Rochelle ends with the surrender of the Huguenots after fourteen months.

Q815175.name: Siege of Mantua
Q815175.blurb: The siege of Mantua ends after eight months when Count Dagobert Sigmund von Wurmser surrenders the fortress of Mantua to Napoleon Bonaparte. The fall of Mantua secures French control over Northern Italy and marks the beginning of the conclusion of the Italian campaign of 1796-1797, and sets the stage for the end of the War of the First Coalition.

Q815177.name: Siege of Lisbon
Q815177.blurb: Reconquista: After a siege of four months, crusader knights conquer Lisbon.

Q815195.name: Siege of Petersburg
Q815195.blurb: American Civil War: In Virginia during the Siege of Petersburg, Confederate forces temporarily capture Fort Stedman from the Union before being repulsed.

Q815203.name: Siege of Rouen
Q815203.blurb: Hundred Years' War: The siege of Rouen ended with English troops capturing the city from Norman French forces.

Q815204.name: Siege of Seringapatam
Q815204.blurb: Fourth Anglo-Mysore War: The Battle of Seringapatam: The siege of Seringapatam ends when the city is invaded and Tipu Sultan killed by the besieging British army, under the command of General George Harris.

Q815213.name: Siege of Syracuse
Q815213.blurb: Syracuse, Sicily, is captured by the Muslim Aghlabids after a nine-month siege.

Q815216.name: Siege of Sevastopol
Q815216.blurb: Crimean War: The Siege of Sevastopol comes to an end when Russian forces abandon the city.

Q815224.name: Siege of Vidin
Q815224.blurb: Serbian forces begin their siege of the Bulgarian city of Vidin; the siege is later called off when the war ends.

Q815226.name: Sack of Wexford
Q815226.blurb: Cromwell's New Model Army sacks Wexford, killing over 2,000 Irish Confederate troops and 1,500 civilians.

Q815228.name: Siege of Toulon
Q815228.blurb: War of the First Coalition: The Siege of Toulon ends when Napoleon's French artillery forces the British to abandon the city, securing southern France from invasion.

Q815234.name: Siege of Drogheda
Q815234.blurb: Siege of Drogheda ends: Oliver Cromwell's Parliamentarian troops take the town and execute its garrison.

Q815420.name: Belfast Blitz
Q815420.blurb: World War II:  In the Belfast Blitz, 200 bombers of the German Luftwaffe attack Belfast, killing some 1,000 people.

Q815436.name: The Troubles
aliases: Northern Ireland Troubles (Legacy and Reconciliation) Act 2023
Q815436.blurb: The Troubles: The Ulster Volunteer Force shoots dead six Irish Catholic civilians in County Armagh, Northern Ireland. The next day, gunmen would shoot dead ten Protestant civilians nearby in retaliation.

Q815567.name: 1988 Spitak earthquake
Q815567.blurb: The 6.8 Ms Armenian earthquake shakes the northern part of the country with a maximum MSK intensity of X (Devastating), killing 25,000–50,000 and injuring 31,000–130,000.

Q815718.name: 2009 Sumatra earthquakes
Q815718.blurb: The 7.6 Mw Sumatra earthquake leaves 1,115 people dead.

Q816220.name: Beltway sniper attacks
Q816220.blurb: The Beltway sniper attacks begin in Washington, D.C., extending over three weeks and killing 10 people.

Q817206.name: Cambodian Civil War
aliases: Use of children in the Cambodian Civil War
War crimes in the Cambodian Civil War
Q817206.blurb: During the Cambodian Civil War, massacre of the Vietnamese minority results in 800 bodies flowing down the Mekong river into South Vietnam.

Q817281.name: combined oral contraceptive pill
Q817281.blurb: The United States Food and Drug Administration declares Enovid to be the first officially approved combined oral contraceptive pill in the world.

Q819264.name: colour revolution
aliases: Liberal revolutionary movements in post-communist Eastern Europe
Post-communist liberal revolutionary movements in Eastern Europe
Q819264.blurb: Colour revolutions: During protests over irregularities in the Yugoslavian general election, a wheel-loader was driven into the Radio Television of Serbia building, giving the protests the nickname "Bulldozer Revolution".

Q819274.name: German occupation of Norway
aliases: German occupation of Norway during World War II
occupation of Norway by Nazi Germany
German military occupation of Norway during World War II
German occupation of Norway during the Second World War
German occupation of Norway in World War II
Occupation of Norway in World War II
Q819274.blurb: World War II: Military resistance to the German occupation of Norway ends.

Q819999.name: Siege of Kehl
Q819999.blurb: War of the First Coalition: The siege of Kehl by Habsburg and Württembergian forces ended when French troops withdrew from their fortifications.

Q820307.name: Rockslide of Elm
Q820307.blurb: In the Swiss state of Glarus, a rockslide buries parts of the village of Elm, destroying 83 buildings and killing 115 people.

Q821041.name: Battle of Poznań
Q821041.blurb: World War II: Capitulation of German garrison in Poznań. The city is liberated by Soviet and Polish forces.

Q821120.name: Battle of Wiesloch
Q821120.blurb: War of the Second Coalition: Battle of Wiesloch: Austrian Lieutenant Field Marshal Anton Sztáray defeats the French at Wiesloch.

Q821283.name: Battle of Warsaw
Q821283.blurb: Polish–Soviet War: The Battle of Warsaw begins and will last till August 25. The Red Army is defeated.

Q822472.name: Akō Incident
aliases: The revenge of the forty-seven rōnin
Q822472.blurb: Forty-seven rōnin, under the command of Ōishi Kuranosuke, avenged the death of their master, by killing Kira Yoshinaka.

Q822853.name: Lufthansa Flight 502
Q822853.blurb: 36 people are killed when Lufthansa Flight 502 crashes on approach to Rio de Janeiro/Galeão International Airport in Brazil.

Q823401.name: Kuban bridgehead
Q823401.blurb: World War II: The German 17th Army begins its evacuation of the Kuban bridgehead (Taman Peninsula) in southern Russia and moves across the Strait of Kerch to the Crimea.

Q823433.name: Oregon Treaty
aliases: Treaty with Great Britain, in Regard to Limits Westward of the Rocky Mountains
Q823433.blurb: The Oregon Treaty extends the border between the United States and British North America, established by the Treaty of 1818, westward to the Pacific Ocean.

Q824165.name: Treaty of London
Q824165.blurb: First World War: Britain, France and Russia signed a secret treaty promising territory to Italy if it joined the war on their side.

Q827212.name: Gadsden Purchase
Q827212.blurb: Gadsden Purchase: The United States buys land from Mexico to facilitate railroad building in the Southwest.

Q827436.name: Giselle
Q827436.blurb: Giselle (title role pictured), a ballet by the French composer Adolphe Adam, was first performed at the Théâtre de l'Académie Royale de Musique in Paris.

Q827472.name: Battle of Ascalon
Q827472.blurb: First Crusade: Battle of Ascalon Crusaders under the command of Godfrey of Bouillon defeat Fatimid forces led by Al-Afdal Shahanshah. This is considered the last engagement of the First Crusade.

Q829443.name: Battle of Savenay
Q829443.blurb: The Battle of Savenay: A decisive defeat of the royalist counter-revolutionaries in War in the Vendée during the French Revolution.

Q829836.name: Palace of Justice Siege
aliases: Assauls to the Palace of Justice of Bogata (1985)
Takeover of the Palace of Justice
Q829836.blurb: Colombian conflict: leftist guerrillas of the 19th of April Movement seize control of the Palace of Justice in Bogotá.

Q829839.name: Grand Mosque Seizure
Q829839.blurb: Grand Mosque seizure: About 200 Sunni Muslims revolt in Saudi Arabia at the site of the Kaaba in Mecca during the pilgrimage and take about 6,000 hostages. The Saudi government receives help from French special forces to put down the uprising.

Q829875.name: Nigerian Civil War
aliases: Foreign involvement in the Nigerian Civil War
Q829875.blurb: Nigerian Civil War: Biafran rebels surrender following an unsuccessful 32-month fight for independence from Nigeria.

Q830166.name: Ohi Day
Q830166.blurb: World War II: Greece rejects Italy's ultimatum. Italy invades Greece through Albania a few hours later.

Q830626.name: Battle of Bouvines
Q830626.blurb: Battle of Bouvines: Philip II of France decisively defeats Imperial, English and Flemish armies, effectively ending John of England's Angevin Empire.

Q830878.name: Battle of Stiklestad
Q830878.blurb: Ladejarl-Fairhair succession wars: Battle of Stiklestad: King Olaf II fights and dies trying to regain his Norwegian throne from the Danes.

Q831134.name: Gale of January 1976
Q831134.blurb: The Gale of January 1976 begins, resulting in coastal flooding around the southern North Sea coasts, affecting countries from Ireland to Yugoslavia and causing at least 82 deaths and US$1.3 billion in damage.

Q831522.name: First Council of Lyon
Q831522.blurb: Pope Innocent IV arrives at Lyon for the First Council of Lyon.

Q831714.name: 2001 World Aquatics Championships
Q831714.blurb: At the World Aquatics Championships in Fukuoka, Japan, Australian Ian Thorpe  became the first swimmer to win six gold medals at a single FINA world championship.

Q832508.name: Constitution of France
aliases: Constitution of the Fifth French Republic
Constitution of the French Fifth Republic
Q832508.blurb: The current constitution of France is adopted.

Q832683.name: Battle of Pavón
Q832683.blurb: Argentine Civil Wars: The State of Buenos Aires defeats the Argentine Confederation at the Battle of Pavón.

Q833096.name: 1999 champions league final
aliases: Manchester United have reached the promised land
Q833096.blurb: Manchester United won the UEFA Champions League final to become the first English football club to win three major championships in the same season.

Q833441.name: Transylvanian peasant revolt
Q833441.blurb: Nine leaders of the Transylvanian peasant revolt are executed at Torda.

Q833861.name: Battle of Saragossa
Q833861.blurb: War of the Spanish Succession: A multinational army led by the Austrian commander Guido Starhemberg defeats the Spanish-Bourbon army commanded by Alexandre Maître, Marquis de Bay in the Battle of Saragossa.

Q833926.name: Sacco and Vanzetti
aliases: Sacco and Vanzetti Trial, Dedham, Mass., 1921
Q833926.blurb: US authorities arrest Nicola Sacco and Bartolomeo Vanzetti for alleged robbery and murder.

Q834456.name: 2002–2004 SARS outbreak
aliases: 2002 severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus outbreak
2002-04 severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus outbreak
2002-2004 severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus outbreak
2002–04 severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus outbreak
2002–2004 severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus outbreak
2002—04 severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus outbreak
2002—2004 severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus outbreak
Q834456.blurb: The first cases of the 2002–2004 SARS outbreak are traced to Foshan, Guangdong Province, China.

Q835180.name: Battle of Wofla
Q835180.blurb: Turkish–Portuguese War: Battle of Wofla: The Portuguese are scattered, their leader Christovão da Gama is captured and later executed.

Q835616.name: Tianjing Incident
Q835616.blurb: The Tianjing incident takes place in Nanjing, China.

Q835881.name: Operation Bodenplatte
Q835881.blurb: World War II: The German Luftwaffe launches Operation Bodenplatte, a massive, but failed, attempt to knock out Allied air power in northern Europe in a single blow.

Q835912.name: 1985 World Snooker Championship final
Q835912.blurb: The black-ball final, one of the most famous snooker matches in history, began between Steve Davis and Dennis Taylor.

Q835929.name: Kashmir Princess
Q835929.blurb: The Air India Kashmir Princess is bombed and crashes in a failed assassination attempt on Zhou Enlai by the Kuomintang.

Q836386.name: Orange Revolution
Q836386.blurb: The Orange Revolution begins in Ukraine, resulting from the presidential elections.

Q836424.name: Treaty of Speyer
Q836424.blurb: The Principality of Transylvania is established after John II Zápolya renounces his claim as King of Hungary in the Treaty of Speyer.

Q836844.name: Battle of al-Qadisiyyah
Q836844.blurb: The Rashidun Caliphate defeats the Sasanian Empire at the Battle of al-Qādisiyyah in Iraq.

Q836897.name: massacre of Oradour-sur-Glane
Q836897.blurb: World War II: Six hundred forty-three men, women and children are massacred at Oradour-sur-Glane, France.

Q836944.name: Battle of the Frigidus
Q836944.blurb: Battle of the Frigidus: Roman emperor Theodosius I defeats and kills Eugenius the usurper. His Frankish magister militum Arbogast escapes but commits suicide two days later.

Q836963.name: Treaty of Cateau-Cambrésis
Q836963.blurb: The second of two treaties making up the Peace of Cateau-Cambrésis is signed, ending the Italian Wars.

Q837787.name: Battle of Novara
Q837787.blurb: The Austrians defeat the Piedmontese at the Battle of Novara.

Q837887.name: cruise missile strikes on Afghanistan and Sudan
Q837887.blurb: U.S. embassy bombings: The United States launches cruise missile attacks against alleged al-Qaeda camps in Afghanistan and a suspected chemical weapons plant in Sudan in retaliation for the August 7 bombings of American embassies in Kenya and Tanzania.

Q838278.name: Black Saturday bushfires
aliases: Australia Unites - The Victorian Bushfire Appeal
Economic impact of the Black Saturday bushfires
Victorian Bushfire Reconstruction and Recovery Authority
Q838278.blurb: Bushfires in Victoria leave 173 dead in the worst natural disaster in Australia's history.

Q838526.name: Digest
Q838526.blurb: The Digest, the great collection of all Roman jurists' law, is issued together with a new official law textbook for legal schools, The Institutes.

Q838695.name: First Congo War
aliases: Foreign involvement in the First Congo War
Q838695.blurb: The First Congo War came to an end when Laurent-Désiré Kabila proclaimed himself president of Zaire, which was also renamed the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Q838794.name: jubilee
Q838794.blurb: Pope Clement VI issues the papal bull Unigenitus, laying out the scriptural justification for indulgences, identifying only the Pope and episcopate as capable of accessing the treasury of merit, and establishing a jubilee year every half century.

Q838958.name: Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court
aliases: Rome Statute for the International Criminal Court
Statute of the International Criminal Court
Q838958.blurb: A diplomatic conference adopts the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court, establishing the permanent international court in The Hague, to prosecute individuals for genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes, and the crime of aggression.

Q838980.name: May Revolution
aliases: Dia de la Revolucion de Mayo
Día de la Revolución de Mayo
Q838980.blurb: May Revolution: Citizens of Buenos Aires expel Viceroy Baltasar Hidalgo de Cisneros during the "May Week", starting the Argentine War of Independence.

Q839191.name: 2005 Liberian general election
Q839191.blurb: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf is elected president of Liberia and becomes the first woman to lead an African country.

Q839396.name: London Protocol of 1830
Q839396.blurb: The London Protocol of 1830 establishes the full independence and sovereignty of Greece from the Ottoman Empire as the final result of the Greek War of Independence.

Q839710.name: Lidice massacre
Q839710.blurb: World War II: The Lidice massacre is perpetrated as a reprisal for the assassination of Obergruppenführer Reinhard Heydrich.

Q840289.name: 2000 UEFA Cup Final
Q840289.blurb: Following the killing of two English football fans by Galatasaray supporters in the previous month, British and Turkish hooligans rioted on the day of the UEFA Cup Final in Copenhagen, Denmark.

Q840847.name: Three Mile Island accident
aliases: President's Commission on the Accident at Three Mile Island
Q840847.blurb: A coolant leak at the Three Mile Island's Unit 2 nuclear reactor outside Harrisburg, Pennsylvania leads to the core overheating and a partial meltdown.

Q841278.name: Battle of San Jacinto
Q841278.blurb: Texas Revolution: The Battle of San Jacinto: Republic of Texas forces under Sam Houston defeat troops under Mexican General Antonio López de Santa Anna.

Q842026.name: PMTair Flight 241
Q842026.blurb: PMTair Flight 241 crashes in the Dâmrei Mountains in Kampot Province, Cambodia, killing all 22 people on board.

Q842316.name: Treaty of Shaoxing
Q842316.blurb: A peace treaty ends the Jin–Song wars.

Q842380.name: Second Sudanese Civil War
aliases: Child soldiers in the Second Sudanese Civil War
Foreign interventions in the Second Sudanese Civil War
Impact of the Second Sudanese Civil War
Q842380.blurb: Sudan's government imposes Islamic law nationwide, worsening the civil war between the country's Muslim north and Christian south.

Q842621.name: 2010 Pichilemu earthquakes
Q842621.blurb: During the inauguration of Chilean president Sebastián Piñera, earthquakes registering 6.9 and 7.0 .mw-parser-output .tooltip-dotted{border-bottom:1px dotted;cursor:help}Mw struck the O'Higgins Region near the city of Pichilemu, causing widespread damage.

Q842774.name: Polish–Ukrainian War
Q842774.blurb: World War I: A new Polish government in western Galicia is established, triggering the Polish–Ukrainian War.

Q842796.name: First Battle of St Albans
aliases: The First Battle of St Albans
The First Battle of St. Albans
Q842796.blurb: Start of the Wars of the Roses: At the First Battle of St Albans, Richard, Duke of York, defeats and captures King Henry VI of England.

Q842831.name: Caspian Airlines Flight 7908
Q842831.blurb: Caspian Airlines Flight 7908 crashes near Jannatabad, Qazvin, Iran, killing 168.

Q843669.name: boxing at the 1960 Summer Olympics
Q843669.blurb: Muhammad Ali (then known as Cassius Clay) wins the gold medal in the light heavyweight boxing competition at the Olympic Games in Rome.

Q843687.name: Black Friday
Q843687.blurb: Black Friday (1869): Gold prices plummet after United States President Ulysses S. Grant orders the Treasury to sell large quantities of gold after Jay Gould and James Fisk plot to control the market.

Q843912.name: 2009 satellite collision
Q843912.blurb: The satellites Iridium 33 and Kosmos 2251 destroyed each other in the first accidental hypervelocity collision between two intact satellites in low Earth orbit.

Q843962.name: Saffron Revolution
Q843962.blurb: Buddhist monks join anti-government protesters in Myanmar, starting what some call the Saffron Revolution.

Q844449.name: Panic of 1907
Q844449.blurb: A run on the stock of the Knickerbocker Trust Company sets events in motion that will spark the Panic of 1907.

Q844495.name: Lindbergh kidnapping
Q844495.blurb: Ten weeks after his abduction, Charles Jr., the infant son of Charles Lindbergh, is found dead near Hopewell, New Jersey, just a few miles from the Lindberghs' home.

Q844505.name: July 2009 Ürümqi riots
aliases: Wu1 lou5 muk6 cai4 7.5 sou1 lyun6
乌鲁木齐七·五暴力事件
烏魯木齊七·五暴力事件
Q844505.blurb: A series of violent riots break out in Ürümqi, the capital city of the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region in China.

Q844886.name: Siege of Jerusalem
aliases: Roman destruction of the temple mount
Q844886.blurb: Siege of Jerusalem: Titus, son of emperor Vespasian, storms the Fortress of Antonia north of the Temple Mount. The Roman army is drawn into street fights with the Zealots.

Q845203.name: Operation Chastise
Q845203.blurb: Operation Chastise is undertaken by RAF Bomber Command with specially equipped Avro Lancasters to destroy the Mohne, Sorpe, and Eder dams in the Ruhr valley.

Q845627.name: 1947 World Series
Q845627.blurb: The 1947 World Series begins. It is the first to be televised, to include an African-American player, to exceed $2 million in receipts, to see a pinch-hit home run, and to have six umpires on the field.

Q845737.name: Treaty of Brussels
Q845737.blurb: Belgium, France, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom sign the Treaty of Brussels, a precursor to the North Atlantic Treaty establishing NATO.

Q846007.name: 2008 Mongolian legislative election
Q846007.blurb: Rioting erupted in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, over allegations of fraud surrounding the recent legislative election.

Q846291.name: Vietnam Airlines Flight 815
aliases: เวียดนามแอร์ไลน์ เที่ยวบินที่ 815
Q846291.blurb: Vietnam Airlines Flight 815 (Tupolev Tu-134) crashes on approach into Phnom Penh airport, killing 64.

Q846529.name: 1919 World Series
Q846529.blurb: The Cincinnati Reds win the World Series, resulting in the Black Sox Scandal.

Q846674.name: Battles of Saratoga
Q846674.blurb: American Revolutionary War: British forces win a tactically expensive victory over the Continental Army in the First Battle of Saratoga.

Q846708.name: Pruth River Campaign
Q846708.blurb: The treaty of Adrianople ends the Russo-Turkish War of 1710–1713, which restores territory to the Ottomans while allowing the Russians to focus on their war against the Swedes.

Q846848.name: Stuart Restoration
Q846848.blurb: English Restoration: The Fifth Monarchists unsuccessfully attempt to seize control of London, England. The revolt is suppressed after a few days.

Q846876.name: Stockholm Bloodbath
Q846876.blurb: More than 50 people are sentenced and executed in the Stockholm Bloodbath.

Q847094.name: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
Q847094.blurb: BBC Radio 4 began broadcasting Douglas Adams's The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, a science fiction radio series that was later adapted into novels, a television series, and other formats.

Q847137.name: Treaty of Paris (1898)
aliases: Treaty of Peace between the United States of America and the Kingdom of Spain
United States annexation of Puerto Rico
Q847137.blurb: Spanish–American War: The Treaty of Paris, a peace treaty between the United States and Spain, is ratified by the United States Senate.

Q847287.name: Battle of Montgisard
Q847287.blurb: Baldwin IV of Jerusalem and Raynald of Châtillon defeat Saladin at the Battle of Montgisard.

Q847664.name: constitution of Spain
aliases: Amendments to the Spanish Constitution of 1978
Q847664.blurb: Spain ratifies the Spanish Constitution of 1978 in a referendum.

Q847827.name: Super Bowl I
aliases: First World Championship Game AFL versus NFL
First World Championship Game AFL vs NFL
First World Championship Game AFL vs. NFL
The First AFL-NFL World Championship Game
Q847827.blurb: The first Super Bowl is played in Los Angeles. The Green Bay Packers defeat the Kansas City Chiefs 35–10.

Q847839.name: transfer of sovereignty over Macau
Q847839.blurb: Portugal transferred the sovereignty over Macau, which it had administered since the mid–16th century, to China.

Q848222.name: Matsukawa derailment
Q848222.blurb: Matsukawa derailment: Unknown saboteurs cause a passenger train to derail and overturn in Fukushima Prefecture, Japan, killing three crew members and igniting a political firestorm between the Japanese Communist Party and the government of Occupied Japan that will eventually lead to the Japanese Red Purge.

Q849176.name: Kościuszko Uprising
Q849176.blurb: In Kraków, Tadeusz Kościuszko announces a general uprising against Imperial Russia and the Kingdom of Prussia, and assumes the powers of the Commander in Chief of all of the Polish forces.

Q849286.name: Treaty of Bucharest
Q849286.blurb: Imperial Russia signs the Treaty of Bucharest, ending the Russo-Turkish War. The Ottoman Empire cedes Bessarabia to Russia.

Q849465.name: Halle train collision
Q849465.blurb: Two trains collide in the Halle train collision in Halle, Belgium, killing 19 and injuring 171 people.

Q849653.name: Battle of Thapsus
Q849653.blurb: Julius Caesar defeats Caecilius Metellus Scipio and Marcus Porcius Cato (Cato the Younger) at the Battle of Thapsus.

Q849719.name: Hurricane Wilma
aliases: Effects of Hurricane Wilma in Bahamas
Effects of Hurricane Wilma in The Bahamas
Q849719.blurb: Hurricane Wilma becomes the most intense Atlantic hurricane on record with a minimum pressure of 882 mb.

Q849759.name: Punch
Q849759.blurb: The comic novel The Diary of a Nobody by brothers George and Weedon Grossmith first appeared in serial form in Punch.

Q849810.name: Miss Macao
Q849810.blurb: The storming of the cockpit of the Miss Macao passenger seaplane, operated by a subsidiary of the Cathay Pacific Airways, marks the first aircraft hijacking of a commercial plane.

Q850188.name: Bruges Matins
Q850188.blurb: Bruges Matins, the nocturnal massacre of the French garrison in Bruges by members of the local Flemish militia.

Q850497.name: Second Treaty of Brömsebro
Q850497.blurb: Sweden and Denmark sign Peace of Brömsebro.

Q852088.name: Myanmar conflict
aliases: International responses to the internal conflict in Myanmar
Q852088.blurb: Internal conflict in Myanmar: The Burmese military junta and ethnic armies begin three days of violent clashes in the Kokang Special Region.

Q852133.name: internal conflict in Peru
Q852133.blurb: Peruvian internal conflict: Fourteen members of the Túpac Amaru Revolutionary Movement provoke a hostage crisis by taking over the Japanese embassy in Lima.

Q852236.name: Sayfo
Q852236.blurb: Russia withdraws from its occupation of northwestern Iran, enabling a subsequent Ottoman invasion and massacres of Assyrians and Armenians.

Q852292.name: May Thirtieth Movement
Q852292.blurb: May Thirtieth Movement: Shanghai Municipal Police Force shoot and kill 13 protesting workers.

Q852365.name: Tunisia campaign
Q852365.blurb: World War II: Tunisia Campaign: General Hans-Jürgen von Arnim's Fifth Panzer Army launches a counter-attack against Allied positions in Tunisia.

Q852377.name: New Culture Movement
Q852377.blurb: New Culture Movement: Chen Duxiu establishes the New Youth magazine in Shanghai.

Q853685.name: Treaty of Nöteborg
Q853685.blurb: The Treaty of Nöteborg between Sweden and Novgorod Republic is signed, regulating the border between the two countries for the first time.

Q853754.name: Battle of Saule
Q853754.blurb: The Samogitians defeat the Livonian Brothers of the Sword in the Battle of Saule.

Q853860.name: Red Bull Stratos
Q853860.blurb: Felix Baumgartner jumped from a helium balloon in the stratosphere to become the first person to break the sound barrier without vehicular power.

Q853976.name: First Battle of Ypres
Q853976.blurb: World War I: The First Battle of Ypres begins.

Q854206.name: 2009 Iranian presidential election protests
Q854206.blurb: Iranian election protests: On the Day of Ashura in Tehran, Iran, government security forces fire upon demonstrators.

Q855050.name: Bhoja Air Flight 213
Q855050.blurb: One hundred twenty-seven people are killed when a plane crashes in a residential area near the Benazir Bhutto International Airport near Islamabad, Pakistan.

Q855271.name: Battle of Jemappes
Q855271.blurb: Battle of Jemappes in the French Revolutionary Wars.

Q855429.name: Battle of Ligny
Q855429.blurb: Battle of Ligny and Battle of Quatre Bras, two days before the Battle of Waterloo.

Q856129.name: Kitchen Debate
Q856129.blurb: Soviet premier Nikita Khrushchev and U.S. vice president Richard Nixon held an impromptu debate (pictured) at the opening of the American National Exhibition at Sokolniki Park in Moscow.

Q856168.name: Pastry War
Q856168.blurb: The French Army captures Veracruz in the Pastry War.

Q856216.name: Beaver Wars
Q856216.blurb: Beaver Wars: At Ticonderoga (now Crown Point, New York), Samuel de Champlain shoots and kills two Iroquois chiefs on behalf of his native allies.

Q856650.name: Iraqi invasion of Kuwait
aliases: Reactions to the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait
Q856650.blurb: Iraqi invasion of Kuwait: Iraq invades Kuwait and temporarily establishes the Republic of Kuwait puppet state on the orders of Saddam Hussein, eventually leading to the Gulf War.

Q856670.name: 1973 Chilean coup d'état
aliases: Commemoration of the 1973 Chilean coup d'état
Declaration of the Breakdown of Chile's Democracy
Declaration of the Breakdown of Chile’s Democracy
Golpe de Estado en Chile de 1973
Q856670.blurb: A coup in Chile, headed by General Augusto Pinochet, topples the democratically elected president Salvador Allende.

Q857982.name: First Matabele War
Q857982.blurb: First Matabele War: A patrol of 34 British South Africa Company soldiers is ambushed and annihilated by more than 3,000 Matabele warriors on the Shangani River in Matabeleland.

Q858145.name: Space Shuttle Challenger disaster
Q858145.blurb: The Space Shuttle Challenger disintegrated 73 seconds into its tenth mission (video featured), killing all seven crew members.

Q858415.name: 1978 FIFA World Cup Final
Q858415.blurb: Hosts Argentina defeat the Netherlands by a score of 3–1 in the final to win their first ever FIFA World Cup.

Q858734.name: Superga air disaster
Q858734.blurb: The entire Torino football team (except for two players who did not take the trip: Sauro Tomà, due to an injury and Renato Gandolfi, because of coach request) is killed in a plane crash.

Q858778.name: Late Show with David Letterman
aliases: The Late Show with David Letterman
Biff Henderson's Cavalcade of Surprisingly Spot-On Superstar Celebrity Look-Alikes
Q858778.blurb: After his terminal-cancer diagnosis, Warren Zevon made his last public appearance on the Late Show with David Letterman, giving the advice to "enjoy every sandwich".

Q860150.name: Battle of Charleroi
Q860150.blurb: World War I: The Battle of Charleroi, a successful German attack across the River Sambre that pre-empted a French offensive in the same area.

Q860295.name: Siege of Port Hudson
Q860295.blurb: Second Assault on the Confederate works at the Siege of Port Hudson during the American Civil War.

Q860423.name: 2006 Thai coup d'état
aliases: International reactions to the 2006 Thai coup d'etat
International reactions to the 2006 Thailand coup d'etat
International reactions to the 2006 Thailand coup d'état
Q860423.blurb: The Thai army stages a coup. The Constitution is revoked and martial law is declared.

Q862054.name: 1972 Nixon visit to China
aliases: U.S. President Richard Nixon's 1972 visit to China
Visit to Beijing by President Richard Nixon
Q862054.blurb: Cold War: Following President Richard Nixon's visit to the People's Republic of China, the two countries agree to establish liaison offices.

Q862099.name: 1993 Russian constitutional crisis
Q862099.blurb: Tanks bombard the Russian parliament, while demonstrators against President Yeltsin rally outside.

Q862187.name: Bonanza
Q862187.blurb: Bonanza, the first regularly scheduled TV program presented in color, is launched in the United States.

Q862257.name: King Philip's War
Q862257.blurb: The Great Swamp Fight, a pivotal battle in King Philip's War, gives the English settlers a bitterly won victory.

Q862443.name: Vicksburg Campaign
Q862443.blurb: American Civil War: During the Vicksburg Campaign, gunboats commanded by acting Rear Admiral David Dixon Porter run downriver past Confederate artillery batteries at Vicksburg.

Q862543.name: Fourth Council of Constantinople (Eastern Orthodox)
Q862543.blurb: Emperor Basil I ratifies the decrees of the Fourth Council of Constantinople, confirming the reinstatement of patriarch Photios I of Constantinople.

Q862548.name: Turkish Airlines Flight 1951
Q862548.blurb: Turkish Airlines Flight 1951 crashes during landing at the Amsterdam Schiphol Airport, Netherlands, primarily due to a faulty radio altimeter, resulting in the death of nine passengers and crew including all three pilots.

Q862586.name: September Massacres
Q862586.blurb: During what became known as the September Massacres of the French Revolution, rampaging mobs slaughter three Roman Catholic bishops, more than two hundred priests, and prisoners believed to be royalist sympathizers.

Q862751.name: Battle of Long Island
Q862751.blurb: British forces led by William Howe defeated the Continental Army under George Washington at the Battle of Long Island, the largest battle of the American Revolutionary War.

Q864684.name: 2008 Bhutanese National Assembly election
Q864684.blurb: Bhutan officially becomes a democracy, with its first ever general election.

Q864847.name: Second Zhili–Fengtian War
Q864847.blurb: Second Zhili–Fengtian War: Warlord Feng Yuxiang, with the covert support of the Empire of Japan, stages a coup in Beijing against his erstwhile superiors in the Zhili clique, crippling their nearly victorious war effort against the Fengtian clique and forcing them to withdraw from northern China.

Q865344.name: Genocide Convention
aliases: Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide
Convention of the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide
Convention on Prevention and Punishment of Genocide
Convention on Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide
Convention on the Prevention & Punishment of the Crime of Genocide
Convention on the Prevention and Punishment
Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of Genocide
UN Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide
United Nations Convention on Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide

Q865365.name: Jim Crow laws
aliases: Racial laws of the Southern United States
Racial policy of the Southern United States
Q865365.blurb: The Journey of Reconciliation, the first interracial Freedom Ride begins through the upper South in violation of Jim Crow laws. The riders wanted enforcement of the United States Supreme Court's 1946 Irene Morgan decision that banned racial segregation in interstate travel.

Q865513.name: Helios Airways Flight 522
aliases: Greece Helios Airways Boeing 737-300 air disaster
Q865513.blurb: Helios Airways Flight 522, en route from Larnaca, Cyprus to Prague, Czech Republic via Athens, crashes in the hills near Grammatiko, Greece, killing 121 passengers and crew.

Q865870.name: TAM Airlines Flight 3054
aliases: July 18, 2007 Tam Airlines Crash in Sao Paulo
Q865870.blurb: TAM Airlines Flight 3054, an Airbus A320, crashes into a warehouse after landing too fast and missing the end of the São Paulo–Congonhas Airport runway, killing 199 people.

Q866240.name: Bulgarian republic referendum
Q866240.blurb: A referendum abolishes the monarchy in Bulgaria.

Q866653.name: 2010 Shanghai fire
Q866653.blurb: A fire in a high-rise apartment building in Shanghai, China kills 58 people.

Q866680.name: President of Vietnam
aliases: Commander-in-Chief of the People's Army of Vietnam
President of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam
President of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam
Q866680.blurb: A military coup against President Ngô Đình Diệm of South Vietnam is crushed.

Q867316.name: Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire
aliases: Significance of the Triangle Shirtwaist Fire
Victims of the Triangle Shirt Waist Fire of 1911
Q867316.blurb: In New York City, the Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire kills 146 garment workers.

Q867691.name: May 2006 Java earthquake
Q867691.blurb: The 6.4 Mw Yogyakarta earthquake shakes central Java with an MSK intensity of VIII (Damaging), leaving more than 5,700 dead and 37,000 injured.

Q867778.name: People's Republic of Kampuchea
Q867778.blurb: The Cambodian–Vietnamese War formally ended with the withdrawal of Vietnamese forces from the People's Republic of Kampuchea, a client state it had implemented to overthrow Democratic Kampuchea and the Khmer Rouge.

Q868027.name: Battle of Clontarf
Q868027.blurb: Battle of Clontarf: High King of Ireland Brian Boru defeats Viking invaders, but is killed in battle.

Q868249.name: Battle of Colenso
Q868249.blurb: British Army forces are defeated at the Battle of Colenso in Natal, South Africa, the third and final battle fought during the Black Week of the Second Boer War.

Q868261.name: Black Monday
Q868261.blurb: Black Monday: The Dow Jones Industrial Average falls by 22%, 508 points.

Q868393.name: Underground Railroad
aliases: National Underground Railroad Network to Freedom
Q868393.blurb: Harriet Tubman (pictured) escaped from slavery in the U.S. state of Maryland, and later orchestrated the rescues of other slaves via the Underground Railroad.

Q868481.name: Battle of Hampton Roads
aliases: Battle of the Monitor and Merrimack
Q868481.blurb: American Civil War: USS Monitor and CSS Virginia (rebuilt from the engines and lower hull of the USS Merrimack) fight to a draw in the Battle of Hampton Roads, the first battle between two ironclad warships.

Q869045.name: Queen Anne's War
Q869045.blurb: In Queen Anne's War, French forces and Native Americans stage a raid on Deerfield, Massachusetts Bay Colony, killing 56 villagers and taking more than 100 captive.

Q869488.name: 1999 Orissa cyclone
Q869488.blurb: A large cyclone devastates Odisha, India.

Q869500.name: Montreux Convention
aliases: Montreux Convention Regarding the Regime of the Straits (Turkish)
Montreux Convention Regarding the Regime of the Turkish Straits
Montreux Convention Regarding the Regime of the Turkish Straits/Treaty text
Q869500.blurb: The Montreux Convention is signed in Switzerland, authorizing Turkey to fortify the Dardanelles and Bosphorus but guaranteeing free passage to ships of all nations in peacetime.

Q870124.name: Bombing of Kassel in World War II
Q870124.blurb: World War II: In the second firestorm raid on Germany, the British Royal Air Force conducts an air raid on the town of Kassel, killing 10,000 and rendering 150,000 homeless.

Q870196.name: Russo-Swedish War of 1788–1790
Q870196.blurb: Russo-Swedish War: During the Battle of Svensksund in the Baltic Sea, the Swedish Navy captured a third of the Russian fleet.

Q871366.name: Battle of Sluys
Q871366.blurb: Hundred Years' War: Battle of Sluys: The French fleet is almost completely destroyed by the English fleet commanded personally by King Edward III.

Q871407.name: Treaty of Rapallo
Q871407.blurb: Italy and the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes sign the Treaty of Rapallo.

Q871937.name: CARE package
Q871937.blurb: CARE (then the Cooperative for American Remittances to Europe) is founded to send CARE Packages of food relief to Europe after World War II.

Q873485.name: Colgan Air Flight 3407
Q873485.blurb: Colgan Air Flight 3407 crashes into a house in Clarence Center, New York while on approach to Buffalo Niagara International Airport, killing all 49 on board and one on the ground.

Q874209.name: Spanish transition to democracy
Q874209.blurb: Spanish transition to democracy: Neo-fascists attacked an office in Madrid, killing five people and injuring four others.

Q874235.name: Sack of Antwerp
Q874235.blurb: Eighty Years' War: In Flanders, Spain captures Antwerp (which is nearly destroyed after three days).

Q874784.name: Bar Confederation
Q874784.blurb: Polish nobles form the Bar Confederation.

Q875738.name: Brown v. Board of Education
aliases: Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka
Oliver Brown, et al. v. Board of Education of Topeka, et al.
Brooks v. Board of Education of the City of Moberly, Missouri
Brown V Board Of Education Of Topeka Kansas
Brown V. Board Of Education Of Topeka Kansas
Brown v Board of Education of Topeka
Brown v Topeka Board of Ed.
Brown v. Bd. of Educ. of Topeka
Brown v. Board of Education II
Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka (1954)
Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka, Kansas
Brown v. Topeka Board of Education
Brown v. school board of Topeka, KS
Brown v. school board of Topeka, Kansas
Brown v. the board of education
Brown versus topeka board of education
Brown vs Board of Education of Topeka
Brown vs the Board of Education
Brown vs. Board of Education of Topeka
Kans. Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka
Oliver Brown et al. v. Board of Education of Topeka et al.
Oliver Brown et al. v. The Board of Education of Topeka, Kansas
Oliver Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka
Oliver L. Brown et al. v. the Board of Education of Topeka
Q875738.blurb: The United States Supreme Court hands down a unanimous decision in Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka, Kansas, outlawing racial segregation in public schools.

Q876206.name: 1998 United States embassy bombings
aliases: 1998 bombing of the United States embassies
1998 bombings of U.S. Embassies in Africa
1998 bombings of US embassies in Kenya and Tanzania
1998 bombings of the United States embassies
Attack against the American Embassies in Kenya and Tanzania
Bombing of the American Embassies in Kenya and Uganda in 1998
Q876206.blurb: Bombings at United States embassies in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania and Nairobi, Kenya kill approximately 212 people.

Q876357.name: Peterloo Massacre
Q876357.blurb: Peterloo Massacre: Seventeen people die and over 600 are injured in cavalry charges at a public meeting at St. Peter's Field, Manchester, England.

Q876417.name: Second Battle of the Marne
aliases: Battle of the Mountain of Reims
The Second Battle of the Marne
Q876417.blurb: World War I: The Second Battle of the Marne begins near the River Marne with a German attack.

Q877399.name: North Atlantic Treaty
aliases: Article 4 of the North Atlantic Treaty
Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty
Protocol to the North Atlantic Treaty
Q877399.blurb: Twelve nations signed the North Atlantic Treaty, establishing NATO, an international military alliance whereby its member states agree to mutual defense in response to an attack by any external party.

Q877450.name: Laotian Civil War
aliases: The secret war on laos, history
Q877450.blurb: The United States government acknowledges the existence of the "Secret War" in Laos and dedicates the Laos Memorial in honor of Hmong and other "Secret War" veterans.

Q877777.name: Battle of Gammelsdorf
Q877777.blurb: Louis the Bavarian defeats his cousin Frederick I of Austria at the Battle of Gammelsdorf.

Q878985.name: modernism
Q878985.blurb: The Tritons' Fountain in Valletta, one of Malta's most important Modernist landmarks, was turned on for the first time.

Q879267.name: Bizerte crisis
Q879267.blurb: Tunisia imposes a blockade on the French naval base at Bizerte; the French would capture the entire town four days later.

Q879980.name: Black Hawk War
Q879980.blurb: Black Hawk War: Around 300 United States 6th Infantry troops leave St. Louis, Missouri to fight the Sauk Native Americans.

Q882204.name: Dahlerau train disaster
Q882204.blurb: The Dahlerau train disaster, the worst railway accident in West Germany, kills 46 people and injures 25 near Wuppertal.

Q882925.name: Jewish revolt against Constantius Gallus
Q882925.blurb: The Jewish revolt against Constantius Gallus breaks out after his arrival at Antioch.

Q883089.name: Paninternational Flight 112
Q883089.blurb: Paninternational Flight 112 crashes on the Bundesautobahn 7 highway near Hamburg Airport, in Hamburg, Germany, killing 22.

Q883298.name: Jeltoqsan
Q883298.blurb: The Jeltoqsan riots erupt in Alma-Ata, Kazakh SSR, in response to Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev's dismissal of ethnic Kazakh Dinmukhamed Kunaev, the First Secretary of the Communist Party of Kazakhstan, and his replacement with Gennady Kolbin, an ethnic Russian from the Russian SFSR.

Q883433.name: Great Sejm
Q883433.blurb: The Great Sejm of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth ratified the first codified national constitution in Europe.

Q885019.name: Operation Queen
Q885019.blurb: World War II: Operation Queen commenced with one of the heaviest Allied tactical bombings of the war, attacking German targets in the Rur valley.

Q885269.name: Bloody Friday
Q885269.blurb: The Troubles: Bloody Friday: The Provisional IRA detonate 22 bombs in central Belfast, Northern Ireland, United Kingdom in the space of 80 minutes, killing nine and injuring 130.

Q886480.name: massacre in front of the Reichstag on 13 January 1920
Q886480.blurb: The Reichstag Bloodbath of January 13, 1920, the bloodiest demonstration in German history.

Q886485.name: 1977 Atocha massacre
Q886485.blurb: The Atocha massacre occurs in Madrid during the Spanish transition to democracy.

Q886799.name: Bloody Sunday
Q886799.blurb: Irish War of Independence: On "Bloody Sunday" in Dublin, the Irish Republican Army (IRA) assassinated a group of British Intelligence agents, and British forces killed 14 civilians at a Gaelic football match at Croke Park.

Q886842.name: Carolinas Campaign
Q886842.blurb: American Civil War: The last battle of the Carolinas Campaign, the Battle of Bentonville, began, which contributed to the ultimate Union victory in the war.

Q886856.name: Knoxville Campaign
Q886856.blurb: American Civil War: Siege of Knoxville begins: During the Knoxville campaign, Confederate forces under General James Longstreet besiege the city of Knoxville, Tennessee and its Union defenders led by General Ambrose Burnside.

Q887817.name: Year of the Six Emperors
Q887817.blurb: During the year of Six Emperors, forces of Gordian I and Gordian II are defeated by those of Maximinus Thrax in the battle of Carthage.

Q889358.name: 1993 Bombay bombings
Q889358.blurb: Several bombs explode in Mumbai, India, killing about 300 people and injuring hundreds more.

Q890629.name: American Airlines Flight 1
Q890629.blurb: American Airlines Flight 1 crashes into Jamaica Bay in New York, killing 95.

Q891808.name: Bombing of Plaza de Mayo
Q891808.blurb: In a futile effort to topple Argentine President Juan Perón, rogue aircraft pilots of the Argentine Navy drop several bombs upon an unarmed crowd demonstrating in favor of Perón in Buenos Aires, killing 364 and injuring at least 800. At the same time on the ground, some soldiers attempt to stage a coup but are suppressed by loyal forces.

Q891853.name: Harrods bombing
Q891853.blurb: Provisional IRA members detonate a car bomb at Harrods Department Store in London. Three police officers and three civilians are killed.

Q891856.name: Brighton hotel bombing
Q891856.blurb: The Provisional Irish Republican Army fail to assassinate Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher and her cabinet.  The bomb kills five people and wounds at least 31 others.

Q891864.name: Islamabad Marriott Hotel bombing
Q891864.blurb: A dump truck full of explosives detonates in front of the Marriott hotel in Islamabad, Pakistan, killing 54 people and injuring 266 others.

Q891865.name: Piazza Fontana bombing
Q891865.blurb: The Piazza Fontana bombing; a bomb explodes at the headquarters of Banca Nazionale dell'Agricoltura (the National Agricultural Bank) in Piazza Fontana in Milan, Italy, killing 17 people and wounding 88. The same afternoon, three more bombs are detonated in Rome and Milan, and another is found unexploded.

Q891868.name: St Nedelya Church assault
aliases: Bombing of the St Nedelya Church
Bombing of the St. Nedelya Church
Q891868.blurb: During the Communist St Nedelya Church assault in Sofia, Bulgaria, 150 are killed and 500 are wounded.

Q891869.name: Hyde Park and Regent's Park bombings
Q891869.blurb: Hyde Park and Regent's Park bombings: The Provisional IRA detonates two bombs in Hyde Park and Regent's Park in central London, killing eight soldiers, wounding forty-seven people, and leading to the deaths of seven horses.

Q891873.name: Wall Street bombing
Q891873.blurb: The Wall Street bombing: A bomb in a horse wagon explodes in front of the J. P. Morgan building in New York City killing 38 and injuring 400.

Q891877.name: Myyrmanni bombing
Q891877.blurb: A bomb attack in a Myyrmanni shopping mall in Vantaa, Finland kills seven.

Q891878.name: Birmingham pub bombings
Q891878.blurb: The Birmingham pub bombings kill 21 people. The Birmingham Six are sentenced to life in prison for the crime but are later exonerated.

Q891879.name: Guildford pub bombings
Q891879.blurb: Bombs planted by the PIRA in pubs in Guildford kill four British soldiers and one civilian.

Q891895.name: 2006 Mumbai train bombings
Q891895.blurb: Mumbai train bombings: 209 people are killed in a series of bomb attacks in Mumbai, India.

Q892144.name: Twelfth Council of Toledo
Q892144.blurb: Twelfth Council of Toledo: King Erwig of the Visigoths initiates a council in which he implements diverse measures against the Jews in Spain.

Q892990.name: L'Oiseau Blanc
Q892990.blurb: Attempting to make the first non-stop transatlantic flight from Paris to New York, French war heroes Charles Nungesser and François Coli disappear after taking off aboard The White Bird biplane.

Q894486.name: War of the Straits
Q894486.blurb: War of the Straits: The Battle of the Bosporus is fought in a stormy sea into the night between the Genoese, Venetian, Aragonese, and Byzantine fleets.

Q896479.name: Brabant Revolution
Q896479.blurb: The Brabant Revolution, sometimes considered to be the first expression of Belgian nationalism, began with the invasion of the Austrian Netherlands by an émigré army from the Dutch Republic.

Q896666.name: 2007–2008 financial crisis
aliases: Causes of the financial crisis of 2007-2008
Causes of the financial crisis of 2007–2008
Global economic and financial crisis of 2008-09
Global economic and financial crisis of 2008–09
Global financial crisis of September and October 2008
Global stock market crash of September 2008
Q896666.blurb: Prelude to the 2008 financial crisis: Northern Rock bank experiences the first bank run in the United Kingdom in 150 years.

Q897768.name: Cocoanut Grove fire
Q897768.blurb: In Boston, Massachusetts, a fire in the Cocoanut Grove nightclub kills 492 people.

Q897772.name: Iroquois Theatre fire
Q897772.blurb: A fire at the Iroquois Theater in Chicago, Illinois kills at least 605.

Q897785.name: Fire of Moscow
Q897785.blurb: The 1812 Fire of Moscow dies down after destroying more than three-quarters of the city. Napoleon returns from the Petrovsky Palace to the Moscow Kremlin, spared from the fire.

Q897786.name: Burning of Washington
Q897786.blurb: British troops capture Washington, D.C. and set the Presidential Mansion, Capitol, Navy Yard and many other public buildings ablaze.

Q897803.name: 2011 Monterrey casino attack
Q897803.blurb: Fifty-two people are killed during an arson attack caused by members of the drug cartel Los Zetas.

Q897808.name: Sivas massacre
Q897808.blurb: A mob sets fire to the Hotel Madımak in Sivas, Turkey, where an Alevi cultural festival was taking place, killing 37 people.

Q900693.name: Seminole Wars
aliases: United States Senate Select Committee on the Seminole War
Q900693.blurb: American Indian Wars: Second Seminole War ends, with the Seminoles forced from Florida.

Q900945.name: Battle of Lodi
Q900945.blurb: War of the First Coalition: Napoleon wins a victory against Austrian forces at Lodi bridge over the Adda River in Italy. The Austrians lose some 2,000 men.

Q901263.name: Battle of Dak To
Q901263.blurb: Vietnam War: The Battle of Dak To begins.

Q901714.name: Norman invasion of Ireland
Q901714.blurb: Anglo-Norman invasion of Ireland: The Kingdom of Dublin falls to Anglo-Norman invaders.

Q903199.name: Cimbrian War
Q903199.blurb: Cimbrian War: Defeat at the Battle of Arausio of the Roman army of the mid-Republic

Q903472.name: Battle of Vyazma
Q903472.blurb: Napoleon's armies are defeated at the Battle of Vyazma.

Q903876.name: Singapore strategy
Q903876.blurb: The Singapore Naval Base, the cornerstone of the Singapore strategy, a British naval defence policy, was opened.

Q904715.name: Yemenia Flight 626
Q904715.blurb: Yemenia Flight 626, an Airbus A310-300, crashes into the Indian Ocean near Comoros, killing 152 of the 153 people on board. A 14-year-old girl named Bahia Bakari survives the crash.

Q905063.name: 1918 Irish general election
Q905063.blurb: At the general election in Ireland, Constance Markievicz was elected to the House of Commons of the United Kingdom as the first female member of Parliament, although she never took her seat.

Q906018.name: Battle of Great Bridge
Q906018.blurb: American Revolutionary War: After their loss in the Battle of Great Bridge, British authorities were forced to evacuate from the Colony of Virginia.

Q906232.name: Disney Renaissance
Q906232.blurb: Walt Disney Pictures released The Little Mermaid to theatres, beginning the Disney Renaissance.

Q906650.name: second round of simplified Chinese characters
Q906650.blurb: With the approval of the State Council, China's two largest newspapers, the People's Daily and the Guangming Daily, publish in full for the first time the Second Chinese Character Simplification Scheme.

Q906912.name: Battle of Wakefield
Q906912.blurb: Wars of the Roses: At the Battle of Wakefield, Lancastrian forces destroyed the Yorkist army and killed Richard of York  at Sandal Magna in West Yorkshire, England.

Q906933.name: Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting
aliases: Mass murder at Sandy Hook Elementary School
Q906933.blurb: Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting: Twenty-eight people, including the gunman, are killed in Sandy Hook, Connecticut.

Q907519.name: 1929 Grand Banks earthquake
Q907519.blurb: Grand Banks earthquake: Off the south coast of Newfoundland in the Atlantic Ocean, a Richter magnitude 7.2 submarine earthquake, centered on the  Grand Banks, breaks 12 submarine transatlantic telegraph cables and triggers a tsunami that destroys many south coast communities in the Burin Peninsula.

Q908101.name: Battle of Andernach
Q908101.blurb: Frankish forces led by Louis the Younger prevent a West Frankish invasion and defeat emperor Charles II ("the Bald").

Q908708.name: Neighbours
Q908708.blurb: The first episode of the soap opera Neighbours was broadcast on the Seven Network, later becoming the longest-running drama in Australian television history.

Q908717.name: TWA Flight 800
Q908717.blurb: TWA Flight 800: Off the coast of Long Island, New York, a Paris-bound TWA Boeing 747 explodes, killing all 230 on board.

Q908988.name: Mursili's eclipse
Q908988.blurb: Mursili II launches a campaign against the Kingdom of Azzi-Hayasa.

Q909551.name: 1982 FIFA World Cup Final
Q909551.blurb: Italy defeats West Germany 3–1 to win the FIFA World Cup.

Q909737.name: Tlatelolco massacre
aliases: Massacre of Tlatelolco, Mexico City, Mexico, 1968
Night ot Tlatelolco, Mexico City, Mexico, 1968
Q909737.blurb: Mexican President Gustavo Díaz Ordaz orders soldiers to suppress a demonstration of unarmed students, ten days before the start of the 1968 Summer Olympics.

Q909869.name: China Northern Airlines Flight 6136
Q909869.blurb: A China Northern Airlines MD-82 plunges into the Yellow Sea, killing 112 people.

Q910261.name: Greece during World War I
Q910261.blurb: World War I: Greece joins the Allied powers.

Q911131.name: Battle of La Brossinière
Q911131.blurb: Hundred Years' War: A French army defeats the English at the Battle of La Brossinière.

Q911295.name: 2011 Cricket World Cup
aliases: O Prithibi Ebar Ese Bangladesh Nao Chine
Q911295.blurb: India wins the Cricket World Cup for the second time in history under the captaincy of MS Dhoni.

Q911448.name: Battle of Amiens
aliases: Black Day of the German Army
