Q911448.blurb: The Battle of Amiens began in northern France, marking the start of the Allies' Hundred Days Offensive through the German front lines that ultimately led to the end of World War I.

Q911972.name: Dunkirk evacuation
Q911972.blurb: World War II: Operation Dynamo: In northern France, Allied forces begin a massive evacuation from Dunkirk, France. The Battle of Dunkirk begins simultaneously as Allied defenders fight to slow down the German offensive.

Q912835.name: 1971 San Fernando earthquake
Q912835.blurb: The 6.5–6.7 Mw Sylmar earthquake hits the Greater Los Angeles Area with a maximum Mercalli intensity of XI (Extreme), killing 64 and injuring 2,000.

Q913604.name: Battle of Alma
Q913604.blurb: Crimean War: British and French troops defeat Russians at the Battle of Alma.

Q913640.name: Great Smog of London
Q913640.blurb: Beginning of the Great Smog in London. A cold fog combines with air pollution and brings the city to a standstill for four days. Later, a Ministry of Health report estimates 4,000 fatalities as a result of it.

Q913644.name: An Act to provide for the admission of the State of Alaska into the Union
Q913644.blurb: US President Dwight D. Eisenhower signs the Alaska Statehood Act into law.

Q913747.name: shooting of Trayvon Martin
Q913747.blurb: Seventeen-year-old African-American student Trayvon Martin is shot to death by neighborhood watch coordinator George Zimmerman in an altercation in Sanford, Florida.

Q916295.name: Battle of Northampton
Q916295.blurb: Richard Neville, 16th Earl of Warwick, defeats the king's Lancastrian forces and takes King Henry VI prisoner in the Battle of Northampton.

Q916495.name: Second Anglo-Dutch War
Q916495.blurb: The Second Anglo-Dutch War ended with the signing of the Treaty of Breda.

Q917138.name: 37th Academy Awards
Q917138.blurb: My Fair Lady wins Best Picture at the 37th Academy Awards.

Q917143.name: 36th Academy Awards
Q917143.blurb: At the Academy Awards, Sidney Poitier becomes the first African-American man to win the Best Actor award for the 1963 film Lilies of the Field.

Q917435.name: July Crisis
Q917435.blurb: July Crisis: Austria-Hungary issues a series of demands in an ultimatum to the Kingdom of Serbia demanding Serbia to allow the Austrians to determine who assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand. Serbia accepts all but one of those demands and Austria declares war on July 28.

Q917606.name: Brioni Agreement
Q917606.blurb: Upon the expiration of the Brioni Agreement, Croatia and Slovenia sever all official relations with Yugoslavia.

Q917629.name: World Chess Championship 2013
Q917629.blurb: Norwegian chess grandmaster Magnus Carlsen (pictured) defeated India's Viswanathan Anand to become world chess champion.

Q917709.name: Hundred Days' Reform
Q917709.blurb: The Hundred Days' Reform, a planned movement to reform social, political, and educational institutions in China, is started by the Guangxu Emperor, but is suspended by Empress Dowager Cixi after 104 days. (The failed reform led to the abolition of the Imperial examination in 1905.)

Q918093.name: Britches
Q918093.blurb: University of California, Riverside 1985 laboratory raid: Animal Liberation Front rescues 467 animals being tested in a lab at University of California, Riverside in Riverside, California, causing $700,000 in damages to the laboratory, in advocacy for animal rights.

Q918147.name: Anglo-Polish alliance
Q918147.blurb: The United Kingdom and Poland form a military alliance in which the UK promises to defend Poland in case of invasion by a foreign power.

Q918160.name: Operation Herrick
Q918160.blurb: Britain withdraws from Afghanistan at the end of Operation Herrick, after 12 years four months and seven days.

Q918162.name: 2006 transatlantic aircraft plot
Q918162.blurb: At least 21 suspected terrorists are arrested in the 2006 transatlantic aircraft plot that happened in the United Kingdom. The arrests are made in London, Birmingham, and High Wycombe in an overnight operation.

Q918286.name: 1924 British Mount Everest Expedition
Q918286.blurb: British Mount Everest expedition: British mountaineers Andrew Irvine and George Mallory go missing.

Q918397.name: 1945 United Kingdom general election
Q918397.blurb: The United Kingdom holds its first general election in 10 years, which would be won by Clement Attlee's Labour Party.

Q918430.name: 1966 United Kingdom general election
Q918430.blurb: The Labour Party under Harold Wilson wins the 1966 United Kingdom general election.

Q918450.name: 1979 United Kingdom general election
Q918450.blurb: The Conservative Party wins the United Kingdom general election. The following day, Margaret Thatcher becomes the first female British Prime Minister.

Q918503.name: 1997 United Kingdom general election
Q918503.blurb: The Labour Party wins the 1997 General Election and Tony Blair is elected as Prime Minister.

Q918544.name: 1984–85 UK miners' strike
Q918544.blurb: In the United Kingdom, a walkout at Cortonwood Colliery in Brampton Bierlow signals the start of a strike that lasted almost a year and involved the majority of the country's miners.

Q918595.name: British Eagle International Airlines Flight 802
Q918595.blurb: British Eagle International Airlines Flight 802/6 crashes into the Glungezer mountain in the Tux Alps of Austria, killing all 75 people aboard.

Q918604.name: British European Airways Flight 706
Q918604.blurb: British European Airways Flight 706 crashes near Aarsele, Belgium, killing 63.

Q920894.name: First Italian War of Independence
Q920894.blurb: The Italian tricolour is adopted for the flag of the Kingdom of Sardinia by Charles Albert of Sardinia during the First Italian War of Independence.

Q921174.name: Opération Harmattan
Q921174.blurb: First Libyan Civil War: The French Air Force launched Opération Harmattan, beginning foreign military intervention in Libya.

Q921452.name: Pearl Continental hotel bombing
Q921452.blurb: An explosion kills 17 people and injures at least 46 at a hotel in Peshawar, Pakistan.

Q921497.name: 2009 Samoa earthquake
Q921497.blurb: The 8.1 Mw Samoa earthquake results in a tsunami that kills over 189 and injures hundreds.

Q922661.name: 1986 United States bombing of Libya
Q922661.blurb: The United States launches Operation El Dorado Canyon, its bombing raids against Libyan targets in response to a discotheque bombing in West Germany that killed two U.S. servicemen.

Q922790.name: Battle of Hubbardton
Q922790.blurb: American forces retreating from Fort Ticonderoga are defeated in the Battle of Hubbardton.

Q924138.name: Operation Hurricane
Q924138.blurb: The United Kingdom successfully tests a nuclear weapon in the Montebello Islands, Western Australia, to become the world's third nuclear power.

Q924446.name: 1972 Nicaragua earthquake
Q924446.blurb: A 6.5 magnitude earthquake strikes the Nicaraguan capital of Managua killing more than 10,000.

Q924600.name: War against Sigismund
Q924600.blurb: The Linköping Bloodbath takes place on Maundy Thursday in Linköping, Sweden: five Swedish noblemen are publicly beheaded in the aftermath of the War against Sigismund (1598–1599).

Q924625.name: 2010 Nigerien coup d'état
Q924625.blurb: In a coup d'état, military rebels attacked the presidential palace in Niamey, Niger, and replaced President Mamadou Tandja with a ruling junta, the Supreme Council for the Restoration of Democracy.

Q925176.name: 1909 Giro d'Italia
Q925176.blurb: The first edition of the Giro d'Italia, a long-distance multiple-stage bicycle race, begins in Milan; the Italian cyclist Luigi Ganna was the eventual winner.

Q925618.name: Texas City disaster
Q925618.blurb: An explosion on board a freighter in port causes Texas City in the state of Texas, United States, to catch fire, killing almost 600 people.

Q925737.name: Akihabara massacre
Q925737.blurb: Seven people are killed and 11 more are injured in a massacre in Akihabara.

Q926447.name: Treaty of Gulistan
Q926447.blurb: Treaty of Gulistan: The Russo-Persian War of 1804-1813 comes to a close with the signing of the Treaty of Gulistan, under which terms Qajar Iran agrees to cede the bulk of its Caucasian territories, which comprise much of modern Dagestan, Georgia, Armenia, and Azerbaijan, to the Russian Empire.

Q926483.name: 1869 college football season
Q926483.blurb: In New Brunswick, New Jersey, Rutgers College defeats Princeton University (then known as the College of New Jersey), 6–4, in the first official intercollegiate American football game.

Q926594.name: Ukrainian independence referendum
Q926594.blurb: A referendum held to ratify the Act of Declaration of Independence of Ukraine passed with more than 92 percent of the vote.

Q927194.name: Polish Round Table Agreement
Q927194.blurb: The Round Table Talks start in Poland, thus marking the beginning of the overthrow of communism in Eastern Europe.

Q927262.name: 1956 European Cup Final
Q927262.blurb: Spanish football club Real Madrid CF wins the inaugural European Cup, UEFA's premier club competition, by winning 4–3 against French club Stade de Reims in the final.

Q927606.name: Treaty of Vereeniging
Q927606.blurb: Second Boer War: The Treaty of Vereeniging ends the war and ensures British control of South Africa.

Q928079.name: Bishkek Protocol
Q928079.blurb: The signing of the Bishkek Protocol between Armenia and Azerbaijan effectively freezes the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict.

Q928629.name: Pike River Mine disaster
Q928629.blurb: The first of four explosions takes place at the Pike River Mine in New Zealand. Twenty-nine people are killed in the nation's worst mining disaster since 1914.

Q928848.name: Treaty of Stolbovo
Q928848.blurb: Sweden signed the Treaty of Stolbovo to end the Ingrian War with Russia, making large territorial gains.

Q928955.name: June 2009 Washington Metro train collision
Q928955.blurb: Two Metro trains collided in Washington, D.C., killing nine people and injuring eighty others.

Q929589.name: The Bill
Q929589.blurb: The last episode of The Bill, the longest-running police drama in British television history, was broadcast.

Q929721.name: USAir Flight 427
Q929721.blurb: USAir Flight 427, on approach to Pittsburgh International Airport, suddenly crashes in clear weather killing all 132 aboard, resulting in the most extensive aviation investigation in world history and altering manufacturing practices in the industry.

Q930521.name: Battle of Jodoigne
Q930521.blurb: The Spanish Duke of Alba defeats a Dutch rebel force under William the Silent.

Q931024.name: 1447 papal conclave
Q931024.blurb: Election of Pope Nicholas V following the death of Pope Eugene IV on 23 February 1447.

Q931125.name: Raid on Drvar
Q931125.blurb: The Wehrmacht and their collaborationist allies launched Operation Rösselsprung, a failed attempt to assassinate the Yugoslav Partisan leader Josip Broz Tito.

Q931492.name: START I
Q931492.blurb: The United States and Soviet Union both sign the START I Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty, the first to reduce (with verification) both countries' stockpiles.

Q931943.name: 1971 Turkish military memorandum
Q931943.blurb: The 1971 Turkish military memorandum is sent to the Süleyman Demirel government of Turkey and the government resigns.

Q931982.name: Treaty of Fes
aliases: Traité conclu entre la France et le Maroc le 30 mars 1912, pour l'organisation du protectorat français dans l'Empire chérifien
Treaty Concluded Between France and Morocco on 30 March 1912, for the Organization of the French Protectorate in the Sharifian Empire
Treaty Concluded Between France and Morocco on March 30, 1912, for the Organization of the French Protectorate in the Sherifien Empire
Q931982.blurb: Sultan Abd al-Hafid signed the Treaty of Fes, making Morocco a French protectorate.

Q932228.name: Battle of Klushino
Q932228.blurb: The Battle of Klushino is fought between forces of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth and Russia during the Polish–Russian War, after which Polish troops entered Moscow.

Q932519.name: Battle of Mbororé
Q932519.blurb: Guaraní forces living in the Jesuit reductions defeat bandeirantes loyal to the Portuguese Empire at the Battle of Mbororé in present-day Panambí, Argentina.

Q932613.name: Battle of Castillon
Q932613.blurb: Battle of Castillon: The last battle of the Hundred Years' War, the French under Jean Bureau defeat the English under the Earl of Shrewsbury, who is killed in the battle in Gascony.

Q932701.name: Summer of Love
aliases: If It Feels Good Do It movement
Q932701.blurb: Counterculture of the 1960s: The Human Be-In takes place in San Francisco, California's Golden Gate Park, launching the Summer of Love.

Q933067.name: Hurricane Ivan
Q933067.blurb: Hurricane Ivan made landfall on Grenada and devastated at least 85 percent of buildings on the island.

Q933745.name: Treaty of Osimo
Q933745.blurb: Treaty of Osimo between Yugoslavia and Italy

Q933963.name: Marcomannic Wars
Q933963.blurb: Marcomannic Wars: The Roman army in Moravia is encircled by the Quadi, who have broken the peace treaty (171). In a violent thunderstorm, emperor Marcus Aurelius defeats and subdues them in the so-called "miracle of the rain".

Q934157.name: Battle of Ayacucho
aliases: Battle Of Pampa De La Quinua
Q934157.blurb: Patriot forces led by General Antonio José de Sucre defeat a Royalist army in the Battle of Ayacucho, putting an end to the Peruvian War of Independence.

Q934470.name: Istanbul pogrom
Q934470.blurb: Istanbul's Greek, Jewish, and Armenian minorities are the target of a government-sponsored pogrom; dozens are killed in ensuing riots.

Q934626.name: Battle of Valcour Island
Q934626.blurb: American Revolution: A fleet of American boats on Lake Champlain is defeated by the Royal Navy, but delays the British advance until 1777.

Q934889.name: Operation Slapstick
Q934889.blurb: World War II: The Allies land at Salerno and Taranto, Italy.

Q935088.name: Battle of Lipany
Q935088.blurb: Hussite Wars: Battle of Lipany: End of the war, the Utraquist defeat and annihilate Taborite forces.

Q935682.name: Sudan Airways Flight 139
Q935682.blurb: Sudan Airways Flight 139 crashes near Port Sudan Airport during an emergency landing attempt, killing 116 of the 117 people on board.

Q935881.name: Treaty of Kars
Q935881.blurb: The Treaty of Kars is ratified in Yerevan, Armenia.

Q936604.name: internment of Japanese Americans
aliases: Americans of Japanese descent, interned during World War 2
Internment of Japanese Americans during World War II
Internment of Japanese in the United States
Japanese American internment during World War II
Japanese internment camps in the USA
Japanese internment camps in the United States
Japanese internment in the United States
List of Japanese American Confinement Sites
World War 2 internment of those of Japanese descent
Q936604.blurb: Japanese American internment: U.S. President Ronald Reagan signs the Civil Liberties Act of 1988, providing $20,000 payments to Japanese Americans who were either interned in or relocated by the United States during World War II.

Q936847.name: 1957 Canadian federal election
Q936847.blurb: John Diefenbaker leads the Progressive Conservative Party of Canada to a stunning upset in the 1957 Canadian federal election, ending 22 years of Liberal Party government.

Q937255.name: Polish-Lithuanian-Teutonic War
Q937255.blurb: Polish–Lithuanian–Teutonic War: Battle of Grunwald: The allied forces of the Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania defeat the army of the Teutonic Order.

Q937332.name: Battle of Kircholm
Q937332.blurb: The armies of Sweden are defeated by the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth in the Battle of Kircholm.

Q938495.name: Action of Picheuta
Q938495.blurb: Crossing of the Andes: Many soldiers of Juan Gregorio de las Heras are captured during the action of Picheuta.

Q938552.name: Routemaster
Q938552.blurb: AEC Routemaster, the iconic London bus was introduced.

Q939106.name: 2005 Sumatra earthquake
Q939106.blurb: An earthquake shakes northern Sumatra with a magnitude of 8.6 and killing over 1000 people.

Q939336.name: Cyclone Kyrill
Q939336.blurb: The strongest storm in the United Kingdom in 17 years kills 14 people and Germany sees the worst storm since 1999 with 13 deaths. Cyclone Kyrill causes at least 44 deaths across 20 countries in Western Europe.

Q939570.name: Battle of Maritsa
Q939570.blurb: Serbian–Turkish wars: Ottoman Turks fought against a Serbian army at the Battle of Maritsa.

Q939819.name: Valencia Metro derailment
Q939819.blurb: The Valencia Metro derailment kills 41 people.

Q939846.name: Super Bowl III
Q939846.blurb: The New York Jets of the American Football League defeat the Baltimore Colts of the National Football League to win Super Bowl III in what is considered to be one of the greatest upsets in sports history.

Q940026.name: Battle of Arsuf
Q940026.blurb: Third Crusade: Battle of Arsuf: Richard I of England defeats Saladin at Arsuf.

Q940076.name: Boundary treaty of 1881 between Chile and Argentina
Q940076.blurb: The Boundary Treaty of 1881 between Chile and Argentina is signed in Buenos Aires.

Q940959.name: Battle of Englefield
Q940959.blurb: Battle of Englefield: The Vikings clash with ealdorman Æthelwulf of Berkshire. The invaders are driven back to Reading (East Anglia); many Danes are killed.

Q941312.name: Massacre at Béziers
Q941312.blurb: Massacre at Béziers: The first major military action of the Albigensian Crusade.

Q941322.name: Third Battle of Gaza
Q941322.blurb: World War I: The Third Battle of Gaza ends, with British forces capturing Gaza from the Ottoman Empire.

Q941606.name: 1986 FBI Miami shootout
Q941606.blurb: FBI Miami Shootout: A gun battle in broad daylight in Dade County, Florida, between two bank/armored car robbers and pursuing FBI agents. During the firefight, FBI agents Jerry L. Dove and Benjamin P. Grogan are killed, while five other agents are wounded. As a result, the popular .40 S&W cartridge was developed.

Q941612.name: American Airlines Flight 965
Q941612.blurb: American Airlines Flight 965, a Boeing 757, crashes into a mountain 50 km north of Cali, Colombia, killing 159 of the 163 people on board.

Q942257.name: Battle of Famars
Q942257.blurb: Battle of Famars during the Flanders Campaign of the War of the First Coalition.

Q942894.name: Khodynka Tragedy
Q942894.blurb: Khodynka Tragedy: A mass panic on Khodynka Field in Moscow during the festivities of the coronation of Russian Tsar Nicholas II results in the deaths of 1,389 people.

Q942901.name: Second Battle of Benghazi
Q942901.blurb: Libyan Civil War: After the failure of Muammar Gaddafi's forces to take Benghazi, the French Air Force launches Opération Harmattan, beginning foreign military intervention in Libya.

Q943044.name: 1995 Quebec referendum
Q943044.blurb: Quebec citizens narrowly vote (50.58% to 49.42%) in favour of remaining a province of Canada in their second referendum on national sovereignty.

Q943277.name: Battle of Shiloh
Q943277.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Shiloh begins: In Tennessee, forces under Union General Ulysses S. Grant meet Confederate troops led by General Albert Sidney Johnston.

Q944941.name: Irish Rebellion of 1798
aliases: Battles during the Irish Rebellion of 1798
Q944941.blurb: The Irish Rebellion of 1798 led by the United Irishmen against British rule begins.

Q945030.name: Coronation Street
aliases: Most controversial storylines of Coronation Street
Q945030.blurb: The first episode of Coronation Street, the world's longest-running television soap opera, is broadcast in the United Kingdom.

Q945396.name: Battle of Soissons
Q945396.blurb: Battle of Soissons: King Robert I of France is killed and King Charles the Simple is arrested by the supporters of Duke Rudolph of Burgundy.

Q945596.name: Battle of Golymin
Q945596.blurb: Battles of Pultusk and Golymin: Russian forces hold French forces under Napoleon.

Q945700.name: Chad–Sudan Conflict
Q945700.blurb: The Chadian Civil War begins when rebel groups, allegedly backed by neighbouring Sudan, launch an attack in Adré.

Q945970.name: 1974 FIFA World Cup Final
Q945970.blurb: West Germany won the FIFA World Cup final against the Netherlands at the Munich Olympiastadion.

Q946054.name: Burr–Hamilton duel
Q946054.blurb: A duel occurs in which the Vice President of the United States Aaron Burr mortally wounds former Secretary of the Treasury Alexander Hamilton.

Q946298.name: Battle of Montecatini
Q946298.blurb: Battle of Montecatini: The army of the Republic of Pisa, commanded by Uguccione della Faggiuola, wins a decisive victory against the joint forces of the Kingdom of Naples and the Republic of Florence despite being outnumbered.

Q947050.name: Treaty of Edinburgh
Q947050.blurb: The Treaty of Edinburgh is signed by Scotland and England.

Q947093.name: April 2009 Moldovan parliamentary election
Q947093.blurb: Mass protests began across Moldova against the results of the parliamentary election.

Q947452.name: ValuJet Flight 592
Q947452.blurb: After the aircraft's departure from Miami, a fire started by improperly handled chemical oxygen generators in the cargo hold of Atlanta-bound ValuJet Airlines Flight 592 causes the Douglas DC-9 to crash in the Florida Everglades, killing all 110 on board.

Q947605.name: First Air Flight 6560
Q947605.blurb: First Air Flight 6560 crashes 1 mile from the Resolute Bay runway, killing 12 of the 15 aboard.

Q948130.name: 2012 Romanian protests
Q948130.blurb: Violent protests occur in Bucharest, Romania, as two-day-old demonstrations continue against President Traian Băsescu's economic austerity measures. Clashes are reported in numerous Romanian cities between protesters and law enforcement officers.

Q948704.name: Marrakech Agreement
aliases: Agreement establishing the World Trade Organization
Q948704.blurb: Marrakesh Agreement relating to foundation of World Trade Organization is adopted.

Q948810.name: Battle of Schöngrabern
Q948810.blurb: Napoleonic Wars: Battle of Schöngrabern: Russian forces under Pyotr Bagration delay the pursuit by French troops under Joachim Murat.

Q949020.name: USAir Flight 1493
aliases: Los Angeles International Airport crash of 1991
Q949020.blurb: A runway collision between USAir Flight 1493 and SkyWest Flight 5569 at Los Angeles International Airport results in the deaths of 34 people, and injuries to 30 others.

Q949635.name: Battle of Kambula
Q949635.blurb: Anglo-Zulu War: Battle of Kambula: British forces defeat 20,000 Zulus.

Q949724.name: Battle of Naseby
Q949724.blurb: English Civil War: Battle of Naseby: Twelve thousand Royalist forces are beaten by fifteen thousand Parliamentarian soldiers.

Q950273.name: 1986 Mozambican Tupolev Tu-134 crash
Q950273.blurb: The president of Mozambique and a prominent leader of FRELIMO, along with 33 others, die when their aircraft crashes into the Lebombo Mountains.

Q950694.name: Happy Birthday, Mr. President
Q950694.blurb: Actress Marilyn Monroe performed a sultry rendition of "Happy Birthday to You" during a televised celebration for U.S. President John F. Kennedy.

Q951088.name: Iran Air Flight 277
Q951088.blurb: Iran Air Flight 277 crashes near Urmia in the northwest of the country, in icy conditions, killing 78 people.

Q951383.name: The Portuguese discovery of the sea route to India
Q951383.blurb: Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama discovers the sea route to India when he arrives at Kozhikode (previously known as Calicut), India.

Q952260.name: Battle of Levounion
Q952260.blurb: Battle of Levounion: The Pechenegs are defeated by Byzantine Emperor Alexios I Komnenos.

Q952516.name: 2010 San Fernando massacre
Q952516.blurb: In San Fernando, Tamaulipas, Mexico, 72 illegal immigrants are killed by Los Zetas and eventually found dead by Mexican authorities.

Q952728.name: 2017 Turkish Airlines cargo plane crash
Q952728.blurb: Turkish Airlines Flight 6491 crashes into a residential area near Manas International Airport in Kyrgyzstan, killing 39 people.

Q952774.name: Invasion of Quebec (1775)
Q952774.blurb: American Revolutionary War: The invasion of Quebec by the Continental Army begins with the Siege of Fort St. Jean.

Q952881.name: Second French intervention in Mexico
aliases: France-Mexico Arrangement relative to the Assignment of Customs Revenues
France–Mexico Arrangement relative to the Assignment of Customs Revenues
Treaty for the Settlement of French Claims in Mexico
Q952881.blurb: During the French intervention in Mexico, Mexico City is captured by French troops.

Q953063.name: Treaty of Westminster
Q953063.blurb: England and the Netherlands sign the Treaty of Westminster, ending the Third Anglo-Dutch War. A provision of the agreement transfers the Dutch colony of New Amsterdam to England.

Q953326.name: Battle of Taipale
Q953326.blurb: Winter War: The Red Army's advance on the Karelian Isthmus is stopped by Finns at the Mannerheim Line during the Battle of Taipale.

Q953414.name: Joelma fire
Q953414.blurb: A fire in the 25-story Joelma Building in São Paulo, Brazil kills 189 and injures 293.

Q953597.name: Little Round Top
Q953597.blurb: American Civil War: On the second day of the Battle of Gettysburg - the Battle of Little Round Top takes place and results in a Union victory after the Confederate troops unsuccessfully try to assault the Union left flank.

Q954152.name: 1846 conclave
Q954152.blurb: The Papal conclave of 1846 elects Pope Pius IX, beginning the longest reign in the history of the papacy.

Q954923.name: Siege of Zhongdu
Q954923.blurb: A Mongol army under Genghis Khan captured Zhongdu (modern Beijing), the capital of the Jin dynasty of China.

Q955075.name: Max Headroom broadcast signal intrusion
Q955075.blurb: The Max Headroom signal hijacking incident takes place, in which a pirate broadcast interrupts television broadcasts in Chicago.

Q955457.name: Dominican Civil War
Q955457.blurb: Civil war breaks out in the Dominican Republic when Colonel Francisco Caamaño overthrows the triumvirate that had been in power since the coup d'état against Juan Bosch.

Q956098.name: Battle of La Concepción
Q956098.blurb: War of the Pacific: Chile suffers its last military defeat in the Battle of La Concepción when a garrison of 77 men is annihilated by a 1,300-strong Peruvian force, many of them armed with spears.

Q956475.name: Greek government-debt crisis
Q956475.blurb: Mass protests in Greece erupt in response to austerity measures imposed by the government as a result of the Greek government-debt crisis.

Q957012.name: 1994 South African general election
Q957012.blurb: South African general election: The first democratic general election in South Africa, in which black citizens could vote. The Interim Constitution comes into force.This marked the end of Apartheid.

Q957155.name: Battle of Dujaila
Q957155.blurb: World War I: A British force unsuccessfully attempts to relieve the siege of Kut (present-day Iraq) in the Battle of Dujaila.

Q957317.name: Exposition Universelle of 1889
Q957317.blurb: The Eiffel Tower is officially opened to the public at the Universal Exposition in Paris.

Q957586.name: Turkish–Armenian War
Q957586.blurb: Following more than a month of Turkish–Armenian War, the Turkish-dictated Treaty of Alexandropol is concluded.

Q957806.name: Genuuva Accords
Q957806.blurb: In a United Nations ceremony in Geneva, Switzerland, the Soviet Union signs an agreement pledging to withdraw its troops from Afghanistan.

Q960449.name: Siege of Krujë
Q960449.blurb: Albanian commander Skanderbeg entered Krujë, breaking a 10-month siege by Ottoman forces.

Q960723.name: Battle of White Plains
Q960723.blurb: American Revolutionary War: British troops under General William Howe attack General George Washington's Continental Army and capture Chatterton Hill in the Battle of White Plains during the New York and New Jersey campaign.

Q960894.name: 1923 Bulgarian coup d'état
Q960894.blurb: Bulgaria's military takes over the government in a coup.

Q961243.name: Battle of Dun Nechtain
Q961243.blurb: The Battle of Dun Nechtain is fought between a Pictish army under King Bridei III and the invading Northumbrians under King Ecgfrith, who are decisively defeated.

Q961430.name: Ottoman–Venetian War of 1570–1573
Q961430.blurb: A peace treaty brought the Ottoman–Venetian War to an end, ceding Cyprus from the Republic of Venice to the Ottoman Empire.

Q962370.name: Battle of Hanoi
aliases: Hanoi during 60 Days and Nights of Blood and Flowers
Q962370.blurb: First Indochina War: The French gain complete control of Hanoi after forcing the Viet Minh to withdraw to the mountains.

Q962450.name: St. Clair's Defeat
Q962450.blurb: Northwest Indian War: The Western Confederacy of American Indians wins a major victory over the United States in the Battle of the Wabash.

Q962966.name: BOAC Flight 781
Q962966.blurb: BOAC Flight 781, a de Havilland DH.106 Comet 1, explodes and falls into the Tyrrhenian Sea, killing 35 people.

Q963303.name: Union of Lublin
Q963303.blurb: Union of Lublin: The Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania confirm a real union; the united country is called the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth or the Republic of Both Nations.

Q963444.name: Battle of Cut Knife
Q963444.blurb: Cree and Assiniboine warriors win the Battle of Cut Knife, their largest victory over Canadian forces during the North-West Rebellion.

Q964226.name: Battle of Pelekanon
Q964226.blurb: The Battle of Pelekanon is the last attempt of the Byzantine Empire to retain its cities in Asia Minor.

Q964619.name: Seventeenth Council of Toledo
Q964619.blurb: At the Seventeenth Council of Toledo, Egica, a king of the Visigoths of Hispania, accuses Jews of aiding Muslims, sentencing all Jews to slavery.

Q965136.name: Shuttle Radar Topography Mission
Q965136.blurb: Space Shuttle Endeavour is launched on STS-99 to conduct the Shuttle Radar Topography Mission.

Q965291.name: One million voices against FARC
Q965291.blurb: Civic mobilizations in Colombia against FARC, under the name A million voices against the FARC.

Q965477.name: Grossaktion Warsaw
Q965477.blurb: Grossaktion Warsaw: The systematic deportation of Jews from the Warsaw ghetto begins.

Q966312.name: Battle of Anchialus
Q966312.blurb: The Byzantine army of emperor Constantine V defeats the Bulgarian forces in the Battle of Anchialus.

Q966386.name: Battle of Vézeronce
Q966386.blurb: The Franks are defeated by the Burgundians in the Battle of Vézeronce.

Q967331.name: Quemados case
Q967331.blurb: Rodrigo Rojas and Carmen Gloria Quintana are burnt alive during a street demonstration against the dictatorship of General Augusto Pinochet in Chile in the Quemados case.

Q967844.name: 1999 Russian apartment bombings
aliases: Allegations of FSB involvement in the Russian apartment bombings
Conspiracy theories of Russian apartment bombings
Conspiracy theories of the Russian apartment bombings
Explanation attempts for the Russian apartment bombings
Theories of the Russian apartment bombings
Theory of FSB involvement in the Russian apartment bombings
Q967844.blurb: The first of a series of bombings in Moscow kills one person and wounds 40 others.

Q967981.name: 1980 Surinamese coup d'état
Q967981.blurb: The government of Suriname is overthrown by a military coup led by Dési Bouterse.

Q968126.name: Crossing the Andes
Q968126.blurb: Crossing of the Andes: Many soldiers of Juan Gregorio de las Heras are captured during the action of Picheuta.

Q971176.name: French Constitution of 1791
Q971176.blurb: King Louis XVI accepts the new French constitution.

Q971248.name: Battle of Marj Dabiq
Q971248.blurb: The Ottoman Empire under Selim I defeats the Mamluk Sultanate and captures present-day Syria at the Battle of Marj Dabiq.

Q971507.name: Battle of Zela
Q971507.blurb: Julius Caesar defeats Pharnaces II of Pontus in the battle of Zela.

Q973118.name: coronation of Napoleon I
Q973118.blurb: At Notre Dame Cathedral in Paris, Napoleon Bonaparte crowns himself Emperor of the French.

Q973919.name: Terra Nova Expedition
Q973919.blurb: Eight months after perishing during the ill-fated Terra Nova Expedition, the bodies of Robert Falcon Scott (pictured) and his companions were discovered on the Ross Ice Shelf in Antarctica.

Q973979.name: 1997 Qayen earthquake
Q973979.blurb: An earthquake registering 7.3 Mw struck near Qaen, Iran, killing at least 1,567 and leaving around 50,000 others homeless.

Q974160.name: Cudgel War
Q974160.blurb: The last battle of the Cudgel War takes place on the Santavuori Hill in Ilmajoki, Ostrobothnia.

Q974166.name: Battle of Montenotte
Q974166.blurb: War of the First Coalition: Napoleon Bonaparte wins his first victory as an army commander at the Battle of Montenotte, splitting the Austrian and Piedmontese armies away from each other, and marking the beginning of the Piedmontese surrender in the war.

Q975050.name: Ixtoc I oil spill
Q975050.blurb: A blowout at the Ixtoc I oil well in the southern Gulf of Mexico causes at least 3,000,000 barrels (480,000 m3) of oil to be spilled into the waters, the second-worst accidental oil spill ever recorded.

Q975058.name: Gerboise bleue
Q975058.blurb: With the success of a nuclear test codenamed "Gerboise Bleue", France becomes the fourth country to possess nuclear weapons.

Q975430.name: Tajbeg Palace assault
Q975430.blurb: Soviet–Afghan War: Soviet troops stormed Tajbeg Palace outside Kabul and killed Afghan president Hafizullah Amin and his 100–150 elite guards.

Q975593.name: British Antarctic Expedition (1907–1909)
Q975593.blurb: British explorer Aeneas Mackintosh, a member of the Nimrod Expedition, escaped death by fleeing across ice floes.

Q976655.name: Battle of Montereau
Q976655.blurb: Napoleonic Wars: The Battle of Montereau.

Q976820.name: Battle of Newburn
Q976820.blurb: Second Bishop's War: King Charles I's English army loses to a Scottish Covenanter force at the Battle of Newburn.

Q976887.name: 1954 Guatemalan coup d'état
Q976887.blurb: Carlos Castillo Armas leads an invasion force across the Guatemalan border, setting in motion the 1954 Guatemalan coup d'état.

Q977496.name: Hurricane Ismael
Q977496.blurb: Hurricane Ismael formed off the southwest coast of Mexico; it went on to kill over a hundred people in the country.

Q977657.name: Nyon Conference
Q977657.blurb: Nine nations attend the Nyon Conference to address international piracy in the Mediterranean Sea.

Q977868.name: Church of the Company Fire
Q977868.blurb: Between two and three thousand churchgoers die in the Church of the Company Fire, possibly the largest single building fire by number of victims in modern history.

Q978823.name: Battle of Civetot
Q978823.blurb: First Crusade: At the Battle of Civetot, the Seljuk forces of Kilij Arslan destroyed the army of the People's Crusade as it marched toward Nicaea.

Q979607.name: Deep Blue versus Kasparov, 1996, Game 1
Q979607.blurb: Deep Blue defeated Garry Kasparov in a game of chess, the first ever game won by a chess-playing computer against a World Chess Champion under chess tournament conditions.

Q979633.name: Sack of Rome
Q979633.blurb: Pope Leo IV was consecrated without imperial consent following the Saracen sack of Rome.

Q979845.name: Naxalite–Maoist insurgency
Q979845.blurb: Naxalite–Maoist insurgency: Insurgents from the Communist Party of India (Maoist) ambushed a Central Reserve Police Force convoy in Dantewada district, India, killing 76 officers.

Q980853.name: Battle of Gela
Q980853.blurb: World War II: Allied invasion of Sicily: German and Italian troops launch a counter-attack on Allied forces in Sicily.

Q981031.name: First Siege of Gibraltar
Q981031.blurb: The First siege of Gibraltar takes place in the context of the Spanish Reconquista pitting the forces of the Kingdom of Castile against the Emirate of Granada resulting in a Castilian victory.

Q981327.name: Haditha massacre
Q981327.blurb: Iraq War: A group of United States Marines massacred 25 people in the town of Haditha.

Q981711.name: 2012 Brindisi school bombing
Q981711.blurb: Three gas cylinder bombs explode in front of a vocational school in the Italian city of Brindisi, killing one person and injuring five others.

Q984109.name: Centennial Exposition
aliases: International Exhibition of Arts, Manufactures and Products of the Soil and Mine
Q984109.blurb: The Centennial Exposition is opened in Philadelphia.

Q985684.name: Jonestown
Q985684.blurb: In Jonestown, Guyana, Jim Jones leads his Peoples Temple to a mass murder–suicide that claimed 918 lives in all, 909 of them in Jonestown itself, including over 270 children.

Q987349.name: Battle of Jinyang
Q987349.blurb: Spring and Autumn period: The house of Zhao defeats the house of Zhi, ending the Battle of Jinyang, a military conflict between the elite families of the State of Jin.

Q989092.name: First Anglo-Afghan War
aliases: Causes of the First Anglo-Afghan War
Q989092.blurb: First Anglo-Afghan War: William Brydon, an assistant surgeon in the British Army, was the sole European of the 14,000 people retreating from Kabul to Jalalabad who evaded capture or death.

Q989115.name: First Italo-Ethiopian War
Q989115.blurb: First Italo-Ethiopian War: The war's opening battle, the Battle of Coatit, occurs; it is an Italian victory.

Q990715.name: Battle of Lake Erie
Q990715.blurb: The United States defeats a British Fleet at the Battle of Lake Erie during the War of 1812.

Q994316.name: Battle of Maysalun
Q994316.blurb: Franco-Syrian War: At the Battle of Maysalun, forces of the Arab Kingdom of Syria were defeated by a French army moving to occupy the territory allocated to them by the San Remo conference.

Q994581.name: Japan Air Lines Flight 350
Q994581.blurb: Japan Air Lines Flight 350 crashes near Haneda Airport in an attempted pilot mass murder-suicide, killing 24 of the 174 people on board.

Q995553.name: Yellowstone fires of 1988
Q995553.blurb: "Black Saturday" of the Yellowstone fire in Yellowstone National Park

Q999143.name: 1949 Armistice Agreements
Q999143.blurb: The Armistice Agreements are signed, to formally end the hostilities of the 1948 Arab-Israeli War.

Q1000158.name: Panic of 1857
Q1000158.blurb: The Panic of 1857 begins, setting off one of the most severe economic crises in United States history.

Q1000658.name: Budapest Memorandum
aliases: Memorandum on Security Assurances in connection with Ukraine's accession to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons
The Budapest Memorandum on Security Assurances
Q1000658.blurb: The Budapest Memorandum is signed at the OSCE conference in Budapest, Hungary.

Q1001093.name: Battle of Turckheim
Q1001093.blurb: Battle of Colmar: The French army defeats forces from Austria and Brandenburg.

Q1001479.name: Battle of Cape Finisterre
Q1001479.blurb: Napoleonic Wars: War of the Third Coalition: Battle of Cape Finisterre: An inconclusive naval action is fought between a combined French and Spanish fleet under Admiral Pierre-Charles Villeneuve of France and a British fleet under Admiral Robert Calder.

Q1003174.name: Battle of Forum Gallorum
Q1003174.blurb: War of Mutina: Despite initial success, troops loyal to Mark Antony were defeated near the Via Aemilia in northern Italy by legions loyal to the Roman Senate.

Q1003780.name: Freedom of Information Act
aliases: Freedom of Information Act of the United States
Q1003780.blurb: In response to a Freedom of Information Act request, the CIA acknowledged the existence of Area 51 (diagram pictured), a secretive U.S. Air Force facility in Nevada and a subject of various UFO, and other, conspiracy theories.

Q1003866.name: arrest and assassination of Ngo Dinh Diem
Q1003866.blurb: South Vietnamese President Ngô Đình Diệm is assassinated following a military coup.

Q1006312.name: Hungarian Declaration of Independence
Q1006312.blurb: Hungary declares itself independent of Austria with Lajos Kossuth as its leader.

Q1012788.name: Bristow Flight 56C
Q1012788.blurb: After being struck by lightning the crew of Bristow Helicopters Flight 56C are forced to ditch. All 18 aboard are later rescued.

Q1012810.name: Steve Bartman incident
Q1012810.blurb: The Steve Bartman Incident takes place at Wrigley Field in Chicago, Illinois.

Q1014253.name: Mongol conquest of the Jin dynasty
Q1014253.blurb: Mongol–Jin War: The Mongols begin their siege on Kaifeng, the capital of the Jin dynasty.

Q1014658.name: Andersen Air Force Base B-2 accident
Q1014658.blurb: A B-2 Spirit stealth bomber crashed on the runway shortly after takeoff from Andersen Air Force Base in Guam in the most expensive crash in U.S. Air Force history.

Q1016749.name: Burnden Park
Q1016749.blurb: Thirty-three people were killed in a human crush at Burnden Park, a football stadium in Bolton, England.

Q1017321.name: Black Thursday
Q1017321.blurb: The largest Australian bushfires in a populous region in recorded history take place in the state of Victoria.

Q1017322.name: 2003 Canberra bushfires
Q1017322.blurb: A bushfire kills four people and destroys more than 500 homes in Canberra, Australia.

Q1017328.name: Black Friday
Q1017328.blurb: The Black Friday bushfires burn 20,000 square kilometres (7,700 sq mi) of land in Australia, claiming the lives of 71 people.

Q1017340.name: Ash Wednesday bushfires
Q1017340.blurb: The Ash Wednesday bushfires in Victoria and South Australia kill 75.

Q1017811.name: Konginkangas bus disaster
Q1017811.blurb: The Konginkangas bus disaster kills 23 and injures 14 people in Äänekoski, Finland.

Q1018682.name: Nisour Square massacre
Q1018682.blurb: Security guards working for Blackwater Worldwide shoot and kill 17 Iraqis in Nisour Square, Baghdad.

Q1018743.name: Ludlow Massacre
Q1018743.blurb: Nineteen men, women, and children participating in a strike are killed in the Ludlow Massacre during the Colorado Coalfield War.

Q1021160.name: Armagnac–Burgundian Civil War
Q1021160.blurb: Armagnac–Burgundian Civil War: Parisians slaughter sympathizers of Bernard VII, Count of Armagnac, along with all prisoners, foreign bankers, and students and faculty of the College of Navarre.

Q1021172.name: Republic of the Congo civil war
Q1021172.blurb: The Second Republic of the Congo Civil War begins.

Q1023993.name: COMDEX
Q1023993.blurb: The first smartphone, the IBM Simon, is introduced at COMDEX in Las Vegas, Nevada.

Q1025404.name: assassination of Abraham Lincoln
aliases: Assasination of U. S. President Abraham Lincoln
Assasination of U. S. Prwsident Abraham Lincoln
Now he belongs to the ages
Now he belongs to the angels
Q1025404.blurb: U.S. President Abraham Lincoln is shot in Ford's Theatre by John Wilkes Booth; Lincoln dies the following day.

Q1025466.name: assassination of Julius Caesar
Q1025466.blurb: The assassination of Julius Caesar, the dictator of the Roman Republic, by a group of senators takes place on the Ides of March.

Q1028014.name: Grayrigg derailment
Q1028014.blurb: A train derails on an evening express service near Grayrigg, Cumbria, England, killing one person and injuring 88. This results in hundreds of points being checked over the UK after a few similar accidents.

Q1028247.name: Battle of Groix
Q1028247.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: In what became known as Cornwallis's Retreat, a British Royal Navy squadron led by Vice Admiral William Cornwallis strongly resists a much larger French Navy force and withdraws largely intact, setting up the French Navy defeat at the Battle of Groix six days later.

Q1028296.name: Battle of Grozny
Q1028296.blurb: The First Chechen War: The Russian Ground Forces begin a New Year's storming of Grozny.

Q1029367.name: Pure Food and Drug Act
aliases: Pure Food and Drug Act of 1906
Q1029367.blurb: The United States Congress passes the Meat Inspection Act and Pure Food and Drug Act.

Q1029489.name: candle demonstration
Q1029489.blurb: The Candle demonstration in Bratislava is the first mass demonstration of the 1980s against the communist regime in Czechoslovakia.

Q1030061.name: Field of the Cloth of Gold
Q1030061.blurb: The Field of the Cloth of Gold, a summit meeting between Henry VIII of England and Francis I of France, ends.

Q1030084.name: Sakai incident
Q1030084.blurb: Sakai incident: Japanese samurai kill 11 French sailors in the port of Sakai, Osaka.

Q1031430.name: Habsburg Netherlands
Q1031430.blurb: Two hundred Dutch noblemen, led by Hendrick van Brederode, force themselves into the presence of Margaret of Parma and present the Petition of Compromise, denouncing the Spanish Inquisition in the Seventeen Provinces.

Q1031465.name: Anglo-Persian capture of Hormuz
Q1031465.blurb: Anglo-Persian forces combined to capture the Portuguese garrison at Hormuz Island in the Persian Gulf.

Q1031706.name: Discovery Expedition (1901-1904)
Q1031706.blurb: The Discovery Expedition under Robert Falcon Scott attains a Farthest South at 82°17′S in Antarctica.

Q1032059.name: Canadian Caper
Q1032059.blurb: Six American diplomats who had evaded capture in the Iran hostage crisis escaped with the help of Canadian government officials to Zürich, Switzerland.

Q1033330.name: same-sex marriage in the United Kingdom
Q1033330.blurb: The first same-sex marriages in England and Wales are performed.

Q1033970.name: 1972 Black Hills flood
Q1033970.blurb: Severe rainfall causes a dam in the Black Hills of South Dakota to burst, creating a flood that kills 238 people and causes $160 million in damage.

Q1034162.name: Raid on Málaga
Q1034162.blurb: The Raid on Málaga takes place during the Anglo-Spanish War.

Q1035922.name: Kassa attack
Q1035922.blurb: World War II: Soviet planes bomb Kassa, Hungary (now Košice, Slovakia), giving Hungary the impetus to declare war the next day.

Q1036636.name: Battle of Hwangsanbeol
Q1036636.blurb: Silla forces under general Kim Yu-sin defeat the army of Baekje at the Battle of Hwangsanbeol.

Q1036702.name: Reykjavík Summit
Q1036702.blurb: Ronald Reagan and Mikhail Gorbachev meet in Iceland to continue discussions about scaling back IRBM arsenals in Europe.

Q1037676.name: Black May
Q1037676.blurb: Three days of popular protests against the government of Prime Minister of Thailand Suchinda Kraprayoon begin in Bangkok, leading to a military crackdown that results in 52 officially confirmed deaths, hundreds of injuries, many disappearances, and more than 3,500 arrests.

Q1037873.name: 2009 Lahore police academy attacks
Q1037873.blurb: Twelve gunmen attack the Manawan Police Academy in Lahore, Pakistan.

Q1037884.name: Turkish Airlines flight 634
Q1037884.blurb: Turkish Airlines Flight 634 crashes near Diyarbakır Airport, Turkey, killing the entire crew and 70 of the 75 passengers.

Q1038788.name: Hyatt Regency walkway collapse
Q1038788.blurb: A structural failure leads to the collapse of a walkway at the Hyatt Regency in Kansas City, Missouri, killing 114 people and injuring more than 200.

Q1038900.name: Guangzhou Uprising
Q1038900.blurb: Guangzhou Uprising: Communist Red Guards launch an uprising in Guangzhou, China, taking over most of the city and announcing the formation of a Guangzhou Soviet.

Q1041111.name: Truce of Ratisbon
Q1041111.blurb: Emperor Leopold I and French king Louis XIV agree to an armistice in the truce of Ratisbon.

Q1041813.name: Manchu Restoration
Q1041813.blurb: Chinese General Zhang Xun seizes control of Beijing and restores the monarchy, installing Puyi, last emperor of the Qing dynasty, to the throne. The restoration is reversed just shy of two weeks later, when Republican troops regain control of the capital.

Q1042914.name: Ganlu incident
Q1042914.blurb: Sweet Dew Incident: Emperor Wenzong of the Tang dynasty conspires to kill the powerful eunuchs of the Tang court, but the plot is foiled.

Q1044092.name: Asama-Sansō incident
Q1044092.blurb: Japanese police stormed a mountain lodge near Karuizawa, Nagano Prefecture, to end a ten-day siege by members of the paramilitary group United Red Army.

Q1044829.name: Polish–Muscovite War
Q1044829.blurb: The Battle of Klushino is fought between forces of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth and Russia during the Polish–Russian War, after which Polish troops entered Moscow.

Q1045029.name: Tsurumi rail accident
Q1045029.blurb: The Tsurumi rail accident on the Tōkaidō Main Line in Yokohama kills 162 people.

Q1047091.name: Battle of Rạch Gầm-Xoài Mút
Q1047091.blurb: Invading Siamese forces attempt to exploit the political chaos in Vietnam, but are ambushed and annihilated at the Mekong river by the Tây Sơn in the Battle of Rạch Gầm-Xoài Mút.

Q1047607.name: Spanish colonization of the Americas
aliases: Spain in the Age of Discovery
Spanish colonization of the New World
Q1047607.blurb: Tegucigalpa, capital city of Honduras, is claimed by the Spaniards.

Q1048129.name: 2008 Chinese milk scandal
Q1048129.blurb: A tainted milk powder scandal broke in China which ultimately involved an estimated 300,000 victims, the vast majority infants, with 54,000 hospitalized with kidney problems and six deaths.

Q1048169.name: Treaty of Berlin of 1878
Q1048169.blurb: Treaty of Berlin: The European powers redraw the map of the Balkans. Serbia, Montenegro and Romania become completely independent of the Ottoman Empire.

Q1048401.name: Battle of Versinikia
Q1048401.blurb: Battle of Versinikia: The Bulgars led by Krum defeat the Byzantine army near Edirne. Emperor Michael I is forced to abdicate in favor of Leo V the Armenian.

Q1048750.name: 1976 Argentine coup d'état
Q1048750.blurb: The Frente de Liberación Homosexual made their final public appearance, shortly before the group's dissolution due to political repression after the Argentine coup d'état.

Q1049092.name: October 2010 Sumatra earthquake and tsunami
Q1049092.blurb: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake strikes off Indonesia's Mentawai Islands, triggering a tsunami that kills at least 400 people.

Q1049343.name: Quartering Acts
Q1049343.blurb: Great Britain passes the Quartering Act, which requires the Thirteen Colonies to house British troops.

Q1049395.name: Treaty of New Echota
Q1049395.blurb: The Treaty of New Echota is signed, ceding all the lands of the Cherokee east of the Mississippi River to the United States.

Q1049530.name: Battle of Karuse
Q1049530.blurb: Livonian Crusade: In the Battle of Karuse, the Grand Duchy of Lithuania achieved a decisive victory over the Livonian Order on the frozen surface of the Baltic Sea.

Q1049630.name: Super Bowl XXXVIII
Q1049630.blurb: During the halftime show of Super Bowl XXXVIII, Janet Jackson's breast was exposed by Justin Timberlake in what was later referred to as a "wardrobe malfunction", resulting in an immediate crackdown and widespread debate on perceived indecency in U.S. broadcasting.

Q1049697.name: Battle of Płowce
Q1049697.blurb: The Battle of Płowce is fought, between the Kingdom of Poland and the Teutonic Order. The Poles are defeated but their leaders escape capture.

Q1049741.name: Beijing Coup
Q1049741.blurb: Second Zhili–Fengtian War: Warlord Feng Yuxiang, with the covert support of the Empire of Japan, stages a coup in Beijing against his erstwhile superiors in the Zhili clique, crippling their nearly victorious war effort against the Fengtian clique and forcing them to withdraw from northern China.

Q1049838.name: 1944 Tōnankai earthquake
Q1049838.blurb: An earthquake along the coast of Wakayama Prefecture in Japan causes a tsunami which kills 1,223 people.

Q1049945.name: Jacobite rising of 1745
Q1049945.blurb: Second Jacobite rising: Bonnie Prince Charlie occupies Stirling.

Q1050199.name: Collision in Korea
Q1050199.blurb: Before a crowd of about 165,000 at the Rungrado 1st of May Stadium, Ric Flair and Antonio Inoki competed in the main event of Collision in Korea, the highest attended professional wrestling event of all time.

Q1050309.name: Hurricane Andrew
aliases: Effects of Hurricane Andrew in The Bahamas
Q1050309.blurb: Hurricane Andrew makes landfall in Homestead, Florida as a Category 5 hurricane, causing up to $25 billion (1992 USD) in damages.

Q1050350.name: Teatro dell'Opera di Roma
Q1050350.blurb: The opera Cavalleria rusticana by Pietro Mascagni, premieres at the Teatro Costanzi in Rome, beginning the verismo period in Italian opera.

Q1050999.name: Turkish invasion of Cyprus
Q1050999.blurb: Turkish invasion of Cyprus: Forces from Turkey invade Cyprus after a coup d'état, organized by the dictator of Greece, against president Makarios.

Q1051320.name: Garley Building fire
Q1051320.blurb: A fire breaks out in an office building in Hong Kong, killing 41 people and injuring 81.

Q1051734.name: Open Door Policy
Q1051734.blurb: American statesman and diplomat John Hay announces the Open Door Policy to promote trade with China.

Q1052060.name: Cayuse War
Q1052060.blurb: Missionaries Dr. Marcus Whitman, his wife Narcissa, and 15 others are killed by Cayuse and Umatilla Indians, causing the Cayuse War.

Q1052120.name: East African Campaign
aliases: Italian East Africa in World War II
The Italian Invasion of British Somaliland
Q1052120.blurb: World War II: British troops launch a general counter-offensive against Italian East Africa.

Q1052332.name: Somali Civil War
Q1052332.blurb: War in Somalia: Somali National Army forces and their AMISOM and Raskamboni allies launched an offensive against Al-Shabaab in the latter's last major stronghold of Kismayo.

Q1052651.name: Battle of Madagascar
Q1052651.blurb: World War II: The British Army carries out an amphibious landing on Madagascar to re-launch Allied offensive operations in the Madagascar Campaign.

Q1052780.name: Sherman's March to the Sea
Q1052780.blurb: American Civil War: Sherman's March to the Sea: Union cavalry forces defeat Confederate cavalry in the Battle of Waynesboro, Georgia, opening the way for General William T. Sherman's army to approach the coast.

Q1053476.name: 1989 Loma Prieta earthquake
Q1053476.blurb: The Eastern span replacement of the San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge opens at 10:15 pm at a cost of $6.4 billion, after the 1989 Loma Prieta earthquake damaged the old span.

Q1054478.name: Century 21 Exposition
Q1054478.blurb: The Seattle World's Fair (Century 21 Exposition) opens. It is the first World's Fair in the United States since World War II.

Q1054868.name: Battle of Hondschoote
Q1054868.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: Battle of Hondschoote.

Q1054975.name: Battle of Preveza
Q1054975.blurb: Ottoman–Venetian War: The Ottoman Navy scores a decisive victory over a Holy League fleet in the Battle of Preveza.

Q1055742.name: Azawadi declaration of independence
Q1055742.blurb: Azawad declares itself independent from the Republic of Mali.

Q1056439.name: Treaty of Tartu
Q1056439.blurb: The Tartu Peace Treaty is signed between Estonia and Russia.

Q1056771.name: Patent Cooperation Treaty
aliases: Chapter II of the Patent Cooperation Treaty
International Searching and Preliminary Examining Authorities
PCT international preliminary reports on patentability
Written opinion of the International Searching Authority
Q1056771.blurb: The first international applications under the Patent Cooperation Treaty are filed.

Q1057839.name: Matsumoto sarin attack
Q1057839.blurb: Members of the Aum Shinrikyo cult release sarin gas in Matsumoto, Japan. Seven people are killed, 660 injured.

Q1058248.name: Judgment of Paris
Q1058248.blurb: The Judgment of Paris takes place in France, launching California as a worldwide force in the production of quality wine.

Q1059024.name: Balvano train disaster
Q1059024.blurb: A freight train carrying stowaway passengers stalls in a tunnel shortly after departing from Balvano, Basilicata, Italy just after midnight, with 517 dying from carbon monoxide poisoning.

Q1059090.name: 2010 Thai political protests
Q1059090.blurb: The Royal Thai Armed Forces concludes its crackdown on protests by forcing the surrender of United Front for Democracy Against Dictatorship leaders.

Q1059215.name: dissolution of Czechoslovakia
Q1059215.blurb: Dissolution of Czechoslovakia: Czechoslovakia is divided into the Czech Republic and Slovak Republic.

Q1059245.name: Cathay Pacific Flight 700Z bombing
Q1059245.blurb: Cathay Pacific Flight 700Z is destroyed by a bomb over Pleiku, Vietnam (then South Vietnam) and kills 81 people.

Q1059463.name: Rock Springs massacre
Q1059463.blurb: Rock Springs massacre: In Rock Springs, Wyoming, 150 white miners, who are struggling to unionize so they could strike for better wages and work conditions, attack their Chinese fellow workers, killing 28, wounding 15 and forcing several hundred more out of town.

Q1059658.name: German invasion of Hungary
Q1059658.blurb: World War II: The German army occupies Hungary.

Q1059732.name: Battle of Wattignies
Q1059732.blurb: War of the First Coalition: French victory at the Battle of Wattignies forces Austria to raise the siege of Maubeuge.

Q1060156.name: Typhoon Vera
Q1060156.blurb: Typhoon Vera, the strongest typhoon to hit Japan in recorded history, makes landfall, killing 4,580 people and leaving nearly 1.6 million others homeless.

Q1060780.name: Chambre introuvable
Q1060780.blurb: Louis XVIII of France has to dissolve the Chambre introuvable ("Unobtainable Chamber").

Q1061008.name: December 2009 lunar eclipse
Q1061008.blurb: Both a blue moon and a lunar eclipse occur.

Q1061090.name: Battle of Philippi
Q1061090.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Philippi (also called the Philippi Races): Union forces rout Confederate troops in Barbour County, Virginia, now West Virginia.

Q1061228.name: Battle of Puebla
Q1061228.blurb: Cinco de Mayo: Troops led by Ignacio Zaragoza halt a French invasion in the Battle of Puebla in Mexico.

Q1061891.name: Selma to Montgomery marches
Q1061891.blurb: Bloody Sunday: A group of 600 civil rights marchers are brutally attacked by state and local police in Selma, Alabama.

Q1062375.name: 2010 Lakki Marwat suicide bombing
Q1062375.blurb: A suicide car bomber detonates at a volleyball tournament in Lakki Marwat, Pakistan, killing 105 and injuring 100 more.

Q1062468.name: Soviet–Japanese Joint Declaration of 1956
Q1062468.blurb: The Soviet Union and Japan sign a Joint Declaration, officially ending the state of war between the two countries that had existed since August 1945.

Q1062615.name: Battle of Auray
Q1062615.blurb: During the Hundred Years' War, Anglo-Breton forces defeat the Franco-Breton army in Brittany, ending the War of the Breton Succession.

Q1062771.name: Isshi Incident
Q1062771.blurb: Isshi Incident: Prince Naka-no-Ōe and Fujiwara no Kamatari assassinate Soga no Iruka during a coup d'état at the imperial palace.

Q1062923.name: Whitechapel murders
Q1062923.blurb: Frances Coles was killed in the last of eleven unsolved murders of women that took place in or near the impoverished Whitechapel district in the East End of London.

Q1063735.name: Second Battle of the Somme
Q1063735.blurb: World War I: The Second Battle of the Somme begins.

Q1064335.name: Pig War
Q1064335.blurb: Ambiguity in the Oregon Treaty leads to the "Northwestern Boundary Dispute" between American and British/Canadian settlers.

Q1064550.name: PIA Flight 268
Q1064550.blurb: A Pakistan International Airlines flight crashes into a hill in Nepal, killing all 167 passengers and crew.

Q1064952.name: Ashura protests
Q1064952.blurb: Pro-government counter-demonstrators held rallies (pictured) in several Iranian cities in response to recent anti-government protests on the holy day of Ashura.

Q1065912.name: 1966 FIFA World Cup Final
Q1065912.blurb: In London, the England national football team won the FIFA World Cup, winning the final against West Germany 4–2 after extra time.

Q1066174.name: 2012 East Azerbaijan earthquakes
Q1066174.blurb: At least 306 people are killed and 3,000 others injured in a pair of earthquakes near Tabriz, Iran.

Q1066253.name: Siege of Vicksburg
aliases: Consequences of the Battle of Vicksburg
Q1066253.blurb: American Civil War: Siege of Vicksburg: The Confederate army in Vicksburg, Mississippi surrenders to Union forces under Ulysses S. Grant after 47 days of siege, contributing to the Union capture of the Mississippi River.

Q1066650.name: Battle of Los Angeles
Q1066650.blurb: The Battle of Los Angeles: A false alarm leads to an anti-aircraft barrage that lasts into the early hours of February 25.

Q1067545.name: Achille Lauro hijacking
Q1067545.blurb: Four men from the Palestine Liberation Front hijack the MS Achille Lauro off the coast of Egypt.

Q1069698.name: Major League Baseball All-Star Game
Q1069698.blurb: The first Major League Baseball All-Star Game is played in Chicago's Comiskey Park. The American League defeated the National League 4–2.

Q1069736.name: Croat–Bosniak War
aliases: Conflict between Croatia and Bosnian and Herzegovina
Q1069736.blurb: Stari Most, the "old bridge" in the Bosnian city of Mostar, built in 1566, collapses after several days of bombing by Croat forces during the Croat–Bosniak War.

Q1069936.name: Battle of Rivoli
Q1069936.blurb: The Battle of Rivoli is fought with a decisive French victory by Napoleon Bonaparte, marking the beginning of the end of the War of the First Coalition and the start of French hegemony over Italy for two decades.

Q1070119.name: 1925 serum run to Nome
Q1070119.blurb: Serum run to Nome: Dog sleds reach Nome, Alaska with diphtheria serum, inspiring the Iditarod race.

Q1070337.name: Cherokee Phoenix
Q1070337.blurb: Initial issue of the Cherokee Phoenix is the first periodical to use the Cherokee syllabary invented by Sequoyah.

Q1070761.name: LNER Class A4 4468 “Mallard”
Q1070761.blurb: World speed record for a steam locomotive is set in England, by the Mallard, which reaches a speed of 125.88 miles per hour (202.58 km/h).

Q1071992.name: Chicago Seven
Q1071992.blurb: The Chicago Seven are found not guilty of conspiring to incite riots at the 1968 Democratic National Convention.

Q1072042.name: War in Somalia
Q1072042.blurb: War in Somalia: The militaries of Somalia's Transitional Federal Government and Ethiopian troops capture Mogadishu unopposed.

Q1072330.name: Treaty of Saint Clair-sur-Epte
Q1072330.blurb: Signing of the Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte between Charles the Simple and Rollo of Normandy.

Q1072592.name: Battle of Spion Kop
Q1072592.blurb: Second Boer War: The Battle of Spion Kop between the forces of the South African Republic and the Orange Free State and British forces ends in a British defeat.

Q1072889.name: Chilean War of Independence
Q1072889.blurb: Chilean War of Independence: Chilean forces captured the city of Valdivia.

Q1073177.name: China Airlines Flight 642
Q1073177.blurb: China Airlines Flight 642 crashes at Hong Kong International Airport, killing three people and injuring 208 more.

Q1073358.name: Battle of Vaslui
Q1073358.blurb: Stephen III of Moldavia defeats the Ottoman Empire at the Battle of Vaslui.

Q1073476.name: Northern Expedition
Q1073476.blurb: Second Northern Expedition: The National Revolutionary Army captures Beijing, whose name is changed to Beiping ("Northern Peace").

Q1073488.name: 2009 Honduran coup d'état
Q1073488.blurb: Honduran president Manuel Zelaya is ousted by a local military coup following a failed request to hold a referendum to rewrite the Honduran Constitution. This was the start of the 2009 Honduran constitutional crisis.

Q1073849.name: Battle of Maipú
Q1073849.blurb: In the Battle of Maipú, Chile's independence movement, led by Bernardo O'Higgins and José de San Martín, win a decisive victory over Spain, leaving 2,000 Spaniards and 1,000 Chilean patriots dead.

Q1074596.name: Our Lady of La Salette
Q1074596.blurb: Two French shepherd children, Mélanie Calvat and Maximin Giraud, experience a Marian apparition on a mountaintop near La Salette, France, now known as Our Lady of La Salette.

Q1074621.name: Whitewater controversy
Q1074621.blurb: Whitewater controversy: President Bill Clinton gives a 41⁄2 hour videotaped testimony for the defense.

Q1076246.name: Battle of Posada
Q1076246.blurb: At the Battle of Posada, Basarab I of Wallachia defeats the Hungarian army of Charles I Robert.

Q1076469.name: Peace of Riga
Q1076469.blurb: The second Peace of Riga is signed between Poland and the Soviet Union.

Q1078359.name: Battle of Yamen
Q1078359.blurb: A Mongol victory at the Battle of Yamen ends the Song dynasty in China.

Q1080711.name: Ottoman–Hungarian Wars
Q1080711.blurb: Hungarian–Ottoman Wars: Wallachian forces led by Vlad Dracula attacked an Ottoman camp at night in an unsuccessful attempt to assassinate Sultan Mehmed II.

Q1081278.name: Battle of Alcatraz
Q1081278.blurb: In San Francisco Bay, U.S. Marines from the nearby Treasure Island Naval Base stop a two-day riot at Alcatraz Federal Penitentiary.  Five people are killed in the riot.

Q1081409.name: 2009 Nevsky Express bombing
Q1081409.blurb: Nevsky Express bombing: A bomb explodes on the Nevsky Express train between Moscow and Saint Petersburg, derailing it and causing 28 deaths and 96 injuries.

Q1082410.name: Battle of St. Matthew's Day
Q1082410.blurb: Livonian Crusade: The Estonian leader Lembitu and Livonian leader Caupo of Turaida are killed in the Battle of St. Matthew's Day.

Q1083391.name: Nanjing Decade
Q1083391.blurb: Nanjing decade: In the first battle of the Warlord Rebellion in northeastern Shandong against the Nationalist government of China, a 24,000-strong rebel force led by Zhang Zongchang was defeated at Zhifu by 7,000 NRA troops.

Q1083872.name: Glorious First of June
Q1083872.blurb: The battle of the Glorious First of June is fought, the first naval engagement between Britain and France during the French Revolutionary Wars.

Q1085253.name: Battle of the Kondurcha River
Q1085253.blurb: Tokhtamysh–Timur war: Battle of the Kondurcha River: Timur defeats Tokhtamysh of the Golden Horde in present-day southeast Russia.

Q1085392.name: Battle of Neerwinden
Q1085392.blurb: Flanders Campaign of the French Revolution, Battle of Neerwinden.

Q1085401.name: Battle of Katzbach
Q1085401.blurb: War of the Sixth Coalition: An impromptu battle takes place when French and Prussian-Russian forces accidentally run into each other near Liegnitz, Prussia (now Legnica, Poland).

Q1086489.name: massacre of Vassy
Q1086489.blurb: Sixty-three Huguenots are massacred in Wassy, France, marking the start of the French Wars of Religion.

Q1087721.name: 2011 Zhanaozen riots
Q1087721.blurb: The Zhanaozen massacre occurs when violent protests by oil workers take place in Zhanaozen, Kazakhstan, resulting in security forces killing at least 14 and injuring 100 more.

Q1087835.name: Candid Camera
Q1087835.blurb: Candid Camera makes its television debut after being on radio for a year as The Candid Microphone.

Q1088364.name: Battle of the Lys
Q1088364.blurb: World War I: The Battle of the Lys: The Portuguese Expeditionary Corps is crushed by the German forces during what is called the Spring Offensive on the Belgian region of Flanders.

Q1089270.name: Paris–Rouen
Q1089270.blurb: The first ever motor race is held in France between the cities of Paris and Rouen. The fastest finisher was the Comte Jules-Albert de Dion, but the "official" victory was awarded to Albert Lemaître driving his three-horsepower petrol engined Peugeot.

Q1089579.name: Grand Prix motor racing
Q1089579.blurb: The 1906 French Grand Prix, the first Grand Prix motor racing competition, began near Le Mans.

Q1089686.name: Champ de Mars Massacre
Q1089686.blurb: Members of the French National Guard under the command of General Lafayette open fire on a crowd of radical Jacobins at the Champ de Mars, Paris, during the French Revolution, killing scores of people.

Q1090177.name: Bath School disaster
Q1090177.blurb: The Bath School disaster: Forty-five people, including many children, are killed by bombs planted by a disgruntled school-board member in Bath Township, Michigan.

Q1090952.name: W. R. Myers High School shooting
Q1090952.blurb: A 14-year-old former student in Taber, Alberta, opened fire at his high school, killing one student and wounding another in Canada's first fatal school shooting in more than two decades.

Q1091051.name: NATO intervention in Bosnia and Herzegovina
Q1091051.blurb: Yugoslav Wars: The Dayton Agreement is signed in Paris by the leaders of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, Croatia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina.  On the same day, NATO began ground peacekeeping operations in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

Q1091247.name: Chūetsu Earthquake
Q1091247.blurb: A powerful earthquake and its aftershocks hit Niigata Prefecture in northern Japan, killing 35 people, injuring 2,200, and leaving 85,000 homeless or evacuated.

Q1091648.name: Chicago Race Riot of 1919
Q1091648.blurb: The Chicago Race Riot erupts after a racial incident occurred on a South Side beach, leading to 38 fatalities and 537 injuries over a five-day period.

Q1091654.name: Siege of Gaeta
Q1091654.blurb: Italian unification: The Siege of Gaeta ends with the capitulation of the defending fortress, effectively bringing an end of the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.

Q1092034.name: World Chess Championship 1975
Q1092034.blurb: Bobby Fischer refuses to play in a chess match against Anatoly Karpov, giving Karpov the title of World Champion by default.

Q1092510.name: First Red Scare
Q1092510.blurb: First Red Scare: The anarchist followers of Luigi Galleani (pictured) set off eight bombs in eight cities across the United States.

Q1092673.name: Ciompi Revolt
Q1092673.blurb: Unrepresented labourers revolted and violently took over the government of the Republic of Florence (depicted), demanding that they be granted political office.

Q1092872.name: 1906 French Grand Prix
Q1092872.blurb: The first Grand Prix motor race is held at Le Mans.

Q1093069.name: Convention on Cybercrime
Q1093069.blurb: The Budapest Convention on Cybercrime is signed in Budapest, Hungary.

Q1093286.name: Battle of Mondovì
Q1093286.blurb: War of the First Coalition: In the climax of the Montenotte Campaign, Napoleon Bonaparte decisively defeats the army of Piedmont at the Battle of Mondovi, leading to Piedmont's surrender a week later and decisively turning the Italian campaign in France's favor.

Q1093598.name: USAir Flight 405
Q1093598.blurb: USAir Flight 405 crashes shortly after takeoff from New York City's LaGuardia Airport, leading to a number of studies into the effect that ice has on aircraft.

Q1094155.name: wedding of Charles, Prince of Wales, and Lady Diana Spencer
aliases: wedding of Prince Charles and Lady Diana Spencer
Q1094155.blurb: A worldwide television audience of around 750 million people watch the wedding of Charles, Prince of Wales, and Lady Diana Spencer at St Paul's Cathedral in London.

Q1094996.name: Battle of Dayr al-Aqul
Q1094996.blurb: The Battle of Dayr al-'Aqul saves Baghdad from the Saffarids.

Q1096151.name: Battle of Delville Wood
Q1096151.blurb: The Battle of Delville Wood began as an action within the Battle of the Somme, lasting until 3 September 1916.

Q1100322.name: Hurricane Jeanne
Q1100322.blurb: Over 3,000 people die in Haiti after Hurricane Jeanne produces massive flooding and mudslides.

Q1102584.name: Iași pogrom
Q1102584.blurb: Romanian authorities launch one of the most violent pogroms in Jewish history in the city of Iași, resulting in the murder of at least 13,266 Jews.

Q1104917.name: Ådalen shootings
Q1104917.blurb: Five unarmed civilians are killed in the Ådalen shootings, as the Swedish military is called in to deal with protesting workers.

Q1106980.name: Conquest of Majorca
Q1106980.blurb: James I the Conqueror, King of Aragon, enters Medina Mayurqa (now known as Palma de Mallorca, Spain), thus consummating the Christian reconquest of the island of Mallorca.

Q1107846.name: Hurricane Fran
Q1107846.blurb: Hurricane Fran makes landfall near Cape Fear, North Carolina as a Category 3 storm with 115 mph sustained winds. Fran caused over $3 billion in damage and killed 27 people.

Q1109261.name: Sack of Thessalonica
Q1109261.blurb: Sack of Thessalonica: Saracen raiders under Leo of Tripoli sack Thessaloniki, the Byzantine Empire's second-largest city, after a short siege, and plunder it for a week.

Q1112854.name: Ming–Hồ War
Q1112854.blurb: Ming–Hồ War: Retired King Hồ Quý Ly and his son King Hồ Hán Thương of Hồ dynasty are captured by the Ming armies.

Q1113659.name: Battle of Fulford
Q1113659.blurb: At the Battle of Fulford, Harald Hardrada defeats earls Morcar and Edwin.

Q1116495.name: 1956 Grand Canyon mid-air collision
Q1116495.blurb: A TWA Super Constellation and a United Airlines DC-7 collide above the Grand Canyon in Arizona and crash, killing all 128 on board both airliners.

Q1116626.name: Battle of Worcester
Q1116626.blurb: The Battle of Worcester is the last significant action in the Wars of the Three Kingdoms.

Q1116646.name: Anglo-Swedish War
Q1116646.blurb: Sweden declares war on its ally the United Kingdom to begin the Anglo-Swedish War, although no fighting ever takes place.

Q1121402.name: South Lebanon conflict
Q1121402.blurb: The Israel Defense Forces launch Operation Litani, a seven-day campaign to invade and occupy southern Lebanon.

Q1121532.name: Battle of Alcácer Quibir
aliases: Battle of Al Kasr al Kebir
The Battle of Ksar El Kebir
The Battle of the Three Kings
Q1121532.blurb: Battle of Al Kasr al Kebir: The Moroccans defeat the Portuguese but both the Moroccan king Abd al-Malik and the Portuguese king Sebastian die. Ahmad al-Mansur follows Abd al-Malik as sultan of Morocco while the death of Sebastian leads to a succession crisis in Portugal.

Q1122487.name: Battle of Boquerón
Q1122487.blurb: The Battle of Boquerón, the first major battle of the Chaco War, commences.

Q1122799.name: Comstock Act of 1873
Q1122799.blurb: Censorship in the United States: The U.S. Congress enacts the Comstock Law, making it illegal to send any "obscene literature and articles of immoral use" through the mail.

Q1123201.name: Spanish American wars of independence
aliases: Wars of independence from Spain in the Americas
Q1123201.blurb: The Spanish American wars of independence ended with the death of King Ferdinand VII, with what had once been the Spanish Empire disintegrating into independent Latin American states.

Q1123353.name: Battle of Rorke's Drift
Q1123353.blurb: Anglo-Zulu War:  the Battle of Rorke's Drift, just some 15 km (9.3 mi) away from Isandlwana, results in a British victory.

Q1126268.name: Deir Yassin massacre
Q1126268.blurb: Fighters from the Irgun and Lehi Zionist terror groups attacked Deir Yassin near Jerusalem, killing over 100 Palestinians.

Q1127302.name: Estonian War of Independence
Q1127302.blurb: Estonian War of Independence: The decisive defeat of the Baltische Landeswehr in the Battle of Cēsis; this date is celebrated as Victory Day in Estonia.

Q1127353.name: Battle of Ad Decimum
Q1127353.blurb: The Byzantines under Belisarius defeated the Vandal King Gelimer at the Battle of Ad Decimum near Carthage, and began the "Reconquest of the West" under Byzantine Emperor Justinian I.

Q1128871.name: March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom
aliases: Great March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom
March for Washington for Jobs and Freedom
March on Washington for Jobs & Freedom
The Great March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom
The March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom
Q1128871.blurb: March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom: Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. gives his I Have a Dream speech.

Q1129089.name: Great Molasses Flood
Q1129089.blurb: Great Molasses Flood: A wave of molasses released from an exploding storage tank sweeps through Boston, Massachusetts, killing 21 and injuring 150.

Q1129096.name: Constitution of May 3, 1791
aliases: Constitution of the third of May
Q1129096.blurb: The Constitution of May 3 (the first modern constitution in Europe) is proclaimed by the Sejm of Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.

Q1129214.name: Controlled Impact Demonstration
Q1129214.blurb: NASA conducts the Controlled Impact Demonstration, wherein an airliner is deliberately crashed in order to test technologies and gather data to help improve survivability of crashes.

Q1129412.name: Egypt–Israel Peace Treaty
aliases: Peace Treaty Between the State of Israel and the Arab Republic of Egypt
Q1129412.blurb: In accord with the Egypt–Israel peace treaty, Israel begins its withdrawal from the Sinai Peninsula.

Q1129674.name: Battle of Lewis's Farm
Q1129674.blurb: American Civil War: The Appomattox campaign opened with the Battle of Lewis's Farm, in which the Confederate Army of Northern Virginia was forced into a series of retreats that would culminate in their surrender.

Q1130017.name: 1995 Rugby World Cup
Q1130017.blurb: Rugby World Cup: South Africa defeats New Zealand and Nelson Mandela presents Francois Pienaar with the Webb Ellis Cup in an iconic post-apartheid moment.

Q1130275.name: Swedish calendar
Q1130275.blurb: February 29 is followed by February 30 in Sweden, in a move to abolish the Swedish calendar for a return to the Julian calendar.

Q1130507.name: Hundred Days Offensive
aliases: Final Advance in Artois and Flanders
Q1130507.blurb: World War I: The Battle of Amiens begins a string of almost continuous Allied victories with a push through the German front lines (Hundred Days Offensive).

Q1130522.name: Operation Mincemeat
Q1130522.blurb: World War II: The British submarine HMS Seraph surfaces near Huelva to cast adrift a dead man dressed as a courier and carrying false invasion plans.

Q1130525.name: Battle of Compiègne
Q1130525.blurb: Ragenfrid defeats Theudoald at the Battle of Compiègne.

Q1130792.name: Treaty of Fredrikshamn
Q1130792.blurb: Peace between Sweden and Russia in the Finnish War; the territory that will become Finland is ceded to Russia by the Treaty of Fredrikshamn.

Q1131431.name: Copperbelt strike of 1935
Q1131431.blurb: A strike by copper miners in Northern Rhodesia ended after six workers were shot and killed by police.

Q1131442.name: Massacre in the Great Temple of Tenochtitlan
Q1131442.blurb: The massacre at the festival of Tóxcatl takes place during the Fall of Tenochtitlan, resulting in turning the Aztecs against the Spanish.

Q1131780.name: Declaration of Independence of the Mexican Empire
Q1131780.blurb: The Declaration of Independence of the Mexican Empire is drafted. It will be made public on 13 October.

Q1131784.name: Montenegrin independence referendum
Q1131784.blurb: The Republic of Montenegro holds a referendum proposing independence from the State Union of Serbia and Montenegro; 55% of Montenegrins vote for independence.

Q1131857.name: Iranian events of 1921
Q1131857.blurb: Rezā Shāh takes control of Tehran during a successful coup.

Q1131956.name: 2009 Fiordland earthquake
Q1131956.blurb: A .mw-parser-output .tooltip-dotted{border-bottom:1px dotted;cursor:help}Mw 7.8 earthquake struck a remote region of Fiordland, New Zealand, the country's largest earthquake magnitude since the 1931 Hawke's Bay earthquake.

Q1132306.name: Battle of Tzirallum
Q1132306.blurb: Civil wars of the Tetrarchy: An outnumbered army led by Roman emperor Licinius defeated his rival Maximinus II's forces at the Battle of Tzirallum.

Q1132579.name: Battle of Princeton
Q1132579.blurb: American Revolutionary War: American forces under General George Washington defeat British forces at the Battle of Princeton, helping boost patriot morale.

Q1132835.name: 1946 Iran crisis
Q1132835.blurb: U.S.-backed Iranian troops brought an end to the Iran crisis when they marched on the breakaway Republic of Mahabad and recaptured the territory.

Q1133692.name: State funeral of John F. Kennedy
Q1133692.blurb: State funeral of John F. Kennedy; after lying in state at the United States Capitol, a Requiem Mass takes place at Cathedral of St. Matthew the Apostle and the President is buried at Arlington National Cemetery.

Q1134220.name: Mongol invasion of Kievan Rus'
Q1134220.blurb: Mongol invasion of Kievan Rus': Mongol forces defeated a Kievan Rus' army at the Battle of the Kalka River in present-day Ukraine.

Q1134635.name: 1994 World Series
