Q1134635.blurb: Major League Baseball players go on strike, eventually forcing the cancellation of the 1994 World Series.

Q1134649.name: Battle of the Aegates Islands
Q1134649.blurb: First Punic War: Battle of the Aegates: The Romans sink the Carthaginian fleet bringing the First Punic War to an end.

Q1134821.name: Bananas Massacre in Colombia
Q1134821.blurb: The government of Colombia sends military forces to suppress a month-long strike by United Fruit Company workers, resulting in an unknown number of deaths.

Q1135634.name: Manila hostage crisis
Q1135634.blurb: The Manila hostage crisis occurred near the Quirino Grandstand in Manila, Philippines killing 9 people including the perpetrator while injuring 9 others.

Q1135895.name: Qantas Flight 32
Q1135895.blurb: Qantas Flight 32, an Airbus A380, suffers an uncontained engine failure over Indonesia shortly after taking off from Singapore, crippling the jet. The crew manage to safely return to Singapore, saving all 469 passengers and crew.

Q1136002.name: Revolt of Lyon against the National Convention
Q1136002.blurb: French Revolution: After a month-long siege, the leaders of Lyon surrendered, ending their revolt against the National Convention.

Q1136021.name: 2001 Indian-Bangladesh border conflict
Q1136021.blurb: India and Bangladesh began a six-day conflict over their disputed border, which ended in a stalemate.

Q1136114.name: Russian submarine Kursk explosion
Q1136114.blurb: The Russian Navy submarine Kursk explodes and sinks in the Barents Sea during a military exercise, killing her entire 118-man crew.

Q1136370.name: General Hospital
Q1136370.blurb: About 30 million people watched the fictional couple Luke Spencer and Laura Webber wed on the television show General Hospital in the highest-rated hour in American soap opera history.

Q1136414.name: Battle of Havana
Q1136414.blurb: War of Jenkins' Ear: A British squadron wins a tactical victory over a Spanish squadron off Havana.

Q1136575.name: Vandalic War
Q1136575.blurb: Vandalic War: Byzantine general Belisarius defeats the Vandals, commanded by King Gelimer, at the Battle of Tricamarum.

Q1136870.name: Battle of Sandwich (1217)
Q1136870.blurb: An English fleet defeats a French fleet in the battle of Sandwich, cutting of Prince Louis of France from supplies and diminishing his hopes to gain the English throne during the First Barons' War.

Q1137047.name: Hainan Island incident
Q1137047.blurb: The detained crew of a United States EP-3E aircraft that landed in Hainan, China, after a collision with a J-8 fighter, is released.

Q1137302.name: Battle of Omdurman
Q1137302.blurb: Battle of Omdurman: British and Egyptian troops defeat Sudanese tribesmen and establish British dominance in Sudan.

Q1137483.name: 2008–2011 Icelandic financial crisis
Q1137483.blurb: During a national financial crisis, thousands of people protested (pictured) at the Icelandic parliament in Reykjavík.

Q1137957.name: 1948 Czechoslovak coup d'état
Q1137957.blurb: In a coup d'état led by Klement Gottwald, the Communist Party of Czechoslovakia takes control of government in Prague to end the Third Czechoslovak Republic.

Q1137980.name: Battle of Ravenna
Q1137980.blurb: War of the League of Cambrai: Franco-Ferrarese forces led by Gaston de Foix and Alfonso I d'Este win the Battle of Ravenna against the Papal-Spanish forces.

Q1138460.name: Battle of Annual
Q1138460.blurb: Rif War: The Spanish Army suffers its worst military defeat in modern times to the Berbers of the Rif region of Spanish Morocco.

Q1138687.name: Battle of Monte Porzio
Q1138687.blurb: Battle of Monte Porzio: A Roman army supporting Pope Alexander III is defeated by Christian of Buch and Rainald of Dassel.

Q1139080.name: Hurricane Gilbert
Q1139080.blurb: Hurricane Gilbert devastates Jamaica; it turns towards Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula two days later, causing an estimated $5 billion in damage.

Q1139109.name: Crawford expedition
Q1139109.blurb: American Revolutionary War: US Colonel William Crawford began a failed expedition to destroy British-allied American Indian towns along the Sandusky River in the Ohio Country.

Q1139479.name: Macedonia naming dispute
aliases: Application of the Interim Accord of 13 September 1995
Application of the Interim Accord of 13 September 1995 (the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia v. Greece)
List of states that have recognized Macedonia under its constitutional name
Q1139479.blurb: The country known as the Republic of Macedonia renames itself the Republic of North Macedonia in accordance with the Prespa agreement, settling a long-standing naming dispute with Greece.

Q1139536.name: Republic Day
Q1139536.blurb: The Constitution of India comes into force, forming a republic. Rajendra Prasad is sworn in as the first President of India. Observed as Republic Day in India.

Q1139615.name: Qibya massacre
Q1139615.blurb: Israeli military commander Ariel Sharon and his Unit 101 special forces attacked the village of Qibya on the West Bank, destroying 45 buildings, killing 42 villagers, and wounding 15 others.

Q1139638.name: 1953 Ionian Earthquake
Q1139638.blurb: The 7.2 Ms Ionian earthquake shakes the southern Ionian Islands with a maximum Mercalli intensity of X (Extreme). Between 445 and 800 people are killed.

Q1139876.name: Yemeni unification
Q1139876.blurb: North and South Yemen are unified to create the Republic of Yemen.

Q1139887.name: Russo-Persian War of 1804–13
Q1139887.blurb: Treaty of Gulistan: The Russo-Persian War of 1804-1813 comes to a close with the signing of the Treaty of Gulistan, under which terms Qajar Iran agrees to cede the bulk of its Caucasian territories, which comprise much of modern Dagestan, Georgia, Armenia, and Azerbaijan, to the Russian Empire.

Q1139930.name: 1975 Cricket World Cup
Q1139930.blurb: The inaugural edition of the Cricket World Cup, the premier international championship of men's One Day International cricket, began in England.

Q1140009.name: Typhoon Nancy
Q1140009.blurb: Typhoon Nancy, with possibly the strongest winds ever measured in a tropical cyclone, makes landfall in Osaka, Japan, killing 173 people.

Q1140134.name: Invasion of Ryukyu
Q1140134.blurb: Daimyō (Lord) Shimazu Tadatsune of the Satsuma Domain in southern Kyūshū, Japan, completes his successful invasion of the Ryūkyū Kingdom in Okinawa.

Q1140155.name: Great Train Robbery
Q1140155.blurb: Great Train Robbery: In England, a gang of 15 train robbers steal £2.6 million in bank notes.

Q1140492.name: Smolensk War
Q1140492.blurb: Smolensk War: Forces from the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth broke the Russian siege of Smolensk (depicted).

Q1140646.name: Battle of Formigny
Q1140646.blurb: Battle of Formigny: Toward the end of the Hundred Years' War, the French attack and nearly annihilate English forces, ending English domination in Northern France.

Q1140920.name: 20th Congress of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union
aliases: Twentieth Congress of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union
Q1140920.blurb: In a speech to the 20th Congress of the Communist Party, Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev denounced the personality cult and dictatorship of his predecessor Joseph Stalin.

Q1141380.name: Battle of Wake Island
Q1141380.blurb: World War II: The Imperial Japanese Navy suffers its first loss of surface vessels during the Battle of Wake Island.

Q1141485.name: Treaty of Åbo
Q1141485.blurb: The Treaty of Åbo ends the 1741–1743 Russo-Swedish War.

Q1141784.name: Sicilian Baroque
Q1141784.blurb: The most powerful earthquake recorded in Italy struck the island of Sicily, causing 60,000 deaths and prompting a period of architectural revival.

Q1141918.name: Typhoon Ketsana
Q1141918.blurb: Typhoon Ketsana hits the Philippines, China, Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos and Thailand, causing 700 fatalities.

Q1141997.name: 2006 Southern Leyte mudslide
Q1141997.blurb: A massive mudslide occurs in Southern Leyte, Philippines; the official death toll is set at 1,126.

Q1142248.name: Exhibition of the Industry of All Nations
Q1142248.blurb: Opening of the first major US world's fair, the Exhibition of the Industry of All Nations in New York City.

Q1142553.name: Tragic Week
Q1142553.blurb: Begin of the Tragic Week in Barcelona in response to troop mobilisations for the Rif War.

Q1142780.name: Ctrl+Alt+Del
Q1142780.blurb: Artist Tim Buckley published "Loss" as part of his webcomic Ctrl+Alt+Del.

Q1142936.name: Australia Post
Q1142936.blurb: A man shot and killed eight people at the Australia Post building in Melbourne, before jumping to his death.

Q1143044.name: Battles of Kawanakajima
Q1143044.blurb: Fourth Battle of Kawanakajima: Takeda Shingen defeats Uesugi Kenshin in the climax of their ongoing conflicts.

Q1143209.name: 27th G8 summit
Q1143209.blurb: Twenty-three-year-old Italian anti-globalist Carlo Giuliani was shot dead by a police officer while protesting outside the 27th G8 summit held in Genoa, Italy.

Q1143379.name: 1991–1992 South Ossetia War
aliases: war between Georgia and South Ossetia
war between South Ossetia and Georgia
Q1143379.blurb: Georgian troops attacked Tskhinvali, the South Ossetian capital, beginning the First South Ossetia War.

Q1144135.name: 1946 Aleutian Islands earthquake
Q1144135.blurb: The 8.6 Mw Aleutian Islands earthquake shakes the Aleutian Islands with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VI (Strong). A destructive tsunami reaches the Hawaiian Islands resulting in dozens of deaths, mostly in Hilo, Hawaii.

Q1144602.name: Sumgait pogrom
Q1144602.blurb: Sumgait pogrom: The Armenian community in Sumgait, Azerbaijan is targeted in a violent pogrom.

Q1144824.name: Battle of Messines
Q1144824.blurb: World War I: Battle of Messines: Allied soldiers detonate a series of mines underneath German trenches at Messines Ridge, killing 10,000 German troops.

Q1144908.name: SS Fort Stikine
Q1144908.blurb: The freighter Fort Stikine, carrying cotton bales, gold and ammunition, exploded in the harbour of Bombay, India, sinking surrounding ships and causing about 800 deaths.

Q1144988.name: Chios massacre
Q1144988.blurb: Greek War of Independence: Ottoman troops began a massacre of tens of thousands of Greeks (depicted) on the island of Chios.

Q1145246.name: partition of the Ottoman Empire
Q1145246.blurb: The Treaty of Lausanne was signed to settle part of the partition of the Ottoman Empire, establishing the boundaries of Greece, Bulgaria and Turkey.

Q1145378.name: Operation Flavius
Q1145378.blurb: The Troubles: In Operation Flavius, the Special Air Service killed three volunteers of the Provisional Irish Republican Army conspiring to bomb a parade of British military bands in Gibraltar.

Q1145411.name: Grito de Dolores
Q1145411.blurb: With the Grito de Dolores, Father Miguel Hidalgo begins Mexico's fight for independence from Spain.

Q1145682.name: Ilinden–Preobrazhenie Uprising
Q1145682.blurb: The Ilinden–Preobrazhenie Uprising against the Ottoman Empire begins.

Q1145764.name: Guiding Light
Q1145764.blurb: The Guiding Light debuts on NBC radio from Chicago. In 1952 it moves to CBS television, where it remains until September 18, 2009.

Q1146739.name: Tokyo subway sarin attack
aliases: Sarin gas attack on the Tokyo subway
Sarin attack on the Tokyo subway
Sarin gas attack on the Tokyo Metro
Q1146739.blurb: The Japanese cult Aum Shinrikyo carries out a sarin gas attack on the Tokyo subway, killing 14 and wounding over 6,200 people.

Q1147270.name: Great Mississippi Flood of 1927
Q1147270.blurb: Torrential rains caused the Mississippi River to break out of its levee system in at least 145 places, resulting in the worst flooding in the history of the United States.

Q1147471.name: Treaty of Zaragoza
Q1147471.blurb: Treaty of Zaragoza divides the eastern hemisphere between Spain and Portugal along a line 297.5 leagues (1,250 kilometres (780 mi)) east of the Moluccas.

Q1147833.name: Morea expedition
Q1147833.blurb: Morea expedition: The city of Patras, Greece, is liberated by the French expeditionary force.

Q1148306.name: Yan'an Rectification Movement
Q1148306.blurb: Mao Zedong makes a speech on "Reform in Learning, the Party and Literature", which puts into motion the Yan'an Rectification Movement.

Q1148320.name: transit of Venus, 2004
Q1148320.blurb: The first Venus Transit in well over a century takes place, the previous one being in 1882.

Q1148862.name: Battle of Fariskur
Q1148862.blurb: Seventh Crusade: The Ayyubid Sultanate of Egypt defeated and captured King Louis IX of France at the Battle of Fariskur.

Q1149869.name: Battle of Westport
Q1149869.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Westport is the last significant engagement west of the Mississippi River, ending in a Union victory.

Q1149912.name: 2005 Belize unrest
Q1149912.blurb: In Belmopan, Belize, the unrest over the government's new taxes erupts into riots.

Q1150410.name: Battle of Boyacá
Q1150410.blurb: Simón Bolívar triumphs over Spain in the Battle of Boyacá.

Q1150465.name: Operation Barras
Q1150465.blurb: Operation Barras successfully frees six British soldiers held captive for over two weeks and contributes to the end of the Sierra Leone Civil War.

Q1150578.name: 1740 Batavia massacre
Q1150578.blurb: Dutch colonists and Javanese natives begin a massacre of the ethnic Chinese population in Batavia, eventually killing at least 10,000.

Q1150855.name: Great Lakes Storm of 1913
Q1150855.blurb: The first day of the Great Lakes Storm of 1913, a massive blizzard that ultimately killed 250 and caused over $5 million (about $159,243,000 in 2024 dollars) damage. Winds reach hurricane force on this date.

Q1151276.name: CSX 8888 incident
Q1151276.blurb: A runaway train loaded with hazardous chemicals traveled driverless for 66 miles (106 km) through Ohio before being stopped near Kenton.

Q1151775.name: 2011 Mumbai bombings
Q1151775.blurb: Mumbai is rocked by three bomb blasts during the evening rush hour, killing 26 and injuring 130.

Q1151804.name: Santika Club fire
Q1151804.blurb: Sixty-six people die in a nightclub fire in Bangkok, Thailand.

Q1151913.name: First Anglo-Dutch War
Q1151913.blurb: First Anglo-Dutch War: The Battle of the Gabbard begins, lasting until the following day.

Q1151917.name: Women's March on Versailles
Q1151917.blurb: French Revolution: The Women's March on Versailles effectively terminates royal authority.

Q1152440.name: Pickett's Charge
Q1152440.blurb: American Civil War: The final day of the Battle of Gettysburg culminates with Pickett's Charge.

Q1152894.name: Siege of Louisbourg
Q1152894.blurb: A New England colonial army captures the French fortifications at Louisbourg (New Style).

Q1153159.name: Dunblane school massacre
Q1153159.blurb: The Dunblane massacre leads to the death of sixteen primary school children and one teacher in Dunblane, Scotland.

Q1153249.name: Kenya Airways Flight 431
Q1153249.blurb: Kenya Airways Flight 431 crashes into the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of Ivory Coast, killing 169.

Q1153299.name: Short Parliament
Q1153299.blurb: King Charles I of England dissolves the Short Parliament.

Q1153331.name: Second Ottoman–Venetian War
Q1153331.blurb: Ottoman–Venetian War (1499–1503): The Ottomans capture Methoni, Messenia.

Q1153610.name: Shenandoah Valley Campaign
Q1153610.blurb: American Civil War: Stonewall Jackson concludes his successful Shenandoah Valley Campaign with a victory in the Battle of Port Republic.

Q1154050.name: Peninsula Campaign
Q1154050.blurb: American Civil War: Peninsula Campaign: The Battle of Seven Pines (or the Battle of Fair Oaks) ends inconclusively, with both sides claiming victory.

Q1154073.name: Lod Airport massacre
Q1154073.blurb: Members of the Japanese Red Army carried out the Lod Airport massacre in Tel Aviv, Israel, on behalf of PFLP External Operations, killing over 20 people and injuring almost 80 others.

Q1154330.name: 10 August insurrection
Q1154330.blurb: French Revolution: Storming of the Tuileries Palace: Louis XVI is arrested and taken into custody as his Swiss Guards are massacred by the Parisian mob.

Q1154365.name: 2008 Zimbabwean presidential election
Q1154365.blurb: In a highly scrutinized election, President of Zimbabwe Robert Mugabe is re-elected in a landslide after his opponent Morgan Tsvangirai had withdrawn a week earlier, citing violence against his party's supporters.

Q1154912.name: Iraqi Kurdish Civil War
Q1154912.blurb: The Turkish Armed Forces withdraw from northern Iraq after assisting the Kurdistan Democratic Party in the Iraqi Kurdish Civil War.

Q1154983.name: First Ottoman–Venetian War
Q1154983.blurb: The Treaty of Constantinople ends the 16-year-long First Ottoman–Venetian War.

Q1156671.name: Katowice Trade Hall roof collapse
Q1156671.blurb: The roof of one of the buildings at the Katowice International Fair in Poland collapses due to the weight of snow, killing 65 and injuring more than 170 others.

Q1157002.name: Lawrence v. Texas
Q1157002.blurb: The U.S. Supreme Court rules in Lawrence v. Texas that sex-based sodomy laws are unconstitutional.

Q1157030.name: Malta Summit
Q1157030.blurb: In a meeting off the coast of Malta, U.S. President George H. W. Bush and Soviet General Secretary Mikhail Gorbachev release statements indicating that the Cold War between NATO and the Warsaw Pact may be coming to an end.

Q1160895.name: Treaty of London
Q1160895.blurb: The Treaty of London establishes Belgium as a kingdom and guarantees its neutrality.

Q1161889.name: 1877 Iquique earthquake
Q1161889.blurb: An earthquake struck northern Chile, leading to the deaths of 2,385 people, mostly victims of the ensuing tsunami, as far away as Hawaii and Fiji.

Q1162294.name: Expedition Endurance
Q1162294.blurb: Imperial Trans-Antarctic Expedition: Seven survivors of the Ross Sea party are rescued after being stranded for several months.

Q1163038.name: 1952 Kern County earthquake
Q1163038.blurb: The 7.3 Mw Kern County earthquake strikes Southern California with a maximum Mercalli intensity of XI (Extreme), killing 12 and injuring hundreds.

Q1163186.name: Battle of Svolder
Q1163186.blurb: Battle of Svolder during the Viking Age.

Q1164169.name: Burmese–Siamese War of 1547–1549
Q1164169.blurb: Forces of the Burmese Toungoo dynasty led by King Tabinshwehti (depicted) departed Martaban to begin an invasion of the Ayutthaya Kingdom.

Q1164263.name: Saint Valentine's Day Massacre
Q1164263.blurb: Saint Valentine's Day Massacre: Seven people, six of them gangster rivals of Al Capone's gang, are murdered in Chicago.

Q1164547.name: Khrushchev thaw
Q1164547.blurb: In Moscow City Court, the Rokotov–Faibishenko show trial begins, despite the Khrushchev Thaw to reverse Stalinist elements in Soviet society.

Q1164558.name: The Concert for Bangladesh
Q1164558.blurb: The Concert for Bangladesh, organized by former Beatle George Harrison, is held at Madison Square Garden in New York City.

Q1164870.name: Prestige oil spill
Q1164870.blurb: The Greek oil tanker Prestige split in two and sank off the coast of Galicia after spilling 420 thousand barrels (17.8 million US gallons) of oil, in the worst environmental disaster in Spanish and Portuguese history.

Q1165440.name: Battle of Mauron
Q1165440.blurb: War of the Breton Succession: Anglo-Bretons defeat the French in the Battle of Mauron.

Q1170696.name: 1979 Red River Valley tornado outbreak
Q1170696.blurb: Red River Valley tornado outbreak: A tornado lands in Wichita Falls, Texas, killing 42 people.

Q1172388.name: Berlin Victory Parade of 1945
Q1172388.blurb: The Berlin Victory Parade of 1945 is held.

Q1172638.name: Treaty of Mignano
Q1172638.blurb: Pope Innocent II confirms in the treaty of Mignano the investiture of the sons of Roger II of Sicily to their fiefs and abandons support for the barons opposed to Roger.

Q1182065.name: The Declaration of the Independence of New Zealand
aliases: He Whakaputanga o te Rangatiratanga o Niu Tīreni
He Whakaputanga o te Rangatiratanga o Nu Tireni
Q1182065.blurb: The United Tribes of New Zealand are established with the signature of the Declaration of Independence.

Q1184775.name: Comair Flight 5191
Q1184775.blurb: Comair Flight 5191 crashes on takeoff from Blue Grass Airport in Lexington, Kentucky, bound for Hartsfield–Jackson Atlanta International Airport in Atlanta. Of the passengers and crew, 49 of 50 are confirmed dead in the hours following the crash.

Q1184780.name: Delta Air Lines Flight 191
Q1184780.blurb: Delta Air Lines Flight 191, a Lockheed L-1011 TriStar, crashes at Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport killing 137.

Q1184935.name: Lourdes apparitions
Q1184935.blurb: The last apparition of the Blessed Virgin Mary to Bernadette Soubirous in Lourdes, France.

Q1185525.name: 1956 Georgian demonstrations
Q1185525.blurb: Soviet forces suppress mass demonstrations in the Georgian SSR, reacting to Nikita Khrushchev's de-Stalinization policy.

Q1185980.name: Phnom Penh stampede
Q1185980.blurb: During the Cambodian water festival, a stampede in Koh Pich, Phnom Penh, kills 347 people.

Q1186260.name: Creek War
Q1186260.blurb: Creek War: Fort Mims massacre: Creek "Red Sticks" kill over 500 settlers (including over 250 armed militia) in Fort Mims, north of Mobile, Alabama.

Q1186448.name: demon core
Q1186448.blurb: While working with a mass of plutonium known as the demon core, Manhattan Project physicist Louis Slotin accidentally exposed himself to a lethal dose of hard radiation, making him the second victim of a criticality accident in history.

Q1186774.name: Texas Declaration of Independence
Q1186774.blurb: Texas Revolution: The Declaration of independence of the Republic of Texas from Mexico is adopted.

Q1187072.name: Texas annexation
Q1187072.blurb: The United States annexes the Republic of Texas and admits it as the 28th state.

Q1187550.name: assassination of Robert F. Kennedy
aliases: Assassination of Senator Robert F. Kennedy
Q1187550.blurb: Sirhan Sirhan is convicted of assassinating Robert F. Kennedy.

Q1187909.name: Battle of the Sexes
Q1187909.blurb: Billie Jean King beats Bobby Riggs in the Battle of the Sexes tennis match at the Houston Astrodome.

Q1187969.name: START II
Q1187969.blurb: In Moscow, Russia, George H. W. Bush and Boris Yeltsin sign the second Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty (START).

Q1188691.name: Peace Bridge
Q1188691.blurb: The Peace Bridge opens between Fort Erie, Ontario and Buffalo, New York.

Q1188883.name: Brazzaville arms dump blasts
Q1188883.blurb: A series of explosions is reported at a munitions dump in Brazzaville, the capital of the Republic of the Congo, killing at least 250 people.

Q1188930.name: İstanbul earthquake of 1509
Q1188930.blurb: An earthquake known as "The Lesser Judgment Day" hits Constantinople.

Q1189910.name: 1964 New York World's Fair
Q1189910.blurb: The 1964–1965 New York World's Fair opens for its second and final season.

Q1190969.name: Aeroflot Flight 411
Q1190969.blurb: While attempting to return to Sheremetyevo International Airport, Aeroflot Flight 411, an Ilyushin Il-62, crashes near Mendeleyevo, Moscow Oblast, killing all 90 people on board.

Q1191077.name: Secret Treaty of Dover
Q1191077.blurb: Charles II and Louis XIV signed a secret treaty, requiring England to aid France in its war against the Dutch Republic and the future conversion of Charles to Catholicism, in return for Louis making large payments to Charles and promising to aid him if there was a rebellion in England.

Q1191088.name: Diamond Jubilee of Elizabeth II
Q1191088.blurb: The pageant for the Diamond Jubilee of Elizabeth II takes place on the River Thames.

Q1191091.name: Webster–Ashburton Treaty
Q1191091.blurb: The Webster–Ashburton Treaty is signed, establishing the United States–Canada border east of the Rocky Mountains.

Q1191151.name: Tiananmen incident
Q1191151.blurb: In China, the April Fifth Movement leads to the Tiananmen Incident.

Q1191557.name: Ikedaya Incident
Q1191557.blurb: Ikedaya Incident: The Choshu Han shishis planned Shinsengumi sabotage on Kyoto, Japan at Ikedaya.

Q1191854.name: Battle of Gonzales
Q1191854.blurb: Texas Revolution: Mexican troops attempt to disarm the people of Gonzales, but encounter stiff resistance from a hastily assembled militia.

Q1192212.name: Emancipation reform of 1861
aliases: Abolition of serfdom in the Russian Empire
Emancipation of the Russian Serfs in 1861
Emancipation of the serfs in Russia
Q1192212.blurb: Alexander II of Russia signs the Emancipation Manifesto, freeing serfs.

Q1192616.name: Battle of Didgori
Q1192616.blurb: Battle of Didgori: The Georgian army under King David IV wins a decisive victory over the famous Seljuk commander Ilghazi.

Q1192659.name: Vela incident
Q1192659.blurb: A bright flash, resembling the detonation of a nuclear weapon, is observed near the Prince Edward Islands. Its cause is never determined.

Q1192865.name: Xuanwu Gate Incident
Q1192865.blurb: Li Shimin (pictured) led his forces to assassinate his rival brothers in a coup for the imperial throne of Tang China.

Q1192867.name: Battle of Pułtusk
Q1192867.blurb: Battles of Pultusk and Golymin: Russian forces hold French forces under Napoleon.

Q1192894.name: Flight to Varennes
Q1192894.blurb: King Louis XVI, disguised as a valet, and the French royal family attempt to flee Paris during the French Revolution.

Q1193136.name: Execution of Saddam Hussein
Q1193136.blurb: Saddam Hussein, the former president of Iraq, was executed after being found guilty of crimes against humanity by the Iraqi High Tribunal.

Q1193370.name: 1979 Mississauga train derailment
Q1193370.blurb: A 106-car Canadian Pacific freight train carrying explosive and poisonous chemicals from Windsor, Ontario, Canada derails in Mississauga, Ontario.

Q1193959.name: Battle of Toba-Fushimi
Q1193959.blurb: Boshin War: The Battle of Toba–Fushimi begins, between forces of the Tokugawa shogunate and pro-Imperial factions; it will end in defeat for the shogunate, and is a pivotal point in the Meiji Restoration.

Q1194400.name: April 9 tragedy
Q1194400.blurb: Tbilisi massacre: An anti-Soviet peaceful demonstration and hunger strike in Tbilisi, demanding restoration of Georgian independence, is dispersed by the Soviet Army, resulting in 20 deaths and hundreds of injuries.

Q1194699.name: Treaty of Amity and Commerce
Q1194699.blurb: United States and Japan sign the Harris Treaty.

Q1194993.name: International Meridian Conference
Q1194993.blurb: The International Meridian Conference designates the Royal Observatory, Greenwich as the world's prime meridian.

Q1195058.name: Shanghai massacre of 1927
Q1195058.blurb: Shanghai massacre of 1927: Chiang Kai-shek orders the Chinese Communist Party members executed in Shanghai, ending the First United Front.

Q1195251.name: Treaty of Seville
Q1195251.blurb: Spain, France and Great Britain sign the Treaty of Seville.

Q1195263.name: Battle of Ekeren
Q1195263.blurb: The Battle of Ekeren between a Dutch force and a French force.

Q1196236.name: Tumu Crisis
Q1196236.blurb: Tumu Crisis: The Mongols capture the Emperor of China.

Q1196554.name: Battle of Minorca
Q1196554.blurb: Royal Navy Admiral John Byng was executed by firing squad for failing to "do his utmost" during the Battle of Minorca at the start of the Seven Years' War.

Q1196587.name: Exxon Valdez disaster
Q1196587.blurb: In Prince William Sound in Alaska, the Exxon Valdez spills 240,000 barrels (38,000 m3) of crude oil after running aground.

Q1196836.name: The Six Million Dollar Man
Q1196836.blurb: The Northrop M2-F2 crashes on landing, becoming the inspiration for the novel Cyborg and TV series The Six Million Dollar Man.

Q1197271.name: Treaty of Saint Petersburg
Q1197271.blurb: The Treaty of Saint Petersburg between Japan and Russia is ratified, providing for the exchange of Sakhalin for the Kuril Islands.

Q1197995.name: Frankokratia
Q1197995.blurb: Troops of the Fourth Crusade entered Constantinople and began a sack of the city, temporarily dissolving the Byzantine Empire.

Q1198240.name: Proclamation of the Irish Republic
aliases: Irish Republic poster saying POBLACHT NA hÉIREANN poblacht na heireann
The Proclamation of the Irish Republic
Q1198240.blurb: Easter Rising: Irish rebels, led by Patrick Pearse and James Connolly, launch an uprising in Dublin against British rule and proclaim an Irish Republic.

Q1198569.name: The Eternal Jew
Q1198569.blurb: The Nazi exhibition Der ewige Jude ("The Eternal Jew") opens in Munich.

Q1200928.name: Japanese invasion of Thailand
Q1200928.blurb: World War II: Japanese forces simultaneously invade Shanghai International Settlement, Malaya, Thailand, Hong Kong, the Philippines, and the Dutch East Indies. (See December 7 for the concurrent attack on Pearl Harbor in the Western Hemisphere.)

Q1201263.name: Warlord Era
Q1201263.blurb: Republic of China leader Chiang Kai-shek was kidnapped by Marshal Chang Hsueh-liang, a former warlord of Manchuria.

Q1201935.name: transit of Venus, 2012
Q1201935.blurb: Last transit of Venus until the year 2117.

Q1202078.name: Italian invasion of British Somaliland
Q1202078.blurb: World War II: Italian forces began a conquest of British Somaliland, capturing the region in 16 days.

Q1203203.name: Marikana miners' strike
Q1203203.blurb: The Marikana massacre begins near Rustenburg, South Africa, resulting in the deaths of 47 people.

Q1203233.name: 1951 Pan American Games
Q1203233.blurb: After being postponed due to World War II, the inaugural edition of the Pan American Games opened in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

Q1204796.name: Metapolitefsi
Q1204796.blurb: The Metapolitefsi period began with Konstantinos Karamanlis (pictured) taking office as Prime Minister of Greece after the collapse of the military junta.

Q1205521.name: Chinese economic reform
aliases: Academic studies about Chinese economic reform
Economic reform in the People's Republic of China
Economic reforms in the People's Republic of China
Q1205521.blurb: The pivotal Third Plenum of the 11th National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party is held in Beijing, with Deng Xiaoping reversing Mao-era policies to pursue a program for the reform and opening up.

Q1205622.name: Burning of Smyrna
Q1205622.blurb: After nine days, the great fire of Smyrna was extinguished (aftermath pictured), having caused at least ten thousand deaths.

Q1207310.name: Battle of Orsha
Q1207310.blurb: Battle of Orsha: In one of the biggest battles of the century, Lithuanians and Poles defeat the Russian army.

Q1207617.name: Pequot War
Q1207617.blurb: Pequot War: A combined English and Mohegan force under John Mason attacks a village in Connecticut, massacring approximately 500 Pequots.

Q1207697.name: Jingnan Campaign
Q1207697.blurb: Nanjing surrenders to Zhu Di without a fight, ending the Jingnan campaign. The Jianwen Emperor disappears and his family is incarcerated.

Q1208996.name: Battle of Lushunkou
Q1208996.blurb: Port Arthur, China, falls to the Japanese, a decisive victory of the First Sino-Japanese War; Japanese troops are accused of massacring the remaining inhabitants.

Q1209169.name: War in Abkhazia
Q1209169.blurb: War in Abkhazia: Siege of Tkvarcheli: A helicopter carrying evacuees from Tkvarcheli is shot down, resulting in at least 52 deaths, including 25 children. The incident catalyses more concerted Russian military intervention on behalf of Abkhazia.

Q1209808.name: Battle of Jiuliancheng
Q1209808.blurb: First Sino-Japanese War: Battle of Jiuliancheng: Under the command of General Yamagata Aritomo, the Imperial Japanese Army covertly crosses the Yalu River into Qing territory and launches an assault on the fortifications at Hushan.

Q1210277.name: Ezeiza masacre
Q1210277.blurb: Snipers fire upon left-wing Peronists in Buenos Aires, Argentina, in what is known as the Ezeiza massacre. At least 13 are killed and more than 300 are injured.

Q1210794.name: H-dagurinn
Q1210794.blurb: H-dagurinn in Iceland: Traffic changes from driving on the left to driving on the right overnight.

Q1212980.name: History Will Absolve Me
Q1212980.blurb: Cuban revolutionary Fidel Castro delivers his "History Will Absolve Me" speech, and is sentenced to 15 years' imprisonment by the Fulgencio Batista government for leading an attack on the Moncada Barracks.

Q1214667.name: Great Disappointment
Q1214667.blurb: The Millerites (followers of Baptist preacher William Miller) anticipate the end of the world in conjunction with the Second Advent of Christ. The following day becomes known as the Great Disappointment.

Q1215310.name: Battle of San Juan Hill
aliases: Battle for the San Juan Heights
Q1215310.blurb: Spanish–American War: The Battle of San Juan Hill is fought in Santiago de Cuba, Cuba.

Q1216882.name: The Tracey Ullman Show
Q1216882.blurb: The fictional Simpson family made their first appearance in the short "Good Night", aired in a segment of the The Tracey Ullman Show.

Q1217655.name: Balmis Expedition
aliases: The royal philanthropic expedition of the vaccine
royal philanthropic expedition of the vaccine
Q1217655.blurb: The Balmis Expedition starts in Spain with the aim of vaccinating millions against smallpox in Spanish America and Philippines.

Q1224313.name: 1933 Diexi earthquake
Q1224313.blurb: The Diexi earthquake strikes Mao County, Sichuan, China and kills 9,000 people.

Q1224601.name: Lincoln's House Divided Speech
Q1224601.blurb: Abraham Lincoln delivers his House Divided speech in Springfield, Illinois.

Q1225170.name: Magellan-Elcano expedition
Q1225170.blurb: Magellan–Elcano circumnavigation: Victoria arrives at Seville, completing the first circumnavigation.

Q1225409.name: Moro conflict
Q1225409.blurb: Philippines signs a peace accord with the largest Muslim rebel group, the Moro Islamic Liberation Front, ending decades of conflict.

Q1225445.name: 1929 Murchison earthquake
Q1225445.blurb: The town of Murchison, New Zealand is rocked by a 7.8 magnitude earthquake killing 17. At the time it was New Zealand's worst natural disaster.

Q1229305.name: Julian's Persian expedition
Q1229305.blurb: Roman emperor Julian leaves Antioch with an army of 90,000 to attack the Sasanian Empire, in a campaign which would bring about his own death.

Q1229395.name: Distant Early Warning Line
Q1229395.blurb: Canada and the United States agree to construct the Distant Early Warning Line, a system of radar stations in the far northern Arctic regions of Canada and Alaska.

Q1230348.name: praetorian prefecture of the East
Q1230348.blurb: Rufinus, praetorian prefect of the East, is murdered by Gothic mercenaries under Gainas.

Q1230874.name: 2004 enlargement of the European Union
Q1230874.blurb: European Union enlargement: The EU announces that Cyprus, the Czech Republic, Estonia, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Slovakia, and Slovenia will become members on May 1, 2004.

Q1230986.name: Patriation
Q1230986.blurb: Constitution Act, 1982 Patriation of the Canadian constitution in Ottawa by Proclamation of Elizabeth II, Queen of Canada.

Q1231697.name: Driving car
Q1231697.blurb: Roman emperor Julian is fatally wounded by Sassanid troops in a skirmish close to Samarra while retreating from his failed siege of Ctesiphon.

Q1233004.name: Operation Claymore
Q1233004.blurb: World War II: The United Kingdom launches Operation Claymore on the Lofoten Islands, the first large-scale British Commando raid.

Q1233475.name: Battle of Roncevaux Pass
Q1233475.blurb: The Battle of Roncevaux Pass takes place between the army of Charlemagne and a Basque army.

Q1236473.name: Third Council of Toledo
Q1236473.blurb: Reccared I opens the Third Council of Toledo, marking the entry of Visigothic Spain into the Catholic Church.

Q1236797.name: 2000 Ivorian presidential election
Q1236797.blurb: A wave of protests forces Robert Guéï to step down as president after the Ivorian presidential election.

Q1237867.name: Liberal Wars
Q1237867.blurb: The Battle of Asseiceira is fought; it was the final and decisive engagement of the Liberal Wars in Portugal.

Q1238338.name: Caesar's Civil War
Q1238338.blurb: Caesar's Civil War: Battle of Pharsalus: Julius Caesar decisively defeats Pompey at Pharsalus and Pompey flees to Egypt.

Q1241936.name: Battle of Pákozd
Q1241936.blurb: The Battle of Pákozd is a stalemate between Hungarian and Croatian forces and is the first battle of the Hungarian Revolution.

Q1245004.name: Costa Concordia disaster
Q1245004.blurb: The Italian cruise ship Costa Concordia (pictured) ran aground on a reef and capsized off Isola del Giglio, Tuscany.

Q1247241.name: Hill Street Blues
aliases: List of Hill Street Blues cast members
Q1247241.blurb: The American serial police-procedural television show Hill Street Blues aired its pilot episode, "Hill Street Station".

Q1247268.name: Get Smart
Q1247268.blurb: Mel Brooks and Buck Henry's spy-comedy series Get Smart premieres on NBC Television.

Q1247283.name: Winter of Discontent
Q1247283.blurb: British prime minister James Callaghan was defeated by one vote in a vote of no confidence after his government struggled to cope with widespread strikes during the Winter of Discontent.

Q1247701.name: Last of the Summer Wine
Q1247701.blurb: Last of the Summer Wine, the longest-running sitcom in the world, premiered as an episode of the BBC's Comedy Playhouse.

Q1247957.name: Battle of Trois-Rivières
Q1247957.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Continental Army attackers are driven back at the Battle of Trois-Rivières.

Q1248605.name: Battle of Beachy Head
Q1248605.blurb: Nine Years' War: French naval forces led by Anne Hilarion de Tourville, fresh from their victory at Beachy Head, sail West and launch a raid on the small English town of Teignmouth, leaving it devastated.

Q1250132.name: 1066 Granada Anti-Jewish massacre
Q1250132.blurb: Granada massacre: A Muslim mob storms the royal palace in Granada, crucifies Jewish vizier Joseph ibn Naghrela and massacres most of the Jewish population of the city.

Q1250976.name: Los Alfaques disaster
Q1250976.blurb: Los Alfaques disaster: A truck carrying liquid gas crashes and explodes at a coastal campsite in Tarragona, Spain, killing 216 tourists.

Q1251468.name: 1976 Sabah Air GAF Nomad crash
Q1251468.blurb: A plane crashed near Kota Kinabalu International Airport, Malaysia, killing politicians Fuad Stephens (pictured) and Peter Joinud Mojuntin, along with nine others.

Q1251686.name: Northeast blackout of 1965
Q1251686.blurb: Several U.S. states and parts of Canada are hit by a series of blackouts lasting up to 13 hours in the Northeast blackout of 1965.

Q1251705.name: Doug
Q1251705.blurb: Nickelodeon's first line of "Nicktoons" (Doug, Rugrats & Ren & Stimpy) premiere on the channel.

Q1252684.name: Battle of Toski
Q1252684.blurb: An Anglo-Eyptian army defeats a Mahdist-Sudanese army in the battle of Toski.

Q1252887.name: Operation Redwing
Q1252887.blurb: In Operation Redwing, the first United States airborne hydrogen bomb is dropped over Bikini Atoll in the Pacific Ocean.

Q1252915.name: Siege of Jerusalem
Q1252915.blurb: The first siege of Jerusalem by the Neo-Babylonian Empire ends with the city surrendering to king Nebuchadnezzar II.

Q1254804.name: massacre of Glencoe
Q1254804.blurb: Massacre of Glencoe: Almost 80 Macdonalds at Glen Coe, Scotland are killed early in the morning for not promptly pledging allegiance to the new king, William of Orange.

Q1254917.name: 2003 Istanbul bombings
Q1254917.blurb: The first day of the 2003 Istanbul bombings, in which two car bombs, targeting two synagogues, explode, kill 25 people and wound 300 more.

Q1256503.name: 1946 Faroese independence referendum
Q1256503.blurb: Six days after a referendum, King Christian X of Denmark annuls the declaration of independence of the Faroe Islands.

Q1257296.name: State of Vietnam referendum
Q1257296.blurb: The State of Vietnam voted in a referendum to become a republic.

Q1259139.name: Croatian European Union membership referendum
Q1259139.blurb: Croatia held a referendum in which it voted to become a member of the European Union.

Q1259218.name: Third Battle of Panipat
Q1259218.blurb: The Third Battle of Panipat, the largest battle of the 18th century, is fought in India between the Afghan Durrani Empire under Ahmad Shah Durrani, and the Maratha Empire under Sadashivrao Bhau.

Q1259237.name: Third Anglo-Afghan War
Q1259237.blurb: The Third Anglo-Afghan War ended with the United Kingdom signing a treaty to recognise the independence of the Emirate of Afghanistan.

Q1259275.name: Treaty of San Ildefonso
aliases: The Third Treaty of San Ildefonso
Q1259275.blurb: Via the Third Treaty of San Ildefonso, Spain cedes Louisiana to France, which would sell the land to the United States thirty months later.

Q1260137.name: Mayerling Incident
Q1260137.blurb: Archduke Crown Prince Rudolf of Austria, heir to the Austro-Hungarian crown, is found dead with his mistress Baroness Mary Vetsera in the Mayerling.

Q1260627.name: Milan Decree
Q1260627.blurb: Napoleonic Wars: France issues the Milan Decree, which confirms the Continental System.

Q1261894.name: 1946 Yugoslav Constitution
Q1261894.blurb: Cold War: Yugoslavia's new constitution, modeling that of the Soviet Union, establishes six constituent republics (Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Macedonia, Montenegro, Serbia and Slovenia).

Q1262377.name: Macedonian Front
aliases: Macedonian Campaign of World War I
Q1262377.blurb: World War I: Allied troops break through the Bulgarian defenses on the Macedonian front.

Q1262485.name: Treaty of Rome
Q1262485.blurb: In accordance with the Treaty of Rome, Fiume becomes annexed as part of Italy.

Q1262739.name: JAT Flight 367
Q1262739.blurb: JAT Flight 367 is destroyed by a terrorist bomb, killing 27 of the 28 people on board the DC-9. Flight attendant Vesna Vulović survives with critical injuries.

Q1263360.name: Kandahar massacre
Q1263360.blurb: A U.S. soldier kills 16 civilians in the Panjwayi District of Afghanistan near Kandahar.

Q1264908.name: Battle of Chrysopolis
Q1264908.blurb: Constantine the Great decisively defeats Licinius in the Battle of Chrysopolis, establishing Constantine's sole control over the Roman Empire.

Q1265114.name: Father Rale's War
Q1265114.blurb: Dummer's War begins along the Maine-Massachusetts border.

Q1265674.name: Diocletianic Persecution
Q1265674.blurb: The Diocletianic Persecution, the last and most severe episode of the persecution of Christians in the Roman Empire, began with the publication of a first edict by Roman emperor Diocletian.

Q1265750.name: Battle of Callinicum
Q1265750.blurb: Battle of Callinicum: A Byzantine army under Belisarius is defeated by the Persians at Raqqa (northern Syria).

Q1268842.name: 1996 Croatia USAF CT-43 crash
Q1268842.blurb: A U.S. Air Force CT-43 crashed into a mountainside while attempting an instrument approach to Dubrovnik Airport in Croatia, killing all 35 people on board, including Secretary of Commerce Ron Brown.

Q1269777.name: Dano-Swedish War of 1808-1809
Q1269777.blurb: Dano-Swedish War of 1808–1809: The Battle of Trangen takes place at Trangen in Flisa, Hedemarkens Amt, between Swedish and Norwegian troops.

Q1271324.name: Thrilla in Manila
aliases: Muhammad Ali vs. Joe Frazier III
Q1271324.blurb: Muhammad Ali defeats Joe Frazier in a boxing match in Manila, Philippines.

Q1272132.name: Battle of Stones River
Q1272132.blurb: The Battle of Stones River in Murfreesboro, Tennessee, began with an engagement in which both sides would suffer their highest casualty rates in the American Civil War.

Q1272213.name: SilkAir Flight 185
Q1272213.blurb: SilkAir Flight 185 crashes into the Musi River, near Palembang in Indonesia, killing 104.

Q1273678.name: Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs
Q1273678.blurb: The Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs is signed in New York City.

Q1274389.name: People Power Revolution
aliases: Justice for Aquino Justice for All
Q1274389.blurb: After the 1986 People Power Revolution, the Philippines enacts a new constitution.

Q1274517.name: Treaty on the Prohibition of the Emplacement of Nuclear Weapons and Other Weapons of Mass Destruction on the Sea-Bed and the Ocean Floor and in the Subsoil thereof
Q1274517.blurb: Cold War: The Seabed Arms Control Treaty opens for signature, outlawing nuclear weapons on the ocean floor in international waters.

Q1275200.name: Battle of the Sound
Q1275200.blurb: Second Northern War: Naval forces of the Dutch Republic defeat the Swedes in the Battle of the Sound.

Q1277677.name: Narváez expedition
Q1277677.blurb: Pánfilo de Narváez departs Spain to explore Florida with 600 men – by 1536 only four survive.

Q1278112.name: Eastern Air Lines Flight 663
Q1278112.blurb: Eastern Air Lines Flight 663 crashes into the Atlantic Ocean and explodes, killing all 84 people on board.

Q1278544.name: World War II persecution of Serbs
Q1278544.blurb: World War II: Presaging a campaign of genocide against the Serbs of Croatia, around 190 people were massacred by members of the Ustaše movement in Gudovac.

Q1280245.name: Albanian revolt of 1912
Q1280245.blurb: The Albanian revolt ended when the Ottoman government agreed to meet most of the rebels' demands.

Q1281559.name: Battle of Isonzo
Q1281559.blurb: Theodoric, king of the Ostrogoths, defeats Odoacer at the Battle of Isonzo, forcing his way into Italy.

Q1282732.name: Guatemalan Civil War
aliases: Foreign involvement in the Guatemalan Civil War
Guatemalan Civil War & Genocide of Mayans
Israel's role in the Guatemalan Civil War
Israeli involvement in the Guatemalan Civil War
United States involvement in the Guatemalan Civil War
Q1282732.blurb: Guatemala and leaders of Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unity sign a peace accord ending a 36-year civil war.

Q1284627.name: Edict of Amboise
Q1284627.blurb: The Edict of Amboise is signed, ending the first phase of the French Wars of Religion and granting certain freedoms to the Huguenots.

Q1285054.name: Mise of Amiens
Q1285054.blurb: King Louis IX of France issued the Mise of Amiens, a settlement between King Henry III of England and barons led by Simon de Montfort heavily favouring the former, which later led to the Second Barons' War.

Q1286314.name: Honda Point disaster
Q1286314.blurb: Honda Point disaster: Nine US Navy destroyers run aground off the California coast. Seven are lost, and twenty-three sailors killed.

Q1286657.name: Versailles rail accident
Q1286657.blurb: A train derails and catches fire in Paris, killing between 52 and 200 people.

Q1287158.name: Tay Bridge disaster
Q1287158.blurb: Tay Bridge disaster: The central part of the Tay Rail Bridge in Dundee, Scotland, United Kingdom collapses as a train passes over it, killing 75.

Q1288821.name: Battle of Abu Klea
Q1288821.blurb: A British force defeats a large Dervish army at the Battle of Abu Klea in the Sudan.

Q1290184.name: Congress of Monastir
Q1290184.blurb: The Congress of Manastir establishes the Albanian alphabet.

Q1290260.name: From Hell letter
Q1290260.blurb: The "From Hell" letter allegedly sent by Jack the Ripper is received by investigators.

Q1290590.name: Siege of Jerusalem
aliases: Destruction of Jerusalem by the Babylonians
Q1290590.blurb: The Neo-Babylonian Empire sacks Jerusalem and destroys the First Temple.

Q1290650.name: Council of Agde
Q1290650.blurb: The bishops of Visigothic Gaul meet in the Council of Agde.

Q1290938.name: Government Junta of Chile
Q1290938.blurb: First Government Junta in Chile. Though supposed to rule only during the Peninsular War in Spain, it is in fact the first step towards independence from Spain, and is commemorated as such.

Q1291963.name: Battle of Lake Poyang
Q1291963.blurb: The five-week Battle of Lake Poyang begins, in which the forces of two Chinese rebel leaders (Chen Youliang and Zhu Yuanzhang) meet to decide who will supplant the Yuan dynasty.

Q1292787.name: Fourth Council of Toledo
Q1292787.blurb: Fourth Council of Toledo opens, presided over by Isidore of Seville.

Q1297380.name: Vlieter incident
Q1297380.blurb: The entire Dutch fleet is captured by British forces under the command of Sir Ralph Abercromby and Admiral Sir Charles Mitchell during the War of the Second Coalition.

Q1297556.name: Treaty of Athis-sur-Orge
Q1297556.blurb: A peace treaty between the Flemish and the French is signed at Athis-sur-Orge.

Q1298798.name: Revolt of the Lash
Q1298798.blurb: The crews of three Brazilian warships – all commissioned only months before – and several smaller vessels mutinied against perceived "slavery" being practised in the Brazilian Navy.

Q1300742.name: Battle of Flodden
Q1300742.blurb: James IV of Scotland is defeated and dies in the Battle of Flodden, ending Scotland's involvement in the War of the League of Cambrai.

Q1302237.name: That Was The Week That Was
Q1302237.blurb: The influential British satirical television programme That Was the Week That Was is first broadcast.

Q1305130.name: War of Saint Sabas
Q1305130.blurb: War of Saint Sabas: In the Battle of Trapani, the Venetians defeat a larger Genoese fleet, capturing all its ships.

Q1307876.name: Siege of Fort Ticonderoga
Q1307876.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Siege of Fort Ticonderoga: After a bombardment by British artillery under General John Burgoyne, American forces retreat from Fort Ticonderoga, New York.

Q1308854.name: La Noche Triste
Q1308854.blurb: Spanish conquistadors led by Hernán Cortés fight their way out of Tenochtitlan after nightfall.

Q1311060.name: Melbourne Cup
aliases: The race that stops the nation
Q1311060.blurb: The first Melbourne Cup horse race is held in Melbourne, Australia.

Q1311978.name: Gare de Lyon rail accident
Q1311978.blurb: The Gare de Lyon rail accident in Paris, France, kills 56 people.

Q1311979.name: Newark Bay rail accident
Q1311979.blurb: A Central Railroad of New Jersey commuter train runs through an open drawbridge at the Newark Bay, killing 48.

Q1311998.name: Frankford Junction train wreck
Q1311998.blurb: Pennsylvania Railroad's premier train derails at Frankford Junction in Philadelphia, killing 79 people and injuring 117 others.

Q1312009.name: Wreck of the Old 97
Q1312009.blurb: "Wreck of the Old 97": an American rail disaster, in which 11 people are killed; it later becomes the subject of a popular ballad.

Q1312027.name: Harrow and Wealdstone rail crash
Q1312027.blurb: The Harrow and Wealdstone rail crash in England kills 112 people.

Q1312066.name: El Virilla train accident
Q1312066.blurb: The El Virilla train accident, Costa Rica, kills 248 people and wounds another 93 when a train falls off a bridge over the Río Virilla between Heredia and Tibás.

Q1312088.name: Ashtabula River Railroad Disaster
Q1312088.blurb: The Ashtabula River railroad disaster occurs, leaving 64 injured and 92 dead at Ashtabula, Ohio.

Q1312242.name: Graniteville, South Carolina train crash
Q1312242.blurb: A train collision in Graniteville, South Carolina, United States, releases about 60 tons of chlorine gas.

Q1312258.name: Hammond circus train wreck
Q1312258.blurb: The Hammond Circus Train Wreck kills 86 and injures 127 near Hammond, Indiana.

Q1312335.name: Malbone Street Wreck
Q1312335.blurb: Malbone Street wreck: The worst rapid transit accident in US history occurs under the intersection of Malbone Street and Flatbush Avenue, Brooklyn, New York City, with at least 102 deaths.

Q1312413.name: Quintinshill rail disaster
Q1312413.blurb: Three trains collide in the Quintinshill rail disaster near Gretna Green, Scotland, killing 227 people and injuring 246.

Q1312430.name: 1995 Russell Hill subway accident
Q1312430.blurb: The Russell Hill subway accident in Toronto kills 3 and injures 30, due to a combination of human error and a safety system design flaw.

Q1312534.name: Woodbridge train derailment
Q1312534.blurb: A train derailed while crossing a temporary wooden trestle in Woodbridge, New Jersey, causing 85 deaths.

Q1314054.name: Battle of the Herrings
Q1314054.blurb: English forces under Sir John Fastolf defend a supply convoy carrying rations to the army besieging Orléans in the Battle of the Herrings.

Q1315700.name: Battle of Concepción
Q1315700.blurb: In the first major engagement of the Texas Revolution, the Texian Army repelled a Mexican attack at the grounds of Mission Concepcion south of Downtown San Antonio.

Q1316711.name: Battle of Veracruz
Q1316711.blurb: Mexican Revolution: The last of U.S. forces withdraw from Veracruz, occupied seven months earlier in response to the Tampico Affair.

Q1320031.name: Battle of Binh Gia
Q1320031.blurb: Vietnam War: Viet Cong regiments penetrated the eastern perimeters of the village of Bình Giã, beginning the Battle of Binh Gia.

Q1320053.name: German-occupied Europe
aliases: German-occupied Europe during World War II
Territories occupied by Germany during World War II
Territories occupied by the Nazi Germany
Q1320053.blurb: The Holocaust: Nazi Germany prohibits Jews from emigrating, including in its occupied territories.

Q1320380.name: Alitalia Flight 771
Q1320380.blurb: Alitalia Flight 771 crashes in Junnar, Maharashtra, India, killing 94 people.

Q1321586.name: Moscow Armistice
Q1321586.blurb: World War II: The Moscow Armistice between Finland and the Soviet Union is signed, which officially ended the Continuation War.

Q1322760.name: Naval Battle of Hakodate
Q1322760.blurb: The four-day Naval Battle of Hakodate begins. The newly formed Imperial Japanese Navy defeats the remnants of the Tokugawa shogunate navy in the Sea of Japan off the city of Hakodate, leading to the surrender of the Ezo Republic on May 17.

Q1322777.name: 1987 Rugby World Cup
Q1322777.blurb: First ever Rugby World Cup kicks off with New Zealand playing Italy at Eden Park in Auckland, New Zealand.

Q1323183.name: capture of Mogadishu
Q1323183.blurb: Somali Civil War: Troops of Somalia's Transitional Federal Government and their Ethiopian allies captured Mogadishu unopposed.

Q1323799.name: El Al Flight 1862
Q1323799.blurb: El Al Flight 1862 crashes into two apartment buildings in Amsterdam, killing 43 including 39 on the ground.

Q1324198.name: Treaty of Ghent
Q1324198.blurb: The United States ratifies the Treaty of Ghent – signed in late 1814 – formally ending the War of 1812.

Q1324553.name: Cals cabinet
Q1324553.blurb: The Dutch Cals cabinet fell after Norbert Schmelzer, the leader of the government party, filed a successful motion against the budget, in what later became known as the Night of Schmelzer.

Q1325388.name: Bloody Sunday
Q1325388.blurb: Bloody Sunday clashes in central London.

Q1325495.name: Battle of Santa Cruz de Tenerife
Q1325495.blurb: English Admiral Robert Blake destroys a Spanish silver fleet, under heavy fire from the shore, at the Battle of Santa Cruz de Tenerife.

Q1326489.name: savings and loan crisis
Q1326489.blurb: Savings and loan crisis: The United States Senate Ethics Committee issues a stern censure of California senator Alan Cranston for his "dealings" with savings-and-loan executive Charles Keating.

Q1326527.name: Battle of Cowpens
Q1326527.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Battle of Cowpens: Continental troops under Brigadier General Daniel Morgan defeat British forces under Lieutenant Colonel Banastre Tarleton at the battle in South Carolina.

Q1326831.name: Jingkang Incident
Q1326831.blurb: Jin–Song Wars: Invading Jurchen soldiers from the Jin dynasty besiege and sack Bianjing (Kaifeng), the capital of the Song dynasty of China, and abduct Emperor Qinzong of Song and others, ending the Northern Song period.

Q1326918.name: Ethiopian Airlines Flight 961
Q1326918.blurb: Ethiopian Airlines Flight 961 is hijacked, then crashes into the Indian Ocean off the coast of Comoros after running out of fuel, killing 125.

Q1327790.name: Battle of Chickamauga
Q1327790.blurb: American Civil War: The first day of the Battle of Chickamauga, in northwestern Georgia, the bloodiest two-day battle of the conflict, and the only significant Confederate victory in the war's Western Theater.

Q1328380.name: Battle of Inab
Q1328380.blurb: Raymond of Poitiers is defeated and killed at the Battle of Inab by Nur ad-Din Zangi.

Q1328537.name: Battle of Ourique
Q1328537.blurb: Battle of Ourique: The Almoravids, led by Ali ibn Yusuf, are defeated by Prince Afonso Henriques who is proclaimed King of Portugal.

Q1330826.name: FedEx Express Flight 80
Q1330826.blurb: FedEx Express Flight 80: A McDonnell Douglas MD-11 flying from Guangzhou, China crashes at Tokyo's Narita International Airport, killing both the captain and the co-pilot.

Q1332160.name: Indonesian National Revolution
Q1332160.blurb: Indonesian National Revolution: The Renville Agreement between the Netherlands and Indonesian republicans was ratified, in an ultimately unsuccessful attempt to resolve disputes arising from the Linggadjati Agreement of 1946.

Q1332211.name: Flight 19
Q1332211.blurb: Flight 19, a group of TBF Avengers, disappears in the Bermuda Triangle.

Q1333129.name: 1937 Finnish presidential election
Q1333129.blurb: Risto Ryti, the Prime Minister of Finland,  is elected President of the Republic of Finland in a presidential election, which is exceptionally held by the 1937 electoral college.

Q1333894.name: Ho–Sainteny agreement
Q1333894.blurb: Ho Chi Minh signs an agreement with France which recognizes Vietnam as an autonomous state in the Indochinese Federation and the French Union.

Q1334888.name: Iberia Airlines Flight 610
Q1334888.blurb: A Boeing 727 operating as Iberia Flight 610 crashes Mount Oiz in Spain, killing 148; it is the deadliest accident to occur in Iberia's history and the deadliest to occur in Basque County.

Q1334924.name: Treaty of Brétigny
Q1334924.blurb: The Treaty of Brétigny is ratified, marking the end of the first phase of the Hundred Years' War.

Q1336847.name: Great Fire of Meireki
Q1336847.blurb: The Great Fire of Meireki begins in Edo (now Tokyo), Japan, causing more than 100,000 deaths before it exhausts itself three days later.

Q1337059.name: Battle of Tewkesbury
Q1337059.blurb: Wars of the Roses: The Battle of Tewkesbury: Edward IV defeats a Lancastrian Army and kills Edward of Westminster, Prince of Wales.

Q1338655.name: The Tonight Show
Q1338655.blurb: After 30 seasons Johnny Carson hosts his penultimate episode and last featuring guests (Robin Williams and Bette Midler) of The Tonight Show.

Q1339729.name: 1994 FIFA World Cup qualification (CAF)
Q1339729.blurb: Thirty people died, including players and staff of the Zambia football team and the crew, in a plane crash en route to play a World Cup qualifying match against Senegal.

Q1339735.name: Ems Ukaz
Q1339735.blurb: The secret decree of Ems Ukaz is issued by Russian Tsar Alexander II in the German city of Bad Ems, aimed at stopping the printing and distribution of Ukrainian-language publications in the Russian Empire.

Q1339928.name: Battle of Evesham
Q1339928.blurb: Second Barons' War: Battle of Evesham: The army of Prince Edward (the future king Edward I of England) defeats the forces of rebellious barons led by Simon de Montfort, 6th Earl of Leicester, killing de Montfort and many of his allies.

Q1341539.name: Saur Revolution
Q1341539.blurb: The Saur Revolution begins in Afghanistan, ending the following morning with the murder of Afghan President Mohammed Daoud Khan and the establishment of the Democratic Republic of Afghanistan.

Q1341655.name: 1919-1920 Arab riots in Palestine
Q1341655.blurb: The four-day Nebi Musa riots commence.

Q1341797.name: 2004 World Series
Q1341797.blurb: The Boston Red Sox completed a sweep of the St. Louis Cardinals to win the 2004 World Series, breaking the so-called "Curse of the Bambino".

Q1341824.name: Battle of Lyndanisse
Q1341824.blurb: Northern Crusades: Danish victory at the Battle of Lindanise (modern-day Tallinn) establishes the Danish Duchy of Estonia.

Q1341972.name: Battle of Aljubarrota
Q1341972.blurb: Portuguese Crisis of 1383–85: Battle of Aljubarrota: Portuguese forces commanded by John I of Portugal defeat the Castilian army of John I of Castile.

Q1342285.name: Operation Lumberjack
Q1342285.blurb: World War II: At the beginning of the Battle of Remagen, Allied forces unexpectedly captured the Ludendorff Bridge, which possibly hastened the war's conclusion.

Q1342568.name: Third Anglo-Dutch War
Q1342568.blurb: The Third Anglo-Dutch War: The Battle of Ronas Voe results in the Dutch East India Company ship Wapen van Rotterdam being captured with a death toll of up to 300 Dutch crew and soldiers.

Q1342672.name: Anglo-Powhatan Wars
Q1342672.blurb: The Third Anglo-Powhatan War begins in the Colony of Virginia.

Q1343040.name: Battle of Ushant
Q1343040.blurb: The Battle of Ushant, the first encounter between the French and British fleets in the American Revolutionary War, ended indecisively and led to political disputes in both countries.

Q1343802.name: Madrid Conference of 1991
aliases: Madrid Middle East Peace Conference of 1991.
Q1343802.blurb: The Madrid Conference, an attempt by the international community to revive the Israeli–Palestinian peace process through negotiations, convened.

Q1344365.name: Ensisheim
Q1344365.blurb: The Ensisheim meteorite, the oldest meteorite with a known date of impact, strikes the Earth in a wheat field outside the village of Ensisheim, Alsace, France.

Q1344861.name: kidnapping of Jaycee Lee Dugard
Q1344861.blurb: Eleven-year-old Jaycee Lee Dugard is kidnapped in South Lake Tahoe, California; she would remain a captive until 2009.

Q1344952.name: Relief of Douglas MacArthur
Q1344952.blurb: Korean War: President Truman relieves Douglas MacArthur of the command of American forces in Korea and Japan.

Q1344973.name: dekulakization
Q1344973.blurb: The Politburo of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union orders the confiscation of lands belonging to the Kulaks in a campaign of Dekulakization, resulting in the executions and forced deportations of millions.

Q1344988.name: Expo 67
Q1344988.blurb: Expo 67 officially opens in Montreal, Quebec, Canada with a large opening ceremony broadcast around the world. It opens to the public the next day.

Q1345035.name: 1923 FA Cup Final
Q1345035.blurb: The FA Cup final (crowd and police pictured) between Bolton Wanderers and West Ham United was held on the opening day of the Empire Stadium in London.

Q1345258.name: National Protection War
Q1345258.blurb: The National Protection War breaks out against the Empire of China, as military leaders Cai E and Tang Jiyao proclaim the independence of Yunnan and begin a campaign to restore the Republic.

Q1345835.name: Loving v. Virginia
Q1345835.blurb: The United States Supreme Court in Loving v. Virginia declares all U.S. state laws that prohibit interracial marriage to be unconstitutional.

Q1346429.name: Treaty of Leoben
Q1346429.blurb: War of the First Coalition: The Peace of Leoben is signed by Napoleon Bonaparte and Maximilian, Count of Merveldt, creating an armistice between France and Austria, setting the stage for the Treaty of Campo Formio and ending the War of the First Coalition.[citation needed]

Q1346578.name: 2012 Lamma Island ferry collision
Q1346578.blurb: A ferry collision off the coast of Hong Kong kills 38 people and injures 102 others.

Q1347682.name: firefight at the O.K. Corral
aliases: Gunfight at the O K Corral
Gunfight at the O. K. Corral
Q1347682.blurb: Wyatt Earp and Doc Holliday participate in the Gunfight at the O.K. Corral in Tombstone, Arizona.

Q1347812.name: Treaty of Alexandropol
Q1347812.blurb: Following more than a month of Turkish–Armenian War, the Turkish-dictated Treaty of Alexandropol is concluded.

Q1348781.name: 1786 Kangding-Luding earthquake
Q1348781.blurb: Ten days after being formed by an earthquake, a landslide dam on the Dadu River in China was destroyed by an aftershock, causing a flood that killed an estimated 100,000 people.

Q1348785.name: Basuto Gun War
Q1348785.blurb: The Basuto Gun War breaks out after the Basuto launch a rebellion against the Cape Colony.

Q1348841.name: 1946 Dominican Republic earthquake
Q1348841.blurb: An earthquake of magnitude 8.0 hits northern Dominican Republic. One hundred are killed and 20,000 are left homeless.

Q1348861.name: Gediz earthquake of 1970
Q1348861.blurb: An earthquake strikes western Turkey at about 23:05 local time, killing 1,086 and injuring at least 1,200.

Q1348866.name: 1920 Haiyuan earthquake
Q1348866.blurb: The Haiyuan earthquake of 8.5Mw rocks the Gansu province in China, killing an estimated 200,000.

Q1348869.name: 1783 Calabrian earthquakes
aliases: Earthquake followed by tsunami in Calabria
Q1348869.blurb: The first of five strong earthquakes hit the region of Calabria on the Italian Peninsula, killing more than 32,000 people over a period of nearly two months.

Q1348884.name: 1980 Irpinia earthquake
Q1348884.blurb: The 6.9 Mw Irpinia earthquake shakes southern Italy with a maximum Mercalli intensity of X (Extreme), killing 2,483–4,900, and injuring 7,700–8,934.

Q1348904.name: 2005 Zarand earthquake
Q1348904.blurb: The 6.4 Mw Zarand earthquake shakes the Kerman province of Iran with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VIII (Severe), leaving 612 people dead and 1,411 injured.

Q1348910.name: 1908 Messina earthquake
Q1348910.blurb: The 7.1 Mw Messina earthquake shakes Southern Italy with a maximum Mercalli intensity of XI (Extreme), killing between about 80,000.

Q1348911.name: 1575 Valdivia earthquake
Q1348911.blurb: An earthquake with an estimated magnitude of 8.5Mw strikes Valdivia, Chile.

Q1348954.name: 365 Crete earthquake
Q1348954.blurb: The Crete earthquake occurs with a maximum Mercalli intensity of XI (Extreme), causing a destructive tsunami that affects the coasts of Libya and Egypt, especially Alexandria. Many thousands are killed.

Q1348955.name: Reapers' War
Q1348955.blurb: Reapers' War: The Junta de Braços (parliamentary assembly) of the Principality of Catalonia accepts the proposal of establishment of the Catalan Republic, under French protection.

Q1348976.name: July 2006 Java earthquake
Q1348976.blurb: The 7.7 Mw Pangandaran tsunami earthquake severely affects the Indonesian island of Java, killing 668 people, and leaving more than 9,000 injured.

Q1349539.name: Kyshtym disaster
Q1349539.blurb: The Kyshtym disaster is the third-worst nuclear accident ever recorded.

Q1349804.name: Council of Pisa
Q1349804.blurb: The Council of Pisa convenes, in an attempt to heal the Western Schism.

Q1349904.name: aftermath of World War II
aliases: Aftermath of the Second World War
Aftermath of the World War II
Economic effects of World War II
Economic history of World War II
Global effects of World War II
Q1349904.blurb: Aftermath of World War II: In Tokyo, the International Military Tribunal for the Far East sentences seven Japanese military and government officials, including General Hideki Tojo, to death for their roles in World War II.

Q1350221.name: Erfurt latrine disaster
Q1350221.blurb: Erfurt latrine disaster: At a Hoftag, a meeting with local notables, organized by Henry VI, the building collapses and many of the nobles in attendance drown in the sewage pits below.

Q1351111.name: Dove World Outreach Center Quran-burning controversy
Q1351111.blurb: After protests against the burning of the Quran turn violent, a mob attacks a United Nations compound in Mazar-i-Sharif, Afghanistan, resulting in the deaths of fourteen people, including seven UN workers.

Q1351498.name: Operation Solomon
Q1351498.blurb: Israel conducts Operation Solomon, evacuating Ethiopian Jews to Israel.

Q1351598.name: Gol Transportes Aéreos Flight 1907
Q1351598.blurb: A Boeing 737 and an Embraer 600 collide in mid-air, killing 154 people and triggering a Brazilian aviation crisis.

Q1352215.name: Polish–Russian War of 1792
aliases: War in Defence of the Constitution
War in Defense of the Constitution
War in defence of the consitution
War in the Defence of the Constitution
War in the defence of constitution
Q1352215.blurb: The Great Sejm of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth was disbanded following the Russian invasion of Poland.

Q1352401.name: Bombardment of Kagoshima
Q1352401.blurb: The Anglo-Satsuma War begins between the Satsuma Domain of Japan and the United Kingdom (Traditional Japanese date: July 2, 1863).

Q1353216.name: 2012 India blackouts
Q1353216.blurb: A power grid failure in Delhi leaves more than 300 million people without power in northern India.

Q1354080.name: Battle of Muret
Q1354080.blurb: Albigensian Crusade: Simon de Montfort, 5th Earl of Leicester, defeats Peter II of Aragon at the Battle of Muret.

Q1354172.name: McMahon Line
Q1354172.blurb: China launches simultaneous offensives in Ladakh and across the McMahon Line, igniting the Sino-Indian War.

Q1355145.name: Italian War of 1494–1495
Q1355145.blurb: First Italian War: Battle of Fornovo: Charles VIII defeats the Holy League.

Q1355161.name: Cusco Declaration
Q1355161.blurb: The Cusco Declaration is signed in Cusco, Peru, establishing the South American Community of Nations.

Q1355177.name: Battle of Pankalia
Q1355177.blurb: Byzantine forces loyal to emperor Basil II under Bardas Phokas the Younger defeat rebel forces under Bardas Skleros in the battle of Pankaleia (approximate date).

Q1355391.name: Battle of Appomattox Court House
aliases: Surrender of Robert E. Lee to Ulysses S. Grant
The Battle of Appomattox Court House
Q1355391.blurb: American Civil War: Robert E. Lee surrenders the Army of Northern Virginia (26,765 troops) to Ulysses S. Grant at Appomattox Court House, Virginia, effectively ending the war.

Q1355516.name: People's Olympiad
Q1355516.blurb: Spanish Civil War: The CNT and UGT call a general strike in Spain – mobilizing workers' militias against the Nationalist forces. People's Olympiad of Barcelona cancelled.

Q1356047.name: execution of the Romanov family
aliases: Execution of the Romanov family by Bolsheviks
Q1356047.blurb: Tsar Nicholas II of Russia and his immediate family and retainers are executed by Bolshevik Chekists at the Ipatiev House in Yekaterinburg, Russia.

Q1356165.name: discovery of Neptune
Q1356165.blurb: Astronomers Urbain Le Verrier, John Couch Adams and Johann Gottfried Galle collaborate on the discovery of Neptune.

Q1357802.name: Treaty of Compiègne
Q1357802.blurb: Signing of the Treaty of Compiègne between France and the Netherlands.

Q1358166.name: Curse of the Bambino
Q1358166.blurb: The Boston Red Sox completed a sweep of the St. Louis Cardinals to win the 2004 World Series, breaking the so-called "Curse of the Bambino".

Q1358264.name: Zappas Olympics
Q1358264.blurb: Sponsored by Greek businessman Evangelos Zappas, the first modern revival of the Olympic Games took place in Athens.

Q1358726.name: 1130 papal election
Q1358726.blurb: The troubled 1130 papal election exposes a rift within the College of Cardinals.

Q1359529.name: Government of India Act 1858
Q1359529.blurb: The Government of India Act 1858 replaces Company rule in India with that of the British Raj.

Q1359641.name: Battle of Tolentino
Q1359641.blurb: Neapolitan War: Joachim Murat, King of Naples, is defeated by the Austrians at the Battle of Tolentino, the decisive engagement of the war.

Q1361124.name: The Ren & Stimpy Show
aliases: Quest for the Shaven Yak Starring Ren Hoek and Stimpy
Quest for the Shaven Yak Starring Ren Hoëk and Stimpy
Ren & Stimpy in Quest for the Shaven Yak
Q1361124.blurb: Nickelodeon's first line of "Nicktoons" (Doug, Rugrats & Ren & Stimpy) premiere on the channel.

Q1361210.name: Battle of Christmas Island
Q1361210.blurb: World War II: Japanese forces invade Christmas Island, then a British possession.

Q1361354.name: Nine Years' War
Q1361354.blurb: Nine Years' War: Battle of the Yellow Ford: Irish forces under Hugh O'Neill, Earl of Tyrone, defeat an English expeditionary force under Henry Bagenal.

Q1361674.name: Treaties of Velasco
Q1361674.blurb: The Treaties of Velasco are signed in Velasco, Texas.

Q1361929.name: Indonesia–Malaysia confrontation
Q1361929.blurb: Indonesia–Malaysia confrontation: British forces repelled a surprise Indonesian attack on a base at Plaman Mapu in Sarawak.

Q1362021.name: Siege of Corinth
Q1362021.blurb: American Civil War: The Siege of Corinth begins as Union forces under General Henry Halleck move to engage Confederate forces led by General P. G. T. Beauregard.

Q1362188.name: Battle of Talikota
Q1362188.blurb: The Deccan Sultanates defeat Rama Raya of the Vijayanagara Empire at the Battle of Talikota, resulting in over 100,000 casualties and the destruction of the capital Vijayanagara.

Q1363925.name: Battle of Port Arthur
Q1363925.blurb: Japanese forces launch a surprise attack against Russian-controlled Port Arthur, marking the start of the Russo-Japanese war.

Q1363982.name: 1991 Russian presidential election
Q1363982.blurb: In modern Russia's first democratic election, Boris Yeltsin is elected as the President of Russia.

Q1364902.name: Whitman massacre
Q1364902.blurb: Missionaries Dr. Marcus Whitman, his wife Narcissa, and 15 others are killed by Cayuse and Umatilla Indians, causing the Cayuse War.

Q1365425.name: San Remo conference
Q1365425.blurb: At the San Remo conference, the principal Allied Powers of World War I adopt a resolution to determine the allocation of Class "A" League of Nations mandates for administration of the former Ottoman-ruled lands of the Middle East.

Q1365483.name: Treaty of Alcañices
Q1365483.blurb: The Treaty of Alcañices, mediated by the pope, between the king Denis of Portugal and king Ferdinand IV of Castile defines the border between the two countries and establishes an alliance of friendship.

Q1365513.name: Typhoon Xangsane
Q1365513.blurb: Typhoon Xangsane passes over Manila after impacting parts of Southern Luzon and Eastern Visayas, becoming the strongest to affect the Philippine capital in 11 years.

Q1366089.name: Battle of Fort Henry
Q1366089.blurb: American Civil War: Forces under the command of Ulysses S. Grant and Andrew H. Foote give the Union its first victory of the war, capturing Fort Henry, Tennessee in the Battle of Fort Henry.

Q1366196.name: Gothic War of 376–382
Q1366196.blurb: Gothic War: Battle of Adrianople: A large Roman army led by Emperor Valens is defeated by the Visigoths. Valens is killed along with over half of his army.

Q1366606.name: 1993 Zambia national football team plane crash
Q1366606.blurb: Most of the Zambia national football team lose their lives in a plane crash off Libreville, Gabon en route to Dakar, Senegal to play a 1994 FIFA World Cup qualifying match against Senegal.

Q1368313.name: Comayagua prison fire
Q1368313.blurb: Three hundred and sixty people die in a fire at a Honduran prison in the city of Comayagua.

Q1368318.name: National Assembly of Thailand
Q1368318.blurb: Thailand elects Orapin Chaiyakan, the first female member of Thailand's Parliament.

Q1369379.name: Battle of Bạch Đằng
Q1369379.blurb: Mongol invasions of Vietnam: Yuan forces are defeated by Trần forces in the Battle of Bach Dang in present-day northern Vietnam.

Q1369423.name: Toledo War
Q1369423.blurb: The Toledo War unofficially ends as the "Frostbitten Convention" votes to accept Congress' terms for admitting Michigan as a U.S. state.

Q1370527.name: Brazilian military government (1964–1985)
aliases: Labour Rights in the Brazilian Military Dictatorship
United States support for the military dictatorship in Brazil
Q1370527.blurb: Carlos Lamarca leads the first urban guerrilla action against the military dictatorship of Brazil in São Paulo, by robbing two banks.

Q1374042.name: 1967 USS Forrestal fire
Q1374042.blurb: Vietnam War: Off the coast of North Vietnam the USS Forrestal catches on fire in the worst U.S. naval disaster since World War II, killing 134.

Q1375813.name: Battle of Oriskany
Q1375813.blurb: The Battle of Oriskany, one of the bloodiest battles of the American Revolutionary War, was fought about 6 mi (10 km) east of Fort Stanwix, New York.

Q1376234.name: 1939 conclave
Q1376234.blurb: Cardinal Eugenio Pacelli is elected Pope and takes the name Pius XII.

Q1376434.name: Corfu Channel incident
Q1376434.blurb: United Nations Security Council Resolution 22 relating to Corfu Channel incident is adopted.

Q1377385.name: Tōkaimura criticality accident
Q1377385.blurb: The Tokaimura nuclear accident causes the deaths of two technicians in Japan's second-worst nuclear accident.

Q1377536.name: Latvian–Soviet Peace Treaty (1920)
Q1377536.blurb: The Latvian–Soviet Peace Treaty, which relinquished Russia's authority and pretenses to Latvia, is signed, ending the Latvian War of Independence.

Q1377639.name: Gettysburg campaign
Q1377639.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Aldie in the Gettysburg campaign.

Q1378244.name: Washington Agreement
Q1378244.blurb: Bosnia's Bosniaks and Croats sign the Washington Agreement, ending war between the Croatian Republic of Herzeg-Bosnia and the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and establishing the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

Q1378270.name: Battle of Jerusalem
Q1378270.blurb: World War I: Field Marshal Allenby captures Jerusalem from the Ottoman Empire.

Q1379845.name: Kravica attack
Q1379845.blurb: Bosnian War: The Bosnian Army executes a surprise attack at the village of Kravica in Srebrenica.

Q1380261.name: We begin bombing in five minutes
Q1380261.blurb: "We begin bombing in five minutes": United States President Ronald Reagan, while running for re-election, jokes while preparing to make his weekly Saturday address on National Public Radio.

Q1384023.name: Varlık Vergisi
Q1384023.blurb: The Turkish parliament passes the Varlık Vergisi, a capital tax mostly levied on non-Muslim citizens with the unofficial aim to inflict financial ruin on them and end their prominence in the country's economy.

Q1384586.name: Enschede fireworks disaster
Q1384586.blurb: A fireworks storage depot explodes in a residential neighborhood in Enschede, Netherlands, killing 23 people and injuring 950 others.

Q1384607.name: 2008 Gërdec explosions
Q1384607.blurb: Stockpiles of obsolete ammunition explode at an ex-military ammunition depot in the village of Gërdec, Albania, killing 26 people.

Q1387983.name: First Battle of Memphis
Q1387983.blurb: American Civil War: The First Battle of Memphis, a naval engagement fought on the Mississippi River, results in the capture of Memphis, Tennessee by Union forces from the Confederates.

Q1388058.name: Battle of Magersfontein
Q1388058.blurb: Second Boer War: In the Battle of Magersfontein the Boers commanded by general Piet Cronjé inflict a defeat on the forces of the British Empire commanded by Lord Methuen trying to relieve the Siege of Kimberley.

Q1392134.name: 1999 Oklahoma tornado outbreak
Q1392134.blurb: The southwestern portion of Oklahoma City is devastated by an F5 tornado, killing forty-five people, injuring 665, and causing $1 billion in damage. The tornado is one of 66 from the 1999 Oklahoma tornado outbreak. This tornado also produces the highest wind speed ever recorded, measured at 484 ± 32 kilometres per hour (301 ± 20 mph). In meteorology, the term "May 3" is synonymous with the F5 tornado.

Q1392596.name: Franco-Italian Agreement
Q1392596.blurb: Benito Mussolini and French Foreign Minister Pierre Laval sign the Franco-Italian Agreement.

Q1392699.name: Battle of Blood River
Q1392699.blurb: Great Trek: Battle of Blood River: Voortrekkers led by Andries Pretorius and Sarel Cilliers defeat Zulu impis, led by Dambuza (Nzobo) and Ndlela kaSompisi in what is today KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa.

Q1393367.name: Fairness Doctrine
Q1393367.blurb: The Federal Communications Commission rescinds the Fairness Doctrine which had required radio and television stations to give equal time to opposing views.

Q1394698.name: Falls Curfew
Q1394698.blurb: The Troubles: The "Falls Curfew" begins in Belfast, Northern Ireland.

Q1397233.name: Trial of Nicolae and Elena Ceaușescu
