Q1397233.blurb: Romanian Revolution: Communist dictator Nicolae Ceaușescu and his wife Elena were condemned to death on a wide range of charges and executed.

Q1398233.name: Pogrom of Armenians in Baku
Q1398233.blurb: A seven-day pogrom breaks out against the Armenian civilian population of Baku, Azerbaijan, during which Armenians were beaten, tortured, murdered, and expelled from the city.

Q1400402.name: Reconquest of Constantinople
Q1400402.blurb: The city of Constantinople is recaptured by Nicaean forces under the command of Alexios Strategopoulos, re-establishing the Byzantine Empire.

Q1400684.name: 869 Jōgan earthquake
Q1400684.blurb: The 8.4–9.0 Mw Sanriku earthquake strikes the area around Sendai in northern Honshu, Japan. Inundation from the tsunami extended several kilometers inland.

Q1401251.name: Profumo Affair
Q1401251.blurb: Profumo affair: During the trial of Stephen Ward, Mandy Rice-Davies uttered the phrase "Well he would, wouldn't he?"

Q1401416.name: computer animation
Q1401416.blurb: Steve Jobs purchased Pixar from Lucasfilm and launched it as an independent computer-animation studio.

Q1402078.name: Warsaw Uprising
aliases: After effects of the Warsaw Uprising
Military description of the Warsaw Uprising
Military history of the Warsaw Uprising
Warsaw Uprising facts, figures, and statistics
Warsaw uprising facts, figures and statistics
Q1402078.blurb: World War II: The Warsaw Uprising against the Nazi German occupation breaks out in Warsaw, Poland.

Q1402751.name: Battle of Pichincha
Q1402751.blurb: Battle of Pichincha: Antonio José de Sucre secures the independence of the Presidency of Quito.

Q1404472.name: Italian Renaissance
Q1404472.blurb: Duccio's Maestà, a seminal artwork of the early Italian Renaissance, is unveiled and installed in Siena Cathedral in Siena, Italy.

Q1406897.name: Battle of Roundway Down
Q1406897.blurb: English Civil War: Battle of Roundway Down: In England, Henry Wilmot, 1st Earl of Rochester, commanding the Royalist forces, heavily defeats the Parliamentarian forces led by Sir William Waller.

Q1409271.name: Fettmilch Rising
Q1409271.blurb: Fettmilch uprising: Jews are expelled from Frankfurt, Holy Roman Empire, following the plundering of the Judengasse.

Q1411096.name: Conquest of California
Q1411096.blurb: US troops occupy Monterey and Yerba Buena, thus beginning the US conquest of California.

Q1412033.name: The Day the Music Died
Q1412033.blurb: Rock and roll musicians Buddy Holly, Ritchie Valens, and J. P. "The Big Bopper" Richardson are killed in a plane crash along with the pilot near Clear Lake, Iowa, an event later known as The Day the Music Died.

Q1413732.name: Kashmir conflict
aliases: Civil unrest in Jammu and Kashmir
Kashmir - the most dangerous place in the world
Q1413732.blurb: United Nations Security Council Resolution 47 relating to Kashmir conflict is adopted.

Q1414409.name: Sedan
Q1414409.blurb: As a part of Operation Plowshare, the Sedan nuclear test takes place.

Q1414593.name: Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
aliases: 2010 Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
Comprehensive 1099 Taxpayer Protection and Repayment of Exchange Subsidy Overpayments Act of 2011
Criticism of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
Delay in application of the Individual Health Insurance Mandate
Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act 2010
Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act of 2010
Public opinion on the Affordable Care Act
Service Members Home Ownership Tax Act of 2009
The Patient Protection & Affordable Care Act
The Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
Q1414593.blurb: The Affordable Care Act becomes law in the United States.

Q1414752.name: Pacific Air Lines Flight 773
Q1414752.blurb: Pacific Airlines Flight 773 is hijacked by Francisco Gonzales and crashes in Contra Costa County, California, killing 44.

Q1414900.name: El Mozote massacre
Q1414900.blurb: El Mozote massacre: Armed forces in El Salvador kill an estimated 900 civilians in an anti-guerrilla campaign during the Salvadoran Civil War.

Q1414998.name: Battle of the Tenaru
Q1414998.blurb: World War II: The Imperial Japanese Army lost the Battle of the Tenaru, the first of its three major land offensives during the Guadalcanal campaign.

Q1416369.name: Battle of Crysler's Farm
Q1416369.blurb: War of 1812: Battle of Crysler's Farm: British and Canadian forces defeat a larger American force, causing the Americans to abandon their Saint Lawrence campaign.

Q1417059.name: First Fitna
aliases: The Fitna of the Killing of Uthman
Q1417059.blurb: First Fitna: In the Battle of Siffin, troops led by Ali ibn Abu Talib clash with those led by Muawiyah I.

Q1417205.name: Battle of Mons
Q1417205.blurb: World War I: During the retreat from Mons, the British II Corps commanded by General Sir Horace Smith-Dorrien fights a vigorous and successful defensive action at Le Cateau.

Q1417338.name: 1981 Irish hunger strike
Q1417338.blurb: After a 66-day hunger strike, Irish republican Bobby Sands died of starvation in HM Prison Maze.

Q1417490.name: 1929 Hebron massacre
Q1417490.blurb: Hebron Massacre during the 1929 Palestine riots: Arab attacks on the Jewish community in Hebron in the British Mandate of Palestine occur, continuing until the next day, resulting in the death of 65–68 Jews and the remaining Jews being forced to leave the city.

Q1417787.name: Finno-Soviet Treaty of 1948
Q1417787.blurb: The Finno-Soviet Treaty is signed in Moscow.

Q1417847.name: Long Depression
Q1417847.blurb: Der Krach: The Vienna stock exchange crash begins the Panic of 1873 and heralds the Long Depression.

Q1418582.name: Russo-Persian War of 1722–23
aliases: Persian Expedition of Peter the Great
Persian campaign of Peter the Great
Q1418582.blurb: After a siege and bombardment by cannon, Baku surrenders to the Russians.

Q1418831.name: Operation Demetrius
Q1418831.blurb: The Troubles: British forces began arresting and interning suspected Irish republican militants in Northern Ireland.

Q1419459.name: Battle of the Chesapeake
Q1419459.blurb: Battle of the Chesapeake in the American Revolutionary War: The British Navy is repelled by the French Navy, contributing to the British surrender at Yorktown.

Q1419491.name: 2012 Mount Salak Sukhoi Superjet crash
Q1419491.blurb: The pilots of a Sukhoi Superjet, ignoring alerts from the terrain warning system, crashed the aircraft into Mount Salak in Indonesia, resulting in the deaths of all 45 people on board.

Q1420115.name: Russo-Persian War of 1826–28
Q1420115.blurb: Russo-Persian War: The Russian army under Ivan Paskevich storms Yerevan, ending a millennium of Muslim domination of Armenia.

Q1420226.name: Port Chicago disaster
Q1420226.blurb: Port Chicago disaster: Near the San Francisco Bay, two ships laden with ammunition for the war explode in Port Chicago, California, killing 320.

Q1420382.name: Battle of Tel el-Kebir
Q1420382.blurb: Anglo-Egyptian War: The Battle of Tel el-Kebir is fought.

Q1420512.name: Nixon Shock
Q1420512.blurb: President Richard Nixon completes the break from the gold standard by ending convertibility of the United States dollar into gold by foreign investors.

Q1420526.name: Tenentism
Q1420526.blurb: Brazilian Army rebels took over Fort Copacabana and launched a rebellion in Rio de Janeiro against President Epitácio Pessoa and President-elect Artur Bernardes.

Q1421431.name: October 1978 conclave
Q1421431.blurb: Cardinal Karol Wojtyła is elected to the papacy as Pope John Paul II, he becomes the first non-Italian pontiff since 1523.

Q1423559.name: Larry King Live
Q1423559.blurb: Appearing on the talk show Larry King Live, U.S. industrialist Ross Perot announced that he would begin a presidential campaign if "ordinary people" wanted him to run for office.

Q1424076.name: Battle of Mursa Major
Q1424076.blurb: Constantius II defeats the usurper Magnentius.

Q1424647.name: Comprehensive Peace Agreement
Q1424647.blurb: The Sudan People's Liberation Movement and the Government of Sudan sign the Comprehensive Peace Agreement to end the Second Sudanese Civil War.

Q1425362.name: Battle of Cajamarca
Q1425362.blurb: Spanish conquest of Peru: Conquistador Francisco Pizarro orchestrated a surprise attack in Cajamarca, capturing the Inca emperor, Atahualpa.

Q1425658.name: Battle of Chacabuco
Q1425658.blurb: An Argentine/Chilean patriotic army, after crossing the Andes, defeats Spanish troops at the Battle of Chacabuco.

Q1425882.name: Battle of the Wilderness
Q1425882.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of the Wilderness begins in Spotsylvania County.

Q1426448.name: Smiling Buddha
Q1426448.blurb: India conducted its first nuclear test explosion at Pokhran, the first confirmed nuclear test by a nation outside the five permanent members of the United Nations Security Council.

Q1427012.name: Northwest Airlines Flight 253
Q1427012.blurb: Aboard Northwest Airlines Flight 253, Umar Farouk Abdulmutallab attempted to detonate plastic explosives hidden in his underwear.

Q1427211.name: Flash Airlines Flight 604
Q1427211.blurb: Flash Airlines Flight 604 crashes into the Red Sea, resulting in 148 deaths, making it one of the deadliest aviation accidents in Egyptian history.

Q1427217.name: 2010 Flash Crash
Q1427217.blurb: In just 36 minutes, the Dow Jones Industrial Average plunges nearly 1,000 points in what is known as the 2010 Flash Crash.

Q1427630.name: Battle of Adrianople
Q1427630.blurb: Combined Bulgarian and Cuman army under Kalojan ambushes and defeats forces of the Latin Empire of Constantinople in the Battle of Adrianople.

Q1428147.name: Banat Air Flight 166
Q1428147.blurb: Banat Air Flight 166 crashes in Sommacampagna near Verona Villafranca Airport in Verona, Italy, killing 49.

Q1428169.name: Battle of Barnet
Q1428169.blurb: In England, the Yorkists under Edward IV defeat the Lancastrians under the Earl of Warwick at the Battle of Barnet; the Earl is killed and Edward resumes the throne.

Q1429256.name: War of the League of Cognac
aliases: The War of the League of Cognac
Q1429256.blurb: War of the League of Cognac: The French army under Francis de Bourbon was destroyed in Lombardy, Italy, by the Spanish army.

Q1429332.name: Convention on Psychotropic Substances
Q1429332.blurb: The Convention on Psychotropic Substances is signed at Vienna.

Q1430504.name: Flight of the Earls
Q1430504.blurb: The Flight of the Earls takes place in Ireland (14 September N.S.).

Q1430939.name: Battle of Fontenoy
Q1430939.blurb: In the Battle of Fontenay-en-Puisaye, forces led by Charles the Bald and Louis the German defeat the armies of Lothair I of Italy and Pepin II of Aquitaine.

Q1431007.name: Treaty of Breda
Q1431007.blurb: The treaty of Breda ends the second Anglo-Dutch War and grants England in possession of New Amsterdam.

Q1431686.name: Spirou
Q1431686.blurb: Belgian artist Peyo's comic characters, the Smurfs, make their debut in Spirou magazine.

Q1432624.name: Genkō War
Q1432624.blurb: Genkō War: Forces loyal to Emperor Go-Daigo seize Tōshō-ji during the Siege of Kamakura. Hōjō Takatoki and other members of the Hōjō clan commit suicide, ending the rule of the Kamakura shogunate.

Q1433190.name: Iraq disarmament crisis
Q1433190.blurb: Iraq disarmament crisis: UNMOVIC Executive Chairman Hans Blix reports to the United Nations Security Council that disarmament inspectors have found no weapons of mass destruction in Ba'athist Iraq.

Q1434037.name: Sknyliv air show disaster
Q1434037.blurb: Ukraine airshow disaster: A Sukhoi Su-27 fighter crashes during an air show at Lviv, Ukraine killing 77 and injuring more than 500 others, making it the deadliest air show disaster in history.

Q1434045.name: 1943 Gibraltar B-24 crash
Q1434045.blurb: The aircraft carrying Władysław Sikorski, prime minister of the Polish government-in-exile, crashed off Gibraltar, killing him and fifteen others and leading to several conspiracy theories.

Q1434047.name: 1988 Remscheid A-10 crash
Q1434047.blurb: A United States Air Force A-10 Thunderbolt II crashes into an apartment complex in Remscheid, Germany, killing five people and injuring 50 others.

Q1434078.name: Interflug Flight 450
Q1434078.blurb: An Ilyushin Il-62 airliner crashes near Königs Wusterhausen, East Germany killing 156 people.

Q1434082.name: 1945 Empire State Building B-25 crash
Q1434082.blurb: A U.S. Army B-25 bomber crashes into the 79th floor of the Empire State Building killing 14 and injuring 26.

Q1434099.name: Interflug Flight 102
Q1434099.blurb: Interflug Flight 102 crashes during a rejected takeoff from Berlin Schönefeld Airport, killing 21 people.

Q1434101.name: 1960 Munich Convair 340 crash
Q1434101.blurb: Munich C-131 crash: Twenty passengers and crew on board as well as 32 people on the ground are killed.

Q1434107.name: Stockport air disaster
Q1434107.blurb: Seventy-two people are killed when a Canadair C-4 Argonaut crashes at Stockport in England.

Q1434437.name: 2012 Krasnodar Krai floods
Q1434437.blurb: At least 172 people are killed in a flash flood in the Krasnodar Krai region of Russia.

Q1434556.name: Flying Tiger Line Flight 923
Q1434556.blurb: Flying Tiger Line Flight 923, a Lockheed L-1049H Super Constellation registered as N6923C, ditches into the Atlantic Ocean killing 28 out the 76 occupants onboard. The remaining 48 were rescued six hours later.

Q1434602.name: Libyan–Egyptian War
Q1434602.blurb: The start of the four-day-long Libyan–Egyptian War.

Q1435156.name: Methuen Treaty
Q1435156.blurb: Portugal and England sign the Methuen Treaty which allows Portugal to export wines to England on favorable trade terms.

Q1436140.name: 1940 Finnish presidential election
Q1436140.blurb: Risto Ryti, the Prime Minister of Finland,  is elected President of the Republic of Finland in a presidential election, which is exceptionally held by the 1937 electoral college.

Q1436705.name: Battle of Tuttlingen
Q1436705.blurb: Thirty Years' War: Holy Roman Empire, Bavarian and Spanish forces led by Franz von Mercy defeated the French army in Germany led by Marshal Josias von Rantzau at the Battle of Tuttlingen.

Q1437630.name: solar eclipse of August 21, 2017
Q1437630.blurb: A solar eclipse traverses the continental United States.

Q1438180.name: Battle of Plymouth
Q1438180.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Plymouth begins: Confederate forces attack Plymouth, North Carolina.

Q1438686.name: Battle of Plymouth
Q1438686.blurb: Battle of Plymouth: Inconclusive naval action between the fleets of Michiel de Ruyter and George Ayscue in the First Anglo-Dutch War.

Q1439106.name: Army–Navy Game
Q1439106.blurb: Instant replay makes its debut during the Army-Navy football game in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States.

Q1439449.name: gymnastics at the 1976 Summer Olympics – women's uneven bars
aliases: gymnastics at the 1976 Summer Olympics - women's uneven bars
Q1439449.blurb: At the Olympic Games in Montreal, Nadia Comăneci (pictured) became the first gymnast to score a perfect 10 for her routine on the uneven bars.

Q1439744.name: Alitalia Flight 4128
Q1439744.blurb: Alitalia Flight 4128 crashes into the Tyrrhenian Sea while on approach to Falcone Borsellino Airport in Palermo, Italy, killing 108.

Q1441451.name: Guayaquil Conference
Q1441451.blurb: José de San Martín arrives in Guayaquil, Ecuador, to meet with Simón Bolívar.

Q1442050.name: Battle of Maldon
Q1442050.blurb: Battle of Maldon: The English, led by Byrhtnoth, Ealdorman of Essex, are defeated by a band of inland-raiding Vikings near Maldon, Essex.

Q1442715.name: 2004 SuperFerry 14 bombing
Q1442715.blurb: A bombing of a SuperFerry by Abu Sayyaf in the Philippines' worst terrorist attack kills more than 100 passengers.

Q1443091.name: Battle of Garigliano
Q1443091.blurb: The Battle of Garigliano was fought between a Spanish army under Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba and a French army commanded by Ludovico II, Marquess of Saluzzo.

Q1443926.name: Treaty on the Creation of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics
aliases: Agreement on the formation of the USSR
Founding document of the Soviet Union
Treaty of Creation of the Soviet Union
Treaty of Creation of the USSR
Treaty on the Creation of the Soviet Union
Treaty on the Creation of the USSR
Treaty on the Formation of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics
Q1443926.blurb: The Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR) is formed.

Q1444930.name: Philadelphia campaign
Q1444930.blurb: American Revolutionary War: British troops capture and begin the occupation of Philadelphia, which had been serving as the American capital city, during the Philadelphia campaign.

Q1445532.name: Battle of Lule Burgas
Q1445532.blurb: Bulgaria defeats the Ottoman Empire in the Battle of Lule Burgas, the bloodiest battle of the First Balkan War, which opens her way to Constantinople.

Q1447505.name: Operation Avalanche
Q1447505.blurb: World War II: The Allies land at Salerno and Taranto, Italy.

Q1451644.name: Cato Street Conspiracy
Q1451644.blurb: Cato Street Conspiracy: A plot to murder all the British cabinet ministers is exposed and the conspirators arrested.

Q1455240.name: Peace of Prague
Q1455240.blurb: Thirty Years' War: The Peace of Prague is signed.

Q1455917.name: Umayyad conquest of Hispania
aliases: Muslim conquest of the Iberian Peninsula
Arab conquest of the Iberian Peninsula
Islamic conquest of the Iberian Peninsula
Umayyad conquest of the Iberian peninsula
Umayyad conquest of the Visigothic Kingdom
Q1455917.blurb: Islamic conquest of Hispania: Moorish troops led by Tariq ibn Ziyad land at Gibraltar to begin their invasion of the Iberian Peninsula (Al-Andalus).

Q1456086.name: Nez Perce War
Q1456086.blurb: Nez Perce War: Both the Nez Perce and the United States Army suffered numerous casualties at the Battle of the Big Hole, which ended conclusively.

Q1456414.name: Treaty of Anagni
Q1456414.blurb: The Treaty of Anagni, an attempt mediated by the papacy to end the War of the Sicilian Vespers, is signed by the crown of Aragon, the kingdom of France and kingdom of Naples.

Q1456454.name: Anglo-Afghan Treaty of 1919
Q1456454.blurb: The Anglo-Afghan Treaty of 1919 is signed. It establishes peaceful relations between Afghanistan and the UK, and confirms the Durand line as the mutual border. In return, the UK is no longer obligated to subsidize the Afghan government.

Q1456533.name: Battle of Guinegate
Q1456533.blurb: Battle of Guinegate: French troops of King Louis XI are defeated by the Burgundians led by Archduke Maximilian of Habsburg.

Q1456635.name: Treaty of Lodi
Q1456635.blurb: The Treaty of Lodi is signed, establishing a balance of power among northern Italian city-states for almost 50 years.

Q1456660.name: Treaty of Värälä
Q1456660.blurb: The Treaty of Wereloe ended the 1788–1790 Russo-Swedish War.

Q1458570.name: 2014 Scottish independence referendum
aliases: Results of the Scottish independence referendum, 2014
Should Scotland Be An Independent Country?
Q1458570.blurb: Scotland votes against independence from the United Kingdom, by 55% to 45%.

Q1458777.name: Tri-State Tornado
Q1458777.blurb: The 1925 Tri-State tornado hits the Midwestern states of Missouri, Illinois, and Indiana, killing 695 people.

Q1459010.name: Northwest Airlines Flight 255
aliases: Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport crash of 1987
Q1459010.blurb: Northwest Airlines Flight 255, a McDonnell Douglas MD-82, crashes after takeoff in Detroit, Michigan, killing 154 of the 155 on board, plus two people on the ground.

Q1459058.name: Battle of Curlew Pass
Q1459058.blurb: Nine Years' War: Battle of Curlew Pass: Irish forces led by Hugh Roe O'Donnell successfully ambush English forces, led by Sir Conyers Clifford, sent to relieve Collooney Castle.

Q1459494.name: Battle of Klokotnitsa
Q1459494.blurb: Bulgarian Tsar Ivan Asen II defeats Theodore of Epirus in the Battle of Klokotnitsa.

Q1461047.name: 1957 Upper Voltan Territorial Assembly election
Q1461047.blurb: Elections to the Territorial Assembly of the French colony Upper Volta are held. After the elections PDU and MDV form a government.

Q1461147.name: Irish Rebellion of 1641
Q1461147.blurb: Irish Catholic gentry in Ulster tried to seize control of Dublin Castle, the seat of English rule in Ireland, to force concessions to Catholics.

Q1463516.name: Nicaraguan Revolution
Q1463516.blurb: Nicaraguan Revolution: The FSLN seizes the National Congress of Nicaragua, along with over a thousand hostages.

Q1463832.name: Sack of Rome
Q1463832.blurb: Sack of Rome: Vandals enter Rome, and plunder the city for two weeks.

Q1463845.name: 410 sack of Rome
Q1463845.blurb: Rome was sacked for the first time in approximately 800 years by the Visigoths under Alaric I.

Q1463941.name: Estates General of 1789
Q1463941.blurb: In France, the Estates-General convenes for the first time since 1614.

Q1463967.name: Luxair Flight 9642
Q1463967.blurb: A Fokker 50 crashes near Luxembourg Airport, killing 20 and injuring three.

Q1464154.name: Weenen massacre
Q1464154.blurb: In the Weenen massacre, hundreds of Voortrekkers along the Blaukraans River, Natal are killed by Zulus.

Q1464620.name: Battle of La Motta
Q1464620.blurb: War of the League of Cambrai: Spain defeats Venice.

Q1466527.name: Treaty of Fort Jackson
Q1466527.blurb: American Indian Wars: The Creek sign the Treaty of Fort Jackson, giving up huge parts of Alabama and Georgia.

Q1467946.name: Malaysian Airline System Flight 653
Q1467946.blurb: Malaysian Airline System Flight 653 is hijacked and crashes in Tanjong Kupang, Johor, killing 100.

Q1469307.name: Lülin
Q1469307.blurb: Rebels sack the Chinese capital Chang'an during a peasant rebellion.

Q1470995.name: Chickasaw Campaign of 1736
Q1470995.blurb: The Battle of Ackia is fought near the present site of Tupelo, Mississippi. British and Chickasaw soldiers repel a French and Choctaw attack on the then-Chickasaw village of Ackia.

Q1471139.name: Evian Accords
Q1471139.blurb: The Évian Accords end the Algerian War of Independence, which had begun in 1954.

Q1472704.name: New Zealand dollar
Q1472704.blurb: New Zealand decimalises its former currency to the modern-day New Zealand dollar.

Q1473165.name: Miljevci plateau incident
Q1473165.blurb: Croatian War of Independence: The Battle of the Miljevci Plateau ended after a failed counterattack by forces of the Republic of Serbian Krajina against the Croatian Army who had captured the plateau.

Q1473273.name: Hurricane Irene–Olivia
Q1473273.blurb: Having weakened after making landfall in Nicaragua the previous day, Hurricane Irene regains enough strength to be renamed Hurricane Olivia, making it the first known hurricane to cross from the Atlantic Ocean into the Pacific.

Q1473300.name: Gulf Cartel
Q1473300.blurb: Arturo Guzmán Decena, founder of Los Zetas and high-member of the Gulf Cartel, is killed in a shoot-out with the Mexican Army and the police.

Q1473722.name: Dekemvriana
Q1473722.blurb: Greek Civil War: Fighting breaks out in Athens between the ELAS and government forces supported by the British Army.

Q1473919.name: Operation Grapes of Wrath
Q1473919.blurb: Operation Grapes of Wrath: Israeli forces shelled Qana, Lebanon, killing at least 100 civilians and injuring more than 110 others at a United Nations compound.

Q1474180.name: Battle of Belleau Wood
Q1474180.blurb: World War I: The 26-day Battle of Belleau Wood near the Marne River in France ended with American forces finally clearing that forest of German troops.

Q1475005.name: Treaty of Ancón
aliases: Treaty of Friendship and Peace between the Republics of Chile and Peru
Q1475005.blurb: Peru and Chile sign the Treaty of Ancón, by which the Tarapacá province is ceded to the latter, bringing an end to Peru's involvement in the War of the Pacific.

Q1475243.name: Battle of Cape Esperance
Q1475243.blurb: World War II: Off Guadalcanal, United States Navy ships intercept and defeat a Japanese force.

Q1475679.name: Battle of Tassafaronga
Q1475679.blurb: World War II: Battle of Tassafaronga; A smaller squadron of Imperial Japanese Navy destroyers led by Raizō Tanaka defeats a U.S. Navy cruiser force under Carleton H. Wright.

Q1476042.name: Operation Anaconda
Q1476042.blurb: U.S. invasion of Afghanistan: Operation Anaconda begins in eastern Afghanistan.

Q1477050.name: Chattanooga campaign
Q1477050.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Chattanooga begins: Union forces led by General Ulysses S. Grant reinforce troops at Chattanooga, Tennessee, and counter-attack Confederate troops.

Q1477118.name: Operation Starlite
Q1477118.blurb: Vietnam War: Operation Starlite begins: United States Marines destroy a Viet Cong stronghold on the Van Tuong peninsula in the first major American ground battle of the war.

Q1477456.name: Glasgow Airport attack
Q1477456.blurb: A Jeep Cherokee filled with propane canisters drives into the entrance of Glasgow Airport, Scotland in a failed terrorist attack. This was linked to the 2007 London car bombs that had taken place the day before.

Q1478267.name: Truce of Yam-Zapolsky
Q1478267.blurb: Truce of Yam-Zapolsky: Russia cedes Livonia to the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.

Q1478359.name: Battle of Jilib
Q1478359.blurb: War in Somalia: Transitional Federal Government forces attacked the last stronghold of the Islamic Courts Union in the town of Jilib.

Q1478525.name: Battle of Edgehill
Q1478525.blurb: The Battle of Edgehill is the first major battle of the English Civil War.

Q1478559.name: Devil's Footprints
Q1478559.blurb: A series of hoof-like marks in the snow continuing through the countryside for some 40 to 100 miles (60 to 160 km) were discovered in Devon, England.

Q1479198.name: Christmas Meeting 1888
Q1479198.blurb: The Christmas Meeting of 1888, considered to be the official start of the Faroese independence movement.

Q1481878.name: Simele massacre
Q1481878.blurb: The Kingdom of Iraq slaughters over 3,000 Assyrians in the village of Simele. This date is recognized as Martyrs Day or National Day of Mourning by the Assyrian community in memory of the Simele massacre.

Q1481920.name: Battle of Alarcos
Q1481920.blurb: Battle of Alarcos: Almohad forces defeat the Castilian army of Alfonso VIII and force its retreat to Toledo.

Q1481957.name: Treaty of Fort Laramie
Q1481957.blurb: Red Cloud (pictured), a Native American leader of the Oglala Lakota tribe, signed the Treaty of Fort Laramie, ending Red Cloud's War and establishing the Great Sioux Reservation.

Q1482369.name: Markale massacres
Q1482369.blurb: Markale massacres, more than 60 people are killed and some 200 wounded as a mortar shell explodes in a downtown marketplace in Sarajevo.

Q1484007.name: 2008 G20 Washington summit
Q1484007.blurb: The first G-20 economic summit opens in Washington, D.C.

Q1486456.name: Oka Crisis
Q1486456.blurb: Oka Crisis: First Nations land dispute in Quebec begins.

Q1488817.name: Battle of Orewin Bridge
Q1488817.blurb: Battle of Orewin Bridge: Llywelyn ap Gruffudd, the last native Prince of Wales, is killed at Cilmeri near Builth Wells in mid-Wales.

Q1488972.name: UTA 772 bombing
Q1488972.blurb: A bomb destroys UTA Flight 772 in mid-air above the Tùnùrù Desert, Niger, killing all 170 passengers and crew.

Q1491406.name: Constantinople earthquake of 557
Q1491406.blurb: Constantinople is severely damaged by an earthquake, which cracks the dome of Hagia Sophia.

Q1494794.name: Garuda Indonesia Flight 200
Q1494794.blurb: Garuda Indonesia Flight 200 crashes at Adisutjipto International Airport in the Special Region of Yogyakarta, Indonesia, killing 21 people.

Q1495317.name: Gaspée affair
Q1495317.blurb: The British schooner Gaspee is burned in Narragansett Bay, Rhode Island.

Q1495481.name: Battle of Stoke Field
Q1495481.blurb: Battle of Stoke Field: King Henry VII of England defeats the leaders of a Yorkist rebellion in the final engagement of the Wars of the Roses.

Q1495544.name: Nyköping Banquet
Q1495544.blurb: The Nyköping Banquet: Birger, King of Sweden treacherously seizes his two brothers, dukes Valdemar and Erik, who are subsequently starved to death in the dungeon of Nyköping Castle.

Q1495944.name: Polish–Lithuanian War
Q1495944.blurb: Polish–Lithuanian War: The Polish Army launches the Vilna offensive to capture Vilnius in modern Lithuania.

Q1497909.name: Battle of Ball's Bluff
Q1497909.blurb: American Civil War: Union forces under Colonel Edward Baker are defeated by Confederate troops in the second major battle of the war.

Q1497933.name: Battle of Haelen
Q1497933.blurb: World War I: The Battle of Halen a.k.a. Battle of the Silver Helmets a clash between large Belgian and German cavalry formations at Halen, Belgium.

Q1497969.name: Battle of Sailor's Creek
Q1497969.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Sailor's Creek: Confederate General Robert E. Lee's Army of Northern Virginia fights and loses its last major battle while in retreat from Richmond, Virginia, during the Appomattox Campaign.

Q1497996.name: Battle of Tulagi and Gavutu–Tanambogo
Q1497996.blurb: World War II: U.S. Marines initiated the first American offensive of the Guadalcanal campaign, with landings on Tulagi (pictured), Gavutu–Tanambogo and Guadalcanal in the Solomon Islands.

Q1498481.name: Secret Meeting of 20 February 1933
Q1498481.blurb: Adolf Hitler secretly meets with German industrialists to arrange for financing of the Nazi Party's upcoming election campaign.

Q1498881.name: Norrmalmstorg robbery
Q1498881.blurb: A bank robbery gone wrong in Stockholm, Sweden, turns into a hostage crisis; over the next five days the hostages begin to sympathise with their captors, leading to the term "Stockholm syndrome".

Q1500314.name: Battle of Harran
Q1500314.blurb: The Seljuk emirs of Mosul and Mardin defeat the Crusader States of Antioch and Edessa.

Q1500532.name: Battle of Cravant
Q1500532.blurb: Hundred Years' War: Battle of Cravant: A Franco-Scottish army is defeated by the Anglo-Burgundians at Cravant on the banks of the river Yonne.

Q1501196.name: Catalan Company
aliases: The Catalan Company of the East
Q1501196.blurb: Battle of Halmyros: The Catalan Company defeats Walter V, Count of Brienne to take control of the Duchy of Athens, a Crusader state in Greece.

Q1501525.name: Mabo v Queensland (No 2)
Q1501525.blurb: Australian Aboriginal land rights are recognised in Mabo v Queensland (No 2), a case brought by Torres Strait Islander Eddie Mabo which led to the Native Title Act 1993  overturning the long-held colonial assumption of terra nullius.

Q1501724.name: Portuguese Restoration War
Q1501724.blurb: Portuguese Restoration War: Portuguese and Spanish forces both claim victory in the Battle of Montijo.

Q1503007.name: Ip massacre
Q1503007.blurb: Ip massacre: The Hungarian Army, supported by local Hungarians, kill 158 Romanian civilians in Ip, Sălaj, a village in Northern Transylvania, an act of ethnic cleansing.

Q1504861.name: United Nations Conference on International Organization
aliases: Meeting that established the United Nations
Q1504861.blurb: United Nations Conference on International Organization: Founding negotiations for the United Nations begin in San Francisco.

Q1505845.name: Arctic convoys of World War II
aliases: Allied shipping to the Soviet Union
Arctic convoys in World War II
Q1505845.blurb: Second World War: The German battleship Scharnhorst was sunk at the Battle of the North Cape during an attempt to attack Arctic convoys.

Q1506788.name: North-West Rebellion
Q1506788.blurb: North-West Rebellion: The four-day Battle of Batoche, pitting rebel Métis against the Canadian government, comes to an end with a decisive rebel defeat.

Q1508820.name: Battle of Junín
Q1508820.blurb: Peruvian War of Independence: Patriot forces led by Simón Bolívar defeat the Spanish Royalist army in the Battle of Junín.

Q1509619.name: Battle of Bapheus
Q1509619.blurb: Battle of Bapheus: Decisive Ottoman victory over the Byzantines opening up Bithynia for Turkish conquest.

Q1509663.name: Battle of Dunbar
Q1509663.blurb: First War of Scottish Independence: John Balliol's Scottish army is defeated by an English army commanded by John de Warenne, 6th Earl of Surrey at the Battle of Dunbar.

Q1510144.name: Wairau Affray
Q1510144.blurb: The Wairau Affray, the first serious clash of arms between Māori and British settlers in the New Zealand Wars, takes place.

Q1511005.name: Battle of Valdejunquera
Q1511005.blurb: Rout of an alliance of Christian troops from Navarre and Léon against the Muslims at the Battle of Valdejunquera.

Q1511107.name: Anti-austerity movement in Greece
Q1511107.blurb: Mass protests in Greece erupt in response to austerity measures imposed by the government as a result of the Greek government-debt crisis.

Q1512810.name: Jintian Uprising
Q1512810.blurb: Taiping Rebellion: Hong Xiuquan proclaims the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom, starting the Jintian Uprising.

Q1514690.name: 1958 Tybee Island mid-air collision
Q1514690.blurb: After a mid-air collision with a fighter plane during a practice exercise off Tybee Island, Georgia, a U.S. Air Force bomber jettisoned a Mark 15 nuclear bomb, which was presumed lost.

Q1514764.name: Cyclone Klaus
Q1514764.blurb: Cyclone Klaus makes landfall near Bordeaux, France, causing 26 deaths as well as extensive disruptions to public transport and power supplies.

Q1514908.name: Cuban War of Independence
Q1514908.blurb: Revolution breaks out in Baire, a town near Santiago de Cuba, beginning the Cuban War of Independence; the war ends along with the Spanish–American War in 1898.

Q1515362.name: 1920 Duluth lynchings
Q1515362.blurb: Three African-American circus workers were lynched by a mob in Duluth, Minnesota, a crime that shocked the country for having taken place in the Northern United States.

Q1516968.name: 1623 papal conclave
Q1516968.blurb: After the death of Gregory XV, a papal conclave in Rome elected Maffeo Barberini as Pope Urban VIII.

Q1517252.name: 1996 Mount Everest disaster
Q1517252.blurb: A blizzard strikes Mount Everest, killing eight climbers by the next day.

Q1517749.name: Battle of the Winwaed
Q1517749.blurb: Battle of the Winwaed: Penda of Mercia is defeated by Oswiu of Northumbria.

Q1518023.name: Maguindanao massacre
Q1518023.blurb: The Maguindanao massacre occurs in Ampatuan, Philippines; 58 opponents of Andal Ampatuan Jr. are kidnapped and killed.

Q1518266.name: Battle of Simancas
Q1518266.blurb: Battle of Simancas: King Ramiro II of León defeats the Moorish army under Caliph Abd-al-Rahman III near the city of Simancas.

Q1518358.name: 1963 conclave
Q1518358.blurb: Cardinal Giovanni Battista Montini is elected as Pope Paul VI.

Q1518787.name: Battle of Moore's Creek Bridge
Q1518787.blurb: American Revolutionary War: The Battle of Moore's Creek Bridge in North Carolina breaks up a Loyalist militia.

Q1518944.name: 1905 French law on the Separation of the Churches and the State
Q1518944.blurb: In France, a law separating church and state is passed.

Q1518946.name: Law for the Prevention of Hereditarily Diseased Offspring
aliases: Law for the Prevention of Descendants with Hereditary Diseases
Q1518946.blurb: Nazi eugenics programme begins with the proclamation of the Law for the Prevention of Hereditarily Diseased Offspring requiring the compulsory sterilization of any citizen who suffers from alleged genetic disorders.

Q1519015.name: 1994 Northridge earthquake
Q1519015.blurb: The 6.7 Mw Northridge earthquake shakes the Greater Los Angeles Area with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent), leaving 57 people dead and more than 8,700 injured.

Q1519185.name: Operation Hastings
Q1519185.blurb: Vietnam War: The United States and South Vietnam begin Operation Hastings to push the North Vietnamese out of the Vietnamese Demilitarized Zone.

Q1519203.name: Battle of Mobile Bay
Q1519203.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Mobile Bay begins at Mobile Bay near Mobile, Alabama, Admiral David Farragut leads a Union flotilla through Confederate defenses and seals one of the last major Southern ports.

Q1520241.name: Yamasee War
Q1520241.blurb: The Pocotaligo Massacre triggers the start of the Yamasee War in colonial South Carolina.

Q1521636.name: Elizabethan Religious Settlement
Q1521636.blurb: The Book of Common Prayer, a major component of the Elizabethan religious settlement, was introduced as the liturgy of the Church of England through the Act of Uniformity 1558.

Q1523324.name: Battle of Arnemuiden
Q1523324.blurb: The Battle of Arnemuiden, in which a French force defeats the English, is the first naval battle of the Hundred Years' War and the first naval battle in which gunpowder artillery is used.

Q1524096.name: Northwest Airlines Flight 6231
Q1524096.blurb: Northwest Orient Airlines Flight 6231, another Boeing 727, crashes northwest of John F. Kennedy International Airport.

Q1526883.name: Battle of the Dunes
Q1526883.blurb: Franco-Spanish War: Turenne and the French army win a decisive victory over the Spanish at the battle of the Dunes.

Q1527286.name: Battle of Nocera
Q1527286.blurb: Battle of Nocera between Ranulf II of Alife and Roger II of Sicily.

Q1527386.name: Battle of Rignano
Q1527386.blurb: Ranulf of Apulia defeats Roger II of Sicily at the Battle of Rignano, securing his position as duke until his death two years later.

Q1529863.name: Scandinavian Airlines System Flight 751
Q1529863.blurb: Scandinavian Airlines System Flight 751 crashes in Gottröra in the Norrtälje Municipality in Sweden, injuring 92.

Q1532351.name: Scottish Reformation
Q1532351.blurb: John Knox returns from exile to Scotland to become the leader of the nascent Scottish Reformation.

Q1533038.name: Gnadenhutten massacre
Q1533038.blurb: Gnadenhutten massacre: Ninety-six Native Americans in Gnadenhutten, Ohio, who had converted to Christianity, are killed by Pennsylvania militiamen in retaliation for raids carried out by other Indian tribes.

Q1535602.name: Golden age of alpinism
Q1535602.blurb: A seven-man mountaineering team made the first ascent of the Matterhorn, marking the end of the golden age of alpinism.

Q1536103.name: Battle of Lund
Q1536103.blurb: The Battle of Lund occurs, and is the bloodiest battle in Scandinavian history.

Q1536533.name: Colombian-Peruvian War
Q1536533.blurb: A speech by Laureano Gómez leads to the escalation of the Leticia Incident.

Q1536618.name: Battle of Chapultepec
Q1536618.blurb: Mexican–American War: the Battle of Chapultepec begins.

Q1536983.name: Stono Rebellion
Q1536983.blurb: Stono Rebellion, the largest slave uprising in Britain's mainland North American colonies prior to the American Revolution, erupts near Charleston, South Carolina.

Q1538124.name: Gordon Riots
Q1538124.blurb: The anti-Catholic Gordon Riots in London leave an estimated 300 to 700 people dead.

Q1538397.name: 2010 Baja California earthquake
Q1538397.blurb: A magnitude 7.2 earthquake hits south of the Mexico-USA border, killing at least two and damaging buildings across the two countries.

Q1538874.name: Battle of Spotsylvania Court House
Q1538874.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Spotsylvania Court House: Union troops assault a Confederate salient known as the "Mule Shoe", with some of the fiercest fighting of the war, much of it hand-to-hand combat, occurring at "the Bloody Angle" on the northwest.

Q1538940.name: Lillehammer affair
Q1538940.blurb: In Lillehammer, Norway, Mossad agents kill a waiter whom they mistakenly thought was involved in the 1972 Munich Olympics Massacre.

Q1539453.name: Battle of St. Quentin
Q1539453.blurb: World War I: Start of the Battle of St. Quentin in which the French Fifth Army counter-attacked the invading Germans at Saint-Quentin, Aisne.

Q1539513.name: Battle of Camden
Q1539513.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Battle of Camden: The British defeat the Americans near Camden, South Carolina.

Q1540446.name: Memorial Day massacre of 1937
Q1540446.blurb: Memorial Day massacre: Chicago police shoot and kill ten labor demonstrators.

Q1540695.name: January Events
aliases: Day of the Defenders of Freedom
Q1540695.blurb: Soviet Union troops attack Lithuanian independence supporters in Vilnius, killing 14 people and wounding around 1,000 others.

Q1540820.name: Battle of Aliwal
Q1540820.blurb: The Battle of Aliwal, India, is won by British troops commanded by Sir Harry Smith.

Q1541340.name: Battle of Cape Spartivento
Q1541340.blurb: World War II: At the Battle of Cape Spartivento, the Royal Navy engages the Regia Marina in the Mediterranean Sea.

Q1542208.name: 1st Annual Grammy Awards
Q1542208.blurb: The 1st Annual Grammy Awards are held.

Q1542423.name: Downing Street mortar attack
Q1542423.blurb: The Troubles: The Provisional IRA launches a mortar attack on 10 Downing Street in London, the headquarters of the British government.

Q1542601.name: Prague Slavic Congress
Q1542601.blurb: The Slavic Congress opens in Prague.

Q1542647.name: Battle of Brissarthe
Q1542647.blurb: Battle of Brissarthe: The Franks led by Robert the Strong are defeated by a joint Breton-Viking army.

Q1542829.name: Battle of South Mountain
Q1542829.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of South Mountain, part of the Maryland Campaign, is fought.

Q1543066.name: Meet the Press
aliases: Meet the Press with Chuck Todd
Meet the Press with Kristen Welker
Meet the Press with David Gregory
Meet the Press with Tim Russert
Q1543066.blurb: Meet the Press, the longest running television program in history, makes its debut on NBC Television.

Q1543109.name: Henley Royal Regatta
Q1543109.blurb: The first Henley Royal Regatta is held.

Q1543656.name: Grattan massacre
Q1543656.blurb: American Indian Wars: In Nebraska, 700 soldiers under United States General William S. Harney avenge the Grattan massacre by attacking a Sioux village and killing 100 men, women and children.

Q1545288.name: Veronese Easters
Q1545288.blurb: Citizens of Verona begin an unsuccessful eight-day rebellion against the French occupying forces.

Q1545405.name: New Zealand Wars
Q1545405.blurb: New Zealand Wars: Carl Sylvius Völkner, a Protestant missionary, was killed by Hauhau militants in Ōpōtiki for working as an agent for New Zealand governor-general George Grey.

Q1546173.name: Capture of Fort Ticonderoga
Q1546173.blurb: American Revolutionary War: A small Colonial militia led by Ethan Allen and Colonel Benedict Arnold captures Fort Ticonderoga.

Q1547128.name: Grito de Lares
Q1547128.blurb: The Grito de Lares occurs in Puerto Rico against Spanish rule.

Q1547791.name: Pueblo Revolt
Q1547791.blurb: The Pueblo Revolt begins in New Mexico.

Q1548600.name: Independence of Brazil
Q1548600.blurb: Dom Pedro I declares Brazil independent from Portugal on the shores of the Ipiranga Brook in São Paulo.

Q1549050.name: Great Storm of 1703
Q1549050.blurb: The great storm of 1703, one of the most severe storms to strike southern Great Britain, destroyed the first Eddystone Lighthouse off Plymouth.

Q1550228.name: Courrières mine disaster
Q1550228.blurb: The Courrières mine disaster, Europe's worst ever, kills 1099 miners in northern France.

Q1550466.name: Battle of Seven Pines
Q1550466.blurb: American Civil War: Peninsula Campaign: The Battle of Seven Pines (or the Battle of Fair Oaks) ends inconclusively, with both sides claiming victory.

Q1550913.name: Pinjarra massacre
Q1550913.blurb: The Pinjarra massacre occurs in the Swan River Colony. An estimated 30 Noongar people are killed by British colonists.

Q1551794.name: Japanese invasion of Manchuria
Q1551794.blurb: Japanese invasion of Manchuria: Japan leaves the League of Nations after it approves the Lytton Report that ruled in favour of China.

Q1552718.name: Granada War
aliases: Día de la Toma de Granada
Q1552718.blurb: Granada War: Forces of Aragon and Castile began a siege of Málaga, a Muslim city in the south of the Iberian Peninsula.

Q1559370.name: Edict of Pîtres
Q1559370.blurb: The Edict of Pistres of Charles the Bald orders defensive measures against the Vikings.

Q1559974.name: Hurricane Carla
Q1559974.blurb: Hurricane Carla strikes the Texas coast as a Category 4 hurricane, the second strongest storm ever to hit the state.

Q1563435.name: Battle of Loznica
Q1563435.blurb: World War II: Serbian paramilitary forces defeat Germans in the Battle of Loznica.

Q1564366.name: Second voyage of HMS Beagle
Q1564366.blurb: Charles Darwin embarks on his journey aboard HMS Beagle, during which he will begin to formulate his theory of evolution.

Q1565008.name: kamikaze
Q1565008.blurb: Mongol invasion of Japan: The Mongolian fleet of Kublai Khan is destroyed by a "divine wind" for the second time in the Battle of Kōan.

Q1565234.name: Battle of Wittenweiher
Q1565234.blurb: An army under Bernard of Saxe-Weimar defeats imperial troops at the battle of Wittenweiher.

Q1565693.name: Battle of Harpers Ferry
Q1565693.blurb: American Civil War: Confederate forces capture Harpers Ferry, Virginia.

Q1566313.name: Medicine Lodge Treaty
Q1566313.blurb: The Medicine Lodge Treaty is signed by southern Great Plains Indian leaders. The treaty requires Native American Plains tribes to relocate to a reservation in the western Indian Territory.

Q1566327.name: Hague Congress
Q1566327.blurb: The Council of Europe is founded during the Hague Congress.

Q1566367.name: Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction
aliases: Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction
Q1566367.blurb: Proceedings on the Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction conclude.

Q1566410.name: Treaty of Benevento
Q1566410.blurb: The treaty of Benevento between Pope Adrian IV and William I of Sicily is concluded.

Q1566835.name: Uprising in Montenegro
aliases: Italian occupation of Montenegro and Sangiaccato
Q1566835.blurb: World War II: Montenegrins begin the Trinaestojulski ustanak (Thirteenth of July Uprising), a popular revolt against the Axis powers.

Q1566992.name: 1342 papal conclave
Q1566992.blurb: In Avignon, France, Cardinal Pierre Roger is elected Pope and takes the name Clement VI.

Q1567023.name: 1993 shootings at CIA Headquarters
Q1567023.blurb: Five people are shot outside the CIA Headquarters in Langley, Virginia. Two are killed and three wounded.

Q1567698.name: Muscovite-Lithuanian Wars
Q1567698.blurb: Muscovite–Lithuanian Wars: The Grand Duchy of Lithuania achieved one of the greatest Lithuanian victories against the Tatars at the Battle of Kletsk.

Q1568374.name: Wye River Memorandum
Q1568374.blurb: Israel and the Palestinian Authority sign the Wye River Memorandum.

Q1568540.name: Rome General Peace Accords
Q1568540.blurb: The Rome General Peace Accords end a 16-year civil war in Mozambique.

Q1568837.name: Jay's Treaty
aliases: Treaty of Amity, Commerce, and Navigation, Between His Britannic Majesty and The United States of America
Q1568837.blurb: The Jay Treaty between the United States and Great Britain comes into force, facilitating ten years of peaceful trade between the two nations.

Q1568891.name: 1903 World Series
Q1568891.blurb: The Boston Red Sox win the first modern World Series, defeating the Pittsburgh Pirates in the eighth game.

Q1568932.name: Battle of Lowestoft
Q1568932.blurb: James Stuart, Duke of York (later to become King James II of England), defeats the Dutch fleet off the coast of Lowestoft.

Q1569137.name: Piper Alpha
Q1569137.blurb: The Piper Alpha drilling platform in the North Sea is destroyed by explosions and fires. One hundred sixty-seven oil workers are killed, making it the world's worst offshore oil disaster in terms of direct loss of life.

Q1571353.name: Assyrian eclipse
Q1571353.blurb: Assyrians record a solar eclipse that is later used to fix the chronology of Mesopotamian history.

Q1571843.name: Red Purge
Q1571843.blurb: Matsukawa derailment: Unknown saboteurs cause a passenger train to derail and overturn in Fukushima Prefecture, Japan, killing three crew members and igniting a political firestorm between the Japanese Communist Party and the government of Occupied Japan that will eventually lead to the Japanese Red Purge.

Q1572233.name: We shall fight on the beaches
Q1572233.blurb: Second World War: The remaining Allied forces protecting the Dunkirk evacuation surrendered, ending the Battle of Dunkirk; in response, British prime minister Winston Churchill gave a speech in which he declared "We shall fight on the beaches".

Q1572785.name: Battle of Rabaul
Q1572785.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Rabaul commences Japan's invasion of Australia's Territory of New Guinea.

Q1573466.name: Constitution of Greece
aliases: Article 16 of the Constitution of the Hellenic Republic
Q1573466.blurb: Prime Minister of Greece Ioannis Metaxas suspends parliament and the Constitution and establishes the 4th of August Regime.

Q1573486.name: LOT Polish Airlines Flight 007
Q1573486.blurb: LOT Polish Airlines Flight 007 crashes during final approach near Warsaw, Poland, killing 87 people, including a 14-man American boxing team.

Q1573825.name: Battle of Sobraon
Q1573825.blurb: First Anglo-Sikh War: Battle of Sobraon: British defeat Sikhs in the final battle of the war.

Q1574009.name: Air France Flight 8969
Q1574009.blurb: Air France Flight 8969 is hijacked on the ground at Houari Boumediene Airport, Algiers, Algeria. Over the course of three days three passengers are killed, as are all four terrorists.

Q1574076.name: Newburgh Conspiracy
Q1574076.blurb: In an emotional speech in Newburgh, New York, George Washington asks his officers not to support the Newburgh Conspiracy. The plea is successful, and the threatened coup d'état never takes place.

Q1575036.name: 2012 Delhi gang rape case
aliases: 2012 Delhi gang rape and murder incident
2012 Delhi gang rape case gang rape of a 23-year-old student on a public bus
Q1575036.blurb: A woman was gang-raped and fatally assaulted on a bus in Delhi, generating protests across India against inadequate security for women.

Q1575474.name: Sabena Flight 548
Q1575474.blurb: Sabena Flight 548 crashes in Belgium, killing 73, including the entire United States figure skating team along with several of their coaches and family members.

Q1575996.name: Kyiv Arsenal January Uprising
Q1575996.blurb: Ukrainian–Soviet War: An armed uprising organized by the Bolsheviks in anticipation of the encroaching Red Army begins at the Kiev Arsenal, which will be put down six days later.

Q1576717.name: Battle of Dungeness
Q1576717.blurb: Defeat at the Battle of Dungeness causes the Commonwealth of England to reform its navy.

Q1576861.name: Libyan Arab Airlines Flight 114
Q1576861.blurb: After accidentally straying into the airspace of the Israeli-occupied Sinai Peninsula, Libyan Arab Airlines Flight 114 was shot down by two Israeli fighter aircraft, killing 108 of the 113 people on board.

Q1578852.name: Battle of Marcellae
Q1578852.blurb: Kardam of Bulgaria defeats Byzantine Emperor Constantine VI at the Battle of Marcellae.

Q1580637.name: 1724 papal conclave
Q1580637.blurb: Following the death of Pope Innocent XIII, a papal conclave convened in Rome to elect a new pope.

Q1581794.name: Million Man March
Q1581794.blurb: The Million Man March takes place in Washington, D.C. About 837,000 attend.

Q1582486.name: Battle of Auberoche
Q1582486.blurb: Hundred Years' War: The English victory at the Battle of Auberoche marked a change in the military balance of power in Aquitaine, with the subsequent collapse of the French position.

Q1583213.name: Russian Constitution of 1906
Q1583213.blurb: The Russian Constitution of 1906 is adopted (on April 23 by the Julian calendar).

Q1583411.name: Pacific Southwest Airlines Flight 1771
Q1583411.blurb: Pacific Southwest Airlines Flight 1771, a British Aerospace 146-200A, crashes near Paso Robles, California, killing all 43 on board, after a disgruntled passenger shoots his ex-boss traveling on the flight, then shoots both pilots and steers the plane into the ground.

Q1585207.name: Estonian Provincial Assembly
Q1585207.blurb: The Estonian Provincial Assembly declares itself the sovereign power of Estonia.

Q1585785.name: Operation Cyclone
Q1585785.blurb: U.S. President Jimmy Carter signs the first directive for secret aid to the opponents of the pro-Soviet regime in Kabul.

Q1587893.name: Battle of Tinchebray
Q1587893.blurb: In the Battle of Tinchebray in Normandy, the invading King Henry I of England captured his brother Robert Curthose.

Q1588295.name: Ehime Maru and USS Greeneville collision
aliases: collision between the U.S. Navy Submarine USS Greeneville and Japanese Motor Vessel Ehime Maru
Q1588295.blurb: The Ehime Maru and USS Greeneville collision takes place, killing nine of the thirty-five people on board the Japanese fishery high-school training ship Ehime Maru, leaving the USS Greeneville (SSN-772) with US $2 million in repairs, at Pearl Harbor.

Q1591801.name: Hay–Pauncefote Treaty
Q1591801.blurb: Britain and the United States sign the Hay–Pauncefote Treaty, which nullifies the Clayton–Bulwer Treaty and withdraws British objections to an American-controlled canal in Panama.

Q1600541.name: Action of the Hohenzollern Redoubt
Q1600541.blurb: First World War: The Battle of the Hohenzollern Redoubt marks the end of the Battle of Loos.

Q1600902.name: Iberia Airlines Flight 602
Q1600902.blurb: Iberia Flight 602 crashes near Ibiza Airport, killing all 104 people on board.

Q1604442.name: Ruby Ridge
Q1604442.blurb: The 11-day Ruby Ridge standoff ends with Randy Weaver surrendering to federal authorities.

Q1604816.name: Lithuanian–Soviet War
Q1604816.blurb: Vincas Mickevičius-Kapsukas declared the formation of the Lithuanian Soviet Socialist Republic, a puppet state created by Soviet Russia to justify the Lithuanian–Soviet War.

Q1605349.name: Volkswagen Law
Q1605349.blurb: The German Volkswagen Act comes into force.

Q1606520.name: Plan of ayala
Q1606520.blurb: Final stage of the Mexican War of Independence from Spain with Plan of Iguala.

Q1606958.name: Battle of Bogesund
Q1606958.blurb: Sten Sture the Younger, the Regent of Sweden, is mortally wounded at the Battle of Bogesund and dies on February 3.

Q1612417.name: Battle of Fleurus
Q1612417.blurb: War of the Grand Alliance: Marshal de Luxembourg triumphs over an Anglo-Dutch army at the battle of Fleurus.

Q1613521.name: Battle of Roslin
Q1613521.blurb: The English are defeated at the Battle of Roslin, in the First War of Scottish Independence.

Q1615396.name: UPS Airlines Flight 6
Q1615396.blurb: After taking off from Dubai International Airport, UPS Airlines Flight 6 develops an in-flight fire in the cargo hold and crashes near Nad Al Sheba, killing both crew members on board.

Q1616064.name: Mithridatic Wars
Q1616064.blurb: Pompey the Great celebrates his third triumph for victories over the pirates and the end of the Mithridatic Wars on his 45th birthday.

Q1619120.name: Representation of the People Act 1832
Q1619120.blurb: The Great Reform Act of England and Wales receives royal assent.

Q1620408.name: Battle of Chesma
Q1620408.blurb: The Battle of Chesma between the Russian Empire and the Ottoman Empire begins, resulting in one of the worst naval defeats of the Ottomans since Lepanto.

Q1625317.name: Holy Cross dispute
Q1625317.blurb: In Belfast, Protestant loyalists begin a picket of Holy Cross, a Catholic primary school for girls.

Q1626179.name: Battle of Opequon
Q1626179.blurb: American Civil War: Union troops under Philip Sheridan defeat a Confederate force commanded by Jubal Early. With over 50,000 troops engaged, it was the largest battle fought in the Shenandoah Valley.

Q1626369.name: Battle of Fort Stevens
Q1626369.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Fort Stevens; Confederate forces attempt to invade Washington, D.C.

Q1628057.name: Battle of Monterrey
Q1628057.blurb: Mexican–American War: General Zachary Taylor captures Monterrey.

Q1628477.name: Battle of Diu
Q1628477.blurb: The Portuguese navy defeats a joint fleet of the Ottoman Empire, the Republic of Venice, the Sultan of Gujarat, the Mamlûk Burji Sultanate of Egypt, the Zamorin of Calicut, and the Republic of Ragusa at the Battle of Diu in Diu, India.

Q1628984.name: 2009 Malagasy political crisis
Q1628984.blurb: Rioting breaks out in Antananarivo, Madagascar, sparking a political crisis that will result in the replacement of President Marc Ravalomanana with Andry Rajoelina.

Q1629355.name: Disaster of Curalaba
Q1629355.blurb: Battle of Curalaba: The revolting Mapuche, led by cacique Pelentaru, inflict a major defeat on Spanish troops in southern Chile.

Q1629818.name: San Juanico disaster
Q1629818.blurb: San Juanico disaster: A series of explosions at the Pemex petroleum storage facility at San Juan Ixhuatepec in Mexico City starts a major fire and kills about 500 people.

Q1630982.name: 1986 Hotel New World disaster
Q1630982.blurb: Collapse of Hotel New World: Thirty-three people die when the Hotel New World in Singapore collapses.

Q1631029.name: Battle of Perryville
Q1631029.blurb: American Civil War: The Confederate invasion of Kentucky is halted at the Battle of Perryville.

Q1631834.name: Shackleton–Rowett Expedition
Q1631834.blurb: Antarctic explorer Ernest Shackleton (pictured) died of a heart attack during his final expedition.

Q1632838.name: Second Guangzhou Uprising
Q1632838.blurb: The Second Canton Uprising takes place in Guangzhou, Qing China, but is suppressed.

Q1634609.name: kidnapping of Aldo Moro
Q1634609.blurb: Former Prime Minister of Italy Aldo Moro was kidnapped in Rome by Mario Moretti and the Red Brigades.

Q1634613.name: 1988 Maldives coup d'état attempt
Q1634613.blurb: Sri Lankan Tamil mercenaries attempt to overthrow the Maldivian government. At President Maumoon Abdul Gayoom's request, the Indian military suppresses the rebellion within 24 hours.

Q1634968.name: Battle of Ortona
Q1634968.blurb: World War II: After eight days of brutal house-to-house fighting, the Battle of Ortona concludes with the victory of the 1st Canadian Infantry Division over the German 1st Parachute Division and the capture of the Italian town of Ortona.

Q1635328.name: Four days of Naples
Q1635328.blurb: World War II: After the Four Days of Naples, Allied troops enter the city.

Q1636055.name: September 2007 Sumatra earthquakes
Q1636055.blurb: Two earthquakes measuring 8.4 and 7.9 on the Richter Scale hits the Indonesian island of Sumatra, killing 25 people and injuring 161.

Q1636063.name: March 2–3, 2012 tornado outbreak
Q1636063.blurb: A tornado outbreak occurs over a large section of the Southern United States and into the Ohio Valley region, resulting in 40 tornado-related fatalities.

Q1636123.name: 1700 papal conclave
Q1636123.blurb: A papal conclave, which had been deadlocked due to concerns over how a successor would respond to the impending death of Charles II of Spain, ended with the election of Clement XI.

Q1636166.name: Southern Cross Expedition
Q1636166.blurb: The Southern Cross expedition led by Carsten Borchgrevink achieves a new Farthest South of 78° 50'S, making the first landing at the Great Ice Barrier.

Q1636526.name: Human Be-In
Q1636526.blurb: Counterculture of the 1960s: The Human Be-In takes place in San Francisco, California's Golden Gate Park, launching the Summer of Love.

Q1636652.name: Battle of Steenkerque
Q1636652.blurb: British-Dutch forces under William III defending the city of Brussels fight an inconclusive battle at Steenkerque against a French army under the duke of Luxembourg, with both sides suffering heavy casualties.

Q1636800.name: Battle of Cape Spada
Q1636800.blurb: World War II: Battle of Cape Spada: The Royal Navy and the Regia Marina clash; the Italian light cruiser Bartolomeo Colleoni sinks, with 121 casualties.

Q1637896.name: 1983–1985 famine in Ethiopia
Q1637896.blurb: Band Aid, a supergroup consisting of more than 30 leading British and Irish pop musicians, recorded the song "Do They Know It's Christmas?" to raise money for famine relief in Ethiopia.

Q1638031.name: Battle of Brunkeberg
Q1638031.blurb: Sten Sture the Elder, the Regent of Sweden, with the help of farmers and miners, repels an attack by King Christian I of Denmark.

Q1638488.name: Battle of Monmouth
Q1638488.blurb: American Revolutionary War: The American Continentals engage the British in the Battle of Monmouth Courthouse resulting in standstill and British withdrawal under cover of darkness.

Q1638557.name: Hurricane Camille
Q1638557.blurb: Category 5 Hurricane Camille hits the U.S. Gulf Coast, killing 256 and causing $1.42 billion in damage.

Q1638587.name: Ma'alot massacre
Q1638587.blurb: Ma'alot massacre: Members of the Democratic Front for the Liberation of Palestine attack and take hostages at an Israeli school; a total of 31 people are killed, including 22 schoolchildren.

Q1639273.name: Battle of Anzen
Q1639273.blurb: Battle of Anzen: The Byzantine emperor Theophilos suffers a heavy defeat by the Abbasids.

Q1640107.name: Ifni War
Q1640107.blurb: The Moroccan Army of Liberation ambushes a Spanish patrol in the Battle of Edchera.

Q1640209.name: Battle of Aizkraukle
Q1640209.blurb: The Livonian Order is defeated in the Battle of Aizkraukle by the Grand Duchy of Lithuania.

Q1641241.name: Battle of Guadalajara
Q1641241.blurb: Spanish Civil War: The Battle of Guadalajara begins.

Q1642045.name: Kafr Qasim massacre
Q1642045.blurb: Israeli Border Police massacred 48 Arab citizens of Kafr Qasim, among them women and children who were returning from work.

Q1642249.name: Miranda v. Arizona
Q1642249.blurb: The United States Supreme Court rules in Miranda v. Arizona that the police must inform suspects of their Fifth Amendment rights before questioning them (colloquially known as "Mirandizing").

Q1643006.name: 30 September Movement
Q1643006.blurb: At dawn, seven Indonesian Army officers and a police inspector were assassinated by the September 30 Movement at Lubang Buaya, East Jakarta. In addition, two more officers were killed in Yogyakarta. The Army pinned the murders to the Communist Party of Indonesia, resulting in mass killings of suspected leftists.

Q1643008.name: Battle of the Gebora
Q1643008.blurb: Peninsular War: Outnumbered French forces under Édouard Mortier routed and nearly destroyed Spanish troops at the Battle of the Gebora near Badajoz, Spain.

Q1643153.name: Niue Constitution Act 1974
Q1643153.blurb: Niue becomes a self-governing colony of New Zealand.

Q1644435.name: Treaty of Easton
Q1644435.blurb: The Treaty of Easton establishes the first American Indian reservation, at Indian Mills, New Jersey, for the Lenape.

Q1646284.name: Actions along the Matanikau
aliases: Second and Third Battles of the Matanikau
Q1646284.blurb: World War II: Last day of the Matanikau action on Guadalcanal as United States Marines barely escape after being surrounded by Japanese forces.

Q1648673.name: Battle of Otterburn
Q1648673.blurb: The Battle of Otterburn, a border skirmish between the Scottish and the English in Northern England, is fought near Otterburn.

Q1649932.name: Tel Aviv-Jerusalem bus 405 suicide attack
Q1649932.blurb: The Tel Aviv–Jerusalem bus 405 suicide attack: Sixteen bus passengers are killed when a member of the Palestinian Islamic Jihad took control of the bus and drove it over a cliff.

Q1650725.name: Operation Homecoming
Q1650725.blurb: A Lockheed C-141 Starlifter, dubbed the Hanoi Taxi, makes the last flight of Operation Homecoming.

Q1656048.name: 1902 Ibrox disaster
Q1656048.blurb: A stand box collapses at Ibrox Park (now Ibrox Stadium) in Glasgow, Scotland, which led to the deaths of 25 and injuries to more than 500 supporters during an international association football match between Scotland and England.

Q1657839.name: Ten Days' Campaign
Q1657839.blurb: French intervention forces William I of the Netherlands to abandon his attempt to suppress the Belgian Revolution.

Q1661772.name: Proclamation of Indonesian Independence
Q1661772.blurb: The independence of Indonesia was proclaimed by Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta , igniting a revolution against the Dutch Empire.

Q1661958.name: First Five-Year Plan
Q1661958.blurb: The Soviet Union introduces its first five-year plan.

Q1666086.name: Raid on Anuradhapura Air Force Base
Q1666086.blurb: A raid on Anuradhapura Air Force Base is carried out by 21 Tamil Tiger commandos, with all except one dying in this attack. Eight Sri Lanka Air Force planes are destroyed and ten damaged.

Q1666958.name: London International Surrealist Exhibition
Q1666958.blurb: The London International Surrealist Exhibition opens.

Q1667658.name: TWA Flight 3
Q1667658.blurb: Crash of TWA Flight 3, killing all 22 aboard, including film star Carole Lombard.

Q1669285.name: Sack of Amorium
Q1669285.blurb: The Arabs under Caliph al-Mu'tasim storm and sack the city of Amorium, killing half the population and enslaving the other.

Q1669489.name: Battle of Taillebourg
Q1669489.blurb: Battle of Taillebourg: Louis IX of France puts an end to the revolt of his vassals Henry III of England and Hugh X of Lusignan.

Q1671791.name: Invicta International Airlines Flight 435
Q1671791.blurb: Invicta International Airlines Flight 435 crashes in a snowstorm on approach to Basel, Switzerland, killing 108 people.

Q1672808.name: Irish Confederate Wars
Q1672808.blurb: Irish Confederate Wars: Donough MacCarty, 1st Earl of Clancarty, signed the First Ormond Peace for the Confederates in exchange for greater freedom of religion.

Q1678340.name: Battle of Cable Street
Q1678340.blurb: The Metropolitan Police and various anti-fascist organizations violently clash in the Battle of Cable Street.

Q1678637.name: Battle of Dorylaeum
Q1678637.blurb: Seljuk Turks defeat German crusaders under Conrad III at the Battle of Dorylaeum.

Q1681634.name: Pamir Airways Flight 112
Q1681634.blurb: Pamir Airways Flight 112 crashes in Afghanistan's Shakardara District, killing 44.

Q1687078.name: Operation Earnest Will
Q1687078.blurb: Iran–Iraq War: In opposition to the American plan to protect Kuwaiti tankers, Iran laid mines and damaged the SS Bridgeton, resulting in a propaganda victory for Iran.

Q1693466.name: Pan-American Exposition
Q1693466.blurb: U.S. president William McKinley was fatally shot by anarchist Leon Czolgosz at the Pan-American Exposition in Buffalo, New York, and died eight days later.

Q1694094.name: Second Battle of the Aisne
Q1694094.blurb: World War I: Several French army corps began a massive assault against the German-occupied Chemin des Dames ridge, south of Laon, France.

Q1697391.name: Convention on preventing and combating violence against women and domestic violence
aliases: Council of Europe Convention on Preventing and Combating Violence Against Women and Domestic Violence
Q1697391.blurb: The Istanbul Convention is signed in Istanbul, Turkey.

Q1702253.name: 1990 Romanian general election
Q1702253.blurb: The first post-Communist presidential and parliamentary elections are held in Romania.

Q1703402.name: Harrying of the North
Q1703402.blurb: Robert de Comines, Earl of Northumbria, was killed in Durham, causing William the Conqueror to embark on a campaign to subjugate northern England.

Q1704268.name: Battle of Assandun
Q1704268.blurb: The Danes defeat the English in the Battle of Assandun.

Q1704625.name: 2012 Kazakhstan Antonov An-72 crash
Q1704625.blurb: An Antonov An-72 plane crashes close to the city of Shymkent, killing 27 people.

Q1709493.name: July 2010 Kampala attacks
Q1709493.blurb: The Islamist militia group Al-Shabaab carries out multiple suicide bombings in Kampala, Uganda, killing 74 people and injuring 85 others.

Q1710916.name: Battle of Cedar Creek
Q1710916.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Cedar Creek ends the last Confederate threat to Washington, DC.

Q1716388.name: Athenian coup of 411 BC
Q1716388.blurb: The Athenian coup succeeds, forming a short-lived oligarchy.

Q1719427.name: Battle of Lalakaon
Q1719427.blurb: Major Byzantine victory at the Battle of Lalakaon against an Arab raid.

Q1719918.name: presidency of George W. Bush
Q1719918.blurb: The controversial US presidential election is later resolved in the Bush v. Gore Supreme Court case, electing George W. Bush as the 43rd President of the United States.

Q1728201.name: 1933 NFL Championship Game
Q1728201.blurb: The first NFL Championship Game is played at Wrigley Field in Chicago between the New York Giants and Chicago Bears. The Bears win 23–21.

Q1729627.name: Karine A Affair
Q1729627.blurb: Israeli–Palestinian conflict: Israeli forces seize the Palestinian freighter Karine A in the Red Sea, finding 50 tons of weapons.

Q1735004.name: 1700 Cascadia earthquake
Q1735004.blurb: An earthquake with a moment magnitude of around 9.0 occurred off the Pacific Northwest coast of North America, as evidenced by Japanese records of tsunamis.

Q1738747.name: Kengir uprising
Q1738747.blurb: Beginning of the Kengir uprising in the Gulag.

Q1739099.name: Kenya Airways Flight 507
Q1739099.blurb: Kenya Airways Flight 507 crashes after takeoff from Douala International Airport in Douala, Cameroon, killing all 114 aboard, making it the deadliest aircraft disaster in Cameroon.

Q1739881.name: New Mexico Campaign
Q1739881.blurb: American Civil War: The Confederate Army began an attempt to gain control of the Southwest with a major victory in the Battle of Valverde.

Q1746935.name: Naroda Patiya massacre
Q1746935.blurb: During the religious violence in Gujarat, 97 people are killed in the Naroda Patiya massacre and 69 in the Gulbarg Society massacre.

Q1747156.name: 2002 Gujarat violence
Q1747156.blurb: Violent riots, perceived to have been instigated by a train fire that killed 59 Hindu pilgrims, broke out in the Indian state of Gujarat, killing at least 1,000 people, mostly Muslims, over three days.

Q1748198.name: Treaty of San Germano
Q1748198.blurb: Treaty of San Germano is signed at San Germano between Holy Roman Emperor Frederick II and Pope Gregory IX. A Dominican named Guala is responsible for the negotiations.

Q1748450.name: Battle of Hedgeley Moor
Q1748450.blurb: A Yorkist army under the Baron Montagu defeats a Lancastrian army under the Duke of Somerset in the battle of Hedgeley Moor during the Wars of the Roses.

Q1749007.name: German–Soviet Axis talks
Q1749007.blurb: World War II: Soviet Foreign Minister Vyacheslav Molotov arrives in Berlin to discuss the possibility of the Soviet Union joining the Axis Powers.

Q1750892.name: Siege of Constantinople
Q1750892.blurb: Constantinople falls to the Crusaders of the Fourth Crusade, temporarily ending the Byzantine Empire.

Q1752689.name: Battle of Nashville
Q1752689.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Nashville begins at Nashville, Tennessee, and ends the following day with the destruction of the Confederate Army of Tennessee under General John Bell Hood as a fighting force by the Union Army of the Cumberland under General George H. Thomas.

Q1752752.name: Battle of Mbwila
Q1752752.blurb: Portuguese forces defeat the Kingdom of Kongo and decapitate King António I of Kongo, also known as Nvita a Nkanga.

Q1752783.name: Battle of the Chateauguay
Q1752783.blurb: War of 1812: British forces and Mohawk allies under Charles de Salaberry repulsed an American attempt to invade Canada.

Q1753578.name: Battle of the Bismarck Sea
Q1753578.blurb: World War II: During the Battle of the Bismarck Sea Allied aircraft defeat a Japanese attempt to ship troops to New Guinea.

Q1754313.name: Battle of Bennington
Q1754313.blurb: American Revolutionary War: American forces routed British and German troops at the Battle of Bennington in Walloomsac, New York.

Q1754441.name: August 1978 conclave
Q1754441.blurb: Papal conclave: Albino Luciani is elected as Pope John Paul I.

Q1754443.name: Battle of Edson's Ridge
Q1754443.blurb: World War II: First day of the Battle of Edson's Ridge during the Guadalcanal Campaign. U.S. Marines protecting Henderson Field are attacked by Imperial Japanese Army troops.

Q1754732.name: Battle of Agnadello
Q1754732.blurb: Battle of Agnadello: In northern Italy, French forces defeat the Republic of Venice.

Q1754797.name: Landing at Cape Helles
Q1754797.blurb: World War I: The Battle of Gallipoli begins: The invasion of the Turkish Gallipoli Peninsula by British, French, Indian, Newfoundland, Australian and New Zealand troops begins with landings at Anzac Cove and Cape Helles.

Q1756207.name: United States occupation of the Dominican Republic
Q1756207.blurb: The American occupation of the Dominican Republic ends after eight years.

Q1756366.name: Aeroflot Flight 6833
Q1756366.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 6833 is hijacked en route from Tbilisi to Leningrad. After returning to Tbilisi, the aircraft is subsequently raided on the ground, resulting in seven deaths.

Q1757487.name: Battle of Seven Oaks
Q1757487.blurb: Battle of Seven Oaks between North West Company and Hudson's Bay Company, near Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada.

Q1758028.name: 1980 Turkish coup d'état
aliases: American involvement in the 1980 Turkish coup d'etat
US involvement in the 1980 Turkish coup d'etat
Q1758028.blurb: The 43rd government of Turkey is overthrown in a coup d'état led by General Kenan Evren.

Q1758473.name: Battle of Hatfield Chase
Q1758473.blurb: Battle of Hatfield Chase: King Edwin of Northumbria is defeated and killed by an alliance under Penda of Mercia and Cadwallon of Gwynedd.

Q1758572.name: Hook and Cod Wars
Q1758572.blurb: Margaret II, Countess of Hainaut and Holy Roman Empress and her son William I, Duke of Bavaria, sign a peace treaty ending the Hook and Cod wars.

Q1759544.name: Palmer Raids
Q1759544.blurb: The second Palmer Raid, ordered by the US Department of Justice, results in 6,000 suspected communists and anarchists being arrested and held without trial.

Q1760231.name: Battle of Clontibret
Q1760231.blurb: A Gaelic Irish army successfully ambushes an English force in the battle of Clontibret during the Nine Years' War.

Q1762806.name: RusAir Flight 9605
Q1762806.blurb: RusAir Flight 9605 crashes in Besovets during approach to Petrozavodsk Airport, killing 47.

Q1764124.name: Third Mithridatic War
Q1764124.blurb: Third Mithridatic War: The military of the Roman Republic subdues Armenia.

Q1765847.name: Attack on H3
Q1765847.blurb: Iran–Iraq War: The Islamic Republic of Iran Air Force mounts an attack on H-3 Airbase and destroys about 50 Iraqi aircraft.

Q1765888.name: Otłoczyn railway accident
Q1765888.blurb: Otłoczyn railway accident: In Poland's worst post-war railway accident, 67 people lose their lives and a further 62 are injured.

Q1766751.name: Constellation program
Q1766751.blurb: NASA successfully launches the Ares I-X mission, the only rocket launch for its short-lived Constellation program.

Q1767332.name: Battle of Landen
Q1767332.blurb: War of the Grand Alliance: Battle of Landen: France wins a victory over Allied forces in the Netherlands.

Q1767634.name: Air Bagan Flight 11
Q1767634.blurb: Air Bagan Flight 011, a Fokker 100, crashes on approach to Heho Airport in Heho, Myanmar, killing two people.

Q1769884.name: Comorian independence referendum, 1974
Q1769884.blurb: Grande Comore, Anjouan and Mohéli vote to become the independent nation of Comoros. Mayotte remains under French administration.

Q1770727.name: Battle of Sark
Q1770727.blurb: Scotland wins a decisive victory over England at the Battle of Sark, the last pitched battle to be fought between the two kingdoms during the Medieval period.

Q1771974.name: Norwegian union dissolution referendum
Q1771974.blurb: Norwegians vote to end the union with Sweden.

Q1772340.name: Battle of Elaia–Kalamas
Q1772340.blurb: World War II: First day of Battle of Elaia–Kalamas between the Greeks and the Italians.

Q1772463.name: Battle of Reading
Q1772463.blurb: Glorious Revolution: Williamite forces defeat Jacobites at Battle of Reading, forcing James II to flee England.

Q1773668.name: Warsaw Pact invasion of Czechoslovakia
aliases: Invaze vojsk Varšavské smlouvy do Československa
Vpád vojsk Varšavskej zmluvy do Česko-Slovenska
Warsaw Pact invasion of Czechoslovakia in 1968
Q1773668.blurb: Cold War: Warsaw Pact troops invade Czechoslovakia, crushing the Prague Spring. East German participation is limited to a few specialists due to memories of the recent war. Only Albania and Romania refuse to participate.

Q1773926.name: Congo Crisis
Q1773926.blurb: Congo Crisis: The State of Katanga breaks away from the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Q1773984.name: Battle of Chamdo
aliases: People's Liberation Army invasion of Tibet
People's Liberation Army invasion of Tibet (1950-1951)
People's Liberation Army invasion of Tibet (1950–1951)
People's Liberation Army liberation of Tibet (1950-1951)
People's Liberation Army liberation of Tibet (1950–1951)
People's Liberation Army operations in Tibet (1950-1951)
People's Liberation Army operations in Tibet (1950–1951)
Q1773984.blurb: China defeats the Tibetan Army at Chambo.

Q1775068.name: Alitalia Flight 112
Q1775068.blurb: Alitalia Flight 112 crashes into Mount Longa near Palermo, Sicily, killing all 115 aboard, making it the deadliest single-aircraft disaster in Italy.

Q1775286.name: deportation of the Crimean Tatars
Q1775286.blurb: Deportation of Crimean Tatars by the Soviet Union.

Q1775296.name: Space Shuttle program
Q1775296.blurb: Space Shuttle program: STS-72 launches from the Kennedy Space Center marking the start of the 74th Space Shuttle mission and the 10th flight of Endeavour.

Q1775801.name: Battle of Sari Bair
Q1775801.blurb: World War I: Battle of Sari Bair: The Allies mount a diversionary attack timed to coincide with a major Allied landing of reinforcements at Suvla Bay.

Q1779428.name: Siege of Fort St. Jean
Q1779428.blurb: American Revolutionary War: The invasion of Quebec by the Continental Army begins with the Siege of Fort St. Jean.

Q1779439.name: Battle of The Cedars
Q1779439.blurb: American Revolutionary War: A Continental Army garrison surrenders in the Battle of The Cedars.

Q1780216.name: Angolan War of Independence
Q1780216.blurb: The Angolan War of Independence and the greater Portuguese Colonial War begin.

Q1780431.name: 1952 Egyptian revolution
aliases: Causes of the Egyptian revolution of 1952
Q1780431.blurb: The Egyptian revolution of 1952 ends with the overthrow of the Muhammad Ali dynasty and the declaration of the Republic of Egypt.

Q1780548.name: Shankill Road bombing
Q1780548.blurb: The Troubles: A Provisional IRA bomb prematurely detonates in Belfast, killing the bomber and nine civilians.

Q1780931.name: Battle of Fort Royal
Q1780931.blurb: American Revolutionary War: British and French ships clash in the Battle of Fort Royal off the coast of Martinique.

Q1781104.name: Southern Airways Flight 242
Q1781104.blurb: Southern Airways Flight 242 crashes in New Hope, Paulding County, Georgia, killing 72.

Q1781240.name: Greysteel massacre
Q1781240.blurb: The Troubles: Three members of the Ulster Defence Association opened fire in a crowded pub during a Halloween party, killing eight people and wounding nineteen others.

Q1781531.name: Atrocities in the Congo Free State
Q1781531.blurb: As a result of numerous atrocities in the territory, the Congo Free State was annexed to Belgium to form the Belgian Congo.

Q1782419.name: Treaty of the Triple Alliance
Q1782419.blurb: The Empire of Brazil, Argentina, and Uruguay sign the Treaty of the Triple Alliance.

Q1783157.name: Cave of the Patriarchs massacre
Q1783157.blurb: American-Israeli extremist Baruch Goldstein commits a mass shooting at the Cave of the Patriarchs mausoleum, leaving 29 dead and over 100 injured before he is disarmed and beaten to death by survivors.

Q1783607.name: Salvadoran Civil War
aliases: Guerra civil de El Salvador en 1951
United States involvement in the Salvadoran Civil War
Q1783607.blurb: Salvadoran Civil War: The FMLN launches its first major offensive, gaining control of most of Morazán and Chalatenango departments.

Q1784617.name: Battle of May Island
