Q1784617.blurb: A series of accidental collisions due to poor visibility leads to the loss of two Royal Navy submarines with over a hundred lives, and damage to another five British warships.

Q1784770.name: Constitution of Chile
aliases: Political Constitution of the Republic of Chile
Q1784770.blurb: A new constitution of Chile is established under the influence of then Chilean dictator Augusto Pinochet, which is subject to controversy in Chile today.

Q1784832.name: Battle of Vicy
Q1784832.blurb: Battle of Vincy between Charles Martel and Ragenfrid.

Q1784900.name: Lincoln County War
Q1784900.blurb: Competition between two American merchants in Lincoln County, New Mexico Territory, turned into a range war when a member of one faction was murdered by the other.

Q1784968.name: assassination of Benazir Bhutto
aliases: Benazir Bhutto killed in suicide attack
Assassination of Former Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto
Riots in reaction of Benazir Bhutto Assassination
Riots in reaction to Benazir Bhutto assassination
Riots in reaction to the assassination of Benazir Bhutto
United Nations Commission of Inquiry into the facts and circumstances of the assassination of former Pakistani Prime Minister Mohtarma Benazir Bhutto
Q1784968.blurb: Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto was assassinated while leaving a Pakistan People's Party political rally at Liaqat National Bagh in Rawalpindi.

Q1785309.name: Myall Creek massacre
Q1785309.blurb: Myall Creek massacre: Twenty-eight Aboriginal Australians are murdered.

Q1785910.name: Battle of Horseshoe Bend
Q1785910.blurb: War of 1812: In central Alabama, U.S. forces under General Andrew Jackson defeat the Creek at the Battle of Horseshoe Bend.

Q1786733.name: República Cromañón nightclub fire
Q1786733.blurb: A fire in the República Cromagnon nightclub in Buenos Aires, Argentina, kills 194.

Q1786801.name: Battle of the Crater
Q1786801.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of the Crater: Union forces attempt to break Confederate lines at Petersburg, Virginia by exploding a large bomb under their trenches.

Q1787252.name: Battle of Lenzen
Q1787252.blurb: Battle of Lenzen: Slavic forces (the Redarii and the Obotrites) are defeated by a Saxon army near the fortified stronghold of Lenzen in Brandenburg.

Q1787448.name: Pride's Purge
Q1787448.blurb: Pride's Purge removes royalist sympathizers from Parliament so that the High Court of Justice could put the King on trial.

Q1788040.name: July 12, 2007 Baghdad airstrike
Q1788040.blurb: Two U.S. Army AH-64 Apache helicopters (pictured) conducted a series of air-to-ground attacks in Baghdad.

Q1788393.name: Battle of Shiroyama
Q1788393.blurb: The Battle of Shiroyama is a decisive victory of the Imperial Japanese Army over the Satsuma Rebellion.

Q1788823.name: German Imperial War Council of 8 December 1912
Q1788823.blurb: Leaders of the German Empire hold an Imperial War Council to discuss the possibility that war might break out.

Q1789376.name: Battle of Kwajalein
Q1789376.blurb: World War II: During the Gilbert and Marshall Islands campaign, U.S. Army and Marine forces seize Kwajalein Atoll from the defending Japanese garrison.

Q1791483.name: Summer Street Bridge Disaster
Q1791483.blurb: Boston Elevated Railway Company's streetcar No. 393 smashes through the warning gates of the open Summer Street drawbridge in Boston, Massachusetts, plunging into the frigid waters of Fort Point Channel, killing 46 people.

Q1792643.name: Battle of Río Salado
Q1792643.blurb: Reconquista: Portuguese and Castilian forces halt a Muslim invasion at the Battle of Río Salado.

Q1793109.name: Battle of Chippawa
Q1793109.blurb: War of 1812: Battle of Chippawa: American Major General Jacob Brown defeats British General Phineas Riall at Chippawa, Ontario.

Q1797867.name: LANSA Flight 508
Q1797867.blurb: LANSA Flight 508 is struck by lightning and crashes in the Puerto Inca District in the Department of Huánuco in Peru, killing 91.

Q1798567.name: 1985 Mexico City earthquake
Q1798567.blurb: A strong earthquake kills thousands and destroys about 400 buildings in Mexico City.

Q1801770.name: Lancaster House Agreement
Q1801770.blurb: Lancaster House Agreement: An independence agreement for Rhodesia is signed in London by Lord Carrington, Sir Ian Gilmour, Robert Mugabe, Joshua Nkomo, Bishop Abel Muzorewa and S.C. Mundawarara.

Q1802702.name: death of Marilyn Monroe
Q1802702.blurb: American actress Marilyn Monroe is found dead at her home from a drug overdose.

Q1804983.name: Battle of Baghdad
Q1804983.blurb: Iraq War: U.S. troops capture Baghdad; Saddam Hussein's Ba'athist regime falls two days later.

Q1806552.name: Rebellion of Túpac Amaru II
Q1806552.blurb: The Rebellion of Túpac Amaru II against Spanish rule in the Viceroyalty of Peru begins.

Q1807251.name: Battle of La Higueruela
Q1807251.blurb: The Battle of La Higueruela takes place in Granada, leading to a modest advance of the Kingdom of Castile during the Reconquista.

Q1808373.name: Ronan Point
Q1808373.blurb: A gas explosion in Ronan Point (collapse pictured) causes a corner of the building to collapse, leading to a loss of public confidence in high-rise residential buildings.

Q1808450.name: Battle of Buena Vista
Q1808450.blurb: Mexican–American War: The Battle of Buena Vista: Five thousand American troops defeat 15,000 Mexican troops.

Q1810832.name: Operation Carthage
Q1810832.blurb: World War II: Operation Carthage: Royal Air Force planes bomb Gestapo headquarters in Copenhagen, Denmark. They also accidentally hit a school, killing 125 civilians.

Q1811438.name: Battle of Waxhaws
Q1811438.blurb: American Revolutionary War: At the Waxhaws Massacre, the British continue attacking after the Continentals lay down their arms, killing 113 and critically wounding all but 53 that remained.

Q1814248.name: Battle of Haarlemmermeer
Q1814248.blurb: The Battle of Haarlemmermeer, a naval engagement in the Eighty Years' War.

Q1814324.name: Vinnytsia massacre
Q1814324.blurb: Sergei Kirov is assassinated, paving way for the repressive Great Purge, and Vinnytsia massacre by General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union, Joseph Stalin.

Q1814439.name: Kishinev pogrom
aliases: Victims of the Pogrom of 1903 Memorial
Q1814439.blurb: The Kishinev pogrom in Kishinev (Bessarabia) begins, forcing tens of thousands of Jews to later seek refuge in Palestine and the Western world.

Q1814446.name: King David Hotel bombing
aliases: Bombing of the King David Hotel
Bombing of the King David Hotel in 1946
Q1814446.blurb: King David Hotel bombing: A Zionist underground organisation, the Irgun, bombs the King David Hotel in Jerusalem, site of the civil administration and military headquarters for Mandatory Palestine, resulting in 91 deaths.

Q1814824.name: Kraków pogrom
Q1814824.blurb: Poles in Kraków engage in a pogrom against Jews in the city, killing one and wounding five.

Q1816176.name: 2008 Georgian presidential election
Q1816176.blurb: Mikheil Saakashvili was decisively re-elected as President of Georgia in "the first genuinely competitive presidential election" in the history of the country.

Q1816505.name: Philippine Airlines Flight 434
Q1816505.blurb: A bomb explodes on Philippine Airlines Flight 434, en route from Manila, Philippines, to Tokyo, Japan, killing one. The captain is able to land the plane safely.

Q1817678.name: Tropical Storm Zeta
Q1817678.blurb: Tropical Storm Zeta forms in the open Atlantic Ocean, tying the record for the latest tropical cyclone ever to form in the North Atlantic basin.

Q1818410.name: Battle of Maserfield
Q1818410.blurb: Battle of Maserfield: Penda of Mercia defeats and kills Oswald of Northumbria.

Q1818854.name: Battle of Monte Castello
Q1818854.blurb: World War II:  the Brazilian Expeditionary Force defeat the German forces in the Battle of Monte Castello on the Italian front.

Q1821843.name: Battle of Fort Pillow
Q1821843.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Fort Pillow: Confederate forces kill most of the African American soldiers that surrendered at Fort Pillow, Tennessee.

Q1824714.name: Tulsa Race Massacre
Q1824714.blurb: The Tulsa race massacre kills at least 39, but other estimates of black fatalities vary from 55 to about 300.

Q1826682.name: 1981 protests in Kosovo
Q1826682.blurb: Hundreds of students protest in the University of Pristina in Kosovo, then part of Yugoslavia, to give their province more political rights. The protests then became a nationwide movement.

Q1827267.name: Byzantine–Seljuq Wars
Q1827267.blurb: Byzantine–Seljuk wars: Seljuk Turks led by Alp Arslan captured Byzantine emperor Romanos IV at the Battle of Manzikert.

Q1827323.name: Pan Am Flight 214
Q1827323.blurb: Pan Am Flight 214, a Boeing 707, is struck by lightning and crashes near Elkton, Maryland, killing all 81 people on board.

Q1834148.name: Siege of Rome
Q1834148.blurb: Siege of Rome: The Ostrogoth army under king Vitiges begins the siege of the capital. Belisarius conducts a delaying action outside the Flaminian Gate; he and a detachment of his bucellarii are almost cut off.

Q1840117.name: Battle of Quebec
Q1840117.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Battle of Quebec: British forces under General Guy Carleton repulse an attack by Continental Army General Richard Montgomery in a snowstorm.

Q1844815.name: Battle of Dynekilen
Q1844815.blurb: The Battle of Dynekilen forces Sweden to abandon its invasion of Norway.

Q1846324.name: Omaha Race Riot of 1919
Q1846324.blurb: Race riots begin in Omaha, Nebraska, United States.

Q1847006.name: 1976 Guatemala earthquake
Q1847006.blurb: In Guatemala and Honduras an earthquake kills more than 22,000.

Q1848392.name: Super Bowl XVIII
Q1848392.blurb: During Super Bowl XVIII, Apple Computer introduced the Macintosh, the first successful personal computer to use a graphical user interface, with the television commercial "1984".

Q1848590.name: Battle of Tốt Động – Chúc Động
Q1848590.blurb: Lam Sơn uprising: Lam Sơn rebels emerge victorious against the Ming army in the Battle of Tốt Động – Chúc Động taking place in Đông Quan, in now Hanoi.

Q1848807.name: Lam Sơn uprising
Q1848807.blurb: Lam Sơn uprising: Lam Sơn rebels emerge victorious against the Ming army in the Battle of Tốt Động – Chúc Động taking place in Đông Quan, in now Hanoi.

Q1850527.name: Battle of Baltimore
Q1850527.blurb: Battle of Baltimore: The poem Defence of Fort McHenry is written by Francis Scott Key. The poem is later used as the lyrics of The Star-Spangled Banner.

Q1850800.name: Battle of the Saintes
Q1850800.blurb: American Revolution: A Royal Navy fleet led by Admiral George Rodney defeats a French fleet led by the Comte de Grasse at the Battle of the Saintes off Dominica in the Caribbean Sea.

Q1851018.name: Primeiro Comando da Capital
Q1851018.blurb: Mass unrest by the Primeiro Comando da Capital begins in São Paulo (Brazil), leaving at least 150 dead.

Q1851212.name: Batepá massacre
Q1851212.blurb: The Batepá massacre occurs in São Tomé when the colonial administration and Portuguese landowners unleash a wave of violence against the native creoles known as forros.

Q1851858.name: Dakota War of 1862
Q1851858.blurb: Dakota War: During an uprising in Minnesota, Lakota warriors decide not to attack heavily defended Fort Ridgely and instead turn to the settlement of New Ulm, killing white settlers along the way.

Q1851980.name: Malév Flight 240
Q1851980.blurb: Malév Flight 240 crashes into the Mediterranean Sea while on approach to Beirut International Airport in Beirut, Lebanon, killing 60.

Q1852373.name: Battle of the Standard
Q1852373.blurb: Battle of the Standard between Scotland and England.

Q1853552.name: Battle of Campbell's Station
Q1853552.blurb: American Civil War: In the Battle of Campbell's Station, Confederate troops unsuccessfully attack Union forces which allows General Ambrose Burnside to secure Knoxville, Tennessee.

Q1855461.name: Battle of Lincoln
Q1855461.blurb: The Second Battle of Lincoln is fought near Lincoln, England, resulting in the defeat of Prince Louis of France by William Marshal, 1st Earl of Pembroke.

Q1859259.name: 1960 Turkish coup d'état
Q1859259.blurb: In Turkey, a military coup removes President Celâl Bayar and the rest of the democratic government from office.

Q1859354.name: Operation Dawn 5
Q1859354.blurb: Iran launches Operation Dawn 5, a major offensive during the Iran–Iraq War targeting the Basra–Baghdad highway, resulting in heavy casualties on both sides.

Q1860257.name: Cromwellian conquest of Ireland
Q1860257.blurb: Cromwellian conquest of Ireland: Oliver Cromwell's New Model Army ended the Siege of Drogheda, took over the town and massacred its garrison.

Q1860316.name: Battle of Dogger Bank
Q1860316.blurb: British and Dutch ships engage in the second Battle of Dogger Bank.

Q1861319.name: Battle of Slivnitsa
Q1861319.blurb: Serbo-Bulgarian War: The decisive Battle of Slivnitsa begins.

Q1861428.name: Battle of the Heligoland Bight
Q1861428.blurb: World War II: The Battle of the Heligoland Bight, the first major air battle of the war, takes place.

Q1862475.name: Battle of Marsaglia
Q1862475.blurb: Nine Years' War: Piedmontese troops are defeated by the French.

Q1864998.name: Lagos armoury explosion
Q1864998.blurb: An explosion at a military storage facility in Lagos, Nigeria, kills at least 1,100 people and displaces over 20,000 others.

Q1865863.name: Cavalese cable car disaster
Q1865863.blurb: Cavalese cable car disaster: A United States military pilot causes the death of 20 people when his low-flying plane cuts the cable of a cable-car near Trento, Italy.

Q1872409.name: Love Canal
Q1872409.blurb: U.S. President Jimmy Carter declares a federal emergency at Love Canal due to toxic waste that had been disposed of negligently.

Q1874172.name: Federal Express Flight 705
Q1874172.blurb: Auburn Calloway attempts to destroy Federal Express Flight 705 in order to allow his family to benefit from his life insurance policy.

Q1874850.name: Treaty of Moscow
Q1874850.blurb: Treaty of Moscow: Soviet Russia recognizes the independence of the Democratic Republic of Georgia only to invade the country six months later.

Q1875552.name: Attack on Broome
Q1875552.blurb: World War II: Ten Japanese warplanes raid Broome, Western Australia, killing more than 100 people.

Q1875586.name: Coventry Blitz
Q1875586.blurb: World War II: In England, Coventry is heavily bombed by German Luftwaffe bombers. Coventry Cathedral is almost completely destroyed.

Q1875659.name: Lufthansa CityLine Flight 5634
Q1875659.blurb: Four people are killed when Lufthansa CityLine Flight 5634 crashes on approach to Charles de Gaulle Airport in Roissy-en-France, France.

Q1875662.name: Lufthansa heist
Q1875662.blurb: The Lufthansa heist is committed by a group led by Lucchese family associate Jimmy Burke. It was the largest cash robbery ever committed on American soil, at that time.

Q1877202.name: Bolivian gas conflict
Q1877202.blurb: Bolivian gas conflict: Bolivian President Gonzalo Sánchez de Lozada is forced to resign and leave Bolivia.

Q1879847.name: Sterling Hall bombing
Q1879847.blurb: Vietnam War protesters bomb Sterling Hall at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, leading to an international manhunt for the perpetrators.

Q1883854.name: St. Mary Magdalene's flood
Q1883854.blurb: St. Mary Magdalene's flood is the worst such event on record for central Europe.

Q1885246.name: Barcelona May Days
Q1885246.blurb: Spanish Civil War: The Largo Caballero government resigns in the wake of the Barcelona May Days, leading Juan Negrín to form a government, without the anarcho-syndicalist CNT, in its stead.

Q1887009.name: Battle of Morlaix
Q1887009.blurb: Battle of Morlaix is fought in the Hundred Years' War.

Q1887057.name: Battle of Halidon Hill
Q1887057.blurb: Wars of Scottish Independence: The English win a decisive victory over the Scots in the battle of Halidon Hill.

Q1887247.name: Malet coup of 1812
Q1887247.blurb: General Claude François de Malet begins a conspiracy to overthrow Napoleon, claiming that the Emperor died in the Russian campaign.

Q1887494.name: Battle of Uji
Q1887494.blurb: First Battle of Uji, starting the Genpei War in Japan.

Q1887932.name: Battle of Castelfidardo
Q1887932.blurb: Wars of Italian Unification: Battle of Castelfidardo: Royal Sardinian Army defeats forces of the Papal States, resulting in the conquest of Umbria and Marche by the Kingdom of Italy.

Q1889748.name: Strategic Offensive Reductions Treaty
Q1889748.blurb: Russia and the United States sign the Moscow Treaty.

Q1890554.name: Mann Gulch fire
Q1890554.blurb: In Montana, 12 smokejumper firefighters and a US Forest Service fire guard are killed in the Mann Gulch Fire.

Q1890705.name: 1968 Olympics Black Power salute
Q1890705.blurb: Tommie Smith and John Carlos are ejected from the US Olympic team for participating in the Olympics Black Power salute.

Q1891307.name: Gildonic revolt
Q1891307.blurb: End of the Gildonic rebellion after Gildo's forces are defeated by forces loyal to Western Roman Emperor Honorius under Gildo's brother Mascezel and Gildo's subsequent death.

Q1892489.name: Battle of Grand Couronné
Q1892489.blurb: World War I: Start of the Battle of Grand Couronné, a German assault against French positions on high ground near the city of Nancy.

Q1894062.name: Battle of Tagliacozzo
Q1894062.blurb: The Battle of Tagliacozzo: The army of Prince Conradin is nearly destroyed by Charles of Anjou, ending Hohenstaufen control over the Kingdom of Sicily and leaving the Angevins in control.

Q1897862.name: 1945 French legislative election
Q1897862.blurb: In the 1945 French legislative election French women vote for the first time.

Q1899132.name: Black Friday
Q1899132.blurb: Black Friday, a massacre by soldiers against protesters in Tehran, results in 88 deaths, it marks the beginning of the end of the monarchy in Iran.

Q1901096.name: Battle of Carthage
Q1901096.blurb: During the year of Six Emperors, forces of Gordian I and Gordian II are defeated by those of Maximinus Thrax in the battle of Carthage.

Q1907348.name: Thammasat University massacre
Q1907348.blurb: Dozens are killed by Thai police and right-wing paramilitaries in the Thammasat University massacre; afterwards, the Seni Pramoj government is toppled in a military coup led by Sangad Chaloryu.

Q1907402.name: Karantina massacre
Q1907402.blurb: Lebanese Christian militias kill at least 1,000 in Karantina, Beirut.

Q1907538.name: Accra Sports Stadium disaster
Q1907538.blurb: In Ghana, 129 football fans die in what became known as the Accra Sports Stadium disaster. The deaths are caused by a stampede (caused by the firing of tear gas by police personnel at the stadium) that followed a controversial decision by the referee.

Q1908014.name: Mat Salleh Rebellion
Q1908014.blurb: Datu Muhammad Salleh is killed in Kampung Teboh, Tambunan, ending the Mat Salleh Rebellion.

Q1911564.name: Mauritius campaign
Q1911564.blurb: Mauritius campaign of 1809–1811: A French frigate squadron under Guy-Victor Duperré defeated a convoy of three British East Indiamen near the Comoro Islands.

Q1913209.name: Battle of Axpoele
Q1913209.blurb: William Clito defeated Thierry of Alsace in a battle over the succession to the title of Count of Flanders.

Q1915188.name: Surinamese Interior War
Q1915188.blurb: The Surinamese military attacks the village of Moiwana during the Suriname Guerrilla War, killing at least 39 civilians, mostly women and children.

Q1915698.name: Mecklenburg Resolves
Q1915698.blurb: American Revolution: The Mecklenburg Resolves are adopted in the Province of North Carolina.

Q1922071.name: Indo-Pakistani War of 1971
aliases: Indian military intervention in Pakistani Civil War
Indian military intervention in the Pakistani Civil War
List of films about 1971 India-Pakistan war
Q1922071.blurb: Indo-Pakistani War of 1971: Pakistan launches a pre-emptive strike against India and a full-scale war begins.

Q1922654.name: Henan Airlines Flight 8387
Q1922654.blurb: Henan Airlines Flight 8387 crashes at Yichun Lindu Airport in Yichun, Heilongjiang, China, killing 44 out of the 96 people on board.

Q1924192.name: Hotel Polen fire
Q1924192.blurb: The Hotel Polen in Amsterdam was destroyed by fire (pictured), leaving 33 people dead.

Q1925730.name: 1979 energy crisis
Q1925730.blurb: Ronald Reagan lifts remaining domestic petroleum price and allocation controls in the United States, helping to end the 1979 energy crisis and begin the 1980s oil glut.

Q1926157.name: Meuse-Argonne Offensive
Q1926157.blurb: World War I: The Meuse-Argonne Offensive began which would last until the total surrender of German forces.

Q1926257.name: Pancho Villa Expedition
Q1926257.blurb: Six days after Pancho Villa and his cross-border raiders attacked Columbus, New Mexico, U.S. general John J. Pershing led a punitive expedition into Mexico to pursue him.

Q1927362.name: Operation Pedestal
Q1927362.blurb: World War II: Operation Pedestal: The oil tanker SS Ohio reaches the island of Malta barely afloat carrying vital fuel supplies for the island's defenses.

Q1929123.name: Hadassah medical convoy massacre
Q1929123.blurb: In an ambush, 78 Jewish doctors, nurses and medical students from Hadassah Hospital, and a British soldier, are massacred by Arabs in Sheikh Jarrah. This event came to be known as the Hadassah medical convoy massacre.

Q1930278.name: Battle of Karameh
Q1930278.blurb: Battle of Karameh in Jordan between the Israel Defense Forces and the combined forces of the Jordanian Armed Forces and PLO.

Q1934137.name: Battle of Torvioll
Q1934137.blurb: Skanderbeg defeats an Ottoman invasion force at Torvioll.

Q1934345.name: Battle of Malvern Hill
Q1934345.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Malvern Hill takes place. It is the last of the Seven Days Battles, part of George B. McClellan's Peninsula Campaign.

Q1935163.name: 1960 South Vietnamese coup attempt
Q1935163.blurb: A coup attempt by the Army of the Republic of Vietnam against President Ngô Đình Diệm was crushed after he falsely promised reform, allowing loyalists to rescue him.

Q1935947.name: Battle of Eniwetok
Q1935947.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Eniwetok begins. The battle ends in an American victory on February 22.

Q1936381.name: 2010 Salang avalanches
Q1936381.blurb: Over 2 miles (3.2 km) of road are buried after a storm in the Hindu Kush mountains of Afghanistan triggers a series of avalanches, killing at least 172 people and trapping over 2,000 others.

Q1940446.name: Monmouth Rebellion
Q1940446.blurb: Monmouth Rebellion: James Scott, 1st Duke of Monmouth declares himself King of England at Bridgwater.

Q1945321.name: Pulkovo Aviation Enterprise Flight 612
Q1945321.blurb: Pulkovo Aviation Enterprise Flight 612 crashes near the Russian border over eastern Ukraine, killing all 170 people on board.

Q1949177.name: Sunday Times Golden Globe Race
Q1949177.blurb: British yachtsman Sir Robin Knox-Johnston wins the Sunday Times Golden Globe Race and completes the first solo non-stop circumnavigation of the world.

Q1952979.name: Northern Virginia Campaign
Q1952979.blurb: American Civil War: Confederate forces under General Stonewall Jackson inflict heavy casualties in the Battle of Chantilly during the Union withdrawal from the Northern Virginia campaign.

Q1960121.name: 1958 NFL Championship Game
Q1960121.blurb: "Greatest Game Ever Played": The Baltimore Colts defeat the New York Giants in the first ever National Football League sudden death overtime game at New York's Yankee Stadium to win the NFL Championship.

Q1960983.name: Great Seimas of Vilnius
Q1960983.blurb: The Great Seimas of Vilnius met to discuss national concerns within Lithuania: they decided to demand wide political autonomy within the Russian Empire.

Q1962709.name: Ingrian War
Q1962709.blurb: Sweden signed the Treaty of Stolbovo to end the Ingrian War with Russia, making large territorial gains.

Q1964751.name: Nansen's Fram expedition (1893–1896)
aliases: Norwegian Arctic Expedition in the Fram
Q1964751.blurb: An Arctic expedition led by Norwegian explorer Fridtjof Nansen (pictured) reached 86°13.6′N, almost three degrees beyond the previous Farthest North latitude.

Q1965086.name: 2005 Palestinian presidential election
Q1965086.blurb: Mahmoud Abbas wins the election to succeed Yasser Arafat as President of the Palestinian National Authority, replacing interim president Rawhi Fattouh.

Q1966827.name: Pawłokoma massacre
Q1966827.blurb: A Polish Home Army unit massacred at least 150 Ukrainian civilians in Pawłokoma, Poland.

Q1967582.name: Pangkor Treaty of 1874
Q1967582.blurb: The Treaty of Pangkor is signed between the British and Sultan Abdullah of Perak, paving the way for further British colonization of Malaya.

Q1967790.name: Battle of Oliwa
Q1967790.blurb: The Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth Navy has its greatest and last naval victory in the Battle of Oliwa.

Q1968528.name: Operation Black Buck
Q1968528.blurb: Operation Black Buck: The Royal Air Force attacks the Argentine Air Force during the Falklands War.

Q1968718.name: Great Syrian Revolt
Q1968718.blurb: Great Syrian Revolt: Rebels led by Fawzi al-Qawuqji capture Hama from the French Mandate of Syria.

Q1968883.name: Battle of Methven
Q1968883.blurb: The Earl of Pembroke's army defeats Bruce's Scottish army at the Battle of Methven.

Q1970005.name: Battle of Keren
Q1970005.blurb: World War II: Free French and British forces began the Battle of Keren to capture the strategic town of Keren in Italian East Africa.

Q1970159.name: Battle of Grenada
Q1970159.blurb: Battle of Grenada: The French defeat British naval forces in the Caribbean during the American Revolutionary War.

Q1970207.name: Battle of Cross Keys
Q1970207.blurb: American Civil War: A Confederate victory by forces under General Stonewall Jackson at the Battle of Cross Keys, along with the Battle of Port Republic the next day, prevents Union forces from reinforcing General George B. McClellan in his Peninsula campaign.

Q1970760.name: Tropical Storm Alpha
Q1970760.blurb: Tropical Storm Alpha forms in the Atlantic Basin, making the 2005 Atlantic hurricane season the most active Atlantic hurricane season until surpassed by the 2020 season.

Q1970833.name: Scottish National Antarctic Expedition
Q1970833.blurb: Scottish National Antarctic Expedition: Led by William Speirs Bruce, the Antarctic region of Coats Land is discovered from the Scotia.

Q1971473.name: Ridolfi plot
Q1971473.blurb: Thomas Howard, 4th Duke of Norfolk is tried and found guilty of treason for his part in the Ridolfi plot to restore Catholicism in England.

Q1972096.name: Battle of Grozny
Q1972096.blurb: Second Chechen War: As the Battle of Grozny came to a close, Russian forces summarily executed at least 60 civilians in Grozny's Novye Aldi suburb.

Q1973105.name: 2010 Times Square car bombing attempt
Q1973105.blurb: Faisal Shahzad attempts to detonate a car bomb in Times Square, but the bomb fails to go off.

Q1973800.name: Battle of the Yellow Ford
Q1973800.blurb: Nine Years' War: Battle of the Yellow Ford: Irish forces under Hugh O'Neill, Earl of Tyrone, defeat an English expeditionary force under Henry Bagenal.

Q1975512.name: 1977 Moscow bombings
Q1975512.blurb: Three bombs explode in Moscow, Russia, Soviet Union, within 37 minutes, killing seven. The bombings are attributed to an Armenian separatist group.

Q1975720.name: 1999 Armenian parliament shooting
Q1975720.blurb: Gunmen open fire in the Armenian Parliament, killing the Prime Minister and seven others.

Q1977453.name: second-wave feminism
aliases: Feminist Movement in the United States (1963-1982)
Feminist Movement in the United States (1963–1982)
Feminist movement in the United States (1963-82)
Feminist movement in the United States (1963–82)
Women's Movement in the United States (1963-1982)
Q1977453.blurb: Betty Friedan's The Feminine Mystique, a non-fiction book credited with sparking the beginning of second-wave feminism in the United States, was first published.

Q1977699.name: Battle of Muizenberg
Q1977699.blurb: Britain seizes the Dutch Cape Colony in southern Africa to prevent its use by the Batavian Republic.

Q1980316.name: EDSA Revolution of 2001
Q1980316.blurb: President of the Philippines Joseph Estrada is ousted in a nonviolent four-day revolution, and is succeeded by Gloria Macapagal Arroyo.

Q1980621.name: Treaty of Constantinople
Q1980621.blurb: The Treaty of Constantinople ends the 16-year-long First Ottoman–Venetian War.

Q1981024.name: Siege of Ryazan (1237)
Q1981024.blurb: The city of Ryazan is sacked by the Mongol army of Batu Khan.

Q1981397.name: Holmes's Bonfire
Q1981397.blurb: Second Anglo-Dutch War: Rear Admiral Robert Holmes leads a raid on the Dutch island of Terschelling, destroying 116 to 160 merchant ships, an act later known as "Holmes's Bonfire".

Q1981631.name: attempted assassination of Harry S. Truman
Q1981631.blurb: Puerto Rican nationalists Griselio Torresola and Oscar Collazo attempt to assassinate US President Harry S. Truman at Blair House.

Q1982745.name: Spanish Revolution
Q1982745.blurb: The July 1936 military uprising in Barcelona is defeated by anarchist militias and Republican loyalists, beginning the Spanish Revolution of 1936.

Q1983009.name: Futurist Manifesto
Q1983009.blurb: Publication of the Futurist Manifesto in the French journal Le Figaro.

Q1983034.name: Second Continental Congress
Q1983034.blurb: American Revolutionary War: The Second Continental Congress takes place in Philadelphia.

Q1983926.name: Battle of Sidi Bou Zid
Q1983926.blurb: World War II: Tunisia Campaign: General Hans-Jürgen von Arnim's Fifth Panzer Army launches a counter-attack against Allied positions in Tunisia.

Q1985730.name: Homestead Strike
Q1985730.blurb: The Homestead Strike begins near Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

Q1985934.name: Battle of Winchelsea
Q1985934.blurb: Battle of Winchelsea (or Les Espagnols sur Mer): The English naval fleet under King Edward III defeats a Castilian fleet of 40 ships.

Q1987213.name: Battle of Dyrrhachium
Q1987213.blurb: The Normans defeat the Byzantine Empire in the Battle of Dyrrhachium.

Q1987713.name: Operation Blue Star
aliases: Siege of the Holy Sikh Temple
Q1987713.blurb: Operation Blue Star, a military offensive, is launched by the Indian government at Harmandir Sahib, also known as the Golden Temple, the holiest shrine for Sikhs, in Amritsar. The operation continues until June 6, with casualties, most of them civilians, in excess of 5,000.

Q1988505.name: Great Famine of 1315–1317
Q1988505.blurb: The Great Famine of Europe becomes so dire that even the king of England has difficulties buying bread for himself and his entourage.

Q1989779.name: Union of Transylvania with Romania
Q1989779.blurb: Transylvania unites with Romania, following the incorporation of Bessarabia (March 27) and Bukovina (November 28) and thus concluding the Great Union.

Q1990627.name: 2003 Bam earthquake
Q1990627.blurb: The 6.6 Mw Bam earthquake shakes southeastern Iran with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent), leaving more than 26,000 dead and 30,000 injured.

Q1992231.name: Battle of Albert
Q1992231.blurb: First World War: The first day of the Battle of Albert, the opening phase of the Battle of the Somme, became the bloodiest day in the British Army's history, with 57,470 casualties, including 19,240 deaths.

Q1992574.name: Battle of Basing
Q1992574.blurb: Battle of Basing: The West Saxons led by King Æthelred I are defeated by the Danelaw Vikings at Basing.

Q1992677.name: Quit India Movement
Q1992677.blurb: Quit India Movement is launched in India against the British rule in response to Mohandas Gandhi's call for swaraj or complete independence.

Q1992706.name: Battle of Glenmama
Q1992706.blurb: Battle of Glenmama: The combined forces of Munster and Meath under king Brian Boru inflict a crushing defeat on the allied armies of Leinster and Dublin near Lyons Hill in Ireland.

Q1993171.name: 1919 Egyptian revolution
aliases: Causes of the Egyptian revolution of 1919
Q1993171.blurb: During the Egyptian Revolution, British authorities arrested rebel leader Saad Zaghloul and exiled him to Malta.

Q1993476.name: death of Adolf Hitler
aliases: Death by suicide of Adolf Hitler
Q1993476.blurb: World War II: German radio broadcasts news of Adolf Hitler's death, falsely stating that he has "fallen at his command post in the Reich Chancellery fighting to the last breath against Bolshevism and for Germany". The Soviet flag is raised over the Reich Chancellery, by order of Stalin. Up to 2,500 people die in a mass suicide in Demmin following the advance of the Red Army.

Q1993575.name: Adbusters
Q1993575.blurb: Adbusters, a Canadian anti-consumerist publication, organized a protest against corporate influence on democracy at Zuccotti Park in New York City that became known as Occupy Wall Street.

Q1993848.name: South African Border War
aliases: Foreign involvement in the South African Border War
Q1993848.blurb: The South African Border War starts with the battle at Omugulugwombashe.

Q1993878.name: 1975 Tan Son Nhut C-5 accident
Q1993878.blurb: Vietnam War: A United States Air Force Lockheed C-5A Galaxy transporting orphans, crashes near Saigon, South Vietnam shortly after takeoff, killing 172 people.

Q1994106.name: Tear down this wall!
aliases: Remarks at Brandenburg Gate, Berlin, Germany
Mr Gorbachev, tear down this wall
Mr. Gorbachev, tear down this wall
Mr. Gorbachev, tear down this wall!
Q1994106.blurb: Cold War: At the Brandenburg Gate, U.S. President Ronald Reagan publicly challenges Mikhail Gorbachev to tear down the Berlin Wall.

Q1994753.name: Ziggy Stardust Tour
Q1994753.blurb: David Bowie retires his stage persona Ziggy Stardust with the surprise announcement that it is "the last show that we'll ever do" on the last day of the Ziggy Stardust Tour.

Q1995107.name: Lake Bodom murders
Q1995107.blurb: The Lake Bodom murders occur in Finland.

Q1995471.name: Treaty of Worms
Q1995471.blurb: Great Britain, Austria and the Kingdom of Sardinia sign the Treaty of Worms.

Q1997384.name: Norco shootout
Q1997384.blurb: In Norco, California, United States, five masked gunmen hold up a Security Pacific bank, leading to a violent shoot-out and one of the largest pursuits in California history. Two of the gunmen and one police officer are killed and thirty-three police and civilian vehicles are destroyed in the chase.

Q1999769.name: Battle of Luneberg Heath
Q1999769.blurb: Battle of Lüneburg Heath: King Louis III of France is defeated by the Norse Great Heathen Army at Lüneburg Heath in Saxony.

Q1999889.name: Battle of Santiago de Cuba
Q1999889.blurb: A Spanish squadron, led by Pascual Cervera y Topete, is defeated by an American squadron under William T. Sampson in the Battle of Santiago de Cuba.

Q2000493.name: Classical World Chess Championship 1995
Q2000493.blurb: The first game of the PCA World Chess Championship 1995, pitting incumbent champion Garry Kasparov against challenger Viswanathan Anand, takes place on the 107th floor of the World Trade Center's South Tower in New York City.

Q2001581.name: 1707 Hōei earthquake
Q2001581.blurb: The 1707 Hōei earthquake causes more than 5,000 deaths in Japan.

Q2001802.name: 1990 Serbian general election
Q2001802.blurb: In Serbia's first multi-party election, Slobodan Milošević won the presidential election and the Socialist Party of Serbia won the majority of seats in the National Assembly.

Q2002064.name: New START
aliases: Measures for the Further Reduction and Limitation of Strategic Offensive Arms
Measures to Further Reduction and Limitation of Strategic Offensive Arms
Q2002064.blurb: U.S. President Barack Obama and Russian President Dmitry Medvedev sign the New START Treaty.

Q2002270.name: Mozambican War of Independence
Q2002270.blurb: The Mozambican War of Independence against Portugal begins.

Q2002975.name: Nepalese Civil War
aliases: List of political parties registered ahead of the 2006 Nepalese municipal election
Q2002975.blurb: The Nepalese Civil War is initiated in the Kingdom of Nepal by the Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist Centre).

Q2003277.name: Miss Universe 1952
Q2003277.blurb: The first Miss Universe pageant is held. Armi Kuusela from Finland wins the title of Miss Universe 1952.

Q2003519.name: Air Canada Flight 797
Q2003519.blurb: After an emergency landing because of an in-flight fire, twenty-three passengers aboard Air Canada Flight 797 are killed when a flashover occurs as the plane's doors open. Because of this incident, numerous new safety regulations are put in place.

Q2003949.name: Battle of Le Cateau
Q2003949.blurb: World War I: During the retreat from Mons, the British II Corps commanded by General Sir Horace Smith-Dorrien fights a vigorous and successful defensive action at Le Cateau.

Q2004345.name: 1790 United States Census
Q2004345.blurb: The first United States Census is conducted.

Q2005090.name: Ponary massacre
Q2005090.blurb: Austrian soldier Anton Schmid was executed for rescuing Jews from the Ponary massacre in Vilnius.

Q2005392.name: Treaty of Andelot
Q2005392.blurb: Treaty of Andelot: King Guntram of Burgundy recognizes Childebert II as his heir.

Q2006877.name: Georgian era
Q2006877.blurb: George, Elector of Hanover, becomes King George I of Great Britain, marking the beginning of the Georgian era of British history.

Q2007212.name: Battle of Otlukbeli
Q2007212.blurb: The Battle of Otlukbeli: Mehmed the Conqueror of the Ottoman Empire decisively defeats Uzun Hassan of Aq Qoyunlu.

Q2007565.name: Battle of Mons-en-Pévèle
Q2007565.blurb: The Battle of Mons-en-Pévèle is fought to a draw between the French army and the Flemish militias.

Q2008448.name: Battle of Jaffa
Q2008448.blurb: Richard I of England defeats Saladin in the battle of Jaffa, which enables him to conclude a favourable treaty for the crusaders.

Q2008986.name: First Ostend Raid
Q2008986.blurb: First World War: The British Royal Navy launched unsuccessful raids on Ostend and Zeebrugge in German-occupied Belgium.

Q2009193.name: 2009 attack on the Dutch royal family
aliases: Dutch royal family attempted ramming attack
Q2009193.blurb: Seven civilians and the perpetrator are killed and another ten injured at a Queen's Day parade in Apeldoorn, Netherlands in an attempted assassination on Queen Beatrix.

Q2009425.name: Kizlyar-Pervomayskoye hostage crisis
Q2009425.blurb: First Chechen War: Chechen separatists launched raids in the city of Kizlyar, Dagestan, which turned into a massive hostage crisis involving thousands of civilians.

Q2009640.name: Indian Airlines flight 814 hijacking
Q2009640.blurb: Indian Airlines Flight 814 is hijacked in Indian airspace between Kathmandu, Nepal, and Delhi, India. The aircraft landed at Kandahar in Afghanistan. The incident ended on December 31 with the release of 190 survivors (one passenger is killed).

Q2011177.name: Battle of Kostiuchnówka
Q2011177.blurb: First World War: Russian troops won a victory in the Battle of Kostiuchnówka, with the Polish Legions playing a key role on the Austro-Hungarian side.

Q2015343.name: Cairo Fire
Q2015343.blurb: Black Saturday in Egypt: rioters burn Cairo's central business district, targeting British and upper-class Egyptian businesses.

Q2018804.name: Battle of Mill Springs
Q2018804.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Mill Springs: The Confederacy suffers its first significant defeat in the conflict.

Q2019589.name: Bashkir rebellion of 1704–1711
Q2019589.blurb: Battle of Zlatoust: Battle between Bashkir and Tatar rebels and the government troops of the Tsardom of Russia. It is one of the events of the Bashkir rebellion of 1704–1711.

Q2020397.name: Aria Air Flight 1525
Q2020397.blurb: Aria Air Flight 1525 crashes at Mashhad International Airport, killing 16.

Q2020716.name: 1948 Oujda and Jerada Anti-Jewish pogrom
Q2020716.blurb: Anti-Jewish riots in Oujda and Jerada take place.

Q2022139.name: Night attack at Târgoviște
Q2022139.blurb: Vlad the Impaler attempts to assassinate Mehmed II (The Night Attack at Târgovişte), forcing him to retreat from Wallachia.

Q2025205.name: Sosoliso Airlines Flight 1145
Q2025205.blurb: Sosoliso Airlines Flight 1145 crashes at Port Harcourt International Airport in Nigeria, killing 108 people.

Q2025874.name: Battle of Liaoluo Bay
Q2025874.blurb: At the Battle of Liaoluo Bay Ming Chinese naval forces defeated a Dutch East India Company fleet in the Taiwan Strait, the largest naval encounter between Chinese and European forces before the First Opium War more than two hundred years later.

Q2025973.name: Operation Babylift
Q2025973.blurb: Vietnam War: Operation Babylift, a mass evacuation of children in the closing stages of the war begins.

Q2026003.name: Operation Carpetbagger
Q2026003.blurb: World War II: Operation Carpetbagger, involving the dropping of arms and supplies to resistance fighters in Europe, begins.

Q2026016.name: Operation Cartwheel
Q2026016.blurb: World War II: U.S. Marines made a landing on Emirau Island in the Bismarck Archipelago to develop an airbase as part of Operation Cartwheel.

Q2026028.name: Operation Crimp
aliases: Battle of the Ho Bo Woods
Q2026028.blurb: Vietnam War: United States and Australian troops ended Operation Crimp; during the military operation, troops discovered an extensive tunnel network used by the Viet Cong.

Q2026122.name: 2006 Hezbollah cross-border raid
Q2026122.blurb: A cross-border raid by Hezbollah militants starts the 2006 Lebanon War.

Q2026138.name: Operation Hailstone
Q2026138.blurb: World War II: Operation Hailstone begins: U.S. naval air, surface and submarine attack against Truk Lagoon, Japan's main base in the central Pacific, in support of the Eniwetok invasion.

Q2026265.name: Landing at Aitape
Q2026265.blurb: World War II: Operation Persecution is initiated: Allied forces land in the Hollandia (currently known as Jayapura) area of New Guinea.

Q2026308.name: Operation Praying Mantis
Q2026308.blurb: The United States launches Operation Praying Mantis against Iranian naval forces in the largest naval battle since World War II.

Q2026406.name: Operation Southern Watch
Q2026406.blurb: Operation Southern Watch: U.S.A.F., U.S.N., R.A.F. and French Air Force jets attack AAA and SAM sites in Southern Iraq.

Q2026439.name: Operation Tan No. 2
Q2026439.blurb: World War II:  The Imperial Japanese Navy attempts a large-scale kamikaze attack on the U.S. Pacific Fleet anchored at Ulithi atoll in Operation Tan No. 2.

Q2026496.name: Operation Accountability
Q2026496.blurb: Israel launches a massive attack against Lebanon in what the Israelis call Operation Accountability, and the Lebanese call the Seven-Day War.

Q2026616.name: Battle of Grand Harbour
Q2026616.blurb: World War II: Battle of Grand Harbour, British forces on Malta destroy an attack by the Italian Decima Flottiglia MAS. Fort St Elmo Bridge covering the harbour is demolished in the process.

Q2026758.name: 1995 Okinawa rape incident
Q2026758.blurb: The 1995 Okinawa rape occurred, when 3 US servicemen abducted and raped a schoolchild.  This would cause widespread protest against the US military presence on the prefecture.

Q2027138.name: Kfar Etzion massacre
Q2027138.blurb: Arab–Israeli War: The Kfar Etzion massacre occurs, a day prior to the Israeli Declaration of Independence.

Q2027167.name: occupation of Gori
Q2027167.blurb: Russo-Georgian War: Russian units occupy the Georgian city of Gori.

Q2031282.name: Second Battle of Newbury
Q2031282.blurb: Second Battle of Newbury in the English Civil War.

Q2032101.name: 2007 Argentine general election
Q2032101.blurb: In the Argentine general election, Cristina Fernández de Kirchner became the first woman to be elected president of Argentina.

Q2032413.name: Orzeł incident
Q2032413.blurb: World War II: The Estonian military boards the Polish submarine ORP Orzeł in Tallinn, sparking a diplomatic incident that the Soviet Union will later use to justify the annexation of Estonia.

Q2033524.name: Red Wings Airlines Flight 9268
Q2033524.blurb: A Tupolev Tu-204 airliner crashes in a ditch between the airport fence and the M3 highway after overshooting a runway at Vnukovo International Airport in Moscow, Russia, killing five people and leaving three others critically injured.

Q2034912.name: Battle of Harim
Q2034912.blurb: Battle of Harim: Nur ad-Din Zangi defeats the Crusader armies of the County of Tripoli and the Principality of Antioch.

Q2035455.name: Battle of Kings Mountain
Q2035455.blurb: American Revolutionary War: American militia defeat royalist irregulars led by British major Patrick Ferguson at the Battle of Kings Mountain in South Carolina, often regarded as the turning point in the war's Southern theater.

Q2038126.name: Tuscarora War
Q2038126.blurb: The first attacks of the Tuscarora War begin in present-day North Carolina.

Q2038907.name: Battle of Wuhan
Q2038907.blurb: Second Sino-Japanese War: The Battle of Wuhan starts.

Q2039487.name: Battle of Afabet
Q2039487.blurb: Eritrean War of Independence: Eritrean People's Liberation Front troops encircled Ethiopian forces in the Battle of Afabet, gaining a decisive victory three days later.

Q2041743.name: Our World
Q2041743.blurb: More than an estimated 400 million people viewed Our World, the first live international satellite television production.

Q2042421.name: bombing of Bucharest in World War II
Q2042421.blurb: World War II: First bombardment of oil refineries in Bucharest by Anglo-American forces kills 3,000 civilians.

Q2043000.name: 1933 United Airlines Boeing 247 mid-air explosion
Q2043000.blurb: A United Airlines Boeing 247 is destroyed by sabotage, the first such proven case in the history of commercial aviation.

Q2043320.name: Battle of Jackson
Q2043320.blurb: American Civil War: Union troops captured Jackson, the capital of Mississippi.

Q2043711.name: Battle of Tampere
Q2043711.blurb: Finnish Civil War: The battle of Tampere begins.

Q2049158.name: USS Panay incident
Q2049158.blurb: Second Sino-Japanese War: USS Panay incident: Japanese aircraft bomb and sink U.S. gunboat USS Panay on the Yangtze river in China.

Q2050460.name: Allied occupation of Iceland
Q2050460.blurb: The US occupation of Iceland replaces the UK's occupation.

Q2052376.name: First Battle of Kernstown
Q2052376.blurb: American Civil War: The First Battle of Kernstown, Virginia, marks the start of Stonewall Jackson's Valley Campaign. Although a Confederate defeat, the engagement distracts Federal efforts to capture Richmond.

Q2052417.name: Paris Agreements
Q2052417.blurb: The General Treaty, by which France, Britain and the United States recognize the sovereignty of West Germany, comes into effect.

Q2052948.name: 1907 Finnish parliamentary election
Q2052948.blurb: The first parliamentary elections of Finland (at the time the Grand Duchy of Finland) are held.

Q2057259.name: 107th United States Congress
Q2057259.blurb: The Aviation and Transportation Security Act is enacted by the 107th United States Congress in the immediate aftermath of the September 11, 2001 attacks. The Act created the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).

Q2057725.name: Adlertag
Q2057725.blurb: World War II: The German Luftwaffe launches an air operation, codenamed Adlertag, during the Battle of Britain in an attempt to destroy the British Royal Air Force.

Q2058454.name: First Battle of Newbury
Q2058454.blurb: First English Civil War: The First Battle of Newbury was fought in Berkshire; Parliamentarian forces were allowed to pass Royalist troops to retreat the next morning.

Q2060306.name: Red Cloud's War
Q2060306.blurb: Red Cloud (pictured), a Native American leader of the Oglala Lakota tribe, signed the Treaty of Fort Laramie, ending Red Cloud's War and establishing the Great Sioux Reservation.

Q2060419.name: Battle of Brunete
Q2060419.blurb: Spanish Civil War: End of the Battle of Brunete with the Nationalist victory.

Q2060524.name: Treaty of Zuhab
Q2060524.blurb: The treaty of Zuhab ends the fifteen-year-long war between the Ottomans and the Safavids.

Q2060853.name: Treaty of Orebro
Q2060853.blurb: The Treaties of Orebro end both the Anglo-Russian and Anglo-Swedish Wars.

Q2062178.name: Kegworth air disaster
Q2062178.blurb: Kegworth air disaster: British Midland Flight 92, a Boeing 737-400, crashes into the M1 motorway, killing 47 of the 126 people on board.

Q2063204.name: Crown Heights riot
Q2063204.blurb: Crown Heights riot in New York City begins.

Q2063236.name: Majuba Hill
Q2063236.blurb: First Boer War: The Battle of Majuba Hill takes place.

Q2063617.name: Battle of the Gabbard
Q2063617.blurb: First Anglo-Dutch War: The Battle of the Gabbard begins, lasting until the following day.

Q2064142.name: Battle of Halmyros
Q2064142.blurb: Battle of Halmyros: The Catalan Company defeats Walter V, Count of Brienne to take control of the Duchy of Athens, a Crusader state in Greece.

Q2064289.name: Quebec referendum, 1980
Q2064289.blurb: In a referendum in Quebec, the population rejects, with 60% of the vote, a government proposal to move towards independence from Canada.

Q2064362.name: Battle of Texel
Q2064362.blurb: The Dutch fleet defeats an Anglo-French fleet under Prince Rupert in the battle of Texel.

Q2065046.name: Battle of Reading
Q2065046.blurb: Battle of Reading: Æthelred of Wessex and his brother Alfred are defeated by a Danish invasion army.

Q2065299.name: Rum Rebellion
Q2065299.blurb: The Rum Rebellion is the only successful (albeit short-lived) armed takeover of the government in New South Wales.

Q2066129.name: Battle of St. Quentin
Q2066129.blurb: Battle of St. Quentin: Spanish victory over the French in the Italian War of 1551–59.

Q2067651.name: 2009 Hotel Shamo bombing
Q2067651.blurb: A suicide bombing at a hotel in Mogadishu, Somalia, kills 25 people, including three ministers of the Transitional Federal Government.

Q2068462.name: 1834 Concepción earthquake
Q2068462.blurb: The 1835 Concepción earthquake destroys Concepción, Chile.

Q2069091.name: 1992 Albanian parliamentary election
Q2069091.blurb: Fall of communism in Albania: The Democratic Party of Albania wins a decisive majority in the parliamentary election.

Q2069434.name: 1974 Cypriot coup d'état
Q2069434.blurb: Turkish invasion of Cyprus: Forces from Turkey invade Cyprus after a coup d'état, organized by the dictator of Greece, against president Makarios.

Q2070370.name: subsequent Nuremberg trials
aliases: Trials of War Criminals before the Nuremberg Military Tribunals
Q2070370.blurb: The subsequent Nuremberg trials begin with the Doctors' Trial, prosecuting physicians and officers alleged to be involved in Nazi human experimentation and mass murder under the guise of euthanasia.

Q2070808.name: Jilava massacre
Q2070808.blurb: The Iron Guard killed 64 political detainees at a penitentiary near Bucharest and followed up with several high-profile assassinations, including that of former Romanian prime minister Nicolae Iorga.

Q2071090.name: Amiriyah shelter bombing
Q2071090.blurb: Gulf War: Two laser-guided "smart bombs" destroy the Amiriyah shelter in Baghdad. Allied forces said the bunker was being used as a military communications outpost, but over 400 Iraqi civilians inside were killed.

Q2072080.name: Battle of San Domingo
Q2072080.blurb: Battle of San Domingo: British naval victory against the French in the Caribbean.

Q2072316.name: Battle of the Chinese Farm
Q2072316.blurb: Yom Kippur War: Egyptian forces retreated from the Battle of the Chinese Farm, allowing Israeli forces to build their first bridge across the Suez Canal.

Q2073490.name: 31 March Incident
Q2073490.blurb: The 31 March Incident leads to the overthrow of Sultan Abdul Hamid II.

Q2074041.name: Battle of the Basque Roads
Q2074041.blurb: Battle of the Basque Roads: Admiral Lord Gambier fails to support Captain Lord Cochrane, leading to an incomplete British victory over the French fleet.

Q2077856.name: Kharkiv Pact
Q2077856.blurb: The controversial Kharkiv Pact (Russian Ukrainian Naval Base for Gas Treaty) is signed in Kharkiv, Ukraine, by Ukrainian president Viktor Yanukovych and Russian president Dmitry Medvedev; it was unilaterally terminated by Russia on March 31, 2014.

Q2078341.name: Upshot-Knothole Grable
Q2078341.blurb: Nuclear weapons testing: At the Nevada Test Site, the United States conducts its first and only nuclear artillery test.

Q2078515.name: Appeal of 18 June
Q2078515.blurb: World War II: Appeal of 18 June by Charles de Gaulle.

Q2078823.name: 1960 New York air disaster
Q2078823.blurb: A United Air Lines Douglas DC-8 and a TWA Lockheed Super Constellation collide over Staten Island, New York and crash, killing all 128 people aboard both aircraft and six more on the ground.

Q2078945.name: Operation Paula
Q2078945.blurb: World War II: During the Battle of France, the Luftwaffe bombs Paris.

Q2079536.name: 1691 papal conclave
Q2079536.blurb: A papal conclave convened to select a new pope after the death of Pope Alexander VIII.

Q2079873.name: Battle of Orthez
Q2079873.blurb: Peninsular War: In the south of France, Spanish, British and Portuguese soldiers under the command of the Marquess of Wellington defeated French soldiers in the Battle of Orthez, causing the French to retreat east.

Q2081172.name: 1580 Dover Straits earthquake
Q2081172.blurb: One of the largest earthquakes recorded in the history of England, Flanders, or Northern France, takes place.

Q2081446.name: Outer Mongolian Revolution of 1921
Q2081446.blurb: Mongolian Revolution of 1921: The Mongolian People's Army defeats local Chinese forces at Altanbulag, Selenge (then known as Maimachen). This battle was seen as the birthday of the People's Army and completed the expulsion of Chinese militants in Mongolia.

Q2081494.name: The Ed Sullivan Show
Q2081494.blurb: The Beatles make their first appearance on The Ed Sullivan Show, performing before a record-setting audience of 73 million viewers across the United States.

Q2081944.name: Battle of Aqaba
Q2081944.blurb: In the leadup to the Battle of Aqaba, T. E. Lawrence and his Arab forces defeat a battalion of  Ottomans at Abu al-Lissan.

Q2083072.name: Siege of Tkvarcheli
Q2083072.blurb: War in Abkhazia: Siege of Tkvarcheli: A helicopter carrying evacuees from Tkvarcheli is shot down, resulting in at least 52 deaths, including 25 children. The incident catalyses more concerted Russian military intervention on behalf of Abkhazia.

Q2083368.name: Siege of Edessa
Q2083368.blurb: The capital of the crusader County of Edessa falls to Imad ad-Din Zengi, the atabeg of Mosul and Aleppo.

Q2083668.name: German occupation of Lithuania during World War II
Q2083668.blurb: The Lithuanian Activist Front declares independence from the Soviet Union and forms the Provisional Government of Lithuania; it lasts only briefly as the Nazis will occupy Lithuania a few weeks later.

Q2086153.name: Semiramis Hotel bombing
Q2086153.blurb: The Semiramis Hotel bombing kills at least 23 people.

Q2086498.name: First Barons' War
Q2086498.blurb: First Barons' War: English forces under William Marshal defeated French troops at the Battle of Lincoln.

Q2087151.name: Italian Wars of 1499–1504
Q2087151.blurb: The Treaty of Lyon ends the Italian War, confirming French domination of northern Italy, while Spain receives the Kingdom of Naples.

Q2087165.name: 1978 Tabas earthquake
Q2087165.blurb: The 7.4 Mw Tabas earthquake affects the city of Tabas, Iran with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent). At least 15,000 people are killed.

Q2087443.name: Battle of Galveston Harbor
Q2087443.blurb: American Civil War: After a naval battle in Galveston Harbor, Texas, Confederate commanders negotiated the surrender of the city to Union forces.

Q2087792.name: Adana massacre
Q2087792.blurb: Muslims in the Ottoman Empire begin a massacre of Armenians in Adana.

Q2088199.name: Capture of Guam
Q2088199.blurb: The United States captures Guam from Spain. The few warning shots fired by the U.S. naval vessels are misinterpreted as salutes by the Spanish garrison, which was unaware that the two nations were at war.

Q2088471.name: Phoenix Park murders
Q2088471.blurb: Irish civil servants Thomas Henry Burke and Lord Frederick Cavendish were stabbed to death by members of the radical Irish National Invincibles in Phoenix Park, Dublin.

Q2090204.name: Pacers–Pistons brawl
Q2090204.blurb: The worst brawl in NBA history results in several players being suspended. Several players and fans are charged with assault and battery.

Q2090584.name: Siege of Mafeking
Q2090584.blurb: Second Boer War: The Siege of Mafeking in South Africa was lifted after 217 days, a decisive victory for the British against the Boers.

Q2090886.name: North American Ice Storm of 1998
Q2090886.blurb: A massive ice storm hits eastern Canada and the northeastern United States, continuing through January 10 and causing widespread destruction.

Q2091385.name: Battle of Arawe
Q2091385.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Arawe begins during the New Britain campaign.

Q2091449.name: Battle of Mactan
Q2091449.blurb: Battle of Mactan: Explorer Ferdinand Magellan is killed by natives in the Philippines led by chief Lapulapu.

Q2092033.name: Conquest of Mecca
Q2092033.blurb: Conquest of Mecca: Muhammad and his followers conquer the city, and the Quraysh association of clans surrenders.

Q2092225.name: Congress of Arras
Q2092225.blurb: The Treaty of Arras is promulgated, causing Burgundy to switch sides in the Hundred Years' War.

Q2092338.name: Battle of Swally
Q2092338.blurb: The Battle of Swally takes place, which loosens the Portuguese Empire's hold on India.

Q2092429.name: Serbian Revolution
Q2092429.blurb: Battle of Mišar during the Serbian Revolution begins. The battle ends two days later with a Serbian victory over the Ottomans.

Q2092480.name: Panic of 1837
Q2092480.blurb: Panic of 1837: New York City banks suspend the payment of specie, triggering a national banking crisis and an economic depression whose severity was not surpassed until the Great Depression.

Q2093724.name: 2002 Grozny truck bombing
Q2093724.blurb: Two truck bombs kill 72 and wound 200 at the pro-Moscow headquarters of the Chechen government in Grozny, Chechnya, Russia.

Q2095499.name: Pinckney's Treaty
Q2095499.blurb: The United States and Spain sign the Treaty of Madrid, which establishes the boundaries between Spanish colonies and the U.S.

Q2095678.name: Battle of Assaye
Q2095678.blurb: Second Anglo-Maratha War: The Battle of Assaye is fought between the British East India Company and the Maratha Empire in India.

Q2095768.name: Operation Lam Son 719
Q2095768.blurb: Operation Lam Son 719: South Vietnamese General Do Cao Tri was killed in a helicopter crash en route to taking control of the faltering campaign.

Q2096814.name: Direct Action Day
Q2096814.blurb: Mass riots in Kolkata begin; more than 4,000 people would be killed in 72 hours.

Q2097266.name: Battle of Largs
Q2097266.blurb: The Battle of Largs is fought between Norwegians and Scots.

Q2099969.name: Sack of Damietta
Q2099969.blurb: A Byzantine fleet sacks and destroys undefended Damietta in Egypt.

Q2100623.name: 1945 Tripoli pogrom
Q2100623.blurb: The three-day anti-Jewish riots in Tripolitania commence.

Q2103752.name: Battle of Iuka
Q2103752.blurb: American Civil War: Union troops under William Rosecrans defeat a Confederate force commanded by Sterling Price.

Q2105495.name: 1383–1385 Portuguese Interregnum
Q2105495.blurb: Portuguese Crisis of 1383–85: Battle of Aljubarrota: Portuguese forces commanded by John I of Portugal defeat the Castilian army of John I of Castile.

Q2112088.name: Linggadjati Agreement
Q2112088.blurb: Indonesian National Revolution: The Renville Agreement between the Netherlands and Indonesian republicans was ratified, in an ultimately unsuccessful attempt to resolve disputes arising from the Linggadjati Agreement of 1946.

Q2112779.name: Capture of Brielle
Q2112779.blurb: In the Eighty Years' War, the Watergeuzen capture Brielle from the Seventeen Provinces, gaining the first foothold on land for what would become the Dutch Republic.

Q2113036.name: Expédition d'Irlande
Q2113036.blurb: War of the First Coalition: The French navy launched an expedition to Ireland to assist the Society of United Irishmen in a rebellion against the British.

Q2113284.name: Battle of the Rice Boats
Q2113284.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Patriot militiamen from Georgia and South Carolina attempted to resist the British action to seize and remove supply ships anchored at Savannah, Georgia.

Q2115151.name: 2005 Egyptian presidential election
Q2115151.blurb: Egypt holds its first-ever multi-party presidential election.

Q2116320.name: Final War of the Roman Republic
aliases: Civil war between Antony and Octavian
Last War of the Roman Republic
Two Caesars are one too many
Q2116320.blurb: War of Actium: Octavian defeated the forces of Mark Antony and Cleopatra at Alexandria, establishing Roman Egypt.

Q2116681.name: Bradford City stadium fire
Q2116681.blurb: Fifty-six spectators die and more than 200 are injured in the Bradford City stadium fire.

Q2117322.name: Battle of Yashima
Q2117322.blurb: Battle of Yashima: the Japanese forces of the Taira clan are defeated by the Minamoto clan.

Q2118311.name: Yugoslav coup d'état
Q2118311.blurb: World War II: A group of Serbian-nationalist officers of the Royal Yugoslav Air Force carried out a coup d'état after Yugoslavia joined the Axis powers.

Q2118432.name: 2012 Mexico Learjet 25 crash
Q2118432.blurb: A plane crash in Mexico kills seven people including singer Jenni Rivera.

Q2119319.name: Peace of Amasya
Q2119319.blurb: The Ottoman Empire and the Safavid Empire sign a peace treaty to end the Ottoman–Safavid War of 1532–1555.

Q2119849.name: Battle of Vlaardingen
Q2119849.blurb: Count Dirk III defeats an army sent by Emperor Henry II in the Battle of Vlaardingen.

Q2120252.name: Siamese revolution of 1932
aliases: Abolishment of absolute monarchy in Siam
Abolishment of absolute monarchy in Thailand
Abolition of absolute monarchy in Siam
Abolition of absolute monarchy in Thailand
Q2120252.blurb: A bloodless revolution instigated by the People's Party ends the absolute power of King Prajadhipok of Siam (now Thailand).

Q2121187.name: Wisconsin Sikh temple shooting
Q2121187.blurb: The Wisconsin Sikh temple shooting took place in Oak Creek, Wisconsin, killing six victims; the perpetrator committed suicide after being wounded by police.

Q2123570.name: 1950s quiz show scandals
Q2123570.blurb: Quiz show scandals: Twenty-One game show contestant Charles Van Doren admits to a Congressional committee that he had been given questions and answers in advance.

Q2125491.name: Battle of Front Royal
Q2125491.blurb: American Civil War: Confederate troops under Stonewall Jackson defeated a Union force at the Battle of Front Royal in Virginia, taking around 700 prisoners.

Q2127150.name: Texas City Refinery explosion
Q2127150.blurb: A fire and explosion at an oil refinery in Texas City, the third-largest in the United States, killed 15 workers.

Q2127633.name: Siege of Grave
Q2127633.blurb: The Spanish-held Dutch town of Grave capitulates to a besieging Dutch and English army under the command of Maurice of Orange.

Q2136664.name: 1956 Egyptian referendum
Q2136664.blurb: In a nationwide referendum, Gamal Abdel Nasser (pictured) was elected President of Egypt, a post he held until his death in 1970.

Q2136977.name: The Jakarta Post
Q2136977.blurb: The first issue of The Jakarta Post was published in Indonesia.

Q2137777.name: Battle of Bagrevand
Q2137777.blurb: The Battle of Bagrevand puts an end to an Armenian rebellion against the Abbasid Caliphate. Muslim control over the South Caucasus is solidified and its Islamization begins, while several major Armenian nakharar families lose power and their remnants flee to the Byzantine Empire.

Q2143253.name: Urabi revolt
Q2143253.blurb: Nationalist riots break out in Alexandria directed against foreign domination. More than 50 Europeans are killed, including the British consul.

Q2143633.name: Voyage of the James Caird
Q2143633.blurb: Sailing in the lifeboat James Caird, Ernest Shackleton arrives at South Georgia after a journey of 800 nautical miles from Elephant Island.

Q2144114.name: Rainhill Trials
Q2144114.blurb: Stephenson's Rocket wins the Rainhill Trials.

Q2145024.name: 1292–94 papal election
aliases: papal election from April 5, 1292 to July 5, 1294
Q2145024.blurb: Election of pope Celestine V following the death of pope Nicholas IV two years prior.

Q2146780.name: Revenue Act of 1861
aliases: An Act to provide increased Revenue from imports, to pay Interest on the Public Debt, and for other Purposes
Q2146780.blurb: American Civil War: In order to help pay for the war effort, the United States government levies the first income tax as part of the Revenue Act of 1861 (3% of all incomes over US$800; rescinded in 1872).

Q2151872.name: Arkansas in the American Civil War
Q2151872.blurb: American Civil War: Arkansas secedes from the Union.

Q2154485.name: Sack of Thessalonica
Q2154485.blurb: Sack of Thessalonica by the Normans.

Q2156347.name: Lebanon hostage crisis
Q2156347.blurb: In Lebanon, pro-Iran kidnappers claim to have abducted American writer Edward Tracy (he is released in August 1991).

Q2157083.name: Silent Sentinels
Q2157083.blurb: Ten suffragists, members of the Silent Sentinels, are arrested while picketing the White House in favor of women's suffrage in the United States.

Q2157450.name: USS Liberty incident
Q2157450.blurb: Six-Day War: The USS Liberty incident: A United States Navy spy ship is attacked by the Israeli Air Force and Navy, resulting in 34 deaths and 171 wounded.

Q2157600.name: Monongah Mining disaster
Q2157600.blurb: A coal mine explosion at Monongah, West Virginia, kills 362 workers.

Q2160850.name: Qafa e Vishës bus accident
Q2160850.blurb: A bus accident near Himara, Albania kills 13 people and injures 21 others.

Q2161150.name: Battle of Big Black River Bridge
Q2161150.blurb: American Civil War: At the Battle of Big Black River Bridge in Mississippi, Union forces under John A. McClernand defeated a Confederate rearguard and captured around 1,700 men.

Q2161196.name: Mexican oil expropriation
Q2161196.blurb: Mexico creates Pemex by expropriating all foreign-owned oil reserves and facilities.

Q2161912.name: Tichborne case
Q2161912.blurb: In one of the longest cases ever heard in an English court, the claimant in the Tichborne case was convicted of perjury for attempting to assume the identity of the missing heir to the Tichborne baronetcy.

Q2163513.name: American Eagle Flight 4184
Q2163513.blurb: American Eagle Flight 4184 crashes near Roselawn, Indiana killing all 68 people on board.

Q2163922.name: Second Battle of Bedriacum
Q2163922.blurb: In the Second Battle of Bedriacum, troops loyal to Vespasian defeat those of Emperor Vitellius.

Q2164009.name: Battle of Lewes
Q2164009.blurb: Battle of Lewes: Henry III of England is captured and forced to sign the Mise of Lewes, making Simon de Montfort the effective ruler of England.

Q2164320.name: Arkankergen mass murder
Q2164320.blurb: The Arkankergen massacre in Kazakhstan's Alakol District kills 15 people.

Q2164344.name: Sand Creek massacre
Q2164344.blurb: Colorado War: Colorado volunteers led by Colonel John Chivington massacre at least 150 Cheyenne and Arapaho noncombatants at Sand Creek inside Colorado Territory.

Q2164870.name: Eureka Rebellion
Q2164870.blurb: An estimated crowd of more than 10,000 demonstrators swore allegiance to the Eureka Flag (pictured) as a symbol of defiance in advance of the Eureka Rebellion in Ballarat, Australia.

Q2164950.name: Battle of Lens
Q2164950.blurb: The Battle of Lens is the last major military confrontation of the Thirty Years' War, contributing to the signing of the Peace of Westphalia in October that year.

Q2165331.name: Treaty of Picquigny
Q2165331.blurb: France signed the Treaty of Picquigny with England, freeing Louis XI to deal with the threat posed by Charles the Bold, Duke of Burgundy.

Q2165376.name: Battle of Tarakan
Q2165376.blurb: World War II: Japanese forces attack Tarakan in Borneo, Netherlands Indies (Battle of Tarakan)

Q2165486.name: Battle of Empress Augusta Bay
Q2165486.blurb: World War II: A U.S. Navy task force turned away an Imperial Japanese Navy formation at the Battle of Empress Augusta Bay, thus protecting the landings at Cape Torokina.

Q2166330.name: Trent Affair
Q2166330.blurb: American Civil War: The "Trent Affair": The USS San Jacinto stops the British mail ship Trent and arrests two Confederate envoys, sparking a diplomatic crisis between the UK and US.

Q2170921.name: Battle of Bristoe Station
Q2170921.blurb: American Civil War: Confederate troops under the command of A. P. Hill fail to drive the Union Army completely out of Virginia.

Q2171443.name: Action of 1 January 1800
Q2171443.blurb: Quasi-War: An American convoy of four merchant vessels escorted by a schooner was attacked by a squadron of armed barges manned by Haitians.

Q2174038.name: Interwar Estonia
Q2174038.blurb: Supported by the Estonian army, Konstantin Päts staged a coup d'état, beginning the Era of Silence.

Q2174777.name: Eastbourne manslaughter
Q2174777.blurb: The trial of the Eastbourne manslaughter, which later became an important legal precedent in the United Kingdom for discussions of corporal punishment in schools, began in Lewes.

Q2174847.name: 1954 Rugby League World Cup
Q2174847.blurb: Great Britain defeats France to capture the first ever Rugby League World Cup in Paris in front of around 30,000 spectators.

Q2175155.name: 2007 London car bombs
Q2175155.blurb: A Jeep Cherokee filled with propane canisters drives into the entrance of Glasgow Airport, Scotland in a failed terrorist attack. This was linked to the 2007 London car bombs that had taken place the day before.

Q2175943.name: Wallachian Revolution of 1848
Q2175943.blurb: In the Wallachian Revolution, Ion Heliade Rădulescu and Christian Tell issue the Proclamation of Islaz and create a new republican government.

Q2177009.name: Russian invasion of Manchuria
Q2177009.blurb: Russian invasion of Manchuria: Russia completes its occupation of Manchuria with 100,000 troops.

Q2185405.name: Battle of Hatteras Inlet Batteries
Q2185405.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Hatteras Inlet Batteries gives Federal forces control of Pamlico Sound.

Q2190013.name: Battle of Wyoming
Q2190013.blurb: American Revolutionary War: The Iroquois, allied with Britain, massacre 360 Patriot soldiers during the Battle of Wyoming.

Q2193276.name: death of Diana, Princess of Wales
Q2193276.blurb: Diana, Princess of Wales, her partner, Dodi Fayed, and driver Henri Paul die in a car crash in Paris.

Q2198292.name: Triple Alliance
Q2198292.blurb: The French Royal Army crosses the border into the Spanish Netherlands, starting the War of Devolution opposing France to the Spanish Empire and the Triple Alliance.

Q2202322.name: S7 Airlines Flight 778
Q2202322.blurb: One hundred and twenty-five people are killed when S7 Airlines Flight 778, an Airbus A310 passenger jet, veers off the runway while landing in wet conditions at Irkutsk Airport in Siberia.

Q2204399.name: Battle of Neville's Cross
Q2204399.blurb: The English capture King David II of Scotland at Neville's Cross and imprison him for eleven years.

Q2208597.name: Kam Air Flight 904
Q2208597.blurb: One hundred five people are killed when Kam Air Flight 904 crashes in the Pamir Mountains in Afghanistan.

Q2215044.name: 2011 Joplin tornado
Q2215044.blurb: An EF5 tornado strikes Joplin, Missouri, killing 158 people and wreaking $2.8 billion in damages, the costliest and seventh-deadliest single tornado in U.S. history.

Q2215946.name: Salzburg Conference
Q2215946.blurb: At the Salzburg Conference, Adolf Hitler demanded the replacement of much of Slovakia's cabinet.

Q2219890.name: Siege of Calais
Q2219890.blurb: World War II: The Siege of Calais ends with the surrender of the British and French garrison.

Q2220035.name: 2004 Georgian presidential election
Q2220035.blurb: Mikheil Saakashvili is elected President of Georgia following the November 2003 Rose Revolution.

Q2221183.name: Cadereyta Jiménez massacre
Q2221183.blurb: Forty-nine dismembered bodies are discovered by Mexican authorities on Mexican Federal Highway 40.

Q2229399.name: Bombing of Nijmegen
Q2229399.blurb: World War II: American aircraft mistakenly bomb the Dutch towns of Nijmegen, Arnhem, Enschede and Deventer, resulting in 800 dead in Nijmegen alone.

Q2230310.name: Treaty of York
Q2230310.blurb: England and Scotland sign the Treaty of York, establishing the location of their common border.

Q2231356.name: Operation Pierce Arrow
Q2231356.blurb: Vietnam War: Operation Pierce Arrow: American aircraft from carriers USS Ticonderoga and USS Constellation bomb North Vietnam in retaliation for strikes against U.S. destroyers in the Gulf of Tonkin.

Q2231652.name: Relief of Goes
Q2231652.blurb: Eighty Years' War: Three thousand Spanish soldiers wade through fifteen miles of water in one night to effect the relief of Goes.

Q2234632.name: Battle of Rymnik
Q2234632.blurb: Battle of Rymnik: Alexander Suvorov's Russian and allied army defeats superior Ottoman Empire forces.

Q2236812.name: Battle of Riachuelo
Q2236812.blurb: The Naval Battle of the Riachuelo is fought on the rivulet Riachuelo (Argentina), between the Paraguayan Navy on one side and the Brazilian Navy on the other. The Brazilian victory was crucial for the later success of the Triple Alliance (Brazil, Uruguay, and Argentina) in the Paraguayan War.

Q2236909.name: Battle of Gran
Q2236909.blurb: An imperial coalition army under Charles of Lorraine defeats the Ottoman army that had been besieging Esztergom.

Q2236963.name: Battle of Gravelines
Q2236963.blurb: Battle of Gravelines: In France, Spanish forces led by Count Lamoral of Egmont defeat the French forces of Marshal Paul de Thermes at Gravelines.

Q2237043.name: Battle of New Market
Q2237043.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of New Market, Virginia: Students from the Virginia Military Institute fight alongside the Confederate army to force Union General Franz Sigel out of the Shenandoah Valley.

Q2237111.name: Battle of Plattsburgh
Q2237111.blurb: War of 1812: The climax of the Battle of Plattsburgh, a major United States victory in the war.

Q2237194.name: Battle of Forts Clinton and Montgomery
Q2237194.blurb: American Revolutionary War: British forces capture Forts Clinton and Montgomery on the Hudson River.

Q2237307.name: Battle of Andrassos
Q2237307.blurb: Battle of Andrassos: Byzantines under Leo Phokas the Younger score a crushing victory over the Hamdanid Emir of Aleppo, Sayf al-Dawla.

Q2237365.name: Battle of Ashdown
Q2237365.blurb: Æthelred I and Alfred the Great lead a West Saxon army to repel an invasion by Danelaw Vikings.

Q2237461.name: Battle of Cropredy Bridge
Q2237461.blurb: Charles I of England defeats a Parliamentarian detachment at the Battle of Cropredy Bridge.

Q2237467.name: Battle of Cassel
Q2237467.blurb: Battle of Cassel: French troops stop an uprising of Flemish farmers.

Q2237484.name: Battle of Ceresole
Q2237484.blurb: Italian War of 1542–1546: French and Spanish forces fought a massive pitched battle in the Piedmont region of Italy.

Q2237537.name: Battle of Fallen Timbers
Q2237537.blurb: Northwest Indian War: United States troops force a confederacy of Shawnee, Mingo, Delaware, Wyandot, Miami, Ottawa, Chippewa, and Potawatomi warriors into a disorganized retreat at the Battle of Fallen Timbers.

Q2237576.name: Battle of Heliopolis
Q2237576.blurb: Battle of Heliopolis: The Muslim Arab army under 'Amr ibn al-'As defeat the Byzantine forces near Heliopolis (Egypt).

Q2237622.name: Battle of Kōan
Q2237622.blurb: Mongol invasion of Japan: The Mongolian fleet of Kublai Khan is destroyed by a "divine wind" for the second time in the Battle of Kōan.

Q2237713.name: Battle of Paardeberg
Q2237713.blurb: Second Boer War: Imperial forces suffer their worst single-day loss of life on Bloody Sunday, the first day of the Battle of Paardeberg.

Q2237751.name: Battle of Rovine
Q2237751.blurb: Battle of Rovine: The Wallachians defeat an invading Ottoman army.

Q2238546.name: Gilbert and Marshall Islands Campaign
aliases: Japanese invasion of the Gilbert Islands
Q2238546.blurb: World War II: During the Gilbert and Marshall Islands campaign, U.S. Army and Marine forces seize Kwajalein Atoll from the defending Japanese garrison.

Q2238843.name: Battle of Brustem
Q2238843.blurb: Battle of Brustem: Charles the Bold defeats Prince-Bishopric of Liège.

Q2239140.name: Spantax Flight 995
Q2239140.blurb: Spantax Flight 995 crashes at Málaga Airport during a rejected takeoff, killing 50 of the 394 people on board.

Q2240494.name: Turkish Airlines Flight 452
Q2240494.blurb: Turkish Airlines Flight 452 hits the Taurus Mountains, outskirt of Karatepe, Turkey, killing all 154 passengers and crew.

Q2245714.name: Battle of Buffington Island
Q2245714.blurb: American Civil War: Morgan's Raid: At Buffington Island in Ohio, Confederate General John Hunt Morgan's raid into the north is mostly thwarted when a large group of his men are captured while trying to escape across the Ohio River.

Q2246835.name: Challenge of Barletta
Q2246835.blurb: Challenge of Barletta: Tournament between 13 Italian and 13 French knights near Barletta.

Q2248707.name: Fasci Siciliani
Q2248707.blurb: On Labor Day in Catania, Sicily, workers establish the first successful Fascio Siciliano, launching a movement of peasants and laborers protesting poverty, landlordism, taxation, and economic hardship across Sicily.

Q2252463.name: Battle of Madonna dell'Olmo
Q2252463.blurb: War of the Austrian Succession: France and Spain defeat Sardinia at the Battle of Madonna dell'Olmo, but soon have to withdraw from Sardinia.

Q2253305.name: Battle of Richmond
Q2253305.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Richmond: Confederates under Edmund Kirby Smith rout Union forces under General William "Bull" Nelson.

Q2253625.name: Aeroflot Flight 4225
Q2253625.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 4225 crashes near Almaty International Airport in the Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic (present day Kazakhstan), killing all 166 people on board.

Q2253682.name: Battle of Tettenhall
Q2253682.blurb: The last major Danish army to raid England for nearly a century is defeated at the Battle of Tettenhall by the allied forces of Mercia and Wessex, led by King Edward the Elder and Æthelred, Lord of the Mercians.

Q2253960.name: Wuhan Airlines Flight 343
Q2253960.blurb: Wuhan Airlines Flight 343 is struck by lightning and crashes into Wuhan's Hanyang District, killing 49 people.

Q2254354.name: Iran Air Flight 291
Q2254354.blurb: Iran Air Flight 291 crashes in the Alborz Mountains while on approach to Mehrabad International Airport in Tehran, Iran, killing 128 people.

Q2254414.name: ČSA Flight 511 (March 1961)
Q2254414.blurb: ČSA Flight 511 crashes in Igensdorf, Germany, killing 52.

Q2254436.name: China Southwest Airlines Flight 4146
Q2254436.blurb: China Southwest Airlines Flight 4146 crashes near Chongqing Baishiyi Airport, killing all 98 passengers and 10 crew members.

Q2254501.name: Aviaco Flight 118
Q2254501.blurb: Aviaco Flight 118 crashes on approach to A Coruña Airport in A Coruña, Spain, killing all 85 people on the plane and one other one the ground.

Q2254515.name: Viasa Flight 742
Q2254515.blurb: A Viasa McDonnell Douglas DC-9 crashes in Maracaibo, Venezuela, killing 155.

Q2254605.name: Turkish Airlines Flight 278
Q2254605.blurb: Turkish Airlines Flight 278 (a Boeing 737-400) crashes on approach to Van Ferit Melen Airport in Van, Turkey, killing 57 of the 76 people on board.

Q2254625.name: Aeroflot Flight 1491
