Q2254625.blurb: During approach to Kharkiv International Airport, Aeroflot Flight 1491 crashes near Ruska Lozova, killing all 112 aboard.

Q2254794.name: Aeroflot Flight 1691
Q2254794.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 1691 crashes on approach to Vnukovo International Airport, killing 58.

Q2254868.name: Olympic Airways Flight 954
Q2254868.blurb: Olympic Airways Flight 954 strikes a mountain outside of Keratea, Greece, killing 90 people in the worst crash of a Douglas DC-6 in history.

Q2254949.name: Air France Flight 1611
Q2254949.blurb: Air France Flight 1611 crashes off Nice, France, killing 89 passengers and six crew.

Q2254983.name: Pan Am Flight 759
Q2254983.blurb: Pan Am Flight 759 crashes in Kenner, Louisiana, killing all 145 people on board and eight others on the ground.

Q2255524.name: Battle of Antioch
Q2255524.blurb: Battle of Antioch: With the support of the Syrian legions, Elagabalus defeats the forces of emperor Macrinus.

Q2257461.name: 1915 Avezzano earthquake
Q2257461.blurb: The 6.7 Mw Avezzano earthquake shakes the Province of L'Aquila in Italy with a maximum Mercalli intensity of XI (Extreme), killing between 29,978 and 32,610.

Q2257955.name: Coonan Cross Oath
Q2257955.blurb: By the Coonan Cross Oath, the Eastern Church in India cuts itself off from colonial Portuguese tutelage.

Q2258726.name: Herzegovina Uprising
Q2258726.blurb: The Herzegovinian rebellion against the Ottoman Empire begins.

Q2258876.name: 1993 Singaporean presidential election
Q2258876.blurb: Singaporean presidential election: Former Deputy Prime Minister Ong Teng Cheong is elected President of Singapore. Although it is the first presidential election to be determined by popular vote, the allowed candidates consist only of Ong and a reluctant whom the government had asked to run to confer upon the election the semblance of an opposition.

Q2259031.name: Battle of Cascina
Q2259031.blurb: Troops of the Republic of Pisa and the Republic of Florence clash in the Battle of Cascina.

Q2260521.name: Italian constitutional referendum, 1946
Q2260521.blurb: Birth of the Italian Republic: In a referendum, Italians vote to turn Italy from a monarchy into a Republic. After the referendum, King Umberto II of Italy is exiled.

Q2264242.name: proclamation of the abolition of the monarchy
Q2264242.blurb: French Revolution: The National Convention abolishes the monarchy.

Q2264459.name: Battle of Cerignola
Q2264459.blurb: The Battle of Cerignola is fought. It is noted as one of the first European battles in history won by small arms fire using gunpowder.

Q2264910.name: Dissolution of the union between Norway and Sweden
Q2264910.blurb: Norway's parliament dissolves its union with Sweden. The vote was confirmed by a national plebiscite on August 13 of that year.

Q2266004.name: Soviet occupation of Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina
aliases: Occupation of Bassarabia by the Soviet Union
Occupation of Bessarabia by the Soviet Union
Soviet annexation of Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina
Soviet invasion and occupation of Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina
Soviet invasion of Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina
Soviet occupation of Bessarabia, Northern Bukovina and the Hertsa Region
Q2266004.blurb: World War II: Under the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact, the Soviet Union presents an ultimatum to Romania requiring it to cede Bessarabia and the northern part of Bukovina.

Q2267264.name: Age of Liberty
Q2267264.blurb: King Gustav III completes his coup d'état by adopting a new Constitution, ending half a century of parliamentary rule in Sweden and installing himself as an enlightened despot.

Q2268189.name: 1st National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party
Q2268189.blurb: The first National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party opened in a house in Shanghai.

Q2268427.name: Treaty of Bucharest
Q2268427.blurb: World War I: Romania signs a secret treaty with the Entente Powers. According to the treaty, Romania agreed to join the war on the Allied side.

Q2268969.name: 2007 Catania football violence
Q2268969.blurb: Police officer Filippo Raciti is killed when a clash breaks out in the Sicily derby between Catania and Palermo, in the Serie A, the top flight of Italian football. This event led to major changes in stadium regulations in Italy.

Q2269195.name: First Aceh Expedition
Q2269195.blurb: A Dutch military expedition was launched to bombard Banda Aceh, the capital of the Aceh Sultanate in present-day Indonesia, beginning the Aceh War.

Q2271637.name: Rendlesham Forest incident
Q2271637.blurb: Witnesses report the first of several sightings of unexplained lights near RAF Woodbridge, in Rendlesham Forest, Suffolk, England, United Kingdom, an incident called "Britain's Roswell".

Q2273348.name: Maraghar massacre
Q2273348.blurb: First Nagorno-Karabakh War: Dozens of Armenian civilians were massacred in the village of Maraga by Azerbaijani forces.

Q2276449.name: French European Constitution referendum, 2005
Q2276449.blurb: France rejects the Constitution of the European Union in a national referendum.

Q2276692.name: New Guinea campaign
aliases: New Guinea in World War II
Papua New Guinea during World War II
Papua New Guinea in World War II
Q2276692.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Rabaul commences Japan's invasion of Australia's Territory of New Guinea.

Q2276724.name: Operation Defensive Shield
Q2276724.blurb: In reaction to the Passover massacre two days prior, Israel launches Operation Defensive Shield against Palestinian militants, its largest military operation in the West Bank since the 1967 Six-Day War.

Q2276912.name: Shangani Patrol
Q2276912.blurb: First Matabele War: A patrol of 34 British South Africa Company soldiers is ambushed and annihilated by more than 3,000 Matabele warriors on the Shangani River in Matabeleland.

Q2277035.name: Battle for Henderson Field
Q2277035.blurb: World War II: The Battle for Henderson Field begins on Guadalcanal.

Q2279790.name: Government of Ireland Act 1914
Q2279790.blurb: The Irish Home Rule Act becomes law, but is delayed until after World War I.

Q2280517.name: Battle of San Marino
Q2280517.blurb: World War II: German forces are attacked by the Allies in the Battle of San Marino.

Q2280708.name: Kecksburg UFO incident
Q2280708.blurb: Kecksburg UFO incident: A fireball is seen from Michigan to Pennsylvania; with witnesses reporting something crashing in the woods near Pittsburgh.

Q2281470.name: Operation Provide Comfort
Q2281470.blurb: In a friendly fire incident during Operation Provide Comfort in northern Iraq, two U.S. Air Force aircraft mistakenly shoot-down two U.S. Army helicopters, killing 26 people.

Q2281774.name: Battle of Marj al-Rahit
Q2281774.blurb: Battle of Marj Rahit: Umayyad partisans defeat the supporters of Ibn al-Zubayr and cement Umayyad control of Syria.

Q2281806.name: 1929 Arab riots in Palestine
Q2281806.blurb: The 1929 Palestine riots break out in Mandatory Palestine between Palestinian Arabs and Jews and continue until the end of the month. In total, 133 Jews and 116 Arabs are killed.

Q2282207.name: Battle of Helena
Q2282207.blurb: American Civil War: Union forces repulse a Confederate army at the Battle of Helena in Arkansas. The battle thwarts a Rebel attempt to relieve pressure on the besieged city of Vicksburg, and paves the way for the Union capture of Little Rock.

Q2282672.name: 2008 Guinean coup d'état
Q2282672.blurb: A coup d'état occurs in Guinea hours after the death of President Lansana Conté.

Q2286332.name: Battle of Oravais
Q2286332.blurb: Finnish War: Russians defeat the Swedes at the Battle of Oravais.

Q2287308.name: Treaty of Constantinople
Q2287308.blurb: Signing of the treaty of Constantinople between Britain, France, Russia and the Ottoman Empire, which outlines the borders of the new kingdom of Greece.

Q2288195.name: Battle of Brown's Ferry
Q2288195.blurb: American Civil War: Union forces led by General William F. Smith defeat Confederate forces in the Battle of Brown's Ferry, opening up a supply line to the besieged city of Chattanooga, Tennessee.

Q2288824.name: Dinamo Zagreb–Red Star Belgrade riot
Q2288824.blurb: The Dinamo–Red Star riot takes place at Maksimir Stadium in Zagreb, Croatia, between the Bad Blue Boys (fans of Dinamo Zagreb) and the Delije (fans of Red Star Belgrade).

Q2290814.name: Battle of Wadi al-Khaznadar
Q2290814.blurb: The Ilkhanate ruler Ghazan defeats a Mamluk army that opposes his invasion into Syria in the Battle of Wadi al-Khaznadar near Homs.

Q2290851.name: 2010 Filair Let L-410 crash
Q2290851.blurb: A Filair Let L-410 Turbolet crashes on approach to Bandundu Airport, killing 20.

Q2291501.name: Skandalkonzert
Q2291501.blurb: Arnold Schoenberg conducted the Vienna Concert Society in a concert of expressionist music that so shocked the audience that they began to riot.

Q2292026.name: Battle of the Gates of Trajan
Q2292026.blurb: Byzantine–Bulgarian wars: Battle of the Gates of Trajan: The Bulgarians under the Comitopuli Samuel and Aron defeat the Byzantine forces at the Gate of Trajan, with Byzantine Emperor Basil II barely escaping.

Q2292449.name: Treaty of Craiova
Q2292449.blurb: Romania returns Southern Dobruja to Bulgaria under the Treaty of Craiova.

Q2292497.name: 2001 Linate Airport runway collision
Q2292497.blurb: A twin engine Cessna and a Scandinavian Airlines System jetliner collide in heavy fog during takeoff from Milan, Italy, killing 118 people.

Q2295317.name: Second Battle of Olmedo
Q2295317.blurb: The Second Battle of Olmedo takes places as part of a succession conflict between Henry IV of Castile and his half-brother Alfonso, Prince of Asturias.

Q2297059.name: Battle of the Solent
Q2297059.blurb: The English warship Mary Rose sank outside Portsmouth during the Battle of the Solent; it was raised from the seabed in 1982.

Q2297338.name: Combat of the Thirty
Q2297338.blurb: Combat of the Thirty: Thirty Breton knights call out and defeat thirty English knights.

Q2298421.name: Treaty of Granada (1500)
Q2298421.blurb: Treaty of Granada: Louis XII of France and Ferdinand II of Aragon agree to divide the Kingdom of Naples between them.

Q2299845.name: Battle of Tigranocerta
Q2299845.blurb: Third Mithridatic War: The military of the Roman Republic subdues Armenia.

Q2302161.name: Miracle of the Sun
Q2302161.blurb: The "Miracle of the Sun" is witnessed by an estimated 70,000 people in the Cova da Iria in Portugal.

Q2302456.name: TWA Flight 847
Q2302456.blurb: Thirty-nine American hostages from the hijacked TWA Flight 847 are freed in Beirut after being held for 17 days.

Q2302736.name: Personal rule of Charles I
Q2302736.blurb: Charles I dissolves the Parliament of England, beginning the eleven-year period known as the Personal Rule.

Q2302974.name: Mongolian Revolution of 1990
Q2302974.blurb: Mongolian Revolution: At the country's first open pro-democracy public demonstration, Tsakhiagiin Elbegdorj announces the establishment of the Mongolian Democratic Union.

Q2303215.name: NLM CityHopper Flight 431
Q2303215.blurb: NLM CityHopper Flight 431 crashes in Moerdijk after taking off from Rotterdam The Hague Airport in the Netherlands, killing all 17 people on board.

Q2305019.name: Battle of Curupaity
Q2305019.blurb: The Battle of Curupayty is Paraguay's only significant victory in the Paraguayan War.

Q2305266.name: Soviet invasion of Poland
aliases: Accession of the Western Ukraine and Western Belarus to the USSR
Occupation of East Poland by Soviet Union
Q2305266.blurb: World War II: The Soviet invasion of Poland begins.

Q2306347.name: Space Patrol
Q2306347.blurb: The first U.S. experimental 3D television broadcast shows an episode of Space Patrol on Los Angeles ABC affiliate KECA-TV.

Q2308186.name: German invasion of Denmark
Q2308186.blurb: World War II: Operation Weserübung: Germany invades Denmark and Norway.

Q2309409.name: Morean War
Q2309409.blurb: Morean War: The 49-day Siege of Coron ends with the surrender and massacre of its garrison by the Venetians.

Q2309601.name: Japanese embassy hostage crisis
Q2309601.blurb: Peruvian internal conflict: Fourteen members of the Túpac Amaru Revolutionary Movement provoke a hostage crisis by taking over the Japanese embassy in Lima.

Q2310933.name: 1977 Spanish general election
Q2310933.blurb: After the death of dictator Francisco Franco in 1975, the first democratic elections take place in Spain.

Q2310964.name: Morgan's Raid
Q2310964.blurb: American Civil War: Morgan's Raid ends; At Salineville, Ohio, Confederate cavalry leader John Hunt Morgan and 360 of his volunteers are captured by Union forces.

Q2311171.name: Operation Panzerfaust
Q2311171.blurb: World War II: Germany replaces the Hungarian government after Hungary announces an armistice with the Soviet Union.

Q2311799.name: Battle of Santander
Q2311799.blurb: Spanish Civil War: Santander falls to the Nationalists and the Republican Interprovincial Council is dissolved.

Q2312213.name: Bronze Night
Q2312213.blurb: Controversy surrounding the relocation of the Bronze Soldier of Tallinn, a Soviet Red Army World War II memorial in Tallinn, Estonia, erupted into mass protests and riots.

Q2313440.name: 2013 Houphouët-Boigny stampede
Q2313440.blurb: At least 60 people are killed and 200 injured in a stampede after celebrations at Félix Houphouët-Boigny Stadium in Abidjan, Ivory Coast.

Q2314453.name: Operation Ke
Q2314453.blurb: World War II: Japan begins Operation Ke, the successful operation to evacuate its forces from Guadalcanal during the Guadalcanal campaign.

Q2315131.name: Orange River Convention
Q2315131.blurb: The Orange River Convention was signed in Bloemfontein, with the United Kingdom agreeing to recognise the independence of the Orange Free State in present-day South Africa.

Q2316150.name: U-boat campaign
Q2316150.blurb: U-boat Campaign: The Imperial German Navy institutes unrestricted submarine warfare in the waters around Great Britain and Ireland.

Q2316201.name: Tudor period
Q2316201.blurb: The Tudor warship Mary Rose sinks off Portsmouth; in 1982 the wreck is salvaged in one of the most complex and expensive projects in the history of maritime archaeology.

Q2316233.name: 2009 Icelandic financial crisis protests
Q2316233.blurb: A protest movement in Iceland culminates as the 2009 Icelandic financial crisis protests start.

Q2316727.name: Ba Congress
Q2316727.blurb: Representatives of the Chetnik movement began a four-day congress to organise political opposition to the Allied support of the communist-led Yugoslav Partisans in Yugoslavia.

Q2318597.name: French referendum on Algerian self-determination
Q2318597.blurb: In France a referendum supports Charles de Gaulle's policies in Algeria.

Q2320123.name: West Caribbean Airways Flight 708
Q2320123.blurb: West Caribbean Airways Flight 708, a McDonnell Douglas MD-82, crashes in Machiques, Venezuela, killing all 160 people on board.

Q2320981.name: Williamite War in Ireland
aliases: The War of the Two Kings
Q2320981.blurb: James II of England lands at Kinsale, starting the Williamite War in Ireland.

Q2321680.name: Tashkent Declaration
Q2321680.blurb: Tashkent Declaration, a peace agreement between India and Pakistan signed that resolved the Indo-Pakistani War of 1965.

Q2323805.name: Alliance Air Flight 7412
Q2323805.blurb: During approach to Lok Nayak Jayaprakash Airport, Alliance Air Flight 7412 suddenly crashes into a residential neighborhood in Patna, India, killing 60 people.

Q2326099.name: Byzantine–Sassanid War of 602–628
Q2326099.blurb: Byzantine–Sasanian War of 602–628: Sassanid troops under general Shahrbaraz conquer the town of Zenobia.

Q2327438.name: Bogotazo
Q2327438.blurb: Jorge Eliécer Gaitán's assassination provokes a violent riot in Bogotá (the Bogotazo), and a further ten years of violence in Colombia.

Q2328052.name: Russification of Finland
Q2328052.blurb: The Second Period of Russification: The teaching of the Russian language and Russian history in Finnish schools is ordered to be considerably increased as part of the forced Russification program in Finland run by Tsar Nicholas II.

Q2329367.name: Test No. 6
Q2329367.blurb: Nuclear weapons testing: China announces a successful test of its first thermonuclear weapon.

Q2330335.name: Mongol invasion of Central Asia
Q2330335.blurb: Genghis Khan defeats the renegade Khwarazmian prince Jalal al-Din at the Battle of the Indus, completing the Mongol conquest of Central Asia.

Q2331555.name: Battle of Neuve Chapelle
Q2331555.blurb: The Battle of Neuve Chapelle, the first deliberately planned British offensive of the First World War, began.

Q2333674.name: Battle of Jonesborough
Q2333674.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Jonesborough, alongside the overall Atlanta campaign, culminates in a Union victory for General William T. Sherman as Confederate General John Bell Hood orders the evacuation of Atlanta.

Q2334343.name: 1948 KLM Constellation air disaster
Q2334343.blurb: A KLM Lockheed L-049 Constellation crashes on approach to Glasgow Prestwick Airport, killing 40.

Q2334896.name: 1809 Swedish coup d'état
Q2334896.blurb: Gustav IV Adolf of Sweden is deposed in the Coup of 1809.

Q2335101.name: 1935 Quetta earthquake
Q2335101.blurb: A 7.7 Mw earthquake destroys Quetta in modern-day Pakistan killing 40,000.

Q2335276.name: Steagles
Q2335276.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles and Pittsburgh Steelers of the NFL merge for one season due to player shortages caused by World War II.

Q2335758.name: Gulf Air Flight 771
Q2335758.blurb: Gulf Air Flight 771 is destroyed by a bomb, killing all 112 people on board.

Q2336262.name: 2012 Dnipropetrovsk explosions
Q2336262.blurb: At least four explosions hit the Ukrainian city of Dnipropetrovsk with at least 27 people injured.

Q2337340.name: Cenepa War
Q2337340.blurb: The Cenepa War between Peru and Ecuador ends on a ceasefire brokered by the UN.

Q2339774.name: Wolseley Expedition
Q2339774.blurb: The Wolseley expedition reaches Manitoba to end the Red River Rebellion.

Q2340487.name: Over the Edge
Q2340487.blurb: Professional wrestler Owen Hart died immediately before a World Wrestling Federation match after dropping 70 feet (21 m) onto the ring during a botched entrance.

Q2341052.name: Kazan Operation
Q2341052.blurb: Russian Civil War: The Red Army captures Kazan.

Q2341090.name: murder of John Lennon
aliases: Conspiracy theories about the murder of John Lennon
Q2341090.blurb: Mark David Chapman is sentenced to 20 years to life in prison for murdering John Lennon.

Q2341407.name: Carandiru massacre
Q2341407.blurb: Military police storm the Carandiru Penitentiary in São Paulo, Brazil during a prison riot. The resulting massacre leaves 111 prisoners dead.

Q2341456.name: Newlands Resolution
Q2341456.blurb: US president William McKinley signed the Newlands Resolution, annexing Hawaii as a territory of the United States.

Q2342042.name: Maryland Campaign
Q2342042.blurb: American Civil War Maryland Campaign: General Robert E. Lee takes the Army of Northern Virginia, and the war, into the North.

Q2342102.name: Indochina Wars
Q2342102.blurb: Indochina Wars: Democratic Kampuchea naval forces capture the SS Mayaguez.

Q2343232.name: BOAC Flight 777
Q2343232.blurb: BOAC Flight 777 is shot down over the Bay of Biscay by German Junkers Ju 88s, killing British actor Leslie Howard and leading to speculation that it was actually an attempt to kill British Prime Minister Winston Churchill.

Q2344220.name: 2012 Indonesian Air Force Fokker F27 crash
Q2344220.blurb: An Indonesian Air Force Fokker F27 Friendship crashes near Halim Perdanakusuma International Airport, killing 11.

Q2344809.name: KLM Flight 844
Q2344809.blurb: KLM Flight 844 crashes off the Schouten Islands in present day Indonesia (then Netherlands New Guinea), killing 58 people.

Q2344888.name: First Great Awakening
Q2344888.blurb: Reverend Jonathan Edwards preaches to his congregation in Enfield, Connecticut his most famous sermon, "Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God"; an influence for the First Great Awakening.

Q2344929.name: Battle of Raymond
Q2344929.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Raymond: Two divisions of James B. McPherson's XVII Corps turn the left wing of Confederate General John C. Pemberton's defensive line on Fourteen Mile Creek, opening up the interior of Mississippi to the Union Army during the Vicksburg Campaign.

Q2345573.name: Expulsion of the Moriscos
Q2345573.blurb: Philip III of Spain issues the decree of the "Expulsion of the Moriscos".

Q2345927.name: Revolt of 1173–1174
Q2345927.blurb: William I of Scotland, a key rebel in the Revolt of 1173–74, is captured at Alnwick by forces loyal to Henry II of England.

Q2346041.name: Battle of Fort Beauséjour
Q2346041.blurb: After a two-week siege, the French commander of Fort Beauséjour in present-day New Brunswick, Canada, surrendered to British forces, marking the end of Father Le Loutre's War.

Q2346983.name: Battle of Kumanovo
Q2346983.blurb: First Balkan War: The Battle of Kumanovo concludes with the Serbian victory against the Ottoman Empire.

Q2347183.name: Spanish European Constitution referendum, 2005
Q2347183.blurb: Spain becomes the first country to vote in a referendum on ratification of the proposed Constitution of the European Union, passing it by a substantial margin, but on a low turnout.

Q2349651.name: Anarchy at Samarra
Q2349651.blurb: The Abbasid caliph al-Mutawakkil was assassinated by his guards, beginning the Anarchy at Samarra.

Q2350145.name: Siege of Alkmaar
Q2350145.blurb: The Spanish siege of Alkmaar ends with the first Dutch victory in the Eighty Years' War.

Q2350607.name: Rumbula massacre
Q2350607.blurb: The Holocaust: The SS-Einsatzgruppen round up roughly 25,000 Jews from the Riga Ghetto and kill them in the Rumbula massacre.

Q2350993.name: Michelade
Q2350993.blurb: During the French War of Religion, Protestant coup officials in Nîmes massacre Catholic priests in an event now known as the Michelade.

Q2351002.name: 1891 Nōbi earthquake
Q2351002.blurb: The Mino–Owari earthquake, the largest inland earthquake in Japan's history, occurs.

Q2351714.name: Battle of Zonchio
Q2351714.blurb: First engagement of the Battle of Zonchio between Venetian and Ottoman fleets.

Q2352036.name: 1999 Pakistani coup d'état
Q2352036.blurb: Pervez Musharraf takes power in Pakistan from Nawaz Sharif through a bloodless coup.

Q2352263.name: Farhud
Q2352263.blurb: The Farhud, a massive pogrom in Iraq, starts and as a result, many Iraqi Jews are forced to leave their homes.

Q2353599.name: Battle of Belmont
Q2353599.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Belmont: In Belmont, Missouri, Union forces led by General Ulysses S. Grant overrun a Confederate camp but are forced to retreat when Confederate reinforcements arrive.

Q2353739.name: 2003 Georgian parliamentary election
Q2353739.blurb: Rose Revolution: Eduard Shevardnadze resigned as President of Georgia following weeks of mass protests over disputed election results.

Q2354422.name: Battle of the Dalmatian channels
Q2354422.blurb: Croatian War of Independence: Croatian naval commandos attacked the Yugoslav patrol boat Mukos, starting the Battle of the Dalmatian Channels.

Q2354629.name: Malayan Emergency
aliases: The MCP and the Malayan Emergency
War crimes in the Malayan Emergency
Q2354629.blurb: Members of the Malayan Communist Party kill three British plantation managers in Sungai Siput; in response, British Malaya declares a state of emergency.

Q2355470.name: 1989 Polish legislative election
Q2355470.blurb: Solidarity's victory in the 1989 Polish legislative election occurs, the first election since the Communist Polish United Workers' Party abandoned its monopoly of power. It sparks off the Revolutions of 1989 in Eastern Europe.

Q2355732.name: Battle of Santa Rosa Island
Q2355732.blurb: American Civil War: Union troops repel a Confederate attempt to capture Fort Pickens in the Battle of Santa Rosa Island.

Q2357384.name: Portuguese conquest of Goa
Q2357384.blurb: Portuguese conquest of Goa: Portuguese naval forces under the command of Afonso de Albuquerque, and local mercenaries working for privateer Timoji, seize Goa from the Bijapur Sultanate, resulting in 451 years of Portuguese colonial rule.

Q2357517.name: Port Arthur massacre
Q2357517.blurb: Port Arthur massacre, Tasmania: A gunman, Martin Bryant, opens fire at the Broad Arrow Cafe in Port Arthur, Tasmania, killing 35 people and wounding 23 others.

Q2358366.name: Omagh bombing
Q2358366.blurb: Northern Ireland: Omagh bombing takes place; 29 people (including a woman pregnant with twins) killed and some 220 others injured.

Q2359563.name: Tel al-Zaatar massacre
Q2359563.blurb: Between 1,000 and 3,500 Palestinians are killed in the Tel al-Zaatar massacre, one of the bloodiest events of the Lebanese Civil War.

Q2360546.name: Renault Formula One crash controversy
Q2360546.blurb: The Singapore Grand Prix is held as Formula One's inaugural night race, with Fernando Alonso winning the event. Almost a year later it was revealed that Alonso's team-mate Nelson Piquet Jr. had been ordered to crash his car to help bring out the safety car and give Alonso the advantage and win.

Q2360975.name: 2009 Indonesian Air Force C-130H Hercules crash
Q2360975.blurb: An Indonesian Air Force Lockheed L-100 Hercules crashes in Magetan Regency, killing 99.

Q2361214.name: Battle of Sirte
Q2361214.blurb: First Libyan Civil War: Muammar Gaddafi, the deposed Libyan leader, was captured by rebel forces during the Battle of Sirte, and was killed shortly thereafter.

Q2362167.name: assassination of Pim Fortuyn
Q2362167.blurb: Dutch politician Pim Fortuyn is assassinated following a radio interview at the Mediapark in Hilversum.

Q2362482.name: First Persian invasion of Greece
Q2362482.blurb: Battle of Marathon: The conventionally accepted date for the Battle of Marathon. The Athenians and their Plataean allies defeat the first Persian invasion force of Greece.

Q2363420.name: 2011 southern Israel cross-border attacks
Q2363420.blurb: A terrorist attack on Israel's Highway 12 near the Egyptian border kills 16 and injures 40.

Q2363565.name: Dhofar Rebellion
Q2363565.blurb: Dhofar Rebellion: British SAS units help the Omani government against Popular Front for the Liberation of Oman rebels in the Battle of Mirbat.

Q2363601.name: Golden Bull of Sicily
Q2363601.blurb: The Golden Bull of Sicily is issued to confirm the hereditary royal title in Bohemia for the Přemyslid dynasty.

Q2366970.name: Battle of Cartagena de Indias
Q2366970.blurb: The Battle of Cartagena de Indias (part of the War of Jenkins' Ear) begins.

Q2367644.name: Awa'uq Massacre
Q2367644.blurb: Russian colonization of North America: Awa'uq Massacre: The Russian fur trader Grigory Shelikhov storms a Kodiak Island Alutiit refuge rock on Sitkalidak Island, killing 500+ Alutiit.

Q2368123.name: Battle of Pinkie
Q2368123.blurb: The Battle of Pinkie, the last full-scale military confrontation between England and Scotland, resulting in a decisive victory for the forces of Edward VI.

Q2368479.name: wedding of Victoria, Crown Princess of Sweden, and Daniel Westling
aliases: Wedding of Crown Princess Victoria of Sweden, and Daniel Westling
Q2368479.blurb: The royal wedding of Victoria, Crown Princess of Sweden, and Daniel Westling took place in Stockholm Cathedral.

Q2370272.name: Unification Act
aliases: 71st anniversary of the signing of the Act Zluky
Day of Collegiality and Ukrainian Freedom
Day of Unity and Liberty of Ukraine
Q2370272.blurb: Act Zluky is signed, unifying the Ukrainian People's Republic and the West Ukrainian National Republic.

Q2372093.name: Siege of Izmail
Q2372093.blurb: The Turkish fortress of Izmail is stormed and captured by Alexander Suvorov and his Russian armies.

Q2372347.name: Vladivostok Air Flight 352
Q2372347.blurb: Vladivostok Air Flight 352 crashes on approach to Irkutsk Airport killing all 145 people on board.

Q2372837.name: Air Florida Flight 90
Q2372837.blurb: Shortly after takeoff, Air Florida Flight 90, a Boeing 737 jet, crashes into Washington, D.C.'s 14th Street Bridge and falls into the Potomac River, killing 78 including four motorists.

Q2374330.name: Battle of Atlanta
Q2374330.blurb: American Civil War: In the  Battle of Atlanta, Confederate General John Bell Hood leads an unsuccessful attack on Union troops under General William T. Sherman on Bald Hill outside Atlanta.

Q2375128.name: 1979 Dniprodzerzhynsk mid-air collision
Q2375128.blurb: Two Aeroflot passenger jets collided in mid-air near Dniprodzerzhynsk in the Ukrainian SSR, killing all 178 people on both aircraft.

Q2375242.name: This was their finest hour
Q2375242.blurb: World War II: The "Finest Hour" speech is delivered by Winston Churchill.

Q2375246.name: 2004 Russian aircraft bombings
Q2375246.blurb: Ninety passengers die after two airliners explode after flying out of Domodedovo International Airport, near Moscow. The explosions are caused by suicide bombers from Chechnya.

Q2375420.name: Aeroflot Flight 3352
Q2375420.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 3352 crashes into maintenance vehicles upon landing in Omsk, Russia, killing 178.

Q2377743.name: Union of Bessarabia with Romania
Q2377743.blurb: The National Council of Bessarabia proclaims union with the Kingdom of Romania.

Q2378829.name: German–Soviet military parade in Brest-Litovsk
Q2378829.blurb: A joint military parade by the troops of Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union took place in Brest-Litovsk to celebrate their partition of Poland.

Q2379080.name: Northwest Territories division plebiscite, 1982
Q2379080.blurb: The Parliament of Canada passes the Nunavut Act leading to the 1999 creation of Nunavut, dividing the Northwest Territories into arctic (Inuit) and sub-arctic (Dene) lands based on a plebiscite.

Q2379101.name: 1947–1948 Civil War in Mandatory Palestine
aliases: 1948 Civil War in the British Mandate of Palestine
Spillover of the 1947-48 Civil War in Mandatory Palestine
Spillover of the 1947–48 Civil War in Mandatory Palestine
Q2379101.blurb: Civil War in Mandatory Palestine: The Jewish paramilitary group Haganah captured Haifa from the Arab Liberation Army.

Q2379380.name: evacuation of East Prussia
Q2379380.blurb: World War II: Germany begins the evacuation of 1.8 million people from East Prussia, a task which will take nearly two months.

Q2381192.name: Mexicana de Aviación Flight 940
Q2381192.blurb: Mexicana de Aviación Flight 940 crashes into the Sierra Madre Oriental mountain range near the Mexican town of Maravatío, killing 167.

Q2383784.name: Treaty of The Hague
Q2383784.blurb: The Treaty of The Hague is signed by Portugal and the Dutch Republic.

Q2384201.name: Rojava Revolution
aliases: Kurdish participation in the 2011-2012 Syrian uprising
Kurdish participation in the 2011–2012 Syrian uprising
Kurdish participation in the Syrian civil war
Kurds during the Syrian civil war
Q2384201.blurb: Rojava conflict: The Jazira Canton declares its autonomy from the Syrian Arab Republic.

Q2384685.name: Sinai Interim Agreement
Q2384685.blurb: The Sinai Interim Agreement relating to the Arab–Israeli conflict is signed.

Q2385882.name: Bangladesh Rifles revolt
Q2385882.blurb: Soldiers of the Bangladesh Rifles mutiny at their headquarters in Pilkhana, Dhaka, Bangladesh, resulting in 74 deaths, including 57 army officials.

Q2387981.name: Republican Revolution
Q2387981.blurb: Republican Revolution: On the night of the 1994 United States midterm elections, Republicans make historic electoral gains by securing massive majorities in both houses of Congress (54 seats in the House and eight seats in the Senate, additionally), thus bringing to a close four decades of Democratic domination.

Q2388649.name: Tailhook scandal
Q2388649.blurb: At the Tailhook Association symposium in Las Vegas, U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aviators were alleged to have sexually assaulted 90 persons.

Q2389817.name: 1721 papal conclave
Q2389817.blurb: In the Papal States, Cardinal Michelangelo dei Conti is elected Pope, and takes the name Innocent XIII.

Q2390461.name: Siege of Weinsberg
Q2390461.blurb: After a siege of several weeks, the city of Weinsberg and its castle surrender to Conrad III of Germany.

Q2392480.name: 1994 Major League Baseball season
Q2392480.blurb: The rest of the Major League Baseball season is canceled because of a strike.

Q2392991.name: Battle of Ambon
Q2392991.blurb: World War II: Japanese forces invade the island of Ambon in the Dutch East Indies. Some 300 captured Allied troops are killed after the surrender. One-quarter of the remaining POWs remain alive at the end of the war.

Q2393199.name: 2007 Karachi bombing
Q2393199.blurb: Karachi bombing: A suicide attack on a motorcade carrying former Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto kills 139 and wounds 450 more. Bhutto herself is uninjured.

Q2394303.name: Koli Point action
Q2394303.blurb: World War II: The Koli Point action begins during the Guadalcanal campaign and ends on November 12.

Q2394315.name: Battle of Mount Austen, the Galloping Horse, and the Sea Horse
Q2394315.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Mount Austen, the Galloping Horse, and the Sea Horse begins during the Guadalcanal campaign.

Q2394344.name: Battle of Sarmin
Q2394344.blurb: Roger of Salerno's Crusader army defeats a numerically superior Seljuk army in the battle of Sarmin

Q2394918.name: Battle of Callao
Q2394918.blurb: Peruvian defenders fight off the Spanish fleet at the Battle of Callao.

Q2395085.name: Easter Offensive
Q2395085.blurb: Vietnam War: The Easter Offensive begins after North Vietnamese forces cross into the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) of South Vietnam.

Q2395126.name: 6th United States Congress
Q2395126.blurb: The 6th United States Congress recesses, and the process of moving the Federal government of the United States from Philadelphia to Washington, D.C., begins the following day.

Q2395162.name: Matanikau Offensive
Q2395162.blurb: World War II: Matanikau Offensive begins during the Guadalcanal campaign and ends three days later with an American victory.

Q2395922.name: transatlantic telegraph cable
Q2395922.blurb: The first permanent transatlantic telegraph cable is successfully completed, stretching from Valentia Island, Ireland, to Heart's Content, Newfoundland.

Q2397066.name: Mongol invasions of the Levant
Q2397066.blurb: The Bahri Mamluks defeat the Ilkhanate in the battle of Marj al-Saffar, marking the end of the Mongol incursions into Syria.

Q2397117.name: Battle of Caishi
Q2397117.blurb: Battle of Caishi: A Song dynasty fleet fights a naval engagement with Jin dynasty ships on the Yangtze river during the Jin–Song Wars.

Q2397594.name: 2010 Peshawar bombings
Q2397594.blurb: Up to 50 people are killed and another 100 injured in two militant suicide bombings and attacks in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan: the first on an Awami National Party rally in Timergara; the second on the U.S. Consulate in Peshawar.

Q2398589.name: Siege of Cusco
Q2398589.blurb: The Siege of Cuzco commences, in which Incan forces attempt to retake the city of Cuzco from the Spanish.

Q2401825.name: Matthew Shepard Act
aliases: Matthew Shepard and James Byrd, Jr. Hate Crimes Prevention Act
Q2401825.blurb: US President Barack Obama signs the Matthew Shepard and James Byrd Jr. Hate Crimes Prevention Act.

Q2403171.name: Ten Cent Beer Night
Q2403171.blurb: Major League Baseball's Cleveland Indians hosted Ten-Cent Beer Night, but had to forfeit the game to the Texas Rangers due to rioting by drunken fans.

Q2403418.name: May Coup
Q2403418.blurb: In the May Coup, Alexander I, King of Serbia, and Queen Draga, are assassinated in Belgrade by the Black Hand (Crna Ruka) organization.

Q2409166.name: Battle of Hsimucheng
Q2409166.blurb: Russo-Japanese War: Battle of Hsimucheng: Units of the Imperial Japanese Army defeat units of the Imperial Russian Army in a strategic confrontation.

Q2411274.name: 2009 Boko Haram uprising
Q2411274.blurb: The militant Nigerian Islamist group Boko Haram attacks a police station in Bauchi, leading to reprisals by the Nigeria Police Force and four days of violence across multiple cities.

Q2411998.name: eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79
aliases: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 A.D.
Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 CE
Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in AD 79
The eruption of Vesuvius in 79 AD
Q2411998.blurb: Pompeii was severely damaged by a strong earthquake, which may have been a precursor to the eruption of Mount Vesuvius that destroyed the town 17 years later.

Q2415901.name: allied-occupied Germany
Q2415901.blurb: Cold War: The Western occupying powers approve the Basic Law and establish a new German state, the Federal Republic of Germany.

Q2418042.name: United States bombing of the Chinese embassy in Belgrade
aliases: NATO bombing of the Chinese embassy in Belgrade
bombing of the Chinese embassy in Belgrade
Bombing of Chinese embassy in Belgrade
NATO bombing of the People's Republic of China embassy in Belgrade
U.S. bombing of the Chinese embassy in Belgrade
U.S. bombing of the People's Republic of China embassy in Belgrade
US bombing of the Chinese embassy in Belgrade
US bombing of the People's Republic of China embassy in Belgrade
Q2418042.blurb: Kosovo War: Three Chinese citizens are killed and 20 wounded when a NATO aircraft inadvertently bombs the Chinese embassy in Belgrade, Serbia.

Q2418422.name: Panic of 1893
Q2418422.blurb: A crowd of workers, unemployed due to the Panic of 1893, concluded the first significant popular protest march on Washington D.C.

Q2419855.name: Ukrainian–Soviet War
aliases: Group of forces in battle with the counterrevolution in the South of Russia
Group of forces in fight with counter revolution in the South Russia
Soviet Union invasion of the Ukraine
Ukraine in the Russian Civil War
Ukraine in the aftermath of the Russian Revolution
Q2419855.blurb: Ukrainian–Soviet War: The Bolshevik Red Army, on its way to besiege Kyiv, is met by a small group of military students at the Battle of Kruty.

Q2420139.name: Project 596
Q2420139.blurb: China detonates its first nuclear weapon.

Q2420736.name: Battle of Chantilly
Q2420736.blurb: American Civil War: Confederate forces attacked retreating troops (map shown) of the Union Army during a rainstorm in Chantilly, Virginia, but the battle ended inconclusively.

Q2420811.name: Battle of Mount Tabor
Q2420811.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: The Battle of Mount Tabor: Napoleon drives Ottoman Turks across the River Jordan near Acre.

Q2421268.name: First Taiwan Strait Crisis
Q2421268.blurb: The People's Liberation Army begins shelling the Republic of China-controlled islands of Quemoy, starting the First Taiwan Strait Crisis.

Q2422135.name: occupation of Araucanía
Q2422135.blurb: Indigenous Mapuche began an uprising against the occupation of Araucanía by Chile.

Q2422839.name: Siege of Nicaea
Q2422839.blurb: Fall of Nicaea to the Ottoman Turks after a siege.

Q2422973.name: Armavia Flight 967
Q2422973.blurb: Armavia Flight 967 crashes into the Black Sea near Sochi International Airport in Sochi, Russia, killing 113 people.

Q2423283.name: Mantell UFO incident
Q2423283.blurb: Kentucky Air National Guard pilot Thomas Mantell crashes while in pursuit of a supposed UFO.

Q2425434.name: Battle of Longue-Pointe
Q2425434.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Ethan Allen and a small force of American and Quebec militia failed to capture the city of Montreal from British forces.

Q2425884.name: New York City blackout of 1977
Q2425884.blurb: Amidst a period of financial and social turmoil, New York City experiences an electrical blackout lasting nearly 24 hours that leads to widespread fires and looting.

Q2426040.name: Siege of Thessalonica
Q2426040.blurb: After an eight-year siege, the Ottoman Empire captured the city of Thessalonica from the Republic of Venice.

Q2426368.name: Battle of Bardia
Q2426368.blurb: Second World War: Australian and British troops defeated Italian forces in Bardia, Libya, the first battle of the war in which an Australian Army formation took part.

Q2426625.name: Colloquy at Poissy
Q2426625.blurb: The ultimately unsuccessful Colloquy of Poissy opens in an effort to reconcile French Catholics and Protestants.

Q2427013.name: Battle of Tudela
Q2427013.blurb: French and Poles defeat the Spanish at Battle of Tudela.

Q2427419.name: Guaraní War
Q2427419.blurb: Guaraní War: The leader of the Guaraní rebels, Sepé Tiaraju, is killed in a skirmish with Spanish and Portuguese troops.

Q2428844.name: 1999 Seattle WTO protests
aliases: protests surrounding the WTO Ministerial Conference in 1999 year
Q2428844.blurb: A series of protests by anti-globalization activists against the World Trade Organization Ministerial Conference of 1999 in Seattle forced the cancellation of the opening ceremonies.

Q2434476.name: Tintin in Tibet
Q2434476.blurb: Tintin in Tibet, the twentieth volume of The Adventures of Tintin by the Belgian cartoonist Hergé and which he regarded as his favourite in the series, began serialisation.

Q2436102.name: drownings at Nantes
Q2436102.blurb: French Revolution: Ninety dissident Roman Catholic priests are executed by drowning at Nantes.

Q2436825.name: Spanish coup of July 1936
Q2436825.blurb: Spanish Civil War: An Armed Forces rebellion against the recently elected leftist Popular Front government of Spain starts the civil war.

Q2440191.name: Battle of Liaoyang
Q2440191.blurb: Russo-Japanese War: The Battle of Liaoyang begins.

Q2440618.name: Saudia Flight 163
Q2440618.blurb: Saudia Flight 163, a Lockheed L-1011 TriStar burns after making an emergency landing at Riyadh International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, killing 301 people.

Q2441248.name: Anglo-Russian War
Q2441248.blurb: The Treaties of Orebro end both the Anglo-Russian and Anglo-Swedish Wars.

Q2441292.name: Mäntsälä rebellion
Q2441292.blurb: The Mäntsälä rebellion begins when members of the far-right Lapua Movement start shooting at the social democrats' event in Mäntsälä, Finland.

Q2441400.name: 2001 Gujarat earthquake
Q2441400.blurb: An earthquake in the Indian state of Gujarat killed at least 20,000 people, injured 167,000 others and destroyed nearly 400,000 homes.

Q2443167.name: Spithead and Nore mutinies
Q2443167.blurb: The Spithead mutiny begins, immobilising the Channel fleet.

Q2444352.name: 1655 papal conclave
Q2444352.blurb: After a conclave lasting eighty days, the College of Cardinals elected Fabio Chigi as Pope Alexander VII.

Q2444955.name: Rhodesian Bush War
Q2444955.blurb: Rhodesian Bush War: Zimbabwe African National Liberation Army cadres in Gwelo attacked Zimbabwe People's Revolutionary Army troops, killing over 60 of them and starting the 1981 Entumbane uprising.

Q2445317.name: Battle of Dumlupınar
Q2445317.blurb: Battle of Dumlupınar: The final battle in the Greco-Turkish War (Turkish War of Independence).

Q2445761.name: Battle of Saucourt-en-Vimeu
Q2445761.blurb: Battle of Saucourt-en-Vimeu: Louis III of France defeats the Vikings, an event celebrated in the poem Ludwigslied.

Q2445978.name: 1304–05 papal conclave
Q2445978.blurb: Election of Pope Clement V following the death of Pope Benedict XI in the previous year.

Q2446520.name: Iran newspaper cockroach cartoon controversy
Q2446520.blurb: Iranian Azeris interpret a cartoon published in an Iranian magazine as insulting, resulting in massive riots throughout the country.

Q2446643.name: Battle of Raate Road
Q2446643.blurb: Winter War: Battle of Raate Road: The Finnish 9th Division finally defeat the numerically superior Soviet forces on the Raate-Suomussalmi road.

Q2448644.name: Mongol invasions of Vietnam
Q2448644.blurb: Mongol invasions of Vietnam: Yuan forces are defeated by Trần forces in the Battle of Bach Dang in present-day northern Vietnam.

Q2449358.name: Battle of Fort Necessity
Q2449358.blurb: French and Indian War: George Washington surrenders Fort Necessity to French forces.

Q2449925.name: Dawson's Field hijackings
Q2449925.blurb: The Dawson's Field hijackers release 88 of their hostages. The remaining hostages, mostly Jews and Israeli citizens, are held until September 25.

Q2451365.name: occupation of Smyrna
Q2451365.blurb: Greek occupation of Smyrna. During the occupation, the Greek army kills or wounds 350 Turks; those responsible are punished by Greek commander Aristides Stergiades.

Q2452289.name: KLM Flight 633
Q2452289.blurb: KLM Flight 633 crashes into the River Shannon in Shannon, County Clare, Ireland, killing 28.

Q2453355.name: Dartmouth workshop
aliases: Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence
Q2453355.blurb: The Dartmouth workshop is the first conference on artificial intelligence.

Q2453505.name: Third Partition of Poland
aliases: Third Partition of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
Third Partition of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth
Q2453505.blurb: Poland is completely consumed by Russia, Prussia and Austria.

Q2456110.name: Battle of Larga
Q2456110.blurb: The Battle of Larga between the Russian Empire and the Ottoman Empire takes place.

Q2457479.name: 2011 Albanian opposition demonstrations
Q2457479.blurb: Anti-government demonstrations take place in Tirana, Albania. Four people die from gunshots, allegedly fired from armed police protecting the Prime Minister's office.

Q2457646.name: Diet of Porvoo
Q2457646.blurb: At the Diet of Porvoo, Finland's four Estates pledge allegiance to Alexander I of Russia, commencing the secession of the Grand Duchy of Finland from Sweden.

Q2459925.name: Battle of Uclés
Q2459925.blurb: Battle of Uclés: Almoravid troops under the command of Tamim ibn Yusuf defeat a Castile and León alliance under the command of Prince Sancho Alfónsez.

Q2461485.name: 1994 Summer War
Q2461485.blurb: The Democratic Republic of Yemen unsuccessfully attempts to secede from the Republic of Yemen; a war breaks out.

Q2465037.name: Battle of Marton
Q2465037.blurb: Æthelred of Wessex is defeated by a Danish invasion army at the Battle of Marton.

Q2465049.name: Minsk Offensive
Q2465049.blurb: World War II: The Minsk Offensive clears German troops from the city.

Q2465567.name: 2008 Mauritanian coup d'état
Q2465567.blurb: A military junta led by Mohamed Ould Abdel Aziz stages a coup d'état in Mauritania, overthrowing president Sidi Ould Cheikh Abdallahi.

Q2467248.name: Treaty of Granada
Q2467248.blurb: The siege of Granada, the last Moorish stronghold in Spain, ends with the Treaty of Granada.

Q2467678.name: Battle of Bolimów
Q2467678.blurb: World War I: Germany is the first to make large-scale use of poison gas in warfare in the Battle of Bolimów against Russia.

Q2469718.name: Battle of Gainesville
Q2469718.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Gainesville: Confederate forces defeat Union troops near Gainesville, Florida.

Q2470023.name: Flagstaff War
Q2470023.blurb: Flagstaff War: Unhappy with translational differences regarding the Treaty of Waitangi, chiefs Hōne Heke, Kawiti and Māori tribe members chop down the British flagpole for a fourth time and drive settlers out of Kororāreka, New Zealand.

Q2471567.name: Operations Manna and Chowhound
Q2471567.blurb: World War II:  Allied airdrops of food begin over German-occupied regions of the Netherlands.

Q2472593.name: attempted assassination of Pope John Paul II
aliases: Pope John Paul II assassination attempt
1981 Attack on Pope John Paul II
1981 Pope John Paul II assassination attempt
Assassination attempt of Pope John Paul II
Assassination attempt on John Paul II
Attack on Pope John Paul II
Attempted assassination of John Paul II
Q2472593.blurb: Mehmet Ali Ağca attempts to assassinate Pope John Paul II in St. Peter's Square in Rome. The Pope is rushed to the Agostino Gemelli University Polyclinic to undergo emergency surgery and survives.

Q2473448.name: Battle of Lissa
Q2473448.blurb: A French and Italian fleet is defeated by a British squadron off the island of Vis in the Adriatic during the Napoleonic Wars.

Q2473814.name: First Battle of Olmedo
Q2473814.blurb: John II of Castile defeats the Infantes of Aragon at the First Battle of Olmedo.

Q2474047.name: 2005 Amman bombings
Q2474047.blurb: Suicide bombers attack three hotels in Amman, Jordan, killing at least 60 people.

Q2475657.name: Battle of Adwalton Moor
Q2475657.blurb: Royalists loyal to King Charles I led by the Earl of Newcastle defeat Parliamentarian troops commanded by Lord Fairfax in the battle of Adwalton Moor, allowing them to capture Bradford and Leeds.

Q2475745.name: Siberia Airlines Flight 1812
Q2475745.blurb: Siberia Airlines Flight 1812 crashes after being struck by an errant Ukrainian missile. Seventy-eight people are killed.

Q2475925.name: 1963 Syrian coup d'état
aliases: Ba'ath takeover of Syria and Iraq
Ba'ath takes power in Syria and Iraq
Q2475925.blurb: The Ba'ath Party came to power in a coup d'état by a clique of quasi-leftist Syrian Army officers calling themselves the National Council for the Revolutionary Command.

Q2476810.name: Treaty of Nymphaeum
Q2476810.blurb: The Byzantine Empire and the Republic of Genoa sign a permanent treaty against the Venetians at Nymphaeum.

Q2477486.name: Battle off Texel
Q2477486.blurb: Off the coast of the Dutch island of Texel, a British naval squadron sank the German 7th Half Flotilla of torpedo boats in the Battle off Texel.

Q2478311.name: 1981 Brixton riot
Q2478311.blurb: A massive riot in Brixton, south London, results in almost 300 police injuries and 65 serious civilian injuries.

Q2478583.name: Compact of Free Association
Q2478583.blurb: The Compact of Free Association becomes law, granting the Federated States of Micronesia and the Marshall Islands independence from the United States.

Q2478732.name: 13 September 2008 Delhi bombings
Q2478732.blurb: Five bomb blasts took place in Delhi, India, killing at least 20 people as part of a series of attacks perpetrated by the Indian Mujahideen.

Q2479606.name: Ukrainian War of Independence
Q2479606.blurb: Ukrainian War of Independence: The All-Ukrainian Central Executive Committee outlaws the Makhnovshchina by decree, igniting the Bolshevik–Makhnovist conflict.

Q2482795.name: Rally to Restore Sanity and/or Fear
Q2482795.blurb: American comedians Jon Stewart and Stephen Colbert hosted the Rally to Restore Sanity and/or Fear in Washington, D.C.

Q2482906.name: Battle of Grand Gulf
Q2482906.blurb: Confederate forts at Grand Gulf survived a bombardment by Union gunboats, preventing Ulysses S. Grant's troops from crossing the Mississippi River at that point.

Q2484108.name: Battle of Jutas
Q2484108.blurb: Finnish War: In the Battle of Jutas, Swedish forces under Lieutenant General Georg Carl von Döbeln beat the Russians, making von Döbeln a Swedish war hero.

Q2484240.name: Battle of Vertières
Q2484240.blurb: The Battle of Vertières, the last major battle of the Haitian Revolution, is fought, leading to the establishment of the Republic of Haiti, the first black republic in the Western Hemisphere.

Q2485365.name: Battle of Glen Shiel
Q2485365.blurb: Jacobite risings: Battle of Glen Shiel.

Q2487876.name: Battle of the Cremera
Q2487876.blurb: Battle of the Cremera as part of the Roman–Etruscan Wars. Veii ambushes and defeats the Roman army.

Q2488483.name: Battle of Columbus
Q2488483.blurb: Mexican Revolution: Pancho Villa leads nearly 500 Mexican raiders in an attack against the border town of Columbus, New Mexico.

Q2488800.name: Battle of Warns
Q2488800.blurb: Friso-Hollandic Wars: Frisians defeat Holland in the Battle of Warns.

Q2489794.name: Price’s Missouri Expedition
Q2489794.blurb: American Civil War: During Price's Missouri Expedition, Union troops defeated Sterling Price's Confederate army in three successive battles: Marais des Cygnes, Mine Creek, and Marmiton River.

Q2493908.name: Siege of Malta
Q2493908.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: Facing starvation and a death rate of 100 soldiers per day, the French garrison in Malta surrendered to British forces, ending a two-year siege.

Q2495117.name: United Airlines Flight 736
Q2495117.blurb: United Air Lines Flight 736 collides with a United States Air Force fighter jet near Arden, Nevada in what is now Enterprise, Nevada.

Q2496712.name: 1963 demonstrations in Iran
Q2496712.blurb: Movement of 15 Khordad: Protests against the arrest of Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini by the Shah of Iran, Mohammad Reza Pahlavi. In several cities, masses of angry demonstrators are confronted by tanks and paratroopers.

Q2497839.name: Bellview Airlines Flight 210
Q2497839.blurb: Bellview Airlines Flight 210 crashes in Nigeria, killing all 117 people on board.

Q2501125.name: Battle of Wauhatchie
Q2501125.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Wauhatchie: Forces under Union General Ulysses S. Grant repel a Confederate attack led by General James Longstreet in one of the few night battles of the war, protecting the Union's recently opened supply line into Chattanooga, Tennessee.

Q2501743.name: Battle of Jersey
Q2501743.blurb: In the Battle of Jersey, the British defeat the last attempt by France to invade Jersey in the Channel Islands.

Q2502052.name: UM Airlines Flight 4230
Q2502052.blurb: Ukrainian-Mediterranean Airlines Flight 4230 crashes in the Turkish town of Maçka, killing 75.

Q2502519.name: Red River campaign
Q2502519.blurb: American Civil War: After ten weeks, the Union Army's Red River Campaign ends in failure.

Q2504085.name: Rosariazo
Q2504085.blurb: Civil unrest in Rosario, Argentina, known as Rosariazo, following the death of a 15-year-old student.

Q2504556.name: 2009 Guinean protests
Q2504556.blurb: The military junta leading Guinea attacks a protest rally, killing or wounding 1,400 people.

Q2506366.name: Vargas tragedy
Q2506366.blurb: Torrential rains cause flash floods in Vargas, Venezuela, resulting in tens of thousands of deaths, the destruction of thousands of homes, and the complete collapse of the state's infrastructure.

Q2506432.name: Wars in Lombardy
Q2506432.blurb: Peace of Ferrara between Republic of Venice, Duchy of Milan, Republic of Florence and House of Gonzaga: ending of the second campaign of the Wars in Lombardy fought until the Treaty of Lodi in 1454, which will then guarantee the conditions for the development of the Italian Renaissance.

Q2506639.name: Malagasy Uprising
Q2506639.blurb: The Malagasy Uprising against French colonial rule begins in Madagascar.

Q2506756.name: Priestley Riots
Q2506756.blurb: Beginning of Priestley Riots (to 17 July) in Birmingham targeting Joseph Priestley as a supporter of the French Revolution.

Q2508091.name: Peace of Etaples
Q2508091.blurb: Peace of Etaples between Henry VII of England and Charles VIII of France.

Q2508152.name: Fredonian Rebellion
Q2508152.blurb: Mexican soldiers and Texan militiamen marched into Nacogdoches, Texas, to end the Fredonian Rebellion.

Q2508958.name: Battle of the Terek River
Q2508958.blurb: Tokhtamysh–Timur war: At the Battle of the Terek River, Timur defeats the army of the Golden Horde, beginning the khanate's permanent military decline.

Q2509895.name: 28 October 2009 Peshawar bombing
Q2509895.blurb: The 28 October 2009 Peshawar bombing kills 117 and wounds 213.

Q2510511.name: Second Battle of Abukir
Q2510511.blurb: War of the Second Coalition: At the Battle of Abukir, a British force under Sir Ralph Abercromby lands in Egypt with the aim of ending the French campaign in Egypt and Syria.

Q2510875.name: Battle of Baia
Q2510875.blurb: Stephen III of Moldavia defeats Matthias Corvinus of Hungary, with the latter being injured thrice, at the Battle of Baia.

Q2511385.name: Primera Junta y messi
Q2511385.blurb: The Primera Junta, the first independent government in Argentina, was established in an open cabildo in Buenos Aires, marking the end of the May Revolution.

Q2512802.name: Battle of Olustee
Q2512802.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Olustee: The largest battle fought in Florida during the war.

Q2516056.name: Great Fire of New York
Q2516056.blurb: The second Great Fire of New York destroys 53,000 square metres (13 acres) of New York City's Financial District.

Q2517983.name: Galileo affair
Q2517983.blurb: Galileo Galilei is formally banned by the Roman Catholic Church from teaching or defending the view that the earth orbits the sun.

Q2518540.name: Constitution of Pakistan
aliases: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan
Q2518540.blurb: Pakistan's National Assembly passes a constitutional amendment to make the "Qur'an and Sunnah" the "supreme law" but the bill is defeated in the Senate.

Q2518913.name: Treaty of Ried
Q2518913.blurb: The Treaty of Ried is signed between Bavaria and Austria.

Q2519192.name: Indian removal
Q2519192.blurb: U.S. president Andrew Jackson signed the Indian Removal Act into law, authorizing him to negotiate with Native Americans for their removal from their ancestral homelands.

Q2522212.name: Franklin–Nashville campaign
Q2522212.blurb: American Civil War: John Bell Hood begins the Franklin–Nashville Campaign in an unsuccessful attempt to draw William Tecumseh Sherman back out of Georgia.

Q2523448.name: Plan de Sánchez massacre
Q2523448.blurb: Two hundred sixty-eight Guatemalan campesinos ("peasants" or "country people") are slain in the Plan de Sánchez massacre.

Q2524228.name: Italian War of 1551–1559
Q2524228.blurb: Battle of St. Quentin: Spanish victory over the French in the Italian War of 1551–59.

Q2526840.name: Night of the Pencils
Q2526840.blurb: Night of the Pencils: In the city of La Plata, Argentina, a group of high-school students were kidnapped and later tortured, raped and murdered during the Argentinian military dictatorship

Q2528398.name: Battle of Mansurah
Q2528398.blurb: Seventh Crusade: Crusaders engage Ayyubid forces in the Battle of Al Mansurah.

Q2530200.name: Battle of Mentana
Q2530200.blurb: Giuseppe Garibaldi and his followers are defeated in the Battle of Mentana and fail to end the Pope's Temporal power in Rome (it would be achieved three years later).

Q2530931.name: Battle of Cibalae
Q2530931.blurb: Constantine I defeats Licinius, who loses his European territories.

Q2532458.name: 1990 Greek legislative election
Q2532458.blurb: The conservative New Democracy party of Constantine Mitsotakis is elected in the Greek parliamentary election.

Q2532815.name: Armero tragedy
Q2532815.blurb: The volcano Nevado del Ruiz (pictured) erupted, causing a volcanic mudslide that buried the town of Armero, Colombia, killing approximately 23,000 people.

Q2534916.name: Act of 5th November
Q2534916.blurb: The Kingdom of Poland is proclaimed by the Act of 5th November of the emperors of Germany and Austria-Hungary.

Q2535988.name: Capture of Cadiz
Q2535988.blurb: Anglo-Spanish War: English and Dutch troops sack the Spanish city of Cádiz before leaving the next day.

Q2538456.name: Treaty of Florence
Q2538456.blurb: Treaty of Florence is signed, ending the war between the French Republic and the Kingdom of Naples.

Q2539665.name: 2006 Emirati parliamentary election
Q2539665.blurb: United Arab Emirates holds its first-ever elections.

Q2540011.name: Armistice of Salonica
Q2540011.blurb: World War I:  Bulgaria signs the Armistice of Salonica ending its participation.

Q2540075.name: Hinton train collision
Q2540075.blurb: Twenty-three people are killed when a VIA Rail passenger train collides with a Canadian National freight train near the town of Hinton, Alberta, making it one of the worst rail accidents in Canada.

Q2540658.name: Battle of Călugăreni
Q2540658.blurb: Long Turkish War: Wallachian prince Michael the Brave confronts the Ottoman army in the Battle of Călugăreni and achieves a tactical victory.

Q2543603.name: Valley Campaigns of 1864
Q2543603.blurb: American Civil War: Union cavalrymen defeat Confederate forces at Toms Brook, Virginia during Sheridan's Shenandoah Valley campaign.

Q2543997.name: Siege of Ladysmith
Q2543997.blurb: Second Boer War: Having already besieged the fortress at Ladysmith, Boer forces attack it, but are driven back by British defenders.

Q2550247.name: El Al Flight 402
Q2550247.blurb: El Al Flight 402 is shot down by two fighter jets after straying into Bulgarian air space. All 58 people on board are killed.

Q2551797.name: Siege of Yorktown
Q2551797.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Yorktown begins.

Q2553656.name: Battle of the Tarigo Convoy
Q2553656.blurb: World War II: The Italian-German Tarigo convoy is attacked and destroyed by British ships.

Q2554614.name: 11th National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party
Q2554614.blurb: The pivotal Third Plenum of the 11th National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party is held in Beijing, with Deng Xiaoping reversing Mao-era policies to pursue a program for the reform and opening up.

Q2557070.name: 1975 Haicheng earthquake
Q2557070.blurb: Haicheng earthquake (magnitude 7.3 on the Richter scale) occurs in Haicheng, Liaoning, China.

Q2557155.name: Battle of Sedgemoor
Q2557155.blurb: Battle of Sedgemoor: Last battle of the Monmouth Rebellion. Troops of King James II defeat troops of James Scott, 1st Duke of Monmouth.

Q2558636.name: Interregnum
Q2558636.blurb: English Interregnum: The Protectorate: Oliver Cromwell becomes Lord Protector of the Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland.

Q2559684.name: 2009 Tel Aviv gay centre shooting
Q2559684.blurb: A shooting at a branch of the Israeli LGBT organization the Aguda in Tel Aviv resulted in two deaths.

Q2563605.name: June deportation
Q2563605.blurb: June deportation: The first major wave of Soviet mass deportations of Estonians, Latvians, and Lithuanians from the occupied Baltic states begins.

Q2564536.name: First Battle of Svensksund
Q2564536.blurb: The first naval battle of the Svensksund began in the Gulf of Finland.

Q2564664.name: Bhutan War
Q2564664.blurb: Treaty of Sinchula is signed whereby Bhutan cedes the areas east of the Teesta River to the British East India Company.

Q2564923.name: Sylacauga meteorite
Q2564923.blurb: A meteorite crashed through a roof in Sylacauga, Alabama, and hit a sleeping woman in the first verified case of a human being injured by an extraterrestrial object.

Q2567011.name: Assault on Copenhagen
Q2567011.blurb: The assault on Copenhagen by Swedish forces is beaten back with heavy losses.

Q2567468.name: 2006 Fijian coup d'état
Q2567468.blurb: Commodore Frank Bainimarama overthrows the government in Fiji.

Q2569675.name: Treaty of Greenwich
Q2569675.blurb: Having been defeated in the Battle of Solway Moss in the previous year, the Scots conclude the peace Treaty of Greenwich with the Kingdom of England. In it, they also agree to a marriage between the infant Queen Mary and Prince Edward, son of Henry VIII.

Q2570156.name: 1926 Lithuanian coup d'état
Q2570156.blurb: A coup d'état by the Lithuanian military replaced the democratically elected President Kazys Grinius with Antanas Smetona.

Q2570177.name: Battle of Kennesaw Mountain
Q2570177.blurb: American Civil War: Confederate forces defeat Union forces during the Battle of Kennesaw Mountain during the Atlanta campaign.

Q2570588.name: Merano derailment
Q2570588.blurb: Merano derailment: A rail accident in South Tyrol kills nine people and injures a further 28.

Q2572351.name: treaty of Saigon
Q2572351.blurb: As the Treaty of Saigon is signed, ceding parts of southern Vietnam to France, the guerrilla leader Trương Định decides to defy Emperor Tự Đức of Vietnam and fight on against the Europeans.

Q2572804.name: Battle of Dunkeld
Q2572804.blurb: The Battle of Dunkeld in Scotland.

Q2572835.name: 2008–2009 Battle of Kilinochchi
Q2572835.blurb: Sri Lankan civil war: The Sri Lankan army captured the town of Kilinochchi from the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam, concluding the Battle of Kilinochchi.

Q2572890.name: Operation Baytown
Q2572890.blurb: World War II: British and Canadian troops land on the Italian mainland. On the same day, Walter Bedell Smith and Giuseppe Castellano sign the Armistice of Cassibile, although it is not announced for another five days.

Q2574400.name: Battle of the Rosebud
Q2574400.blurb: American Indian Wars: Battle of the Rosebud: One thousand five hundred Sioux and Cheyenne led by Crazy Horse beat back General George Crook's forces at Rosebud Creek in Montana Territory.

Q2575844.name: Penobscot Expedition
Q2575844.blurb: American Revolutionary War: The Royal Navy defeats the Penobscot Expedition with the most significant loss of United States naval forces prior to the attack on Pearl Harbor.

Q2575889.name: Battle of Rhode Island
Q2575889.blurb: American Revolutionary War: British and American forces battle indecisively at the Battle of Rhode Island.

Q2577289.name: Lithuanian Civil War of 1389–92
Q2577289.blurb: Lithuanian Civil War (1389–1392): The Teutonic Knights begin a five-week siege of Vilnius.

Q2577392.name: Battle of Gravia Inn
Q2577392.blurb: Greek War of Independence: The Greeks defeat the Turks at the Battle of Gravia Inn.

Q2577588.name: sinking of the RMS Titanic
aliases: Shut up, Shut up, I’m working Cape Race
The sinking of the RMS Titanic
Timeline of the sinking of RMS Titanic
Timeline of the sinking of the RMS Titanic
Q2577588.blurb: The British passenger liner RMS Titanic sinks in the North Atlantic at 2:20 a.m., two hours and forty minutes after hitting an iceberg. Only 710 of 2,224 passengers and crew on board survive.

Q2577772.name: Wars of the Three Kingdoms
aliases: The Civil Wars in Britain and Ireland
The Wars of the Three Kingdoms
Q2577772.blurb: Wars of the Three Kingdoms: In Scotland, the Battle of Inverlochy results in a Royalist/Irish victory.

Q2578008.name: Acteal massacre
Q2578008.blurb: Acteal massacre: Attendees at a prayer meeting of Roman Catholic activists for indigenous causes in the small village of Acteal in the Mexican state of Chiapas are massacred by paramilitary forces.

Q2578241.name: Ramadan Revolution
Q2578241.blurb: The regime of Prime Minister of Iraq Abd al-Karim Qasim is overthrown by the Ba'ath Party.

Q2578430.name: Battle of Svensksund
Q2578430.blurb: The Swedish Navy captures one third of the Russian Baltic fleet.

Q2578587.name: Greater Wrath
aliases: Finland during the Great Northern War
Q2578587.blurb: The Cossacks of the Tsardom of Russia kill about 800 people overnight in Hailuoto during the Great Wrath.

Q2579077.name: Massacre of Kalavryta
Q2579077.blurb: World War II: The Massacre of Kalavryta by German occupying forces in Greece.

Q2579458.name: KLM Cityhopper Flight 433
Q2579458.blurb: Three people are killed when KLM Cityhopper Flight 433 crashes at Amsterdam Airport Schiphol.

Q2579501.name: Battle of Valtetsi
Q2579501.blurb: The first major battle of the Greek War of Independence against the Turks is fought in Valtetsi.

Q2580246.name: 15 February 2003 anti-war protest
Q2580246.blurb: Protests against the Iraq war take place in over 600 cities worldwide. It is estimated that between eight million and 30 million people participate, making this the largest peace demonstration in history.

Q2583015.name: ghetto in Nazi-occupied Europe
aliases: Ghettos in Europe during the Holocaust
Q2583015.blurb: The Holocaust in Ukraine: The SS executes 588 Jewish residents of the Podolian town of Zinkiv (Khmelnytska oblast). The Zoludek Ghetto (in Belarus) is destroyed and all its inhabitants executed or deported.

Q2583092.name: Liberators' Civil War
aliases: Assassins of Caesar and their allies
Q2583092.blurb: Liberators' civil war: Triumvirs Mark Antony and Octavian fight to a draw Caesar's assassins Brutus and Cassius in the first part of the Battle of Philippi, where Cassius commits suicide believing the battle is lost.

Q2583161.name: Unilateral Declaration of Egyptian Independence
Q2583161.blurb: The United Kingdom ends its protectorate over Egypt through a Unilateral Declaration of Independence.

Q2583213.name: Draupner wave
Q2583213.blurb: The Draupner wave in the North Sea in Norway is detected, confirming the existence of freak waves.

Q2583734.name: Indonesian invasion of East Timor
Q2583734.blurb: East Timor is annexed and becomes the 27th province of Indonesia.

Q2584397.name: 3 September 1843 Revolution
Q2584397.blurb: The Greek Army rebels (OS date: September 3) against the autocratic rule of king Otto of Greece, demanding the granting of a constitution.

Q2584439.name: First Egyptian-Ottoman War
Q2584439.blurb: Egyptian–Ottoman War: Egyptian forces decisively defeat Ottoman troops at the Battle of Konya.

Q2585513.name: 2007 United States Air Force nuclear weapons incident
Q2585513.blurb: Six nuclear warheads were mistakenly loaded onto a United States Air Force heavy bomber that flew from Minot Air Force Base in North Dakota to Barksdale Air Force Base in Louisiana.

Q2586098.name: 2004 unrest in Kosovo
Q2586098.blurb: Unrest in Kosovo: More than 22 are killed and 200 wounded. Thirty-five Serbian Orthodox shrines in Kosovo and two mosques in Serbia are destroyed.

Q2587808.name: The Holocaust in Poland
Q2587808.blurb: The Holocaust in Poland: At the end of Yom Kippur, Germans order Jews to permanently move from Konstantynów to Biała Podlaska.

Q2588984.name: Sloterdijk train collision
Q2588984.blurb: Two trains are involved in a head-on collision near Sloterdijk, Amsterdam, in the Netherlands, killing one person and injuring 116 others.

Q2589203.name: Battle off Lizard Point
Q2589203.blurb: Eighty Years' War: Off the coast of Cornwall, a Spanish fleet intercepted an Anglo-Dutch merchant convoy of forty-four vessels escorted by six men-of-war, destroying or capturing twenty ships.

Q2589837.name: 1957 Haitian general election
Q2589837.blurb: François Duvalier (pictured), nicknamed Papa Doc, was elected President of Haiti as a populist before consolidating power and ruling as a dictator for the rest of his life.

Q2590023.name: Siege of Tripolitsa
Q2590023.blurb: Tripolitsa, Greece, is captured by Greek rebels during the Greek War of Independence.

Q2590336.name: Decian persecution
Q2590336.blurb: Pope Fabian is martyred during the Decian persecution.

Q2591374.name: Zinoviev letter
Q2591374.blurb: The Zinoviev letter, which Zinoviev himself denied writing, is published in the Daily Mail; the Labour party would later blame this letter for the Conservatives' landslide election win four days later.

Q2592295.name: Constitutionalist Revolution
Q2592295.blurb: In Brazil, four students are shot and killed during a manifestation against the Brazilian dictator Getúlio Vargas, which resulted in the outbreak of the Constitutionalist Revolution several weeks later.

Q2594176.name: Siege of Geertruidenberg
Q2594176.blurb: The Dutch city of Geertruidenberg held by the Spanish, capitulates to a besieging Dutch and English army led by Maurice of Nassau.

Q2594536.name: 2005 Baghdad bridge stampede
Q2594536.blurb: The 2005 Al-Aaimmah bridge stampede in Baghdad kills 953 people.

Q2594768.name: Geneva Convention on Prisoners of War
aliases: Convention Relative to the Treatment of Prisoners of War
Convention of 1929 on Prisoners of War
Convention on Prisoners of War of 1929
Geneva Convention of 1929 on Prisoners of War
Geneva Convention on Prisoners of War of 1929
Q2594768.blurb: The Geneva Convention of 1929, dealing with treatment of prisoners-of-war, is signed by 53 nations.

Q2595990.name: Currency Reform of 1948
Q2595990.blurb: In Western Allied-occupied Germany, the Currency Reform of 1948 goes into effect, introducing the Deutsche Mark. The Soviet Military Administration in Germany responded by imposing the Berlin Blockade four days later.

Q2597490.name: Noar Linhas Aéreas Flight 4896
Q2597490.blurb: Noar Linhas Aéreas Flight 4896 crashes in Boa Viagem, Recife, killing all 16 people on board.

Q2597500.name: 18 of the Copacabana Fort revolt
Q2597500.blurb: Brazilian Army rebels took over Fort Copacabana and launched a rebellion in Rio de Janeiro against President Epitácio Pessoa and President-elect Artur Bernardes.

Q2597597.name: Battle of Krasny Bor
Q2597597.blurb: World War II: Attempting to completely lift the Siege of Leningrad, the Soviet Red Army engages German troops and Spanish volunteers in the Battle of Krasny Bor.

Q2599254.name: Battle of Alavus
Q2599254.blurb: The Finnish War: The Battle of Alavus is fought.

Q2599340.name: War of the Sicilian Vespers
Q2599340.blurb: The Treaty of Anagni, an attempt mediated by the papacy to end the War of the Sicilian Vespers, is signed by the crown of Aragon, the kingdom of France and kingdom of Naples.

Q2599492.name: Double Eagle II
Q2599492.blurb: Double Eagle II becomes first balloon to cross the Atlantic Ocean when it lands in Miserey, France near Paris, 137 hours after leaving Presque Isle, Maine.

Q2599844.name: Battle of Kletsk
Q2599844.blurb: The Grand Duchy of Lithuania defeats the Crimean Khanate in the Battle of Kletsk.

Q2600471.name: 2008 K2 disaster
Q2600471.blurb: Eleven mountaineers from international expeditions die on K2, the second-highest mountain on Earth, in the worst single accident in the history of K2 mountaineering.

Q2600516.name: Kyiv offensive
Q2600516.blurb: Polish–Soviet War: Kyiv offensive: Polish troops led by Józef Piłsudski and Edward Rydz-Śmigły and assisted by a symbolic Ukrainian force capture Kyiv only to be driven out by the Red Army counter-offensive a month later.

Q2600584.name: Battle of Lapua
Q2600584.blurb: The Finnish War: the Battle of Lapua is fought.

Q2600932.name: 2008 Armenian presidential election
Q2600932.blurb: The Armenian police clash with peaceful opposition rally protesting against allegedly fraudulent presidential elections; as a result ten people are killed.

Q2602070.name: Colorado War
Q2602070.blurb: Colorado War: Colorado volunteers led by Colonel John Chivington massacre at least 150 Cheyenne and Arapaho noncombatants at Sand Creek inside Colorado Territory.

Q2602211.name: Battle of Port Republic
Q2602211.blurb: American Civil War: A Confederate victory by forces under General Stonewall Jackson at the Battle of Cross Keys, along with the Battle of Port Republic the next day, prevents Union forces from reinforcing General George B. McClellan in his Peninsula campaign.

Q2602266.name: Treaty of Nonsuch
Q2602266.blurb: The Treaty of Nonsuch signed by Elizabeth I of England and the Dutch Rebels.

Q2602809.name: 1924 Estonian coup d'état attempt
Q2602809.blurb: A Soviet-backed communist 1924 Estonian coup d'état attempt fails in Estonia.

Q2602904.name: Battle of Cocherel
Q2602904.blurb: Hundred Years' War: Bertrand du Guesclin and a French army defeat the Anglo-Navarrese army of Charles the Bad at Cocherel.

Q2603955.name: Gulf of Sidra incident
Q2603955.blurb: Second Gulf of Sidra incident: A pair of Libyan MiG-23 "Floggers" are shot down by a pair of US Navy F-14 Tomcats during an air-to-air confrontation.

Q2604253.name: Gulf of Sidra incident
Q2604253.blurb: Gulf of Sidra Incident: United States F-14A Tomcat fighters intercept and shoot down two Libyan Sukhoi Su-22 fighter jets over the Gulf of Sidra.

Q2604268.name: Carlson's patrol
Q2604268.blurb: World War II: Carlson's patrol during the Guadalcanal campaign ends.

Q2604547.name: Capture of Rome
Q2604547.blurb: The Bersaglieri corps enter Rome through the Porta Pia, and complete the unification of Italy.

Q2605231.name: Algiers putsch of 1961
Q2605231.blurb: During the Algiers putsch by French generals, President Charles de Gaulle announces he has assumed emergency powers, and calls on troops and civilians to support him.

Q2605977.name: Battle of Dunbar
Q2605977.blurb: Victory over the royalists in the Battle of Dunbar opens the way to Edinburgh for the New Model Army in the Third English Civil War.

Q2606324.name: Raid on Alexandria
Q2606324.blurb: World War II: Limpet mines placed by Italian divers heavily damage HMS Valiant and HMS Queen Elizabeth in Alexandria harbour.

Q2606937.name: Voronezh–Kastornoye Offensive
Q2606937.blurb: World War II: The Soviet counter-offensive at Voronezh begins.

Q2607760.name: 2008 Iceland earthquake
Q2607760.blurb: A doublet earthquake, of combined magnitude 6.1, strikes Iceland near the town of Selfoss, injuring 30 people.

Q2608162.name: assassination of Yitzhak Rabin
Q2608162.blurb: Israeli prime minister Yitzhak Rabin (pictured) was assassinated by Yigal Amir, a right-wing extremist, at a peace rally at Kings of Israel Square in Tel Aviv.

Q2608588.name: Cubana Flight 455
Q2608588.blurb: Cubana de Aviación Flight 455 is destroyed by two bombs, placed on board by an anti-Castro militant group.

Q2609193.name: Guinea-Bissau War of Independence
Q2609193.blurb: The Guinea-Bissau War of Independence officially begins when PAIGC guerrilla fighters attack the Portuguese Army stationed in Tite.

Q2609430.name: 1997 Umbria and Marche earthquake
aliases: Terremoto di Umbria e Marche del 1997
Q2609430.blurb: An earthquake strikes the Italian regions of Umbria and the Marche, causing part of the Basilica of St. Francis at Assisi to collapse.

Q2610182.name: Surinam Airways Flight 764
Q2610182.blurb: Surinam Airways Flight 764 crashes on approach to Paramaribo-Zanderij International Airport in Suriname because of pilot error, killing 176 of 187 aboard.

Q2615472.name: Mexican Border War
Q2615472.blurb: Mexican Revolution: Battle of Ambos Nogales: U.S. Army forces skirmish against Mexican Carrancistas as part of the Mexican Border War.

Q2615532.name: Battle of Chmielnik
Q2615532.blurb: First Mongol invasion of Poland: Mongols overwhelm Polish armies in Kraków in the Battle of Chmielnik and plunder the city.

Q2617147.name: Fall of Osaka Castle
Q2617147.blurb: Pro-Imperial forces capture Osaka Castle from the Tokugawa shogunate and burn it to the ground.

Q2617813.name: Battle of Manila
Q2617813.blurb: Seven Years' War: The British capture Manila from Spain and occupy it.

Q2618099.name: Siege of Moscow
Q2618099.blurb: The Golden Horde, led by Khan Tokhtamysh, begins the Siege of Moscow, which ends four days later with the storming of the city and the death of Muscovite Prince Ostei.

Q2618441.name: 1880 Zagreb earthquake
Q2618441.blurb: A major earthquake strikes Zagreb and destroys many buildings, including Zagreb Cathedral.

Q2618713.name: Homestuck
Q2618713.blurb: Andrew Hussie's webcomic Homestuck debuted, and later concluded on the same day in 2016.

Q2619606.name: Treaty of Novgorod
Q2619606.blurb: The Treaty of Novgorod delineates borders between Russia and Norway in Finnmark.

Q2620078.name: solar eclipse of April 8, 2024
Q2620078.blurb: Solar eclipse: A total solar eclipse takes place at the Moon's ascending node, visible across North America.

Q2620862.name: Battle of Konotop
Q2620862.blurb: At the Battle of Konotop the Ukrainian armies of Ivan Vyhovsky defeat the Russians led by Prince Trubetskoy.

Q2621757.name: Lal Masjid Siege
Q2621757.blurb: The Pakistani military storms the Lal Masjid mosque in Islamabad, which had been seized by Islamist militants.

Q2622002.name: abolition of feudalism in France
Q2622002.blurb: France: abolition of feudalism by the National Constituent Assembly.

Q2622938.name: July 1276 papal conclave
Q2622938.blurb: Election of pope Adrian V under the influence of Charles I of Anjou following the death of pope Gregory X earlier that year. Adrian V dies the following month.

Q2623686.name: 1996 Belgian Air Force Hercules accident
Q2623686.blurb: A Belgian Air Force C-130 Hercules carrying the Royal Netherlands Army marching band crashes on landing at Eindhoven Airport.

Q2623793.name: Battle of Ula
Q2623793.blurb: The Grand Duchy of Lithuania defeats the Tsardom of Russia in the Battle of Ula during the Livonian War.

Q2623909.name: Operation Trident
Q2623909.blurb: Indo-Pakistani War: The Indian Navy launched a successful attack against the Pakistan Navy at Karachi, sinking three ships with no Indian casualties.

Q2624745.name: 2011 Charsadda bombing
Q2624745.blurb: Two bombs explode in the Charsadda District of Pakistan killing 98 people and wounding 140 others.

Q2624963.name: Landing at Anzac Cove
