Q2624963.blurb: World War I: The Battle of Gallipoli begins: The invasion of the Turkish Gallipoli Peninsula by British, French, Indian, Newfoundland, Australian and New Zealand troops begins with landings at Anzac Cove and Cape Helles.

Q2624975.name: Lachine massacre
Q2624975.blurb: Beaver Wars: Fifteen hundred Iroquois attack Lachine in New France.

Q2625364.name: 2001 southern Peru earthquake
Q2625364.blurb: The 8.4 Mw southern Peru earthquake shakes coastal Peru with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VIII (Severe). A destructive tsunami followed, leaving at least 74 people dead, and 2,687 injured.

Q2626134.name: British Airtours Flight 28M
Q2626134.blurb: British Airtours Flight 28M suffers an engine fire during takeoff at Manchester Airport. The pilots abort but due to inefficient evacuation procedures 55 people are killed, mostly from smoke inhalation.

Q2627940.name: 1962 South Vietnamese Independence Palace bombing
Q2627940.blurb: Two dissident Republic of Vietnam Air Force pilots bombed the Independence Palace in Saigon in a failed attempt to assassinate President Ngo Dinh Diem.

Q2628015.name: Battle of Kapetron
Q2628015.blurb: Battle of Kapetron between a combined Byzantine-Georgian army and a Seljuq army.

Q2628082.name: Battle of Elbistan
Q2628082.blurb: The Mamluk Sultanate defeats the Mongols in the battle of Elbistan.

Q2628122.name: Moldavian–Ottoman Wars
Q2628122.blurb: Moldavian–Ottoman Wars: Stephen the Great led Moldavian forces to defeat an Ottoman attack under Hadım Suleiman Pasha near Vaslui in present-day Romania.

Q2628454.name: Sack of Rome
Q2628454.blurb: Siege of Rome: The Ostrogoths under king Totila plunder the city, by bribing the Eastern Roman garrison.

Q2628742.name: Athens Polytechnic uprising
Q2628742.blurb: The Athens Polytechnic uprising, a massive demonstration of popular rejection of the Greek military junta of 1967–74, begins.

Q2628859.name: Battle of Bucharest
Q2628859.blurb: World War I: The Central Powers capture Bucharest.

Q2629126.name: Treaty of Bern
Q2629126.blurb: The Universal Postal Union is created by the Treaty of Bern.

Q2629370.name: Expo 2020
Q2629370.blurb: The 2020 World Expo in Dubai begins. Its opening was originally scheduled for 20 October 2020 but was delayed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

Q2630073.name: Disappearance of Frederick Valentich
Q2630073.blurb: Australian civilian pilot Frederick Valentich vanishes over the Bass Strait south of Melbourne, after reporting contact with an unidentified aircraft.

Q2630469.name: New York and New Jersey Campaign
Q2630469.blurb: American Revolutionary War: British troops under General William Howe attack General George Washington's Continental Army and capture Chatterton Hill in the Battle of White Plains during the New York and New Jersey campaign.

Q2631076.name: Siege of Belgrade
Q2631076.blurb: Austro-Turkish War of 1716–18: The month-long Siege of Belgrade ends with Prince Eugene of Savoy's Austrian troops capturing the city from the Ottoman Empire.

Q2631085.name: Deep Blue versus Kasparov, 1997, Game 6
Q2631085.blurb: Deep Blue, a chess-playing supercomputer, defeats Garry Kasparov in the last game of the rematch, becoming the first computer to beat a world-champion chess player in a classic match format.

Q2631349.name: Air Inter Flight 148
Q2631349.blurb: Air Inter Flight 148, an Airbus A320-111, crashes into a mountain near Strasbourg, France, killing 87 of the 96 people on board.

Q2631464.name: history of Arsenal F.C. from 1886 to 1966
Q2631464.blurb: The London-based football club Arsenal, then known as Dial Square, played their first match on the Isle of Dogs.

Q2631954.name: Case of Trotskyist Anti-Soviet Military Organization
Q2631954.blurb: Great Purge: The Soviet Union under Joseph Stalin executes eight army leaders.

Q2632428.name: Air Ontario Flight 1363
Q2632428.blurb: Air Ontario Flight 1363, a Fokker F-28 Fellowship, crashes at Dryden Regional Airport in Dryden, Ontario, Canada, killing 24.

Q2632754.name: Norwegian rocket incident
Q2632754.blurb: The Norwegian rocket incident: Russia almost launches a nuclear attack after it mistakes Black Brant XII, a Norwegian research rocket, for a US Trident missile.

Q2632927.name: Battle of Chickasaw Bayou
Q2632927.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Chickasaw Bayou begins as Union General William T. Sherman starts landing his troops in an attempt to advance on Vicksburg, Mississippi.

Q2633171.name: Wilt Chamberlain's 100-point game
aliases: New York Knicks at Philadelphia Warriors, 2 March 1962
Q2633171.blurb: Wilt Chamberlain sets the single-game scoring record in the National Basketball Association by scoring 100 points.

Q2633177.name: Japanese coup d'état in French Indochina
Q2633177.blurb: World War II: A coup d'état by Japanese forces in French Indochina removes the French from power.

Q2633504.name: Soviet–Finnish Non-Aggression Pact
Q2633504.blurb: Finland and the Soviet Union sign a non-aggression treaty.

Q2633598.name: Chalk's Ocean Airways Flight 101
Q2633598.blurb: Chalk's Ocean Airways Flight 101 crashes into the Government Cut channel immediately after takeoff from Miami Seaplane Base, killing 20.

Q2633683.name: Siege of Cádiz
Q2633683.blurb: Peninsular War: Siege of Cádiz begins.

Q2634583.name: Nyamiha disaster
Q2634583.blurb: 53 people are killed in a stampede at the Nyamiha metro station in Minsk, Belarus.

Q2634783.name: Revolution of 1930
Q2634783.blurb: A bloodless coup d'état in Brazil ends the First Republic, replacing it with the Vargas Era.

Q2634895.name: Nigeria Airways Flight 2120
Q2634895.blurb: Nigeria Airways Flight 2120 crashes in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, killing all 261 passengers and crew on board.

Q2635052.name: Modoc War
Q2635052.blurb: The Modoc War begins with the Battle of Lost River.

Q2635063.name: Valuev Circular
Q2635063.blurb: The Valuev Circular bans the publication of religious, educational and training books in Ukrainian in the Russian Empire.

Q2635992.name: Second Ostend Raid
Q2635992.blurb: World War I: Germany repels Britain's second attempt to blockade the port of Ostend, Belgium.

Q2636209.name: Action of 22 September 1914
Q2636209.blurb: A German submarine sinks three British cruisers over a seventy-minute period, killing almost 1,500 sailors.

Q2636946.name: Penny Red
Q2636946.blurb: A Penny Red with perforations becomes the first perforated postage stamp to be officially issued for distribution.

Q2637132.name: Assassination of the monks of Tibhirine
Q2637132.blurb: The seven Trappist monks of Tibhirine who were abducted on March 27 are killed under uncertain circumstances.

Q2638227.name: partition of Ireland
Q2638227.blurb: Ireland is partitioned under British law by the Government of Ireland Act 1920, creating Northern Ireland and Southern Ireland.

Q2639320.name: Treaty of Yandabo
Q2639320.blurb: The signing of the Treaty of Yandabo marks the end of the First Anglo-Burmese War.

Q2639377.name: Sieges of Kolberg
Q2639377.blurb: Seven Years' War: After a four-month siege, the Russians under Pyotr Rumyantsev take the Prussian fortress of Kołobrzeg.

Q2640918.name: Black July
Q2640918.blurb: The Black July anti-Tamil riots begin in Sri Lanka, killing between 400 and 3,000. Black July is generally regarded as the beginning of the Sri Lankan Civil War.

Q2640981.name: Battle of Nezib
Q2640981.blurb: An Egyptian army under Ibrahim Pascha routs an Ottoman army under Hafiz Pasha in the battle of Nezib.

Q2641750.name: Battle of Goose Green
Q2641750.blurb: Falklands War: The British Army defeats the Argentine Army at the Battle of Goose Green.

Q2641872.name: 2011 Royal Moroccan Air Force Lockheed C-130 Hercules crash
Q2641872.blurb: A Royal Moroccan Air Force Lockheed C-130 Hercules crashes near Guelmim Airport in Guelmim, Morocco. All 80 people on board are killed.

Q2643015.name: Operation Perch
Q2643015.blurb: World War II: After several failed attempts, the British Army abandons Operation Perch, its plan to capture the German-occupied town of Caen.

Q2646343.name: second cholera pandemic
Q2646343.blurb: Asian cholera reaches Quebec, brought by Irish immigrants, and kills about 6,000 people in Lower Canada.

Q2647284.name: Alitalia Flight 404
Q2647284.blurb: While on approach to Zurich Airport, Alitalia Flight 404 crashes into Stadlerberg Mountain near Weiach, killing 46.

Q2649081.name: German invasion of the Netherlands
Q2649081.blurb: World War II: The Battle of the Netherlands: After fierce fighting, the poorly trained and equipped Dutch troops surrender to Germany, marking the beginning of five years of occupation.

Q2656382.name: Christmas Uprising
Q2656382.blurb: Montenegrin guerrilla fighters rebel against the planned annexation of Montenegro by Serbia, but fail.

Q2656995.name: Northwest Indian War
Q2656995.blurb: Northwest Indian War: The Big Bottom massacre is committed by Lenape and Wyandot warriors in the Ohio Country, North America.

Q2657479.name: Raid on Scarborough, Hartlepool and Whitby
Q2657479.blurb: World War I: Admiral Franz von Hipper commands a raid on Scarborough, Hartlepool and Whitby.

Q2657536.name: Battle of Boroughbridge
Q2657536.blurb: Despenser War: A royalist army defeated troops loyal to Thomas, 2nd Earl of Lancaster, in the Battle of Boroughbridge, which allowed King Edward II of England to hold on to power for another five years.

Q2658255.name: Byzantine Civil War of 1341–1347
Q2658255.blurb: The Byzantine civil war of 1341–47 ends with a power-sharing agreement between John VI Kantakouzenos and John V Palaiologos.

Q2658429.name: Chagai-I
Q2658429.blurb: Nuclear testing: Pakistan responds to a series of nuclear tests by India with five of its own codenamed Chagai-I, prompting the United States, Japan, and other nations to impose economic sanctions. Pakistan celebrates Youm-e-Takbir annually.

Q2658487.name: Lwów pogrom
Q2658487.blurb: A pogrom takes place in Lwów (now Lviv); over three days, at least 50 Jews and 270 Ukrainian Christians are killed by Poles.

Q2658524.name: 1940 Vrancea earthquake
Q2658524.blurb: The 1940 Vrancea earthquake strikes Romania killing an estimated 1,000 and injuring approximately 4,000 more.

Q2658753.name: Binghamton shootings
Q2658753.blurb: Jiverly Antares Wong opens fire at the American Civic Association immigration center in Binghamton, New York, killing thirteen and wounding four before committing suicide.

Q2659098.name: Battle of Athos
Q2659098.blurb: Russo-Turkish War: Admiral Dmitry Senyavin destroys the Ottoman fleet in the Battle of Athos.

Q2659241.name: Tiananmen Square self-immolation incident
Q2659241.blurb: Five people attempt to set themselves on fire in Beijing's Tiananmen Square, an act that many people later claim is staged by the Chinese Communist Party to frame Falun Gong and thus escalate their persecution.

Q2659473.name: Attack on Sydney Harbour
Q2659473.blurb: World War II: The crews of three Japanese submarines scuttled their vessels and committed suicide after entering Sydney Harbour and launching a failed attack.

Q2660012.name: First Battle of İnönü
Q2660012.blurb: Greco-Turkish War: The First Battle of İnönü, the first battle of the war, begins near Eskişehir in Anatolia.

Q2660905.name: Passover massacre
Q2660905.blurb: Passover massacre: A Palestinian suicide bomber kills 29 people at a Passover seder in Netanya, Israel.

Q2661579.name: 2009 Sayano-Shushenskaya power station accident
Q2661579.blurb: An accident at the Sayano-Shushenskaya Dam in Khakassia, Russia, kills 75 and shuts down the hydroelectric power station, leading to widespread power failure in the local area.

Q2662170.name: Riga Offensive
Q2662170.blurb: World War II: The Soviet Riga Offensive captures the city.

Q2662518.name: Vnukovo Airlines Flight 2801
Q2662518.blurb: Vnukovo Airlines Flight 2801, a Tupolev Tu-154, crashes into a mountain on the Arctic island of Spitsbergen, killing all 141 aboard.

Q2662861.name: death of Edgar Allan Poe
Q2662861.blurb: American writer Edgar Allan Poe  died under mysterious circumstances at Washington Medical College four days after being found on the streets of Baltimore, Maryland, in a delirious and incoherent state.

Q2663279.name: Battle of Palikao
Q2663279.blurb: Second Opium War: An Anglo-French force defeats Chinese troops at the Battle of Palikao.

Q2663784.name: Festival of Britain
Q2663784.blurb: London's Royal Festival Hall opens with the Festival of Britain.

Q2663849.name: Battle of Colachel
Q2663849.blurb: King Marthanda Varma of Travancore defeats the Dutch East India Company at the Battle of Colachel, effectively bringing about the end of the Dutch colonial rule in India.

Q2664602.name: War of the Two Peters
Q2664602.blurb: An Aragonese cavalry force defeats a superior Castilian cavalry force in the Battle of Araviana during the War of the Two Peters.

Q2665185.name: Lisbon Regicide
Q2665185.blurb: Lisbon Regicide: King Carlos I of Portugal and Infante Luis Filipe are shot dead in Lisbon.

Q2665403.name: Indonesian occupation of East Timor
Q2665403.blurb: The Indonesian military began a lengthy occupation of East Timor under the pretext of anti-colonialism.

Q2665576.name: Auspicious Incident
Q2665576.blurb: In the Auspicious Incident, the Janissary mutiny against Sultan Mahmud II is defeated and the Janissary corps is disbanded as a result.

Q2665626.name: Battle of Beersheba
Q2665626.blurb: World War I: Battle of Beersheba: The "last successful cavalry charge in history".

Q2665637.name: Fall of Baghdad
Q2665637.blurb: World War I: Mesopotamian campaign: Baghdad falls to Anglo-Indian forces commanded by General Frederick Stanley Maude.

Q2665991.name: 1978 Georgian demonstrations
Q2665991.blurb: Tbilisi demonstrations: Thousands of Georgians demonstrate against Soviet attempts to change the constitutional status of the Georgian language.

Q2666234.name: 1873–74 Scottish Cup
Q2666234.blurb: Renton defeated Kilmarnock 2–0 in the opening match of the inaugural Scottish Cup.

Q2666386.name: Royal Question
Q2666386.blurb: At the height of a political crisis known as the royal question, four workers were shot dead by the Belgian Gendarmerie at a strike in Grâce-Berleur.

Q2666975.name: 1995 Neftegorsk earthquake
Q2666975.blurb: The 7.0 Mw Neftegorsk earthquake shakes the former Russian settlement of Neftegorsk with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent). Total damage was $64.1–300 million, with 1,989 deaths and 750 injured. The settlement was not rebuilt.

Q2667561.name: Battle of Nikopol
Q2667561.blurb: The Imperial Russian army under Grand Duke Nicholas defeats the Ottoman army and takes the city of Nikopol (modern Bulgaria).

Q2667645.name: Mongol invasion of Poland
Q2667645.blurb: First Mongol invasion of Poland: Mongols overwhelm Polish armies in Kraków in the Battle of Chmielnik and plunder the city.

Q2668875.name: Battle of Bereza Kartuska
Q2668875.blurb: The Battle of Bereza Kartuska, the first serious armed conflict of the Polish–Soviet War, took place near present-day Biaroza, Belarus.

Q2669939.name: Lithuanian Civil War of 1432–1438
Q2669939.blurb: The first battle between the forces of Švitrigaila and Sigismund Kęstutaitis is fought near the town of Oszmiana (Ashmyany), launching the most active phase of the Lithuanian Civil War.

Q2669947.name: O. J. Simpson murder case
aliases: murder trial of O. J. Simpson
If it doesn't fit, you must acquit
OJ Simpson being accused of murder
People of the State of California v. O. J. Simpson
People of the State of California v. Orenthal James Simpson
People of the State of California vs. Orenthal James Simpson
The People of the State of California v. Orenthal James Simpson
Q2669947.blurb: O. J. Simpson murder case: O. J. Simpson is acquitted of the murders of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman.

Q2670007.name: transfer of the Portuguese Court to Brazil
Q2670007.blurb: The Portuguese royal family arrives in Brazil after fleeing the French army's invasion of Portugal two months earlier.

Q2670013.name: Insurgency in Aceh
Q2670013.blurb: The Helsinki Agreement between the Free Aceh Movement and the Government of Indonesia was signed, ending almost three decades of fighting.

Q2670249.name: Bombardment of Alexandria
Q2670249.blurb: The British Mediterranean Fleet begins the Bombardment of Alexandria in Egypt as part of the Anglo-Egyptian War.

Q2670327.name: Siege of Kazan
Q2670327.blurb: Russo-Kazan Wars: Russian troops enter Kazan.

Q2670487.name: My Trach Massacre
Q2670487.blurb: French forces carry out a massacre at Mỹ Trạch, Vietnam during the First Indochina War.

Q2670873.name: Battle of Makin
Q2670873.blurb: World War II: At the battle of Makin the USS Liscome Bay is torpedoed near Tarawa and sinks, killing 650 men.

Q2670926.name: Battle of Seminara
Q2670926.blurb: A French force heavily defeats a much larger Neapolitan and Spanish army at the battle of Seminara, leading to the creation of the Tercios by Gonzalo de Córdoba.

Q2670974.name: Poland's Wedding to the Sea
Q2670974.blurb: Józef Haller de Hallenburg performs the symbolic wedding of Poland to the sea, celebrating restitution of Polish access to open sea.

Q2671443.name: Battle of St. Lucia
Q2671443.blurb: American Revolutionary War: At the Battle of St. Lucia, the Royal Navy prevented French Navy ships from reaching their garrison on Saint Lucia in the West Indies.

Q2672115.name: Burning of Cork
Q2672115.blurb: Irish War of Independence: In retaliation for a recent IRA ambush, British forces burn and loot numerous buildings in Cork city. Many civilians report being beaten, shot at, robbed and verbally abused by British forces.

Q2672202.name: Battle of Fort Sanders
Q2672202.blurb: American Civil War: Union forces under General Ambrose Burnside successfully defend Knoxville, Tennessee from an attack by Confederate forces under General James Longstreet in the Battle of Fort Sanders during the Siege of Knoxville.

Q2672432.name: Mongol invasion of Java
Q2672432.blurb: Mongols depart Java after the failed Mongol invasion against King Kertanegara of Singhasari.

Q2673191.name: Invasion of Tulagi
Q2673191.blurb: Second World War: Japanese forces began an invasion of Tulagi and nearby islands in the British Solomon Islands, enabling them to threaten and intercept supply and communication routes between the United States and Australasia.

Q2673524.name: Sudan Airways Flight 109
Q2673524.blurb: Sudan Airways Flight 109 crashes at Khartoum International Airport, killing 30 people.

Q2676019.name: Second Battle of Fort Wagner
aliases: Battle of Fort Wagner, Morris Island
Q2676019.blurb: American Civil War: Second Battle of Fort Wagner: One of the first formal African American military units, the 54th Massachusetts Volunteer Infantry, supported by several white regiments, attempts an unsuccessful assault on Confederate-held Battery Wagner.

Q2682171.name: Battle of Fort Charlotte
Q2682171.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Spanish forces capture Fort Charlotte in Mobile, Alabama, the last British frontier post capable of threatening New Orleans.

Q2683146.name: Operation Auca
Q2683146.blurb: Operation Auca: Five U.S. missionaries are killed by the Waorani of Ecuador shortly after making first contact.

Q2683571.name: Battle of Lookout Mountain
Q2683571.blurb: American Civil War: As part of the Chattanooga campaign in Chattanooga, Tennessee, Union forces captured Lookout Mountain, helping them to begin breaking the Confederate siege of the city.

Q2687368.name: Battle of Missionary Ridge
Q2687368.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Missionary Ridge: Union forces led by General Ulysses S. Grant break the Siege of Chattanooga by routing Confederate troops under General Braxton Bragg at Missionary Ridge in Tennessee.

Q2688393.name: Normanton Incident
Q2688393.blurb: Normanton incident: As the British merchant vessel Normanton sinks off the coast of Japan, her European officers appear to commandeer the ship's lifeboats for themselves, leaving her Asian crew and passengers to die and conjuring significant political outrage in Japan.

Q2689466.name: Dolphinarium discotheque suicide bombing
Q2689466.blurb: Dolphinarium discotheque massacre: A Hamas suicide bomber kills 21 at a disco in Tel Aviv.

Q2690249.name: Scottish devolution referendum of 1997
Q2690249.blurb: After a nationwide referendum, Scotland votes to establish a devolved parliament within the United Kingdom.

Q2692278.name: Battle of Lihula
Q2692278.blurb: Sweden is defeated by Estonian tribes in the Battle of Lihula.

Q2694984.name: Battle of Remagen
Q2694984.blurb: World War II: The American 9th Armored Division unexpectedly captures an intact bridge over the Rhine.

Q2697152.name: Avianca Flight 203
Q2697152.blurb: Avianca Flight 203: A Boeing 727 explodes in mid-air over Colombia, killing all 107 people on board and three people on the ground. The Medellín Cartel claimed responsibility for the attack.

Q2697981.name: Argentine Civil Wars
aliases: Guerra de la Independencia y Guerras civiles argentinas
Q2697981.blurb: Argentine Civil Wars: The State of Buenos Aires defeats the Argentine Confederation at the Battle of Pavón.

Q2698266.name: 1955 Le Mans disaster
Q2698266.blurb: Eighty-three spectators are killed and at least one hundred are injured after an Austin-Healey and a Mercedes-Benz collide at the 24 Hours of Le Mans, the deadliest ever accident in motorsports.

Q2700708.name: Capture of New Orleans
Q2700708.blurb: American Civil War: The Capture of New Orleans by Union forces under David Farragut.

Q2701253.name: Siege of Calais
Q2701253.blurb: French troops, led by Francis, Duke of Guise, take Calais, the last continental possession of England.

Q2704441.name: Chilean Civil War of 1891
Q2704441.blurb: Chilean Civil War: The ironclad Blanco Encalada is sunk at Caldera Bay by torpedo boats.

Q2704666.name: Operation Badr
Q2704666.blurb: Egypt and Syria launch coordinated attacks against Israel, beginning the Yom Kippur War.

Q2706283.name: 1693 Sicily earthquake
Q2706283.blurb: Sicily earthquake: The first of two earthquakes destroys parts of Sicily and Malta. After the second quake on 11 January, the death toll is estimated at between 60,000 and 100,000 people.

Q2706523.name: Operation Spring
Q2706523.blurb: World War II: Operation Spring near Caen is one of the bloodiest days for the First Canadian Army during the war.

Q2707120.name: Treaty of Wuchale
Q2707120.blurb: The Treaty of Wuchale was signed, ending the Italo-Ethiopian War, but differences in translation later led to another war.

Q2707293.name: Great Retreat
Q2707293.blurb: World War I: The British Expeditionary Force and the French Fifth Army begin their Great Retreat before the German Army.

Q2708273.name: Sicilian revolution of 1848
Q2708273.blurb: The Palermo rising takes place in Sicily against the Bourbon Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.

Q2708643.name: Anglo-Irish Agreement
Q2708643.blurb: The Anglo-Irish Agreement is signed at Hillsborough Castle by British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher and Irish Taoiseach Garret FitzGerald.

Q2710498.name: Attica Prison riot
Q2710498.blurb: The four-day Attica Prison riot begins, eventually resulting in 39 dead, most killed by state troopers retaking the prison.

Q2711484.name: 2001 El Salvador earthquake
Q2711484.blurb: An earthquake hits El Salvador, killing more than 800.

Q2712908.name: Westroads Mall shooting
Q2712908.blurb: Westroads Mall shooting: Nineteen-year-old Robert A. Hawkins kills nine people, including himself, with a WASR-10 at a Von Maur department store in Omaha, Nebraska.

Q2712928.name: Battle of Spercheios
Q2712928.blurb: Battle of Spercheios: Bulgarian forces of Tsar Samuel are defeated by a Byzantine army under general Nikephoros Ouranos at the Spercheios River in Greece.

Q2713834.name: USS Iowa turret explosion
Q2713834.blurb: A gun turret explodes on the USS Iowa, killing 47 sailors.

Q2717440.name: Victoria de paraguay
Q2717440.blurb: Battle of Acosta Ñu: A Paraguayan battalion largely made up of children is massacred by the Brazilian Army during the Paraguayan War.

Q2720985.name: Battle of Kirk Kilisse
Q2720985.blurb: First Balkan War: The Battle of Kirk Kilisse concludes with a Bulgarian victory against the Ottoman Empire.

Q2721619.name: Romanian presidential impeachment referendum
Q2721619.blurb: President of Romania Traian Băsescu survives an impeachment referendum and returns to office from suspension.

Q2722368.name: Siege of Béxar
Q2722368.blurb: Texas Revolution: The Texian Army captures San Antonio following the Siege of Béxar.

Q2722527.name: Battle of Romani
Q2722527.blurb: World War I: Battle of Romani: Allied forces, under the command of Archibald Murray, defeat an attacking Ottoman army under the command of Friedrich Freiherr Kress von Kressenstein, securing the Suez Canal and beginning the Ottoman retreat from the Sinai Peninsula.

Q2723005.name: Grass Fight
Q2723005.blurb: Texas Revolution: Texian forces attacked a Mexican pack train, capturing 40 saddlebags of grass.

Q2723024.name: Enron scandal
Q2723024.blurb: Less than two months after disclosing accounting violations, the Texas-based energy firm Enron filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, evaporating nearly $11 billion in shareholder wealth.

Q2723587.name: Expulsion of the Acadians
Q2723587.blurb: Great Upheaval: New England planters arrive to claim land in Nova Scotia, Canada, taken from the Acadians.

Q2724459.name: 29 October 2005 Delhi bombings
Q2724459.blurb: Bombings in Delhi, India kill 67 and injure over 200 people.

Q2726232.name: Emergency
aliases: Indira Gandhi's seizure of emergency powers
The emergency rule of Indira Gandhi
Q2726232.blurb: Prime Minister Indira Gandhi declares a state of internal emergency in India.

Q2728539.name: Ladbroke Grove rail crash
Q2728539.blurb: The Ladbroke Grove rail crash in West London kills 31 people.

Q2729231.name: Jarrow March
Q2729231.blurb: The Jarrow March sets off for London.

Q2730371.name: Bellum Siculum
Q2730371.blurb: The Sicilian revolt against the Second Triumvirate of the Roman Republic ended when the fleet of Sextus Pompey, the rebel leader, was defeated at the Battle of Naulochus.

Q2732058.name: 2010 Madeira floods and mudslides
Q2732058.blurb: Severe flooding and mudslides on the island of Madeira, Portugal, killed 51 people.

Q2732255.name: Battle of Marj al-Saffar
Q2732255.blurb: The Bahri Mamluks defeat the Ilkhanate in the battle of Marj al-Saffar, marking the end of the Mongol incursions into Syria.

Q2733432.name: Battle of São Mamede
Q2733432.blurb: Battle of São Mamede, near Guimarães: Forces led by Afonso I defeat forces led by his mother Teresa of León and her lover Fernando Pérez de Traba.

Q2734129.name: Battle of Toro
Q2734129.blurb: Forces of the Catholic Monarchs engage the combined Portuguese-Castilian armies of Afonso V and Prince John at the Battle of Toro.

Q2735551.name: Stampede in Luzhniki on 20th October 1982
Q2735551.blurb: During the UEFA Cup match between FC Spartak Moscow and HFC Haarlem, 66 people are crushed to death in the Luzhniki disaster.

Q2736004.name: Battle of Palo Alto
Q2736004.blurb: Mexican–American War: American forces led by Zachary Taylor defeat a Mexican force north of the Rio Grande in the first major battle of the war.

Q2736155.name: Seneca Falls Convention
Q2736155.blurb: The two-day Seneca Falls Convention, the first women's-rights and feminist convention held in the United States, opened in Seneca Falls, New York.

Q2736986.name: Battle of Karnal
Q2736986.blurb: Battle of Karnal: The army of Iranian ruler Nader Shah defeats the forces of the Mughal emperor of India, Muhammad Shah.

Q2737025.name: 2011 Irish presidential election
Q2737025.blurb: Michael D. Higgins (pictured) was elected President of Ireland with far more votes than any politician in the country's history.

Q2737232.name: Battle of Old Byland
Q2737232.blurb: Robert the Bruce of Scotland defeats King Edward II of England at the Battle of Old Byland, forcing Edward to accept Scotland's independence.

Q2737918.name: Ciaculli massacre
Q2737918.blurb: Ciaculli bombing: a car bomb, intended for Mafia boss Salvatore Greco, kills seven police officers and military personnel near Palermo.

Q2738493.name: Thalit massacre
Q2738493.blurb: The Thalit massacre begins in Algeria; all but one of the 53 inhabitants of Thalit are killed by guerrillas.

Q2740393.name: Great Fire of New York
aliases: Great Fire of New York in 1776
Q2740393.blurb: Part of New York City is burned shortly after being occupied by British forces.

Q2740637.name: 2011 end times prediction
Q2740637.blurb: Radio broadcaster Harold Camping predicted that the world would end on this date.

Q2741117.name: April 25–28, 2011 tornado outbreak
Q2741117.blurb: The 2011 Super Outbreak devastates parts of the Southeastern United States, especially the states of Alabama, Mississippi, Georgia, and Tennessee. Two hundred five tornadoes touched down on April 27 alone, killing more than 300 and injuring hundreds more.

Q2741550.name: 2010 China floods
Q2741550.blurb: China Floods: A mudslide in Zhugqu County, Gansu, China, kills more than 1,400 people.

Q2742723.name: Great Flood of 1993
Q2742723.blurb: Great Flood of 1993: Levees near Kaskaskia, Illinois rupture, forcing the entire town to evacuate by barges operated by the Army Corps of Engineers.

Q2743200.name: 2007 Kenyan general election
Q2743200.blurb: Riots erupt in Mombasa, Kenya, after Mwai Kibaki is declared the winner of the presidential election, triggering a political, economic, and humanitarian crisis.

Q2743386.name: Great Vancouver Fire
Q2743386.blurb: A fire devastates much of Vancouver, British Columbia.

Q2744086.name: Hurricane Hazel
Q2744086.blurb: Hurricane Hazel devastates the eastern seaboard of North America, killing 95 and causing massive floods as far north as Toronto.

Q2744242.name: Battle of Sheriffmuir
Q2744242.blurb: Jacobite rising in Scotland: Battle of Sheriffmuir: The forces of the Kingdom of Great Britain halt the Jacobite advance, although the action is inconclusive.

Q2744875.name: Siege of Savannah
Q2744875.blurb: American Revolutionary War: The Franco-American Siege of Savannah begins.

Q2744988.name: dictatorship of Primo de Rivera
Q2744988.blurb: The Spanish anarchist group Los Solidarios unsuccessfully attempted to launch an insurrection against the dictatorship of Miguel Primo de Rivera.

Q2745155.name: 1926 United Kingdom general strike
Q2745155.blurb: The 1926 United Kingdom general strike ends.

Q2745246.name: Hurricane Charley
Q2745246.blurb: Merely 22 hours after Tropical Storm Bonnie struck the U.S. state of Florida, Hurricane Charley inflicted further damage to the region (example pictured).

Q2745368.name: Siege of Veracruz
Q2745368.blurb: Mexican–American War: The Siege of Veracruz began, the first large-scale amphibious assault conducted by United States military forces.

Q2745374.name: Conference of Zamora
aliases: Summit between Afonso Henriques of Portugal and Alfonso VII of León
Q2745374.blurb: With the signing of the Treaty of Zamora, King Alfonso VII of León and Castile recognises Portugal as a Kingdom.

Q2745432.name: Spanish Constitution of 1931
Q2745432.blurb: The Constituent Cortes approves a constitution which establishes the Second Spanish Republic.

Q2746040.name: Battle of Landriano
Q2746040.blurb: French forces are driven out of northern Italy by Spain at the Battle of Landriano during the War of the League of Cognac.

Q2746536.name: Killing of Muhammad al-Durrah
aliases: Shooting of Jamal and Muhammad al-Durrah
Q2746536.blurb: Twelve-year-old Muhammad al-Durrah was shot dead in the Gaza Strip; the Israel Defense Forces initially accepted responsibility but retracted it five years later.

Q2746913.name: Air Canada Flight 621
Q2746913.blurb: Air Canada Flight 621 crashes in Brampton, Ontario, Canada, killing all 109 people on board.

Q2747635.name: Night of the Big Wind
Q2747635.blurb: The Night of the Big Wind, the most damaging storm in 300 years, sweeps across Ireland, damaging or destroying more than 20% of the houses in Dublin.

Q2748375.name: Black Friday
Q2748375.blurb: World War II: A force of Allied aircraft unsuccessfully attack a German destroyer in Førdefjorden, Norway.

Q2748496.name: Exercise Tiger
Q2748496.blurb: World War II: Nine German E-boats attack US and UK units during Exercise Tiger, the rehearsal for the Normandy landings, killing 946.

Q2748708.name: German military administration in occupied France during World War II
aliases: German occupation of France during World War II
German occupation of France in World War II
Military Administration in France (World War II)
Occupation of France by Nazi Germany
Occupation of France in World War II
Territory of the Military Commander in France
Q2748708.blurb: Second World War: The port of Saint-Nazaire in German-occupied France was disabled  by British naval forces.

Q2749287.name: May 1998 riots of Indonesia
Q2749287.blurb: Race riots break out in Jakarta, Indonesia, where shops owned by Indonesians of Chinese descent are looted and women raped.

Q2750233.name: Siege of Montségur
Q2750233.blurb: Over 200 Cathars who refuse to recant are burnt to death after the Fall of Montségur.

Q2750283.name: third voyage of James Cook
Q2750283.blurb: Captain James Cook begins his third voyage.

Q2750389.name: Battle of Mišar
Q2750389.blurb: Battle of Mišar during the Serbian Revolution begins. The battle ends two days later with a Serbian victory over the Ottomans.

Q2750968.name: Battle of Alexandria
Q2750968.blurb: The Battle of Alexandria is fought between British and French forces near the ruins of Nicopolis near Alexandria in Egypt.

Q2752928.name: Second Revolution
Q2752928.blurb: The Second Revolution breaks out against the Beiyang government, as Li Liejun proclaims Jiangxi independent from the Republic of China.

Q2754865.name: Fort Capuzzo
Q2754865.blurb: World War II: The British Army's 11th Hussars assault and take Fort Capuzzo in Libya from Italian forces.

Q2756743.name: assassination of Anwar Sadat
Q2756743.blurb: Egyptian President Anwar Sadat is murdered by Islamic extremists.

Q2757553.name: Diet of Speyer
Q2757553.blurb: Beginning of the Protestant Reformation: After the Second Diet of Speyer bans Lutheranism, a group of rulers (German: Fürst) and independent cities protest the reinstatement of the Edict of Worms.

Q2758693.name: Siege of Maastricht
Q2758693.blurb: Start of the Siege of Maastricht, part of the Eighty Years' War.

Q2765370.name: Lhasa riot of 1750
Q2765370.blurb: Riots break out in Lhasa after the murder of the Tibetan regent.

Q2776402.name: lynching of Thomas Shipp and Abram Smith
aliases: J. Thomas Shipp and Abraham S. Smith
Thomas Shipp and Abram Smith killing
Thomas Shipp and Abram Smith lynching
Thomas Shipp and Abram Smith murder
Thomas Shipp and Abram Smith's killing
Thomas Shipp and Abram Smith's lynching
Thomas Shipp and Abram Smith's murder
killing of Thomas Shipp and Abram Smith
murder of Thomas Shipp and Abram Smith
Q2776402.blurb: The last confirmed lynching of black people in the Northern United States occurs in Marion, Indiana; two men, Thomas Shipp and Abram Smith, are murdered.

Q2777814.name: Operation Bringing Home the Goods
Q2777814.blurb: Operation Bringing Home the Goods: Israeli troops raid an American-supervised Palestinian prison in Jericho to capture six Palestinian prisoners, including PFLP chief Ahmad Sa'adat.

Q2778149.name: 1982 kidnapping of Iranian diplomats
Q2778149.blurb: Three Iranian diplomats and a journalist are kidnapped in Lebanon by Phalange forces, and their fate remains unknown.

Q2778755.name: naval operations in the Dardanelles Campaign
Q2778755.blurb: World War I: The first naval attack on the Dardanelles begins when a strong Anglo-French task force bombards Ottoman artillery along the coast of Gallipoli.

Q2783102.name: London Beer Flood
Q2783102.blurb: Eight people die in the London Beer Flood.

Q2784101.name: First aerial crossing of the South Atlantic
Q2784101.blurb: Portuguese naval aviators Gago Coutinho and Sacadura Cabral complete the first aerial crossing of the South Atlantic.

Q2784125.name: Singapore Airlines Flight 117
Q2784125.blurb: Singapore Airlines Flight 117 is hijacked by four Pakistani terrorists and diverted to Changi Airport.

Q2786767.name: Battle of Blaauwberg
Q2786767.blurb: The Dutch Cape Colony in southern Africa becomes the British Cape Colony as a result of the Battle of Blaauwberg.

Q2788282.name: Treaty of Alliance
Q2788282.blurb: American Revolutionary War: In Paris the Treaty of Alliance and the Treaty of Amity and Commerce are signed by the United States and France signaling official recognition of the new republic.

Q2789421.name: Battle of Prairie Grove
Q2789421.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Prairie Grove ended a Confederate attempt to regain control of northwestern Arkansas.

Q2791318.name: First Battle of Gaza
Q2791318.blurb: World War I: First Battle of Gaza: British troops are halted after 17,000 Turks block their advance.

Q2792009.name: Battle of Portopí
Q2792009.blurb: Battle of Portopí: The Aragonese army under the command of James I of Aragon disembarks at Santa Ponça, Mallorca, with the purpose of conquering the island.

Q2794675.name: L'Innovation Department Store fire
Q2794675.blurb: L'Innovation department store in Brussels, Belgium, burns down, resulting in 323 dead or missing and 150 injured, the most devastating fire in Belgian history.

Q2798534.name: Tulle murders
Q2798534.blurb: World War II: Ninety-nine civilians are hanged from lampposts and balconies by German troops in Tulle, France, in reprisal for maquisards attacks.

Q2799746.name: Battle of Hausbergen
Q2799746.blurb: Battle of Hausbergen between bourgeois militias and the army of the bishop of Strasbourg.

Q2801192.name: June 2011 Christchurch earthquake
Q2801192.blurb: A 6.0 Mw earthquake (aftermath pictured) caused up to NZ$6 billion of additional damage to Christchurch, New Zealand, which was still recovering from an earthquake four months earlier.

Q2804685.name: Battle of Marks' Mills
Q2804685.blurb: American Civil War: In the Battle of Marks' Mills, a force of 8,000 Confederate soldiers attacks 1,800 Union soldiers and a large number of wagon teamsters, killing or wounding 1,500 Union combatants.

Q2805651.name: Treaty of Cahuenga
Q2805651.blurb: The Treaty of Cahuenga ends the Mexican–American War in California.

Q2813755.name: Koriša bombing
Q2813755.blurb: Kosovo War: NATO bombs the village of Koriša, killing at least 87 people.

Q2815155.name: 23rd Canadian Parliament
Q2815155.blurb: The 23rd Canadian Parliament becomes the only one to be personally opened by the Queen of Canada.

Q2815407.name: Siege of Fredriksten
Q2815407.blurb: Great Northern War: King Charles XII of Sweden dies during a siege of the fortress of Fredriksten in Norway.

Q2817295.name: Byzantine conquest of Bulgaria
Q2817295.blurb: Byzantine general Eustathios Daphnomeles blinds and captures Ibatzes of Bulgaria by a ruse, thereby ending Bulgarian resistance against Emperor Basil II's conquest of Bulgaria.

Q2822708.name: 2005 Iranian Air Force C-130 crash
Q2822708.blurb: An Iranian Air Force C-130 military transport aircraft crashes into a ten-floor apartment building in a residential area of Tehran, killing all 94 on board and 12 more on the ground.

Q2822710.name: 2003 Iran Ilyushin Il-76 crash
Q2822710.blurb: An Ilyushin Il-76 military aircraft crashes near Kerman, Iran, killing 275.

Q2822712.name: Chappaquiddick incident
Q2822712.blurb: Chappaquiddick incident: U.S. Senator Ted Kennedy crashes his car into a tidal pond at Chappaquiddick Island, Massachusetts, killing his passenger Mary Jo Kopechne.

Q2822721.name: 1994 Black Hawk shootdown incident
Q2822721.blurb: In a friendly fire incident during Operation Provide Comfort in northern Iraq, two U.S. Air Force aircraft mistakenly shoot-down two U.S. Army helicopters, killing 26 people.

Q2822723.name: 1973 Paris Air Show crash
Q2822723.blurb: At the Paris Air Show, a Tupolev Tu-144 broke up in mid-air, killing all six members of its crew and eight bystanders on the ground.

Q2822729.name: Hatfield rail crash
Q2822729.blurb: The Hatfield rail crash leads to the collapse of Railtrack.

Q2822730.name: Ufton Nervet rail crash
Q2822730.blurb: An express train collides with a stationary car near the village of Ufton Nervet, England, killing seven and injuring 120.

Q2822795.name: Schengen Agreement
Q2822795.blurb: Five member nations of the European Economic Community sign the Schengen Agreement establishing a free travel zone with no border controls.

Q2823553.name: Charter of 1815
aliases: Additional Act to the Constitutions of the Empire
Q2823553.blurb: Napoleon promulgates a revised Constitution after it passes a plebiscite.

Q2823577.name: Act of the Re-Establishment of the State of Lithuania
Q2823577.blurb: Lithuania declares independence from the Soviet Union.

Q2824547.name: presidency of Jimmy Carter
Q2824547.blurb: U.S. president Jimmy Carter gives his "malaise speech".

Q2824550.name: presidency of Bill Clinton
Q2824550.blurb: The United States, under the Clinton administration, returns Haiti's first democratically elected president, Jean-Bertrand Aristide, to the island.

Q2824580.name: presidency of George Washington
Q2824580.blurb: George Washington (pictured) took the oath of office as the first president of the United States at Federal Hall in New York City.

Q2825895.name: Susurluk scandal
Q2825895.blurb: Abdullah Çatlı, a leader of the ultra-nationalist Grey Wolves, was killed in a car crash near Susurluk, Turkey, sparking a scandal that exposed the depth of the state's complicity in organized crime.

Q2825948.name: Charonne Métro Station massacre
Q2825948.blurb: Nine protestors are killed at Charonne station, Paris, by French police under the command of ex-Vichy official and Parisian Prefect of Police Maurice Papon.

Q2826012.name: Grenelle camp affair
Q2826012.blurb: Grenelle camp affair, a failed uprising by supporters of Gracchus Babeuf against the French Directory

Q2835454.name: Operation Samen-ol-A'emeh
Q2835454.blurb: Iran–Iraq War: Iran broke the Iraqi siege of Abadan by Operation Samen-ol-A'emeh.

Q2842206.name: Eastern Air Lines Flight 66
Q2842206.blurb: Eastern Air Lines Flight 66 encounters severe wind shear and crashes on final approach to New York's JFK Airport killing 113 of the 124 passengers on board, making it the deadliest U.S. plane crash at the time. This accident led to decades of research into downburst and microburst phenomena and their effects on aircraft.

Q2842407.name: Camp Chapman attack
Q2842407.blurb: A suicide bomber kills nine people at Forward Operating Base Chapman, a key facility of the Central Intelligence Agency in Afghanistan.

Q2843914.name: The Amos 'n Andy Show
Q2843914.blurb: The highly influential American radio comedy show Amos 'n' Andy made its debut.

Q2853075.name: TAP Portugal Flight 425
Q2853075.blurb: TAP Air Portugal Flight 425 crashes in the Madeira Islands, killing 131.

Q2854228.name: occupation of Istanbul
Q2854228.blurb: World War I: Allied troops occupy Constantinople, the capital of the Ottoman Empire.

Q2855373.name: Battle of Petroe
Q2855373.blurb: An army under Isaac I Komnenos defeat forces loyal to rival emperor Michael VI Bringas in the battle of Hades.

Q2862267.name: Korean Armistice Agreement
aliases: 국제련합군 총사령관을 일방으로 하고 조선인민군 최고사령관 및 중국인민지원군 사령원을 다른 일방으로 하는 한국 군사 정전에 관한 협정
Q2862267.blurb: An armistice was signed  to end hostilities in the Korean War, officially making the division of Korea indefinite by creating a 4 km wide (2.5 mi) demilitarized zone across the Korean Peninsula.

Q2862948.name: Army of the Danube
Q2862948.blurb: War of the Second Coalition: In their second battle in seven days, the French Army of the Danube and Habsburg forces battled for control of the Hegau region.

Q2865741.name: Articles of Capitulation of Quebec
Q2865741.blurb: French and Indian War: The Articles of Capitulation of Quebec are signed.

Q2865994.name: Battle of Port Gibson
Q2865994.blurb: American Civil War: During the Vicksburg campaign, Union forces under Ulysses S. Grant win the Battle of Port Gibson and establish a firm presence on the east side of the Mississippi River.

Q2866961.name: Letelier assassination
Q2866961.blurb: Orlando Letelier is assassinated in Washington, D.C., at the order of Augusto Pinochet.

Q2866970.name: assassination of John the Fearless
Q2866970.blurb: John the Fearless, Duke of Burgundy is assassinated by adherents of the Dauphin, the future Charles VII of France.

Q2866972.name: assassination of James A. Garfield
Q2866972.blurb: Charles J. Guiteau shoots and fatally wounds U.S. President James A. Garfield (who will die of complications from his wounds on September 19).

Q2866985.name: assassination of William McKinley
Q2866985.blurb: U.S. president William McKinley was fatally shot by anarchist Leon Czolgosz at the Pan-American Exposition in Buffalo, New York, and died eight days later.

Q2867093.name: First National Assembly at Epidaurus
Q2867093.blurb: The Greek Constitution of 1822 is adopted by the First National Assembly at Epidaurus.

Q2869905.name: 1984 Rajneeshee bioterror attack
Q2869905.blurb: Followers of Bhagwan Shree Rajneesh (pictured) began deliberately infecting people in The Dalles, Oregon, with Salmonella in the first and largest bioterrorist attack in United States history.

Q2869956.name: 1954 United States Capitol shooting
Q2869956.blurb: Armed Puerto Rican nationalists attack the United States Capitol building, injuring five Representatives.

Q2869958.name: Church Street bombing
Q2869958.blurb: Church Street bombing: A car bomb planted by UMkhonto we Sizwe explodes on Church Street in South Africa's capital, Pretoria, killing 19 people and injuring 217 others.

Q2869966.name: Russell Street bombing
Q2869966.blurb: A car bomb explodes outside Russell Street Police HQ in Melbourne, Australia, killing one police officer and injuring 21 people.

Q2869975.name: Ghriba synagogue bombing
Q2869975.blurb: The Ghriba synagogue bombing by al-Qaeda kills 21 in Tunisia.

Q2869976.name: Orly Airport attack
Q2869976.blurb: An attack at Orly Airport in Paris is launched by Armenian militant organisation ASALA, leaving eight people dead and 55 injured.

Q2869983.name: Khobar Towers bombing
Q2869983.blurb: The Khobar Towers bombing in Saudi Arabia kills 19 U.S. servicemen.

Q2869988.name: La Mon restaurant bombing
Q2869988.blurb: The Troubles: The Provisional Irish Republican Army carried out a bombing of a restaurant near Belfast, Northern Ireland, killing twelve people and injuring thirty others.

Q2869996.name: assassination of Juvénal Habyarimana and Cyprien Ntaryamira
aliases: assassination of Juvenal Habyarimana and Cyprien Ntaryamira
Q2869996.blurb: The aircraft carrying Rwandan president Juvénal Habyarimana and Burundian president Cyprien Ntaryamira was shot down in Kigali; the event became the catalyst for the Rwandan genocide.

Q2869998.name: Sbarro restaurant suicide bombing
Q2869998.blurb: Second Intifada: A suicide bomber attacked a pizza restaurant in Jerusalem, killing 15 people and wounding 130 others.

Q2870011.name: Riyadh compound bombings
Q2870011.blurb: The Riyadh compound bombings in Saudi Arabia, carried out by al-Qaeda, kill 39 people.

Q2870012.name: Warrington bombings
Q2870012.blurb: The Troubles: A Provisional IRA bomb kills two children in Warrington, England. It leads to mass protests in both Britain and Ireland.

Q2870013.name: Maxim restaurant suicide bombing
Q2870013.blurb: The Maxim restaurant suicide bombing in Israel kills twenty-one Israelis, both Jews and Arabs.

Q2870015.name: Dublin and Monaghan bombings
Q2870015.blurb: The Troubles: Thirty-three civilians are killed and 300 injured when the Ulster Volunteer Force (UVF) detonates four car bombs in Dublin and Monaghan, Ireland.

Q2870018.name: 11 April 2007 Algiers bombings
aliases: Terrorist attacks in Algiers, Algeria kill 23 people and wound 162
Q2870018.blurb: Algiers bombings: Two bombings in Algiers kill 33 people and wound a further 222 others.

Q2870026.name: 2006 Dahab bombings
Q2870026.blurb: Bombings in the Egyptian resort city of Dahab kill 23 people and injure about 80.

Q2870041.name: 21 July 2005 London bombings
Q2870041.blurb: Four attempted bomb attacks by Islamist extremists disrupt part of London's public transport system.

Q2877472.name: 1531 Lisbon earthquake
Q2877472.blurb: The 6.4–7.1 Mw Lisbon earthquake kills about thirty thousand people.

Q2881842.name: second voyage of James Cook
Q2881842.blurb: Captain James Cook leads the first expedition to sail south of the Antarctic Circle.

Q2883469.name: 2004 Haitian coup d'état
Q2883469.blurb: Haitian president Jean-Bertrand Aristide was overthrown following popular rebel uprising.

Q2883956.name: Samu Incident
Q2883956.blurb: In response to Fatah raids against Israelis near the West Bank border, Israel launches an attack on the village of As-Samu.

Q2885072.name: Cambodian genocide
aliases: Genocide & Crimes against humanity of the Khmer Rouge
International support for the Khmer Rouge
Q2885072.blurb: The Cambodian Civil War ends and the Cambodian Genocide begins. The Khmer Rouge captures the capital Phnom Penh and Cambodian government forces surrender.

Q2885195.name: Battle of Toulouse
Q2885195.blurb: Allied forces under the Duke of Wellington attack Toulouse held by Marshall Soult, driving out the French after fierce fighting.

Q2885880.name: 1990 Luzon earthquake
Q2885880.blurb: The Luzon earthquake strikes the Philippines with an intensity of 7.7, affecting Benguet, Pangasinan, Nueva Ecija, La Union, Aurora, Bataan, Zambales and Tarlac.

Q2887811.name: Battle of Adré
Q2887811.blurb: The Chadian Civil War begins when rebel groups, allegedly backed by neighbouring Sudan, launch an attack in Adré.

Q2887822.name: Battle of Alfarrobeira
Q2887822.blurb: The Battle of Alfarrobeira is fought, establishing the House of Braganza as a principal royal family of Portugal.

Q2887837.name: Battle of Amba Sel
Q2887837.blurb: Abyssinian–Adal war: The Adal Sultanate seizes southern Ethiopia.

Q2887840.name: Battle of Amba Aradam
Q2887840.blurb: Second Italo-Ethiopian War: The Battle of Amba Aradam began, ending nine days later in a decisive tactical victory for Italy and the neutralisation of almost the entire Ethiopian army as a fighting force.

Q2887847.name: Battle of Ampfing
Q2887847.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: Austrian forces, led by Archduke John of Austria, defeated two divisions of the French First Republic, led by Paul Grenier, at the Battle of Ampfing.

Q2887851.name: Battle of Ameixial
Q2887851.blurb: Portuguese Restoration War: Portuguese victory at the Battle of Ameixial ensures Portugal's independence from Spain.

Q2887868.name: Battle of Adrianople
Q2887868.blurb: First Balkan War: After a five-month siege, Bulgarian and Serbian forces captured the Ottoman city of Adrianople.

Q2887887.name: Battle of Arkinholm
Q2887887.blurb: Scottish Royal forces loyal to King James II defeat a rebel army of the Black Douglases in the battle of Arkinholm.

Q2887891.name: Battle of Arracourt
Q2887891.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Arracourt begins.

Q2887897.name: Battle of Arica
Q2887897.blurb: War of the Pacific: The Battle of Arica, the assault and capture of Morro de Arica (Arica Cape), ends the Campaña del Desierto (Desert Campaign).

Q2887900.name: Battle of Aspindza
Q2887900.blurb: The Georgian king, Erekle II, abandoned by his Russian ally Count Totleben, wins a victory over Ottoman forces at Aspindza.

Q2887902.name: Battle of Asseiceira
Q2887902.blurb: The Battle of Asseiceira is fought; it was the final and decisive engagement of the Liberal Wars in Portugal.

Q2887916.name: Battle of Aughrim
Q2887916.blurb: Battle of Aughrim (Julian calendar): The decisive victory of William III of England's forces in Ireland.

Q2887924.name: Battle of Azaz
Q2887924.blurb: The Battle of Azaz ends with a humiliating retreat of the Byzantine emperor, Romanos III Argyros, against the Mirdasid rulers of Aleppo. The retreat degenerates into a rout, in which Romanos himself barely escapes capture.

Q2887933.name: Battle of Elands River
Q2887933.blurb: Second Boer War: Boers capture a squadron of the 17th Lancers at the Battle of Elands River.

Q2887939.name: Battle of el-Hri
Q2887939.blurb: Zaian War: Berber tribesmen inflict the heaviest defeat of French forces in Morocco at the Battle of El Herri.

Q2887945.name: Battle of Embabo
Q2887945.blurb: The Shewan army defeated Gojjame forces at the Battle of Embabo, an event that contributed to the supremacy of Shewa within the Ethiopian Empire.

Q2887977.name: Battle of Hormozdgan
Q2887977.blurb: The Battle of Hormozdgan is fought. Ardashir I defeats and kills Artabanus V, effectively ending the Parthian Empire.

Q2887988.name: Battle of Nsamankow
Q2887988.blurb: The Ashantis defeat British forces in the Gold Coast during the First Anglo-Ashanti War.

Q2887993.name: Battle of Inverkeithing
Q2887993.blurb: Wars of the Three Kingdoms: After crossing the Firth of Forth, English Commonwealth forces defeated a Scottish army at the Battle of Inverkeithing, opening the rest of the country to occupation.

Q2888010.name: Battle of Ishibashiyama
Q2888010.blurb: Genpei War: In the Battle of Ishibashiyama in Japan, the new military commander of the Minamoto clan, Minamoto no Yoritomo, is routed by Ōba Kagechika of the Taira clan.

Q2888024.name: Battle of Orbetello
Q2888024.blurb: Franco-Spanish War: French and Spanish fleets fought the inconclusive Battle of Orbetello, with sailing vessels of both sides having to be towed into action by galleys due to light winds.

Q2888038.name: Battle of Otumba
Q2888038.blurb: Spanish conquistadores defeat a larger Aztec army at the Battle of Otumba.

Q2888096.name: Battle of Ballynahinch
Q2888096.blurb: Irish Rebellion of 1798: Battle of Ballynahinch.

Q2888101.name: Battle of Ballon
Q2888101.blurb: The first duke of Brittany, Nominoe, defeats the Frankish king Charles the Bald at the Battle of Ballon near Redon.

Q2888113.name: Battle of Batoche
Q2888113.blurb: North-West Rebellion: The four-day Battle of Batoche, pitting rebel Métis against the Canadian government, comes to an end with a decisive rebel defeat.

Q2888116.name: Battle of Bear Valley
Q2888116.blurb: Battle of Bear Valley: The last battle of the American Indian Wars.

Q2888138.name: Battle of Besançon
Q2888138.blurb: French Wars of Religion: Catholic forces defeated an armed group of Huguenots attempting to capture Besançon, from which they had previously been expelled.

Q2888152.name: Battle of Blood River Poort
Q2888152.blurb: Second Boer War: A Boer column defeats a British force at the Battle of Blood River Poort.

Q2888162.name: Battle of Bizani
Q2888162.blurb: First Balkan War: The Greek army engages the Turks at Bizani, resulting in victory two days later.

Q2888175.name: Battle of Borghetto
Q2888175.blurb: War of the First Coalition: In the Battle of Borghetto, Napoleon Bonaparte manages to cross the Mincio River against the Austrian army. This crossing forces the Austrians to abandon Lombardy and retreat to the Tyrol, leaving the fortress of Mantua as the sole remaining Austrian stronghold in Northern Italy.

Q2888227.name: Battle of Ban Me Thuot
Q2888227.blurb: Ho Chi Minh Campaign: North Vietnam began its final push for victory over South Vietnam with an attack on Ban Me Thuot.

Q2888269.name: Battle of Castlebar
Q2888269.blurb: Wolfe Tone's United Irish and French forces clash with the British Army in the Battle of Castlebar, part of the Irish Rebellion of 1798, resulting in the creation of the French puppet Republic of Connacht.

Q2888281.name: Battle of Cerro Gordo
Q2888281.blurb: American victory at the battle of Cerro Gordo opens the way for invasion of Mexico.

Q2888296.name: Conquest of Ceuta
Q2888296.blurb: Henry the Navigator leads Portuguese forces to victory over the Marinids at the Conquest of Ceuta.

Q2888305.name: Battle of Shubra Khit
Q2888305.blurb: The French Armée d'Orient under Napoleon Bonaparte defeats a Mamluk army under Murad Bey in battle of Shubra Khit.

Q2888324.name: Battle of Coatit
Q2888324.blurb: First Italo-Ethiopian War: The war's opening battle, the Battle of Coatit, occurs; it is an Italian victory.

Q2888366.name: Crossbarry Ambush
Q2888366.blurb: Irish War of Independence: One of the biggest engagements of the war takes place at Crossbarry, County Cork. About 100 Irish Republican Army (IRA) volunteers escape an attempt by over 1,300 British forces to encircle them.

Q2888378.name: Battle of Taegu
Q2888378.blurb: Korean War: United Nations forces repelled an attempt by North Korea to capture the city of Taegu.

Q2888407.name: Battle of Derna
Q2888407.blurb: Forces sent by Yusuf Karamanli of Tripoli to retake Derna from the Americans attack the city.

Q2888426.name: Battle of Dojran
Q2888426.blurb: Second Balkan War: The Greeks defeat the Bulgarians in the Battle of Doiran.

Q2888432.name: Battle of Dormans
Q2888432.blurb: Roman Catholic forces under Henry I, Duke of Guise, defeat the Protestants, capturing Philippe de Mornay among others.

Q2888457.name: Dull Knife Fight
Q2888457.blurb: American Indian Wars: In retaliation for the American defeat at the Battle of the Little Bighorn, United States Army troops sack the sleeping village of Cheyenne Chief Dull Knife at the headwaters of the Powder River.

Q2888469.name: Siege of Detroit
Q2888469.blurb: War of 1812: American General William Hull surrenders Fort Detroit without a fight to the British Army.

Q2888486.name: Battle of Eutaw Springs
Q2888486.blurb: American Revolutionary War: The Battle of Eutaw Springs in South Carolina, the war's last significant battle in the Southern theater, ends in a narrow British tactical victory.

Q2888502.name: Battle of Flamborough Head
Q2888502.blurb: American Revolutionary War: John Paul Jones, naval commander of the United States, on board the USS Bonhomme Richard, wins the Battle of Flamborough Head.

Q2888504.name: Battle of Fishguard
Q2888504.blurb: A force of 1,400 French soldiers invade Britain at Fishguard in support of the Society of United Irishmen. They were defeated by 500 British reservists.

Q2888523.name: Battle of Fort Dearborn
Q2888523.blurb: War of 1812: Potawatomi warriors ambushed a United States Army convoy after it had evacuated Fort Dearborn (site pictured), in present-day Chicago, and razed the fort.

Q2888531.name: Fort Mims massacre
Q2888531.blurb: Creek War: Fort Mims massacre: Creek "Red Sticks" kill over 500 settlers (including over 250 armed militia) in Fort Mims, north of Mobile, Alabama.

Q2888779.name: Battle of Halmstad
Q2888779.blurb: Scanian War: Swedish forces defeated Danish troops at the Battle of Halmstad.

Q2888820.name: Battle of Huamachuco
Q2888820.blurb: War of the Pacific: Chileans led by Alejandro Gorostiaga defeat Andrés Avelino Cáceres's Peruvian army at the Battle of Huamachuco, hastening the end of the war.

Q2888837.name: Battle of Greece
aliases: German invasion of Greece and Yugoslavia
Q2888837.blurb: World War II: German forces invaded Greece and Yugoslavia.

Q2888864.name: Battle of Jengland
Q2888864.blurb: Battle of Jengland: Erispoe defeats Charles the Bald near the Breton town of Jengland, halting the expansion of West Francia.

Q2888925.name: Battle of Quifangondo
Q2888925.blurb: In Angola, the MPLA decisively defeated the FNLA in the Battle of Quifangondo, while Portugal simultaneously withdrew all its colonial and military personnel from Luanda.

Q2888946.name: Battle of Killiecrankie
Q2888946.blurb: Glorious Revolution: The Battle of Killiecrankie is a victory for the Jacobites.

Q2889112.name: Battle of Las Piedras
Q2889112.blurb: Battle of Las Piedras: The first great military triumph of the revolution of the Río de la Plata in Uruguay led by José Artigas.

Q2889133.name: Battle of Leliefontein
Q2889133.blurb: Second Boer War: The Battle of Leliefontein takes place, during which the Royal Canadian Dragoons win three Victoria Crosses.

Q2889153.name: Battle of Lonato
Q2889153.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: Napoleon leads the French Army of Italy to victory in the Battle of Lonato.

Q2889154.name: Battle of Loncomilla
Q2889154.blurb: Conservative Santiago-based government troops defeat rebels at the Battle of Loncomilla, signaling the end of the 1851 Chilean Revolution.

Q2889157.name: Battle of Long Sault
Q2889157.blurb: The Battle of Long Sault concludes after five days in which French colonial militia, with their Huron and Algonquin allies, are defeated by the Iroquois Confederacy.

Q2889191.name: Battle of Magdhaba
Q2889191.blurb: World War I: Battle of Magdhaba: Allied forces defeat Turkish forces in the Sinai Peninsula.

Q2889222.name: Battle of Malta
Q2889222.blurb: Roger of Lauria, commanding the Aragonese fleet, defeats an Angevin fleet sent to put down a rebellion on Malta.

Q2889252.name: Battle of Mărășești
Q2889252.blurb: World War I: Battle of Mărășești between the Romanian and German armies begins.

Q2889268.name: Battle of Marmiton River
Q2889268.blurb: American Civil War: During Price's Missouri Expedition, Union troops defeated Sterling Price's Confederate army in three successive battles: Marais des Cygnes, Mine Creek, and Marmiton River.

Q2889272.name: Battle of Marseille
Q2889272.blurb: World War II: Marseille is liberated by the Allied forces.

Q2889283.name: First Battle of Maryang-san
Q2889283.blurb: Korean War: The First Battle of Maryang San pits Commonwealth troops against communist Chinese troops.

Q2889293.name: Treaty of Lisbon
Q2889293.blurb: The Treaty of Lisbon defines the boundaries between Spain and Portugal and abolishes the Couto Misto microstate.

Q2889310.name: Battle of Melle
Q2889310.blurb: French victory in the Battle of Melle allows them to capture Ghent in the days after.

Q2889338.name: Battle of Mirbat
Q2889338.blurb: Dhofar Rebellion: British SAS units help the Omani government against Popular Front for the Liberation of Oman rebels in the Battle of Mirbat.

Q2889349.name: Battle of Mizushima
Q2889349.blurb: Genpei War: The Battle of Mizushima takes place off the Japanese coast, where Minamoto no Yoshinaka's invasion force is intercepted and defeated by the Taira clan.

Q2889383.name: Battle of Montes Claros
Q2889383.blurb: Battle of Montes Claros: Portugal definitively secures independence from Spain in the last battle of the Portuguese Restoration War.

Q2889392.name: Battle of Montijo
Q2889392.blurb: Portuguese Restoration War: Portuguese and Spanish forces both claim victory in the Battle of Montijo.

Q2889417.name: Battle of Morotai
Q2889417.blurb: World War II: American and Australian forces landed on the Japanese-occupied island of Morotai.

Q2889477.name: Raid of Nassau
Q2889477.blurb: American Revolutionary War: The first amphibious landing of the United States Marine Corps begins the Battle of Nassau.

Q2889481.name: Battle of N'Djamena
Q2889481.blurb: The United Front for Democratic Change's attack on the Chadian capital of N'Djamena is repelled by the Chadian army

Q2889540.name: Battle of Noáin
Q2889540.blurb: Spanish forces defeat a combined French and Navarrese army at the Battle of Noáin during the Spanish conquest of Iberian Navarre.

Q2889551.name: Battle of Nui Bop
Q2889551.blurb: Sino-French War: Beginning of the Battle of Núi Bop.

Q2889584.name: Action of 10 July 1651
Q2889584.blurb: The Venetian fleet under  Alvise Mocenigo engages with an Ottoman fleet under Hosambegzade Ali Pasha south of Naxos, defeating it after three days.

Q2889607.name: Battle of Peyrestortes
Q2889607.blurb: War of the Pyrenees: France defeats a Spanish force at the Battle of Peyrestortes.

Q2889635.name: Final operations in Slovenia
Q2889635.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Poljana, the final skirmish in Europe, is fought near Prevalje, Slovenia.

Q2889660.name: Battle of Pontvallain
Q2889660.blurb: Hundred Years' War: In two separate engagements in the Battle of Pontvallain (depicted), French forces wiped out an English army which had split up because of a dispute between the commanders.

Q2889670.name: Battle of Port-Républicain
Q2889670.blurb: Haitian Revolution: Battle of Port-Républicain: British troops capture the capital of Saint-Domingue.

Q2889681.name: Battle of Sapienza
Q2889681.blurb: War of the Straits: The Genoese fleet under Paganino Doria defeats and captures the entire Venetian fleet under Niccolò Pisani at the Battle of Sapienza.

Q2889742.name: Battle of Radzymin
Q2889742.blurb: The Battle of Radzymin, one of the bloodiest and most intense battles of the Polish–Soviet War, concluded with a Polish victory.

Q2889750.name: Battle of Redinha
Q2889750.blurb: Peninsular War: A day after a successful rearguard action, French Marshal Michel Ney once again successfully delays the pursuing Anglo-Portuguese force at the Battle of Redinha.

Q2889754.name: Battle of Red Bank
Q2889754.blurb: American Revolutionary War: American defenders of Fort Mercer on the Delaware River repulse repeated Hessian attacks in the Battle of Red Bank.

Q2889791.name: Battle of Ridgeway
Q2889791.blurb: The Fenians defeat Canadian forces at Ridgeway and Fort Erie, but the raids end soon after.

Q2889853.name: Battle of Saint Cast
Q2889853.blurb: Battle of Saint Cast: France repels British invasion during the Seven Years' War.

Q2889912.name: Battle of San Juan de Ulúa
aliases: Battle of San Juan de Ulua
Q2889912.blurb: Spanish naval forces defeat an English fleet, under the command of John Hawkins, at the Battle of San Juan de Ulúa near Veracruz.

Q2889928.name: Battle of San Marcial
Q2889928.blurb: Peninsular War: Spanish troops repel a French attack in the Battle of San Marcial.

Q2889946.name: Battle of Sarantaporo
Q2889946.blurb: First Balkan War: The day after the Battle of Sarantaporo, Greek troops liberate the city of Kozani.

Q2890025.name: Battle of Solway Moss
Q2890025.blurb: Having been defeated in the Battle of Solway Moss in the previous year, the Scots conclude the peace Treaty of Greenwich with the Kingdom of England. In it, they also agree to a marriage between the infant Queen Mary and Prince Edward, son of Henry VIII.

Q2890044.name: Battle of Sprimont
Q2890044.blurb: More than a year after the Battle of Sprimont, the Austrian Netherlands (present-day Belgium) are officially annexed by Revolutionary France.

Q2890055.name: Battle of St. George's Caye
Q2890055.blurb: The week long battle of St. George's Caye begins between Spain and Britain off the coast of Belize.

Q2890263.name: East Sea Campaign
Q2890263.blurb: Vietnam War: The North Vietnamese Army completes its capture of all parts of South Vietnam-held Trường Sa Islands.

Q2890273.name: Battle of Tweebosch
Q2890273.blurb: Second Boer War: Boers, led by Koos de la Rey, defeat the British at the Battle of Tweebosch.

Q2890303.name: Battle of Vegkop
Q2890303.blurb: Great Trek: Afrikaner voortrekkers repulse a Matabele attack, but lose their livestock.

Q2890338.name: Battle of Villalar
Q2890338.blurb: Battle of Villalar: King Charles I of Spain defeats the Comuneros.

Q2890346.name: Battle of Vinegar Hill
Q2890346.blurb: Irish convicts formerly involved at the Battle of Vinegar Hill during the Irish Rebellion of 1798 began an uprising against British colonial authorities in New South Wales, Australia.

Q2890351.name: Battle of Vinjesvingen
Q2890351.blurb: World War II: Norwegian campaign: Norwegian squads in Hegra Fortress and Vinjesvingen capitulate to German forces after all other Norwegian forces in southern Norway had laid down their arms.

Q2890373.name: Battle of Wanat
Q2890373.blurb: Battle of Wanat begins when Taliban and al-Qaeda guerrillas attack US Army and Afghan National Army troops in Afghanistan. The U.S. deaths were, at that time, the most in a single battle since the beginning of operations in 2001.

Q2890378.name: Battle of Waynesboro, Georgia
Q2890378.blurb: American Civil War: Sherman's March to the Sea: Union cavalry forces defeat Confederate cavalry in the Battle of Waynesboro, Georgia, opening the way for General William T. Sherman's army to approach the coast.

Q2890384.name: Battle of White Bird Canyon
Q2890384.blurb: American Indian Wars: Battle of White Bird Canyon: The Nez Perce defeat the U.S. Cavalry at White Bird Canyon in the Idaho Territory.

Q2890385.name: Battle of White Marsh
Q2890385.blurb: American Revolutionary War: British commander-in-chief Sir William Howe withdrew his troops from the Battle of White Marsh to Philadelphia.

Q2890439.name: Battle of Yungay
Q2890439.blurb: In the Battle of Yungay, Chile defeats an alliance between Peru and Bolivia.

Q2890458.name: Battle of Zutphen
Q2890458.blurb: Eighty Years' War: Spanish forces defeated an Anglo-Dutch army at the Battle of Zutphen.

Q2890473.name: Battle of the Overpass
Q2890473.blurb: Walter Reuther and members of the United Auto Workers (UAW) clash with Ford Motor Company security guards at the River Rouge Complex in Dearborn, Michigan, during the Battle of the Overpass.

Q2890512.name: Battle of Croix-des-Bouquets
Q2890512.blurb: Battle of Croix-des-Bouquets: Black slave insurgents gain a victory in the first major battle of the Haitian Revolution.

Q2890526.name: Invasion of Dominica
Q2890526.blurb: American Revolutionary War: France invades Dominica in the British West Indies, before Britain is even aware of France's involvement in the war.

Q2890596.name: Battle of Vuelta de Obligado
Q2890596.blurb: Anglo-French blockade of the Río de la Plata: Battle of Vuelta de Obligado.

Q2890600.name: Battle of Hudson's Bay
Q2890600.blurb: War of the Grand Alliance : A French warship commanded by Captain Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville defeated an English squadron at the Battle of Hudson's Bay.

Q2890604.name: Battle of Walcheren Causeway
Q2890604.blurb: World War II: Units of the British Army land at Walcheren.

Q2890708.name: Battle of Dagu Forts
Q2890708.blurb: Boxer Rebellion: Western Allied and Japanese forces capture the Taku Forts in Tianjin, China.

Q2890728.name: Battle of 4 May
Q2890728.blurb: Brazilian War of Independence: A Brazilian squadron led by Lord Cochrane engages a Portuguese squadron under João de Campos off Salvador, Bahia.

Q2890741.name: Battle of the Bogside
Q2890741.blurb: The Troubles: Riots erupted in the neighbourhood of Bogside in Derry, and spread across much of Northern Ireland.

Q2890742.name: Battle of Cap-Français
Q2890742.blurb: Haitian Revolution: The Battle of Cap-Français ends with French Republican troops and black slave insurgents capturing the city.

Q2890743.name: Battle of Boulou
Q2890743.blurb: War of the Pyrenees: France regained nearly all the land it lost to Spain the previous year with its victory in the Second Battle of Boulou.

Q2890781.name: Battle of Hamel
Q2890781.blurb: World War I: The Battle of Hamel, a successful attack by the Australian Corps against German positions near the town of Le Hamel on the Western Front.

Q2890815.name: Battle of the Puig
Q2890815.blurb: Spanish Reconquista: The Battle of the Puig between the Moorish forces of Taifa of Valencia against the Crown of Aragon culminates in an Aragonese victory.

Q2890829.name: Battle of Devil's Hole
Q2890829.blurb: Seneca warriors defeat British forces at the Battle of Devil's Hole during Pontiac's War.

Q2890901.name: Battle of Nam River
Q2890901.blurb: Korean War: A North Korean attack was repelled by Allied forces at the Battle of Nam River.

Q2890905.name: Battle of the Samichon River
Q2890905.blurb: The Battle of the Samichon River, the last engagement of the Korean War, ended a few hours before the signing of the Korean Armistice Agreement.

Q2890908.name: Battle of Lake Borgne
Q2890908.blurb: War of 1812: The Royal Navy seizes control of Lake Borgne, Louisiana.

Q2891775.name: Japan Air Lines flight 1628 incident
Q2891775.blurb: The flight crew of Japan Airlines Flight 1628 are involved in a UFO sighting incident while flying over Alaska.

Q2892384.name: Scilly naval disaster of 1707
Q2892384.blurb: Four British naval vessels run aground on the Isles of Scilly because of faulty navigation. In response, the first Longitude Act is enacted in 1714.

Q2893373.name: Chilean takeover of the Strait of Magellan
aliases: Takeover of the Strait of Magellan
Q2893373.blurb: The first of a series of auctions of sheep farming land in southern Patagonia takes place impacting established settlers.

Q2893461.name: Reich Chancellery meeting of 12 December 1941
Q2893461.blurb: The Holocaust: At a Nazi Party meeting in the Reich Chancellery, Adolf Hitler declared the imminent destruction of the Jewish people.

Q2893596.name: October 2000 events
Q2893596.blurb: Israeli–Palestinian conflict: Palestinians protest the killing of 12-year-old Muhammad al-Durrah by Israeli police in northern Israel, beginning the "October 2000 events".

Q2893606.name: 1992 Peruvian self-coup d'état
Q2893606.blurb: Alberto Fujimori, president of Peru, dissolves the Peruvian congress by military force.

Q2894099.name: 1997 Atlantic hurricane season
Q2894099.blurb: Hurricane Erika, the strongest and longest-lasting hurricane of the 1997 Atlantic hurricane season, dissipated after causing flooding and power outages throughout Puerto Rico.

Q2895260.name: Battle of Monte Grappa
Q2895260.blurb: World War I: beginning of the First Battle of Monte Grappa (in Italy known as the "First Battle of the Piave"). The Austro-Hungarian Armed Forces, despite help from the German Alpenkorps and numerical superiority, will fail their offensive against the Italian Army now led by its new chief of staff Armando Diaz.

Q2896309.name: Southern Airways Flight 932
Q2896309.blurb: Southern Airways Flight 932 crashes in the mountains near Huntington, West Virginia, killing 75, including almost all of the Marshall University football team.

Q2896313.name: 2002 Mombasa attacks
Q2896313.blurb: Suicide bombers blow up an Israeli-owned hotel in Mombasa, Kenya; their colleagues fail in their attempt to bring down Arkia Israel Airlines Flight 582 with surface-to-air missiles.

Q2896424.name: Battle of Yad Mordechai
Q2896424.blurb: Arab–Israeli War: Egypt captures the Israeli kibbutz of Yad Mordechai, but the five-day effort gives Israeli forces time to prepare enough to stop the Egyptian advance a week later.

Q2898431.name: Great Baltimore Fire
Q2898431.blurb: The Great Baltimore Fire begins in Baltimore, Maryland; it destroys over 1,500 buildings in 30 hours.

Q2903305.name: Assassination of Rehavam Ze'evi
Q2903305.blurb: Israeli tourism minister Rehavam Ze'evi is assassinated by Hamdi Quran, a member of the PFLP, thus becoming the highest-ranking Israeli to be killed by a Palestinian.

Q2905082.name: Safra massacre
Q2905082.blurb: During the Lebanese Civil War, 83 Tiger militants are killed during what will be known as the Safra massacre.

Q2907294.name: Haifa bus 37 suicide bombing
Q2907294.blurb: In Haifa, 17 Israeli civilians are killed in the Haifa bus 37 suicide bombing.

Q2907585.name: Pan Am Flight 73
Q2907585.blurb: Pan Am Flight 73 from Mumbai, India with 358 people on board is hijacked at Karachi International Airport.

Q2909136.name: 1966 Kansas City Chiefs season
Q2909136.blurb: The first Super Bowl is played in Los Angeles. The Green Bay Packers defeat the Kansas City Chiefs 35–10.

Q2909615.name: Bombing of Tan Son Nhut Air Base
Q2909615.blurb: Vietnam War: Operation Frequent Wind: The U.S. begins to evacuate U.S. citizens from Saigon before an expected North Vietnamese takeover. U.S. involvement in the war comes to an end. This happens after the Bombing of Tan Son Nhut Air Base.

Q2909812.name: 1997 Israeli helicopter disaster
Q2909812.blurb: En route to Lebanon, two Israeli Sikorsky CH-53 troop-transport helicopters collide in mid-air over northern Galilee, Israel, killing 73.

Q2910386.name: Bonus Army
Q2910386.blurb: Bonus Army: Around a thousand World War I veterans amass at the United States Capitol as the U.S. Senate considers a bill that would give them certain benefits.

Q2910683.name: United Airlines Flight 629
Q2910683.blurb: The bombing of United Air Lines Flight 629 occurs near Longmont, Colorado, killing all 39 passengers and five crew members aboard the Douglas DC-6B airliner.

Q2912379.name: Bombing of the Bezuidenhout
Q2912379.blurb: World War II: In poor visibility, the RAF mistakenly bombs the Bezuidenhout area of The Hague, Netherlands, killing 511 people.

Q2912473.name: January 2013 Pakistan bombings
Q2912473.blurb: More than 100 people are killed and 270 injured in several bomb blasts in the Quetta area of Pakistan.

Q2912780.name: 1073 papal election
Q2912780.blurb: Gregory VII was elected pope following the death of Alexander II.

Q2912880.name: shoe-banging incident
Q2912880.blurb: Soviet Premier Nikita Khrushchev pounds his shoe on a desk at the United Nations to protest a Philippine assertion.

Q2914382.name: Portella della Ginestra massacro
Q2914382.blurb: Portella della Ginestra massacre against May Day celebrations in Sicily by the bandit and separatist leader Salvatore Giuliano where 11 persons are killed and 33 wounded.

Q2914928.name: Australian gold rush
Q2914928.blurb: James McBrien made the first official discovery of gold in Australia at Fish River in New South Wales.

Q2914954.name: Battle of Kinburn
Q2914954.blurb: Russians under Alexander Suvorov defeat the Turks at Kinburn.

Q2915118.name: Mercaz HaRav massacre
Q2915118.blurb: A suicide bomber kills 68 people (including first responders) in Baghdad on the same day that a gunman kills eight students in Jerusalem.

Q2915203.name: Ethiopian–Adal War
Q2915203.blurb: Abyssinian–Adal war: The Adal Sultanate seizes southern Ethiopia.

Q2915250.name: Gentlemen's Agreement of 1907
Q2915250.blurb: Japan and the United States signed a gentleman's agreement whereby the former would not permit further emigration to the U.S., while the latter would not limit Japanese immigration.

Q2915803.name: Attack on the Saudi Embassy in Khartoum
Q2915803.blurb: Black September storms the Saudi embassy in Khartoum, Sudan, resulting in the assassination of three Western hostages.

Q2915943.name: October Incident
Q2915943.blurb: A secret society in the Imperial Japanese Army launches an abortive coup d'état attempt.

Q2916092.name: White Night riots
Q2916092.blurb: White Night riots in San Francisco following the manslaughter conviction of Dan White for the assassinations of George Moscone and Harvey Milk.

Q2916113.name: Bangladesh genocide
Q2916113.blurb: The Concert for Bangladesh, a pair of benefit concerts organised by George Harrison and Ravi Shankar for refugees of the Bangladesh genocide, took place at Madison Square Garden in New York.

Q2917062.name: 1977 Israeli legislative election
Q2917062.blurb: Likud party wins the 1977 Israeli legislative election, with Menachem Begin, its founder, as the sixth Prime Minister of Israel.

Q2917077.name: Battle of Buna–Gona
Q2917077.blurb: World War II: Australian and American forces defeat Japanese army and navy units in the bitterly fought Battle of Buna–Gona.

Q2917367.name: Salamaua–Lae campaign
Q2917367.blurb: World War II: In the Pacific Theater, the 503rd Parachute Infantry Regiment lands and occupies Lae Nadzab Airport, near Lae during the Salamaua–Lae campaign.

Q2917519.name: 1991 Racha earthquake
Q2917519.blurb: The 7.0 Mw Racha earthquake affects Georgia with a maximum MSK intensity of IX (Destructive), killing 270 people.

Q2918175.name: 2006 al-Askari mosque bombing
Q2918175.blurb: At approximately 6:44 a.m.  local Iraqi time, explosions occurred at the al-Askari Shrine in Samarra, Iraq. The attack on the shrine, one of the holiest sites in Shia Islam, caused the escalation of sectarian tensions in Iraq into a full-scale civil war.
