Q2918225.name: Bolivian Declaration of Independence
Q2918225.blurb: The Bolivian Declaration of Independence is proclaimed.

Q2918340.name: German occupation of Estonia during World War I
Q2918340.blurb: World War I: German forces capture Tallinn to virtually complete the occupation of Estonia.

Q2918374.name: funeral of Diana, Princess of Wales
Q2918374.blurb: The funeral of Diana, Princess of Wales takes place in London. Well over a million people line the streets and 21⁄2 billion watch around the world on television.

Q2918433.name: El Al Flight 426
Q2918433.blurb: The only successful hijacking of an El Al aircraft takes place when a Boeing 707 carrying ten crew and 38 passengers is taken over by three members of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine. The aircraft was en route from Rome, Italy to Lod, Israel.

Q2918913.name: Operation Mole Cricket 19
Q2918913.blurb: Lebanon War: The Israeli Air Force carried out Operation Mole Cricket 19, successfully suppressing Syrian air defenses in the Beqaa Valley, Lebanon.

Q2919552.name: Timurid invasions of Georgia
Q2919552.blurb: Timur of Samarkand captures and sacks the Georgian capital of Tbilisi, taking King Bagrat V of Georgia captive.

Q2919945.name: SEALAB
Q2919945.blurb: American aquanaut Berry L. Cannon dies of carbon dioxide poisoning while attempting to repair a leak in the SEALAB III underwater habitat. The SEALAB project was subsequently abandoned.

Q2920414.name: Battle of Basian
Q2920414.blurb: Georgian–Seljuk wars: At the Battle of Basian the Kingdom of Georgia defeats the Sultanate of Rum.

Q2923878.name: 1981 Brink's robbery
Q2923878.blurb: Two police officers and a Brink's armored car guard are killed during an armed robbery carried out by members of the Black Liberation Army and Weather Underground in Nanuet, New York.

Q2933988.name: California Jam
Q2933988.blurb: The first California Jam festival takes place at the Ontario Motor Speedway in Ontario, California. Co-headlined by Deep Purple and Emerson, Lake & Palmer. The festival set what were then records for the loudest amplification system ever installed, the highest paid attendance, and highest gross in history.

Q2935371.name: Cochinchina campaign
Q2935371.blurb: Cochinchina Campaign: The French Navy captures the Citadel of Saigon, a fortress manned by 1,000 Nguyễn dynasty soldiers, en route to conquering Saigon and other regions of southern Viet Nam.

Q2941587.name: Second Battle of Springfield
Q2941587.blurb: American Civil War: Second Battle of Springfield.

Q2946372.name: Mali War
Q2946372.blurb: The Mali War begins when Tuareg militias start fighting the Malian government for independence.

Q2963045.name: Chevauchée of the Black Prince 1356
Q2963045.blurb: Hundred Years' War: A large-scale mounted raid by Anglo-Gascon forces began under the command of Edward the Black Prince.

Q2963047.name: Crécy campaign
Q2963047.blurb: Hundred Years' War: The French town of Calais capitulated to English forces after an eleven-month siege, ending the Crécy campaign.

Q2975371.name: Shinpūren Rebellion
Q2975371.blurb: Shinpūren rebellion: Upset at the Westernisation of Meiji Japan and the abolition of the Tokugawa feudal hierarchy, the Keishintō, a group of extremist Shinto former samurai, launch a surprise attack against the Meiji government in Kumamoto Prefecture.

Q2976024.name: Georgian Airways Flight 834
Q2976024.blurb: Georgian Airways Flight 834 crashes at N'djili Airport in Kinshasa, killing 32.

Q2976183.name: New's Divine nightclub tragedy
Q2976183.blurb: Twelve people are killed, including nine clubgoers and three police officers, during a crowd crush in Mexico City.

Q2976715.name: Second Seminole War
Q2976715.blurb: Second Seminole War: American general Zachary Taylor leads 1,100 troops against the Seminoles at the Battle of Lake Okeechobee.

Q2978443.name: Northern Illinois University shooting
Q2978443.blurb: Northern Illinois University shooting: A gunman opens fire in a lecture hall of Northern Illinois University in DeKalb County, Illinois, resulting in six fatalities (including the gunman) and 21 injuries.

Q2978493.name: Treaty of Giyanti
Q2978493.blurb: Treaty of Giyanti signed by VOC, Pakubuwono III and Prince Mangkubumi. The treaty divides the Javanese kingdom of Mataram into two: Sunanate of Surakarta and Sultanate of Yogyakarta.

Q2978742.name: Clean Water Act
aliases: An Act to amend the Federal Water Pollution Control Act
Federal Water Pollution Control Act Amendments of 1972
Q2978742.blurb: The Cuyahoga River catches fire in Cleveland, Ohio, drawing national attention to water pollution, and spurring the passing of the Clean Water Act and the creation of the Environmental Protection Agency.

Q2980084.name: Treaty of Erzurum
Q2980084.blurb: Qajar Iran and the Ottoman Empire determine their international boundary in the second treaty of Erzurum.

Q2981049.name: Red Summer of 1919
Q2981049.blurb: Red Summer: Race riots erupted in Chicago after a racial incident occurred on a South Side beach, leading to 38 fatalities and 537 injuries.

Q2981297.name: Battle of Konya
Q2981297.blurb: Egyptian–Ottoman War: Egyptian forces decisively defeat Ottoman troops at the Battle of Konya.

Q2981856.name: Battle of Cocos
Q2981856.blurb: SMS Emden is sunk by HMAS Sydney in the Battle of Cocos.

Q2982599.name: 1993 Long Island Rail Road shooting
Q2982599.blurb: Long Island Rail Road shooting: Passenger Colin Ferguson murders six people and injures 19 others on the LIRR in Nassau County, New York.

Q2983513.name: 1973 Nantes Mid-Air Collision
Q2983513.blurb: An Iberia McDonnell Douglas DC-9 collides in mid-air with a Spantax Convair 990 Coronado over Nantes, France, killing all 68 people aboard the DC-9, including music manager Michael Jeffery.

Q2984282.name: French occupation of Malta
Q2984282.blurb: Following the successful French invasion of Malta, the Knights Hospitaller surrendered Malta to Napoleon, initiating two years of occupation.

Q2984671.name: Treaty of Almizra
Q2984671.blurb: The crown of Aragon and the crown of Castile agree in the Treaty of Almizra on the limits of their respective expansion into al-Andalus.

Q2984928.name: USS Constellation vs L'Insurgente
Q2984928.blurb: Quasi-War: USS Constellation captured the French frigate Insurgente in a single-ship action in the Caribbean Sea.

Q2984961.name: Action of 6 November 1794
Q2984961.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: Two British ships were intercepted by a French squadron, leading to the French seizure of HMS Alexander.

Q2985003.name: Battle of Rossignol
Q2985003.blurb: First World War: German forces captured Rossignol  in Belgium, taking more than 3,800 French prisoners.

Q2986185.name: 2009 G20 Pittsburgh summit
Q2986185.blurb: The G20 summit begins in Pittsburgh with 30 global leaders in attendance.

Q2988161.name: Southern theater of the American Revolutionary War
Q2988161.blurb: American Revolutionary War: The Battle of Eutaw Springs in South Carolina, the war's last significant battle in the Southern theater, ends in a narrow British tactical victory.

Q2988180.name: March Days
Q2988180.blurb: Beginning of the bloody March Events in Baku and other locations of Baku Governorate.

Q2988530.name: Iraqi 14 July revolution
Q2988530.blurb: In the 14 July Revolution in Iraq, the monarchy is overthrown by popular forces led by Abd al-Karim Qasim, who becomes the nation's new leader.

Q2988608.name: Battle of Westbroek
Q2988608.blurb: Battle of Westbroek: An army of 4,000 to 5,000 soldiers raised by David of Burgundy, Bishop of Utrecht, attacks an armed mob of people from nearby Utrecht who were trying to avenge the massacre of the inhabitants of Westbroek.

Q2989488.name: 2012 Pakistan garment factory fires
Q2989488.blurb: A total of 315 people are killed in two garment factory fires in Pakistan.

Q2989671.name: Great Fire of Turku
Q2989671.blurb: The Great Fire of Turku almost completely destroys Finland's former capital city.

Q2991463.name: Protocol on Environmental Protection to the Antarctic Treaty
Q2991463.blurb: The Protocol on Environmental Protection to the Antarctic Treaty is opened for signature.

Q2991760.name: Northeast blackout of 2003
Q2991760.blurb: A widescale power blackout affects the northeast United States and Canada.

Q2992024.name: Lateran Council of 769
Q2992024.blurb: The Lateran Council ends by condemning the Council of Hieria and anathematizing its iconoclastic rulings.

Q2992361.name: Operation Rosary
Q2992361.blurb: Argentine special forces invaded the Falkland Islands, sparking the Falklands War against the United Kingdom.

Q2992403.name: Franco-Syrian War
Q2992403.blurb: Franco-Syrian War: At the Battle of Maysalun, forces of the Arab Kingdom of Syria were defeated by a French army moving to occupy the territory allocated to them by the San Remo conference.

Q2992979.name: Operation Polo
Q2992979.blurb: Operation Polo is terminated after the Indian Army accepts the surrender of the army of Hyderabad.

Q2993582.name: Spanish conquest of Guatemala
Q2993582.blurb: The Kaqchikel Maya rebel against their former Spanish allies during the Spanish conquest of Guatemala.

Q2993585.name: Panjdeh Incident
Q2993585.blurb: The Battle for Kushka triggers the Panjdeh Incident which nearly gives rise to war between the Russian and British Empires.

Q2994973.name: Cambodian campaign
Q2994973.blurb: Vietnam War: US President Richard Nixon formally authorizes American combat troops to take part in the Cambodian campaign.

Q2995893.name: counterculture of the 1960s
aliases: Counterculture of the 1960s in the United States
Q2995893.blurb: Counterculture of the 1960s: The Human Be-In takes place in San Francisco, California's Golden Gate Park, launching the Summer of Love.

Q2996241.name: British-Russian Convention
Q2996241.blurb: Russia and the United Kingdom sign the Anglo-Russian Convention, by which the UK recognizes Russian preeminence in northern Persia, while Russia recognizes British preeminence in southeastern Persia and Afghanistan. Both powers pledge not to interfere in Tibet.

Q2996243.name: Annapolis Convention
Q2996243.blurb: The beginning of the Annapolis Convention.

Q2996249.name: Convention of 1836
Q2996249.blurb: A convention of delegates from 57 Texas communities convenes in Washington-on-the-Brazos, Texas, to deliberate independence from Mexico.

Q2996302.name: Fenian raids
Q2996302.blurb: One thousand eight hundred Fenian raiders are repelled back to the United States after looting and plundering the Saint-Armand and Frelighsburg areas of Canada East.

Q2997849.name: Corpus de Sang
Q2997849.blurb: Corpus de Sang in Barcelona: Catalan reapers riot against Spanish Royal soldiers and officers, killing the Viceroy of Catalonia, Dalmau de Queralt. Escalation of hostilities between the Principality of Catalonia and the Spanish Monarchy, leading to the Reapers' War.

Q2997855.name: 1848 French presidential election
Q2997855.blurb: French presidential election: Having won the popular vote in a landslide, Louis Napoleon Bonaparte is inaugurated in the chamber of the National Assembly as the first (and only) president of the French Second Republic.

Q2998924.name: 1987 Fijian coups d'état
Q2998924.blurb: Fijian Prime Minister Timoci Bavadra is ousted from power in a coup d'état led by Lieutenant colonel Sitiveni Rabuka.

Q2998926.name: 1915 Portuguese coup d'état
Q2998926.blurb: The May 14 Revolt takes place in Lisbon, Portugal.

Q2998931.name: Leonardopoulos–Gargalidis coup d'état attempt
Q2998931.blurb: The royalist Leonardopoulos–Gargalidis coup d'état attempt fails in Greece, discrediting the monarchy and paving the way for the establishment of the Second Hellenic Republic.

Q3002737.name: May 1958 crisis in France
Q3002737.blurb: May 1958 crisis: A group of French military officers lead a coup in Algiers demanding that a government of national unity be formed with Charles de Gaulle at its head in order to defend French control of Algeria.

Q3002755.name: 6 February 1934 crisis
Q3002755.blurb: Far-right leagues rally in front of the Palais Bourbon in an attempted coup against the French Third Republic, creating a political crisis in France.

Q3002758.name: 16 May 1877 crisis
Q3002758.blurb: The 16 May 1877 crisis occurs in France, ending with the dissolution of the National Assembly 22 June and affirming the interpretation of the Constitution of 1875 as a parliamentary rather than presidential system. The elections held in October 1877 led to the defeat of the royalists as a formal political movement in France.

Q3003203.name: Cruise of the Kings
Q3003203.blurb: The Cruise of the Kings, a royal cruise organised by the Queen Consort of Greece, Frederica of Hanover, departs from Marseille, France.

Q3007076.name: Battle of Poison Spring
Q3007076.blurb: American Civil War: African-American Union soldiers were massacred and mutilated during and after the Battle of Poison Spring.

Q3008537.name: Cyclone Mala
Q3008537.blurb: Cyclone Mala made landfall near Thandwe, Myanmar, causing 37 deaths.

Q3010371.name: Bois Caïman
Q3010371.blurb: Enslaved Africans in Saint-Domingue, led by Dutty Boukman, held a Vodou ceremony that became a pivotal act of resistance. This gathering sparked a mass uprising against slavery, marking the beginning of the Haitian Revolution.

Q3018913.name: Harmar Campaign
Q3018913.blurb: Northwest Indian War: Native American forces defeat the United States, ending the Harmar Campaign.

Q3019306.name: Mutiny on the Meermin
Q3019306.blurb: Enslaved Malagasy captives on the Dutch East India Company slave ship Meermin began a mutiny that led to the ship's destruction on Cape Agulhas in present-day South Africa and the recapture of the instigators.

Q3019344.name: Camp Grant massacre
Q3019344.blurb: The Camp Grant massacre takes place in Arizona Territory.

Q3023525.name: Siege of Mecca
Q3023525.blurb: During the Siege of Mecca, the Kaaba catches fire and is burned down.

Q3024756.name: Battle of Porto Bello
Q3024756.blurb: Start of the Battle of Porto Bello between British and Spanish forces during the War of Jenkins' Ear.

Q3025332.name: Second English Civil War
Q3025332.blurb: Second English Civil War: The Siege of Colchester ends when Royalist Forces surrender to the Parliamentary Forces after eleven weeks.

Q3025374.name: Second Partition of Poland
aliases: Second Partition of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
Second Partition of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth
Second Treaty of Partition of Poland

Q3028762.name: Austral Líneas Aéreas Flight 2553
Q3028762.blurb: Austral Líneas Aéreas Flight 2553 crashes and explodes in Uruguay, killing 74.

Q3030165.name: Bruges speech
Q3030165.blurb: British prime minister Margaret Thatcher (pictured) gave a landmark speech at the Belfry of Bruges, Belgium, against federalism in the European Economic Community.

Q3030207.name: Rivers of Blood speech
Q3030207.blurb: English politician Enoch Powell makes his controversial "Rivers of Blood" speech.

Q3032218.name: Treaty of Huế
Q3032218.blurb: France and Viet Nam sign the Treaty of Huế, recognizing a French protectorate over Annam and Tonkin.

Q3034445.name: 2004 Indonesian presidential election
Q3034445.blurb: Indonesia held its first direct presidential elections, which resulted in the election of Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono as President of Indonesia after the second round on September 20.

Q3038322.name: Downing Street Declaration
Q3038322.blurb: The Troubles: The Downing Street Declaration is issued by British Prime Minister John Major and Irish Taoiseach Albert Reynolds.

Q3041786.name: Yên Bái Mutiny
Q3041786.blurb: The Việt Nam Quốc Dân Đảng launches the failed Yên Bái mutiny in hope of overthrowing French protectorate over Vietnam.

Q3042457.name: Platine War
Q3042457.blurb: The Argentine Confederation was defeated in the Platine War by an alliance consisting of Brazil, Uruguay and the Argentine provinces of Entre Ríos and Corrientes.

Q3042463.name: Uruguayan War
Q3042463.blurb: Uruguayan War: The Siege of Paysandú ends as the Brazilians and Coloradans capture Paysandú, Uruguay.

Q3042701.name: 1918 United Kingdom general election
Q3042701.blurb: The 1918 United Kingdom general election occurs, the first where women were permitted to vote. In Ireland the Irish republican political party Sinn Féin wins a landslide victory with nearly 47% of the popular vote.

Q3042917.name: discovery of Brazil
Q3042917.blurb: A fleet commanded by Pedro Álvares Cabral (pictured) anchored off present-day Brazil; he later claimed the land for the Portuguese Empire.

Q3042919.name: Libertadora Revolution
Q3042919.blurb: The military coup to unseat President Juan Perón of Argentina is launched at midnight.

Q3043388.name: Saguenay Flood
Q3043388.blurb: Storms provoke severe flooding on the Saguenay River, beginning one of Quebec's costliest natural disasters ever.

Q3043389.name: Montreal Flood of 1987
Q3043389.blurb: More than 100 mm (3.9 in) of rain fell in a two-and-a-half-hour period in parts of Montreal, causing severe flooding.

Q3045037.name: 1959 Escuminac hurricane
Q3045037.blurb: A rare June hurricane strikes Canada's Gulf of St. Lawrence killing 35.

Q3045041.name: Summerland disaster
Q3045041.blurb: A flash fire kills 50 people at the Summerland amusement centre at Douglas, Isle of Man.

Q3045050.name: Erzincan earthquake of 1939
Q3045050.blurb: The 7.8 Mw Erzincan earthquake shakes eastern Turkey with a maximum Mercalli intensity of XI (Extreme). At least 32,700 people were killed.

Q3046072.name: Air Algérie Flight 6289
Q3046072.blurb: Air Algérie Flight 6289 crashes at the Aguenar – Hadj Bey Akhamok Airport in Tamanrasset, Algeria, killing 102 out of the 103 people on board.

Q3046548.name: Raid on Deerfield
Q3046548.blurb: Queen Anne's War: French and Native American forces raided the English settlement of Deerfield, Massachusetts, killing more than 50 colonists.

Q3048031.name: ADC Airlines Flight 53
Q3048031.blurb: ADC Airlines Flight 053 crashes after takeoff from Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport in Abuja, Nigeria killing 96 people and injuring nine.

Q3050397.name: Operation Motorman
Q3050397.blurb: The Troubles: In Operation Motorman, the British Army re-takes the urban no-go areas of Northern Ireland. It is the biggest British military operation since the Suez Crisis of 1956, and the biggest in Ireland since the Irish War of Independence. Later that day, nine civilians are killed by car bombs in the village of Claudy.

Q3050672.name: Siege of Louisbourg
Q3050672.blurb: French and Indian War: Siege of Louisbourg: James Wolfe's attack at Louisbourg, Nova Scotia, commences.

Q3050824.name: 2010 Ladakh floods
Q3050824.blurb: Flash floods across a large part of Jammu and Kashmir, India, damages 71 towns and kills at least 255 people.

Q3051491.name: Capture of Valdivia
Q3051491.blurb: Chilean War of Independence: Chilean forces captured the city of Valdivia.

Q3053271.name: Byzantine Empire under the Komnenos dynasty
Q3053271.blurb: The Komnenos dynasty came to full power with the coronation of Alexios I Komnenos (pictured) as Byzantine emperor.

Q3054185.name: Cowra breakout
Q3054185.blurb: World War II: At least 1,104 Japanese POWs in Australia attempt to escape from a camp at Cowra, New South Wales; 545 temporarily succeed but are later either killed, commit suicide, or are recaptured.

Q3055337.name: Meeting at Hendaye
Q3055337.blurb: Adolf Hitler and Francisco Franco meet at Hendaye to discuss the possibility of Spain entering the Second World War.

Q3056596.name: Congress of Soviets
Q3056596.blurb: The Congress of Soviets approved the GOELRO plan, the first Soviet plan for national economic recovery and development.

Q3061033.name: Action of 13 January 1797
Q3061033.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: A naval battle between a French ship of the line and two British frigates off the coast of Brittany ends with the French vessel running aground, resulting in over 900 deaths.

Q3061338.name: Gospel Riots
Q3061338.blurb: Gospel riots: Bloody clashes take place in Athens following the translation of the Gospels into demotic Greek.

Q3061949.name: Napoleon I's exile to St. Helena
Q3061949.blurb: Napoleon begins his exile on Saint Helena in the South Atlantic Ocean.

Q3062188.name: La Coubre explosion
Q3062188.blurb: The French freighter La Coubre explodes in Havana, Cuba, killing 100.

Q3062332.name: Battle of Kittanning
Q3062332.blurb: French and Indian War: Kittanning Expedition.

Q3062383.name: Benedict Arnold's expedition to Quebec
Q3062383.blurb: Benedict Arnold's expedition to Quebec leaves Cambridge, Massachusetts.

Q3062437.name: 1950 French Annapurna expedition
Q3062437.blurb: Herzog and Lachenal of the French Annapurna expedition become the first climbers to reach the summit of an 8,000-metre peak.

Q3062714.name: execution of Louis XVI
Q3062714.blurb: After being found guilty of treason by the French National Convention, Louis XVI of France is executed by guillotine.

Q3064186.name: Bahr El-Baqar primary school bombing
Q3064186.blurb: Bahr El-Baqar primary school bombing: Israeli bombers strike an Egyptian school. Forty-six children are killed.

Q3066445.name: Siege of Algeciras
Q3066445.blurb: The Siege of Algeciras, one of the first European military engagements where gunpowder was used, comes to an end.

Q3067133.name: Fastnet Lighthouse (2nd)
Q3067133.blurb: The passenger ship Stephen Whitney is wrecked in thick fog off the southern coast of Ireland, killing 92 of the 110 on board. The disaster results in the construction of the Fastnet Rock lighthouse.

Q3069867.name: Second Triumvirate
Q3069867.blurb: Gervasio Antonio de Posadas joins Argentina's Second Triumvirate.

Q3075488.name: Italian occupation of Corsica
Q3075488.blurb: World War II: German troops occupy Corsica and Kosovo-Metohija ending the Italian occupation of Corsica.

Q3078122.name: South African Airways Flight 201
Q3078122.blurb: South African Airways Flight 201: A de Havilland DH.106 Comet 1 crashes into the sea during night killing 21 people.

Q3078508.name: Fortification of Dorchester Heights
Q3078508.blurb: American Revolutionary War: The Continental Army fortifies Dorchester Heights with cannon, leading the British troops to abandon the Siege of Boston.

Q3078655.name: Hurricane Alicia
Q3078655.blurb: Hurricane Alicia hits the Texas coast, killing 21 people and causing over US$1 billion in damage (1983 dollars).

Q3078994.name: Siege of Port Royal
Q3078994.blurb: Port Royal, the capital of French Acadia, falls in a siege by British forces.

Q3079213.name: Byzantine Papacy
Q3079213.blurb: Pope Pelagius I is consecrated following Imperial approval by Emperor Justinian I.

Q3079315.name: Trans-Canada Air Lines Flight 831
Q3079315.blurb: Trans-Canada Air Lines Flight 831 crashes shortly after takeoff from Montreal-Dorval International Airport, killing all 118 people on board.

Q3081812.name: Operation Alphabet
Q3081812.blurb: World War II: The completion of Operation Alphabet, the evacuation of Allied forces from Narvik at the end of the Norwegian campaign.

Q3082211.name: London tornado of 1091
Q3082211.blurb: London tornado of 1091: A tornado thought to be of strength T8/F4 strikes the heart of London.

Q3082702.name: Brazilian War of Independence
Q3082702.blurb: Brazilian War of Independence: A Brazilian squadron led by Lord Cochrane engages a Portuguese squadron under João de Campos off Salvador, Bahia.

Q3083143.name: Air France Flight 422
Q3083143.blurb: Air France Flight 422 crashes after taking off from El Dorado International Airport in Bogotá, Colombia, killing all 53 people on board.

Q3085493.name: Croatian independence referendum
Q3085493.blurb: Croatians vote for independence in a referendum.

Q3087069.name: Avianca Flight 410
Q3087069.blurb: A Colombian Boeing 727 jetliner, Avianca Flight 410, crashes into a mountainside near the Venezuelan border killing 143.

Q3087650.name: Hurricane Betsy
Q3087650.blurb: Hurricane Betsy makes its second landfall near New Orleans, leaving 76 dead and $1.42 billion ($10–12 billion in 2005 dollars) in damages, becoming the first hurricane to cause over $1 billion in unadjusted damage.

Q3088738.name: 2006 Hawaii earthquake
Q3088738.blurb: An earthquake registering 6.7 Mw occurred off the northwestern coast of the island of Hawaii.

Q3089201.name: separation of Panama from Colombia
Q3089201.blurb: With the encouragement of the United States, Panama separates from Colombia.

Q3089540.name: Soviet westward offensive of 1918–1919
Q3089540.blurb: The Soviet Forces move against Estonia when the 6th Red Rifle Division strikes the border town of Narva, marking the beginning of the Estonian War of Independence.

Q3090028.name: French Constitutional Laws of 1875
Q3090028.blurb: The 16 May 1877 crisis occurs in France, ending with the dissolution of the National Assembly 22 June and affirming the interpretation of the Constitution of 1875 as a parliamentary rather than presidential system. The elections held in October 1877 led to the defeat of the royalists as a formal political movement in France.

Q3090983.name: death and state funeral of Joseph Stalin
Q3090983.blurb: Joseph Stalin, the longest serving leader of the Soviet Union, dies at his Volynskoe dacha in Moscow after suffering a cerebral hemorrhage four days earlier.

Q3091173.name: Wild Bill Hickok – Davis Tutt shootout
Q3091173.blurb: In the market square of Springfield, Missouri, Wild Bill Hickok shoots and kills Davis Tutt in what is regarded as the first western showdown.

Q3098353.name: Air India Flight 855
Q3098353.blurb: Air India Flight 855, a Boeing 747, crashes into the Arabian Sea off the coast of Bombay, India, due to instrument failure, spatial disorientation, and pilot error, killing all 213 people on board.

Q3098727.name: same-sex marriage in France
Q3098727.blurb: Noël Mamère, Mayor of Bègles, celebrates marriage for two men for the first time in France.

Q3100531.name: Provisional Government of the Algerian Republic
Q3100531.blurb: The French government and representatives of the Provisional Government of the Algerian Republic reach a settlement to end the Algerian war in the Évian Accords.

Q3104871.name: TAROM Flight 371
Q3104871.blurb: TAROM Flight 371, an Airbus A310-300, crashes near Balotesti, Romania, killing all 60 people on board.

Q3108282.name: Siege of Valenciennes
Q3108282.blurb: Franco-Dutch War: France captured the town of Valenciennes in the Spanish Netherlands.

Q3112644.name: Greek government-in-exile
Q3112644.blurb: Georgios Papandreou becomes head of the Greek government-in-exile based in Egypt.

Q3112788.name: 2003 Afro-Asian Games
Q3112788.blurb: The inaugural Afro-Asian Games opened in Hyderabad, with 2,040 athletes from 96 nations competing.

Q3113093.name: 1966 Green Bay Packers season
Q3113093.blurb: The first Super Bowl is played in Los Angeles. The Green Bay Packers defeat the Kansas City Chiefs 35–10.

Q3113897.name: 1929 Monaco Grand Prix
Q3113897.blurb: The inaugural Monaco Grand Prix takes place in the Principality of Monaco. William Grover-Williams wins driving a Bugatti Type 35.

Q3114717.name: Great Genna Martyrdom
Q3114717.blurb: Fifty-five Christians are executed in Nagasaki during the Great Genna Martyrdom.

Q3115081.name: 1957 Valencia flood
Q3115081.blurb: At least 81 people are killed in the most devastating flood in the history of the Spanish city of Valencia.

Q3116400.name: War-responsibility trials in Finland
Q3116400.blurb: Andrei Zhdanov, Chairman of the Finnish Allied Commission, submits to the Finnish War Criminal Court an interrogation report by General Erich Buschenhagen, a German prisoner of war, on the contacts between Finnish and German military personnel before the Continuation War and a copy of Hitler's Barbarossa plan.

Q3116941.name: 2010 eruptions of Mount Merapi
Q3116941.blurb: Mount Merapi in Central Java, Indonesia, began an increasingly violent series of eruptions that lasted over a month.

Q3118367.name: Asbestos Strike
Q3118367.blurb: The Asbestos Strike begins in Canada. The strike marks the beginning of the Quiet Revolution in Quebec.

Q3118386.name: 1912 Lawrence Textile Strike
Q3118386.blurb: Immigrant textile workers in Lawrence, Massachusetts, go on strike when wages are reduced in response to a mandated shortening of the work week.

Q3118392.name: Seattle General Strike
Q3118392.blurb: The five-day Seattle General Strike begins, as more than 65,000 workers in the city of Seattle, Washington, walk off the job.

Q3118393.name: 2007 Guinean general strike
Q3118393.blurb: A general strike begins in Guinea in an attempt to get President Lansana Conté to resign.

Q3118399.name: Flint Sit-Down Strike
Q3118399.blurb: The Flint sit-down strike ends when General Motors recognizes the United Auto Workers trade union.

Q3118940.name: Father Le Loutre's War
Q3118940.blurb: After a two-week siege, the French commander of Fort Beauséjour in present-day New Brunswick, Canada, surrendered to British forces, marking the end of Father Le Loutre's War.

Q3119017.name: Ugandan Bush War
Q3119017.blurb: The National Resistance Army of Uganda launches an attack on a Ugandan Army installation in the central Mubende District to begin the Ugandan Bush War.

Q3119043.name: Six-Day War
aliases: Six Day War in the Congo
Q3119043.blurb: The Six-Day War in Kisangani begins in Kisangani, in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, between Ugandan and Rwandan forces. A large part of the city is destroyed.

Q3119385.name: Avianca Flight 011
Q3119385.blurb: Avianca Flight 011: A Boeing 747 crashes near Madrid's Barajas Airport, killing 181.

Q3124214.name: Hurricane Iniki
Q3124214.blurb: Hurricane Iniki strikes the island of Kauaʻi, Hawaii, killing 7 and causing $3.1bn in economic damages.

Q3125096.name: Meiji era
Q3125096.blurb: Shinpūren rebellion: Upset at the Westernisation of Meiji Japan and the abolition of the Tokugawa feudal hierarchy, the Keishintō, a group of extremist Shinto former samurai, launch a surprise attack against the Meiji government in Kumamoto Prefecture.

Q3128939.name: Haitian occupation of Santo Domingo
Q3128939.blurb: Haiti attacks the newly established Dominican Republic on the other side of the island of Hispaniola.

Q3132158.name: 1933 Spanish general election
Q3132158.blurb: The Union of the Right, a coalition of right-wing parties, won the majority of seats in the 1933 Spanish general election, the first election in the country with suffrage extended to women.

Q3133143.name: 1998 Papua New Guinea earthquake
Q3133143.blurb: The 7.0 Mw Papua New Guinea earthquake triggers a tsunami that destroys ten villages in Papua New Guinea, killing up to 2,700 people, and leaving several thousand injured.

Q3133590.name: Evacuation Day
Q3133590.blurb: American Revolutionary War: The last British troops leave New York City, three months after the signing of the Treaty of Paris.

Q3133630.name: 15 October 2011 global protests
Q3133630.blurb: Global demonstrations against economic inequality, corporate influence on government, and other issues, were held in more than 950 cities in 82 countries.

Q3133675.name: Beni Ali massacre
Q3133675.blurb: Beni Ali massacre occurs in Algeria, leaving 60 to 100 people dead.

Q3136592.name: 1689 Boston revolt
Q3136592.blurb: Bostonians rise up in rebellion against Sir Edmund Andros.

Q3142505.name: First English Civil War
Q3142505.blurb: First English Civil War: Despite being vastly outnumbered, a Parliamentarian force under James Chudleigh defeated a Royalist army near Okehampton, Devon, at the Battle of Sourton Down.

Q3149826.name: Ålesund Fire
Q3149826.blurb: Ålesund Fire: The Norwegian coastal town Ålesund is devastated by fire, leaving 10,000 people homeless and one person dead. Kaiser Wilhelm II funds the rebuilding of the town in Jugendstil style.

Q3149831.name: Burning of the Parliament Buildings in Montreal
Q3149831.blurb: The Governor General of Canada, Lord Elgin, signs the Rebellion Losses Bill, outraging Montreal's English population and triggering the Montreal Riots.

Q3149842.name: Club Cinq-Sept fire
Q3149842.blurb: Club Cinq-Sept fire in Saint-Laurent-du-Pont, France kills 146 young people.

Q3149846.name: Laurier Palace Theatre fire
Q3149846.blurb: A fire at the Laurier Palace movie theatre in Montreal, Quebec, Canada, kills 78 children.

Q3149853.name: fire of the Mont Blanc tunnel
Q3149853.blurb: A lorry carrying margarine and flour catches fire inside the Mont Blanc Tunnel, creating an inferno that kills 39 people.

Q3149897.name: Mount Hakkōda disaster
Q3149897.blurb: In the most fatal recorded mountaineering accident, 199 of the 210 members of an Imperial Japanese Army unit perished in a blizzard on the Hakkōda Mountains.

Q3150348.name: Battle of Plains Store
Q3150348.blurb: American Civil War: The Union Army succeeds in closing off the last escape route from Port Hudson, Louisiana, in preparation for the coming siege.

Q3150989.name: Pasta de Conchos mine disaster
Q3150989.blurb: A methane explosion in a coal mine in Nueva Rosita, Mexico, trapped and killed 65 miners.

Q3151731.name: Dirty War
Q3151731.blurb: The Festival Rock y Ruedas de Avándaro rock festival is held in the State of Mexico. It attracted more than 100,000 attendees during the Mexican Dirty War, a period marked by widespread political repression.

Q3152955.name: Siege of Palermo
Q3152955.blurb: Giuseppe Garibaldi begins the Siege of Palermo, part of the wars of Italian unification.

Q3153818.name: Abbasid invasion of Asia Minor
Q3153818.blurb: Arab–Byzantine wars: The Abbasid army departed Raqqa in northern Syria to begin an invasion of Byzantine-controlled Asia Minor.

Q3153850.name: Martinair Flight 495
Q3153850.blurb: A Dutch DC-10, flight Martinair MP 495, crashes at Faro Airport, Portugal, killing 56.

Q3156912.name: Air Philippines Flight 541
Q3156912.blurb: Air Philippines Flight 541 crashes in Samal, Davao del Norte, killing all 131 people on board.

Q3161000.name: 1968 Casiguran earthquake
Q3161000.blurb: An earthquake hits Casiguran, Aurora, Philippines killing more than 270 people and wounding 261.

Q3161519.name: Tenterfield Oration
Q3161519.blurb: Henry Parkes delivers the Tenterfield Oration, effectively starting the federation process in Australia.

Q3174545.name: Battle of Pamplona
Q3174545.blurb: Ignatius of Loyola is seriously wounded in the Battle of Pampeluna.

Q3175954.name: Japanese occupation of the Philippines
Q3175954.blurb: Japan completes its last reparation to the Philippines for war crimes committed during imperial Japan's conquest of the country in the Second World War.

Q3177188.name: TAM Transportes Aéreos Regionais Flight 402
Q3177188.blurb: TAM Transportes Aéreos Regionais Flight 402 crashes in São Paulo, Brazil, killing 99 people.

Q3177722.name: Braddock Expedition
Q3177722.blurb: The Braddock Expedition is soundly defeated by a smaller French and Native American force in its attempt to capture Fort Duquesne in what is now downtown Pittsburgh.

Q3178361.name: December 11, 2007 Algiers bombings
Q3178361.blurb: Insurgency in the Maghreb: Two car bombs explode in Algiers, Algeria, one near the Supreme Constitutional Court and the other near the offices of the United Nations.

Q3178783.name: Siege of Jaffa
Q3178783.blurb: Napoleon Bonaparte captures Jaffa in Palestine and his troops proceed to kill more than 2,000 Albanian captives.

Q3178811.name: Mutiny of Aranjuez
Q3178811.blurb: Charles IV, king of Spain, abdicates after riots and a popular revolt at the winter palace Aranjuez. His son, Ferdinand VII, takes the throne.

Q3178839.name: first voyage of James Cook
Q3178839.blurb: On his first voyage, British explorer James Cook and the crew of HMS Endeavour (pictured) landed at Botany Bay, making the first recorded European landfall on the eastern coast of Australia.

Q3179558.name: Tropical Storm Allison
Q3179558.blurb: Tropical Storm Allison makes landfall on the upper-Texas coastline as a strong tropical storm and dumps large amounts of rain over Houston. The storm causes $5.5 billion in damages, making Allison the second costliest tropical storm in U.S. history.

Q3179646.name: Bulo Marer hostage rescue attempt
Q3179646.blurb: One French soldier and 17 militants are killed in a failed attempt to free a French hostage in Bulo Marer, Somalia.

Q3179803.name: Impeachment of Fernando Lugo
Q3179803.blurb: Paraguayan President Fernando Lugo is removed from office by impeachment and succeeded by Federico Franco.

Q3180238.name: Arrow Air Flight 1285R
Q3180238.blurb: Arrow Air Flight 1285R, a McDonnell Douglas DC-8, crashes after takeoff in Gander, Newfoundland, killing all 256 people on board, including 236 members of the United States Army's 101st Airborne Division.

Q3182543.name: 1934 Latvian coup d'état
Q3182543.blurb: A self coup by prime minister Kārlis Ulmanis succeeds in Latvia, suspending its constitution and dissolving its Saeima.

Q3182723.name: Hindenburg disaster
Q3182723.blurb: Hindenburg disaster: The German zeppelin Hindenburg catches fire and is destroyed within a minute while attempting to dock at Lakehurst, New Jersey. Thirty-six people are killed.

Q3184519.name: Battle of Deçiq
Q3184519.blurb: During the Battle of Deçiq, Dedë Gjon Luli Dedvukaj, leader of the Malësori Albanians, raises the Albanian flag in the town of Tuzi, Montenegro, for the first time after George Kastrioti (Skanderbeg).

Q3186762.name: Evacuation Day
Q3186762.blurb: American Revolutionary War: The British Army evacuates Boston, ending the Siege of Boston, after George Washington and Henry Knox place artillery in positions overlooking the city.

Q3187015.name: Day of the Barricades
Q3187015.blurb: French Wars of Religion: Henry III of France flees Paris after Henry I, Duke of Guise, enters the city and a spontaneous uprising occurs.

Q3195891.name: Battle of Alnwick
Q3195891.blurb: Battle of Alnwick: in an English victory over the Scots, Malcolm III of Scotland, and his son Edward, are killed.

Q3200076.name: 2006 youth protests in France
Q3200076.blurb: At least one million union members, students and unemployed take to the streets in France in protest at the government's proposed First Employment Contract law.

Q3231705.name: 2010 Gansu mudslide
Q3231705.blurb: A massive mudslide in the Chinese province of Gansu killed at least 1,471 people.

Q3235083.name: Siege of Charleston
Q3235083.blurb: American Revolutionary War: In the largest defeat of the Continental Army, Charleston, South Carolina is taken by British forces.

Q3236265.name: 2009 Heilongjiang mine explosion
Q3236265.blurb: A mine explosion in Heilongjiang, China kills 108.

Q3237019.name: Sino-Burmese War
Q3237019.blurb: Sino-Burmese War: The war ends with the Qing dynasty withdrawing from Burma forever.

Q3237787.name: Liberty's Kids
Q3237787.blurb: American animated edutainment show Liberty's Kids aired its first episode.

Q3238000.name: Battle of Saint-Malo
Q3238000.blurb: World War II: Allied forces attacked German fortifications at Saint-Malo, France, beginning the Battle of Saint-Malo (pictured).

Q3239069.name: Jnaneswari Express train derailment
Q3239069.blurb: A train derailment and collision in the West Midnapore district of West Bengal, India, caused the deaths of at least 148 passengers.

Q3239539.name: 1980 Summer Olympics boycott
aliases: American-led boycott of the 1980 Summer Olympics
Boycot of the Summer Olympics of 1980
Boycott of the 1980 Summer Olympic Games
Boycott of the Summer Olympics of 1980
International boycott of the 1980 Summer Olympics
US boycott of the 1980 Summer Olympics
United States at the 1980 Summer Olympics
United States boycott of the 1980 Summer Olympics
Q3239539.blurb: Cold War: American President Jimmy Carter announces a United States boycott of the 1980 Summer Olympics in Moscow to protest the Soviet–Afghan War.

Q3240757.name: 1985 Santiago jimin
Q3240757.blurb: A magnitude 8.3 earthquake strikes the Valparaíso Region of Chile, killing 177 and leaving nearly a million people homeless.

Q3241038.name: Hurricane Elena
Q3241038.blurb: Hurricane Elena, an unpredictable and damaging tropical cyclone that affected eastern and central portions of the United States Gulf Coast, made landfall near Biloxi, Mississippi, as a Category 3 major hurricane.

Q3241047.name: Amish school shooting
Q3241047.blurb: Five Amish girls are murdered in a shooting at a school in Pennsylvania, United States.

Q3241199.name: Israeli–Lebanese conflict
Q3241199.blurb: Israel invaded Southern Lebanon, marking the fifth Israeli invasion of Lebanon since 1978.

Q3241797.name: Sita Air Flight 601
Q3241797.blurb: Sita Air Flight 601 crashes in Madhyapur Thimi, Nepal, killing all 19 passengers and crew.

Q3242848.name: First War of Scottish Independence
Q3242848.blurb: First War of Scottish Independence: John Balliol's Scottish army is defeated by an English army commanded by John de Warenne, 6th Earl of Surrey at the Battle of Dunbar.

Q3243642.name: Hurricane Flora
Q3243642.blurb: Hurricane Flora kills 6,000 in Cuba and Haiti.

Q3243984.name: Hurricane Fifi–Orlene
Q3243984.blurb: Hurricane Fifi strikes Honduras with 110 mph winds, killing 5,000 people.

Q3244543.name: Peshtigo fire
Q3244543.blurb: Slash-and-burn land management, months of drought, and the passage of a strong cold front cause the Peshtigo Fire, the Great Chicago Fire and the Great Michigan Fires to break out.

Q3245204.name: 1970 Ancash earthquake
Q3245204.blurb: The 7.9 Mw Ancash earthquake shakes Peru with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VIII (Severe) and a landslide buries the town of Yungay, Peru. Between 66,794 and 70,000 were killed and 50,000 were injured.

Q3246568.name: Hurricane Audrey
Q3246568.blurb: Hurricane Audrey makes landfall near the Texas–Louisiana border, killing over 400 people, mainly in and around Cameron, Louisiana.

Q3247561.name: Cross of Gold speech
Q3247561.blurb: William Jennings Bryan delivers his Cross of Gold speech advocating bimetallism at the 1896 Democratic National Convention in Chicago.

Q3247927.name: Securitas depot robbery
Q3247927.blurb: The Securitas depot robbery was the UK's largest heist. Almost £53m (about $92.5 million or €78 million) was stolen from a Securitas depot in Tonbridge, Kent.

Q3267305.name: China Eastern Airlines Flight 5210
Q3267305.blurb: China Eastern Airlines Flight 5210 crashes after takeoff from Baotou Donghe Airport, killing 55.

Q3267605.name: Varig Flight 820
Q3267605.blurb: Varig Flight 820 crashes near Paris on approach to Orly Airport, killing 123 of the 134 on board. In response, the FAA bans smoking in airplane lavatories.

Q3267709.name: Battle of Grathe Heath
Q3267709.blurb: The Battle of Grathe Heath ends the Danish Civil War.

Q3268356.name: Battle of San Lorenzo
Q3268356.blurb: José de San Martín defeats a Spanish royalist army at the Battle of San Lorenzo, part of the Argentine War of Independence.

Q3269580.name: bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers
Q3269580.blurb: Lehman Brothers files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, the largest bankruptcy filing in U.S. history.

Q3269760.name: Battle of Indus
Q3269760.blurb: Genghis Khan defeats the renegade Khwarazmian prince Jalal al-Din at the Battle of the Indus, completing the Mongol conquest of Central Asia.

Q3269922.name: Operation Paraquet
Q3269922.blurb: British prime minister Margaret Thatcher told journalists in Downing Street to "rejoice" upon hearing news of the successful recapture of South Georgia from Argentine forces in the Falklands War.

Q3270072.name: Pokhran-II
Q3270072.blurb: India conducts three underground atomic tests in Pokhran.

Q3270393.name: LOT Polish Airlines Flight 5055
Q3270393.blurb: LOT Flight 5055 Tadeusz Kościuszko crashes after takeoff in Warsaw, Poland, killing all 183 people on board.

Q3270739.name: Battle of Pakchon
Q3270739.blurb: Korean War: The 27th British Commonwealth Brigade succeeded in preventing a Chinese breakthrough at the Battle of Pakchon.

Q3271041.name: Battle of Canhe Slope
Q3271041.blurb: Later Yan is defeated by its former vassal Northern Wei at the Battle of Canhe Slope.

Q3271228.name: Battle of Bound Brook
Q3271228.blurb: American Revolutionary War: American forces are ambushed and defeated in the Battle of Bound Brook, New Jersey.

Q3271307.name: 1957 Andreanof Islands earthquake
Q3271307.blurb: The 8.6 Mw Andreanof Islands earthquake shakes the Aleutian Islands, causing over $5 million in damage from ground movement and a destructive tsunami.

Q3271379.name: Gulf Air Flight 072
Q3271379.blurb: Gulf Air Flight 072 crashes into the Persian Gulf near Manama, Bahrain, killing 143.

Q3271607.name: 1868 Arica earthquake
Q3271607.blurb: The 8.5–9.0 Mw Arica earthquake struck southern Peru with a maximum Mercalli intensity of XI (Extreme), causing 25,000+ deaths and a destructive basin wide tsunami that affected Hawaii and New Zealand.

Q3272511.name: Zhongshan Warship Incident
Q3272511.blurb: Chiang Kai-shek initiates a purge of communist elements within the National Revolutionary Army in Guangzhou.

Q3272636.name: 1993 Michael Jackson sexual abuse allegations
Q3272636.blurb: The jury acquits pop singer Michael Jackson of his charges for allegedly sexually molesting a child in 1993.

Q3273519.name: Naval Battle of Casablanca
Q3273519.blurb: Casablanca, starring Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman, premiered at the Hollywood Theatre in New York City to coincide with the Allied invasion of French North Africa and the capture of Casablanca.

Q3273647.name: EgyptAir Flight 648
Q3273647.blurb: Gunmen hijack EgyptAir Flight 648 en route from Athens to Cairo. When the plane lands in Malta, Egyptian commandos storm the aircraft, but 60 people die in the raid.

Q3274581.name: Garuda Indonesia Flight 865
Q3274581.blurb: Garuda Indonesia flight 865 crashes during takeoff from Fukuoka Airport, killing three people and injuring 170.

Q3274745.name: evacuation of Manchukuo
Q3274745.blurb: Evacuation of Manchukuo: At Talitzou by the Sino-Korean border, Puyi, then the Kangde Emperor of Manchukuo, formally renounces the imperial throne, dissolves the state, and cedes its territory to the Republic of China.

Q3275284.name: Siege of Fushimi
Q3275284.blurb: Ishida Mitsunari's Western Army commences the Siege of Fushimi Castle, which is lightly defended by a much smaller Tokugawa garrison led by Torii Mototada.

Q3277071.name: Bid Kaneh explosion
Q3277071.blurb: A blast in Iran's Shahid Modarres missile base leads to the death of 17 of the Revolutionary Guards members, including Hassan Tehrani Moghaddam, a key figure in Iran's missile program.

Q3277151.name: 2007 Elie, Manitoba tornado
Q3277151.blurb: The small town of Elie, Manitoba is hit by Canada's most intense tornado on record.

Q3284177.name: assassination of Olof Palme
Q3284177.blurb: Olof Palme, 26th Prime Minister of Sweden, is assassinated in Stockholm.

Q3286392.name: Recapture of Salvador
Q3286392.blurb: Dutch–Portuguese War: Portuguese and Spanish forces recaptured the Brazilian city of Bahia, which had previously been captured by the Dutch Republic.

Q3286965.name: Portuguese conquest of French Guiana
Q3286965.blurb: Combined British, Portuguese and colonial Brazilian forces begin the Invasion of Cayenne during the Napoleonic Wars.

Q3289676.name: March for Women's Lives
Q3289676.blurb: The March for Women's Lives brings over one million protesters, mostly pro-choice, to Washington D.C. to protest the Partial-Birth Abortion Ban Act of 2003, and other restrictions on abortion.

Q3291135.name: Wedding of Prince Charles and Camilla Parker Bowles
Q3291135.blurb: Charles, Prince of Wales, married Camilla Parker Bowles in a civil ceremony at the Windsor Guildhall.

Q3291561.name: 2008 Studénka train accident
Q3291561.blurb: A EuroCity train en route to Prague struck a part of a motorway bridge that had fallen onto the track near Studénka station and derailed, killing 8 people and injuring 64 others.

Q3291682.name: Castle Romeo
Q3291682.blurb: Nuclear weapons testing: The Romeo shot of Operation Castle is detonated at Bikini Atoll. Yield: 11 megatons.

Q3291913.name: Battle of Jenkins' Ferry
Q3291913.blurb: American Civil War: Confederate forces led by General E. Kirby Smith attack federal troops retreating across the Saline at Jenkins' Ferry, Arkansas.

Q3293566.name: Battle of Cape Gloucester
Q3293566.blurb: World War II: In the Battle of Cape Gloucester, American and Australian forces bombarded Japanese positions on New Britain in the Territory of New Guinea while U.S. Marines invaded from two sides of the island.

Q3293979.name: Operation Grapple
Q3293979.blurb: Operation Grapple X, Round C1: The United Kingdom conducts its first successful hydrogen bomb test over Kiritimati in the Pacific.

Q3294643.name: Revolution of the Park
Q3294643.blurb: In Buenos Aires, Argentina the Revolución del Parque takes place, forcing President Miguel Ángel Juárez Celman's resignation.

Q3296937.name: Battle of Gulnabad
Q3296937.blurb: The Safavid Empire of Iran is defeated by an army from Afghanistan at the Battle of Gulnabad.

Q3297309.name: Battle of Tukaroi
Q3297309.blurb: Mughal Emperor Akbar defeats Sultan of Bengal Daud Khan Karrani's army at the Battle of Tukaroi.

Q3297436.name: Yekatit 12
Q3297436.blurb: Yekatit 12: During a public ceremony at the Viceregal Palace (the former Imperial residence) in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, two Ethiopian nationalists of Eritrean origin attempt to kill viceroy Rodolfo Graziani with a number of grenades.

Q3297456.name: Safsaf massacre
Q3297456.blurb: Israeli-Palestinian conflict: Safsaf massacre: Israeli soldiers capture the Palestinian village of Safsaf in the Galilee; afterwards, between 52 and 64 villagers are massacred by the IDF.

Q3297470.name: Yelwa massacre
Q3297470.blurb: The Yelwa massacre concludes. It began on 4 February 2004 when armed Muslims killed 78 Christians at Yelwa, Nigeria. In response, about 630 Muslims were killed by Christians on May 2.

Q3297473.name: Sant'Anna di Stazzema massacre
Q3297473.blurb: Waffen-SS troops massacre 560 people in Sant'Anna di Stazzema.

Q3298746.name: War of the Portuguese Succession
Q3298746.blurb: War of the Portuguese Succession: Spanish victory at the Battle of Alcântara brings about the Iberian Union.

Q3298759.name: United States occupation of Haiti
Q3298759.blurb: The United States begins a 19-year occupation of Haiti.

Q3299165.name: Varig Flight 797
Q3299165.blurb: Varig Flight 797 crashes near Akouré in the Ivory Coast, resulting in 50 deaths.

Q3299278.name: 2009 Costa Rica earthquake
Q3299278.blurb: A 6.1-magnitude earthquake in northern Costa Rica kills 15 people and injures 32.

Q3299864.name: Aden Emergency
Q3299864.blurb: The Aden Emergency: The Battle of the Crater in which the British Argyll and Sutherland Highlanders retake the Crater district following the Arab Police mutiny.

Q3300379.name: shooting of Mark Duggan
Q3300379.blurb: A series of riots broke out in several London boroughs and in cities and towns across England in response to the shooting of Mark Duggan by Metropolitan Police officers.

Q3301991.name: Hurricane Diane
Q3301991.blurb: Hurricane Diane, the first Atlantic hurricane to cause more than $1 billion in damages, formed between the Lesser Antilles and Cape Verde.

Q3305198.name: 1905 Calabria earthquake
Q3305198.blurb: The 7.2 Mw Calabria earthquake shakes southern Italy with a maximum Mercalli intensity of XI (Extreme), killing between 557 and 2,500 people.

Q3305247.name: Edmonton tornado
Q3305247.blurb: A tornado occurs in Edmonton, Alberta, killing 27 people.

Q3305494.name: 1964 Gabon coup d'état
Q3305494.blurb: Gabonese military officers overthrew President Léon M'ba, but French forces, honouring a 1960 treaty, forcibly reinstated him two days later.

Q3305554.name: Byzantine civil war of 1373–1379
Q3305554.blurb: Andronikos IV Palaiologos enters Constantinople by force and captures his father, emperor John V Palaiologos, and his younger brothers during the Byzantine civil war of 1373–1379.

Q3309019.name: Boston Police Strike
Q3309019.blurb: The Boston police strike ended after four days of rule by the state militia, the deaths of nine people, and accusations that striking officers were "agents of Lenin".

Q3310304.name: Second War of Scottish Independence
Q3310304.blurb: Second War of Scottish Independence: Scottish forces under Sir Archibald Douglas were heavily defeated by the English at the Battle of Halidon Hill while trying to relieve Berwick-upon-Tweed.

Q3311679.name: 1939 Chillán earthquake
Q3311679.blurb: The deadliest earthquake in Chilean history strikes Chillán, killing approximately 28,000 people.

Q3312328.name: Spanish conquest of Iberian Navarre
Q3312328.blurb: The Spanish conquest of Iberian Navarre commences with the capture of Goizueta.

Q3313588.name: Protocol of Corfu
Q3313588.blurb: The Protocol of Corfu is signed, recognising full autonomy to Northern Epirus under nominal Albanian sovereignty.

Q3316780.name: Mission Accomplished speech
Q3316780.blurb: Invasion of Iraq: In what becomes known as the "Mission Accomplished" speech, on board the USS Abraham Lincoln (off the coast of California), U.S. President George W. Bush declares that "major combat operations in Iraq have ended".

Q3317226.name: Invasion of Algiers in 1830
Q3317226.blurb: Beginning of the Invasion of Algiers: Thirty-four thousand French soldiers land 27 kilometers west of Algiers, at Sidi Ferruch.

Q3317347.name: LAPA Flight 3142
Q3317347.blurb: A LAPA Boeing 737-200 crashes during takeoff from Jorge Newbury Airport in Buenos Aires, killing 65, including two on the ground.

Q3320910.name: Battle of Topeter
Q3320910.blurb: War of the Pacific: The Battle of Topáter, the first battle of the war, is fought between Chile and the joint forces of Bolivia and Peru.

Q3321690.name: Young Ireland rebellion
Q3321690.blurb: Great Famine of Ireland: Tipperary Revolt: In County Tipperary, Ireland, then in the United Kingdom, an unsuccessful nationalist revolt against British rule is put down by police.

Q3322608.name: German occupation of Estonia during World War II
Q3322608.blurb: World War II: Soviet Air Forces bomb the evacuated town of Narva in German-occupied Estonia, destroying the entire historical Swedish-era town.

Q3328100.name: Casas Viejas incident
Q3328100.blurb: Casas Viejas incident: 22 peasants killed by the Security and Assault Corps in Casas Viejas, Spain.

Q3333118.name: Boston bomb scare
Q3333118.blurb: Emergency officials in Boston mistakenly identify battery-powered LED placards depicting characters from Aqua Teen Hunger Force as Improvised explosive devices (IEDs), causing a panic.

Q3337680.name: Berbice Slave Uprising
Q3337680.blurb: Berbice slave uprising in Guyana: The first major slave revolt in South America.

Q3339083.name: New Zealand Nuclear Free Zone, Disarmament, and Arms Control Act 1987
Q3339083.blurb: New Zealand's Labour government establishes a national nuclear-free zone under the New Zealand Nuclear Free Zone, Disarmament, and Arms Control Act 1987.

Q3347903.name: assassination of Indira Gandhi
aliases: Assassination of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi
Q3347903.blurb: After the assassination of Indira Gandhi, Prime Minister of India on 31 October 1984, by two of her Sikh bodyguards, anti-Sikh riots erupt.

Q3350154.name: assassination of Mahatma Gandhi
Q3350154.blurb: Following the assassination of Mahatma Gandhi in his home compound, India's prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, broadcasts to the nation, saying "The light has gone out of our lives". The date of the assassination becomes observed as "Martyrs' Day" in India.

Q3351820.name: 2001 Indian Parliament attack
Q3351820.blurb: Indian Parliament attack: Sansad Bhavan, the building housing the Indian Parliament, is attacked by five Jaish-e-Mohammed terrorists. Twelve people are killed, including the terrorists.

Q3351948.name: 2008 Ahmedabad blasts
Q3351948.blurb: Fifty-six people are killed and over 200 people are injured, in the Ahmedabad bombings in India.

Q3354415.name: Internal resistance to South African apartheid
Q3354415.blurb: South African anti-apartheid activist Steve Biko dies in police custody.

Q3354640.name: Operation Azalee
Q3354640.blurb: Bob Denard and a group of mercenaries take the islands of the Comoros in a coup.

Q3354670.name: Operation Camargue
Q3354670.blurb: First Indochina War: The French Union withdraws its forces from Operation Camargue against the Viet Minh in central Vietnam.

Q3354683.name: Operation Michoacán
Q3354683.blurb: Felipe Calderón, the president of Mexico, launches a military-led offensive to put down the drug cartel violence in the state of Michoacán. This effort is often regarded as the first event in the Mexican drug war.

Q3354729.name: Operation Igloo White
Q3354729.blurb: Operation Igloo White, a US electronic surveillance system to stop communist infiltration into South Vietnam begins installation.

Q3354803.name: Operation Panther's Claw
Q3354803.blurb: War in Afghanistan: British forces began Operation Panther's Claw, in which more than 350 troops made an aerial assault on Taliban positions in southern Afghanistan.

Q3354892.name: Operation Windsor
Q3354892.blurb: Second World War: Canadian troops defeated the last German counterattacks against Carpiquet, Normandy, France.

Q3354894.name: Operation Southern Move
Q3354894.blurb: The Croatian Army and Croatian Defence Council launched Operation Southern Move, their last offensive in the Bosnian War.

Q3357987.name: Battle of Tarapacá
Q3357987.blurb: War of the Pacific: Battle of Tarapacá: The confrontation between the Chilean Army and the Peruvian Army takes place in Tarapacá, the Peruvian victory is consummated with the death of the 2 generals and the capture the Chilean general in said place of battle, headed by the Peruvian victory of General Juan Buendía y Noregia.

Q3358382.name: Hurricane Edna
Q3358382.blurb: Hurricane Edna hits New England (United States) as a Category 2 hurricane, causing significant damage and 29 deaths.

Q3358934.name: Klaipėda Revolt
Q3358934.blurb: Lithuanian residents of the Klaipėda Region began a revolt, ahead of a League of Nations decision on their future which they expected to be against their interest.

Q3359318.name: 2008 South China floods
Q3359318.blurb: Severe flooding begins in eastern and southern China that will ultimately cause 148 deaths and force the evacuation of 1.3 million.

Q3360074.name: sinking of the MS Estonia
Q3360074.blurb: The cruise ferry MS Estonia sinks in the Baltic Sea, killing 852 people.

Q3362859.name: Battle of Kauhajoki
Q3362859.blurb: Finnish War: Swedish forces led by General von Döbeln defeat Russian forces led by General Šepelev in the Battle of Kauhajoki.

Q3365103.name: Paris–Bordeaux–Paris race
Q3365103.blurb: Paris–Bordeaux–Paris, sometimes called the first automobile race in history or the "first motor race", takes place.

Q3365353.name: Paris in World War II
Q3365353.blurb: World War II: The German occupation of Paris begins.

Q3373219.name: 1977 Convair CV-300 crash
Q3373219.blurb: A plane carrying the rock band Lynyrd Skynyrd crashes in woodland in Mississippi, United States. Six people, including three band members, are killed.

Q3378809.name: 2011 Mazar-i-Sharif attack
Q3378809.blurb: After protests against the burning of the Quran turn violent, a mob attacks a United Nations compound in Mazar-i-Sharif, Afghanistan, resulting in the deaths of fourteen people, including seven UN workers.

Q3380481.name: Battle of Lottorf
Q3380481.blurb: Danish troops defeat a Schleswig-Holstein force in the town of Lottorf, Schleswig-Holstein.

Q3381142.name: Battle of Flers–Courcelette
Q3381142.blurb: Tanks (example pictured), the "secret weapons" of the British Army during the First World War, were first used in combat at the Battle of Flers–Courcelette in France.

Q3382350.name: Venezuela Declaration of Independence
Q3382350.blurb: The Venezuelan Declaration of Independence is adopted by a congress of the provinces.

Q3391315.name: Cham-Vietnamese War
Q3391315.blurb: Champa–Đại Việt War: Emperor Lê Thánh Tông of Đại Việt formally launches his attack against Champa.

Q3392743.name: Battle of Monastir
Q3392743.blurb: First Balkan War: The Serbian Army captures Bitola, ending the five-century-long Ottoman rule of Macedonia.

Q3394840.name: First Siege of Missolonghi
Q3394840.blurb: Greek War of Independence: The First Siege of Missolonghi begins.

Q3394869.name: Battle of Samos
Q3394869.blurb: Greek War of Independence: Konstantinos Kanaris leads a Greek fleet to victory against Ottoman and Egyptian naval forces in the Battle of Samos.

Q3396146.name: Croatian-Ottoman Wars
Q3396146.blurb: Croatian–Ottoman wars: After the execution of feudal lord Petar Kružić, Croatian forces at Klis surrendered to the Ottoman forces in exchange for their safe passage to northern locations.

Q3399565.name: Ottoman–Egyptian invasion of Mani
Q3399565.blurb: Maniots defeat Egyptians under Ibrahim Pasha in the Battle of Vergas.

Q3401685.name: Founding Congress of the Comintern
Q3401685.blurb: Communist, revolutionary-socialist, and syndicalist delegates met in Moscow to establish the Communist International.

Q3401697.name: first inauguration of Ronald Reagan
Q3401697.blurb: Twenty minutes after Ronald Reagan is inaugurated as the 40th President of the United States of America, Iran releases 52 American hostages.

Q3401918.name: First Battle of Saltville
Q3401918.blurb: American Civil War: Confederates defeat a Union attack on Saltville, Virginia. A massacre of wounded Union prisoners ensues.

Q3402214.name: Invasion of Portugal
Q3402214.blurb: The Portuguese royal family arrives in Brazil after fleeing the French army's invasion of Portugal two months earlier.

Q3403123.name: Royal Charter Storm
Q3403123.blurb: The Royal Charter Storm kills at least eight hundred people in the British Isles.

Q3403857.name: Invasion of Isle de France
Q3403857.blurb: Napoleonic Wars: British troops rendezvoused at Grand Baie to launch an invasion of Isle de France, now known as Mauritius.

Q3403859.name: Capture of Grenada
Q3403859.blurb: American Revolutionary War: French troops landed near St. George's, Grenada, and began their capture of the island.

Q3404150.name: Senghenydd Colliery Disaster
Q3404150.blurb: Senghenydd colliery disaster, the United Kingdom's worst coal mining accident, claims the lives of 439 miners.

Q3405472.name: Treaty of Aberconwy
Q3405472.blurb: The Treaty of Aberconwy, a humiliating settlement forced on Llywelyn ap Gruffudd by King Edward I of England, brings a temporary end to the Welsh Wars.

Q3409504.name: Skopje fire of 1689
Q3409504.blurb: General Enea Silvio Piccolomini of Austria burns down Skopje to prevent the spread of cholera; he dies of the disease soon afterwards.

Q3411960.name: 1465 Fez revolt
Q3411960.blurb: During the 1465 Moroccan revolution which overthrows the Marinid dynasty, the Jewish mellah is attacked by the population of Fez, though the extent of the massacre is debated.

Q3423445.name: assassination of Rajiv Gandhi
Q3423445.blurb: Former Indian prime minister Rajiv Gandhi was assassinated by a suicide bomber in Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu.

Q3424555.name: Åsta accident
Q3424555.blurb: A Norwegian passenger train departing from Trondheim, collides with a local train coming from Hamar in Åsta in Åmot Municipality; 19 people are killed and 68 injured in the accident.

Q3427286.name: Great Hinckley Fire
Q3427286.blurb: Over 400 people die in the Great Hinckley Fire, a forest fire in Hinckley, Minnesota.

Q3427309.name: Representation of the People Act 1918
Q3427309.blurb: British women over the age of 30 who meet minimum property qualifications, get the right to vote when  Representation of the People Act 1918 is passed by Parliament.

Q3427966.name: transition from Ming to Qing
Q3427966.blurb: Transition from Ming to Qing: The Chongzhen Emperor, the last Emperor of Ming China, commits suicide during a peasant rebellion led by Li Zicheng.

Q3428188.name: 2010 Thai military crackdown
Q3428188.blurb: The Royal Thai Armed Forces concludes its crackdown on protests by forcing the surrender of United Front for Democracy Against Dictatorship leaders.

Q3430256.name: Battle of Køge
Q3430256.blurb: British troops under Sir Arthur Wellesley defeat a Danish militia outside Copenhagen in the Battle of Køge.

Q3431465.name: Siege of Sidon
Q3431465.blurb: An army led by Baldwin I of Jerusalem and Sigurd the Crusader of Norway captures Sidon at the end of the First Crusade.

Q3432920.name: Night of Schmelzer
Q3432920.blurb: The Dutch Cals cabinet fell after Norbert Schmelzer, the leader of the government party, filed a successful motion against the budget, in what later became known as the Night of Schmelzer.

Q3434323.name: Izbica massacre
Q3434323.blurb: Kosovo War: Serbian police and special forces killed around 93 Kosovo Albanians in the village of Izbica.

Q3434355.name: death of Ayrton Senna
Q3434355.blurb: Three-time Formula One champion Ayrton Senna is killed in an accident during the San Marino Grand Prix.

Q3436252.name: 6 January Dictatorship
Q3436252.blurb: King Alexander of the Serbs, Croats and Slovenes suspends his country's constitution, starting the January 6th Dictatorship.

Q3439047.name: War of Dominican Independence
Q3439047.blurb: One of the most important battles of the Dominican War of Independence from Haiti takes place near the city of Santiago de los Caballeros.

Q3439107.name: Slovenian independence referendum, 1990
Q3439107.blurb: About 88 percent of eligible voters in Slovenia voted to secede from the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

Q3443006.name: Podgorica Assembly
Q3443006.blurb: The Podgorica Assembly convened in Montenegro, with the intention of uniting with the Kingdom of Serbia.

Q3443265.name: Rough Wooing
Q3443265.blurb: During the Rough Wooing, an English army carried out the Burning of Edinburgh.

Q3444492.name: Regulator Movement
Q3444492.blurb: The Battle of Alamance, a pre-American Revolutionary War battle between local militia and a group of rebels called The "Regulators", occurs in present-day Alamance County, North Carolina.

Q3444697.name: 2001 Kunlun earthquake
Q3444697.blurb: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake strikes a remote part of the Tibetan Plateau. It has the longest known surface rupture recorded on land (~400 km) and is the best documented example of a supershear earthquake.

Q3444768.name: assassination of Zoran Đinđić
Q3444768.blurb: Zoran Đinđić, Prime Minister of Serbia, is assassinated in Belgrade.

Q3446062.name: Communist insurgency in Malaysia
Q3446062.blurb: The Peace Agreement of Hat Yai is signed and ratified by the Malayan Communist Party (MCP) and the governments of Malaysia and Thailand, ending the over two-decade-long communist insurgency in Malaysia.

Q3454843.name: Chilean national plebiscite, 1988
Q3454843.blurb: A Chilean opposition coalition defeats Augusto Pinochet in his re-election attempt.

Q3454865.name: Western Australian secession referendum, 1933
Q3454865.blurb: The Australian state of Western Australia voted to secede from the federation, but efforts to implement the result proved to be unsuccessful.

Q3454881.name: Greek monarchy referendum, 1935
Q3454881.blurb: In a widely criticised referendum, almost 98 percent of Greek voters supported the restoration of George II (pictured) as King of the Hellenes.

Q3454904.name: Panama Canal expansion referendum, 2006
Q3454904.blurb: A Panama Canal expansion proposal is approved by 77.8% of voters in a national referendum.

Q3458285.name: Theriso revolt
Q3458285.blurb: Eleftherios Venizelos calls for Crete's union with Greece, and begins what is to be known as the Theriso revolt.

Q3458313.name: New York Slave Revolt of 1712
Q3458313.blurb: The New York Slave Revolt of 1712 begins near Broadway.

Q3461001.name: Sacrament of Miracle
Q3461001.blurb: Brussels massacre: An estimated 13 Jews are murdered and the rest of the Jewish community is banished from Brussels, Belgium, in an anti-Semitic attack, for allegedly desecrating consecrated Host.

Q3467730.name: Battle of Rafa
Q3467730.blurb: World War I: The Battle of Rafa is fought near the Egyptian border with Palestine.

Q3474969.name: Sacking of Lawrence
Q3474969.blurb: A crowd of about 800 pro-slavery Americans ransacked the town of Lawrence, Kansas.

Q3475344.name: Disruption of 1843
Q3475344.blurb: The Disruption in Edinburgh of the Free Church of Scotland from the Church of Scotland.

Q3477165.name: Second Battle of Fort McAllister
Q3477165.blurb: American Civil War: Sherman's March to the Sea: The Second Battle of Fort McAllister ends with the fort being seized by Union forces under General William B. Hazen, threatening the city of Savannah with investment.

Q3478362.name: Semaine sanglante
Q3478362.blurb: French troops invade the Paris Commune and engage its residents in street fighting. By the close of "Bloody Week", some 20,000 communards have been killed and 38,000 arrested.

Q3480181.name: Linköping Bloodbath
Q3480181.blurb: The Linköping Bloodbath takes place on Maundy Thursday in Linköping, Sweden: five Swedish noblemen are publicly beheaded in the aftermath of the War against Sigismund (1598–1599).

Q3481304.name: 1949 anti-NATO riot in Iceland
Q3481304.blurb: Cold War: A riot breaks out in Austurvöllur square in Reykjavík, when Iceland joins NATO.

Q3485734.name: World Trade Organization Ministerial Conference of 2005
Q3485734.blurb: Anti-World Trade Organization protesters riot in Wan Chai, Hong Kong.

Q3485852.name: Siege of Carcassonne
Q3485852.blurb: Albigensian Crusade: The Cathar stronghold of Carcassonne falls to the crusaders.

Q3485855.name: Siege of Cambrai
Q3485855.blurb: The French army captures the town of Cambrai held by Spanish troops.

Q3485870.name: Siege of Cuautla
Q3485870.blurb: The Siege of Cuautla during the Mexican War of Independence ends with both sides claiming victory.

Q3485885.name: Siege of Fort Detroit
Q3485885.blurb: Pontiac's War begins with Pontiac's attempt to seize Fort Detroit from the British.

Q3485913.name: Siege of Kimberley
Q3485913.blurb: Second Boer War: British cavalry led by John French defeated Boer forces to end a 124-day siege of Kimberley in present-day South Africa.

Q3485953.name: Battle of Mello
Q3485953.blurb: Battle of Mello: The peasant forces of the Jacquerie are crushed by the army of the French nobility.

Q3485984.name: Siege of Paris
Q3485984.blurb: An army led by Alexander Farnese, Duke of Parma forces Henry IV of France to lift the siege of Paris.

Q3485986.name: Siege of Paris
Q3485986.blurb: Viking expansion: Viking raiders, possibly led by the legendary Ragnar Lodbrok, plundered and occupied Paris, holding the city for a large ransom.

Q3485993.name: Siege of Port-au-Prince
Q3485993.blurb: The French troops led by Léger-Félicité Sonthonax defeat the slaves settlers in the Siege of Port-au-Prince.

Q3485995.name: Siege of Pondicherry
Q3485995.blurb: American Revolutionary War: British forces begin besieging the French outpost at Pondichéry.

Q3486019.name: Siege of San Sebastián
Q3486019.blurb: At the final stage of the Peninsular War, British-Portuguese troops capture the town of Donostia (now San Sebastián), resulting in a rampage and eventual destruction of the town.

Q3486020.name: Siege of St. Augustine
Q3486020.blurb: Georgia provincial governor James Oglethorpe begins an unsuccessful attempt to take Spanish Florida during the Siege of St. Augustine.

Q3486031.name: Siege of Termes
Q3486031.blurb: The Castle of Termes falls to Simon de Montfort after a four-month siege during the Albigensian Crusade.

Q3487055.name: 2009 Handlová mine blast
Q3487055.blurb: Twenty people are killed in Handlová, Trenčín Region, in the deadliest mining disaster in Slovakia's history.

Q3487920.name: Intelligenzaktion
Q3487920.blurb: As part of their plan to eradicate the Polish intellectual elite, the Gestapo arrested 184 professors, students and employees of the Jagiellonian University (location pictured) in Kraków.

Q3488717.name: TABSO Flight 101
Q3488717.blurb: Bulgarian TABSO Flight 101 crashes near Bratislava, Czechoslovakia, killing all 82 people on board.

Q3489516.name: Pottawatomie Massacre
Q3489516.blurb: John Brown and his men kill five slavery supporters at Pottawatomie Creek, Kansas.

Q3489934.name: 1967 Arab League summit
Q3489934.blurb: At an Arab League summit, eight nations issued the Khartoum Resolution, declaring that there would be "no peace with Israel, no recognition of Israel, [and] no negotiations with it".

Q3490568.name: Battle of Tirad Pass
Q3490568.blurb: Philippine–American War: The Battle of Tirad Pass, known as the "Filipino Thermopylae", is fought.

Q3491891.name: Battle of Komarów
Q3491891.blurb: Polish–Soviet War: A decisive Polish victory in the Battle of Komarów.

Q3492593.name: 1934 Bihar earthquake
Q3492593.blurb: The 8.0 Mw Nepal–Bihar earthquake strikes Nepal and Bihar with a maximum Mercalli intensity of XI (Extreme), killing an estimated 6,000–10,700 people.

Q3493779.name: Humberto Vidal Explosion
Q3493779.blurb: Humberto Vidal explosion: Thirty-three people die when a Humberto Vidal shoe shop in Río Piedras, Puerto Rico explodes.

Q3495710.name: 2005 Mauritanian coup d'état
Q3495710.blurb: Mauritanian president Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya was overthrown in a military coup while he attended the funeral of King Fahd of Saudi Arabia.

Q3497601.name: 2003 Colima earthquake
Q3497601.blurb: A 7.6 magnitude earthquake strikes the Mexican state of Colima, killing 29 and leaving approximately 10,000 people homeless.

Q3499552.name: 1980 El Asnam earthquake
Q3499552.blurb: The 7.1 Mw El Asnam earthquake shakes northern Algeria, killing 2,633 and injuring 8,369.

Q3500162.name: Bijeljina massacre
Q3500162.blurb: Forty-two civilians are massacred in the town of Bijeljina in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

Q3500734.name: 2012 Sana'a bombing
Q3500734.blurb: A suicide bombing kills more than 120 people in Sanaa, Yemen.

Q3501420.name: June 2012 Afghanistan earthquakes
Q3501420.blurb: Seventy-five people die in a landslide triggered by two earthquakes in Afghanistan; an entire village is buried.

Q3503541.name: Garuda Indonesia Flight 152
Q3503541.blurb: A Garuda Indonesia Airbus A300 crashes near Medan airport, killing 234.

Q3504102.name: Battle of Guararapes
Q3504102.blurb: The Second Battle of Guararapes takes place, effectively ending Dutch colonization efforts in Brazil.

Q3504310.name: 1984 anti-Sikh riots
aliases: Attacks on Sikhs in Delhi in 1984
Q3504310.blurb: Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi is assassinated by two Sikh security guards. Riots break out in New Delhi and other cities and around 3,000 Sikhs are killed.

Q3504562.name: 1982 North Yemen earthquake
Q3504562.blurb: The 6.0 Ms North Yemen earthquake shakes southwestern Yemen with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VIII (Severe), killing 2,800, and injuring 1,500.

Q3504617.name: Battle of Cerro Corá
Q3504617.blurb: Marshal F. S. López dies during the Battle of Cerro Corá thus marking the end of the Paraguayan War.

Q3505096.name: Düzce earthquake of 1999
Q3505096.blurb: The 7.2 Mw Düzce earthquake shakes northwestern Turkey with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent). At least 845 people are killed and almost 5,000 are injured.

Q3505835.name: Lookout Air Raids
Q3505835.blurb: World War II: A Japanese floatplane drops incendiary bombs on Oregon.

Q3506821.name: Battle of Baton Rouge
Q3506821.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Baton Rouge: Along the Mississippi River near Baton Rouge, Louisiana, Confederate troops attempt to take the city, but are driven back by fire from Union gunboats.

Q3510571.name: 1969 Portugal earthquake
Q3510571.blurb: The 1969 Portugal earthquake hits Portugal, Spain and Morocco.

Q3510577.name: 2001 Nisqually earthquake
Q3510577.blurb: The 2001 Nisqually earthquake, having a moment magnitude of 6.8, with epicenter in southern Puget Sound, damages the Seattle metropolitan area.

Q3510661.name: 2012 United States Olympic Trials
aliases: 2012 USA Outdoor Track and Field Championships
Q3510661.blurb: Ashton Eaton breaks the decathlon world record at the United States Olympic Trials.

Q3514809.name: Action off Galveston Light
Q3514809.blurb: American Civil War: CSS Alabama encounters and sinks the USS Hatteras off Galveston Lighthouse in Texas.

Q3517855.name: Columbus Day storm of 1962
Q3517855.blurb: The Columbus Day Storm strikes the U.S. Pacific Northwest with record wind velocities. There was at least U.S. $230 million in damages and 46 people died.

Q3517876.name: Tropical Storm Bonnie
Q3517876.blurb: Merely 22 hours after Tropical Storm Bonnie struck the U.S. state of Florida, Hurricane Charley inflicted further damage to the region (example pictured).

Q3517986.name: first-wave feminism
Q3517986.blurb: Thousands of women marched in Washington, D.C., "in a spirit of protest" against the exclusion of women from American society.

Q3518182.name: Skirmish of Strasbourg
Q3518182.blurb: Louis Napoleon launches the unsuccessful Strasbourg Coup to overthrow the July Monarchy in France

Q3519518.name: Royal Indian Navy mutiny
Q3519518.blurb: Sailors of the Royal Indian Navy mutiny in Bombay harbour, from where the action spreads throughout the Provinces of British India, involving 78 ships, twenty shore establishments and 20,000 sailors

Q3521932.name: The Mother of All Demos
Q3521932.blurb: Douglas Engelbart gave what became known as "The Mother of All Demos", publicly debuting the computer mouse, hypertext, and the bit-mapped graphical user interface using the oN-Line System (NLS).

Q3525320.name: Goyang Geumjeong Cave Massacre
Q3525320.blurb: The Goyang Geumjeong Cave massacre in Korea begins.

Q3533326.name: 1977 riots in Sri Lanka
Q3533326.blurb: The Sri Lanka Riots: Targeting the minority Sri Lankan Tamils, begin, less than a month after the United National Party came to power. Over 300 Tamils are killed.

Q3533435.name: Operation Python
Q3533435.blurb: Indo-Pakistani War: The Indian Navy launches an attack on West Pakistan's port city of Karachi.

Q3535444.name: The Beatles' 1965 US tour
Q3535444.blurb: The Beatles play to nearly 60,000 fans at Shea Stadium in New York City, an event later regarded as the birth of stadium rock.

Q3535454.name: Australian cricket team in England in 1948
Q3535454.blurb: The Australian cricket team's Invincibles tour of England concluded; they had played 34 matches, including five Tests, without defeat.

Q3535458.name: 1981 South Africa rugby union tour of New Zealand
Q3535458.blurb: The first game of the 1981 South Africa rugby union tour of New Zealand and the United States is held in Gisborne, New Zealand.

Q3535523.name: Godhra train burning
Q3535523.blurb: Godhra train burning: A Muslim mob torches a train returning from Ayodhya, killing 59 Hindu pilgrims.

Q3535947.name: Burning of Jaffna library
Q3535947.blurb: An organized mob of police and government-sponsored Sinhalese paramilitary forces began three days of attacks that led to the burning of the Jaffna Public Library (renovated building pictured) in Sri Lanka, destroying more than 97,000 items in one of the most violent 20th-century examples of ethnic biblioclasm.

Q3536143.name: Bandaranaike Airport attack
Q3536143.blurb: The Bandaranaike Airport attack is carried out by 14 Tamil Tiger commandos, resulting in military and civilian casualties and destroyed aircraft.

Q3536729.name: Treaty of Antwerp
Q3536729.blurb: Eighty Years' War: Spain and the Dutch Republic sign the Treaty of Antwerp to initiate twelve years of truce.

Q3536851.name: Treaty of Paris
Q3536851.blurb: Treaty of Paris of 1323 is signed.

Q3536871.name: Treaty of Rio de Janeiro
