Q3536871.blurb: Portuguese and Brazilian diplomats sign the Treaty of Rio de Janeiro, which has Portugal recognise Brazilian independence, formally ending the Brazilian War of Independence. The treaty will be ratified by the King of Portugal three months later.

Q3537644.name: transit of Venus, 1639
Q3537644.blurb: Jeremiah Horrocks and William Crabtree made the first successful observation  of a transit of Venus (example pictured) from Earth.

Q3537646.name: transit of Venus, 1882
Q3537646.blurb: Transit of Venus, second and last of the 19th century.

Q3537730.name: Nagorno-Karabakh independence referendum
Q3537730.blurb: The Nagorno-Karabakh independence referendum is held, with 99.98% voting in favor of independence.

Q3538392.name: Kandyan Convention
Q3538392.blurb: Signing of the Kandyan Convention treaty by British invaders and the leaders of the Kingdom of Kandy.

Q3539853.name: Battle of Ngọc Hồi–Đống Đa
Q3539853.blurb: Tây Sơn forces emerge victorious against Qing armies and liberate the capital Thăng Long.

Q3540197.name: Third English Civil War
Q3540197.blurb: Castle Cornet in Guernsey, the last stronghold which had supported the King in the Third English Civil War, surrenders.

Q3542881.name: Battle of Ware Bottom Church
Q3542881.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Ware Bottom Church: In the Virginia Bermuda Hundred campaign, 10,000 troops fight in this Confederate victory.

Q3544130.name: 856 Damghan earthquake
Q3544130.blurb: Damghan earthquake: An earthquake near the Persian city of Damghan kills an estimated 200,000 people, the sixth deadliest earthquake in recorded history.

Q3545065.name: Battle of Grahovac
Q3545065.blurb: Montenegrin forces under Grand Duke Mirko Petrović-Njegoš defeat an Ottoman army under Hussein Pasha in the battle of Grahovac. The battle is a significant step towards formal independence and quickly becomes a part of national folklore.

Q3545134.name: 1959 Hebgen Lake earthquake
Q3545134.blurb: Quake Lake is formed by the magnitude 7.2 1959 Hebgen Lake earthquake near Hebgen Lake in Montana.

Q3545524.name: Manila Peninsula rebellion
Q3545524.blurb: During their trial for the 2003 Oakwood mutiny, Philippine soldiers led by Senator Antonio Trillanes mutinied and seized a conference room at The Peninsula Manila in Makati.

Q3547325.name: adding machine
Q3547325.blurb: The first successful adding machine in the United States is patented by William Seward Burroughs.

Q3548032.name: July Ultimatum
Q3548032.blurb: July Crisis: Austria-Hungary issues a series of demands in an ultimatum to the Kingdom of Serbia demanding Serbia to allow the Austrians to determine who assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand. Serbia accepts all but one of those demands and Austria declares war on July 28.

Q3550076.name: Union of Brittany and France
Q3550076.blurb: Union of Brittany and France: The Duchy of Brittany is absorbed into the Kingdom of France.

Q3551767.name: First Mass in the Philippines
Q3551767.blurb: Ferdinand Magellan and members of his crew participated in the first Catholic Mass in the Philippines.

Q3553264.name: 1995 Paris Metro bombings
Q3553264.blurb: A gas bottle explodes in Saint Michel station of line B of the RER (Paris regional train network). Eight are killed and 80 wounded.

Q3555069.name: Cyprus Convention
Q3555069.blurb: Cyprus Convention: The Ottoman Empire cedes Cyprus to the United Kingdom but retains nominal title.

Q3555354.name: 2009 Peruvian political crisis
Q3555354.blurb: After 65 straight days of civil disobedience, at least 31 people are killed in clashes between security forces and indigenous people near Bagua, Peru.

Q3557524.name: Capture of Klisura Pass
Q3557524.blurb: World War II: The Greek army captures Kleisoura.

Q3559235.name: Battle of Nicopolis
Q3559235.blurb: The forces of Ali Pasha of Janina defeat the French and capture the town of Preveza in the Battle of Nicopolis.

Q3560385.name: 1966 Syrian coup d'état
Q3560385.blurb: In Syria, Ba'ath Party member Salah Jadid leads an intra-party military coup that replaces the previous government of General Amin al-Hafiz, also a Baathist.

Q3561500.name: Vive le Québec libre
Q3561500.blurb: During an official state visit to Canada, French President Charles de Gaulle declares to a crowd of over 100,000 in Montreal: Vive le Québec libre! ("Long live free Quebec!"); the statement angered the Canadian government and many Anglophone Canadians.

Q3562565.name: Air Moorea Flight 1121
Q3562565.blurb: Air Moorea Flight 1121 crashes after takeoff from Moorea Airport in French Polynesia, killing all 20 people on board.

Q3562567.name: Avioimpex Flight 110
Q3562567.blurb: North Macedonia's deadliest aviation disaster occurs when Avioimpex Flight 110, a Yakovlev Yak-42, crashes near Ohrid Airport, killing all 116 people on board.

Q3562568.name: Air France Flight 117
Q3562568.blurb: Air France Flight 117 crashes on approach to Pointe-à-Pitre International Airport in Guadeloupe, killing 112 people.

Q3562572.name: Inex-Adria Aviopromet Flight 1308
Q3562572.blurb: Inex-Adria Aviopromet Flight 1308, a McDonnell Douglas MD-80, crashes in Corsica, killing all 180 people on board.

Q3562580.name: Flight 2605 by Western Airlines
Q3562580.blurb: Western Airlines Flight 2605 crashes on landing in Mexico City, killing 73 people.

Q3562612.name: Qantas Flight 72
Q3562612.blurb: Qantas Flight 72 experiences an in-flight upset near Learmonth, Victoria, Australia, injuring 112.

Q3562629.name: XL Airways Germany Flight 888T
Q3562629.blurb: XL Airways Germany Flight 888T: An Airbus A320 performing a flight test crashes near the French commune of Canet-en-Roussillon, killing all seven people on board.

Q3562643.name: Eastern Air Lines Flight 980
Q3562643.blurb: Eastern Air Lines Flight 980 crashes into Mount Illimani in Bolivia, killing all 29 aboard.

Q3565040.name: Wadōkaichin
Q3565040.blurb: Copper coins are minted in Japan for the first time (Traditional Japanese date: August 10, 708).

Q3565441.name: Battle of Guruslău
Q3565441.blurb: Long War: Austria captures Transylvania in the Battle of Goroszló.

Q3566435.name: Czechoslovak Constitution of 1920
Q3566435.blurb: The Czechoslovak National Assembly adopts the Constitution.

Q3566884.name: Evangelos Florakis Naval Base explosion
Q3566884.blurb: Ninety-eight containers of explosives self-detonate killing 13 people in Zygi, Cyprus.

Q3566941.name: We choose to go to the Moon
aliases: Address at Rice University on the Nation's Space Effort
Q3566941.blurb: In a speech at Rice Stadium in Houston, U.S. president John F. Kennedy reiterated an aspiration to land a man on the Moon before 1970 (video featured).

Q3586280.name: 1905 Alberta general election
Q3586280.blurb: The Province of Alberta, Canada, holds its first general election.

Q3586421.name: 1976 Quebec general election
Q3586421.blurb: René Lévesque and the Parti Québécois take power to become the first Quebec government of the 20th century clearly in favor of independence.

Q3586439.name: 1944 Saskatchewan general election
Q3586439.blurb: In the Saskatchewan general election, the CCF, led by Tommy Douglas, is elected and forms the first socialist government in North America.

Q3586943.name: 1936 Spanish general election
Q3586943.blurb: The Popular Front wins the 1936 Spanish general election.

Q3588238.name: Richard Riot
Q3588238.blurb: Ice hockey fans in Montreal rioted to protest the suspension of Montreal Canadiens star Maurice Richard for hitting an official.

Q3588241.name: Baltimore riot of 1861
Q3588241.blurb: American Civil War: Baltimore riot of 1861: A pro-Secession mob in Baltimore attacks United States Army troops marching through the city.

Q3588245.name: Koza riot
Q3588245.blurb: Koza riot: After a series of hit-and-runs and other vehicular incidents involving American service personnel, roughly 5,000 Okinawans take to the streets, clashing with American law enforcement in protest against the U.S. occupation of Okinawa.

Q3591470.name: 1985 United States – Canadian tornado outbreak
Q3591470.blurb: United States–Canada tornado outbreak: Forty-one tornadoes hit Ohio, Pennsylvania, New York, and Ontario, leaving 76 dead.

Q3591480.name: 1902 eruption of Santa María
Q3591480.blurb: Guatemala's Santa María volcano begins to erupt, becoming the third-largest eruption of the 20th century.

Q3591483.name: 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora
Q3591483.blurb: Mount Tambora (pictured) in Indonesia began the most powerful volcanic eruption in recorded history, killing at least 71,000 people and affecting temperatures worldwide.

Q3591485.name: 1888 eruption of Mount Bandai
Q3591485.blurb: The stratovolcano Mount Bandai erupts, killing approximately 500 people in Fukushima Prefecture, Japan.

Q3591486.name: 1792 eruption of Mount Unzen
Q3591486.blurb: A lava dome collapses on Mount Unzen, near the city of Shimbara on the Japanese island of Kyūshū, creating a deadly tsunami that killed nearly 15,000 people.

Q3592743.name: June 1962 Alcatraz escape
Q3592743.blurb: Frank Morris, John Anglin and Clarence Anglin allegedly become the only prisoners to escape from the prison on Alcatraz Island.

Q3595843.name: 2010 Pune bombing
Q3595843.blurb: A bomb explodes in the city of Pune, Maharashtra, India, killing 17 and injuring 60 more.

Q3610236.name: 1982 British Army Gazelle friendly fire incident
Q3610236.blurb: Falklands War: The Royal Navy destroyer HMS Cardiff engaged and destroyed a British Army helicopter in a friendly-fire incident.

Q3611049.name: Everett Massacre
Q3611049.blurb: The Everett massacre takes place in Everett, Washington as political differences lead to a shoot-out between the Industrial Workers of the World organizers and local police.

Q3623133.name: Armistice of Bologna
Q3623133.blurb: War of the First Coalition: Napoleon signed the Armistice of Bologna, agreeing a ceasefire between France and the Papal States.

Q3625432.name: Siege of Mirandola
Q3625432.blurb: The Italian Duchy of Mirandola surrenders to the Pope.

Q3625539.name: Siege of Uthman
Q3625539.blurb: After a prolonged siege by rebels who demand his abdication, caliph Uthman is assassinated as the rebels enter his palace.

Q3628440.name: athletics at the 1968 Summer Olympics – men's long jump
aliases: athletics at the 1968 Summer Olympics - men's long jump
Q3628440.blurb: At the Summer Olympics in Mexico City, American athlete Bob Beamon (pictured) achieved a distance of 8.90 m (29.2 ft) in the long jump event, setting a world record that stood for 23 years.

Q3628531.name: athletics at the 1960 Summer Olympics – men's marathon
aliases: athletics at the 1960 Summer Olympics - men's marathon
Q3628531.blurb: Running barefoot in the marathon event at the Rome Olympics, Abebe Bikila became the first athlete from sub-Saharan Africa to win an Olympic gold medal.

Q3628839.name: Lathen train collision
Q3628839.blurb: Twenty-three people were killed in a maglev train collision in Lathen, Germany.

Q3629102.name: 2003 Nasiriyah bombing
Q3629102.blurb: Iraq War: In Nasiriyah, Iraq, at least 23 people, among them the first Italian casualties of the 2003 invasion of Iraq, are killed in a suicide bomb attack on an Italian police base.

Q3629959.name: 1991 Uttarkashi earthquake
Q3629959.blurb: An earthquake struck the Indian state of Uttarakhand, killing at least 768 people and destroying thousands of homes.

Q3636256.name: Battle of Aubers Ridge
Q3636256.blurb: World War I: British forces launched the Battle of Aubers, an offensive on the Western Front, as part of the larger Second Battle of Artois.

Q3636296.name: Battle of Coyotepe Hill
Q3636296.blurb: U.S. forces defeat Nicaraguan rebels at the Battle of Coyotepe Hill.

Q3636319.name: Battle of Alexandria
Q3636319.blurb: Mark Antony wins a final cavalry battle against Octavian in the battle of Alexandria, but his infantry is defeated and the next day his fleet and troops start to desert to Octavian.

Q3636337.name: Alid revolt of 762–763
aliases: Revolt of Muhammad the Pure Soul
Q3636337.blurb: Following the Battle of Bakhamra between Alids and Abbasids near Kufa, the Alid rebellion ends with the death of Ibrahim, brother of Isa ibn Musa.

Q3636355.name: Battle of Broodseinde
Q3636355.blurb: World War I: The Battle of Broodseinde is fought between the British and German armies in Flanders.

Q3636370.name: Battle of Carlow
Q3636370.blurb: United Irishmen Rebellion: Battle of Carlow begins; executions of suspected rebels at Carnew and at Dunlavin Green take place.

Q3636391.name: Battle of Khotyn
Q3636391.blurb: Second Battle of Khotyn in Ukraine: Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth forces under the command of Jan Sobieski defeat the Ottoman army. In this battle, rockets made by Kazimierz Siemienowicz are successfully used.

Q3636398.name: Battle of Cisterna
Q3636398.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Cisterna, part of Operation Shingle, begins in central Italy.

Q3636438.name: Battle of Fort George
Q3636438.blurb: War of 1812: In Canada, American forces capture Fort George.

Q3636616.name: Operation Fustian
Q3636616.blurb: World War II: Operation Fustian, an Allied operation to capture the Primosole Bridge in Sicily, was launched.

Q3641960.name: Bombing of Rome in World War II
Q3641960.blurb: World War II: Rome is heavily bombed by more than 500 Allied aircraft, inflicting thousands of casualties.

Q3645480.name: Mexican general election, 2000
Q3645480.blurb: Vicente Fox Quesada is elected the first President of México from an opposition party, the Partido Acción Nacional, after more than 70 years of continuous rule by the Partido Revolucionario Institucional, in the 2000 Mexican general election.

Q3646805.name: 1920 Gori earthquake
Q3646805.blurb: An earthquake kills between 114 and 130 in Georgia and heavily damages the town of Gori.

Q3647744.name: Battle of Avay
Q3647744.blurb: Paraguayan War: Brazilian troops defeat the Paraguayan Army at the Battle of Avay.

Q3647761.name: Treaty of Asunción
aliases: Treaty Establishing a Common Market Between the Argentine Republic, the Federative Republic of Brazil, the Republic of Paraguay and the Eastern Republic of Uruguay
Q3647761.blurb: Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay and Paraguay sign the Treaty of Asunción, establishing Mercosur, the South Common Market.

Q3648797.name: 1991 Georgian independence referendum
Q3648797.blurb: Georgian independence referendum: Nearly 99 percent of the voters support the country's independence from the Soviet Union.

Q3651327.name: 1990 Georgian Supreme Soviet election
Q3651327.blurb: Georgia holds its only free election under Soviet rule.

Q3651696.name: Anglo-French War of 1778–1783
Q3651696.blurb: Anglo-French War: Having established an alliance with the United States, France invaded the Caribbean island of Dominica and captured its British fort.

Q3653895.name: 1971 Ugandan coup d'état
Q3653895.blurb: Idi Amin leads a coup deposing Milton Obote and becomes Uganda's president.

Q3656148.name: Deepwater Horizon explosion
Q3656148.blurb: An explosion on Deepwater Horizon, an offshore rig in the Gulf of Mexico, resulted in the largest marine oil spill in history.

Q3656504.name: Battle of Västerås
Q3656504.blurb: Swedish War of Liberation: Swedish troops defeat a Danish force in the Battle of Västerås.

Q3657999.name: Novye Aldi massacre
Q3657999.blurb: Russian forces massacre at least 60 civilians in the Novye Aldi suburb of Grozny, Chechnya.

Q3661284.name: 1952 Severo-Kurilsk tsunami
Q3661284.blurb: An earthquake struck the Kamchatka Peninsula, triggering a major tsunami that affected the Kuril Islands and other parts of the Pacific Ocean.

Q3662192.name: Continental Express Flight 2574
Q3662192.blurb: Continental Express Flight 2574 crashes in Colorado County, Texas, near Eagle Lake, killing 11 passengers and three crew.

Q3666607.name: Erzincan earthquake of 1992
Q3666607.blurb: The Mw 6.6 Erzincan earthquake strikes eastern Turkey with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VIII (Severe).

Q3667179.name: Erzurum earthquake of 1983
Q3667179.blurb: A magnitude 6.6 earthquake in the Turkish provinces of Erzurum and Kars leaves approximately 1,340 people dead.

Q3671565.name: Uludere airstrike
Q3671565.blurb: Kurdish–Turkish conflict: Acting on information that Kurdish militants were crossing the border from Iraqi territory, two Turkish F-16 jets fired at a group of villagers, killing 34 people.

Q3675479.name: 1997 military memorandum
Q3675479.blurb: A Turkish military memorandum results in the collapse of the coalition government in Turkey.

Q3677176.name: Cinema Statuto fire
Q3677176.blurb: A cinema fire in Turin, Italy, kills 64 people.

Q3677888.name: Hakkari earthquake of 1930
Q3677888.blurb: The 7.1 Mw Salmas earthquake shakes northwestern Iran and southeastern Turkey with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent). Up to three-thousand people were killed.

Q3678419.name: Karlıova earthquake of 1949
Q3678419.blurb: The 6.7 Ms Karlıova earthquake shakes eastern Turkey with a maximum Mercalli intensity of X (Extreme), leaving 320–450 dead.

Q3686286.name: 1159 papal election
Q3686286.blurb: Pope Alexander III was chosen to succeed of Adrian IV in a disputed election.

Q3686843.name: Tiepolo conspiracy
Q3686843.blurb: The Tiepolo conspiracy, seeking to seize power in the Republic of Venice, is thwarted after bloody street clashes in Venice. The suppression of the revolt will lead to the creation of the Council of Ten.

Q3687154.name: Muslim conquest of Sicily
Q3687154.blurb: Arab–Byzantine wars: The city of Syracuse was captured by the Aghlabids (pictured) as part of the Muslim conquest of Sicily.

Q3704511.name: Decimal Day
Q3704511.blurb: The decimalisation of the currencies of the United Kingdom and Ireland is completed on Decimal Day.

Q3704801.name: Capture of Salvador
Q3704801.blurb: Dutch–Portuguese War: Portuguese and Spanish forces recaptured the Brazilian city of Bahia, which had previously been captured by the Dutch Republic.

Q3709255.name: Cavalese cable car disaster
Q3709255.blurb: Forty-two people die in the Cavalese cable car disaster, the deadliest cable car accident in history.

Q3718431.name: Fragheto massacre
Q3718431.blurb: In the Fragheto massacre, soldiers belonging to the German 356th Infantry Division kill 30 Italian civilians and 15 partisans near Casteldelci in central-northern Italy.

Q3718434.name: Kindu atrocity
Q3718434.blurb: Thirteen Italian Air Force servicemen, deployed to the Congo as a part of the UN peacekeeping force, are massacred by a mob in Kindu.

Q3718708.name: 62 Pompeii earthquake
Q3718708.blurb: An earthquake with an estimated intensity between IX or X on the Mercalli scale occurs in Pompeii, Italy.

Q3722103.name: 1088 papal election
Q3722103.blurb: Election of Urban II as the 159th Pope of the Catholic Church. He is best known for initiating the Crusades.

Q3722531.name: 1989 Brazilian presidential election
Q3722531.blurb: Fernando Collor de Mello defeats Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the second round of the Brazilian presidential election, becoming the first democratically elected President in almost 30 years.

Q3722557.name: 2000 Yugoslavian general election
Q3722557.blurb: Colour revolutions: During protests over irregularities in the Yugoslavian general election, a wheel-loader was driven into the Radio Television of Serbia building, giving the protests the nickname "Bulldozer Revolution".

Q3727894.name: 2012 Tel Aviv bus bombing
Q3727894.blurb: At least 28 are wounded after a bomb is thrown onto a bus in Tel Aviv.

Q3735267.name: attempted assassination of Leonid Brezhnev
Q3735267.blurb: Soviet leader Leonid Brezhnev (pictured) survived what was seen as an assassination attempt, an incident that was not revealed to the public until after the fall of the Soviet Union.

Q3736097.name: Soviet OMON assaults on Lithuanian border posts
Q3736097.blurb: Soviet Special Purpose Police Unit troops killed seven Lithuanian customs officials in Medininkai in the most serious attack of their campaign against Lithuanian border posts.

Q3738423.name: Siege of Tartu
Q3738423.blurb: The Livonian Brothers of the Sword, a Catholic military order, occupy Tarbatu (today Tartu) as part of the Livonian Crusade.

Q3742303.name: Finnair Flight 405
Q3742303.blurb: Finnair Flight 405 is hijacked by Aarno Lamminparras in Oulu, Finland.

Q3744498.name: Tartu Offensive
Q3744498.blurb: World War II: Soviet forces capture the city of Tartu, Estonia.

Q3745599.name: 1990 FIFA World Cup Final
Q3745599.blurb: West Germany win the FIFA World Cup final against defending champions Argentina, with Andreas Brehme scoring the game's only goal.

Q3750271.name: Kiss nightclub fire
Q3750271.blurb: Two hundred and forty-two people die in a nightclub fire in the Brazilian city of Santa Maria, Rio Grande do Sul.

Q3751758.name: Santoña Agreement
Q3751758.blurb: Spanish Civil War: the Basque Army surrenders to the Italian Corpo Truppe Volontarie following the Santoña Agreement.

Q3757546.name: Galeas per montes
Q3757546.blurb: The Peace of Cremona ends the war between the Republic of Venice and the Duchy of Milan, after the victorious Venetian enterprise of military engineering of the Galeas per montes.

Q3769089.name: Second Fitna
Q3769089.blurb: Second Fitna: Pro-Alid forces defeated the Umayyad Caliphate at the Battle of Khazir, allowing them to take control of Mosul in present-day Iraq.

Q3771812.name: 2009 Massereene Barracks shooting
Q3771812.blurb: Massereene Barracks shooting: The Real Irish Republican Army kills two British soldiers and injures two other soldiers and two civilians at Massereene Barracks, the first British military deaths in Northern Ireland since the end of The Troubles.

Q3773859.name: Anarchist insurrection of January 1933
Q3773859.blurb: Anarchist insurrection of January 1933 breaks out in Barcelona, Spain.

Q3775537.name: New York Conspiracy of 1741
Q3775537.blurb: New York governor George Clarke's complex at Fort George is burned in an arson attack, starting the New York Conspiracy of 1741.

Q3775989.name: Battle of Sauchieburn
Q3775989.blurb: The Battle of Sauchieburn is fought between rebel Lords and James III of Scotland, resulting in the death of the king.

Q3777641.name: Miami Showband killings
Q3777641.blurb: The Troubles: Three members of a popular cabaret band and two gunmen are killed during a botched paramilitary attack in Northern Ireland.

Q3778598.name: Italo-Ethiopian War of 1887–1889
Q3778598.blurb: The Treaty of Wuchale was signed, ending the Italo-Ethiopian War, but differences in translation later led to another war.

Q3778609.name: Despenser War
Q3778609.blurb: Despenser War: A royalist army defeated troops loyal to Thomas, 2nd Earl of Lancaster, in the Battle of Boroughbridge, which allowed King Edward II of England to hold on to power for another five years.

Q3778618.name: Lancastrian War
Q3778618.blurb: The English invasion of France begins when English king Henry V lands in France.

Q3778732.name: Byzantine–Venetian War of 1296–1302
Q3778732.blurb: The Byzantine–Venetian War comes to an end.

Q3778746.name: Sioux Wars
Q3778746.blurb: The First Sioux War begins when United States Army soldiers kill Lakota chief Conquering Bear and in return are massacred.

Q3780506.name: Operation Red Dawn
Q3780506.blurb: Iraq War: Operation Red Dawn: Former Iraqi President Saddam Hussein is captured near his home town of Tikrit.

Q3780839.name: Treaty of Blois
Q3780839.blurb: England and France sign an alliance against Spain in the treaty of Blois.

Q3788426.name: Battle of Turtle Gut Inlet
Q3788426.blurb: The first privateer battle of the American Revolutionary War, the Battle of Turtle Gut Inlet, was fought near Cape May, New Jersey (map of location, pictured).

Q3792606.name: Glasnost Meeting
Q3792606.blurb: The "glasnost meeting" took place in Moscow, becoming the first demonstration in the Soviet Union after World War II and marking the beginning of the civil rights movement in the country.

Q3797641.name: Sabena Flight 503
Q3797641.blurb: Twenty-nine people are killed when Sabena Flight 503 crashes into Monte Terminillo near Rieti, Italy.

Q3797657.name: Airbus Industrie Flight 129
Q3797657.blurb: An Airbus A330-300 crashes during a test flight at Toulouse–Blagnac Airport, killing all seven people on board.

Q3797766.name: coronation of Elizabeth II
aliases: Coronation of Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom
Coronation of Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom
Q3797766.blurb: The coronation of Queen Elizabeth II at Westminster Abbey becomes the first British coronation, and one of the first major international events, to be televised.

Q3798246.name: 1958 Venezuelan coup d'état
Q3798246.blurb: After a general uprising and rioting in the streets, President Marcos Pérez Jiménez leaves Venezuela.

Q3800671.name: The Nixon Interviews
Q3800671.blurb: The first of The Nixon Interviews (12 will be recorded over four weeks) is videotaped with British journalist David Frost interviewing former United States President Richard Nixon about the Watergate scandal and the Nixon tapes.

Q3809270.name: abolition of the Ottoman caliphate
Q3809270.blurb: Abolition of the Ottoman sultanate: The last sultan of the Ottoman Empire, Mehmed VI, abdicates.

Q3809499.name: 2000 UEFA Cup final riots
Q3809499.blurb: Arsenal and Galatasaray fans clash in the 2000 UEFA Cup Final riots in Copenhagen.

Q3809578.name: 2013 Uribana prison riot
Q3809578.blurb: At least 50 people are killed and 120 people are injured in a prison riot in Barquisimeto, Venezuela.

Q3813618.name: July 1936 military uprising in Barcelona
Q3813618.blurb: The July 1936 military uprising in Barcelona begins.

Q3815421.name: Dominican Restoration War
Q3815421.blurb: The Dominican Restoration War begins when Gregorio Luperón raises the Dominican flag in Santo Domingo after Spain had recolonized the country.

Q3817010.name: Operation Deadstick
Q3817010.blurb: World War II: Capture of the Caen canal and Orne river bridges by British paratroopers, also known as Operation Coup de Main (incorrectly referred to as Operation Deadstick.)

Q3817182.name: Battle of Araviana
Q3817182.blurb: An Aragonese cavalry force defeats a superior Castilian cavalry force in the Battle of Araviana during the War of the Two Peters.

Q3817235.name: Battle of Manolada
Q3817235.blurb: The Burgundian and Majorcan claimants of the Principality of Achaea meet in the Battle of Manolada.

Q3817778.name: Anglo-Cherokee War
Q3817778.blurb: Anglo-Cherokee War: Cherokee warriors defeat British forces at the Battle of Echoee near present-day Otto, North Carolina.

Q3820587.name: Siege of the Castle of Saint George
Q3820587.blurb: A joint Venetian–Spanish fleet captures the Castle of St. George on the island of Cephalonia.

Q3820712.name: Siege of Paysandú
Q3820712.blurb: Uruguayan War: The Siege of Paysandú ends as the Brazilians and Coloradans capture Paysandú, Uruguay.

Q3846240.name: Bombing of Wieluń
Q3846240.blurb: German forces attacked multiple locations in Poland, including Wieluń and Westerplatte, starting World War II in Europe.

Q3849563.name: Siege of Jerusalem
Q3849563.blurb: Siege of Jerusalem: The city surrenders to the Khwarazmiyya, ending Christian control of the Jerusalem for the next 672 years.

Q3850896.name: Columbine Mine massacre
Q3850896.blurb: Columbine Mine massacre: Striking coal miners are allegedly attacked with machine guns by a detachment of Colorado state police dressed in civilian clothes.

Q3850904.name: Fântâna Albă massacre
Q3850904.blurb: Fântâna Albă massacre: Between two hundred and two thousand Romanian civilians are killed by Soviet Border Troops.

Q3854317.name: Battle of Marais des Cygnes
Q3854317.blurb: American Civil War: During Price's Missouri Expedition, Union troops defeated Sterling Price's Confederate army in three successive battles: Marais des Cygnes, Mine Creek, and Marmiton River.

Q3860401.name: history of Portugal (1834–1910)
Q3860401.blurb: History of Portugal: The first attempt at a Portuguese republican revolution breaks out in the northern city of Porto.

Q3863238.name: death of Benito Mussolini
Q3863238.blurb: World War II: Benito Mussolini, the deposed fascist dictator of Italy, was executed by partisans in Giulino.

Q3866667.name: SCAT Airlines Flight 760
Q3866667.blurb: SCAT Airlines Flight 760 crashes near the Kazakh city of Almaty, killing 21 people.

Q3873368.name: Tragedy of Otranto
Q3873368.blurb: In the Tragedy of Otranto, the Italian Navy vessel Sibilla collided with the Albanian civilian vessel Kateri i Radës, causing the latter to sink and leading to dozens of deaths.

Q3874682.name: 2008 riot in Mongolia
Q3874682.blurb: Riots erupt in Mongolia in response to allegations of fraud surrounding the 2008 legislative elections.

Q3875690.name: 16th Street Baptist Church bombing
Q3875690.blurb: Baptist Church bombing: Four children are killed in the bombing of an African-American church in Birmingham, Alabama, United States.

Q3881008.name: De Bono's invasion of Abyssinia
Q3881008.blurb: Second Italo-Abyssinian War: Italy invades Ethiopia.

Q3882202.name: assassination of Anna Politkovskaya
Q3882202.blurb: Anna Politkovskaya (pictured), a Russian journalist and human-rights activist, was assassinated in the elevator of her apartment block in Moscow.

Q3882218.name: Bro of Tupac Shakur
Q3882218.blurb: American rapper Tupac Shakur (pictured) was shot by an unknown assailant in Las Vegas, dying from his injuries six days later.

Q3883948.name: Operation Chopper
Q3883948.blurb: Vietnam War: Operation Chopper, the first American combat mission and first American helicopter assault in the war, takes place.

Q3883950.name: Operation Colossus
Q3883950.blurb: In the first airborne operation undertaken by the British military, a small force of paratroopers landed near Calitri, Italy, to destroy an aqueduct.

Q3885257.name: Fall of the Fascist regime in Italy
Q3885257.blurb: World War II: The Allied invasion of Sicily begins, leading to the downfall of Mussolini and forcing Hitler to break off the Battle of Kursk.

Q3885396.name: Ordinance of Nullification
Q3885396.blurb: South Carolina passes the Ordinance of Nullification, declaring that the Tariffs of 1828 and 1832 were null and void in the state, beginning the Nullification Crisis.

Q3915497.name: final offensive of the Spanish Civil War
Q3915497.blurb: Nationalist forces began their final offensive of the Spanish Civil War, at the end of which they controlled almost the entire country.

Q3921580.name: First Battle of Passchendaele
Q3921580.blurb: World War I: The First Battle of Passchendaele takes place resulting in the largest single-day loss of life in New Zealand history.

Q3927614.name: Nazi book burnings
aliases: Destruction of Jewish books during the Holocaust
Q3927614.blurb: Censorship: In Germany, the Nazis stage massive public book burnings.

Q3930436.name: Raid of the Ghetto of Rome
Q3930436.blurb: Holocaust in Italy: Raid on the Roman Ghetto.

Q3931610.name: United Kingdom European Communities membership referendum, 1975
Q3931610.blurb: The United Kingdom holds its first country-wide referendum on membership of the European Economic Community (EEC).

Q3944738.name: Anglo-French blockade of the Río de la Plata
aliases: Anglo-French blockade of the Rio de la Plata
Q3944738.blurb: Anglo-French blockade of the Río de la Plata: Battle of Vuelta de Obligado.

Q3944788.name: Event Horizon Telescope
aliases: First image of a black hole
First picture of a black hole
Q3944788.blurb: Scientists from the Event Horizon Telescope project released the first image of the black hole at the center of the galaxy M87.

Q3944923.name: 2012 Caracas prison riot
Q3944923.blurb: A prison riot in the Venezuelan capital, Caracas, kills at least 20 people.

Q3950956.name: Battle of Qatwan
Q3950956.blurb: Yelü Dashi, the Liao dynasty general who founded the Qara Khitai, defeats the Seljuq and Kara-Khanid forces at the Battle of Qatwan.

Q3951255.name: Landings at Cape Torokina
Q3951255.blurb: World War II: A U.S. Navy task force turned away an Imperial Japanese Navy formation at the Battle of Empress Augusta Bay, thus protecting the landings at Cape Torokina.

Q3952696.name: 2008 UEFA Cup Final riots
Q3952696.blurb: Battle of Piccadilly Gardens in Manchester city centre between Zenit supporters and Rangers supporters and the Greater Manchester Police; 39 policemen injured, one police dog injured and 39 arrested.

Q3952797.name: Niterói circus fire
Q3952797.blurb: Niterói circus fire: Fire breaks out during a performance by the Gran Circus Norte-Americano in the city of Niterói, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, killing more than 500.

Q3953976.name: Second Battle of Villers-Bretonneux
Q3953976.blurb: World War I: First tank-to-tank combat, during the second Battle of Villers-Bretonneux. Three British Mark IVs meet three German A7Vs.

Q3960716.name: Silvertown explosion
Q3960716.blurb: Silvertown explosion: A blast at a munitions factory in London kills 73 and injures over 400. The resulting fire causes over £2,000,000 worth of damage.

Q3966440.name: Portolà expedition
Q3966440.blurb: An expedition led by Gaspar de Portolá leaves its base in San Diego and sets out to find the Port of Monterey (now Monterey, California).

Q3966442.name: 1954 Italian Karakoram expedition to K2
Q3966442.blurb: A team of Italian climbers became the first to reach the summit of K2, the world's second-highest mountain.

Q3975695.name: 1990 Italian Air Force MB-326 crash
Q3975695.blurb: A military jet of the Italian Air Force, abandoned by its pilot after an on-board fire, crashed into a high school near Bologna, Italy, killing 12 students and injuring 88 other people.

Q3975725.name: 1973 Rome airport attack and hijacking
Q3975725.blurb: Thirty passengers are killed in an attack by Palestinian terrorists on Rome's Leonardo da Vinci–Fiumicino Airport.

Q3975763.name: massacre of Via D'Amelio
Q3975763.blurb: A car bomb kills Judge Paolo Borsellino and five members of his escort.

Q3984673.name: 1638 Calabrian earthquakes
Q3984673.blurb: The first of four destructive Calabrian earthquakes strikes southern Italy. Measuring magnitude 6.8 and assigned a Mercalli intensity of XI, it kills 10,000–30,000 people.

Q3984693.name: 1883 Casamicciola earthquake
Q3984693.blurb: A moderate earthquake measuring magnitude 4.3–5.2 strikes the Italian island of Ischia, killing over 2,300 people.

Q3984715.name: 1481 Rhodes earthquake
Q3984715.blurb: The largest of three earthquakes strikes the island of Rhodes and causes an estimated 30,000 casualties.

Q3997251.name: Green Cross Tragedy
Q3997251.blurb: LAN-Chile Flight 621 crashes in the Andes mountains, killing 21 people, including Argentinian football player Eliseo Mouriño.

Q4016225.name: Aero Trasporti Italiani Flight 460
Q4016225.blurb: Aero Trasporti Italiani Flight 460 crashes near Conca di Crezzo, Italy, killing all 37 people on board.

Q4016228.name: Air India Flight 101
Q4016228.blurb: Air India Flight 101 crashes into Mont Blanc.

Q4016236.name: Cebu Pacific Flight 387
Q4016236.blurb: Cebu Pacific Flight 387 crashes into Mount Sumagaya in the Philippines, killing all 104 people on board.

Q4025998.name: United States 1–0 England
Q4025998.blurb: The United States defeated England during the FIFA World Cup in one of the greatest upsets in the competition's history.

Q4036598.name: Cosmic Call
Q4036598.blurb: The 70-metre Yevpatoria Planetary Radar sends a METI message (Cosmic Call 2) to five stars: Hip 4872, HD 245409, 55 Cancri (HD 75732), HD 10307 and 47 Ursae Majoris (HD 95128). The messages will arrive to these stars in 2036, 2040, 2044, and 2049, respectively.

Q4041231.name: Tampere conference of 1905
aliases: 1st Conference of the Russian Social Democratic Labour Party
Q4041231.blurb: The Tampere conference, where Vladimir Lenin and Joseph Stalin meet for the first time, is held in Tampere, Finland.

Q4055755.name: 2011 Antonov An-148 crash
Q4055755.blurb: An Antonov An-148 crashes in Russia's Alexeyevsky District, Belgorod Oblast during a test flight, killing all seven aboard.

Q4055757.name: Pulkovo Aviation Enterprise Flight 9560
Q4055757.blurb: Pulkovo Aviation Enterprise Flight 9560 crashes after takeoff from Sheremetyevo International Airport in Moscow, Russia, killing 14 of the 16 people on board.

Q4055760.name: 1981 Pushkin Tu-104 crash
Q4055760.blurb: A plane crash at Pushkin Airport kills 50 people, including 16 members of the Pacific Fleet.

Q4055762.name: Aeroflot Flight 6502
Q4055762.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 6502 crashes while landing at Kuibyshev Airport (now Kuromoch International Airport) in Kuibyshev (now present-day Samara, Russia), killing 70 people.

Q4055763.name: Aeroflot Flight 5463
Q4055763.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 5463 crashes into Dolan Mountain while approaching Almaty International Airport in present-day Kazakhstan, killing all 90 people on board.

Q4055767.name: Baikal Airlines Flight 130
Q4055767.blurb: Baikal Airlines Flight 130 crashes near Mamoney, Irkutsk, Russia, resulting in 125 deaths.

Q4055770.name: Aeroflot Flight 7425
Q4055770.blurb: An Aeroflot Tupolev Tu-154 stalls and crashes near Uchkuduk, Uzbekistan (then part of the Soviet Union), killing all 200 people on board in the USSR's worst-ever airline disaster.

Q4055775.name: JS Air Flight 201
Q4055775.blurb: JS Air Flight 201 crashes after takeoff from Jinnah International Airport in Karachi, Pakistan, killing all 21 aboard.

Q4055776.name: Agni Air Flight 101
Q4055776.blurb: Agni Air Flight 101 crashes near Shikharpur, Makwanpur, Nepal, killing all 14 people on board.

Q4055779.name: 1950 Sverdlovsk air disaster
Q4055779.blurb: In the Sverdlovsk air disaster, all 19 of those on board are killed, including almost the entire national ice hockey team (VVS Moscow) of the Soviet Air Force – 11 players, as well as a team doctor and a masseur.

Q4055780.name: 1961 Yuba City B-52 crash
Q4055780.blurb: A USAF B-52 bomber carrying nuclear weapons crashes near Yuba City, California.

Q4055781.name: 2011 Chinook shootdown in Afghanistan
Q4055781.blurb: War in Afghanistan: A United States military helicopter is shot down, killing 30 American special forces members and a working dog, seven Afghan soldiers, and one Afghan civilian. It was the deadliest single event for the United States in the War in Afghanistan.

Q4055782.name: 1961 Ndola United Nations DC-6 crash
Q4055782.blurb: An aircraft crashed near Ndola in Northern Rhodesia, resulting in the deaths of 16 people, including United Nations secretary-general Dag Hammarskjöld.

Q4055786.name: 1961 Goldsboro B-52 Crash
Q4055786.blurb: Goldsboro B-52 crash: A bomber carrying two H-bombs breaks up in mid-air over North Carolina. The uranium core of one weapon remains lost.

Q4055787.name: Cyprus Airways Flight 284
Q4055787.blurb: A bomb explodes on board Cyprus Airways Flight 284 while flying over the Mediterranean Sea, killing 66.

Q4062556.name: Treaty of Allahabad
Q4062556.blurb: Treaty of Allahabad is signed. The Treaty marks the political and constitutional involvement and the beginning of Company rule in India.

Q4064874.name: 1919 United States anarchist bombings
Q4064874.blurb: Anarchists simultaneously set off bombs in eight separate U.S. cities.

Q4068786.name: Simon de Montfort's Parliament
Q4068786.blurb: The first English parliament to include not only Lords but also representatives of the major towns holds its first meeting in the Palace of Westminster, now commonly known as the "Houses of Parliament".

Q4069143.name: Arzamas train disaster
Q4069143.blurb: Three cars on a train carrying hexogen to Kazakhstan explode in Arzamas, Gorky Oblast, USSR, killing 91 and injuring about 1,500.

Q4071388.name: Japan Airlines Flight 2
Q4071388.blurb: Japan Air Lines Flight 2 accidentally ditches in San Francisco Bay while on approach to San Francisco International Airport. No one is injured.

Q4071933.name: Battle of Sullivan's Island
Q4071933.blurb: American Revolutionary War: The Battle of Sullivan's Island ends with the American victory, leading to the commemoration of Carolina Day.

Q4077534.name: Baptist War
Q4077534.blurb: The Great Jamaican Slave Revolt begins; up to 20% of Jamaica's slaves mobilize in an ultimately unsuccessful fight for freedom.

Q4087313.name: Battle of Peking
Q4087313.blurb: Battle of Peking: The Eight-Nation Alliance occupies Beijing, China, in a campaign to end the bloody Boxer Rebellion in China.

Q4087314.name: Battle of Kępa Oksywska
Q4087314.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Kępa Oksywska concludes, with Polish losses reaching roughly 14% of all the forces engaged.

Q4087354.name: Battle on Pyana River
Q4087354.blurb: Russian troops are defeated by forces of the Blue Horde Khan Arapsha in the Battle on Pyana River.

Q4087392.name: Battle of Perehonivka
Q4087392.blurb: The Revolutionary Insurgent Army of Ukraine defeated the White Russian Volunteer Army at the Battle of Peregonovka.

Q4087407.name: Battle of Adramyttium
Q4087407.blurb: Latin forces under Henry of Flanders defeat a Nicaean army under Constantine Laskaris in the Battle of Adramyttion.

Q4087408.name: Battle of Alford
Q4087408.blurb: Wars of the Three Kingdoms: Battle of Alford.

Q4087410.name: Battle of Marj Ardabil
Q4087410.blurb: Battle of Marj Ardabil: The Khazars annihilate an Umayyad army and kill its commander, al-Jarrah ibn Abdallah al-Hakami.

Q4087424.name: Battle of Inverlochy
Q4087424.blurb: Wars of the Three Kingdoms: In Scotland, the Battle of Inverlochy results in a Royalist/Irish victory.

Q4087431.name: Battle of Carbisdale
Q4087431.blurb: The Battle of Carbisdale: A Royalist army from Orkney invades mainland Scotland but is defeated by a Covenanter army.

Q4087434.name: Battle of Kilsyth
Q4087434.blurb: A Royalist army under the Marquess of Montrose defeats a Covenanter army in the battle of Kilsyth.

Q4087439.name: Battle of Langside
Q4087439.blurb: Mary, Queen of Scots, is defeated at the Battle of Langside, part of the civil war between Queen Mary and the supporters of her son, James VI.

Q4087464.name: Battle of Samugarh
Q4087464.blurb: Battle of Samugarh: Decisive battle in the struggle for the throne during the Mughal war of succession (1658–1659).

Q4087469.name: Battle of Tippermuir
Q4087469.blurb: Battle of Tippermuir: James Graham, 1st Marquess of Montrose defeats the Earl of Wemyss's Covenanters, reviving the Royalist cause.

Q4087476.name: Battle of Philiphaugh
Q4087476.blurb: Wars of the Three Kingdoms: Scottish Royalists are defeated by Covenanters at the Battle of Philiphaugh.

Q4090317.name: Battle of Machias
Q4090317.blurb: The Battle of Machias, the first naval engagement of the American Revolutionary War, commenced in and around the port of Machias in what is now eastern Maine.

Q4090467.name: Chenogne massacre
Q4090467.blurb: World War II: In retaliation for the massacre of captured Americans by Waffen SS soldiers, U.S. Army personnel killed an estimated 80 Wehrmacht prisoners near Chenogne, Belgium.

Q4093055.name: bombing of Helsinki in World War II
Q4093055.blurb: World War II: The Great Raids Against Helsinki begins.

Q4110397.name: 2008 Minsk bombing
Q4110397.blurb: A bomb explodes at a concert in Minsk's Independence Square, injuring 50 people.

Q4110406.name: Torre Ejecutiva Pemex explosion
Q4110406.blurb: A gas leak underneath the Pemex Executive Tower in Mexico City caused an explosion (aftermath pictured) that killed at least 37 people and injured another 121.

Q4110453.name: Capture of Malacca
Q4110453.blurb: Afonso de Albuquerque of Portugal conquers Malacca, the capital of the Malacca Sultanate.

Q4114548.name: 1996 Nigerien coup d'état
Q4114548.blurb: In a military coup, Colonel Ibrahim Baré Maïnassara deposes the first democratically elected president of Niger, Mahamane Ousmane.

Q4114551.name: 1958 Pakistani coup d'état
Q4114551.blurb: The 1958 Pakistani coup d'état inaugurates a prolonged period of military rule.

Q4114552.name: 1977 Pakistani military coup
Q4114552.blurb: The Pakistan Armed Forces under Muhammad Zia-ul-Haq seize power in Operation Fair Play and begin 11 years of martial law. Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, the first elected Prime Minister of Pakistan, is overthrown.

Q4115029.name: seizure of Abu Musa and the Greater and Lesser Tunbs
Q4115029.blurb: Iran seizes the Greater and Lesser Tunbs from the Emirates of Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah.

Q4115048.name: 2004 Morocco earthquake
Q4115048.blurb: The 6.3 Mw Al Hoceima earthquake strikes northern Morocco with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent). At least 628 people are killed, 926 are injured, and up to 15,000 are displaced.

Q4115361.name: Åbo Bloodbath
Q4115361.blurb: Åbo Bloodbath: Fourteen noblemen who opposed Duke Charles are decapitated in the Old Great Square of Turku (Swedish: Åbo) for their involvement in the War against Sigismund.

Q4115703.name: 1992 Cairo earthquake
Q4115703.blurb: A 5.8 earthquake occurred in Cairo, Egypt. At least 510 died.

Q4115715.name: Operation Nimble Archer
Q4115715.blurb: The United States Navy conducts Operation Nimble Archer, an attack on two Iranian oil platforms in the Persian Gulf.

Q4115786.name: TWA Flight 903
Q4115786.blurb: TWA Flight 903 crashes near Itay El Barud, Egypt, killing all 55 aboard.

Q4115893.name: Egyptian raid on Larnaca International Airport
Q4115893.blurb: Egyptian forces raid Larnaca International Airport in an attempt to intervene in a hijacking, without authorisation from the Republic of Cyprus authorities. The Cypriot National Guard and Police forces kill 15 Egyptian commandos and destroy the Egyptian C-130 transport plane in open combat.

Q4115899.name: 2008 Egyptian general strike
Q4115899.blurb: The 2008 Egyptian general strike starts led by Egyptian workers later to be adopted by April 6 Youth Movement and Egyptian activists.

Q4116108.name: Canal Hotel bombing
Q4116108.blurb: A truck-bomb attack on United Nations headquarters in Iraq kills the agency's top envoy Sérgio Vieira de Mello and 21 other employees.

Q4116581.name: 2012 Turkish F-4 Phantom shootdown
Q4116581.blurb: A Turkish Air Force McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom II fighter plane is shot down by the Syrian Armed Forces, killing both of the plane's pilots and worsening already-strained relations between Turkey and Syria.

Q4117937.name: Libyan Arab Airlines Flight 1103
Q4117937.blurb: During approach to Tripoli International Airport, a Boeing 727 operating as Libyan Arab Airlines Flight 1103 collides in mid-air with a Libyan Air Force Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23, killing 157 people.

Q4118051.name: First Battle of Bud Dajo
Q4118051.blurb: Moro Rebellion: United States Army troops bring overwhelming force against the native Moros in the First Battle of Bud Dajo, leaving only six survivors.

Q4118294.name: Klaipėda Convention
Q4118294.blurb: The Klaipėda Convention is signed formally incorporating Klaipėda Region (Memel Territory) into Lithuania. It would come back to Germany in 1939.

Q4118471.name: 1959 Turkish Airlines Gatwick crash
Q4118471.blurb: A Turkish Airlines Vickers Viscount crashes near Gatwick Airport, killing 14; Turkish prime minister Adnan Menderes survives the crash.

Q4118683.name: Siege of Algeciras
Q4118683.blurb: Spanish Reconquista: the forces of the Kingdom of Castile initiate the ultimately futile Siege of Algeciras against the Emirate of Granada.

Q4118844.name: Sack of Baltimore
Q4118844.blurb: The Sack of Baltimore: The Irish village of Baltimore is attacked by Barbary slave traders.

Q4119077.name: United Air Lines Flight 608
Q4119077.blurb: United Air Lines Flight 608 crashes in the Bryce Canyon National Park in Garfield County, Utah, while attempting an emergency landing at Bryce Canyon Airport, killing 52 people.

Q4120018.name: Marias Massacre
Q4120018.blurb: American Indian Wars: In the Marias Massacre, the United States Army killed about 200 Piegan Blackfeet, mostly women, children, and the elderly.

Q4120079.name: Operation Soap
Q4120079.blurb: Operation Soap: The Metropolitan Toronto Police Force raids four gay bathhouses in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, arresting just under 300, triggering mass protest and rallies.

Q4120226.name: 17 July Revolution
Q4120226.blurb: Abdul Rahman Arif is overthrown and the Ba'ath Party is installed as the governing power in Iraq with Ahmed Hassan al-Bakr as the new Iraqi President.

Q4120811.name: Siege of Corfu
Q4120811.blurb: The Russo-Ottoman siege of Corfu ends with the surrender of the French garrison.

Q4120993.name: Tashkent earthquake (1966)
Q4120993.blurb: The magnitude 5.1 Tashkent earthquake affects the largest city in Soviet Central Asia with a maximum MSK intensity of VII (Very strong). Tashkent is mostly destroyed and 15–200 are killed.

Q4126349.name: Jack Cade's Rebellion
Q4126349.blurb: Jack Cade and his followers enter London unhindered by the government of king Henry VI.

Q4126745.name: Eighth Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
aliases: 8th Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
Q4126745.blurb: Ireland votes to repeal the Eighth Amendment of their constitution that prohibits abortion in all but a few cases, choosing to replace it with the Thirty-sixth Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland.

Q4128034.name: Second Battle of Kernstown
Q4128034.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Kernstown: Confederate General Jubal Early defeats Union troops led by General George Crook in an effort to keep them out of the Shenandoah Valley.

Q4130830.name: Concert of The Hague
Q4130830.blurb: In the Concert of The Hague, the Dutch Republic, the Commonwealth of England and the Kingdom of France set out their views on how the Second Northern War should end.

Q4132794.name: 2008 Chatsworth train collision
Q4132794.blurb: The 2008 Chatsworth train collision in Los Angeles between a Metrolink commuter train and a Union Pacific freight train kills 25 people.

Q4135498.name: Luby's massacre
Q4135498.blurb: George Hennard runs amok in Killeen, Texas, killing 23 and wounding 20.

Q4139793.name: Lithuanian independence referendum, 1991
Q4139793.blurb: Dissolution of the Soviet Union: Voters in Lithuania vote for independence from the Soviet Union.

Q4141167.name: Shakee Massacre
Q4141167.blurb: Shameen Incident: British Army and French Army soldiers stationed in the concession of Shameen open fire on Chinese protesters, resulting in at least 52 deaths.

Q4141460.name: Second Battle of Athenry
Q4141460.blurb: The Second Battle of Athenry takes place near Athenry during the Bruce campaign in Ireland.

Q4157877.name: Monetary reform in Russia, 1998
Q4157877.blurb: Following a currency reform, Russia begins to circulate new rubles to stem inflation and promote confidence.

Q4158587.name: deportation of the Kalmyks
Q4158587.blurb: Soviet authorities launch Operation Ulussy, beginning the deportation of the Kalmyk nation to Siberia and Central Asia.

Q4160483.name: Georgetown-IBM experiment
Q4160483.blurb: Georgetown–IBM experiment: The first public demonstration of a machine translation system is held in New York at the head office of IBM.

Q4162202.name: Pinnacle Airlines Flight 3701
Q4162202.blurb: Pinnacle Airlines Flight 3701 crashes in Jefferson City, Missouri. The two pilots (the aircraft's only occupants) are killed.

Q4162685.name: Rwandan Revolution
Q4162685.blurb: Dominique Mbonyumutwa, one of the few Hutu sub-chiefs in colonial Rwanda, was attacked by Tutsi activists, precipitating the Rwandan Revolution.

Q4166560.name: 1975 Beirut bus massacre
Q4166560.blurb: Beirut bus massacre: A confrontation between Phalangist paramilitaries and PLO militia marks the start of the 15-year Lebanese Civil War.

Q4167569.name: Illinois campaign
Q4167569.blurb: American Revolutionary War: U.S. forces under George Clark capture Kaskaskia during the Illinois campaign.

Q4170280.name: exhumation of Richard III of England
aliases: exhumation and reburial of Richard III of England
Q4170280.blurb: The skeleton of King Richard III of England was discovered under a car park in Leicester.

Q4187825.name: 2004 Fallujah ambush
Q4187825.blurb: Iraq War in Anbar Province: In Fallujah, Iraq, four American private military contractors working for Blackwater USA, are killed after being ambushed.

Q4188866.name: 1988 Ordzhonikidze bus hijacking
Q4188866.blurb: Five armed men hijacked a bus carrying schoolchildren and a teacher in Ordzhonikidze (now Vladikavkaz, Russia), and were later given an Ilyushin Il-76 aircraft and ransom for the release of the hostages.

Q4188867.name: Capture of Sint Eustatius
Q4188867.blurb: American Revolutionary War: British forces seize the Dutch-owned Caribbean island Sint Eustatius.

Q4189392.name: UTAGE Flight 141
Q4189392.blurb: UTA Flight 141, a Boeing 727-223, crashes at the Cotonou Airport in Benin, killing 141 people.

Q4190996.name: Land Run of 1893
Q4190996.blurb: Settlers make a land run for prime land in the Cherokee Strip in Oklahoma.

Q4191053.name: 1139 Ganja earthquake
Q4191053.blurb: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake strikes the Caucasus mountains in the Seljuk Empire, causing mass destruction and killing up to 300,000 people.

Q4191082.name: 1692 Jamaica earthquake
Q4191082.blurb: An earthquake registering approximately 7.5 Mw caused Port Royal, Jamaica, to sink below sea level and killed approximately 5,000 people.

Q4200400.name: impeachment of Bill Clinton
Q4200400.blurb: The Senate trial in the impeachment of U.S. President Bill Clinton begins.

Q4200836.name: Indo-Pakistani Naval War of 1971
Q4200836.blurb: The PNS Ghazi, a Pakistan Navy submarine, sinks during the course of the Indo-Pakistani Naval War of 1971.

Q4201115.name: Trial of Joan of Arc
Q4201115.blurb: The trial of Joan of Arc begins in Rouen.

Q4202299.name: Wounded Knee incident
Q4202299.blurb: A 71-day standoff between federal authorities and the American Indian Movement members occupying the Pine Ridge Reservation at Wounded Knee, South Dakota ends with the surrender of the militants.

Q4202305.name: 1981 Armenia mid-air collision
Q4202305.blurb: A Canadair CL-44 and Sukhoi Su-15 collide in mid-air near Yerevan, Armenia, killing four.

Q4202311.name: Iraqi attack on USS Stark
Q4202311.blurb: An Iraqi jet fired two Exocet missiles at the American frigate USS Stark, killing 37 personnel and injuring 21 others.

Q4204624.name: Battle of Lake Pontchartrain
Q4204624.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Captain William Pickles of the Continental Navy boarded and captured the British sloop HMS West Florida at the Battle of Lake Pontchartrain.

Q4204647.name: 1833 Sumatra earthquake
Q4204647.blurb: A massive undersea earthquake, estimated magnitude between 8.7 and 9.2, rocks Sumatra, producing a massive tsunami all along the Indonesian coast.

Q4205186.name: Beaumont children disappearance
Q4205186.blurb: The three Beaumont children disappear from a beach in Glenelg, South Australia, resulting in one of the country's largest-ever police investigations.

Q4205775.name: June Uprising in Lithuania
Q4205775.blurb: The Lithuanian Activist Front declares independence from the Soviet Union and forms the Provisional Government of Lithuania; it lasts only briefly as the Nazis will occupy Lithuania a few weeks later.

Q4207409.name: expulsion of Asians from Uganda
Q4207409.blurb: Ugandan President Idi Amin announces that Uganda is no longer responsible for the care of British subjects of Asian origin, beginning the expulsions of Ugandan Asians.

Q4207890.name: Martinair Flight 138
Q4207890.blurb: Martinair Flight 138 crashes into the Saptha Kanya mountain range in Maskeliya, Sri Lanka, killing 191.

Q4208419.name: Sampit conflict
Q4208419.blurb: Sampit conflict: Inter-ethnic violence between Dayaks and Madurese breaks out in Sampit, Central Kalimantan, Indonesia, ultimately resulting in more than 500 deaths and 100,000 Madurese displaced from their homes.

Q4208426.name: Battle of Pasir Panjang
Q4208426.blurb: World War II: Battle of Pasir Panjang contributes to the fall of Singapore.

Q4217215.name: 1972 Svetlogorsk An-24 crash
Q4217215.blurb: An Antonov An-24 crashes into a kindergarten building in Svetlogorsk, killing 35.

Q4217221.name: Pakistan International Airlines Flight 705
Q4217221.blurb: One hundred twenty-one people are killed when Pakistan International Airlines Flight 705 crashes at Cairo International Airport.

Q4217224.name: Aeroflot Flight 2808
Q4217224.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 2808 crashes on approach to Ivanovo Yuzhny Airport, killing all 84 aboard.

Q4217227.name: 2002 Khankala Mi-26 crash
Q4217227.blurb: Khankala Mi-26 crash: A Russian Mil Mi-26 helicopter carrying troops is hit by a Chechen missile outside Grozny, killing 118 soldiers.

Q4219257.name: 1911 Kebin earthquake
Q4219257.blurb: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake destroys the city of Almaty in Russian Turkestan.

Q4231480.name: Synod of Constantinople (1484)
Q4231480.blurb: Under the influence of the Ottoman government, patriarch Symeon I convenes a synod of the Eastern Orthodox Churches in Constantinople which defines the ritual for admitting Catholics to the Eastern Orthodox Churches and condemns the church union of Ferrara-Florence.

Q4231692.name: Iranian Islamic Republic referendum, March 1979
Q4231692.blurb: Iran becomes an Islamic republic by a 99% vote, officially overthrowing the Shah.

Q4231925.name: Iranian constitutional referendum, December 1979
Q4231925.blurb: Following the result of a two-day referendum, the current Constitution of Iran was adopted.

Q4233963.name: coronation of Nicholas II and Alexandra Feodorovna
Q4233963.blurb: Nicholas II is crowned as the last Tsar of Imperial Russia.

Q4242644.name: Sukkur rail disaster
Q4242644.blurb: In Pakistan's deadliest train accident an overloaded passenger train collides with an empty freight train, resulting in 307 deaths and 700 injuries.

Q4261519.name: MGM Grand fire
Q4261519.blurb: A deadly fire breaks out at the MGM Grand Hotel in Paradise, Nevada (now Bally's Las Vegas). Eighty-five people are killed and more than 650 are injured in the worst disaster in Nevada history.

Q4261830.name: TACA Flight 390
Q4261830.blurb: TACA Flight 390 overshoots the runway at Toncontín International Airport in Tegucigalpa, Honduras and crashes, killing five people.

Q4272689.name: Liaoshen Campaign
Q4272689.blurb: The People's Liberation Army launched the Liaoshen campaign, the first of the three major military campaigns during the late stage of the Chinese Civil War.

Q4273067.name: Dutch pacification campaign on Formosa
Q4273067.blurb: Dutch pacification campaign on Formosa: Soldiers from the Dutch East India Company (flag depicted) razed the village of Mattau, now part of modern-day Tainan, Taiwan.

Q4283206.name: March of the Iron Will
Q4283206.blurb: March of the Iron Will: Italian troops occupy Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

Q4296967.name: Battle of Fairfax Court House
Q4296967.blurb: The first land battle of the American Civil War after Fort Sumter took place in the village of Fairfax, Virginia.

Q4296979.name: Battle of Vienna
Q4296979.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Vienna, Virginia.

Q4298662.name: Young Turk Revolution of 1908
Q4298662.blurb: Start of the Young Turk Revolution in the Ottoman Empire, forcing Sultan Abdul Hamid II leads to restore the Constitution of 1876 and reconvene the parliament.

Q4301653.name: Mongol conquest of Anatolia
Q4301653.blurb: Mongol conquest of Anatolia: Mongols achieved a decisive victory over the Seljuk Turks, leading to the decline and disintegration of the Seljuk state.

Q4305909.name: German referendum of 1934
Q4305909.blurb: The German referendum of 1934 approves Adolf Hitler's appointment as head of state with the title of Führer.

Q4312941.name: Galashki ambush
Q4312941.blurb: Second Chechen War: Chechen separatists ambush Russian paramilitary forces in the Republic of Ingushetia.

Q4335259.name: Operation Grand Slam
Q4335259.blurb: India retaliates following Pakistan's Operation Grand Slam which results in the Indo-Pakistani War of 1965 that ends in a stalemate followed by the signing of the Tashkent Declaration.

Q4335282.name: Operation Pocket Money
Q4335282.blurb: Vietnam War: U.S. President Richard Nixon announces his order to place naval mines in major North Vietnamese ports in order to stem the flow of weapons and other goods to that nation.

Q4335318.name: Operation Chengiz Khan
Q4335318.blurb: Indo-Pakistani War of 1971: Pakistan launches a pre-emptive strike against India and a full-scale war begins.

Q4335326.name: Samashki massacre
Q4335326.blurb: First Chechen War: Russian paramilitary troops begin a massacre of civilians in Samashki, Chechnya.

Q4337398.name: Siege of Malacca
Q4337398.blurb: Dutch–Portuguese War: The Dutch siege of Malacca against the Portuguese ended when Dutch troops seized the city's citadel (depicted).

Q4337436.name: Siege of the International Legations
Q4337436.blurb: Armies of the Eight-Nation Alliance capture Tientsin during the Boxer Rebellion.

Q4338038.name: Ottoman–Mamluk War of 1516–17
Q4338038.blurb: Second Ottoman–Mamluk War: Mamluks fail to stop the Ottoman advance towards Egypt at the Battle of Yaunis Khan.

Q4340192.name: Cornwallis's Retreat
Q4340192.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: In what became known as Cornwallis's Retreat, a British Royal Navy squadron led by Vice Admiral William Cornwallis strongly resists a much larger French Navy force and withdraws largely intact, setting up the French Navy defeat at the Battle of Groix six days later.

Q4340680.name: Federation Treaty
Q4340680.blurb: The Treaty of Federation is signed in Moscow.

Q4346080.name: VASP Flight 168
Q4346080.blurb: VASP Flight 168 crashes in Pacatuba, Ceará, Brazil, killing 128 people.

Q4346140.name: February 2013 nor'easter
Q4346140.blurb: A blizzard kills at least 18 and leaves hundreds of thousands of people without electricity in the northeastern United States and parts of Canada.

Q4346961.name: RAF Fauld explosion
Q4346961.blurb: World War II: RAF Fauld explosion: An explosion at a Royal Air Force ammunition dump in Staffordshire kills seventy people.

Q4348111.name: Pingjin Campaign
Q4348111.blurb: Chinese Civil War: The Communist forces take over Tianjin from the Nationalist government.

Q4348117.name: German occupation of Latvia during World War II
Q4348117.blurb: The Holocaust: During the German occupation of Latvia, a number of synagogues in Riga were set on fire, killing many Jews who were confined within.

Q4349327.name: 1993 Latur earthquake
Q4349327.blurb: The 6.2 Mw Latur earthquake shakes Maharashtra, India with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VIII (Severe) killing 9,748 and injuring 30,000.

Q4349848.name: Government of Ireland Bill 1886
Q4349848.blurb: William Ewart Gladstone introduces the first Irish Home Rule Bill into the British House of Commons.

Q4350095.name: 1962 Burmese coup d'état
Q4350095.blurb: In Burma, the army led by General Ne Win seizes power in a coup d'état.

Q4350192.name: transfer of Crimea to Ukraine
Q4350192.blurb: Transfer of Crimea: The Soviet Politburo of the Soviet Union orders the transfer of the Crimean Oblast from the Russian SFSR to the Ukrainian SSR.

Q4352718.name: 1993 Bishopsgate bombing
Q4352718.blurb: An IRA bomb devastates the Bishopsgate area of London.

Q4352841.name: 893 Dvin earthquake
Q4352841.blurb: An earthquake destroys the city of Dvin, Armenia.

Q4353495.name: Castle Hill convict rebellion
Q4353495.blurb: Castle Hill Rebellion: Irish convicts rebel against British colonial authority in the Colony of New South Wales.

Q4353506.name: 1202 B.C. Syria Earthshake
Q4353506.blurb: A major earthquake hits Syria, widely felt between Sicily and Iraq.

Q4354098.name: Partition Sejm
Q4354098.blurb: The Polish Partition Sejm met to discuss the First Partition of Poland, carried out the previous year by Russia, Prussia and Austria.

Q4354181.name: Plaza Miranda bombing
Q4354181.blurb: A bomb exploded in the Liberal Party campaign rally in Plaza Miranda, Manila, Philippines with several anti-Marcos political candidates injured.

Q4355551.name: 1997 Ardabil earthquake
Q4355551.blurb: An earthquake in northern Iran is responsible for about 1,100 deaths.

Q4361469.name: Petrozavodsk phenomenon
Q4361469.blurb: A series of celestial phenomena of disputed nature was observed in the western Soviet Union, Finland and Denmark.

Q4366141.name: Mountjoy Prison helicopter escape
Q4366141.blurb: Three Provisional Irish Republican Army members escaped from Mountjoy Prison in Dublin aboard a hijacked helicopter that landed in the prison's exercise yard.

Q4366914.name: St Scholastica Day riot
Q4366914.blurb: The St Scholastica Day riot breaks out in Oxford, England, leaving 63 scholars and perhaps 30 locals dead in two days.

Q4368592.name: 1995 Baku Metro fire
Q4368592.blurb: The Baku Metro fire sees 289 people killed and 270 injured.

Q4368596.name: Richmond Theatre fire
Q4368596.blurb: A theater fire in Richmond, Virginia kills 72 people, including the Governor of Virginia George William Smith and the president of the First National Bank of Virginia Abraham B. Venable.

Q4368598.name: Fire in the Winter Palace
Q4368598.blurb: A fire in the Winter Palace of Saint Petersburg kills 30 guards.

Q4372935.name: Aeroflot Flight 3739
Q4372935.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 3379 is hijacked by the Ovechkin family and diverted to Veshchevo in the Soviet Union.

Q4377502.name: Razing of Kandanos
Q4377502.blurb: World War II: The Wehrmacht razes the Greek village of Kandanos to the ground and murders 180 of its inhabitants.

Q4381720.name: 1968 Democratic National Convention protest activity
Q4381720.blurb: Police and protesters clash during 1968 Democratic National Convention protests as protesters chant "The whole world is watching".

Q4388358.name: Huế Phật Đản shootings
Q4388358.blurb: South Vietnamese soldiers under the Roman Catholic President Ngo Dinh Diem open fire on Buddhists defying a ban on the flying of the Buddhist flag on Vesak, killing nine and sparking the Buddhist crisis.

Q4389204.name: 1855 Ansei Edo earthquake
Q4389204.blurb: A powerful earthquake occurs in Edo, Japan, causing considerable damage in the Kantō region from the shaking and subsequent fires. It had a death toll of 7,000–10,000 people and destroyed around 14,000 buildings.

Q4390259.name: breakup of Yugoslavia
aliases: Causes of the breakup of Yugoslavia
Q4390259.blurb: Breakup of Yugoslavia: With the local Serb population boycotting the referendum, Croatians voted in favour of independence from Yugoslavia.

Q4391287.name: Battle of Brier Creek
Q4391287.blurb: American Revolutionary War: The Continental Army is routed at the Battle of Brier Creek near Savannah, Georgia.

Q4398181.name: Peace Mission 2005
Q4398181.blurb: The first-ever joint military exercise between Russia and China, called Peace Mission 2005 begins.

Q4400513.name: Russian polar expedition of 1900–02
Q4400513.blurb: Baron Eduard Toll, leader of the Russian Polar Expedition of 1900, departs Saint Petersburg in Russia on the explorer ship Zarya, never to return.

Q4402025.name: 1930 Argentine coup
Q4402025.blurb: Democratically elected Argentine president Hipólito Yrigoyen is deposed in a military coup.

Q4410330.name: Great New Orleans Fire
Q4410330.blurb: A fire in New Orleans leaves most of the town in ruins.

Q4412151.name: Northern Taurida Operation
Q4412151.blurb: Russian Civil War: The Russian Army retreats to Crimea, after a successful offensive by the Red Army and Revolutionary Insurgent Army of Ukraine.

Q4412225.name: Aimo Cajander's third cabinet
Q4412225.blurb: World War II: A day after the beginning of the Winter War in Finland, the Cajander III Cabinet resigns and is replaced by the Ryti I Cabinet, while the Finnish Parliament move from Helsinki to Kauhajoki to escape the Soviet airstrikes.

Q4414118.name: Bolivian National Revolution (1952-1964)
Q4414118.blurb: Bolivian National Revolution: Rebels take over Palacio Quemado.

Q4416705.name: Serbian–Ottoman Wars
Q4416705.blurb: Serbia declares war on the Ottoman Empire, leading to the Serbian Wars for Independence.

Q4422669.name: 2013 conclave
Q4422669.blurb: The 2013 papal conclave elects Cardinal Jorge Mario Bergoglio taking the name Pope Francis as the 266th Pope of the Catholic Church.

Q4424090.name: Kenneth Arnold UFO sighting
Q4424090.blurb: Kenneth Arnold makes the first widely reported UFO sighting near Mount Rainier, Washington.

Q4424402.name: death and state funeral of Boris Yeltsin
Q4424402.blurb: Boris Yeltsin's funeral: The first to be sanctioned by the Russian Orthodox Church for a head of state since the funeral of Emperor Alexander III in 1894.

Q4426783.name: 1979 U.S. embassy burning in Islamabad
Q4426783.blurb: The United States Embassy in Islamabad, Pakistan, is attacked by a mob and set on fire, killing four.

Q4431988.name: The X Factor
aliases: The Brittish X Factor (British TV series)
The X Factor (United Kingdom TV series)
The X Factor - The Greatest Hits
The X Factor – The Greatest Hits
Q4431988.blurb: The English-Irish boy band One Direction were formed while auditioning for the 2010 series of the British singing competition The X Factor.

Q4438364.name: Battle of Lost River
Q4438364.blurb: The Modoc War begins with the Battle of Lost River.

Q4438386.name: Battle of the Big Hole
Q4438386.blurb: American Indian Wars: Battle of the Big Hole: A small band of Nez Percé Indians clash with the United States Army.

Q4438421.name: Battle of Chaffin's Farm
Q4438421.blurb: The Battle of Chaffin's Farm is fought in the American Civil War.

Q4438423.name: Battle of Zhangjiawan
Q4438423.blurb: Second Opium War: Battle of Zhangjiawan: Now heading towards Beijing after having recently occupied Tianjin, the allied Anglo-French force engages and defeats a larger Qing Chinese army at Zhangjiawan.

Q4442934.name: 1988 Black Sea bumping incident
Q4442934.blurb: Cold War: The 1988 Black Sea bumping incident: The U.S. missile cruiser USS Yorktown (CG-48) is intentionally rammed by the Soviet frigate Bezzavetnyy in the Soviet territorial waters, while Yorktown claims innocent passage.

Q4446152.name: Jurchen campaigns against the Song dynasty
Q4446152.blurb: Jin–Song Wars: Invading Jurchen soldiers from the Jin dynasty besiege and sack Bianjing (Kaifeng), the capital of the Song dynasty of China, and abduct Emperor Qinzong of Song and others, ending the Northern Song period.

Q4449390.name: Battle of Montgomery's Tavern
Q4449390.blurb: The Battle of Montgomery's Tavern, the only battle of the Upper Canada Rebellion, takes place in Toronto, where the rebels are quickly defeated.

Q4450183.name: Tacnazo
Q4450183.blurb: El Tacnazo:  Francisco Morales Bermúdez, Peruvian Prime Minister carries out a coup d'état in the city of Tacna, forcing the sitting President of Peru, Juan Velasco Alvarado, to resign and assuming his place as the new President.

Q4450643.name: 1916 United States House of Representatives elections
aliases: United States House of Representatives elections, 1916
Q4450643.blurb: In the congressional elections, Jeannette Rankin became the first woman elected to the United States House of Representatives.

Q4451428.name: resignation of Pope Benedict XVI
Q4451428.blurb: The Vatican confirms that Pope Benedict XVI will resign the papacy as a result of his advanced age.

Q4456251.name: 2009 Karachi bombing
Q4456251.blurb: Forty-three people die in a suicide bombing in Karachi, Pakistan, where Shia Muslims are observing the Day of Ashura.

Q4461528.name: Totskoye nuclear exercise
Q4461528.blurb: In a top secret nuclear test, a Soviet Tu-4 bomber drops a 40 kiloton atomic weapon just north of Totskoye village.

Q4462586.name: Third Battle of Petersburg
Q4462586.blurb: American Civil War: Defeat at the Third Battle of Petersburg forces the Army of Northern Virginia and the Confederate government to abandon Richmond, Virginia.

Q4465891.name: Ottoman–Persian War of 1743–46
Q4465891.blurb: Ottoman–Persian War: In the Battle of Kars, the Ottoman army is routed by Persian forces led by Nader Shah.

Q4475947.name: NATO bombing of the Radio Television of Serbia headquarters
Q4475947.blurb: NATO bombs the headquarters of Radio Television of Serbia, as part of their aerial campaign against the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

Q4484483.name: 1927 FA Cup Final
Q4484483.blurb: Cardiff City defeat Arsenal in the FA Cup Final, the only time it has been won by a team not based in England.

Q4492484.name: French constitutional referendum, October 1946
Q4492484.blurb: France adopts the constitution of the Fourth Republic.

Q4493716.name: Battle of the Buffet
Q4493716.blurb: English football club Manchester United defeated rivals Arsenal 2–0 in the Battle of the Buffet, ending the latter's record-breaking unbeaten run.

Q4493724.name: Argentina v England
Q4493724.blurb: The famous Hand of God goal, scored by Diego Maradona in the quarter-finals of the 1986 FIFA World Cup match between Argentina and England, ignites controversy. This was later followed by the Goal of the Century. Argentina wins 2–1 and later goes on to win the World Cup.

Q4497452.name: Khiva campaign (1873)
aliases: colonization of the Khanate of Khiva
Q4497452.blurb: Russian forces under General von Kaufmann capture the city of Khiva from the Khanate of Khiva.

Q4499410.name: The Holocaust in Ukraine
Q4499410.blurb: The Holocaust in Ukraine: In Terebovlia, Germans order 1,100 Jews to undress and march through the city to the nearby village of Plebanivka, where they are shot and buried in ditches.

Q4502380.name: Brazilian Military Junta of 1930
Q4502380.blurb: The Pacification Junta deposed Brazillian president Washington Luís, ending the Brazilian Revolution of 1930.

Q4515839.name: Chicago Tylenol murders
Q4515839.blurb: Tylenol products are recalled after bottles in Chicago laced with cyanide cause seven deaths.

Q4520158.name: Battle of Shanhai Pass
Q4520158.blurb: Manchu regent Dorgon defeats rebel leader Li Zicheng of the Shun dynasty at the Battle of Shanhai Pass, allowing the Manchus to enter and conquer the capital city of Beijing.

Q4540741.name: 1559 papal conclave
Q4540741.blurb: Pope Pius IV is elected, four months after his predecessor's death.

Q4546576.name: 1124 papal election
Q4546576.blurb: Lamberto Scannabecchi was elected pope, taking the name Honorius II.

Q4546888.name: 10 May 2012 Damascus bombings
Q4546888.blurb: The Damascus bombings are carried out using a pair of car bombs detonated by suicide bombers outside a military intelligence complex in Damascus, Syria, killing 55 people.

Q4547180.name: 10th United States Congress
Q4547180.blurb: The Territory of Illinois is created by the 10th United States Congress.

Q4547554.name: 1169 Sicily earthquake
Q4547554.blurb: A strong earthquake strikes the Ionian coast of Sicily, causing tens of thousands of injuries and deaths, especially in Catania.

Q4548624.name: 1293 Kamakura earthquake
Q4548624.blurb: An earthquake strikes Kamakura, Kanagawa, Japan, killing about 23,000.

Q4549356.name: 13 June 2012 Iraq attacks
Q4549356.blurb: A series of bombings across Iraq, including Baghdad, Hillah and Kirkuk, kills at least 93 people and wounds over 300 others.

Q4549898.name: 1498 Meiō earthquake
Q4549898.blurb: The Nankai tsunami washes away the building housing the Great Buddha at Kōtoku-in; it has been located outside ever since.

Q4551686.name: 1667 Shamakhi earthquake
Q4551686.blurb: A deadly earthquake rocks Shemakha in the Caucasus, killing 80,000 people.

Q4552449.name: 1712 Huilliche rebellion
Q4552449.blurb: Huilliches in Chiloé rebel against Spanish encomenderos.

Q4552537.name: 1721 Tabriz earthquake
Q4552537.blurb: A massive earthquake devastates the Iranian city of Tabriz.

Q4552629.name: 1730 Valparaíso earthquake
Q4552629.blurb: An estimated magnitude 8.7 earthquake causes a tsunami that damages more than 1,000 km (620 mi) of Chile's coastline.

Q4552666.name: 1733 slave insurrection on St. John
Q4552666.blurb: The start of the 1733 slave insurrection on St. John in what was then the Danish West Indies.

Q4552798.name: 1746 Lima - Callao earthquake
Q4552798.blurb: The 1746 Lima–Callao earthquake causes up to 6,000 deaths in Peru, the deadliest in its history up to that point.

Q4553252.name: 1783 New Jersey earthquake
Q4553252.blurb: A 5.3 magnitude earthquake strikes New Jersey.

Q4553468.name: 1797 Riobamba earthquake
Q4553468.blurb: The Riobamba earthquake strikes Ecuador, causing up to 40,000 casualties.

Q4553950.name: 1811 German Coast Uprising
Q4553950.blurb: Charles Deslondes leads an unsuccessful slave revolt in the North American settlements of St. Charles and St. James, Louisiana.

Q4554104.name: 1819 Rann of Kutch earthquake
aliases: Terremoto del Rann de Kutch de 1819
Q4554104.blurb: A major earthquake strikes the Kutch district of western India, killing over 1,543 people and raising a 6-metre-high (20 ft), 6-kilometre-wide (3.7 mi), ridge, extending for at least 80 kilometres (50 mi), that was known as the Allah Bund ("Dam of God").

Q4554596.name: 1842 Slave Revolt in the Cherokee Nation
Q4554596.blurb: A slave revolt in the Cherokee Nation commences.

Q4554827.name: 1851 Chilean Revolution
Q4554827.blurb: Conservative Santiago-based government troops defeat rebels at the Battle of Loncomilla, signaling the end of the 1851 Chilean Revolution.

Q4554936.name: 1856 Last Island hurricane
Q4554936.blurb: The Last Island hurricane strikes Louisiana, resulting in over 200 deaths.

Q4554978.name: 1858 Bradford sweets poisoning
Q4554978.blurb: Approximately 20 people die in Bradford, England, UK, after being poisoned from ingesting sweets that had been accidentally adulterated with arsenic trioxide.

Q4554983.name: 1858 Christiania fire
Q4554983.blurb: The 1858 Christiania fire severely destroys several city blocks near Stortorvet in Christiania, Norway, and about 1,000 people lose their homes.

Q4555041.name: 1860 Republican National Convention
Q4555041.blurb: United States presidential election: Abraham Lincoln wins the Republican Party presidential nomination over William H. Seward, who later becomes the United States Secretary of State.

Q4555044.name: 1860 Open Championship
Q4555044.blurb: The Open Championship, the oldest of the four major championships in men's golf, was first played at Prestwick Golf Club in Scotland.

Q4555312.name: 1871 Scotland versus England rugby union match
Q4555312.blurb: The first international rugby football match, when Scotland defeats England in Edinburgh at Raeburn Place.

Q4555458.name: 1874 Scottish Cup Final
Q4555458.blurb: Queen's Park defeated Clydesdale 2–0 in the final of the inaugural Scottish Cup.

Q4555940.name: 1883 Rochester tornado
Q4555940.blurb: An F5 tornado strikes Rochester, Minnesota, leading to the creation of the Mayo Clinic.

Q4556120.name: 1885–86 Scottish Cup
Q4556120.blurb: The Scottish Cup match between Arbroath and Bon Accord ended 36–0, which is still a world record for an unrigged professional association football match.

Q4556632.name: 1892 New Orleans general strike
Q4556632.blurb: The New Orleans general strike begins, uniting black and white American trade unionists in a successful four-day general strike action for the first time.

Q4556932.name: 1895 Ljubljana earthquake
Q4556932.blurb: The 1895 Ljubljana earthquake, both the most and last destructive earthquake in the area, occurs.

Q4557043.name: 1896 Democratic National Convention
Q4557043.blurb: William Jennings Bryan delivers his Cross of Gold speech advocating bimetallism at the 1896 Democratic National Convention in Chicago.

Q4557071.name: 1896 St. Louis – East St. Louis tornado
Q4557071.blurb: One of the deadliest and most destructive tornadoes in U.S. history struck St. Louis, Missouri, and East St. Louis, Illinois, killing more than 255 people and injuring at least 1,000 others.

Q4557319.name: 1898 Western Pennsylvania All-Star football team
