Q4557319.blurb: The Duquesne Country and Athletic Club defeats an all-star collection of early football players 16–0, in what is considered to be the first all-star game for professional American football.

Q4557405.name: 1899 New Richmond tornado
Q4557405.blurb: New Richmond tornado: The ninth deadliest tornado in U.S. history kills 117 people and injures around 200.

Q4557994.name: 1902 Guatemala earthquake
Q4557994.blurb: The 7.5 Mw Guatemala earthquake shakes Guatemala with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VIII (Severe), killing between 800 and 2,000.

Q4558378.name: 1905 Kangra earthquake
Q4558378.blurb: In India, an earthquake hits the Kangra Valley, killing 20,000, and destroying most buildings in Kangra, McLeod Ganj and Dharamshala.

Q4558563.name: 1906 Valparaíso earthquake
Q4558563.blurb: An earthquake registering approximately 8.2 Mw struck Valparaíso, Chile, killing 3,882 people.

Q4558694.name: 1907 Kingston earthquake
Q4558694.blurb: An earthquake in Kingston, Jamaica kills more than 1,000 people.

Q4558717.name: 1907 Qaratog earthquake
Q4558717.blurb: The 1907 Qaratog earthquake hits the borders of Uzbekistan and Tajikistan, killing between 12,000 and 15,000 people.

Q4558903.name: 1908 World Series
Q4558903.blurb: The Chicago Cubs defeat the Detroit Tigers, 2–0, clinching the 1908 World Series; this would be their last until winning the 2016 World Series.

Q4559130.name: 190th Fighter Squadron, Blues and Royals friendly fire incident
Q4559130.blurb: In a friendly fire incident, two American A-10 Thunderbolt II aircraft attack British tanks participating in the 2003 invasion of Iraq, killing one soldier.

Q4559319.name: 1911 Eastern North America heat wave
Q4559319.blurb: A massive heat wave strikes the northeastern United States, killing 380 people in eleven days and breaking temperature records in several cities.

Q4560078.name: 1915 Singapore Mutiny
Q4560078.blurb: Sepoys of Indian Muslim background mutinied against their British officers in Singapore.

Q4560081.name: 1915 Stanley Cup Finals
Q4560081.blurb: The Vancouver Millionaires win the 1915 Stanley Cup Final, the first championship played between the Pacific Coast Hockey Association and the National Hockey Association.

Q4560473.name: 1918 Cloquet Fire
aliases: Cloquet, Duluth, and Moose Lake Fires
Q4560473.blurb: A massive forest fire kills 453 people in Minnesota.

Q4560520.name: 1918 San Fermín earthquake
Q4560520.blurb: The 7.1 Mw San Fermín earthquake shakes Puerto Rico. The quake and resulting tsunami kill up to 116 people.

Q4560534.name: 1918 Vancouver general strike
Q4560534.blurb: The first general strike in Canadian history takes place in Vancouver.

Q4560833.name: 1920 Georgian coup attempt
Q4560833.blurb: A Bolshevik coup fails in the Democratic Republic of Georgia.

Q4560848.name: 1920 Louisiana hurricane
Q4560848.blurb: The Louisiana hurricane dissipates over Kansas after forcing around 4,500 people to evacuate and causing $1.45 million in damages.

Q4560879.name: 1920 Republican National Convention
Q4560879.blurb: During the U.S. Republican National Convention in Chicago, U.S. Republican Party leaders gather in a room at the Blackstone Hotel to come to a consensus on their candidate for the U.S. presidential election, leading the Associated Press to coin the political phrase "smoke-filled room".

Q4560986.name: 1921 Buckingham and Carnatic Mills Strike
Q4560986.blurb: Workers of Buckingham and Carnatic Mills in the city of Chennai, India, begin a four-month strike.

Q4561067.name: 1921 World Series
Q4561067.blurb: The World Series is the first to be broadcast on radio.[citation needed]

Q4561228.name: 1922 Swatow typhoon
Q4561228.blurb: A typhoon hits Shantou, Republic of China, killing more than 50,000 people.

Q4561361.name: 1923 Imperial Conference
Q4561361.blurb: The 1923 Imperial Conference opened in London.

Q4561697.name: 1925 Charlevoix–Kamouraska earthquake
Q4561697.blurb: The Charlevoix-Kamouraska earthquake strikes northeastern North America.

Q4561706.name: 1925 Dali earthquake
Q4561706.blurb: An earthquake (measuring around 7.0 magnitude) occurs in Dali, China, killing an estimated 5,000 people.

Q4562073.name: 1927 Gulang earthquake
Q4562073.blurb: Near Xining, China, an 8.3 magnitude earthquake causes 200,000 deaths in one of the world's most destructive earthquakes.

Q4562290.name: 1928 Thames flood
Q4562290.blurb: A disastrous flood of the River Thames kills 14 people and causes extensive damage to much of riverside London.

Q4562427.name: 1929 Koppeh Dagh earthquake
Q4562427.blurb: The 7.2 Mw Kopet Dag earthquake shakes the Iran–Turkmenistan border region with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent), killing up to 3,800 and injuring 1,121.

Q4562522.name: Capture of Garadaghly
Q4562522.blurb: First Nagorno-Karabakh War: Armenian troops massacre more than 20 Azerbaijani civilians during the Capture of Garadaghly.

Q4562866.name: 1931 Nicaragua earthquake
Q4562866.blurb: An earthquake in Nicaragua destroys Managua; killing 2,000.

Q4563009.name: 1932 Changma earthquake
Q4563009.blurb: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake in Gansu, China kills 275 people.

Q4563052.name: 1932 NFL Playoff Game
Q4563052.blurb: The Chicago Bears defeat the Portsmouth Spartans in the first NFL playoff game to win the NFL Championship.

Q4563086.name: 1932 Washington Bicentennial
Q4563086.blurb: The United States Post Office Department issues a set of 12 stamps commemorating the 200th anniversary of George Washington's birth.

Q4563222.name: 1933 Imperial Airways Diksmuide crash
Q4563222.blurb: After an on-board fire that may have been the first incident of airliner sabotage, the Imperial Airways biplane City of Liverpool broke apart in mid-air, killing fifteen people.

Q4563233.name: 1933 Long Beach earthquake
Q4563233.blurb: The Long Beach earthquake affects the Greater Los Angeles Area, leaving around 108 people dead.

Q4563431.name: 1934 Muroto typhoon
Q4563431.blurb: A large typhoon hits western Honshū, Japan, killing more than 3,000 people.

Q4563463.name: 1934 West Coast waterfront strike
Q4563463.blurb: "Bloody Thursday": The police open fire on striking longshoremen in San Francisco.

Q4563884.name: 1936 Tupelo–Gainesville tornado outbreak
Q4563884.blurb: Tupelo–Gainesville tornado outbreak: An F5 tornado kills 233 in Tupelo, Mississippi.

Q4564265.name: 1938 Gettysburg reunion
Q4564265.blurb: On the 75th anniversary of the end of the Battle of Gettysburg, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt dedicated the Eternal Light Peace Memorial.

Q4564585.name: 1939 Waynesburg vs. Fordham football game
Q4564585.blurb: NBC broadcasts the first televised American football game.

Q4564700.name: 1940 Brocklesby mid-air collision
Q4564700.blurb: Two Avro Ansons collide in mid-air over New South Wales, Australia, remain locked together, then land safely.

Q4564768.name: Soviet ultimatum to Lithuania
Q4564768.blurb: The Soviet Union presents an ultimatum to Lithuania, resulting in Lithuanian loss of independence.

Q4565209.name: 1943 Argentine coup d'état
Q4565209.blurb: A military coup in Argentina ousts Ramón Castillo.

Q4565545.name: 1945 El Teniente mining accident
Q4565545.blurb: The Smoke Tragedy leaves 355 workers dead in the underground copper mine of El Teniente, Chile.

Q4565608.name: 1945 Venezuelan coup d'état
Q4565608.blurb: A group of the Venezuelan Armed Forces, led by Mario Vargas, Marcos Pérez Jiménez and Carlos Delgado Chalbaud, stages a coup d'état against president Isaías Medina Angarita, who is overthrown by the end of the day.

Q4565824.name: 1946 Vancouver Island earthquake
Q4565824.blurb: The 1946 Vancouver Island earthquake strikes Vancouver Island, British Columbia, Canada.

Q4566193.name: 1948 Airborne Transport DC-3 (DST) disappearance
Q4566193.blurb: The DC-3 airliner NC16002 disappears 80 kilometres (50 mi) south of Miami.

Q4566207.name: 1948 Ashes series
Q4566207.blurb: Australia  set a world record for the highest successful run-chase in Test cricket history during the Fourth Test of the Ashes series against England.

Q4566250.name: 1948 Donora smog
Q4566250.blurb: A deadly smog event begins in Donora, Pennsylvania, eventually killing 20 and sickening thousands.

Q4566348.name: 1948 Summer Olympics torch relay
Q4566348.blurb: In Olympia, Greece, the Summer Olympics torch relay, nicknamed the "relay of peace", began.

Q4566350.name: 1948 Tinker Air Force Base tornadoes
Q4566350.blurb: The first successful tornado forecast predicts that a tornado will strike Tinker Air Force Base, Oklahoma.

Q4566609.name: 1949 Queen Charlotte Islands earthquake
Q4566609.blurb: The Queen Charlotte earthquake is Canada's strongest since the 1700 Cascadia earthquake.

Q4566775.name: 1950 Air France multiple Douglas DC-4 accidents
Q4566775.blurb: An Air France Douglas DC-4 crashes near Bahrain International Airport, killing 46 people.

Q4566785.name: 1950 Australian National Airways Douglas DC-4 crash
Q4566785.blurb: A Douglas DC-4 Skymaster aircraft crashed after departing from Perth, becoming the worst peacetime aviation accident in Australia's history.

Q4567118.name: 1951 Canadian Pacific Air Lines Douglas DC-4 disappearance
Q4567118.blurb: Canadian Pacific Air Lines Flight 3505 disappears while flying from Vancouver to Tokyo. The aircraft and its 37 occupants are never found.

Q4567214.name: 1951 Pulitzer Prize
Q4567214.blurb: Korean War: Associated Press photographer Max Desfor photographs hundreds of Korean refugees crossing a downed bridge in the Taedong River: 1951 Pulitzer Prize winner Flight of Refugees Across Wrecked Bridge in Korea.

Q4567449.name: 1952 Farnborough Airshow DH.110 crash
Q4567449.blurb: A prototype aircraft crashes at the Farnborough Airshow in Hampshire, England, killing 29 spectators and the two on board.

Q4567715.name: 1953 British Mount Everest Expedition
Q4567715.blurb: The mountaineers Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay became the first people to reach the summit of Mount Everest.

Q4567745.name: 1953 Flint – Beecher tornado
Q4567745.blurb: An F5 tornado hits Beecher, Michigan, United States, killing 116, injuring 844, and destroying 340 homes.

Q4568343.name: 1955 Cincinnati mid-air collision
Q4568343.blurb: A Martin 2-0-2 and Douglas DC-3 collide over Boone County, Kentucky, killing 15 people.

Q4568376.name: 1955 Hawaii R6D-1 crash
Q4568376.blurb: A United States Navy Douglas R6D-1 Liftmaster crashes into Hawaii's Waiʻanae Range, killing 66.

Q4568972.name: 1957 Blackbushe Viking accident
Q4568972.blurb: A Vickers VC.1 Viking crashes while attempting to return to Blackbushe Airport in Yateley, killing 34.

Q4569320.name: Catalina affair
Q4569320.blurb: Catalina affair: A Swedish DC-3 shot down by a Soviet MiG-15 in 1952 over the Baltic Sea is finally recovered after years of work.

Q4569491.name: 1958 riots in Ceylon
Q4569491.blurb: The 1958 riots in Ceylon become a watershed in the race relations of various ethnic communities of Sri Lanka. The total deaths are estimated at 300, mostly Tamils.

Q4569610.name: 1959 Daytona 500
Q4569610.blurb: Lee Petty wins the first Daytona 500.

Q4569679.name: 1959 Okinawa F-100 crash
Q4569679.blurb: A United States Air Force F-100 Super Sabre from Kadena Air Base, Okinawa, crashes into a nearby elementary school, killing 11 students plus six residents from the local neighborhood.

Q4569721.name: TAI Flight 307
Q4569721.blurb: TAI Flight 307 crashes during takeoff from Bordeaux–Mérignac Airport in Bordeaux, Nouvelle-Aquitaine, France, killing 55 people.

Q4569951.name: 1960 Ethiopian coup attempt
Q4569951.blurb: With Haile Selassie (pictured), Emperor of Ethiopia, out of the country, four conspirators staged a coup attempt to install Crown Prince Asfaw Wossen on the throne.

Q4570317.name: 1961 Derby Aviation crash
Q4570317.blurb: A Douglas Dakota IV operated by Derby Aviation (later renamed to British Midland International) crashes in Canigou, France, killing 34 people.

Q4570436.name: 2006 Trincomalee massacre of NGO workers
Q4570436.blurb: A massacre is carried out by Sri Lankan government forces, killing 17 employees of the French INGO Action Against Hunger (known internationally as Action Contre la Faim, or ACF).

Q4571060.name: 1963 BAC One-Eleven test crash
Q4571060.blurb: A BAC One-Eleven prototype airliner crashes in UK with the loss of all on board.

Q4571109.name: 1963 Honduran coup d'état
Q4571109.blurb: A violent coup in Honduras begins two decades of military rule.

Q4571240.name: 1963 Togolese coup d'état
Q4571240.blurb: Coup d'état in Togo results in the assassination of president Sylvanus Olympio.

Q4571496.name: 1964 Brazilian military regime
aliases: Foreign involvement in the 1964 Brazilian coup d'état
Golpe de estado no Brasil em 1964
Q4571496.blurb: The Brazilian Armed Forces overthrew President João Goulart, establishing a military dictatorship that lasted 21 years.

Q4571501.name: 1964 East Pakistan riots
Q4571501.blurb: Anti-Muslim riots break out in Calcutta, in response to anti-Hindu riots in East Pakistan. About one hundred people are killed.

Q4571611.name: 1964 Pulitzer Prize
Q4571611.blurb: Lee Harvey Oswald, the assassin of President John F. Kennedy, is killed by Jack Ruby on live television. Robert H. Jackson takes a photograph of the shooting that will win the 1964 Pulitzer Prize in Photography.

Q4571631.name: 1964 South Vietnamese coup
Q4571631.blurb: Having deposed them in a January coup South Vietnamese leader Nguyễn Khánh has rival Generals Trần Văn Đôn and Lê Văn Kim convicted of "lax morality".

Q4571641.name: 1964 T-39 shootdown incident
Q4571641.blurb: Three U.S. Air Force pilots aboard an unarmed T-39 Sabreliner were killed when the aircraft was shot down over Erfurt, East Germany, by a Soviet MiG-19.

Q4571935.name: 1965 Los Angeles Dodgers season
Q4571935.blurb: Juan Marichal, pitcher for the San Francisco Giants, strikes John Roseboro, catcher for the Los Angeles Dodgers, on the head with a bat, sparking a 14-minute brawl, one of the most violent on-field incidents in sports history.

Q4572004.name: 1965 San Francisco Giants season
Q4572004.blurb: Juan Marichal, pitcher for the San Francisco Giants, strikes John Roseboro, catcher for the Los Angeles Dodgers, on the head with a bat, sparking a 14-minute brawl, one of the most violent on-field incidents in sports history.

Q4572012.name: 1965 South Vietnamese coup
Q4572012.blurb: South Vietnamese Colonel Phạm Ngọc Thảo, a formerly undetected communist spy and double agent, is hunted down and killed by unknown individuals after being sentenced to death in absentia for a February 1965 coup attempt against Nguyễn Khánh.

Q4572362.name: 1966 NASA T-38 crash
Q4572362.blurb: A NASA T-38 Talon crashes into the McDonnell Aircraft factory while attempting a poor-visibility landing at Lambert Field, St. Louis, killing astronauts Elliot See and Charles Bassett.

Q4572764.name: 1967 Newark riots
Q4572764.blurb: Riots begin in Newark, New Jersey.

Q4572786.name: 1967 Pulitzer Prize
Q4572786.blurb: March Against Fear: African-American civil rights activist James Meredith is wounded in an ambush by white sniper James Aubrey Norvell. Meredith and Norvell are photographed by Jack R. Thornell, whose photo will receive the 1967 Pulitzer Prize in Photography, the last one to be awarded in the category.

Q4573221.name: 1968 Special Olympics World Summer Games
Q4573221.blurb: The first games of the Special Olympics (athletes pictured), for athletes with intellectual disabilities, were held at Soldier Field in Chicago.

Q4573472.name: 1969 Aswan Ilyushin Il-18 crash
Q4573472.blurb: A United Arab Airlines (now Egyptair) Ilyushin Il-18 crashes at Aswan International Airport, killing 100 people.

Q4573536.name: 1969 EC-121 shootdown incident
Q4573536.blurb: The EC-121 shootdown incident: North Korea shoots down a United States Navy aircraft over the Sea of Japan, killing all 31 on board.

Q4573630.name: 1969 Northern Ireland riots
Q4573630.blurb: The Troubles: British troops are deployed in Northern Ireland as political and sectarian violence breaks out, marking the start of the 37-year Operation Banner.

Q4574047.name: 1970 Lubbock tornado
Q4574047.blurb: The 1970 Lubbock tornado kills 26 and causes $250 million in damage.

Q4574199.name: 1970 Tonghai earthquake
Q4574199.blurb: A magnitude-7.1 earthquake occurred in Tonghai County, China, killing at least 15,000 people.

Q4574284.name: 1970s energy crisis
Q4574284.blurb: U.S. President Gerald Ford creates the Strategic Petroleum Reserve in response to the 1970s energy crisis.

Q4574525.name: 1971 Indian Ocean Vickers Viscount crash
Q4574525.blurb: A Merpati Nusantara Airlines Vickers Viscount crashes into the Indian Ocean near Padang, West Sumatra, Indonesia, killing all 69 people on board.

Q4574531.name: 1971 JVP Insurrection
Q4574531.blurb: In Sri Lanka, Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna launches a revolt against the United Front government of Sirimavo Bandaranaike.

Q4574780.name: Sture Murders
Q4574780.blurb: Erik XIV of Sweden and his guards murder five incarcerated Swedish nobles.

Q4574802.name: 1971 killing of Bengali intellectuals
Q4574802.blurb: Bangladesh Liberation War: Over 200 of East Pakistan's intellectuals are executed by the Pakistan Army and their local allies. (The date is commemorated in Bangladesh as Martyred Intellectuals Day.)

Q4574920.name: 1972 Aldershot bombing
Q4574920.blurb: The Official Irish Republican Army detonates a car bomb at Aldershot barracks, killing seven and injuring nineteen others.

Q4575011.name: 1972 Donegall Street bombing
Q4575011.blurb: The Troubles: The first car bombing by the Provisional IRA in Belfast kills seven people and injures 148 others in Northern Ireland.

Q4575042.name: 1972 Iran blizzard
Q4575042.blurb: The first day of the seven-day 1972 Iran blizzard, which would kill at least 4,000 people, making it the deadliest snowstorm in history.

Q4575470.name: 1973 Belmont Stakes
Q4575470.blurb: The racehorse Secretariat, of Meadow Stables (racing colors pictured), won the Belmont Stakes by 31 lengths, achieving the first American Triple Crown victory in a quarter of a century.

Q4575544.name: EgyptAir Flight 741
Q4575544.blurb: EgyptAir Flight 741 crashes into the Kyrenia Mountains in Cyprus, killing 37 people.

Q4575590.name: 1973 Kentucky Derby
Q4575590.blurb: Secretariat wins the 1973 Kentucky Derby in 1:59.4, an as-yet-unbeaten record.

Q4575699.name: 1973 Rwandan coup d'état
Q4575699.blurb: Juvénal Habyarimana (pictured) orchestrated a bloodless coup d'état of the Rwandan government and began a totalitarian dictatorship.

Q4575745.name: 1973 Thai popular uprising
Q4575745.blurb: In the Thammasat student uprising, over 100,000 people protest in Thailand against the military government. Seventy-seven are killed and 857 are injured by soldiers.

Q4575837.name: 1198 papal election
Q4575837.blurb: Lotario dei Conti was elected as Pope Innocent III; he later worked to restore papal power in Rome.

Q4576247.name: 1243 papal election
Q4576247.blurb: Election of Pope Innocent IV following the death of Pope Celestine IV in 1241.

Q4576289.name: 1974 White House helicopter incident
Q4576289.blurb: Robert K. Preston, a disgruntled U.S. Army private, buzzes the White House in a stolen helicopter.

Q4576516.name: 1975 AIA building hostage crisis
Q4576516.blurb: The Japanese Red Army takes more than 50 hostages at the AIA Building housing several embassies in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. The hostages include the U.S. consul and the Swedish Chargé d'affaires. The gunmen win the release of five imprisoned comrades and fly with them to Libya.

Q4576657.name: 1975 Kinnaur earthquake
Q4576657.blurb: An earthquake registering 6.8 Ms struck northern Himachal Pradesh in India, causing extensive damage to the region.

Q4577217.name: 1976 Moro Gulf Erdbeben
aliases: Terremoto del Golfo de Moro de 1976
Q4577217.blurb: A magnitude 7.9 earthquake hits off the coast of Mindanao, Philippines, triggering a destructive tsunami, killing between 5,000 and 8,000 people and leaving more than 90,000 homeless.

Q4577581.name: 1977 Benghazi Libyan Arab Airlines Tu-154 crash
Q4577581.blurb: A Tupolev Tu-154 crashes near Benghazi, Libya, killing 59.

Q4577608.name: 1977 Chicago Loop derailment
Q4577608.blurb: A Chicago Transit Authority elevated train rear-ends another and derails, killing 11 and injuring 180, the worst accident in the agency's history.

Q4577626.name: 1977 Dan-Air Boeing 707 crash
Q4577626.blurb: A Dan-Air Boeing 707 leased to IAS Cargo Airlines crashes on approach to Lusaka International Airport in Lusaka, Zambia, killing six people.

Q4577655.name: 1977 Hanafi Siege
Q4577655.blurb: The Hanafi Siege: In a 39-hour standoff, armed Hanafi Muslims seize three Washington, D.C., buildings.

Q4577780.name: 1977 Pulitzer Prize
Q4577780.blurb: The Pulitzer Prize winners are announced. It was the first time since 1977 that no book won the Fiction Prize.

Q4578073.name: 1978 Balkan Bulgarian Tupolev Tu-134 crash
Q4578073.blurb: A Balkan Bulgarian Airlines Tupolev Tu-134 crashes near Gabare, Bulgaria, killing 73.

Q4578676.name: 1979 Daytona 500
Q4578676.blurb: Richard Petty wins a then-record sixth Daytona 500 after leaders Donnie Allison and Cale Yarborough crash on the final lap of the first NASCAR race televised live flag-to-flag.

Q4579001.name: 1979 vote of no confidence in the Callaghan ministry
Q4579001.blurb: The British House of Commons passes a vote of no confidence against James Callaghan's government by one vote, precipitating a general election.

Q4579282.name: 1980 Kalamazoo tornado
Q4579282.blurb: An F3 tornado hits Kalamazoo County, Michigan. President Jimmy Carter declares it a federal disaster area.

Q4579410.name: 1980 State of Origin game
Q4579410.blurb: The inaugural 1980 State of Origin game is won by Queensland who defeat New South Wales 20–10 at Lang Park.

Q4580141.name: 1981 warning strike in Poland
Q4580141.blurb: The Solidarity movement in Poland stages a warning strike, in which at least 12 million Poles walk off their jobs for four hours.

Q4580321.name: 1982 Bangladesh coup d'état
Q4580321.blurb: Bangladeshi President Abdus Sattar is deposed in a bloodless coup led by Army Chief Lieutenant general Hussain Muhammad Ershad, who suspends the Constitution and imposes martial law.

Q4580906.name: 1983 America's Cup
Q4580906.blurb: The racing yacht Australia II, captained by John Bertrand, won the America's Cup and ended the New York Yacht Club's 132-year defence of the trophy.

Q4580942.name: 1983 British Airways Sikorsky S-61 crash
Q4580942.blurb: Sikorsky S-61 disaster: A helicopter crashes off the Isles of Scilly, causing 20 fatalities.

Q4581086.name: 1983 Melbourne dust storm
Q4581086.blurb: A dust storm hits Melbourne, resulting in the worst drought on record and severe weather conditions in the city.

Q4581198.name: 1983 Sea of Japan earthquake
aliases: Terremoto del Mar de Japón de 1983
Q4581198.blurb: The 7.8 Mw Sea of Japan earthquake shakes northern Honshu with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VIII (Severe). A destructive tsunami is generated that leaves about 100 people dead.

Q4581203.name: 1983 Soviet nuclear false alarm incident
Q4581203.blurb: Soviet Air Force officer Stanislav Petrov identifies a report of an incoming nuclear missile as a computer error and not an American first strike, thus preventing nuclear war.

Q4581223.name: 1983 TAAG Angola Airlines 737 Boeing crash
Q4581223.blurb: TAAG Angola Airlines Flight 462 crashes after takeoff from Lubango Airport killing all 130 people on board. UNITA claims to have shot down the aircraft, though this is disputed.

Q4581262.name: 1983 United States Senate bombing
Q4581262.blurb: United States Senate bombing: A bomb explodes inside the United States Capitol. No one is injured, but an estimated $250,000 in damage is caused.

Q4581613.name: 1984 Cameroonian coup attempt
Q4581613.blurb: Members of Cameroon's Republican Guard unsuccessfully attempt to overthrow the government headed by Paul Biya.

Q4581738.name: 1984 Mannar massacre
Q4581738.blurb: Sri Lankan Civil War: Sri Lankan Army soldiers kill 107–150 civilians in Mannar.

Q4581824.name: 1984 PKK attacks
Q4581824.blurb: The Kurdistan Workers' Party in Turkey starts a campaign of armed attacks upon the Turkish Armed Forces with an attack on police and gendarmerie bases in Şemdinli and Eruh.

Q4581897.name: 1984 Summer Olympics boycott
Q4581897.blurb: The Soviet Union announced the boycott of the Summer Olympics in Los Angeles, citing security concerns.

Q4582156.name: 1985 Aeroflot Antonov An-12 shoot-down
Q4582156.blurb: A Soviet Air Force Antonov An-12 is shot down near Menongue in Angola's Cuando Cubango Province, killing 21.

Q4582353.name: 1985 Kenilworth Road riot
Q4582353.blurb: One of England's worst incidents of football hooliganism occurred when supporters of Luton Town and Millwall rioted before a match at Kenilworth Road stadium.

Q4582419.name: 1985 Narita International Airport bombing
Q4582419.blurb: A terrorist bomb explodes at Narita International Airport near Tokyo, killing two and injuring four. An hour later, the same group detonates a second bomb aboard Air India Flight 182, bringing the Boeing 747 down off the coast of Ireland killing all 329 aboard.

Q4582441.name: 1985 Newry mortar attack
Q4582441.blurb: The Provisional Irish Republican Army carries out a mortar attack on the Royal Ulster Constabulary police station at Newry, killing nine officers.

Q4582489.name: Battle of Mount Tumbledown
Q4582489.blurb: Battles of Tumbledown and Wireless Ridge, during the Falklands War.

Q4582496.name: 1985 Puerto Rico floods
Q4582496.blurb: The Mameyes landslide kills almost 200 people in Puerto Rico.

Q4582505.name: 1985 Rajneeshee assassination plot
Q4582505.blurb: Two followers of the Indian mystic Rajneesh were convicted of a 1985 plot to assassinate Charles Turner, the U.S. attorney for the District of Oregon.

Q4582884.name: 1986 British International Helicopters Chinook crash
Q4582884.blurb: Sumburgh disaster: A British International Helicopters Boeing 234LR Chinook crashes 2.5 miles (4.0 km) east of Sumburgh Airport killing 45 people. It is the deadliest civilian helicopter crash on record.

Q4583056.name: 1986 Jamaica floods
Q4583056.blurb: A stationary front began over the central Caribbean Sea, leading to severe floods that over two weeks killed dozens of people in Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Haiti and Jamaica.

Q4583210.name: 1986 San Salvador earthquake
Q4583210.blurb: A 5.7 Mw San Salvador earthquake shakes El Salvador, killing 1,500.

Q4583594.name: 1987 Burundian coup d'état
Q4583594.blurb: In a coup d'état in Burundi, President Jean-Baptiste Bagaza is deposed by Major Pierre Buyoya.

Q4583758.name: 1987 Maryland train collision
Q4583758.blurb: The Maryland train collision: An Amtrak train en route to Boston from Washington, D.C., collides with Conrail engines in Chase, Maryland, United States, killing 16 people.

Q4583774.name: Battle of Kettle Creek
Q4583774.blurb: American Revolutionary War: The Battle of Kettle Creek is fought in Georgia.

Q4583989.name: 1987 Whittier Narrows earthquake
Q4583989.blurb: The 5.9 Mw Whittier Narrows earthquake shakes the San Gabriel Valley with a Mercalli intensity of VIII (Severe), killing eight and injuring 200.

Q4584046.name: Battle of Fort Cumberland
Q4584046.blurb: During the American Revolutionary War, the Battle of Fort Cumberland, Nova Scotia, comes to an end with the arrival of British reinforcements.

Q4584589.name: 1988 Nepal earthquake
Q4584589.blurb: The 6.9 Mw Nepal earthquake shakes the Nepal–India border with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VIII (Severe), leaving 709–1,450 people killed and thousands injured.

Q4585341.name: 1989 Newcastle earthquake
Q4585341.blurb: A magnitude 5.6 earthquake hits Newcastle, New South Wales, Australia, killing 13 people.

Q4585384.name: 1989 Philippine coup attempt
Q4585384.blurb: Philippine coup attempt: The right-wing military rebel Reform the Armed Forces Movement attempts to oust Philippine President Corazon Aquino in a failed bloody coup d'état.

Q4585489.name: 1989 Valvettiturai massacre
Q4585489.blurb: A massacre is carried out by an Indian Peace Keeping Force in Sri Lanka killing 64 ethnic Tamil civilians.

Q4585858.name: 1990 Batticaloa massacre
Q4585858.blurb: Batticaloa massacre: Massacre of 184 Tamil civilians by the Sri Lankan Army in Batticaloa District.

Q4586222.name: 1990 Plainfield tornado
Q4586222.blurb: An F5 tornado strikes the Illinois cities of Plainfield and Joliet, killing 29 people.

Q4586309.name: 1990 Strangeways Prison riot
Q4586309.blurb: The longest prison riot in British penal history began at Strangeways Prison in Manchester, lasting 25 days.

Q4586693.name: 1991 Andover, Kansas tornado outbreak
Q4586693.blurb: Fifty-five tornadoes break out in the central United States. Before the outbreak's end, Andover, Kansas, would record the year's only F5 tornado.

Q4586915.name: 1991 Kokkadichcholai massacre
Q4586915.blurb: Kokkadichcholai massacre: The Sri Lankan Army massacres 152 minority Tamil civilians in the village of Kokkadichcholai near the Eastern Province town of Batticaloa.

Q4587079.name: 1991 Sacramento hostage crisis
Q4587079.blurb: Forty-one people are taken hostage inside a Good Guys! Electronics store in Sacramento, California. Three of the hostage takers and three hostages are killed.

Q4587156.name: 1991 Washington, D.C. riot
Q4587156.blurb: A riot breaks out in the Mt. Pleasant section of Washington, D.C. after police shoot a Salvadoran man.

Q4587819.name: 1992 Nigerian Air Force C-130 crash
Q4587819.blurb: A Nigerian Air Force Lockheed C-130 Hercules crashes in Ejigbo, Lagos, killing 159.

Q4589576.name: 1994 Mindoro earthquake
Q4589576.blurb: A magnitude 7.1 earthquake hits the central Philippine island of Mindoro, killing 78 people, injuring 430 and triggering a tsunami up to 8.5 m (28 ft) high.

Q4589739.name: 1994 Stanley Cup Finals
Q4589739.blurb: The 1994 Vancouver Stanley Cup riot occurs after the New York Rangers defeat the Vancouver Canucks to win the Stanley Cup, causing an estimated C$1.1 million, leading to 200 arrests and injuries.

Q4589790.name: 1994 United States Figure Skating Championships
Q4589790.blurb: U.S. figure skater Nancy Kerrigan is attacked and injured by an assailant hired by her rival Tonya Harding's ex-husband during the U.S. Figure Skating Championships.

Q4589796.name: 1994 Vancouver Stanley Cup riot
Q4589796.blurb: The 1994 Vancouver Stanley Cup riot occurs after the New York Rangers defeat the Vancouver Canucks to win the Stanley Cup, causing an estimated C$1.1 million, leading to 200 arrests and injuries.

Q4590155.name: 1995 Air St. Martin Beech 1900 crash
Q4590155.blurb: An Air Saint Martin (now Air Caraïbes) Beechcraft 1900 crashes near the Haitian commune of Belle Anse, killing 20.

Q4590384.name: 1995 Fox River Grove bus–train collision
Q4590384.blurb: A commuter train slams into a school bus in Fox River Grove, Illinois, killing seven students.

Q4590816.name: 1995 enlargement of the European Union
Q4590816.blurb: Austria, Finland and Sweden join the EU.

Q4591238.name: 1996 Biak earthquake
Q4591238.blurb: The 8.2 Mw Biak earthquake shakes the Papua province of eastern Indonesia with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VIII (Severe). A large tsunami followed, leaving 166 people dead or missing and 423 injured.

Q4591257.name: 1996 Burundian coup d'état
Q4591257.blurb: In a military coup in Burundi, Pierre Buyoya deposes Sylvestre Ntibantunganya.

Q4591277.name: 1996 Channel Tunnel fire
Q4591277.blurb: A fire occurs on a train traveling through the Channel Tunnel from France to England causing several injuries and damaging approximately 500 metres (1,600 ft) of tunnel.

Q4591320.name: 1996 Democratic National Convention
Q4591320.blurb: Chicago Seven defendant David Dellinger, antiwar activist Bradford Lyttle, Civil Rights Movement historian Randy Kryn, and eight others are arrested by the Federal Protective Service while protesting in a demonstration at the Kluczynski Federal Building in downtown Chicago during that year's Democratic National Convention.

Q4591331.name: 1996 Docklands bombing
Q4591331.blurb: Breaking a seventeen-month ceasefire, the Provisional Irish Republican Army detonated a powerful truck bomb in the London Docklands, killing two people and injuring more than a hundred others.

Q4591514.name: 1996 Manchester bombing
Q4591514.blurb: The Troubles: The Provisional Irish Republican Army (IRA) detonates a powerful truck bomb in the middle of Manchester, England, devastating the city centre and injuring 200 people.

Q4591568.name: 1996 New Hampshire Learjet crash
Q4591568.blurb: A Learjet 35 crashes into Smarts Mountain near Dorchester, New Hampshire, killing both pilots on board.

Q4591684.name: 1996 Silver Spring, Maryland train collision
Q4591684.blurb: Eleven people died in a train collision in Silver Spring, Maryland, leading to the creation of comprehensive U.S. federal rules for the design of passenger cars.

Q4591921.name: 1996–1997 strikes in South Korea
Q4591921.blurb: The Federation of Korean Trade Unions called on its 1.2 million members to refuse to work, beginning the largest organized strike in South Korean history.

Q4593058.name: 1997 nationalist riots in Northern Ireland
Q4593058.blurb: The Troubles: In response to the Drumcree dispute, five days of mass protests, riots and gun battles begin in Irish nationalist districts of Northern Ireland.

Q4593350.name: 1998 Ariana Afghan Airlines crash
Q4593350.blurb: An Ariana Afghan Airlines Boeing 727 crashes on approach to Kabul International Airport, killing all 45 on board.

Q4593711.name: 1998 Iranian diplomats murder in Afghanistan
Q4593711.blurb: The Iranian consulate in Mazar-i-Sharif, Afghanistan, is raided by Taliban, leading to the deaths of ten Iranian diplomats and a journalist.

Q4593737.name: 1998 Kissimmee tornado outbreak
Q4593737.blurb: In the United States, tornadoes in central Florida destroy or damage 2,600 structures and kill 42 people.

Q4593756.name: 1998 Lignes Aériennes Congolaises crash
Q4593756.blurb: A Lignes Aériennes Congolaises jetliner is shot down by rebels in Kindu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, killing 41 people.

Q4593767.name: 1998 MIAT Mongolian Airlines crash
Q4593767.blurb: A MIAT Mongolian Airlines Harbin Y-12 crashes near Erdenet, Orkhon Province, Mongolia, resulting in 28 deaths.

Q4594025.name: 1998 Temple of the Tooth attack
Q4594025.blurb: The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam detonated a truck bomb at the sacred Buddhist Temple of the Tooth in Kandy, killing 17 people.

Q4594461.name: 1999 Air Botswana incident
Q4594461.blurb: Air Botswana pilot Chris Phatswe steals an ATR 42 from Sir Seretse Khama International Airport and later crashes it into two other aircraft at the airport, killing himself.

Q4594542.name: 1999 Bridge Creek – Moore tornado
Q4594542.blurb: The southwestern portion of Oklahoma City is devastated by an F5 tornado, killing forty-five people, injuring 665, and causing $1 billion in damage. The tornado is one of 66 from the 1999 Oklahoma tornado outbreak. This tornado also produces the highest wind speed ever recorded, measured at 484 ± 32 kilometres per hour (301 ± 20 mph). In meteorology, the term "May 3" is synonymous with the F5 tornado.

Q4594673.name: 1999 FIFA Women's World Cup Final
aliases: 1999 FIFA Women's World Cup Match 32, USA v China
Q4594673.blurb: The United States defeated China in the final match of the third FIFA Women's World Cup, setting records in both attendance and television ratings for women's sports.

Q4594753.name: 1999 Hector Mine earthquake
Q4594753.blurb: The magnitude 7.1 Hector Mine earthquake strikes Southern California

Q4595070.name: 1999 Salt Lake City tornado
Q4595070.blurb: A tornado struck downtown Salt Lake City, damaging 120 homes and injuring over 100 people.

Q4595096.name: 1999 South Dakota Learjet crash
aliases: Accidente del Learjet en Dakota del Sur de 1999
Q4595096.blurb: A Learjet 35 crashes in Mina near Aberdeen, South Dakota, killing all six people on board, including PGA golfer Payne Stewart and golf course designer Bruce Borland.

Q4595154.name: 1999 Sydney hailstorm
Q4595154.blurb: A severe hailstorm strikes Sydney, Australia causing A$2.3 billion in insured damages, the most costly natural disaster in Australian history.

Q4596281.name: 1st Conference of the Communist Parties of Latin America
Q4596281.blurb: The 1st Conference of the Communist Parties of Latin America is held in Buenos Aires.

Q4596352.name: 1st Grey Cup
Q4596352.blurb: The first Grey Cup, the championship game of the Canadian Football League, was held in Toronto.

Q4597199.name: 2000 Baku earthquake
Q4597199.blurb: The 2000 Baku earthquake, with a Richter magnitude of 7.0 kills 26 people dead in Baku, Azerbaijan, being the strongest earthquake in the region in 158 years.

Q4597495.name: 2000 Hezbollah cross-border raid
Q4597495.blurb: Israeli-Palestinian conflict: Hezbollah militants capture three Israeli Defense Force soldiers in a cross-border raid.

Q4598453.name: 2001 Angola train attack
Q4598453.blurb: The 2001 Angola train attack occurred, causing 252 deaths.

Q4598489.name: 2001 Avjet Gulfstream III crash
Q4598489.blurb: A Gulfstream III crashes on approach to Aspen/Pitkin County Airport in Aspen, Colorado. All 18 people on board are killed.

Q4598493.name: 2001 BBC bombing
Q4598493.blurb: BBC bombing: A massive car bomb explodes in front of the BBC Television Centre in London, seriously injuring one person; the attack was attributed to the Real IRA.

Q4598814.name: 2001 Jammu and Kashmir legislative assembly attack
Q4598814.blurb: Militants attack the state legislature building in Kashmir, killing 38.

Q4599790.name: 2002 Buin Zahra earthquake
Q4599790.blurb: A magnitude-6.5 earthquake struck northwestern Iran, killing at least 230 people and injuring 1,300 others; the official response, perceived to be slow, later caused widespread public anger.

Q4600245.name: 2002 Mahane Yehuda Market bombing
Q4600245.blurb: A suicide bomber blows herself up at the entrance to Jerusalem's Mahane Yehuda Market, killing seven people and wounding 104.

Q4600275.name: 2002 Mindanao earthquake
Q4600275.blurb: An earthquake in Mindanao, Philippines, kills 15 people and injures more than 100.

Q4600511.name: 2002 State of the Union Address
Q4600511.blurb: In his State of the Union address, President George W. Bush describes "regimes that sponsor terror" as an Axis of evil, in which he includes Iraq, Iran and North Korea.

Q4600673.name: 2002 airtanker crashes
Q4600673.blurb: A Consolidated PB4Y-2 Privateer crashes near Estes Park, Colorado, killing both crew members.

Q4601221.name: 2003 Chicago balcony collapse
Q4601221.blurb: An overloaded balcony collapsed in Chicago, United States, killing 13 people and injuring 57 others.

Q4601438.name: 2003 Tokachi earthquake
Q4601438.blurb: The 8.3 Mw Hokkaidō earthquake strikes just offshore Hokkaidō, Japan.

Q4602814.name: 2004 Forward Operating Base Marez bombing
Q4602814.blurb: Iraq War: A suicide bomber kills 22 at the forward operating base next to the main U.S. military airfield at Mosul, Iraq, the single deadliest suicide attack on American soldiers in Iraq.

Q4602932.name: 2004 Erbil bombings
Q4602932.blurb: Double suicide attack in Erbil on the offices of Iraqi Kurdish political parties by members of Jama'at al-Tawhid wal-Jihad

Q4603071.name: 2004 Morecambe Bay cockling disaster
Q4603071.blurb: At least 21 cockle-gatherers were drowned by an incoming tide in Morecambe Bay, England, prompting the establishment of the British government's Gangmasters Licensing Authority.

Q4603179.name: 2004 Osama bin Laden video
Q4603179.blurb: The Arabic-language news network Al Jazeera broadcasts an excerpt from a 2004 Osama bin Laden video in which the terrorist leader first admits direct responsibility for the September 11, 2001 attacks and references the 2004 U.S. presidential election.

Q4603285.name: 2004 Sinai bombings
Q4603285.blurb: Three bombs explode at Taba and Nuweiba in the Sinai Peninsula, Egypt, killing 34.

Q4604020.name: 2005 Bangladesh bombings
Q4604020.blurb: Over 500 bombs are set off by terrorists at 300 locations in 63 out of the 64 districts of Bangladesh.

Q4604038.name: 2005 Birmingham tornado
Q4604038.blurb: Britain's costliest tornado struck Birmingham, injuring 39 people and causing £40 million of damage across the city.

Q4604214.name: 2005 Equatorial Express crash
aliases: Plane crash in Equatorial Guinea kills 55
Q4604214.blurb: An Antonov An-24 crashes near Baney in Bioko Norte, Equatorial Guinea, killing 60 people.

Q4604451.name: 2005 Java–Bali blackout
Q4604451.blurb: A massive power blackout hits the Indonesian island of Java; affecting almost 100 million people, it is one of the largest and most widespread power outages in history.

Q4605943.name: 2006 Chadian coup d'état attempt
Q4605943.blurb: The 2006 Chadian coup d'état attempt ends in failure.

Q4606471.name: 2006 Jama Masjid explosions
Q4606471.blurb: Twin blasts triggered by crude bombs during Asr prayer in the Jama Masjid mosque in Delhi injure 13 people.

Q4607109.name: 2006 Varanasi bombings
Q4607109.blurb: The terrorist organisation Lashkar-e-Taiba coordinates a series of bombings in Varanasi, India.

Q4607210.name: 2006 Sanaa prison escape
Q4607210.blurb: Al-Qaeda insurgency in Yemen: 23 convicts, including several militants associated with al-Qaeda, escaped from a prison administered by the Political Security Organization in Sanaa, Yemen.

Q4607307.name: 2006 shelling of Beit Hanoun
Q4607307.blurb: Israeli-Palestinian conflict: The Israeli Defense Force kill 19 Palestinian civilians in their homes during the shelling of Beit Hanoun.

Q4607654.name: 2006–07 Southeast Asian floods
Q4607654.blurb: The first of a series of floods strikes Malaysia. The death toll of all flooding is at least 118, with over 400,000 people displaced.

Q4607752.name: 2006–2007 Brazilian aviation crisis
Q4607752.blurb: A Boeing 737 and an Embraer 600 collide in mid-air, killing 154 people and triggering a Brazilian aviation crisis.

Q4608538.name: 2007 Georgia helicopter incident
Q4608538.blurb: Georgian authorities accused Russia of orchestrating a helicopter attack in the Kodori Valley, in the breakaway territory of Abkhazia.

Q4608686.name: 2007 Iraqi Parliament bombing
Q4608686.blurb: A suicide bomber penetrates the Green Zone and detonates in a cafeteria within a parliament building, killing Iraqi MP Mohammed Awad and wounding more than twenty other people.

Q4609127.name: 2007 Phoenix news helicopter collision
Q4609127.blurb: While covering a police pursuit in Phoenix, Arizona, two news helicopters collided in mid-air, killing both crews.

Q4609691.name: 2007 Zahedan bombings
Q4609691.blurb: The first of several bombings in Zahedan, Iran, killed 18 members of the Revolutionary Guards.

Q4609695.name: 2007 al-Khilani Mosque bombing
Q4609695.blurb: The al-Khilani Mosque bombing in Baghdad leaves 78 people dead and another 218 injured.

Q4609700.name: 2007 al-Askari mosque bombing
Q4609700.blurb: Insurgents carried out a second bombing at the al-Askari Mosque, one of the holiest sites in Shia Islam.

Q4610566.name: 2008 Aéreo Ruta Maya crash
Q4610566.blurb: A Cessna 208 Caravan crashes in Cabañas, Zacapa, Guatemala, killing 11 people.

Q4610597.name: 2008 Beni Amrane bombings
Q4610597.blurb: Two bombs explode at a train station near Algiers, Algeria, killing at least 13 people.

Q4610744.name: 2008 Channel Tunnel fire
Q4610744.blurb: A major Channel Tunnel fire breaks out on a freight train, resulting in the closure of part of the tunnel for six months.

Q4610763.name: 2008 Chișinău Antonov An-32 crash
Q4610763.blurb: Kata Air Transport Flight 007 crashes while attempting an emergency landing at Chișinău International Airport, killing eight.

Q4610765.name: 2008 Christmas massacres
Q4610765.blurb: The Lord's Resistance Army, a Ugandan rebel group, began attacks on several villages in the north of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, killing hundreds and committing numerous atrocities.

Q4610813.name: 2008 Conviasa Boeing 737 crash
Q4610813.blurb: A Conviasa Boeing 737 crashes into Illiniza Volcano in Ecuador, killing all three people on board.

Q4611360.name: 2008 Karmah Bombing
Q4611360.blurb: A suicide bomber dressed as an Iraqi policeman detonates an explosive vest, killing 25 people.

Q4611652.name: 2008 New York Philharmonic visit to North Korea
Q4611652.blurb: The New York Philharmonic performs in Pyongyang, North Korea; this was the first such event to take place in North Korea.

Q4611923.name: 2008 South Carolina Learjet 60 crash
Q4611923.blurb: A Learjet 60 carrying musicians Travis Barker and Adam "DJ AM" Goldstein crashes during a rejected takeoff from Colombia Metropolitan Airport in West Columbia, South Carolina, killing four of the six people on board. Barker and Goldstein both survive.

Q4613202.name: 2009 Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister helicopter crash
Q4613202.blurb: The Andhra Pradesh, India helicopter crash occurred near Rudrakonda Hill, 40 nautical miles (74 km) from Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh, India. Fatalities included Y. S. Rajasekhara Reddy, the Chief Minister of the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh.

Q4613829.name: 2009 Fijian constitutional crisis
Q4613829.blurb: Fijian President Ratu Josefa Iloilo announced that he had suspended the constitution and assumed all governance in the country after it was ruled that the government of Prime Minister Frank Bainimarama was illegal.

Q4613899.name: 2009 Georgian demonstrations
Q4613899.blurb: In Tbilisi, Georgia, up to 60,000 people protest against the government of Mikheil Saakashvili.

Q4613951.name: 2009 Hermosillo daycare center fire in the hole
Q4613951.blurb: A fire at a day-care center kills 49 people in Hermosillo, Mexico.

Q4613973.name: 2009 Hudson River mid-air collision
Q4613973.blurb: Nine people died when a tour helicopter and a small private airplane collided over the Hudson River in Hoboken, New Jersey.

Q4614016.name: 2009 Ilyushin Il-76 crash
Q4614016.blurb: An Ilyushin Il-76 crashes near the Mir mine after takeoff from Mirny Airport in Yakutia, killing all 11 aboard.

Q4614415.name: 2009 Napier shootings
Q4614415.blurb: Police in Napier, New Zealand, began a 40-hour siege of the home of a former New Zealand Army member who had shot at officers during the routine execution of a search warrant.

Q4614418.name: 2009 Nakumatt supermarket fire
Q4614418.blurb: At least 113 people are killed in Kenya and over 200 injured following an oil spillage ignition in Molo, days after a massive fire at a Nakumatt supermarket in Nairobi killed at least 25 people.

Q4615035.name: 2009 USS Port Royal grounding
Q4615035.blurb: The United States Navy guided missile cruiser  Port Royal ran aground (pictured) on a coral reef off the island of Oahu.

Q4615375.name: 2009 imprisonment of American journalists by North Korea
Q4615375.blurb: Two American journalists, having been arrested for illegal entry into North Korea, were sentenced to twelve years hard labor before being pardoned two months later.

Q4615467.name: 2009 suicide air raid on Colombo
Q4615467.blurb: Two Tamil Tigers aircraft packed with C4 explosives en route to the national airforce headquarters are shot down by the Sri Lankan military before reaching their target, in a kamikaze style attack.

Q4616704.name: 2010 Badakhshan massacre
Q4616704.blurb: Ten members of International Assistance Mission Nuristan Eye Camp team are killed by persons unknown in Kuran wa Munjan District of Badakhshan Province, Afghanistan.

Q4616939.name: Christmas Island boat disaster
Q4616939.blurb: A boat carrying 90 asylum seekers crashes into rocks off the coast of Christmas Island, Australia, killing 48 people.

Q4617645.name: 2010 Karachi riots
Q4617645.blurb: Widespread rioting erupts in Karachi, Pakistan, after the assassination of a local politician, leaving at least 85 dead and at least 17 billion Pakistani rupees (US$200 million) in damage.

Q4618178.name: 2010 Philippine Bar exam bombing
Q4618178.blurb: The Philippine Bar exam bombing occurs near the De La Salle University in Taft Avenue, Manila injuring 47 people.

Q4618322.name: San Bruno pipeline explosion
Q4618322.blurb: A natural-gas pipeline in San Bruno, California, exploded and "shot a fireball more than 1,000 feet (300 m) in the air", killing eight people.

Q4618739.name: 2010 United Kingdom government formation
Q4618739.blurb: Gordon Brown resigned as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom and Leader of the Labour Party after failing to strike a coalition agreement with the Liberal Democrats.

Q4620729.name: 2011 Chilean Air Force CASA 212 crash
Q4620729.blurb: Bad weather caused a Chilean Air Force aircraft to crash into the Pacific Ocean, killing all 21 people on board.

Q4621984.name: 2011 New England tornado outbreak
Q4621984.blurb: A rare tornado outbreak occurs in New England; a strong EF3 tornado strikes Springfield, Massachusetts, during the event, killing four people.

Q4622322.name: 2011 San Fernando massacre
Q4622322.blurb: Mexican drug war: Authorities discovered 59 bodies in clandestine mass graves linked to earlier bus hijackings in San Fernando, Tamaulipas.

Q4623178.name: 2011 in Mexico
Q4623178.blurb: A helicopter crash just outside Mexico City kills seven, including Francisco Blake Mora the Secretary of the Interior of Mexico.

Q4624536.name: 2012-2013 Tana River District clashes
Q4624536.blurb: Ethnic clashes over grazing rights for cattle in Kenya's Tana River District result in more than 52 deaths.

Q4624967.name: 2012 Burlington VIA derailment
Q4624967.blurb: A train derails in Burlington, Ontario, Canada killing at least three people and injuring 45.

Q4625098.name: 2012 Carterton hot air balloon crash
Q4625098.blurb: A hot air balloon crashes near Carterton, New Zealand, killing all 11 people on board.

Q4625300.name: 2012 Deir ez-Zor bombing
Q4625300.blurb: A car bomb explodes near a military complex in the Syrian city of Deir ez-Zor, killing nine people.

Q4625842.name: 2012 Indian Ocean migrant boat disaster
Q4625842.blurb: A boat carrying more than 200 migrants capsizes in the Indian Ocean between the Indonesian island of Java and Christmas Island, killing 17 people and leaving 70 others missing.

Q4626051.name: 2012 Ljubljana Marshes hot air balloon crash
Q4626051.blurb: A hot-air balloon crashes near the Slovenian capital of Ljubljana, killing six people and injuring 28 others.

Q4626364.name: 2012 Nobel Peace Prize
Q4626364.blurb: The European Union wins the 2012 Nobel Peace Prize.

Q4626587.name: 2012 Pulitzer Prize
Q4626587.blurb: The Pulitzer Prize winners are announced. It was the first time since 1977 that no book won the Fiction Prize.

Q4627258.name: 2012 Welikada prison riot
Q4627258.blurb: At least 27 people are killed and dozens are wounded in conflicts between inmates and guards at Welikada prison in Colombo.

Q4629505.name: 2013 Kumbh Mela stampede
Q4629505.blurb: Thirty-six people are killed and 39 others are injured in a stampede in Allahabad, India, during the Kumbh Mela festival.

Q4630585.name: 20 March 2012 Iraq attacks
Q4630585.blurb: At least 52 people are killed and more than 250 injured in a wave of terror attacks across ten cities in Iraq.

Q4630977.name: 21 April 2004 Basra bombings
Q4630977.blurb: Five suicide car bombers target police stations in and around Basra, killing 74 people and wounding 160.

Q4631563.name: 23 February 2012 Iraq attacks
Q4631563.blurb: A series of attacks across Iraq leave at least 83 killed and more than 250 injured.

Q4631578.name: 23 November 2006 Sadr City bombings
Q4631578.blurb: A series of bombings kills at least 215 people and injures 257 others in Sadr City, making it the second deadliest sectarian attack since the beginning of the Iraq War in 2003.

Q4632180.name: 25 October 2009 Baghdad bombings
Q4632180.blurb: The October 2009 Baghdad bombings kill 155 and wound at least 721.

Q4634100.name: 3-19 shooting incident
Q4634100.blurb: March 19 Shooting Incident: The Republic of China (Taiwan) president Chen Shui-bian is shot just before the country's presidential election on March 20.

Q4634328.name: 300 million yen robbery
Q4634328.blurb: Japan's biggest heist, the still-unsolved "300 million yen robbery", is carried out in Tokyo.

Q4636492.name: 3 February 2007 Baghdad market bombing
Q4636492.blurb: A Baghdad market bombing kills at least 135 people and injures a further 339.

Q4642523.name: 6 March 2008 Baghdad bombing
Q4642523.blurb: A suicide bomber kills 68 people (including first responders) in Baghdad on the same day that a gunman kills eight students in Jerusalem.

Q4644763.name: 847 Antioch earthquake
Q4644763.blurb: An earthquake hits Syria, causing multiple casualties and damages in Antioch, Damascus and Mosul.

Q4645433.name: 8th National People's Congress
Q4645433.blurb: The Macao Basic Law is adopted by the Eighth National People's Congress of China to take effect December 20, 1999. Resumption by China of the Exercise of Sovereignty over Macao

Q4646435.name: 9 September 2012 Iraq attacks
Q4646435.blurb: A wave of attacks kills more than 100 people and injure 350 others across Iraq.

Q4651082.name: ADC Airlines Flight 86
Q4651082.blurb: ADC Airlines Flight 086 crashes into the Lagos Lagoon in Epe, Lagos State, Nigeria, killing all 144 people on board.

Q4651994.name: AIRES Flight 8250
Q4651994.blurb: AIRES Flight 8250 crashes at Gustavo Rojas Pinilla International Airport in San Andrés, San Andrés y Providencia, Colombia, killing two people.

Q4652401.name: ALM Flight 980
Q4652401.blurb: ALM Flight 980 ditches in the Caribbean Sea near Saint Croix, killing 23.

Q4655029.name: AVAir Flight 3378
Q4655029.blurb: A Fairchild Swearingen Metroliner operating as AVAir Flight 3378 crashes in Cary, North Carolina, killing 12.

Q4661508.name: Chelyabinsk meteor
Q4661508.blurb: A meteor explodes over Russia, injuring 1,500 people as a shock wave blows out windows and rocks buildings. This happens unexpectedly only hours before the expected closest ever approach of the larger and unrelated asteroid 2012 DA14.

Q4667872.name: Abington School District v. Schempp
Q4667872.blurb: The United States Supreme Court rules 8–1 in Abington School District v. Schempp against requiring the reciting of Bible verses and the Lord's Prayer in public schools.

Q4671621.name: Battle of Damascus
Q4671621.blurb: Having defeated forces of Vichy France, Allied forces capture Damascus.

Q4677257.name: Action of 14 February 1944
Q4677257.blurb: World War II: In the action of 14 February 1944, a Royal Navy submarine sinks a German-controlled Italian Regia Marina submarine in the Strait of Malacca.

Q4677281.name: Action of 18 November 1809
Q4677281.blurb: Napoleonic Wars:  In a naval action, French frigates defeat British East Indiamen in the Bay of Bengal.

Q4677285.name: Action of 19 December 1796
Q4677285.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: Two British frigates under Commodore Horatio Nelson and two Spanish frigates under Commodore Don Jacobo Stuart engage in battle off the coast of Murcia.

Q4677294.name: Action of 21 April 1806
Q4677294.blurb: Action of 21 April 1806: A French frigate escapes British forces off the coast of South Africa.

Q4677352.name: Action of 31 March 1800
Q4677352.blurb: After fighting through the night, the French Navy ship of the line Guillaume Tell surrendered to a British squadron in the Malta Channel.

Q4677355.name: Action of 3 July 1810
Q4677355.blurb: Mauritius campaign of 1809–1811: A French frigate squadron under Guy-Victor Duperré defeated a convoy of three British East Indiamen near the Comoro Islands.

Q4677374.name: Action of 6 April 1809
Q4677374.blurb: Napoleonic Wars: British forces captured the French frigate Niémen in the Bay of Biscay.

Q4677390.name: Action of 8 September 1796
Q4677390.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: A naval engagement between French and British fleets off the coast of Sumatra ended inconclusively.

Q4677393.name: Action of 9 February 1945
Q4677393.blurb: World War II: Battle of the Atlantic: HMS Venturer sinks U-864 off the coast of Fedje, Norway, in a rare instance of submarine-to-submarine combat.

Q4677395.name: Action of 9 November 1822
Q4677395.blurb: USS Alligator engaged three pirate schooners off the coast of Cuba in one of the West Indies anti-piracy operations of the United States.

Q4684104.name: Adolf Hitler's 50th birthday
Q4684104.blurb: Adolf Hitler's 50th birthday was celebrated as a national holiday in Nazi Germany.

Q4684105.name: Adolf Hitler's rise to power
Q4684105.blurb: Adolf Hitler's rise to power: Hitler takes office as the Chancellor of Germany.

Q4688260.name: Aeroflot Flight 217
Q4688260.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 217 crashes outside Moscow, killing 174.

Q4688261.name: Aeroflot Flight 331
Q4688261.blurb: A plane crash at José Martí International Airport in Havana, Cuba, kills 67.

Q4688264.name: Aeroflot Flight 418
Q4688264.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 418 crashes in Bioko, Equatorial Guinea, killing 46.

Q4688331.name: Aeroméxico Flight 230
Q4688331.blurb: While landing at Chihuahua International Airport, Aeromexico Flight 230 overshoots the runway. Thirty-two of the 66 passengers and crew on board the DC-9 are killed.

Q4688341.name: Aeroméxico Flight 229
Q4688341.blurb: Aeroméxico Flight 229 crashes on approach to Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz International Airport, killing all 27 people on board.

Q4688400.name: Aeropostal Alas de Venezuela Flight 108
Q4688400.blurb: Aeropostal Alas de Venezuela Flight 109 crashes in Venezuela, killing 45.

Q4688478.name: Aerosvit Flight 241
Q4688478.blurb: Aerosvit Flight 241: A Yakovlev Yak-42 crashes into the Pierian Mountains near Thessaloniki Airport in Thessaloniki, Greece, killing all 70 people on board.

Q4690967.name: Agadir air disaster
Q4690967.blurb: A privately chartered Boeing 707 strikes a mountain peak and crashes near Agadir, Morocco, killing 188.

Q4697761.name: Air Battle of South Korea
Q4697761.blurb: After a month-long campaign, the majority of North Korea's Air Force was destroyed by anti-communist forces.

Q4697779.name: Air Canada Flight 189
Q4697779.blurb: Air Canada Flight 189, flying to Toronto, overruns the runway and crashes into the Etobicoke Creek ravine. Two of the 107 passengers on board perish.

Q4697989.name: Air France Flight 2005
Q4697989.blurb: Air France Flight 2005 crashes near Rabat–Salé Airport, in Rabat, Morocco, killing 77 people.

Q4697990.name: Air France Flight 212 (1968)
Q4697990.blurb: Air France Flight 212 crashes into La Grande Soufrière, killing all 63 aboard.

Q4697992.name: Air France Flight 007
Q4697992.blurb: At Paris Orly Airport, Air France Flight 007 overruns the runway and explodes when the crew attempts to abort takeoff, killing 130.

Q4697994.name: Air France Flight 406
Q4697994.blurb: Air France Flight 406 is destroyed by a bomb over the Sahara, killing 78.

Q4698060.name: Air Lanka Flight 512
Q4698060.blurb: Twenty-one people are killed and forty-one are injured after a bomb explodes on Air Lanka Flight 512 at Colombo airport in Sri Lanka.

Q4698169.name: Air Rhodesia Flight 825
Q4698169.blurb: During the Rhodesian Bush War a group of ZIPRA guerrillas shot down civilian Vickers Viscount aircraft (Air Rhodesia Flight 825) with a Soviet-made SAM Strela-2; of 56 passengers and crew 38 people died in crash, 10 were massacred by the guerrillas at the site.

Q4698253.name: Air Vietnam Flight 706 hijacking
Q4698253.blurb: Air Vietnam Flight 706 is hijacked, then crashes while attempting to land with 75 on board.

Q4698807.name: Airlink Flight 8911
Q4698807.blurb: South African Airlink Flight 8911 crashes near Durban International Airport in Durban, South Africa, killing the captain and injuring the rest of the crew.

Q4700349.name: Akashi pedestrian bridge accident
Q4700349.blurb: At the conclusion of a fireworks display on Okura Beach in Akashi, Hyōgo, Japan, 11 people are killed and more than 120 are injured when a pedestrian footbridge connecting the beach to JR Asagiri Station becomes overcrowded and people leaving the event fall down in a domino effect.

Q4701333.name: Akkaraipattu massacre
Q4701333.blurb: Akkaraipattu massacre: the Sri Lankan Army massacres 80 Tamil farm workers in eastern Sri Lanka.

Q4702067.name: May 1605 papal conclave
Q4702067.blurb: After a scuffle in which one cardinal had several bones broken, a papal conclave convened in Rome elected Camillo Borghese as Pope Paul V.

Q4702950.name: Corrupted Blood incident
Q4702950.blurb: A software bug caused a simulated pandemic in the online video game World of Warcraft, serving as a model for epidemiologists to understand how human interaction influences disease outbreaks.

Q4708406.name: Alas Chiricanas Flight 901
Q4708406.blurb: Alas Chiricanas Flight 00901 is destroyed by a bomb after takeoff from Enrique Adolfo Jiménez Airport in Colón, Panama, killing 21.

Q4708491.name: Alaska Airlines Flight 1866
Q4708491.blurb: Alaska Airlines Flight 1866 crashes near Juneau, Alaska, killing all 111 people on board.

Q4709163.name: Albanian revolt of 1910
Q4709163.blurb: The Ottoman Empire captures the city of Shkodër, putting down the Albanian Revolt of 1910.

Q4715652.name: December 2009 Baghdad bombings
Q4715652.blurb: Bombings in Baghdad, Iraq kill 127 people and injure 448 others.

Q4729188.name: All Nippon Airways Flight 533
Q4729188.blurb: All Nippon Airways Flight 533 crashes into the Seto Inland Sea near Matsuyama Airport in Japan, killing 50 people.

Q4729189.name: All Nippon Airways Flight 60
Q4729189.blurb: All Nippon Airways Flight 60 plunges into Tokyo Bay, killing 133.

Q4729190.name: All Nippon Airways Flight 58
Q4729190.blurb: An All Nippon Airways Boeing 727 and a Japanese Air Force F-86 collide over Morioka, Iwate, Japan, killing 162.

Q4729199.name: All Nippon Airways Flight 61
Q4729199.blurb: ANA Flight 61 is hijacked in Tokyo, Japan by Yuji Nishizawa.

Q4731272.name: Allegheny Airlines Flight 736
Q4731272.blurb: Allegheny Airlines Flight 736 crashes on approach to Bradford Regional Airport, killing 20.

Q4731274.name: Allegheny Airlines Flight 737
Q4731274.blurb: Allegheny Airlines Flight 737 crashes in Lafayette Township, McKean County, Pennsylvania, United States, killing 11.

Q4731275.name: Allegheny Airlines Flight 853
Q4731275.blurb: Allegheny Airlines Flight 863 collides in mid-air with a Piper PA-28 Cherokee over Moral Township, Shelby County, Indiana, killing all 83 people on board both aircraft.

Q4735638.name: Deepwater Horizon oil spill
aliases: BP Gulf of Mexico Oil Spill of 2010
BP Gulf of Mexico oil spill
BP oil spill in the Gulf
British Petroleum Deepwater Horizon oil spill
Consequences of the Deepwater Horizon oil spill
Deepwater Horizon blowout and oil spill
Deepwater Horizon explosion and oil spill
Deepwater Horizon oil rig failure and leak
Deepwater Horizon rig explosion and oil spill
Gulf of Mexico oil rig disaster
Gulf of Mexico oil spill of 2010
Q4735638.blurb: The leaking oil well in the Deepwater Horizon oil spill is sealed.

Q4741179.name: Battle of Bita Paka
Q4741179.blurb: World War I: Australia invades German New Guinea, defeating a German contingent at the Battle of Bita Paka.

Q4742943.name: American Airlines Flight 28
Q4742943.blurb: All 12 passengers and crewmen aboard American Airlines Flight 28 are killed when it collides with a U.S. Army Air Force bomber near Palm Springs, California.

Q4742946.name: American Airlines Flight 383
Q4742946.blurb: American Airlines Flight 383 crashes in Constance, Kentucky, killing 58.

Q4742948.name: American Airlines Flight 320
Q4742948.blurb: Sixty-five people are killed when American Airlines Flight 320 crashes into the East River on approach to LaGuardia Airport in New York City.

Q4742949.name: American Airlines Flight 625
Q4742949.blurb: Thirty-seven people are killed when American Airlines Flight 625 crashes at Cyril E. King Airport in Saint Thomas, U.S. Virgin Islands.

Q4742954.name: American Airlines Flight 444
Q4742954.blurb: A package from Unabomber Ted Kaczynski begins smoking in the cargo hold of a flight from Chicago to Washington, D.C., forcing the plane to make an emergency landing.

Q4742959.name: American Airlines Flight 723
Q4742959.blurb: American Airlines Flight 723 crashes in Colonie, New York, killing 28 people.

Q4743789.name: American Flyers Airline Flight 280
Q4743789.blurb: American Flyers Airline Flight 280/D crashes on approach to Ardmore Municipal Airport in Ardmore, Oklahoma, killing 83.

Q4744568.name: American National Exhibition
Q4744568.blurb: At the opening of the American National Exhibition in Moscow, U.S. vice president Richard Nixon and Soviet premier Nikita Khrushchev have a "Kitchen Debate".

Q4754577.name: 1933 Andorran parliamentary election
Q4754577.blurb: The Integral Nationalist Group wins the 1933 Andorran parliamentary election, the first election in Andorra held with universal male suffrage.

Q4763587.name: Anglo-American loan
Q4763587.blurb: The UK settles its Anglo-American loan, post-WWII loan debt.

Q4763625.name: Anglo-French Convention of 1882
Q4763625.blurb: The Anglo-French Convention of 1882 marks the territorial boundaries between Guinea and Sierra Leone.

Q4763741.name: Angola Horror
Q4763741.blurb: In Angola, New York, the last coach of a Lake Shore Railway train derailed, plunged 40 feet (12 m) down a gully, and caught fire, resulting in approximately 49 deaths.

Q4770640.name: Ansett-ANA Flight 149
Q4770640.blurb: Twenty-four people are killed when Ansett-ANA Flight 149 crashes in Winton, Queensland, Australia.

Q4770648.name: Ansett New Zealand Flight 703
Q4770648.blurb: Ansett New Zealand Flight 703 crashes into the Tararua Range during approach to Palmerston North Airport on the North Island of New Zealand, killing four.

Q4774241.name: 1933 anti-Nazi boycott
Q4774241.blurb: Nazi Germany and the Zionist Federation of Germany signed the Haavara Agreement. The agreement was a major factor in breaking the anti-Nazi boycott of 1933 and facilitated Jewish emigration from Germany and into British Mandate of Palestine.

Q4774312.name: anti-abolitionist riots of 1834
Q4774312.blurb: In New York City, four nights of rioting against abolitionists began.

Q4774367.name: Anti-globalization protests in Prague
Q4774367.blurb: Anti-globalization protests in Prague (some 20,000 protesters) turn violent during the IMF and World Bank summits.

Q4774984.name: Antinomian Controversy
Q4774984.blurb: Anne Hutchinson was expelled from the Massachusetts Bay Colony for her participation in the Antinomian Controversy.

Q4779013.name: Apalachee massacre
Q4779013.blurb: The Apalachee massacre: A combined British and Muscogee force from the Province of Carolina destroys the main fortified mission of Ayubale, breaking Spain's hold on Spanish Florida.

Q4780158.name: Apodaca prison riot
Q4780158.blurb: Forty-four people are killed in a prison brawl in Apodaca, Nuevo León, Mexico.

Q4780292.name: Apollo 8 Genesis reading
Q4780292.blurb: Apollo program: The crew of Apollo 8 enters into orbit around the Moon, becoming the first humans to do so. They performed ten lunar orbits, took the Earthrise photograph, broadcast live TV pictures, and read the first ten verses of Genesis.

Q4781946.name: April 2010 Maoist attack in Dantewada
Q4781946.blurb: Maoist rebels kill 76 CRPF officers in Dantewada district, India.

Q4784054.name: Arana-Southern Treaty
Q4784054.blurb: The Arana–Southern Treaty is ratified, ending "the existing differences" between Great Britain and Argentina.

Q4784936.name: Arbroath 36–0 Bon Accord
Q4784936.blurb: Arbroath 36–0 Bon Accord, a world record scoreline in professional association football.

Q4785855.name: Battle of Boxtel
Q4785855.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: Arthur Wellesley (later Duke of Wellington) sees his first combat at the Battle of Boxtel during the Flanders Campaign.

Q4789386.name: Argentine Constitution of 1819
Q4789386.blurb: The Argentine Constitution of 1819 is promulgated.

Q4789443.name: 1946 Argentine general election
Q4789443.blurb: Colonel Juan Perón, founder of the political movement that became known as Peronism, is elected to his first term as President of Argentina.

Q4789451.name: September 1973 Argentine general election
Q4789451.blurb: Argentine general election: Juan Perón returns to power in Argentina.

Q4789489.name: Argentine surrender in the Falklands War
Q4789489.blurb: Falklands War: British prime minister Margaret Thatcher announced that white flags were flying over Port Stanley, in advance of the formal surrender of Argentine forces.

Q4790211.name: Ariana Afghan Airlines Flight 701
Q4790211.blurb: Ariana Afghan Airlines Flight 701 crashes in Fernhill, West Sussex, UK, while on approach to Gatwick Airport, killing 50 people.

Q4795368.name: Arnon Street killings
Q4795368.blurb: In newly formed Northern Ireland, six Catholics are murdered in the Arnon Street killings, one week after six others were killed in the  McMahon killings.

Q4801174.name: Second Battle of Petersburg
Q4801174.blurb: American Civil War: The Second Battle of Petersburg begins.

Q4808502.name: assassination of Benigno Aquino, Jr.
Q4808502.blurb: Philippine opposition leader Benigno Aquino Jr. is assassinated at Manila International Airport (now renamed Ninoy Aquino International Airport in his honor).

Q4808508.name: assassination of George Tiller
Q4808508.blurb: American physician George Tiller, one of the few doctors in the country who performed late-term abortions, was shot and killed by Scott Roeder, an anti-abortion activist.

Q4808511.name: assassination of Hrant Dink
Q4808511.blurb: Turkish-Armenian journalist Hrant Dink is assassinated in front of his newspaper's Istanbul office by 17-year-old Turkish ultra-nationalist Ogün Samast.

Q4808515.name: assassination of Lalith Athulathmudali
Q4808515.blurb: Sri Lankan politician Lalith Athulathmudali is assassinated while addressing a gathering, approximately four weeks ahead of the Provincial Council elections for the Western Province.

Q4808531.name: assassination of the recruiter Bazin
Q4808531.blurb: Members of the Việt Nam Quốc Dân Đảng assassinate the labor recruiter Bazin, prompting a crackdown by French colonial authorities.

Q4810109.name: Dujail Massacre
Q4810109.blurb: A failed assassination attempt against Iraqi president Saddam Hussein results in the Dujail Massacre over the next several months.

Q4816127.name: Atlanta Race Riot
Q4816127.blurb: Racial tensions exacerbated by rumors lead to the Atlanta Race Riot, further increasing racial segregation.

Q4816365.name: United Express Flight 6291
Q4816365.blurb: A British Aerospace Jetstream 41 operating as United Express Flight 6291 crashes in Gahanna, Ohio, killing five of the eight people on board.

Q4816543.name: Atlantic Southeast Airlines Flight 2254
Q4816543.blurb: An Embraer EMB 120 Brasilia collides in mid-air with a Cessna 172 over Gadsden, Alabama, killing both of the Cessna's occupants.

Q4816544.name: Atlantic Southeast Airlines Flight 2311
Q4816544.blurb: An ASA EMB 120 crashes in Brunswick, Georgia, killing all 23 aboard, including Sen. John Tower and astronaut Sonny Carter.

Q4817269.name: Atomic Energy Act of 1946
aliases: United States Senate Special Committee on Atomic Energy,
Q4817269.blurb: The United Kingdom publicly announced that it was independently developing nuclear weapons, after the US Atomic Energy Act of 1946 ended cooperation on the matter.

Q4817327.name: Battle of Çamurlu
Q4817327.blurb: Mehmed Çelebi and his army defeat the army of his brother Musa Çelebi in the battle of Çamurlu. Musa is captured and executed.

Q4817850.name: Muslim conquest of Transoxiana
Q4817850.blurb: Muslim conquest of Transoxiana: Türgesh tribesmen attacked and captured the exposed baggage train of the Umayyad army, sent ahead of the main force.

Q4817990.name: Attack on Derryard checkpoint
Q4817990.blurb: The Troubles: Attack on Derryard checkpoint: The Provisional Irish Republican Army launches an attack on a British Army temporary vehicle checkpoint near Rosslea, Northern Ireland. Two British soldiers are killed and two others are wounded.

Q4818018.name: Attack on the USNS Card
Q4818018.blurb: Vietnam War: An explosion sinks the American aircraft carrier USNS Card while it is docked at Saigon. Two Viet Cong combat swimmers had placed explosives on the ship's hull. She is raised and returned to service less than seven months later.

Q4818177.name: Attempts at reconciliation in Somalia
Q4818177.blurb: Somali Civil War: Hussein Farrah Aidid relinquishes the disputed title of President of Somalia by signing the Cairo Declaration, in Cairo, Egypt. It is the first major step towards reconciliation in Somalia since 1991.

Q4818683.name: Operation Hammer
Q4818683.blurb: The Turkish Armed Forces withdraw from northern Iraq after assisting the Kurdistan Democratic Party in the Iraqi Kurdish Civil War.

Q4821674.name: 1975 spring offensive
aliases: General Offensive and Uprising of the Spring 1975
Q4821674.blurb: Vietnam War: Ho Chi Minh Campaign: North Vietnamese troops attack Ban Mê Thuột in the South on their way to capturing Saigon in the final push for victory over South Vietnam.

Q4822495.name: Siege of Nagykanizsa
Q4822495.blurb: Tiryaki Hasan Pasha, an Ottoman provincial governor, routs the Habsburg forces commanded by Archduke Ferdinand II of Austria who were besieging Nagykanizsa.

Q4823381.name: Austral Líneas Aéreas Flight 046
Q4823381.blurb: Austral Líneas Aéreas Flight 046, a McDonnell Douglas MD-81, crashes short of the runway at Libertador General José de San Martín Airport, killing all 22 people on board.

Q4824364.name: 2010 Australian Labor Party leadership spill
Q4824364.blurb: Julia Gillard was sworn in as the first female prime minister of Australia after incumbent Kevin Rudd declined to contest a leadership spill in the Labor Party.

Q4825132.name: 1967 Australian referendum (Aboriginals)
aliases: 1967 Australian referendum on legislating for Aboriginal people
Q4825132.blurb: Australians vote in favor of a constitutional referendum granting the Australian government the power to make laws to benefit Indigenous Australians and to count them in the national census.

Q4826029.name: Auto-Lite strike
Q4826029.blurb: The U.S. Auto-Lite strike begins, culminating in a five-day melee between Ohio National Guard troops and 6,000 strikers and picketers.

Q4828570.name: Avianca Flight 671
Q4828570.blurb: Avianca Flight 671 crashes at Montego Bay, Jamaica airport, killing 37 people.

Q4828607.name: Aviateca Flight 901
Q4828607.blurb: Aviateca Flight 901 crashes into the San Vicente volcano in El Salvador, killing all 65 people on board.

Q4832380.name: Azerbaijan Airlines Flight 217
Q4832380.blurb: An Antonov An-140, Azerbaijan Airlines Flight 217 from Baku, Azerbaijan, to Aktau, Kazakhstan, heading across the Caspian Sea, crashes, killing 23 people.

Q4835218.name: BCPA Flight 304
Q4835218.blurb: BCPA Flight 304 DC-6 crashes near San Francisco.

Q4836175.name: BOAC Flight 712
Q4836175.blurb: BOAC Flight 712 catches fire shortly after takeoff. As a result of her actions in the accident, Barbara Jane Harrison is awarded a posthumous George Cross, the only GC awarded to a woman in peacetime.

Q4836516.name: BSAA Star Tiger disappearance
Q4836516.blurb: British South American Airways' Tudor IV Star Tiger disappears over the Bermuda Triangle.

Q4841116.name: Badrashin railway accident
Q4841116.blurb: A train carrying Egyptian Army recruits derails near Giza, Greater Cairo, killing 19 and injuring 120 others.

Q4842568.name: Bahia incident
Q4842568.blurb: American Civil War: A US Navy ship captures a Confederate raider in a Brazilian seaport.

Q4842737.name: Bahrain Bloody Thursday
Q4842737.blurb: Arab Spring: Bahraini security forces killed four protesters in a pre-dawn raid at the Pearl Roundabout in Manama, while the "Day of Rage" took place in Libya with nationwide protests against Muammar Gaddafi's government.

Q4845763.name: Battle of Loc Ninh
Q4845763.blurb: Vietnam War: Communist forces overrun the South Vietnamese town of Loc Ninh.

Q4846093.name: 2013 Lahad Datu standoff
Q4846093.blurb: Militants claiming to be from the Sultanate of Sulu invade Lahad Datu District, Sabah, Malaysia, beginning the Lahad Datu standoff.

Q4848678.name: Passaleão incident
Q4848678.blurb: Passaleão incident: João Maria Ferreira do Amaral, the governor of Portuguese Macau, is assassinated by a group of Chinese locals, triggering a military confrontation between China and Portugal at the Battle of Passaleão three days after.

Q4848754.name: Baixa de Cassanje revolt
Q4848754.blurb: A protest by agricultural workers in Baixa de Cassanje, Portuguese Angola, turns into a revolt, opening the Angolan War of Independence, the first of the Portuguese Colonial Wars.

Q4850948.name: Baling Talks
Q4850948.blurb: Chin Peng, David Marshall and Tunku Abdul Rahman meet in Baling, Malaya to try to resolve the Malayan Emergency situation.

Q4851435.name: Ballantyne's fire
Q4851435.blurb: The Ballantyne's Department Store fire in Christchurch, New Zealand, kills 41; it is the worst fire disaster in the history of New Zealand.

Q4852130.name: Ballygawley bus bombing
Q4852130.blurb: The Troubles: Eight British soldiers are killed and 28 wounded when their bus is hit by an IRA roadside bomb in Ballygawley, County Tyrone.

Q4852983.name: Baltimore municipal strike of 1974
Q4852983.blurb: The Baltimore municipal strike of 1974 begins.

Q4857928.name: Bar Harbor Airlines Flight 1808
Q4857928.blurb: Bar Harbor Airlines Flight 1808 crashes near Auburn/Lewiston Municipal Airport in Auburn, Maine, killing all eight people on board including peace activist and child actress Samantha Smith.

Q4859251.name: Battle of Romania
Q4859251.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Romania begins with a major Soviet Union offensive.

Q4859409.name: Burning of Parliament
Q4859409.blurb: Much of the ancient structure of the Palace of Westminster in London burns to the ground.

Q4867604.name: Disco Demolition Night
Q4867604.blurb: Rowdy fans at Comiskey Park in Chicago stormed the field during a Major League Baseball promotional event at which a crate of disco records was blown up.

Q4868601.name: Raid on Griessie
Q4868601.blurb: Napoleonic Wars: British ships began a raid on Griessie after the Dutch captain refused a British demand for surrender.

Q4870137.name: Battle at Springmartin
Q4870137.blurb: The Troubles: A car bombing outside a crowded pub in Belfast sparks a two-day gun battle involving the Provisional IRA, Ulster Volunteer Force and British Army. Seven people are killed and over 66 injured.

Q4870261.name: Battle of Algeciras
Q4870261.blurb: The naval Battle of Algeciras takes place in the context of the Spanish Reconquista resulting in a victory for the Emirate of Granada and the Maranid Dynasty over the Kingdom of Castile.

Q4870264.name: Battle of Alhandic
Q4870264.blurb: The Battle of Alhandic is fought between Ramiro II of León and Abd-ar-Rahman III at Zamora in the context of the Spanish Reconquista. The battle resulted in a victory for the Emirate of Córdoba.

Q4870281.name: Battle of Alton
Q4870281.blurb: English Civil War: The Battle of Alton takes place in Hampshire.

Q4870288.name: Battle of Ambos Nogales
Q4870288.blurb: Mexican Revolution: Battle of Ambos Nogales: U.S. Army forces skirmish against Mexican Carrancistas as part of the Mexican Border War.

Q4870321.name: Battle of Arakere
Q4870321.blurb: The British under Charles Cornwallis defeat a Mysorean army under Tipu Sultan in the battle of Arakere.

Q4870336.name: Battle of Arklow
Q4870336.blurb: Irish Rebellion of 1798: Battles of Arklow and Saintfield.

Q4870388.name: Battle of Baguashan
