Q4870388.blurb: Japanese invasion of Taiwan: Battle of Baguashan: The Empire of Japan decisively defeats a smaller Formosan army at Changhua, crippling the short-lived Republic of Formosa and leading to its surrender two months later.

Q4870400.name: Battle of Ballantyne Pier
Q4870400.blurb: Police in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada, clash with striking longshoremen, resulting in a total of 60 injuries and 24 arrests.

Q4870422.name: February 2013 Quetta bombing
Q4870422.blurb: A bomb blast at a market in Hazara Town, Quetta, Pakistan kills more than 80 people and injures 190 others.

Q4870439.name: Battle of Beaumont
Q4870439.blurb: Battle of Beaumont during the Flanders Campaign of the War of the First Coalition.

Q4870474.name: Battle of Bessang Pass
Q4870474.blurb: World War II: Filipino troops of the Philippine Commonwealth Army liberate the captured in Ilocos Sur and start the Battle of Bessang Pass in Northern Luzon.

Q4870477.name: Battle of Bhopal
Q4870477.blurb: A peace treaty is signed between Peshwa Bajirao and Jai Singh II following Maratha victory in the Battle of Bhopal.

Q4870499.name: Battle of Bliska
Q4870499.blurb: Mladen II Šubić of Bribir is deposed as the Croatian Ban after the Battle of Bliska.

Q4870503.name: Battle of Bloody Gulch
Q4870503.blurb: World War II: German combat elements, reinforced by the 17th SS Panzergrenadier Division, launch a counterattack on American forces near Carentan.

Q4870506.name: Battle of Bloody Run
Q4870506.blurb: Odawa Chief Pontiac's forces defeat British troops at the Battle of Bloody Run during Pontiac's War.

Q4870552.name: Battle of Brice's Cross Roads
Q4870552.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Brice's Crossroads: Confederate troops under Nathan Bedford Forrest defeat a much larger Union force led by General Samuel D. Sturgis in Mississippi.

Q4870555.name: Battle of Britain Day
Q4870555.blurb: World War II: The climax of the Battle of Britain, when the Luftwaffe launches its largest and most concentrated attack of the entire campaign.

Q4870585.name: Battle of Buffalo
Q4870585.blurb: War of 1812: British soldiers burn Buffalo, New York.

Q4870587.name: Battle of Bukit Timah
Q4870587.blurb: World War II: Second day of the Battle of Bukit Timah is fought in Singapore.

Q4870590.name: Battle of Bull's Gap
Q4870590.blurb: American Civil War: The three-day Battle of Bull's Gap ends in a Union rout as Confederates under Major General John C. Breckinridge pursue them to Strawberry Plains, Tennessee.

Q4870594.name: Battle of Burki
Q4870594.blurb: Following the Battle of Burki, the Indian Army captures Dograi in during the Indo-Pakistani War of 1965.

Q4870598.name: Battle of Burton Bridge
Q4870598.blurb: First English Civil War: Royalist forces defeated the Parliamentarians at the Battle of Burton Bridge, securing a crossing of the River Trent for a convoy of supplies travelling with Queen Henrietta Maria.

Q4870599.name: Battle of Bushy Run
Q4870599.blurb: Pontiac's War: Battle of Bushy Run: British forces led by Henry Bouquet defeat Chief Pontiac's Indians at Bushy Run.

Q4870653.name: Battle of Carberry Hill
Q4870653.blurb: Mary, Queen of Scots, and her new husband Bothwell are confronted by disgruntled Scottish nobles in the encounter at Carberry Hill. The stand-off ends with the surrender of queen Mary.

Q4870679.name: Battle of Caulk's Field
Q4870679.blurb: War of 1812: American militia forces repelled a British force at the Battle of Caulk's Field, killing 41 people including Captain Peter Parker of the Royal Navy.

Q4870720.name: Battle of Gujranwala
Q4870720.blurb: The Battle of Chawinda is fought between Pakistan and India.

Q4870727.name: Battle of Chillianwala
Q4870727.blurb: Second Anglo-Sikh War: Battle of Chillianwala: British forces retreat from the Sikhs.

Q4870755.name: Battle of Ciudad-Real
Q4870755.blurb: Peninsular War: A combined Franco-Polish force defeats the Spanish in the Battle of Ciudad Real.

Q4870758.name: Battle of Cixi
Q4870758.blurb: Taiping Rebellion: The Ever Victorious Army defeats Taiping forces at the Battle of Cixi.

Q4870787.name: Battle of Cooch's Bridge
Q4870787.blurb: American Revolutionary War: During the Battle of Cooch's Bridge, the Flag of the United States is flown in battle for the first time.

Q4870789.name: Battle of Coral–Balmoral
Q4870789.blurb: Vietnam War: The 1st Australian Task Force began the defence of Fire Support Base Coral in the largest unit-level action of the war for the Australian Army.

Q4870811.name: Battle of Crucifix Hill
Q4870811.blurb: World War II: Captain Bobbie Brown earns a Medal of Honor for his actions during the Battle of Crucifix Hill, just outside Aachen.

Q4870862.name: Battle of Delhi
Q4870862.blurb: The Battle of Delhi, during the Second Anglo-Maratha War, between British troops under General Lake, and Marathas of Scindia's army under General Louis Bourquin ends in a British victory.

Q4870864.name: Battle of Dengbu Island
Q4870864.blurb: Chinese Civil War: The Battle of Dengbu Island occurs.

Q4870872.name: Battle of Diamond Rock
Q4870872.blurb: French and Spanish forces begin the assault against British forces occupying Diamond Rock, Martinique.

Q4870894.name: Battle of Dong Dang
Q4870894.blurb: Sino-French War: French Army gains an important victory in the Battle of Đồng Đăng in the Tonkin region of Vietnam.

Q4870922.name: Battle of Droop Mountain
Q4870922.blurb: American Civil War: A Union brigade defeated a Confederate force at the Battle of Droop Mountain in Pocahontas County, West Virginia.

Q4870928.name: Battle of Drumclog
Q4870928.blurb: The Scottish Covenanters defeat John Graham of Claverhouse at the Battle of Drumclog.

Q4870948.name: Battle of Echoee
Q4870948.blurb: Anglo-Cherokee War: Cherokee warriors defeat British forces at the Battle of Echoee near present-day Otto, North Carolina.

Q4870959.name: Battle of Elands River
Q4870959.blurb: The Battle of Elands River during the Second Boer War ends after a 13-day siege is lifted by the British. The battle had begun when a force of between 2,000 and 3,000 Boers had surrounded a force of 500 Australians, Rhodesians, Canadians and British soldiers at a supply dump at Brakfontein Drift.

Q4870962.name: Battle of Elephant Point
Q4870962.blurb: Second World War: British and Indian forces conducted a successful airborne assault on a Japanese artillery battery during the advance to liberate Rangoon, Burma.

Q4870993.name: Battle of Ezra Church
Q4870993.blurb: American Civil War: In the Battle of Ezra Church, Confederate troops make a third unsuccessful attempt under General John Bell Hood to prevent Union forces led by General William T. Sherman from approaching Atlanta, Georgia.

Q4870994.name: Battle of Fair Oaks & Darbytown Road
Q4870994.blurb: American Civil War: A Union attack on the Confederate capital of Richmond is repulsed.

Q4871018.name: Battle of Firenzuola
Q4871018.blurb: Battle of Firenzuola: Lombard forces under King Rudolph II and Adalbert I, margrave of Ivrea, defeat the dethroned Emperor Berengar I of Italy at Firenzuola (Tuscany).

Q4871019.name: Battle of Fishdam Ford
Q4871019.blurb: American Revolutionary War: In the Battle of Fishdam Ford a force of British and Loyalist troops fail in a surprise attack against the South Carolina Patriot militia under Brigadier General Thomas Sumter.

Q4871043.name: Battle of Fort Erie
Q4871043.blurb: The Fenians defeat Canadian forces at Ridgeway and Fort Erie, but the raids end soon after.

Q4871048.name: Battle of Fort Peter
Q4871048.blurb: British troops captured Fort Peter in St. Marys, in the only battle of the War of 1812 to take place in the state of Georgia.

Q4871074.name: Battle of Gang Toi
Q4871074.blurb: Vietnam War: In the Battle of Gang Toi, one of the earliest battles between the two sides, Viet Cong forces repelled an Australian attack.

Q4871079.name: Battle of Garibpur
Q4871079.blurb: Indian troops, partly aided by Mukti Bahini (Bengali guerrillas), defeat the Pakistan army in the Battle of Garibpur.

Q4871084.name: Battle of Gazipur
Q4871084.blurb: Battle of Gazipur: Pakistani forces are defeated as India cedes Gazipur to Bangladesh.

Q4871090.name: Battle of George Square
Q4871090.blurb: The Battle of George Square takes place in Glasgow, Scotland, during a campaign for shorter working hours.

Q4871100.name: Battle of Gifu Castle
Q4871100.blurb: Battle of Gifu Castle: The eastern forces of Tokugawa Ieyasu defeat the western Japanese clans loyal to Toyotomi Hideyori, leading to the destruction of Gifu Castle and serving as a prelude to the Battle of Sekigahara.

Q4871102.name: Battle of Glasgow
Q4871102.blurb: American Civil War: The Union garrison of Glasgow, Missouri surrenders to Confederate forces.

Q4871114.name: Battle of Globe Tavern
Q4871114.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Globe Tavern: Union forces try to cut a vital Confederate supply-line into Petersburg, Virginia, by attacking the Wilmington and Weldon Railroad.

Q4871143.name: Battle of Groton Heights
Q4871143.blurb: American Revolutionary War: The Battle of Groton Heights takes place, resulting in a British victory.

Q4871158.name: Battle of Guantánamo Bay
Q4871158.blurb: Spanish–American War: In the Battle of Guantánamo Bay, U.S. Marines begin the American invasion of Spanish-held Cuba.

Q4871176.name: Battle of Haifa
Q4871176.blurb: World War I: The Battle of Haifa takes place in present-day Israel, part of the Ottoman Empire at that time.

Q4871178.name: Battle of Haifa
Q4871178.blurb: Arab–Israeli War: The port city of Haifa is captured by Jewish forces.

Q4871197.name: Battle of Hayes Pond
Q4871197.blurb: Members of the Lumbee tribe arrived to protest at a Ku Klux Klan rally near Maxton, North Carolina, which turned into an armed confrontation between the two groups (pictured).

Q4871202.name: Battle of Hegra Fortress
Q4871202.blurb: World War II: Norwegian campaign: Norwegian squads in Hegra Fortress and Vinjesvingen capitulate to German forces after all other Norwegian forces in southern Norway had laid down their arms.

Q4871210.name: Battle of Heraklion
Q4871210.blurb: World War II: German paratroopers began the Battle of Heraklion on the island of Crete, capturing the airfield and port in Heraklion ten days later.

Q4871221.name: Battle of Hill 170
Q4871221.blurb: World War II: The end of fighting in the Battle of Hill 170 during the Burma Campaign, in which the British 3 Commando Brigade repulsed a Japanese counterattack on their positions and precipitated a general retirement from the Arakan Peninsula.

Q4871225.name: Battle of Hill 282
Q4871225.blurb: Korean War: The Battle of Hill 282 is the first US friendly-fire incident on British military personnel since World War II.

Q4871254.name: Battle of Hulao
Q4871254.blurb: Battle of Hulao: Li Shimin, the son of the Chinese emperor Gaozu, defeats the numerically superior forces of Dou Jiande near the Hulao Pass (Henan). This victory decides the outcome of the civil war that followed the Sui dynasty's collapse in favour of the Tang dynasty.

Q4871255.name: Battle of Huoyi
Q4871255.blurb: Battle of Huoyi: Li Yuan defeats a Sui dynasty army, opening the path to his capture of the imperial capital Chang'an and the eventual establishment of the Tang dynasty.

Q4871281.name: Battle of Inverurie
Q4871281.blurb: Robert the Bruce, king of Scots, defeats John Comyn, earl of Buchan, decisively in the battle of Inverurie.

Q4871284.name: Battle of Iron Works Hill
Q4871284.blurb: American Revolutionary War: American troops, overwhelmed by British reinforcements, retreated from the Battle of Iron Works Hill.

Q4871299.name: Battle of Jaffna
Q4871299.blurb: Sri Lankan Civil War: Sri Lanka's government announces the conquest of the Tamil stronghold of Jaffna.

Q4871326.name: Battle of Jerusalem Plank Road
Q4871326.blurb: American Civil War: The Battle of Jerusalem Plank Road begins.

Q4871346.name: Battle of Johnsonville
Q4871346.blurb: American Civil War: Nathan Bedford Forrest led a cavalry division in an attack on a Union Army supply base at Johnsonville, Tennessee, resulting in the capture of 150 prisoners.

Q4871359.name: Battle of Kabul
Q4871359.blurb: The Battle of Kabul ends in a Taliban victory; an Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan is established.

Q4871367.name: Battle of Kaiapit
Q4871367.blurb: World War II: Australian troops led by Gordon Grimsley King defeated Imperial Japanese forces at the Battle of Kaiapit in New Guinea.

Q4871411.name: Battle of Kenapacomaqua
Q4871411.blurb: American troops destroy the Miami town of Kenapacomaqua near the site of present-day Logansport, Indiana in the Northwest Indian War.

Q4871422.name: Battle of Kherlen
Q4871422.blurb: The Battle of Kherlen is the second significant victory over Ming dynasty China by the Mongols since 1368.

Q4871455.name: Battle of Kismayo
Q4871455.blurb: Somali and African Union forces launch a coordinated assault on the Somali port of Kismayo to take back the city from al-Shabaab militants.

Q4871464.name: Battle of Knockdoe
Q4871464.blurb: In Ireland, the Hiberno-Norman de Burghs (Burkes) and Cambro-Norman Fitzgeralds fight in the Battle of Knockdoe.

Q4871482.name: Battle of Kororareka
Q4871482.blurb: Māori forces, led by chiefs Te Ruki Kawiti and Hōne Heke, attacked the British settlement of Kororāreka, New Zealand, beginning the Flagstaff War.

Q4871484.name: Battle of Kosmidion
Q4871484.blurb: Ottoman Interregnum: Süleyman Çelebi defeats his brother Musa Çelebi outside the Byzantine capital, Constantinople.

Q4871489.name: Battle of Kowloon
Q4871489.blurb: Battle of Kowloon: British vessels open fire on Chinese war junks enforcing a food sales embargo on the British community in China in the first armed conflict of the First Opium War.

Q4871496.name: Battle of Kuala Lumpur
Q4871496.blurb: World War II: Japanese forces capture Kuala Lumpur, the capital of the Federated Malay States.

Q4871519.name: Battle of La Rochelle
Q4871519.blurb: Hundred Years' War: Battle of La Rochelle.

Q4871527.name: Battle of Lake Okeechobee
Q4871527.blurb: Second Seminole War: American general Zachary Taylor leads 1,100 troops against the Seminoles at the Battle of Lake Okeechobee.

Q4871541.name: Battle of Las Tres Acequias
Q4871541.blurb: Chilean War of Independence: Infighting between the rebel forces of José Miguel Carrera and Bernardo O'Higgins erupts in the Battle of Las Tres Acequias.

Q4871548.name: Capture of Lemnos
Q4871548.blurb: First Balkan War: The Greek navy completes the capture of the island of Lemnos for use as a forward base against the Dardanelles.

Q4871551.name: Battle of Lewisham
Q4871551.blurb: Members of the British National Front (NF) clash with anti-NF demonstrators in Lewisham, London, resulting in 214 arrests and at least 111 injuries.

Q4871558.name: Battle of Lima Site 85
Q4871558.blurb: Vietnam War/Laotian Civil War: North Vietnamese and Pathet Lao forces overwhelmed the American, Laotian, Thai, and Hmong defenders of Lima Site 85.

Q4871565.name: Battle of Linuesa
Q4871565.blurb: The Battle of Linuesa is fought in the context of the Spanish Reconquista between the forces of the Emirate of Granada and the combined army of the Kingdom of Castile and of Jaén resulting in a Castilian victory.

Q4871583.name: Battle of Lochmaben Fair
Q4871583.blurb: Battle of Lochmaben Fair: A 500-man raiding party led by Alexander Stewart, Duke of Albany and James Douglas, 9th Earl of Douglas are defeated by Scots forces loyal to Albany's brother James III of Scotland; Douglas is captured.

Q4871591.name: Battle of Long Khanh
Q4871591.blurb: Vietnam War: Australian forces attacked a heavily fortified North Vietnamese base camp at the Battle of Long Khánh.

Q4871597.name: Battle of Longwoods
Q4871597.blurb: War of 1812: Americans defeat British forces at the Battle of Longwoods between London, Ontario and Thamesville, near present-day Wardsville, Ontario.

Q4871616.name: Battle of Lumphanan
Q4871616.blurb: King Macbeth of Scotland is killed at the Battle of Lumphanan by the forces of Máel Coluim mac Donnchada.

Q4871622.name: Battle of Mabitac
Q4871622.blurb: Philippine–American War: Filipinos under Juan Cailles defeat Americans under Colonel Benjamin F. Cheatham Jr. at Mabitac.

Q4871639.name: Battle of Maidstone
Q4871639.blurb: The Roundheads defeat the Cavaliers at the Battle of Maidstone in the Second English Civil War.

Q4871641.name: Battle of Majadahonda
Q4871641.blurb: Peninsular War: French troops engage British-Portuguese forces in the Battle of Majadahonda.

Q4871659.name: Battle of Mang Yang Pass
Q4871659.blurb: First Indochina War: Battle of Mang Yang Pass: Viet Minh troops belonging to the 803rd Regiment ambush G.M. 100 of France in An Khê.

Q4871677.name: Battle of Marilao River
Q4871677.blurb: Philippine–American War: American forces defeated troops commanded by Philippine president Emilio Aguinaldo at the Battle of Marilao River.

Q4871686.name: Battle of Marstrand
Q4871686.blurb: Scanian War: Denmark–Norway captures the harbor town of Marstrand from Sweden.

Q4871703.name: Battle of Mbumbi
Q4871703.blurb: Portuguese forces score a military victory over the Kingdom of Kongo at the Battle of Mbumbi in present-day Angola.

Q4871740.name: Battle of Mine Creek
Q4871740.blurb: American Civil War: During Price's Missouri Expedition, Union troops defeated Sterling Price's Confederate army in three successive battles: Marais des Cygnes, Mine Creek, and Marmiton River.

Q4871751.name: Battle of Moclín
Q4871751.blurb: The Spanish Reconquista: In the Battle of Moclín the Emirate of Granada ambush a superior pursuing force, killing most of them in a military disaster for the Kingdom of Castile.

Q4871760.name: Battle of Moira
Q4871760.blurb: The Battle of Moira is fought between the High King of Ireland and the Kings of Ulster and Dál Riata. It is claimed to be the largest battle in the history of Ireland.

Q4871771.name: Battle of Mont Sorrel
Q4871771.blurb: World War I: The Battle of Mont Sorrel in the Ypres Salient came to an end as a Canadian assault led German forces to withdraw to their original lines.

Q4871823.name: Battle of Mullaitivu
Q4871823.blurb: Battle of Mullaitivu: The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam capture the Sri Lanka Army's base, killing over 1,200 soldiers.

Q4871827.name: Battle of Muong Khoua
Q4871827.blurb: First Indochina War: Viet Minh forces overran a French and Laotian garrison at Muong Khoua, leaving only four survivors.

Q4871872.name: Battle of Nassau
Q4871872.blurb: War of the Quadruple Alliance: Spanish forces began a failed assault on the British settlement of Nassau in the Bahamas.

Q4871874.name: Negro Fort
Q4871874.blurb: Seminole Wars: The Battle of Negro Fort ends when a hot shot cannonball fired by US Navy Gunboat No. 154 explodes the fort's Powder Magazine, killing approximately 275. It is considered the deadliest single cannon shot in US history.

Q4871883.name: Battle of New Ross
Q4871883.blurb: Battle of New Ross: The attempt to spread the United Irish Rebellion into Munster is defeated.

Q4871911.name: Battle of North Point
Q4871911.blurb: Battle of North Point: an American detachment halts the British land advance to Baltimore in the War of 1812.

Q4871930.name: Battle of Ocho Rios
Q4871930.blurb: Anglo-Spanish War: Spanish forces fail to retake Jamaica at the Battle of Ocho Rios.

Q4871941.name: Battle of Olongapo
Q4871941.blurb: Philippine-American War:  the American Asiatic Squadron destroys a Filipino battery at the Battle of Olongapo.

Q4871945.name: Battle of Onjong
Q4871945.blurb: The People's Volunteer Army ambushed the South Korean II Corps at the Battle of Onjong, and elsewhere engaged the 1st Infantry Division at the Battle of Unsan, marking China's entry into the Korean War.

Q4871958.name: Battle of Osuchy
Q4871958.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Osuchy in Osuchy, Poland, one of the largest battles between Nazi Germany and Polish resistance forces, ends with the defeat of the latter.

Q4871960.name: Battle of Oulart Hill
Q4871960.blurb: The Battle of Oulart Hill takes place in Wexford, Ireland; Irish rebel leaders defeat and kill a detachment of militia.

Q4871978.name: Battle of Palonegro
Q4871978.blurb: Thousand Days' War: The Colombian Conservative Party turns the tide of war in their favor with victory against the Colombian Liberal Party in the Battle of Palonegro.

Q4872032.name: Battle of Phu Lam Tao
Q4872032.blurb: Sino-French War: Chinese victory in the Battle of Phu Lam Tao near Hưng Hóa, northern Vietnam.

Q4872035.name: Battle of Piedmont
Q4872035.blurb: American Civil War: Battle of Piedmont: Union forces under General David Hunter defeat a Confederate army at Piedmont, Virginia, taking nearly 1,000 prisoners.

Q4872072.name: Battle of Pokoku and Irrawaddy River operations
Q4872072.blurb: World War II: The British Indian Army and Imperial Japanese Army begin a series of battles known as the Battle of Pokoku and Irrawaddy River operations.

Q4872076.name: Battle of Polygon Wood
Q4872076.blurb: World War I: The Battle of Polygon Wood begins.

Q4872102.name: Battle of Pratapgarh
Q4872102.blurb: Chattrapati Shivaji Maharaj, Maratha King kills Afzal Khan, Adilshahi in the battle popularly known as Battle of Pratapgarh.

Q4872125.name: Battle of Pulang Lupa
Q4872125.blurb: Filipino insurgents defeat a small American column in the Battle of Pulang Lupa, during the Philippine–American War.

Q4872135.name: Battle of Qian Shui Yuan
Q4872135.blurb: The Tang dynasty scores a decisive victory over their rival Xue Rengao at the Battle of Qianshuiyuan.

Q4872161.name: Battle of Randeniwela
Q4872161.blurb: Portuguese forces are defeated by the Kingdom of Kandy at the Battle of Randeniwela in Sri Lanka.

Q4872177.name: Battle of Rhodes
Q4872177.blurb: Italy begins the invasion and occupation of the Ottoman island of Rhodes.

Q4872181.name: Battle of Ridgefield
Q4872181.blurb: American Revolutionary War: British Army regulars defeated Patriot militias in the Battle of Ridgefield, galvanizing resistance in the Connecticut Colony.

Q4872186.name: Battle of Rio Nuevo
Q4872186.blurb: Anglo-Spanish War: The largest battle ever fought on Jamaica, the three-day Battle of Rio Nuevo, began.

Q4872193.name: Battle of Roatán
Q4872193.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Spain captured the island of Roatán from England off the coast of what is now Honduras.

Q4872207.name: Battle of Rowton Heath
Q4872207.blurb: The Battle of Rowton Heath in England occurs, ending in a Parliamentarian victory over a Royalist army commanded in person by King Charles I.

Q4872215.name: Battle of Rullion Green
Q4872215.blurb: At least 3,000 men of the Royal Scots Army led by Tam Dalyell of the Binns defeat about 900 Covenanter insurgents led by James Wallace of Auchens in the Battle of Rullion Green.

Q4872237.name: Battle of Saintfield
Q4872237.blurb: Irish Rebellion of 1798: Battles of Arklow and Saintfield.

Q4872265.name: Battle of San Carlos
Q4872265.blurb: Falklands War: A British amphibious assault during Operation Sutton leads to the Battle of San Carlos.

Q4872278.name: Battle of San Juan
Q4872278.blurb: Anglo-Spanish War: After a 15-day siege Spanish troops in San Juan, modern-day Puerto Rico, surrendered to an English force under Sir George Clifford.

Q4872284.name: Battle of San Juan del Monte
Q4872284.blurb: Philippine Revolution: After Spanish victory in the Battle of San Juan del Monte, eight provinces in the Philippines are declared under martial law by the Spanish Governor-General Ramón Blanco y Erenas.

Q4872286.name: Battle of San Nicolás
Q4872286.blurb: Argentine War of Independence: A royalist fleet defeats a small flotilla of revolutionary ships in the Battle of San Nicolás on the River Plate.

Q4872288.name: Battle of San Pasqual
Q4872288.blurb: Mexican–American War: American and Mexican forces clashed at the Battle of San Pasqual, a series of skirmishes near San Diego, California.

Q4872308.name: Battle of Santiago (1844)
Q4872308.blurb: One of the most important battles of the Dominican War of Independence from Haiti takes place near the city of Santiago de los Caballeros.

Q4872324.name: Battle of Sattelberg
Q4872324.blurb: World War II: Australian forces launched an assault on Sattelberg, New Guinea, against Japanese forces, initiating the Battle of Sattelberg.

Q4872337.name: Battle of Seattle
Q4872337.blurb: First Battle of Seattle: Marines from the USS Decatur drive off Native American attackers after all-day battle with settlers.

Q4872346.name: Battle of Segale
Q4872346.blurb: Negus Mikael, marching on the Ethiopian capital in support of his son Emperor Iyasu V, is defeated by Fitawrari Habte Giyorgis, securing the throne for Empress Zewditu I.

Q4872384.name: Battle of Sio
Q4872384.blurb: World War II: American and Australian troops won the Battle of Sio against Japanese forces as part of the New Guinea campaign.

Q4872392.name: Battle of Slater's Knoll
Q4872392.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Slater's Knoll on Bougainville comes to an end.

Q4872407.name: Battle of Sobota
Q4872407.blurb: Battle of Sobota: The Swedish Empire led by Charles X Gustav defeats the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.

Q4872415.name: Battle of Sourton Down
Q4872415.blurb: First English Civil War: Despite being vastly outnumbered, a Parliamentarian force under James Chudleigh defeated a Royalist army near Okehampton, Devon, at the Battle of Sourton Down.

Q4872423.name: Battle of Spring Hill
Q4872423.blurb: American Civil War: The Confederate Army of Tennessee misses an opportunity to crush the Union Army of the Ohio in the Battle of Spring Hill during the Franklin–Nashville campaign.

Q4872426.name: Battle of Springfield
Q4872426.blurb: American Revolution: Battle of Springfield fought in and around Springfield, New Jersey (including Short Hills, formerly of Springfield, now of Millburn Township).

Q4872434.name: Battle of Stanhope Park
Q4872434.blurb: First War of Scottish Independence: James Douglas leads a raid into Weardale and almost kills Edward III of England.

Q4872440.name: Battle of Stillman's Run
Q4872440.blurb: The Battle of Stillman's Run, the first battle of the Black Hawk War, is fought.

Q4872467.name: Battle of Suomenlinna
Q4872467.blurb: Åland War: The Battle of Suomenlinna begins.

Q4872470.name: Battle of Suwon Airfield
Q4872470.blurb: Korean War: Five North Korean aircraft attacked an American air convoy above Suwon Air Base in the first air engagement of the Korean War.

Q4872474.name: Battle of Sylhet
Q4872474.blurb: The Battle of Sylhet is fought between the Pakistani military and the Indian Army.

Q4872492.name: Battle of Takur Ghar
Q4872492.blurb: Afghanistan: Seven American Special Operations Forces soldiers and 200 Al-Qaeda Fighters are killed as American forces attempt to infiltrate the Shah-i-Kot Valley on a low-flying helicopter reconnaissance mission.

Q4872498.name: Battle of Tamatave
Q4872498.blurb: A British squadron under Charles Marsh Schomberg defeated a French force off Tamatave, Madagascar, that was attempting to reinforce the French garrison on Mauritius.

Q4872500.name: Battle of Tangier
Q4872500.blurb: Battle of Tangier: a Portuguese expeditionary force initiates a failed attempt to seize the Moroccan citadel of Tangier.

Q4872566.name: Battle of Tom's Brook
Q4872566.blurb: American Civil War: Union cavalrymen defeat Confederate forces at Toms Brook, Virginia during Sheridan's Shenandoah Valley campaign.

Q4872579.name: Battle of Torrington
Q4872579.blurb: Battle of Torrington, Devon: The last major battle of the First English Civil War.

Q4872585.name: Battle of Trangen
Q4872585.blurb: Dano-Swedish War of 1808–1809: The Battle of Trangen takes place at Trangen in Flisa, Hedemarkens Amt, between Swedish and Norwegian troops.

Q4872598.name: Battle of Tsimba Ridge
Q4872598.blurb: World War II: Australian troops advanced along the northern part of Bougainville Island (in present-day Papua New Guinea) and began fighting Japanese forces in the Battle of Tsimba Ridge.

Q4872612.name: Battle of Turnham Green
Q4872612.blurb: First English Civil War: Battle of Turnham Green: The Royalist forces withdraw in the face of the Parliamentarian army and fail to take London.

Q4872646.name: Battle of Valparaíso
Q4872646.blurb: War of 1812: In the Battle of Valparaíso, two American naval vessels are captured by two Royal Navy vessels.

Q4872649.name: Van Buren raid
Q4872649.blurb: American Civil War: Union forces defeated a Confederate cavalry unit in the Van Buren raid, capturing three steamboats, Confederate troops, and various supplies.

Q4872652.name: Battle of Vasai
Q4872652.blurb: The Battle of Vasai commences as the Marathas move to invade Portuguese-occupied territory.

Q4872665.name: Battle of Vianden
Q4872665.blurb: World War II: Thirty members of the Luxembourgish resistance defend the town of Vianden against a larger Waffen-SS attack in the Battle of Vianden.

Q4872670.name: Battle of Vilanova
Q4872670.blurb: The Battle of Vilanova is fought between Portugal and Spain during the Portuguese Restoration War.

Q4872690.name: Battle of Vinh Yen
Q4872690.blurb: First Indochina War: The Battle of Vĩnh Yên begins.

Q4872694.name: Battle of Voltri
Q4872694.blurb: War of the First Coalition: A surprise Austrian attack at the Battle of Voltri marks the beginning of the Italian Campaign, the decisive campaign under Napoleon Bonaparte that will end the war a year later.

Q4872697.name: Battle of Vrbanja Bridge
Q4872697.blurb: Bosnian War: Forces of the Army of Republika Srpska captured a United Nations post at Vrbanja Bridge in Sarajevo; six soldiers of both sides were killed when French forces retook the post later in the day.

Q4872710.name: Battle of Wareo
Q4872710.blurb: World War II: Australian forces began the Battle of Wareo by conducting clearing operations between Bonga and North Hill.

Q4872743.name: Battle of Wireless Ridge
Q4872743.blurb: Battles of Tumbledown and Wireless Ridge, during the Falklands War.

Q4872751.name: Battle of Wolf Mountain
Q4872751.blurb: Crazy Horse and his warriors fight their last battle against the United States Cavalry at Wolf Mountain, Montana Territory.

Q4872753.name: Battle of Woody Point
Q4872753.blurb: Survivors of an attack the previous day by Tla-o-qui-aht on board the Pacific Fur Company's ship Tonquin intentionally detonate a powder magazine on the ship, destroying it and killing about 100 attackers.

Q4872768.name: Battle of Yancheng
Q4872768.blurb: Song dynasty general Yue Fei defeats an army led by Jin dynasty general Wuzhu at the Battle of Yancheng during the Jin–Song Wars.

Q4872776.name: Battle of Yaunis Khan
Q4872776.blurb: Second Ottoman–Mamluk War: Mamluks fail to stop the Ottoman advance towards Egypt at the Battle of Yaunis Khan.

Q4872786.name: Battle of Yongdong
Q4872786.blurb: Korean War: After American troops withdrew, North Korean forces captured the village of Yongdong in South Korea.

Q4872788.name: Battle of Yongju
Q4872788.blurb: Korean War: Heavy fighting begins between British and Australian forces and North Koreans during the Battle of Yongju.

Q4872814.name: Battle of Zsibó
Q4872814.blurb: Rákóczi's War of Independence: The Habsburg Empire and Denmark win a military victory over the Kurucs from Hungary in the Battle of Zsibó.

Q4872836.name: Battle of the Baggage
Q4872836.blurb: The Turgesh drive back an Umayyad invasion of Khuttal, follow them south of the Oxus, and capture their baggage train.

Q4872851.name: Battle of the Black River
Q4872851.blurb: British forces under Edward Despard complete the reconquest of the Black River settlements on the Mosquito Coast from the Spanish.

Q4872896.name: Battle of the Curragh
Q4872896.blurb: Richard Marshal, Earl of Pembroke, was defeated by knights loyal to King Henry III of England at the Battle of the Curragh in County Kildare, Ireland.

Q4872897.name: Battle of the Counts
Q4872897.blurb: The Aragonese fleet under Roger of Lauria defeats a Angevin fleet in the Battle of the Counts close to Naples.

Q4872926.name: Battle of the Gulf of Naples
Q4872926.blurb: Battle of the Gulf of Naples: Roger of Lauria, admiral to King Peter III of Aragon, destroys the Neapolitan fleet and captures Charles of Salerno.

Q4872954.name: Battle of the Mississinewa
Q4872954.blurb: War of 1812: U.S. forces attack a Lenape village in the Battle of the Mississinewa.

Q4872981.name: Battle of the Orontes
Q4872981.blurb: Major Fatimid victory over the Byzantine Empire at the Battle of the Orontes.

Q4872997.name: Battle of the Rhyndacus
Q4872997.blurb: Battle of the Rhyndacus: The Latin emperor Henry of Flanders defeats the Nicaean emperor Theodore I Laskaris.

Q4873030.name: Battle of the Transdanubian Hills
Q4873030.blurb: World War II: Bulgaria and the Soviet Union successfully complete their defense of the north bank of the Drava River as the Battle of the Transdanubian Hills concludes.

Q4873033.name: Battle of the Tugela Heights
Q4873033.blurb: The British Army begins the Battle of the Tugela Heights in an effort to lift the Siege of Ladysmith.

Q4873048.name: Battle of the Îles Saint-Marcouf
Q4873048.blurb: War of the First Coalition: A British garrison repelled a French attack on the Îles Saint-Marcouf off the Normandy coast, inflicting heavy losses.

Q4873054.name: Battle of Étreux
Q4873054.blurb: World War I: Battle of Étreux: A British rearguard action by the Royal Munster Fusiliers during the Great Retreat.

Q4873073.name: Battle on Snowshoes
Q4873073.blurb: French and Indian War: French regulars, Canadien militia and Indigenous forces ambushed Rogers' Rangers forces in the Battle on Snowshoes.

Q4874155.name: Bay View Massacre
Q4874155.blurb: Workers marching for the eight-hour day in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, are shot at by Wisconsin National Guardsmen in what becomes known as the Bay View Massacre.

Q4874200.name: Bay of Fundy Campaign
Q4874200.blurb: The first wave of the Expulsion of the Acadians from the present-day Canadian Maritime provinces by the British began with the Bay of Fundy campaign at Chignecto.

Q4880101.name: Cullen–Harrison Act
Q4880101.blurb: Cullen–Harrison Act: President Franklin D. Roosevelt signs an amendment to the Volstead Act, legalizing the manufacture and sale of "3.2 beer" (3.2% alcohol by weight, approximately 4% alcohol by volume) and light wines.

Q4881454.name: Beit Lid massacre
Q4881454.blurb: Israeli–Palestinian conflict: Beit Lid suicide bombing: In central Israel, near Netanya, two Gazans blow themselves up at a military transit point, killing 19 Israeli soldiers.

Q4887658.name: Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829
Q4887658.blurb: Sati, the Hindu funeral custom of a widow's self-immolation on her husband's pyre, was prohibited by Lord William Bentinck  in parts of British India after years of campaigning by Ram Mohan Roy (pictured).

Q4894124.name: Berners Street Hoax
Q4894124.blurb: The Berners Street hoax is perpetrated by Theodore Hook in the City of Westminster, London.

Q4899564.name: Beverly Hills Supper Club fire
Q4899564.blurb: The Beverly Hills Supper Club in Southgate, Kentucky, is engulfed by fire, killing 165 people inside.

Q4899882.name: Beylerbeyi event
Q4899882.blurb: The janissaries revolt in response to the debasement of coins.

Q4907005.name: Bigod's Rebellion
Q4907005.blurb: Bigod's Rebellion, an armed insurrection attempting to resist the English Reformation, begins.

Q4914342.name: Binh Tai Massacre
Q4914342.blurb: Vietnam War: the Republic of Korea Army commits the Binh Tai Massacre.

Q4914541.name: Binter Mediterráneo Flight 8261
Q4914541.blurb: Four people are killed when Binter Mediterráneo Flight 8261 crashes into the N-340 highway near Málaga Airport.

Q4917202.name: Bisbee Deportation
Q4917202.blurb: The Bisbee Deportation occurs as vigilantes kidnap and deport nearly 1,300 striking miners and others from Bisbee, Arizona.

Q4919446.name: 1970 Cambodian coup d'état
Q4919446.blurb: Lon Nol ousts Prince Norodom Sihanouk of Cambodia.

Q4919790.name: Thai Airways International Flight 311
Q4919790.blurb: Thai Airways International Flight 311 crashes into a mountain north of Kathmandu, Nepal, killing all 113 people on board.

Q4920802.name: Black Friday
Q4920802.blurb: In their campaign for women's voting rights, hundreds of suffragettes march to the British Parliament in London. Several are beaten by police, newspaper attention embarrasses the authorities, and the march is dubbed Black Friday.

Q4921303.name: Black Monday
Q4921303.blurb: Supporters of the Malta Labour Party ransack and destroy the Times of Malta building and other locations associated with the Nationalist Party.

Q4921639.name: Black River Settlement
Q4921639.blurb: British forces under Edward Despard complete the reconquest of the Black River settlements on the Mosquito Coast from the Spanish.

Q4921953.name: Black Sunday
Q4921953.blurb: The Black Sunday dust storm, considered one of the worst storms of the Dust Bowl, sweeps across the Oklahoma and Texas panhandles and neighboring areas.

Q4924393.name: Siege of Colchester
Q4924393.blurb: Second English Civil War: The Siege of Colchester ends when Royalist Forces surrender to the Parliamentary Forces after eleven weeks.

Q4925231.name: Blantyre mining disaster
Q4925231.blurb: The Blantyre mining disaster in Scotland kills 207 miners.

Q4925340.name: Cavalier Parliament
Q4925340.blurb: King Charles II of England dissolves the Cavalier Parliament.

Q4927226.name: Blockade of Almeida
Q4927226.blurb: The Anglo-Portuguese army under Lord Wellington tries to halt a larger French army under Marshal Masséna marching to relieve Almeida in the Battle of Fuentes de Oñoro. After intense fighting, the French are repulsed.

Q4927230.name: Blockade of Saint-Domingue
Q4927230.blurb: Five French warships attempting to escape the Royal Naval blockade of Saint-Domingue are all seized by British warships, signifying the end of the Haitian Revolution.

Q4927945.name: Hurricane Cleo
Q4927945.blurb: Hurricane Cleo dissipated after causing 156 deaths, mainly in Haiti, and causing roughly US$187 million in damages across the Caribbean and southeastern United States.

Q4928061.name: Bloody Falls Massacre
Q4928061.blurb: Bloody Falls massacre: Chipewyan chief Matonabbee, traveling as the guide to Samuel Hearne on his Arctic overland journey, massacres a group of unsuspecting Inuit.

Q4928065.name: Bloody Gulch massacre
Q4928065.blurb: Korean War: Bloody Gulch massacre: Seventy-five American POWs are massacred by the North Korean Army.

Q4928107.name: Bloody Sunday
Q4928107.blurb: Belfast's Bloody Sunday occurs with 20 killings, at least 100 wounded and 200 homes destroyed during rioting and gun battles in Belfast, Northern Ireland.

Q4930640.name: Bluff Cove Air Attacks
Q4930640.blurb: Bluff Cove Air Attacks during the Falklands War: Fifty-six British servicemen are killed by an Argentine air attack on two landing ships, RFA Sir Galahad and RFA Sir Tristram.

Q4940204.name: Bolton Massacre
Q4940204.blurb: English Civil War: Bolton Massacre by Royalist troops under the command of James Stanley, 7th Earl of Derby.

Q4940502.name: Bombardment of Cherbourg
Q4940502.blurb: World War II: United States Navy and British Royal Navy ships bombard Cherbourg to support United States Army units engaged in the Battle of Cherbourg.

Q4940507.name: Bombardment of Fort Stevens
Q4940507.blurb: World War II: A Japanese submarine surfaces near the Columbia River in Oregon, firing 17 shells at Fort Stevens in one of only a handful of attacks by Japan against the United States mainland.

Q4940687.name: Bombing of Bangkok in World War II
Q4940687.blurb: World War II: The Allies bombard Bangkok, leading Thailand, then under Japanese control, to declare war against the United States and United Kingdom.

Q4940688.name: Bombing of Banski dvori
Q4940688.blurb: Croatian War of Independence: Bombing of the Banski Dvori in Zagreb, Croatia.

Q4940732.name: Bombing of Wilhelmshaven in World War II
Q4940732.blurb: World War II: Five hundred aircraft of the U.S. 8th Air Force devastate Wilhelmshaven harbor in Germany.

Q4947346.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina independence referendum, 1992
Q4947346.blurb: A referendum is begun in Bosnia and Herzegovina for the determination of Bosnian independence.

Q4950234.name: Bourne End rail crash
Q4950234.blurb: The Bourne End rail crash, in Hertfordshire, England, kills 43.

Q4951955.name: Boxing from St. Nicholas Arena
Q4951955.blurb: After going bankrupt in 1955, the American broadcaster DuMont Television Network makes its final broadcast, a boxing match from St. Nicholas Arena in New York in the Boxing from St. Nicholas Arena series.

Q4953154.name: Braathens SAFE Flight 139
Q4953154.blurb: Braathens SAFE Flight 139 is hijacked on approach to Oslo Airport, Fornebu. Special forces arrest the hijacker and there are no fatalities.

Q4957361.name: Braniff Flight 352
Q4957361.blurb: Eighty-five people are killed when Braniff International Airways Flight 352 crashes near Dawson, Texas.

Q4957364.name: Braniff Flight 542
Q4957364.blurb: A Lockheed L-188 Electra crashes in Buffalo, Texas, killing 34 people.

Q4968393.name: Brink's-MAT robbery
Q4968393.blurb: Brink's-Mat robbery: In London, 6,800 gold bars worth nearly £26 million are stolen from the Brink's-Mat vault at Heathrow Airport.

Q4968828.name: Bristol Bus Boycott, 1963
Q4968828.blurb: The Bristol Bus Boycott is held in Bristol to protest the Bristol Omnibus Company's refusal to employ Black or Asian bus crews, drawing national attention to racial discrimination in the United Kingdom.

Q4969947.name: British European Airways Flight 548
Q4969947.blurb: Staines air disaster: One hundred eighteen people are killed when a BEA H.S. Trident crashes minutes after takeoff from London's Heathrow Airport.

Q4971968.name: Broad Street Riot
Q4971968.blurb: The Broad Street Riot occurs in Boston, fueled by ethnic tensions between Yankees and Irish.

Q4972356.name: Broadwater Farm riot
Q4972356.blurb: Police constable Keith Blakelock was killed during rioting in the Broadwater Farm housing estate in Tottenham, London.

Q4976778.name: Brownsville Affair
Q4976778.blurb: The all black infantrymen of the U.S. Army's 25th Infantry Regiment are accused of killing a white bartender and wounding a white police officer in Brownsville, Texas, despite exculpatory evidence; all are later dishonorably discharged. (Their records were later restored to reflect honorable discharges but there were no financial settlements.)

Q4978527.name: Bruce campaign in Ireland
Q4978527.blurb: The Second Battle of Athenry takes place near Athenry during the Bruce campaign in Ireland.

Q4979089.name: Brunner Mine disaster
Q4979089.blurb: An explosion at the Brunner Mine near Greymouth, New Zealand, kills 65 coal miners in the country's worst industrial accident.

Q4979780.name: Brussels Agreement, 1984
Q4979780.blurb: Under the Brussels Agreement signed between the governments of the United Kingdom and Spain, the former agrees to enter into discussions with Spain over Gibraltar, including sovereignty.

Q4984261.name: Buddhist Uprising
Q4984261.blurb: During the Buddhist Uprising, South Vietnamese Prime Minister Nguyễn Cao Kỳ personally attempts to lead the capture of the restive city of Đà Nẵng before backing down.

Q4986899.name: Bukit Ho Swee Fire
Q4986899.blurb: A fire broke out at a squatter settlement in Bukit Ho Swee, Singapore, rendering approximately 16,000 people homeless.

Q4992083.name: Sterling Airways Flight 296
Q4992083.blurb: Sterling Airways Flight 296 crashes near Kalba, United Arab Emirates while on approach to Dubai International Airport, killing 112 people.

Q4992248.name: Assassination of Luis Carrero Blanco
Q4992248.blurb: Assassination of Luis Carrero Blanco: A car bomb planted by ETA in Madrid kills three people, including the Prime Minister of Spain, Admiral Luis Carrero Blanco.

Q4993694.name: Danish Maastricht Treaty referendum
Q4993694.blurb: Riots in Nørrebro, Copenhagen, caused by the approval of the four Danish exceptions in the Maastricht Treaty referendum. Police open fire against civilians for the first time since World War II and injure 11 demonstrators.

Q4996248.name: 1934 Bulgarian coup d'état
Q4996248.blurb: Zveno and the Bulgarian Army engineer a coup d'état and install Kimon Georgiev as the new Prime Minister of Bulgaria.

Q4999914.name: Burning of Edinburgh
Q4999914.blurb: The Burning of Edinburgh by an English army is the first action of the Rough Wooing.

Q5000644.name: Burst of Joy
Q5000644.blurb: The Pulitzer Prize–winning photograph Burst of Joy is taken, depicting a former prisoner of war being reunited with his family, which came to symbolize the end of United States involvement in the Vietnam War.

Q5001014.name: Burunga massacre
Q5001014.blurb: Bangladesh Liberation War: The Pakistan Army slaughters at least 71 Hindus in Burunga, Sylhet, Bangladesh.

Q5003056.name: Buttevant Rail Disaster
Q5003056.blurb: A train crash kills 18 people and injures over 170 more in County Cork, Ireland.

Q5008496.name: CAAC Flight 301
Q5008496.blurb: CAAC Flight 301 overshoots the runway at Kai Tak Airport and crashes into Kowloon Bay, killing seven people.

Q5013224.name: Brussels Airport diamond heist
Q5013224.blurb: Armed robbers steal a haul of diamonds worth $50 million during a raid at Brussels Airport in Belgium.

Q5018202.name: Cal Poly football team plane crash
Q5018202.blurb: An airplane carrying the Cal Poly football team crashes on takeoff in Toledo, Ohio.

Q5019415.name: Caledonian Airways Flight 153
Q5019415.blurb: A Caledonian Airways Douglas DC-7 crashes shortly after takeoff from Cameroon, killing 111 – the worst crash of a DC-7.

Q5020216.name: California Agricultural Labor Relations Act
aliases: Alatorre-Zenovich-Dunlap-Berman Agricultural Labor Relations Act of 1975
Q5020216.blurb: Governor Jerry Brown signed the California Agricultural Labor Relations Act, one of the first laws in the United States guaranteeing collective bargaining rights to farmworkers.

Q5021265.name: 2003 California gubernatorial recall election
Q5021265.blurb: California gubernatorial recall: Then Governor of California Gray Davis announces that the state would face a record budget deficit of $35 billion, roughly double the figure reported during his reelection campaign one month earlier.

Q5023193.name: death march
Q5023193.blurb: World War II: A death march from Dachau to the Austrian border is halted by the segregated, all-Nisei 522nd Field Artillery Battalion of the U.S. Army in southern Bavaria, saving several hundred prisoners.

Q5026437.name: Cameroon Airlines Flight 3701
Q5026437.blurb: Cameroon Airlines Flight 3701 crashes on approach to Douala International Airport in Douala, Cameroon, killing 71 of the 76 people on board.

Q5027352.name: Camp Liberty killings
Q5027352.blurb: An American soldier in Iraq opens fire on a counseling center at Camp Liberty in Baghdad, killing five other US soldiers and wounding three.

Q5027837.name: Campaign of Danture
Q5027837.blurb: Troops of the Portuguese Empire are defeated on Sri Lanka, bringing an end to the Campaign of Danture.

Q5027839.name: Filibuster War
Q5027839.blurb: A group of American mercenaries led by William Walker set sail from San Francisco to conquer Nicaragua.

Q5029693.name: Canadian Arctic Expedition (1913–1918)
Q5029693.blurb: The Karluk, flagship of the Canadian Arctic Expedition, sinks after being crushed by ice.

Q5030419.name: Canadian Pacific Air Lines Flight 21
Q5030419.blurb: Canadian Pacific Air Lines Flight 21 is destroyed by a bomb near 100 Mile House, Canada, killing 52.

Q5032419.name: caning of Charles Sumner
Q5032419.blurb: Senator Charles Sumner (pictured) was assaulted by Representative Preston Brooks in the United States Senate chamber in retaliation for a speech in which Sumner fiercely criticized slaveholders.

Q5032915.name: Canoe River train crash
Q5032915.blurb: Two trains collided near Valemount, Canada, killing 21 people; the subsequent trial brought future prime minister John Diefenbaker to greater political attention.

Q5035447.name: Capital Airlines Flight 20
aliases: Charles City County plane crash of 1960
Q5035447.blurb: Capital Airlines Flight 20 crashes into a farm in Charles City County, Virginia, killing all 50 aboard, the third fatal Capital Airlines crash in as many years.

Q5035448.name: Capital Airlines Flight 67
Q5035448.blurb: Capital Airlines Flight 67 crashes in Tittabawassee Township, Michigan, near Freeland Tri-City Airport, killing 47.

Q5035895.name: Capitol Hill massacre
Q5035895.blurb: Capitol Hill massacre: A gunman kills six people before taking his own life at a party in Seattle's Capitol Hill neighborhood.

Q5035992.name: Capitulation of Tainan
Q5035992.blurb: The capitulation of Tainan completes the Japanese conquest of Taiwan.

Q5035993.name: Capitulation of Stettin
Q5035993.blurb: War of the Fourth Coalition: Convinced that he is facing a much larger force, Prussian General von Romberg, commanding 5,300 men, surrenders the city of Stettin to 800 French soldiers.

Q5036985.name: Capture of Berwick
Q5036985.blurb: Edward I sacks Berwick-upon-Tweed, during armed conflict between Scotland and England.

Q5036989.name: Capture of Berwick
Q5036989.blurb: The Treaty of Fotheringhay is signed between the English and Alexander Stewart, Duke of Albany, the rebellious brother of king James III of Scotland.

Q5037000.name: Capture of Columbia
Q5037000.blurb: American Civil War: Columbia, South Carolina, is burned as Confederate forces flee from advancing Union forces.

Q5037002.name: Capture of Damascus
Q5037002.blurb: World War I: The Egyptian Expeditionary Force captures Damascus.

Q5037012.name: Capture of Fort Erie
Q5037012.blurb: War of 1812: American forces capture Fort Erie from British troops in Upper Canada.

Q5037013.name: Capture of Fort Rocher
Q5037013.blurb: The Capture of Fort Rocher takes place during the Anglo-Spanish War.

Q5037031.name: Capture of Malolos
Q5037031.blurb: Philippine–American War: Malolos, capital of the First Philippine Republic, is captured by American forces.

Q5037033.name: Capture of Mexicali
Q5037033.blurb: Mexican Revolution: Mexicali is captured by the Mexican Liberal Party, igniting the Magonista rebellion of 1911.

Q5037052.name: Capture of Roxburgh
Q5037052.blurb: The Kingdom of Scotland captures Roxburgh, one of the last English strongholds in Scotland, following a siege.

Q5037058.name: Capture of Savannah
Q5037058.blurb: American Revolutionary War: British forces under the command of Lieutenant Colonel Archibald Campbell defeat American forces under Major General Robert Howe and capture the port city of Savannah, Georgia.

Q5037062.name: Capture of Trincomalee
Q5037062.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: The invasion of Ceylon ended with Johan van Angelbeek, the Batavian governor of the island, surrendering Colombo to British forces.

Q5037067.name: Capture of USS President
Q5037067.blurb: War of 1812: American frigate USS President, commanded by Commodore Stephen Decatur, is captured by a squadron of four British frigates.

Q5037073.name: Capture of the sloop Anne
Q5037073.blurb: Roberto Cofresí, one of the last successful Caribbean pirates, is defeated in combat and captured by authorities.

Q5038376.name: Cardiff Blitz
Q5038376.blurb: World War II: The Cardiff Blitz severely damages the cathedral in Cardiff, Wales.

Q5044019.name: Carnew massacre
Q5044019.blurb: United Irishmen Rebellion: Battle of Carlow begins; executions of suspected rebels at Carnew and at Dunlavin Green take place.

Q5046647.name: Carrollton bus collision
Q5046647.blurb: Carrollton bus collision: A drunk driver traveling the wrong way on Interstate 71 near Carrollton, Kentucky, hits a converted school bus carrying a church youth group. Twenty-seven die in the crash and ensuing fire.

Q5047972.name: Casablanca Fair of 1915
Q5047972.blurb: The Casablanca Fair (poster pictured) opened in the French protectorate in Morocco.

Q5050093.name: Castle Gate Mine disaster
Q5050093.blurb: A mine disaster kills 172 coal miners near Castle Gate, Utah.

Q5051355.name: Catalpa rescue
Q5051355.blurb: Catalpa rescue: The rescue of six Fenian prisoners from Fremantle Prison in Western Australia.

Q5053955.name: murder of Catrine da Costa
Q5053955.blurb: Parts of the dismembered body of Swedish prostitute Catrine da Costa were found in Stockholm.

Q5060415.name: Central Bank bombing
Q5060415.blurb: An explosives-filled truck rams into the gates of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka in Colombo, killing at least 86 people and injuring 1,400.

Q5062182.name: Centralia Massacre
Q5062182.blurb: The Industrial Workers of the World attack an Armistice Day parade in Centralia, Washington, ultimately resulting in the deaths of five people.

Q5066829.name: Chagai-II
Q5066829.blurb: Nuclear Testing: Pakistan conducts an underground test in the Kharan Desert. It is reported to be a plutonium device with yield of 20kt TNT equivalent.

Q5069681.name: Raid on Chambersburg
Q5069681.blurb: American Civil War: Confederate troops conduct a raid on Chambersburg, Pennsylvania.

Q5073209.name: Tunam massacre
Q5073209.blurb: Chaplain–Medic massacre: American POWs are massacred by North Korean Army.

Q5084679.name: Norwegian Campaign
Q5084679.blurb: World War II: Norwegian campaign: Norwegian squads in Hegra Fortress and Vinjesvingen capitulate to German forces after all other Norwegian forces in southern Norway had laid down their arms.

Q5091143.name: Chencholai bombing
Q5091143.blurb: Sri Lankan Civil War: Sixty-one schoolgirls killed in Chencholai bombing by Sri Lanka Air Force air strike.

Q5092505.name: Cherry Valley massacre
Q5092505.blurb: Cherry Valley massacre: Loyalists and Seneca Indian forces attack a fort and village in eastern New York during the American Revolutionary War, killing more than forty civilians and soldiers.

Q5096252.name: Chicken Kiev speech
Q5096252.blurb: U.S. president George H. W. Bush delivered a speech in the Ukrainian parliament in Kiev warning against independence from the Soviet Union.

Q5098739.name: Chilean Constitution of 1833
Q5098739.blurb: The Chilean Constitution of 1833 is promulgated.

Q5098799.name: Chilean nationalization of copper
Q5098799.blurb: The nationalization of all large copper mines in Chile is completed.

Q5098852.name: Chilean silver rush
Q5098852.blurb: A Chilean prospecting party led by José Díaz Gana discovers the silver ores of Caracoles in the Bolivian portion of Atacama Desert,  leading to the last of the Chilean silver rushes  and a diplomatic dispute over its taxation between Chile and Bolivia.

Q5099564.name: China Airlines Flight 204
Q5099564.blurb: China Airlines Flight 204 crashes after takeoff from Hualien Airport in Taiwan, killing all 54 people on board.

Q5099569.name: China Airlines Flight 605
Q5099569.blurb: China Airlines Flight 605, a brand-new 747-400, overruns the runway at Hong Kong Kai Tak Airport.

Q5099695.name: China General Aviation Flight 7552
Q5099695.blurb: China General Aviation Flight 7552 crashes during takeoff from Nanjing Dajiaochang Airport, killing 108.

Q5099822.name: China Northern Airlines Flight 6901
Q5099822.blurb: China Northern Airlines Flight 6901 crashes on approach to Ürümqi Diwopu International Airport in Ürümqi, China, killing 12 people.

Q5099824.name: China Northwest Airlines Flight 2119
Q5099824.blurb: China Northwest Airlines Flight 2119 crashes during takeoff from Yinchuan Xihuayuan Airport in Yinchuan, Ningxia, China, killing 55 people.

Q5099830.name: China Northwest Airlines Flight 2303
Q5099830.blurb: China Northwest Airlines Flight 2303 crashes near Xi'an Xianyang International Airport, killing all 160 people on board.

Q5099905.name: China Southern Airlines Flight 3943
Q5099905.blurb: China Southern Airlines Flight 3943 crashes on approach to Guilin Qifengling Airport in Guilin, China, killing all 141 people on board.

Q5099909.name: China Southern Airlines Flight 3456
Q5099909.blurb: China Southern Airlines Flight 3456 crashes on approach into Bao'an International Airport, killing 35 people.

Q5100835.name: Los Angeles Chinese massacre of 1871
Q5100835.blurb: An estimated 17 to 22 Chinese immigrants are lynched in Los Angeles, California.

Q5100941.name: Chinese stock bubble of 2007
Q5100941.blurb: Chinese stock bubble of 2007: The Shanghai Stock Exchange falls 9%, the largest daily fall in ten years, following speculation about a crackdown on illegal share offerings and trading, and fears about accelerating inflation.

Q5103591.name: Siege of Málaga
Q5103591.blurb: The Siege of Málaga commences during the Spanish Reconquista.

Q5104052.name: Peruman railway accident
Q5104052.blurb: The Island Express train travelling from Bangalore to Kanyakumari derails on the Peruman bridge and falls into Ashtamudi Lake, Kerala in India killing 105 passengers and injuring over 200 more.

Q5110707.name: Christie Pits riot
Q5110707.blurb: Christie Pits riot takes place in Toronto, Ontario.

Q5113246.name: Christopher Smart's asylum confinement
Q5113246.blurb: English poet Christopher Smart is admitted into St Luke's Hospital for Lunatics in London, beginning his six-year confinement to mental asylums.

Q5114183.name: Chronology of Provisional Irish Republican Army actions
Q5114183.blurb: A British soldier is killed in the Inglis Barracks bombing in London, England.

Q5115965.name: December 2001 riots in Argentina
Q5115965.blurb: Argentine economic crisis: December riots: Riots erupt in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

Q5116036.name: Chuknagar massacre
Q5116036.blurb: In the Chuknagar massacre, Pakistani forces massacre thousands, mostly Bengali Hindus.

Q5116509.name: Chuquisaca Revolution
Q5116509.blurb: Chuquisaca Revolution: Patriot revolt in Chuquisaca (modern-day Sucre) against the Spanish Empire, sparking the Latin American wars of independence.

Q5120355.name: Cincinnati riots of 1884
Q5120355.blurb: A mob in Cincinnati, Ohio, United States attacks members of a jury which had returned a verdict of manslaughter in what was seen as a clear case of murder; over the next few days the mob would riot and burn down the courthouse.

Q5123708.name: City of Greater New York
Q5123708.blurb: New York, New York annexes land from surrounding counties, creating the City of Greater New York. The four initial boroughs, Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, and The Bronx, are joined on January 25 by Staten Island to create the modern city of five boroughs.

Q5123963.name: Bloody Sunday
Q5123963.blurb: Second Boer War: Imperial forces suffer their worst single-day loss of life on Bloody Sunday, the first day of the Battle of Paardeberg.

Q5124398.name: Civil Air Transport Flight 106
Q5124398.blurb: A Curtiss C-46 Commando crashes in the Shengang District of Taiwan, killing 57 people.

Q5125870.name: Clapham Junction rail crash
Q5125870.blurb: The Clapham Junction rail crash kills thirty-five and injures hundreds after two collisions of three commuter trains—one of the worst train crashes in the United Kingdom.

Q5127664.name: Clarkston explosion
Q5127664.blurb: A gas explosion kills 22 people at a shopping centre near Glasgow, Scotland.

Q5129487.name: Claudy bombing
Q5129487.blurb: The Troubles: Hours after the British Army's Operation Motorman brought an end to the self-declared autonomous area of Free Derry (Free Derry Corner pictured) in Northern Ireland, three car bombs exploded in the village of Claudy.

Q5130457.name: Clean Air Act 1956
Q5130457.blurb: The "Great Smog of London" (pictured) began and lasted for five days, causing 12,000 deaths and leading to the Clean Air Act 1956.

Q5132076.name: Cleveland Browns relocation controversy
Q5132076.blurb: Cleveland Browns relocation controversy: Art Modell announces that he signed a deal that would relocate the Cleveland Browns to Baltimore.

Q5132101.name: Cleveland Clinic fire of 1929
Q5132101.blurb: A fire at the Cleveland Clinic in Cleveland, Ohio kills 123.

Q5132125.name: Cleveland East Ohio Gas explosion
Q5132125.blurb: Liquefied natural gas leaks from storage tanks in Cleveland and then explodes, leveling 30 blocks and killing 130 people.

Q5132233.name: Stockton schoolyard shooting
Q5132233.blurb: Patrick Purdy opens fire at an elementary school in Stockton, California, killing five and wounding 31 others.

Q5144758.name: Colfax massacre
Q5144758.blurb: The Colfax massacre: More than 60 to 150 black men are murdered in Colfax, Louisiana, while surrendering to a mob of former Confederate soldiers and members of the Ku Klux Klan.

Q5144772.name: Colgan Air Flight 9446
Q5144772.blurb: A Beechcraft 1900 operating as Colgan Air Flight 9446 crashes after taking off from Barnstable Municipal Airport in Yarmouth, Massachusetts, killing both pilots on board.

Q5147475.name: Collinwood school fire
Q5147475.blurb: The Collinwood school fire, Collinwood near Cleveland, Ohio, kills 174 people.

Q5148759.name: Colorado Coalfield War
Q5148759.blurb: Nineteen men, women, and children participating in a strike are killed in the Ludlow Massacre during the Colorado Coalfield War.

Q5149908.name: Columbia University protests of 1968
Q5149908.blurb: Vietnam War: Student protesters at Columbia University in New York City take over administration buildings and shut down the university.

Q5150488.name: Comair Flight 3272
Q5150488.blurb: Comair Flight 3272 crashes in Raisinville Township in Monroe County, Michigan, killing 29 people.

Q5151469.name: Comedy Playhouse
Q5151469.blurb: Last of the Summer Wine, the longest-running sitcom in the world, premiered as an episode of the BBC's Comedy Playhouse.

Q5156631.name: Complexo do Alemão massacre
Q5156631.blurb: The Brazilian Military Police invades the favelas of Complexo do Alemão in an episode which is remembered as the Complexo do Alemão massacre.

Q5158727.name: conclusion of the American Civil War
Q5158727.blurb: American Civil War: The Confederate government is declared dissolved at Washington, Georgia.

Q5159340.name: Condor Flugdienst Flight 3782
Q5159340.blurb: Condor Flugdienst Flight 3782 crashes near Seferihisar, Turkey, killing 16 people.

Q5159748.name: Confederate States presidential election
Q5159748.blurb: American Civil War: The 109 electors of the several states of the Confederate States of America unanimously elect Jefferson Davis as President and Alexander H. Stephens as Vice President.

Q5160909.name: Congress of the People
Q5160909.blurb: The South African Congress Alliance adopts the Freedom Charter at the Congress of the People in Kliptown.

Q5161033.name: 2013 Hyderabad blasts
Q5161033.blurb: At least 17 people are killed and 119 injured following several bombings in the Indian city of Hyderabad.

Q5162445.name: Conquest of Santarém
Q5162445.blurb: Afonso I of Portugal captures in a surprise attack the city of Santarem from the Almoravids.

Q5163064.name: 1990 Conservative Party (UK) leadership election
Q5163064.blurb: British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher withdraws from the Conservative Party leadership election, confirming the end of her Premiership.

Q5165236.name: Continental Airlines Flight 11
Q5165236.blurb: Continental Airlines Flight 11 crashes in Unionville, Missouri after bombs explode on board, killing 45.

Q5165237.name: Continental Airlines Flight 1713
Q5165237.blurb: Continental Airlines Flight 1713 crashes during takeoff from Stapleton International Airport in Denver, Colorado, killing 25.

Q5166252.name: Convention for the Protection of Producers of Phonograms Against Unauthorized Duplication of Their Phonograms
Q5166252.blurb: Sound recordings are granted U.S. federal copyright protection for the first time.

Q5166258.name: Convention of 1833
Q5166258.blurb: The Convention of 1833, a political gathering of settlers in Mexican Texas to help draft a series of petitions to the Mexican government, begins in San Felipe de Austin.

Q5166259.name: Convention of 1832
Q5166259.blurb: The first political gathering of colonists (president pictured) in Mexican Texas convened to seek reforms from the Mexican government.

Q5166621.name: Convoy HX 300
Q5166621.blurb: World War II: The largest trade convoy of the world wars arrives safely in the Western Approaches.

Q5167679.name: dissolution of the Soviet Union
aliases: the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics fell
Break up of the Soviet Union
Causes of the collapse of the Soviet Union
Causes of the dissolution of the Soviet Union
Disintegration of the former Soviet Union
Dissolution of the Union of Socialist Soviet Republics
Dissolution of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics
Effects of the dissolution of the Soviet Union on China
Fall of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics
The Dissolution of the Soviet Union
The collapse of the Soviet Union
The fall of the Soviet Union
The fall of the Soviet Union in 1991
Q5167679.blurb: Dissolution of the Soviet Union: The Central Committee of the Soviet Communist Party agrees to give up its monopoly on power.

Q5167832.name: Cooper Union speech
Q5167832.blurb: Abraham Lincoln makes a speech at Cooper Union in the city of New York that plays an important role in his election to the Presidency.

Q5168156.name: Copa Airlines Flight 201
Q5168156.blurb: Copa Airlines Flight 201 breaks apart in mid-air and crashes into the Darién Gap in Panama, killing all 47 aboard.

Q5171686.name: Cornerstone Speech
Q5171686.blurb: Alexander H. Stephens gives the Cornerstone Speech.

Q5172236.name: coronation of George VI and Elizabeth
aliases: Coronation of King George VI and Queen Elizabeth
Q5172236.blurb: King George VI and Queen Elizabeth of the United Kingdom are crowned in Westminster Abbey.

Q5172397.name: Corporate Airlines Flight 5966
Q5172397.blurb: Thirteen people are killed when Corporate Airlines Flight 5966 crashes in Adair County, Missouri, while on approach to Kirksville Regional Airport.

Q5177976.name: Coup of 25 November 1975
Q5177976.blurb: Coup of 25 November 1975, a failed military coup d'état by Portuguese far-left activists seeking to hijack the  Portuguese transition to democracy to establish a communist regime.

Q5177978.name: Coup of Cao Mao
Q5177978.blurb: Sima Zhao's regicide of Cao Mao: The figurehead Wei emperor Cao Mao personally leads an attempt to oust his regent, Sima Zhao; the attempted coup is crushed and the emperor killed.

Q5184298.name: Cresap's War
Q5184298.blurb: A treaty between Pennsylvania and Maryland ends the Conojocular War with settlement of a boundary dispute and exchange of prisoners.

Q5185838.name: Cripple Creek miners' strike of 1894
Q5185838.blurb: The Cripple Creek miner's strike, led by the Western Federation of Miners, begins in Cripple Creek, Colorado, United States.

Q5192131.name: Cubana de Aviación Flight 310
Q5192131.blurb: Cubana de Aviación Flight 310, a Yakovlev Yak-42, crashes near Bejuma, Carabobo State, Venezuela, killing 22 people.

Q5192132.name: Cubana de Aviación Flight 1216
Q5192132.blurb: Cubana de Aviación Flight 1216 overshoots the runway at La Aurora International Airport, killing 18.

Q5192135.name: Cubana de Aviación Flight 9646
Q5192135.blurb: Cubana de Aviación Flight 9046 crashes into a residential area of Havana shortly after takeoff from José Martí International Airport, killing 150.

Q5193032.name: Cullin la Ringo massacre
Q5193032.blurb: Aboriginal Australians kill nineteen Europeans in the Cullin-la-ringo massacre.

Q5194930.name: Curragh Incident
Q5194930.blurb: In the Curragh incident, over 100 British Army officers threaten to resign if ordered to march against the Ulster Volunteers.

Q5197348.name: Cy Young's perfect game
Q5197348.blurb: Pitching for the Boston Americans, Cy Young threw the first perfect game in modern professional baseball.

Q5198801.name: Cyclone Glenda
Q5198801.blurb: Cyclone Glenda, one of the strongest tropical cyclones in the Australian region makes landfall near Onslow, Western Australia.

Q5213021.name: Dan-Air Flight 240
Q5213021.blurb: Dan-Air Flight 240, flying to East Midlands Airport, crashes in Nailstone, Leicestershire. All three crew members perish.

Q5213023.name: Dan-Air Flight 1008
Q5213023.blurb: One hundred forty-six people are killed when Dan-Air Flight 1008 crashes near Los Rodeos Airport in Tenerife, Canary Islands.

Q5224211.name: Darr Mine Disaster
Q5224211.blurb: Two hundred thirty-nine coal miners die in the Darr Mine Disaster in Jacobs Creek, Pennsylvania.

Q5228013.name: Daulatpur–Saturia tornado
Q5228013.blurb: The deadliest known tornado strikes Central Bangladesh, killing upwards of 1,300, injuring 12,000, and leaving as many as 80,000 homeless.

Q5231565.name: The Price Is Right
Q5231565.blurb: The Price Is Right premieres on CBS. It currently is the longest running game show on American television.

Q5242942.name: Day of Rage
Q5242942.blurb: Arab Spring: On the Day of Rage, Bahraini youths began an uprising against the government in 55 marches across 25 locations.

Q5247270.name: Death and funeral of Kim Il-sung
Q5247270.blurb: Kim Jong Il begins to assume supreme leadership of North Korea upon the death of his father, Kim Il Sung.

Q5247276.name: Death and state funeral of King Hussein
Q5247276.blurb: Crown Prince Abdullah becomes the King of Jordan on the death of his father, King Hussein.

Q5247407.name: death of Charlotte Shaw
Q5247407.blurb: Fourteen-year-old English schoolgirl Charlotte Shaw drowned on Dartmoor, becoming the first person to die in connection with the annual Ten Tors challenge.

Q5247467.name: death of Joseph Smith
Q5247467.blurb: Joseph Smith, founder of the Latter Day Saint movement, and his brother Hyrum Smith, are killed by a mob at the Carthage, Illinois jail.

Q5247487.name: death of Linda Norgrove
Q5247487.blurb: Scottish aid worker Linda Norgrove and three Afghan colleagues were kidnapped by members of the Taliban in Kunar Province, Afghanistan.

Q5247494.name: death of Marvin Gaye
Q5247494.blurb: Singer Marvin Gaye is shot to death by his father in his home in Arlington Heights, Los Angeles, California.

Q5247504.name: death of Muhammad Zia-ul-Haq
Q5247504.blurb: President of Pakistan Muhammad Zia-ul-Haq and U.S. Ambassador Arnold Raphel are killed in a plane crash.

Q5247537.name: death of Stevie Ray Vaughan
Q5247537.blurb: American musician Stevie Ray Vaughan, one of the most influential guitarists in the revival of blues in the 1980s, was killed in a helicopter crash.

Q5248943.name: December 1964 South Vietnamese coup
Q5248943.blurb: The ruling junta of South Vietnam, led by Nguyễn Khánh, initiated a coup, dissolving the High National Council, a civilian advisory body.

Q5248978.name: December 2005 protest for democracy in Hong Kong
Q5248978.blurb: Tens of thousands of people in Hong Kong protest for democracy and call on the government to allow universal and equal suffrage.

Q5251995.name: Operation Arctic Fox
Q5251995.blurb: World War II: Hjalmar Siilasvuo ordered Finnish forces to halt their assault against Soviet forces near Salla, concluding Operation Arctic Fox.

Q5254563.name: Delta Air Lines Flight 1288
Q5254563.blurb: A McDonnell Douglas MD-88 operating as Delta Air Lines Flight 1288 experiences a turbine engine failure during takeoff from Pensacola International Airport, killing two and injuring five of the 147 people on board.

Q5254564.name: Delta Air Lines Flight 1141
Q5254564.blurb: Delta Air Lines Flight 1141 crashes during takeoff from Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport, killing 14.

Q5254567.name: Delta Air Lines Flight 723
Q5254567.blurb: A Delta Air Lines jetliner, flight DL 723, crashes while landing in fog at Logan International Airport, Boston, Massachusetts, killing 89.

Q5254589.name: opposition to United States involvement in the Vietnam War
Q5254589.blurb: Vietnam War protests: At an anti-war rally in New York City, David J. Miller burned his draft card (example pictured), the first such act to result in arrest under a new amendment to the Selective Service Act.

Q5255169.name: Demerara rebellion of 1823
Q5255169.blurb: At least 9,000 enslaved people rebelled in the British colony in Demerara-Essequibo (in present-day Guyana), demanding emancipation.

Q5258192.name: Tragedia del Ycua
Q5258192.blurb: A supermarket fire kills 424 people and injures 360 others in Asunción, Paraguay.

Q5260046.name: deorbit of Mir
Q5260046.blurb: The Russian Mir space station is disposed of, breaking up in the atmosphere before falling into the southern Pacific Ocean near Fiji.

Q5260602.name: Depayin massacre
Q5260602.blurb: Depayin massacre: At least 70 people associated with the National League for Democracy are killed by government-sponsored mob in Burma. Aung San Suu Kyi flees the scene, but is arrested soon afterwards.

Q5260701.name: deportation of Armenian intellectuals on 24 April 1915
Q5260701.blurb: The arrest of 250 Armenian intellectuals and community leaders in Istanbul marks the beginning of the Armenian genocide.

Q5265992.name: 1943 Detroit race riot
Q5265992.blurb: The Detroit race riot breaks out and continues for three more days.

Q5272242.name: Dibbles Bridge coach crash
Q5272242.blurb: Dibbles Bridge coach crash near Grassington, in North Yorkshire, England, kills 33, the highest ever death toll in a road accident in the United Kingdom.

Q5282772.name: Dissident Irish Republican campaign
Q5282772.blurb: Dissident Irish republican campaign: Two off-duty British Army soldiers were shot dead by Real IRA paramilitaries outside Massereene Barracks in Antrim, Northern Ireland.

Q5284398.name: Divinity School Address
Q5284398.blurb: Ralph Waldo Emerson delivers the Divinity School Address at Harvard Divinity School, discounting Biblical miracles and declaring Jesus a great man, but not God. The Protestant community reacts with outrage.

Q5286741.name: Dobrinja mortar attack
Q5286741.blurb: Dobrinja mortar attack: Thirteen are killed and 133 wounded when Serb mortar shells are fired at a soccer game in Dobrinja, west of Sarajevo.

Q5288383.name: 1957 Cebu Douglas C-47 crash
Q5288383.blurb: A plane crash in Cebu, Philippines kills Philippine President Ramon Magsaysay and 24 others.

Q5288914.name: Dole Air Race
Q5288914.blurb: The Dole Air Race begins from Oakland, California, to Honolulu, Hawaii, during which six out of the eight participating planes crash or disappear.

Q5290887.name: Dominicana DC-9 air disaster
Q5290887.blurb: Dominicana de Aviación Flight 603 crashes into the Caribbean Sea after takeoff from Las Américas International Airport, killing 102, including members of the Puerto Rico women's national volleyball team and lightweight boxer Carlos Cruz.

Q5299185.name: Dos Palmas kidnappings
Q5299185.blurb: Twenty tourists were kidnapped by Abu Sayyaf militants in Palawan, Philippines, triggering a hostage crisis that lasted for more than a year.

Q5299875.name: Double Seven Day scuffle
Q5299875.blurb: The secret police of Ngô Đình Nhu, brother and chief political adviser of South Vietnamese president Ngô Đình Diệm, attacked a group of American journalists who were covering a protest during the Buddhist crisis.

Q5299899.name: Double Tenth Incident
Q5299899.blurb: World War II: The Kempeitai, the military police arm of the Imperial Japanese Army, arrested and tortured fifty-seven civilians and civilian internees on suspicion of their involvement in a raid on Singapore Harbour.

Q5299900.name: Double Tenth Agreement
Q5299900.blurb: The Double Tenth Agreement is signed by the Communist Party and the Kuomintang about the future of China.

Q5301756.name: Douglas MacArthur's escape from the Philippines
Q5301756.blurb: World War II: After being forced to flee the Philippines for Australia, US Army general Douglas MacArthur announced: "I came through and I shall return."

Q5304755.name: Draft-card burning
Q5304755.blurb: Vietnam War protests: At an anti-war rally in New York City, David J. Miller burned his draft card (example pictured), the first such act to result in arrest under a new amendment to the Selective Service Act.

Q5307342.name: Drexel Mission Fight
Q5307342.blurb: Following the Wounded Knee Massacre, the United States Army and Lakota warriors face off in the Drexel Mission Fight.

Q5308485.name: Droppin Well bombing
Q5308485.blurb: The Troubles: The Irish National Liberation Army bombs a pub frequented by British soldiers in Ballykelly, Northern Ireland, killing  eleven soldiers and six civilians.

Q5316047.name: Dupont Plaza Hotel arson
Q5316047.blurb: Three disgruntled employees set fire to the Dupont Plaza Hotel in San Juan, Puerto Rico, killing more than 90 people and injuring 140 others, making it the second-deadliest hotel fire in American history.

Q5324434.name: ETA's 2006 ceasefire declaration
Q5324434.blurb: Basque nationalist group ETA detonated a van bomb at Madrid–Barajas Airport in Spain, ending a nine-month ceasefire.

Q5327275.name: Tsunami of 1343, Naples
Q5327275.blurb: A tsunami, caused by an earthquake in the Tyrrhenian Sea, devastates Naples and the Maritime Republic of Amalfi, among other places.

Q5328000.name: East Cape War
Q5328000.blurb: East Cape War: The Völkner Incident in New Zealand.

Q5329907.name: Easter Sunday Raid
Q5329907.blurb: World War II: The Imperial Japanese Navy launches a carrier-based air attack on Colombo, Ceylon during the Indian Ocean raid. Port and civilian facilities are damaged and the Royal Navy cruisers HMS Cornwall and HMS Dorsetshire are sunk southwest of the island.

Q5329956.name: Eastern Air Lines Flight 212
Q5329956.blurb: Eastern Air Lines Flight 212 crashes in Charlotte, North Carolina, killing 69 passengers and two crew.

Q5329960.name: Eastern Air Lines Flight 375
Q5329960.blurb: Eastern Airlines flight 375 crashes on takeoff from Boston's Logan International Airport, killing 62 people of the 72 aboard.

Q5329961.name: Eastern Air Lines Flight 512
Q5329961.blurb: Eastern Air Lines Flight 512 crashes at Idlewild Airport, killing 25 people.

Q5330553.name: Eastern University massacre
Q5330553.blurb: Sri Lankan Civil War: Sri Lankan Army soldiers slaughter 158 civilians.

Q5338335.name: Edirne Incident
Q5338335.blurb: A janissary revolt forces the deposition of Ottoman sultan Mustafa II.

Q5347927.name: Eggnog Riot
Q5347927.blurb: The Eggnog Riot at the United States Military Academy begins that night, wrapping up the following morning.

Q5348314.name: EgyptAir Flight 843
Q5348314.blurb: An EgyptAir Boeing 737-500 crashes on approach to Tunis–Carthage International Airport, killing 14 people.

Q5348315.name: EgyptAir Flight 864
Q5348315.blurb: EgyptAir Flight 864, a Boeing 707-366C, crashes on approach to Don Mueang International Airport, killing 71 people.

Q5353272.name: Elaine Race Riot
Q5353272.blurb: The Elaine massacre in Arkansas commences.

Q5368439.name: Ely and Littleport riots of 1816
Q5368439.blurb: A riot broke out in Littleport, England, over high unemployment and rising grain costs, spreading to Ely the next day before being quelled by troops.

Q5378356.name: English Reformation Parliament
Q5378356.blurb: Sir Francis Bigod began an armed rebellion against King Henry VIII and the English Parliament.

Q5381891.name: 2013 Luxor hot air balloon crash
Q5381891.blurb: A hot air balloon crashed near Luxor, Egypt, killing 19 people in the deadliest ballooning disaster in history.

Q5384006.name: Epsom Riot
Q5384006.blurb: Hundreds of Canadian soldiers rioted in Epsom, England,  leading to the death of a British police officer.

Q5385763.name: Erfurt massacre
Q5385763.blurb: Erfurt massacre: Outbreak of an antisemitic pogrom in Erfurt, Germany, during which between 100 and up to 3000 Jews were killed by Christians after being accused of causing the Black Death.

Q5390656.name: First Battle of the Stronghold
Q5390656.blurb: A group of Modoc warriors defeats the United States Army in the First Battle of the Stronghold, part of the Modoc War.

Q5392943.name: Montenotte Campaign
