Q5392943.blurb: War of the First Coalition: In the climax of the Montenotte Campaign, Napoleon Bonaparte decisively defeats the army of Piedmont at the Battle of Mondovi, leading to Piedmont's surrender a week later and decisively turning the Italian campaign in France's favor.

Q5395044.name: great Oulu fire of 1882
Q5395044.blurb: The great fire destroys a large part of Oulu's city center in Oulu Province, Finland.

Q5396089.name: Ervadi fire incident
Q5396089.blurb: Erwadi fire incident: Twenty-eight mentally ill persons tied to a chain are burnt to death at a faith based institution at Erwadi, Tamil Nadu.

Q5401553.name: Estonian European Union membership referendum, 2003
Q5401553.blurb: In a referendum, Estonia approves joining the European Union.

Q5406414.name: Frog Lake Massacre
Q5406414.blurb: Canadian Cree warriors attack the village of Frog Lake, killing nine.

Q5410510.name: United Airlines Flight 615
Q5410510.blurb: United Air Lines Flight 615 crashes near Decoto, California, killing 50 people.

Q5419908.name: Executive Order 9981
aliases: Executive Order 9981 dated July 26, 1948 in which President Harry S. Truman bans the segregation of the Armed Forces. (NAID 300009)
Q5419908.blurb: U.S. president Harry S. Truman signs Executive Order 9981, desegregating the military of the United States.

Q5421754.name: Expulsion of Montoneros from Plaza de Mayo
Q5421754.blurb: Argentine president Juan Perón expelled Montoneros from a demonstration in the Plaza de Mayo in Buenos Aires, forcing the group to become a clandestine organization.

Q5432157.name: Fall of Kabul
Q5432157.blurb: War in Afghanistan: Afghan Northern Alliance fighters take over the capital Kabul.

Q5432160.name: Fall of Kampala
Q5432160.blurb: Ugandan dictator Idi Amin is deposed.

Q5432163.name: fall of communism in Albania
Q5432163.blurb: Fall of communism in Albania: The Democratic Party of Albania wins a decisive majority in the parliamentary election.

Q5432166.name: Fall of Tripoli
Q5432166.blurb: Following weeks of bombardment, the city of Tripoli falls to the Mamluks under Qalawun. The Mamluks massacre all men they find and enslave the women and children.

Q5435902.name: Farmington Mine disaster
Q5435902.blurb: A total of 78 miners are killed in an explosion at the Consolidated Coal Company's No. 9 mine in Farmington, West Virginia in the Farmington Mine disaster.

Q5438057.name: Faucett Flight 251
Q5438057.blurb: Faucett Perú Flight 251 crashes in the Andes; all 123 passengers and crew are killed.

Q5439728.name: February 13, 1979 windstorm
Q5439728.blurb: An intense windstorm strikes western Washington and sinks a 0.5-mile (0.80 km) long section of the Hood Canal Bridge.

Q5439854.name: February 4, 1998 Afghanistan earthquake
Q5439854.blurb: The 5.9 Mw Afghanistan earthquake shakes the Takhar Province with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VII (Very strong). With 2,323 killed, and 818 injured, damage is considered extreme.

Q5439889.name: FedEx Express Flight 14
Q5439889.blurb: FedEx Express Flight 14 crashes at Newark International Airport, injuring five.

Q5440467.name: Federal Trade Commission Act
Q5440467.blurb: The United States Federal Trade Commission is established by the Federal Trade Commission Act.

Q5444368.name: April 1981 Fermanagh and South Tyrone by-election
aliases: Fermanagh and South Tyrone by-election, April 1981
Q5444368.blurb: Imprisoned IRA hunger striker Bobby Sands is elected to Westminster as the MP for Fermanagh and South Tyrone, Northern Ireland. He died twenty-six days later.

Q5447484.name: Fifth Battle of Ypres
Q5447484.blurb: World War I: The Fifth Battle of Ypres begins.

Q5447556.name: Fifth Test, 1948 Ashes series
Q5447556.blurb: Australia won the fifth Test of the 1948 Ashes series, becoming the first Test cricket team to go undefeated in England, earning them the nickname "The Invincibles".

Q5452172.name: Firozabad rail disaster
Q5452172.blurb: The Firozabad rail disaster kills 358 people in Firozabad, India.

Q5452504.name: First Battle of Cannanore
Q5452504.blurb: The First Battle of Cannanore commences, seeing the first use of the naval line of battle.[citation needed]

Q5452548.name: First Battle of Wissembourg
Q5452548.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: Austro-Prussian victory over Republican France at the First Battle of Wissembourg.

Q5452962.name: First English Civil War, 1646
Q5452962.blurb: First English Civil War: Charles I surrendered himself to Scottish Covenanter leader David Leslie near Newark, England.

Q5453494.name: 1st Parliament of Great Britain
aliases: first Parliament of the Kingdom of Great Britain
Q5453494.blurb: The First Parliament of the Kingdom of Great Britain convenes.

Q5453870.name: First Taranaki War
Q5453870.blurb: The First Taranaki War begins in Taranaki, New Zealand, a major phase of the New Zealand Wars.

Q5454079.name: First Whitlam Ministry
Q5454079.blurb: Gough Whitlam took office as the 21st Prime Minister of Australia and formed a duumvirate with his deputy Lance Barnard, ending 23 years of Liberal–Country Party government.

Q5454119.name: First and Second Battles of Wonju
Q5454119.blurb: Korean War: North Korean troops attacked United Nations forces in the first of two battles at Wonju.

Q5454126.name: first ascent of the Matterhorn
Q5454126.blurb: The first ascent of the Matterhorn is completed by Edward Whymper and his party, four of whom die on the descent.

Q5454145.name: First campaign in the Goguryeo–Tang War
Q5454145.blurb: Goguryeo–Tang War: Led by Emperor Taizong, the Tang army was forced to abandon a siege of Ansi Fortress.

Q5454155.name: First day on the Somme
Q5454155.blurb: World War I: First day on the Somme: On the first day of the Battle of the Somme 19,000 soldiers of the British Army are killed and 40,000 wounded.

Q5454184.name: first inauguration of George Washington
Q5454184.blurb: George Washington's reception at Trenton is hosted by the Ladies of Trenton as he journeys to New York City for his first inauguration.

Q5454185.name: first inauguration of Franklin D. Roosevelt
Q5454185.blurb: Franklin D. Roosevelt is inaugurated as the 32nd President of the United States.

Q5454196.name: first inauguration of Lyndon B. Johnson
Q5454196.blurb: U.S. President John F. Kennedy is assassinated and Texas Governor John Connally is seriously wounded by Lee Harvey Oswald, who also kills Dallas Police officer J. D. Tippit after fleeing the scene. Vice President Lyndon B. Johnson is sworn in as the 36th President of the United States afterwards.

Q5454202.name: first indoor ice hockey game
Q5454202.blurb: The first indoor game of ice hockey was played at the Victoria Skating Rink in Montreal by James Creighton and students of McGill University.

Q5457361.name: Flanders Campaign
Q5457361.blurb: Flanders Campaign of the French Revolution, Battle of Neerwinden.

Q5459626.name: Flint–Worcester tornado outbreak sequence
Q5459626.blurb: The Flint–Worcester tornado outbreak sequence kills 94 people in Massachusetts.

Q5461720.name: 2000 United States presidential election recount in Florida
Q5461720.blurb: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled in Bush v. Gore that the recount of ballots cast in Florida for the presidential election be stopped, effectively making George W. Bush (pictured) the winner.

Q5463542.name: Flying Tiger Line Flight 282
Q5463542.blurb: Flying Tiger Line Flight 282 crashes after takeoff from San Francisco International Airport, killing three.

Q5463543.name: Flying Tiger Line Flight 66
Q5463543.blurb: Flying Tiger Line Flight 066 crashes into a hill near Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Malaysia, killing four.

Q5463546.name: Flying Tiger Line Flight 739
Q5463546.blurb: Flying Tiger Line Flight 739 disappears in the western Pacific Ocean with all 107 aboard missing and presumed dead.

Q5468024.name: Gerald Ford assassination attempt in Sacramento
Q5468024.blurb: Sacramento, California: Lynette Fromme attempts to assassinate U.S. President Gerald Ford.

Q5470224.name: Formosa Air Battle
Q5470224.blurb: A  four-day air battle over Taiwan ended with a decisive American victory, destroying hundreds of Japanese aircraft and military facilities.

Q5475172.name: Four Four Bravo
Q5475172.blurb: Thirteen Sri Lanka Army soldiers are killed after a deadly ambush by the militant Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam.

Q5476175.name: Fourth Test, 1948 Ashes series
aliases: Fourth Test of the Ashes series
Q5476175.blurb: Australia  set a world record for the highest successful run-chase in Test cricket history during the Fourth Test of the Ashes series against England.

Q5484440.name: Tierra del Fuego gold rush
Q5484440.blurb: The French steamship Arctique ran aground on the northern coast of Cape Virgenes in Argentina; gold was discovered during the rescue effort, triggering the Tierra del Fuego gold rush.

Q5493470.name: Lapua Cartridge Factory Explosion
Q5493470.blurb: Forty workers die in the Lapua Cartridge Factory explosion, the deadliest industrial accident in modern Finnish history.

Q5494346.name: Freckleton Air Disaster
Q5494346.blurb: Freckleton air disaster: A United States Army Air Forces B-24 Liberator bomber crashes into a school in Freckleton, England, killing 61 people.

Q5502260.name: French invasion of the Isle of Wight
Q5502260.blurb: The first landing of French troops on the coast of the Isle of Wight during the French invasion of the Isle of Wight.

Q5511513.name: Fédon's rebellion
Q5511513.blurb: The Fédon Rebellion breaks out in Grenada, the rebels seizing Grenville and later Gouyave.

Q5514367.name: GP Express Flight 861
Q5514367.blurb: GP Express Airlines Flight 861 crashes on approach to Anniston Regional Airport in Anniston, Alabama, killing three.

Q5517354.name: Gaisal train disaster
Q5517354.blurb: The Gaisal train disaster claims 285 lives in Assam, India.

Q5517740.name: Gal Oya riots
Q5517740.blurb: Start of Gal Oya riots, the first reported ethnic riots that target minority Sri Lankan Tamils in the Eastern Province. The total number of deaths is reportedly 150.

Q5518110.name: Galaxy Airlines Flight 203
Q5518110.blurb: Galaxy Airlines Flight 203 crashes near Reno–Tahoe International Airport in Reno, Nevada, killing 70 people.

Q5524465.name: Garuda Indonesia Flight 035
Q5524465.blurb: Garuda Indonesia Flight 032 crashes at Medan Airport, killing 23.

Q5532041.name: General Motors Chapter 11 reorganization
Q5532041.blurb: General Motors files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy. It is the fourth largest United States bankruptcy in history.

Q5532992.name: Geneva Conference
Q5532992.blurb: The Geneva Conference on the Arab–Israeli conflict opens.

Q5551458.name: German referendum, 1933
Q5551458.blurb: Nazi Germany uses a referendum to ratify its withdrawal from the League of Nations.

Q5557072.name: Ghost Dance War
Q5557072.blurb: Sioux Wars: The United States Army killed 250 to 300 Lakota men, women and children at the Wounded Knee Massacre, beginning the Ghost Dance War.

Q5558879.name: Gibbet Rath massacre
Q5558879.blurb: United Irishmen Rebellion: Between 300 and 500 United Irishmen are executed as rebels by the British Army in County Kildare, Ireland.

Q5567521.name: Gleision Colliery mining accident
Q5567521.blurb: Four miners are killed in the Gleision Colliery mining accident in the Swansea Valley, Wales.

Q5572919.name: Warrenpoint ambush
Q5572919.blurb: The Troubles: Eighteen British soldiers are killed at the Warrenpoint ambush by the Provisional Irish Republican Army near Warrenpoint, Northern Ireland, in the deadliest attack on British forces during Operation Banner. An IRA bomb also kills British royal family member Lord Mountbatten and three others on his boat at Mullaghmore, Republic of Ireland.

Q5575873.name: Maletinazo
Q5575873.blurb: An airport police officer discovered a suitcase containing approximately US$800,000 as it passed through security at Jorge Newbery Airfield in Buenos Aires, sparking an international scandal involving Venezuela and Argentina.

Q5579337.name: Golden Dragon massacre
Q5579337.blurb: The Golden Dragon massacre takes place in San Francisco.

Q5587844.name: Gothenburg discothèque fire
Q5587844.blurb: The Gothenburg discothèque fire in Sweden kills 63 and injures over 200.

Q5592478.name: Graffito of Esmet-Akhom
Q5592478.blurb: The Graffito of Esmet-Akhom, the latest known inscription in Egyptian hieroglyphs, is written.

Q5598537.name: Grdelica train bombing
Q5598537.blurb: During the NATO bombing of Yugoslavia, an American McDonnell Douglas F-15E Strike Eagle shoots a passenger train, killing between 20 and 60 people.

Q5598659.name: Great Appalachian Storm of November 1950
Q5598659.blurb: The "Great Appalachian Storm", a large extratropical cyclone, struck the east coast of the United States before moving northeast.

Q5598782.name: Great Blue Norther of November 11, 1911
Q5598782.blurb: Many cities in the Midwestern United States break their record highs and lows on the same day as a strong cold front rolls through.

Q5598969.name: Great Coastal Gale of 2007
Q5598969.blurb: Winter storms cause the Chehalis River to flood many cities in Lewis County, Washington, and close a 32-kilometre (20 mi) portion of Interstate 5 for several days. At least eight deaths and billions of dollars in damages are blamed on the floods.

Q5599044.name: Great Dayton Flood
Q5599044.blurb: More than 360 were killed and 20,000 homes were destroyed in the Great Dayton Flood in Dayton, Ohio, U.S.

Q5599111.name: Great Ejection
Q5599111.blurb: The 1662 Book of Common Prayer is legally enforced as the liturgy of the Church of England, precipitating the Great Ejection of Dissenter ministers from their benefices.

Q5599179.name: Great Fire of 1901
Q5599179.blurb: The Great Fire of 1901 begins in Jacksonville, Florida.

Q5599180.name: Great Fire of 1892
Q5599180.blurb: St. John's, Newfoundland is devastated in the Great Fire of 1892.

Q5599181.name: Great Fire of 1910
Q5599181.blurb: Extreme fire weather in the Inland Northwest of the United States causes many small wildfires to coalesce into the Great Fire of 1910, burning approximately 3 million acres (12,000 km2) and killing 87 people.

Q5599244.name: Great German Pilgrimage of 1064–1065
Q5599244.blurb: The Great German Pilgrimage is attacked on Good Friday by Beduin bandits, suffering heavy losses.

Q5599260.name: Great Gold Robbery
Q5599260.blurb: Thieves stole 224 pounds (102 kg) of gold from a train travelling from London to Folkestone, England.

Q5599308.name: Great Heck rail crash
Q5599308.blurb: A high-speed train crash occurred near Selby in North Yorkshire, England, killing 10 and injuring 82.

Q5599610.name: Great Natchez Tornado
Q5599610.blurb: The Great Natchez Tornado strikes Natchez, Mississippi killing 317 people. It is the second deadliest tornado in United States history.

Q5599747.name: Great Phenol Plot
Q5599747.blurb: A story in New York World newspaper reveals that the Imperial German government had purchased excess phenol from Thomas Edison that could be used to make explosives for the war effort and diverted it to Bayer for aspirin production.

Q5599829.name: Great Railroad Strike of 1922
Q5599829.blurb: The Great Railroad Strike of 1922 begins in the United States.

Q5599833.name: Great Railroad Strike of 1877
Q5599833.blurb: After rioting by Baltimore and Ohio Railroad workers and the deaths of nine rail workers at the hands of the Maryland militia, workers in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, stage a sympathy strike that is met with an assault by the state militia.

Q5599946.name: Great Seattle Fire
Q5599946.blurb: The Great Seattle Fire destroys all of downtown Seattle.

Q5600047.name: Great Storm of 1975
Q5600047.blurb: The Great Storm spawned the first of 45 tornadoes over a three-day period in the Southeastern United States.

Q5600061.name: Great Swamp Fight
Q5600061.blurb: The Great Swamp Fight, a pivotal battle in King Philip's War, gives the English settlers a bitterly won victory.

Q5600356.name: Great fire of Newcastle and Gateshead
Q5600356.blurb: In England the Great fire of Newcastle and Gateshead leads to 53 deaths and hundreds injured.

Q5601730.name: Greek-Serbian Alliance of 1913
Q5601730.blurb: The Greek–Serbian Treaty of Alliance is signed, paving the way for the Second Balkan War.

Q5601760.name: Greek Constitution of 1822
Q5601760.blurb: The Greek Constitution of 1822 is adopted by the First National Assembly at Epidaurus.

Q5601763.name: Greek Constitution of 1844
Q5601763.blurb: King Otto of Greece is forced to grant a constitution following an uprising in Athens.

Q5602050.name: Greek republic referendum, 1973
Q5602050.blurb: Greeks vote to abolish the monarchy, beginning the first period of the Metapolitefsi.

Q5602054.name: Greek republic referendum, 1974
Q5602054.blurb: A plebiscite results in the abolition of monarchy in Greece.

Q5603101.name: Green Ramp disaster
Q5603101.blurb: A United States Air Force (USAF) F-16 aircraft collides with a USAF C-130 at Pope Air Force Base and then crashes, killing 24 United States Army soldiers on the ground alongside destroying a Starlifter by accident. This later became known as the Green Ramp disaster.

Q5604092.name: Greenham Common Women's Peace Camp
Q5604092.blurb: The first women arrive at what becomes Greenham Common Women's Peace Camp in the UK.

Q5604469.name: Greensboro sit-ins
Q5604469.blurb: Four black students stage the first of the Greensboro sit-ins at a lunch counter in Greensboro, North Carolina.

Q5607565.name: Gresford disaster
Q5607565.blurb: The Gresford disaster in Wales kills 266 miners and rescuers.

Q5611952.name: Grue Church fire
Q5611952.blurb: At least 113 people die in the Grue Church fire, the biggest fire disaster in Norway's history.

Q5613191.name: Guadalajara train disaster
Q5613191.blurb: Over 600 people are killed in Guadalajara, Mexico, when a train plunges off the tracks into a deep canyon.

Q5613440.name: Guam Organic Act of 1950
Q5613440.blurb: Guam is organized as an unincorporated territory of the United States as the President Harry S. Truman signs the Guam Organic Act.

Q5614269.name: Guatemaljose Revolution
Q5614269.blurb: Guatemalan Revolution: The Guatemalan Congress passed Decree 900, redistributing unused land greater than 224 acres (0.91 km2) in area to local peasants.

Q5614677.name: Gudovac massacre
Q5614677.blurb: The Ustaše massacre nearly 200 Serbs in the village of Gudovac, the first massacre of their genocidal campaign against Serbs of the Independent State of Croatia.

Q5617260.name: Gulbarg Society massacre
Q5617260.blurb: During the religious violence in Gujarat, 97 people are killed in the Naroda Patiya massacre and 69 in the Gulbarg Society massacre.

Q5617496.name: Gulf Hotel fire
Q5617496.blurb: A fire at the Gulf Hotel in Houston kills 55 people.

Q5638475.name: Haft-e Tir bombing
Q5638475.blurb: A powerful bomb explodes in Tehran, killing 73 officials of the Islamic Republican Party.

Q5642243.name: Halifax Riot
Q5642243.blurb: The Halifax riot starts when thousands of civilians and servicemen rampage through Halifax, Nova Scotia.

Q5644307.name: Hamburg Massacre
Q5644307.blurb: The Hamburg massacre prior to the 1876 United States presidential election results in the deaths of six African-Americans of the Republican Party, along with one white assailant.

Q5645476.name: Hamlet chicken processing plant fire
Q5645476.blurb: A fire killed 25 people locked inside a burning chicken processing plant in Hamlet, North Carolina, U.S.

Q5647565.name: Hands Across America
Q5647565.blurb: The Hands Across America event takes place.

Q5655243.name: Hard Hat Riot
Q5655243.blurb: Construction workers attacked students and others who were protesting the Vietnam War in New York City.

Q5656105.name: Spantax Flight 275
Q5656105.blurb: Spantax Flight 275 crashes during takeoff from Tenerife North–Ciudad de La Laguna Airport, killing all 155 people on board.

Q5665286.name: Harrisburg Seven
Q5665286.blurb: The Harrisburg Seven: Rev. Philip Berrigan and five other activists are indicted on charges of conspiring to kidnap Henry Kissinger and of plotting to blow up the heating tunnels of federal buildings in Washington, D.C.

Q5674582.name: Hartford circus fire
Q5674582.blurb: The Hartford circus fire, one of America's worst fire disasters, kills approximately 168 people and injures over 700 in Hartford, Connecticut.

Q5674884.name: Hartley Colliery Disaster
Q5674884.blurb: Hartley Colliery disaster: Two hundred and four men and boys killed in a mining disaster, prompting a change in UK law which henceforth required all collieries to have at least two independent means of escape.

Q5676669.name: Harvard–Yale Regatta
Q5676669.blurb: Harvard University wins the first Boat Race between Yale University and Harvard. The race is also known as the first ever American intercollegiate athletic event.

Q5676938.name: Harvey's Resort Hotel bombing
Q5676938.blurb: After John Birges plants a bomb at Harvey's Resort Hotel in Stateline, Nevada, in the United States, the FBI inadvertently detonates the bomb during its disarming.

Q5684126.name: Havørn Accident
Q5684126.blurb: A Junkers Ju 52 aircraft of Norwegian Air Lines crashed into a mountainside near Hyllestad, Norway, killing all seven people on board.

Q5684258.name: Hawaii Clipper
Q5684258.blurb: Hawaii Clipper disappears between Guam and Manila as the first loss of an airliner in trans-Pacific China Clipper service.

Q5695892.name: Hebrew University bombing
Q5695892.blurb: Hamas attackers detonated a bomb at the Mount Scopus campus of the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, killing nine students and injuring about 100 more.

Q5698794.name: Heidi
Q5698794.blurb: Viewers of the Raiders–Jets football game in the eastern United States are denied the opportunity to watch its exciting finish when NBC broadcasts Heidi instead, prompting changes to sports broadcasting in the U.S.

Q5708037.name: Siege of Jaén
Q5708037.blurb: The Siege of Jaén begins, in the context of the Spanish Reconquista.

Q5710620.name: attempted assassination of Augusto Pinochet
Q5710620.blurb: Chilean dictator Augusto Pinochet survives an assassination attempt by the FPMR; five of Pinochet's bodyguards are killed.

Q5722426.name: Battle of Eisenach
Q5722426.blurb: Battle of Eisenach: An invading Hungarian force defeats an East Frankish army under Duke Burchard of Thuringia.

Q5722659.name: Battle of Los Alporchones
Q5722659.blurb: Reconquista: Combined Castilian and Murcian forces defeated the Emirate of Granada at the Battle of Los Alporchones around the city of Lorca.

Q5722787.name: Battle of Peralonso
Q5722787.blurb: Thousand Days' War: Columbian Liberal rebels repelled a Conservative government attack at the Battle of Peralonso.

Q5723017.name: Battle of Tampico
Q5723017.blurb: An expedition led by Isidro Barradas at Tampico, sent by the Spanish crown to retake Mexico, surrenders at the Battle of Tampico, marking the effective end of Spain's resistance to Mexico's campaign for independence.

Q5725356.name: 1997 Bojnurd earthquake
Q5725356.blurb: The Bojnurd earthquake measuring Mw 6.5 strikes Iran. With a Mercalli intensity of VIII, it kills at least 88 and damages 173 villages.

Q5731032.name: Wedding of Alfonso XII and Victoria Eugenie of Battenburg
Q5731032.blurb: The attempted regicide of Spanish King Alfonso XIII and Queen Victoria Eugenie on their wedding day instead kills 24.

Q5758838.name: Vega de Tera disaster
Q5758838.blurb: The Vega de Tera dam fails, triggering a disastrous flood that nearly destroys the town of Ribadelago and kills 144 residents.

Q5759146.name: 1993 Highland Towers collapse
Q5759146.blurb: A block of the Highland Towers condominium complex collapses following a landslide caused by heavy rain and water flowing from a construction site at Ampang district in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. 48 of its residents die, including one who died in hospital after being rescued alive, leaving only two survivors.

Q5765923.name: Hindawi affair
Q5765923.blurb: Nezar Hindawi is sentenced to 45 years in prison, the longest sentence handed down by a British court, for the attempted bombing of an El Al flight at Heathrow Airport.

Q5775114.name: history of Australia (1788–1850)
Q5775114.blurb: The third and main part of First Fleet arrives at Botany Bay, beginning the British colonization of Australia. Arthur Phillip decides that Port Jackson is a more suitable location for a colony.

Q5782939.name: Mexico–Guatemala conflict
Q5782939.blurb: The Guatemalan Air Force sinks several Mexican fishing boats alleged to have breached maritime borders, killing three and sparking international tension.

Q5783195.name: Bala Hissar uprising
Q5783195.blurb: In Afghanistan, Maoists undertake the Bala Hissar uprising against the Leninist government.

Q5793320.name: Fourth voyage of Christopher Columbus
Q5793320.blurb: Christopher Columbus sets off from Cádiz for his fourth voyage.

Q5803619.name: 1996 shootdown of Brothers to the Rescue aircraft
Q5803619.blurb: Two civilian airplanes operated by the Miami-based group Brothers to the Rescue are shot down in international waters by the Cuban Air Force.

Q5838804.name: Ayotzinapa Rural Teachers’ College
aliases: Raúl Isidro Burgos Rural Teachers’ College
Q5838804.blurb: Forty-three students of the Ayotzinapa Rural Teachers' College in Iguala, Mexico, were kidnapped and probably later killed.

Q5853295.name: Almagro's expedition to Chile
Q5853295.blurb: Diego de Almagro leaves the recently conquered Inca capital of Cuzco to lead an expedition to Chile.

Q5858325.name: Colombian peace process
Q5858325.blurb: The government of Colombia and the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia–People's Army sign a revised peace deal, bringing an end to the country's more than 50-year-long civil war.

Q5869184.name: Brooklyn Dodgers
Q5869184.blurb: Jackie Robinson debuts for the Brooklyn Dodgers, breaking baseball's color line.

Q5873956.name: Ho Chi Minh City ITC fire
Q5873956.blurb: A fire destroys a luxurious department store in Ho Chi Minh City, where 1,500 people are shopping. More than 60 people die and over 100 are unaccounted for in the deadliest peacetime disaster in Vietnam.

Q5882598.name: Hollywood Black Friday
Q5882598.blurb: A six-month strike by Hollywood set decorators turns into a bloody riot at the gates of the Warner Brothers studio.

Q5883952.name: Holocaust of Kedros
Q5883952.blurb: World War II: Holocaust of Kedros in Crete by German forces.

Q5883955.name: Holocaust of Viannos
Q5883955.blurb: World War II: The Wehrmacht starts a three-day retaliatory operation targeting several Greek villages in the region of Viannos, whose death toll would eventually exceed 500 persons.

Q5887012.name: Evander Holyfield vs. Mike Tyson II
Q5887012.blurb: Holyfield–Tyson II: Mike Tyson is disqualified in the third round for biting a piece off Evander Holyfield's ear.

Q5891687.name: Homosexual Law Reform Act 1986
Q5891687.blurb: The New Zealand Parliament passes the Homosexual Law Reform Act legalising homosexuality in New Zealand.

Q5892720.name: 1902 Turkestan earthquake
Q5892720.blurb: At least 6,000 people are killed by the magnitude 7.7 Kashgar earthquake in the Tien Shan mountains.

Q5892959.name: Honduran fourth ballot box referendum
Q5892959.blurb: Honduran president Manuel Zelaya is ousted by a local military coup following a failed request to hold a referendum to rewrite the Honduran Constitution. This was the start of the 2009 Honduran constitutional crisis.

Q5894966.name: 1920 Xalapa earthquake
Q5894966.blurb: Over 640 are killed after a magnitude 6.4 earthquake strikes the Mexican states Puebla and Veracruz.

Q5904113.name: 1922 Guayaquil general strike
Q5904113.blurb: At least 300 are massacred during a general strike in Guayaquil, Ecuador.

Q5912856.name: Hough Riots
Q5912856.blurb: A racially charged incident in a bar sparks the six-day Hough riots in Cleveland, Ohio; 1,700 Ohio National Guard troops intervene to restore order.

Q5914903.name: Quito Ultratumba nightclub fire
Q5914903.blurb: The Quito Ultratumba nightclub fire in Quito, Ecuador, kills 19 people and injures at least 24 more.

Q5919478.name: Invasion of the Waikato
Q5919478.blurb: The New Zealand Wars resumed as British forces led by General Duncan Cameron began the invasion of the Waikato.

Q5919490.name: Third Spanish Armada
Q5919490.blurb: King Philip II of Spain sends his third and final armada against England, but it ends in failure due to storms. The remaining ships are captured or sunk by the English.

Q5925721.name: Savoyard crusade
Q5925721.blurb: The Byzantine Empire retakes Gallipoli with the help of the Savoyard Crusade.

Q5926471.name: 1959 Coatzacoalcos earthquake
Q5926471.blurb: The Coatzacoalcos earthquake struck near the Mexican state of Veracruz, killing 25 people.

Q5930951.name: 1954 Chlef earthquake
Q5930951.blurb: The 6.7 Mw Chlef earthquake shakes northern Algeria with a maximum Mercalli intensity of XI (Extreme). At least 1,243 people were killed and 5,000 were injured.

Q5931401.name: 1965 La Ligua earthquake
Q5931401.blurb: An Mw 7.4 earthquake in Chile sets off a series of tailings dam failures, burying the town of El Cobre and killing at least 500 people.

Q5933013.name: 1956 Amorgos earthquake
Q5933013.blurb: The 7.7 Mw Amorgos earthquake shakes the Cyclades island group in the Aegean Sea with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent). The shaking and the destructive tsunami that followed left fifty-three people dead. A damaging M7.2 aftershock occurred minutes after the mainshock.

Q5933282.name: 1981 Iranian Air Force C-130 crash
Q5933282.blurb: An Iranian Air Force Lockheed C-130 Hercules military transport aircraft crashes into a firing range near Kahrizak, Iran, killing 80 people.

Q5933331.name: Hughes Airwest Flight 706
Q5933331.blurb: Hughes Airwest Flight 706 collides with a McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom II of the United States Marine Corps over the San Gabriel Mountains, killing 50.

Q5933851.name: Staten Island Peace Conference
Q5933851.blurb: British–American peace conference on Staten Island fails to stop nascent American Revolutionary War.

Q5933860.name: Abbasid Revolution
Q5933860.blurb: Abbasid Revolution: The Hashimi rebels under Abu Muslim Khorasani take Merv, capital of the Umayyad province Khorasan, marking the consolidation of the Abbasid revolt.

Q5936879.name: 1981 Iranian Prime Minister's office bombing
Q5936879.blurb: Iranian president Mohammad-Ali Rajai and prime minister Mohammad-Javad Bahonar were assassinated in a bombing committed by the People's Mojahedin Organization of Iran.

Q5941438.name: Iraqi invasion of Iran
Q5941438.blurb: Iraq invades Iran, sparking the nearly eight year Iran–Iraq War.

Q5941752.name: 1999 Luzon earthquake
Q5941752.blurb: A magnitude 7.3 earthquake hits the Philippines's main island of Luzon, killing six people, injuring 40, and causing power outages that affected the capital Manila.

Q5941784.name: 1981 Gulf of Corinth earthquakes
Q5941784.blurb: The 6.7 Ms Gulf of Corinth earthquake affects Central Greece with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VIII (Severe). Twenty-two people are killed, 400 are injured, and damage totals $812 million.

Q5942412.name: 1979 Tumaco earthquake
Q5942412.blurb: The 8.2 Mw Tumaco earthquake shakes Colombia and Ecuador with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent), killing 300–600, and generating a large tsunami.

Q5942486.name: 1986 Kalamata earthquake
Q5942486.blurb: A magnitude 6.0 earthquake strikes Kalamata, Greece with a maximum Modified Mercalli intensity of X (Extreme), killing at least 20 and causing heavy damage in the city.

Q5942627.name: 1995 Aigio earthquake
Q5942627.blurb: Western Greece was struck by an earthquake registering 6.4–6.5 Mw that killed 26 people.

Q5943056.name: 1999 Ambrym earthquake
Q5943056.blurb: The 7.5 Mw Ambrym earthquake shakes Vanuatu and a destructive tsunami follows. Ten people were killed and forty were injured.

Q5943658.name: 1988 Lancang-Gengma earthquakes
Q5943658.blurb: Lancang–Gengma earthquakes: At least 730 are killed after two powerful earthquakes rock the China–Myanmar border in Yunnan Province.

Q5947277.name: Hurricane Carrie
Q5947277.blurb: Pamir, a four-masted barque, was shipwrecked and sank off the Azores during Hurricane Carrie.

Q5947514.name: Hurricane Esther
Q5947514.blurb: The United States National Hurricane Research Project drops eight cylinders of silver iodide into the eyewall of Hurricane Esther. Wind speed reduces by 10%, giving rise to Project Stormfury.

Q5951632.name: Huế chemical attacks
Q5951632.blurb: Soldiers of the South Vietnamese Army attack protesting Buddhists in Huế with liquid chemicals from tear-gas grenades, causing 67 people to be hospitalized for blistering of the skin and respiratory ailments.

Q5955315.name: International Women's Day in 1979 in Iran
aliases: International Women's Day Protests in Tehran, 1979
Q5955315.blurb: 1979 International Women's Day protests in Tehran: Protestor involvement peaks with 15,000 Iranian women and girls performing a three‐hour-long sit‐in at the Courthouse of Tehran.

Q5958275.name: Kashf-e hijab
Q5958275.blurb: Kashf-e hijab decree is made and immediately enforced by Reza Shah, Iran's head of state, banning the wearing of Islamic veils in public.

Q5960512.name: Coronation of Mohammad Reza Pahlavi
aliases: Coronation of Mohammad Reza Pahlavi and Farah Diba
Coronation of Mohammad Reza Pahlavi and Farah Pahlavi
Q5960512.blurb: Mohammad Reza Pahlavi crowns himself Emperor of Iran.

Q5962857.name: Siege of Inabayama Castle
Q5962857.blurb: The siege of Inabayama Castle, the final battle in Oda Nobunaga's campaign to conquer Mino Province, began; it culminated in a decisive victory for Nobunaga.

Q5967210.name: I've Been to the Mountaintop
Q5967210.blurb: Martin Luther King Jr. delivers his "I've Been to the Mountaintop" speech; he was assassinated the next day.

Q5967550.name: I-40 bridge disaster
Q5967550.blurb: The tugboat Robert Y. Love collides with a support pier of Interstate 40 on the Arkansas River near Webbers Falls, Oklahoma, resulting in 14 deaths and 11 others injured.

Q5973845.name: National Geographic
Q5973845.blurb: A picture showing the bare breasts of a woman appears in National Geographic magazine for the first time.

Q5976484.name: Limazo
Q5976484.blurb: Riots break out in Lima, Peru after the police forces go on strike the day before. The uprising (locally known as the Limazo) is bloodily suppressed by the military dictatorship.

Q5985739.name: Icelandic Airlines Flight 001
Q5985739.blurb: A chartered Douglas DC-8 crashes near Colombo, Sri Lanka, killing 183.

Q5991464.name: Igandu train disaster
Q5991464.blurb: The Igandu train disaster in Tanzania kills 281, the worst train accident in African history.

Q6003043.name: Imam Ali Mosque bombing
Q6003043.blurb: Sayed Ayatollah Mohammed Baqir al-Hakim, the Shia Muslim leader in Iraq, is assassinated in a terrorist bombing, along with nearly 100 worshippers as they leave a mosque in Najaf.

Q6004996.name: Immigration Act of 1917
Q6004996.blurb: The Congress of the United States passes the Immigration Act of 1917 over President Woodrow Wilson's veto.

Q6013761.name: inauguration of John Adams
Q6013761.blurb: John Adams is inaugurated as the 2nd President of the United States of America, becoming the first President to begin his presidency on March 4.

Q6013811.name: inauguration of Zachary Taylor
Q6013811.blurb: Zachary Taylor, 12th President of the United States of America and Millard Fillmore, 12th Vice President, did not take their respective oaths of office (they did so the following day), leading to the erroneous theory that outgoing President pro tempore of the United States Senate David Rice Atchison had assumed the role of acting president for one day.

Q6019798.name: Indian Airlines Flight 440
Q6019798.blurb: Indian Airlines Flight 440 crashes near Palam Airport in Delhi, killing 48.

Q6019803.name: Indian Airlines Flight 257
Q6019803.blurb: Indian Airlines Flight 257, a Boeing 737-200, crashes during approach to Imphal Airport, killing all 69 people on board.

Q6019809.name: Indian Airlines Flight 605
Q6019809.blurb: Ninety-two people are killed when Indian Airlines Flight 605 crashes in Bangalore, India.

Q6021584.name: Indian Slavery Act, 1843
Q6021584.blurb: Slavery is abolished in the British Empire as the Slavery Abolition Act 1833 comes into force, although it remains legal in the possessions of the East India Company until the passage of the Indian Slavery Act, 1843.

Q6022577.name: Indian intervention in the Sri Lankan civil war
Q6022577.blurb: Indian intervention in the Sri Lankan Civil War ends with the last ship of Indian Peace Keeping Force leaving Sri Lanka.

Q6023927.name: Indianapolis Streetcar Strike of 1913
Q6023927.blurb: The Indianapolis Streetcar Strike and subsequent riot begins.

Q6026252.name: 1955 Indonesian legislative election
Q6026252.blurb: The first Indonesian legislative election resulted in an unexpectedly poor result for the Masyumi Party of incumbent prime minister Burhanuddin Harahap (pictured).

Q6028822.name: Infamy Speech
aliases: a date which will live in infamy
Q6028822.blurb: World War II: U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt declares December 7 to be "a date which will live in infamy", after which the U.S. declares war on Japan.

Q6045658.name: Interception of the Rex
Q6045658.blurb: During an exercise to demonstrate air power, United States Army Air Corps bomber aircraft intercepted the Italian ocean liner SS Rex (pictured) 620 nautical miles (1,100 km) off the US Atlantic coast.

Q6051642.name: 1766 Istanbul earthquake
Q6051642.blurb: A large earthquake causes heavy damage and loss of life in Istanbul and the Marmara region.

Q6055316.name: international yard and pound agreement
Q6055316.blurb: Specific values for the international yard, avoirdupois pound and derived units (e.g. inch, mile and ounce) are adopted after agreement between the US, the United Kingdom and other Commonwealth countries.

Q6059644.name: Invasion of Gozo
Q6059644.blurb: The Knights Hospitaller surrendered the Castello of Gozo to the Ottoman Empire following a brief siege, leading to the mass enslavement and dispersal of the Gozitan population.

Q6059673.name: Invasion of Jamaica
Q6059673.blurb: The Invasion of Jamaica begins during the Anglo-Spanish War.

Q6059706.name: Invasion of Trinidad
Q6059706.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: Sir Ralph Abercromby and a fleet of 18 British warships invade Trinidad.

Q6061810.name: Parliament of Negrete
Q6061810.blurb: Parliament of Negrete between Mapuche and Spanish authorities in Chile brings an end to the Mapuche uprising of 1723–26.

Q6066728.name: Iran Aseman Airlines Flight 746
Q6066728.blurb: Iran Aseman Airlines Flight 746 crashes near Natanz, Iran, killing all 66 people on board.

Q6067801.name: Anbar campaign (2003–2011)
aliases: Al Anbar Governorate in the Iraq War
Q6067801.blurb: Iraq War in Anbar Province: In Fallujah, Iraq, four American private military contractors working for Blackwater USA, are killed after being ambushed.

Q6067958.name: Iraqi Airways Flight 163
Q6067958.blurb: Iraqi Airways Flight 163, a Boeing 737-270C, is hijacked and crashes in Arar, Saudi Arabia, killing 63 people.

Q6087321.name: 43rd government of Turkey
Q6087321.blurb: The 43rd government of Turkey is overthrown in a coup d'état led by General Kenan Evren.

Q6093105.name: Italian campaign of 1524–1525
Q6093105.blurb: French troops lay siege to Pavia.

Q6102087.name: Great Offensive
Q6102087.blurb: Greco-Turkish War (1919–22): Turkish army launched what has come to be known to the Turks as the Great Offensive (Büyük Taarruz). The major Greek defense positions were overrun.

Q6102465.name: Mapuche uprising of 1723
Q6102465.blurb: Parliament of Negrete between Mapuche and Spanish authorities in Chile brings an end to the Mapuche uprising of 1723–26.

Q6107218.name: 1969 Libyan coup d'état
Q6107218.blurb: A coup in Libya brings Muammar Gaddafi to power.

Q6107732.name: JAT Airways Flight 769
Q6107732.blurb: JAT Airways Flight 769 crashes into the Maganik mountain range while on approach to Titograd Airport, killing 35 passengers and six crew.

Q6117386.name: Jackson State killings
Q6117386.blurb: Police opened fire during a confrontation with a group of Jackson State College students, killing two students and injuring twelve others.

Q6121975.name: Jaffna hospital massacre
Q6121975.blurb: The Jaffna hospital massacre is carried out by Indian peacekeeping forces in Sri Lanka, killing 70 Tamil patients, doctors and nurses.

Q6121977.name: Jaffna lagoon massacre
Q6121977.blurb: Sri Lankan Civil War: The Sri Lanka Navy kill 35–100 civilians on the Jaffna Lagoon.

Q6127215.name: Jamaat al Muslimeen coup attempt
Q6127215.blurb: The Jamaat al Muslimeen attempt a coup d'état in Trinidad and Tobago.

Q6130126.name: Siege of Sinope
Q6130126.blurb: The port city of Sinope surrenders to the Seljuq Turks.

Q6139084.name: Preparedness Day Bombing
Q6139084.blurb: Preparedness Day Bombing: In San Francisco, a bomb explodes on Market Street during a parade, killing ten and injuring 40.

Q6143212.name: 1837 Valdivia earthquake
Q6143212.blurb: An earthquake in Valdivia, south-central Chile, causes a tsunami that leads to significant destruction along Japan's coast.

Q6143782.name: Pan Am Flight 202
Q6143782.blurb: Pan Am Flight 202 crashes into the Amazon basin near Carolina, Maranhão, Brazil, killing 50 people.

Q6151502.name: The tragedy of gate 12
Q6151502.blurb: Seventy-four people were killed and 150 others injured in a stampede at a football match between Boca Juniors and Club Atlético River Plate in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

Q6155580.name: Janszoon voyage of 1606
Q6155580.blurb: The Janszoon voyage of 1605–06 becomes the first European expedition to set foot on Australia, although it is mistaken as a part of New Guinea.

Q6155798.name: January 2012 al-Midan bombing
Q6155798.blurb: Twenty-six people are killed and 63 wounded when a suicide bomber blows himself up at a police station in Damascus.

Q6156488.name: Japan Airlines Flight 471
Q6156488.blurb: Japan Air Lines Flight 471 crashes on approach to Palam International Airport (now Indira Gandhi International Airport) in New Delhi, India, killing 82 of the 87 people on board and four more people on the ground.

Q6156491.name: Japan Airlines Flight 472 (1972)
Q6156491.blurb: Japan Airlines Flight 472 lands at Juhu Aerodrome instead of Santacruz Airport in Bombay, India, overrunning the runway and resulting in 11 injuries.

Q6156492.name: Japan Airlines Flight 715
Q6156492.blurb: Japan Airlines Flight 715 crashes on approach to Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang, Malaysia, killing 34 of the 79 people on board.

Q6161350.name: Mekong River massacre
Q6161350.blurb: In the Mekong River massacre, two Chinese cargo boats are hijacked and 13 crew members murdered.

Q6164557.name: Jathibhanga massacre
Q6164557.blurb: Bangladesh Liberation War: The Pakistan Army and Razakars massacre approximately 3,000 Hindu emigrants in the Jathibhanga area of East Pakistan (now Bangladesh).

Q6164961.name: Cubana de Aviación Flight 389
Q6164961.blurb: Eighty people are killed when Cubana de Aviación Flight 389 crashes during a rejected takeoff from the Old Mariscal Sucre International Airport in Quito, Ecuador.

Q6165289.name: Guo Huaiyi Rebellion
Q6165289.blurb: Around 15,000 Han farmers and militia rebel against Dutch rule on Taiwan.

Q6165880.name: Soviet invasion of Manchuria
aliases: Greater East Asia War in Manchuria
War crimes in the Soviet invasion of Manchuria
Q6165880.blurb: The Red Army invades Japanese-occupied Manchuria.

Q6172500.name: Jebel Akhdar War
Q6172500.blurb: The forces of the Sultanate of Muscat occupy the last strongholds of the Imamate of Oman, Saiq and Shuraijah, marking the end of Jebel Akhdar War in Oman.

Q6223430.name: John Brown's raid on Harpers Ferry
aliases: John Brown's raid on Harper's Ferry
Q6223430.blurb: Origins of the American Civil War: Abolitionist John Brown and his supporters launch a raid on Harpers Ferry, Virginia (now West Virginia).

Q6266376.name: Johnny Bright incident
Q6266376.blurb: The "Johnny Bright incident" occurs during a football game between the Drake Bulldogs and Oklahoma A&M Aggies.

Q6268420.name: Johnson Space Center shooting
Q6268420.blurb: Johnson Space Center shooting: William Phillips barricades himself with a handgun in NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston, Texas, before killing a male hostage and himself.

Q6269697.name: Jokela rail accident
Q6269697.blurb: Four people are killed and 75 are injured in a train accident in Jokela, Finland.

Q6273740.name: Proclamation of Islaz
Q6273740.blurb: In the Wallachian Revolution, Ion Heliade Rădulescu and Christian Tell issue the Proclamation of Islaz and create a new republican government.

Q6302931.name: Judicial Procedures Reform Bill of 1937
aliases: FDR New Deal Supreme Court expansion plan
Franklin Roosevelt Supreme Court expansion plan
Q6302931.blurb: New Deal: The United States Senate votes down President Franklin D. Roosevelt's proposal to add more justices to the Supreme Court of the United States.

Q6310567.name: July 2009 Mindanao bombings
Q6310567.blurb: The first of four days of bombings begins on the southern Philippine island group of Mindanao.

Q6312013.name: June 1966 tornado outbreak sequence
Q6312013.blurb: Topeka, Kansas, United States is devastated by a tornado that registers as an "F5" on the Fujita scale, exceeding US$200 million in damages. Seventeen people are killed, over five hundred more injured, and thousands of homes damaged or destroyed.

Q6312034.name: June 1988 Haitian coup d'état
Q6312034.blurb: Haitian president Leslie Manigat is ousted from power in a coup d'état led by Lieutenant General Henri Namphy.

Q6312086.name: June 2007 Hunter Region and Central Coast storms
Q6312086.blurb: A major storm caused the bulk carrier Pasha Bulker to run aground in New South Wales, Australia.

Q6312181.name: 1979 Ghanaian coup d'état
Q6312181.blurb: Flight Lieutenant Jerry Rawlings takes power in Ghana after a military coup in which General Fred Akuffo is overthrown.

Q6356796.name: Night of the Long Knives
Q6356796.blurb: In an unprecedented action, British Prime Minister Harold Macmillan dismisses seven members of his Cabinet, marking the effective end of the National Liberals as a distinct force within British politics.

Q6357708.name: Kamień Pomorski homeless hostel fire
Q6357708.blurb: A fire destroys a homeless hostel and kills at least 22 people in Kamień Pomorski, Poland.

Q6364195.name: Kano air disaster
Q6364195.blurb: A chartered Boeing 707 explodes in flames upon landing at Kano Airport, Nigeria, killing 176.

Q6364933.name: Kansas City massacre
Q6364933.blurb: Union Station massacre: In Kansas City, Missouri, four FBI agents and captured fugitive Frank Nash are gunned down by gangsters attempting to free Nash.

Q6387278.name: Ken Ballew raid
Q6387278.blurb: The Alcohol, Tobacco, and Firearms Division of the U.S. Internal Revenue Service raids the home of Ken Ballew for illegal possession of hand grenades.

Q6389258.name: Noble train of artillery
Q6389258.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Using artillery transported from Ticonderoga, the Continental Army occupied Dorchester Heights, forcing the British to abandon Boston two weeks later.

Q6400364.name: Khanna rail disaster
Q6400364.blurb: The Khanna rail disaster takes 212 lives in Khanna, Ludhiana, India.

Q6403042.name: Battle of Fakhkh
Q6403042.blurb: A Hasanid Alid uprising in Mecca is crushed by the Abbasids at the Battle of Fakhkh.

Q6407890.name: Killough massacre
Q6407890.blurb: A Cherokee band attacked settlers near Larissa, Texas, killing or abducting 18 people.

Q6408028.name: Kilmichael Ambush
Q6408028.blurb: Irish War of Independence: Kilmichael Ambush: The Irish Republican Army ambush a convoy of British Auxiliaries and kill seventeen.

Q6408274.name: Kilvenmani massacre
Q6408274.blurb: Kilvenmani massacre: Forty-four Dalits (untouchables) are burnt to death in Kizhavenmani village, Tamil Nadu, a retaliation for a campaign for higher wages by Dalit laborers.

Q6413525.name: Kingston Fossil Plant coal fly ash slurry spill
Q6413525.blurb: An ash dike ruptures at a solid waste containment area for a Tennessee Valley Authority coal-fired power plant in Roane County, Tennessee, releasing 4.2 million m3 (1.1 billion US gal) of coal fly ash slurry in the largest industrial spill in U.S. history.

Q6416483.name: Kish Air Flight 7170
Q6416483.blurb: Forty-three people are killed and three are injured when a Fokker 50 crashes near Sharjah International Airport.

Q6422063.name: Knickerbocker Storm
Q6422063.blurb: Knickerbocker Storm: Washington, D.C.'s biggest snowfall, causes a disaster when the roof of the Knickerbocker Theatre collapses, killing over 100 people.

Q6426557.name: Kokang incident
Q6426557.blurb: The Myanmar military junta and ethnic armies began three days of violent clashes in the region of Kokang.

Q6428897.name: Konbaung–Hanthawaddy War
Q6428897.blurb: Start of Konbaung–Hanthawaddy War, a new phase in the Burmese Civil War (1740–57).

Q6439286.name: Krulak Mendenhall mission
Q6439286.blurb: The Kennedy administration sent Victor H. Krulak and Joseph Mendenhall on a mission to assess the progress of the Vietnam War.

Q6446139.name: Kurkse tragedy
Q6446139.blurb: Kurkse tragedy: Fourteen Estonian soldiers of the Baltic Battalion are drowned or die of hypothermia during a training exercise in the Kurkse Strait.

Q6455722.name: L'Express Airlines Flight 508
Q6455722.blurb: A Beechcraft Model 99 crashes near Birmingham Municipal Airport (now Birmingham–Shuttlesworth International Airport) in Birmingham, Alabama, killing 13 of the 15 people on board.

Q6457042.name: LANSA Flight 502
Q6457042.blurb: LANSA Flight 502 crashes after takeoff from Alejandro Velasco Astete International Airport in Cusco, Peru, killing 99 of the 100 people on board, as well as two people on the ground.

Q6459604.name: LOT Flight 703
Q6459604.blurb: LOT Polish Airlines Flight 703 crashes in Białobrzegi, Podkarpackie Voivodeship, Poland, killing one person and injuring several more.

Q6464343.name: La Paz Revolution
Q6464343.blurb: The city of La Paz, in what is today Bolivia, declares its independence from the Spanish Crown during the La Paz revolution and forms the Junta Tuitiva, the first independent government in Spanish America, led by Pedro Domingo Murillo.

Q6467353.name: Labouchère Amendment
Q6467353.blurb: Playwright, poet and novelist Oscar Wilde is convicted of "committing acts of gross indecency with other male persons" and sentenced to serve two years in prison.

Q6470690.name: Si Zerrouk massacre
Q6470690.blurb: About 50 people are killed in the Si Zerrouk massacre in Algeria.

Q6470701.name: Souhane massacre
Q6470701.blurb: Souhane massacre in Algeria; over 60 people are killed and 15 kidnapped.

Q6470782.name: Rais massacre
Q6470782.blurb: At least 98 villagers are killed by the Armed Islamic Group of Algeria GIA in the Rais massacre, Algeria.

Q6475222.name: Lake Central Flight 527
Q6475222.blurb: Lake Central Airlines Flight 527 crashes near Marseilles, Ohio, killing 38.

Q6479359.name: Lakewood, Washington police officer shooting
Q6479359.blurb: Maurice Clemmons shoots and kills four police officers inside a coffee shop in Lakewood, Washington.

Q6484626.name: Landing at Nadzab
Q6484626.blurb: World War II: American and Australian airborne forces landed at Nadzab as part of the New Guinea campaign against Japan.

Q6484628.name: Landing at Saidor
Q6484628.blurb: World War II: United States and Australian forces successfully landed in Papua New Guinea in an attempt to cut off a Japanese retreat.

Q6484643.name: Landing on Emirau
Q6484643.blurb: World War II: U.S. Marines made a landing on Emirau Island in the Bismarck Archipelago to develop an airbase as part of Operation Cartwheel.

Q6487841.name: Laoag International Airlines Flight 585
Q6487841.blurb: A Fokker F27 Friendship operating as Laoag International Airlines Flight 585 crashes into Manila Bay shortly after takeoff from Ninoy Aquino International Airport, killing 19 people.

Q6497151.name: Lattimer massacre
Q6497151.blurb: Lattimer massacre: A sheriff's posse kills 19 unarmed striking immigrant miners in Lattimer, Pennsylvania, United States.

Q6497833.name: Last battle of the battleship Bismarck
Q6497833.blurb: World War II: The German battleship Bismarck was sunk by gun and torpedo fire by the British battleships HMS Rodney and HMS King George V and supporting cruisers.

Q6500827.name: Japanese asset price bubble
Q6500827.blurb: The Nikkei 225 for the Tokyo Stock Exchange hits its all-time intra-day high of 38,957.44 and closing high at 38,915.87, serving as the apex of the Japanese asset price bubble.

Q6507837.name: Le Van Khoi revolt
Q6507837.blurb: A revolt broke out in southern Vietnam against Emperor Minh Mang, who had desecrated the deceased mandarin Le Van Duyet.

Q6514328.name: Norwegian monarchy plebiscite
Q6514328.blurb: Norway holds a referendum resulting in popular approval of the Storting's decision to authorise the government to make the offer of the throne of the newly independent country.

Q6514477.name: Widerøe Flight 933
Q6514477.blurb: Fifteen people are killed when Widerøe Flight 933 crashes into the Barents Sea near Gamvik, Norway.

Q6516946.name: Widerøe Flight 710
Q6516946.blurb: All thirty-six passengers and crew are killed when Widerøe Flight 710 crashes into Mt. Torghatten in Brønnøy.

Q6522605.name: Leningrad première of Shostakovich's Symphony No. 7
Q6522605.blurb: Shostakovich's Symphony No. 7 was premiered in Leningrad while the city was under siege by Nazi forces.

Q6531759.name: Élysée Accords
Q6531759.blurb: President of France Vincent Auriol and ex-Vietnamese emperor Bảo Đại sign the Élysée Accords, giving Vietnam greater independence from France and creating the State of Vietnam to oppose Viet Minh-led Democratic Republic of Vietnam.

Q6540361.name: surrender of Japan
aliases: Surrender of the Empire of Japan
Q6540361.blurb: The Stanley Internment Camp in Hong Kong was liberated following the announcement of the surrender of Japan in World War II.

Q6541032.name: Liberation of Arnhem
Q6541032.blurb: Second World War: British and Canadian forces concluded the Liberation of Arnhem in the Netherlands from German occupation.

Q6553185.name: Line Item Veto Act of 1996
Q6553185.blurb: In Clinton v. City of New York, the United States Supreme Court decides that the Line Item Veto Act of 1996 is unconstitutional.

Q6553353.name: Linea Aeropostal Venezolana Flight 253 (June 1956)
Q6553353.blurb: A Venezuelan Super-Constellation crashes in the Atlantic Ocean off Asbury Park, New Jersey, killing 74 people.

Q6554197.name: Linjeflyg Flight 618
Q6554197.blurb: Linjeflyg Flight 618 crashes in Kälvesta near Stockholm Bromma Airport in Stockholm, Sweden, killing 22 people.

Q6555394.name: Lion Air Flight 538
Q6555394.blurb: A McDonnell Douglas MD-82, operating as Lion Air Flight 538, overran the runway at Adisoemarmo Airport and crashed, killing 25 people.

Q6556186.name: Operation Tiger
Q6556186.blurb: Croatian War of Independence: The Croatian Army concluded Operation Tiger, advancing 17 kilometres (11 miles) into the Dubrovnik hinterland.

Q6556541.name: 1991 Hindu Kush earthquake
Q6556541.blurb: A magnitude 6.8 earthquake strikes the Hindu Kush region, killing at least 848 people in Afghanistan, Pakistan and present-day Tajikistan.

Q6569289.name: Şahkulu Revolt
Q6569289.blurb: Resettled Shiite Muslims rise up in the Şahkulu rebellion under the leadership of Şahkulu against the Ottoman Empire.

Q6581708.name: 2000 UEFA Cup semi-final violence
Q6581708.blurb: Fan violence broke out before a UEFA Cup semifinal in Istanbul, Turkey, resulting in two Leeds United supporters being stabbed to death and Galatasaray supporters being banned from attending the second leg in England.

Q6583055.name: Tropical Storm Linda
Q6583055.blurb: Tropical Storm Linda makes landfall in the Mekong Delta in Vietnam, causing more than 3,000 deaths.

Q6585266.name: 1991 Thai coup d'état
Q6585266.blurb: In Thailand, General Sunthorn Kongsompong leads a bloodless coup d'état, deposing Prime Minister Chatichai Choonhavan.

Q6649989.name: Little Feller
Q6649989.blurb: Nuclear weapons testing: The "Small Boy" test shot Little Feller I becomes the last atmospheric test detonation at the Nevada National Security Site.

Q6665169.name: Lochry's Defeat
Q6665169.blurb: American Revolutionary War: A small force of Pennsylvania militia is ambushed and overwhelmed by an American Indian group, which forces George Rogers Clark to abandon his attempt to attack Detroit.

Q6669368.name: Lombard Street Riot
Q6669368.blurb: The Lombard Street riot erupts in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States.

Q6671126.name: 2000 London mayoral election
Q6671126.blurb: Ken Livingstone becomes the first Mayor of London (an office separate from that of the Lord Mayor of London).

Q6675594.name: Loomis Fargo Bank Robbery
Q6675594.blurb: The second largest cash robbery in U.S. history occurs in North Carolina.

Q6682248.name: Los Angeles Jewish Community Center shooting
Q6682248.blurb: One person is killed and five people are injured in the Los Angeles Jewish Community Center shooting.

Q6682364.name: Los Angeles Times bombing
Q6682364.blurb: A large bomb destroys the Los Angeles Times building, killing 21.

Q6686191.name: Loughgall Ambush
Q6686191.blurb: A British Special Air Service unit ambushed a Provisional Irish Republican Army (IRA) unit in Loughgall, Northern Ireland, killing eight IRA members and one civilian.

Q6689579.name: Louisville sewer explosions
Q6689579.blurb: A series of sewer explosions destroys more than two miles of streets in Louisville, Kentucky.

Q6692532.name: Lovettsville air disaster
Q6692532.blurb: Pennsylvania Central Airlines Trip 19 crashes near Lovettsville, Virginia. The CAB investigation of the accident is the first investigation to be conducted under the Bureau of Air Commerce act of 1938.

Q6694023.name: lowest temperature recorded on Earth
Q6694023.blurb: The world's lowest temperature in an inhabited location is recorded at Vostok Station, Antarctica at −89.2 °C (−128.6 °F).

Q6706220.name: Luxembourg Coup of 1856
Q6706220.blurb: The Coup of 1856 leads to Luxembourg's unilateral adoption of a new, reactionary constitution.

Q6709815.name: Lyons–Seward Treaty of 1862
Q6709815.blurb: The United States and the United Kingdom agree in the Lyons–Seward Treaty to suppress the African slave trade.

Q6710402.name: 1933 Lyttelton by-election
Q6710402.blurb: Elizabeth McCombs becomes the first woman elected to the New Zealand Parliament.

Q6713893.name: M62 coach bombing
Q6713893.blurb: M62 coach bombing: The Provisional Irish Republican Army (IRA) explodes a bomb on a bus carrying off-duty British Armed Forces personnel in Yorkshire, England. Nine soldiers and three civilians are killed.

Q6721586.name: Battle of Mabila
Q6721586.blurb: Spanish conquistador Hernando de Soto's forces destroy the fortified town of Mabila in present-day Alabama, killing Tuskaloosa.

Q6722105.name: MacRobertson Miller Airlines Flight 1750
Q6722105.blurb: MacRobertson Miller Airlines Flight 1750 crashes near Port Hedland, Western Australia, killing all 26 people on board.

Q6728635.name: Madrid Runway Disaster
Q6728635.blurb: An Iberia Airlines Boeing 727 collides with an Aviaco DC-9 in dense fog while the two airliners are taxiing down the runway at Madrid–Barajas Airport, killing 93 people.

Q6733375.name: Maharashtra floods of 2005
Q6733375.blurb: Mumbai, India receives 99.5cm of rain (39.17 inches) within 24 hours, resulting in floods killing over 5,000 people.

Q6734465.name: Mahmud Barzanji revolts
Q6734465.blurb: Sheikh Mahmud Barzanji, a Kurdish sheikh and at-the-time governor of the Slêmanî Province of British Iraq, initiates the first Mahmud Barzanji revolt.

Q6741498.name: 1994 Malawian general election
Q6741498.blurb: Malawi holds its first multi-party elections.

Q6742048.name: 1969 Malaysian general election
Q6742048.blurb: In the aftermath of the 1969 Malaysian general election, Sino-Malay sectarian violence erupts in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

Q6744844.name: Maltese divorce referendum, 2011
Q6744844.blurb: Malta votes on the introduction of divorce; the proposal was approved by 53% of voters, resulting in a law allowing divorce under certain conditions being enacted later in the year.

Q6745211.name: Malê Revolt
Q6745211.blurb: Slaves in Salvador da Bahia, Brazil, stage a revolt, which is instrumental in ending slavery there 50 years later.

Q6756695.name: March 1504 lunar eclipse
Q6756695.blurb: Christopher Columbus uses his knowledge of a lunar eclipse that night to convince Jamaican natives to provide him with supplies.

Q6757026.name: Marchioness disaster
Q6757026.blurb: The pleasure boat Marchioness sinks on the River Thames following a collision. Fifty-one people are killed.

Q6762017.name: Marian civil war
Q6762017.blurb: Mary, Queen of Scots, is defeated at the Battle of Langside, part of the civil war between Queen Mary and the supporters of her son, James VI.

Q6763709.name: Marin County Civic Center attacks
Q6763709.blurb: Jonathan Jackson took hostages in a courthouse in Marin County, California, to coerce the release of the Soledad Brothers, resulting in the deaths of judge Harold Haley and three others.

Q6776962.name: Martin and Mitchell defection
Q6776962.blurb: Cold War: Two cryptographers working for the United States National Security Agency left for vacation to Mexico, and from there defected to the Soviet Union.

Q6781554.name: Maryland in the American Civil War
Q6781554.blurb: Maryland in the American Civil War: Maryland's House of Delegates votes not to secede from the Union.

Q6784091.name: Mass suicide in Demmin
Q6784091.blurb: World War II: German radio broadcasts news of Adolf Hitler's death, falsely stating that he has "fallen at his command post in the Reich Chancellery fighting to the last breath against Bolshevism and for Germany". The Soviet flag is raised over the Reich Chancellery, by order of Stalin. Up to 2,500 people die in a mass suicide in Demmin following the advance of the Red Army.

Q6784466.name: Massacre at Ayyadieh
Q6784466.blurb: Believing Saladin had reneged on ransom promises, Richard I of England initiates the massacre at Ayyadieh, beheading 2,700 captive Muslim soldiers and another 300 women and children seized at the Fall of Acre.

Q6784475.name: Massacre of Aleppo
Q6784475.blurb: Riots start, which lead to a massacre in Aleppo.

Q6784480.name: Massacre of Dunlavin Green
Q6784480.blurb: United Irishmen Rebellion: Battle of Carlow begins; executions of suspected rebels at Carnew and at Dunlavin Green take place.

Q6786062.name: 6th Congress of the Workers' Party of Korea
Q6786062.blurb: The 6th Congress of the Workers' Party ended, having anointed North Korean President Kim Il Sung's son Kim Jong Il as his successor.

Q6796325.name: May 2006 São Paulo violence
Q6796325.blurb: Mass unrest by the Primeiro Comando da Capital begins in São Paulo (Brazil), leaving at least 150 dead.

Q6796396.name: May 30, 1998 Afghanistan earthquake
Q6796396.blurb: The 6.5 Mw Afghanistan earthquake shakes the Takhar Province of northern Afghanistan with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VII (Very strong), killing around 4,000–4,500.

Q6797090.name: Mayerthorpe tragedy
Q6797090.blurb: James Roszko murders four Royal Canadian Mounted Police constables during a drug bust at his property in Rochfort Bridge, Alberta, then commits suicide. This is the deadliest peace-time incident for the RCMP since 1885 and the North-West Rebellion.

Q6798401.name: Maze Prison escape
Q6798401.blurb: Thirty-eight IRA prisoners, armed with six handguns, hijack a prison meals lorry and smash their way out of the Maze Prison.

Q6801530.name: McGurk's Bar bombing
Q6801530.blurb: The Troubles: The Ulster Volunteer Force, an Ulster-loyalist paramilitary group, detonated a bomb at a Catholic-owned pub in Belfast, Northern Ireland, killing 15 people.

Q6808488.name: Battle of Pyongyang (1950)
Q6808488.blurb: Korean War: The Battle of Pyongyang ends in a United Nations victory. Hours later, the Chinese Army begins crossing the border into Korea.

Q6809080.name: Meghna Heli Bridge
Q6809080.blurb: Indo-Pakistani War: The Indian Air Force executes an airdrop of Indian Army units, bypassing Pakistani defences.

Q6814184.name: Memali Incident
Q6814184.blurb: Police in Baling, Malaysia, lay siege to houses occupied by an Islamic sect of about 400 people led by Ibrahim Mahmud.

Q6815868.name: Memphis Riots of 1866
Q6815868.blurb: The Memphis Race Riots begin. Over three days, 46 blacks and two whites were killed. Reports of the atrocities influenced passage of the Fourteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution.

Q6815871.name: Memphis Sanitation Strike
Q6815871.blurb: Following the deaths of two employees on the job, black sanitation workers in Memphis, Tennessee, began a strike that lasted more than two months.

Q6816645.name: Mendiola massacre
Q6816645.blurb: Philippine security forces open fire on a crowd of 10,000–15,000 demonstrators at Malacañang Palace, Manila, killing 13.

Q6841321.name: Middle East Airlines Flight 438
Q6841321.blurb: A bomb explodes on board Middle East Airlines Flight 438 over Qaisumah, Saudi Arabia, killing all 81 people on board.

Q6843375.name: Midwest Express Airlines Flight 105
Q6843375.blurb: Midwest Express Airlines Flight 105 crashes near Milwaukee Mitchell International Airport in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, killing all 31 people on board.

Q6851773.name: 1st Congress of the Workers' Party of North Korea
Q6851773.blurb: The Workers' Party of North Korea, predecessor of the ruling Workers' Party of Korea, is founded at a congress held in Pyongyang, North Korea.

Q6854309.name: Hurricane Flossy
Q6854309.blurb: A tropical storm originating in the eastern Pacific Ocean passes into the Gulf of Mexico and is upgraded and named Hurricane Flossy just hours before striking the Gulf Coast and causing 15 deaths and an estimated US$24.8 million in damages.

Q6857906.name: Militia Acts of 1792
Q6857906.blurb: U.S. President George Washington invokes the Militia Acts of 1792 to suppress the Whiskey Rebellion in western Pennsylvania.

Q6860084.name: Milltown Cemetery attack
Q6860084.blurb: Michael Stone, an Ulster loyalist, attacked the funeral of three Provisional IRA members, killing three attendees and injuring at least sixty others.

Q6861694.name: Milwaukee Bridge War
Q6861694.blurb: After the Milwaukee Bridge War, the United States towns of Juneautown and Kilbourntown unify to create the City of Milwaukee.

Q6864869.name: Ming–Kotte War
Q6864869.blurb: Ming China's Admiral Zheng He returns to Nanjing after the third treasure voyage and presents the Sinhalese king, captured during the Ming–Kotte War, to the Yongle Emperor.

Q6868032.name: Minneapolis Teamsters Strike of 1934
Q6868032.blurb: Labor unrest in the U.S.: Police in Minneapolis fire upon striking truck drivers, during the Minneapolis Teamsters Strike of 1934, killing two and wounding sixty-seven.

Q6868827.name: Minnie Pit Disaster
Q6868827.blurb: The Minnie Pit Disaster coal mining accident occurs in Halmer End, Staffordshire, in which 155 men and boys die.

Q6872041.name: Mir EO-19
Q6872041.blurb: Mir EO-19, the first expedition to the Russian space station Mir launched on an American Space Shuttle, returned to Earth after approximately 75 days in space.

Q6889422.name: Battle of Philippeville
Q6889422.blurb: Battle of Philippeville: In Morocco, a force of Berbers from the Atlas Mountains region of Algeria raid two rural settlements and kill 77 French nationals.

Q6893760.name: Mohawk Airlines Flight 405
Q6893760.blurb: Mohawk Airlines Flight 405 crashes as a result of a control malfunction and insufficient training in emergency procedures.

Q6899715.name: 1993 Mongolian presidential election
Q6899715.blurb: Punsalmaagiin Ochirbat wins the first presidential election in Mongolia.

Q6900329.name: the Blitz
aliases: Bombing of London in World War II
Q6900329.blurb: World War II: The German Luftwaffe begins the Blitz, bombing London and other British cities for over 50 consecutive nights.

Q6900391.name: Thai Airways Flight 365
Q6900391.blurb: Thai Airways Flight 365 crashes into the ocean near Ko Phuket, Thailand, killing all 83 aboard.

Q6909299.name: Moratorium to End the War in Vietnam
Q6909299.blurb: Vietnam War: In Washington, D.C., 250,000–500,000 protesters staged a peaceful demonstration against the war, including a symbolic "March Against Death".

Q6915535.name: Moscow Summit
Q6915535.blurb: U.S. President Ronald Reagan begins his first visit to the Soviet Union when he arrives in Moscow for a superpower summit with the Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev.

Q6931428.name: Mud March
Q6931428.blurb: The Mud March is the first large procession organised by the National Union of Women's Suffrage Societies (NUWSS).

Q6937882.name: murder of Huang Na
Q6937882.blurb: Eight-year-old Huang Na was abducted and murdered; her body was found three weeks later after a search across Singapore and Malaysia.

Q6938040.name: murder of Ross Parker
Q6938040.blurb: Ross Parker is murdered in Peterborough, England, by a gang of ten British Pakistani youths.

Q6938050.name: murder of Selena
Q6938050.blurb: Selena is murdered by her fan club president Yolanda Saldívar at a Days Inn in Corpus Christi, Texas.

Q6943099.name: Mussel Slough Tragedy
Q6943099.blurb: Seven people are killed in the Mussel Slough Tragedy, a gun battle in California.

Q6950605.name: Ariane flight V88
Q6950605.blurb: The first flight of Ariane 5 explodes after roughly 37 seconds. It was a Cluster mission.

Q6958257.name: Nag Hammadi massacre
Q6958257.blurb: In Nag Hammadi, Egypt, Muslim gunmen opened fire on a crowd of Coptic Christians leaving church after attending Christmas Liturgy, killing eight of them, as well as one Muslim bystander.

Q6958778.name: Nagerkovil school bombing
Q6958778.blurb: The Nagerkovil school bombing is carried out by the Sri Lanka Air Force in which at least 34 die, most of them ethnic Tamil schoolchildren.

Q6966493.name: Narva Offensive February 1944
Q6966493.blurb: World War II: The Narva Offensive begins.

Q6967898.name: Nat Turner's slave rebellion
Q6967898.blurb: Nat Turner's rebellion of enslaved Virginians is suppressed.

Q6970261.name: National Airlines Flight 2511
Q6970261.blurb: National Airlines Flight 2511 is destroyed in mid-air by a bomb, while en route from New York City to Miami.

Q6970264.name: National Airlines Flight 967
Q6970264.blurb: National Airlines Flight 967 explodes in mid-air over the Gulf of Mexico, killing all 42 aboard.

Q6974232.name: National March on Washington for Lesbian and Gay Rights
aliases: 1979 National March on Washington for Lesbian & Gay Rights
1979 National March on Washington for Lesbian and Gay Rights
First National March on Washington for Lesbian & Gay Rights
First National March on Washington for Lesbian and Gay Rights
National Lesbian & Gay Rights March on Washington, Washington, D.C., 1979
National March on Washington for Lesbian & Gay Rights, Washington, D.C., 1979
National March on Washington for Lesbian and Gay Rights (1979)
Q6974232.blurb: The first National March on Washington for Lesbian and Gay Rights draws approximately 100,000 people.

Q6980067.name: Native Title Act 1993
Q6980067.blurb: Australian Aboriginal land rights are recognised in Mabo v Queensland (No 2), a case brought by Torres Strait Islander Eddie Mabo which led to the Native Title Act 1993  overturning the long-held colonial assumption of terra nullius.

Q6982062.name: Navaly church bombing
Q6982062.blurb: The Navaly church bombing is carried out by the Sri Lanka Air Force killing 125 Tamil civilian refugees.

Q6983410.name: German crimes against Poles
Q6983410.blurb: Nazi crimes against the Polish nation: Nazi troops massacre Polish scientists and writers in the captured Ukrainian city of Lviv.

Q6984367.name: Near East earthquakes of 1759
Q6984367.blurb: An earthquake hits the Mediterranean destroying Beirut and Damascus and killing 30,000–40,000.

Q6990213.name: Nellore train fire
Q6990213.blurb: A train fire kills 32 passengers and injures 27 on the Tamil Nadu Express in Andhra Pradesh, India.

Q6994574.name: Nepal–Britain Treaty of 1923
Q6994574.blurb: Nepal and the United Kingdom signed the first treaty that defined the international status of Nepal as an independent and a sovereign nation.

Q7016166.name: 1999 New Zealand general election
Q7016166.blurb: The Labour Party defeated the governing National Party in the New Zealand general election, with Labour's Helen Clark becoming the country's first female prime minister to have won office at an election.

Q7018976.name: Newport Rising
Q7018976.blurb: Newport Rising: The last large-scale armed rebellion against authority in mainland Britain.

Q7019609.name: Newsboys Strike of 1899
Q7019609.blurb: Newsboys from Long Island City turned over a distribution wagon for the New York Journal, marking the start of the Newsboys' strike of 1899.

Q7022421.name: Ngo Dinh Diem presidential visit to Australia
Q7022421.blurb: President Ngô Đình Diệm of South Vietnam becomes the first foreign head of state to make a state visit to Australia.

Q7032791.name: Nigeria Airways Flight 357
Q7032791.blurb: Nigeria Airways Flight 357 crashes at Kaduna International Airport in Kaduna, Nigeria, killing 11 people and injuring 66.

Q7033051.name: 1993 Nigerian presidential election
Q7033051.blurb: An election takes place in Nigeria and is won by Moshood Kashimawo Olawale Abiola. Its results are later annulled by the military government of Ibrahim Babangida.

Q7039190.name: Ninth Avenue derailment
Q7039190.blurb: The Ninth Avenue derailment occurs in New York City, killing 13.

Q7041997.name: Nixon White House tapes
Q7041997.blurb: President Nixon rejects an Appeals Court decision that he turn over the Watergate tapes.

Q7053851.name: North American Regional Broadcasting Agreement
Q7053851.blurb: The North American Regional Broadcasting Agreement goes into effect at 03:00 local time.

Q7054721.name: North Central Airlines Flight 458
Q7054721.blurb: North Central Airlines Flight 458 crashes at O'Hare International Airport, killing 28.

Q7056258.name: North Pacific Fur Seal Convention of 1911
aliases: North Pacific Fur Seal Treaty of 1911
Treaty for the Preservation and Protection of Fur Seals
Q7056258.blurb: The United States, UK, Japan, and Russia sign the North Pacific Fur Seal Convention of 1911 banning open-water seal hunting, the first international treaty to address wildlife preservation issues.

Q7057126.name: North Vietnamese đồng
Q7057126.blurb: The Democratic Republic of Vietnam introduces the đồng to replace the French Indochinese piastre at par.

Q7057810.name: Northeast Airlines Flight 823
Q7057810.blurb: Northeast Airlines Flight 823 crashes on Rikers Island in New York City, killing 20 people and injuring 78 others.

Q7057813.name: Northeast Airlines Flight 946
Q7057813.blurb: A Fairchild F-27 crashes into Moose Mountain while on approach to Lebanon Municipal Airport in Lebanon, New Hampshire, killing 32 people.

Q7058145.name: Northern Bank robbery
Q7058145.blurb: A gang of thieves steal £26.5 million worth of currency from the Donegall Square West headquarters of Northern Bank in Belfast, Northern Ireland, United Kingdom, one of the largest bank robberies in British history.

Q7058486.name: Northern Ireland Constitutional Convention
Q7058486.blurb: The Northern Ireland Constitutional Convention is formally dissolved in Northern Ireland, resulting in direct rule of Northern Ireland from London by the British parliament.

Q7058495.name: Northern Ireland Executive (1974)
Q7058495.blurb: British and Irish authorities sign the Sunningdale Agreement in an attempt to establish a power-sharing Northern Ireland Executive and a cross-border Council of Ireland.

Q7060142.name: Northwest Orient Airlines Flight 307
Q7060142.blurb: Northwest Orient Airlines Flight 307 crashes in Lynnhurst, Minneapolis, killing 15 people.

Q7060144.name: Northwest Airlines Flight 705
Q7060144.blurb: Northwest Orient Airlines Flight 705 crashes into the Everglades shortly after takeoff from Miami International Airport, killing all 45 people on board.

Q7060145.name: Northwest Orient Airlines Flight 710
Q7060145.blurb: Northwest Orient Airlines Flight 710 crashes in Tobin Township, Perry County, Indiana, killing 63.

Q7060146.name: Northwest Orient Airlines Flight 706
Q7060146.blurb: Northwest Orient Airlines Flight 706 crashes during takeoff from O'Hare International Airport in Chicago, Illinois, killing all 37 people on board.

Q7074218.name: Oaks explosion
Q7074218.blurb: Oaks explosion: The worst mining disaster in England kills 361 miners and rescuers.

Q7074336.name: Oakwood mutiny
Q7074336.blurb: During their trial for the 2003 Oakwood mutiny, Philippine soldiers led by Senator Antonio Trillanes mutinied and seized a conference room at The Peninsula Manila in Makati.

Q7075770.name: German occupation of the Baltic states during World War II
Q7075770.blurb: Whole territory of Estonia is occupied by Nazi Germany.

Q7089272.name: Olympus scandal
Q7089272.blurb: Michael Woodford was dismissed as the CEO of the optics manufacturer Olympus after uncovering internal financial misconduct, escalating the corporate scandal into one of the largest in Japanese business history.

Q7096009.name: Open Door
Q7096009.blurb: Della Aleksander co-presented an episode of Open Door on transgender women's lives.

Q7096523.name: Opening of the Liverpool and Manchester Railway
Q7096523.blurb: The Liverpool to Manchester railway line opens; British MP William Huskisson becomes the first widely reported railway passenger fatality when he is struck and killed by the locomotive Rocket.

Q7096792.name: Operation Barrel Roll
Q7096792.blurb: Operation Barrel Roll, a covert American bombing campaign in Laos to stop communist infiltration of South Vietnam, ends.

Q7096800.name: Operation Berlin
Q7096800.blurb: World War II: Surviving elements of the British 1st Airborne Division withdraw from Arnhem via Oosterbeek.

Q7096876.name: Operation Catechism
Q7096876.blurb: World War II: The Royal Air Force sink the German battleship Tirpitz, moored off Tromsø, Norway.

Q7096909.name: Operation Coburg
Q7096909.blurb: Vietnam War: The 1st Australian Task Force launches Operation Coburg against the North Vietnamese Army and Viet Cong during wider fighting around Long Bình and Biên Hòa.

Q7096915.name: Operation Collar
Q7096915.blurb: World War II: Operation Collar, the first British Commando raid on occupied France, by No 11 Independent Company.

Q7096923.name: Operation Commando Hunt
Q7096923.blurb: Vietnam War: Operation Commando Hunt initiated. The goal is to interdict men and supplies on the Ho Chi Minh trail, through Laos into South Vietnam.

Q7096964.name: Operation Deckhouse Five
Q7096964.blurb: Vietnam War: United States Marine Corps and ARVN troops launch "Operation Deckhouse Five" in the Mekong River delta.

Q7097061.name: Operation Freedom Deal
Q7097061.blurb: Vietnam War: The US Air Force bombing of Cambodia ends.

Q7097151.name: Operation Hump
Q7097151.blurb: The 173rd Airborne is ambushed by over 1,200 Viet Cong in Operation Hump during the Vietnam War, while the 1st Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment fight one of the first set-piece engagements of the war between Australian forces and the Viet Cong at the Battle of Gang Toi.

Q7097188.name: Operation Jefferson Glenn
