Q7097188.blurb: Vietnam War: Operation Jefferson Glenn begins: The United States 101st Airborne Division and the South Vietnamese 1st Infantry Division initiate a new operation in Thừa Thiên–Huế Province.

Q7097223.name: Operation Leader
Q7097223.blurb: World War II: Allied forces executed Operation Leader, an air raid against German shipping near Bodø, Norway.

Q7097347.name: Operation OAU
Q7097347.blurb: Operation OAU begins during the Nigerian Civil War.

Q7097380.name: Operation Pawan
Q7097380.blurb: Start of Operation Pawan by Indian forces in Sri Lanka. Thousands of civilians, insurgents, soldiers die.

Q7097605.name: Operation Swift
Q7097605.blurb: Vietnam War: Operation Swift begins when U.S. Marines engage the North Vietnamese in battle in the Que Son Valley.

Q7097661.name: Operation Truong Cong Dinh
Q7097661.blurb: Vietnam War: The United States and South Vietnam began Operation Truong Cong Dinh to sweep the area surrounding the Mekong Delta town of Mỹ Tho to root out Viet Cong forces in the area.

Q7097691.name: Operation Whirlwind
Q7097691.blurb: Croatian War of Independence: The Croatian Army retreated after the failure of Operation Whirlwind, destroying their tanks to avoid their capture.

Q7098557.name: Oppenheimer security hearing
Q7098557.blurb: The security clearance of American nuclear physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer, head of Project Y, was revoked.

Q7098695.name: Grand Ole Opry
aliases: List of Grand Ole Opry broadcasts
Q7098695.blurb: The Grand Ole Opry begins broadcasting in Nashville, Tennessee, as the WSM Barn Dance.

Q7099791.name: Orangeburg massacre
Q7099791.blurb: American civil rights movement: An attack on Black students from South Carolina State University who are protesting racial segregation leaves three dead and 28 injured in Orangeburg, South Carolina.

Q7116630.name: Ozone Disco Club fire
Q7116630.blurb: A nightclub fire in Quezon City, Philippines kills 162 people.

Q7119310.name: PIA Flight 688
Q7119310.blurb: A Pakistan International Airlines Fokker F27 Friendship crashes near Multan International Airport, killing all 45 people on board.

Q7119313.name: PIA Flight 740
Q7119313.blurb: Pakistan International Airlines Flight 740 crashes near Taif in Mecca Province, Saudi Arabia, killing all 156 people on board.

Q7120079.name: PP-VLU
Q7120079.blurb: Varig Flight 967 disappeared shortly after takeoff from Tokyo's Narita International Airport en route to Rio de Janeiro.

Q7122767.name: Pacific Western Airlines Flight 314
Q7122767.blurb: Pacific Western Airlines Flight 314 crashes at the Cranbrook/Canadian Rockies International Airport in Cranbrook, British Columbia, Canada with 42 deaths and seven survivors.

Q7123099.name: Pacoima aircraft accident
Q7123099.blurb: Eight people (five total crew from two aircraft and three on the ground) in Pacoima, California are killed following the mid-air collision between a Douglas DC-7 airliner and a Northrop F-89 Scorpion fighter jet.

Q7123142.name: Pactum Sicardi
Q7123142.blurb: Pactum Sicardi, a peace treaty between the Principality of Benevento and the Duchy of Naples, is signed.

Q7126013.name: Jacquerie
Q7126013.blurb: Battle of Mello: The peasant forces of the Jacquerie are crushed by the army of the French nobility.

Q7126582.name: Palair Macedonian Airlines Flight 301
Q7126582.blurb: Palair Macedonian Airlines Flight 301 crashes at Skopje International Airport in Petrovec, North Macedonia, killing 83.

Q7129567.name: Pan Am Flight 526A
Q7129567.blurb: Pan Am Flight 526A ditches near San Juan-Isla Grande Airport in San Juan, Puerto Rico, after experiencing an engine failure, killing 52 people.

Q7129570.name: Pan Am Flight 7
Q7129570.blurb: Pan Am Flight 7 disappears between San Francisco and Honolulu. Wreckage and bodies are discovered a week later.

Q7129571.name: Pan Am Flight 806
Q7129571.blurb: Pan Am Flight 806 crashes near Pago Pago International Airport in American Samoa, killing 97.

Q7129572.name: Pan Am Flight 812
Q7129572.blurb: Pan Am Flight 812 crashes on approach to Ngurah Rai International Airport in Denpasar, Bali, Indonesia, killing all 107 people on board.

Q7129574.name: Pan Am Flight 845/26
Q7129574.blurb: Pan Am Flight 845/26 ditches in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Oregon, killing four.

Q7129575.name: Pan Am Flight 830
Q7129575.blurb: A bomb explodes on Pan Am Flight 830, en route from Tokyo, Japan to Honolulu, Hawaii, killing one passenger and injuring 15 others.

Q7129577.name: Pan Am Flight 816
Q7129577.blurb: Pan Am Flight 816 crashes after takeoff from Faa'a International Airport in Papeete, French Polynesia, killing 78.

Q7129990.name: 1999 Panamanian general election
Q7129990.blurb: Panamanian general election: Mireya Moscoso becomes the first woman to be elected President of Panama.

Q7132440.name: 1669–70 papal conclave
Q7132440.blurb: Emilio Altieri is elected pope after a four-month conclave and takes the name Clement X.

Q7138897.name: Parliament (Qualification of Women) Act 1918
Q7138897.blurb: The Parliament (Qualification of Women) Act 1918 is passed, allowing women to stand for Parliament in the UK.

Q7148890.name: PauknAir Flight 4101
Q7148890.blurb: PauknAir Flight 4101, a British Aerospace 146, crashes near Melilla Airport in Melilla, Spain, killing 38 people.

Q7154829.name: Paulet Affair
Q7154829.blurb: Lord George Paulet occupies the Kingdom of Hawaii in the name of Great Britain in the Paulet affair.

Q7160186.name: Peekskill Riots
Q7160186.blurb: Paul Robeson performs a second concert in Peekskill, New York eight days after the Peekskill riots.

Q7165608.name: crackdown on Tiananmen Square protests of 1989
Q7165608.blurb: The 1989 Tiananmen Square protests are suppressed in Beijing by the People's Liberation Army, with between 241 and 10,000 dead (an unofficial estimate).

Q7170213.name: Persian Gulf campaign of 1809
Q7170213.blurb: A British flotilla arrived at Ras Al Khaimah and launched an amphibious assault on the town, as a part of the Persian Gulf campaign of 1809.

Q7184945.name: Philippine Airlines Flight 158
Q7184945.blurb: Philippine Air Lines Flight 158 crashes in Antipolo, near Manila International Airport in the Philippines, killing 45 people.

Q7185387.name: Philippine resistance against Japan
Q7185387.blurb: Philippine resistance against Japan: Cebuano fishermen discovered the Koga papers after a plane crash killed Admiral Mineichi Koga, commander-in-chief of the Imperial Japanese Navy's Combined Fleet.

Q7185401.name: Philippine women suffrage plebiscite, 1937
Q7185401.blurb: The Commonwealth of the Philippines holds a plebiscite for Filipino women on whether they should be extended the right to suffrage; over 90% would vote in the affirmative.

Q7185896.name: Phillips Disaster of 1989
Q7185896.blurb: An explosion at the Houston Chemical Complex in Pasadena, Texas, which registered a 3.5 on the Richter magnitude scale, kills 23 and injures 314.

Q7185949.name: Phillips explosion of 2000
Q7185949.blurb: A Phillips Petroleum plant explosion in Pasadena, Texas kills one person and injures 71 others.

Q7191299.name: Pidjiguiti massacre
Q7191299.blurb: Portugal's state police force PIDE fires upon striking workers in Bissau, Portuguese Guinea, killing over 50 people.

Q7191488.name: Piedmont Airlines Flight 22
Q7191488.blurb: Piedmont Airlines Flight 22, a Piedmont Airlines Boeing 727-22, and a twin-engine Cessna 310 collide over Hendersonville, North Carolina, USA. Both aircraft are destroyed and all passengers and crew are killed, including John T. McNaughton, an advisor to Robert McNamara.

Q7191489.name: Piedmont Airlines Flight 349
Q7191489.blurb: Piedmont Airlines Flight 349 crashes on approach to Charlottesville–Albemarle Airport in Albemarle County, Virginia, killing 26 of the 27 on board.

Q7193689.name: Pikku Kakkonen
Q7193689.blurb: The first episode of Finnish children's TV show Pikku Kakkonen ("Little Number Two") is aired on Yle TV2.

Q7195930.name: Pink's War
Q7195930.blurb: The Royal Air Force began a bombardment and strafing campaign against the mountain strongholds of Mahsud tribesmen in South Waziristan, present-day Pakistan.

Q7199283.name: Pittsburgh flood of 1936
aliases: The Great St. Patrick’s Day flood
Q7199283.blurb: Warmer-than-normal temperatures rapidly melt snow and ice on the upper Allegheny and Monongahela rivers, leading to a major flood in Pittsburgh.

Q7200933.name: Plan of Tuxtepec
Q7200933.blurb: The Plan of Tuxtepec is announced.

Q7205859.name: 1919 Plymouth Sutton by-election
Q7205859.blurb: Nancy Astor becomes the first woman to speak in the House of Commons of the United Kingdom following her election as a Member of Parliament (MP) three months earlier.

Q7211121.name: Esing Bakery incident
Q7211121.blurb: In British Hong Kong, hundreds of Europeans were non-lethally poisoned by arsenic in bread from a locally owned bakery, leading to geopolitical tension.

Q7225532.name: Poll Tax Riots
Q7225532.blurb: Approximately 200,000 protesters take to the streets of London to protest against the newly introduced Poll Tax.

Q7232803.name: Portuguese transition to democracy
Q7232803.blurb: Coup of 25 November 1975, a failed military coup d'état by Portuguese far-left activists seeking to hijack the  Portuguese transition to democracy to establish a communist regime.

Q7234526.name: Postville Raid
Q7234526.blurb: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement conducts the largest-ever raid of a workplace in Postville, Iowa, arresting nearly 400 immigrants for identity theft and document fraud.

Q7237681.name: Prague Party Conference
aliases: 6th All-Russian Conference of the Russian Social Democratic Labour Party
Q7237681.blurb: The sixth All-Russian Conference of the Russian Social Democratic Labour Party (Prague Party Conference) opens. In the course of the conference, Vladimir Lenin and his supporters break from the rest of the party to form the Bolshevik movement.

Q7240397.name: premiership of Margaret Thatcher
Q7240397.blurb: British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher withdraws from the Conservative Party leadership election, confirming the end of her Premiership.

Q7240401.name: Premiership of Stephen Harper
Q7240401.blurb: Stephen Harper becomes Prime Minister of Canada.

Q7241106.name: presidency of Richard Nixon
Q7241106.blurb: Watergate scandal: Five White House operatives are arrested for burgling the offices of the Democratic National Committee during an attempt by members of the administration of President Richard M. Nixon to illegally wiretap the political opposition as part of a broader campaign to subvert the democratic process.

Q7242056.name: Prestonsburg, Kentucky bus disaster
Q7242056.blurb: A school bus in Floyd County, Kentucky hits a wrecker truck and plunges down an embankment into the rain-swollen Levisa Fork river. The driver and 26 children die in one of the worst school bus accidents in U.S. history.

Q7242180.name: Pretoria Pit Disaster
Q7242180.blurb: An underground explosion at the Hulton Bank Colliery No. 3 Pit in Over Hulton, Westhoughton, England, kills 344 miners.

Q7247423.name: Proclamation 2714
Q7247423.blurb: President Harry S. Truman officially proclaims the end of hostilities in World War II.

Q7248975.name: Project 571
Q7248975.blurb: Following a failed coup attempt, Mao Zedong's second-in-command Lin Biao died in a plane crash while attempting to flee China.

Q7257331.name: Public Broadcasting Act of 1967
Q7257331.blurb: US President Lyndon B. Johnson signs the Public Broadcasting Act of 1967, establishing the Corporation for Public Broadcasting.

Q7258596.name: Puerto Rico campaign
Q7258596.blurb: Spanish–American War: After more than two months of sea-based bombardment, the United States invaded Puerto Rico.

Q7261005.name: Purdue Wreck
Q7261005.blurb: The Purdue Wreck, a railroad train collision in Indianapolis, kills 17 people, including 14 players of the Purdue University football team.

Q7263697.name: Italian campaigns of the French Revolutionary Wars
Q7263697.blurb: The Battle of Castiglione in Napoleon's first Italian campaigns of the French Revolutionary Wars results in a French victory.

Q7266508.name: Qantas Flight 1
Q7266508.blurb: Qantas Flight 1 overruns a runway in Bangkok during a storm, causing minor injuries to some passengers.

Q7267836.name: Qinghe Special Steel Corporation disaster
Q7267836.blurb: A ladle spilled 30 tonnes (33 tons) of molten steel in a factory in Liaoning, China, killing 32 workers.

Q7269864.name: Quebecair Flight 255
Q7269864.blurb: Quebecair Flight 255 crashes after takeoff from Québec City Jean Lesage International Airport in Quebec City, killing 17.

Q7270522.name: Queen Street massacre
Q7270522.blurb: A man shot and killed eight people at the Australia Post building in Melbourne, before jumping to his death.

Q7272294.name: Quinn brothers' killings
Q7272294.blurb: The Ulster Volunteer Force attack a house in Ballymoney, County Antrim, Northern Ireland with a petrol bomb, killing the Quinn brothers.

Q7278301.name: R v Penguin Books Ltd.
Q7278301.blurb: Penguin Books is found not guilty of obscenity in the trial R v Penguin Books Ltd, the Lady Chatterley's Lover case.

Q7283728.name: Raid of the Redeswire
Q7283728.blurb: The Raid of the Redeswire is the last major battle between England and Scotland.

Q7283740.name: Raid on Dunkirk
Q7283740.blurb: War of the Second Coalition: The British Royal Navy force attacked the well-defended French anchorage of Dunkirk (depicted), capturing a French frigate.

Q7283751.name: Raid on Lunenburg, Nova Scotia
Q7283751.blurb: Raid on Lunenburg: American privateers attack the British settlement of Lunenburg, Nova Scotia.

Q7293530.name: Ruhollah Khomeini's return to Iran
Q7293530.blurb: Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini returned from exile and soon led the Iranian Revolution to overthrow the Pahlavi dynasty.

Q7294648.name: Ras Burqa massacre
Q7294648.blurb: Seven Israeli vacationers, including four children, are killed in a mass shooting at Ras Burqa in the Sinai Peninsula by an Egyptian soldier.

Q7301548.name: Reassertion of British sovereignty over the Falkland Islands
aliases: British occupation of the Falkland Islands
Q7301548.blurb: Captain James Onslow, in the Clio, reasserts British sovereignty over the Falkland Islands.

Q7301565.name: Reavey and O'Dowd killings
Q7301565.blurb: The Troubles: In response to the killings of six Catholics the previous night, South Armagh Republican Action Force gunmen killed ten Protestants in County Armagh, Northern Ireland.

Q7302105.name: Rebellion of Cao Qin
Q7302105.blurb: Ming Chinese general Cao Qin staged a failed coup against the Tianshun Emperor.

Q7308456.name: Regina Cyclone
Q7308456.blurb: The Regina Cyclone, Canada's deadliest tornado event, kills 28 people in Regina, Saskatchewan.

Q7311736.name: Remembrance Day bombing
Q7311736.blurb: Remembrance Day bombing: A Provisional IRA bomb explodes in Enniskillen, Northern Ireland during a ceremony honouring those who had died in wars involving British forces. Twelve people are killed and sixty-three wounded.

Q7312198.name: Removal of Hungary's border fence
Q7312198.blurb: Cold War: Hungary begins dismantling its border fence with Austria, which allows a number of East Germans to defect.

Q7312201.name: Removal of the Stone of Scone in 1950
aliases: 1950 removal of the Stone of Scone
Q7312201.blurb: The Stone of Scone, removed months earlier by Scottish students, was found on the altar of Arbroath Abbey.

Q7314469.name: Georgia in the American Civil War
Q7314469.blurb: American Civil War: Union General William Tecumseh Sherman begins his March to the Sea through Georgia towards the city of Savannah.

Q7316936.name: rehabilitation trial of Joan of Arc
Q7316936.blurb: A retrial verdict acquits Joan of Arc of heresy 25 years after her execution.

Q7321053.name: Rhodesia's Unilateral Declaration of Independence
Q7321053.blurb: Southern Rhodesia's Prime Minister Ian Smith unilaterally declares the colony independent as the unrecognised state of Rhodesia.

Q7330727.name: Richmond explosion
Q7330727.blurb: In the downtown district of Richmond, Indiana, a double explosion kills 41 and injures 150.

Q7332264.name: Rico Linhas Aéreas Flight 4815
Q7332264.blurb: Rico Linhas Aéreas Flight 4815 crashes into the Amazon rainforest during approach to Eduardo Gomes International Airport in Manaus, Brazil, killing 33 people.

Q7332265.name: Rico Linhas Aéreas Flight 4823
Q7332265.blurb: Rico Linhas Aéreas Flight 4823 crashes on approach to Rio Branco International Airport, killing 23 of the 31 people on board.

Q7333843.name: death of Rigoberto Alpizar
Q7333843.blurb: Rigoberto Alpizar, a passenger on American Airlines Flight 924 who allegedly claimed to have a bomb, is shot and killed by a team of U.S. federal air marshals at Miami International Airport.

Q7339072.name: Rizal Day bombings
Q7339072.blurb: Rizal Day bombings: A series of bombs explode in various places in Metro Manila, Philippines within a period of a few hours, killing 22 and injuring about a hundred.

Q7357049.name: Rodney Riots
Q7357049.blurb: Kingston, Jamaica is rocked by the Rodney riots, inspired by the barring of Walter Rodney from the country.

Q7362078.name: 1974 Mitsubishi heavy industries explosion incident
Q7362078.blurb: A powerful bomb explodes at the Mitsubishi Heavy Industries headquarters in Marunouchi, Tokyo. Eight are killed, 378 are injured. Eight left-wing activists are arrested on May 19, 1975, by Japanese authorities.

Q7366802.name: Roquebert's Expedition to the Caribbean
Q7366802.blurb: Napoleonic Wars: While transporting supplies to Guadeloupe, French commodore François

Q7369575.name: Ross Perot presidential campaign, 1992
Q7369575.blurb: Appearing on the talk show Larry King Live, U.S. industrialist Ross Perot announced that he would begin a presidential campaign if "ordinary people" wanted him to run for office.

Q7370452.name: Rotherham child sexual exploitation scandal
Q7370452.blurb: The Jay Report into the Rotherham child sexual exploitation scandal is published.

Q7373628.name: Royal Air Maroc Flight 630
Q7373628.blurb: Royal Air Maroc Flight 630 crashes in Douar Izounine, Morocco, killing all 44 people on board.

Q7373856.name: Royal Brunei Airlines Flight 238
Q7373856.blurb: Royal Brunei Airlines Flight 839 crashes in the Lambir Hills National Park while on approach to Miri Airport in Malaysia, killing 10.

Q7375105.name: Royalist attack on Chaves
Q7375105.blurb: Henrique Mitchell de Paiva Couceiro leads an unsuccessful royalist attack against the First Portuguese Republic in Chaves.

Q7375127.name: Royalton Raid
Q7375127.blurb: American Revolutionary War: The British-led Royalton raid is the last Native American raid on New England.

Q7376831.name: Rudd Concession
Q7376831.blurb: The Rudd Concession is granted by Matabeleland to agents of Cecil Rhodes.

Q7388498.name: SAETA Flight 232
Q7388498.blurb: SAETA Flight 011 crashes into the Chimborazo volcano in Ecuador, killing all 59 people on board; the wreckage is not discovered until 2002.

Q7388641.name: SAM Colombia Flight 501
Q7388641.blurb: SAM Colombia Flight 501 crashes on approach to José María Córdova International Airport in Medellín, Colombia, killing 132.

Q7388896.name: SA de Transport Aérien Flight 730
Q7388896.blurb: SA de Transport Aérien Flight 730 crashes near Madeira Airport in Funchal, Madeira, Portugal, killing 36.

Q7395297.name: SY Aurora's drift
Q7395297.blurb: Imperial Trans-Antarctic Expedition: The SY Aurora breaks loose from its anchorage during a gale, beginning a 312-day ordeal.

Q7395672.name: Saar Statute referendum, 1955
Q7395672.blurb: The people of the Saar region vote in a referendum to unite with West Germany instead of France.

Q7396805.name: Sack of Aquileia
Q7396805.blurb: Sack of Aquileia: After an earlier defeat on the Catalaunian Plains, Attila lays siege to the metropolis of Aquileia and eventually destroys it.

Q7401401.name: Saint James Church massacre
Q7401401.blurb: The Saint James Church massacre occurs in Kenilworth, Cape Town, South Africa.

Q7403376.name: Salad Bowl strike
Q7403376.blurb: Organized by Mexican American labor union leader César Chávez, the Salad Bowl strike, the largest farm worker strike in U.S. history, begins.

Q7404255.name: Salem witchcraft trial
Q7404255.blurb: The last witchcraft trial held in the United States begins in Salem, Massachusetts, after Lucretia Brown, an adherent of Christian Science, accused Daniel Spofford of attempting to harm her through his mental powers.

Q7406521.name: 1991 Salvadoran legislative election
Q7406521.blurb: 1991 Salvadoran legislative election: The Nationalist Republican Alliance wins 39 of the 84 seats in the Legislative Assembly of El Salvador.

Q7413450.name: San Bernardino train disaster
Q7413450.blurb: The San Bernardino train disaster kills four people, only to be followed a week later by an underground gasoline pipeline explosion, which kills two more people.

Q7414139.name: San Francisco Zoo tiger attacks
Q7414139.blurb: A Siberian tiger named Tatania escapes her exhibit at the San Francisco Zoo and attacks three people, killing one and injuring two more.

Q7414187.name: San Francisco plague of 1900–1904
Q7414187.blurb: A Chinese immigrant in San Francisco falls ill to bubonic plague in the first plague epidemic in the continental United States.

Q7424558.name: expulsion of the Jews from the territories of the Crowns of Castile and Aragon
aliases: Expulsion of the Jews from Spain in the year 1492
The Expulsion of the Jews from Spain in the year 1492
expulsion of Jews from the territories of the Crowns of Castile and Aragon
expulsion of the Jews from Spain
Q7424558.blurb: The Crown's decision to expel the Jews is announced in Zaragoza, Aragon, to the kingdom's procurators.

Q7429941.name: Scandinavian Airlines System Flight 871
Q7429941.blurb: Scandinavian Airlines System Flight 871 crashes near Ankara Esenboğa Airport in Turkey, killing all 42 aboard.

Q7433311.name: Schäffer affair
Q7433311.blurb: Unsuccessful in his attempt to conquer the Kingdom of Hawaiʻi for the Russian-American Company, Georg Anton Schäffer is forced to admit defeat and leave Kauaʻi.

Q7434245.name: Scofield Mine disaster
Q7434245.blurb: The Scofield Mine disaster kills over 200 men in Scofield, Utah in what is to date the fifth-worst mining accident in United States history.

Q7441665.name: Search for a Star
Q7441665.blurb: The Filipino singer Rachelle Ann Go won the reality talent show Search for a Star, performing a cover of Mariah Carey's "Through the Rain" in the grand final.

Q7441977.name: Seat of Government Surrender Act 1909
Q7441977.blurb: New South Wales Premier Charles Wade signs the Seat of Government Surrender Act 1909, formally completing the transfer of State land to the Commonwealth to create the Australian Capital Territory.

Q7443069.name: Second Battle of Anandpur
Q7443069.blurb: Second Battle of Anandpur: In the Second Battle of Anandpur, Aurangzeb's two generals, Wazir Khan and Zaberdast Khan executed two children of Guru Gobind Singh, Zorawar Singh aged eight and Fateh Singh aged five, by burying them alive into a wall.

Q7443076.name: Second Battle of Caloocan
Q7443076.blurb: Filipino forces led by General Antonio Luna launch counterattacks for the first time against the American forces during the Philippine–American War. The Filipinos fail to regain Manila from the Americans.

Q7443093.name: Second Battle of Fort Fisher
Q7443093.blurb: American Civil War: The Union Army captured Fort Fisher, the last seaport of the Confederacy.

Q7443116.name: Second Battle of Rivas
Q7443116.blurb: Second Battle of Rivas: Juan Santamaría burns down the hostel where William Walker's filibusters are holed up.

Q7443118.name: Second Battle of Tijuana
Q7443118.blurb: Mexican Revolution: Government forces bring an end to the Magonista rebellion of 1911 in the Second Battle of Tijuana.

Q7443327.name: Second Great Fire of London
Q7443327.blurb: World War II:  in the Second Great Fire of London, the Luftwaffe fire-bombs London, England, killing almost 200 civilians.

Q7443435.name: Second National March on Washington for Lesbian and Gay Rights
Q7443435.blurb: An estimated 750,000 people attended the "Great March" in Washington, D.C., to demand greater civil rights for the LGBT community.

Q7443488.name: Second Raid on Schweinfurt
Q7443488.blurb: World War II: During the second raid on Schweinfurt, the U.S. 8th Air Force suffered so many losses that it lost air supremacy over Germany for several months.

Q7443727.name: second inauguration of William McKinley
Q7443727.blurb: William McKinley is inaugurated President of the United States for the second time; Theodore Roosevelt is vice president.

Q7445004.name: Security Treaty Between the United States and Japan
aliases: Nipponkoku to Amerikagasshūkoku to no aida no anzen hoshōjōyaku
Q7445004.blurb: The US Senate ratifies the Security Treaty between the United States and Japan.

Q7446412.name: Seguro Obrero massacre
Q7446412.blurb: Chile: A group of youths affiliated with the fascist National Socialist Movement of Chile are executed after surrendering during a failed coup.

Q7447497.name: Selarang Barracks Incident
Q7447497.blurb: British and Australian prisoners of war in Singapore revolted against their Japanese captors, who required them to pledge not to escape.

Q7450869.name: Sennichi Department Store Building fire
Q7450869.blurb: A fire occurs in the Sennichi Department Store in Osaka, Japan. Blocked exits and non-functional elevators result in 118 fatalities (many victims leaping to their deaths).

Q7451679.name: Seoul National University Hospital Massacre
Q7451679.blurb: Korean War: The Korean People's Army kills almost a thousand doctors, nurses, inpatient civilians and wounded soldiers in the Seoul National University Hospital massacre.

Q7452110.name: September 1964 South Vietnamese coup attempt
Q7452110.blurb: Charges in a military court against generals Dương Văn Đức and Lâm Văn Phát of leading a coup attempt against South Vietnamese leader Nguyễn Khánh, were dropped..

Q7452125.name: September 1988 Haitian coup d'état
Q7452125.blurb: General Henri Namphy, president of Haiti, is ousted from power in a coup d'état led by General Prosper Avril.

Q7452181.name: September 2012 southern Israel cross-border attack
Q7452181.blurb: Three Egyptian militants open fire on a group of Israeli soldiers in a southern Israel cross-border attack.

Q7453539.name: Bek Air Flight 2100
Q7453539.blurb: Bek Air Flight 2100 crashes during takeoff from Almaty International Airport in Almaty, Kazakhstan, killing 13.

Q7491256.name: Shawinigan Handshake
Q7491256.blurb: Then-Prime Minister of Canada Jean Chrétien applies a chokehold to protester Bill Clennett, an incident later named the Shawinigan Handshake.

Q7493668.name: Shell House massacre
Q7493668.blurb: In South Africa, African National Congress security guards kill dozens of Inkatha Freedom Party protesters.

Q7499101.name: Shishou incident
Q7499101.blurb: Mass riots involving over 10,000 people and 10,000 police officers break out in Shishou, China, over the dubious circumstances surrounding the death of a local chef.

Q7501758.name: Short Creek raid
Q7501758.blurb: In Short Creek, Arizona, police conducted a mass arrest of approximately 400 Mormon fundamentalists for polygamy.

Q7502395.name: Shot Heard 'Round the World
Q7502395.blurb: In Major League Baseball, the New York Giants' Bobby Thomson hit the "Shot Heard 'Round the World", a game-winning home run, to win the National League pennant.

Q7506756.name: Siamese revolution of 1688
Q7506756.blurb: King Narai nominates Phetracha as regent, leading to the revolution of 1688 in which Phetracha becomes king of the Ayutthaya Kingdom.

Q7507785.name: Sid El-Antri massacre
Q7507785.blurb: The Sid El-Antri massacre in Algeria kills between 50 and 100 people.

Q7508662.name: Battle of Sidi Barrani
Q7508662.blurb: World War II: Operation Compass: British and Indian troops under the command of Major-General Richard O'Connor attack Italian forces near Sidi Barrani in Egypt.

Q7509911.name: Siege of Catubig
Q7509911.blurb: Philippine–American War: Filipino guerrillas launch a surprise attack on U.S. infantry and begin a four-day siege of Catubig, Philippines.

Q7509935.name: Siege of Château Gaillard
Q7509935.blurb: The Siege of Château Gaillard ends in a French victory over King John of England, who loses control of Normandy to King Philip II Augustus.

Q7509956.name: Invasion of Curaçao
Q7509956.blurb: War of the Second Coalition: Britain takes control of the Dutch colony of Curaçao.

Q7509987.name: Siege of Dunlap's Station
Q7509987.blurb: The Siege of Dunlap's Station begins near Cincinnati during the Northwest Indian War.

Q7510006.name: Siege of Fort Erie
Q7510006.blurb: War of 1812: The ultimately unsuccessful Siege of Fort Erie begins as British forces attempt to recapture the fort and drive American forces out of Canada.

Q7510011.name: Siege of Fort Harrison
Q7510011.blurb: War of 1812: The Siege of Fort Harrison begins when the fort is set on fire.

Q7510016.name: Siege of Fort Morgan
Q7510016.blurb: American Civil War: The Union Navy captures Fort Morgan, Alabama, thus breaking Confederate dominance of all ports on the Gulf of Mexico except Galveston, Texas.

Q7510020.name: Siege of Fort Mose
Q7510020.blurb: A combined force of Spanish, free blacks and allied Indians defeat a British garrison at the Siege of Fort Mose near St. Augustine during the War of Jenkins' Ear.

Q7510022.name: Siege of Fort Recovery
Q7510022.blurb: Northwest Indian War: Native American forces under Blue Jacket attack Fort Recovery.

Q7510027.name: Siege of Fort Stanwix
Q7510027.blurb: British forces abandon the Siege of Fort Stanwix after hearing rumors of Continental Army reinforcements.

Q7510052.name: Siege of Godesberg
Q7510052.blurb: The Siege of Godes­berg, the first major siege of the Cologne War, began.

Q7510105.name: Siege of Inverness
Q7510105.blurb: Jacobite rising of 1745: The siege of Inverness ended with British forces surrendering to the Jacobite army.

Q7510143.name: Siege of Kamakura
Q7510143.blurb: Genkō War: Forces loyal to Emperor Go-Daigo seize Tōshō-ji during the Siege of Kamakura. Hōjō Takatoki and other members of the Hōjō clan commit suicide, ending the rule of the Kamakura shogunate.

Q7510178.name: Siege of La Charité
Q7510178.blurb: Hundred Years' War: Joan of Arc unsuccessfully besieges La Charité.

Q7510255.name: Siege of Multan
Q7510255.blurb: Second Anglo-Sikh War: The Siege of Multan ends after nine months when the last Sikh defenders of Multan, Punjab, surrender.

Q7510313.name: Siege of Plei Me
Q7510313.blurb: Vietnam War: The Siege of Plei Me began with the first major confrontation between soldiers of the North Vietnamese Army and the U.S. Army.

Q7510328.name: Siege of Prague
Q7510328.blurb: Third Silesian War: The Austrian victory at the Battle of Kolín forced Prussian leader Frederick the Great to give up the Siege of Prague and retreat to Saxony.

Q7510378.name: Siege of Santo Domingo
Q7510378.blurb: The Siege of Santo Domingo begins during the Anglo-Spanish War, and fails seven days later.

Q7510387.name: Siege of Schenkenschans
Q7510387.blurb: Eighty Years' War: The Spanish capture the strategic Dutch fortress of Schenkenschans.

Q7510393.name: Siege of Seville
Q7510393.blurb: Conquest of Seville by Christian troops under King Ferdinand III of Castile.

Q7510412.name: Siege of Smerwick
Q7510412.blurb: Second Desmond Rebellion: The Siege of Smerwick ends with the Catholic garrison surrendering to the English forces under Arthur Grey. The majority of the garrison is massacred the next day.

Q7510414.name: Siege of Smolensk
Q7510414.blurb: Smolensk War: Forces from the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth broke the Russian siege of Smolensk (depicted).

Q7510533.name: Siege of the Alamo
Q7510533.blurb: Texas Revolution: The Siege of the Alamo (prelude to the Battle of the Alamo) begins in San Antonio, Texas.

Q7510538.name: Siege of the British Residency in Kabul
Q7510538.blurb: Siege of the British Residency in Kabul: British envoy Sir Louis Cavagnari and 72 men of the Guides are massacred by Afghan troops while defending the British Residency in Kabul. Their heroism and loyalty became famous and revered throughout the British Empire.

Q7512984.name: signing of the United States Declaration of Independence
Q7512984.blurb: American Revolution: The signing of the United States Declaration of Independence by the Second Continental Congress takes place.

Q7514632.name: Silent Parade
Q7514632.blurb: Anti-lynching movement: The Silent Parade takes place in New York City, in protest against murders, lynchings, and other violence directed towards African Americans.

Q7516094.name: Silver Jubilee of Queen Elizabeth II
Q7516094.blurb: Five hundred million people watch the high day of the Silver Jubilee of Queen Elizabeth II begin on television.

Q7522918.name: Singapore cable car crash
Q7522918.blurb: Singapore cable car crash: Panamanian-registered oil rig, Eniwetok, strikes the cables of the Singapore Cable Car system linking the mainland and Sentosa Island, causing two cabins to fall into the water and killing seven people and leaving thirteen others trapped for hours.

Q7524594.name: Sinking of HMS Peacock
Q7524594.blurb: Sinking of HMS Peacock by USS Hornet on the Demerara River, Guyana.

Q7525051.name: Sinsinawa Mound raid
Q7525051.blurb: Black Hawk War: Three men working in a cornfield were attacked by Sauk Native Americans, resulting in two deaths.

Q7539172.name: Slave Trade Act of 1794
Q7539172.blurb: The Slave Trade Act of 1794 bans the export of slaves from the United States, and prohibits American citizens from outfitting a ship for the purpose of importing slaves.

Q7545227.name: Smith Mine disaster
Q7545227.blurb: The Smith Mine #3 in Bearcreek, Montana, explodes, killing 74 men.

Q7550813.name: Social Security Act
Q7550813.blurb: Franklin D. Roosevelt signs the Social Security Act, creating a government pension system for the retired.

Q7556539.name: solar eclipse of May 3, 1715
Q7556539.blurb: A total solar eclipse is visible across northern Europe and northern Asia, as predicted by Edmond Halley to within four minutes accuracy.

Q7559133.name: Somali Airlines Flight 40
Q7559133.blurb: Somali Airlines Flight 40 crashes in Balad, Somalia, killing 50 people.

Q7563178.name: 1993 Sopore massacre
Q7563178.blurb: Indian Border Security Force units kill 55 Kashmiri civilians in Sopore, Jammu and Kashmir, in revenge after militants ambushed a BSF patrol.

Q7565425.name: South African Airways Flight 228
Q7565425.blurb: South African Airways Flight 228 crashes near J.G. Strijdom Airport in South West Africa (now Hosea Kutako International Airport in Namibia), killing 123 people.

Q7565818.name: South African apartheid referendum, 1992
Q7565818.blurb: A referendum to end apartheid in South Africa is passed 68.7% to 31.2%.

Q7568082.name: South Ossetian independence referendum, 2006
Q7568082.blurb: Although the Georgian government declared it illegal, South Ossetia held a referendum on independence, with more than 99 percent of voters in favour of preserving the region's status as a de facto independent state.

Q7568743.name: 1959 South Vietnamese parliamentary election
Q7568743.blurb: South Vietnamese opposition figure Phan Quang Dan was elected to the National Assembly despite soldiers being bussed in to vote for President Ngo Dinh Diem's candidate.

Q7568748.name: 1967 South Vietnamese presidential election
Q7568748.blurb: After coming second to Nguyễn Văn Thiệu in a rigged presidential election, Trương Đình Dzu was jailed by a South Vietnamese military court for illicit currency transactions.

Q7568749.name: 1971 South Vietnamese presidential election
Q7568749.blurb: South Vietnamese President Nguyen Van Thieu is re-elected in a one-man election.

Q7569598.name: Southern Airways Flight 49
Q7569598.blurb: Southern Airways Flight 49 from Birmingham, Alabama is hijacked and, at one point, is threatened with crashing into the nuclear installation at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory. After two days, the plane lands in Havana, Cuba, where the hijackers are jailed by Fidel Castro.

Q7569693.name: Southern Bread Riots
Q7569693.blurb: American Civil War: The largest in a series of Southern bread riots occurs in Richmond, Virginia.

Q7570228.name: Southern Ontario Tornado Outbreak of 2005
Q7570228.blurb: Thunderstorms in southern Ontario, Canada, spawned at least three tornadoes that caused over C$500 million in damage.

Q7570428.name: Southern Rhodesian government referendum, 1922
Q7570428.blurb: A referendum in Rhodesia rejects the country's annexation to the South African Union.

Q7570540.name: Southern Television broadcast interruption
Q7570540.blurb: An unidentified hijacker named Vrillon, claiming to be the representative of the "Ashtar Galactic Command", takes over Britain's Southern Television for six minutes, starting at 5:12 pm.

Q7571208.name: Southwest Airlines Flight 1763
Q7571208.blurb: An air rage incident occurs on board Southwest Airlines Flight 1763 when 19-year-old Jonathan Burton attempts to storm the cockpit, but he is subdued by other passengers and dies from his injuries.

Q7573442.name: Spanish attempts to reconquer Mexico
Q7573442.blurb: Spain recognizes the independence of Mexico with the signing of the Santa María–Calatrava Treaty.

Q7578157.name: Spiritwood Incident
Q7578157.blurb: A shootout happens in Spiritwood, Canada, killing two Royal Canadian Mounted Police and wounding a third officer.

Q7604669.name: Statute of Westminster Adoption Act 1942
Q7604669.blurb: Australia's Statute of Westminster Adoption Act 1942 receives royal assent.

Q7604846.name: Stavropolskaya Aktsionernaya Avia Flight 1023
Q7604846.blurb: The tail of a Russian Antonov An-24 charter plane breaks off while en route to Turkey, causing the plane to crash and killing all 50 people on board.

Q7605761.name: Steel strike of 1919
Q7605761.blurb: The steel strike of 1919 ends in failure for the Amalgamated Association of Iron, Steel and Tin Workers labor union.

Q7622106.name: Strathfield massacre
Q7622106.blurb: Strathfield massacre: In Sydney, New South Wales, Australia, taxi driver Wade Frankum shoots and kills seven people and injures six others before turning the gun on himself.

Q7622258.name: Stratton Brothers case
Q7622258.blurb: The trial in the Stratton Brothers case begins in London, England; it marks the first time that fingerprint evidence is used to gain a conviction for murder.

Q7627759.name: Student Strike of 1970
Q7627759.blurb: Vietnam War: A student anti-war strike erupts in response to U.S. and South Vietnamese forces attacking Vietnamese communists in a Cambodian Campaign.

Q7636593.name: Sultan Abdul Halim ferry terminal bridge collapse
Q7636593.blurb: Thirty-two people are killed and 1,674 injured when a bridge at the Sultan Abdul Halim ferry terminal collapses in Butterworth, Penang, Malaysia.

Q7637906.name: Summit Tunnel fire
Q7637906.blurb: The Summit Tunnel fire, one of the largest transportation tunnel fires in history, burns after a freight train carrying over one million liters of gasoline derails near the town of Todmorden, England, in the Pennines.

Q7650334.name: Sutton United 2–1 Coventry City
Q7650334.blurb: Sutton United, a team in the fifth tier of English league football, defeated top-tier Coventry City in one of the biggest upsets in FA Cup history.

Q7650341.name: Sutton Wick air crash
Q7650341.blurb: Sutton Wick air crash: A Blackburn Beverley of 53 Squadron, Royal Air Forces, crashes into the village of Sutton Wick, Berkshire (now Oxfordshire), killing most of the crew and passengers and two local residents.

Q7654539.name: Swedenborgian Church
Q7654539.blurb: The first New Church place of worship the Birmingham New Jerusalem Temple was dedicated on the 19th day of June, 1791, in Birmingham, England. The auspiciousness of this date was noted at the time.

Q7656607.name: swimming at the 1980 Summer Olympics – men's 4 × 100 metre medley relay
aliases: swimming at the 1980 Summer Olympics - men's 4 x 100 metre medley relay
Q7656607.blurb: The Australian swimming team, nicknamed the Quietly Confident Quartet, won the men's 4 × 100 metre medley relay at the Moscow Olympics, the only time that the United States, which boycotted the games, has not won the event at the Olympics.

Q7659034.name: Swissair Flight 316
Q7659034.blurb: Swissair Flight 316 crashes at Ellinikon International Airport in Athens, Greece, killing 14.

Q7659970.name: Sydney Hilton bombing
Q7659970.blurb: Hilton bombing: A bomb explodes in a refuse truck outside the Hilton Hotel in Sydney, Australia, killing two refuse collectors and a policeman.

Q7660108.name: Sydney Riot of 1879
Q7660108.blurb: England's cricket team, led by Lord Harris, is attacked in a riot during a match in Sydney.

Q7660111.name: Sydney River McDonald's murders
Q7660111.blurb: Three employees at a McDonald's Restaurant in Sydney, Nova Scotia, Canada, are brutally murdered and a fourth permanently disabled after a botched robbery. It is the first "fast-food murder" in Canada.

Q7662540.name: Synod of Rome of 963
Q7662540.blurb: Synod of Rome: Emperor Otto I calls a council at St. Peter's Basilica in Rome. Pope John XII is deposed on charges of an armed rebellion against Otto.

Q7667673.name: Sơn Tây Campaign
Q7667673.blurb: Tonkin Campaign: French forces capture the Sơn Tây citadel.

Q7669220.name: TAESA Flight 725
Q7669220.blurb: TAESA Flight 725 crashes after takeoff from Uruapan International Airport in Uruapan, Michoacán, Mexico, killing all 18 people on board.

Q7669292.name: 1983 TAME 737-200 crash
Q7669292.blurb: A TAME airline Boeing 737-200 crashes near Cuenca, Ecuador, killing all 119 passengers and crew on board.

Q7669317.name: TANS Perú Flight 222
Q7669317.blurb: TANS Perú Flight 222 crashes on approach to Chachapoyas Airport in Chachapoyas, Peru, killing 46 people.

Q7672515.name: 1994 St. Louis Airport collision
Q7672515.blurb: A Trans World Airlines McDonnell Douglas MD-80 and Cessna 441 Conquest II aircraft collide on the runway at St. Louis Lambert International Airport in Bridgeton, Missouri, killing two people and injuring eight.

Q7672517.name: TWA Flight 514
Q7672517.blurb: TWA Flight 514, a Boeing 727, crashes northwest of Dulles International Airport, killing all 92 people on board.

Q7672518.name: TWA Flight 529
Q7672518.blurb: TWA Flight 529 crashed shortly after takeoff from Midway Airport in Chicago, killing all 78 people on board. At the time, it was the deadliest single plane disaster in U.S. history.

Q7672520.name: TWA Flight 553
Q7672520.blurb: Trans World Airlines Flight 553 crashes in a field in Concord Township, Ohio, following a mid-air collision with a Beechcraft Baron, killing 26 people.

Q7672521.name: TWA Flight 599
Q7672521.blurb: A Transcontinental & Western Air airliner crashes near Bazaar, Kansas, killing eight, including University of Notre Dame head football coach Knute Rockne.

Q7676655.name: Taiyuan Massacre
Q7676655.blurb: The Governor of Shanxi province in North China orders the execution of 45 foreign Christian missionaries and local church members, including children.

Q7682001.name: Tan-Sahsa Flight 414
Q7682001.blurb: TAN-SAHSA Flight 414 crashed in approach to Toncontín International Airport killing 131 out of 146 people onboard.

Q7687390.name: Tasman Bridge disaster
Q7687390.blurb: The Tasman Bridge in Tasmania, Australia, is struck by the bulk ore carrier Lake Illawarra, killing twelve people.

Q7688846.name: Tauranga campaign
Q7688846.blurb: New Zealand Wars: A British victory against the Māori King Movement brought the Tauranga campaign to an end.

Q7690850.name: Te Kooti's War
Q7690850.blurb: Te Kooti's War: After surviving a five-day siege in the pā at Ngātapa, Māori leader Te Kooti escaped from New Zealand's Armed Constabulary.

Q7705444.name: Tesco bomb campaign
Q7705444.blurb: Robert Edward Dyer was sentenced to 16 years' imprisonment for conducting a six-month-long letter-bomb campaign against the British supermarket chain Tesco.

Q7707777.name: Texas International Airlines Flight 655
Q7707777.blurb: Texas International Airlines Flight 655 crashes into the Black Fork Mountain Wilderness near Mena, Arkansas, killing all 11 people on board.

Q7709135.name: Thai Nguyen uprising
Q7709135.blurb: Vietnamese prison guards led by Trịnh Văn Cấn mutiny at the Thái Nguyên penitentiary against local French authority.

Q7709878.name: Thames Diamond Jubilee Pageant
Q7709878.blurb: The pageant for the Diamond Jubilee of Elizabeth II takes place on the River Thames.

Q7731362.name: Earl of Essex Rebellion
Q7731362.blurb: Robert Devereux, 2nd Earl of Essex, unsuccessfully rebels against Queen Elizabeth I.

Q7738879.name: The Hardest Day
Q7738879.blurb: World War II: The Hardest Day air battle, part of the Battle of Britain, takes place. At that point, it is the largest aerial engagement in history with heavy losses sustained on both sides.

Q7755846.name: The PTL Club
Q7755846.blurb: American televangelist Jim Bakker resigned as the host of The PTL Club in the midst of a sex scandal.

Q7774670.name: The Who concert disaster
aliases: Eleven die at a concert of The Who in Cincinnati
Q7774670.blurb: Eleven people were crushed in a human stampede at a concert by British rock band the Who in Cincinnati, Ohio, U.S.

Q7784779.name: Third Battle of Nanking
Q7784779.blurb: Taiping Rebellion: Third Battle of Nanking: The Qing dynasty finally defeats the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom.

Q7796515.name: Thornton Affair
Q7796515.blurb: Thornton Affair: Open conflict begins over the disputed border of Texas, triggering the Mexican–American War.

Q7802238.name: Tillamook Burn
Q7802238.blurb: Loggers cause a forest fire in the Coast Range of Oregon, later known as the first forest fire of the Tillamook Burn;  destroying 240,000 acres (970 km2) of land.

Q7810218.name: Tītokowaru's War
Q7810218.blurb: The last of Tītokowaru's forces surrender to the New Zealand government, ending his uprising.

Q7811223.name: To my peoples
Q7811223.blurb: World War I: In the culmination of the July Crisis, Austria-Hungary declares war on the Kingdom of Serbia and begins the Great War.

Q7813573.name: Tokhtamysh–Timur War
Q7813573.blurb: Tokhtamysh–Timur war: At the Battle of the Terek River, Timur defeats the army of the Golden Horde, beginning the khanate's permanent military decline.

Q7821460.name: Tonight Starring Jack Paar
Q7821460.blurb: Tonight Starring Jack Paar premieres on NBC with Jack Paar beginning the modern day talk show.

Q7828458.name: Tottenham Outrage
Q7828458.blurb: Two men committed an armed robbery in Tottenham, London, and led police on a two-hour chase, partially by tram, that ended in the perpetrators' suicides.

Q7833286.name: Tran Cao rebellion
Q7833286.blurb: A group of imperial guards, led by Trịnh Duy Sản, murder Emperor Lê Tương Dực and flee, leaving the capital Thăng Long undefended.

Q7833505.name: Trans-Canada Air Lines Flight 810
Q7833505.blurb: Trans-Canada Air Lines Flight 810-9, a Canadair North Star, crashes near Hope, British Columbia, Canada, killing all 62 people on board.

Q7833655.name: Trans Australia Airlines Flight 538
Q7833655.blurb: Trans Australia Airlines Flight 538 crashes near Mackay Airport in Mackay, Queensland, Australia, killing 29.

Q7833750.name: Transair Georgia airliner shootdowns
Q7833750.blurb: A Transair Georgian Airlines Tu-134 is shot down by a missile in the Black Sea near Sokhumi, Georgia.

Q7833816.name: Transbrasil Flight 303
Q7833816.blurb: Transbrasil Flight 303, a Boeing 727, crashes on approach to Hercílio Luz International Airport in Florianópolis, Brazil. Fifty-five out of the 58 people on board are killed.

Q7836981.name: Treaty of Bergerac
Q7836981.blurb: The Treaty of Bergerac is signed between King Henry III of France and the Huguenots.

Q7836985.name: Treaty of Berwick
Q7836985.blurb: The Treaty of Berwick is signed by England and the Lords of the Congregation of Scotland, establishing the terms under which English armed forces were to be permitted in Scotland in order to expel occupying French troops.

Q7837060.name: Treaty of Fort Pitt
Q7837060.blurb: The Treaty of Fort Pitt is signed. It is the first formal treaty between the United States and a Native American tribe.

Q7837100.name: Treaty of Hopewell
Q7837100.blurb: The first Treaty of Hopewell is signed, by which the United States acknowledges Cherokee lands in what is now East Tennessee.

Q7837102.name: Treaty of Jaffa (1192)
Q7837102.blurb: The Treaty of Jaffa is signed between Richard I of England and Saladin, leading to the end of the Third Crusade.

Q7837119.name: Treaty of Lewistown
Q7837119.blurb: The Treaty of Lewistown is signed by the Shawnee and Seneca peoples, exchanging land in Ohio for land west of the Mississippi River.

Q7837128.name: Treaty of Loudun
Q7837128.blurb: Treaty of Loudun ends a French civil war.

Q7837140.name: Treaty of Mangalore
Q7837140.blurb: The signing of the Treaty of Mangalore brings the Second Anglo-Mysore War to an end.

Q7837154.name: Treaty of Montgomery
Q7837154.blurb: The Treaty of Montgomery recognises Llywelyn ap Gruffudd as Prince of Wales, but only as a vassal of King Henry III.

Q7837298.name: Treaty of Westminster (1462)
Q7837298.blurb: The Treaty of Westminster is finalised between Edward IV of England and the Scottish Lord of the Isles.

Q7837318.name: Treaty of the Danish West Indies
Q7837318.blurb: According to the terms of the Treaty of the Danish West Indies, the islands become American possessions.

Q7839971.name: trial of Anders Behring Breivik
Q7839971.blurb: The trial for Anders Behring Breivik, the perpetrator of the 2011 Norway attacks, begins in Oslo, Norway.

Q7839988.name: Trial of Louis Riel
Q7839988.blurb: After a five-day trial following the North-West Rebellion, Louis Riel, a Canadian Métis leader and "Father of Manitoba", was hanged for high treason.

Q7839993.name: trial of Slobodan Milošević
Q7839993.blurb: The trial of Slobodan Milošević, the former President of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, begins at the United Nations International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia in The Hague, Netherlands. He dies four years later before its conclusion.

Q7843957.name: Trisakti shootings
Q7843957.blurb: Four students were shot and killed by Indonesian soldiers at Trisakti University in Jakarta, which led to widespread riots and the resignation of President Suharto nine days later.

Q7845067.name: Trois Glorieuses
Q7845067.blurb: President Fulbert Youlou was overthrown in the Republic of Congo, after a three-day uprising in the capital.

Q7845858.name: Tropical Storm Beryl
Q7845858.blurb: Tropical Storm Beryl formed over southeastern Louisiana, making it one of the few tropical cyclones to form over land.

Q7845880.name: Tropical Storm Cecil
Q7845880.blurb: Tropical Storm Cecil dissipated over Laos after devastating Quảng Nam province, Vietnam, and causing the deaths of 751 people.

Q7845908.name: Tropical Storm Domoina
Q7845908.blurb: Tropical Storm Domoina makes landfall in southern Mozambique, eventually causing 214 deaths and some of the most severe flooding so far recorded in the region.

Q7846115.name: Tropical Storm Thelma
Q7846115.blurb: Tropical Storm Thelma causes flash floods in the Philippine city of Ormoc, killing more than 4,900 people.

Q7846536.name: Troude's expedition to the Caribbean
Q7846536.blurb: Napoleonic Wars: After a three-day chase, the French ship D'Hautpoul was captured off Puerto Rico by a British squadron under Alexander Cochrane.

Q7855224.name: Turkish Airlines flight 158
Q7855224.blurb: Turkish Airlines Flight 158 crashes at Ankara Esenboğa Airport in Ankara, Turkey, killing 47 and injuring 20.

Q7855225.name: Turkish Airlines flight 345
Q7855225.blurb: Turkish Airlines Flight 345 crashes into the Sea of Marmara near Istanbul Yeşilköy Airport, killing 42.

Q7855227.name: Turkish Airlines flight 5904
Q7855227.blurb: Turkish Airlines Flight 5904 crashes near Ceyhan in southern Turkey, killing six people.

Q7858292.name: Twin Shaft Disaster
Q7858292.blurb: An explosion in the Newton Coal Company's Twin Shaft Mine in Pittston, Pennsylvania results in a massive cave-in that kills 58 miners.

Q7861107.name: Typhoon Angela
Q7861107.blurb: Typhoon Xangsane passes over Manila after impacting parts of Southern Luzon and Eastern Visayas, becoming the strongest to affect the Philippine capital in 11 years.

Q7861310.name: Typhoon Rusa
Q7861310.blurb: Typhoon Rusa, the most powerful typhoon to hit South Korea in 43 years, made landfall, killing at least 236 people.

Q7861312.name: Typhoon Sarah
Q7861312.blurb: Typhoon Sarah dissipated after causing extensive damage along an erratic path across the Western Pacific, killing 71 in Taiwan, the Philippines, and the Gotō Islands.

Q7861342.name: Typhoon Wayne
Q7861342.blurb: Typhoon Wayne formed over the South China Sea, going on to become one of the longest-lived tropical cyclones in the north-western Pacific, lasting 21 days.

Q7861804.name: Mike Tyson vs. Buster Douglas
Q7861804.blurb: Buster Douglas, a 42:1 underdog, knocks out Mike Tyson in ten rounds at Tokyo to win boxing's world Heavyweight title.

Q7863424.name: U.S. Steel Recognition Strike of 1901
Q7863424.blurb: The U.S. Steel recognition strike by the Amalgamated Association of Iron and Steel Workers begins.

Q7865889.name: USAir Flight 5050
Q7865889.blurb: USAir Flight 5050 crashes into Bowery Bay during a rejected takeoff from LaGuardia Airport, killing two people.

Q7866458.name: USMC R4Q NROTC crash
Q7866458.blurb: The largest number of United States midshipman casualties in a single event results from an aircraft crash in Florida, killing 44.

Q7868544.name: USS Constitution vs HMS Guerriere
Q7868544.blurb: War of 1812: American frigate USS Constitution defeats the British frigate HMS Guerriere off the coast of Nova Scotia, Canada earning the nickname "Old Ironsides".

Q7875834.name: USAir Flight 1016
Q7875834.blurb: USAir Flight 1016 crashes near Charlotte Douglas International Airport, killing 37 of the 57 people on board.

Q7877579.name: Uganda Airlines Flight 775
Q7877579.blurb: Uganda Airlines Flight 775 crashes at Rome–Fiumicino International Airport, in Rome, Italy, killing 33 people.

Q7879625.name: Battle of the Seelow Heights
Q7879625.blurb: World War II: The Red Army begins the final assault on German forces around Berlin, with nearly one million troops fighting in the Battle of the Seelow Heights.

Q7880063.name: Ulster Workers' Council strike
Q7880063.blurb: Northern Ireland's power-sharing Sunningdale Agreement collapses following a general strike by loyalists.

Q7883438.name: Underarm bowling incident of 1981
Q7883438.blurb: The Underarm bowling incident of 1981 occurred when Trevor Chappell bowls underarm on the final delivery of a game between Australia and New Zealand at the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG).

Q7885422.name: Battle for Narva
Q7885422.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Narva on the Eastern Front ends with a defensive German victory.

Q7885742.name: Sieges of Boulogne
Q7885742.blurb: Italian War of 1542–46: The first Siege of Boulogne begins.

Q7887343.name: United Airlines Flight 227
Q7887343.blurb: United Air Lines Flight 227 crashes at Salt Lake City International Airport, killing 43.

Q7887345.name: United Airlines Flight 266
Q7887345.blurb: United Airlines Flight 266 crashes into Santa Monica Bay killing all 32 passengers and six crew members.

Q7887351.name: United Airlines Flight 521
Q7887351.blurb: United Airlines Flight 521 crashes at LaGuardia Airport, killing 43.

Q7887358.name: United Airlines Flight 624
Q7887358.blurb: United Air Lines Flight 624, a Douglas DC-6, crashes near Mount Carmel, Pennsylvania, killing all 43 people on board.

Q7887394.name: United Arab Airlines Flight 749
Q7887394.blurb: United Arab Airlines Flight 749 crashes on approach to Cairo International Airport in Cairo, Egypt, killing 30 people.

Q7887735.name: United Express Flight 2415
Q7887735.blurb: United Express Flight 2415 crashes on approach to the Tri-Cities Airport in Pasco, Washington, killing all six people on board.

Q7887737.name: United Express Flight 5925
Q7887737.blurb: A Beechcraft 1900 and a Beechcraft King Air collide at Quincy Regional Airport in Quincy, Illinois, killing 14.

Q7888194.name: Brexit
aliases: British withdrawal from the European Union
United Kingdom's withdrawal from the EU
United Kingdom's withdrawal from the European Union
withdrawal of the United Kingdom from the EU
withdrawal of the United Kingdom from the European Union
Britain to leave the European Union
Britain's withdrawal from the European Union
British disengagement from the European Union
British exit from the European Union
Exit of Britain from the European Union
Exit of the UK from the EU
Impact of Brexit on the UK
Impact of Brexit on the United Kingdom
Possible exit of United Kingdom from European Union
UK exit from the European Union
UK withdrawal from the European Union
UK's withdrawal from the European Union
United Kingdom ceasing to be a member of the European Union
United Kingdom remaining in the European Union
United Kingdom withdrawal from the EU
United Kingdom withdrawal from the European Union
Withdrawal from the European Union by the United Kingdom
Withdrawel of the United Kingdom from the European Union
Q7888194.blurb: Under pressure over her handling of Brexit, British Prime Minister Theresa May announces her resignation as Leader of the Conservative Party, effective as of June 7.

Q7888320.name: United Nations 1956 Supplementary Convention on the Abolition of Slavery
aliases: Supplementary Convention on the Abolition of Slavery, the Slave Trade, and Institutions and Practices Similar to Slavery
Q7888320.blurb: Supplementary Convention on the Abolition of Slavery enters into force.

Q7889582.name: United States Bicentennial
Q7889582.blurb: The United States Treasury Department reintroduces the two-dollar bill as a Federal Reserve Note on Thomas Jefferson's 233rd birthday as part of the United States Bicentennial celebration.

Q7889599.name: 1998 United States Capitol shooting
Q7889599.blurb: Russell Eugene Weston Jr. bursts into the United States Capitol and opens fire, killing two police officers. He is later ruled to be incompetent to stand trial.

Q7889924.name: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum shooting
Q7889924.blurb: Eighty-eight year-old James Wenneker von Brunn opens fire inside the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum and fatally shoots Museum Special Police Officer Stephen Tyrone Johns. Other security guards returned fire, wounding von Brunn, who was apprehended.

Q7891621.name: 1966 United States Senate election in Massachusetts
aliases: United States Senate election in Massachusetts, 1966
Q7891621.blurb: Former Massachusetts Attorney General Edward Brooke becomes the first African American elected to the United States Senate since Reconstruction.

Q7891770.name: Operation Kraai
Q7891770.blurb: Indonesian National Revolution: The Dutch military captures Yogyakarta, the temporary capital of the newly formed Republic of Indonesia.

Q7891830.name: 2000 United States Senate election in New York
aliases: 2000 US Senate election in New York
United States Senate election in New York, 2000
Q7891830.blurb: Hillary Clinton was elected as a US senator from New York, the first time a first lady had been elected to public office.

Q7892122.name: 2012 United States Senate election in Wisconsin
aliases: United States Senate election in Wisconsin, 2012
Q7892122.blurb: Tammy Baldwin becomes the first openly gay politician to be elected to the United States Senate.

Q7892405.name: United States declaration of war on Germany
aliases: Formal U.S. Declaration of War with Germany
Q7892405.blurb: American entry into World War I: President Wilson asks the U.S. Congress for a declaration of war on Germany.

Q7892409.name: United States declaration of war on Japan
Q7892409.blurb: World War II: U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt declares December 7 to be "a date which will live in infamy", after which the U.S. declares war on Japan.

Q7892410.name: United States declaration of war on Mexico
Q7892410.blurb: Mexican–American War: The United States declares war on the Federal Republic of Mexico following a dispute over the American annexation of the Republic of Texas and a Mexican military incursion.

Q7892411.name: United States declaration of war on the United Kingdom
aliases: US Declaration of War against the United Kingdom
Q7892411.blurb: The United States declaration of war upon the United Kingdom is signed by President James Madison, beginning the War of 1812.

Q7892412.name: United States declaration of war on Spain
Q7892412.blurb: Spanish–American War: The United States Congress declares that a state of war between the U.S. and Spain has existed since April 21, when an American naval blockade of the Spanish colony of Cuba began.

Q7892454.name: 1994 United States elections
Q7892454.blurb: Republican Revolution: On the night of the 1994 United States midterm elections, Republicans make historic electoral gains by securing massive majorities in both houses of Congress (54 seats in the House and eight seats in the Senate, additionally), thus bringing to a close four decades of Democratic domination.

Q7893231.name: United States v. Manning
Q7893231.blurb: The trial of United States Army private Chelsea Manning for leaking classified material to WikiLeaks begins in Fort Meade, Maryland.

Q7894457.name: Universities Tests Act 1871
Q7894457.blurb: The Universities Tests Act 1871 allows students to enter the universities of Oxford, Cambridge and Durham without religious tests (except for those intending to study theology).

Q7895381.name: University of Evansville men's basketball team plane crash
Q7895381.blurb: Air Indiana Flight 216 crashes near Evansville Regional Airport, killing 29, including the University of Evansville basketball team, support staff, and boosters of the team.

Q7897916.name: UpStairs Lounge arson attack
Q7897916.blurb: The UpStairs Lounge arson attack takes place at a gay bar located on the second floor of the three-story building at 141 Chartres Street in the French Quarter of New Orleans, Louisiana, US. Thirty-two people die as a result of fire or smoke inhalation.

Q7898494.name: Upper Big Branch Mine disaster
Q7898494.blurb: Twenty-nine coal miners are killed in an explosion at the Upper Big Branch Mine in West Virginia.

Q7902616.name: Ute Wars
Q7902616.blurb: Ute Wars: On behalf of Utah territorial governor Brigham Young, militia leader Daniel H. Wells drafted an order for the Utah Territorial Militia to exterminate Timpanogos men deemed hostile, leading to the Provo River Massacre.

Q7907995.name: Vachathi case
Q7907995.blurb: The special court in India convicted all 269 accused officials for atrocity on Dalits and 17 for rape in the Vachathi case.

Q7926752.name: Victoria Hall disaster
Q7926752.blurb: The Victoria Hall theatre panic in Sunderland, England, kills 183 children.

Q7928485.name: Vietnam Airlines Flight 831
Q7928485.blurb: Vietnam Airlines Flight 831 crashes in Khu Khot, Thailand, while on approach to Don Muang International Airport, killing 76.

Q7930518.name: Villa Tunari Massacre
Q7930518.blurb: Villa Tunari massacre: Bolivian anti-narcotics police kill nine to 12 and injure over a hundred protesting coca-growing peasants.

Q7931177.name: Vilna offensive
Q7931177.blurb: Polish–Lithuanian War: The Polish Army launches the Vilna offensive to capture Vilnius in modern Lithuania.

Q7944876.name: Völkner Incident
Q7944876.blurb: East Cape War: The Völkner Incident in New Zealand.

Q7959475.name: Wagalla massacre
Q7959475.blurb: Kenyan soldiers kill an estimated 5,000 ethnic Somali Kenyans in the Wagalla massacre.

Q7959702.name: Wah Mee massacre
Q7959702.blurb: Thirteen people die and one is seriously injured in the Wah Mee massacre in Seattle. It is said to be the largest robbery-motivated mass-murder in U.S. history.

Q7959771.name: Wahhabi sack of Karbala
Q7959771.blurb: Twelve thousand Wahhabis sack Karbala, killing over three thousand inhabitants.

Q7963839.name: Walsh Street police shootings
Q7963839.blurb: Two officers of the Victoria Police are gunned down execution-style in the Walsh Street police shootings, Australia.

Q7967806.name: Whanganui campaign
Q7967806.blurb: Shooting of a Māori by an English sailor results in the opening of the Wanganui Campaign of the New Zealand Wars.

Q7970865.name: Wars of Castro
Q7970865.blurb: The Italian city of Castro is completely destroyed by the forces of Pope Innocent X, ending the Wars of Castro.

Q7971587.name: Washington's crossing of the Delaware River
aliases: George Washington's crossing of the Delaware River
Q7971587.blurb: American Revolutionary War: General George Washington and the Continental Army cross the Delaware River at night to attack Hessian forces serving Great Britain at Trenton, New Jersey, the next day.

Q7973969.name: Waterfall rail accident
Q7973969.blurb: The Waterfall rail accident occurs near Waterfall, New South Wales, Australia.

Q7979109.name: wedding of Frederik, Crown Prince of Denmark, and Mary Donaldson
Q7979109.blurb: Crown Prince Frederik of Denmark and Mary Donaldson are married at Copenhagen Cathedral.

Q7979110.name: wedding of Prince Albert, Duke of York, and Lady Elizabeth Bowes-Lyon
aliases: Wedding of George VI and Elizabeth
Q7979110.blurb: The Duke of York (the future King George VI) weds Lady Elizabeth Bowes-Lyon at Westminster Abbey.

Q7979113.name: wedding of Princess Anne and Mark Philips
aliases: Wedding of Anne, Princess Royal, and Mark Philips
Wedding of Princess Anne of the United Kingdom and Mark Philips
Wedding of The Princess Anne and Mark Philips
Wedding of The Princess Anne of the United Kingdom and Mark Philips
Q7979113.blurb: In the United Kingdom, Princess Anne marries Captain Mark Phillips, in Westminster Abbey.

Q7979114.name: wedding of Princess Elizabeth and Philip Mountbatten
aliases: Wedding of Elizabeth II and Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh
Wedding of Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh
Wedding of The Princess Elizabeth and Philip Mountbatten
Q7979114.blurb: The Princess Elizabeth (the future Queen) marries Lieutenant Philip Mountbatten, who becomes the Duke of Edinburgh, at Westminster Abbey in London.

Q7984763.name: West Coast Airlines Flight 956
Q7984763.blurb: West Coast Airlines Flight 956 crashes with no survivors in Oregon. This accident marks the first loss of a DC-9.

Q7985528.name: West Indies anti-piracy operations of the United States
Q7985528.blurb: USS Alligator engaged three pirate schooners off the coast of Cuba in one of the West Indies anti-piracy operations of the United States.

Q7989283.name: Westmoreland County coal strike of 1910–1911
Q7989283.blurb: A seventeen-month-long strike, which at its peak involved 15,000 coal miners represented by the United Mine Workers across 65 mines, began in Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania, U.S.

Q7990281.name: Weyauwega, Wisconsin derailment
Q7990281.blurb: A derailed train in Weyauwega, Wisconsin (USA) causes the emergency evacuation of 2,300 people for 16 days.

Q7990590.name: Wham Paymaster Robbery
Q7990590.blurb: An attack upon a U.S. Army paymaster and escort results in the theft of over $28,000 and the award of two Medals of Honor.

Q7991897.name: Wheatland hop riot
Q7991897.blurb: An agricultural workers' strike in Wheatland degenerated into a riot, becoming one of the first major farm-labor confrontations in California.

Q7994669.name: White Earthquake
Q7994669.blurb: The Chilean government declares state of emergency in the southern half of the country in response to an event of intense, cold, wind, rain and snowfall known as the White Earthquake.

Q7994880.name: White House Farm murders
Q7994880.blurb: Five members of the Bamber family were found murdered at a farmhouse in Tolleshunt D'Arcy, England.

Q7995467.name: White Terror (Taiwan)
Q7995467.blurb: Nationalist soldiers fired on protesters in Taipei (crowd pictured), triggering widespread uprisings and violent suppression in the White Terror.

Q7998164.name: Wichita State University football team plane crash
Q7998164.blurb: An aircraft carrying the Wichita State University football team, administrators, and supporters crashes in Colorado, killing 31 people.

Q7998695.name: Widerøe Flight 744
Q7998695.blurb: Widerøe Flight 744 crashes in Overhalla Municipality, Norway, killing six people.

Q7998696.name: Widerøe Flight 839
Q7998696.blurb: Widerøe Flight 839 crashes after takeoff from Værøy Airport in Norway, killing five people.

Q7999112.name: Wien Consolidated Airlines Flight 55
Q7999112.blurb: Wien Consolidated Airlines Flight 55 crashes into Pedro Bay, Alaska, killing all 39 people on board.

Q8000068.name: Wilaya of Relizane massacres of 30 December 1997
Q8000068.blurb: In the worst incident in Algeria's insurgency, the Wilaya of Relizane massacres, 400 people from four villages are killed.

Q8003319.name: Willamette Valley Flood of 1996
Q8003319.blurb: Willamette Valley Flood: Floods in the Willamette Valley of Oregon, United States, causes over US$500 million in property damage throughout the Pacific Northwest.

Q8022327.name: Willow Island disaster
Q8022327.blurb: Willow Island disaster: In the deadliest construction accident in United States history, 51 construction workers are killed when a cooling tower under construction collapses at the Pleasants Power Station in Willow Island, West Virginia.

Q8022766.name: Wilmington Insurrection of 1898
Q8022766.blurb: White supremacists seized power and massacred black Americans during the Wilmington massacre, the only instance of a municipal government being overthrown in United States history.

Q8024951.name: Winecoff Hotel fire
Q8024951.blurb: A fire at the Winecoff Hotel in Atlanta, Georgia kills 119 people, the deadliest hotel fire in U.S. history.

Q8025209.name: Wingfoot Air Express crash
Q8025209.blurb: The dirigible Wingfoot Air Express crashes into the Illinois Trust and Savings Building in Chicago, killing 12 people.

Q8026318.name: Winter Soldier Investigation
Q8026318.blurb: The Winter Soldier Investigation, organized by the Vietnam Veterans Against the War to publicize alleged war crimes and atrocities by Americans and allies in Vietnam, begins in Detroit.

Q8030700.name: Woman Suffrage Procession
Q8030700.blurb: Thousands of women march in the Woman Suffrage Procession in Washington, D.C.

Q8035350.name: World Airways Flight 30
Q8035350.blurb: World Airways Flight 30 overshoots the runway at Logan International Airport in Boston, Massachusetts, and crashes into Boston Harbor. Two people are missing and presumed dead.

Q8041409.name: X-15 Flight 3-65-97
Q8041409.blurb: The only fatality of the North American X-15 program occurs during the 191st flight when Air Force test pilot Michael J. Adams loses control of his aircraft which is destroyed mid-air over the Mojave Desert.

Q8046810.name: Alwaziri coup
Q8046810.blurb: The Al-Waziri coup briefly ousts the ruling Hamidaddin dynasty of Yemen; Imam Yahya Muhammad Hamid ed-Din is killed.

Q8048675.name: Yangzhou massacre
Q8048675.blurb: Yangzhou massacre: The ten day massacre of the residents of the city of Yangzhou, part of the Transition from Ming to Qing.

Q8049080.name: Yaoundé train explosion
Q8049080.blurb: An oil tanker train collides with a freight train in Yaoundé, Cameroon, spilling fuel oil. One person scavenging the oil created a massive explosion which killed 120.

Q8059449.name: Ypiranga incident
Q8059449.blurb: Ypiranga incident: A German arms shipment to Mexico is intercepted by the U.S. Navy near Veracruz.

Q8060104.name: Yuba City bus disaster
Q8060104.blurb: Twenty-nine people are killed in the Yuba City bus disaster in Martinez, California.

Q8063357.name: Z Plan
Q8063357.blurb: Philippine resistance against Japan: Cebuano fishermen discovered the Koga papers after a plane crash killed Admiral Mineichi Koga, commander-in-chief of the Imperial Japanese Navy's Combined Fleet.

Q8064768.name: Zaian War
Q8064768.blurb: Zaian War: Berber tribesmen inflict the heaviest defeat of French forces in Morocco at the Battle of El Herri.

Q8094772.name: 1883 eruption of Krakatoa
Q8094772.blurb: The 1883 eruption of Krakatoa begins its final, paroxysmal, stage.

Q8186827.name: Dan-Air Flight 1903
Q8186827.blurb: Dan-Air Flight 1903 crashes into the Les Agudes mountain in the Montseny Massif near the village of Arbúcies in Catalonia, Spain, killing all 112 people aboard.

Q8244136.name: Battle of Quart de Poblet
Q8244136.blurb: El Cid and his forces defeat a larger army of the Almoravids in the battle of Cuarte.

Q8641370.name: Operation Overlord
aliases: List of Battle of Normandy leaders
Q8641370.blurb: World War II: Commencement of Operation Overlord: The Allied invasion of Normandy begins with the execution of Operation Neptune—commonly referred to as D-Day—the largest seaborne invasion in history. Nearly 160,000 Allied troops cross the English Channel with about 5,000 landing and assault craft, 289 escort vessels, and 277 minesweepers participating. By the end of the day, the Allies have landed on five invasion beaches and are pushing inland.

Q8673406.name: Battle of Hanoi
aliases: Second Battle of the Citadel of Hanoi
Q8673406.blurb: French and Vietnamese troops clash in Tonkin, when Commandant Henri Rivière seizes the citadel of Hanoi with a small force of marine infantry.

Q8676049.name: 1987 Tunisian coup d'état
Q8676049.blurb: Tunisian prime minister Zine El Abidine Ben Ali deposed and replaced President Habib Bourguiba by declaring him medically unfit for the duties of the office.

Q8964623.name: 1952 Cuban coup d'état
Q8964623.blurb: Fulgencio Batista leads a successful coup in Cuba.

Q9030108.name: Tenmei famine
Q9030108.blurb: Mount Asama (pictured) in Japan began a climactic eruption, which exacerbated the Great Tenmei famine and led to thousands of deaths.

Q9030262.name: Goliad massacre
Q9030262.blurb: At least 425 Texian prisoners of war were executed in the Goliad massacre, under orders from Mexican president Antonio López de Santa Anna.

Q9035653.name: Death of Neda Agha-Soltan
Q9035653.blurb: Iranian student Neda Agha-Soltan was shot dead in Tehran during the presidential election protests; footage of her death was widely distributed over the Internet, making it "probably the most widely witnessed death in human history".

Q9063028.name: Events of 6 October
Q9063028.blurb: Revolution of 1934: The President of the autonomous government of Catalonia, Lluís Companys, proclaims the Catalan State with the support of the Worker's Alliance.

Q9066084.name: Tropical Storm Irina
Q9066084.blurb: Tropical Storm Irina kills over 75 as it passes through Madagascar.

Q9067174.name: Magonista rebellion of 1911
Q9067174.blurb: Mexican Revolution: The Magonista rebellion began when Mexican Liberal Party troops captured the town of Mexicali.

Q9068534.name: Revolution of 11 September 1852
Q9068534.blurb: Outbreak of Revolution of September 11 resulting in the State of Buenos Aires declaring independence as a Republic.

Q9094823.name: TAME Flight 120
Q9094823.blurb: TAME Flight 120, a Boeing 727-100, crashes in the Andes mountains in southern Colombia, killing 94.

Q9108414.name: Anarchist insurrection of December 1933
Q9108414.blurb: Anarchist insurrection breaks out in Zaragoza, Spain.

Q9172576.name: Battle of Seival
Q9172576.blurb: The Riograndense Republic is proclaimed by rebels after defeating Empire of Brazil's troops in the Battle of Seival, during the Ragamuffin War.

Q9172722.name: Battle of Ain Salm
Q9172722.blurb: Tutush, brother of Seljuk sultan Malik Shah, defeats Suleiman ibn Qutalmish, the Turkish ruler of Anatolia in the battle of Ain Salm.

Q9305225.name: 1994 Swedish European Union membership referendum
Q9305225.blurb: In a referendum, voters in Sweden decide to join the European Union.

Q9366875.name: Siege of Trebizond in 1461
Q9366875.blurb: Byzantine–Ottoman wars: The Empire of Trebizond, the longest-surviving Byzantine successor state, was conquered by Ottoman forces following a month-long siege.

Q9386436.name: assassination of Gabriel Narutowicz
Q9386436.blurb: Gabriel Narutowicz (pictured), the first president of Poland, was assassinated only five days after having taken office.

Q10297227.name: Battle of Buyur Lake
Q10297227.blurb: During the Battle of Buyur Lake, General Lan Yu leads a Ming army forward to crush the Mongol hordes of Tögüs Temür, the Khan of Northern Yuan.

Q10310765.name: 2013 Argentina floods
Q10310765.blurb: More than 50 people die in floods resulting from record-breaking rainfall in La Plata and Buenos Aires, Argentina.

Q10325205.name: March of the Family with God for Liberty
Q10325205.blurb: Over 500,000 Brazilians attend the March of the Family with God for Liberty, in protest against the government of João Goulart and against communism.

Q10354157.name: proclamation of the German Empire
Q10354157.blurb: Wilhelm I of Germany is proclaimed Kaiser Wilhelm in the Hall of Mirrors of the Palace of Versailles (France) towards the end of the Franco-Prussian War. Wilhelm already had the title of German Emperor since the constitution of 1 January 1871, but he had hesitated to accept the title.

Q10360246.name: 1936 Naval Revolt
Q10360246.blurb: The crews of Portuguese Navy frigate NRP Afonso de Albuquerque and destroyer Dão mutinied against the Salazar dictatorship's support of General Franco's coup and declared their solidarity with the Spanish Republic.

Q10372024.name: 1909 Benavente earthquake
Q10372024.blurb: In Portugal, a magnitude 6.0 earthquake strikes near Lisbon, killing at least 60 people and injuring 75.

Q10392496.name: SATA Air Açores Flight 530M
Q10392496.blurb: SATA Air Açores Flight 530M crashes into Pico da Esperança on São Jorge Island in the Azores, killing 35.

Q10392510.name: Transbrasil Flight 801
Q10392510.blurb: Transbrasil Flight 801 crashes into a slum near São Paulo/Guarulhos International Airport, killing 25 people.

Q10428879.name: 1971 Yugoslav Embassy shooting
Q10428879.blurb: Three armed members of the Croatian National Resistance hijacked Scandinavian Airlines System Flight 130 in an attempt to force the release of those arrested for the assassination of the Yugoslav ambassador the previous year.

Q10497077.name: Scandinavian Airlines System Flight 130
Q10497077.blurb: Three armed members of the Croatian National Resistance hijacked Scandinavian Airlines System Flight 130 in an attempt to force the release of those arrested for the assassination of the Yugoslav ambassador the previous year.

Q10511142.name: Revolution of 1772
aliases: Coup d'état of Gustav III of Sweden
Q10511142.blurb: Gustav III of Sweden stages a coup d'état, in which he assumes power and enacts a new constitution that divides power between the Riksdag and the King.

Q10537330.name: Isle of Wight Festival 1969
Q10537330.blurb: On the final day of the Isle of Wight Festival 1969, attended by approximately 150,000 people over three days, Bob Dylan appeared in his first gig in three years.

Q10540838.name: 1717 Guatemala earthquake
Q10540838.blurb: An earthquake strikes Antigua Guatemala, destroying much of the city's architecture.

Q10671336.name: Battle of Länkipohja
Q10671336.blurb: Finnish Civil War: Battle of Länkipohja is infamous for its bloody aftermath as the Whites execute 70–100 capitulated Reds.

Q10674369.name: 1970 Spantax Convair crash
Q10674369.blurb: A Spantax Convair CV-990 Coronado crashes during takeoff from Stockholm Arlanda Airport, killing five people.
