Q10681317.name: 1993 Storm of the Century
Q10681317.blurb: The 1993 Storm of the Century affects the eastern United States, dropping feet of snow in many areas.

Q10745598.name: 1958 Lituya Bay earthquake and megatsunami
Q10745598.blurb: A 7.8 Mw strike-slip earthquake in Alaska causes a landslide that produces a megatsunami. The runup from the waves reached 525 m (1,722 ft) on the rim of Lituya Bay; five people were killed.

Q10751080.name: 1811 Independence Movement
Q10751080.blurb: Salvadoran priest José Matías Delgado rings the bells of La Merced church in San Salvador, calling for insurrection and launching the 1811 Independence Movement.

Q10751243.name: Siege of Namur
Q10751243.blurb: World War I: German troops capture Namur.

Q10786861.name: Velika Ivanča shooting
Q10786861.blurb: At least 13 people are killed and another three injured after a man goes on a spree shooting in the Serbian village of Velika Ivanča.

Q10798381.name: 2013 Bushehr earthquake
Q10798381.blurb: A 6.1–magnitude earthquake strikes Iran killing 32 people and injuring over 850 people.

Q10834930.name: 1942 Matagorda hurricane
Q10834930.blurb: The Matagorda hurricane, the most intense and costliest tropical cyclone of the 1942 Atlantic hurricane season, dissipated after causing $26.5 million in damages and eight deaths.

Q10843834.name: 1867 Keelung earthquake
Q10843834.blurb: A magnitude 7.0 earthquakes strikes off the coast of Taiwan, triggering a tsunami and killing at least 580 people.

Q10854932.name: YH incident
Q10854932.blurb: Female workers of YH Trading in South Korea held a sit-in protest in response to the company's unilateral shutdown.

Q10855109.name: Kapsan Faction Incident
Q10855109.blurb: Having purged a group of rivals, Supreme Leader of North Korea Kim Il Sung delivered the "May 25 teaching", entrenching his son Kim Jong Il as his designated successor.

Q10856357.name: Tainei-ji incident
Q10856357.blurb: A coup by the military establishment of Japan's Ōuchi clan forces their lord to commit suicide, and their city is burned.

Q10858950.name: Reinhard Heydrich assassination
Q10858950.blurb: World War II: In Operation Anthropoid, Reinhard Heydrich is fatally wounded in Prague; he dies of his injuries eight days later.

Q10858954.name: assassination of Malcolm X
Q10858954.blurb: American Black nationalist Malcolm X (pictured) was assassinated while giving a speech in New York City's Audubon Ballroom.

Q10858956.name: Plot of the rue Saint-Nicaise
Q10858956.blurb: The Plot of the rue Saint-Nicaise fails to kill Napoleon Bonaparte.

Q10861133.name: 1946 Nankai earthquake
Q10861133.blurb: An earthquake in Nankaidō, Japan causes a tsunami which kills at least one thousand people and destroys 36,000 homes.

Q10863956.name: January Storm
Q10863956.blurb: Cultural Revolution: The Shanghai People's Commune is established following the seizure of power from local city officials by revolutionaries.

Q10865450.name: Japan Air Lines Flight 301
Q10865450.blurb: Japan Air Lines Flight 301 crashes into Mount Mihara, Izu Ōshima, Japan, killing 37.

Q10869269.name: Hong Kong Typhoon of 1906
Q10869269.blurb: The 1906 Hong Kong typhoon kills an estimated 10,000 people.

Q10872057.name: proclamation of the People's Republic of China
Q10872057.blurb: The People's Republic of China is established.

Q10878635.name: September 13 incident
Q10878635.blurb: Following a failed coup attempt, Mao Zedong's second-in-command Lin Biao died in a plane crash while attempting to flee China.

Q10884583.name: Zhongkang solar eclipse
Q10884583.blurb: A solar eclipse occurs over China, one of the earliest recorded in human history, reportedly resulting in the executions of two astronomers who failed to predict it.

Q10884944.name: Yi-Ta Incident
Q10884944.blurb: Chinese police open fire on protesters in Yining, Xinjiang, killing at least five people and wounding a dozen others.

Q10885051.name: Xinjiang 61st Regiment Farm fire
aliases: Xinjiang 61st Regiment Farm fire and stampede
Q10885051.blurb: The Xinjiang 61st Regiment Farm fire started during Chinese New Year when a firecracker ignited memorial wreaths of the late Mao Zedong, killing 694 personnel. It remains the deadliest fireworks accident in the world.

Q10893876.name: Merpati Nusantara Airlines Flight 5601
Q10893876.blurb: Merpati Nustantara Airlines Flight 5601 crashes into Mount Papandayan near the town of Garut in West Java, Indonesia, killing 31.

Q10903028.name: Lion Air Flight 904
Q10903028.blurb: Lion Air Flight 904 crashes on approach to Ngurah Rai International Airport in Denpasar, Indonesia, injuring 40 people.

Q10931534.name: Palace plot of Renyin year
Q10931534.blurb: Palace plot of Renyin year: A group of Ming dynasty palace women fail to murder the Jiajing Emperor, and are executed by slow-slicing.

Q10931943.name: Overthrow of the Hawaiian Kingdom
Q10931943.blurb: Lorrin A. Thurston, along with the Citizens' Committee of Public Safety, led the Overthrow of the Kingdom of Hawaii and the government of Queen Liliʻuokalani.

Q10974750.name: 7th March Speech of Bangabandhu
aliases: The struggle this time is the struggle for our independence
Q10974750.blurb: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, political leader of then East Pakistan (present day-Bangladesh), delivers his historic 7th March speech in the Racecourse Field (Now Suhrawardy Udyan) in Dhaka.

Q11030407.name: Second Desmond Rebellion
Q11030407.blurb: Second Desmond Rebellion: The Siege of Smerwick ends with the Catholic garrison surrendering to the English forces under Arthur Grey. The majority of the garrison is massacred the next day.

Q11078546.name: Operation Ripper
Q11078546.blurb: Korean War: Operation Ripper: United Nations troops led by General Matthew Ridgway begin an assault against Chinese forces.

Q11086137.name: Boston Marathon bombings
aliases: Conspiracy theories about the Boston Marathon bombing
Q11086137.blurb: Two bombs explode near the finish line at the Boston Marathon in Boston, Massachusetts, killing three people and injuring over 500 others.

Q11087883.name: Yongle Emperor's campaigns against the Mongols
Q11087883.blurb: In a decisive battle at Onon River, the Mongol forces of Oljei Temur were decimated by the Chinese armies of the Yongle Emperor.

Q11103189.name: 2013 Boston Marathon
Q11103189.blurb: Two bombs explode near the finish line at the Boston Marathon in Boston, Massachusetts, killing three people and injuring over 500 others.

Q11108995.name: Xá Lợi Pagoda raids
Q11108995.blurb: Xá Lợi Pagoda raids: The Army of the Republic of Vietnam Special Forces loyal to Ngô Đình Nhu, brother of President Ngo Dinh Diem, vandalizes Buddhist pagodas across the country, arresting thousands and leaving an estimated hundreds dead.

Q11127665.name: death of Mao Zedong
Q11127665.blurb: The Xinjiang 61st Regiment Farm fire started during Chinese New Year when a firecracker ignited memorial wreaths of the late Mao Zedong, killing 694 personnel. It remains the deadliest fireworks accident in the world.

Q11129260.name: Civil Air Transport Flight 10
Q11129260.blurb: Civil Air Transport Flight 010 crashes near Shongshan Airport in Taiwan, killing 21 of the 63 people on board and one more on the ground.

Q11136035.name: London Protocol
Q11136035.blurb: King Christian IX of Denmark signs the November constitution that declares Schleswig to be part of Denmark. This is seen by the German Confederation as a violation of the London Protocol and leads to the German–Danish war of 1864.

Q11153274.name: Battle of Lake Baikal
Q11153274.blurb: The Battle of Lake Baikal was fought between the Czechoslovak Legion and the Red Army.

Q11157381.name: Typhoon Nora
Q11157381.blurb: Typhoon Nora, the fourth-most intense tropical cyclone on record, dissipated after killing 40 people and leaving more than a million homeless across Taiwan and the Philippines.

Q11158136.name: 2013 Sistan and Baluchestan earthquake
Q11158136.blurb: A 7.8-magnitude earthquake strikes Sistan and Balochistan province, Iran, killing at least 35 people and injuring 117 others.

Q11173933.name: death and funeral of Margaret Thatcher
Q11173933.blurb: The ceremonial funeral of former British prime minister Margaret Thatcher takes place at St Paul's Cathedral.

Q11193140.name: 15 April 2013 Iraqi bombings
Q11193140.blurb: A wave of bombings across Iraq kills at least 75 people.

Q11202294.name: Kidal attack of April 2013
Q11202294.blurb: Two suicide bombers kill three Chadian soldiers and injure dozens of civilians at a market in Kidal, Mali.

Q11211553.name: Attack on the Moncada Barracks
Q11211553.blurb: Cold War: Fidel Castro leads an unsuccessful attack on the Moncada Barracks, thus beginning the Cuban Revolution. The movement took the name of the date: 26th of July Movement

Q11216473.name: 2012 Bucharest hair salon shooting
Q11216473.blurb: Two people are killed and six more are injured in a shooting at a hair salon in Bucharest, Romania.

Q11256383.name: assassination of Inejiro Asanuma
Q11256383.blurb: Japan Socialist Party leader Inejirō Asanuma (pictured) was assassinated during a live television recording by a far-right ultra-nationalist using a short sword.

Q11261090.name: Saar status referendum, 1935
Q11261090.blurb: A plebiscite in Saarland shows that 90.3% of those voting wish to no more being a "region occupied and governed by the United Kingdom and France".

Q11306135.name: San Felipe incident (1596)
Q11306135.blurb: The Spanish ship San Felipe runs aground on the coast of Japan and its cargo is confiscated by local authorities.

Q11333034.name: West Fertilizer Company explosion
Q11333034.blurb: An explosion at a fertilizer plant in the city of West, Texas, kills 15 people and injures 160 others.

Q11349248.name: The Beatles' rooftop concert
Q11349248.blurb: The Beatles' last public performance, on the roof of Apple Records in London. The impromptu concert is broken up by the police.

Q11355226.name: Mishima incident
Q11355226.blurb: After failing to instigate a military coup to restore the powers of the Emperor of Japan, author Yukio Mishima and a member of his militia committed ritual suicide.

Q11391098.name: Bombing of Yawata on June 1944
Q11391098.blurb: World War II: The United States Army Air Forces began the first air raid of its strategic bombing campaign against the Japanese archipelago, although little damage was caused.

Q11442711.name: 1586 Tenshō earthquake
Q11442711.blurb: The magnitude 7.9 Tenshō earthquake strikes Honshu, Japan, killing 8,000 people and triggering a tsunami.

Q11457612.name: Prince of Ning rebellion
Q11457612.blurb: On the third day of battle, philosopher and general Wang Yangming defeats Zhu Chenhao, ending the Prince of Ning rebellion against the reign of the Ming dynasty's Zhengde Emperor.

Q11475843.name: LOT Polish Airlines Flight 165 (1969)
Q11475843.blurb: LOT Polish Airlines Flight 165 crashes into the Polica mountain near Zawoja, Poland, killing 53.

Q11501879.name: 1968 Shinjuku Riot
Q11501879.blurb: At the height of the Japanese university protests, protesters occupied Shinjuku Station in Tokyo and clashed violently with police.

Q11508994.name: Japan Air Lines Cargo Flight 1045
Q11508994.blurb: Japan Air Lines Cargo Flight 1045, a Douglas DC-8 jet, crashes onto the runway during takeoff from Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport, killing five.

Q11514810.name: 1925 Hama uprising
Q11514810.blurb: Great Syrian Revolt: Rebels led by Fawzi al-Qawuqji capture Hama from the French Mandate of Syria.

Q11547847.name: 2013 Lushan earthquake
Q11547847.blurb: A 6.6-magnitude earthquake strikes Lushan County, Ya'an, in China's Sichuan province, killing at least 193 people and injuring thousands.

Q11597894.name: Tachikawa air disaster
Q11597894.blurb: A Douglas C-124 Globemaster II aircraft crashed just after takeoff from Tachikawa, Japan, killing all 129 people on board.

Q11636595.name: Battle of Boulogne
Q11636595.blurb: Second World War: German troops captured Boulogne-sur-Mer, France, forcing British forces to evacuate via Dunkirk.

Q11679964.name: Indictment and arrest of Augusto Pinochet
Q11679964.blurb: Former Chilean dictator Augusto Pinochet is arrested in London on a murder extradition warrant.

Q11688119.name: Battle of Acre
Q11688119.blurb: War of Saint Sabas: In the Battle of Acre, the Venetians defeat a larger Genoese fleet sailing to relieve Acre.

Q11737210.name: Aeroflot Flight 6551
Q11737210.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 6551 crashes in Semey, Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic (now Kazakhstan), killing all 63 aboard.

Q11737212.name: Aeroflot Flight 8641
Q11737212.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 8641 crashes in Mazyr, Belarus, killing 132 people.

Q11737216.name: Iran Air Tours Flight 956
Q11737216.blurb: An Iran Airtour Tupolev Tu-154 crashes in the mountains outside Khorramabad, Iran while descending for a landing at Khorramabad Airport, killing 119.

Q11737221.name: Tajikistan Airlines Flight 3183
Q11737221.blurb: Tajikistan Airlines Flight 3183 crashes in the desert near Sharjah, United Arab Emirates, killing 85.

Q11737223.name: Uzbekistan Airways Flight 1154
Q11737223.blurb: Uzbekistan Airways Flight 1154 crashes while landing at Tashkent International Airport, killing 37.

Q11737225.name: Lake Nyos disaster
Q11737225.blurb: A limnic eruption of Lake Nyos in Cameroon released a cloud of carbon dioxide, suffocating 1,746 people and 3,500 livestock.

Q11737229.name: MS Jan Heweliusz disaster
Q11737229.blurb: Sinking of the MS Jan Heweliusz: In Poland's worst peacetime maritime disaster, ferry MS Jan Heweliusz sinks off the coast of Rügen, drowning 55 passengers.

Q11774398.name: Cyclone Manou
Q11774398.blurb: Cyclone Manou formed in the Indian Ocean; over the next two weeks it struck Madagascar and left more than 100,000 people homeless.

Q11794876.name: Siege of Corfu
Q11794876.blurb: Seventh Ottoman–Venetian War: Ottoman forces suddenly abandoned their siege of Corfu, allowing the Republic of Venice to preserve its rule over the Ionian Islands.

Q11821309.name: Treaty of Belgrade
Q11821309.blurb: The Treaty of Belgrade is signed, whereby Austria cedes lands south of the Sava and Danube rivers to the Ottoman Empire.

Q11838739.name: 2013 Savar building collapse
Q11838739.blurb: A building collapses near Dhaka, Bangladesh, killing 1,134 people and injuring about 2,500 others.

Q11862160.name: 8th World Festival of Youth and Students
Q11862160.blurb: Beginning of the 8th World Festival of Youth and Students.

Q11862675.name: August Storm of 1890
Q11862675.blurb: The strongest storm in Finnish history kills at least three people.

Q11867970.name: Jussi Awards 1944
Q11867970.blurb: The Jussi Awards, the Finnish film award ceremony, is held for the first time at Restaurant Adlon in Helsinki.

Q11868586.name: Ståhlberg kidnapping
Q11868586.blurb: The former and first President of Finland, K. J. Ståhlberg, and his wife, Ester Ståhlberg, are kidnapped from their home by members of the far-right Lapua Movement.

Q11870881.name: 1949 Kemi strike
Q11870881.blurb: 1949 Kemi strike: Two protesters die in the scuffle between the police and the strikers' protest procession in Kemi, Finland.

Q11885643.name: Åland War
Q11885643.blurb: Åland War: The British navy destroys merchant ships and about 16,000 tar barrels of the wholesale stocks area in Oulu, Grand Duchy of Finland.

Q11886114.name: Great Oulu Fire of 1705
Q11886114.blurb: A fire in Oulu, Finland almost completely destroyed the fourth district, which covered the southern part of the city and was by far the largest of the city districts.

Q11896174.name: Peasant March
Q11896174.blurb: The Finnish far-right Lapua Movement organises the Peasant March demonstration in Helsinki to put pressure on the government to prohibit communist activities.

Q11898725.name: Turenki rail accident
Q11898725.blurb: The most destructive train accident in Finnish history kills 39 and injures 69 people in Turenki, Janakkala.

Q11900368.name: Takeover of Vanha
aliases: Occupation of the Old Student House
Q11900368.blurb: The Old Student House in Helsinki, Finland is occupied by a large group of University of Helsinki students.

Q11903403.name: Dar es Salaam building collapse
Q11903403.blurb: At least 36 people are killed when a 16-floor building collapses in the commercial capital Dar es Salaam, Tanzania.

Q11908761.name: Battle of Qantish
Q11908761.blurb: Berber forces led by Sulayman ibn al-Hakam defeat the Umayyad caliph Muhammad II of Córdoba in the Battle of Qantish.

Q11908797.name: Battle of the Bosporus
Q11908797.blurb: War of the Straits: The Battle of the Bosporus is fought in a stormy sea into the night between the Genoese, Venetian, Aragonese, and Byzantine fleets.

Q11908798.name: Battle of Porto Conte
Q11908798.blurb: War of the Straits and Sardinian–Aragonese war: The Battle of Alghero results in a crushing victory of the allied Aragonese and Venetian fleet over the Genoese fleet, most of which is captured.

Q11909584.name: Liceu bombing
Q11909584.blurb: An anarchist throws two bombs in Barcelona's Liceu opera house, killing 20.

Q11915297.name: Siege of Barcelona
Q11915297.blurb: King Louis the Pious captures Barcelona from the Moors after a siege of several months.

Q11915301.name: Conquest of Murcia
Q11915301.blurb: Mudéjar revolt: King James I of Aragon entered the formerly Muslim-held city of Murcia following its surrender three days earlier.

Q11945463.name: Alt Llobregat insurrection
Q11945463.blurb: Alt Llobregat insurrection breaks out in Central Catalonia, Spain.

Q11946474.name: Hungarian raid in Spain
Q11946474.blurb: A Magyar raiding army defeats forces of the Muslim frontier state of Fraxinetum.

Q11996114.name: U.S. postal strike of 1970
Q11996114.blurb: U.S. postal workers began an eight-day strike after Congress  raised their wages by only 4 percent despite increasing its own pay by 41 percent.

Q12029011.name: Kaunas massacre of October 29, 1941
Q12029011.blurb: The Holocaust: In the Kaunas Ghetto, over 10,000 Jews are shot by German occupiers at the Ninth Fort, a massacre known as the "Great Action".

Q12033079.name: ČSA Flight 540
Q12033079.blurb: ČSA Flight 540 crashes on approach to Damascus International Airport in Damascus, Syria, killing 126 people.

Q12052728.name: Action of 7 February 1813
Q12052728.blurb: In the action of 7 February 1813 near the Îles de Los, the frigates Aréthuse and Amelia batter each other, but neither can gain the upper hand.

Q12055176.name: Angolan Civil War
aliases: Child soldiers in the Angolan Civil War
Q12055176.blurb: Angolan Civil War: The MPLA and UNITA agree to the Bicesse Accords, which are formally signed on May 31 in Lisbon.

Q12059474.name: Hands Across Hawthorne
Q12059474.blurb: Residents of Portland, Oregon, held a rally called Hands Across Hawthorne in response to an attack against a gay couple holding hands while crossing the Hawthorne Bridge.

Q12061900.name: Mississippi in the American Civil War
Q12061900.blurb: Mississippi becomes the second state to secede from the Union before the outbreak of the American Civil War.

Q12064441.name: Northeastern United States blizzard of 1978
Q12064441.blurb: The Blizzard of 1978, one of the worst Nor'easters in New England history, hit the region, with sustained winds of 65 mph and snowfall of four inches an hour.

Q12065527.name: Penlee lifeboat disaster
Q12065527.blurb: Sixteen lives are lost when the Penlee lifeboat goes to the aid of the stricken coaster Union Star in heavy seas.

Q12163419.name: Ukraine–European Union Association Agreement
aliases: Association Agreement between the European Union and its Member States, of the one part, and Ukraine, of the other part
Q12163419.blurb: Massive protests start in Ukraine after President Viktor Yanukovych suspended signing the Ukraine–European Union Association Agreement.

Q12223939.name: 2013 Prague explosion
Q12223939.blurb: A powerful explosion occurs in an office building in Prague, believed to have been caused by natural gas, and injures 43 people.

Q12234212.name: Llandow air disaster
Q12234212.blurb: The Llandow air disaster kills 80 people when the aircraft they are travelling in crashes near Sigingstone, Wales. At the time this was the world's deadliest air disaster.

Q12241913.name: Khan Yunis massacre
Q12241913.blurb: Suez Crisis: The Khan Yunis killings by the Israel Defense Forces in Egyptian-controlled Gaza result in the deaths of 275 Palestinians.

Q12257020.name: National Airlines Flight 102
Q12257020.blurb: National Airlines Flight 102, a Boeing 747-400 freighter aircraft, crashes during takeoff from Bagram Airfield in Parwan Province, Afghanistan, killing all seven people on board.

Q12273318.name: Battle of Sofia
Q12273318.blurb: Russo-Turkish War (1877–78): Sofia is liberated from Ottoman rule.

Q12279131.name: Drama Uprising
Q12279131.blurb: World War II: The Drama uprising against the Bulgarian occupation in northern Greece begins.

Q12296445.name: Asiatic-Pacific Theater
Q12296445.blurb: World War II: Japanese forces evacuate New Georgia Island in the Pacific Theater of Operations during World War II.

Q12375644.name: Battle of Cape St. Vincent
Q12375644.blurb: Admiral Charles Napier vanquishes the navy of the Portuguese usurper Dom Miguel at the third Battle of Cape St. Vincent.

Q12406742.name: New Britain campaign
Q12406742.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Arawe begins during the New Britain campaign.

Q12427302.name: Battle of Chausa
Q12427302.blurb: Afghan Sur forces under Sher Shah Suri defeat a Mughal army under Humayun in the battle of Chausa.

Q12579932.name: October 27th Buddhist Persecution
Q12579932.blurb: The Chun Doo-hwan government forcibly arrests and investigates monks and personnel of the Jogye Order.

Q12609176.name: Uljin–Samcheok Landings
Q12609176.blurb: A squad of 120 North Korean Army commandos land in boats along a 25-mile long section of the eastern coast of South Korea in a failed attempt to overthrow the dictatorship of Park Chung Hee and bring about the reunification of Korea.

Q12628176.name: Sanjak of Bosnia
Q12628176.blurb: Ottoman wars in Europe: A large Croatian army intercepted Ottoman forces returning to the Sanjak of Bosnia, but was defeated.

Q12653918.name: Soviet economic blockade of Lithuania
Q12653918.blurb: Singing Revolution: The Soviet economic blockade of Lithuania (pictured) was lifted when the Lithuanian parliament agreed to suspend the effects of their act to re-establish Lithuania as a state.

Q12660036.name: Siege of Kaunas
Q12660036.blurb: Lithuanian Crusade: After a month-long siege, the Teutonic Order captured and destroyed Kaunas Castle, which was defended by troops of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania.

Q12665039.name: Siege of Medvėgalis
Q12665039.blurb: The Teutonic Knights successfully besieged the hillfort of Medvėgalis (pictured) in Samogitia, Lithuania, and baptised the defenders in the Catholic rite.

Q12687629.name: 1964 race riots in Singapore
Q12687629.blurb: A series of racial riots break out in Singapore. In the next six weeks, 23 die with 454 others injured.

Q12717504.name: Siege of St. Augustine
Q12717504.blurb: English colonists under the command of James Moore besiege Spanish St. Augustine during Queen Anne's War.

Q12717505.name: Siege of Pensacola
Q12717505.blurb: The first Siege of Pensacola comes to an end with the failure of the British to capture Pensacola, Florida.

Q12750464.name: Serbian civil war of 1331
Q12750464.blurb: King Stefan Uroš III, after months of anarchy, surrenders to his son and rival Stefan Dušan, who succeeds as King of Serbia.

Q12754327.name: Battle of Kunovica
Q12754327.blurb: Christian forces defeat the Turks in the battle of Kunovica.

Q12760314.name: Sarajevo wedding attack
Q12760314.blurb: A Bosnian-Serb wedding procession was attacked in Sarajevo, resulting in what is widely considered the first casualty of the Bosnian War.

Q12790010.name: Battle of the Vikhra River
Q12790010.blurb: The Grand Duchy of Lithuania decisively won the Battle of the Vikhra River, forcibly making the Principality of Smolensk a vassal state.

Q12858131.name: dord
Q12858131.blurb: In one of the most famous errors in lexicography, the erroneous word dord was discovered in Webster's New International Dictionary by an editor.

Q12880420.name: Battle of Meligalas
Q12880420.blurb: World War II: Start of the Battle of Meligalas between the Greek Resistance forces of the Greek People's Liberation Army (ELAS) and the collaborationist security battalions.

Q12881604.name: Battle of Andros
Q12881604.blurb: Russo-Turkish war (1787–1792): Greek privateer Lambros Katsonis loses three of his ships in the Battle of Andros.

Q12912943.name: kidnappings of Amanda Berry, Gina DeJesus, and Michelle Knight
Q12912943.blurb: Three women, kidnapped and missing for more than a decade, are found alive in Cleveland, Ohio, in the United States.

Q12976096.name: Siege of Cuddalore
Q12976096.blurb: American Revolutionary War: The war's last action, the Siege of Cuddalore, is ended by a preliminary peace agreement.

Q13107359.name: 2013 Reyhanlı bombings
Q13107359.blurb: Fifty-two people are killed in a bombing in Reyhanlı, Turkey.

Q13107466.name: April 2013 Bachu unrest
Q13107466.blurb: Violence in Bachu County, Kashgar Prefecture, of China's Xinjiang results in death of 21 people.

Q13311324.name: May 2013 Iraq attacks
Q13311324.blurb: An upsurge in violence in Iraq leaves more than 389 people dead over three days.

Q13360358.name: Moore tornado
Q13360358.blurb: A tornado struck Moore, Oklahoma, United States, killing 24 people and causing an estimated $2 billion of damage.

Q13367650.name: murder of Lee Rigby
Q13367650.blurb: Fusilier Lee Rigby is murdered by two Islamic extremists in Woolwich, Southeast London.

Q13372646.name: 2013 VIA Rail Canada terrorism plot
Q13372646.blurb: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police arrested two men who were plotting to commit terrorist attacks against Via Rail operations.

Q13381733.name: I-5 Skagit River Bridge collapse
Q13381733.blurb: A freeway bridge carrying Interstate 5 over the Skagit River collapses in Mount Vernon, Washington.

Q13402557.name: 2013 Naxal attack in Darbha valley
Q13402557.blurb: Suspected Maoist rebels kill at least 28 people and injure 32 others in an attack on a convoy of Indian National Congress politicians in Chhattisgarh, India.

Q13404967.name: The Satanic Verses controversy
Q13404967.blurb: Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini of Iran issued a fatwa calling for the death of Salman Rushdie, the author of The Satanic Verses, a novel considered to be blasphemous by some Muslims.

Q13410316.name: Gezi Park protests
aliases: 2013 Taksim Gezi Park protests in Turkey
Q13410316.blurb: Start of the Gezi Park protests in Turkey.

Q13415790.name: Jilin Baoyuanfeng poultry plant fire
Q13415790.blurb: At least 119 people are killed in a fire at a poultry farm in Jilin Province in northeastern China.

Q13417205.name: 2013 El Reno tornado
Q13417205.blurb: A record breaking 2.6 mile wide tornado strikes near El Reno, Oklahoma, United States, causing eight fatalities (including three storm chasers) and over 150 injuries.

Q13419956.name: 86th Academy Awards
Q13419956.blurb: The Oscar Selfie, regarded as one of the most influential and important images of all time, is taken at the 86th Academy Awards.

Q13441139.name: Intercontinental de Aviación Flight 256
Q13441139.blurb: 51 people are killed in a plane crash in María La Baja, Colombia.

Q13452201.name: 2013 Czech political corruption scandal
Q13452201.blurb: Some of the closest advisors and collaborators of Czech prime minister Petr Nečas were arrested for corruption.

Q13490083.name: Siege of Knodsenburg
Q13490083.blurb: The Duke of Parma is defeated near the Dutch city of Nijmegen by an Anglo-Dutch force led by Maurice of Orange.

Q13507070.name: 2013 North India floods
Q13507070.blurb: A multi-day cloudburst, centered on the North Indian state of Uttarakhand, causes devastating floods and landslides, becoming the country's worst natural disaster since the 2004 tsunami.

Q13511605.name: 1975 LaGuardia Airport bombing
Q13511605.blurb: A bomb explodes at LaGuardia Airport in New York City, killing 11 people and injuring more than 75.

Q13530561.name: 2013 Nanga Parbat massacre
Q13530561.blurb: Militants storm a high-altitude mountaineering base camp near Nanga Parbat in Gilgit–Baltistan, Pakistan, killing ten climbers and a local guide.

Q13534617.name: Immaculate Reception
Q13534617.blurb: The Immaculate Reception is caught by Franco Harris to win the Pittsburgh Steelers their first ever playoff victory, after defeating the Oakland Raiders.

Q13554386.name: Siege of Rome
Q13554386.blurb: The Ostrogoths, under King Totila, conquer Rome after a long siege, by bribing the Isaurian garrison.

Q13557549.name: Annexation of Tibet by the People's Republic of China
aliases: Incorporation of Tibet into the People's Republic of China
People's Republic of China annexation of Tibet
Q13557549.blurb: Annexation of Tibet by the People's Republic of China: The People's Liberation Army ceases all military operations in Tibet, ending the Battle of Chamdo.

Q13559823.name: June 2013 Xinjiang Riots
Q13559823.blurb: Riots in China's Xinjiang region kill at least 36 people and injure 21 others.

Q13580335.name: Baga massacre
Q13580335.blurb: The 2013 Baga massacre is started when Boko Haram militants engage government soldiers in Baga.

Q13581412.name: Yarnell Hill Fire
Q13581412.blurb: Nineteen firefighters die controlling a wildfire near Yarnell, Arizona.

Q13593376.name: 2013 Aceh earthquake
Q13593376.blurb: A magnitude 6.1 earthquake strikes Aceh, Indonesia, killing at least 42 people and injuring 420 others.

Q13605743.name: 2013 Egyptian coup d'état
aliases: International reaction to the 2013 Egyptian coup d'état
International reactions to the 2013 Egyptian coup d'état
Removal of Mohamed Morsi from office
Q13605743.blurb: President of Egypt Mohamed Morsi is removed from office by the military after four days of protests all over the country calling for his resignation, to which he did not respond. The president of the Supreme Constitutional Court of Egypt, Adly Mansour, is declared acting president until further elections are held.

Q13627958.name: Lac-Mégantic derailment
Q13627958.blurb: A 73-car oil train derails in the town of Lac-Mégantic, Quebec and explodes into flames, killing at least 47 people and destroying more than 30 buildings in the town's central area.

Q13628966.name: Asiana Airlines Flight 214
aliases: Asiana Boeing 777 crashes upon landing at San Francisco International Airport
Q13628966.blurb: A Boeing 777 operating as Asiana Airlines Flight 214 crashes at San Francisco International Airport, killing three and injuring 181 of the 307 people on board.

Q13634057.name: Soap Box Derby
Q13634057.blurb: The first All-American Soap Box Derby is held in Dayton, Ohio.

Q13634281.name: Yobe State school shooting
Q13634281.blurb: At least 42 people are killed in a shooting at a school in Yobe State, Nigeria.

Q13642546.name: 2013 Rediske Air DHC-3 Otter crash
Q13642546.blurb: A De Havilland Otter air taxi crashes in Soldotna, Alaska, killing ten people.

Q13652394.name: Negros Revolution
Q13652394.blurb: Negrese nationalists revolt against Spanish rule and establish the short-lived Republic of Negros.

Q13835935.name: Brétigny-sur-Orge train crash
Q13835935.blurb: Six people are killed and 200 injured in a French passenger train derailment in Brétigny-sur-Orge.

Q13846599.name: Typhoon Soulik
Q13846599.blurb: Typhoon Soulik kills at least nine people and affects more than 160 million in East China and Taiwan.

Q13859829.name: 1783 Great Meteor
Q13859829.blurb: A huge fireball meteor is seen across Great Britain as it passes over the east coast.

Q14058896.name: Bihar school meal poisoning incident
Q14058896.blurb: As many as 27 children die and 25 others are hospitalized after eating lunch served at their school in eastern India.

Q14086691.name: Tang campaigns against the Western Turks
Q14086691.blurb: A qaghan of the Western Turkic Khaganate is assassinated in a Chinese palace by Eastern Turkic rivals after the approval of Tang emperor Gaozu.

Q14104517.name: Detroit bankruptcy
Q14104517.blurb: The Government of Detroit, with up to $20 billion in debt, files for the largest municipal bankruptcy in U.S. history.

Q14168886.name: 2013 Dingxi earthquakes
Q14168886.blurb: Dingxi earthquakes: A series of earthquakes in Dingxi, China, kills at least 89 people and injures more than 500 others.

Q14186580.name: 2013 Colombian clashes
Q14186580.blurb: Seventeen government soldiers are killed in an attack by FARC revolutionaries in the Colombian department of Arauca.

Q14246267.name: Santiago de Compostela derailment
Q14246267.blurb: Santiago de Compostela derailment: A high-speed train derails in Spain rounding a curve with an 80 km/h (50 mph) speed limit at 190 km/h (120 mph), killing 78 passengers.

Q14303815.name: Battle of Castle Itter
Q14303815.blurb: World War II: Battle of Castle Itter, one of only two battles in that war in which American and German troops fought cooperatively.

Q14364948.name: Granges-près-Marnand train crash
Q14364948.blurb: Two passenger trains collide in the Swiss municipality of Granges-près-Marnand near Lausanne injuring 25 people.

Q14375588.name: Taeyunkak Hotel Fire
Q14375588.blurb: A fire at the Daeyeonggak Hotel in Seoul, South Korea kills 164 people.

Q14476275.name: Tadjena massacre
Q14476275.blurb: Eighty-one people are killed by armed groups in Algeria.

Q14532654.name: 2013 Rosario gas explosion
Q14532654.blurb: A gas leak caused an explosion that collapsed a building and led to the deaths of 22 people in Rosario, Argentina.

Q14538993.name: 8 August 2013 Quetta bombing
Q14538993.blurb: A suicide bombing at a funeral in the Pakistani city of Quetta kills at least 31 people.

Q14565619.name: Battle of Shumshu
Q14565619.blurb: Soviet-Japanese War: Battle of Shumshu: Soviet forces land at Takeda Beach on Shumshu Island and launch the Battle of Shumshu; the Soviet Union's Invasion of the Kuril Islands commences.

Q14566965.name: UPS Airlines Flight 1354
Q14566965.blurb: UPS Airlines Flight 1354 crashes short of the runway at Birmingham–Shuttlesworth International Airport, killing both crew members on board.

Q14575581.name: August 2013 Rabaa massacre
Q14575581.blurb: Security forces raided two camps of supporters of the ousted Egyptian president Mohamed Morsi in Cairo, leading to the deaths of at least 595 civilians.

Q14624806.name: Dhamara Ghat train accident
Q14624806.blurb: The Dhamara Ghat train accident kills at least 37 people in the Indian state of Bihar.

Q14625613.name: Post-unification Italian brigandage
Q14625613.blurb: Pica Law (Legge Pica), a form of martial law, is established as the Italian government passes this anti-brigandage law to suppress resistance to Italian Unification.

Q14626794.name: August 2013 Ghouta chemical attack
Q14626794.blurb: Hundreds of people are reported killed by chemical attacks in the Ghouta region of Syria.

Q14656243.name: 2013 Palmasola prison riot
Q14656243.blurb: A riot at the Palmasola prison complex in Santa Cruz, Bolivia kills 31 people.

Q14680788.name: Colbert raid
Q14680788.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Colbert's Raid: A Spanish garrison under Captain Jacobo du Breuil defeat British irregulars at Arkansas Post.

Q14690569.name: Heath High School shooting
Q14690569.blurb: Fourteen-year-old Michael Carneal opens fire at a group of students in Heath High School in West Paducah, Kentucky, killing three and injuring five.

Q14706162.name: assassination of Meir Kahane
Q14706162.blurb: Rabbi Meir Kahane, founder of the far-right Kach movement, is shot dead after a speech at a New York City hotel.

Q14711893.name: United Airlines Flight 2860
Q14711893.blurb: United Airlines Flight 2860 crashes near Kaysville, Utah, killing all three crew members on board.

Q14714402.name: 1972 Lake Winnebago mid-air collision
Q14714402.blurb: A Convair CV-580 and De Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter collide above Lake Winnebago near Appleton, Wisconsin, killing 13.

Q14714675.name: Blackwater fire of 1937
Q14714675.blurb: A lightning strike starts the Blackwater Fire of 1937 in Shoshone National Forest, killing 15 firefighters within three days and prompting the United States Forest Service to develop their smokejumper program.

Q14716050.name: Worcester Cold Storage Warehouse fire
Q14716050.blurb: In Worcester, Massachusetts, firefighters responded to a fire at the Worcester Cold Storage and Warehouse Co. facility, which takes the lives of 6 firefighters.

Q14746872.name: Syrian revolution
aliases: civil uprising phase of the Syrian Revolution

Q14756553.name: 1971 Ibrox disaster
Q14756553.blurb: The second Ibrox disaster kills 66 fans at a Rangers-Celtic association football match.

Q14766991.name: violence against Muslims in independent India
Q14766991.blurb: Anti-Muslim riots break out in Calcutta, in response to anti-Hindu riots in East Pakistan. About one hundred people are killed.

Q14774038.name: Sugarloaf Massacre
Q14774038.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Sugarloaf massacre: A small detachment of militia from Northampton County, Pennsylvania, are attacked by Native Americans and Loyalists near Little Nescopeck Creek.

Q14778492.name: Aeroflot Flight 528
Q14778492.blurb: Aeroflot Flight N-528 crashes at Berdiansk Airport in present-day Ukraine, killing eight people.

Q14814571.name: Twilight Zone accident
Q14814571.blurb: A helicopter crashed during the filming of Twilight Zone: The Movie in Valencia, California, killing actor Vic Morrow and two child actors.

Q14874259.name: Nicoll Highway collapse
Q14874259.blurb: An incomplete tunnel leading to the Nicoll Highway MRT station in Singapore collapsed, resulting in four deaths and the station's relocation.

Q14875706.name: MK Airlines Flight 1602
Q14875706.blurb: MK Airlines Flight 1602 crashes during takeoff from Halifax Stanfield International Airport, killing all seven people on board.

Q14916841.name: Yumiko-chan incident
Q14916841.blurb: A white U.S. soldier raped and murdered a five-year-old local girl in Kadena, Okinawa.

Q14918135.name: Washington Navy Yard shooting
Q14918135.blurb: A gunman kills twelve people at the Washington Navy Yard in Washington, D.C.

Q14927387.name: Typhoon Usagi
Q14927387.blurb: Twenty-five people are killed after Typhoon Usagi passes Hong Kong and China.

Q14934902.name: Milperra massacre
Q14934902.blurb: Seven people are shot and killed and 12 wounded in the Milperra massacre, a shootout between the rival motorcycle gangs Bandidos and Comancheros in Sydney, Australia.

Q14941568.name: Westgate shopping mall shooting
Q14941568.blurb: Unidentified gunmen began a three-day attack on the upmarket Westgate shopping mall in Nairobi, Kenya, resulting in the deaths of 67 people with at least another 175 wounded.

Q14941833.name: Peshawar church bombing
Q14941833.blurb: At least 75 people are killed in a suicide bombing at a Christian church in Peshawar, Pakistan.

Q14943147.name: destruction of Syria's chemical weapons
Q14943147.blurb: The last of Syria's declared chemical weapons are shipped out for destruction.

Q14944216.name: 2013 Balochistan earthquakes
Q14944216.blurb: A 7.7-magnitude earthquake strikes southern Pakistan, killing at least 327 people.

Q14954807.name: 22 January 2007 Baghdad bombings
Q14954807.blurb: At least 88 people are killed when two car bombs explode in the Bab Al-Sharqi market in central Baghdad, Iraq.

Q14972756.name: Gujba college massacre
Q14972756.blurb: Over 42 people are killed by members of Boko Haram at the College of Agriculture in Nigeria.

Q15040730.name: 1986 Aerovias Guatemala air crash
Q15040730.blurb: An Aerovías Sud Aviation Caravelle crashes on approach to Mundo Maya International Airport in Flores, Petén, Guatemala, killing all 94 people on board.

Q15041902.name: 2013 Mediterranean Sea migrant shipwreck
Q15041902.blurb: At least 360 migrants are killed when their boat sinks near the Italian island of Lampedusa.

Q15071846.name: 2013 Philippines earthquake
Q15071846.blurb: A 7.2-magnitude earthquake struck Bohol in the Philippines, resulting in 222 deaths.

Q15073008.name: 2013 Madhya Pradesh stampede
Q15073008.blurb: A stampede occurs in India during the Hindu festival Navratri, killing 115 and injuring more than 110.

Q15075468.name: Lao Airlines Flight 301
Q15075468.blurb: Lao Airlines Flight 301 crashes on approach to Pakse International Airport in Laos, killing 49 people.

Q15080583.name: 1993 Tehran mid-air collision
Q15080583.blurb: An Iran Air Tours Tupolev Tu-154 and an Iranian Air Force Sukhoi Su-24 collide mid-air near Qods, Iran, killing all 133 people on board both aircraft.

Q15081036.name: 2013 Buenos Aires train crash
Q15081036.blurb: One hundred and five people are injured in a train crash in Buenos Aires.

Q15092854.name: 1991 Paris Peace Accords
aliases: Agreements on a Comprehensive Political Settlement of the Cambodia Conflict
Q15092854.blurb: Signing of the Paris Peace Accords which ends the Cambodian–Vietnamese War.

Q15106049.name: Sabena Flight 571
Q15106049.blurb: Four members of Black September hijacked Sabena Flight 571 to demand the release of 315 Palestinians convicted on terrorism charges.

Q15109939.name: Rojava–Islamist conflict (2013–present)
Q15109939.blurb: Syrian civil war: The Battle of Ras al-Ayn resumes between the People's Protection Units (YPG) and Islamist forces, beginning the Rojava–Islamist conflict.

Q15116212.name: 2013 Tiananmen Square car attack
Q15116212.blurb: Five people are killed and 38 are injured after a car crashes into barriers at Tiananmen Square in China.

Q15136651.name: Typhoon Haiyan
Q15136651.blurb: Typhoon Haiyan, one of the strongest tropical cyclones ever recorded, strikes the Visayas region of the Philippines; the storm left at least 6,340 people dead with over 1,000 still missing, and caused $2.86 billion (2013 USD; equivalent to $3.95 billion in 2025) in damage.

Q15145481.name: Battle of Cartagena de Indias
Q15145481.blurb: Sir Francis Drake with an English force captures and occupies the Spanish colonial port of Cartagena de Indias for two months, obtaining a ransom and booty.

Q15178350.name: Siege of Fort Wayne
Q15178350.blurb: War of 1812: The Siege of Fort Wayne begins when Chief Winamac's forces attack two soldiers returning from the fort's outhouses.

Q15179354.name: Alikianos executions
Q15179354.blurb: World War II: German paratroopers murder Greek civilians in the villages of Kondomari and Alikianos.

Q15196571.name: Action of 18 June 1799
Q15196571.blurb: Action of 18 June 1799: A frigate squadron under Rear-admiral Jean-Baptiste Perrée is captured by the British fleet under Lord Keith.

Q15197370.name: Battle of Nazareth
Q15197370.blurb: World War I: The Battle of Nazareth ended with the British Empire victorious over the Ottomans.

Q15197384.name: Battle of Orgreave
Q15197384.blurb: A major clash between about 5,000 police and a similar number of striking miners takes place at Orgreave, South Yorkshire, during the 1984–85 UK miners' strike.

Q15198571.name: Tatarstan Airlines Flight 363
Q15198571.blurb: Fifty people are killed when Tatarstan Airlines Flight 363 crashes at Kazan Airport, Russia.

Q15211039.name: 2013 Iranian embassy bombing
Q15211039.blurb: A double suicide bombing at the Iranian embassy in Beirut kills 23 people and injures 160 others.

Q15213260.name: death of James Dean
Q15213260.blurb: American film actor James Dean suffered fatal injuries in a head-on car accident near Cholame, California.

Q15220536.name: Riga supermarket roof collapse
Q15220536.blurb: Fifty-four people are killed when the roof of a shopping center collapses in Riga, Latvia.

Q15222832.name: Aeroflot Flight 51
Q15222832.blurb: Aeroflot Flight L-51 crashes near Liepāja International Airport in Liepāja, Latvia, killing 43.

Q15222844.name: 1978 cyclone in Eastern province (Sri Lanka)
Q15222844.blurb: Cyclone kills about 1,000 people in eastern Sri Lanka.

Q15224161.name: Caungula air disaster
Q15224161.blurb: A Lockheed L-188 Electra crashes in Jamba, Cuando, Angola, killing 141 people.

Q15224558.name: Euromaidan
aliases: Prelude to the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2014
Q15224558.blurb: Dozens of Euromaidan anti-government protesters die in Ukraine's capital Kyiv, many reportedly killed by snipers.

Q15229396.name: Joint Plan of Action
Q15229396.blurb: Iran signs an interim agreement with the P5+1 countries, limiting its nuclear program in exchange for reduced sanctions.

Q15242981.name: Loughinisland massacre
Q15242981.blurb: The Troubles: Members of the Ulster Volunteer Force (UVF) attack a crowded pub with assault rifles in Loughinisland, Northern Ireland. Six Catholic civilians are killed and five wounded. It was crowded with people watching the 1994 FIFA World Cup.

Q15243731.name: 2013–14 Thai political crisis
Q15243731.blurb: Prayut Chan-o-cha (pictured), the commander-in-chief of the Royal Thai Army, launched a coup d'état against the caretaker government following six months of political crisis.

Q15253897.name: 1918 protest in Zagreb
Q15253897.blurb: National Guards and Sokol volunteers protested in Zagreb, leading to an armed clash with regiments of the Home Guard and former Common Army.

Q15260756.name: LAM Mozambique Airlines Flight 470
Q15260756.blurb: LAM Mozambique Airlines 470 crashes in the Bwabata National Park in a pilot mass murder-suicide, killing all 33 people on board.

Q15264163.name: Operation Hydra (1943)
Q15264163.blurb: World War II: The Royal Air Force begins Operation Hydra, the first air raid of the Operation Crossbow strategic bombing campaign against Germany's V-weapon program.

Q15274532.name: 1982 Salang Tunnel fire
Q15274532.blurb: The Salang Tunnel fire in Afghanistan kills 150–2000 people.

Q15281242.name: 2013 Sana'a attack
Q15281242.blurb: Militants attack a Defense Ministry compound in Sanaa, Yemen, killing at least 56 people and injuring 200 others.

Q15292454.name: December 2013 Bintaro train crash
Q15292454.blurb: At least seven are dead and 63 are injured following a train accident near Bintaro, Indonesia.

Q15293256.name: 2013 Little India riot
Q15293256.blurb: Riots break out in Singapore, after a fatal accident in Little India.

Q15353665.name: South Sudanese Civil War
aliases: Sexual violence in the South Sudanese Civil War
Q15353665.blurb: A reported coup attempt in South Sudan leads to continued fighting and hundreds of casualties.

Q15360475.name: Parañaque bus accident
Q15360475.blurb: A bus falls from an elevated highway in Manila, capital of the Philippines, killing at least 18 people with 20 injured.

Q15401938.name: Truce of Focșani
Q15401938.blurb: World War I: The Kingdom of Romania signs the Armistice of Focșani with the Central Powers.

Q15407469.name: 1961 President Airlines Douglas DC-6 crash
Q15407469.blurb: A President Airlines Douglas DC-6 crashes just after takeoff from Shannon Airport, Ireland. All 83 passengers and crew are killed.

Q15421709.name: 2013 Irkutsk Antonov An-12 crash
Q15421709.blurb: An Irkut-Avia Antonov An-12 crashes on approach to Irkutsk Northwest Airport, killing all nine people on board.

Q15427640.name: 1921 Women's World Games
Q15427640.blurb: The 1921 Women's Olympiad begins in Monte Carlo, becoming the first international women's sports event.

Q15456623.name: December 2013 Volgograd bombings
Q15456623.blurb: A suicide bomb attack at the Volgograd-1 railway station in the southern Russian city of Volgograd kills at least 18 people and wounds 40 others.

Q15473934.name: Siege of Kaifeng (1232)
Q15473934.blurb: Mongol–Jin War: The Mongols begin their siege on Kaifeng, the capital of the Jin dynasty.

Q15489392.name: Second Battle of Wissembourg
Q15489392.blurb: Second Battle of Wissembourg: France defeats Austria.

Q15499423.name: December 2013 Kinshasa attacks
Q15499423.blurb: More than 100 people are killed when anti-government forces attack key buildings in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Q15542964.name: Italian War of 1542–46 Un penesote
Q15542964.blurb: Italian War of 1542–46: A French army defeats Habsburg forces at the Battle of Ceresole, but fails to exploit its victory.

Q15618496.name: Benefits Street
Q15618496.blurb: The first episode of the documentary series Benefits Street aired on Channel 4, prompting discussion in the United Kingdom about welfare dependency.

Q15621133.name: 1952 Moses Lake C-124 crash
Q15621133.blurb: A United States Air Force C-124 crashes and burns in Moses Lake, Washington, killing 87 of the 115 people on board.

Q15621252.name: Aeroflot Flight 3603
Q15621252.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 3603 crashes during landing at Norilsk Airport, killing 99.

Q15632253.name: 1893 New Zealand general election
Q15632253.blurb: Women's suffrage in New Zealand concludes with the 1893 New Zealand general election.

Q15634716.name: June 2013 Egyptian protests
Q15634716.blurb: Protests begin around Egypt against President Mohamed Morsi and the ruling Freedom and Justice Party, leading to their overthrow during the 2013 Egyptian coup d'état.

Q15637808.name: coronation of Queen Victoria
Q15637808.blurb: Coronation of Queen Victoria of the United Kingdom.

Q15642802.name: Aeroflot Flight 2230
Q15642802.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 2230 crashes near Koltsovo Airport, killing 107.

Q15647805.name: Struma disaster
Q15647805.blurb: Seven hundred ninety-one Romanian Jewish refugees and crew members are killed after the MV Struma is torpedoed by the Soviet Navy.

Q15650559.name: War of the Catalans
Q15650559.blurb: Siege of Barcelona: Barcelona, capital city of the Principality of Catalonia, surrenders to Spanish and French Bourbon armies in the War of the Catalans, the last phase of the War of the Spanish Succession.

Q15662857.name: 1995 Alaska Boeing E-3 Sentry accident
Q15662857.blurb: An E-3B AWACS crashes outside Elmendorf Air Force Base, Alaska after multiple bird strikes to two of the four engines soon after takeoff; all 24 on board are killed.

Q15665692.name: Prince of Anhua rebellion
Q15665692.blurb: The Prince of Anhua rebellion begins when Zhu Zhifan kills all the officials invited to a banquet and declares his intent on ousting the powerful Ming dynasty eunuch Liu Jin during the reign of the Zhengde Emperor.

Q15678865.name: Northwest Airlines Flight 421
Q15678865.blurb: Northwest Airlines Flight 421 crashes in Fountain City, Wisconsin, killing all 37 aboard.

Q15692881.name: Siege of Caizhou
Q15692881.blurb: Caizhou, the capital of the Jin dynasty, was captured by the Mongol Empire and their Song allies, bringing an end to Jurchen rule.

Q15700578.name: Khabarovsk United Air Group Flight 3949
Q15700578.blurb: Khabarovsk United Air Group Flight 3949 crashes into the Bo-Dzhausa Mountain, killing 98.

Q15708337.name: 2014 Moscow school shooting
Q15708337.blurb: A school shooting in Moscow, Russia leaves two people dead and one wounded.

Q15726739.name: 2014 Algerian Air Force C-130 crash
aliases: Algerian Air Force accident on 11 February 2014
Lockheed C-130H-30 Hercules accident on 11 February 2014
Q15726739.blurb: A military transport plane crashes in a mountainous area of Oum El Bouaghi Province in eastern Algeria, killing 77 people.

Q15727158.name: August 2013 Beirut bombing
Q15727158.blurb: At least 27 people are killed and 226 injured in an explosion in southern Beirut near a complex used by Lebanon's militant group Hezbollah in Lebanon. A previously unknown Syrian Sunni group claims responsibility in an online video.

Q15729274.name: 1951 Miami Airlines C-46 crash
Q15729274.blurb: A Miami Airlines Curtiss C-46 Commando crashes in Elizabeth, New Jersey, killing all 58 aboard including dancer Doris Ruby.

Q15732645.name: Coronation of Edward VII and Alexandra
aliases: Coronation of King Edward VII and Queen Alexandra
Q15732645.blurb: In a ceremony at Westminster Abbey, Edward VII and Alexandra were crowned King and Queen of the United Kingdom and the British Dominions, and Emperor and Empress of India.

Q15733401.name: Revolution of Dignity
aliases: Blockage of the traffic in Ukraine (February 2014)
Q15733401.blurb: Revolution of Dignity: At least 76 people are killed and hundreds are injured in clashes between riot police and demonstrators in Kyiv, Ukraine.

Q15788823.name: Bitburg controversy
Q15788823.blurb: Ronald Reagan visits the military cemetery at Bitburg and the site of the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp, where he makes a speech.

Q15838763.name: 2014 Crimean status referendum
Q15838763.blurb: Crimea votes in a controversial referendum to secede from Ukraine to join Russia.

Q15856657.name: 2014 Kunming attack
Q15856657.blurb: Thirty-five people are killed and 143 injured in a mass stabbing at Kunming Railway Station in China.

Q15860072.name: Russo-Ukrainian war
aliases: Special operation on the territory of Ukraine
2014 Military intervention of Russia in Ukraine
2014 Russian military intervention in the Ukraine
Alleged August 2014 Russian invasion of Ukraine
Historical background of the Russo-Ukrainian War
Human rights violations during the Russo-Ukrainian War
International reactions to the Russo-Ukrainian War
Military intervention of Russia in Ukraine 2014
War crimes in the Russo-Ukrainian war
Q15860072.blurb: Russo-Ukrainian War: Days after recognising Donetsk and Luhansk as independent states, Russian president Vladimir Putin orders the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine.

Q15871713.name: 2014 pro-Russian unrest in Ukraine
aliases: 2014 unrest in southern and eastern Ukraine
List of states that declared independence during the unrest in East Ukraine
Q15871713.blurb: Russo-Ukrainian War: Forty-eight people were killed during a confrontation between pro-Russian protesters and pro-Ukrainian unity protesters in the southern Ukrainian port city of Odesa.

Q15902820.name: Typhoon Ellen
Q15902820.blurb: Typhoon Ellen dissipated after destroying hundreds of homes across Hong Kong and the Philippines.

Q15904347.name: Final Battle of San Salvador
Q15904347.blurb: Dutch–Portuguese War: Second Battle of San Salvador: The Dutch force the Spanish garrison at San Salvador (modern day Keelung, Taiwan) to surrender, ending the short-lived Spanish colony on Formosa and replacing it with a new Dutch administration.

Q15907682.name: rescue of Roger Mallinson and Roger Chapman
Q15907682.blurb: A 76-hour multinational rescue effort in the Celtic Sea resulted in the Rescue of Roger Mallinson and Roger Chapman.

Q15908324.name: Malaysia Airlines Flight 370
Q15908324.blurb: In one of aviation's greatest mysteries, Malaysia Airlines Flight 370, carrying a total of 239 people, disappears en route from Kuala Lumpur to Beijing. The fate of the flight remains unknown.

Q15911326.name: Malaysia Airlines Flight 2133
Q15911326.blurb: Malaysia Airlines Flight 2133 crashes at Tawau Airport in Malaysia, killing 34.

Q15920546.name: Russian annexation of Crimea
aliases: Accession of Autonomous Republic of Crimea and the city of Sevastopol to the Russian Federation
Accession of Crimea and Sevastopol to the Russian Federation
Accession of Crimea to the Russia Federation
Accession of Crimea to the Russian Federation
Annexation of Crimea by the Russian Federation
Annexation of Crimea to the Russian Federation
Annexation of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea
Annexation or Accession of Crimea to the Russian Federation
Incorporation of Crimea into the Russian Federation
Incorporation of the Republic of Crimea into the Russian Federation
Persecution of Crimean Tatars by the Russian Federation
Regaining of Crimea by the Russian Federation
Reunification of Crimea with the Russian Federation
Reunification of Republic of Crimea and Sevastopol with Russia
Treaty on Accession of the Republic of Crimea to Russia
Treaty on the Accession of Crimea to Russia
Treaty on the Adoption of the Republic of Crimea to Russia
Q15920546.blurb: The parliaments of Russia and Crimea sign an accession treaty.

Q15924516.name: Alia Royal Jordanian Flight 600
Q15924516.blurb: Alia Royal Jordanian Flight 600 crashes at Doha International Airport, killing 45 people.

Q15926885.name: 2014 FIFA World Cup Final
Q15926885.blurb: Germany won the FIFA World Cup final against Argentina, with Mario Götze scoring the game's only goal (pictured) in the extra time.

Q15930212.name: 2014 East Harlem gas explosion
aliases: 2014 explosion of apartment buildings in East Harlem
Q15930212.blurb: A gas explosion in the New York City neighborhood of East Harlem kills eight and injures 70 others.

Q15935778.name: 1668 Shandong earthquake
Q15935778.blurb: A magnitude 8.5 earthquake strikes eastern China, killing over 43,000 people.

Q15942402.name: Formosa Airlines Flight 7601
Q15942402.blurb: Sixteen people are killed when Formosa Airlines Flight 7601 crashes near Beigan Airport in the Matsu Islands of Taiwan.

Q15948989.name: Indian Airlines Flight 171
Q15948989.blurb: Indian Airlines Flight 171 crashes at Santacruz Airport in Bombay, India, killing 95.

Q15961958.name: Aeroflot Flight 3519
Q15961958.blurb: After experiencing an engine fire, Aeroflot Flight 3519 attempts to make an emergency landing at Krasnoyarsk International Airport but crashes, killing 110 of the 111 people on board.

Q15972178.name: 2014 Kabul Serena Hotel attack
Q15972178.blurb: Four suspected Taliban members attack the Kabul Serena Hotel, killing at least nine people.

Q15978276.name: Oso mudslide
Q15978276.blurb: A massive landslide in Oso, Washington, killed 43 people after engulfing a rural neighborhood, the largest death toll for a standalone landslide in U.S. history.

Q15989108.name: Western African Ebola virus epidemic
aliases: 2014 Ebola virus epidemic in West Africa
Ebola virus epidemic in West Africa
Ebola outbreak in West Africa in 2014
Ebola virus disease cases in Nigeria
Ebola virus outbreak in West Africa in 2014
West African Ebola virus disease epidemic
Q15989108.blurb: The World Health Organization declared the Western African Ebola epidemic, which began in December 2013, to be a public health emergency of international concern.

Q15991222.name: Independence of Singapore Agreement 1965
aliases: Agreement Relating to the Separation of Singapore from Malaysia as an Independent and Sovereign State
Q15991222.blurb: The State of Singapore separated from the Malaysian federation due to a heated ideological conflict between their ruling parties.[citation needed][needs copy edit]

Q15994229.name: Lufthansa Flight 615
Q15994229.blurb: The three surviving perpetrators of the Munich massacre are released from prison in exchange for the hostages of the hijacked Lufthansa Flight 615.

Q16000534.name: 1068 Near East earthquake
Q16000534.blurb: An earthquake in the Levant and the Arabian Peninsula leaves up to 20,000 dead.

Q16000629.name: 1901 Black Sea earthquake
Q16000629.blurb: A magnitude 7.2 earthquake struck the Black Sea, the most powerful ever recorded in the area.

Q16013569.name: murder of Fernando Balderas Sánchez and Yolanda Figueroa
aliases: Fernando Balderas Sánchez and Yolanda Figueroa killing
Fernando Balderas Sánchez and Yolanda Figueroa murder
Fernando Balderas Sánchez and Yolanda Figueroa's killing
Fernando Balderas Sánchez and Yolanda Figueroa's murder
killing of Fernando Balderas Sánchez and Yolanda Figueroa
Q16013569.blurb: Journalists Fernando Balderas Sánchez and Yolanda Figueroa and their three children are murdered in a case that initially prompted speculation about links to organized crime, corruption, or their journalistic work.

Q16015460.name: murder of Milly Dowler
Q16015460.blurb: The last edition of the British tabloid News of the World was published, closing due to allegations that it hacked the voicemails of murdered schoolgirl Milly Dowler, victims of the 7/7 attacks and relatives of deceased British soldiers.

Q16016666.name: 2014 Fort Hood shooting
Q16016666.blurb: A spree shooting occurs at the Fort Hood army base in Texas, with four dead, including the gunman, and 16 others injured.

Q16017561.name: Goleta postal facility shootings
Q16017561.blurb: The Goleta postal facility shootings occur, killing seven people before the perpetrator took her own life.

Q16052990.name: 1989 Iranian Supreme Leader election
Q16052990.blurb: In the 1989 Iranian supreme leader election, Ali Khamenei is elected as the new Supreme Leader of Iran after the death and funeral of Ruhollah Khomeini.

Q16056284.name: Chilembwe Uprising
Q16056284.blurb: Rebels led by John Chilembwe attacked local plantation owners, beginning an uprising regarded as a key moment in the history of Malawi.

Q16056961.name: 1940 Field Marshal Ceremony
Q16056961.blurb: Field Marshal Ceremony: First occasion in World War II that Adolf Hitler appoints field marshals due to military achievements.

Q16057002.name: 1961 Commonwealth Prime Ministers' Conference
Q16057002.blurb: At the 1961 Commonwealth Prime Ministers' Conference, South Africa announces that it will withdraw from the Commonwealth when the South African Constitution of 1961 comes into effect.

Q16057076.name: 1981 Iraqi embassy bombing
Q16057076.blurb: A suicide car bombing targeting the Iraqi embassy in Beirut, Lebanon, levels the embassy and kills 61 people, including Iraq's ambassador to Lebanon. The attack is considered the first modern suicide bombing.

Q16057118.name: 1991 Rudrapur bombings
Q16057118.blurb: Rudrapur bombings by Sikh separatists, who explode two bombs, during a Ramlila Hindu celebration in Rudrapur, Uttarakhand, killing 41 people.

Q16057343.name: 2013 Mahabubnagar bus accident
Q16057343.blurb: Forty-five people are killed and seven injured after a bus catches fire in Mahabubnagar district, Andhra Pradesh (present-day Telangana), India.

Q16057426.name: 2014 Medina hotel fire
Q16057426.blurb: A hotel fire in Medina, Saudi Arabia, kills 15 Egyptian pilgrims with 130 others injured.

Q16058056.name: Action of 6 May 1801
Q16058056.blurb: Captain Thomas Cochrane in the 14-gun HMS Speedy captures the 32-gun Spanish frigate El Gamo.

Q16062345.name: 1983 Argentine general election
Q16062345.blurb: The first democratic elections in Argentina, after seven years of military rule, are held.

Q16116167.name: 1918 occupation of Međimurje
Q16116167.blurb: Region of Međimurje is captured by the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes from Hungary.

Q16146777.name: 1984 US embassy bombing in Beirut
Q16146777.blurb: A suicide bomber in a car attacks the U.S. embassy in Beirut, Lebanon, killing twenty-two people.

Q16146801.name: Invasion of Darfur
Q16146801.blurb: A British army defeats a force of the Darfur Sultanate under Sultan Ali Dinar due to its superior firepower in the battle of Beringia.

Q16148527.name: armistice between Russia and the Central Powers
Q16148527.blurb: World War I: An armistice between Russia and the Central Powers is signed.

Q16149795.name: impeachment of Andrew Johnson
Q16149795.blurb: Impeachment of Andrew Johnson: President Andrew Johnson is acquitted by one vote in the United States Senate.

Q16150804.name: Act Anent the demission of the Crown in favour of our Sovereign Lord, and his Majesty's Coronation 1567
Q16150804.blurb: Mary, Queen of Scots, is forced to abdicate and be replaced by her one-year-old son James VI.

Q16151533.name: 2009 Honduran constitutional crisis
Q16151533.blurb: The 2009 Honduran constitutional crisis ends when Porfirio Lobo Sosa becomes the new President of Honduras.

Q16155782.name: 1899 Carrabelle hurricane
Q16155782.blurb: A Category 1 hurricane (map pictured) made landfall in Azua Province in the Dominican Republic, destroying three large schooners at Santo Domingo; only one crew member on the three vessels survived.

Q16155921.name: 1913 Great Meteor Procession
Q16155921.blurb: A group of meteors is visible across much of the eastern seaboard of the Americas, leading astronomers to conclude the source had been a small, short-lived natural satellite of the Earth.

Q16156276.name: 2016 Democratic National Convention
Q16156276.blurb: Hillary Clinton becomes the first female nominee for president of the United States by a major political party at the Democratic National Convention in Philadelphia.

Q16158139.name: Action of Faial
Q16158139.blurb: The Action of Faial, Azores. The Portuguese carrack Cinco Chagas, loaded with slaves and treasure, is attacked and sunk by English ships with only 13 survivors out of over 700 on board.

Q16158877.name: Battle of Alamance
Q16158877.blurb: The Battle of Alamance, a pre-American Revolutionary War battle between local militia and a group of rebels called The "Regulators", occurs in present-day Alamance County, North Carolina.

Q16165653.name: retreat of the government of Republic of China to Taiwan
Q16165653.blurb: Chinese Civil War: The Government of the Republic of China moves from Nanjing to Taipei, Taiwan.

Q16173877.name: Seongsu Bridge collapse
Q16173877.blurb: In Seoul, South Korea, 32 people are killed when a span of the Seongsu Bridge collapses.

Q16176384.name: Kantō Massacre
Q16176384.blurb: Kantō Massacre: Amid rumors that Koreans had been conducting acts of sabotage in the aftermath of the 1923 Great Kantō earthquake, lynch mobs of Japanese begin massacring thousands of civilians over the course of several weeks, mainly ethnic minorities such as Koreans and Chinese.

Q16202320.name: Pakistan International Airlines Flight 404
aliases: 1989 Pakistan International Airlines Fokker Friendship disappearance
Q16202320.blurb: Pakistan International Airlines Flight 404, carrying 54 people, disappears over the Himalayas after takeoff from Gilgit Airport in Pakistan. The aircraft was never found.

Q16204297.name: 2003 Etobicoke gas explosion
Q16204297.blurb: A backhoe breached a pipeline in Toronto, Canada, which caused a gas explosion that killed seven people.

Q16205928.name: 1966 Nigerian coup d'etat
Q16205928.blurb: The First Nigerian Republic, led by Abubakar Tafawa Balewa is overthrown in a military coup d'état.

Q16207110.name: Battle of Canton
Q16207110.blurb: Second Opium War: Dissatisfied with imperial commissioner Ye Mingchen's reparations for the alleged slighting of a British-owned vessel and at Consul Harry Parkes's urging, British Rear-Admiral Michael Seymour launches an assault on the Barrier Forts outside Canton in the first military engagement of the Second Opium War.

Q16207122.name: Battle of Chios
Q16207122.blurb: A Knights Hospitaller fleet scores a crushing victory over an Aydinid fleet off Chios.

Q16207219.name: Battle of Narela
Q16207219.blurb: Forces of the Maratha Empire are defeated by the Durrani Empire in the Battle of Narela.

Q16209266.name: Corporate Air Services HPF821
Q16209266.blurb: Eugene Hasenfus's plane was shot down by Nicaraguan forces while carrying weapons to the Contra rebels on behalf of the U.S. government; he was subsequently captured, leading to an international controversy.

Q16210048.name: 2013 Hawija clashes
Q16210048.blurb: At least 111 people are killed and 233 injured as violence breaks out in Hawija, Iraq.

Q16210239.name: 19 March 2013 Iraq attacks
Q16210239.blurb: A series of bombings and shootings kills at least 98 people and injures 240 others across Iraq.

Q16210461.name: Kawit shooting
Q16210461.blurb: A gunman kills eight people in a house-to-house rampage in Kawit, Cavite, Philippines.

Q16211090.name: Newhall massacre
Q16211090.blurb: Newhall massacre: Four California Highway Patrol officers are killed in a shootout.

Q16211294.name: Opération 14 juillet
Q16211294.blurb: French DGSE personnel abort an operation to rescue Íngrid Betancourt from FARC rebels in Colombia, causing a political scandal when details are leaked to the press.

Q16211460.name: June 2013 Quetta attacks
Q16211460.blurb: A bomb explodes on a bus in the Pakistani city of Quetta, killing at least 25 people and wounding 22 others.

Q16219320.name: Aeroflot Flight 1802
Q16219320.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 1802 crashes near Viktorivka, Chernihiv Raion, Chernihiv Oblast, killing 52.

Q16238739.name: Siege of Athlone
Q16238739.blurb: A Williamite army under Godert de Ginkell takes the city of Athlone from the Jacobites after a short siege.

Q16240286.name: 1965 Palm Sunday tornado outbreak
Q16240286.blurb: The Palm Sunday tornado outbreak of 1965: Fifty-five tornadoes hit in six Midwestern states of the United States, killing 266 people.

Q16240353.name: 1976 Conference of Communist and Workers Parties of Europe
Q16240353.blurb: The Conference of Communist and Workers Parties of Europe convenes in East Berlin.

Q16242999.name: Apartheid-era South Africa and the Olympics
Q16242999.blurb: South Africa is banned from the Olympic Games due to the country's racist policies.

Q16243583.name: Battle of Pantelleria
Q16243583.blurb: Anglo–Spanish War: A convoy of English ships from the Levant Company manage to repel a fleet of eleven Spanish and Maltese galleys off the Mediterranean island of Pantelleria.

Q16252594.name: Bagbati massacre
Q16252594.blurb: Pakistani forces massacre over 200 civilians, mostly Bengali Hindus, in the Bagbati massacre.

Q16253733.name: Battle of Rio de Janeiro
Q16253733.blurb: Battle of Rio de Janeiro: Portuguese forces under the command of Estácio de Sá definitively drive the French out of Rio de Janeiro.

Q16256909.name: Centralia mine fire
Q16256909.blurb: The Centralia mine fire is ignited in the town's landfill above a coal mine.

Q16257379.name: 1981 Entumbane uprising
Q16257379.blurb: Rhodesian Bush War: Zimbabwe African National Liberation Army cadres in Gwelo attacked Zimbabwe People's Revolutionary Army troops, killing over 60 of them and starting the 1981 Entumbane uprising.

Q16258108.name: China Clipper
Q16258108.blurb: The China Clipper inaugurates the first commercial transpacific air service, connecting Alameda, California with Manila.

Q16324921.name: Great Fire of Valparaíso
Q16324921.blurb: The Great Fire of Valparaíso ravages the Chilean city of Valparaíso, killing 16 people, displacing nearly 10,000, and destroying more than 2,500 homes.

Q16326847.name: Overland Park Jewish Community Center shooting
Q16326847.blurb: Three people are killed in a shooting in Overland Park, Kansas.

Q16330738.name: Massacre of Kommeno
Q16330738.blurb: World War II: 317 Greek civilians are murdered by soldiers of the German 1st Mountain Division in the village of Kommeno, Greece.

Q16331929.name: Battle of Fardykambos
Q16331929.blurb: World War II: The Battle of Fardykambos, one of the first major battles between the Greek Resistance and the occupying Royal Italian Army, begins. It ends on 6 March with the surrender of an entire Italian battalion and the liberation of the town of Grevena.

Q16334391.name: April 2014 Abuja bombing
Q16334391.blurb: Two bombs detonate at a bus station in Nyanya, Nigeria, killing at least 88 people and injuring hundreds. Boko Haram claims responsibility.

Q16335075.name: War in Donbas
aliases: 2014 insurgency in Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts
International Coalition in support of Ukraine
Q16335075.blurb: War in Donbas: An Ilyushin Il-76 transport aircraft of the Ukrainian Air Force was shot down by forces of the self-proclaimed Luhansk People's Republic, killing all 49 people on board.

Q16338015.name: sinking of the MV Sewol
aliases: Sinking of the ferry MV Sewol
Q16338015.blurb: The ferry MV Sewol capsized and sank off Donggeochado, South Korea, killing 306 people, mainly students from Danwon High School.

Q16362506.name: Lithuanian Crusade
Q16362506.blurb: Lithuanian Crusade: After a month-long siege, the Teutonic Order captured and destroyed Kaunas Castle, which was defended by troops of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania.

Q16419396.name: 1975 Icelandic women's strike
Q16419396.blurb: In Iceland, 90% of women take part in a national strike, refusing to work in protest of gender inequality.

Q16426791.name: 1995 Súðavík avalanche
Q16426791.blurb: An avalanche hits the Icelandic village Súðavík, destroying 25 homes and burying 26 people, 14 of whom died.

Q16485580.name: Aeroflot Flight 200
Q16485580.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 200 crashes while attempting to land at Vnukovo International Airport, killing 28.

Q16486635.name: 1976 Anapa mid-air collision
Q16486635.blurb: Two Aeroflot flights collide in mid-air over Anapa, Soviet Union, killing 70.

Q16487613.name: Aeroflot Flight 558
Q16487613.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 558 crashes in the Abzelilovsky District in Bashkortostan, Russia (then the Soviet Union), killing all 102 people aboard.

Q16487620.name: 1992 Russian Air Force Mi-8 shootdown
Q16487620.blurb: War in Abkhazia: Siege of Tkvarcheli: A helicopter carrying evacuees from Tkvarcheli is shot down, resulting in at least 52 deaths, including 25 children. The incident catalyses more concerted Russian military intervention on behalf of Abkhazia.

Q16488142.name: Aeroflot Flight 20/101
Q16488142.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 101/X-20 crashes on approach to Alma-Ata Airport, killing 64 people.

Q16491432.name: Obligation to Negotiate Access to the Pacific Ocean
Q16491432.blurb: The International Court of Justice rules that Chile is not obliged to negotiate access to the Pacific Ocean with Bolivia.

Q16494605.name: Second Battle of the Corunna Road
Q16494605.blurb: Spanish Civil War: Nationalists and Republicans both withdraw after suffering heavy losses, ending the Second Battle of the Corunna Road.

Q16499676.name: Turkish Straits crisis
Q16499676.blurb: The Soviet Union informed Turkey that the way in which the latter was handling the Turkish Straits no longer represented the security interests of Turkey's fellow Black Sea nations, escalating the Turkish Straits crisis.

Q16529009.name: Assassination of the Duke of Berry
Q16529009.blurb: The Assassination of the Duke of Berry takes place in Paris. The Duke of Berry, nephew of Louis XVIII, is stabbed to death while attending the Paris Opera.

Q16609395.name: death and state funeral of Vladimir Lenin
Q16609395.blurb: Six days after his death, Vladimir Lenin's body is carried into a specially erected mausoleum.

Q16630128.name: Aeroflot Flight 773
Q16630128.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 773 is destroyed by a bomb over Moscow Oblast, killing 25.

Q16630286.name: French invasion of Malta
Q16630286.blurb: Following the successful French invasion of Malta, the Knights Hospitaller surrendered Malta to Napoleon, initiating two years of occupation.

Q16647239.name: Bangkok Airways Flight 125
Q16647239.blurb: Bangkok Airways Flight 125 crashes on approach to Samui Airport, killing 38.

Q16662312.name: 1991 Jakarta Indonesian Air Force C-130 crash
aliases: 1991 Indonesian Air Force Lockheed C-130 Hercules crash
Q16662312.blurb: An Indonesian Air Force C-130 crash kills 135 people.

Q16662322.name: Aeroflot Flight 315 (1959)
Q16662322.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 315 crashes on approach to Lviv Airport, killing all 40 people on board.

Q16662323.name: Aeroflot Flight 315 (1960)
Q16662323.blurb: A Kyiv-bound Aeroflot airliner crashes on approach to Snilow Airport in Lviv, killing 32 of the 33 people on board.

Q16662339.name: Aeroflot Flight 63
Q16662339.blurb: Aeroflot Flight N-63 crashes on approach to Vinnytsia Airport, killing 48.

Q16662348.name: Aeroflot Flight 601
Q16662348.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 601 crashes during takeoff from Leshukonskoye Airport, Russia, killing 44 of the 49 people on board.

Q16662368.name: Aeroflot Flight 13
Q16662368.blurb: Aeroflot Flight A-13 crashes after takeoff from Baku-Bina International Airport in Azerbaijan, killing 56 people and injuring eight.

Q16662381.name: Aeroflot Flight 1668
Q16662381.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 1668 crashes near Olyokminsk, killing 45.

Q16662450.name: Aeroflot Flight 191
Q16662450.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 191 crashes while landing at Aşgabat International Airport, killing 12.

Q16662460.name: Aeroflot Flight 1770
Q16662460.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 1770 crashes while landing at Vnukovo International Airport, killing 16.

Q16662465.name: Aeroflot Flight 15
Q16662465.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 15 crashes Irkutsk Oblast, Soviet Union, due to a loss of control. Eighty-three of the 84 occupants onboard die. The exact cause of the accident is unknown.

Q16662473.name: ČSA Flight 511
Q16662473.blurb: ČSA Flight 511 crashes at Casablanca–Anfa Airport in Morocco, killing 72.

Q16662475.name: Aeroflot Flight 36 (1960)
Q16662475.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 036 crashes in Soviet Ukraine, killing 34.

Q16662479.name: 1974 Leningrad Aeroflot Il-18 crash
Q16662479.blurb: One hundred nine people are killed in a plane crash near Pulkovo Airport.

Q16662497.name: 1988 Soviet Air Force Il-76 crash
Q16662497.blurb: A Soviet Air Force Il-76 aircraft crashes while participating in the Armenian earthquake relief, killing 78 people.

Q16662534.name: Aeroflot Flight 3739 (1976)
Q16662534.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 3739, a Tupolev Tu-104, crashes during takeoff from Irkutsk Airport, killing 24.

Q16662552.name: Aeroflot Flight 109
Q16662552.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 109 is hijacked mid-flight and the aircraft is subsequently destroyed when the hijacker's bomb explodes, killing all 82 people on board.

Q16662554.name: Aeroflot Flight 65
Q16662554.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 065 crashes during take-off from Sheremetyevo International Airport, killing 21.

Q16662560.name: Aeroflot Flight 2022
Q16662560.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 2022 crashes in the Soviet Union's (now Russia) Volokolamsky District, killing all 51 aboard, including four Lithuanian doctors.

Q16662562.name: Aeroflot Flight 3630
Q16662562.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 3630, a Tupolev Tu-124 en route from southern Russia to Lithuania, crashes after the pilots lost control of the aircraft at cruise altitude between Rostov-on-Don Airport and Vilnius Airport, on the second leg of the flight; all 37 passengers and crew are killed.

Q16662566.name: Aeroflot Flight 513
Q16662566.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 513 crashes during takeoff from Kuybyshev Airport, killing 30 and injuring 9.

Q16662578.name: Azerbaijan Airlines Flight 56
Q16662578.blurb: Azerbaijan Airlines Flight A-56 crashes near Nakhchivan International Airport in Nakhchivan, Azerbaijan, killing 52 people.

Q16662589.name: Aeroflot Flight 2306
Q16662589.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 2306 crashes while attempting an emergency landing at Syktyvkar Airport in Syktyvkar, in present-day Komi Republic, Russia, killing 54 people.

Q16662591.name: 1978 Yegoryevsk Tu-144 crash
Q16662591.blurb: A Tupolev Tu-144 crashes near the Russian town of Yegoryevsk, killing two.

Q16662594.name: Aeroflot Flight 8556
Q16662594.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 8556 crashes at Pulkovo Airport, killing 13.

Q16662596.name: 1992 Tbilisi Tupolev Tu-154 crash
Q16662596.blurb: A Tupolev Tu-154 crashes during takeoff from Tbilisi International Airport, killing all 24 aboard and four more people on the ground.

Q16662613.name: 1993 Tajik Air Yakovlev Yak-40 incident
Q16662613.blurb: A Tajikistan Airlines Yakovlev Yak-40 crashes during takeoff from Khorog Airport in Tajikistan, killing 82.

Q16662643.name: Aeroflot Flight 1080
Q16662643.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 1080 crashes after takeoff from Koltsovo International Airport, killing 38.

Q16662645.name: Aeroflot Flight X-167
Q16662645.blurb: Aeroflot Flight X-167 crashes during takeoff from Semey Airport, killing 32 people.

Q16662654.name: 1980 Plesetsk launch pad disaster
Q16662654.blurb: A Vostok-2M rocket at Plesetsk Cosmodrome Site 43 explodes during a fueling operation, killing 48 people.

Q16685818.name: 1886 eruption of Mount Tarawera
Q16685818.blurb: Mount Tarawera in New Zealand erupts, killing 153 people and burying the famous Pink and White Terraces. Eruptions continue for three months creating a large, 17 km (11 mi) long fissure across the mountain peak.

Q16725863.name: Chibok schoolgirls kidnapping
Q16725863.blurb: Boko Haram abducts 276 girls from a school in Chibok, Nigeria.

Q16741311.name: 2014 Ürümqi attack
