Q16741311.blurb: A bomb blast in Ürümqi, China kills three people and injures 79 others.

Q16743981.name: 2014 Badakhshan mudslides
Q16743981.blurb: Two mudslides in Badakhshan, Afghanistan, leave up to 2,500 people missing.

Q16820617.name: Cygnus CRS Orb-3
Q16820617.blurb: A rocket carrying NASA's Cygnus CRS Orb-3 resupply mission to the International Space Station explodes seconds after taking off from the Mid-Atlantic Regional Spaceport in Wallops Island, Virginia.

Q16821007.name: Kanalkampf
Q16821007.blurb: World War II: Six days before Adolf Hitler issues his Directive 16 to the combined Wehrmacht armed forces for Operation Sea Lion, the Kanalkampf shipping attacks begin against British maritime convoys in the leadup to initiating the Battle of Britain.

Q16821095.name: 1954 Detroit Red Wings prison game
Q16821095.blurb: The Detroit Red Wings played in the first outdoor hockey game by any NHL team in an exhibition against the Marquette Branch Prison Pirates in Marquette, Michigan.

Q16821356.name: Nottingham Blitz
Q16821356.blurb: World War II: The German Luftwaffe launches a bombing raid on Nottingham and Derby.

Q16821555.name: 2001 Ramna Batamul bombings
Q16821555.blurb: Series of bombings at Ramna Park in Dhaka during the Bengali New Year celebrations leave 10 people dead and dozens other injured.

Q16821882.name: Benton fireworks disaster
Q16821882.blurb: An explosion at an illegal fireworks factory near Benton, Tennessee, killed eleven people.

Q16822708.name: Battle of Sesimbra Bay
Q16822708.blurb: Anglo-Spanish War: The English navy defeated a Spanish–Portuguese fleet off Sesimbra, Portugal, and captured a carrack.

Q16822746.name: Battle of the Narrow Seas
aliases: Battle of the Goodwin Sands, Battle of the Dover Straits
Q16822746.blurb: Anglo-Spanish War: An English fleet intercepted and attacked six Spanish ships at the Battle of the Narrow Seas (pictured).

Q16823304.name: Birmingham riot of 1963
Q16823304.blurb: African Americans rioted in Birmingham, Alabama, in response to two bombings, perceiving local police to be complicit with the perpetrators.

Q16824925.name: Mapuche uprising of 1881
Q16824925.blurb: The Mapuche uprising of 1881 begins in Chile.

Q16825708.name: 1940 New England hurricane
Q16825708.blurb: The 1940 New England hurricane formed over the Atlantic Ocean; it would go on to cause widespread damage despite never making landfall in the United States.

Q16825829.name: 1946 American Overseas Airlines Douglas DC-4 crash
Q16825829.blurb: An American Overseas Airlines Douglas DC-4 crashes near Ernest Harmon Air Force Base in Stephenville, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada, killing 39.

Q16830128.name: Venetian Crusade
Q16830128.blurb: The city of Tyre falls to the Venetian Crusade after a siege of 19 weeks.

Q16846287.name: Iberia Airlines Flight 062
Q16846287.blurb: Iberia Flight 062 crashes in Blackdown, West Sussex, killing all 37 people on board including British actress June Thorburn.

Q16846834.name: 1907 Imperial Conference
Q16846834.blurb: Four months after the 1907 Imperial Conference, New Zealand and Newfoundland are promoted from colonies to dominions within the British Empire.

Q16848812.name: Islands Voyage
Q16848812.blurb: Islands Voyage: Robert Devereux, 2nd Earl of Essex, and Sir Walter Raleigh set sail on an expedition to the Azores.

Q16852705.name: Knight Air Flight 816
Q16852705.blurb: While attempting to return to Leeds Bradford Airport in the United Kingdom, Knight Air Flight 816 crashes in Dunkeswick, North Yorkshire, killing all 12 people on board.

Q16855053.name: revolt of Lyons
Q16855053.blurb: French Revolution: After a month-long siege, the leaders of Lyon surrendered, ending their revolt against the National Convention.

Q16855833.name: 2012 Guinea-Bissau presidential election
Q16855833.blurb: The Guinea-Bissau military seized control in a coup amid a presidential election, later handing power to a transitional administration under Manuel Serifo Nhamadjo.

Q16868874.name: 1958 C-130 shootdown
aliases: United States Air Force C-130A loss of 1958
Q16868874.blurb: A USAF RC-130 is shot down by fighters over Armenia when it strays into Soviet airspace while conducting a sigint mission. All crew members are killed.

Q16869476.name: Soma mine disaster
Q16869476.blurb: An explosion at an underground coal mine in southwest Turkey kills 301 miners.

Q16874544.name: Marcinelle disaster
Q16874544.blurb: Marcinelle mining disaster in Belgium. 262 coal miners, including a substantial number of Italian migrant workers, are killed in one of the largest mining accidents in Belgian history.

Q16890896.name: Sikkim Expedition
Q16890896.blurb: Start of the Anglo-Tibetan War of 1888.

Q16891192.name: 2014 Lao People's Liberation Army Air Force An-74 crash
Q16891192.blurb: A military plane crash in northern Laos kills 17 people.

Q16895704.name: National Personnel Records Center fire
Q16895704.blurb: A fire destroys the entire sixth floor of the National Personnel Records Center of the United States.

Q16896259.name: Ottawa bus-train crash
Q16896259.blurb: A VIA Rail train crashes into a double-decker bus at a train station in Ottawa, Canada, killing six people and injuring 35 others.

Q16901576.name: Third attack on Anzac Cove
Q16901576.blurb: First World War: Australian and New Zealand troops repelled the third attack on Anzac Cove, inflicting heavy casualties on the attacking Ottoman forces.

Q16902099.name: Turkish Airlines Flight 301
Q16902099.blurb: Turkish Airlines Flight 301 crashes during takeoff from Izmir Cumaovası Airport (now İzmir Adnan Menderes Airport), killing 66 of the 73 people on board the Fokker F28 Fellowship.

Q16902322.name: 1836 U.S. Patent Office fire
Q16902322.blurb: The U.S. Patent Office building in Washington, D.C., nearly burns to the ground, destroying all 9,957 patents issued by the federal government to that date, as well as 7,000 related patent models.

Q16911838.name: Libyan Civil War
Q16911838.blurb: Second Libyan Civil War: The Second Libyan Civil War comes to an end as all parties to the 5+5 Joint Libyan Military Commission agree to a ceasefire.

Q16911841.name: Canadian declaration of war on Germany
aliases: Declaration of a state of war with the German Reich
Q16911841.blurb: World War II: The Canadian declaration of war on Germany receives royal assent.

Q16912881.name: 1974 EgyptAir Tupolev Tu-154 crash
Q16912881.blurb: An EgyptAir Tupolev Tu-154 stalls and crashes at Cairo International Airport, killing all six people on board.

Q16914766.name: 2014 Thai coup d'état
Q16914766.blurb: General Prayut Chan-o-cha becomes interim leader of Thailand in a military coup d'état, following six months of political turmoil.

Q16915197.name: Taipei Metro massacre
Q16915197.blurb: Random killings occur on the Bannan Line of the Taipei MRT, killing four and injuring 24.

Q16918161.name: May 2014 Ürümqi explosion
Q16918161.blurb: An explosion occurs in Ürümqi, capital of China's far-western Xinjiang region, resulting in at least 43 deaths and 91 injuries.

Q16923670.name: Knife attack on Kevin Lau
Q16923670.blurb: Former editor-in-chief of Hong Kong newspaper Ming Pao Kevin Lau was stabbed, prompting concerns and protests about media freedom.

Q16924636.name: April 27 demonstrations
Q16924636.blurb: The April 27 demonstrations, student-led protests responding to the April 26 Editorial, during the Tiananmen Square protests of 1989.

Q16931434.name: Raid on Richmond
Q16931434.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Richmond, Virginia, is burned by British naval forces led by former American general Benedict Arnold.

Q16931459.name: Siege of Saint-Pierre-le-Moûtier
Q16931459.blurb: Armagnac–Burgundian Civil War: Joan of Arc liberates Saint-Pierre-le-Moûtier.

Q16931739.name: USS United States vs HMS Macedonian
Q16931739.blurb: War of 1812: The American frigate, USS United States, commanded by Stephen Decatur, captures the British frigate HMS Macedonian.

Q16932092.name: Soloheadbeg Ambush
Q16932092.blurb: A revolutionary Irish parliament is founded and declares the independence of the Irish Republic. One of the first engagements of the Irish War of Independence takes place.

Q16932373.name: March Against Fear
Q16932373.blurb: March Against Fear: African-American civil rights activist James Meredith is wounded in an ambush by white sniper James Aubrey Norvell. Meredith and Norvell are photographed by Jack R. Thornell, whose photo will receive the 1967 Pulitzer Prize in Photography, the last one to be awarded in the category.

Q16932404.name: Richard Nixon's resignation speech
Q16932404.blurb: President Richard Nixon, in a nationwide television address, announces his resignation from the office of the President of the United States effective noon the next day.

Q16932642.name: 1968 Liberal Party of Canada leadership election
aliases: Liberal Party of Canada leadership election, 1968
Q16932642.blurb: Pierre Elliott Trudeau wins the Liberal Party leadership election, and becomes Prime Minister of Canada soon afterward.

Q16932846.name: Lindal Railway Incident
Q16932846.blurb: A locomotive shunting falls into a hole in the ground, leading to the burial of the locomotive.

Q16933273.name: Spanish Province of Santo Domingo
Q16933273.blurb: Spain would annex annex the Dominican Republic, which would last for four years.

Q16933964.name: Tang campaign against Kucha
Q16933964.blurb: Conquest of Kucha: The forces of Kucha surrender after a forty-day siege led by Tang dynasty general Ashina She'er, establishing Tang control over the northern Tarim Basin in Xinjiang.

Q16934084.name: 1828 London Protocol
Q16934084.blurb: Greek War of Independence: The London Protocol entails the creation of an autonomous Greek state under Ottoman suzerainty, encompassing the Morea and the Cyclades.

Q16934089.name: London Protocol
Q16934089.blurb: In the London Protocol, the three protecting powers (United Kingdom, France and Russia) establish the borders of Greece.

Q16936116.name: 2014 Aegean Sea earthquake
Q16936116.blurb: A 6.4 magnitude earthquake occurs in the Aegean Sea between Greece and Turkey, injuring 324 people.

Q16937453.name: Jewish Museum of Belgium shooting
Q16937453.blurb: At least three people are killed in a shooting at Brussels' Jewish Museum of Belgium.

Q16938335.name: 2014 Isla Vista killings
Q16938335.blurb: Seven people, including the perpetrator, are killed and another 14 injured in a killing spree near the campus of University of California, Santa Barbara.

Q16948890.name: 1892 Wyoming Seminary vs. Mansfield State Normal football game
Q16948890.blurb: The first night game for American football takes place in a contest between Wyoming Seminary and Mansfield State Normal.

Q16949343.name: 1962 Turkish Airlines Taurus Mountains crash
Q16949343.blurb: A Turkish Airlines Fokker F27 Friendship crashes into Mount Medetsiz in the Taurus Mountains of Turkey, killing all 11 people on board.

Q16949845.name: Colectivo
Q16949845.blurb: During a demonstration, pro-government colectivos shoot at disputed President and Speaker of the National Assembly Juan Guaidó and his supporters in Barquisimeto, Venezuela, leaving five injured.

Q16954835.name: Nagorno-Karabakh conflict
Q16954835.blurb: The signing of the Bishkek Protocol between Armenia and Azerbaijan effectively freezes the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict.

Q16956086.name: Bentiu massacre
Q16956086.blurb: In the worst massacre of the South Sudanese Civil War, more than 400 civilians are gunned down after seeking refuge in houses of worship as well as hospitals.

Q16957409.name: 1983 Chicago mayoral election
Q16957409.blurb: Harold Washington was elected as the first African-American mayor of Chicago.

Q16960137.name: Aboriginal Protection Act 1869
Q16960137.blurb: The Victorian Aboriginal Protection Act is enacted in Australia, giving the government control of indigenous people's wages, their terms of employment, where they could live, and of their children, effectively leading to the Stolen Generations.

Q16961079.name: Allegheny Airlines Flight 485
Q16961079.blurb: Allegheny Airlines Flight 485 crashes on approach to Tweed New Haven Airport in New Haven, Connecticut, killing 28 of 31 aboard.

Q16961833.name: Arab Police Mutiny
Q16961833.blurb: The Aden Emergency: The Battle of the Crater in which the British Argyll and Sutherland Highlanders retake the Crater district following the Arab Police mutiny.

Q16965810.name: The Day the Earth Smiled
Q16965810.blurb: The NASA spacecraft Cassini took a photograph of Saturn with Earth in the distance (detail pictured), for which people were invited to "wave at Saturn".

Q16966603.name: Battle of the Crater
Q16966603.blurb: The Aden Emergency: The Battle of the Crater in which the British Argyll and Sutherland Highlanders retake the Crater district following the Arab Police mutiny.

Q16969616.name: Sri Lankan Constitution of 1972
Q16969616.blurb: Ceylon adopts a new constitution, becoming a republic and changing its name to Sri Lanka.

Q16974827.name: Flagship Airlines Flight 3379
Q16974827.blurb: Flagship Airlines Flight 3379 crashes in Morrisville, North Carolina, near Raleigh–Durham International Airport, killing 15.

Q16982393.name: Naperville train disaster
Q16982393.blurb: Two passenger trains collided in Naperville, Illinois, leaving 45 people dead and some 125 injured.

Q16982566.name: Great Flood of 1913
Q16982566.blurb: A tornado outbreak kills more than 240 people in the central United States, while an ongoing flood in the Ohio River watershed was killing 650 people.

Q16983329.name: Aviogenex Flight 130
Q16983329.blurb: Seventy-eight people are killed when Aviogenex Flight 130 crashes on approach to Rijeka Airport in present-day Rijeka, Croatia (then the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia).

Q16984022.name: High Commissioner Attack
Q16984022.blurb: An assassination attempt on the British High Commissioner in Aden kills two people and wounds dozens more.

Q16986203.name: Inex-Adria Aviopromet Flight 450
Q16986203.blurb: Forty-five people are killed when Inex-Adria Aviopromet Flight 450 crashes into Suchdol, Prague, while on approach to Prague Ruzyně Airport (now Václav Havel Airport Prague) in Czechoslovakia (present-day Czech Republic).

Q16992471.name: Joe Frazier vs. George Foreman
Q16992471.blurb: In a bout for the world heavyweight boxing championship in Kingston, Jamaica, challenger George Foreman knocks down champion Joe Frazier six times in the first two rounds before the fight is stopped by referee Arthur Mercante Sr..

Q17001802.name: Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action
aliases: Comprehensive agreement on Iranian nuclear program
Comprehensive agreement on the Iranian nuclear program
Comprehensive agreement on the Iranian nuclear programme
The Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action
Q17001802.blurb: President Barack Obama announces the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, an agreement intended to limit Iran's nuclear program.

Q17002077.name: Cyclone Forrest
Q17002077.blurb: In poor conditions caused by Cyclone Forrest, Vietnam Airlines Flight 474 crashes near Nha Trang, killing 30.

Q17003102.name: 2014 Stade Tata Raphaël disaster
Q17003102.blurb: Fifteen people are killed and 46 injured in Kinshasa, DRC, in a stampede caused by tear gas being thrown into soccer stands by police officers.

Q17004294.name: 2016 Democratic Party presidential primaries
Q17004294.blurb: Donald Trump is elected the 45th President of the United States, defeating Hillary Clinton, the first woman ever to receive a major party's nomination.

Q17011733.name: Sex Disqualification (Removal) Act 1919
Q17011733.blurb: Sex Disqualification (Removal) Act 1919 becomes law in the United Kingdom, allowing women to serve as lawyers, civil servants, and in other professions, as well as to serve on juries.

Q17013132.name: Oslo Accords
aliases: Agreement on Preparatory Transfer of Powers and Responsibilities Between Israel and the PLO
Protocol on Further Transfer of Powers and Responsibilities
Q17013132.blurb: Yasser Arafat, Yitzhak Rabin and Shimon Peres receive the Nobel Peace Prize for their role in the establishment of the Oslo Accords and the framing of future Palestinian self government.

Q17014762.name: China Eastern Airlines Flight 5510
Q17014762.blurb: China Eastern Airlines Flight 5510 crashes after takeoff from Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport, killing 34 of the 40 people on board.

Q17014837.name: 1956 Rafah massacre
Q17014837.blurb: In the midst of the Suez Crisis, Palestinian refugees are shot dead in Rafah by Israel Defense Force soldiers following the invasion of the Gaza Strip.

Q17014851.name: Raid on Żejtun
Q17014851.blurb: Raid on Żejtun: The south east of Malta, and the town of Żejtun, suffer a raid from Ottoman forces. This was the last unsuccessful attempt by the Ottomans to conquer the island of Malta.

Q17015125.name: China Airlines Flight 2265
Q17015125.blurb: China Airlines Flight 2265 crashes into the Pacific Ocean near Penghu Airport in Taiwan, killing all 13 aboard.

Q17017738.name: Decembrist revolution
Q17017738.blurb: Argentine general Juan Lavalle makes a coup against governor Manuel Dorrego, beginning the Decembrist revolution.

Q17017873.name: United Air Lines Flight 553
Q17017873.blurb: United Airlines Flight 553, a Boeing 737, crashes after aborting its landing attempt at Chicago Midway International Airport, killing 45. This is the first-ever loss of a Boeing 737.

Q17019548.name: Smithsonian–Roosevelt African Expedition
Q17019548.blurb: Theodore Roosevelt leaves New York for a post-presidency safari in Africa. The trip is sponsored by the Smithsonian Institution and National Geographic Society.

Q17020474.name: Halloween solar storms, 2003
Q17020474.blurb: Start of the May 2024 solar storms, the most powerful set of geomagnetic storms since the 2003 Halloween solar storms.

Q17025641.name: Tirah Campaign
Q17025641.blurb: Tirah campaign: In the Battle of Saragarhi, ten thousand Pashtun tribesmen suffer several hundred casualties while attacking 21 Sikh soldiers in British service.

Q17027651.name: United Airlines Flight 2885
Q17027651.blurb: United Airlines Flight 2885 crashes after takeoff from Detroit Metropolitan Airport, killing three.

Q17029857.name: Vedaranyam March
Q17029857.blurb: C. Rajagopalachari led the non-violent Vedaranyam March from Trichinopoly towards Vedaranyam.

Q17035545.name: Treaty of Jeddah
aliases: Treaty between His Majesty and His Majesty the King of the Hejaz and of Nejd and Its Dependencies
Q17035545.blurb: Treaty of Jeddah: The United Kingdom recognizes the sovereignty of King Ibn Saud in the Kingdoms of Hejaz and Nejd, which later merge to become the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

Q17039175.name: withdrawal from Aden
Q17039175.blurb: The People's Republic of Southern Yemen gains its independence from the United Kingdom

Q17040602.name: Worms massacre
Q17040602.blurb: First Crusade: Around 800 Jews are massacred in Worms, Germany.

Q17055270.name: 1996 New Zealand general election
Q17055270.blurb: New Zealand holds its first general election under the new mixed-member proportional representation system, which led to Jim Bolger's National Party forming a coalition government with Winston Peters's New Zealand First.

Q17058804.name: 1986 Sudan Airways Fokker F-27 shootdown
Q17058804.blurb: A Sudan Airways Fokker F27 Friendship is shot down near Malakal in present day South Sudan, killing 60.

Q17062699.name: SS Arctic disaster
Q17062699.blurb: The paddle steamer SS Arctic, owned by the Collins Line of New York, sinks off the coast of Newfoundland, following a collision with a smaller vessel, the SS Vesta. Only 88 of over 300 people on board survive. About a dozen of the occupants of the Vesta are killed when their lifeboat is hit by the Arctic.

Q17064684.name: 2013 Thailand refugee camp fire
Q17064684.blurb: At least 37 people are killed and 200 are injured after a fire destroys a camp containing Burmese refugees near Ban Mae, Thailand.

Q17069589.name: 2002 Prestige Airlines Boeing 707 crash
Q17069589.blurb: A Boeing 707 crashes near Bangui M'Poko International Airport in Bangui, Central African Republic, killing 28.

Q17080050.name: 2014 Gikomba bombings
Q17080050.blurb: Twelve people are killed in two explosions in the Gikomba market area of Nairobi, Kenya.

Q17096500.name: 1980 Southern Rhodesian general election
Q17096500.blurb: Nationalist leader Robert Mugabe wins a sweeping election victory to become Zimbabwe's first black prime minister.

Q17096533.name: 1992 Speaker of the British House of Commons election
aliases: Speaker of the British House of Commons election, 1992
Q17096533.blurb: Betty Boothroyd becomes the first woman to be elected Speaker of the British House of Commons in its 700-year history.

Q17103513.name: 1989 Supertaça Cândido de Oliveira
Q17103513.blurb: The first leg of the 1989 Supertaça Cândido de Oliveira is held at the Estádio da Luz in Lisbon, Portugal.

Q17107611.name: Xerox murders
Q17107611.blurb: Honolulu shootings: In the worst mass murder in the history of Hawaii, a gunman shoots at eight people in his workplace, killing seven.

Q17107953.name: Ocoee massacre
Q17107953.blurb: The Ocoee massacre commences in Orange County, Florida on the day of the 1920 United States presidential election.

Q17108094.name: Massacre of the Sixty
Q17108094.blurb: Sixty Ethiopian politicians, aristocrats, military officers, and other persons are executed by the provisional military government.

Q17111026.name: New Orleans massacre of 1866
Q17111026.blurb: Armed Confederate veterans in New Orleans riot against a meeting of Radical Republicans, killing 48 people and injuring another 100.

Q17147133.name: Tropical Storm Zelda
Q17147133.blurb: Operations at the Reagan Test Site were disrupted due to the nearby formation of Tropical Storm Zelda.

Q17163519.name: Nadir of American race relations
Q17163519.blurb: Nadir of American race relations: A mob of white Americans killed eight people in Oconee County, Georgia, as part of a mass lynching.

Q17165824.name: The Thriving Cult of Greed and Power
Q17165824.blurb: Time magazine published the article "The Thriving Cult of Greed and Power" by Richard Behar criticizing the Church of Scientology, leading to years of legal conflict.

Q17181586.name: 2014 Ukrainian Air Force Il-76 shootdown
Q17181586.blurb: A Ukraine military Ilyushin Il-76 airlifter is shot down, killing all 49 people on board.

Q17183365.name: Iraqi Civil War of 2006–2008
Q17183365.blurb: At approximately 6:44 a.m.  local Iraqi time, explosions occurred at the al-Askari Shrine in Samarra, Iraq. The attack on the shrine, one of the holiest sites in Shia Islam, caused the escalation of sectarian tensions in Iraq into a full-scale civil war.

Q17192441.name: Awash rail disaster
Q17192441.blurb: A passenger train plunges into a ravine in Ethiopia, killing 428 in the worst railroad disaster in Africa.

Q17195247.name: 2014 kidnapping of Israeli teens
Q17195247.blurb: Israel launches an offensive on Gaza amid rising tensions following the kidnapping and murder of three Israeli teenagers.

Q17195724.name: 2014 Japanese Grand Prix
Q17195724.blurb: Formula One racing driver Jules Bianchi sustained fatal head injuries in a crash at the Japanese Grand Prix, dying the following year.

Q17199280.name: Camp Speicher massacre
Q17199280.blurb: Between 1,095 and 1,700 Shia Iraqi people are killed in an attack by the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant on Camp Speicher in Tikrit, Iraq. It is the second deadliest act of terrorism in history, only behind 9/11.

Q17279394.name: Spaghetti House siege
Q17279394.blurb: The Spaghetti House siege, in which nine people are taken hostage, takes place in London.

Q17324420.name: 2014 Gaza War
aliases: Economic impact of the 2014 Israel-Gaza conflict
Human rights violations during the 2014 Gaza War
War crimes in the 2014 Gaza War
Q17324420.blurb: Israel launches an offensive on Gaza amid rising tensions following the kidnapping and murder of three Israeli teenagers.

Q17329128.name: Brazil v Germany (2014 FIFA World Cup)
aliases: 2014 FIFA World Cup Match 61, Brasil v Germany
Brazil v. Germany (2014 FIFA World Cup)
Brazil versus Germany (2014 FIFA World Cup)
Brazil vs Germany (2014 FIFA World Cup)
Q17329128.blurb: The Brazil national football team suffers its joint-worst defeat, losing 7–1 to Germany in the semi-finals of the FIFA World Cup, in a match dubbed the Mineiraço.

Q17374096.name: Malaysia Airlines Flight 17
Q17374096.blurb: Malaysia Airlines Flight 17, a Boeing 777, crashes near the border of Ukraine and Russia after being shot down. All 298 people on board are killed.

Q17400785.name: killing of Eric Garner
Q17400785.blurb: Eric Garner is killed by police officer Daniel Pantaleo in New York City, after the latter put him in a prohibited chokehold while arresting him.

Q17402901.name: July 2014 Al-Wadi Al-Gedid attack
Q17402901.blurb: Gunmen ambushed an Egyptian military checkpoint in the Libyan Desert near Farafra, killing 22 soldiers.

Q17404012.name: TransAsia Airways Flight 222
Q17404012.blurb: TransAsia Airways Flight 222 crashes in Xixi village near Huxi, Penghu, during approach to Penghu Airport. Forty-eight of the 58 people on board are killed and five more people on the ground are injured.

Q17410088.name: Air Algérie Flight 5017
Q17410088.blurb: Air Algérie Flight 5017 loses contact with air traffic controllers 50 minutes after takeoff. It was travelling between Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso and Algiers. The wreckage is later found in Mali. All 116 people on board are killed.

Q17438485.name: Yakutsk United Air Group Flight 101/435
Q17438485.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 101/435 is hijacked to China by its first officer.

Q17462908.name: 2014 Kaohsiung gas explosion
Q17462908.blurb: Gas explosions in the southern Taiwanese city of Kaohsiung kill at least 20 people and injure more than 270.

Q17478639.name: 2014 Kunshan explosion
Q17478639.blurb: At least 146 people are killed and more than 114 injured in a factory explosion in Kunshan, Jiangsu, China.

Q17479524.name: 2014 Malin landslide
Q17479524.blurb: Twenty killed and 150 are trapped after a landslide in Maharashtra, India.

Q17483279.name: 2014 Ludian earthquake
Q17483279.blurb: A 6.1 magnitude earthquake kills at least 617 people and injures more than 2,400 in Yunnan, China.

Q17496200.name: Sepahan Airlines Flight 5915
Q17496200.blurb: Forty people are killed when Sepahan Airlines Flight 5915 crashes at Tehran's Mehrabad International Airport.

Q17501769.name: shooting of Michael Brown
aliases: 2014 Michael Brown death and aftermath in Ferguson Missouri
Q17501769.blurb: Michael Brown, an 18-year-old African-American man, was killed by a white police officer in Ferguson, Missouri, resulting in widespread protests and unrest.

Q17505930.name: 2014 Cessna Citation 560 XLS+ crash
Q17505930.blurb: A Cessna Citation Excel crashes in Santos, São Paulo, Brazil killing all seven people aboard, including Brazilian Socialist Party presidential candidate Eduardo Campos.

Q17507595.name: 1963 Moscow protest
Q17507595.blurb: Ghanaian and other African students organized a protest in Moscow's Red Square in response to the alleged murder of medical student Edmund Assare-Addo.

Q17507684.name: War against the Islamic State
aliases: 2014 American-led anti-extremist intervention in the northern Levant
2014 military intervention against the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant
International military intervention against the Islamic State
Military intervention against the Islamic State
Military intervention against the Islamic State of Iraq and Greater Syria
Military intervention against the Islamic State of Iraq and Syria
Military intervention against the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant
War on the Islamic State of Iraq and Greater Syria
War on the Islamic State of Iraq and Syria
War on the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant
Q17507684.blurb: War against the Islamic State: Philippine defense secretary Delfin Lorenzana declares the end of the Siege of Marawi.

Q17509038.name: 1901 State of the Union Address
aliases: Theodore Roosevelt's First State of the Union Address
Q17509038.blurb: In a State of the Union message, U.S. President Theodore Roosevelt delivers a 20,000-word report to the House of Representatives asking Congress to curb the power of trusts "within reasonable limits".  The speech was not delivered in person.

Q17509340.name: 1929 State of the Union Address
aliases: Herbert Hoover's First State of the Union Address
Q17509340.blurb: President Herbert Hoover delivers his first State of the Union message to Congress. It is presented in the form of a written message rather than a speech.

Q17509619.name: 1952 Mount Gannett C-124 crash
Q17509619.blurb: A Douglas C-124 Globemaster II crashes into Mount Gannet, Alaska, killing all 52 aboard.

Q17513696.name: Denguin rail crash
Q17513696.blurb: A French regional train on the Pau-Bayonne line crashes into a high-speed train near the town of Denguin, resulting in at least 25 injuries.

Q17515491.name: Battle of Lechfeld
Q17515491.blurb: Battle of Augsburg: The Hungarians defeat the East Frankish army under King Louis the Child, using the famous feigned retreat tactic of the nomadic warriors.

Q17515504.name: Battle of Picotin
Q17515504.blurb: The Battle of Picotin, between Ferdinand of Majorca and the forces of Matilda of Hainaut, ends in victory for Ferdinand.

Q17540707.name: Fine Air Flight 101
Q17540707.blurb: Fine Air Flight 101 crashes after takeoff from Miami International Airport, killing five people.

Q17560945.name: 2014 Ferguson unrest
aliases: Protests and unrest in Ferguson, Missouri (2014)
Protests over the death of Michael Brown
Q17560945.blurb: Michael Brown, an 18-year-old African-American man, was killed by a white police officer in Ferguson, Missouri, resulting in widespread protests and unrest.

Q17563514.name: 2014 Hiroshima landslides
Q17563514.blurb: Seventy-two people are killed in Japan's Hiroshima Prefecture by a series of landslides caused by a month's worth of rain that fell in one day.

Q17602018.name: 2014 South Napa earthquake
Q17602018.blurb: A magnitude 6.0 earthquake strikes the San Francisco Bay Area; it is the largest in that area since 1989.

Q17614042.name: 2014 Moscow Metro derailment
Q17614042.blurb: A train derails on the Moscow Metro, killing at least 24 and injuring more than 160 others.

Q17621744.name: assassination of Cánovas del Castillo
aliases: Assassination of Antonio Cánovas del Castillo
Q17621744.blurb: Italian anarchist Michele Angiolillo assassinates Spanish Prime Minister Antonio Cánovas del Castillo.

Q17622618.name: Battle of Margate
Q17622618.blurb: Hundred Years' War: An English fleet led by Richard Fitzalan attacked 250 to 360 French, Flemish and Castilian vessels in the Battle of Margate.

Q17627345.name: Kweilin Incident
Q17627345.blurb: Kweilin incident: A Japanese warplane shoots down the Kweilin, a Chinese civilian airliner, killing 14. It is the first recorded instance of a civilian airliner being shot down.

Q17635055.name: Murder of Tina Isa
Q17635055.blurb: A Missouri court sentences the Palestinian militant Zein Isa and his wife Maria to death for the honor killing of their daughter Palestina.

Q17639795.name: solar storm of 2012
Q17639795.blurb: The Solar storm of 2012 was an unusually large coronal mass ejection that was emitted by the Sun which barely missed the Earth by nine days. If it hit, it would have caused up to US$2.6 trillion in damages to electrical equipment worldwide.

Q17640143.name: Treaty of Constantinople (1800)
Q17640143.blurb: The Treaty of Constantinople establishes the Septinsular Republic, the first autonomous Greek state since the Fall of the Byzantine Empire. (Under the Old Style calendar then still in use in the Ottoman Empire, the treaty was signed on 21 March.)

Q17684684.name: 2014 Lesotho political crisis
Q17684684.blurb: Prime Minister of Lesotho Tom Thabane flees to South Africa as the army allegedly stages a coup.

Q17750099.name: 1965 Burundian coup d'état
Q17750099.blurb: A group of ethnic Hutu military officers failed in their attempt to overthrow the Burundian government.

Q17984356.name: Iraqi Civil War of 2014–2017
aliases: Syrian Civil War spillover in Iraq
Timeline of the Iraqi civil war (2014-present)
Q17984356.blurb: Iraqi Civil War: Mosul is declared fully liberated from the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant by the government of Iraq.

Q17989657.name: Bombay Explosion
Q17989657.blurb: The freighter Fort Stikine, carrying cotton bales, gold and ammunition, exploded in the harbour of Bombay, India, sinking surrounding ships and causing about 800 deaths.

Q17996734.name: Aeroflot Flight 542
Q17996734.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 542 crashes in the Yermakovsky District, killing all 31 aboard.

Q18008716.name: Siege of Toledo
Q18008716.blurb: Alfonso VI of Castile takes Toledo, Spain, back from the Moors after a siege.

Q18016068.name: First Battle of Seoul
Q18016068.blurb: Korean War: Packed with its own refugees fleeing Seoul and leaving their 5th Division stranded, South Korean forces blow up the Hangang Bridge in an attempt to slow North Korea's offensive. The city falls later that day.

Q18071930.name: Siege of Kobanî
Q18071930.blurb: The Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant launches its Kobani offensive against Syrian–Kurdish forces.

Q18088261.name: 1984 Biman Bangladesh Airlines Fokker F27 crash
Q18088261.blurb: A Biman Bangladesh Airlines aircraft crashed while attempting to land in Dhaka, killing 49 people in the deadliest aviation accident in Bangladeshi history.

Q18089307.name: Easter Riots
Q18089307.blurb: The Easter Riots break out in Uppsala, Sweden.

Q18108964.name: German occupation of Belgium during World War I
Q18108964.blurb: World War I: British nurse Edith Cavell is executed by a German firing squad for helping Allied soldiers escape from occupied Belgium.

Q18109188.name: 1975 British Mount Everest Southwest Face expedition
Q18109188.blurb: Southwest Face expedition members become the first persons to reach the summit of Mount Everest by any of its faces, instead of using a ridge route.

Q18109195.name: 1986 Black Sea incident
Q18109195.blurb: Claiming the right of innocent passage, the American warships Yorktown and Caron entered Soviet territorial waters in the Black Sea.

Q18124960.name: 2023 Rugby World Cup
Q18124960.blurb: The 2023 Rugby World Cup, the tenth men's Rugby World Cup is held in France. The opening ceremony, directed and written by Jean Dujardin, Olivier Ferracci and Nora Matthey, took place at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis, before the opening match between France and New Zealand, which saw the host nation winning 27 to 13.

Q18145420.name: 2014 Hong Kong protests
aliases: Timeline of the 2014 Hong Kong protests
Q18145420.blurb: The 2014 Hong Kong protests begin in response to restrictive political reforms imposed by the NPC in Beijing.

Q18145950.name: 2014 eruption of Mount Ontake
Q18145950.blurb: 63 people are killed in an eruption of Mount Ontake in Japan.

Q18147604.name: Aero Flight 217
Q18147604.blurb: Finnair's Aero Flight 217 crashes near Mariehamn Airport in Jomala, Åland, killing 22 people.

Q18149796.name: 2001 Marsh Harbour Cessna 402 crash
Q18149796.blurb: American singer Aaliyah and several members of her entourage are killed as their overloaded aircraft crashes shortly after takeoff from Marsh Harbour Airport, Bahamas.

Q18151379.name: March 14, 1891 lynchings
Q18151379.blurb: The 1891 New Orleans Lynchings: 11 Italian immigrants are lynched by a mob in Louisiana, USA after the acquittal of several defendants in a murder case, the largest mass lynching in U.S. history.

Q18162511.name: Battle of Yeghevārd
Q18162511.blurb: Safavid Iran captures Ganja from the Ottoman Empire after defeating them in the battle of Yeghevārd.

Q18162521.name: Siege of Ganja
Q18162521.blurb: Safavid Iran captures Ganja from the Ottoman Empire after defeating them in the battle of Yeghevārd.

Q18195808.name: Cyclone Hudhud
Q18195808.blurb: A snowstorm and avalanche in the Nepalese Himalayas triggered by the remnants of Cyclone Hudhud kills 43 people.

Q18198930.name: 2014 Gorni Lom explosions
Q18198930.blurb: A series of explosions at a gunpowder plant in Bulgaria completely destroys the factory, killing 15 people.

Q18204694.name: Dai Hong Dan incident
Q18204694.blurb: Somali pirates hijacked a North Korean ship in the Indian Ocean northeast of Mogadishu.

Q18206471.name: Battle of Neuburg
Q18206471.blurb: War of the Second Coalition: French forces won a victory at the Battle of Neuburg, ending Austrian control over the River Danube.

Q18213987.name: assassination of Sadi Carnot
Q18213987.blurb: Assassination of the French President, Sadi Carnot by Sante Caserio during the Ère des attentats (1892–1894).

Q18214240.name: Operation Caban
Q18214240.blurb: A French-supported coup d'état in the Central African Empire overthrows Emperor Bokassa I.

Q18216969.name: Invasion of Martinique
Q18216969.blurb: A Dutch assault on the French island of Martinique is repulsed against all odds.

Q18235785.name: 1942 Aeroflot Tupolev ANT-20bis crash
Q18235785.blurb: An Aeroflot Tupolev ANT-20 crashes near Tashkent, killing all 36 people on board.

Q18236869.name: Bush shoeing incident
Q18236869.blurb: During a press conference in Baghdad, Iraqi journalist Muntadhar al-Zaidi threw his shoes at U.S. president George W. Bush and Iraqi prime minister Nouri al-Maliki, yelling "This is for the widows and orphans and all those killed in Iraq".

Q18289650.name: 1456 Central Italy earthquakes
Q18289650.blurb: The first of two earthquakes measuring Mw 7.2 strikes Italy, causing extreme destruction and killing upwards of 70,000 people.

Q18324131.name: Standard Gravure shooting
Q18324131.blurb: The Standard Gravure shooting where Joseph T. Wesbecker, a 47-year-old pressman, killed eight people and injured 12 people at his former workplace, Standard Gravure, before committing suicide.

Q18325532.name: 2014 Mount Dhaulagiri avalanches
Q18325532.blurb: A snowstorm and avalanche in the Nepalese Himalayas triggered by the remnants of Cyclone Hudhud kills 43 people.

Q18327329.name: 2014 Iguala mass kidnapping
Q18327329.blurb: A mass kidnapping of 43 students from a teaching college occurs in Iguala, Mexico.

Q18327521.name: Trial of Thomas Paine
Q18327521.blurb: Thomas Paine (depicted) was found guilty of seditious libel for the publication of the second part of his book Rights of Man.

Q18338238.name: 2014 shootings at Parliament Hill, Ottawa
aliases: One confirmed dead after shooting at National War Memorial in Ottawa
shootings at War Memorial and Parliament Hill
Q18338238.blurb: Michael Zehaf-Bibeau attacks the Parliament of Canada, killing a soldier and injuring three other people.

Q18339453.name: Mitsubishi Materials chemical plant explosion
Q18339453.blurb: An explosion at a Mitsubishi Materials chemical plant in Yokkaichi, Japan, kills at least five people and injures 17 others.

Q18341392.name: murder of Kitty Genovese
Q18341392.blurb: Kitty Genovese is murdered in New York City, prompting research into the bystander effect due to the false story that neighbors witnessed the killing and did nothing to help her.

Q18347005.name: 2014 Serbia v Albania
Q18347005.blurb: The Serbia vs. Albania UEFA qualifying match is canceled after 42 minutes due to several incidents on and off the pitch. Albania is eventually awarded a win.

Q18352881.name: Dutch expedition to Valdivia
Q18352881.blurb: A Dutch fleet establishes a new colony in the ruins of Valdivia in southern Chile.

Q18353917.name: Battle of Matina
Q18353917.blurb: Battle of Mutina: Mark Antony is again defeated in battle by Aulus Hirtius, who is killed. Antony fails to capture Mutina and Decimus Brutus is murdered shortly after.

Q18355861.name: USS Enterprise fire
Q18355861.blurb: USS Enterprise fire: An accidental explosion aboard the USS Enterprise near Hawaii kills 28 people.

Q18356374.name: search for Malaysia Airlines Flight 370
Q18356374.blurb: The search for Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 is announced to be suspended.

Q18356954.name: Battle of Kars
Q18356954.blurb: Ottoman–Persian War: In the Battle of Kars, the Ottoman army is routed by Persian forces led by Nader Shah.

Q18358461.name: Siege of Baghdad (1733)
Q18358461.blurb: The Ottoman army defeats the Iranian army under Nader Shah in the battle of Baghdad.

Q18375297.name: 2014 Badulla landslide
Q18375297.blurb: A mud slide; the 2014 Badulla landslide, in south-central Sri Lanka, kills at least 16 people, and leaves hundreds of people missing.

Q18379474.name: white shift dress of Jean Shrimpton
Q18379474.blurb: English model Jean Shrimpton wore a controversially short minidress to Derby Day at Flemington Racecourse in Melbourne, Australia – a pivotal moment of the introduction of the miniskirt to women's fashion.

Q18380400.name: 2014 Wichita plane crash
Q18380400.blurb: Four people are killed when a Beechcraft Super King Air crashes at Wichita Dwight D. Eisenhower National Airport in Wichita, Kansas.

Q18389097.name: Women’s Boat Race 1927
Q18389097.blurb: In rowing, Oxford defeated Cambridge in the inaugural edition of the Women's Boat Race.

Q18396768.name: 2014 Virgin Galactic crash
Q18396768.blurb: During a test flight, the VSS Enterprise, a Virgin Galactic experimental spaceflight test vehicle, suffers a catastrophic in-flight breakup and crashes in the Mojave Desert, California.

Q18398545.name: Accidente de un Sud Aviation Caravelle de Royal Air Maroc en 1973
Q18398545.blurb: A Royal Air Maroc Sud Aviation Caravelle crashes near Tangier-Boukhalef Airport in Tangier, Morocco, killing 106.

Q18398555.name: 1970 Atlantic Ocean Antonov An-22 crash
Q18398555.blurb: An Antonov An-22 of the Soviet Air Forces crashes into the Atlantic Ocean, killing all 23 aboard.

Q18398586.name: Aeroflot Flight 2723
Q18398586.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 2723 crashes into the Caspian Sea off the Absheron Peninsula, killing 33 people.

Q18398591.name: Aeroflot Flight 213 (1962)
Q18398591.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 213 crashes into a mountain near Chersky Airport, killing 32 people.

Q18398603.name: 1983 Chosonminhang Ilyushin Il-62 crash
Q18398603.blurb: A North Korean Ilyushin Il-62M jet crashed into the Fouta Djallon mountains in Guinea, killing all 23 people on board.

Q18398641.name: 1994 Vanavara air disaster
Q18398641.blurb: A Yakovlev Yak-40 crashes into a river near Vanavara, Russia, killing 24.

Q18402076.name: international recognition of Donetsk People's Republic and Luhansk People's Republic
Q18402076.blurb: Russo-Ukrainian War: Days after recognising Donetsk and Luhansk as independent states, Russian president Vladimir Putin orders the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine.

Q18409574.name: 1990 Mecca tunnel tragedy
Q18409574.blurb: In the 1990 Mecca tunnel tragedy, 1,400 Muslim pilgrims are suffocated to death and trampled upon in a pedestrian tunnel leading to the holy city of Mecca.

Q18418423.name: Catalan self-determination referendum
Q18418423.blurb: A non-binding self-determination consultation is held in Catalonia, asking Catalan citizens their opinion on whether Catalonia should become a state and, if so, whether it should be an independent state.

Q18438915.name: 2006 Tel Aviv shawarma restaurant bombing
Q18438915.blurb: A Palestinian suicide bomber detonates an explosive device in a Tel Aviv restaurant, killing 11 people and injuring 70.

Q18466708.name: 1976 Lloyd Aéreo Boliviano Boeing 707 crash
Q18466708.blurb: A Lloyd Aéreo Boliviano Boeing 707 crashes after takeoff from El Trompillo Airport in Santa Cruz de la Sierra, Bolivia, killing 91.

Q18479704.name: Operation Lava Jato
Q18479704.blurb: President of Peru Pedro Pablo Kuczynski resigns from the presidency amid a mass corruption scandal before certain impeachment by the opposition-majority Congress of Peru.

Q18510562.name: Vietnam Airlines Flight 474
Q18510562.blurb: In poor conditions caused by Cyclone Forrest, Vietnam Airlines Flight 474 crashes near Nha Trang, killing 30.

Q18535080.name: 2014 Armenian Mil Mi-24 shootdown
Q18535080.blurb: An Armenian Mil Mi-24 attack helicopter is shot down by Azerbaijani forces, killing all three people on board.

Q18543266.name: Pan Am Flight 799
Q18543266.blurb: Pan Am Flight 799 crashes during takeoff from Elmendorf Air Force Base, killing three.

Q18545517.name: Bucharest pogrom
Q18545517.blurb: A German officer is killed in Bucharest, Romania, sparking a rebellion and pogrom by the Iron Guard, killing 125 Jews and 30 soldiers.

Q18551886.name: 2014 Jerusalem synagogue attack
Q18551886.blurb: Two Palestinian men attacked the praying congregants of a synagogue in Jerusalem with axes, knives, and a gun, resulting in eight deaths, including the attackers themselves.

Q18575889.name: shooting of Tamir Rice
Q18575889.blurb: While playing with a toy gun in Cleveland, 12-year-old African American Tamir Rice is killed by a white police officer.

Q18600449.name: 1989 Burkinabé coup d'état attempt
Q18600449.blurb: An attempted coup d'état against Burkina Faso president Blaise Compaoré is uncovered and foiled.

Q18603167.name: 2014 Grozny clashes
Q18603167.blurb: Islamic insurgents kill three state police at a traffic circle before taking an empty school and a "press house" in Grozny. Ten state forces die with 28 injured in gun battles ending with ten insurgents killed.

Q18604542.name: 1982 Upper Volta coup d'état
Q18604542.blurb: Colonel Saye Zerbo, president of the military government of Upper Volta, is ousted from power in a coup d'état led by Colonel Gabriel Yoryan Somé.

Q18604615.name: 1980 Upper Volta coup d'état
Q18604615.blurb: Sangoulé Lamizana, president of Upper Volta, is ousted from power in a coup d'état led by Colonel Saye Zerbo.

Q18609065.name: 2014 Kano bombing
Q18609065.blurb: Gunmen set off three bombs at the central mosque in the northern Nigerian city of Kano killing at least 120 people.

Q18638636.name: 2014 Sydney hostage crisis
Q18638636.blurb: A hostage crisis in a Lindt chocolate café in Sydney, Australia, ended with police storming the building, killing the perpetrator and one of the hostages.

Q18641076.name: 2014 Peshawar school attack
aliases: 2014 Taliban attack on the Army Public School
2014 Taliban attack on the Army Public School, Peshawar
Q18641076.blurb: Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan militants attack an Army Public School in Peshawar, Pakistan, killing 150 people, 132 of them schoolchildren.

Q18653444.name: Torreón massacre
Q18653444.blurb: More than 300 Chinese immigrants are killed in the Torreón massacre when the forces of the Mexican Revolution led by Emilio Madero take the city of Torreón from the Federales.

Q18662539.name: UFOs of Pudasjärvi
Q18662539.blurb: The last of its many UFO sightings is made at Pudasjärvi, Finland.

Q18678082.name: Nouvelle-Aquitaine
Q18678082.blurb: TAI Flight 307 crashes during takeoff from Bordeaux–Mérignac Airport in Bordeaux, Nouvelle-Aquitaine, France, killing 55 people.

Q18683047.name: AirAsia Flight 8501
Q18683047.blurb: Indonesia AirAsia Flight 8501 crashes into the Karimata Strait en route from Surabaya to Singapore, killing all 162 people aboard.

Q18698657.name: 2014 Shanghai stampede
Q18698657.blurb: A New Year's Eve celebration stampede in Shanghai kills at least 36 people and injures 49 others.

Q18702324.name: Libyan crisis
Q18702324.blurb: Libyan Crisis: Rebel forces capture Libyan dictator Muammar Gaddafi and his son Mutassim in his hometown of Sirte and kill them shortly thereafter, ending the first Libyan civil war.

Q18718876.name: Charlie Hebdo shooting
Q18718876.blurb: Two gunmen commit mass murder at the offices of Charlie Hebdo in Paris, executing twelve people and wounding eleven others.

Q18720403.name: 2015 Sana'a bombing
Q18720403.blurb: A car bomb explodes outside a police college in the Yemeni capital Sanaa with at least 38 people reported dead and more than 63 injured.

Q18732673.name: 2015 Baga massacre
Q18732673.blurb: Boko Haram militants destroy the entire town of Baga in north-east Nigeria, starting the Baga massacre and killing as many as 2,000 people.

Q18748071.name: Porte de Vincennes siege
Q18748071.blurb: A hostage situation, related to the Charlie Hebdo shooting, occurred at a Jewish market in Vincennes.

Q18758203.name: 2015 Mozambique funeral beer poisoning
Q18758203.blurb: A mass poisoning at a funeral in Mozambique involving beer that was contaminated with Burkholderia gladioli leaves 75 dead and over 230 people ill.

Q18758758.name: January 2015 Kolofata raid
Q18758758.blurb: Government raids kill 143 Boko Haram fighters in Kolofata, Cameroon.

Q18910392.name: 2015 Hellenic Air Force F-16 Los Llanos Air Base crash
Q18910392.blurb: An aircraft crashes at Los Llanos Air Base in Albacete, Spain, killing 11 people and injuring 21 others.

Q18916791.name: 2015 Mamasapano clash
Q18916791.blurb: A clash in Mamasapano, Maguindanao in the Philippines kills 44 members of Special Action Force (SAF), at least 18 from the Moro Islamic Liberation Front and five from the Bangsamoro Islamic Freedom Fighters.

Q18951344.name: TransAsia Airways Flight 235
Q18951344.blurb: TransAsia Airways Flight 235, with 58 people on board, en route from the Taiwanese capital Taipei to Kinmen, crashes into the Keelung River just after takeoff, killing 43 people.

Q19019163.name: Dutch invasions of Brazil
Q19019163.blurb: Dutch forces led by Hendrick Lonck capture Olinda in what was to become part of Dutch Brazil.

Q19032749.name: Alaska Airlines Flight 779
Q19032749.blurb: Alaska Airlines Flight 779 crashes near Shemya Air Force Base in Shemya, Alaska, killing six.

Q19055654.name: Convention of Alessandria
Q19055654.blurb: War of the Second Coalition: The signing of the Convention of Alessandria brought temporary peace between France and Austria.

Q19065445.name: Presidential Proclamation 4311 of September 8, 1974, by President Gerald R. Ford granting a pardon to Richard M. Nixon. (NAID 299996)
Q19065445.blurb: Watergate scandal: US President Gerald Ford signs the pardon of Richard Nixon for any crimes Nixon may have committed while in office.

Q19096422.name: Let Us Continue
Q19096422.blurb: President Lyndon B. Johnson delivered the "Let Us Continue" speech, in which he advocated for civil-rights legislation and national cohesion, to a joint session of the U.S. Congress five days after the assassination of John F. Kennedy.

Q19107489.name: Treaty with the Shawnee, 1825
Q19107489.blurb: The Treaty of St. Louis between the United States and the Shawnee Nation is proclaimed.

Q19331319.name: 2015 Haiti Carnival stampede
Q19331319.blurb: Eighteen people are killed and 78 injured in a stampede at a Mardi Gras parade in Haiti.

Q19358458.name: 2015 Oxnard train derailment
Q19358458.blurb: A Metrolink train derails in Oxnard, California following a collision with a truck, leaving more than 30 injured.

Q19358494.name: Uherský Brod shooting
Q19358494.blurb: At a restaurant in Uherský Brod, Czech Republic, a gunman opened fire in a restaurant, killing eight people before committing suicide.

Q19361002.name: 2015 Afghanistan avalanche
Q19361002.blurb: At least 310 people are killed in avalanches in northeastern Afghanistan.

Q19362904.name: assassination of Boris Nemtsov
Q19362904.blurb: Russian politician Boris Nemtsov is assassinated in Moscow while out walking with his girlfriend.

Q19390475.name: Sterling Airways Flight 901
Q19390475.blurb: Fifteen people are killed when Sterling Airways Flight 901, a Sud Aviation Caravelle, catches fire following a landing gear collapse at Mehrabad International Airport in Tehran, Iran.

Q19413302.name: 2015 Zasyadko mine disaster
Q19413302.blurb: At least 34 miners die in a suspected gas explosion at the Zasyadko coal mine in the rebel-held Donetsk region of Ukraine.

Q19429010.name: 2014 Odesa clashes
Q19429010.blurb: Russo-Ukrainian War: Forty-eight people were killed during a confrontation between pro-Russian protesters and pro-Ukrainian unity protesters in the southern Ukrainian port city of Odesa.

Q19523169.name: Villa Castelli helicopter collision
aliases: Ten killed in helicopter crash in Argentina, French Olympians among the dead
Q19523169.blurb: Two Eurocopter AS350 Écureuil helicopters collide in mid-air over Villa Castelli, Argentina, killing all 10 people on board both aircraft, including French athletes Florence Arthaud, Camille Muffat and Alexis Vastine, as well as producers and guests for the French TV show Dropped.

Q19574749.name: American Airlines Flight 514
Q19574749.blurb: American Airlines Flight 514, a Boeing 707, crashes near the Calverton Executive Airpark in Calverton, New York, killing all five people on board.

Q19601700.name: 1989 Paraguayan coup d'etat
Q19601700.blurb: A military coup overthrows Alfredo Stroessner, dictator of Paraguay since 1954.

Q19611623.name: Battle of Islandbridge
Q19611623.blurb: Battle of Islandbridge: High King Niall Glúndub is killed while leading an Irish coalition against the Vikings of Uí Ímair, led by King Sitric Cáech.

Q19613356.name: Bardo National Museum attack
Q19613356.blurb: Gunmen attacked the Bardo National Museum in Tunisia, killing 24 people.

Q19646470.name: United States invasion of Afghanistan
aliases: invasion of Afghanistan by the US
Q19646470.blurb: The U.S. invasion of Afghanistan begins with an air assault and covert operations on the ground, starting the longest war in American history.

Q19671417.name: Germanwings Flight 9525
Q19671417.blurb: Germanwings Flight 9525 crashes in the French Alps in an apparent pilot mass murder-suicide, killing all 150 people on board.

Q19682450.name: Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war
aliases: Allegations of Saudi war crimes in Yemen
Command of Coalition Forces Supporting Legitimacy, in Yemen
Saudi Arabia in the Yemen War
Saudi intervention in the Yemeni civil war
Saudi-led intervention in Yemeni civil war
Saudi–led intervention in Yemeni civil war
Saudi–led intervention in the Yemeni civil war
Suspension of Qatar from the Yemeni civil war intervention
Q19682450.blurb: Yemen War: A funeral in Sanaa was hit by two consecutive airstrikes  by a Saudi-led coalition, leaving 143–155 civilians dead and more than 525 injured.

Q19692727.name: Makka al-Mukarama hotel attack
Q19692727.blurb: A siege of a hotel in Mogadishu by al-Shabaab militants, which began the previous day and killed at least 20 people, ended with the Somali Armed Forces recapturing the premises.

Q19693134.name: Air Canada Flight 624
Q19693134.blurb: Air Canada Flight 624 skids off the runway at Halifax Stanfield International Airport, after arriving from Toronto shortly past midnight. All 133 passengers and five crews on board survive, with 23 treated for minor injuries.

Q19750438.name: Garissa University College attack
Q19750438.blurb: Gunmen attack Garissa University College in Kenya, killing at least 148 people and wounding 79 others.

Q19752611.name: Battle of Margarana
Q19752611.blurb: Indonesian National Revolution: 96 Indonesian including I Gusti Ngurah Rai were killed during the Battle of Margarana with Dutch forces.

Q19772356.name: Rafz train crash
Q19772356.blurb: Two trains collide in the Swiss town of Rafz resulting in as many as 49 people injured and Swiss Federal Railways cancelling some services.

Q19789001.name: 2015 Venezuelan parliamentary election
Q19789001.blurb: Venezuelan parliamentary election: For the first time in 17 years, the United Socialist Party of Venezuela loses its majority in parliament.

Q19818693.name: 1930 Costești wooden church fire
Q19818693.blurb: A fire kills 118 people at a wooden church in the small Romanian town of Costești, most of them schoolchildren, after starting during Good Friday services.

Q19830062.name: April 2015 Nepal earthquake
Q19830062.blurb: At least 8,962 are killed in Nepal after a massive 7.8 magnitude earthquake strikes Nepal.

Q19838194.name: 2015 Baltimore protests
Q19838194.blurb: A baseball game between the Baltimore Orioles and the Chicago White Sox sets the all-time low attendance mark for Major League Baseball. Zero fans were in attendance for the game, as the stadium was officially closed to the public due to the 2015 Baltimore protests.

Q19840411.name: Massacre of Phocaea
Q19840411.blurb: Massacre of Phocaea: Turkish irregulars slaughter 50 to 100 Greeks and expel thousands of others in an ethnic cleansing operation in the Ottoman Empire.

Q19841872.name: death of Freddie Gray
Q19841872.blurb: Freddie Gray, a 25-year-old African American, died of injuries sustained while in the custody of the Baltimore Police Department.

Q19858399.name: Curtis Culwell Center attack
Q19858399.blurb: Two gunmen launch an attempted attack on an anti-Islam event in Garland, Texas, which was held in response to the Charlie Hebdo shooting.

Q19865585.name: 1937 Fox vault fire
Q19865585.blurb: The silent film archives of Fox Film Corporation are destroyed by the 1937 Fox vault fire.

Q19868186.name: 1979 Coyote Lake earthquake
Q19868186.blurb: An earthquake struck along the Calaveras Fault near Coyote Lake, California, injuring sixteen people.

Q19870163.name: 1961 Syrian coup d'état
Q19870163.blurb: A military coup in Damascus effectively ends the United Arab Republic, the union between Egypt and Syria.

Q19870724.name: 2015 Copa América Final
Q19870724.blurb: Chile claims its first title in international football by defeating Argentina in the 2015 Copa América final.

Q19870743.name: Anglo-French War of 1213–14
Q19870743.blurb: During the Anglo-French War (1213–1214), an English invasion force led by John, King of England, lands at La Rochelle in France.

Q19873129.name: Battle on Vrtijeljka
Q19873129.blurb: Battle of Vrtijeljka between rebels and Ottoman forces.

Q19874865.name: death of James Cook
Q19874865.blurb: James Cook is killed by Native Hawaiians near Kealakekua on the Island of Hawaii.

Q19878399.name: The Great Fire
Q19878399.blurb: The Great Fire of Spokane, Washington destroys some 32 blocks of the city, prompting a mass rebuilding project.

Q19880899.name: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum theft
Q19880899.blurb: Unidentified thieves stole thirteen works of art collectively valued at $500 million from the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum (pictured) in Boston, Massachusetts.

Q19891526.name: 2018 Malaysian general election
Q19891526.blurb: Barisan Nasional, the coalition that had governed Malaysia since the country's independence in 1957, suffer a historic defeat in the 2018 Malaysian general election.

Q19893821.name: Operation Piranha
Q19893821.blurb: Vietnam War: In a follow-up to August's Operation Starlite, United States Marines and South Vietnamese forces initiate Operation Piranha on the Batangan Peninsula.

Q19895686.name: Battle of Raj Mahal
Q19895686.blurb: Mughal Empire annexes Bengal after defeating the Bengal Sultanate at the Battle of Rajmahal.

Q19896230.name: Miracle Valley shootout
Q19896230.blurb: A gunfight breaks out between police officers and members of a religious cult in Arizona. The shootout leaves two cultists dead and dozens of cultists and police officers injured.

Q19898749.name: May 2015 Nepal earthquake
Q19898749.blurb: Massive Nepal earthquake kills 218 people and injures more than 3,500.

Q19901271.name: 2015 Philadelphia train derailment
Q19901271.blurb: A train derailment in Philadelphia, United States, kills eight people and injures more than 200.

Q19901716.name: Treaty of Paris
Q19901716.blurb: Treaty of Paris between Napoleon and Frederick William III of Prussia against Russia is signed.

Q19902208.name: Dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire
Q19902208.blurb: Francis II, Holy Roman Emperor, declares the moribund empire to be dissolved, although he retains power in the Austrian Empire.

Q19903859.name: Coalbrook mining disaster
Q19903859.blurb: A coal mine collapses at Holly Country, South Africa, killing 435 miners.

Q19906874.name: Sakha Avia Flight 301
Q19906874.blurb: Sakha Avia Flight 301 crashes on approach to Aldan Airport, killing all 24 aboard.

Q19908903.name: Kuban Airlines Flight 5719
Q19908903.blurb: Kuban Airlines Flight 5719 crashes during a go-around at Gyumri Shirak International Airport, killing 35 of the 36 people on board.

Q19914124.name: Treaty of Livadia
Q19914124.blurb: Qing China signed the Treaty of Livadia with the Russian Empire, but the terms were so unfavorable that the Chinese government refused to ratify the treaty.

Q19917124.name: Aeroflot Flight 19
Q19917124.blurb: Aeroflot Flight 19 is hijacked and diverted to Vnukovo International Airport, where the aircraft is stormed by authorities.

Q19944333.name: 2015 Colombian landslide
Q19944333.blurb: At least 78 people die in a landslide caused by heavy rains in the Colombian town of Salgar.

Q19947679.name: Siege of Saïo
Q19947679.blurb: Second World War: After a three-month siege, the Italian garrison of Saïo (in modern-day Ethiopia) surrendered to Belgian, British and Ethiopian troops.

Q19949553.name: Refugio Oil Spill
Q19949553.blurb: The Refugio oil spill deposited 142,800 U.S. gallons (3,400 barrels) of crude oil onto an area in California considered one of the most biologically diverse coastlines of the west coast.

Q19979612.name: Beethoven concert of 22 December 1808
Q19979612.blurb: Ludwig van Beethoven conducts and performs in concert at the Theater an der Wien, Vienna, with the premiere of his Fifth Symphony, Sixth Symphony, Fourth Piano Concerto and Choral Fantasy.

Q20012907.name: Acto de Chacarillas
Q20012907.blurb: The Pinochet dictatorship in Chile organises the youth event of Acto de Chacarillas, a ritualised act reminiscent of Francoist Spain.

Q20024465.name: Sinking of Dongfang zhi Xing
aliases: Sinking of Dong Fang Zhi Xing
Sinking of the Dong Fang Zhi Xing
Sinking of the MV Dong Fang Zhi Xing
Q20024465.blurb: A ship carrying 458 people capsizes in the Yangtze river in China's Hubei province, killing 442 people.

Q20050680.name: Froberg mutiny
Q20050680.blurb: The Froberg mutiny on Malta ends when the remaining mutineers blow up the magazine of Fort Ricasoli.

Q20051451.name: 2015 Sabah earthquake
Q20051451.blurb: An earthquake with a moment magnitude of 6.0 strikes Ranau, Sabah, Malaysia, killing 18 people, including hikers and mountain guides on Mount Kinabalu, after mass landslides that occurred during the earthquake. This is the strongest earthquake to strike Malaysia since 1975.

Q20054768.name: Battle of Apamea
Q20054768.blurb: Arab–Byzantine wars: Battle of Apamea: Fatimids defeat a Byzantine army near Apamea.

Q20080729.name: Sierra Pacific Airlines Flight 802
Q20080729.blurb: Sierra Pacific Airlines Flight 802 crashes into the White Mountains near Bishop, California, killing 36.

Q20106628.name: Revolution of 1933
Q20106628.blurb: Andorran Revolution: The Young Andorrans occupy the Casa de la Vall and force the government to hold democratic elections with universal male suffrage.

Q20121517.name: Donald Trump 2016 presidential campaign
Q20121517.blurb: American businessman Donald Trump announces his campaign to run for President of the United States in the upcoming election.

Q20154675.name: 2015 Charleston, South Carolina shooting
aliases: Emanuel African Methodist Episcopal Church shooting
Q20154675.blurb: Nine people are killed in a mass shooting at Emanuel African Methodist Episcopal Church in Charleston, South Carolina.

Q20164399.name: Battle of São Vicente
Q20164399.blurb: Battle of São Vicente takes place off Portuguese Brazil where three English warships led by navigator Edward Fenton fight off three Spanish galleons sinking one in the process.

Q20180147.name: 1627 Gargano earthquake
Q20180147.blurb: An earthquake kills about 5,000 people in Gargano, Italy.

Q20184042.name: The Terror of War
Q20184042.blurb: Vietnam War: Nine-year-old Phan Thị Kim Phúc is burned by napalm, an event captured in a photograph moments later while the young girl is seen running naked down a road, in what would become an iconic, Pulitzer Prize-winning photo.

Q20203013.name: 2015 Kabul Parliament attack
Q20203013.blurb: The Afghan National Assembly building is attacked by gunmen after a suicide bombing. All six of the gunmen are killed and 18 people are injured.

Q20204978.name: Rising of the Priests
Q20204978.blurb: The unsuccessful Rising of the Priests in Malta.

Q20311386.name: Bloody Friday
Q20311386.blurb: Five different terrorist attacks in France, Tunisia, Somalia, Kuwait, and Syria occur on what was dubbed Bloody Friday by international media. Upwards of 750 people are either killed or injured in these uncoordinated attacks.

Q20441220.name: 2015 New Taipei water park explosion
Q20441220.blurb: Formosa Fun Coast fire: A dust fire occurs at a recreational water park in Taiwan, killing 15 people and injuring 497 others, 199 critically.

Q20452334.name: Peace Agreement of Hat Yai 1989
Q20452334.blurb: The Peace Agreement of Hat Yai is signed and ratified by the Malayan Communist Party (MCP) and the governments of Malaysia and Thailand, ending the over two-decade-long communist insurgency in Malaysia.

Q20502634.name: Neve Shalom Synagogue massacre
Q20502634.blurb: In Istanbul, two terrorists from Abu Nidal's organization kill 22 and wound six congregants inside the Neve Shalom Synagogue during Shabbat services.

Q20512994.name: Zurich Protocols
Q20512994.blurb: Armenia and Turkey sign the Zurich Protocols, intended to normalize relations. However, they are never ratified by either side.

Q20556343.name: Conspiracy of the Slaves
Q20556343.blurb: A plot by Muslim slaves in Malta to assassinate Manuel Pinto da Fonseca of the Knights Hospitaller was uncovered.

Q20593793.name: 2015 Indonesia Hercules C-130 crash
Q20593793.blurb: A Hercules C-130 military aircraft with 113 people on board crashes in a residential area in Medan, Indonesia, resulting in at least 116 deaths.

Q20627484.name: Ottoman conquest of Lesbos
Q20627484.blurb: The Ottoman conquest of Lesbos ended upon the surrender of commander Niccolò Gattilusio; the conquering Mehmed II executed 300 Italian soldiers by chopping them in half, claiming he was fulfilling a promise to "spare their heads".

Q20650851.name: assassination of Ali
Q20650851.blurb: The Rashidun Caliphate is effectively ended with the assassination of Ali, the last caliph.

Q20657156.name: Don Larsen's perfect game
Q20657156.blurb: Major League Baseball pitcher Don Larsen threw the only perfect game in World Series history.

Q20671234.name: 2015 Chattanooga shootings
Q20671234.blurb: Four U.S. Marines and a United States Navy Sailor are killed in the a shooting spree targeting military installations in Chattanooga, Tennessee.

Q20679588.name: 2015 Khan Bani Saad bombing
Q20679588.blurb: At least 120 people are killed and 130 injured by a suicide bombing in Diyala Governorate, Iraq.

Q20685047.name: 2015 Suruç bombing
Q20685047.blurb: A huge explosion in the mostly Kurdish border town of Suruç, Turkey, targeting the Socialist Youth Associations Federation, kills at least 31 people and injures over 100.

Q20711515.name: Congress of Përmet
Q20711515.blurb: Congress of Përmet occurs which establishes a provisional government in Albania in areas under partisan control, the first independent Albanian government since 1939. In honor of this the national emblem of Albania inscribed this date from 1946 until 1992.

Q20712873.name: Siege of Lyme Regis
Q20712873.blurb: First English Civil War: Prince Maurice abandoned his siege of Lyme Regis in Dorset after learning of the approach of a Parliamentarian relief force.

Q20712931.name: Battle of Sant Esteve d'en Bas
Q20712931.blurb: Nine Years' War: At the Battle of Sant Esteve d'en Bas, Catalan miquelets attacked a column of French regular infantry and caused them to surrender.

Q20714105.name: Loganair Flight 670A
Q20714105.blurb: Loganair Flight 670A crashes while attempting to make a water landing in the Firth of Forth in Scotland.

Q20715366.name: 1972 Puerto Rico DC-7 crash
Q20715366.blurb: Puerto Rican baseball player Roberto Clemente (pictured) died in a plane crash en route to deliver aid to victims of that year's Nicaragua earthquake.

Q20724066.name: Battle of Tabora
Q20724066.blurb: World War I: During the East African Campaign, colonial forces of the Belgian Congo (Force Publique) under the command of Charles Tombeur capture the town of Tabora after heavy fighting.

Q20732804.name: 2015 Gurdaspur attack
Q20732804.blurb: Seven people are killed and many injured after gunmen attack an Indian police station in Punjab.

Q20743315.name: Capital Airlines Flight 300
Q20743315.blurb: Capital Airlines Flight 300 collides in mid-air with a United States Air Force Lockheed T-33 over Brunswick, Maryland, killing 12.

Q20743978.name: Turkey–Islamic State conflict
Q20743978.blurb: Balçova police station shooting: 4 people, including the perpetrator are killed an attack on a police station in Turkey.

Q20794976.name: 2015 Abha mosque bombing
Q20794976.blurb: A suicide bomb attack kills at least 15 people at a mosque in the Saudi city of Abha.

Q20811016.name: 2015 Houston shooting
Q20811016.blurb: Eight people are killed in a shooting in Harris County, Texas.

Q20811151.name: Latin Carga Convair CV-880 crash
Q20811151.blurb: A Latin Carga Convair CV-880 crashes at Simón Bolívar International Airport in Venezuela, killing four.

Q20816071.name: 2015 Tianjin explosions
Q20816071.blurb: At least two massive explosions kill 173 people and injure nearly 800 more in Tianjin, China.

Q20816219.name: 1966 Flood in Venice
Q20816219.blurb: The Arno River floods Florence, Italy, to a maximum depth of 6.7 m (22 ft), leaving thousands homeless and destroying millions of masterpieces of art and rare books. Venice is also submerged on the same day at its record all-time acqua alta of 194 cm (76 in).

Q20817352.name: 2015 Baghdad truck bombing
Q20817352.blurb: At least 76 people are killed and 212 others are wounded in a truck bombing in Baghdad, Iraq.

Q20819188.name: 2015 Gold King Mine waste water spill
Q20819188.blurb: The Environmental Protection Agency at Gold King Mine waste water spill releases three million gallons of heavy metal toxin tailings and waste water into the Animas River in Colorado.

Q20823597.name: Trigana Air Service Flight 267
Q20823597.blurb: Trigana Air Flight 267, an ATR 42, crashes in Oksibil, Bintang Mountains Regency, killing all 54 people on board.

Q20824991.name: 2015 Attock Suicide Attack
Q20824991.blurb: Suicide bombers assassinated Pakistani politician Shuja Khanzada and killed at least 21 others at his home in Attock District.

Q20826727.name: 2015 Bangkok bombing
Q20826727.blurb: A bomb explodes near the Erawan Shrine in Bangkok, Thailand, killing at least 19 people and injuring 123 others.

Q20827707.name: 2015 Douma market air strikes
Q20827707.blurb: More than 96 people are killed and hundreds injured following a series of air-raids by the Syrian Arab Air Force on the rebel-held market town of Douma.

Q20828539.name: 1997 Namibia mid-air collision
Q20828539.blurb: A German Air Force Tupolev Tu-154 and a United States Air Force Lockheed C-141 Starlifter collide in mid-air near Namibia, killing 33.

Q20857086.name: 2015 Thalys train attack
Q20857086.blurb: Passengers on a Thalys train from Amsterdam to Paris confronted and subdued an attacker who attempted a mass shooting.

Q20857716.name: 2015 Shoreham Airshow crash
aliases: Vintage plane crashes into road during Shoreham Airshow in England
Q20857716.blurb: A former military aircraft crashed at an airshow at Shoreham Airport in southern England, killing eleven people.

Q20870284.name: Action of 27 February 1809
Q20870284.blurb: Action of 27 February 1809: Captain Bernard Dubourdieu captures HMS Proserpine.

Q20870400.name: Macau Incident
Q20870400.blurb: French Revolutionary Wars: In the Macau Incident, French and Spanish warships encountered a British Royal Navy escort squadron in the Wanshan Archipelago; subsequent events, including which side retreated, were disputed by the commanders present.

Q20873020.name: murders of Alison Parker and Adam Ward
Q20873020.blurb: Two U.S. journalists are shot and killed by a disgruntled former coworker while conducting a live report in Moneta, Virginia.

Q20948837.name: Jeannette expedition
Q20948837.blurb: The Jeannette expedition to reach the North Pole from the Pacific Ocean via the Bering Strait came to an end when the USS Jeannette (pictured), after having been trapped in ice for almost two years, was crushed and sank.

Q20966269.name: Mecca crane collapse
aliases: At least 107 killed in Mecca crane collapse
Q20966269.blurb: A crane collapses onto the Masjid al-Haram mosque in Saudi Arabia, killing 111 people and injuring 394 others.

Q20967938.name: Petlawad Explosion
Q20967938.blurb: An explosion involving illegally stored mining detonators in Petlawad, India, killed 104 people and injured more than 150 others.

Q20977854.name: Second Spanish Armada
Q20977854.blurb: The second Spanish armada sets sail to strike against England, but is smashed by storms off Cape Finisterre forcing a retreat to port.

Q20978169.name: 2015 Illapel earthquake
Q20978169.blurb: A 8.3 Mw earthquake strikes the Chilean city of Illapel, killing 15 people, injuring at least 34, leaving at least six missing, and causing extensive damage. One person also dies in Argentina.

Q20981433.name: 2015 Camp Badaber attack
Q20981433.blurb: Two security personnel, 17 worshippers in a mosque, and 13 militants are killed during a Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan attack on a Pakistan Air Force base on the outskirts of Peshawar.

Q20981909.name: Raid on Santorini
Q20981909.blurb: World War II: The SBS launches a raid against the garrison of Santorini in Greece.

Q20982123.name: 1981 Central African Republic coup d'état
Q20982123.blurb: Central African President David Dacko is ousted from power in a bloodless military coup led by General André Kolingba.

Q20986945.name: 1966 Flying Tiger Line Canadair CL-44 crash
Q20986945.blurb: A Canadair CL-44 chartered by the United States military crashes into a small village in South Vietnam, killing 111.

Q20986946.name: Mexicana de Aviación Flight 801
Q20986946.blurb: Mexicana de Aviación Flight 801, a Boeing 727-100 passenger plane, crashes during a landing attempt in Mexico City, killing 27 of the 118 occupants.

Q20986954.name: Paradise Airlines Flight 901A
Q20986954.blurb: Paradise Airlines Flight 901A crashes near Lake Tahoe, Nevada, killing 85.

Q20996801.name: First Battle of Dernancourt
Q20996801.blurb: World War I: British and Australian troops defeated German forces at the First Battle of Dernancourt in northern France.

Q21000630.name: Volkswagen emissions scandal
aliases: Volkswagen common-rail TDI engine emissions scandal
Volkswagen common-rail TDI diesel engine emissions controversy
Volkswagen common-rail TDI diesel engine emissions scandal
Q21000630.blurb: Volkswagen is fined one billion euros over the emissions scandal.

Q21005831.name: assassination of Spencer Perceval
Q21005831.blurb: Prime Minister Spencer Perceval is assassinated by John Bellingham in the lobby of the British House of Commons.

Q21007721.name: 2015 Mina stampede
Q21007721.blurb: At least 1,100 people are killed and another 934 wounded after a stampede during the Hajj in Saudi Arabia.

Q21012091.name: February 2001 El Salvador earthquake
Q21012091.blurb: A magnitude 6.6 earthquake hits El Salvador, killing at least 315.

Q21012112.name: Carlton Complex Fire
Q21012112.blurb: Lightning strikes started four fires in the Methow Valley in the U.S. state of Washington, collectively known as the Carlton Complex Fire.

Q21035207.name: Hurricane Joaquin
Q21035207.blurb: The American cargo vessel SS El Faro sinks with all of its 33 crew after steaming into the eyewall of Hurricane Joaquin.

Q21036673.name: Umpqua Community College shooting
Q21036673.blurb: A gunman kills nine people at a community college in Oregon.

Q21057198.name: 2015 bombing of Médecins Sans Frontières hospital
Q21057198.blurb: Forty-two people are killed and 33 go missing in the Kunduz hospital airstrike in Afghanistan.

Q21057315.name: 2015 El Cambray Dos landslide
Q21057315.blurb: Heavy rains trigger a major landslide in Guatemala, killing 280 people.

Q21083277.name: 2015 Ankara bombings
Q21083277.blurb: Twin bomb blasts in the Turkish capital Ankara kill 109 and injure 500+.

Q21171141.name: Trollhättan school attack
Q21171141.blurb: A sword-wielding man attacked students and teachers at a high school in Trollhättan, killing three people in Sweden's deadliest school attack.

Q21175521.name: Hurricane Patricia
Q21175521.blurb: Hurricane Patricia, the most intense tropical cyclone on record in the Western Hemisphere, peaked with maximum sustained winds of 215 mph (345 km/h) south of Mexico.

Q21187497.name: December 14, 1998 Albanian–Yugoslav border ambush
Q21187497.blurb: Yugoslav Wars: The Yugoslav Army ambushes a group of Kosovo Liberation Army fighters attempting to smuggle weapons from Albania into Kosovo, killing 36.

Q21190134.name: Sardinian–Aragonese War
Q21190134.blurb: War of the Straits and Sardinian–Aragonese war: The Battle of Alghero results in a crushing victory of the allied Aragonese and Venetian fleet over the Genoese fleet, most of which is captured.

Q21190910.name: Yazidi genocide
aliases: Genocide of Yazidis by the Islamic State
International responses to the Yazidi genocide
International responses to the genocide of Yazidis by the Islamic State
Persecution of Yazidis by the Islamic State
Persecution of Yazidis by the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant
Yazidi acts of revenge on Arabs in Sinjar
Yazidi persecution by the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant
Q21190910.blurb: The genocide of Yazidis by ISIL begins.

Q21201293.name: 2015 Hindu Kush earthquake
Q21201293.blurb: A 7.5 magnitude earthquake strikes in the Hindu Kush mountain range in South Asia, killing 399 people and leaving 2,536 people injured.

Q21282782.name: Metrojet Flight 9268
Q21282782.blurb: Metrojet Flight 9268 is bombed over the northern Sinai Peninsula, killing all 224 people on board.

Q21282871.name: Colectiv nightclub fire
Q21282871.blurb: A fire in a nightclub in the Romanian capital of Bucharest kills sixty-four people and leaves more than 147 injured.

Q21334178.name: 2015 Juba plane crash
Q21334178.blurb: A cargo plane crashes shortly after takeoff from Juba International Airport in Juba, South Sudan, killing at least 37 people.

Q21402069.name: Bento Rodrigues dam disaster
Q21402069.blurb: An iron ore tailings dam bursts in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais, flooding a valley, causing mudslides in the nearby village of Bento Rodrigues and causing at least 17 deaths and two missing.

Q21470354.name: 2015 Beirut bombings
Q21470354.blurb: Two suicide bombers detonate explosives in Bourj el-Barajneh, Beirut, killing 43 people and injuring over 200 others.

Q21479779.name: November 2015 Paris attacks
aliases: Timeline of the November 2015 Paris attacks
Q21479779.blurb: Coordinated terrorist attacks in Paris perpetrated by the Islamic State killed 130 people and injured 413 others.

Q21516923.name: 2015 Bamako hotel attack
Q21516923.blurb: Following a hostage siege, at least 19 people are killed in Bamako, Mali.

Q21532155.name: 2015 Brussels lockdown
Q21532155.blurb: The Belgian government imposed a four-day security lockdown in Brussels based on information about potential terrorist attacks.

Q21532387.name: Our Lady of Lourdes
aliases: Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception
The Case against alleged miracles at Lourdes
Q21532387.blurb: Bernadette Soubirous's first vision of the Blessed Virgin Mary occurs in Lourdes, France.

Q21540349.name: 2015 Russian Sukhoi Su-24 shootdown
aliases: Special forces operation to rescue Russian pilot (November 2015)
