Q21540349.blurb: A Russian Sukhoi Su-24 attack aircraft was shot down by a Turkish fighter jet after the former allegedly strayed into Turkish airspace and ignored warnings to change course.

Q21541716.name: 2015 Tunis bombing
Q21541716.blurb: An explosion on a bus carrying Tunisian Presidential Guard personnel in Tunisia's capital Tunis leaves at least 14 people dead.

Q21567762.name: November 2015 Sinai attack
Q21567762.blurb: A terrorist attack on a hotel in Al-Arish, Egypt, kills at least seven people and injures 12 others.

Q21578719.name: 2015 Colorado Springs shooting
Q21578719.blurb: An active shooter inside a Planned Parenthood facility in Colorado Springs, Colorado, shoots at least four police officers. One officer later dies. Two civilians are also killed, and six injured. The shooter later surrendered.

Q21613643.name: 2015 San Bernardino shooting
Q21613643.blurb: San Bernardino attack: Syed Rizwan Farook and Tashfeen Malik kill 14 people and wound 22 at the Inland Regional Center in San Bernardino, California.

Q21707860.name: Paris Agreement
aliases: Paris Agreement under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
Q21707860.blurb: The Paris Agreement is signed, an agreement to help fight global warming.

Q21715205.name: UEFA Euro 2016 finals: Portugal v France
aliases: 2016 UEFA European Championship Match 51, Portugal v France
Q21715205.blurb: Portugal defeats France in the UEFA Euro 2016 Final to win their first European title.

Q21741364.name: Battle of Fukuda Bay
Q21741364.blurb: The first recorded naval battle between Europeans and the Japanese occurred when a flotilla of samurai attacked two Portuguese trade vessels at the Battle of Fukuda Bay in Nagasaki.

Q21812812.name: 2016 United Kingdom European Union membership referendum
aliases: 2016 United Kingdom European Union (EU) membership referendum
2016 United Kingdom referendum on European Union membership
British referendum on membership of the European Union
EU Referendum Rules triggering a 2nd EU Referendum
Referendum on UK membership of the European Union
Referendum on United Kingdom membership of the European Union
Referendum on the UK's continuing membership of the EU
Referendum on the United Kingdom's membership of the European Union

United Kingdom European Union membership referendum 2016
United Kingdom European Union membership referendum, 2016
United Kingdom European Union membership vote
United Kingdom and Gibraltar European Union membership referendum
United Kingdom referendum on membership of the European Union
United Kingdom referendum on the British membership in the European Union
Q21812812.blurb: Citizens of the United Kingdom voted in favour of leaving the European Union.

Q21932366.name: Vanessa Williams and Miss America
aliases: Vanessa L. Williams and Miss America
Q21932366.blurb: Vanessa Williams, the first African-American Miss America, was forced to resign after the magazine Penthouse published nude photos of her without consent.

Q21995232.name: West Air Sweden Flight 294
Q21995232.blurb: West Air Sweden Flight 294 crashes near the Swedish reservoir of Akkajaure; both pilots, the only people on board, are killed.

Q22021750.name: Announcerless Game
Q22021750.blurb: NBC aired the American football match between the New York Jets and the Miami Dolphins without announcers.

Q22022180.name: CommutAir flight 4821
Q22022180.blurb: CommutAir Flight 4821 crashes on approach to Adirondack Regional Airport, in Saranac Lake, New York, killing two people.

Q22022413.name: Downeast Flight 46
Q22022413.blurb: Downeast Airlines Flight 46 crashes on approach to Knox County Regional Airport in Rockland, Maine, killing 17.

Q22039066.name: 2016 Istanbul bombing
Q22039066.blurb: Ten people are killed and 15 wounded in a bombing near the Blue Mosque in Istanbul.

Q22044766.name: Port Phillip v Van Diemen's Land, 1851
Q22044766.blurb: As part of celebrations marking the separation of Victoria from New South Wales, the inaugural first-class cricket match in Australia began at the Launceston Racecourse in Tasmania.

Q22067779.name: 2016 Jakarta attacks
Q22067779.blurb: Multiple explosions reported near the Sarinah Building, Jakarta, followed by shootout between perpetrators and the police, killing seven people. The Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant claimed responsibility.

Q22078513.name: Battle of El Adde
Q22078513.blurb: The Kenyan Army suffers its worst defeat ever in a battle with Al-Shabaab Islamic insurgents in El-Adde, Somalia. An estimated 150 Kenyan soldiers are killed in the battle.

Q22082207.name: 2016 Ouagadougou attacks
Q22082207.blurb: Thirty-three out of 126 freed hostages are injured and 23 killed in terrorist attacks in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso on a hotel and a nearby restaurant.

Q22082245.name: 1 November 1944 reconnaissance sortie over Japan
Q22082245.blurb: World War II: An American F-13 Superfortress made the first flight by an Allied aircraft over Tokyo since the Doolittle Raid in April 1942.

Q22087833.name: 2015 Sabiha Gökçen Airport bombing
Q22087833.blurb: A bomb explodes at Istanbul's Sabiha Gökçen Airport, killing one airport cleaner. The Kurdistan Freedom Hawks claim responsibility for the attack four days later.

Q22087835.name: Taunsa Sharif bombing
Q22087835.blurb: A suicide bomb attack in Tonsa, Pakistan kills at least seven people and injures 13 others.

Q22089890.name: 1946 Bihar riots
Q22089890.blurb: Inter-religious riots in which Hindu mobs targeted Muslim families began in the Indian state of Bihar, resulting in 2,000 to 30,000 deaths.

Q22093752.name: 1963 Camden PA-24 crash
Q22093752.blurb: American country music stars Patsy Cline, Hawkshaw Hawkins, Cowboy Copas and their pilot Randy Hughes are killed in a plane crash in Camden, Tennessee.

Q22093785.name: Pan Am Flight 121
Q22093785.blurb: Pan Am Flight 121 crashes in the Syrian Desert near Mayadin, Syria, killing 15 and injuring 21.

Q22132920.name: execution of Nimr al-Nimr
Q22132920.blurb: Nimr al-Nimr, a prominent Shia cleric in Saudi Arabia, was executed by the Saudi government along with 46 other people.

Q22662663.name: 2016 Kaohsiung earthquake
Q22662663.blurb: An earthquake of magnitude 6.6 strikes southern Taiwan, killing 117 people.

Q22673778.name: 2016 Bad Aibling train crash
Q22673778.blurb: Two passenger trains collide in the German town of Bad Aibling in the state of Bavaria. Twelve people die and 85 others are injured.

Q22703947.name: 2016 Ad Dair shooting
Q22703947.blurb: A man shoots seven people dead at an education center in Jizan Province, Saudi Arabia.

Q22773990.name: Reeve Aleutian Airways Flight 8
Q22773990.blurb: Reeve Aleutian Airways Flight 8 loses one of its propellers in flight resulting in damage to the flight controls. The Lockheed L-188 Electra makes an emergency landing at Anchorage International Airport and there are no injuries.

Q22812485.name: February 2016 Ankara bombing
Q22812485.blurb: Military vehicles explode outside a Turkish Armed Forces barracks in Ankara, Turkey, killing at least 29 people and injuring 61 others.

Q22910769.name: 2016 Kalamazoo shootings
Q22910769.blurb: Six people are killed and two injured in multiple shooting incidents in Kalamazoo County, Michigan.

Q22923830.name: 2020 United States presidential election
aliases: 2020 United States presidential election recount in Wisconsin
2020 election for President of the United States
2020 presidential campaign in the United States
2020 presidential election in the United States
2020 presidential election of the United States
False claims of fraud in the 2020 United States presidential election
False claims of fraud in the 2020 presidential election
False claims of voter fraud in the 2020 presidential election
President of the United States in 2020
United States third party and independent presidential candidates, 2020
United States third-party and independent presidential candidates, 2020
Q22923830.blurb: United States presidential election: Joe Biden launches his presidential campaign.

Q22927624.name: Tara Air Flight 193
Q22927624.blurb: Tara Air Flight 193, a de Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter aircraft, crashes, with 23 fatalities, in Solighopte, Myagdi District, Dhaulagiri Zone, while en route from Pokhara Airport to Jomsom Airport.

Q22935722.name: Battle of the Horns of Hama
Q22935722.blurb: Saladin routs his Muslim opponents, the Zengids, in the battle of the Horns of Hama, consolidating his control over Syria except for Aleppo.

Q22947367.name: Operation Saegheh
Q22947367.blurb: US supertanker SS Bridgeton collides with mines laid by IRGC, causing a 43-square-meter dent in the body of the oil tanker.

Q22947455.name: Ardenne Abbey massacre
Q22947455.blurb: World War II: Battle of Normandy: At Ardenne Abbey, members of the SS Division Hitlerjugend massacre 23 Canadian prisoners of war.

Q22948744.name: Rebellion of the Alpujarras
Q22948744.blurb: A rebellion breaks out in Alpujarras in response to the forced conversions of Muslims in Spain.

Q22949292.name: Battle of Hama
Q22949292.blurb: The Abbasid army under Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Katib defeats the Qarmatians at the Battle of Hama.

Q23009748.name: Great Boston Fire of 1760
Q23009748.blurb: The Great Boston Fire of 1760 destroys 349 buildings.

Q23012840.name: 2016 Hesston shooting
Q23012840.blurb: Three people are killed and fourteen others injured in a series of shootings in the small Kansas cities of Newton and Hesston.

Q23020010.name: Sodder children disappearance
Q23020010.blurb: Five of nine children become missing after their home in Fayetteville, West Virginia, is burned down.

Q23038154.name: 1976 Burundian coup d'état
Q23038154.blurb: Burundian president Michel Micombero is deposed in a bloodless military coup d'état by deputy Jean-Baptiste Bagaza.

Q23039086.name: Indian campaign of Ahmad Shah Durrani
Q23039086.blurb: Ahmad Shah Durrani defeats the Marathas in the Battle of Barari Ghat.

Q23043313.name: Miqdadiyah bombing
Q23043313.blurb: In the Miqdadiyah bombing: at least 40 people are killed and 58 others wounded following a suicide bombing by ISIL at a Shi'ite funeral in the city of Miqdadiyah, Diyala, Iraq.

Q23045756.name: 2016 Grand-Bassam shootings
Q23045756.blurb: Three gunmen attack two hotels in the Ivory Coast town of Grand-Bassam, killing at least 19 people.

Q23045905.name: March 2016 Ankara bombing
Q23045905.blurb: The Ankara bombing kills at least 37 people.

Q23048209.name: Bangladesh Bank heist
Q23048209.blurb: Cybercriminals initiate the Bangladesh Bank robbery, using the SWIFT network to fraudulently transfer $101 million from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York account of Bangladesh Bank.

Q23055386.name: Eurovision Song Contest 2017
Q23055386.blurb: Eurovision Song Contest: Portugal won the contest for the first time, with the song "Amar pelos dois," performed by Salvador Sobral (pictured).

Q23058296.name: 2018 Zimbabwean general election
Q23058296.blurb: Emmerson Mnangagwa (pictured) was elected to his first full term as president, having served as leader since the 2017 Zimbabwean coup d'état.

Q23198514.name: 2016 Maiduguri suicide bombings
Q23198514.blurb: Two suicide bombers detonate their explosives at a mosque during morning prayer on the outskirts of Maiduguri, Nigeria, killing 24 and injuring 18.

Q23253749.name: Flydubai Flight 981
Q23253749.blurb: Flydubai Flight 981 crashes while attempting to land at Rostov-on-Don international airport, killing all 62 on board.

Q23288674.name: 2016 March Istanbul bombing
Q23288674.blurb: An explosion occurs in Taksim Square in Istanbul, Turkey, killing five people and injuring 36.

Q23303373.name: 2015 Oklahoma State University homecoming parade crash
Q23303373.blurb: A driver deliberately crashes into the Oklahoma State Homecoming parade, killing four people and injuring 34.

Q23303624.name: 2016 Peshawar bus bombing
Q23303624.blurb: A bomb detonates in a bus carrying government employees in Peshawar, Pakistan, killing 15 and injuring at least 30.

Q23365300.name: 2016 Brussels bombings
aliases: Explosions at Brussels airport and subway systems
Q23365300.blurb: Three suicide bombers kill 32 people and injure 316 in the 2016 Brussels bombings at the airport and at the Maelbeek/Maalbeek metro station.

Q23540878.name: 1983 Nigerian coup d'état
Q23540878.blurb: In Nigeria, a coup d'état led by Major General Muhammadu Buhari ends the Second Nigerian Republic.

Q23580887.name: highest temperature recorded on Earth
Q23580887.blurb: The air temperature in Furnace Creek, California, reached 134 °F (56.7 °C), recognized by the World Meteorological Organization as the highest recorded on Earth.

Q23609046.name: 2007 enlargement of the European Union
Q23609046.blurb: Bulgaria and Romania join the EU.

Q23638613.name: 2016 Lahore suicide bombing
Q23638613.blurb: A suicide blast in Gulshan-e-Iqbal Park, Lahore claims over 70 lives and leaves almost 300 others injured. The target of the bombing are Christians celebrating Easter.

Q23688698.name: 2016 Nagorno-Karabakh conflict
Q23688698.blurb: The 2016 Nagorno-Karabakh conflict begins along the Nagorno-Karabakh Line of Contact.

Q23701421.name: Manbij offensive
Q23701421.blurb: Syrian civil war: The Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) launch the Manbij offensive, in order to capture the city of Manbij from the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL).

Q23712863.name: Impeachment process against Dilma Rousseff
Q23712863.blurb: Brazil's President Dilma Rousseff is impeached and removed from office.

Q23772755.name: Kollam temple fire
Q23772755.blurb: The Paravur temple accident, in which a devastating fire caused by the explosion of firecrackers stored for Vishu kills more than one hundred people out of the thousands gathered for the seventh day of Bhadrakali worship.

Q23786046.name: 1979 Interflug Ilyushin Il-18 crash
Q23786046.blurb: An Interflug Ilyushin Il-18 crashes at Quatro de Fevereiro Airport during a rejected takeoff, killing 10.

Q23825118.name: 2016 Kumamoto earthquakes
Q23825118.blurb: The foreshock of a major earthquake occurs in Kumamoto, Japan.

Q23835355.name: 2016 Ecuador earthquake
Q23835355.blurb: Ecuador's worst earthquake in nearly 40 years kills 676 and injures more than 230,000.

Q23838164.name: 2016 Afghanistan earthquake
Q23838164.blurb: An earthquake of 6.6 magnitude strikes 39 km west-southwest of Ashkasham, impacting India, Afghanistan, Tajikistan, Srinagar and Pakistan.

Q23926926.name: Abraham Lincoln's Second State of the Union Address
Q23926926.blurb: American Civil War: In his second State of the Union Address, President Abraham Lincoln reaffirms the necessity of ending slavery as ordered ten weeks earlier in the Emancipation Proclamation.

Q24004490.name: 2016 Fort McMurray Wildfire
Q24004490.blurb: The evacuation of nearly 88,000 people began when a wildfire swept through Fort McMurray, Alberta, Canada, and burned for another 14 months, becoming the costliest disaster in Canadian history.

Q24054268.name: 11 May 2016 Baghdad bombings
Q24054268.blurb: One hundred and ten people are killed in an ISIL bombing in Baghdad.

Q24091473.name: EgyptAir Flight 804
Q24091473.blurb: EgyptAir Flight 804 crashes into the Mediterranean Sea while traveling from Paris to Cairo, killing all on board.

Q24185572.name: Death of Ms Dhu
Q24185572.blurb: Julieka Ivanna Dhu, an Aboriginal Australian woman, died in police custody after her deteriorating condition was mocked and ignored.

Q24190721.name: 2019 Canadian federal election
Q24190721.blurb: In Canada, the 2019 Canadian federal election ends, resulting in incumbent Prime Minister Justin Trudeau remaining in office, albeit with the Liberal Party in a minority government.

Q24191110.name: The Great Slave Auction
Q24191110.blurb: The two-day Great Slave Auction, once thought to be the largest such auction in United States history, begins.

Q24196178.name: O'Doherty's Rebellion
Q24196178.blurb: In Ireland, O'Doherty's Rebellion is launched by the Burning of Derry.

Q24196256.name: Burning of Derry
Q24196256.blurb: In Ireland, O'Doherty's Rebellion is launched by the Burning of Derry.

Q24197257.name: Cairngorm Plateau Disaster
Q24197257.blurb: In Britain's worst mountaineering tragedy, the Cairngorm Plateau Disaster, five children and one of their leaders are found dead from exposure in the Scottish mountains.

Q24259918.name: Pittsburgh railroad strike of 1877
Q24259918.blurb: Much of central Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, was burned and looted during the Great Railroad Strike of 1877.

Q24342277.name: 2016 Aktobe shootings
Q24342277.blurb: Two shootings in Aktobe, Kazakhstan, kill six people.

Q24406578.name: Battle of Yanshi
Q24406578.blurb: Transition from Sui to Tang: Wang Shichong decisively defeats Li Mi at the Battle of Yanshi.

Q24558579.name: Pokémon
aliases: List of main characters on Pokemon
Pokemon Appearances in Super Smash Bros.
Pokémon Appearances in Super Smash Bros.
Q24558579.blurb: Burger King and the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission order a recall of plastic Poké Ball containers after they are determined to be a choking hazard.

Q24561572.name: Orlando nightclub shooting
aliases: Reactions to the 2016 Orlando nightclub shooting
Reactions to the Orlando nightclub shooting
Q24561572.blurb: Forty-nine civilians are killed and 58 others injured in an attack on a gay nightclub in Orlando, Florida, United States; the gunman, Omar Mateen, is killed in a gunfight with police.

Q24661988.name: murder of Jo Cox
Q24661988.blurb: Jo Cox, a British Member of Parliament, was murdered in her constituency.

Q24884216.name: Trans-Colorado Airlines Flight 2286
Q24884216.blurb: Trans-Colorado Airlines Flight 2286 crashes in Bayfield, Colorado, killing nine.

Q24906306.name: Kidnapping of Aimee Semple McPherson
Q24906306.blurb: Pentecostal evangelist Aimee Semple McPherson (pictured) was reportedly kidnapped near Venice Beach in Los Angeles before reappearing five weeks later in Mexico.

Q24929357.name: 1505 Lo Mustang earthquake
Q24929357.blurb: The M8.2–8.8 Lo Mustang earthquake affects Tibet and Nepal, causing severe damage in Kathmandu and parts of the Indo-Gangetic plain.

Q24930704.name: Tate murders
Q24930704.blurb: Tate–LaBianca murders: Followers of Charles Manson murder pregnant actress Sharon Tate (wife of Roman Polanski), coffee heiress Abigail Folger, Polish actor Wojciech Frykowski, men's hairstylist Jay Sebring and recent high-school graduate Steven Parent.

Q24963808.name: 1998 Guatemala Student Rapes
Q24963808.blurb: In Santa Lucía Cotzumalguapa, Guatemala, thirteen American students on a school trip are attacked and robbed at gunpoint; five were raped.

Q25007917.name: 2016 Istanbul airport attack
Q25007917.blurb: A terrorist attack in Turkey's Istanbul Atatürk Airport kills 42 people and injures more than 230 others.

Q25039456.name: 1993 Guam earthquake
Q25039456.blurb: The 7.8 Mw Guam earthquake shakes the island with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent), causing around $250 million in damage and injuring up to 71 people.

Q25043458.name: July 1966 Burundian coup d'état
Q25043458.blurb: King Mwambutsa IV of Burundi was deposed in a coup d'état by his son, Prince Charles Ndizi.

Q25051100.name: 2013 Iranian diplomat kidnapping
Q25051100.blurb: Nour Ahmad Nikbakht, an Iranian diplomat in Yemen, was kidnapped by al-Qaeda militants and held hostage for the next two years.

Q25239571.name: 2016–17 UEFA Champions League knockout phase
Q25239571.blurb: The tour bus of the German football team Borussia Dortmund is attacked with roadside bombs in Dortmund, Germany. Three bombs exploded as the bus ferried the team to the Westfalenstadion for the first leg of their quarter-final against Monaco.

Q25339721.name: Women's March
Q25339721.blurb: About 20,000 women marched on Pretoria, South Africa, to protest the introduction of pass laws for black women under apartheid.

Q25414493.name: Henry Morgan's raid on Porto Bello
Q25414493.blurb: Anglo-Spanish War (1654–1660): Henry Morgan with an English privateer force landed at Porto Bello (in modern-day Panama) in an attempt to capture the Spanish city.

Q25439967.name: Portugal in the Eurovision Song Contest 2017
Q25439967.blurb: Eurovision Song Contest: Portugal won the contest for the first time, with the song "Amar pelos dois," performed by Salvador Sobral (pictured).

Q25540102.name: 1978 Qom protest
Q25540102.blurb: Iranian Revolution: Protests took place in Qom after an article insulting Ruhollah Khomeini was published.

Q25631175.name: 2016 shooting of Dallas police officers
aliases: Five police officers killed in Dallas, Texas  during sniper attack
Q25631175.blurb: Ex-US Army soldier Micah Xavier Johnson shoots fourteen policemen, killing five of them, in downtown Dallas, Texas at the end of a protest of recent police killings of Black men. He is subsequently killed by a robot-delivered bomb.

Q25893254.name: 2016 Nice attack
aliases: International reactions to the 2016 Nice attack
International reactions to the 2016 attack in Nice
Q25893254.blurb: A man ploughs a truck into a Bastille Day celebration in Nice, France, killing 86 people and injuring another 434 before being shot by police.

Q25906338.name: 2016 Turkish coup d'état attempt
Q25906338.blurb: Factions of the Turkish Armed Forces attempt a coup.

Q26084467.name: Sagamihara stabbings
Q26084467.blurb: The Sagamihara stabbings occur in Kanagawa Prefecture in Japan. Nineteen people are killed.

Q26236680.name: August 2016 Quetta attacks
Q26236680.blurb: Terrorists attack a government hospital in Quetta, Pakistan with a suicide blast and shooting, killing between 70 and 94 people, and injuring around 130 others.

Q26237347.name: 2016 Ethiopian protests
Q26237347.blurb: Following nationwide protests, Hailemariam Desalegn announced his resignation as prime minister of Ethiopia, remaining in post as a caretaker until he was succeeded by Abiy Ahmed.

Q26436398.name: August 2016 Gaziantep bombing
Q26436398.blurb: Fifty-four people are killed when a suicide bomber detonates himself at a Kurdish wedding party in Gaziantep, Turkey.

Q26689701.name: August 2016 Central Italy earthquake
Q26689701.blurb: An earthquake strikes Central Italy with a magnitude of 6.2, with aftershocks felt as far as Rome and Florence. Around 300 people are killed.

Q26707660.name: killing of Amadou Diallo
Q26707660.blurb: Unarmed West African immigrant Amadou Diallo is shot 19 times by four plainclothes New York City police officers on an unrelated stake-out, inflaming race relations in the city.

Q26799687.name: Austro-Turkish War of 1716–1718
Q26799687.blurb: Austro-Turkish War (1716–1718):The Austrians defeat the Ottomans in the Battle of Petrovaradin. One-fifth of a Turkish army and the Grand Vizier are killed.

Q26809259.name: Anglo-Spanish War
aliases: Spain and the American Revolutionary War
Spain in the American Revolutionary War
Q26809259.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Spain declares war on the Kingdom of Great Britain, and the Great Siege of Gibraltar begins.

Q26834372.name: September 2016 North Korean nuclear test
Q26834372.blurb: The government of North Korea conducts its fifth and reportedly biggest nuclear test. World leaders condemn the act, with South Korea calling it "maniacal recklessness".

Q26910860.name: Siege of Arrah
Q26910860.blurb: Indian Rebellion: Sixty-eight men hold out for eight days against a force of 2,500 to 3,000 mutinying sepoys and 8,000 irregular forces.

Q26916567.name: 2016 New York and New Jersey bombings
Q26916567.blurb: Two bombs explode in Seaside Park, New Jersey, and Manhattan. Thirty-one people are injured in the Manhattan bombing.

Q26929436.name: 2016 Uri attack
Q26929436.blurb: The 2016 Uri attack in Jammu and Kashmir, India by terrorist group Jaish-e-Mohammed results in the deaths of nineteen Indian Army soldiers and all four attackers.

Q27049889.name: 1851 America's Cup
Q27049889.blurb: The yacht America won the race for the Cup of One Hundred Sovereigns (trophy pictured), later renamed the America's Cup, near the Isle of Wight, England.

Q27058656.name: Hurricane Matthew
aliases: Effects of Hurricane Matthew in the Carolinas
Effects of Hurricane Matthew in the United States
Q27058656.blurb: Hurricane Matthew becomes a Category 5 hurricane, making it the strongest hurricane to form in the Caribbean Sea since 2007.

Q27145747.name: Catalan independence referendum, 2017
Q27145747.blurb: An independence referendum, later declared illegal by the Constitutional Court of Spain, takes place in Catalonia.

Q27149688.name: 2016 Sana'a funeral air raid
Q27149688.blurb: Yemen War: A funeral in Sanaa was hit by two consecutive airstrikes  by a Saudi-led coalition, leaving 143–155 civilians dead and more than 525 injured.

Q27230923.name: Spanish conquest of the Muisca
Q27230923.blurb: Bacatá, the main settlement of the Muisca Confederation in present-day Colombia, was conquered by Spanish conquistadors led by Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada.

Q27240039.name: Death and funeral of Bhumibol Adulyadej
Q27240039.blurb: The King of Thailand, Bhumibol Adulyadej, died after 70 years on the throne, at which point was the longest-reigning current monarch.

Q27429856.name: Battle of Mosul
Q27429856.blurb: Iraqi Civil War: Mosul is declared fully liberated from the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant by the government of Iraq.

Q27554442.name: 2016 Quetta police station attack
Q27554442.blurb: Three heavily armed terrorists from the Islamic State – Khorasan Province open fire on and eventually suicide bomb a police training centre in Balochistan, Pakistan, killing at least 59 cadets and injuring more than 165 others.

Q27588890.name: Battle at Fort Utah
Q27588890.blurb: Brigham Young declares war on Timpanogos in the Battle at Fort Utah.

Q27627673.name: Battle of Abu Hamed
Q27627673.blurb: Mahdist War: Anglo-Egyptian soldiers clashed with Mahdist Sudanese rebels in the Battle of Abu Hamed.

Q27628131.name: Operation Appearance
Q27628131.blurb: Operation Appearance takes place to re-establish British Somaliland.

Q27628137.name: 1980 Liberian coup d'état
Q27628137.blurb: The Americo-Liberian government of Liberia is violently deposed.

Q27628424.name: Turkish occupation of northern Syria
Q27628424.blurb: Syrian civil war: Following the completion of the Afrin offensive, the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) initiate an insurgency against the Turkish occupation of the Afrin District.

Q27628585.name: Loss of MV Darlwyne
Q27628585.blurb: The pleasure cruiser MV Darlwyne disappears off the Cornwall coast with the loss of all 31 aboard.

Q27629653.name: Choi Soon-sil gate
Q27629653.blurb: Park Geun-hye, the president of South Korea, was impeached, marking the culmination of the country's political scandal.

Q27629701.name: United Kingdom invocation of Article 50
Q27629701.blurb: British prime minister Theresa May invoked Article 50 of the Treaty on European Union, formally beginning the United Kingdom's withdrawal from the European Union.

Q27630508.name: 2016 Malta Fairchild Merlin crash
Q27630508.blurb: A French surveillance aircraft flying to Libya crashes on takeoff in Malta, killing all five people on board.

Q27761867.name: Raqqa Campaign
Q27761867.blurb: Syrian civil war: The Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) declare victory in the Raqqa campaign.

Q27794967.name: 2016 Indian banknote demonetisation
Q27794967.blurb: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi publicly announces the withdrawal of ₹500 and ₹1000 denomination banknotes.

Q27807478.name: 2016 Croydon tram derailment
Q27807478.blurb: A tram derailment in Croydon, London, killed seven people.

Q27809653.name: first presidency of Donald Trump
aliases: Donald Trump's first term as President of the United States
Drug policy of the Trump administration
Education policy of the first Donald Trump administration
Federal judicial appointments of Donald Trump
Forty-fifth presidency of the United States
Health policy of the Donald Trump administration
Science policy of the Donald Trump administration
Q27809653.blurb: Donald Trump is elected the 45th President of the United States, defeating Hillary Clinton, the first woman ever to receive a major party's nomination.

Q27850765.name: 2016 North Canterbury earthquake
Q27850765.blurb: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake strikes Kaikōura, New Zealand, at a depth of 15 km (9 miles), resulting in the deaths of two people.

Q27915277.name: Battle of al-Bab
Q27915277.blurb: The Turkish-backed Free Syrian Army captures Al-Bab from ISIL.

Q27916528.name: Independence of Finland
Q27916528.blurb: Eduskunta declares itself the supreme state power of Finland, prompting its declaration of independence and secession from Russia.

Q27925924.name: LaMia Flight 2933
aliases: Associação Chapecoense de Futebol plane crash
International reactions to the LaMia Airlines Flight 2933 accident
Q27925924.blurb: LaMia Flight 2933 crashes near Medellín, Colombia, killing 71 of 77 people on board, including members of the Brazilian football club Chapecoense

Q27940416.name: Battle of Khazir
Q27940416.blurb: The Umayyad forces suffer a decisive defeat against the pro-Alid forces under Ibrahim ibn al-Ashtar in the battle of Khazir.

Q27942570.name: Impeachment of Park Geun-hye
Q27942570.blurb: The impeachment of President Park Geun-hye of South Korea in response to a major political scandal is unanimously upheld by the country's Constitutional Court, ending her presidency.

Q27950749.name: 2016 Oakland warehouse fire
Q27950749.blurb: Thirty-six people die in a fire at a converted Oakland, California, warehouse serving as an artist collective.

Q27957408.name: Fifth Virginia Convention
Q27957408.blurb: The Fifth Virginia Convention adopted a declaration of rights, an influential document that proclaimed the inherent rights of men.

Q27958841.name: state funeral of Queen Victoria
aliases: Death and state funeral of Victoria of the United Kingdom
State funeral of Victoria of the United Kingdom
funeral of Victoria of the United Kingdom
Q27958841.blurb: Edward VII is proclaimed King of the United Kingdom after the death of his mother, Queen Victoria.

Q27972892.name: Lyngiades massacre
Q27972892.blurb: World War II: German forces murder 92 civilians in Lingiades, Greece.

Q27988528.name: December 2016 Istanbul bombings
Q27988528.blurb: Two explosions outside a football stadium in Istanbul, Turkey, kill 38 people and injure 166 others.

Q27990600.name: Madagali suicide bombings
Q27990600.blurb: At least 57 people are killed and a further 177 injured when two schoolgirl suicide bombers attack a market area in Madagali, Adamawa, Nigeria in the Madagali suicide bombings.

Q28000229.name: Sarny Massacre
Q28000229.blurb: First day of the Sarny Massacre, perpetrated by Germans and Ukrainians.

Q28036166.name: assassination of Andrei Karlov
aliases: Assassination of Russian Ambassador in turkey
Assassination of Russian Ambassador to turkey
Q28036166.blurb: Russian ambassador to Turkey Andrei Karlov is assassinated while at an art exhibition in Ankara. The assassin, Mevlüt Mert Altıntaş, is shot and killed by a Turkish guard.

Q28036573.name: 2016 Berlin attack
Q28036573.blurb: A vehicular attack in Berlin, Germany, kills 12 and injures 56 people at a Christmas market.

Q28037840.name: 2016 Irkutsk mass methanol poisoning
Q28037840.blurb: The first victims of a mass methanol poisoning which eventually killed over 70 inhabitants of Irkutsk, Russia, began arriving at hospitals.

Q28038710.name: 1856 Heraklion earthquake
Q28038710.blurb: An M 7.7–8.3 earthquake off the Greek island of Crete cause major damage as far as Egypt and Malta.

Q28043715.name: Aerosucr Fliht666
Q28043715.blurb: Aerosucre Flight 157 crashes during takeoff from Germán Olano Airport in Puerto Carreño, Colombia, killing five people.

Q28055770.name: 2016 Russian Defence Ministry Tupolev Tu-154 crash
aliases: 2016 Russian Air Force Tupolev Tu-154 crash
Q28055770.blurb: A Tupolev Tu-154 of the Russian Defence Ministry crashed into the Black Sea shortly after taking off from Sochi International Airport, killing all 92 people on board.

Q28059571.name: 1989 Panamanian coup d'état attempt
Q28059571.blurb: A coup in Panama City is suppressed and 11 participants are executed.

Q28060171.name: Day of Seven Billion
Q28060171.blurb: The global population of humans reaches seven billion. This day is now recognized by the United Nations as the Day of Seven Billion.

Q28094271.name: 2017 Istanbul nightclub attack
aliases: Conspiracy theories about the Istanbul nightclub shooting
Q28094271.blurb: An attack on a nightclub in Istanbul, Turkey, during New Year's celebrations, kills 39 people and injures 79 others.

Q28100410.name: 2017 Women's March
Q28100410.blurb: Over 400 cities across America and 160+ countries worldwide participate in a large-scale women's march, including in Portland, on Donald Trump's first full day as President of the United States.

Q28128279.name: 2017 Indianapolis 500
Q28128279.blurb: Former Formula One driver Takuma Sato wins his first Indianapolis 500, the first Japanese and Asian driver to do so. Double world champion Fernando Alonso retires from the race with an engine issue in his first entry of the event.

Q28130514.name: Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons
aliases: Treaty for the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons
Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW)
UN Treaty for the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons
Q28130514.blurb: The Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons was adopted with 122 countries voting in favour.

Q28133931.name: 2017 Fort Lauderdale Airport shooting
Q28133931.blurb: Five people are killed and six others injured in a mass shooting at Fort Lauderdale–Hollywood International Airport in Broward County, Florida.

Q28135433.name: Australia census 1911
Q28135433.blurb: The Australian Bureau of Statistics conducted the first national census of the country.

Q28136181.name: Sylhet referendum, 1947
Q28136181.blurb: Referendum held in Sylhet to decide its fate in the Partition of India.

Q28136838.name: Trunajaya rebellion
Q28136838.blurb: Trunajaya rebellion: Amangkurat II of Mataram and his bodyguards execute the rebel leader Trunajaya.

Q28154442.name: 2002 Lyon car attack
Q28154442.blurb: The 2002 Lyon car attack takes place.

Q28155290.name: Sack of Shamakhi
Q28155290.blurb: The city of Shamakhi in Safavid Shirvan is sacked.

Q28162777.name: Anglo-Egyptian conquest of Sudan
Q28162777.blurb: Anglo-Egyptian conquest of Sudan: British forces under the command of Horatio Kitchener take Dongola.

Q28162861.name: Siege of Melite
Q28162861.blurb: The city of Melite surrenders to an Aghlabid army following a siege, putting an end to Byzantine Malta.

Q28163691.name: Sempati Air Flight 304
Q28163691.blurb: After takeoff from Husein Sastranegara International Airport, Sempati Air Flight 304 crashes into a residential neighborhood in Bandung, killing 28 people.

Q28169539.name: 1994 Imam Reza shrine bomb explosion
Q28169539.blurb: The 1994 Imam Reza shrine bomb explosion in Iran leaves at least 25 dead and 70 to 300 injured.

Q28169547.name: Chemical bombing of Sardasht
Q28169547.blurb: For the first time in military history, a civilian population is targeted for chemical attack when Iraqi warplanes bomb the Iranian town of Sardasht.

Q28169617.name: Fall of Babylon
Q28169617.blurb: The army of Cyrus the Great of Persia conquer Babylon, ending the Babylonian empire. (Julian calendar)

Q28169835.name: 1936 Tulkarm shooting
Q28169835.blurb: Two Jews were killed near Tulkarm in Mandatory Palestine,  an act widely viewed as the beginning of violence within the Arab revolt.

Q28169846.name: The Bloody Day in Jaffa
Q28169846.blurb: The Jaffa riots commence, initiating the 1936–1939 Arab revolt in Palestine.

Q28197704.name: Victoria & Paddington Station bombing
Q28197704.blurb: The IRA explodes bombs in the early morning at Paddington station and Victoria station in London.

Q28217871.name: 2018 Winter Olympics opening ceremony
Q28217871.blurb: Winter Olympics: Opening ceremony is performed in Pyeongchang County in South Korea.

Q28219689.name: 2016 South Australian blackout
Q28219689.blurb: The 2016 South Australian blackout occurs, lasting up to three days in some areas.

Q28219990.name: Carnival tragedy of 1823
Q28219990.blurb: Carnival tragedy of 1823: About 110 boys are killed during a human crush at the Convent of the Minori Osservanti in Valletta, Malta.

Q28220142.name: 2018 Brazilian general election
Q28220142.blurb: Jair Bolsonaro is elected president of Brazil with 57 million votes, with Workers' Party candidate Fernando Haddad as the runner-up. It is the first time in 16 years that a Workers' Party candidate is not elected president.

Q28221977.name: Council of Blachernae
Q28221977.blurb: A synod at Blachernae convened by anti-Unionist Greek clergy condemns the former pro-Unionist patriarch John XI of Constantinople.

Q28223278.name: 2000 ASA Pesada Antonov An-24 crash
Q28223278.blurb: A chartered Antonov An-24 crashes after takeoff from Luanda, Angola, killing more than 40 people.

Q28224435.name: Air Fiji Flight 121
Q28224435.blurb: Air Fiji flight 121 crashes while en route to Nadi, Fiji, killing all 17 people on board.

Q28230033.name: Razing of Anogeia
Q28230033.blurb: World War II: German troops begin the pillage and razing of Anogeia in Crete that would continue until September 5.

Q28231617.name: National Airlines Flight 83
Q28231617.blurb: National Airlines Flight 83 crashes during landing at Philadelphia International Airport, killing seven passengers and crew.

Q28231738.name: World Airways Flight 802
Q28231738.blurb: World Airways Flight 802 crashes into Mount Dutton in King Cove, Alaska, killing six people.

Q28232969.name: Downpatrick bombing 1990
Q28232969.blurb: An IRA bombing in County Down, Northern Ireland, kills three members of the UDR.

Q28403236.name: University of Texas Tower Shooting
Q28403236.blurb: Charles Whitman kills 15 people at the University of Texas at Austin before being killed by the police.

Q28433149.name: Treaty of Indian Springs
Q28433149.blurb: The Creek cede the last of their lands in Georgia to the United States government by the Treaty of Indian Springs, and migrate west.

Q28433158.name: Treaty of St. Louis
Q28433158.blurb: The Treaty of St. Louis is signed in St. Louis, Missouri.

Q28450472.name: Isaaq Genocide
Q28450472.blurb: Mohammed Said Hersi Morgan sends a "letter of death" to Somali President Siad Barre, proposing the genocide of the Isaaq people.

Q28450603.name: 2000 Marsa Brega Short 360 crash
Q28450603.blurb: A Short 360 aircraft chartered by the Sirte Oil Company crashes off the coast of Brega, Libya, killing 21.

Q28469386.name: Women's March on Portland
Q28469386.blurb: Over 400 cities across America and 160+ countries worldwide participate in a large-scale women's march, including in Portland, on Donald Trump's first full day as President of the United States.

Q28482411.name: 2017-2019 Romanian protests
Q28482411.blurb: An anti-government rally turns into a riot when members of the Romanian Gendarmerie attack the 100,000 people protesting in front of the Victoria Palace, leading to 452 recorded injuries. The authorities alleged that the crowd was infiltrated by hooligans who began attacking law enforcement agents.

Q28485502.name: crisis in Venezuela
Q28485502.blurb: Crisis in Venezuela: Seven people are injured when two drones detonate explosives on Avenida Bolívar, Caracas while president Nicolás Maduro is giving a speech to the Venezuelan National Guard.

Q28549976.name: 2017 Quebec City mosque shooting
Q28549976.blurb: A gunman opens fire at the Islamic Cultural Centre of Quebec City, killing six people and wounding 19 others in a spree shooting.

Q28553907.name: Battle of Adramyttion
Q28553907.blurb: The Battle of Adramyttion begins in which a Christian naval league defeats a Turkish fleet in several encounters.

Q28667972.name: One Piece
aliases: Episode of the Island of Perpetual Winter
List of One Piece home video releases
List of One Piece story arcs
Q28667972.blurb: Written and illustrated by Eiichiro Oda, One Piece, the best-selling manga series in history, debuted in Weekly Shōnen Jump.

Q28713898.name: Death and state funeral of Ruhollah Khomeini
Q28713898.blurb: In the 1989 Iranian supreme leader election, Ali Khamenei is elected as the new Supreme Leader of Iran after the death and funeral of Ruhollah Khomeini.

Q28717575.name: Sack of Aleppo
Q28717575.blurb: The Sack of Aleppo as part of the Arab–Byzantine wars: Under the future Emperor Nicephorus Phocas, Byzantine troops storm the city of Aleppo.

Q28746090.name: Hospitaller conquest of Rhodes
Q28746090.blurb: The city of Rhodes surrenders to the forces of the Knights of St. John, completing their conquest of Rhodes. The knights establish their headquarters on the island and rename themselves the Knights of Rhodes.

Q28836436.name: assassination of Kim Jong-nam
Q28836436.blurb: Kim Jong-nam, brother of North Korean dictator Kim Jong-un, is assassinated at Kuala Lumpur International Airport.

Q29001838.name: 2017 Westminster attack
Q29001838.blurb: A terrorist attack in London near the Houses of Parliament leaves four people dead and at least 20 injured.

Q29025325.name: 1968 Meckering earthquake
Q29025325.blurb: The 6.5 Mw Meckering earthquake shakes the southwest portion of Western Australia with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent), causing $2.2 million in damage and leaving 20–28 people injured.

Q29025615.name: conflict in Rakhine State
Q29025615.blurb: Conflict in Rakhine State (2016–present): One hundred seventy people are killed in at least 26 separate attacks carried out by the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army, leading to the governments of Myanmar and Malaysia designating the group as a terrorist organisation.

Q29025652.name: Battle of Plaman Mapu
Q29025652.blurb: Indonesia–Malaysia confrontation: British forces repelled a surprise Indonesian attack on a base at Plaman Mapu in Sarawak.

Q29026955.name: Battle of Berea
Q29026955.blurb: Led by George Cathcart, British troops defeated Basuto and Taung forces at the Battle of Berea in present-day Lesotho, leading to an offer of peace from King Moshoeshoe I.

Q29027046.name: Mogilev conference
Q29027046.blurb: Operation Barbarossa: A Wehrmacht training event known as the Mogilev Conference began, marking an increase in violence against Jews and other civilians in the areas under General Max von Schenckendorff's command.

Q29043962.name: Battle of Surabaya (1677)
Q29043962.blurb: Trunajaya rebellion: Dutch East India Company forces under Cornelis Speelman began an attack on Surabaya, on the island of Java.

Q29045045.name: forced conversions of Muslims in Spain
Q29045045.blurb: Isabella I issues an edict outlawing Islam in the Crown of Castile, forcing virtually all her Muslim subjects to convert to Christianity.

Q29054585.name: Battle of Ilava
Q29054585.blurb: The Battle of Ilava: The Hungarians defeat the Hussite army.

Q29060321.name: Razing of Vorizia
Q29060321.blurb: World War II: Aerial bombardment by the Luftwaffe razes to the ground the village of Vorizia in Crete.

Q29075160.name: Battle of the Boar's Head
Q29075160.blurb: World War I: In "the day Sussex died", elements of the Royal Sussex Regiment take heavy casualties in the Battle of the Boar's Head at Richebourg-l'Avoué in France.

Q29075256.name: Battle of Pallene
Q29075256.blurb: A Latin Christian fleet defeats a Turkish fleet in the battle of Pallene during the Smyrniote crusades.

Q29097890.name: attack on Richard Nixon's motorcade
Q29097890.blurb: US vice president Richard Nixon's motorcade was attacked by a mob in Caracas, Venezuela.

Q29113584.name: 2017 Saint Petersburg Metro attack
Q29113584.blurb: A bomb explodes in the St Petersburg metro system, killing 14 and injuring several more people.

Q29154471.name: Khan Shaykhun chemical attack
aliases: Gas attack reportedly kills dozens in Syria
Q29154471.blurb: Syria conducts an air strike on Khan Shaykhun using chemical weapons, killing 89 civilians.

Q29197866.name: 2017 Shayrat missile strike
aliases: 7th April American missile strikes in Syria
United States missile strike in Syria
Q29197866.blurb: U.S. military launches 59 Tomahawk cruise missiles at an air base in Syria. Russia describes the strikes as an "aggression", adding they significantly damage US-Russia ties.

Q29213121.name: 2017 Stockholm attack
Q29213121.blurb: A man deliberately drives a hijacked truck into a crowd of people in Stockholm, Sweden, killing five people and injuring fifteen others.

Q29258911.name: Battle of Tabqa
Q29258911.blurb: Syrian civil war: The Syrian Democratic Forces, assisted by the U.S. military, captured the Tabqa Dam and surrounding countryside, completing the Battle of Tabqa.

Q29297504.name: Palm Sunday church bombings
aliases: 2017 St. Markus Church attack in Alexandria
Q29297504.blurb: The Palm Sunday church bombings at Coptic churches in Tanta and Alexandria, Egypt, take place.

Q29354759.name: 2017 attack on Borussia Dortmund team bus
aliases: Borussia Dortmund's team bus hit with explosives before Champions League match, Marc Bartra injured
Q29354759.blurb: The tour bus of the German football team Borussia Dortmund is attacked with roadside bombs in Dortmund, Germany. Three bombs exploded as the bus ferried the team to the Westfalenstadion for the first leg of their quarter-final against Monaco.

Q29385187.name: April 2017 Achin airstrike
Q29385187.blurb: War in Afghanistan: In an airstrike in Nangarhar Province, the U.S. military dropped the most powerful conventional bomb used in combat.

Q29514943.name: Assassination of Guillem Agulló i Salvador
Q29514943.blurb: Guillem Agulló, pro-Catalan independence and anti-fascist Valencian young activist, is assassinated by a group of Spanish nationalists and neo-nazis in Montanejos.

Q29530237.name: Battle of Trahili
Q29530237.blurb: World War II:  Battle of Trahili: Superior German forces surround Cretan partisans, who manage to escape against all odds.

Q29629470.name: Kediri Campaign
Q29629470.blurb: Trunajaya rebellion: After a long and logistically challenging march, the allied Mataram and Dutch troops successfully assault the rebel stronghold of Kediri.

Q29914504.name: Bussa's rebellion
Q29914504.blurb: Bussa, a slave in British-ruled Barbados, leads a slave rebellion, for which he is remembered as the country's first national hero.

Q29957041.name: WannaCry ransomware attack
Q29957041.blurb: The WannaCry ransomware attack impacts over 400,000 computers worldwide, targeting computers of the United Kingdom's National Health Services and Telefónica computers.

Q29998835.name: Humboldt Park riot
Q29998835.blurb: The Humboldt Park riot began in Chicago, resulting in three deaths, three cars in the Humboldt Park lagoon, and increased tension between the Chicago Police Department and the Puerto Rican community.

Q30015850.name: 2017 Manchester Arena bombing
aliases: Broken. from the bottom of my heart, i am so so sorry. i don't have words.
Q30015850.blurb: Twenty-two people are killed at an Ariana Grande concert in the 2017 Manchester Arena bombing.

Q30035999.name: Edmond post office shooting
Q30035999.blurb: In Edmond, Oklahoma, U.S. Postal employee Patrick Sherrill shoots and kills 14 of his co-workers and then commits suicide.

Q30041564.name: Siege of Marawi
Q30041564.blurb: Rodrigo Duterte declared martial law in Mindanao following the Maute Group attack on Marawi.

Q30096291.name: May 2017 Kabul attack
Q30096291.blurb: A car bomb explodes in a crowded intersection in Kabul near the German embassy during rush hour, killing over 90 and injuring 463.

Q30109227.name: Battle of Bamber Bridge
Q30109227.blurb: US military police attempt to arrest a black soldier in Bamber Bridge, England, sparking the Battle of Bamber Bridge mutiny that leaves one dead and seven wounded.

Q30130610.name: Qatar diplomatic crisis
Q30130610.blurb: Six Arab countries—Bahrain, Egypt, Libya, Saudi Arabia, Yemen, and the United Arab Emirates—cut diplomatic ties with Qatar, accusing it of destabilising the region.

Q30140821.name: Battle of Raqqa
Q30140821.blurb: Syrian civil war: The Battle of Raqqa begins with an offensive by the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) to capture the city from the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL).

Q30149289.name: 2017 Myanmar Air Force Shaanxi Y-8 crash
aliases: accidente del Shaanxi Y-8 de la Fuerza Aérea de Birmania
Q30149289.blurb: A Myanmar Air Force Shaanxi Y-8 crashed into the Andaman Sea near Dawei, killing all 122 people on board.

Q30173038.name: 2019 United Kingdom general election
aliases: 2019 general election in the United Kingdom
Media coverage of the 2019 United Kingdom general election
Opinion polling for the 2020 United Kingdom general election
Q30173038.blurb: Jo Swinson (pictured) steps down as Leader of the Liberal Democrats after losing her seat in the 2019 general election making her tenure the shortest in the party's history.

Q30253388.name: 2017–2018 Russian protests
aliases: Demonstrations and protests in Russia in 2017–2018
Q30253388.blurb: Russia-wide anti-corruption protests in 99 cities. The Levada Center survey showed that 38% of surveyed Russians supported protests and that 67 percent held Putin personally responsible for high-level corruption.

Q30274958.name: Grenfell Tower fire
Q30274958.blurb: The Grenfell Tower fire, a catastrophic fire in a high-rise apartment building in North Kensington, London, UK, leaves 72 people dead and another 74 injured.

Q30278163.name: Congressional baseball shooting
Q30278163.blurb: Republican U.S. House Majority Whip Steve Scalise of Louisiana, and three others, are shot and wounded while practicing for the annual Congressional Baseball Game.

Q30325756.name: 2019 Conservative Party (UK) leadership election
Q30325756.blurb: Boris Johnson became Prime Minister of the United Kingdom after winning the Conservative Party leadership election.

Q30327722.name: 2017 Pedrógão Grande Wildfire
Q30327722.blurb: A series of wildfires in central Portugal kill at least 64 people and injure 204 others.

Q30553720.name: June 2017 Pakistan bombings
Q30553720.blurb: A series of terrorist attacks take place in Pakistan, resulting in 96 deaths and wounding 200 others.

Q30600045.name: Battle of Gallipoli
Q30600045.blurb: Battle of Gallipoli: The Venetians under Pietro Loredan defeat a much larger Ottoman fleet off Gallipoli.

Q30600900.name: Battle of Sirhind
Q30600900.blurb: A Mughal army under Humayun and Bairam Khan defeats an Afghan army under Sikandar Shah Suri in the battle of Sirhind, allowing Humayun to capture Delhi and reestablish the Mughal Empire in India.

Q30601771.name: Battle of Modon
Q30601771.blurb: Venetian–Genoese wars: The Genoese fleet under a French admiral is defeated by a Venetian fleet at the Battle of Modon.

Q30603516.name: Viking raid on Seville
Q30603516.blurb: Viking expansion: A Viking fleet arrived near Seville, then part of the Emirate of Córdoba, and began a raid of the city that was eventually repelled by Muslim defenders.

Q30608059.name: Qiyāma
Q30608059.blurb: Hassan II of Alamut proclaims the qiyāma, according to which Ismaili practice would change from traditional Islamic practice.

Q30623679.name: 1939 Coventry bombing
Q30623679.blurb: The Irish Republican Army carries out the 1939 Coventry bombing in which five civilians were killed.

Q30624555.name: 1806 Birgu polverista explosion
Q30624555.blurb: A gunpowder magazine explosion in Birgu, Malta, kills around 200 people.

Q30626292.name: 1634 Valletta explosion
Q30626292.blurb: A gunpowder factory explodes in Valletta, Malta, killing 22 people and damaging several buildings.

Q30643510.name: East Coast Jets Flight 81
Q30643510.blurb: East Coast Jets Flight 81 crashes near Owatonna Degner Regional Airport in Owatonna, Minnesota, killing all eight people on board.

Q30682397.name: 2017-2019 Special Counsel investigation
Q30682397.blurb: The Special Counsel investigation on the 2016 United States presidential election concludes when Robert Mueller submits his report to the United States Attorney General.

Q30715543.name: Battle of Bembezi
Q30715543.blurb: The Battle of Bembezi took place and was the most decisive battle won by the British in the First Matabele War of 1893.

Q30890205.name: 1994 Delhi airport collision
Q30890205.blurb: A collision at Indira Gandhi International Airport kills 9 people.

Q30896184.name: 2020 Four Continents Figure Skating Championships
Q30896184.blurb: Japanese figure skater Yuzuru Hanyu won the Four Continents Championships to become the only man to complete a Super Slam.

Q30898126.name: 2017 cyberattacks on Ukraine
Q30898126.blurb: A series of powerful cyberattacks using the Petya malware target websites of Ukrainian organizations and counterparts with Ukrainian connections around the globe.

Q31043671.name: 2018 FIFA World Cup Final
Q31043671.blurb: Croatian Mario Mandžukić scored the first own goal in a FIFA World Cup final in their defeat to France.

Q31191031.name: 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo
Q31191031.blurb: An eruption of Mount Pinatubo (pictured) in the Philippines deposited large amounts of particulate matter into the atmosphere, enough to briefly lower global temperatures by about 0.5 °C (0.9 °F).

Q34356069.name: 2017 China–India border standoff
Q34356069.blurb: China–India border standoff: China and India both pull their troops out of Doklam, putting an end to a two-month-long stalemate over China's construction of a road in disputed territory.

Q36111293.name: Alexandria train collision
Q36111293.blurb: At least 41 people are killed and another 179 injured after two passenger trains collide in Alexandria, Egypt.

Q36248530.name: Unite the Right rally
aliases: Very fine people on both sides
Q36248530.blurb: The Unite the Right rally occurs in Charlottesville, Virginia, leading to the deaths of 3 and injuring nearly 50 more.

Q37001445.name: 2017 Catalonia attacks
aliases: 2017 Assumption of Mary riots in Spain
Q37001445.blurb: Barcelona attacks: A van is driven into pedestrians in La Rambla, killing 14 and injuring at least 100.

Q37150759.name: 2017 Turku attack
Q37150759.blurb: The Turku terror attack occurs in Finland when a knifeman kills two and injures eight.

Q37347188.name: 2017 Herat mosque attack
Q37347188.blurb: A suicide attack on a mosque in Herat, Afghanistan kills 20 people.

Q37467350.name: Third Silesian War
Q37467350.blurb: Third Silesian War: The Austrian victory at the Battle of Kolín forced Prussian leader Frederick the Great to give up the Siege of Prague and retreat to Saxony.

Q37933184.name: Hurricane Harvey
aliases: Criticism of government response to Hurricane Harvey
Criticism of the government response to Hurricane Harvey
Q37933184.blurb: Hurricane Harvey makes landfall in Texas as a powerful Category 4 hurricane, the strongest hurricane to make landfall in the United States since 2004.

Q38199444.name: Byzantine conquest of Cilicia
Q38199444.blurb: Nikephoros II Phokas captures the city of Tarsus, finalising the Byzantine conquest of Cilicia.

Q38456729.name: 2017 North Korean nuclear test
Q38456729.blurb: North Korea conducted its sixth and most powerful nuclear test at Punggye-ri, causing a magnitude-6.3 earthquake.

Q38685186.name: Hurricane Irma
aliases: Effects of Hurricane Irma in the Leeward Islands
Effects of Hurricane Irma on the Leeward Islands
Q38685186.blurb: Hurricane Irma reached peak intensity near the Caribbean islands of Barbuda, Saint Martin, and Virgin Gorda.

Q38982786.name: 2017 Oaxaca and Chiapas Earthquake
Q38982786.blurb: The 8.2 Mw 2017 Chiapas earthquake strikes southern Mexico, killing at least 60 people.

Q39046971.name: 1986 Lesotho coup d'état
Q39046971.blurb: Leabua Jonathan, Prime Minister of Lesotho, is ousted from power in a coup d'état led by General Justin Lekhanya.

Q39057172.name: assassination of Airey Neave
Q39057172.blurb: Airey Neave, a British Member of Parliament (MP), is killed by a car bomb as he exits the Palace of Westminster. The Irish National Liberation Army claims responsibility.

Q39058384.name: Propair Flight 420
Q39058384.blurb: Propair Flight 420 crashes near Montréal–Mirabel International Airport in Quebec, Canada, killing 11.

Q39886299.name: 2017 Parsons Green bombing
Q39886299.blurb: The Parsons Green bombing takes place in London.

Q39899474.name: Deir ez-Zor campaign (2017–2019)
Q39899474.blurb: Syrian civil war: The Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) pause the Deir ez-Zor campaign due to the Turkish-led invasion of Afrin.

Q40037480.name: Battle of Antioch
Q40037480.blurb: Fighters of the First Crusade defeat Kerbogha of Mosul at the battle of Antioch.

Q40178187.name: Hurricane Maria
aliases: Criticism of government response to Hurricane Maria
Criticism of the government response to Hurricane Maria
Q40178187.blurb: Hurricane Maria makes landfall in Puerto Rico as a powerful Category 4 hurricane, resulting in 2,975 deaths, US$90 billion in damage, and a major humanitarian crisis.

Q40355642.name: 2017 Central Mexico earthquake
Q40355642.blurb: The 2017 Puebla earthquake strikes Mexico, causing 370 deaths and over 6,000 injuries, as well as extensive damage.

Q40563675.name: Christiana Incident
Q40563675.blurb: Christiana Resistance: Escaped slaves led by William Parker fight off and kill a slave owner who, with a federal marshal and an armed party, sought to seize three of his former slaves in Christiana, Pennsylvania, thereby creating a cause célèbre between slavery proponents and abolitionists.

Q41450298.name: disappearance of Lars Mittank
Q41450298.blurb: German citizen Lars Mittank disappeared from Varna Airport, Bulgaria; his last known movements were widely watched on YouTube.

Q41522095.name: 2017 Las Vegas shooting
aliases: Reactions to the 2017 Las Vegas Strip shooting
Reactions to the Las Vegas concert shooting
Q41522095.blurb: Sixty people are killed and 867 others injured in a mass shooting at a country music festival at the Las Vegas Strip in the United States; the gunman, Stephen Paddock, later commits suicide.

Q41616483.name: Tongo Tongo ambush
Q41616483.blurb: Joint Nigerien-American Special Forces are ambushed by Islamic State militants outside the village of Tongo Tongo.

Q41715222.name: Zhengding Missionary Murder
Q41715222.blurb: Murder of 9 Catholic priests in Zhengding, China, who protected the local population from the advancing Japanese army.

Q41715273.name: Warlord Rebellion in northeastern Shandong
Q41715273.blurb: In the first battle of the Warlord Rebellion in northeastern Shandong against the Nationalist government of China, a 24,000-strong rebel force led by Zhang Zongchang was defeated at Zhifu by 7,000 NRA troops.

Q41796018.name: Catalan declaration of independence
aliases: Proclamation of the Catalan Republic of 2017
Declaration from the representatives of Catalonia

Q41806894.name: Hurricane Ophelia
Q41806894.blurb: Storm Ophelia strikes the U.K. and Ireland causing major damage and power loss.

Q42033121.name: October 2017 Mogadishu bombings
Q42033121.blurb: An Al-Shabaab suicide bomber detonated a massive truck bomb at the Zobe junction in Somalia's capital, Mogadishu, killing 587 people, injuring 316 others, and leaving more than 500 missing.

Q42320984.name: Nicaean–Latin wars
Q42320984.blurb: Struggle for Constantinople: Alexios Strategopoulos led Nicaean forces to recapture Constantinople, leading to the reestablishment of the Byzantine Empire and the end of the Latin Empire.

Q42417755.name: Sack of Balbriggan
Q42417755.blurb: Irish War of Independence: British police known as "Black and Tans" burn the town of Balbriggan and kill two local men in revenge for an IRA assassination.

Q42417787.name: Bougainville independence referendum, 2019
Q42417787.blurb: The results of the 2019 Bougainvillean independence referendum are announced. The results are overwhelmingly one-sided. Over 98% of voters vote for Bougainville's independence.

Q42440670.name: 2017 Lower Manhattan attack
Q42440670.blurb: A truck drives into a crowd in Lower Manhattan, New York City, killing eight people.

Q42533899.name: Siege of Antioch
Q42533899.blurb: The Byzantine Empire recovers Antioch from Arab rule.

Q42725753.name: Sutherland Springs church shooting
aliases: Sutherland Springs church shooting conspiracy theories
Q42725753.blurb: Devin Patrick Kelley kills 26 and injures 22 in a church in Sutherland Springs, Texas.

Q42917067.name: 1971 Liberal Party of Australia leadership spill
aliases: Liberal Party of Australia leadership spill, 1971
Q42917067.blurb: John Gorton resigns as Prime Minister of Australia and the leader of the Liberal Party of Australia after a secret ballot vote of confidence, being replaced in both positions by William McMahon.

Q42917074.name: 1939 United Australia Party leadership election
Q42917074.blurb: Robert Menzies, who became Australia's longest-serving prime minister, is elected as leader of the United Australia Party after the death of Prime Minister Joseph Lyons.

Q42955668.name: Levant Crisis
Q42955668.blurb: Beginning of the Levant Crisis between Britain and France in Syria. The latter try to quell nationalist protests but backs down after threat of military action by the British.

Q43041167.name: 2017 Iran–Iraq earthquake
Q43041167.blurb: The 7.3 Mw Kermanshah earthquake shakes the northern Iran–Iraq border with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VIII (Severe). At least 410 people are killed and over 7,000 are injured.

Q43172549.name: 2017 Zimbabwean coup d'état attempt
Q43172549.blurb: Emmerson Mnangagwa (pictured) was elected to his first full term as president, having served as leader since the 2017 Zimbabwean coup d'état.

Q43177417.name: Rancho Tehama Reserve shootings
Q43177417.blurb: A gunman kills four people and injures 12 others during a shooting spree across Rancho Tehama, California. He had earlier murdered his wife in their home.

Q43267724.name: Cyclone Numa
Q43267724.blurb: Cyclone Numa, a rare "medicane", made landfall in Greece to become the worst weather event that the country had experienced since 1977.

Q43401556.name: Emery Worldwide Flight 17
Q43401556.blurb: Emery Worldwide Airlines Flight 17 crashes near Sacramento Mather Airport in Rancho Cordova, California, killing all three aboard.

Q43544477.name: 2017 Sinai mosque attack
aliases: 2017 Egypt mosque bomb and gun attack
Q43544477.blurb: A terrorist attack on a Mosque in Al-Rawda, North Sinai, Egypt kills 311 people and injures 128.

Q43849422.name: Medicane Euredike
Q43849422.blurb: A flood a few miles outside of Athens results in the death of 25 people.

Q43890449.name: wedding of Prince Harry and Meghan Markle
aliases: Wedding of Prince Harry of Wales and Meghan Markle
Wedding of Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, and Meghan Markle
Wedding of Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex
Wedding of Prince Henry of Wales and Meghan Markle
Wedding of Prince Henry, Duke of Sussex, and Meghan Markle
Wedding of Prince Henry, Duke of Sussex, and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex
Royal Wedding of Prince Harry and Meghan Markle
Wedding of Meghan Markle and Prince Harry
Wedding of Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex
Wedding of Prince Henry and Meghan Markle
Q43890449.blurb: The wedding of Prince Harry and Meghan Markle is held at St George's Chapel, Windsor, with an estimated global audience of 1.9 billion.

Q44023338.name: 2019 Japanese imperial transition
aliases: Ceremonies of the Abdication from the Throne
Q44023338.blurb: Naruhito ascends to the throne of Japan succeeding his father Akihito, beginning the Reiwa period.

Q44101462.name: Nainital wedding massacre
Q44101462.blurb: The Nainital wedding massacre occurs, killing 22 members of the Harijan caste.

Q44820247.name: Thomas Fire
Q44820247.blurb: The Thomas Fire starts near Santa Paula in California. It eventually became the largest wildfire in modern California history to date after burning 1,140 square kilometers (440 sq mi) in Ventura and Santa Barbara Counties.

Q45084218.name: Marriage Amendment (Definition and Religious Freedoms) Act 2017
Q45084218.blurb: The Marriage Amendment Bill receives royal assent and comes into effect, making Australia the 26th country to legalize same-sex marriage.

Q45178445.name: Aztec High School shooting
Q45178445.blurb: Aztec High School shooting: William Atchison kills two students at his former high school.

Q45266620.name: United States recognition of Jerusalem as capital of Israel
Q45266620.blurb: Donald Trump's administration officially announces the recognition of Jerusalem as the capital of Israel.

Q45272383.name: 2017 Port Authority Bus Terminal explosion
Q45272383.blurb: New York City Subway bombing: A pipe bomb partially detonates in the New York City Subway, in the Times Square–42nd Street/Port Authority Bus Terminal. Four people are injured, including the perpetrator.

Q45773452.name: 2017 Java Earthquake
Q45773452.blurb: A 6.5Mwearthquake strikes the Indonesian island of Java in the city of Tasikmalaya, resulting in four deaths.

Q46014043.name: 2017 Washington train derailment
Q46014043.blurb: Amtrak Cascades passenger train 501, derailed near DuPont, Washington, a city in United States near Olympia, Washington killing six people, and injuring 70 others.

Q46611403.name: coronation of George V and Mary
aliases: Coronation of King George V and Queen Mary
Q46611403.blurb: George V and Mary of Teck are crowned King and Queen of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland.

Q47004660.name: Milwaukee Police Department bombing
Q47004660.blurb: In Milwaukee, nine members of the Milwaukee Police Department are killed by a bomb, the most deaths in a single event in U.S. police history until the September 11 attacks in 2001.

Q47068137.name: Hennenman–Kroonstad train crash
Q47068137.blurb: Hennenman–Kroonstad train crash: A passenger train operated by Shosholoza Meyl collides with a truck on a level crossing at Geneva Station between Hennenman and Kroonstad, Free State, South Africa. Twenty people are killed and 260 injured.

Q47069660.name: 1732 Irpinia earthquake
Q47069660.blurb: The magnitude 6.6 Irpinia earthquake causes 1,940 deaths in the former Kingdom of Naples, southern Italy.

Q47198426.name: George Washington's resignation as commander-in-chief
Q47198426.blurb: George Washington resigns as commander-in-chief of the Continental Army at the Maryland State House in Annapolis, Maryland.

Q47358577.name: 2018 Hawaii false missile alert
aliases: BALLISTIC MISSILE THREAT INBOUND TO HAWAII.
Q47358577.blurb: A false emergency alert warning of an impending missile strike in Hawaii causes widespread panic in the state.

Q47412160.name: Minneapolis Miracle
Q47412160.blurb: In the "Minneapolis Miracle", American football player Stefon Diggs caught a 61-yard (56 m) touchdown pass that secured the Minnesota Vikings' victory in the National Football Conference divisional playoff game.

Q47452670.name: Mudéjar revolt of 1264–1266
Q47452670.blurb: Mudéjar revolt: King James I of Aragon entered the formerly Muslim-held city of Murcia following its surrender three days earlier.

Q47465940.name: Turkish military operation in Afrin
aliases: Turkish military intervention in Afrin (19 January 2018-present)
Q47465940.blurb: Syrian civil war: Following the completion of the Afrin offensive, the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) initiate an insurgency against the Turkish occupation of the Afrin District.

Q47472535.name: 2000 East Coast Aviation Services British Aerospace Jetstream crash
Q47472535.blurb: Nineteen people are killed in a plane crash in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania.

Q47483533.name: 2018 Djiboutian parliamentary election
Q47483533.blurb: Parliamentary elections are held in Djibouti.

Q47484079.name: 2018 Inter-Continental Hotel Kabul attack
aliases: Ataque al Hotel InterContinental de Kabul
Q47484079.blurb: A group of four or five gunmen attack The Inter-Continental Hotel in Kabul, Afghanistan, sparking a 12-hour battle. The attack kills 40 people and injures many others.

Q47486452.name: 2018 Gulf of Alaska earthquake
Q47486452.blurb: A 7.9 Mw earthquake occurs in the Gulf of Alaska. It is tied as the sixth-largest earthquake ever recorded in the United States, but there are no reports of significant damage or fatalities.

Q47500246.name: 2004 fire in Parque Central Complex
Q47500246.blurb: A fire that lasted over 15 hours destroyed almost one third of the East Tower of the Parque Central Urban Complex in Caracas, Venezuela.

Q47539524.name: 1838 Jesuit slave sale
Q47539524.blurb: The Maryland province of the Jesuits contracted to sell 272 slaves to buyers in Louisiana in one of the largest slave sales in American history.

Q47540245.name: Ariane flight VA241
Q47540245.blurb: An Ariane 5 rocket is launched carrying SES-14, Al Yah 3, and NASA's Global-scale Observations of the Limb and Disk, but the satellites end up in the wrong orbit.

Q47654909.name: disappearance of Harold Holt
Q47654909.blurb: Harold Holt, the prime minister of Australia, disappeared while swimming near Portsea, Victoria; his body was never recovered.

Q48320714.name: 2018 Hong Kong bus accident
Q48320714.blurb: Nineteen people are killed and 66 injured when a Kowloon Motor Bus double decker on route 872 in Hong Kong overturns.

Q48425813.name: Saratov Airlines Flight 703
Q48425813.blurb: Saratov Airlines Flight 703 crashes near Moscow, Russia with 71 deaths and no survivors.

Q48698996.name: Parliament of 1327
Q48698996.blurb: The Parliament of 1327, which was instrumental in the transfer of the English Crown from King Edward II to his son, Edward III, began at the Palace of Westminster.

Q48714898.name: Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School shooting
aliases: 2018 Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School massacre
2018 Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School shooting
2018 Marjory Stonewall Douglas High School shooting
2018 shooting at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School
Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School massacre
Parkland high school shooting conspiracy theories
School shooting at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School
Stoneman Douglas High School shooting conspiracy theories
Q48714898.blurb: A shooting at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida is one of the deadliest school massacres with 17 fatalities and 17 injuries.

Q48719808.name: Battle of Knipawa
Q48719808.blurb: Thirteen Years' War: the beginning of the Battle for Kneiphof.

Q48724683.name: Siege of Chittorgarh
Q48724683.blurb: Chittorgarh falls to the Delhi Sultanate.

Q48726707.name: Siege of Warangal, 1323
Q48726707.blurb: Siege of Warangal: Sultan Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq sends an expeditionary army led by his son, Muhammad bin Tughluq, to the Kakatiya capital Warangal – after ruler Prataparudra has refused to make tribute payments. He besieges the city and finally, after a campaign of 8 months, Prataparudra surrenders on November 9.

Q48733551.name: Blackwater 61 crash
Q48733551.blurb: Blackwater 61 crash: A CASA C-212 Aviocar crashes into the Koh-i-Baba mountain range in Afghanistan, killing six.

Q48733633.name: Battle of Nasiriyah
Q48733633.blurb: The British capture Nasiriyah from the Ottomans during the Mesopotamian campaign.

Q48733987.name: 1969 Somali coup d'état
Q48733987.blurb: The 1969 Somali coup d'état establishes a Marxist–Leninist administration.

Q48767672.name: Convention Parliament
Q48767672.blurb: The Long Parliament of England is dissolved so as to prepare for the new Convention Parliament.

Q48768423.name: Planned French invasion of Britain
Q48768423.blurb: A French fleet anchors nears Fife Ness as part of the planned French invasion of Britain.

Q48779654.name: Siege of Coevorden
Q48779654.blurb: The Dutch city of Coevorden, held by the Spanish, falls to a Dutch and English force.

Q48785102.name: Jacobite rising of 1689
Q48785102.blurb: First Jacobite rising: Scottish and Irish Jacobites defeated Williamite forces at Killiecrankie, Scotland.

Q48790316.name: 2006 Yeti Airlines Twin Otter Crash
Q48790316.blurb: A Yeti Airlines de Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter crashes at Jumla Airport in Nepal, killing nine people.

Q48797719.name: 1999 Aggie Bonfire collapse
aliases: Texas A&M Bonfire Collapse, College Station, Tex., 1999
Q48797719.blurb: Texas A&M University's Aggie Bonfire collapsed (aftermath pictured), killing 12 people and injuring 27 others, and causing the university to officially declare a hiatus on the 90-year-old annual event.

Q48815612.name: wedding of Princess Eugenie and Jack Brooksbank
aliases: Wedding of Princess Eugenie of York and Jack Brooksbank
Q48815612.blurb: Princess Eugenie marries Jack Brooksbank at St. George's Chapel, Windsor Castle.

Q48815883.name: Karpalak ambush
Q48815883.blurb: Albanian rebels ambush a convoy of the Army of the Republic of Macedonia near Tetovo, killing 10 soldiers.

Q48815990.name: Razing of Friesoythe
Q48815990.blurb: World War II:  In what becomes known as the Razing of Friesoythe, the 4th Canadian (Armoured) Division deliberately destroys the German town of Friesoythe on the orders of Major General Christopher Vokes.

Q48816847.name: 1932 Colonial Building riot
Q48816847.blurb: Dominion of Newfoundland: Ten thousand rioters seize the Colonial Building leading to the end of self-government.

Q48816854.name: Austral Líneas Aéreas Flight 205
Q48816854.blurb: Austral Líneas Aéreas Flight 205 crashes into the Atlantic Ocean near Astor Piazzolla International Airport in Mar del Plata, Argentina, killing 51.

Q48817630.name: Candia massacre
Q48817630.blurb: Seven hundred Greek civilians, 17 British guards and the British Consul of Crete are killed by a Turkish mob.

Q48835298.name: 1993 Tennessee Fairchild Merlin crash
Q48835298.blurb: NASCAR champion Alan Kulwicki is killed in a plane crash near the Tri-Cities Regional Airport in Blountville, Tennessee.

Q48837243.name: 1991 Merion mid-air collision
Q48837243.blurb: Senator John Heinz of Pennsylvania and six others are killed when a helicopter collides with their airplane over an elementary school in Merion, Pennsylvania.

Q48838712.name: Parliament of Quillín
Q48838712.blurb: Arauco War: The first Parliament of Quillín is celebrated, putting a temporary hold on hostilities between Mapuches and Spanish in Chile.

Q48978014.name: Yuba County Five
Q48978014.blurb: The Yuba County Five disappear in California. Four of their bodies are found four months later.

Q48980337.name: Rebellion of Bardas Phokas the Younger
Q48980337.blurb: Bardas Phokas the Younger and Bardas Skleros, Byzantine generals of the military elite, begin a wide-scale rebellion against Emperor Basil II.

Q48998655.name: Battle of Trapani
Q48998655.blurb: War of Saint Sabas: In the Battle of Trapani, the Venetians defeat a larger Genoese fleet, capturing all its ships.

Q48998988.name: Battle of Saseno
Q48998988.blurb: War of Saint Sabas: A Genoese fleet captured or sank most of the ships of a Venetian trade convoy off the Albanian coast.

Q49098663.name: Iran Aseman Airlines Flight 3704
Q49098663.blurb: Iran Aseman Airlines Flight 3704 crashes in the Dena sub-range in the Zagros Mountains of Iran, Resulting in 66 Deaths

Q49413597.name: Rif Dimashq offensive (February–April 2018)
Q49413597.blurb: Syria launches the Douma chemical attack during the Eastern Ghouta offensive of the Syrian Civil War.

Q50317608.name: March for Our Lives
Q50317608.blurb: Students across the United States stage the March for Our Lives demanding gun control in response to the Stoneman Douglas High School shooting.

Q50396434.name: 2018 North Korea–United States Singapore Summit
Q50396434.blurb: United States President Donald Trump and Kim Jong-un of North Korea hold the first meeting between leaders of their two countries in Singapore.

Q50404279.name: 2018 Iran Bombardier Challenger crash
Q50404279.blurb: A Bombardier Challenger 604 crashes into the Zagros Mountains near the Iranian city of Shar-e-kord, killing all 11 people on board.

Q50412176.name: US Bangla Airlines Flight 211
Q50412176.blurb: US-Bangla Airlines Flight 211 crashes at Tribhuvan International Airport in Katmandu, killing 51 and injuring 20.

Q50415393.name: poisoning of Sergei and Yulia Skripal
aliases: Poisoning of Yulia and Sergei Skripal
Reactions to the Poisoning of Sergei and Yulia Skripal
Reactions to the poisoning of Yulia and Sergei Skripal
Q50415393.blurb: Former MI6 spy Sergei Skripal and his daughter are poisoned with a Novichok nerve agent in Salisbury, England, causing a diplomatic uproar that results in mass-expulsions of diplomats from all countries involved.

Q51139646.name: 2018–2019 Gaza border protests
aliases: 2018 Gaza border protests and Israeli shootings
Casualties of the 2018 Gaza border protests
Q51139646.blurb: The Israeli Army kills 17 Palestinians and wounds 1,400 in Gaza during Land Day protests.

Q51339458.name: YouTube headquarters shooting
Q51339458.blurb: YouTube headquarters shooting: A 38-year-old gunwoman opens fire at YouTube Headquarters in San Bruno, California, injuring three people before committing suicide.

Q51476459.name: East German balloon escape
Q51476459.blurb: Eight people escape from East Germany to the west in a homemade hot air balloon.

Q51554795.name: Mrauk U riot
Q51554795.blurb: In Mrauk U, Myanmar, police fired into a crowd protesting the ban of an event to mark the anniversary of the end of the Kingdom of Mrauk U, resulting in seven deaths and twelve injuries.

Q51557538.name: China–United States trade war
aliases: International reactions to the China-United States trade war
International reactions to the China–United States trade war
Reactions to the China-United States trade war
Reactions to the China–United States trade war
United States and China trade war
United States' trade war with China
Q51557538.blurb: The China–United States trade war begins when President Donald Trump places tariffs on Chinese solar panels and washing machines.

Q51585429.name: Humboldt Broncos bus crash
Q51585429.blurb: A bus carrying the Humboldt Broncos junior ice hockey team collides with a semi-truck in Saskatchewan, Canada, killing 16 people and injuring 13 others.

Q51629486.name: 2018 Douma chemical attack
Q51629486.blurb: Syria launches the Douma chemical attack during the Eastern Ghouta offensive of the Syrian Civil War.

Q51716967.name: killing of JonBenét Ramsey
Q51716967.blurb: The body of American child beauty queen JonBenét Ramsey was found in her family's Boulder, Colorado, home. Her murder remains unsolved.

Q51722302.name: disappearance of Natalee Holloway
Q51722302.blurb: American student Natalee Holloway disappeared on a high-school graduation trip to Aruba.

Q51723202.name: lynching of Jesse Washington
Q51723202.blurb: Jesse Washington, a teenage African-American farmhand, was lynched in Waco, Texas.

Q51747221.name: 2018 Algerian Air Force Il-76 crash
Q51747221.blurb: An Ilyushin Il-76 owned and operated by the Algerian Air Force crashes near Boufarik, Algeria, killing 257.

Q51881408.name: Bombing of Tokyo (10 March 1945)
Q51881408.blurb: World War II: The U.S. Army Air Force firebombs Tokyo, and the resulting conflagration kills more than 100,000 people, mostly civilians.

Q51885025.name: death of Hu Yaobang
Q51885025.blurb: The death of former Chinese General Secretary Hu Yaobang triggered a series of events that led to the Tiananmen Square protests in Beijing.

Q52152274.name: 2018 Toronto van attack
Q52152274.blurb: A vehicle-ramming attack kills 11 people and injures 15 in Toronto. A 25-year-old suspect, Alek Minassian, is arrested.

Q52222422.name: Panmunjom Declaration
aliases: Panmunjom Declaration for Peace, Prosperity and Unification of the Korean Peninsula
Q52222422.blurb: The Panmunjom Declaration is signed between North and South Korea, officially declaring their intentions to end the Korean conflict.
