Q52705852.name: 1966 Ghanaian coup d'état
Q52705852.blurb: Ghanaian coup d'état by National Liberation Council overthrows Kwame Nkrumah's Government

Q53282087.name: 2018 Paris knife attack
Q53282087.blurb: Paris knife attack: A man is fatally shot by police in Paris after killing one and injuring several others.

Q53679432.name: Avignonet massacre
Q53679432.blurb: Avignonet massacre: A group of Cathars, with the probable connivance of Count Raymond VII of Toulouse, murder the inquisitor William Arnaud and eleven of his companions.

Q53725630.name: Santa Fe High School shooting
Q53725630.blurb: A school shooting at Santa Fe High School in Texas kills ten people.

Q53729870.name: Cubana de Aviación Flight 972
Q53729870.blurb: Cubana de Aviación Flight 972 crashes in Santiago de las Vegas after takeoff from José Martí International Airport in Havana, Cuba, killing 112 of the 113 people on board.

Q53776731.name: Late Ming peasant rebellions
Q53776731.blurb: Ming–Qing transition: The Ming dynasty of China fell when the Chongzhen Emperor committed suicide during a peasant rebellion led by Li Zicheng.

Q54321827.name: Kasenkina Case
Q54321827.blurb: Soviet Consul General in New York, Jacob M. Lomakin is expelled by the United States, due to the Kasenkina Case.

Q54322354.name: Murder of Harry and Harriette Moore
Q54322354.blurb: A bomb explodes at the home of Harry T. Moore and Harriette V. S. Moore, early leaders of the Civil Rights Movement, killing Harry instantly and fatally wounding Harriette.

Q54327853.name: Thirty-sixth Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
aliases: Thirty-sixth Amendment of the Constitution Bill 2018
Q54327853.blurb: Ireland votes to repeal the Eighth Amendment of their constitution that prohibits abortion in all but a few cases, choosing to replace it with the Thirty-sixth Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland.

Q54567414.name: 2018 vote of no confidence in the government of Mariano Rajoy
Q54567414.blurb: For the first time since its transition to democracy, the Congress of Deputies in Spain passed a motion of no confidence against the government.

Q54866655.name: 2015 White Sox–Orioles crowdless game
aliases: 2015 Chicago White Sox–Baltimore Orioles crowdless game
Q54866655.blurb: A baseball game between the Baltimore Orioles and the Chicago White Sox sets the all-time low attendance mark for Major League Baseball. Zero fans were in attendance for the game, as the stadium was officially closed to the public due to the 2015 Baltimore protests.

Q54866668.name: 2016 Indian Line of Control strike
Q54866668.blurb: Eleven days after the Uri attack, the Indian Army conducts "surgical strikes" against suspected militants in Pakistani-administered Kashmir.

Q54874445.name: 1924 Wyoming gubernatorial special election
Q54874445.blurb: In a special election in Wyoming, Nellie Tayloe Ross became the first woman to be elected as a governor in the United States.

Q54953255.name: Treaty of Bosque Redondo
Q54953255.blurb: The Treaty of Bosque Redondo is signed, allowing the Navajo to return to their lands in Arizona and New Mexico.

Q54953887.name: 1923 USA Outdoor Track and Field Championships
Q54953887.blurb: The First American Track and Field championships for women are held.

Q55076583.name: 1923 WAAA Championships
Q55076583.blurb: The first British Track and Field championships for women are held in London, Great Britain.

Q55080471.name: 2018 Osaka earthquake
Q55080471.blurb: An earthquake of magnitude 6.1 strikes northern Osaka.

Q55099279.name: 1982 bombing of the African National Congress headquarters in London
Q55099279.blurb: The South African government bombs the headquarters of the African National Congress in London.

Q55153903.name: Prespa agreement
Q55153903.blurb: The country known as the Republic of Macedonia renames itself the Republic of North Macedonia in accordance with the Prespa agreement, settling a long-standing naming dispute with Greece.

Q55301634.name: Tham Luang cave rescue
aliases: Elon Musk and the Tham Luang cave rescue
Q55301634.blurb: Twelve boys and an assistant coach from a soccer team in Thailand are trapped in a flooding cave, leading to an 18-day rescue operation.

Q55391336.name: 2018 Maryland flood
Q55391336.blurb: Maryland Flood Event: A flood occurs throughout the Patapsco Valley, causing one death, destroying the entire first floors of buildings on Main Street in Ellicott City, and causing cars to overturn.

Q55600341.name: 1170 Syria earthquake
Q55600341.blurb: A major earthquake hits Syria, badly damaging towns such as Hama and Shaizar and structures such as the Krak des Chevaliers and the cathedral of St. Peter in Antioch.

Q55605048.name: Battle of the Lake of Antioch
Q55605048.blurb: A First Crusade army led by Bohemond of Taranto wins a major battle against the Seljuq emir Ridwan of Aleppo during the siege of Antioch.

Q55605667.name: attempted assassination of Bob Marley
Q55605667.blurb: Jamaican reggae musician Bob Marley survived an assassination attempt by seven gunmen in Kingston.

Q55605900.name: Brett Kavanaugh Supreme Court nomination
aliases: nomination of Brett Kavanaugh to the Supreme Court of the United States
Q55605900.blurb: The United States Senate confirms Brett Kavanaugh as a Supreme Court Associate Justice, ending a contentious confirmation process.

Q55606137.name: Bunbury woodchip bombing
Q55606137.blurb: Environmental activists bombed the port facilities in Bunbury, Western Australia, in an attempt to disrupt the woodchipping industry.

Q55606298.name: C23 tragedy
Q55606298.blurb: An explosion on board a Maltese patrol boat disposing of illegal fireworks at sea off Gozo kills seven soldiers and policemen.

Q55620455.name: 2022 FIFA World Cup Final
aliases: 2022 FIFA World Cup Final, Argentina v France
2022 FIFA World Cup Match 64, Argentina v France
2022 World soccer Cup tournament final in Qatar
Q55620455.blurb: Argentina win the FIFA World Cup final, defeating title holders France 4–2 on penalties following a 3–3 draw after extra time.

Q55633164.name: Siege of Thessalonica
Q55633164.blurb: Climax of the Siege of Thessalonica by the Slavs in a three-day assault on the city walls.

Q55695682.name: Kinmen Agreement
Q55695682.blurb: The Red Cross organizations of mainland China and Taiwan sign Kinmen Agreement on repatriation of illegal immigrants and criminal suspects after two days of talks in Kinmen, Fujian Province in response to the two tragedies in repatriation in the previous two months. It is the first agreement reached by private organizations across the Taiwan Strait.

Q55738551.name: 2018 Attica wildfires
Q55738551.blurb: A wildfire in East Attica kills at least 102 people. It is the deadliest wildfire in the history of Greece.

Q55754004.name: 2018 Suwayda attacks
Q55754004.blurb: As-Suwayda attacks: Coordinated attacks occur in Syria.

Q55863781.name: 2019 Afghan presidential election
Q55863781.blurb: Violence and low turnout mar the 2019 Afghan presidential election.

Q55887216.name: Siege of Berwick
Q55887216.blurb: Second War of Scottish Inde­pen­dence: The Scottish-held town of Berwick-upon-Tweed surrendered to English forces, ending a siege led by King Edward III.

Q55966144.name: 2018 Caracas drone attack
Q55966144.blurb: Crisis in Venezuela: Seven people are injured when two drones detonate explosives on Avenida Bolívar, Caracas while president Nicolás Maduro is giving a speech to the Venezuelan National Guard.

Q56036512.name: Expedition 62
Q56036512.blurb: Soyuz MS-16 is launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome, carrying the Expedition 62/63 crew to the International Space Station.

Q56036908.name: 1978 smallpox outbreak in the United Kingdom
Q56036908.blurb: British medical photographer Janet Parker became the last recorded person to die from smallpox, leading to a debate on whether the virus should be preserved.

Q56043230.name: Dahyan airstrike
Q56043230.blurb: A civilian school bus in Dahyan, Yemen, was bombed by Saudi forces, killing at least 40 children.

Q56050557.name: 2018 Horizon Air Q400 incident
Q56050557.blurb: Horizon Air employee Richard Russell hijacks and performs an unauthorized takeoff on a Horizon Air Bombardier Dash 8 Q400 plane at Seattle–Tacoma International Airport in Washington, flying it for more than an hour before crashing the plane and killing himself on Ketron Island in Puget Sound.

Q56057027.name: escape of Viktor Pestek and Siegfried Lederer from Auschwitz
Q56057027.blurb: Siegfried Lederer, a Czech Jew, escaped from Auschwitz with the aid of an SS officer who opposed the Holocaust.

Q56073367.name: Aeroflot Flight 2
Q56073367.blurb: Aeroflot Flight B-2 crashes after takeoff from Vitim Airport in the Sakha Republic, killing 39.

Q56085201.name: 2018 Genoa bridge collapse
Q56085201.blurb: The collapse of the Ponte Morandi bridge in Genoa, Italy, left 16 people injured and 43 people killed.

Q56256213.name: Jacksonville Landing shooting
Q56256213.blurb: Exactly 5 years after the 2018 Jacksonville Landing shooting, there is another shooting in Jacksonville, Florida, leaving 3 people dead.

Q56276309.name: Siege of Almería
Q56276309.blurb: Reconquista: Aragonese forces led by King James II landed on the coast of Almería, beginning an ultimately unsuccessful siege of the city, then held by the Emirate of Granada.

Q56283802.name: The Love Day
Q56283802.blurb: Wars of the Roses: A formal reconciliation ceremony between the Lancastrians and Yorkists led to a brief period of peace.

Q56308427.name: American International Airways Flight 808
Q56308427.blurb: American International Airways Flight 808 crashes at Leeward Point Field at Guantanamo Bay Naval Base in Guantánamo Bay, Cuba, injuring the three crew members.

Q56400471.name: 2024 Finnish presidential election
aliases: Election of the President of the Republic 2024
Q56400471.blurb: 2024 Finnish presidential election: Alexander Stubb is elected as the 13th president of Finland.

Q56401997.name: Battle of Helsinki
Q56401997.blurb: Great Northern War: After losing the Battle of Helsinki to the Russians, the Swedish and Finnish troops burn the entire city, so that it would not remain intact in the hands of the Russians.

Q56441760.name: National Museum of Brazil fire
aliases: 2018 fire in the National Museum of Brazil
Destruction of the National Museum of Brazil
Fire in the National Museum of Brazil
Q56441760.blurb: National Museum of Brazil fire, A massive fire destroys most of the Paço de São Cristóvão, which houses the National Museum of Brazil, in Rio de Janeiro. The museum holds important archaeοlogical and anthropological objects, including the remains of the Luzia Woman, Marajoara vases and Egyptian mummies.

Q56650604.name: Syria missile strikes
aliases: 2018 Russian Air Force Ilyushin Il-18 shootdown
Q56650604.blurb: A Russian reconnaissance aircraft carrying 15 people on board is brought down by a Syrian surface-to-air missile over the Mediterranean Sea.

Q56690070.name: Sinking of the MV Nyerere
Q56690070.blurb: At least 161 people die after a ferry capsizes close to the pier on Ukara Island in Lake Victoria, Tanzania.

Q56721787.name: 1978 massacre at Multan Colony Textile Mills
Q56721787.blurb: On the orders of the President of Pakistan, Muhammad Zia-ul-Haq, paramilitary forces opened fire on peaceful protesting workers in Multan, Pakistan; it is known as 1978 massacre at Multan Colony Textile Mills.

Q56768333.name: 2018 Sulawesi earthquake and tsunami
Q56768333.blurb: The 7.5 Mw 2018 Sulawesi earthquake, which triggered a large tsunami, leaves 4,340 dead and 10,679 injured.

Q56839716.name: United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement
aliases: Agreement between the United States of America, the United Mexican States, and Canada
Tratado entre México, Estados Unidos y Canadá
Q56839716.blurb: The United States Senate ratifies the United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement as a replacement for NAFTA.

Q56855537.name: Ruhollah Khomeini's life in exile
Q56855537.blurb: Ruhollah Khomeini was arrested by SAVAK, the Iranian secret police, and exiled to Turkey.

Q57082056.name: Hurricane Michael
aliases: Effects of Hurricane Michael in Florida
Q57082056.blurb: Hurricane Michael makes landfall in the Florida Panhandle as a catastrophic Category 5 hurricane. It kills 57 people in the United States, 45 in Florida, and causes an estimated $25.1 billion in damage.

Q57417004.name: Kerch Polytechnic College massacre
Q57417004.blurb: A mass shooting and bombing at Kerch Polytechnic College in Crimea kills 21 people including the attacker and injures 70 others.

Q57527214.name: assassination of Jamal Khashoggi
Q57527214.blurb: The Washington Post journalist Jamal Khashoggi is assassinated in the Saudi consulate in Istanbul, Turkey.

Q57580401.name: 2018 Yilan train derailment
Q57580401.blurb: A passenger train derails in Yilan County, Taiwan, killing 18 people and injuring 187.

Q57830735.name: Pittsburgh synagogue shooting
aliases: Tree of Life – Or L'Simcha Congregation shooting
Q57830735.blurb: A gunman opens fire on a Pittsburgh synagogue killing eleven and injuring six, including four police officers.

Q57896166.name: 2018 Leicester City F.C. helicopter crash
Q57896166.blurb: Leicester City F.C. owner Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha dies in a helicopter crash along with four others after a Premier League match against West Ham United at the King Power Stadium in Leicester, England.

Q57912689.name: Lion Air Flight 610 Crash
Q57912689.blurb: A Boeing 737 MAX plane crashes after taking off from Jakarta, Indonesia killing 189 people on board.  This is the first of two crashes that will lead to the plane being grounded worldwide.

Q57997805.name: 1939 Nazi rally at Madison Square Garden
aliases: Pro American Rally and George Washington Birthday Exercises
Q57997805.blurb: Madison Square Garden Nazi rally: The largest ever pro-Nazi rally in United States history is convened in Madison Square Garden, New York City, with 20,000 members and sympathizers of the German American Bund present.

Q58425014.name: Morral affair
Q58425014.blurb: The attempted regicide of Spanish King Alfonso XIII and Queen Victoria Eugenie on their wedding day instead kills 24.

Q59313976.name: 2018 Anchorage earthquake
Q59313976.blurb: A magnitude 7.1 earthquake with its epicenter only 24 km from Anchorage, Alaska causes significant property damage but no deaths.

Q59576416.name: attempted assassination of Rómulo Betancourt
Q59576416.blurb: Venezuelan President Rómulo Betancourt is injured in an assassination attempt.

Q60042839.name: 2018 Sunda Strait tsunami
Q60042839.blurb: A tsunami caused by an eruption of Anak Krakatau in Indonesia kills at least 430 people and injures almost a thousand more.

Q60139328.name: 2018 Puebla helicopter crash
Q60139328.blurb: A helicopter crash kills Martha Érika Alonso, first female Governor of Puebla, Mexico, and her husband Rafael Moreno Valle Rosas, former governor.

Q60175839.name: 2018–2019 United States federal government shutdown
aliases: United States federal government shutdown of 2018–2019
United States federal government shutdown of December 2018
Q60175839.blurb: The 2018–2019 United States federal government shutdown, the second-longest shutdown of the U.S. federal government in history, begins.

Q60289711.name: Sudanese Revolution
Q60289711.blurb: Khartoum massacre: In Sudan, over 100 people are killed when security forces accompanied by Janjaweed militiamen storm and open fire on a sit-in protest.

Q60311957.name: 2018 Magnitogorsk building collapse
Q60311957.blurb: Thirty-nine people are killed after a ten-story building collapses in the industrial city of Magnitogorsk, Russia.

Q60315800.name: Siege of Thessalonica
Q60315800.blurb: The Byzantine city of Thessalonike surrenders to the Ottomans, though rule reverts back to the Byzantines after the battle of Ankara.

Q60441169.name: Koszalin escape room fire
Q60441169.blurb: A fire in an escape room in Koszalin, Poland, kills five teenagers through carbon monoxide poisoning.

Q60521521.name: kidnapping of Jayme Closs
Q60521521.blurb: A 13-year-old American girl, Jayme Closs, is found alive in Gordon, Wisconsin, having been kidnapped 88 days earlier from her parents' home whilst they were murdered.

Q60524397.name: Battle of Entebbe
Q60524397.blurb: Uganda–Tanzania War: Tanzanian forces defeated Ugandan troops and their Libyan allies at the Battle of Entebbe, opening the way for an advance on the Ugandan capital, Kampala.

Q60524415.name: Battle of Masaka
Q60524415.blurb: Uganda–Tanzania War: Ugandan government forces fled Masaka as the Tanzania People's Defence Force bombarded and captured the town.

Q60524433.name: Battle of Philomelion
Q60524433.blurb: The Crusader army of emperor Frederick Barbarossa defeats an army of the Rum Seljuks in the battle of Philomelion.

Q60524439.name: Battle of Porta
Q60524439.blurb: World War II: The two-day Battle of Porta between the Royal Italian Army and the Greek People's Liberation Army begins.

Q60524445.name: Battle of Saint George
Q60524445.blurb: In the Battle of Saint George, the Byzantines under Andronikos Asen ambush and defeat the forces of the Principality of Achaea, securing possession of Arcadia.

Q60524534.name: Siege of Aiguillon
Q60524534.blurb: Hundred Years' War: John, Duke of Normandy, laid siege to the town of Aiguillon.

Q60524541.name: Siege of Canterbury
Q60524541.blurb: Danes capture Canterbury after a siege, taking Ælfheah, archbishop of Canterbury, as a prisoner.

Q60543909.name: Siege of Oxford
Q60543909.blurb: Stephen of Blois's army approached Oxford, beginning the siege of Oxford.

Q60616816.name: 2019 Saha Airlines Boeing 707 crash
Q60616816.blurb: A Saha Airlines Boeing 707 crashes at Fath Air Base near Karaj in Alborz Province, Iran, killing 15 people.

Q60628970.name: 2019 Nairobi attack
Q60628970.blurb: Somali militants attack the DusitD2 hotel in Nairobi, Kenya killing at least 21 people and injuring 19.

Q60683841.name: Tlahuelilpan pipeline explosion
Q60683841.blurb: An oil pipeline explosion near Tlahuelilpan, Hidalgo, Mexico, kills 137 people.

Q60741025.name: Sumpul River massacre
Q60741025.blurb: Salvadoran Civil War: The Sumpul River massacre occurs in Chalatenango, El Salvador.

Q60741110.name: Houston–Mount Everest flight expedition
Q60741110.blurb: First flight over Mount Everest, the British Houston-Mount Everest Flight Expedition, led by the Marquis of Clydesdale and funded by Lucy, Lady Houston.

Q60742339.name: 2024 Pakistani general election
Q60742339.blurb: Pakistan election offices are hit by twin bombings, killing at least 24 people a day before general elections.

Q60750020.name: 2018 Rome escalator accident
Q60750020.blurb: An escalator accident in Rome left 24 people injured, mostly fans of the CSKA Moscow football team who were in town for a UEFA Champions League match against Roma.

Q60755981.name: 2019 W Series
Q60755981.blurb: The inaugural race of the W Series took place at Hockenheimring, Germany, and was won by Jamie Chadwick (pictured), who later became the season's champion.

Q60764387.name: 1987 Burkinabé coup d'état
Q60764387.blurb: A coup d'état in Burkina Faso overthrows and kills then President Thomas Sankara.

Q60766604.name: 1937 tour of Germany by the Duke and Duchess of Windsor
Q60766604.blurb: The Duke and Duchess of Windsor tour Nazi Germany for 12 days and meet Adolf Hitler on 22 October.

Q60785914.name: Byzantine–Venetian treaty of 1268
Q60785914.blurb: A five-year Byzantine–Venetian peace treaty is concluded between Venetian envoys and Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos.

Q60789136.name: First Fatimid invasion of Egypt
Q60789136.blurb: Start of the First Fatimid invasion of Egypt.

Q60789138.name: Second Fatimid invasion of Egypt
Q60789138.blurb: The second Fatimid invasion of Egypt begins, when the Fatimid heir-apparent, al-Qa'im bi-Amr Allah, sets out from Raqqada at the head of his army.

Q60820213.name: 1991-92 Georgian coup d'état
Q60820213.blurb: President of Georgia Zviad Gamsakhurdia flees the country as a result of the military coup.

Q60998244.name: Brumadinho dam disaster
Q60998244.blurb: A mining company's dam collapses in Brumadinho, Brazil, a south-eastern city, killing 270 people.

Q60999874.name: attempted assassination of Jair Bolsonaro
Q60999874.blurb: Brazilian presidential candidate Jair Bolsonaro survives a stabbing at a campaign rally in Juiz de Fora, Minas Gerais.

Q61049946.name: Inter-Allied Women's Conference
Q61049946.blurb: The Inter-Allied Women's Conference (delegates pictured) opened as a counterpart to the Paris Peace Conference, marking the first time that women were allowed formal participation in an international treaty negotiation.

Q61081194.name: Great Union
Q61081194.blurb: Transylvania unites with Romania, following the incorporation of Bessarabia (March 27) and Bukovina (November 28) and thus concluding the Great Union.

Q61732241.name: 2019 Pulwama attack
Q61732241.blurb: Pulwama attack takes place in Lethpora in Pulwama district, Jammu and Kashmir, India in which 40 Central Reserve Police Force personnel and a suicide bomber were killed and 35 were injured.

Q61742338.name: Haitian crisis (2019–present)
Q61742338.blurb: Haitian crisis: Haitian President Jovenel Moïse is assassinated in his residence in the capital of Port-au-Prince.

Q61744701.name: Oulu child sexual exploitation scandal
Q61744701.blurb: The Oulu Police informed the public about the first offence of the much larger child sexual exploitation in Oulu, Finland.

Q61843818.name: Battle of Baghuz Fawqani
Q61843818.blurb: The US-backed Syrian Democratic Forces capture the town of Baghuz in Eastern Syria, declaring military victory over the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant after four years of fighting, although the group maintains a scattered presence and sleeper cells across Syria and Iraq.

Q61846653.name: Atlas Air Flight 3591
Q61846653.blurb: Atlas Air Flight 3591, a Boeing 767 freighter, crashes into Trinity Bay near Anahuac, Texas, killing all three people on board.

Q61881326.name: 2019 Balakot airstrike
Q61881326.blurb: Indian Air Force fighter-jets target Jaish-e-Mohammed terrorist training camps in Balakot, Pakistan.

Q61946226.name: 2003 Guinea-Bissau coup d'état
Q61946226.blurb: Bissau-Guinean President Kumba Ialá is ousted from power in a bloodless military coup led by General Veríssimo Correia Seabra.

Q61946821.name: Beisfjord massacre
Q61946821.blurb: World War II: During the Beisfjord massacre in Norway, 15 Norwegian paramilitary guards help members of the SS to kill 288 political prisoners from Yugoslavia.

Q62018034.name: Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302 Crash
Q62018034.blurb: Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302, a Boeing 737 MAX, crashes shortly after takeoff, killing all 157 passengers and crew. This and the prior Lion Air Flight 610 led to all 387 Boeing 737 MAX aircraft being grounded worldwide.

Q62023294.name: Cyclone Idai
Q62023294.blurb: Cyclone Idai makes landfall near Beira, Mozambique, causing devastating floods and over 1,000 deaths.

Q62027184.name: Boeing 737 MAX groundings
Q62027184.blurb: Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302, a Boeing 737 MAX, crashes shortly after takeoff, killing all 157 passengers and crew. This and the prior Lion Air Flight 610 led to all 387 Boeing 737 MAX aircraft being grounded worldwide.

Q62066211.name: Christchurch mosque shootings
aliases: Royal Commission of Inquiry into the Attack on Christchurch Mosques
The Queen v Brenton Harrison Tarrant
Q62066211.blurb: Fifty-one people are killed in the Christchurch mosque shootings.

Q62116538.name: 2023 Estonian parliamentary election
Q62116538.blurb: The 2023 Estonian parliamentary election is held, with two centre-right liberal parties gaining an absolute majority for the first time.

Q62157533.name: 2019 Xiangshui chemical plant explosion
Q62157533.blurb: The 2019 Xiangshui chemical plant explosion occurs, killing at least 47 people and injuring 640 others.

Q62609017.name: Reiwa era
Q62609017.blurb: Naruhito ascends to the throne of Japan succeeding his father Akihito, beginning the Reiwa period.

Q63033289.name: 1989 murders of Jesuits in El Salvador
Q63033289.blurb: El Salvadoran army troops kill six Jesuit priests and two others at Jose Simeon Canas University.

Q63099653.name: 1985 Sudanese coup d'état
Q63099653.blurb: Sudanese President Gaafar Nimeiry is ousted from power in a coup d'état led by Field Marshal Abdel Rahman Swar al-Dahab.

Q63146684.name: Battles of Bedriacum
Q63146684.blurb: Vitellius, commanding Rhine-based armies, defeats Roman emperor Otho in the First Battle of Bedriacum to take power over Rome.

Q63167656.name: 2019 fire at Notre-Dame de Paris
aliases: Notre Dame cathedral in Paris fire
Burning of the Notre Dame church
Q63167656.blurb: A fire severely damaged Notre-Dame de Paris, destroying the cathedral's timber spire and much of the roof.

Q63241885.name: Joe Biden 2020 presidential campaign
Q63241885.blurb: Joe Biden gives his acceptance speech virtually for the 2020 Democratic presidential nomination at the 2020 Democratic National Convention.

Q63245644.name: 2019 Sri Lanka bombings
aliases: April 2019 Sri Lanka Easter Church bombings
Q63245644.blurb: Eight bombs explode at churches, hotels, and other locations in Sri Lanka on Easter Sunday, killing at least 269.

Q63247729.name: North Korean Embassy in Madrid incident
aliases: Raid on the North Korean embassy in Madrid
Q63247729.blurb: A group broke into the North Korean embassy in Madrid, Spain, and stole several mobile telephones and digital storage devices.

Q63344623.name: Civil war of Finland victory parade in Helsinki
Q63344623.blurb: The victory military parade by the Finnish White Guard is held in Helsinki celebrating their decisive victory in the Finnish Civil War. The day also begin to be celebrated on the Defence Forces Flag Day before it is moved in 1942 to the June 4th.

Q63819987.name: Artemis program
Q63819987.blurb: Artemis Program: NASA launches Artemis 1 on the first flight of the Space Launch System, the start of the program's future missions to the moon.

Q64009002.name: 2019 Surat fire
Q64009002.blurb: Twenty-two students die in a fire in Surat (India).

Q64214898.name: Virginia Beach shooting
Q64214898.blurb: A shooting occurs inside a municipal building at Virginia Beach, Virginia, leaving 13 people dead, including the shooter, and four others injured.

Q64481622.name: Khartoum massacre
Q64481622.blurb: Khartoum massacre: In Sudan, over 100 people are killed when security forces accompanied by Janjaweed militiamen storm and open fire on a sit-in protest.

Q64509602.name: 2019–2020 Hong Kong protests
aliases: 2019 anti Extradition Law Amendment Bill protests
Deaths and fatal injuries in 2019 Hong Kong protests
Deaths and serious injuries in the 2019-20 Hong Kong protests
Deaths and serious injuries in the 2019–20 Hong Kong protests
Economic impact of the 2019 Hong Kong protests
Impact of the 2019-2020 Hong Kong protests

Timeline of the 2019–20 Hong Kong protests (November 2020)
反對逃犯條例修訂草案運動
Q64509602.blurb: Beginning of the 2019–20 Hong Kong protests.

Q64605287.name: 2008 Universal Studios fire
Q64605287.blurb: A fire on the back lot of Universal Studios breaks out, destroying the attraction King Kong Encounter and a large archive of master tapes for music and film, the full extent of which was not revealed until 2019.

Q64740664.name: 2019 Iranian shoot-down of American drone
Q64740664.blurb: Iranian aircraft shot down an American drone over the Strait of Hormuz amid heightened tensions between the two countries.

Q64827196.name: Soham murders
Q64827196.blurb: The Soham murder trial ends at the Old Bailey in London, with Ian Huntley found guilty of two counts of murder.  His girlfriend, Maxine Carr, is found guilty of perverting the course of justice.

Q64831570.name: 2019 FIFA Women's World Cup Final
aliases: 2019 FIFA Women's World Cup Match 52, United States v Netherlands
Q64831570.blurb: The United States defeated the Netherlands 2–0 at the 2019 FIFA Women's World Cup final in Lyon, France.

Q64889987.name: 2019 Koreas–United States Panmunjom Summit
Q64889987.blurb: Donald Trump becomes the first sitting US President to visit the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea).

Q65033611.name: SDF insurgency in Northern Aleppo
Q65033611.blurb: Syrian civil war: Following the completion of the Afrin offensive, the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) initiate an insurgency against the Turkish occupation of the Afrin District.

Q65041294.name: Eddington experiment
Q65041294.blurb: Albert Einstein's theory of general relativity is tested (later confirmed) by Arthur Eddington and Andrew Claude de la Cherois Crommelin.

Q65042005.name: Muharram Rebellion
Q65042005.blurb: British East India Company: Muharram Rebellion: Hada and Mada Miah lead the first anti-British uprising in the subcontinent against Robert Lindsay and his contingents in Sylhet Shahi Eidgah.

Q65045870.name: 1420 Caldera earthquake
Q65045870.blurb: The 8.8–9.4 Caldera earthquake shakes Chile's Atacama Region causing tsunami in Chile, Hawaii, and Japan.

Q65047509.name: Air Transport International Flight 805
Q65047509.blurb: Air Transport International Flight 805 crashes in Swanton, Ohio, near Toledo Express Airport, killing all four people on board.

Q65056942.name: UN retreat from North Korea
Q65056942.blurb: Korean War: UN forces began a retreat from North Korea following defeat at the Battle of the Ch'ongch'on River.

Q65057499.name: Coronation of William IV and Adelaide
Q65057499.blurb: William IV and Adelaide of Saxe-Meiningen were crowned King and Queen of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland.

Q65060958.name: 2019 Hpakant jade mine collapse
Q65060958.blurb: The April 2019 Hpakant jade mine collapse in Myanmar kills four miners and two rescuers, with at least 50 others missing and presumed dead.

Q65069640.name: Battle of Mutukula
Q65069640.blurb: After surrounding Mutukula the previous day, Tanzanian forces attacked the town and caused Ugandan forces to flee.

Q65069862.name: Operation Pheasant
Q65069862.blurb: World War II: Operation Pheasant, an Allied offensive to liberate North Brabant in the Netherlands, ends successfully.

Q65074171.name: 2003 Mosul raid
Q65074171.blurb: Iraq War: Members of 101st Airborne of the United States, aided by Special Forces, attack a compound in Iraq, killing Saddam Hussein's sons Uday and Qusay, along with Mustapha Hussein, Qusay's 14-year-old son, and a bodyguard.

Q65078081.name: Total Linhas Aereas Flight 5561
Q65078081.blurb: Total Linhas Aéreas Flight 5561 crashes near Paranapanema, Brazil, killing both pilots on board.

Q65078467.name: Battle of Orange Walk
Q65078467.blurb: A small British force commanded by a surgeon fought off a surprise attack by the Maya on Orange Walk Town, British Honduras.

Q65079568.name: Fall of Berlin
Q65079568.blurb: The French Army under Napoleon enters Berlin following the Prussian defeat at the Battle of Jena–Auerstedt.

Q65081806.name: Defense of the Cutter Eagle
Q65081806.blurb: War of 1812: The United States Revenue Marine attempts to defend the cutter Eagle from the Royal Navy.

Q65082760.name: wedding of Prince Edward, Duke of Kent, and Katharine Worsley
aliases: wedding of Prince Edward and Katharine Worsley
wedding of Prince Edward, Duke of Kent, and Katharine, Duchess of Kent
Q65082760.blurb: Marriage of Prince Edward, Duke of Kent to Katharine Worsley at York Minster.

Q65088700.name: execution of Charles I
Q65088700.blurb: Charles I of England is executed in Whitehall, London.

Q65090430.name: 1985 Teterboro collision
Q65090430.blurb: A Dassault Falcon 50 and a Piper PA-28 Cherokee collide in mid-air over Fairview, New Jersey, killing six people and injuring eight.

Q65090703.name: 2020 Democratic National Convention
Q65090703.blurb: Joe Biden gives his acceptance speech virtually for the 2020 Democratic presidential nomination at the 2020 Democratic National Convention.

Q65091319.name: 2022 Australian federal election
Q65091319.blurb: Anthony Albanese of the Australian Labor Party is sworn in as the 31st Prime Minister of Australia after winning the 2022 Australian federal election, ending 9 years of conservative rule.

Q65117742.name: Safavid occupation of Basra
Q65117742.blurb: Safavid government troops take control of Basra.

Q65117816.name: Johnson–Jeffries riots
Q65117816.blurb: The Johnson–Jeffries riots occur after African-American boxer Jack Johnson knocks out white boxer Jim Jeffries in the 15th round. Between 11 and 26 people are killed and hundreds more injured.

Q65119127.name: La Matanza
Q65119127.blurb: In a case later termed a "legal lynching", Will P. Brady obtained a guilty verdict and death sentence against 15-year-old León Martínez Jr., five days after his arrest for killing a white woman.

Q65120393.name: Trans International Airlines Flight 863
Q65120393.blurb: Trans International Airlines Flight 863 crashes during takeoff from John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York City, killing all 11 aboard.

Q65120655.name: Dolo hospital airstrike
Q65120655.blurb: The Italian Air Force bombs a Swedish Red Cross hospital during the Second Italo-Abyssinian War.

Q65122502.name: 1985 Nigerian coup d'état
Q65122502.blurb: Major General Muhammadu Buhari, Chairman of the Supreme Military Council of Nigeria, is ousted from power in a coup d'état led by Major General Ibrahim Babangida.

Q65160775.name: Ciudad Juárez cobalt-60 contamination incident
Q65160775.blurb: A radiation detector at Los Alamos National Laboratory in New Mexico, United States, detects radioactivity after a truck carrying rebar accidentally passed through the laboratory's area, revealing a contamination incident that occurred in Ciudad Juárez, Mexico, the previous month.

Q65176926.name: East African Airways Flight 720
Q65176926.blurb: East African Airways Flight 720 crashes during a rejected takeoff from Addis Ababa Bole International Airport in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, killing 43.

Q65563181.name: Skydive Umeå Gippsland GA8 Airvan crash
Q65563181.blurb: A GippsAero GA8 Airvan crashes in Umeå, Sweden, killing all nine aboard.

Q65640303.name: Kyoto Animation arson attack
Q65640303.blurb: A man sets fire to an anime studio in Fushimi-ku, Kyoto, Japan, killing 36 people and injuring dozens of others.

Q65767134.name: 2019 Yuen Long attack
Q65767134.blurb: Yuen Long attack or "721 incident" in Hong Kong. Triad members indiscriminately beat civilians returning from protests while police failed to take action.

Q66011598.name: 2019 Altamira prison riot
Q66011598.blurb: The 2019 Altamira prison riot between rival Brazilian drug gangs leaves 62 dead.

Q66108236.name: 2019 El Paso shooting
aliases: Aftermath of the 2019 El Paso shooting
Shooting at El Paso shopping center
Q66108236.blurb: Twenty-three people are killed and 22 injured in a mass shooting at a Walmart in El Paso, Texas.

Q66120984.name: 2019 Dayton shooting
Q66120984.blurb: Nine people are killed and 26 injured in a shooting in Dayton, Ohio. This comes only 13 hours after another mass shooting in El Paso, Texas, where 23 people were killed.

Q66123117.name: Typhoon Lekima
Q66123117.blurb: Thirty-two are killed and one million are evacuated as Typhoon Lekima makes landfall in Zhejiang, China. Earlier it had caused flooding in the Philippines.

Q66363708.name: Bærum mosque shooting
Q66363708.blurb: Philip Manshaus shoots his stepsister and attacks a mosque in the Bærum mosque shooting.

Q66424571.name: nuclear accident in Russia in August 2019
Q66424571.blurb: An explosion at the State Central Navy Testing Range in Nyonoksa, Russia, kills five people.

Q66467267.name: 2019 heat waves in Europe
Q66467267.blurb: National extreme heat records set this day in the UK, Belgium, The Netherlands and Germany during the July 2019 European heat wave.

Q66554821.name: 17 August 2019 Kabul bombing
Q66554821.blurb: A bomb explodes at a wedding in Kabul killing 63 people and leaving 182 injured.

Q66594425.name: 2019 Papua and West Papua protests
Q66594425.blurb: Twenty people die on the first of two days of rioting in Papua and West Papua over an alleged racist incident.

Q66666935.name: Kon-Tiki expedition
Q66666935.blurb: Thor Heyerdahl and five crew mates set out from Peru on the Kon-Tiki to demonstrate that Peruvian natives could have settled Polynesia.

Q66707597.name: 94th Academy Awards
Q66707597.blurb: At the 94th Academy Awards, Will Smith slapped Chris Rock onstage resulting in Smith being expelled from the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences and banned from its events for ten years.

Q66744666.name: death of Jeffrey Epstein
Q66744666.blurb: Jeffrey Epstein, an American financier and convicted sex offender, was found dead in his cell at the Metropolitan Correctional Center, New York.

Q66764432.name: Hurricane Dorian
Q66764432.blurb: Hurricane Dorian, the most powerful Atlantic hurricane on record outside the tropics, made landfall in the Bahamas at Category 5 intensity.

Q66791584.name: murder of Jonelle Matthews
Q66791584.blurb: Disappearance of Jonelle Matthews from Greeley, Colorado. Her remains were discovered on July 23, 2019, located about 24 km (15 mi) southeast of Jonelle's home. The cause of death "was a gunshot wound to the head."

Q66936918.name: helicopter accident in Alta, Norway, in 2019
Q66936918.blurb: A sightseeing helicopter crashed in the mountains of Skoddevarre in Alta, Norway, killing all six people on board.

Q67031507.name: Sinking of MV Conception
Q67031507.blurb: The dive boat MV Conception catches fire and sinks near Santa Cruz Island, killing 34.

Q67205392.name: September 2019 climate strikes
Q67205392.blurb: Roughly four million people, mostly students, demonstrate across the world to address climate change. Sixteen-year-old Greta Thunberg from Sweden leads the demonstration in New York City.

Q67320741.name: 1275 British earthquake
Q67320741.blurb: An earthquake occurred in the south of Great Britain, notably causing multiple fatalities as well as destroying St Michael's Church on Glastonbury Tor.

Q67527355.name: 2019 Abqaiq-Khurais attack
aliases: 2019 attack on Saudi Arabian oil processing facilities
Q67527355.blurb: Drone attacks on major processing facilities at Abqaiq and Khurais forced Saudi Arabia to cut more than half of its oil production.

Q68531233.name: Freeze 'em all: Live in Antarctica
Q68531233.blurb: Metallica (pictured) played a concert in Antarctica, becoming the first band to perform on all seven continents.

Q68544129.name: 2019 British prorogation controversy
Q68544129.blurb: The Supreme Court of the United Kingdom unanimously ruled that advice given by Prime Minister Boris Johnson to Queen Elizabeth II that Parliament should be prorogued was unlawful.

Q68829949.name: Little Rock Campaign
aliases: Advance of the Union forces upon Little Rock, Ark.
Q68829949.blurb: American Civil War: The Little Rock campaign ended with the Union Army capturing Little Rock, Arkansas.

Q69163529.name: fall of the Berlin Wall
Q69163529.blurb: Cold War: Fall of the Berlin Wall: East Germany opens checkpoints in the Berlin Wall, allowing its citizens to travel to West Berlin.

Q69430137.name: Kuopio school stabbing
Q69430137.blurb: Kuopio school stabbing: One dies and ten are injured when Joel Marin, armed with a sabre, attacks a school class at Savo Vocational College in Kuopio, Finland.

Q69479248.name: 2019–20 Peruvian constitutional crisis
aliases: 2019 dissolution of the Congress of the Republic of Peru
Dissolution of the Congress of the Republic of Peru of 2019
Q69479248.blurb: President Martín Vizcarra dissolved the Congress of Peru, resulting in a constitutional crisis.

Q69551492.name: 2019 Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress crash
Q69551492.blurb: A privately owned Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress conducting a living history exhibition flight crashes shortly after takeoff from Windsor Locks, Connecticut, killing seven.

Q69841946.name: Typhoon Hagibis
Q69841946.blurb: Typhoon Hagibis makes landfall in Japan, killing 10 and forcing the evacuation of one million people.

Q69922225.name: Battle of Babylon Hill
Q69922225.blurb: First English Civil War: Royalist and Parliamentarian forces clashed in the Battle of Babylon Hill, after which both sides claimed victory.

Q70207089.name: 2019 Turkish offensive into north-eastern Syria
aliases: Turkish invasion of northern and eastern Syria
Q70207089.blurb: Turkey begins its military offensive in north-eastern Syria.

Q70636879.name: INEOS 1:59 Challenge
Q70636879.blurb: Eliud Kipchoge from Kenya becomes the first person to run a marathon in less than two hours with a time of 1:59:40 in Vienna.

Q70836732.name: 2019 Chicago Marathon
Q70836732.blurb: At the Chicago Marathon, Kenyan runner Brigid Kosgei (pictured) set the current marathon world record for women running in a mixed-sex race.

Q71443275.name: 17 October Revolution
Q71443275.blurb: The 17 October Revolution starts in Lebanon.

Q71500435.name: 2019–2021 Chilean protests
Q71500435.blurb: Riots in Chile's capital Santiago escalate into open battles, with attacks reported at nearly all of the city's 164 Metro stations. President Sebastián Piñera later announces a 15-day state of emergency in the capital.

Q71936844.name: 2019 Bolivian protests
Q71936844.blurb: President of Bolivia Evo Morales and several of his government resign after 19 days of civil protests and a recommendation from the military.

Q72587856.name: Death of Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi
Q72587856.blurb: Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant founder and leader Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi kills himself and three children by detonating a suicide vest during the U.S. military Barisha raid in northwestern Syria.

Q72856217.name: Battle of Culiacán
Q72856217.blurb: Drug dealers in Culiacan, Sinaloa, Mexico force the government to back down on an arrest.

Q73101291.name: First Venezuelan coup d'etat attempt of 1992
Q73101291.blurb: A coup d'état is led by Hugo Chávez against Venezuelan President Carlos Andrés Pérez.

Q74457482.name: 2019 Bolivian political crisis
Q74457482.blurb: President of Bolivia Evo Morales and several of his government resign after 19 days of civil protests and a recommendation from the military.

Q75034713.name: Saugus High School shooting
Q75034713.blurb: A mass shooting occurs at Saugus High School in Santa Clarita, California, resulting in three deaths, including that of the perpetrator, and three injuries.

Q76529995.name: 2019 Albania earthquake
Q76529995.blurb: A 5.6 Mw earthquake shakes the Albanian port of Durrës. Forty-nine people are injured in the capital, Tirana.

Q77842043.name: Expedition 63
Q77842043.blurb: Soyuz MS-16 is launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome, carrying the Expedition 62/63 crew to the International Space Station.

Q77929275.name: 2019 Whakaari / White Island eruption
Q77929275.blurb: A volcano on Whakaari / White Island, New Zealand, kills 22 people after it erupts.

Q78030156.name: Ostrava hospital attack
Q78030156.blurb: The Ostrava hospital attack in the Czech Republic results in eight deaths, including the perpetrator.

Q78207294.name: 2020 Atlantic hurricane season
Q78207294.blurb: Tropical Storm Alpha forms in the Atlantic Basin, making the 2005 Atlantic hurricane season the most active Atlantic hurricane season until surpassed by the 2020 season.

Q78455589.name: Citizenship (Amendment) Act protests
Q78455589.blurb: Citizenship Amendment Act protests: 10 to 15 local women blockaded a major road in Delhi, India, to protest the exclusion of Muslims from the amended Citizenship Act.

Q78678439.name: Hōjō Coal Mine Disaster
Q78678439.blurb: A gas explosion at Mitsubishi Hōjō coal mine, in Kyushu, Japan, kills 687.

Q78851988.name: 2024 United Kingdom general election
aliases: Glossary of terms from the 2024 United Kingdom general election
List of MPs who are standing down at the next United Kingdom general election
Q78851988.blurb: Keir Starmer led the Labour Party to a landslide victory in the United Kingdom general election, ending fourteen years of Conservative rule.

Q79063280.name: first impeachment of Donald Trump
Q79063280.blurb: The first impeachment of Donald Trump formally moves into its trial phase in the United States Senate.

Q79077052.name: first impeachment trial of Donald Trump
Q79077052.blurb: United States President Donald Trump is acquitted by the United States Senate in his first impeachment trial.

Q79373548.name: Typhoon Phanfone
Q79373548.blurb: Twenty people are killed and thousands are left homeless by Typhoon Phanfone in the Philippines.

Q80101804.name: December 2019 Mogadishu bombing
Q80101804.blurb: A truck bomb is detonated in Mogadishu, Somalia, killing at least 85 people and injuring over 140 more. The militant group Al-Shabaab claims responsibility.

Q80754846.name: assassination of Qasem Soleimani
aliases: Indictment for the Assassination Plot Against Donald Trump
Iranian plot to assassinate Donald Trump
Iranian plots to assassinate Donald Trump
U.S. drone strike on Soleimani convoy in Iraq
Q80754846.blurb: Iranian General Qasem Soleimani is killed by an American airstrike near Baghdad International Airport, igniting global concerns of a potential armed conflict.

aliases: COVID-19 pandemic, People's Republic of China

Controversies related to the 2019–20 coronavirus outbreak
Q81068910.blurb: The COVID-19 pandemic causes all casinos in Macau to be closed down for 15 days.

Q81231211.name: Homs school bombing
Q81231211.blurb: A double bombing of an elementary school in Homs, Syria kills over 50 people.

Q81307590.name: 2020 Puerto Rico earthquake
Q81307590.blurb: The 6.4Mw 2019–20 Puerto Rico earthquakes kill four and injure nine in southern Puerto Rico.

Q81360866.name: Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752
aliases: Crash of Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752 on January 8, 2020
Crash of flight PS752 on January 8, 2020
Q81360866.blurb: Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752 crashes immediately after takeoff at Tehran Imam Khomeini International Airport; all 176 on board are killed. The plane was shot down by an Iranian anti-aircraft missile.

Q81914341.name: 2020–2022 Taal Volcano eruptions
Q81914341.blurb: Taal Volcano in the Philippines erupts and kills 39 people.

Q82452548.name: Shaheen Bagh protests
Q82452548.blurb: Citizenship Amendment Act protests: 10 to 15 local women blockaded a major road in Delhi, India, to protest the exclusion of Muslims from the amended Citizenship Act.

Q83258064.name: George Washington's reception at Trenton
Q83258064.blurb: George Washington's reception at Trenton is hosted by the Ladies of Trenton as he journeys to New York City for his first inauguration.

Q83455501.name: Treaty of London
Q83455501.blurb: The Treaty of London between England and Scotland, ending the Bishops' Wars, is signed.

Q83505810.name: 2020 Conservative Party of Canada leadership election
Q83505810.blurb: Erin O'Toole is elected leader of the Conservative Party of Canada.

Q83554667.name: COVID-19 lockdown in China
Q83554667.blurb: COVID-19 pandemic: China ends its lockdown in Wuhan.

Q83737887.name: 2020 Calabasas helicopter crash
Q83737887.blurb: A Sikorsky S-76 helicopter crashed in Calabasas, California, killing all nine people on board, including former basketball player Kobe Bryant and his daughter Gianna.

Q83780345.name: Liberation of Auschwitz concentration camp
Q83780345.blurb: World War II: The Soviet 322nd Rifle Division liberates the remaining inmates of Auschwitz-Birkenau.

Q84055415.blurb: The region of Uusimaa (with the capital city Helsinki) is temporarily isolated from the rest of Finland due to increased COVID-19 infections.

Q84055514.name: COVID-19 pandemic in India
aliases: Evacuations by India related to the COVID-19 pandemic
Q84055514.blurb: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi announces the country's largest ever self-imposed curfew, in an effort to fight the spread of COVID-19.

Q84080272.name: 2020 Myanmar parliamentary election
Q84080272.blurb: Myanmar holds the 2020 general election, re-electing a government led by the National League for Democracy, which is deposed by the Burmese military the following February during the 2021 Myanmar coup d'état.

Q84080655.name: 2022 Malaysian general election
Q84080655.blurb: Five days after the general elections which resulted in a hung parliament, opposition leader and former deputy prime minister Anwar Ibrahim is officially named as the 10th prime minister of Malaysia.

Q84428052.name: Pegasus Airlines Flight 2193
Q84428052.blurb: Pegasus Airlines Flight 2193 overshoots the runway at Sabiha Gökçen International Airport and crashes, killing three people and injuring 179.

Q84561710.name: Waitangi dildo incident
Q84561710.blurb: New Zealand politician Steven Joyce is hit by a flung rubber dildo in a Waitangi Day protest.

Q84599740.name: Nakhon Ratchasima shootings
Q84599740.blurb: A soldier opens fire in a military camp and a shopping center in Nakhon Ratchasima, Thailand, killing 29 people and injuring 58 others before being shot dead by police the next day. It is considered the deadliest mass shooting in the country's history.

Q84806169.name: 1979 Salvadoran coup d'état
Q84806169.blurb: A coup d'état in El Salvador overthrows President Carlos Humberto Romero and begins the 12 year-long Salvadoran Civil War.

Q85159130.name: 2020 Salvadoran political crisis
Q85159130.blurb: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele has the army soldiers enter the Legislative Assembly to assist in pushing for the approval for a better government security plan, causing a brief political crisis.

Q85503435.name: Ntumbo attack
Q85503435.blurb: At least 22 people are killed in an attack on a village in Northwest Region, Cameroon.

Q85636305.name: 2020 Hanau shootings
Q85636305.blurb: Nine people are killed in two domestic terrorist shootings in Hanau, Hesse, Germany.

Q85719776.name: 1668 North Anatolia earthquake
Q85719776.blurb: The magnitude 8.0 North Anatolia earthquake causes 8,000 deaths in northern Anatolia, Ottoman Empire.

Q85720158.name: 1875 Indianola hurricane
Q85720158.blurb: The Indianola hurricane dissipated over Mississippi after killing around eight hundred people in Texas.

Q85722364.name: 1938 deportation of Jews from Slovakia
Q85722364.blurb: The Hlinka Guard and Slovakian police began the deportation of several thousand Jews from the country.

Q85722610.name: 1946 Rabat Vickers Wellington crash
Q85722610.blurb: A Fleet Air Arm Vickers Wellington crashes into a residential area in Rabat, Malta during a training exercise, killing all four crew members and 16 civilians on the ground.

Q85722739.name: 1948 Gozo luzzu disaster
Q85722739.blurb: A luzzu fishing boat overloaded with passengers capsizes and sinks in the Gozo Channel off Qala, Gozo, Malta, killing 23 of the 27 people on board.

Q85722886.name: 1952 Luqa Avro Lancaster crash
Q85722886.blurb: An RAF Avro Lancaster bomber crashes in Luqa, Malta after an engine failure, killing three crew members and a civilian on the ground.

Q85724597.name: 1975 Żabbar Avro Vulcan crash
Q85724597.blurb: An RAF Avro Vulcan bomber explodes and crashes over Żabbar, Malta after an aborted landing, killing five crew members and one person on the ground.

Q85728271.name: Dave Matthews Band incident
Q85728271.blurb: A tour bus belonging to the Dave Matthews Band dumps approximately 800 pounds of human waste onto a boat full of passengers.

Q85731696.name: 2019 Jammu and Kashmir airstrikes
Q85731696.blurb: Pakistan Air Force JF-17 Thunder downs Indian pilot Abhinandan Varthaman's Mig-21 in an aerial dogfight and captures him after conducting airstrikes in Jammu and Kashmir.

Q85735053.name: 2020 California wildfires
Q85735053.blurb: California wildfires: A pyrotechnic device at a gender reveal party ignited the El Dorado Fire (pictured), burning for 71 days and killing one firefighter.

Q85738839.name: Airborne Express Flight 827
Q85738839.blurb: Airborne Express Flight 827 crashes in Narrows, Virginia, killing all six people on board.

Q85739675.name: Action at Sihayo's Kraal
Q85739675.blurb: Anglo-Zulu War: Natal Native Contingent and British troops defeated Zulu forces in the Action at Sihayo's Kraal.

Q85743109.name: Arsenal Women 11–1 Bristol City Women
Q85743109.blurb: Arsenal Women 11–1 Bristol City Women breaks the record for most goals scored in a FA Women's Super League match, with Vivianne Miedema involved in ten of the eleven Arsenal goals.

Q85744444.name: Axis capture of Tobruk
Q85744444.blurb: World War II: Tobruk falls to Italian and German forces; 33,000 Allied troops are taken prisoner.

Q85745908.name: Battle of Río Bueno
Q85745908.blurb: Arauco War: A Spanish army is defeated by local Mapuche-Huilliches as it tries to cross Bueno River in Southern Chile.

Q85745955.name: Battle of Winnington Bridge
Q85745955.blurb: Parliamentarian forces under John Lambert defeat Royalist forces under George Booth in the battle of Winnington Bridge, ending Booth's Uprising.

Q85745957.name: Battle of al-Mada'in
Q85745957.blurb: Start of the four-day Battle of al-Mada'in, between the Hamdanids of Mosul and the Baridis of Basra over control of the Abbasid capital, Baghdad.

Q85760415.name: Fall of Phnom Penh
Q85760415.blurb: The Khmer Rouge captured Phnom Penh, the capital of the Khmer Republic, ending the Cambodian Civil War and establishing the socialist state of Democratic Kampuchea.

Q85760625.name: Fatimid conquest of Egypt
Q85760625.blurb: The Fatimid general Jawhar leads the Friday prayer in Fustat in the name of Caliph al-Mu'izz li-Din Allah, thereby symbolically completing the Fatimid conquest of Egypt.

Q85776216.name: Leicester balloon riot
Q85776216.blurb: A riot broke out in Leicester, England, at the failed launching of a gas balloon (pictured).

Q85782704.name: Luton Peace Day Riots
Q85782704.blurb: Following Peace Day celebrations marking the end of the First World War, English ex-servicemen unhappy with unemployment and other grievances rioted and burned down Luton Town Hall.

Q85783755.name: Mapuche uprising of 1655
Q85783755.blurb: The Mapuches launch coordinated attacks against the Spanish in Chile beginning the Mapuche uprising of 1655.

Q85791385.name: Ottoman reconquest of the Morea
Q85791385.blurb: Seventh Ottoman–Venetian War: The Ottoman Empire captures Nauplia, the capital of the Republic of Venice's "Kingdom of the Morea", thereby opening the way to the swift Ottoman reconquest of the Morea.

Q85801095.name: Siege of Nauplia
Q85801095.blurb: Seventh Ottoman–Venetian War: The Ottoman Empire captures Nauplia, the capital of the Republic of Venice's "Kingdom of the Morea", thereby opening the way to the swift Ottoman reconquest of the Morea.

Q85801100.name: Siege of Quebec
Q85801100.blurb: French forces commence the siege of Quebec which is held by the British.

Q85801106.name: Siege of Wardour Castle
Q85801106.blurb: First English Civil War: The first siege of Wardour Castle ended after six days with the surrender of the Royalist garrison under Lady Blanche Arundell

Q85810413.name: Trans-Canada Air Lines Flight 9
Q85810413.blurb: A Royal Canadian Air Force Canadair Harvard collides with a Trans-Canada Airlines Canadair North Star over Moose Jaw, Saskatchewan, killing 37 people.

Q85814762.name: Wedding of Constantine II of Greece and Princess Anne-Marie of Denmark
aliases: Wedding of King Constantine II of Greece and Princess Anne-Marie of Denmark
Q85814762.blurb: The wedding of Constantine II of Greece and Princess Anne-Marie of Denmark takes place in Athens.

Q85845265.name: 2023 Manitoba general election
Q85845265.blurb: Wab Kinew is elected to be the first First Nations Premier of a Canadian province in the 2023 Manitoba general election

Q85847045.name: Regent's Park skating disaster
Q85847045.blurb: Forty people die when ice covering the boating lake at Regent's Park, London, collapses.

Q85851457.name: Montreal Campaign
Q85851457.blurb: French and Indian War: French surrender Montreal to the British, completing the latter's conquest of New France.

Q86509170.name: 2020 Malaysian political crisis
Q86509170.blurb: Muhyiddin Yassin is appointed as the 8th Prime Minister of Malaysia, amid the 2020 Malaysian political crisis.

Q86597695.name: COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil
aliases: Brazilian government response to the COVID-19 pandemic
Q86597695.blurb: The traditional Carnival in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil is canceled for the first time because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

Q86661955.name: Cherokee removal
Q86661955.blurb: Cherokee leaders Major Ridge, John Ridge, and Elias Boudinot are assassinated for signing the Treaty of New Echota, which had resulted in the Trail of Tears.

Q86675044.name: Bombing of Genoa in World War II
Q86675044.blurb: World War II: Bombing of Genoa: The Cathedral of San Lorenzo in Genoa, Italy, is struck by a bomb which fails to detonate.

Q86753409.name: Partisan Congress riots
Q86753409.blurb: Several days of anti-Jewish rioting began in Bratislava, instigated by former Slovak partisans opposed to the restitution of Jewish property after the Holocaust in Slovakia.

Q86753827.name: Mapuche uprising of 1766
Q86753827.blurb: Mapuches in Chile launch a series of surprise attacks against the Spanish starting the Mapuche uprising of 1766.

Q87068864.name: COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
aliases: Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in Greece
Q87068864.blurb: Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis announces a national lockdown and the country's first ever self-imposed curfew, in an effort to fight the spread of COVID-19.

Q87202921.name: COVID-19 pandemic in Algeria
Q87202921.blurb: Five thousand people gathered in the town of Kherrata, Bejaia Province to mark the second anniversary of the Hirak protest movement. Demonstrations had been suspended because of the COVID-19 pandemic in Algeria.

Q87223521.name: 2020 Kabul shooting
Q87223521.blurb: 32 people are killed and 82 are injured when gunmen open fire on a ceremony in Kabul, Afghanistan. The Islamic State claims responsibility for the attack.

Q87348909.name: 2020 Italy coronavirus lockdown
Q87348909.blurb: Giuseppe Conte, Prime Minister of Italy, announces in a televised address and signs the decree imposing the first nationwide COVID-19 lockdown in the world.

Q87496123.name: 2020 Russia–Saudi Arabia oil price war
Q87496123.blurb: For the first time in history, oil prices drop below zero, an effect of the 2020 Russia-Saudi Arabia oil price war.

Q87629158.name: 2020 stock market crash
Q87629158.blurb: The Dow Jones Industrial Average falls by 2,997.10, the single largest point drop in history and the second-largest percentage drop ever at 12.93%, an even greater crash than Black Monday (1929). This follows the U.S. Federal Reserve announcing that it will cut its target interest rate to 0–0.25%.

Q87866152.name: COVID-19 pandemic lockdown
Q87866152.blurb: Giuseppe Conte, Prime Minister of Italy, announces in a televised address and signs the decree imposing the first nationwide COVID-19 lockdown in the world.

Q88599208.name: COVID-19 recession
Q88599208.blurb: The COVID-19 recession causes the U.S. unemployment rate to hit 14.9 percent, its worst rate since the Great Depression.

Q89490207.name: COVID-19 pandemic on USS Theodore Roosevelt
aliases: 2020 coronavirus pandemic on USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71)
COVID pandemic on USS Theodore Roosevelt
Q89490207.blurb: COVID-19 pandemic: Acting Secretary of the Navy Thomas Modly resigns for his handling of the COVID-19 pandemic on USS Theodore Roosevelt and the dismissal of Brett Crozier.

Q90500093.name: Alitalia Flight 1553
Q90500093.blurb: Alitalia Flight 1553 crashes at Genoa Cristoforo Colombo Airport in Genoa, Italy, killing four.

Q90500139.name: Garuda Indonesian Airways Flight 892
Q90500139.blurb: Garuda Indonesian Airways Flight 892 crashes near Nala Sopara in India, killing 30.

Q91129213.name: 2020 Nova Scotia shooting
Q91129213.blurb: A killing spree in Nova Scotia, Canada, leaves 22 people and the perpetrator dead, making it the deadliest rampage in the country's history.

Q91661003.name: Expedition 64
Q91661003.blurb: Soyuz MS-18 is launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome, carrying three members of the Expedition 64 crew to the International Space Station.

Q92987578.name: Mongol campaign against the Nizaris
aliases: Mongol campaign against the Nizari Ismaili state
Q92987578.blurb: The Nizari Ismaili garrison of Gerdkuh, Persia surrender after 17 years to the Mongols.

Q93439010.name: murder of Ahmaud Arbery
Q93439010.blurb: Ahmaud Arbery, a 25-year-old African-American citizen, is shot and murdered by three white men after visiting a house under construction while jogging at a neighborhood in Satilla Shores near Brunswick in Glynn County, Georgia.

Q93467772.name: Shutdown of ABS-CBN broadcasting
Q93467772.blurb: Philippine broadcast network ABS-CBN was forced to go off-air by the National Telecommunications Commission after Congress failed to renew its franchise granted in 1995.

Q93990392.name: Aeroméxico Flight 110
Q93990392.blurb: Aeroméxico Flight 110 crashes near Zihuatanejo, Mexico, killing all 18 people on board.

Q94346842.name: 30 January 1939 Reichstag speech
Q94346842.blurb: During a speech in the Reichstag, Adolf Hitler makes a prediction about the end of the Jewish race in Europe if another world war were to occur.

Q95092655.name: Pakistan International Airlines Flight 8303
Q95092655.blurb: Pakistan International Airlines Flight 8303 crashes in Model Colony near Jinnah International Airport in Karachi, Pakistan, killing 98 people.

Q95521351.name: Assault of Nancy Kerrigan
Q95521351.blurb: U.S. figure skater Nancy Kerrigan is attacked and injured by an assailant hired by her rival Tonya Harding's ex-husband during the U.S. Figure Skating Championships.

Q95579249.name: murder of George Floyd
aliases: My stomach hurts, my neck hurts, everything hurts... Man, I can't breathe.
Reaction to the killing of George Floyd
Q95579249.blurb: George Floyd, a black American man, was murdered (memorial pictured) during an arrest by a white police officer in Minneapolis, sparking protests in the U.S. and other countries.

Q95721899.name: shooting of Breonna Taylor
aliases: Arrest the cops that killed Breonna Taylor
Q95721899.blurb: Breonna Taylor is killed by police officers who were forcibly entering her home in Louisville, Kentucky; her death sparked extensive protests against racism and police brutality.

Q95965839.name: George Floyd protests
aliases: protests at the killing of George Floyd
Controversies surrounding the George Floyd protests
Entertainment industry response to George Floyd protests
Mass racial violence in the United States (George Floyd)
Media coverage of the George Floyd protests
Misinformation about the George Floyd protests
Misinformation related to the George Floyd protests
Protest the murder of George Floyd
Protests over the death of George Floyd
Protests over the killing of George Floyd
Use of social media in the George Floyd protests
Q95965839.blurb: Protests triggered by the murder of George Floyd erupt in Minneapolis–Saint Paul, later becoming widespread across the United States and around the world.

Q96066957.name: death of Giovanni López
Q96066957.blurb: Death of Giovanni López: Protests over the death of Giovanni López Ramírez, who had died on 4 May while in custody, begin in Jalisco following the release of a video of his arrest going viral on social media, and inspired by the George Floyd protests. Later, these spread across Mexico.

Q96071867.name: 2020 Norilsk oil spill
aliases: Norilsk-Taymyr Energy Company (NTEK) diesel fuel spill
Q96071867.blurb: An oil spill in Norilsk releases 17,500 tons of diesel oil into nearby rivers.

Q96256092.name: 1913 Romanian Army cholera outbreak
Q96256092.blurb: The 1913 Romanian Army cholera outbreak during the Second Balkan War starts.

Q96354876.name: 1831 Bristol riots
Q96354876.blurb: Rioting broke out in Bristol, England, after the Second Reform Bill failed to pass parliament, causing 250 casualties and £300,000 of damage (pictured).

Q96363593.name: 1978 Mauritanian coup d'état
Q96363593.blurb: President Moktar Ould Daddah of Mauritania is ousted in a bloodless coup d'état.

Q96373265.name: Battle of Mogaung
Q96373265.blurb: World War II: Mogaung is the first place in Burma to be liberated from the Japanese by British Chindits, supported by the Chinese.

Q96379887.name: Great Potosi Mint Fraud of 1649
Q96379887.blurb: As part of the purges following the Great Potosí Mint Fraud of 1649 Francisco Gómez de la Rocha, a rich former corregidor of Potosí, is executed.

Q96381353.name: Huilliche uprising of 1792
Q96381353.blurb: Spanish forces departed Valdivia to suppress the indigenous Huilliche uprising in southern Chile.

Q96382787.name: Invasion of South Kasai
Q96382787.blurb: Congo Crisis: In order to stop the secession of South Kasai from the Republic of Congo, Armée Nationale Congolaise forces launched an invasion of South Kasai.

Q96386376.name: Kronstadt-Toulon naval visits
Q96386376.blurb: During a visit of the French Navy to Kronstadt in Russia, the two nations reached a secret agreement on a joint response to any future war in Europe.

Q96399865.name: Postwar anti-Jewish violence in Slovakia
Q96399865.blurb: Dozens of Jews were injured in the Topoľčany pogrom, one of the worst episodes of anti-Jewish violence in postwar Czechoslovakia.

Q96414365.name: wedding of Princess Margaret and Antony Armstrong-Jones
aliases: Wedding of Princess Margaret and Antony of the United Kingdom Armstrong-Jones
Wedding of Princess Margaret, Countess of Snowdon and Antony Armstrong-Jones, Earl of Snowdon
Wedding of The Princess Margaret and Antony Armstrong-Jones
Wedding of The Princess Margaret and Antony of the United Kingdom Armstrong-Jones
Q96414365.blurb: More than 20 million viewers watch the first televised royal wedding when Princess Margaret marries Antony Armstrong-Jones at Westminster Abbey.

Q96788795.name: 2020 Hpakant jade mine disaster
Q96788795.blurb: A landslide at a jade mine in Hpakant killed 175–200 miners, the deadliest mining accident in Burmese history.

Q97101278.name: 2020 Barquisimeto shooting
Q97101278.blurb: During a demonstration, pro-government colectivos shoot at disputed President and Speaker of the National Assembly Juan Guaidó and his supporters in Barquisimeto, Venezuela, leaving five injured.

Q97160976.name: English expedition to Valdivia
aliases: Sir John Narbrough's voyage to the South-Sea
Q97160976.blurb: The expedition of John Narborough leaves Corral Bay, having surveyed the coast and lost four hostages to the Spanish.

Q97167535.name: Hi-Tek incident
Q97167535.blurb: In Little Saigon, California, a series of protests began when the owner of a video rental store displayed an image of Ho Chi Minh.

Q97180975.name: 1718 Tongwei–Gansu earthquake
Q97180975.blurb: At least 73,000 people die in the 1718 Tongwei–Gansu earthquake due to landslides in the Qing dynasty.

Q97190349.name: Military Operations Command
Q97190349.blurb: Syrian rebel groups led by Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham launch a ground offensive into Syria.

Q97209157.name: Delta Air Lines Flight 9877
Q97209157.blurb: Delta Air Lines Flight 9877 crashes at Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport, killing 19.

Q97269114.name: 1991 eruption of Mount Unzen
Q97269114.blurb: Mount Unzen erupts in Kyūshū, Japan, killing 43 people, all of them either researchers or journalists.

Q97327423.name: Paul Revere's Midnight Ride
Q97327423.blurb: American Revolutionary War: Colonists Paul Revere and William Dawes, later joined by Samuel Prescott, began a midnight ride to warn residents of Lexington and Concord, Massachusetts, about the impending arrival of British troops.

Q97328498.name: Columbus nightclub shooting
Q97328498.blurb: Columbus nightclub shooting: Nathan Gale opens fire at the Alrosa Villa nightclub in Columbus, Ohio, killing former Pantera guitarist Dimebag Darrell and three others before being shot dead by a police officer.

Q97356538.name: 1985 MOVE bombing
Q97356538.blurb: Police bomb MOVE headquarters in Philadelphia, killing six adults and five children, and destroying the homes of 250 city residents.

Q97381399.name: East Timorese civil war
Q97381399.blurb: The Timorese Democratic Union launched a coup in Portuguese Timor, starting the East Timorese civil war.

Q97495305.name: Alitalia Flight 618
Q97495305.blurb: A New York-bound Alitalia airliner crashes into a cemetery in Shannon, Ireland, shortly after takeoff, killing 34 of the 52 persons on board.

Q97610233.name: Battle of Cempoala
Q97610233.blurb: Hernan Cortés defeats Pánfilo de Narváez, sent by Spain to punish him for insubordination.

Q97861115.name: Air Caribbean Flight 309
Q97861115.blurb: Air Caribbean Flight 309 crashes in Residencial Las Casas in San Juan, Puerto Rico, killing six.

Q98073118.name: 2020 Beirut explosions
Q98073118.blurb: Beirut Port explosion: At least 220 people are killed and over 5,000 are wounded when 2,700 tons of ammonium nitrate explodes in Beirut, Lebanon.

Q98078467.name: 2020 Kenai Peninsula mid-air collision
Q98078467.blurb: A mid-air collision in Soldotna, Alaska, United States, killed seven people, including state representative Gary Knopp.

Q98129149.name: Air India Express Flight 1344
aliases: Passenger flight crashes upon landing at Calicut airport in India
Air India Express Flight No IX 1344
Q98129149.blurb: Air India Express Flight 1344 overshoots the runway at Calicut International Airport in the Malappuram district of Kerala, India, and crashes, killing 21 of the 190 people on board.

Q98241393.name: Typhoon Kathleen
Q98241393.blurb: Typhoon Kathleen hits the Kantō region, in Japan killing around 1,000-2,000 people.

Q98274390.name: August 2020 Midwest derecho
Q98274390.blurb: Derecho in Iowa becomes the most costly thunderstorm disaster in U.S. history.

Q98642744.name: 2020 Turkish Grand Prix
Q98642744.blurb: Lewis Hamilton wins the Turkish Grand Prix and secures his seventh drivers' title, equalling the all-time record held by Michael Schumacher.

Q98785100.name: Battle of York
Q98785100.blurb: An army of the Kingdom of Northumbria attempts to recapture York from the Great Heathen Army but is defeated in the battle of York.

Q98855455.name: 2023 Rugby World Cup Final
Q98855455.blurb: The 2023 Rugby World Cup final is held at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis, France. It saw South Africa defeat New Zealand 12 to 11, claiming their fourth Webb Ellis Cup, becoming the first nation to do so.

Q98986740.name: August Complex fire
Q98986740.blurb: The August Complex fire in California burns more than one million acres of land.

Q99207513.name: Bahrain–Israel peace agreement
Q99207513.blurb: Signing of the Bahrain–Israel normalization agreement occurs in Washington, D.C., normalizing relations between Israel and two Arab nations, the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain.

Q99659280.name: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War
aliases: Operation for peace enforcement of Armenia
Q99659280.blurb: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War: Azerbaijan launches an offensive against the self-proclaimed Republic of Artsakh in the Nagorno-Karabakh region, inhabited predominantly by ethnic Armenians.

Q100163806.name: Essential Commodities Reserves Act 1938
Q100163806.blurb: The Essential Commodities Reserves Act, which allowed the British government to build up reserves of essential commodities in anticipation of war, received royal assent.

Q100520438.name: 1984 New York City Subway shooting
Q100520438.blurb: "Subway vigilante" Bernhard Goetz shoots four would-be muggers on a 2 express train in Manhattan section of New York, United States.

Q100537531.name: Nottingham cheese riot
Q100537531.blurb: The Nottingham Cheese Riot breaks out at the Goose Fair in Nottingham, UK, in response to the excessive cost of cheese.

Q100598217.name: El Dorado Fire
Q100598217.blurb: The El Dorado Fire in California, United States, was extinguished after 71 days, having destroyed 20 structures and killed one firefighter.

Q100617691.name: 1837 Surat fire
Q100617691.blurb: The great fire in Surat, India causes more than 500 deaths and destruction of more than 9,000 houses.

Q100626766.name: 2020 Ghazanchetsots Cathedral shelling
Q100626766.blurb: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War: Azerbaijan twice deliberately targeted the Church of the Holy Savior Ghazanchetsots of Shusha.

Q101003145.name: Aegean Sea earthquake of 2020
Q101003145.blurb: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake strikes the Aegean Sea between Greece and Turkey, triggering a tsunami. At least 119 people die mainly due to collapsed buildings.

Q101095813.name: 2020 Vienna attacks
Q101095813.blurb: In Vienna's Innere Stadt district, an ISIL sympathizer shoots and kills four people and injures 23 more, before being shot and killed by the police.

Q101110072.name: 2024 United States presidential election
aliases: 2024 presidential election in the United States
2024 presidential election of the United States
International reactions to the 2024 United States presidential election
Results of the 2024 United States presidential election
Q101110072.blurb: U.S. President Joe Biden announces he will no longer seek a second term and withdraws from the 2024 election, endorsing Vice President Kamala Harris as she launches her own presidential campaign.

Q101231200.name: Tigray war
Q101231200.blurb: The Tigray War begins with Tigrayan rebels launching attacks on Ethiopian command centers.

Q101280264.name: 1839 Ava earthquake
Q101280264.blurb: A massive earthquake destroys the former capital Inwa of the Konbaung dynasty, present-day Myanmar.

Q101280498.name: 1930 Bago earthquake
Q101280498.blurb: The 1930 Bago earthquake, the first of two major earthquakes in southern Burma, kills as many as 7,000 in Yangon and Bago.

Q101305942.name: Battle of Shusha
Q101305942.blurb: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War: Azerbaijani forces defeated the self-proclaimed Republic of Artsakh in the Battle of Shusha, reclaiming the town after 28 years.

Q101369347.name: presidency of Joe Biden
Q101369347.blurb: Joe Biden is confirmed elected as the 46th president of the United States, defeating incumbent Donald Trump.

Q101429497.name: 2020 Nagorno-Karabakh ceasefire agreement
aliases: Statement by the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan, the Prime Minister of Armenia and the President of the Russian Federation
Statement by Azerbaijan, Armenia, and Russian Presidents
Q101429497.blurb: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War: An armistice agreement is signed by Armenia, Azerbaijan and Russia.

Q101436761.name: 2020−2021 Armenian protests
Q101436761.blurb: Armenia and Azerbaijan sign a ceasefire agreement, ending the Second Nagorno-Karabakh War, and prompting protests in Armenia.

Q101437849.name: Typhoon Vamco
Q101437849.blurb: Typhoon Vamco makes landfall in Luzon and several offshore islands, killing 67 people. The storm causes the worst floods in the region since Typhoon Ketsana in 2009.

Q101717588.name: death of Bridget Driscoll
Q101717588.blurb: Bridget Driscoll became the first recorded case of a pedestrian killed in a collision with a motor car in the United Kingdom.

Q101828437.name: death of Naya Rivera
Q101828437.blurb: After a five-day search, the body of American actress and singer Naya Rivera is recovered from Lake Piru in California, where she had drowned.

Q101881990.name: shooting of Yoshihiro Hattori
Q101881990.blurb: Having gone to the wrong house, Japanese student Yoshihiro Hattori is killed by the homeowner in Baton Rouge, Louisiana.

Q102313497.name: 2024 in public domain
Q102313497.blurb: Disney's copyright protection on Steamboat Willie and the original Mickey Mouse expires as they enter the public domain.

Q102314393.name: Strom Thurmond filibuster of the Civil Rights Act of 1957
Q102314393.blurb: U.S. Senator Strom Thurmond begins a filibuster to prevent the United States Senate from voting on the Civil Rights Act of 1957; he stopped speaking 24 hours and 18 minutes later. This would remain the longest speech ever conducted by a single Senator until Cory Booker spoke for 25 hours and five minutes, beginning on March 31, 2025.

Q102421173.name: 1981 Ghanaian coup d'état
Q102421173.blurb: A coup d'état in Ghana removes President Hilla Limann's PNP government and replaces it with the Provisional National Defence Council led by Flight lieutenant Jerry Rawlings.

Q102422710.name: attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election
aliases: disputes surrounding the 2020 United States presidential election results
Q102422710.blurb: Supporters of U.S. president Donald Trump storm the United States Capitol Building to disrupt certification of the 2020 presidential election, resulting in four deaths and evacuation of the U.S. Congress.

Q102443410.name: 1973 Luhuo earthquake
Q102443410.blurb: The Ms 7.6 Luhuo earthquake strikes Sichuan Province, causing widespread destruction and killing at least 2,199 people.

Q104511862.name: 2020 Nashville bombing
Q104511862.blurb: An explosion in Nashville, Tennessee, occurs, leaving three civilians in the hospital.

Q104530713.name: 1995 Qatari coup d'état
Q104530713.blurb: Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani deposes his father Khalifa bin Hamad Al Thani, the Emir of Qatar, in a bloodless coup d'état.

Q104535090.name: 2020 Petrinja earthquake
Q104535090.blurb: A magnitude 6.4 earthquake hits near the town of Petrinja in Sisak-Moslavina County, Croatia, killing seven people.

Q104585205.name: 2020 Aden Airport attack
Q104585205.blurb: A large explosion at the airport in the southern Yemeni city of Aden kills at least 22 people and wounds 50.

Q104686321.name: 2021 in Mexico
Q104686321.blurb: International Women's Day marches in Mexico become violent with 62 police officers and 19 civilians injured in Mexico City alone.
