Q104706517.name: 2020 United States presidential election Electoral College count
Q104706517.blurb: Supporters of U.S. president Donald Trump storm the United States Capitol Building to disrupt certification of the 2020 presidential election, resulting in four deaths and evacuation of the U.S. Congress.

Q104713215.name: second impeachment of Donald Trump
aliases: 2021 efforts to remove Donald Trump from office
Second impeachment inquiry against Donald Trump
Second impeachment proceedings against Donald Trump
Second impeachment process against Donald Trump
Q104713215.blurb: Outgoing U.S. President Donald Trump is impeached for a second time on a charge of incitement of insurrection following the January 6 United States Capitol attack one week prior.

Q104720479.name: 1867 Virgin Islands earthquake and tsunami
Q104720479.blurb: An earthquake strikes the Virgin Islands, triggering the largest tsunami witnessed in the Caribbean and killing dozens.

Q104759345.name: Sriwijaya Air Flight 182
Q104759345.blurb: Sriwijaya Air Flight 182 crashes north of Jakarta, Indonesia, killing all 62 people on board.

Q104776653.name: 1990 Faucett Perú 727 disappearance
Q104776653.blurb: A Faucett Boeing 727 disappears in the Atlantic Ocean while being flown from Malta to Peru.

Q104776742.name: Ryan International Airlines Flight 590
Q104776742.blurb: Ryan International Airlines Flight 590 crashes during takeoff from Cleveland Hopkins International Airport, killing both pilots, the aircraft's only occupants.

Q104787285.name: La Vega massacre
Q104787285.blurb: Twenty-three people are killed in what is described as a police ″massacre″ in La Vega, Caracas, Venezuela.

Q104803838.name: Axum massacre
Q104803838.blurb: Over seven hundred civilians are massacred by the Ethiopian National Defense Force and Eritrean Army in Aksum, Ethiopia.

Q104828966.name: 2021 West Sulawesi earthquake
Q104828966.blurb: A 6.2-magnitude earthquake strikes Indonesia's Sulawesi island killing at least 105 and injuring 3,369 people.

Q104830111.name: second impeachment trial of Donald Trump
Q104830111.blurb: Second impeachment trial of Donald Trump begins.

Q104834123.name: International Conference on the Holocaust and Genocide
Q104834123.blurb: The International Conference on the Holocaust and Genocide opens in Tel Aviv, despite attempts by the Turkish government to cancel it, as it included presentations on the Armenian genocide.

Q104841344.name: Booth's Uprising
Q104841344.blurb: Parliamentarian forces under John Lambert defeat Royalist forces under George Booth in the battle of Winnington Bridge, ending Booth's Uprising.

Q104841659.name: 1948 United States Senate election in Maine
Q104841659.blurb: Margaret Chase Smith of Maine becomes the first woman elected to the United States Senate without completing another senator's term.

Q104849178.name: Battle of Río Bueno
Q104849178.blurb: Spanish forces clash with indigenous Huilliches of southern Chile in the battle of Río Bueno.

Q104853874.name: London garrotting panics
Q104853874.blurb: The garrotting and robbery of James Pilkington, a British member of Parliament, led to a moral panic in London.

Q104864510.name: 1766 food riots
Q104864510.blurb: As part of wider food riots, citizens in Nottingham, England, looted large quantities of cheese; one man was killed during attempts to restore order.

Q104866316.name: Grande Tema incident
Q104866316.blurb: Operatives of the British Special Boat Service boarded the container ship Grande Tema in the Thames Estuary to detain four stowaways who had threatened the crew.

Q104880311.name: 1946 Ancash earthquake
Q104880311.blurb: A magnitude 6.9 earthquake in the Peruvian Andes mountains kills at least 1,400 people.

Q104912693.name: Battle of Crotoy
Q104912693.blurb: The English defeat a French fleet which aimed to bring relief to the besieged Calais in the battle of Crotoy.

Q105063719.name: Siege of Bednore
Q105063719.blurb: Second Anglo-Mysore War: British troops surrendered the fortress of Bednore in southwestern India to French and Mysorean forces; many of the prisoners were later murdered.

Q105095593.name: 1990 Interstate 75 fog disaster
Q105095593.blurb: Several fatal collisions in the 1990 Interstate 75 fog disaster result in a total of 12 deaths and 42 being injured

Q105123499.name: Siege of Taormina
Q105123499.blurb: Taormina, the last Byzantine stronghold in Sicily, is captured by the Aghlabid army, concluding the Muslim conquest of Sicily.

Q105180889.name: 2021 Myanmar coup d'état
aliases: Overthrow of Aung San Suu Kyi
၂၀၂၁ မြန်မာနိုင်ငံစစ်အာဏာသိမ်းခံရခြင်း
Q105180889.blurb: A coup d'état in Myanmar removes Aung San Suu Kyi from power and restores military rule.

Q105246837.name: American Rescue Plan Act of 2021
Q105246837.blurb: US President Joe Biden signs the $1.9 trillion American Rescue Plan into law.

Q105275820.name: Siege of Baghdad (1136)
Q105275820.blurb: Following the surrender of Baghdad, Seljuk Sultan Mas'ud replaces Abbasid caliph Al-Rashid Billah with his uncle Al-Muqtafi.

Q105320780.name: Suffragette bombing and arson campaign
Q105320780.blurb: The cricket pavilion at the Nevill Ground was destroyed in an arson attack (damage pictured) that was attributed to militant suffragettes as part of a country-wide campaign co-ordinated by the Women's Social and Political Union.

Q105347709.name: 1761 Lisbon earthquake
Q105347709.blurb: The 1761 Lisbon earthquake strikes off the Iberian Peninsula with an estimated magnitude of 8.5, six years after another quake destroyed the city.

Q105359547.name: Assassination of Laurent-Désiré Kabila
Q105359547.blurb: Second Congo War: Congolese President Laurent-Désiré Kabila is assassinated by one of his own bodyguards in Kinshasa.

Q105359643.name: death of Mark Saunders
Q105359643.blurb: British barrister Mark Saunders was shot dead by police after a five-hour siege at his home in Chelsea, London.

Q105367670.name: 2021–present Myanmar protests
Q105367670.blurb: Mya Thwe Thwe Khine, a 19-year-old protester, becomes the first known casualty of anti-coup protests that formed in response to the 2021 Myanmar coup d'état.

Q105393680.name: 2021 Farmers' Republic Day violence
Q105393680.blurb: Protesters and farmers storm the Red Fort near Delhi, clashing with police. One protester is killed and more than 80 police officers are injured.

Q105527922.name: 2021 Congo River disaster
Q105527922.blurb: Sixty people drown and hundreds are missing after a boat sinks on the Congo River near the village of Longola Ekoti, Mai-Ndombe Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Q105592508.name: 2021 Texas power crisis
Q105592508.blurb: Texas' worst energy infrastructure failure, the 2021 Texas power crisis, starts.

Q105659414.name: February 2021 Ecuadorian prison riots
Q105659414.blurb: Four simultaneous prison riots leave at least 62 people dead in Ecuador.

Q105690895.name: Zamfara kidnapping
Q105690895.blurb: A total of 279 female students aged between 10 and 17 are kidnapped by bandits in the Zamfara kidnapping in Zamfara State, Nigeria.

Q105694892.name: 2020–2021 U.S. troop withdrawal from Afghanistan
aliases: Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan
Q105694892.blurb: The last remaining American troops leave Afghanistan, ending U.S. involvement in the war.

Q105715701.name: 1741 Kanpō tsunami
Q105715701.blurb: The eruption of Oshima–Ōshima and the Kampo tsunami: At least 2,000 people along the Japanese coast drown in a tsunami caused by the eruption of Oshima.

Q105773158.name: Garowe attack
Q105773158.blurb: Ten people are killed in a bomb attack on a convoy carrying food supplies to a United Nations compound in Garowe in the Somali region of Puntland.

Q105774630.name: 2021 Mogadishu suicide car bombing
Q105774630.blurb: Twenty people are killed and 30 injured in a suicide car bombing in Mogadishu, Somalia.

Q105813896.name: 2021 Bata explosion
Q105813896.blurb: At least 108 die and 615 are injured in the 2021 Bata explosions in Bata, Equatorial Guinea.

Q105982031.name: 2021 Atlanta spa shootings
Q105982031.blurb: Atlanta spa shootings: Eight people are killed and one is injured in a trio of shootings at spas in and near Atlanta, Georgia, U.S. A suspect is arrested the same day.

Q105987834.name: Assassination of Talat Pasha
Q105987834.blurb: At his trial for the assassination of Talaat Pasha, viewed as the main orchestrator of the Armenian genocide, Soghomon Tehlirian was acquitted after arguing: "I have killed a man, but I am not a murderer."

Q106036727.name: 1906 Manasi earthquake
Q106036727.blurb: An Mw 7.9 earthquake strikes Xinjiang, China, killing at least 280.

Q106122126.name: 2021 Boulder shooting
Q106122126.blurb: Ten people are killed in a mass shooting in Boulder, Colorado.

Q106185868.name: 2021 Suez Canal obstruction
aliases: Ever Given grounding in Suez Canal
Ever Given grounding in the Suez Canal
Q106185868.blurb: A container ship runs aground and obstructs the Suez Canal for six days.

Q106317441.name: 2021 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix
Q106317441.blurb: At the season-ending Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, Max Verstappen overtook Lewis Hamilton on the final lap to become World Drivers' Champion.

Q106319526.name: 2021 Hualien train derailment
aliases: 0402臺鐵第408次車清水隧道重大鐵道事故
TRA's Train No. 408 at Qingshui Tunnel
北迴線太魯閣號列車出軌事故
Q106319526.blurb: At least 49 people are killed in a train derailment in Taiwan after a truck accidentally rolls onto the track.

Q106330459.name: April 2021 United States Capitol attack
aliases: April 2021 United States Capitol shooting incident
Q106330459.blurb: A Capitol Police officer is killed and another injured when an attacker rams his car into a barricade outside the United States Capitol.

Q106372191.name: Sinking of the Spanish trawler Sonia
Q106372191.blurb: The Spanish trawler Sonia sank in British waters after a five-hour chase by the Irish Naval Service patrol vessel Aisling, during which almost 600 shots were fired.

Q106434434.name: death and funeral of Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh
aliases: death of Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh
funeral of Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh
Q106434434.blurb: The funeral of Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, takes place at St George's Chapel, Windsor Castle.

Q106477445.name: killing of Daunte Wright
Q106477445.blurb: Twenty-year-old Daunte Wright is shot and killed in Brooklyn Center, Minnesota, by officer Kimberly Potter, sparking protests in the city, when the officer mistakes her pistol for her taser.

Q106504658.name: discharge of radioactive water of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant
aliases: Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant radioactive water discharge
Q106504658.blurb: Japan officially begins discharging treated radioactive water from the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant into the Pacific Ocean, sparking international concerns and condemnation.

Q106514963.name: 2021 Indianapolis shooting
Q106514963.blurb: A mass shooting occurs at a FedEx Ground facility in Indianapolis, Indiana, killing nine and injuring seven.

Q106617073.name: 1833 Bihar–Nepal earthquake
Q106617073.blurb: The great 1833 Kathmandu–Bihar earthquake causes major damage in Nepal, northern India and Tibet, a total of 500 people perish.

Q106651383.name: 2021 Meron crowd crush
Q106651383.blurb: Forty-five men and boys are killed in the Meron stampede in Israel.

Q106671436.name: Types Riot
Q106671436.blurb: In York, Upper Canada, members of the Family Compact destroyed William Lyon Mackenzie's printing press in the Types Riot after Mackenzie accused them of corruption.

Q106679021.name: Mansouri massacre
Q106679021.blurb: Two women and four children are killed after an Israeli helicopter fires rockets at an ambulance in Mansouri, Lebanon.

Q106696167.name: 2021 Mexico City Metro overpass collapse
Q106696167.blurb: Twenty-six people are killed and ninety-eight are injured after an elevated section of the Mexico City Metro collapses.

Q106752909.name: 2024 Senegalese presidential election
Q106752909.blurb: The 2024 Senegalese presidential election is held following anti-government protests.

Q106753709.name: 2022 Hungarian presidential election
Q106753709.blurb: 2022 Hungarian presidential election: The National Assembly of Hungary elects former minister for Family Affairs, Katalin Novák, as president of Hungary in a 137–51 vote, becoming the first female president in the country's history.

Q106768320.name: May 2021 Kabul bombing
Q106768320.blurb: A car bomb explodes in front of a school in Kabul, capital city of Afghanistan killing at least 55 people and wounding over 150.

Q106839672.name: Danish Civil Wars
Q106839672.blurb: The Battle of Grathe Heath ends the Danish Civil War.

Q106856793.name: Franco-German War of 978–980
Q106856793.blurb: Franco-German war of 978–980: Holy Roman Emperor Otto II lifts the siege of Paris and withdraws.

Q106859969.name: 1674 Ambon earthquake and megatsunami
Q106859969.blurb: An earthquake strikes the Indonesian island of Ambon. It triggers a 100 m (330 ft) megatsunami which drowns over 2,300 people.

Q106863147.name: Hermit's Welcome at Theobalds
Q106863147.blurb: Elizabeth I is entertained by the Hermit's Welcome at Theobalds.

Q106901219.name: 1968–69 Japanese university protests
Q106901219.blurb: In response to months of nationwide student protests, thousands of Japanese police stormed the University of Tokyo.

Q106920440.name: 1839 Coringa cyclone
Q106920440.blurb: A cyclone slams into south-eastern India.  An estimated 300,000 deaths resulted from the disaster.

Q106946734.name: Gansu ultramarathon disaster
Q106946734.blurb: Hypothermia kills 21 runners in the 100 km (60-mile) Gansu ultramarathon disaster in China.

Q106949910.name: Ryanair Flight 4978
Q106949910.blurb: Ryanair Flight 4978 is forced to land by Belarusian authorities to detain dissident journalist Roman Protasevich.

Q106951006.name: Stresa-Mottarone cable car disaster
Q106951006.blurb: A cable car falls from a mountain near Lake Maggiore in northern Italy, killing 14 people.

Q106959236.name: Tenmei eruption
Q106959236.blurb: Mount Asama erupts in Japan, killing about 1,400 people (Tenmei eruption). The eruption causes a famine, which results in an additional 20,000 deaths.

Q106991061.name: 2021 San Jose shooting
aliases: 2021 Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority shooting
Q106991061.blurb: Ten people are killed in a shooting at a VTA rail yard in San Jose, California, United States.

Q107017251.name: University of Georgia desegregation riot
Q107017251.blurb: Students at the University of Georgia rioted in an attempt to prevent the attendance of two African-American students.

Q107088359.name: Lonesome Cowboys police raid
Q107088359.blurb: The Lonesome Cowboys police raid occurs in Atlanta, Georgia, leading to the creation of the Georgia Gay Liberation Front.

Q107107935.name: 1946 North Vietnamese legislative election
Q107107935.blurb: The first general election ever in Vietnam is held.

Q107144649.name: 1987 Transkei coup d'état
Q107144649.blurb: Stella Sigcau, Prime minister of the South African Bantustan of Transkei, is ousted from power in a bloodless military coup led by General Bantu Holomisa.

Q107144852.name: Simla Deputation
Q107144852.blurb: A deputation of Muslim leaders led by the Aga Khan III met Indian viceroy Lord Minto to secure greater political representation, eventually leading to the founding of the All-India Muslim League.

Q107177113.name: Somaliland War of Independence
Q107177113.blurb: Somaliland War of Independence: The Somali National Movement launches a major offensive against Somali government forces in Hargeisa and Burao, then the second- and third-largest cities of Somalia.

Q107192473.name: disappearance of Etan Patz
Q107192473.blurb: Six-year-old Etan Patz disappeared on his way to school in New York City, and later became one of the first missing children to have his picture featured on milk cartons.

Q107212707.name: 2021 Shiyan pipeline explosion
Q107212707.blurb: A gas explosion in Zhangwan district of Shiyan city, in Hubei province of China, kills at least 12 people and wounds over 138 others.

Q107242471.name: Atlanta Eagle police raid
Q107242471.blurb: Members of the Atlanta Police Department conducted a raid on a gay bar, with patrons later alleging that their constitutional rights had been violated and the city agreeing to pay over $1 million in settlements.

Q107258217.name: Murder of Yvonne Fletcher
Q107258217.blurb: Metropolitan Police officer Yvonne Fletcher was shot and killed while on duty during a protest outside the Libyan embassy in London, resulting in an 11-day police siege of the building and a breakdown of Libya–United Kingdom relations.

Q107272389.name: 2021 Percy Priest Lake Cessna Citation crash
Q107272389.blurb: A Cessna Citation I/SP crashes into Percy Priest Lake in Tennessee, killing all six people on board, including actor Joe Lara and his wife Gwen Shamblin Lara.

Q107278283.name: murder of James Byrd Jr.
Q107278283.blurb: White supremacists murdered James Byrd Jr., an African American, by chaining him behind a pickup truck and dragging him along an asphalt road in Jasper, Texas.

Q107292932.name: Air France Flight 343
Q107292932.blurb: Air France Flight 343 crashes on approach to Yoff Airport in Senegal, killing all 63 aboard.

Q107304913.name: 1946 La Paz riots
Q107304913.blurb: After weeks of unrest, rioters lynched Bolivian president Gualberto Villarroel, desecrating and hanging his corpse in the streets of La Paz.

Q107337981.name: Surfside condominium collapse
aliases: Collapse of Surfside Champlain Towers South
Q107337981.blurb: A portion of a 12-story condominium building collapsed (aftermath pictured) in Surfside, Florida, United States, killing 98 people and injuring 11 others.

Q107342506.name: 1963 Poonch Indian Air Force helicopter crash
Q107342506.blurb: Five Indian generals are killed in a helicopter crash, due to collision with two parallel lines of telegraph cables.

Q107354956.name: Doha Agreement
aliases: Agreement for Bringing Peace to Afghanistan
The Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan which is not recognized by the United States as a state and is known as the Taliban
Q107354956.blurb: The United States and the Taliban sign the Doha Agreement for bringing peace to Afghanistan.

Q107410571.name: 2019–present Sri Lankan economic crisis
Q107410571.blurb: The 2022 Sri Lankan protests begins amidst Sri Lanka's economic collapse.

Q107431180.name: Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky Air Flight 251 (2021)
Q107431180.blurb: An Antonov An-26 operating as Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky Air Flight 251 crashes on approach to Palana Airport, killing all 28 aboard.

Q107442287.name: assassination of Jovenel Moïse
Q107442287.blurb: Haitian crisis: Haitian President Jovenel Moïse is assassinated in his residence in the capital of Port-au-Prince.

Q107483347.name: Blue Origin NS-16
Q107483347.blurb: American businessman Jeff Bezos flies to space aboard New Shepard NS-16 operated by his private spaceflight company Blue Origin.

Q107751208.name: Battle of the Nijmegen Salient
Q107751208.blurb: World War II:  the Germans commence a counter offensive to retake the Nijmegen salient, this having been captured by the allies during Operation Market Garden.

Q108063861.name: Plymouth shooting
Q108063861.blurb: Six people, five victims and the perpetrator are killed in Keyham, Plymouth in the worst mass shooting in the UK since 2010.

Q108091634.name: 2021 Haiti earthquake
Q108091634.blurb: A magnitude 7.2 earthquake strikes southwestern Haiti, killing at least 2,248 people and causing a humanitarian crisis.

Q108102583.name: Fall of Kabul
aliases: Collapse of the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan
Fall of the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan
Q108102583.blurb: Kabul falls into the hands of the Taliban as Ashraf Ghani flees Afghanistan along with local residents and foreign nationals, effectively reestablishing the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan.

Q108179464.name: 2021 Go North West strike
Q108179464.blurb: Bus drivers in Greater Manchester began an eleven-week strike, one of the longest in British transportation history.

Q108196142.name: assassination of Nikolay Bobrikov
Q108196142.blurb: Eugen Schauman assassinates Nikolay Bobrikov, Governor-General of Finland.

Q108274219.name: 2021 Kabul Airlift
Q108274219.blurb: During the 2021 Kabul airlift, a suicide bombing at Hamid Karzai International Airport kills 13 US military personnel and at least 169 Afghan civilians.

Q108285843.name: 2021 Kabul airport attack
aliases: 2021 attack at Hamid Karzai International Airport
Q108285843.blurb: During the 2021 Kabul airlift, a suicide bombing at Hamid Karzai International Airport kills 13 US military personnel and at least 169 Afghan civilians.

Q108397889.name: wedding of Princess Elizabeth and Frederick V of the Palatinate
Q108397889.blurb: Wedding of Princess Elizabeth and Frederick V of the Palatinate at Whitehall Palace, London.

Q108413429.name: The Masque of Indian and China Knights
Q108413429.blurb: The Masque of Indian and China Knights is performed by courtiers of James VI and I at Hampton Court.

Q108419092.name: 2021 Guinean coup d'état
Q108419092.blurb: The President of Guinea, Alpha Condé is captured by armed forces during a coup d'état.

Q108460025.name: Battle of Ronas Voe
Q108460025.blurb: The Third Anglo-Dutch War: The Battle of Ronas Voe results in the Dutch East India Company ship Wapen van Rotterdam being captured with a death toll of up to 300 Dutch crew and soldiers.

Q108543207.name: 1937 Brazilian coup d'état
Q108543207.blurb: Brazilian president Getúlio Vargas led a coup against his own constitutional government, establishing the dictatorial Estado Novo regime.

Q108547608.name: The London Pageant of 1621
Q108547608.blurb: The London Pageant of 1621 celebrates the inauguration of Edward Barkham (Lord Mayor).

Q108556410.name: Siberian Light Aviation Flight 51
Q108556410.blurb: Siberian Light Aviation Flight 51 crashes short of the runway at Kazachinskoye Airport, killing four.

Q108559655.name: Match of the Century
Q108559655.blurb: In rugby union, the "Match of the Century" is played between Wales and New Zealand at Cardiff Arms Park.

Q108570220.name: 1983 Upper Voltan coup d'état
Q108570220.blurb: Jean-Baptiste Ouédraogo, president of the military government of Upper Volta, is ousted from power in a coup d'état led by Captain Thomas Sankara.

Q108571743.name: 2021 Luxian County Earthquake
Q108571743.blurb: A 6.0 Mw earthquake strikes Lu County, Sichuan, China, killing three and injuring more than 88.

Q108601121.name: 2021 Cumbre Vieja volcanic eruption
Q108601121.blurb: The Cumbre Vieja volcano, on the island of La Palma in the Canary Islands, erupts. The eruption lasts for almost three months, ending on December 13.

Q108761711.name: 2025 German federal election
Q108761711.blurb: A snap election is held in Germany.

Q108803851.name: 1913 Studebaker strike
Q108803851.blurb: In Detroit, autoworkers for car manufacturer Studebaker went on strike in the American auto industry's first major strike action.

Q108809686.name: Coup of Gitarama
Q108809686.blurb: In Gitarama, Rwanda, local and other government officials initiated a coup to overthrow the monarchy and establish a republic.

Q108814962.name: 2021 Milan airplane crash
Q108814962.blurb: Eight people are killed in an airplane crash near Milan, Italy.

Q108857410.name: 1695 Linfen earthquake
Q108857410.blurb: The 1695 Linfen earthquake in Shannxi, Qing dynasty causes extreme damage and kills at least 52,000 people.

Q108860691.name: Siege of Ngatapa
Q108860691.blurb: Te Kooti's War: After surviving a five-day siege in the pā at Ngātapa, Māori leader Te Kooti escaped from New Zealand's Armed Constabulary.

Q108920010.name: 2019–2020 Spanish government formation
Q108920010.blurb: After 253 days without an operational government, a second round of investiture votes produced Spain's first coalition government since the Second Republic.

Q109116318.name: 2021 Rust shooting incident
Q109116318.blurb: Hannah Gutierrez-Reed is found guilty of involuntary manslaughter in the death of Halyna Hutchins on the set of the movie Rust, the first time someone has been found guilty for causing a death on a movie set.

Q109229623.name: 1790 Oran earthquake
Q109229623.blurb: A severe earthquake in northern Algeria causes severe damage and a tsunami in the Mediterranean Sea and kills three thousand.

Q109237454.name: 1716 Algiers earthquake
Q109237454.blurb: The 1716 Algiers earthquake sequence began with an Mw 7.0 mainshock that caused severe damage and killed 20,000 in Algeria.

Q109313008.name: 1923 Irish Hunger Strikes
Q109313008.blurb: After the Irish Civil War the 1923 Irish hunger strikes were undertaken by thousands of Irish republican prisoners protesting the continuation of their internment without trial.

Q109425626.name: 2021 Astroworld stampede
Q109425626.blurb: The Astroworld Festival crowd crush results in 10 deaths and 25 people being hospitalized

Q109466933.name: Marmaduke–Walker duel
Q109466933.blurb: General John S. Marmaduke fatally wounded his Confederate Army colleague Lucius M. Walker in a formal duel in Arkansas.

Q109536126.name: Death and funeral of Mindon Min
Q109536126.blurb: The state funeral of Mindon Min (pictured), who ruled Myanmar for 25 years, took place; his death was reportedly preceded by strange omens, and his senior princes were unable to attend as they had all been arrested.

Q109537808.name: Disappearance of Helena Andersson
Q109537808.blurb: Swedish woman Helena Andersson disappeared in Mariestad, one suspect were ”the man with the pilot glasses".

Q109564460.name: Taking of Encarnación
Q109564460.blurb: Paraguayan anarchists briefly seized the city of Encarnación as part of a larger plan to initiate a social revolution in the country.

Q109619944.name: impeachment trial of Andrew Johnson
Q109619944.blurb: The impeachment trial of Andrew Johnson adjourned after the second and third articles of impeachment did not obtain enough votes from the U.S. Senate to convict.

Q109629709.name: 2019 U.S. airstrike in Baghuz
Q109629709.blurb: Syrian civil war: The U.S. Air Force carried out an airstrike in al-Baghuz Fawqani, killing as many as 80, a disputed number of whom were civilians.

Q109666980.name: 2021 Waukesha Christmas Parade attack
Q109666980.blurb: An SUV plows through a Christmas parade in Waukesha, Wisconsin, killing six and injuring 62.

Q109762353.name: Massacre in Nicosia
Q109762353.blurb: Ottoman–Venetian War: After a 40-day siege, the Cypriot city of Nicosia fell to the Ottomans, leading to a massacre of more than 20,000 citizens.

Q109837841.name: Oxford High School shooting
Q109837841.blurb: A 15-year-old gunman murders four students and injures seven people, including a teacher, in a mass shooting at Oxford High School in Oxford Township, Michigan.

Q109857770.name: Siege of the Acropolis
Q109857770.blurb: Morean War: The Parthenon in Athens, used as a gunpowder depot by the Ottoman garrison, is partially destroyed after being bombarded during the Siege of the Acropolis by Venetian forces.

Q109922209.name: 2021 Semeru eruption
Q109922209.blurb: Semeru on the Indonesian island of Java erupts, killing at least 68 people.

Q110127853.name: 2021 Western Kentucky tornado
Q110127853.blurb: A widespread, deadly, and violent tornado outbreak slams the Central, Midwestern, and Southern regions of the United States. Eighty-nine people are killed by the tornadoes, with most of the fatalities occurring in Kentucky, where a single tornado kills 57 people, and injures hundreds of others. Another tornado in Edwardsville, Illinois strikes an Amazon warehouse, killing six workers.

Q110254389.name: prelude to the Russian invasion of Ukraine
aliases: Prelude to the Russian invasion of Ukraine (2022-present)
Q110254389.blurb: In the prelude to the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine Russian President Vladimir Putin declares the Luhansk People's Republic and Donetsk People's Republic as independent from Ukraine, and moves troops into the region. The action is condemned by the United Nations.

Q110269366.name: 1963 Indiana State Fairgrounds Coliseum gas explosion
Q110269366.blurb: Indiana State Fairgrounds Coliseum gas explosion: A gas explosion at the Indiana State Fairgrounds Coliseum in Indianapolis kills 81 people and injures another 400 during an ice show.

Q110281314.name: Mo So massacre
Q110281314.blurb: Burmese military forces commit the Mo So massacre, killing at least 44 civilians.

Q110413718.name: 2022 Kazakh unrest
Q110413718.blurb: Massive nationwide protests and unrest break out in Kazakhstan over the sudden increase of liquefied petroleum gas prices, leading to 238 people dead and thousands injured by January 11.

Q110516849.name: Golden Jubilee of George III
Q110516849.blurb: Golden Jubilee of George III is celebrated in Britain as he begins the fiftieth year of his reign.

Q110517257.name: 1994 South Pacific Airmotive DC-3 crash
Q110517257.blurb: A Douglas DC-3 ditches in Botany Bay after takeoff from Sydney Airport. All 25 people on board survive.

Q110555282.name: 1948 Columbia River flood
Q110555282.blurb: A dike along the flooding Columbia River breaks, obliterating Vanport, Oregon within minutes. Fifteen people die and tens of thousands are left homeless.

Q110567218.name: 2022 Hunga Tonga–Hunga Haʻapai eruption and tsunami
aliases: 2021-22 Hunga Tonga-Hunga Haʻapai eruption and tsunami
2021–22 Hunga Tonga–Hunga Haʻapai eruption and tsunami
2022 Hunga Tonga-Hunga Ha'apai eruption and tsunami
2022 Hunga Tonga-Hunga Haʻapai eruption and tsunami
2022 Hunga Tonga–Hunga Ha'apai eruption and tsunami
Q110567218.blurb: The Hunga Tonga-Hunga Haʻapai volcano erupts, cutting off communications with Tonga and causing a tsunami across the Pacific.

Q110588588.name: Prince of Wales riots
Q110588588.blurb: Rioting broke out in Bombay, India, during the visit of Edward, Prince of Wales, leading to at least 58 deaths.

Q110612748.name: Spanish colonization attempt of the Strait of Magellan
Q110612748.blurb: A naval expedition led by Pedro Sarmiento de Gamboa founds Nombre de Jesús, the first of two short-lived Spanish settlements in the Strait of Magellan.

Q110613097.name: Myanmar Civil War
aliases: Economic impact of the Myanmar civil war (2021-present)
Economic impact of the Myanmar civil war (2021–present)
International reactions to the Myanmar civil war (2021-present)
International reactions to the Myanmar civil war (2021–present)
Scam centres in the Myanmar civil war (2021-present)
Scam centres in the Myanmar civil war (2021–present)
၂၀၂၁-လက်ရှိ မြန်မာနိုင်ငံ ပြည်သူ့ခုခံတွန်းလှန်စစ်
Q110613097.blurb: Myanmar civil war: Burmese military and police forces killed at least 82 civilians in the Bago massacre, including people protesting a recent coup d'état.

Q110654542.name: 1988 Hargeisa-Burao offensive
Q110654542.blurb: Somaliland War of Independence: The Somali National Movement launches a major offensive against Somali government forces in Hargeisa and Burao, then the second- and third-largest cities of Somalia.

Q110663445.name: January 2022 Burkina Faso coup d'état
Q110663445.blurb: Mutinying Burkinabè soldiers led by Paul-Henri Sandaogo Damiba depose and detain President Roch Marc Christian Kaboré amid widespread anti-government protests.

Q110664430.name: July–September 2022 Conservative Party (UK) leadership election
Q110664430.blurb: Liz Truss is declared the winner of the UK Conservative Party leadership election, beating Rishi Sunak.

Q110664544.name: Battle of the Blacks
Q110664544.blurb: Battle of the Blacks: Uprising by the black African forces of the Fatimid army, along with a number of Egyptian emirs and commoners, against Saladin.

Q110685226.name: Canada convoy protest
aliases: Canada convoy protest class action lawsuit
List of Canada convoy protest people
List of people involved in the Canada convoy protest
Q110685226.blurb: Canadian truck drivers and pedestrians gathered to rally and protest on Parliament Hill against Canadian COVID-19 restrictions, which caused traffic and closures around the city.

Q110797840.name: Burning of British Embassy, Dublin
Q110797840.blurb: The Troubles: Protestors burned the British Embassy in Ireland following the massacre of 14 civilians in Derry by British forces.

Q110819505.name: death of Rayan Aourram
Q110819505.blurb: Five-year-old Moroccan boy Rayan Aourram falls into a 32-meter (105 feet) deep well in Ighran village in Tamorot commune, Chefchaouen Province, Morocco, but dies four days later, before rescue workers reached him.

Q110855140.name: Lunca massacre
Q110855140.blurb: Soviet border guards opened fire on civilians attempting to cross the border from the Soviet Union to Romania near Lunca, killing several hundred people.

Q110900949.name: 1994 Dronka lightning strike
Q110900949.blurb: A lightning strike ruptured three oil tanks near Dronka, Egypt, causing a flood that killed 469 people.

Q110970851.name: Siege of Bukhara (1220)
Q110970851.blurb: Mongol invasion of the Khwarazmian Empire: the city of Bukhara was captured and looted by the Mongol army of Genghis Khan.

Q110999040.name: full-scale Russo-Ukrainian war
aliases: List of military aid to Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian War
War of Resistance against Russian Aggression
Q110999040.blurb: Russian invasion of Ukraine: Russian forces captured the city of Sievierodonetsk, Ukraine, after six weeks of fighting.

Q111014904.name: Battle of Kherson
aliases: Battle for the Antonivka Road Bridge
Battle of the Antonivka Road Bridge
Q111014904.blurb: Russian forces capture the city of Kherson during the Russian invasion of Ukraine, which subsequently began the start of the Russian occupation and military-civilian administration in Kherson. Kherson is the only regional capital in Ukraine that Russia captured.

Q111017791.name: Siege of Mariupol
aliases: Alleged Russian war crimes in Mariupol
Media coverage of the Siege of Mariupol
Q111017791.blurb: Mariupol theatre airstrike during the siege of Mariupol.

Q111032472.name: 1819 Singapore Treaty
Q111032472.blurb: The Treaty of Singapore was signed by Sir Thomas Stamford Raffles, Hussein Shah of Johor, and Temenggong Abdul Rahman, and it is now recognised as the founding of modern Singapore.

Q111078529.name: Battle of Sievierodonetsk
Q111078529.blurb: Russo-Ukrainian War: The Battle of Sievierodonetsk ends after weeks of heavy fighting with the Russian capture of the city, leading to the Battle of Lysychansk.

Q111181270.name: 2024 Portuguese legislative election
Q111181270.blurb: 2024 Portuguese legislative election: Elections are held in Portugal for all 230 seats in the Assembly of the Republic. The Partido Socialista loses its absolute majority to the Partido Social Democrata, winning 77 and 79 seats respectively.

Q111214813.name: Siege of Knoxville
Q111214813.blurb: American Civil War: Siege of Knoxville begins: During the Knoxville campaign, Confederate forces under General James Longstreet besiege the city of Knoxville, Tennessee and its Union defenders led by General Ambrose Burnside.

Q111263729.name: 2022 Fukushima earthquake
Q111263729.blurb: A 7.4-magnitude earthquake occurs off the coast of Fukushima, Japan, killing 4 people and injuring 225.

Q111269621.name: Mariupol theatre airstrike
Q111269621.blurb: Mariupol theatre airstrike during the siege of Mariupol.

Q111291326.name: Siege of Beirut
Q111291326.blurb: Baldwin I of Jerusalem captures the city of Beirut from the Fatimid Caliphate with the help of a Genoese fleet.

Q111313251.name: China Eastern Airlines Flight 5735
Q111313251.blurb: China Eastern Airlines Flight 5735 crashes in Guangxi, China, killing 132 people.

Q111340197.name: 1966 Dayton race riot
Q111340197.blurb: Rioting erupted in Dayton, Ohio, resulting in one death and the mobilization of the Ohio National Guard.

Q111411145.name: Will Smith–Chris Rock slapping incident
aliases: Will Smith slaps Chris Rock at the Oscars
Will Smith-Chris Rock slapping incident at the 2022 Oscars
Q111411145.blurb: At the 94th Academy Awards, Will Smith slapped Chris Rock onstage resulting in Smith being expelled from the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences and banned from its events for ten years.

Q111443581.name: Aeroméxico Flight 111
Q111443581.blurb: Aeronaves de México Flight 111 crashes on approach to Guadalajara International Airport, killing 45.

Q111458253.name: Aragalaya
aliases: 2022 state of emergency in Sri Lanka
Q111458253.blurb: The 2022 Sri Lankan protests begins amidst Sri Lanka's economic collapse.

Q111515850.name: South Amboy powder pier explosion
Q111515850.blurb: A barge containing munitions destined for Pakistan explodes in the harbor at South Amboy, New Jersey, devastating the city.

Q111605785.name: sinking of the Moskva
Q111605785.blurb: Russian invasion of Ukraine: The Russian warship Moskva is struck by two anti-ship missiles and sinks into the Black Sea.

Q111686059.name: Russian occupation of Kherson Oblast
aliases: Russian occupation of the Kherson region
Q111686059.blurb: Russian forces capture the city of Kherson during the Russian invasion of Ukraine, which subsequently began the start of the Russian occupation and military-civilian administration in Kherson. Kherson is the only regional capital in Ukraine that Russia captured.

Q111699632.name: Black Week
Q111699632.blurb: British Army forces are defeated at the Battle of Colenso in Natal, South Africa, the third and final battle fought during the Black Week of the Second Boer War.

Q111711536.name: self-immolation of Wynn Bruce
Q111711536.blurb: American climate activist Wynn Bruce set himself on fire outside the United States Supreme Court Building in an apparent protest against the climate crisis.

Q111739148.name: death of David Oluwale
Q111739148.blurb: Hibiscus Rising, commemorating David Oluwale, is unveiled in Leeds.

Q111775084.name: Fun Lounge police raid
Q111775084.blurb: 109 individuals were arrested in a police raid on a gay bar near Chicago.

Q111868130.name: Sack of Basra
Q111868130.blurb: The Qarmatians of Bahrayn capture and pillage the city of Basra.

Q111944027.name: 2023 Ecuadorian general election
Q111944027.blurb: Ecuadorian presidential candidate Fernando Villavicencio was assassinated in Quito, eleven days before the general election.

Q111949600.name: Larnaca yacht killings
Q111949600.blurb: 3 civilians killed by alleged supporters of the Palestine Liberation Organization in Larnaca yacht killings.

Q111950342.name: 2022 Nobel Peace Prize
Q111950342.blurb: Ales Bialiatski, along with two organisations, Memorial & Center for Civil Liberties, are awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

Q111951161.name: Twosday
Q111951161.blurb: Twosday, the name given to Tuesday, February 22, 2022, at 2:22:22, occurs.

Q111951351.name: Great Mill Disaster
Q111951351.blurb: A dust explosion (depicted) at the world's largest flour mill in Minneapolis resulted in 18 deaths.

Q111954208.name: presidency of Mary Robinson
Q111954208.blurb: Mary Robinson took office as the first female president of Ireland.

Q111954714.name: First Feminist Congress of Yucatán
Q111954714.blurb: The first Feminist Congress of Yucatán (delegates pictured) began in Mérida, Mexico, to propose reforms for women's social, educational, and legal rights.

Q111968640.name: 2022 Kazakh constitutional referendum
Q111968640.blurb: A constitutional referendum is held in Kazakhstan following violent protests and civil unrest against the government.

Q111968653.name: killing of Shireen Abu Akleh
Q111968653.blurb: Palestinian-American journalist Shireen Abu Akleh is killed while covering a raid in Jenin. Israel eventually admitted and apologized for the murder, after initial denials.

Q111971343.name: 2022 State Opening of Parliament
Q111971343.blurb: Queen Elizabeth II misses the State Opening of Parliament for the first time in 59 years. It was the first time that a new session of Parliament was opened by the Prince of Wales and the Duke of Cambridge acting as Counsellors of State.

Q112016492.name: 2022 Buffalo shooting
Q112016492.blurb: Ten people are killed in a mass shooting in Buffalo, New York.

Q112039870.name: 2003 La Paz riots
Q112039870.blurb: Protesters in La Paz and the Bolivian government brokered a deal to end two days of rioting against a proposed salary tax.

Q112114966.name: Battle of Lysychansk
Q112114966.blurb: Russo-Ukrainian War: The Battle of Sievierodonetsk ends after weeks of heavy fighting with the Russian capture of the city, leading to the Battle of Lysychansk.

Q112123052.name: Robb Elementary School shooting
aliases: The sound of children screaming has been removed
Q112123052.blurb: A mass shooting occurs at Robb Elementary School in Uvalde, Texas, United States, resulting in the deaths of 21 people, including 19 children.

Q112163545.name: Tara Air Flight 197
Q112163545.blurb: Tara Air Flight 197 crashes in Nepal's Mustang District, killing 22.

Q112594135.name: 2022 Nobel Prize in Literature
Q112594135.blurb: Annie Ernaux is awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

Q112665883.name: Battle of Mount Street Bridge
Q112665883.blurb: Easter Rising: Battle of Mount Street Bridge.

Q112666390.name: June 2022 Afghanistan earthquake
Q112666390.blurb: An earthquake occurs in eastern Afghanistan resulting in over 1,000 deaths.

Q112683746.name: Castro Sweep
Q112683746.blurb: About 200 members of the San Francisco Police Department instigated a police riot in the Castro following a peaceful protest held by the political group ACT UP.

Q112695273.name: 2022 Oslo shooting
Q112695273.blurb: Two people are killed and 21 more injured after a gunman opens fire at three sites in Oslo in a suspected Islamist anti-LGBTQ+ attack.

Q112716652.name: coronation of Henry VIII and Catherine of Aragon
aliases: coronation of Henry VIII and Catherine
Q112716652.blurb: Henry VIII and Catherine of Aragon are crowned King and Queen of England.

Q112872244.name: 2023 Serbian parliamentary election
Q112872244.blurb: A series of mass protests began in Belgrade, Serbia, alleging electoral irregularities in the Serbian parliament and Belgrade city assembly elections.

Q112945260.name: 2022 United Kingdom government crisis
Q112945260.blurb: Boris Johnson resigns as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, and is replaced by Liz Truss. Their meetings with Queen Elizabeth II at Balmoral Castle were the Queen's final official duties before her death two days later.

Q112958123.name: 1033 Jordan Rift Valley earthquake
Q112958123.blurb: The Jordan Rift Valley earthquake destroys multiple cities across the Levant, triggers a tsunami and kills many.

Q112967003.name: assassination of Shinzō Abe
aliases: Death and funeral of Shinzo Abe
Death and state funeral of Shinzo Abe
Reactions to the assassination of Shinzo Abe
Q112967003.blurb: Former Japanese prime minister Shinzo Abe is shot and killed with an improvised firearm due to resentment against the Unification Church.

Q112976893.name: Sohagpur massacre
Q112976893.blurb: The Sohagpur massacre is perpetrated by the Pakistan Army.

Q113027451.name: 2022 Kherson counteroffensive
Q113027451.blurb: Russo-Ukrainian war: Ukraine begins its southern counteroffensive in the Kherson Oblast, eventually culminating in the liberation of the city of Kherson.

Q113213574.name: assassination of Louis Mountbatten, 1st Earl Mountbatten of Burma
Q113213574.blurb: The Troubles: the IRA ambushed and killed 18 British soldiers near Warrenpoint, and assassinated Lord Mountbatten on his boat at Mullaghmore.

Q113317674.name: 2024 Sri Lankan presidential election
Q113317674.blurb: Anura Kumara Dissanayake is elected as the 9th President Of Sri Lanka.

Q113482234.name: FBI search of Mar-a-Lago
aliases: Federal Bureau of Investigation's raid on Mar-a-Lago
Q113482234.blurb: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) executes a search warrant at former president Donald Trump's residence in Mar-a-Lago, Palm Beach, Florida.

Q113493424.name: Revolution of the Ganhadores
Q113493424.blurb: The Revolution of the Ganhadores begins in Salvador, Bahia, Brazil.

Q113495737.name: 2022 annexation referendums in Russian-occupied Ukraine
Q113495737.blurb: Voting begins in the five-day sham annexation referendums in Russian-occupied Ukraine, leading to Russian annexation of Donetsk, Kherson, Luhansk and Zaporizhzhia oblasts.

Q113512276.name: 2019 LSU vs. Alabama football game
Q113512276.blurb: The Alabama Crimson Tide and LSU Tigers football teams, both with undefeated records thus far that season, played in a "Game of the Century".

Q113514937.name: 2022 Yerevan explosion
Q113514937.blurb: An explosion destroys a market in Armenia, killing six people and injuring dozens.

Q113541286.name: 1935 SMU vs. TCU football game
Q113541286.blurb: A college football game between the SMU Mustangs and the TCU Horned Frogs became the first game in Texas to be broadcast nationally on radio.

Q113561887.name: coronation of James I and Anne
Q113561887.blurb: James VI and I and Anne of Denmark are crowned in Westminster Abbey.

Q113614536.name: 1977 Bab Tangal earthquake
Q113614536.blurb: The Ms 5.8 Bob–Tangol earthquake strikes Kerman Province in Iran, destroying villages and killing 665 people.

Q113634024.name: 1912 China typhoon
Q113634024.blurb: A typhoon strikes China, killing at least 50,000 people.

Q113642056.name: Battle of Dibrivka
Q113642056.blurb: Nestor Makhno and Fedir Shchus led insurgents to successfully ambush the Central Powers that occupied southern Ukraine during World War I.

Q113649166.name: Battle of Dunsinane
Q113649166.blurb: Siward, Earl of Northumbria, invades Scotland and defeats Macbeth, King of Scotland, somewhere north of the Firth of Forth. This is known as the Battle of Dunsinane.

Q113702347.name: German declaration of war on the Soviet Union
Q113702347.blurb: World War II: German minister of foreign affairs Joachim von Ribbentrop presented a declaration of war to the Soviet ambassador Vladimir Dekanozov in Berlin.

Q113711090.name: 2022 Saskatchewan stabbings
Q113711090.blurb: Ten people are killed and 15 are injured in  a stabbing spree in 13 locations on the James Smith Cree Nation and in Weldon, Saskatchewan.

Q113717492.name: 2022 Luding earthquake
Q113717492.blurb: At least 93 people die and 25 are missing after a magnitude 6.8 earthquake strikes Sichuan, China.

Q113835155.name: 1982 Guatemalan coup d'état
Q113835155.blurb: Guatemala's government, headed by Fernando Romeo Lucas García was overthrown in a military coup by right-wing General Efraín Ríos Montt.

Q113865480.name: 2022 Kharkiv counteroffensive
Q113865480.blurb: Russo-Ukrainian war: Ukraine begins its Kharkiv counteroffensive, surprising Russian forces and retaking over 3,000 square kilometers of land, recapturing the entire Kharkiv Oblast west of the Oskil River, within the next week.

Q113903966.name: Raid on Kronstadt
Q113903966.blurb: Russian Civil War: British motor torpedo boats raided the Bolshevik Baltic Fleet's home base of Kronstadt, sinking a depot ship  and damaging a battleship.

Q114051466.name: death of Jina Mahsa Amini
Q114051466.blurb: The death of Mahsa Amini occurred in Tehran, Iran, sparking worldwide protests.

Q114052430.name: 2022 Western México earthquake
Q114052430.blurb: A strong earthquake kills 2 and injures over 30 in Mexico's state of Michoacán.

Q114065797.name: Mahsa Amini protests
Q114065797.blurb: The death of Mahsa Amini occurred in Tehran, Iran, sparking worldwide protests.

Q114160017.name: Hurricane Ian
Q114160017.blurb: Hurricane Ian makes landfall in Cayo Costa State Park, Florida as a category four hurricane, killing 169 and doing $113 billion in damage, becoming Florida's costliest hurricane and the deadliest in 89 years.

Q114233610.name: Izhevsk school shooting
Q114233610.blurb: A mass shooting occurs at a school in Izhevsk, Udmurtia, Russia, resulting in the deaths of 18 people, including 11 children.

Q114258115.name: 2022 Phoenix shooting
Q114258115.blurb: Phoenix shooting: A man opens fire on pedestrians outside of a hotel in Phoenix, Arizona, resulting in the deaths of three people, including the perpetrator.

Q114350394.name: Kanjuruhan Stadium disaster
Q114350394.blurb: One hundred and thirty-five are killed in a human crush following a football match at Kanjuruhan Stadium in East Java, Indonesia.

Q114415247.name: Wedding of Mary I of England and Philip II of Spain
Q114415247.blurb: The royal wedding of Mary I and Philip II of Spain is celebrated at Winchester Cathedral.

Q114451635.name: Death and state funeral of Gamal Abdel Nasser
Q114451635.blurb: Egyptian President Gamal Abdel Nasser dies of a heart attack in Cairo.

Q114496074.name: Day of Eight Billion
Q114496074.blurb: The world population reached eight billion.

Q114501720.name: Creeslough explosion
Q114501720.blurb: Ten people are killed and eight are injured in an explosion at petrol station in Creeslough, Ireland.

Q114565318.name: Eurovision Song Contest 2024
aliases: Controversies of the 2024 Eurovision Song Contest
Controversies of the Eurovision Song Contest 2024
Q114565318.blurb: The 68th edition of the Eurovision Song Contest is held in Malmö, Sweden. Nemo from Switzerland win with their song "The Code", making them the contest's first non-binary winner.

Q114566133.name: 1990 Ciskei coup d'état
Q114566133.blurb: Lennox Sebe, President for life of the South African Bantustan of Ciskei, is ousted from power in a bloodless military coup led by Brigadier Oupa Gqozo.

Q114639536.name: 2022 Bratislava shooting
Q114639536.blurb: 2022 Bratislava shooting, killing 3 (including the perpetrator) and injuring one. The shooting occurred outside of a gay bar in Bratislava known as Tepláreň. Two people (excluding the perpetrator) died as a result of the shooting: Juraj Vankulič, a non-binary person, and Matúš Horváth, a bisexual man. The perpetrator (Juraj Krajčík) was found dead of a self-inflicted gunshot the morning after the attack.

Q114773654.name: Marash earthquake of 1114
Q114773654.blurb: A large earthquake damages the areas of the Crusaders in the Middle East. Antioch, Mamistra, Marash and Edessa are hit by the shocks.

Q114841701.name: Hpakant massacre
Q114841701.blurb: Myanmar civil war: Burmese military forces launched airstrikes that killed at least 80 concertgoers in Kachin State.

Q114896472.name: 1914 Kenwood House ball
Q114896472.blurb: Around 2,000 members of European society attended a ball at Kenwood House, England, in one of the last major social events before the outbreak of the First World War.

Q114912414.name: Itaewon Halloween crowd crush
Q114912414.blurb: At least 156 die at a crowd crush during a Halloween celebration in Itaewon district, Seoul, South Korea.

Q114926903.name: October 2022 Mogadishu bombings
Q114926903.blurb: At least 100 people are killed and over 300 are injured by a double car bombing in Mogadishu, Somalia.

Q114943882.name: 2022 Morbi bridge collapse
Q114943882.blurb: A pedestrian suspension bridge collapses in the city of Morbi, Gujarat, leading to the deaths of at least 135 people.

Q115009121.name: Warren Zevon on the Late Show with David Letterman in 2002
aliases: Warren Zevon on Late Show with David Letterman in 2002
Q115009121.blurb: After his terminal-cancer diagnosis, Warren Zevon made his last public appearance on the Late Show with David Letterman, giving the advice to "enjoy every sandwich".

Q115124248.name: Ethiopia–Tigray peace agreement
aliases: Agreement for Lasting Peace through a Permanent Cessation of Hostilities between the Government of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia and the Tigray People's Liberation Front
Q115124248.blurb: A peace agreement is signed between the Ethiopian government and the Tigray People's Liberation Front, ending the Tigray War.

Q115172927.name: liberation of Kherson
Q115172927.blurb: Russo-Ukrainian War: Ukrainian armed forces enter the city of Kherson following a successful two-month southern counteroffensive.

Q115186737.name: 2022 Dallas airshow crash
aliases: 2022 Wings Over Dallas airshow mid-air collision
Q115186737.blurb: A Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress and a Bell P-63 Kingcobra collide in mid-air over Dallas Executive Airport during an airshow, killing six.

Q115288121.name: 2022 University of Idaho Massacre
Q115288121.blurb: A mass stabbing occurs in Moscow, Idaho in which four University of Idaho students are killed in off-campus housing.

Q115301112.name: Colorado Springs nightclub shooting
Q115301112.blurb: A gunman kills five and injures 17 at Club Q, a gay nightclub in Colorado Springs, Colorado.

Q115301221.name: Byzantine–Venetian treaty of 1285
Q115301221.blurb: The Byzantine Empire and the Republic of Venice conclude a treaty. Apart from agreeing on a ten year truce, the Venetians are alloted a commercial quarter in Constantinople and are restored to earlier privileges.

Q115322003.name: 2022 Cianjur earthquake
Q115322003.blurb: A magnitude 5.6 earthquake on the Indonesian island of Java kills between 335 and 602 people.

Q115366568.name: 2022 Chesapeake shooting
Q115366568.blurb: A shooting at a Walmart in Chesapeake, Virginia leaves seven workers dead, including the shooter, and four others injured.

Q115460037.name: Captain America Comics
Q115460037.blurb: Captain America Comics #1, containing the first appearance of the superhero Captain America, is published.

Q115516667.name: Nihon Shōgakkō fire
Q115516667.blurb: Racially motivated Nihon Shōgakkō fire lit by a serial arsonist kills 10 children in Sacramento, California.

Q115519686.name: Cold War (1947–1948)
Q115519686.blurb: In Shostakovich v. Twentieth Century-Fox Film Corp., a New York trial court declined to issue a permanent injunction in favor of several Soviet composers against the distribution of The Iron Curtain, the first anti-Soviet Hollywood film of the Cold War era.

Q115521966.name: 1916 Berlin strike
Q115521966.blurb: First World War: Around 55,000 workers in Berlin went on strike to protest against the trial of anti-war campaigner Karl Liebknecht.

Q115557630.name: Rus Flight 9633
Q115557630.blurb: Rus Flight 9633 crashes during takeoff from Chkalovsky Airport, killing all 10 people on board.

Q115603322.name: Moore County substation attack
Q115603322.blurb: Massive power outage after Moore County substation attack that leaves 45,000 people without power for five days, leading to an FBI probe.

Q115629687.name: Calais Conference (December 1915)
Q115629687.blurb: World War I: Senior British and French figures, including prime ministers H. H. Asquith and Aristide Briand, met at Calais to discuss the future of the Salonika Front.

Q115629692.name: Calais Conference (July 1915)
Q115629692.blurb: First World War: The British and French prime ministers, H. H. Asquith and René Viviani, met at Calais to discuss future offensives including the Gallipoli campaign.

Q115681322.name: Qatargate
aliases: Qatar corruption scandal at the European Parliament
Q115681322.blurb: Members of the European Parliament, including Vice President Eva Kaili (pictured), and their associates are arrested in connection with the Qatar corruption scandal.

Q115726004.name: 2022 Batang Kali landslide
Q115726004.blurb: A landslide occurs at a camp at an organic farm near the town of Batang Kali in Selangor, Malaysia, trapping 92 people and killing 31.

Q115805260.name: SAETA Flight 011
Q115805260.blurb: SAETA Flight 011 crashes in Pastaza Province, Ecuador, killing all 57 people on board. The wreckage was not discovered until 1984.

Q115809087.name: 1755 Meknes earthquake
Q115809087.blurb: An earthquake in northern Morocco devastates the cities of Fes and Meknes.

Q115812564.name: Northwest Orient Airlines Flight 1-11
Q115812564.blurb: Northwest Orient Airlines Flight 1-11 ditches off Polillo Island in the Philippines, killing one person and injuring 44.

Q115816688.name: 1957 Farsinaj earthquake
Q115816688.blurb: The Mw 6.5 Farsinaj earthquake strikes Iran with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VII, causing at least 1,119 deaths and damaging over 5,000 homes.

Q115819756.name: Siege of Grave
Q115819756.blurb: The French garrison in Grave surrenders the town to a Dutch army after a difficult siege.

Q115821147.name: Battle of Fariskur
Q115821147.blurb: The Battle of Fariskur occurs during the Fifth Crusade.

Q115822001.name: January 2023 Speaker of the United States House of Representatives election
Q115822001.blurb: The longest U.S. House of Representatives speaker election since the December 1859 – February 1860 U.S. speaker election concludes and Kevin McCarthy is elected 55th Speaker of the United States House of Representatives.

Q115822564.name: wedding of Grover Cleveland and Frances Folsom
Q115822564.blurb: The wedding of Grover Cleveland and Frances Folsom (wedding depicted) took place in the White House, in the only time that a U.S. president has married in the building.

Q115822640.name: 9 January 1917 German Crown Council meeting
Q115822640.blurb: World War I: A meeting of the German Crown Council decided upon the resumption of unrestricted submarine warfare.

Q115857891.name: Bir Hakeim rescue
Q115857891.blurb: World War I: Hugh Grosvenor, 2nd Duke of Westminster led a force to rescue 92 prisoners of war from Bir Hakeim, killing the Senussi guards and their families.

Q115862152.name: coronation of Pope Paul VI
Q115862152.blurb: The coronation of Pope Paul VI took place, the last such ceremony before its abandonment by later popes.

Q115862489.name: 1945–1946 Charleston Cigar Factory strike
Q115862489.blurb: Workers at the Cigar Factory in Charleston, South Carolina, began a labor strike against the American Tobacco Company that lasted more than five months.

Q115867060.name: Delta Air Lines Flight 318
Q115867060.blurb: Delta Air Lines Flight 318 crashes near Marshall, Texas, killing 19.

Q115942630.name: 2025 Formula One World Championship
Q115942630.blurb: British racing driver Lando Norris wins the Formula One World Drivers' Championship in 2025 with McLaren.

Q115945951.name: Loddon Bridge disaster
Q115945951.blurb: Three people were killed when falsework collapsed during the construction of the Loddon Bridge in Berkshire, leading to reform of construction practices in the UK.

Q115978447.name: Exeter Theatre Royal fire
Q115978447.blurb: A fire at the Theatre Royal, Exeter kills 186, making it the UK's deadliest ever building fire.

Q116036702.name: 2005 Świnna rail crash
Q116036702.blurb: A passenger train from Sucha Beskidzka to Żywiec in Poland loses its brakes while on a steep downhill part of the route. It is stopped in a controlled collision in Świnna by a train travelling in opposite direction. 2 drivers and 6 passengers are injured.

Q116142022.name: 1995 San Diego tank rampage
Q116142022.blurb: Shawn Nelson steals an M60 tank from the California Army National Guard Armory in San Diego and proceeds to go on a rampage.
